structured_extraction.program_description: 22Beacon's Turnkey Development Program helps charter schools acquire, develop, and finance their facilities, with a pathway toward eventual facility ownership. The program is tailored to each school's unique educational model, student population, and budget, and covers the full process from initial planning and financing through construction.

Schools lease their facility through 22Beacon with the option to purchase. As of the page, 47 schools have exercised their purchase option.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facility acquisition, renovation, construction, and leasing with a pathway to ownership.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is based in Hanover, MD and serves charter schools nationally.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Catapult Fund is a flexible loan fund operated by 22Beacon (formerly Charter Schools Development Corporation) and the Equitable Facilities Fund (EFF) that offers customized, affordable financing to high-impact public charter schools traditionally underserved by conventional lenders. The fund focuses on breaking down financial barriers for schools serving economically disadvantaged students, with priority given to single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch. Loan products include bridge/pre-development loans, working capital loans, tenant improvement loans, and term loans, all at interest rates significantly below comparable market offerings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund offers four loan products: (1) Bridge/Pre-Development loans averaging $750K (max $3M) with terms averaging 12 months (max 24 months); (2) Working Capital loans averaging $250K (max $750K) with terms averaging 12 months (max 36 months); (3) Tenant Improvement loans averaging $1M (max $3M) with terms averaging 36 months (max 60 months); and (4) Term Loans averaging $2M (max $3M) with terms averaging 36 months (max 60 months). Interest rates are significantly below those of comparable market offerings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High-impact public charter schools traditionally underserved by conventional lenders, especially single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-development costs, construction, renovations, tenant improvements, working capital, and other charter school facility financing and growth needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide; contact 22Beacon to determine eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a public charter school
Priority given to single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch
Must serve economically disadvantaged students (focus population)
Must be underserved by conventional lenders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the linked application form at tfaforms.com/5159722, or contact 22Beacon to determine if Catapult is the right fit for your project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program funded by the Laurel Race Course Impact Fund, providing grants to nonprofit and community organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4)) that provide services and facilities benefiting communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course in Anne Arundel County. The program is administered by ACDS Inc. in partnership with Anne Arundel County, with applications reviewed by the LRCIF Advisory Board and a public comment period held in January.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000–$50,000 awarded annually to eligible nonprofit and community organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4)) serving communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course. Applications are reviewed by the LRCIF Advisory Board. FY27 applications closed December 17, 2025; FY27 grant terms run July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027 with budget approval expected June 2026 and agreement execution in Summer 2026. FY28 process will begin in December 2026. Historical funding pools: FY24 $393,000; FY25 $466,637; FY26 $357,143. Eligible uses include equipment purchase, supplies, capital improvements (renovation/remodeling/beautification), program expansion, and pilot programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation makes direct equity investments in innovative for-profit companies that create jobs in Baltimore City, offer social and economic benefits to the community, and provide above-market financial returns. The Foundation invests in both early-stage startups with proprietary innovations and mature companies expanding employment in Baltimore City. Investment focus areas include medical devices, diagnostics, materials, green energy, aerospace, and healthcare technologies. In addition to capital, the Foundation provides value-added support through its experience, knowledge base, and network of local and national connections. The Board of Trustees considers investment requests five times per year on a rolling basis. Applicants submit a company introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary, and a member of the finance team may follow up with questions or schedule a pitch meeting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Initial investments typically range from $150,000 to $500,000. The Foundation makes direct equity investments in startup companies with proprietary innovations and growth capital investments in mature companies expanding operations in Baltimore City. The Board of Trustees reviews investment requests five times per year on a rolling basis (2026 deadlines listed on program page). The Foundation prefers to co-invest alongside other sophisticated investors at closing. Beyond capital, the Foundation provides access to its experience, knowledge base, and local and national networks to support portfolio company success.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides grant funding to nonprofits, government agencies, and fiscally sponsored projects that operate programs in Baltimore City, working to enhance the quality of life in Baltimore. The program has two tracks: Small Grants (requests of $10,000 or less, reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline, decisions communicated within 60 days of submission) and Regular Grants (requests greater than $10,000, reviewed at one of five annual Board meetings per year on a set schedule). Grants support a range of activities including seed funding for innovative pilots and startups, ongoing community programs and services, capital improvements, general operating support, and outreach and advocacy efforts. First-time Small Grant applicants must attend an information session before submitting. First-time Regular Grant applicants must submit a letter of inquiry (LOI) before a full application. Past Regular Grants have ranged from $20,000 to $350,000. In addition to grant funding, the Foundation supports nonprofit partners through connections to local and national networks and the team's deep experience in Baltimore. Grants cannot go to individuals or for-profit businesses, and the Foundation typically does not fund scholarships, fellowships, sponsorships, deficit financing, endowments, or travel.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in two tracks: Small Grants of $10,000 or less (reviewed on a rolling basis, no deadline, decisions within 60 days) and Regular Grants of more than $10,000 (reviewed at one of five annual Board meetings per year, with deadlines posted on the website). Eligible uses include seed funding for startups, pilots, and research; ongoing project support; capital grants for construction, renovation, or equipment; general operating support; and outreach and advocacy efforts. Past grants have ranged from $20,000 to $350,000. Recipients must submit interim and post-grant reports including a narrative description of project outcomes and an accounting of funds expended. Grants cannot go to individuals or for-profit businesses, and the Foundation typically does not fund scholarships, fellowships, sponsorships, deficit financing, endowments, or travel.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides a limited number of mission-related investments (MRIs) to for-profit companies, impact funds, and nonprofits that have innovative ideas to create positive social or economic change in Baltimore City. MRIs take the form of loans, guarantees, equity investments, and limited partnership investments. The Foundation accepts below-market returns in exchange for meaningful mission impact and limited risk of capital loss. The Foundation also acts as a value-added partner, offering experience, knowledge, and connections to support portfolio investments. The Board of Trustees reviews investment requests five times per year, with annual deadlines posted on the Abell Foundation website.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Foundation provides concessionary (below-market) investments — which may include equity investments, loans, guarantees, limited partnership investments, or other capital — to organizations that demonstrate strong mission alignment and limited risk of capital loss. MRI investments to date have ranged from $1 million to $4 million, typically provided at below-market investment returns to leverage additional sources of catalytic capital. Returns are expected to be below market rate in exchange for substantial social or economic benefits. The Foundation prefers to invest alongside experienced financial professionals and to support strategies that thoughtfully mitigate risks of capital losses. Applicants submit a Company Introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary. The Board of Trustees meets five times per year to make funding decisions and notifies applicants of decisions in a timely manner.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; Board meets five times per year with annual deadlines listed on the Abell Foundation website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit companies, impact funds, and nonprofits located in Baltimore City or offering substantial benefits to Baltimore City businesses or residents, with innovative ideas for positive social, economic, or community change aligned with Abell Foundation priorities. structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation offers flexible, below-market or no-cost financing to nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and fiscally sponsored projects in Baltimore City. Program-Related Investments (PRIs) are one-time, catalytic investments designed to address a non-recurring funding need or unique capital challenge where the investment can make a significant impact. PRIs may take the form of low- or no-cost loans, loan guarantees that strengthen credit provided by outside lenders, or other financial instruments. Unlike grants, PRIs must be repaid, which allows the Abell Foundation to recycle the funds to support additional partners. Applicants begin with a letter of inquiry (LOI); if invited, they complete a full application. The Board of Trustees reviews PRI requests at one of five annual Board meetings each year, with applicants notified of decisions within one week of each Board meeting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible, low- or no-cost loans, loan guarantees, or other financial instruments that address a non-recurring funding need or unique capital challenge, including facility redevelopment or other one-time capital requirements. Loan guarantees may enhance credit provided by third-party lenders. PRIs are one-time, catalytic investments and must be repaid, enabling the Foundation to recycle capital to support additional nonprofit and community partners. Applicants must have identified and secured a source of repayment. Specific amounts and terms vary by project. Applications are reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings each year. Cannot be used to fund fundraising campaigns.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addressing a non-recurring funding need or unique capital challenge, such as facility redevelopment or other one-time capital requirements, where a catalytic investment can make a significant impact. Cannot be used to fund fundraising campaigns.

structured_extraction.program_description: The CleanTech Research & Development (CRD) Grant helps Allegany County-based for-profit businesses advance new environmental technology by subsidizing research and development costs contracted through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) Appalachian Laboratory. Businesses gain access to the lab's specialized equipment and expert scientists to develop, test, and refine products and services with environmental and economic impact. The grant provides a 1:1 (dollar-for-dollar) match for eligible research costs, paying the Appalachian Lab directly on behalf of the grantee. Awards are up to $50,000 per project (covering 50% of total project cost), with the fund capitalized at $100,000 at the beginning of each fiscal year. The fund supports companies in Allegany County's circular economy industry and broader environmentally-minded sectors, lowering the cost for companies to access the Lab's environmental science expertise to help shape their processes, products, and services.

Awards are subject to funding availability and are jointly selected by the Appalachian Lab and ACECD based on project alignment with research standards and availability of specialized scientists.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants submit a contact form on the program website or contact ACECD directly. A member of the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team will follow up to discuss the research project and facilitate contact with the Appalachian Lab. structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Expansion Deferred Loan Program (BEDL) provides forgivable loans to small for-profit businesses looking to expand or establish themselves in Allegany County. Loans range from $10,000 to $50,000 at interest rates better than traditional lenders. Up to 50% of the loan can be forgiven based on performance metrics defined by the applicant, such as job creation or increased export capacity. Payments can be deferred for up to six months after loan draw. The program supports businesses seeking to improve their products or services by purchasing essential equipment and other tangible assets that expand productive capacity. It helps new companies establish themselves in Allegany County and helps existing companies grow to create more jobs, increase their ability to sell products outside the area, or improve their local community presence.

structured_extraction.program_name: Allegany County Local Development Council Rocky Gap Slots Revenue Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Allegany County receives 5.5% of slot machine revenues from the Rocky Gap Casino and distributes a portion of those funds through the Local Development Council. Maryland law requires that 20% of that revenue be distributed as capital grants to Allegany County municipalities and nonprofits. The Local Development Council accepts applications annually and awards funds based on community impact and need. In 2024, a total of $534,668 was disbursed among 24 organizations out of 31 applicants; in 2025, the grant pool totals $540,000. A sub-committee of the Local Development Council reviews all requests and makes recommendations to the Allegany County Commissioners, who make the final awards. Awarded funds must be used for capital-related expenditures only (e.g., facility improvements, equipment, infrastructure); operating expenses are not eligible. Awards are announced and disbursed within approximately six weeks of the application deadline.

Award amounts vary and are determined by a sub-committee of the Local Development Council based on community impact and need, with final awards made by the Allegany County Commissioners. structured_extraction.program_name: American Tree Farm System (ATFS) in Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: The American Tree Farm System (ATFS) is a national program of the American Forest Foundation that certifies private forest landowners who commit to sustainable forestry practices. Maryland landowners who own 10 or more acres of forested land and have a written, implemented forest management plan can become certified Tree Farmers at no cost. Certified Tree Farmers receive free professional sustainable forest certification, access to a certified professional forester for periodic consultations, legislative updates affecting forest landowners, participation in national awards programs (including the National Tree Farmer of the Year contest), the right to display Tree Farm signs and certificates, and access to family forest action alerts and resources. There is no cost for membership.
structured_extraction.agency: American Tree Farm System / American Forest Foundation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free professional sustainable forest certification with no membership cost. Benefits include periodic free consultations and inspections with a certified professional forester, information on legislative issues affecting forest landowners, participation in the National Tree Farmer of the Year contest, the right to display Tree Farm signs and certificates, access to family forest action alerts and resources, and recognition through national awards programs. There is no monetary payment or cost-share component directly from this certification program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners in Maryland who own 10 or more acres of forested land and are committed to sustainable forestry practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable forest management certification and recognition; access to professional forester consultations; forest stewardship and management resources; legislative updates and advocacy information.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to private forest landowners throughout Maryland.

Must have a written and implemented forest management plan covering production of forest products, water quality, wildlife habitat, soil conservation, biodiversity, and recreation opportunities

Must meet the ATFS Standards of Sustainability including commitment to sustainable forestry, legal compliance, reforestation, air/water/soil protection, fish/wildlife/biodiversity conservation, forest aesthetics, protection of special sites, and conducting harvests according to a management plan
Must participate in a property inspection with an ATFS certified volunteer tree farm inspector on a five-year cycle

If your property meets the criteria, the State Tree Farm Committee will certify your woodland as a sustainably managed Tree Farm. You can also visit the American Tree Farm System website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annapolis Conservancy Board Conservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis Conservancy Board accepts donations of conservation easements on land with definite conservation or recreation value. Landowners donate a legal agreement to preserve their land in its natural state or enhance its environmental potential without transferring ownership. In return, landowners may receive a 15-year real property tax credit on the unimproved land, a reduction of federal estate taxes, and a reduction of federal income taxes for up to 6 years. The City manages the easement to preserve open space, provide recreational opportunities, and improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural and Woodland District Agreements

Agreements must be renewed every ten years to maintain the tax credit. Both agricultural districts (minimum 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture) and woodland districts (minimum 10 contiguous acres of woodlands) are eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Historic Preservation Tax Credit Program helps property owners offset the cost of rehabilitating historic landmark buildings in the county. Eligible owners can receive a property tax credit of 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses (or 5% for compatible new construction in a Landmark Historic District), applied against county real property taxes. The credit is capped at $50,000 and can be claimed over up to five years. If the annual credit exceeds the real property tax bill for that year, the credit may carry forward up to five years. The program applies to landmark properties and buildings that contribute to a Historic District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses for eligible historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for compatible new construction in a Landmark Historic District. The maximum total credit is $50,000, claimable over a 5-year period, applied against county real property taxes. If the annual credit exceeds the real property tax bill for that year, the credit may carry forward up to five years.

Qualifying work includes in-kind repairs, restoration, structural work, roof repair, masonry repointing, life-safety/ADA improvements, and professional fees. Non-qualifying work includes remodeling, appliances, landscaping, and permits.

Current Landmark Historic Districts include Davidsonville, Linthicum Heights, Owensville, and Woodwardville, plus districts determined eligible for the National Register: West Benning, Glen Burnie, and Odenton.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The process has four parts: (1) Submit Part 1 Certificate of Eligibility — OPZ responds within 30 days. structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's voluntary public financing program for candidates running for County Executive or County Council. For County Executive candidates: $6 per dollar for the first $50 of each qualifying contribution, $4 per dollar for the second $50, and $2 per dollar for the third $50, up to a maximum of $750,000 per election cycle. For County Council candidates: $4 per dollar for the first $50, $3 per dollar for the second $50, and $2 per dollar for the third $50, up to a maximum of $125,000 per election cycle. Qualifying contributions must be between $5 and $250 from county residents. The approved County budget for Fiscal Year 2025 appropriated $1 million to the Public Campaign Financing Fund.

For County Executive certification: collect at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling at least $40,000 from county residents
For County Council certification: collect at least 75 qualifying contributions totaling at least $7,500 from county residents
Each qualifying contribution must be between $5 and $250 from a county resident

May not be a member of a slate
Submit receipts for each qualifying contribution to the State Board of Elections
Treasurer must verify account balance matches MDCRIS

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Anne Arundel County Public Campaign Financing System Summary Guide. 2. Establish a Political Committee via the State Board of Elections electronic filing system (MDCRIS). 3. File a Notice of Intent to Qualify with the State Board of Elections by April 15 of the election year. 4. Open a publicly funded campaign account. 5. Collect the required number and amount of qualifying contributions during the qualifying period (beginning January 1 following the last election for the covered office and ending 45 days before the primary election). 6. Submit receipts via MDCRIS: complete contribution cards, log in to MDCRIS, upload receipts, and link receipts to campaign finance reports. 7. Submit a certification application to the State Board of Elections including a declaration, campaign finance report, and certificate of candidacy. 8. The Board must certify an applicant candidate no later than 10 business days after receiving required documentation. 9. If certified, the County Controller disburses matching public funds to the candidate's publicly funded campaign account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County may receive a credit toward their County real property taxes for the installation of qualified permanent stormwater management practices. Qualifying practices include rain gardens, permeable pavement/pavers, living shorelines, living roofs, sidewalk infiltration planters, bioretention installations, cisterns, and other permanent diversion and infiltration methods approved by the Department of Public Works. The credit applies to County real property taxes only and takes effect in the taxable year following submission of an approved application. Installed practices must pass a County inspection before the credit is approved, and the County retains the right to inspect the practice during the life of the credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: WPRF Credit Program, Appeal, and Stormwater Remediation Fee Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County offers stormwater fee relief programs for property owners subject to the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF). The WPRF Credit Program allows property owners to receive a credit of up to 50% on their annual stormwater fee by installing and maintaining qualifying stormwater management practices (best management practices, or BMPs) on their property — such as rain gardens, dry wells, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting systems, infiltration trenches, or disconnected impervious surfaces. Credits are calculated as: (Treated Impervious Area ÷ Total Impervious Area) × Treatment Value × 50% maximum. Full credit requires treating a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall; partial credit is available for lesser treatment. NPDES-permitted non-marina properties covering their entire site are eligible for the full 50% credit. Marinas can earn up to 25% for NPDES compliance and up to 25% for Clean Marina certification, for a combined maximum of 50%. Once approved, the credit renews automatically each year as long as practices remain in good repair. The credit can be combined with the Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit. Eligible properties include residential, multi-family, non-residential, NPDES-permitted non-marina properties, and certified Clean Marinas. A Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement must be signed by both the property owner and the County before the credit is approved. The WPRF Appeal Program allows property owners to challenge a WPRF bill they believe contains an error. Grounds for appeal include incorrect zoning classification, errors in impervious area calculation, mathematical errors, properties not subject to the charge, exempt property owners, incorrect identification of the property owner, or residential property in a non-residential zone. For HOAs, the total WPRF across all HOA-owned tax accounts is capped at the number of property tax accounts for homes/unimproved lots within HOA boundaries multiplied by 40% of the base rate. If upheld, the county adjusts the billed fee and may issue a refund check going back up to three years per Maryland State Code. A written decision is issued within 45 days of a completed appeal application. Denial of an appeal may be further appealed to the Maryland Tax Court under Article 24, §9-710. Additionally, residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship may apply for a full exemption from the stormwater remediation fee. Applicants must meet at least two qualifying conditions related to income assistance, disability benefits, or income criteria. Eligible property types include detached single-family dwellings, attached dwellings, multifamily residential properties, and mobile home park tenants with a valid lease. At least one property owner must be an occupant of the property. The hardship exemption must be applied for annually (deadline for Fiscal Year 2027 is December 31, 2026) and is administered by the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance under County Code §13-7-106 (Bill No. 2-13).
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners can receive a credit of up to 50% on their annual WPRF (stormwater fee), as capped by §13-7-107 of the Anne Arundel County Code. The credit percentage is calculated as: (Treated Impervious Area ÷ Total Impervious Area) × Treatment Value × 50% maximum. Full credit requires treating a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall; partial credit is available for lesser treatment. NPDES-permitted non-marina properties covering their entire site are eligible for the full 50% credit. Marinas can earn up to 25% for NPDES compliance and up to 25% for Clean Marina certification, for a combined maximum of 50%. A signed Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement between the property owner and the County is required before credit approval. Once approved, the credit renews automatically each year as long as practices remain in good repair. The credit can be combined with the Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit. For appeals, if upheld the county adjusts the billed fee and may issue a refund check; refunds can go back up to three years per Maryland State Code, with a written decision issued within 45 days of a completed appeal application. For HOAs, the total WPRF is capped at the number of property tax accounts for homes/unimproved lots within HOA boundaries multiplied by 40% of the base rate. Credit applications must be submitted by October 1st of the taxable year; appeals are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications postmarked after October 1 are still processed but credit is deferred to the following taxable year. Qualifying residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship may be fully exempted from the stormwater remediation fee; the hardship exemption must be applied for annually (deadline for Fiscal Year 2027 is December 31, 2026) and is submitted to the Office of Finance (taxcredits@aacounty.org).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the taxable year for credits; appeals accepted on an ongoing basis; December 31, 2026 (Fiscal Year 2027) for the financial hardship exemption
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County property owners subject to the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee or stormwater remediation fee, including residential, multi-family, non-residential, HOA, farm, marina, religious institution, school, condo, NPDES permit holder, and charitable nonprofit properties who have privately owned and maintained stormwater management controls, as well as residential property owners (including mobile home park tenants with a valid lease) experiencing substantial financial hardship, and any property owner wishing to appeal their stormwater fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (stormwater fee) by up to 50% for qualifying stormwater management practices; correction or elimination of the fee through appeal for incorrectly billed properties, including refunds up to three years back and HOA fee cap application; or full exemption from the stormwater remediation fee for qualifying residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within Anne Arundel County, Maryland subject to the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee. Program applies county-wide with no sub-county or municipal geographic restrictions, including properties in the city of Annapolis covered under the county program. For the financial hardship exemption, applicant must own (or, for mobile home park tenants, hold a valid lease for) residential property in Anne Arundel County, and at least one property owner must be an occupant of the property.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible property owner or person billed the stormwater fee in Anne Arundel County
Must implement proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls (qualifying BMPs)
Stormwater management practices must be privately owned and maintained
Practices must be located on land with the same owner as the parcel seeking credit (on the landowner's parcel)
Practices must pass a recent inspection by County staff verifying proper design, construction, and maintenance
Practices must provide water quality treatment (minimum of 1 inch of rainfall treated for full credit; partial credit available for less)

Practices must be designed, approved, constructed, and maintained in accordance with Anne Arundel County Standards, the Stormwater Management Practices and Procedures Manual, and/or the 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual
Property must be covered under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management or a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement
Stormwater practice must not be under an existing Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management (for the small-scale WPRF credit track where a new Agreement is required)
All property owners listed on the deed must sign the Credit Agreement
Agreement does not transfer to new property owners — new owners must enter a new agreement to continue the credit
For NPDES or Clean Marina track: property must be regulated under an NPDES permit with stormwater management controls and/or certified by Maryland DNR as a Clean Marina
For NPDES/Clean Marina track: supporting documentation includes MDE NPDES letter, SWPPP, site plan with BMPs, inspection/maintenance reports, and DNR certification as applicable

Credit applications must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year for the credit to apply that year; applications postmarked after October 1 are still processed but credit is deferred to the following taxable year
Applicant must submit photographs of practices and drainage areas, a site plan/sketch showing practice locations, and grading permit plans/stormwater management reports (if available)
Applicants must grant the County permission for site inspections
Projects required by law (e.g., as a condition of new construction) are eligible for the WPRF credit

Valid reasons for appeal include: incorrect residential tier, incorrect property classification, incorrect zoning classification, errors in impervious area calculation for non-residential property, HOA property with unapplied fee cap, mathematical error, exempt property, person billed does not own the property, or residential property in a non-residential zone
Applicant must declare information accuracy under penalty of perjury for appeals
DPW is authorized to inspect property and verify impervious surface area upon submission of appeal
Supporting documentation must be attached for appeals (plans, reports, photos, proof of ownership, proof of location, or proof of approved financial hardship exemption as applicable)
Tax account number and property address must be provided for appeals
Submit the appropriate appeal form: Form 13-1 (residential tier), Form 13-2 (incorrect classification), Form 13-3 (HOA cap), Form 13-4 (math/impervious surface error), or Form 13-5 (exempt status)
For the financial hardship exemption: must be a residential property owner (or mobile home park tenant with valid lease) in Anne Arundel County
For the financial hardship exemption: at least one property owner must be an occupant of the property
For the financial hardship exemption: must demonstrate substantial financial hardship

For the financial hardship exemption: must meet at least two of the following — (i) household income meets Maryland Fuel & Utility Assistance Program guidelines; (ii) household receives energy assistance subsidy; (iii) household member receives SSI or SNAP (food stamps); (iv) household member receives veterans or Social Security disability benefits
Financial hardship exemption must be applied for annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the WPRF credit: submit an online application form via www.aarivers.org or a paper application form to the Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works, Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration. Include photographs of stormwater practices, a site plan, and documentation such as grading permit plans or installation records. Paper applications must be mailed to 2662 Riva Road, MS 7409, Annapolis, MD 21401. Applications must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year; applications received after October 1 are still processed but the credit is deferred to the following taxable year. The County reviews completed applications and issues a written decision within 90 days. If approved, adjustments are made to the billed fee and any refund is mailed separately. No renewal application is required in subsequent years. For the small-scale WPRF credit track: submit a WPRF Credit application; the County will provide an unsigned draft Agreement specific to the property. All owners on the deed must sign and return a hard copy by mail. For appeals: submit an online appeal through the county website (www.aacounty.org/myannearundel or www.aarivers.org) or complete the appropriate paper form (Form 13-1 through 13-5 depending on the type of error) and mail to: Attn: WPRF Appeals, Anne Arundel County DPW, MS 7409, 2662 Riva Road, Annapolis, MD 21401. The county issues a written decision within 45 days of receiving a completed appeal application. If denied, the appeal may be further pursued at the Maryland Tax Court. Appeals are accepted on an ongoing basis. For the financial hardship exemption: complete the Stormwater Fee Substantial Financial Hardship Exemption Application form and submit annually by the December 31 deadline to Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401, or email to taxcredits@aacounty.org. If an email address is provided, a receipt confirmation will be sent within 10 business days. Established under County Code §13-7-106 (Bill No. 2-13).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to caregivers of older relatives, spouses, or grandchildren. Specific amounts not described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Easy Travel Access (ETA) Program, administered by the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities, provides discounted transportation to older adults and people with disabilities through two tracks: (1) ETA Taxi Voucher Program — eligible residents may purchase up to 15 voucher coupon books per month at $5.00 each (each book has a fare value of $10.00), redeemable at participating cab companies within Anne Arundel County for errands, grocery shopping, polling places, medical appointments, and other trips; and (2) ETA Rides-On-Demand — on-demand, door-to-door transportation by a professional driver in an appropriately equipped vehicle at approximately 50% of normal cost, with same-day service available with at least two hours' notice, covering trips within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excluding airport trips). The county provides a subsidy match of up to $75 per month per qualified participant under either program.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents receive a county subsidy of up to $75 per month. Under the Taxi Voucher track, residents purchase coupon books for $5.00 each with a $10.00 fare value (up to 15 books/month), redeemable at participating cab companies within Anne Arundel County. Under the Rides-On-Demand track, fares are offered at approximately 50% of normal cost; professional drivers provide door-to-door service within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (airport trips excluded); same-day service is available with at least two hours' notice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who are 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a documented disability that precludes use of public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized transportation costs including errands, grocery shopping, visiting polling places, medical appointments, and other local trips within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excluding airport trips).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The Rides-On-Demand service area covers Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (airport trips excluded).
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be 55 years of age or older, OR 18 years of age or older with a documented disability
Must be 18–54 years of age with a verifiable disability that precludes ability to use public transportation (for applicants in that age range)
Income at or below $1,255/month (single) or $1,703/month (with spouse)
Disability must be verified by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or qualified social agency program director; disability status (permanent or temporary) must be documented
Must provide a valid Maryland driver's license or MVA-issued state ID showing an Anne Arundel County address (or an MVA change-of-address card if address differs)
Applicants with disabilities aged 18–54 must provide a copy of their most recent SSI or SSDI award letter or a completed Disability Verification Form
Must submit a completed ETA Application and Liability Form
Must submit a completed ETA Order Form (Taxi Voucher or Rides-On-Demand) with payment by check or money order
Participant must sign liability/indemnification waiver
Participant is responsible for scheduling own trips and adhering to service provider requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at either the Heritage Complex (2666 Riva Rd, 2nd Floor, Annapolis) or the North location (7320 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie) during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.), or mail the completed ETA Application, Liability Form, Order Form, required documents, and payment to 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. An online application form may also be available on the Anne Arundel County website (note: the online form may periodically be closed to new submissions). A health care provider (physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or qualified social agency program director) must complete the Disability Verification Form on behalf of applicants with disabilities. Once eligibility is established, reorders for the Taxi Voucher Program require only the Order Form and payment. For Rides-On-Demand, once enrolled, contact the Rides-On-Demand reservations line to schedule rides.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home & Community Based Options Waiver Program (Community Options Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: Community Options Waiver provides services to enable adults 18 and older, whose care needs meet the requirements for nursing home placement, to live in a community setting. The waiver allows services typically covered by Medicaid only in long-term care facilities to be provided to eligible persons in their own homes or in assisted living facilities. The federal government waives certain requirements — such as the requirement that services be provided in a nursing facility — so the state can pay for covered services that allow eligible clients to remain in the community.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State pays for covered Medicaid waiver services — such as personal care, assisted living support, and other long-term care services — provided in the home or community setting rather than in a nursing facility, for eligible adults who meet nursing home level of care criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 and older who meet Medicaid long-term care admission criteria and whose care needs would otherwise require nursing home placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers services that allow eligible adults to live in their own home or an assisted living facility instead of a nursing home, including personal assistance and other community-based long-term care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County who meet eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must meet Medicaid long-term care admission criteria (medical and functional criteria for nursing home level of care)
Must meet Medicaid financial eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities for information on how to apply. Additional information is available through the Maryland Department of Health waiver programs page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Delivers two nutritionally balanced meals — one hot and one cold — to homebound residents who are unable to shop and cook for themselves. Meals are brought to the home Monday through Friday by a volunteer, including holidays. The program can accommodate special diets and serve recipients on a long-term or temporary basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two meals per day (one hot, one cold) delivered to the home Monday through Friday by a volunteer. Special diets can be accommodated. Service typically begins within a few days of application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with disabilities who want to remain in their homes but are unable to shop and cook for themselves.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily meal delivery to homebound residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents.
requirements_list: Must be unable to shop and cook independently
Must reside in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 222-4257 for more information. Service can usually begin within a few days of application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides referrals for free legal counseling, advice, and representation to older adults in Anne Arundel County through the Department of Aging and Disabilities' contracted legal services provider. Issues addressed include Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, housing, credit counseling, guardianship, age discrimination, unemployment, and other civil matters. Persons with issues not handled by the Law Project are referred to other sources of free or low-cost legal assistance.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal counseling, advice, and representation (or referrals to free or low-cost legal assistance) for eligible residents. All services are free, though contributions are welcome.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents age 60 and older, regardless of income or assets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal counseling, advice, and representation on civil matters including Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, housing, utilities, credit counseling, guardianship, age discrimination, abuse and neglect, and other civil issues.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Must be 60 years of age or older
No income or asset requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Department of Aging and Disabilities at 410-222-4257 for more information and a referral.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Family Caregiver Support Program (NFCSP) – Anne Arundel County Family Caregiver Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Family Caregiver Support Program provides grants and support services to family and informal caregivers who care for older adults, individuals with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, or children and adults with disabilities. The program recognizes the demands of caregiving and provides financial support through grants as well as non-monetary assistance. Services include information and referrals, help locating resources, temporary respite (relief) from caregiving responsibilities, supplies or devices to make caregiving easier, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible caregivers based on availability of funds to cover costs such as temporary respite care and supplies or devices that assist with caregiving. Payment is issued approximately 4–6 weeks after receipt of a W-9 form, a Funds Acknowledgement form, and grant approval. Additional non-monetary support includes information and referral services, help locating resources, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult family members and informal caregivers (age 18+) caring for individuals age 60 or older or individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders; and older relatives (age 55+) who are not parents providing care to children under age 18, or older relatives (including parents, age 55+) providing care to adults ages 18–59 with disabilities. The care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary respite (relief) care, supplies or devices to assist with caregiving tasks, and other caregiver support services including support groups, educational workshops, and informational resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Caregiver must be an adult family member or informal caregiver age 18 or older providing care to an individual 60 years of age or older, OR
Caregiver must be an adult family member or informal caregiver age 18 or older providing care to an individual of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, OR
Caregiver must be an older relative (not a parent) age 55 or older providing care to a child under age 18, OR
Caregiver must be an older relative (including parents) age 55 or older providing care to an adult ages 18–59 with disabilities
Care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County
Applicant must submit a W-9 form before payment is disbursed
Applicant must submit a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment is disbursed
Grant award is based on availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Family Caregiver Program by phone at (410) 222-4375/4339 or by email at caregiver_support@aacounty.org to learn about services and apply. If the care recipient is enrolled in a program with a case manager, assistance can be requested through that case manager. Applicants must submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment can be processed. Payment is issued approximately 4–6 weeks after approval.
