structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County ADA Office (within the Department of Aging and Disabilities) lends assistive technology equipment to people with disabilities — and those who support them — free of charge. Borrowers can take equipment home for up to three weeks or schedule a hands-on product demonstration with ADA staff. Equipment includes screen magnifiers, screen readers, communication devices, adaptive keyboards, and more. Staff can also help borrowers find programs to purchase equipment after the loan period ends. Applicants submit a request form online or contact the ADA Office directly to arrange a loan or demonstration.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities / ADA Office
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of assistive technology equipment (e.g., screen magnifiers, screen readers, communication devices, adaptive keyboards) for up to three weeks, or a free hands-on product demonstration with ADA staff. No purchase required. Staff also help identify and connect borrowers with resources to purchase equipment after the loan period ends.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents with disabilities, their families, county employees, professionals, and educators who work with individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing assistive technology equipment to support activities of daily living, workforce participation, communication, learning, and recreation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County employees, residents, their families, professionals, and educators who work with individuals with disabilities.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County employee, resident, family member of a resident, or professional/educator working with individuals with disabilities
Equipment may be borrowed for a maximum of 3 weeks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online request form with your name, phone number, address, and what you are requesting, or contact the ADA Office at (410) 222-4383 to identify available equipment, schedule a demonstration, or arrange a loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Powerful Tools for Caregivers (PTC) is an evidence-based six-week training course designed to support the well-being of family caregivers. Based on Stanford University's Chronic Disease Self-Management Program, the course meets for 90 minutes per week and teaches caregivers how to reduce stress, change negative self-talk, communicate more effectively, manage emotions, and make tough caregiving decisions. Originally developed for caregivers of adults with chronic conditions, the program now also includes classes for parents of children with special needs. The program is offered by multiple county agencies in Maryland, including Anne Arundel County and Howard County, and is available in free virtual (Zoom) and low-cost in-person formats.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities / Howard County Department of Aging and Independence
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free or low-cost six-week educational course (90 minutes per class session) providing family caregivers with practical self-care tools and skills. Topics include stress reduction, self-care strategies, managing negative self-talk, communicating with family and healthcare providers, managing emotions, and making tough caregiving decisions. Available virtually via Zoom and in-person. Participants also gain access to community resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesdays, January 20, 2026 - February 24, 2026 (Anne Arundel); check Howard County portal for current schedule
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers, including those caring for adults with chronic conditions and parents of children with special needs, in Anne Arundel County and Howard County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a six-week caregiver training course covering self-care strategies, stress reduction, managing emotions, communicating with family and healthcare providers, and making tough caregiving decisions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and Howard County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a caregiver for a friend, relative, or child with special needs, or know someone who is a caregiver
Registration required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anne Arundel County: Register online at mdlivingwell.org/hub or via the sign-up link provided, or contact Jennifer Jackson at agjack88@aacounty.org or (410) 222-4335. Howard County: Register online through the Howard County Active Communities registration portal, or contact Kathy Wehr at 410-313-5955 for more information about virtual participation options.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Re-Entry & Community Collaboration program provides holistic support services to formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County residents and those at risk of becoming justice-involved, including veterans and their families. The program connects participants to vocational training (automotive repair, CDL, HVAC, culinary arts and hospitality) leading to industry-recognized credentials, and offers a wide range of wraparound services including workforce development, GED preparation, mental health counseling, housing assistance, legal assistance, transportation, and more. The program is an inter-agency collaboration between the Department of Detention Facilities, the Health Department, the Department of Social Services, the Department of Family Services, and community partners including Anne Arundel Community College and Anne Arundel Workforce Development.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive vocational training in automotive repair, Commercial Driver's License (CDL), HVAC, and culinary arts and hospitality, with industry-recognized credentials upon successful completion. The program also provides transportation to training sites and wraparound support services including workforce development, GED preparation, mental health counseling, housing assistance, legal assistance, food assistance, drug and alcohol treatment, mentoring, life skills, and help obtaining identification documents. Services are available 24/7.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County residents, individuals at risk of becoming justice-involved, veterans and their families seeking community reintegration support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training leading to industry credentials; wraparound support services including housing, legal, food, health, mental health, transportation, GED, workforce development, and more.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County resident, at risk of justice involvement, or a veteran or family member of a veteran
Must complete the Re-Entry & Community Collaboration interest form to express interest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should complete the Re-Entry & Community Collaboration interest form available on the program's webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Road to Recovery Program - Inmate Addiction Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities and the Department of Health jointly provide substance abuse treatment and support services to sentenced inmates through the Road to Recovery Program. Services include methadone maintenance treatment, substance abuse assessments, release planning, family support, gender-specific support groups, peer support, community case management, and referrals to internal and community resources.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program provides methadone maintenance treatment, individual counseling, substance abuse assessments, release planning, family reunification support, gender-specific weekly support groups, peer support services, care coordination, vouchers for document retrieval, and referrals to community and internal programs. Post-release case management follows individuals for 30-60 days after release. Care coordinators follow individuals for a minimum of 6 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates at Anne Arundel County detention facilities who have substance abuse issues, particularly those who were on a community methadone program prior to incarceration or who meet eligibility criteria while incarcerated.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Methadone treatment, counseling, release planning, family support services, care coordination, peer support, and referrals to community resources for substance abuse recovery and re-entry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates housed at Anne Arundel County detention facilities (Ordnance Road Detention Center and JRDC). Post-release case management available to those who reside in Anne Arundel County after release.
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate at an Anne Arundel County detention facility
Must be assessed eligible for the program based on criteria and protocols
Methadone treatment available to those incarcerated while on a community methadone program or those who meet eligibility requirements while incarcerated
Post-release case management available to those residing in Anne Arundel County and requiring substance abuse treatment as a condition of probation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Correctional Unit Counselors screen and refer inmates for Addiction Services during the intake process as part of developing their Inmate Program Agreement (IPA). The Department of Health Addictions Counselor reviews referrals and determines appropriate services. Voluntary participation is available for some programs such as ADEPT at JRDC.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County can create a Special Taxing District to finance, refinance, or reimburse the cost of public infrastructure improvements — such as roads, sewers, water systems, parks, and transit facilities — that support economic development, quality growth management, or redevelopment goals. The County issues special obligation bonds to fund the improvements, then levies an annual special tax on properties within the district to repay the debt. The bonds carry no direct or indirect liability to the County.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Finance
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County issues special obligation bonds to fund public infrastructure improvements within the district. Outstanding debt must not exceed 33% of the appraised property value at bond issuance and must not exceed 10% once development is complete. An annual special tax is levied on properties in the district to cover debt service, reserves, and administration costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers seeking public infrastructure financing for development or redevelopment projects in Anne Arundel County. The district must be requested by at least two-thirds of real property owners by parcel count and assessed valuation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, extension, or alteration of public infrastructure including storm drainage, sewers, water systems, roads, bridges, streets, sidewalks, lighting, parking, parks, libraries, schools, transit facilities, solid waste facilities, and other related infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within defined geographic regions of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Proposed public improvements must meet all requirements of the Special Taxing District Act (Sections 21-501 to 21-523 of the Local Government Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland).
Proposed infrastructure must further goals of the County's General Development Plan and other adopted plans.
Proposed development must be consistent with the County's Comprehensive Zoning Plan and Anne Arundel County zoning and subdivision regulations.
Developer must have significant investment at risk relative to the bond amount.
Development and business plan must be sound, economically feasible, and have a high likelihood of success.
Development must remain economically viable throughout the bond term.
District debt must not exceed 33% of appraised property value at bond issuance, and not exceed 10% once development is complete.
Bond issuance must not adversely affect the County's credit rating.
Project must pose no direct or indirect liability to the County; developer must provide acceptable surety.
All documents must reflect that the County has no financial liability for present or future improvements.
Application must be completed in its entirety using the County's application form.
District creation must be requested by at least two-thirds of real property owners by parcel count and assessed valuation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the County's Special Taxing District application in full. The District review committee — including the Chief Administrative Officer, Budget Officer, Controller, Planning and Zoning Officer, Director of Public Works, Director of Programming, and County Attorney — evaluates the application. The committee recommends approval, denial, or revised terms to the County Executive and County Council. The County Council must hold a public hearing with at least 10 days' notice before creating a District.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credits & Exemptions (Anne Arundel County Overview)
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County has enacted several local property tax credits for the benefit of real property owners located within the county's jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple local property tax credits and exemptions available to eligible real property owners in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of real property located in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Emergent Grasses (Marsh Grasses) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County residents or community associations with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects can receive free emergent marsh grasses for planting in marsh areas along their shoreline. The program provides two types of marsh grasses — smooth cordgrass (Spartina alterniflora) and saltmarsh hay (Spartina patens) — selected based on shore position relative to tides and salinity. County personnel conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions before grasses are provided, assist with initial project planning, provide plant type guidance and spacing calculations, and coordinate with forestry/environmental sections. This program is a joint effort between the Department of Inspections and Permits (Forestry Division) and the Department of Recreation and Parks.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits, Forestry Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free emergent marsh grasses (smooth cordgrass / Spartina alterniflora and saltmarsh hay / Spartina patens) are provided to qualifying Anne Arundel County residents or community associations for planting in marsh areas as part of living shoreline or tidal projects. County personnel conduct a site visit to assess conditions prior to providing plants, assist with initial project planning, provide plant type guidance and spacing calculations, and coordinate with forestry/environmental sections.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Forestry Section, Department of Inspections and Permits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents or community associations with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects along creeks and rivers within Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting marsh grasses in tidal or living shoreline areas on the applicant's private or community association property as part of living shoreline or tidal restoration projects along creeks and rivers in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County residents and community associations only; plantings must be along creeks and rivers within Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident or community association
Must have a qualifying living shoreline or other tidal project along a creek or river in Anne Arundel County
Site visit by county personnel required to evaluate conditions
Applicant must identify specific waterway location for plantings
Proper permits required for any shoreline work beyond plantings
Vegetation Management Plan required if clearing within 100 ft of tidal waters
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application using the Apply Now form (PDF). Contact the Forestry Section at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org for more information. County personnel will conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions, assist with project planning, and provide guidance on plant types and spacing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works offers a Leak Adjustment as a courtesy benefit to utility customers who receive unusually high water bills due to plumbing leaks on their side of the meter. The adjustment reduces, but does not eliminate, excess water consumption charges resulting from an on-property plumbing leak. It may not be approved more than once every five years per property. Subsequent adjustment requests due to plumbing failure after an initial approval will not be considered.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A partial courtesy reduction of excess water consumption charges on a utility bill caused by an on-property plumbing leak. The adjustment reduces but does not eliminate the excess charges and may be approved no more than once every five years per property. Subsequent adjustment requests due to plumbing failure after an initial approval will not be considered. No specific cap or adjustment formula is publicly specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County water utility customers who have experienced unusually high water bills due to a verified plumbing leak on their side of the utility meter.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of excess water consumption charges resulting from an on-property plumbing leak. Approval is considered a courtesy to customers; no specific cap or adjustment formula is publicly specified.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within Anne Arundel County who are utility customers of the county.
requirements_list: Leak must be on the property owner's side of the utility meter (customer responsibility)
Repair must be completed before submitting the application
Must describe the type and location of the leak
Must provide the repair date
Must attach plumber's invoice OR, if DIY, sales receipt for parts plus a repair explanation
Customer must provide account/parcel number, routing number, and property address
For tenants: move-in or occupancy date must be provided
Adjustment may not be approved more than once every five years
Subsequent adjustment requests due to plumbing failure after an initial approval will not be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Leak Adjustment Request Form and email it to custserv@aacounty.org or mail it to Anne Arundel County Customer Service, P.O. Box 427, Annapolis, Maryland 21404. Contact Customer Service at (410) 222-1144 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-licensed Pre-K childcare program for children ages 3, 4, and 5 at the South County Recreation Center in Harwood, Maryland. The program operates Monday through Friday on days Anne Arundel County Public Schools are open. Activities include educational time using the MSDE-approved Frogstreet Curriculum, outdoor play, story and craft time, STEM learning, cooking, music, and a daily rest period. Full-time Pre-K care runs 9am–3pm, Monday–Friday at $460/month (2025-2026 school year). Part-time Pre-K care is also available (Mon/Wed/Fri, 9am–3pm). For Summer 2026, there is one four-week session (July 6–31, 2026) themed 'Worlds of Wonder', including AM snack, literacy, outdoor play, arts & crafts, rest time, and organized games.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Recreation & Parks, Child Care Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-licensed childcare provided at the South County Recreation Center for a fee. Full-time Pre-K care runs 9am–3pm, Monday–Friday at $460/month (2025-2026 school year). Part-time Pre-K care is also available (Mon/Wed/Fri, 9am–3pm). A fee schedule is available on the program website. Fees are subject to change throughout the fiscal year pending Anne Arundel County budget review and approval. Registration is first-come, first-served with a maximum capacity per center. For Summer 2026, there is one four-week session (July 6–31, 2026); payment for that session was due June 10, 2026. Early Bird registration opened February 6, 2026, and General Public registration opened February 9, 2026; both windows have closed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Early Bird: February 6, 2026; General Public: February 9, 2026 (both registration windows have closed as of May 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families in Anne Arundel County with children ages 3, 4, and 5 (as of June 22, 2026 for summer) seeking licensed Pre-K childcare during the school year or summer sessions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensed Pre-K childcare and early education services for children ages 3–5, including full-time and part-time care options, educational programming, outdoor play, STEM learning, cooking, music, arts & crafts, organized games, and field trips.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is located at 4510 Owensville Sudley Road, Harwood, MD 20776 (South County Recreation Center).
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3, 4, or 5 (as of June 22, 2026 for summer sessions)
Registration is first-come, first-served up to center capacity
Completed registration, registration fee, and all required forms must be received before the child's first day
An adult over age 18 with an email address must create an account online
Fees are subject to change throughout the fiscal year pending Anne Arundel County budget review and approval
Withdrawal results in loss of space and priority for subsequent years
Late pick-up and late payment fees apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online by creating an account at the Child Care portal (https://www.aacounty.org/departments/recreation-parks/child-care/), or apply in person or by mail to the Child Care Administrative Office. After registering online, download and submit the Required Forms for Admission along with the registration fee. Enrollment is not complete until all forms and fees are received. For Summer 2026, Early Bird registration opened February 6, 2026 (for current school-year families) and General Public registration opened February 9, 2026; both windows have closed. Payment for the Summer 2026 session was due June 10, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County Department of Recreation and Parks offers a state-licensed before- and after-school child care program for school-age children in kindergarten through 5th grade. The program operates at elementary school locations across the county and provides a safe, structured environment with activities including homework time, outdoor play, crafts, organized games, and community service projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Recreation and Parks
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly fee-based child care program with costs divided into ten equal monthly payments per school year. Fees are determined annually based on program costs and school hours. The first payment for 2026-2027 is due August 10, 2026. There is a $25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session. Fee schedule for 2026-2027 will be communicated to registered families in July 2026. Program includes meals (breakfast, lunch, supper, AM/PM/evening snacks) with CACFP enrollment noted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wait list registration opens to the public by region April 7–14, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 5 and older entering Kindergarten through 5th grade in Anne Arundel County for the 2026-2027 school year
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Before-school care (6:30am to school start) and after-school care (school dismissal to 6:00pm) at elementary school locations across Anne Arundel County, including meals and snacks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at elementary school locations throughout Anne Arundel County, organized by region: Southern, Central, Crofton/Davidsonville, Pasadena, North & West County, and Western Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Child must be at least 5 years old by the first day of school and entering Kindergarten through 5th grade
Child must be toilet trained and self-sufficient in restroom hygiene
State-mandated required forms for admission must be completed and on file on the child's first day, including a Health Inventory with physician's signature

Required admission forms include: Emergency Form, Health Inventory, Blood Lead Testing Certificate, Immunization Certificate (conditional), Acknowledgment of Policies form, Custody Orders (as needed), and medical authorization forms for medications/allergies/asthma/anaphylaxis/seizures as applicable
Emergency Form must be updated annually
Registration is first-come, first-served with a minimum and maximum per center
$25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session
Medical conditions, disabilities, or special needs must be noted on the registration form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account at the Child Care Registration Portal, add child(ren) to the account, and register for available spaces or the wait list by selecting location and session (AM/PM). Wait list registration for the general public opens online by region from April 7–14, 2026. Once offered a space, families must submit required admission forms (available at http://www.aacounty.org/departments/recreation-parks/child-care/forms-and-publications/) and make payment by August 10, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Holiday Sharing Program connects donors with seniors and families in need during Thanksgiving and Christmas. Eligible recipients receive food and/or gifts through donor matches or funds collected by the Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible seniors and families receive food and/or gifts donated by community members. Donors can be matched with a specific family or senior and deliver goods personally, or contribute a tax-deductible cash donation, gift card, or PayPal payment that the program uses to purchase food and gifts on recipients' behalf.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sign up form is now closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors (age 65 and older) and families who have received an invitation from the Department of Social Services and had active SNAP and/or TCA benefits prior to September 1st.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food and gifts for Thanksgiving and Christmas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible residents of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a senior (65+) or a family
Must have received an invitation from the Department of Social Services
Must have had active SNAP and/or TCA benefits prior to September 1st of the relevant year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible recipients are invited by the Department of Social Services. If you move or change phone numbers, contact the program at community.programs@maryland.gov or (410) 269-4462 to update your information.

structured_extraction.program_description: STEP provides sentenced inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) with educational instruction including General Education Development (GED), Pre-GED preparation, Adult Basic Education, Adult Literacy, and Advanced Life Skills courses. The program is offered in partnership with Anne Arundel Community College (AACC). Inmates at the Juvenile Regional Detention Center (JRDC) may also be referred to ORCC educational programming, provided they qualify for progression to ORCC.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Inmates are assessed using the Test of Adult Basic Education (TABE) and other tools, then placed in classes such as GED, Pre-GED, Adult Basic Skills, Advanced Life Skills, or Adult Literacy. An Individual Learning Plan (ILP) is developed and monitored for each participant. Literacy training (volunteer-led) is also available at JRDC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) in Anne Arundel County who are eligible to earn a GED; JRDC inmates may also be referred to ORCC programming if they qualify for progression to ORCC
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational instruction including GED preparation, adult basic education, adult literacy, and life skills development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and Juvenile Regional Detention Center (JRDC) in Anne Arundel County; JRDC inmates must qualify for progression to ORCC to access GED programming
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate at ORCC
Must be eligible to earn a General Education Degree (GED)
Must complete an education assessment (TABE, Maryland Adult Performance Program Competency-Based Assessment, and computer competency interview) as part of intake
JRDC inmates must qualify for progression to ORCC to participate in GED programming
Eligibility and referral tied to inmates' Individualized Program Assessments (IPAs) and progression criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All inmates at ORCC are referred for education assessment during intake. Based on results, inmates are placed on a Candidate's List for the next session. A Class Selection Meeting is held before classes begin to finalize placements. Once placed, an Individual Learning Plan (ILP) is developed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Trauma, Addictions, Mental Health and Recovery (TAMAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: The TAMAR Project offers individual and group trauma treatment, mental health assessment, and case management services to female inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) in Anne Arundel County. The program uses trauma-informed treatment combined with motivational counseling to help participants break cycles of severe trauma, chronic depression, and re-offending. Both pretrial and sentenced women identified as possible victims of abuse or trauma are eligible. Substance abuse education (a 32-hour workshop) and referral to treatment upon completion are also offered at ORCC and JRDC. Participation is voluntary.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides individual and group therapy, trauma-informed treatment, motivational counseling, and post-release case management services. Services are delivered by licensed clinicians. Participation is completely voluntary and available to qualifying female inmates at ORCC. Substance abuse education (a 32-hour workshop) and referral to treatment upon completion are also offered at ORCC and JRDC in cooperation with the Health Department.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Thomas Laue, Assistant Correctional Facility Administrator, ORCC
structured_extraction.program_audience: Female inmates (pretrial and sentenced) at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center who are identified as possible victims of abuse or trauma. Also serves qualifying sentenced and pre-sentenced inmates who abuse drugs or alcohol at JRDC.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Individual and group therapy, trauma-informed treatment, motivational counseling, mental health case management, post-release case management services, and substance abuse education (32-hour workshop) with referral to treatment upon completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and JRDC in Anne Arundel County. Eligibility is facility-based and custody-status-based.
requirements_list: Must be a female inmate (pretrial or sentenced) at Ordnance Road Correctional Center
Must be identified as a possible victim of abuse or trauma through initial screening or staff referral
Participation is completely voluntary
Substance abuse education component (32-hour workshop) available to qualifying sentenced and pre-sentenced inmates who abuse drugs or alcohol at JRDC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Initial screening occurs at admission to ORCC by medical services staff. Women identified as possible victims of abuse or trauma are referred to licensed clinicians for assessment and services. Facility staff may also make referrals. For substance abuse education at JRDC, qualifying inmates are referred through facility and Health Department coordination.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County utility customers can apply for a reduction in sewer charges for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub, provided the water did not enter the sanitary sewer system. Applicants are ineligible if they already received an excess sewer use credit for lawn watering or other outdoor water use in the same quarter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A reduction (credit) on the sewer charges portion of the Anne Arundel County utility bill for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub, as long as the water did not enter the sanitary sewer system. The specific credit amount is not stated on the page. Applicants cannot claim both an excess-use credit (e.g., lawn irrigation) and a pool credit in the same quarter.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 6 months of filling the pool (rolling, applicant-specific deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County utility account holders (residential property owners) who have filled a swimming pool or hot tub with county water
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of sewer charges for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub that did not enter the sanitary sewer system
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to customers with an Anne Arundel County utility account; Anne Arundel County only
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County utility customer
Must certify that the water used to fill the pool or hot tub did not enter the sanitary sewer system
Must complete and submit the Pool Verification Form within 6 months of filling the pool
New pools greater than 24 inches (above or in-ground) require a construction permit number on the form
Cannot claim both an excess sewer use credit (e.g., lawn irrigation) and a pool credit in the same billing quarter
Form requires pool dimensions, gallons filled, fill date, and building permit number if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Swimming Pool Verification Form (available in English and Spanish) within 6 months of the pool fill date. The form requires pool dimensions, gallons filled, fill date, building permit number (if new pool), and a sworn certification that water did not enter the sanitary sewer. Submit by email to pwcust00@aacounty.org or by mail to DPW Customer Relations, 2662 Riva Road, Suite 410, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows residential customers to finance all or a portion of the Capital Facility Connection Charge for water and/or sewer service through installment payment plans over 30 or 40 years. Payments are applied to repayment of bonds used to build public water or wastewater infrastructure. The current charge is $11,340, financed at a 4.8289% annual bond rate, with the current effective period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Customers can finance the Capital Facility Connection Charge ($11,340) through installment agreements over 30 or 40 years at a 4.8289% annual bond rate. The charge is billed annually with the Front Foot Benefit Assessment. Applicants may finance the full charge or make a partial payment and finance the remainder. Any remaining balance must be paid off at the time of property title transfer. Payments begin in January of the calendar year following execution of the agreement. The current effective period is July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Anne Arundel County who need to finance their Capital Facility Connection Charge for water and/or sewer service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Finance the Capital Facility Connection Charge ($11,340) for water and/or sewer service connections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residential customers served by the Bureau of Utility Operations. No explicit geographic restrictions stated beyond the county utility service area.
requirements_list: Must be a residential property owner with a water and/or sewer Capital Facility Connection Charge
Property address and tax account number required
Any remaining balance must be paid off at time of property title transfer
Tax account and SDAT cross-check verification by DPW Financial Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate installment agreement application form (30-year or 40-year for sewer, or 30-year for water). Select one of two financing options: finance the full charge or make a partial payment and finance the remainder. Sign and date the form and submit to Bureau of Utility Operations, Utility Operations Complex, 445 Maxwell Frye Road, MS 4266, Millersville, MD 21108. DPW Financial Services will verify the tax account. Copies are distributed to the Office of Finance, DPW Financial Services, and the property owner.

structured_extraction.program_name: EMS Fee for Service Transport Program – Financial Hardship Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: Non-county residents who were transported by Anne Arundel County EMS and cannot pay their transport charge due to financial hardship may apply for a waiver of those charges. The program supplements operational expenses for providing Fire, Rescue, and EMS services while giving relief to the general fund and taxpayers. Billing occurs post-transport after the patient reaches the hospital. County residents (including City of Annapolis residents) receive transport at no cost regardless of insurance status; non-county residents are subject to billing and may request a hardship waiver if uninsured.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A waiver (reduction or elimination) of EMS transport charges for non-county residents who demonstrate financial hardship. Eligibility requires income at or below 250% of the federal poverty line, or documented catastrophic hardship (severe illness/injury, loss of all income, homelessness). Partial adjustments and payment plans are also available as alternatives to a full waiver. Applicants must submit a completed Hardship Waiver Application with supporting documentation by mail or email.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-Anne Arundel County residents who were transported by Anne Arundel County EMS and are uninsured or unable to pay due to financial hardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver or reduction of EMS ambulance transport charges. Hardship waivers eliminate transport charges entirely for qualifying non-county residents. Payment plans are offered as an alternative. Reimbursement revenues flow to the General Fund and are used to maintain volunteer facilities, provide personal protective equipment and uniforms, fuel apparatus, fund training, and provide Length of Service Awards Program (LOSAP) stipends to volunteers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to non-residents of Anne Arundel County (including City of Annapolis) who were transported by Anne Arundel County EMS. Anne Arundel County residents receive transport at no cost regardless of insurance status. Out-of-county ambulances follow their own jurisdiction's billing policy under mutual aid agreements.
requirements_list: Must be a non-Anne Arundel County resident
Must have been transported by Anne Arundel County EMS
Must be uninsured (no insurance that can be billed for the charge)
Must demonstrate financial hardship: income at or below 250% of the federal poverty line, OR documented catastrophic hardship (severe illness/injury, loss of all income, or homelessness)

Must submit supporting documentation: last 90 days pay stubs, W-2s or unemployment stubs, recent tax return (1040/W-2), Medicaid/assistance applications, employer/welfare forms as applicable; or a notarized statement if no documentation is available
One application per EMS transport incident
Must meet eligibility criteria outlined in the Hardship Waiver Policy (income guidelines based on HHS poverty guidelines, updated annually)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the 'Request for Transport Fee Hardship Waiver' form and submit it along with supporting income documentation (pay stubs from last 90 days, W-2s, unemployment documents, tax returns, Medicaid/assistance applications, or notarized statement). Submit by mail to Anne Arundel County Fire Department, Attn: EMS Billing Manager, 8501 Veterans Highway, Millersville, MD 21108, or by email to fdemsbilling@aacounty.org. The Fire Department Billing Manager reviews within 20 business days and forwards a recommendation to the Fire Chief. The Fire Chief makes the final determination (approve, deny, offer payment plan, or adjust amount). The patient is notified in writing; denied applicants may request review with additional documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Fire Department, in partnership with the Anne Arundel Fire Safety Foundation, provides free smoke alarms and installation assistance to residents who cannot afford to purchase a smoke alarm or need help installing one. Visual smoke alarms for the hearing impaired are also available when state and federal grant funding allows.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke alarms provided and installed by Fire Department personnel. Visual smoke alarms for the hearing impaired are available when state and federal grant funding is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who cannot afford to purchase a smoke alarm or need help installing one, including the hearing impaired.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke alarm equipment and installation for eligible residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Must be unable to afford to purchase a smoke alarm or need assistance installing one
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your closest fire station for assistance, or contact the Public Education Office by email or phone.

structured_extraction.program_description: Private landowners can set up off-site mitigation banks by planting native trees on their property and selling reforestation credits to developers and other landowners who need to meet forest mitigation requirements for development projects. The bank owner plants trees, posts a security bond to ensure survival, and places the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement. In some cases, the bank owner can also preserve existing forested areas to satisfy portions of developers' off-site planting requirements. The program distinguishes between Critical Area and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private landowners plant native trees on their property and sell reforestation credits to developers or other landowners who have reforestation or afforestation mitigation requirements. The bank owner places the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement (such as a conservation easement) and posts a security to ensure tree survival. This can generate income for the landowner while preserving or creating new forests in Anne Arundel County. The program distinguishes between Critical Area and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in Anne Arundel County who want to earn income by planting native trees and selling reforestation credits to developers with mitigation requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees on private property to create reforestation credits that can be sold to developers and landowners needing to satisfy forest mitigation requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to private landowners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The program distinguishes between Critical Area and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.
requirements_list: Plant native trees on private property
Post a security bond to ensure tree survival
Place the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement
May also preserve existing forested areas to satisfy portions of off-site planting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Anne Arundel County Forestry Division at ipmailbox@aacounty.org or (410) 222-7442 for information on setting up a mitigation bank. A contact list of existing reforestation bank operators (including Critical Area and Non-Critical Area banks) is available from the county.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center Office and Work Spaces Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center, located at 41 Community Place in Crownsville, Maryland, offers affordable, flexible office and work spaces to local 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. The renovated facility opened May 1, 2025 and provides a collaborative work environment where nonprofits can build capacity and fulfill their missions. Space options include dedicated private offices, open-space cubicles, shared offices, shared cubicles, and hot desks (sporadic use), ranging from 36 to 312 square feet, with furnished and unfurnished options available. Monthly rates start at $1.10 per square foot per month ($13 per square foot per year) and range up to $3.00 per square foot per month, well below typical co-working rates. Amenities include Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, copy machines, parking, custodial services, and networking opportunities. Organizations sign a one-year license agreement with Anne Arundel County, which can be renewed twice before a new application is required. Priority is given to organizations where at least 75% of clients served are Anne Arundel County residents, those addressing health/wellness or social determinants of health, and small, minority-, or Veteran-led organizations. Space is best suited for administrative functions or tele-services, not in-person direct service delivery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market office and work space available at rates starting at $1.10 per square foot per month and ranging up to $3.00 per square foot per month ($13 per square foot per year), with furnished and unfurnished options available. Space options range from 36 to 312 square feet and include dedicated private offices, open-space cubicles, shared offices, shared cubicles, and hot desks (sporadic use). Monthly licensing fees cover utilities, maintenance, and access to amenities including Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, copy/shred machines, parking, custodial services, kitchenette, wellness room, and resource library. Shared meeting and event spaces are also available. Organizations sign a one-year license agreement with Anne Arundel County's Office of Real Estate, which can be renewed twice before a new application is required. Rates vary by space type and size.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County offers a real property tax credit to property owners who revitalize their commercially or industrially zoned properties in one of the county's designated Commercial Revitalization Areas (also referred to as Commercial Revitalization Districts), including the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. Qualifying activities include renovation or rehabilitation of an existing building, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment of a building site. The credit equals the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from qualifying improvements of at least $100,000, reducing County real property tax liability for up to five years (with an additional five years available for projects funded by at least $10 million in private funds). Property owners must apply within 120 days of receiving the notice of assessment from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The program was extended through April 21, 2032 by Bill No. 117-21 (following prior extensions by Bill No. 94-06, Bill No. 4-12, Bill No. 6-17). Designated areas span commercial corridors including Brooklyn Park, Glen Burnie, Pasadena, Riviera Beach, North Odenton, Maryland City/Russett, Ferndale, Linthicum, and Deale/Churchton.
