The credit is calculated and credited based on the total taxable assessment on conservation land. The credit is granted for a period of five taxable years after an application or continuation application is approved. Late applications (received after June 1) are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of conservation land in Anne Arundel County used for natural area preservation, environmental education, conservation promotion, public natural areas, or wildlife sanctuaries. Renewal applicants must use the Renewal Application form; first-time applicants must use the initial application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property tax liability on conservation land used for natural area preservation, environmental education, conservation promotion, public natural areas, or wildlife sanctuaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be conservation land in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Land must be used to preserve a natural area, for environmental education, to promote conservation, for maintenance of a natural area for public use, or as a wildlife sanctuary
Applicant must provide proof property meets the 'conservation land' definition
IRS verification of Land Trust qualification required (§ 3-2A-01 Natural Resources Article)
Copy of cooperative agreement between land trust and county required
Application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the taxable year beginning July 1 of that year; late applications roll to the next succeeding taxable year
Property subject to perpetual conservation easement donated to land trust on or after July 1, 1991, or subsequently acquired
Renewal applicants must use the Renewal (Continuation) Application form; first-time applicants must use the initial application form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Conservation Land Real Property Tax Credit Application (or Renewal Application for renewals) by June 1. Submit to taxcredits@aacounty.org or by mail to Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401. The form has two parts: Part A (applicant) and Part B (Land Trust representative). Supporting documentation required includes proof the property meets the conservation land definition, IRS verification of Land Trust qualification, and a copy of the cooperative agreement between the land trust and the county. Initial applications and some renewals are reviewed by the Office of Planning and Zoning. If mailing less than 14 days before the deadline, use a traceable form of delivery. TTY users may call 711.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit providing 100% of total Anne Arundel County real property tax on a dwelling for eligible permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, rescue workers, and surviving spouses of fallen officers/workers. The credit applies only to Anne Arundel County real property taxes on a legal residence occupied by no more than two families, and terminates if the applicant ceases to own or reside in the dwelling as a primary residence or is no longer permanently and totally disabled. Authorized under County Code § 4-2-309, most recently updated by Bill No. 89-23 (2023).
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% credit of total Anne Arundel County real property tax due on the eligible dwelling, based on the County Supervisor of Assessments' real property assessment. The credit does not apply to state taxes, other fees, or assessments. Applied after any mandatory credits, supplements, or deferrals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; rolling/ongoing submission to Anne Arundel County Office of Finance Tax Credits department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers (state/county/municipal/federal agencies per MD Public Safety § 1-101(c)), correctional officers (MD Correctional Services § 8-201(e), Anne Arundel County detention facility), career employees of fire/rescue/EMS entities, volunteer fire company or rescue squad members meeting MD Public Safety § 7-202(a) criteria, and surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers or rescue workers. Disability must arise from employment/service, excluding willful misconduct, substance abuse, or non-accidental occupational disease.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction (100% credit) of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on the applicant's primary dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and reside in a dwelling in Anne Arundel County, Maryland as their primary residence. Applicant or surviving spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland for the period specified under § 9-210 of the Tax-Property Article, State Code.
requirements_list: Must be permanently and totally disabled as adjudged by an administrative body or court of competent jurisdiction, with disability arising out of and in the course of employment or service
Eligible categories: disabled law enforcement officer, correctional officer, career fire/rescue/EMS employee, or volunteer fire/rescue member meeting MD Public Safety § 7-202(a) criteria
Surviving spouses of fallen officers/workers are also eligible
Disability must not arise from willful misconduct, alcohol/drug abuse, or occupational disease without accidental injury
Dwelling must have been owned at time of disability adjudgment or death
Dwelling must be acquired within the timeframe required under § 9-210 of the Tax-Property Article
Applicant must own and reside in the dwelling as their primary legal residence
Applicant or surviving spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland within the period specified under § 9-210 of the Tax-Property Article
Credit terminates if applicant is no longer permanently and totally disabled, ceases to own or reside in the dwelling, or (for surviving spouses) upon remarriage
Must submit completed, signed, and notarized application form from the Controller's office with verification of eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain the Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit application form from the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance Controller's office. Complete, sign, notarize, and return the form with required eligibility verification to the Tax Credits department. Renewal applications follow the same process. No specific deadline is stated; submission appears to be on a rolling/continuous basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses in Anne Arundel County. The credit reduces County real property tax liability (not State taxes or other fees) based on the veteran's VA disability rating: 50% of County property tax if the disability rating is 75% or higher, and 25% if the rating is 50–74%. Surviving spouses of qualifying veterans may also be eligible if they have not remarried and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces County real property tax liability (not State taxes or other fees) for qualifying disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. Credit is 50% of County property tax if the veteran's VA disability rating is 75% or higher, or 25% if the rating is between 50% and 74%. The credit is applied after any mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals. Annual re-application by April 1 is required each year to receive the credit. Note: this Anne Arundel County tax credit is separate from the State of Maryland exemption program administered by SDAT.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 annually (April 1, 2026 for FY 2027 cycle — deadline has passed; next cycle deadline April 1, 2027 for FY 2028)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with an honorable discharge and a permanent service-connected VA disability rating of 50% or higher (or 100% nonpermanent rating), and surviving spouses of disabled veterans who were receiving the credit at the time of the veteran's death, have not remarried, have federal adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less, and own and occupy the property as their legal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property tax liability on the applicant's primary residence in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own and occupy property as legal residence in Anne Arundel County. This is a county-level credit only and is not the State of Maryland exemption program (SDAT).
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran with honorable discharge from active U.S. military, naval, or air service (38 U.S.C. § 101) with a permanent service-connected VA disability rating of 50% or higher, or a 100% nonpermanent rating
OR must be the surviving spouse of a qualifying disabled veteran who was receiving the credit at the time of death and has not remarried
Surviving spouses must have federal adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less (based on the prior calendar year tax return)
Must own and occupy the property as legal residence in Anne Arundel County
Property must be occupied by not more than two families
Must submit application each year by April 1 to receive the credit for the upcoming fiscal year
Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year
This Anne Arundel County tax credit application is NOT for the State of Maryland exemption program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit Application (Year 1 Initial Application or Re-Application, for disabled veteran or surviving spouse) on or before April 1 each year. Applications received after April 1 will be treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year. Four forms are available depending on applicant type and whether it is a first-time or renewal application. Submit to: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401. Contact: taxcredits@aacounty.org or (410) 222-1748 (TTY: 711).

structured_extraction.program_name: Foreign Trade Zone Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit against County personal property taxes for personal property located in a foreign trade zone or subzone established under federal law within Anne Arundel County. The program is active through June 30, 2027 (extended by Bill No. 56-22).
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces County personal property tax liability for personal property located in a foreign trade zone or subzone within Anne Arundel County. Does not apply to operating personal property of a public utility. The program is authorized through June 30, 2027 per Bill No. 56-22.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought (e.g., June 1, 2026 for the next taxable year).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with personal property located in a foreign trade zone or subzone within Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County personal property tax liability for property located within a foreign trade zone or subzone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Personal property must be located in a foreign trade zone or subzone established under federal law within Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Personal property must be entirely located within a federal foreign trade zone or subzone within Anne Arundel County
Property must be within Anne Arundel County boundaries, Maryland
Must satisfy § 9-231 of Tax Property Article, State Code
Must satisfy Article 4 § 3
Does not apply to operating personal property of a public utility
Application must be filed on or before June 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
Applicant must obtain certification from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation showing taxable assessment value
Application must be submitted under oath with a perjury declaration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Foreign Trade Zone Personal Property Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Tax Credits division, by June 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought. The application must be submitted under oath with a perjury declaration. Applicants must also obtain certification from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation showing taxable assessment value.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time tax credit from County real property taxes for residential dwellings that use geothermal energy devices installed on or after January 1, 2009. Geothermal energy devices are heating or cooling systems that use ground loop technology. The credit equals the lesser of 50% of installation and materials cost (minus any federal/state grants or credits) or $2,500 maximum, and applies to the building improvement portion of real property taxes only.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time reduction of County real property taxes for residential dwellings with geothermal energy devices (ground loop heating/cooling systems) installed on or after January 1, 2009. Credit equals the lesser of 50% of installation and materials cost (minus any federal/state grants or credits) or $2,500 maximum. Applies to the building improvement portion of real property taxes only. Authorized under County Code § 4-2-310.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually (must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1); next deadline June 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Anne Arundel County who have installed geothermal energy devices (ground loop heating or cooling systems) on their residential dwelling on or after January 1, 2009.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time reduction of County real property tax liability on the residential building improvement, up to a maximum credit of $2,500 (the lesser of 50% of installation and materials costs minus federal/state grants or credits, or $2,500).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own a residential dwelling in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. All applications submitted to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance.
requirements_list: Must be a residential dwelling
Must use a geothermal energy device (heating or cooling device using ground loop technology)
Device must be installed on or after January 1, 2009
Application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1
If application is filed after June 1, the credit is disallowed for that year but treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year
Credit is a one-time credit per property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Geothermal Energy Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 annually. The application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1. Application form available at: https://www.aacounty.org/sites/default/files/2023-03/Geothermal_Tax_Credit_App.pdf

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Building Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit from County real property taxes for high performance buildings, as authorized by §9-242 of the Tax-Property Article of the State Code and implemented under Anne Arundel County Code §4-2-311. Available for both residential and commercial properties. The credit applies to the building assessment only (not the land) and lasts for 5 consecutive taxable years from the year of approval.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces County real property tax liability (on building assessment only, not land) for qualifying high performance residential and commercial buildings. Credit lasts 5 consecutive taxable years from the approval year and cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits. Residential tiers: LEED Silver or NGBS Silver = 40% of county tax on building (max $1,000/building/year); LEED Gold or NGBS Gold = 60% of county tax on building (max $2,000/building/year); LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald = 80% of county tax on building. Commercial tiers: LEED Silver or NGBS Silver = 40% of County property tax on building (max $20,000/building/year); LEED Gold or NGBS Gold = 60% of County property tax on building (max $40,000/building/year); LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald tier maximum not fully captured in source. Credit is non-renewable within the same application cycle but new applications are possible after expiration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually (application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of qualifying high performance residential or commercial buildings in Anne Arundel County. For residential applications, applicant must be the property owner(s) of record. For commercial applications, applicant must be the commercial property owner(s). No restriction on business type or industry for commercial properties beyond green certification requirement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property taxes levied on the building (not the land) for high performance residential and commercial buildings meeting LEED or NGBS certification standards. Credit applies for up to 5 taxable years. Building and systems must be regularly maintained to comply with the applicable standard.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Program applies solely to Anne Arundel County real property taxes.
requirements_list: Building must qualify as a high performance building under §9-242 of the Tax-Property Article of the State Code (Anne Arundel County Code §4-2-311)
Building must meet or exceed a qualifying LEED or NGBS certification tier (minimum Silver), with documentation of rating required
Credit applies to the building assessment only, not the land
Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits
Building and systems must be regularly maintained to comply with the applicable certification standard
Application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1
If application is filed after June 1, it is treated as filed for the next succeeding taxable year
If mailing application less than 14 days before the deadline, use a traceable form of delivery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate High Performance Building Property Tax Credit Application (Residential or Commercial) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1. If submitted after June 1, the application is treated as filed for the next succeeding taxable year. If mailing within 14 days of the deadline, use a traceable delivery method. Contact taxcredits@aacounty.org or (410) 222-1748 for questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property County Tax Exemption for Community or Civic Associations
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County has enacted several local property tax credits and exemptions for the benefit of real property owners located within the county's jurisdiction. Among these is an exemption from County real estate taxes for qualifying community or civic associations, in accordance with §4-2-201(b) of the Anne Arundel County Code. The property must be held in title by a nonprofit community civic association or corporation, dedicated by record plat or deed restrictions to the use of lot owners.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exempts qualifying community or civic associations from County real estate taxes under §4-2-201(b) of the Anne Arundel County Code (1985 Code, Art. 6, §§ 1-103, 1-104; Bill No. 93-88; Bill No. 4-98; Bill No. 23-04). The property must be held in title by a nonprofit community civic association or corporation, dedicated by record plat or deed restrictions to the use of lot owners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadline set in County Code; disclosed on application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit community or civic associations and corporations in Anne Arundel County seeking exemption from County real estate taxes on property dedicated to lot owners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination of County real estate tax liability for qualifying nonprofit community or civic associations whose property is dedicated to lot owners by record plat or deed restrictions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must qualify as a nonprofit community civic association or corporation under §4-2-201(b) of the Anne Arundel County Code
Title to the property must be held by a nonprofit community civic association or corporation
Property must be dedicated by record plat or deed restrictions to the use of lot owners
Submit proof of not-for-profit status (501(c)(3) determination letter)
Submit Maryland state real property record (via SDAT website)
Submit record plat showing dedication to lot owners
Submit deed showing dedication to lot owners
Submit narrative describing proposed use of the property
Submit signed certification under penalty of perjury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the standardized Real Property County Tax Exemption Community or Civic Association Application form and submit the following supporting documents: (1) proof of not-for-profit status (501(c)(3) determination letter), (2) Maryland state real property record from SDAT, (3) record plat showing dedication to lot owners, (4) deed showing dedication to lot owners, (5) narrative describing proposed use, and (6) signed certification under penalty of perjury. Submit by mail (traceable delivery recommended) to Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401, or by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org. Written notification of approval or denial will be provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Payment Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A deferral of County real property taxes for eligible homeowners in Anne Arundel County. Eligible homeowners include those who are at least 62 years old, permanently and totally disabled, or who meet income eligibility requirements, and who have lived in their dwelling for at least five consecutive years as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defers County real property tax payments for qualifying homeowners. The amount deferred cannot exceed the increase in County property tax from the date the homeowner elects to defer, and is capped based on minimum lot size required by zoning district. Deferred taxes are due at the end of a 50-year deferral period, upon death, or upon property transfer. Eligibility requires residing in the dwelling as principal residence for at least 5 consecutive years, combined gross income of $55,000 or less, and meeting one of: age 62 or older; permanently and totally disabled with qualifying federal benefits; or permanently and totally disabled as found by a County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually (applications must be received by June 1 of the taxable year to defer taxes for the succeeding taxable year beginning July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible homeowners in Anne Arundel County who are seniors, disabled, or meet income requirements and have lived in their home for at least 5 consecutive years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of County real property tax payments on residential property only. The amount deferred cannot exceed the increase in County property tax from the date the homeowner elects to defer, and is capped at the minimum lot size required by the zoning district (minimum: dwelling and curtilage per Supervisor of Assessments). Deferred taxes are repaid at end of the 50-year deferral period, upon death, or upon property transfer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own and reside in a residential property in Anne Arundel County, Maryland as principal residence for at least 5 consecutive years.
requirements_list: Owner or at least one owner must have resided in the dwelling as principal residence for at least five consecutive years

Must meet one of: age 62 or older; permanently and totally disabled and qualified for benefits under Social Security Act, Railroad Retirement Act, any federal act for US Armed Forces members, or any federal retirement system; or permanently and totally disabled as found by a County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health
Combined gross income must be $55,000 or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form with required documentation to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 of the taxable year. Required documents include: disability documentation or proof of age 62+ (if not using the age criterion), a valid Maryland government ID with current address, and a Maryland State Income Tax Return for the most recently available tax year. Applications may be submitted by mail (traceable delivery recommended) or by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org. TTY users may call 711.

structured_extraction.program_name: Religious Leased Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit from County real property taxes for the portion of commercially-zoned property leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or related office space in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces County real property taxes for the portion of commercially-zoned property leased, occupied, and used by a §501(c)(3) or (d) religious organization for public religious worship, educational purposes, or related office space. Does not apply to property used for profit or when the religious group no longer occupies the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Religious organizations certified under §501(c)(3) or (d) of the Internal Revenue Code that lease property in a commercial zoning district in Anne Arundel County for religious worship or educational purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property tax liability on leased commercial property used for religious worship or education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be in a commercial zoning district in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Religious organization must be certified under §501(c)(3) or (d) of the Internal Revenue Code
Property must be in a commercial zoning district
Property must be leased, occupied, and used exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support such purposes
Executed lease must be signed by both property owner and religious organization; lease must make religious organization contractually liable for the property
Credit does not apply to property used for profit or when the religious group no longer occupies the property
If application is filed after April 1, the credit shall be disallowed that year but treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Religious Leased Real Property Tax Credit Application by April 1 each year. Submit by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org or by mail to Office of Finance, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401. If mailing less than 14 days before the deadline, use a traceable form of delivery. Required attachments include an executed lease signed by both the property owner and the religious organization.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit from County real property taxes for eligible retired veterans who own a dwelling in Anne Arundel County. Applicants must be age 65 or older and have retired from military service. The credit equals 15% of County property tax imposed on up to $500,000 of assessed dwelling value, after mandatory credits/supplements/deferrals are applied. The credit is available for up to 50 taxable years total, subject to annual application.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces County real property taxes on a dwelling owned by an eligible retired veteran. The credit equals 15% of County property tax imposed on up to $500,000 of assessed dwelling value (after mandatory credits/supplements/deferrals are applied). Does not apply to State property taxes or other fees. Available for up to 50 taxable years per applicant, subject to annual renewal application. Authorized under Anne Arundel County Code § 4-2-318 and § 9-258(A)(3)(II) of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 each year (e.g., April 1, 2027 for tax year July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028). Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired veterans age 65 or older who are retired members of the uniformed services of the United States and own a dwelling in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property tax liability on the applicant's dwelling — 15% of County property tax on up to $500,000 of assessed value, applied after any mandatory credits, supplements, or deferrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own a dwelling in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years old before the start of the fiscal year

Must be a retired member of the uniformed services of the United States (including military reserves) as defined under applicable law (§ 9-258(A)(3)(II) of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland)
Must own a dwelling in Anne Arundel County
Must submit an application each year to receive the credit (Year 1 application for new applicants; renewal application for subsequent years, Years 2–50)
Must provide required documentation per the application
Credit available for a maximum of 50 taxable years per applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Retired Veterans Property Tax Credit Application on or before April 1 each year. New applicants use the Year 1 application; returning applicants use the renewal (Years 2–50) application. Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the following taxable year. Mail completed applications to: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD. Applications available from the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time tax credit from County real property taxes for residential dwellings that use solar energy equipment installed on or after January 1, 2007. Solar energy equipment includes collectors, photovoltaic arrays, solar panels, storage tanks, and all hardware that collects, stores, generates, or distributes energy using sunlight, including any device that uses solar energy to heat or cool the dwelling, generate electricity for use in the dwelling, or provide hot water.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time property tax credit equal to the lesser of 50% of the cost of solar energy equipment and installation (minus any federal or state grants received) or $2,500, applied to the County real property taxes on the dwelling only (not the land). Equipment must be installed on or after January 1, 2007 and includes collectors, photovoltaic arrays, solar panels, storage tanks, and all related hardware that uses sunlight to heat or cool the dwelling, generate electricity, or provide hot water.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually (applications received after June 1 are applied to the next succeeding taxable year beginning July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Anne Arundel County who have installed solar energy equipment on or after January 1, 2007.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time reduction of County real property tax liability (up to $2,500) for residential dwellings using solar energy equipment. The credit applies to the dwelling portion of the tax bill, not the land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own a residential dwelling in Anne Arundel County. No municipal or regional sub-limits; eligibility is tied to the County real property tax jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Must be a residential dwelling

Must use solar energy equipment (collectors, photovoltaic arrays, solar panels, storage tanks, or any device using solar energy to heat or cool the dwelling, generate electricity for use in the dwelling, or provide hot water)
Equipment must be installed on or after January 1, 2007
Credit is one-time per applicant/property (lifetime limit per property owner)
Credit equals the lesser of 50% of equipment and installation costs minus any federal or state grants received, or $2,500
Credit is applied to the dwelling portion of the property tax bill only, not the land

Application must be received on or before June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year beginning July 1; applications filed after June 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Solar Tax Credit Application by June 1 to be considered for the following taxable year. If filed after June 1, the application is applied to the next succeeding taxable year. If mailing close to the deadline, use traceable delivery.

structured_extraction.program_name: Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A permanent property tax credit for surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers, and disabled law enforcement officers and rescue workers, who own property in Anne Arundel County. The credit covers 100% of real property taxes on the qualifying dwelling. Eligible fallen officer/worker categories include state/local law enforcement, federal sworn officers, correctional officers, career fire/rescue/EMS personnel, and volunteer fire/rescue members. The death or disability must have arisen out of employment and must not be the result of willful misconduct, substance abuse, or non-work-related occupational disease. The credit terminates upon remarriage of the surviving spouse or if the officer/worker is determined to be no longer permanently and totally disabled.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% elimination of Anne Arundel County real property taxes on a qualifying dwelling owned by a surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker, or by a disabled law enforcement officer or rescue worker. The credit is applied after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals, and does not apply to state taxes or other charges. The credit ceases upon remarriage of the surviving spouse or a determination that the officer/worker is no longer permanently and totally disabled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No stated deadline; application process is ongoing with renewal provisions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers, and disabled law enforcement officers and rescue workers, who own and occupy property in Anne Arundel County as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction (100%) of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on the qualifying primary residence dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Systems of Care
structured_extraction.program_description: Systems of Care is a multi-tiered approach that connects children, youth, and their families in Anne Arundel County to community resources and supports. It offers a single point of entry where an Intake Coordinator helps families find local services including mental health care, food, housing, utilities, crisis or emergency services, mentoring, and parent training. Families with more complex or multi-faceted needs can be referred to Family Navigation services, where a Family Navigator works one-on-one with the family in their home and community to develop and implement an Individualized Action Plan, identify family strengths, and support self-sufficiency. Spanish-speaking navigators are available. Families with the most intensive needs can also be referred to Local Care Teams (CRICT for school-age children, Early Childhood CRICT for birth to age 5, BRICKIT for homeless families, VS Cares for crime victims) for individualized, team-based support.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County Partnership for Children, Youth and Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, individualized support to connect families to community resources. An Intake Coordinator screens callers and links them to appropriate services. Families with more intensive needs can be matched with a Family Navigator who develops an Individualized Action Plan and provides hands-on, in-home and community-based support to help families become self-sufficient advocates. Spanish-speaking navigators are available. Local Care Teams (CRICT for school-age children K–12, Early Childhood CRICT for children birth to age 5 especially those with developmental disabilities or special health care needs, BRICKIT for homeless families, VS Cares for victims of domestic violence, human and sex trafficking, and other crimes) hold one-hour meetings to create Action Plans and follow up to ensure needs are met.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigation and referral to mental health services, food, housing, utilities, crisis or emergency services, mentoring, parent training and education, development and implementation of an Individualized Action Plan, in-home and community-based support, advocacy skill-building, and connection to other community supports.

BRICKIT serves homeless families

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Systems of Care Resource Line at 1-800-485-0041, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. to speak with an Intake Coordinator. Federal law limits eligibility to manufacturing facilities, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, and certain energy projects. Application fee is $1,000 (credited against User Fee if approved/closed). User Fee for new projects is 1/8 of 1% per year of outstanding principal, payable as a lump-sum at closing or in annual installments.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 13-step process: (1) AAEDC is the initial contact point for all bond attorneys and banks. (2) Lender/underwriter submits underwriting package and Letter of Intent to AAEDC. (3) AAEDC makes a recommendation based on public benefit. Steps continue through internal agency review with approximately 10-day turnarounds, culminating in County Council review approximately 4 weeks from completed application submission. Application fee of $1,000 is required (credited against User Fee if approved/closed). Contact AAEDC's Vice President of Financial Services for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal 10-year program established by Congress in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury that offers tax incentives to encourage investors to reinvest unrealized capital gains into qualified Opportunity Funds dedicated to investing in low-income or underserved communities. Anne Arundel County has four designated Opportunity Zone tracts — one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park — considered economically distressed communities. The program offers three tax incentives: (1) temporary deferral of capital gains reinvested into an Opportunity Fund until the earlier of disposal or December 31, 2026; (2) a step-up in basis of 10% if held for 5 years and an additional 5% if held for 7 years, excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxation; and (3) permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains on investments held for at least 10 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tax incentives for investing through a qualified Opportunity Fund: (1) temporary deferral of capital gains until December 31, 2026 or earlier disposal; (2) step-up in basis of 10% after 5 years and an additional 5% after 7 years, excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxation; (3) permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains accrued after investment if the investment is held for at least 10 years.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment into low-income or underserved urban and rural communities through qualified Opportunity Funds located in designated Opportunity Zone tracts in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four designated Opportunity Zone tracts in Anne Arundel County: one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park. Program is national but this page focuses on Anne Arundel County locations.

Investment must be held for at least 5 years for 10% basis step-up
Investment must be held for at least 7 years for additional 5% basis step-up

Deferred gain must be recognized by December 31, 2026 or upon earlier disposal of the investment

structured_extraction.program_description: The VOLT Growth Fund (VGF) provides flexible loans of up to $100,000 to Maryland-based high-growth, innovative, and technology product companies to help them implement a go-to-market strategy and accelerate sales. The program features flexible underwriting standards and payment terms—including no interest or closing costs—designed to support revenue and workforce growth and facilitate future equity investment. Pre-revenue and minimal revenue companies may apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $100,000 with a term of up to 10 years. No interest or other closing costs. An interest recollection amount of 10% is due at the time of the event of recapture. The event of recapture is triggered when the company raises 5x the original loan amount in equity investment or after 5 years, whichever comes first. After the recapture event, the loan is repaid over 5 years in equal principal monthly payments. Collateral is a blanket lien UCC filing on assets. Personal guaranty required from all active owners with more than 20% ownership.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based high-growth, innovative, and technology product companies seeking to implement a go-to-market strategy and accelerate sales, including pre-revenue and minimal revenue companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing a go-to-market strategy and accelerating sales; growing revenue and workforce; facilitating future equity investment; supporting high-growth business operations and expansion.

Must have an innovative product
Strong management team in place with a proven track record of success
Product must be created/completed and ready to bring to market
Pre-revenue and minimal revenue companies may apply
Applicant must provide realistic financial projections showing cash flow positive within 12 months
Borrower must provide a business plan or investor deck showing pathway to growth and profitability
Personal guaranty from all active owners over 20% ownership
AAEDC will evaluate previous and prospective equity and debt investment to determine viability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the VOLT Growth Fund application portal at https://aaedc.submittable.com/submit/211934/volt-growth-fund. Prospective borrowers may also contact AAEDC directly through the website contact form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program providing up to $50,000 to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. Loans can be used for working capital, business vehicle purchase, equipment, leasehold improvements, and other business expenses that help increase revenue and profit. The program is managed by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) on behalf of the Maryland Department of Commerce, funded by 1.5% of video lottery terminal revenue from Maryland casinos. Eligible businesses must have under $500,000 in revenue, fewer than 10 employees, have graduated a business accelerator program such as the Inclusive Ventures Program, and have been in business for at least 2 years. Approximately half of the fund is targeted to businesses within a 10-mile radius of the six named Maryland casinos.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $50,000 at a fixed 2.00% interest rate. 5-year term with interest-only payments in year one, followed by 4 years of monthly principal and interest payments. No loan fees or closing costs. Approximately half of the fund is targeted to businesses within a 10-mile radius of the six named Maryland casinos (Maryland Live, Hollywood Park, Rocky Gap, Ocean Downs, MGM, Horseshoe).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, if funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland with under $500,000 in revenue, under 10 employees, that have graduated a business accelerator program (such as the Inclusive Ventures Program) and have been in business for at least 2 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, business vehicle purchase, business equipment, leasehold improvements, and other business expenses needed to increase revenue and profit, including starting, relocating, or expanding a business. Excluded uses include adult entertainment, gambling, guns, liquor, unlicensed massage, pawn, tanning, tattoo, residential/transient facilities, non-owner-occupied real estate, startup financing, R&D/new product development, and bank debt refinancing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary business location must be in Maryland. Program is administered by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation on behalf of the Maryland Department of Commerce. Approximately half of the fund is targeted to businesses within a 10-mile radius of the six Maryland casinos (Maryland Live, Hollywood Park, Rocky Gap, Ocean Downs, MGM, Horseshoe).
requirements_list: Must be a minority, woman, Veteran, or small business owner
Company must have under $500,000 in revenue and under 10 employees
Must have successfully graduated a business accelerator program (such as the Inclusive Ventures Program)
Must be in business for at least 2 years
Primary business location must be in Maryland
Company must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Personal guaranty required from all owners with more than 20% ownership
Guarantors must have a minimum credit score of 600 with all accounts current
UCC filing against business assets required

Must submit VOLT application through Submittable, 2024 business tax returns, 2024 personal tax returns, personal financial statement for any owner over 20%, and financial projections showing ability to service the debt
Must provide a breakdown of use of funds with an expansion plan and financial projections showing the effect of funding on business profitability

Ineligible uses include adult entertainment, gambling, guns, liquor, unlicensed massage, pawn, tanning, tattoo, residential/transient facilities, non-owner-occupied real estate, startup financing, R&D/new product development, and bank debt refinancing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a VOLT application online through Submittable along with 2024 business tax returns, 2024 personal tax returns, personal financial statement for any owner over 20%, and financial projections. The fund accepts applications on a rolling basis if funding is available. Contact the AAEDC finance team for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Anne Arundel County farmers and agribusiness owners legally dispose of tires used in farming operations. Because county law prohibits farmers from disposing of agricultural tires the same way as automobile tires, agribusiness owners can bring their scrap tires to T&C Farm, where a collection trailer is available for drop-off. The program is sponsored by the Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau, the county's Soil Conservation District, T&C Farm Services, the Maryland Department of the Environment, and Maryland Environmental Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Agribusiness owners may drop off agricultural scrap tires at T&C Farm, where a collection trailer is available, providing a legal pathway to dispose of tires used in farming operations. This would otherwise be prohibited under county law. The program is sponsored by the Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau, the county's Soil Conservation District, T&C Farm Services, the Maryland Department of the Environment, and Maryland Environmental Service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County agribusiness owners and farmers who need to dispose of tires used in farming operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of scrap tires used in farming operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farmers and agribusiness owners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an agribusiness owner or farmer in Anne Arundel County
Tires must be agricultural tires used in farming operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Bring scrap tires to T&C Farm where a collection trailer is available for drop-off. Contact AAEDC's agricultural representatives for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Childcare Providers Support Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to licensed childcare businesses in Anne Arundel County that experienced significant enrollment decreases due to COVID-19. The program provides working capital to cover operating expenses and pandemic-related costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to cover operating expenses such as rent, payroll, utilities, PPE purchases, sanitary space improvements, and online communications and learning. Grant amount determined by business size and funding availability. Cannot be used for expenses already covered by other COVID-19 relief programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family childcare homes and childcare centers in Anne Arundel County that were open before March 13, 2020 and experienced significant enrollment decreases. Priority given to providers serving low-income communities, childcare desert communities, or children with special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses including rent, payroll, utilities, PPE, sanitary space costs, and online communications and learning tools. Cannot be used for expenses covered by other government COVID-19 programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must have been open and operating prior to March 13, 2020
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must submit a copy of its license issued through the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and a signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through a portal on the AAEDC website. Businesses create an account and complete the entire application process online. Application period was expected to open in early October 2020.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arundel Agricultural Business Improvement Grant (ABIG) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Matching grant program that helps farm-based businesses and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County expand their operations. Awards matching grants of up to $10,000 to fund approved projects such as fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment, and infrastructure upgrades. Applicant must provide a one-to-one match of their own funds equal to the grant amount requested. Applications are scored on their ability to increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations, increase efficiency, and/or provide agricultural education opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $10,000. Applicant must provide a one-to-one match of their own funds equal to the grant amount requested (e.g., a $5,000 grant requires $5,000 from the applicant). Matching funds may not include in-kind labor or state and federal grants or cost-share. Proof of project completion is due within the year of the grant award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farm-based businesses and commercial watermen who are Anne Arundel County residents and either own or operate a farm that is agriculturally tax assessed by the State of Maryland, or hold a Commercial TFL License with a vessel docked in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment, and infrastructure upgrades. Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a resident of Anne Arundel County. Farm must be located in Anne Arundel County and agriculturally tax assessed by the State of Maryland, or applicant must possess a Commercial TFL License with proof of vessel docked in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Must own or operate a farm in Anne Arundel County that is agriculturally tax assessed by the State of Maryland, OR possess a Commercial TFL License with proof of vessel docking in Anne Arundel County
Farm applicants must submit a letter of reference from Soil Conservation, UMD Extension, Farm Bureau, or 4-H/FFA Leader
Must provide all project details including contractor/product estimates (if applicable)
Must provide a one-to-one matching contribution equal to the grant amount requested
Matching funds may not include in-kind labor or state and federal grants or cost-share
Proof of project completion is due within the year of the grant award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open application period. Applications are scored on their ability to increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations, increase efficiency, and/or provide agricultural education opportunities. Farm applicants must include a letter of reference and project details with estimates. Visit https://www.aaedc.org/agriculture/agricultural-business-assistance/abig for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ACR Fund provides zero-interest loans to spur economic activity and improvement in Anne Arundel County's Commercial Revitalization Districts, including the Glen Burnie Town Center, parts of the City of Annapolis, the County's Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, and designated commercial corridors in South County. AAEDC also leverages Maryland's Project Restore funding to help activate vacant commercial properties in eligible areas. In addition to financing, the program includes professional architectural services from a commercial revitalization firm.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero-interest loans up to $100,000, repaid over 3 to 7 years, limited to 90% of total project costs (requiring a 10% match from the applicant). For a limited time, the ACR Fund also includes a grant component of up to 50% of project costs (max $50,000), with improvements of at least $100,000 required and certification by the Office of Planning and Zoning. Eligible uses include renovation and upgrades to building exteriors, site improvements, and landscaping. Borrowers may also be offered a companion loan of up to $500,000 through the VOLT Fund for tenant improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital. Professional architectural services are also included. AAEDC also leverages Maryland's Project Restore funding to activate vacant commercial properties in eligible districts.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kayleigh De La Puente, Town Center/Revitalization Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and business owners with a lease located in Anne Arundel County's Commercial Revitalization Districts (including Glen Burnie Town Center), parts of the City of Annapolis, the Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, or designated commercial corridors in South County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrades to building exteriors, site improvements (including landscaping), activation of vacant commercial properties, tenant improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital (via companion VOLT Fund loan). Also supports activation of vacant commercial properties through Maryland's Project Restore funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Anne Arundel County's eleven Commercial Revitalization Districts (including Glen Burnie Town Center), parts of the City of Annapolis, the Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, and designated commercial corridors in South County (Mayo Rd, Galesville, Churchton, and Deale Commercial Revitalization Districts).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a property owner or a business owner with a lease
Property must be located within an eligible area (Commercial Revitalization District, City of Annapolis revitalization area, Enterprise Zone, or South County commercial corridor)
Loan covers up to 90% of total project costs, requiring a 10% match from the applicant
Interested applicants should contact AAEDC to verify property eligibility
Improvements must be at least $100,000 for grant/tax credit component
Certification by the Office of Planning and Zoning required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AAEDC to verify property location in an eligible district and discuss the process. Verify eligibility with the Office of Planning and Zoning. Then submit an application via the online ACR application portal at https://www.aaedc.org/business/financing-and-tax-credits/acr-fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: Arundel Grown is a free marketing certification program that connects Anne Arundel County farmers and agricultural businesses to local consumers. The program increases awareness of local agriculture and food sourcing by certifying businesses as locally grown and featuring them in promotional materials and guides.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free marketing certification that allows Anne Arundel County agricultural businesses to use the Arundel Grown brand and be featured in the Arundel Agriculture Grown Guide and other promotional materials to connect with local consumers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County farmers and agricultural businesses seeking to market their locally grown products to consumers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marketing and promotion of locally grown agricultural products through certification and directory listing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to agricultural businesses located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County farmer or agricultural business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Agricultural Business Development Director, Shelley Garrett, to become an Arundel Grown Certified business or to find out how to increase local food sourcing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) connects technology and government contracting businesses in Anne Arundel County with complimentary consulting services. Services include DoD technology commercialization support through the DefTech Center, federal contracting guidance through TargetGov (including a free one-hour initial consultation per year), intellectual property and legal consultation, and access to the GovMates teaming partner platform for government contractors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complimentary consulting services for technology and government contracting businesses. Includes: (1) DefTech Center help finding and licensing patents from defense research labs; (2) TargetGov federal contracting guidance with a free one-hour initial consultation per year (additional consulting paid directly to TargetGov); (3) intellectual property and legal consultation via partner law firms; and (4) access to GovMates, a free teaming partner platform for government contractors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs and companies in Anne Arundel County developing innovative technology, working as government contractors, or seeking to commercialize technology for defense or commercial markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and consulting — not a cash award. Services cover market analysis, federal contracting strategy, patent licensing, IP legal consultation, and government contractor teaming.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County-based company or entrepreneur
TargetGov consultation requires a referral from AAEDC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AAEDC for a referral to the appropriate consulting partner. AAEDC will connect businesses with the relevant service provider (DefTech, TargetGov, legal consultants, or GovMates).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides current and aspiring farmers with access to a variety of modern, well-maintained agricultural equipment for rent at affordable daily rates. Equipment supports planting, fencing, livestock handling, and poultry processing, while promoting conservation practices. Eligible businesses and individuals must be located in one of five southern Maryland counties: Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's. Funded through a grant from the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) with in-kind participation from T&C Farm Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equipment available for rent at daily or per-acre rates ranging from $10 to $200 per day. Available equipment includes: Lands Pride Spinner Spreader ($10/day), Mobile Poultry Processing Unit ($75/day), Sioux Cattle Squeeze Chute and SmartScale ($40–$50/rental), 10' Great Plains No-Till Pull Type Drill ($50/day or $10/acre), 12' Great Plains Turbo Till ($125/day), Wheatheart Trailer Mounted Post Driver ($200 first day, $100 additional days), 5' Lands Pride All-Purpose Seeder ($100/day), MillCreek #127 Manure Spreader ($75/day), Model 2550 Series II Raised Bed Mulch Layer ($175/day; materials extra), New Holland 450 Utility Bailer ($9/bale), and Landpride 6' No-Till Compact Drill ($40/day or $10/acre). Renters must provide a certificate of liability insurance for a minimum of $1 million.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Lisa Barge (Agricultural Marketing & Development Manager); Britany Rawlings (Agriculture Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current and aspiring farmers in the 5 southern Maryland counties (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renting agricultural equipment for planting, fencing, livestock handling, and poultry processing. Available equipment includes no-till drills, post drivers, manure spreaders, balers, seeders, squeeze chutes, a turbo till, a raised bed mulch layer, a spinner spreader, and a mobile poultry processing unit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farmers in Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business or individual must be located in Anne Arundel, Calvert, Prince George's, St. Mary's, or Charles County
Must provide a certificate of liability insurance for a minimum of $1 million
AAEDC and Thomas S. Collinson (T&C Farm Service) must be listed as additional insured
Must not have past-due invoices with AAEDC
Insurance must not be expired
Must complete a rental application for each rental
Must complete a post-rental report after each use
Equipment must be returned clean and greased
Renter is liable for non-wear-and-tear repairs and parts/labor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact AAEDC and complete the rental application (separate applications for the Mobile Poultry Processing Unit and all other equipment), uploading the insurance certificate. Step 2: Contact T&C Farm Service (Thomas S. Collinson) to reserve and schedule equipment pick-up. Present approval when picking up. Step 3: Use equipment for the specified rental period. Step 4: Return equipment clean and greased; T&C Farm Service inspects upon return. Step 5: Complete the post-rental report.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Inclusive Ventures Program (IVP) is a free eight-week online business accelerator operated by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) that helps small, minority-owned, women-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses in Anne Arundel County grow and succeed. The program consists of eight online learning sessions held on Wednesday evenings, covering topics such as pricing models, profit margins, monthly expenses and revenue, and sales goals. Participants complete approximately three hours per week of online coursework, interact with peer entrepreneurs, a facilitator, and subject matter experts, and receive exclusive consultations with legal, HR, and accounting experts. Participants who attend all sessions, complete homework assignments, and deliver a final 10–15 minute business growth plan presentation receive a $5,000 operational grant for working capital upon completion. Graduates may also apply for additional financing through the VOLT Fund ($25,000–$500,000) or the VOLT Microloan Fund, and receive ongoing access to program mentors and alumni activities. The program is partially funded by a U.S. Small Business Administration grant and powered by the Maryland Department of Commerce. A Spanish-language version of the program is also offered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free eight-week online cohort program providing business education, mentorship, networking opportunities, and complimentary consultations with legal, HR, and accounting experts. Participants who attend all sessions, complete homework assignments, and deliver a final 10–15 minute business growth plan presentation receive a $5,000 operational grant usable for working capital and operational business expenses. Upon graduation, participants may also apply for low-interest loans through the VOLT Fund ($25,000–$500,000) or the VOLT Microloan Fund, and receive ongoing access to program mentors and alumni activities. The program is partially funded by a U.S. Small Business Administration grant and powered by the Maryland Department of Commerce.

Businesses must have been in operation for at least two years and have employees. Businesses in commercial space are preferred.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational grant proceeds can be used for working capital and operational business expenses as defined by the participant's business growth plan. Program also supports business education, mentorship, networking, and access to capital for business growth and scaling.

Business must be located in Anne Arundel County

Business must have employees
Applicant must complete an application and interview
Preference given to businesses in commercial space

Complete homework assignments prior to each week's class
Give a final 10–15 minute presentation on business growth plan

Qualified applicants will be invited to an interview before being considered for admission. You may also contact AAEDC via the online inquiry form on the program page to learn more and get started.
