structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program for small technology and cybersecurity companies in Anne Arundel County. The fund provides flexible financing to help defense-related tech businesses grow, hire new employees, and cover key operating costs including working capital, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, and cybersecurity compliance certifications.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000. Repayment terms of 1 to 5 years based on company cash flow. Eligible uses include leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, working capital, and cybersecurity compliance certifications. All owners with more than a 20% stake must sign a personal guaranty. Collateral may be required. Startup companies must have a business plan and contracts in place to cover debt service. Standard underwriting practices apply, considering repayment capacity, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small technology and cybersecurity companies with gross revenues under $5 million and fewer than 100 employees that support national defense, including cybersecurity, logistics, and technical support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, and cybersecurity compliance certifications to support business growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to technology companies located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Gross revenues less than $5 million
Fewer than 100 employees
Company supports national defense (e.g., logistics, cybersecurity, technical support)
Employs designers, developers, or producers of materials/components/equipment for national defense OR provides a product or service ancillary to the cyber and defense industry
Financing must help create new full-time jobs within the first year
All owners with more than 20% stake must sign a personal guaranty
Startup companies must have a business plan and contracts in place to cover debt service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through AAEDC's Submittable portal at aaedc.submittable.com/submit. Standard underwriting review will follow, evaluating repayment capacity, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral protection.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Customer and Employee Protection Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to small businesses in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis to purchase products and services needed for safe reopening in compliance with COVID-19 regulations. The program prioritizes minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 to cover costs of PPE, protective shields/dividers, sanitation products and services, digital signage, technology for wellness/communications/e-commerce, delivery vehicles and equipment, professional consultation, and workforce training. The grant may be used as reimbursement for eligible purchases made after March 29, 2020. Funded with $5 million from the federal CARES Act.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer employees in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, with preference for minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses and industries most affected by COVID-19 quarantine rules.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: PPE for employees, protective shields/dividers, sanitation products and services (UV lamps, foggers), digital signage and graphics, technology (hardware, software, wellness scans, virtual meetings, website upgrades, e-commerce), delivery vehicles and equipment, professional consultation (legal, HR), and workforce training for compliance best practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County-based business or located in the City of Annapolis
Must have 50 or fewer employees
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must submit a detailed budget listing all vendors, amounts, and products/services
Must submit financial documents such as business tax returns, Schedule C, or profit and loss statement
Must submit invoices as proof of purchases
Past due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account on the online application portal and complete the entire application. Upload a detailed budget matching the grant request amount, including vendor names, addresses, phone numbers, websites, and itemized products/services. Submit required financial documents. Email grants@aaedc.org with questions before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Infrastructure Improvement Pilot Program (SBIIPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant initiative to help small businesses afford infrastructure improvements necessary to start or expand business operations in Anne Arundel County. The program is funded by $850,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds. Eligible projects include water and sewer improvements that benefit multiple businesses, not just a single entity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by $850,000 in ARPA funds for water and sewer infrastructure improvements. Projects must benefit multiple businesses. Funding is contingent on Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits final approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, nonprofits, and community/business organizations in Anne Arundel County seeking funding for shared infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water and sewer infrastructure improvements that benefit multiple businesses. Applicants must be able to cover soft costs and associated fees during the regulatory approval process.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a for-profit business, nonprofit entity, or community/business organization
Must be properly registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland
Project must benefit multiple businesses, not just a single entity
Letters from neighboring organizations (chambers of commerce, business associations, commercial condominium, homeowners, or community associations) required to demonstrate community support
Applicant must be able to cover soft costs and associated fees through the regulatory process
Funding contingent on Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits final approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application period opened December 13, 2021 and closed January 28, 2022. Applications were submitted through the AAEDC website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial relief fund for Anne Arundel County residents who lost their jobs due to COVID-19 and did not receive unemployment benefits. Eligible residents receive a $500 Visa card to help them begin a path to economic recovery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time $500 Visa prepaid card provided to each approved applicant. AAWDC staff contacts approved residents to schedule pickup at a pop-up distribution site in the county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who earned $25/hour or less before COVID-19, lost their job on or after March 1, 2020, are not currently receiving unemployment benefits, and are not currently working.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General financial relief for workers excluded from unemployment benefits who lost their jobs due to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must have earned $25/hour or less before COVID-19
Must have lost their job on or after March 1, 2020
Must not be currently receiving unemployment benefits
Must not be currently working

Must provide three pieces of documentation: proof of residency (driver's license, postmarked mail, or voter registration card), proof of layoff/termination (letter or email from employer stating layoff/termination and last day), and proof of hourly wage (last pay stub or employer letter on company letterhead)
If required documentation is unavailable, a telephone interview with an AAWDC representative will be conducted to confirm eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the JotForm application link. If you do not have required documentation, submit your application anyway and an AAWDC representative will call you to conduct a telephone interview to confirm eligibility. Once approved, AAWDC staff will contact you to schedule pickup of your Visa card at a pop-up distribution site.

structured_extraction.program_name: Appalachian Regional Initiative for Stronger Economies (ARISE)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program that makes funding available for multi-state projects advancing regional economic growth across the Appalachian region. Eligible activities include planning and implementation efforts related to infrastructure, workforce development, business growth, and community capacity aligned with Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) priorities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for multi-state projects. Full applications are by invitation only. Projects must involve partnership across at least two states.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Full applications (by invitation only) are due May 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public agencies, Tribes, higher education institutions, and nonprofits working in partnership across at least two Appalachian states
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure, workforce development, business growth, and community capacity building aligned with ARC priorities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible applicants in the Appalachian region, including western Maryland counties
requirements_list: Projects must involve partnership across at least two states
Full applications are by invitation only
Eligible applicants include public agencies, Tribes, higher education institutions, and nonprofits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Full applications are by invitation only, due May 15, 2026. Consult ARC for invitation and application guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program administered through Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS) providing funding to nonprofits and community-based organizations for community reinvestment and repair projects in Anne Arundel County. Grants are funded by a portion of the sales tax revenue from adult-use recreational cannabis sales in Maryland and support community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities. Priority is given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) — zip codes with historically high cannabis possession charge rates (21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, and 20755). Strategic priorities include mental health and substance abuse services, education and youth enrichment, housing and homelessness prevention, and workforce development. Total FY2026 grant awards totaled $1,691,200 across 26+ organizations in four service categories.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from the Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF), funded by a portion of the adult-use recreational cannabis sales tax. Total FY2026 grant awards totaled $1,691,200 across 26+ organizations in four service categories: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services (7 organizations, $438,500); Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services (7 organizations, $490,000); Workforce Development and Employment Training (4 organizations, $364,000); Education, Youth Enrichment, and After-School Activities (12 organizations, $398,700). Applications are submitted through the Neighborly Portal. Priority is given to applicants serving residents in designated Disproportionately Impacted Area (DIA) zip codes: 21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, and 20755. FY27 applications opened January 14, 2026, with a deadline of February 25, 2026 at noon.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, and government agencies serving low-income residents and Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health and substance abuse services ($438,500 awarded to 7 organizations in FY2026); housing and homelessness prevention services ($490,000 awarded to 7 organizations in FY2026); workforce development and employment training ($364,000 awarded to 4 organizations in FY2026); education, youth enrichment, and after-school activities ($398,700 awarded to 12 organizations in FY2026); community reinvestment and repair projects

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers two housing rehabilitation assistance options for qualifying low-income homeowners. First, through Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS), eligible homeowners can apply for forgiveness loans of up to $30,000 to cover home improvement work performed by a licensed contractor — no cash is given directly to homeowners. Work is provided at no cost unless the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years; if transferred within that period, the full amount must be repaid within 11 years, with the loan reduced by 20% per year for years 12–15. Typical repairs include roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom remodeling. Second, through Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County, eligible homeowners can receive up to $10,000 worth of free home repairs funded by the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program, with no repayment required. Both programs serve low-income Annapolis homeowners and can assist with most types of repair needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two forms of assistance are available: (1) A forgiveness loan of up to $30,000 covering home improvement work by a licensed contractor, administered by ACDS. No cost to homeowner unless home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years; if transferred, full amount repaid within 11 years with 20% annual reduction in years 12–15. (2) Up to $10,000 in free home repairs at no cost, administered by Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County and funded through CDBG.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in Annapolis, MD. ACDS program requires household income below 60% of Area Median Income. Rebuilding Together program requires household income below 50% of Area Median Income and homeownership for more than 2 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom remodeling, and most other types of home repairs performed by a licensed contractor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a homeowner residing in Annapolis, MD

For ACDS program: combined household income must be less than 60% of Area Median Income
For Rebuilding Together program: combined household income must be less than 50% of Area Median Income

structured_extraction.program_description: The County Executive's Community Support Grant, administered by Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. (ACDS) in partnership with Anne Arundel County's County Executive's Office and the Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center, provides funding to nonprofit organizations for programs and projects that improve the lives of Anne Arundel County residents. The program supports program and project operations, pilot programs, one-time projects, and small equipment purchases. Approximately $2 million in grant funding is anticipated for FY2027 (subject to change), with individual awards ranging from $15,000 to $50,000. Priority is given to proposals addressing underserved populations, community health and well-being, equity and inclusion, and eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education. Collaborative projects are preferred but not required. FY27 applications opened January 7, 2026, with a deadline of February 18, 2026 at noon.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $2 million in grant funding is anticipated for FY2027 (subject to change), with individual awards ranging from $15,000 to $50,000. Grants may cover program/project-specific staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and a proportional share of administrative overhead (max 5% of award). One-time projects, pilot programs, and small equipment purchases are also eligible. Faith-based organizations may receive funds but may not use them for religious purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3)) serving Anne Arundel County residents, with priority given to those serving underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, and eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program and project support including staff costs, consultant fees, supplies, occupancy, insurance, travel, equipment, and administrative overhead proportional to the program budget (max 5% of award); one-time projects; pilot programs; small equipment purchases. Funded proposals should align with the County Executive's priorities, including serving underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, and eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education. Faith-based organizations may receive funds but may not use them for religious purposes; inherently religious activities must be separate in time and location from funded programming. Funds may not pay for capital improvements primarily serving worship or inherently religious activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds are financial instruments the City of Baltimore uses to fund development projects within designated TIF districts. A developer applies to the Board of Finance for a TIF bond. The increase in property tax revenue generated by the development is set aside to repay the bonds. Once the debt is repaid, the TIF district is dissolved and the additional tax revenue flows to the City's general fund. The Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF is a specific TIF initiative targeting rehabilitation of vacant properties across Baltimore City to create affordable and workforce housing.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF bonds allow developers to finance development projects using the projected increase in property tax revenues within a designated district to repay the bonds over time. The developer submits an application to the Board of Finance detailing the district area and estimated future property value increases. TIF bond proceeds are used for public infrastructure improvements including roads, utilities, schools, parks, and other public improvements within the designated TIF district. For the Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF, net bond proceeds of approximately $130.9M of $150M total are structured across four series (Series A: December 2024, Series B: December 2028, Series C: December 2032, Series D: December 2036), financing rehabilitation of approximately 3,560 vacant residential units at an average construction cost of $220,155 per unit (total project cost ~$783.75M). The TIF covers appraisal and affordability gaps for homeownership units (subsidy gap of $16,758–$44,758 per unit), with developer profit capped at 12% of total development costs. Affordable housing is targeted at households up to 115% AMI (~$136,050 for a household of 4; maximum purchase price ~$231,742 for a 4-person household at 100% AMI). Bond series are structured with amortization through June 30, 2066, with incremental property tax revenues pledged to repay bond principal and interest. Park Heights Phase 2 infrastructure includes $11.4M for new streets, street lights, water utilities, bus stops, and stormwater management upgrades. The Perkins Somerset Oldtown TIF allocated $75.2 million of a $155 million total public infrastructure investment, financing a new school, parks, road and infrastructure improvements, and mixed-income housing development. For the PSO TIF, three bond series were issued (Series A: June 15, 2019; Series B: June 15, 2021; Series C: June 15, 2023), with debt service repayment scheduled through approximately 2051–2053. Projected annual property tax revenue from the PSO district increases from ~$80,827 to ~$8.34M at full build-out. Total projected additional revenues from the Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF over the 40-year bond horizon: approximately $56.7 million (Schedule VIII-B).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, nonprofits, community development corporations, and homeowners seeking financing for development projects in Baltimore City through the TIF bond mechanism, particularly for vacancy reduction and affordable housing development targeting households up to 115% AMI. DHCD works with community partners to identify small, emerging, minority, and women-owned businesses and developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding public infrastructure improvements and development projects within a designated TIF district in Baltimore City, including: hard construction costs to restore vacant properties (buildings and lots); new homeownership and rental opportunities for households up to 115% AMI; public infrastructure construction (roads, sidewalks, street trees, stormwater upgrades, street improvements, utilities, bus stops, street lighting); property acquisition through negotiated sale, condemnation, tax sale foreclosure, or donation; developer grants and appraisal gap subsidies for city-sponsored development projects; affordable housing development (rental and homeownership units across 126 neighborhoods); homebuyer down-payment grants/loans; developer incentives to close appraisal gap; live/work incentives; demolition (emergency, planned, blight elimination); property stabilization; operational capacity investment; workforce development facilities; developer technical assistance and CDC support; homeownership coaching and estate planning; non-profit operations support; community engagement and marketing; school facilities (e.g., Dunbar Middle School renovation, City Springs school replacement); parks; mixed-income housing development (market rate, 60% AMI, 30% AMI, 80% AMI, and up to 115% AMI units); commercial and office space; retail; parking; car barn expansion; design/engineering; CitiWatch and public safety infrastructure; debt service reserve fund, capitalized interest, and bond issuance costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to designated TIF districts within Baltimore City. The Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF district encompasses 4,285 properties across 126 neighborhoods citywide, with 1,625 properties in DHCD-designated Impact Investment Areas (IIAs) identified in DHCD's 2019 'A New Era of Neighborhood Investment Framework'. IIAs include: Broadway East (250 properties), Coldstream Homestead Montebello (295 properties), East Baltimore Midway (117 properties), Johnston Square (85 properties), Park Heights (457 properties), Southwest (171 properties), and West (282 properties). Criteria for inclusion: high vacancy rates, proximity to transit/employment centers/anchor institutions/parks, adjacency to stronger-market neighborhoods, and ability to leverage investment. Historically redlined and formerly redlined neighborhoods with highest density of vacant structures are explicitly targeted. Specific neighborhoods referenced include Sandtown-Winchester, Pigtown/Washington Village, Brooklyn, Park Heights, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello. Of the 4,285 properties, 1,299 are owned by the Mayor and City Council and available for redevelopment. 87% of vacant buildings are concentrated in East Baltimore, West Baltimore, and Park Heights. Other TIF districts are project-specific; for example, the Perkins Somerset Oldtown TIF district covers approximately 200 acres bounded by Monument Street (north), Eastern Avenue (south), Little Italy/Jonestown (west), and Broadway (east), encompassing the Perkins, Somerset, Oldtown, and McElderry neighborhoods (specifically Perkins/Middle East, Pleasant View Gardens, Somerset, Broadway/Dunbar, Washington Hill, and Oldtown neighborhoods).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a TIF bond application to the Baltimore City Board of Finance. The application must describe the proposed TIF district and provide estimates of future property value increases. Sample applications are available on the City's website. For the Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF, DHCD works with community partners to identify small, emerging, minority, and women-owned businesses and developers for projects. Pending Board of Finance approval, DHCD requests introduction of TIF legislation at City Council. Once legislation is approved and bonds are ready to be issued, DHCD returns to the Board of Finance for approval of each bond tranche. The program is anticipated to issue bonds in multiple tranches (Series A through D) every few years from 2024 through 2036, with rehabilitation phased at approximately 200 units per year beginning in 2025 and continuing through 2040. For project-specific TIFs such as the Perkins Somerset Oldtown TIF, the process involved a concept application to the Board of Finance followed by legislative approval at City Council and mayoral signature, with the developer (PSO Housing Company) pre-selected as the development partner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Rehabilitation and Restoration Tax Credit (CHAP Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Historic Rehabilitation and Restoration Tax Credit Program (CHAP Tax Credit) encourages property owners to rehabilitate or restore historically designated properties in Baltimore City. The program provides a 10-year property tax credit on the increased assessed property value resulting from qualifying rehabilitation work. To qualify, a property must be historically designated (as a Baltimore City Landmark, National Register individual designation, or contributing to a local or national historic district or the Baltimore National Heritage Area) and the project must invest at least 25% of the property's full cash value in qualifying rehabilitation work. The credit applies to both residential and commercial properties, is computed once at completion, and applies for the full 10-year period. It is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining credit term and appears on the tax bill as a 'Special Credit' after CHAP issues final certification. The credit can be combined with the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit and the Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program, but cannot be combined with any other City property tax credit. Property owners must submit interior and exterior change plans to CHAP staff for review and approval through an online application prior to beginning any work.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation (CHAP)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year property tax credit on the increased assessed value of a property resulting from qualifying historic rehabilitation or restoration work. The credit is computed once at the time of project completion and applies for the full 10-year period. It is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining credit term. For projects with construction costs at or below $5 million, the credit equals 100% of the increase in assessed value per year for all 10 years. For projects with construction costs above $5 million, the credit percentage is tiered: 80% (years 1–5), 70% (year 6), 60% (year 7), 50% (year 8), 40% (year 9), and 30% (year 10). Projects under $3.5 million have two years to complete work (with a one-time two-year extension available); projects over $3.5 million have three years to complete work (with a one-time three-year extension available). The credit cannot be combined with any other City property tax credit but can be combined with the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit and the Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: City-Wide Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing (TIF) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's first non-contiguous Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing (TIF) program, established by City Council Bill 24-0595 signed into law on December 3, 2024, uses TIF bond proceeds to fund affordable housing development citywide with a focus on long-disinvested communities with high vacancy rates. Unlike traditional TIFs focused on specific neighborhoods, this non-contiguous TIF targets 3,991 vacant properties citywide identified through DHCD's whole-block planning efforts in East and West Baltimore neighborhoods including Broadway East, Harlem Park, Druid Heights, Park Heights, Upton, East Baltimore Midway, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello. TIF funds are provided as reimbursement grants to developers, nonprofits, LLCs, and individual residents to rehabilitate vacant properties within the TIF District. Grantees are reimbursed for eligible hard construction costs (such as roofing, framing, flooring, electrical, HVAC, and plumbing) after completing work and meeting inspection requirements. The program also reduces the appraisal gap — the difference between construction costs and the market value of a completed home — which has stalled housing development in neighborhoods where it is most needed. Additional uses include public infrastructure improvements (sidewalks, streets, parks, alleys, utilities) and homeowner grants to help residents qualify for newly rehabbed homes. Bonds are issued in series up to $150 million total, with $65 million authorized in the initial legislation and approximately $18 million available in the first round. The average grant award per property is expected to be around $50,000–$100,000, varying based on property size, condition, end use, affordability level, and appraisal gap. Completed properties must be sold or rented to households earning at or below 115% of Area Median Income and must remain affordable for at least five years. The program prioritizes legacy residents, small and emerging developers, and women- and minority-owned businesses. DHCD anticipates multiple funding rounds as additional bond series are approved and sold.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF funds are awarded as reimbursement grants for eligible hard construction costs to rehabilitate vacant properties in the City-Wide Affordable Housing TIF District. Total program funding is up to $150 million in TIF bonds over time, with $65 million authorized in the initial bond tranche and approximately $15–18 million available in the first round (including approximately $3 million reserved for legacy residents, current TIF District residents, and small/emerging developers on privately owned properties). Average award is expected to be around $50,000–$100,000 per property depending on property size, condition, end use, affordability level, and appraisal gap. Reimbursement is made after work is completed and inspected. Grantees may request draws at project completion (after receiving a Use and Occupancy permit) or in stages: up to 90% of approved costs in one or two draws during construction, one draw upon receiving the Use and Occupancy permit, and one draw upon occupancy. Properties must be completed, permitted, and occupied within 12 months of executing a grant agreement with DHCD. Construction budgets are reviewed by the City's Bond Counsel to confirm eligible use of TIF Bond proceeds. Additional assistance includes: homeowner grants to help residents qualify for rehabbed affordable homes; funding for public infrastructure such as streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, and utilities; rehabilitation or demolition of vacant housing; investment capital for developers rehabilitating vacant housing or converting structures to community green space. Bonds are sold in series, with properties and amounts determined per series based on neighborhood market conditions, readiness, other funding sources, and affordability targets. This is the first in a series of NOFOs; DHCD anticipates multiple future rounds as additional bond series are approved and sold.

Properties must serve households earning up to 115% of Area Median Income (approximately $149,845 for a household of four as of 2025 HUD guidelines); priority given to households at 60% and 80% AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: (1) Hard construction costs including excavation, demolition, grading, foundation, framing, roofing, flooring, interior and exterior finishes, building systems (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, alarms, elevators, fire protection, telecommunications cabling, and other fixed equipment) to rehabilitate vacant properties; (2) Public infrastructure — streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, and water and other utilities — to enable new housing construction; (3) Homeowner grants to help residents qualify for rehabbed affordable homes; (4) Addressing home appraisal gaps to enable affordable housing project completion; (5) Rehabilitation or demolition of vacant housing; (6) Conversion of vacant structures to community green space; (7) Neighborhood-based, block-level redevelopment and vacancy reduction in historically disinvested communities. TIF funds cannot be used for property acquisition, taxes, architectural and engineering fees, soft costs, financing costs such as interest, new construction on vacant lots, community spaces, or reimbursement of work already completed before a grant agreement is executed.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) on DHCD's Affordable Housing TIF webpage. structured_extraction.program_name: Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) — Baltimore City
structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) provides free, nutritious breakfasts and lunches to children and teens in low-income areas of Baltimore City during the summer months when school is not in session. Funded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) through the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), the program is administered locally by the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). Non-profit organizations, churches, day camps, community groups, and city agencies can apply to become meal-serving sites.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved sites receive free, nutritious meals (breakfasts and lunches) to distribute to eligible youth ages 18 and under. The 2026 program runs Monday through Friday, June 17 through August 22. Sites must plan to serve a minimum of 10 eligible youth for at least two weeks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, churches, day camps, community groups, and city agencies in Baltimore City that want to serve free summer meals to children and teens ages 18 and under.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free, nutritious breakfasts and lunches to eligible youth ages 18 and under during the summer months (June 17 – August 22, 2026).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sites must be located within Baltimore City. Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible.
requirements_list: Site must be located in Baltimore City
Site must plan to receive meals for a minimum of two weeks and serve at least 10 eligible youth ages 18 or younger
Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible
Sites requesting breakfast must have adequate refrigeration to store perishables overnight
Sites are subject to a pre-operational inspection and must be approved by program staff
The site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend a mandatory 3-hour training session
Sites must agree to serve all meals in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations can apply online via the SFSP website or download and mail a paper application to the Summer Food Service Program at 1135 N. Gilmor Street, 2nd Floor, Baltimore, MD 21217.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), in partnership with the Baltimore City Water Department, provides site stewards of City-owned and privately owned community open space with access to water for their site during the growing season at a flat rate of $120 per season (March 1 through November 1).
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Site stewards pay a flat fee of $120 per growing season (March 1–November 1) for access to water at a community open space lot. The Water Department installs a device allowing a hose connection. If water access is not available at the requested site, the $120 fee is refunded within 90 days. The fee is not prorated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First week of October (last week to submit applications each season)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Site stewards of City-owned or privately owned community open space in Baltimore City who want water access for gardening or urban agriculture during the growing season.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water access for community open space and garden sites during the growing season.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a site steward of a City-owned or privately owned community open space
Must complete the Water Access Application on the BuyIntoBmore site
Must submit a $120 water access fee with the application
Must return a signed Water Access Agreement before a service request is submitted
Applications are only accepted during the growing season (March 1 through November 1); the application window opens in the first week of February and closes in the first week of October
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the BuyIntoBmore site (baltimore-md-publicity.tolemi.com) by searching for a property address or selecting Water Access under Programs, adding the lot to your cart, and completing the application with the $120 payment. After your application is reviewed, a Water Access Agreement will be emailed to you. Return the signed agreement to initiate the service request. If water is available, an inspector will install the connection device and provide instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Adopt-A-Lot program lets residents, businesses, or neighborhood groups take care of empty city-owned lots near them. Participants can use adopted lots for community gardens, clean and green spaces, or recreational spaces — without paying taxes or other costs associated with owning the land.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free license to adopt and maintain a city-owned vacant lot. No purchase price, taxes, or fees are required. Application is reviewed and finalized within 60 days of approval. Water access applications are also accepted during the garden season (February through early October), with online payment available for water connections.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First Week of October (last week to submit applications each year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, civic or non-profit organizations, school groups, businesses, and neighborhood groups committed to caring for a vacant lot in their neighborhood.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adopted lots may be used for community gardens, clean and green spaces (mowed grass, flower beds, neighborhood signage), or passive recreational spaces (chess parks, horseshoe pits, meditation spaces). Lots cannot be used for parking, carwashes, dog parks, playgrounds, or for-profit businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to city-owned vacant lots within Baltimore City. The program appears to cover neighborhoods citywide across all geographic quadrants of the city.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Baltimore City resident, civic or non-profit organization, school group, business, or neighborhood group
Applicant must commit to caring for the vacant lot
Applications must be submitted via the BuyIntoBmore site
Community garden and recreational space applications require additional vetting and site plans
Applications for water access must be submitted by the first week of October
Garden season runs February through early November
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the BuyIntoBmore site (buyintobmore.baltimorecity.gov). Search by property address or select Adopt-A-Lot under 'Programs' and use spatial tools to identify a lot. Add the lot(s) to your cart, then open your cart, select 'Apply,' and complete the application. Applications are reviewed and finalized within 60 days of approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to Baltimore City and quasi-City agency employees to help them buy a home in Baltimore City. Eligible employees receive a forgivable loan of $5,000 or $10,000 toward closing costs and/or down payment. All incentives are offered as five-year forgivable loans (except Live Near Your Work, which is a grant).
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $5,000 or $10,000 forgivable loan (no repayment required if the buyer stays in the home for five years) for closing costs and/or down payment. As of April 2026, 43 incentives remain available for the current fiscal year. All incentives are offered as five-year forgivable loans (except Live Near Your Work, which is a grant).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding available through June 30 each fiscal year, on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of Baltimore City and quasi-City agencies who have been employed for at least six months and want to buy a home in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance and/or closing cost reduction when purchasing a home in Baltimore City. May also be used for interest rate buydown (up to 2.5% through First-Time Home Buyers Incentive) or property acquisition/rehabilitation loan support (Vacants to Value Booster).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within Baltimore City. Vacants to Value Booster requires property subject to a Vacant Building Notice in Baltimore City. Live Near Your Work eligibility is restricted to participating employers' geographic preferences.
requirements_list: Must be employed by a Baltimore City or quasi-City agency for at least six months
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before purchase
Must contribute at least $1,000 of personal funds toward the purchase
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after application submission
Must provide Title Company's EIN in the application portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register and apply through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Submit application at least 30 days before your closing date. Provide Title Company EIN under Closing Information (Section H) in the portal. Recommended browser is Google Chrome; also compatible with IE v10+, Firefox, and Safari. The portal auto-logs out after 30 minutes of inactivity.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Live Near Your Work Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between participating employers and the City of Baltimore that encourages employees to buy homes near their workplace. Baltimore City matches the employer's contribution toward a home purchase, resulting in a combined grant incentive of $2,000 to $5,000 or more depending on the employer. The base program provides $1,000 from the City and $1,000 from the employer (minimum $2,000 total), with no annual income limits. The grant is forgivable at 20% per year over 5 years, provided the buyer uses the property as their principal residence. Individual employers may add extra eligibility requirements or restrict the program to certain neighborhoods. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis through June 30 of each fiscal year.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Minimum $2,000 grant ($1,000 from the City of Baltimore and $1,000 from the participating employer) toward down payment and closing costs. Employers may contribute more, with the City matching employer contributions between $1,000–$2,500 for total incentives of $2,000–$5,000 or more. No annual income limits. Buyer must contribute at least $1,000 of personal funds toward the purchase. The grant is forgivable at 20% per year over 5 years, provided the buyer uses the property as their principal residence. No repayment is required if conditions are met. As of April 2026, 93 incentives remain available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding available through June 30 each fiscal year, on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees (including first-time homebuyers) of participating employers who want to buy a home near their workplace in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and/or closing costs when purchasing a home near the applicant's place of employment in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within the City of Baltimore, near the applicant's place of employment. Participating employers may further restrict eligible neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Must be employed by a participating Live Near Your Work employer
Must be a first-time homebuyer
Employer must contribute toward the home purchase
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved counseling agency within one year before writing offer
Must contribute at least $1,000 of personal funds toward the purchase
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after application submission
Must provide Title Company's EIN in the application portal
Must use the property as principal residence
Grant is forgivable at 20% per year over 5 years
Must purchase a home near place of employment in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Confirm your employer participates through livebaltimore.com/live-near-your-work, then register and apply through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Register an account with email and password (validated via confirmation link), then log in and complete the application. Submit at least 30 days before closing. You may also contact the program representative at your employer or reach Debra Braxton at Baltimore Housing's Office of Homeownership at 410-396-3124. Additional details available at healthyneighborhoods.org/baltimore-city-live-near-your-work-program/.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore Homeownership Incentive Programs (FTHIP & Buying Into Baltimore)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers homeownership incentive programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) under the B-HIP umbrella. These incentives make buying a home more affordable by lowering closing costs and boosting down payments. The First-Time Homebuyers Incentive Program (FTHIP) helps first-time homebuyers with lower incomes purchase a home in Baltimore City by providing down payment assistance (50% of required down payment as a forgivable loan), a gap loan to reduce the mortgage balance, an interest rate buydown of up to 2.5%, and an additional $5,000 bonus in certain circumstances (e.g., buyers with a disability or a household member with a disability, or buyers purchasing a property they have rented and occupied for at least 6 months). A $10,000 Vacants to Value Booster incentive is also available for properties with a prior Vacant Building Notice of at least one year. The Buying Into Baltimore program awards a $5,000 grant by lottery to people who attend a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour and meet other eligibility conditions. Additional sub-programs under B-HIP serve Baltimore City employees, eligible employers' employees, persons with disabilities, and renters. All incentives except Live Near Your Work are offered as five-year forgivable loans; Live Near Your Work is offered as a grant. Both primary programs require no repayment if conditions are met and are available on a first-come, first-served basis through June 30 of each fiscal year.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FTHIP: Eligible buyers may receive 50% of the required down payment as a forgivable loan, GAP funding to reduce the mortgage loan balance (difference between 30% of annual household income and annual PITI), an interest rate buydown of up to 2.5% of the sales price, up to 50% of closing costs covered, and an additional $5,000 bonus for buyers with a disability or a household member with a disability, or buyers purchasing a property they have rented and occupied for at least 6 months. A $10,000 Vacants to Value Booster incentive is available for properties with a prior Vacant Building Notice of at least one year. All incentives except Live Near Your Work are offered as five-year forgivable loans; Live Near Your Work is offered as a grant. No repayment required if the buyer stays in the home for five years. As of April 2026, $498,239 in funding remains available. Buying Into Baltimore: $5,000 grant awarded by lottery to attendees of a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour. No repayment required. As of April 2026, 30 grants remain available for the current fiscal year. Other B-HIP sub-programs provide forgivable loans ranging from $2,000–$10,000 depending on the sub-program, with the Live Near Your Work sub-program offered as a grant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding available through June 30 each fiscal year, on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Baltimore City at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI), individuals who attend a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour and wish to purchase a home in Baltimore City, Baltimore City employees, eligible employers' employees, persons with disabilities or households with disabled members, and renters who have occupied a rental property for at least 6 months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance (50% of required amount), gap financing to reduce loan balance (difference between 30% of annual household income and annual PITI), interest rate buydown of up to 2.5% of sales price, up to 50% of closing costs covered, conditional $5,000 bonus or $10,000 Vacants to Value Booster incentive, and property rehabilitation/acquisition (Vacants to Value Booster program) when purchasing a home in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (FTHIP)
Household income must be at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (FTHIP)
Must attend a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour (Buying Into Baltimore)
Must meet other program eligibility conditions specific to each sub-program
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved counseling agency within one year before purchase
Must contribute at least $1,000 of personal funds toward the purchase
Housing counselor and lender must complete the online application on the buyer's behalf (FTHIP)
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after application submission
Must provide Title Company's EIN in the application portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For FTHIP: Housing counselor and lender must register and submit the application on the buyer's behalf through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Use the FTHIP Incentives Calculator at cityservices.baltimorecity.gov/fthip to estimate benefits. Submit at least 30 days before closing. For Buying Into Baltimore: Attend a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour, then register and apply through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Submit at least 30 days before closing. Account registration requires email and password with an email validation step. A 30-minute inactivity auto-logout applies; password reset is available through the portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BuyIntoBmore Fixed Pricing Program sells specific City-owned vacant buildings and lots at set, transparent prices to homeowners, developers, nonprofits, and community land trusts. The program prioritizes Baltimore City residents who plan to restore and live in a home as their primary residence, who can purchase eligible vacant buildings or lots for $1. Developers and nonprofits pay slightly higher fixed prices depending on organization size. The program is carried out in phases: Phase One gives priority to future homeowners, Phase Two (Charm City Roots) focuses on properties with familial or legacy ties, and Phase Three opens applications to developers, nonprofits, and community land trusts.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned vacant buildings and lots are sold at fixed, below-market prices based on purchaser type: Homeowners and Community Land Trusts pay $1 for vacant buildings or lots. Small nonprofits (50 or fewer employees) pay $1,000 for vacant buildings and $500 for vacant lots. Large nonprofits (51 or more employees) and for-profit developers pay $3,000 for vacant buildings and $1,000 for vacant lots. All purchasers must obtain a use and occupancy permit within 12 months of settlement. Settlement must occur within 90 days of agreement execution; construction must commence within 30 days of permit issuance. Homeowners must maintain the property as their primary residence for at least 5 years. A $100 application fee is required, which is credited at settlement if approved or refunded if rejected. Homeowner applicants must demonstrate access to at least $90,000 in rehabilitation funding. Up to 12 properties may be applied for per application cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; Phase One homeowner priority period ran April 1 – June 30, 2024; Phase Two (Charm City Roots) intake began April 15, 2024; Phase Three opened July 1, 2024 on a rolling first-come-first-served basis with no stated end date. All phase dates are from 2024 documents and current program status has not been confirmed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who want to become homeowners, as well as developers, nonprofits, and community land trusts interested in rehabilitating vacant City-owned properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and rehabilitation of City-owned vacant buildings and lots for residential, mixed-use with residential component, or eligible green space (side yard) development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must fall within Baltimore City's Housing Market Typology categories E–J (most distressed neighborhoods). Exception: side yard properties can be in typologies A–J if the applicant documents adjacent property ownership as their primary residence. All eligible properties are located within Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must apply for a City-owned vacant building or lot in Baltimore City
Properties must be located in Housing Market Typology categories E–J (side yard properties may be in typologies A–J if applicant owns and occupies the adjacent property)
Homeowners must demonstrate at least $90,000 in available rehabilitation funding per property
Homeowners must maintain the property as their primary residence for at least 5 years after receiving a use and occupancy permit
Use and occupancy permit must be obtained within 12 months of settlement
Settlement must occur within 90 days of agreement execution
Construction must commence within 30 days of permit issuance
Maximum of 12 properties per application cycle
Applicants must not have properties that have been vacant for more than two years without recent rehabilitation work (active permits may satisfy this requirement)
Applicants must not have unresolved legal issues or open/pending criminal cases that could prevent project completion
Applicants must not have unpaid federal or state liens, court orders, or judgments
Business entities must be in good standing with the State of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Community Land Trusts must be registered as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation per Maryland Real Property Article § 14
Applicants must pass Vacant Building Notice assessment
Applicants must pay a $100 application fee (credited at settlement if approved; refunded if rejected)
Purchaser must submit Preliminary and Construction Plans by specified dates and complete improvements per approved plans
Purchaser must comply with Minority and Women's Business Enterprise Program requirements if applicable
Purchaser must pay all recordation costs, documentary stamps, and transfer taxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the Buy Into Bmore interactive map at buyintobmore.baltimorecity.gov (or bit.ly/fixed-pricing) to find a property and submit an application. DHCD reviews applications on a rolling basis and issues award or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. If multiple applicants pass vetting for the same property, applications are reviewed in order of submission. Applicants who do not pass vetting have five business days to remedy the issue. The program proceeds in phases: Phase One (homeowner priority, April 1 – June 30, 2024), Phase Two (Charm City Roots, intake began April 15, 2024), and Phase Three (all fixed pricing applicants, began July 1, 2024 on a rolling basis). Current program status should be confirmed with DHCD directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD's Community Catalyst Grants (CCG) program supports locally-driven community development work through neighborhood-based partner organizations. It complements the Neighborhood Impact Investment Fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to neighborhood-based partner organizations to support community development work in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood-based partner organizations engaged in community development in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Locally-driven community development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must be a neighborhood-based partner organization
Must be engaged in community development work in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through Baltimore City DHCD. See the program page for current application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Developer Incentive Program provides funding to organizations, non-profits, and single-family primary homeowners who are completing extensive renovations of formerly vacant homes. Eligible homes must have a Vacant Building Notice (VBN) and be located in Baltimore City's designated Impact Investment Areas or Middle Neighborhoods. The program supports homeownership projects for households earning no more than 120% of the HUD Area Median Income (AMI). All $3.3 million in available funding has been obligated.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 per property for homeownership renovation projects. Total program funding was $3.3 million ($2.4 million for Impact Investment Areas and $900,000 for Middle Neighborhoods). Funding addresses appraisal gaps between appraised value and sale price for homeownership projects. All funding has been obligated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, non-profits, and single-family primary homeowners renovating formerly vacant homes in Baltimore City's Impact Investment Areas or Middle Neighborhoods for homeownership.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Total development costs for extensive renovation of formerly vacant single-family homes for homeownership projects. Funding addresses appraisal gaps between appraised value and sale price for homeownership projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Baltimore City's designated Impact Investment Areas or Middle Neighborhoods. Homes must have a Vacant Building Notice (VBN). Area eligibility can be verified via the CoDeMap portal at https://cels.baltimorehousing.org/codemapv2ext/
requirements_list: Property must be a formerly vacant home with a Vacant Building Notice (VBN)
Property must be located in a designated Impact Investment Area or Middle Neighborhood
Project must be a single-family homeownership project
Households served must earn no more than 120% of HUD Area Median Income (AMI) as adjusted by household size
Buyer income eligibility applies
Applicant must have financing in place and evidence of site control at time of submission
Applicant must be in good standing with Maryland SDAT
Proof of site control or evidence of acquisition within 3 months required
Background check performed upon submission
Use and occupancy permit required before award
Post-award compliance required: income certification, closing documents, use-and-occupancy permit, and 5-year owner-occupancy affidavit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted via the Neighborly Software platform on a rolling basis until total funding allocation is met. Applicants may apply when projects are ready with financing and evidence of site control. A background check is performed upon submission. DHCD Grant Administrator reviews all applications and confirms address eligibility. Post-award compliance includes income certification, closing documents, use-and-occupancy permit, and a 5-year owner-occupancy affidavit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) accepts donations of vacant buildings and lots from property owners. The program is part of the Reframe Baltimore initiative to eliminate vacant properties and revitalize neighborhoods. The City covers all settlement costs, releasing donors from burdens like unpaid taxes, legal liability, and maintenance costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Baltimore covers all settlement costs associated with donating a vacant property or lot. Donors are relieved of property taxes, liens, legal liability, and maintenance costs. The donation process takes approximately 8–12 months to complete.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of vacant properties or lots in Baltimore City who wish to donate their property to the City, including individuals and companies/corporations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: City covers settlement costs of the property donation. Donated properties are used to eliminate vacancy and support community-driven development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owners of vacant properties located within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Property must be vacant and have a Vacant Building Notice (VBN) issued by DHCD, or be a vacant lot
Property must have a clear title — all non-municipal liens (mortgages, judgments, Federal and State tax liens) must be paid before donating
Donor's name must be on the deed, giving legal right to transfer the property
If multiple names are on the deed, all owners must give permission
Companies and corporations are eligible to donate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Check eligibility (clear title, vacant property with VBN). 2. Submit a brief application form online at the provided JotForm link. 3. DHCD reviews the application and contacts you with a status update. 4. If approved, DHCD submits a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for you to sign and return. 5. Donation goes to Baltimore City's Board of Estimates for approval. 6. Property is prepped for settlement and fully transferred.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) invites qualified development teams to submit Expressions of Interest (EOI) to redevelop specific city-owned properties. The EOI process identifies qualified firms who may then be invited to respond to a Request for Proposals (RFP) for large-scale redevelopment projects in targeted neighborhood investment areas.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Qualified respondents may be invited to submit a full Request for Proposals (RFP) or enter directly into an Exclusive Negotiating Privilege. Currently, 1313 Druid Hill Avenue is listed as an available property.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Large-scale redevelopment of specific city-owned properties in targeted neighborhood investment areas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a qualified development team
Must submit a formal Expression of Interest (EOI) response
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for a specific city-owned property. DHCD reviews each EOI and, based on evaluation, may issue an RFP and invite qualified developers to participate. DHCD may also enter directly into an Exclusive Negotiating Privilege with a qualified respondent. Questions should be emailed to dhcd.eoi@baltimorecity.gov.
