structured_extraction.program_description: The HOME Investment Partnerships Program provides gap financing for affordable housing projects in Baltimore City. Baltimore City's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) uses federal HOME Program funds to support the hard construction costs of affordable housing projects with five or more units. Eligible projects include both rental housing and for-sale housing for income-eligible homebuyers, through new construction or rehabilitation. Funding helps increase the stock of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for low- and very-low-income persons and families.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing in the form of loans for the hard construction costs of affordable housing projects with five or more units. Funding is typically limited to $30,000 per unit, though this limit may be exceeded up to HOME Program regulatory limits at DHCD's discretion. For FY 2026, up to $4,500,000 is available, including a set-aside of up to $975,000 for certified Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs). Developments are expected to repay HOME loans if superior debt allows and/or on a cash flow basis. A $140,000 refinancing fee applies if a HOME loan is refinanced, assigned, assumed, or subordinated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable housing developers (all developers and certified Community Housing Development Organizations) proposing rental or for-sale housing projects for low- and very-low-income households in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hard construction costs (including labor/wages, green building compliance, and demolition) for new construction or rehabilitation of affordable rental or for-sale housing projects with five or more units
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland. Projects must be located in specific targeted impact investment areas or designated zones, including: Park Heights Impact Investment Area; East Impact Investment Area (Johnston Square, Broadway East, East Broadway Midway & Coldstream Homestead Montebello); Southwest Impact Investment Area; West Impact Investment Area (Penn North, Druid Heights, Upton); Communities of Opportunity (2025 Maryland State QAP); Opportunity Zones (2025 QAP); or Sustainable Communities, Empowerment Zones, Federal/Maryland Enterprise Zones, or Main Street/Maple Street Maryland communities. Additionally, sites must comply with HUD site and neighborhood standards evaluated against citywide averages (poverty ≤20%, population of color ≤73%), with exception pathways available.
requirements_list: Project must have five or more units
Project must serve low- and very-low-income persons and families as defined in HOME Program regulations at 24 CFR Part 92
Eligible project types include rental housing and for-sale housing for income-eligible homebuyers
Both new construction and rehabilitation are eligible
Repayment expected if superior debt allows and/or on a cash flow basis
CHDO set-aside requires certified Community Housing Development Organization status

Project must be located in a targeted impact investment area, Opportunity Zone, Sustainable Community, Empowerment Zone, Enterprise Zone, or Main Street/Maple Street Maryland community, OR qualify as a Community of Opportunity under 2025 Maryland State QAP

Site must comply with HUD site and neighborhood standards: not in minority concentration area unless comparable opportunities exist elsewhere, overriding need demonstrated, or transformational redevelopment planned
Neighborhood must not be seriously detrimental to family life or dominated by substandard dwellings unless active remediation program is in progress
Housing must be accessible to social, recreational, educational, commercial, and health facilities equivalent to standard unassisted housing in similar market-rent neighborhoods
Local Hiring Plan required; apprenticeship documentation eligible for bonus points
Davis-Bacon prevailing wage required if federal assistance exceeds $2,000; Baltimore City prevailing wage applies if no Davis-Bacon but assistance exceeds $5,000
Payroll records must be maintained for a minimum of 3 years
Build America, Buy America (BABA) compliance required
Quarterly construction progress reports required
Annual compliance reports required during the affordability period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Neighborly Portal (available beginning November 21, 2025). Applicants may attend the Pre-Proposal Conference on December 11, 2025. Submissions were due January 9, 2026. Review and scoring ran from January 20 to March 17, 2026, with award notifications the week of April 13, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Accelerator Fund and HOME-ARP Notice of Funding Availability
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City DHCD, the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services, and the Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs offered nearly $30 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds for the creation of permanent supportive housing and traditional affordable housing. Funding came from two sources: $15.2 million in State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) and $14.7 million from the HOME Investment Partnerships Program American Rescue Plan Act (HOME-ARP).
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum awards of up to $250,000 per unit for permanent supportive housing construction, up to $100,000 per unit for traditional affordable housing construction, and up to $500,000 for predevelopment costs associated with funded units. Total investment is nearly $30 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and organizations seeking to create permanent supportive housing or traditional affordable housing in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of permanent supportive housing and traditional affordable housing; predevelopment costs associated with funded housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Projects must meet Housing Accelerator Program threshold requirements to be eligible for a Letter of Support for the State's 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) round
Applications submitted through the Neighborly application portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submitted applications through the Neighborly application portal (portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd). A pre-proposal conference and application webinar were held prior to the November 20, 2023 deadline. Inquiries were directed to Paul Stanford, Director of Grants Administration.

structured_extraction.program_name: LIGHT Program (Living Independently with Greater Home-based Tools)
structured_extraction.program_description: LIGHT helps Baltimore City residents get free or low-cost services to make their homes safer, healthier, and more comfortable. LIGHT Coordinators meet with residents to assess their needs and connect them with programs such as home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, and lead hazard reduction. Assistance types include grants, forgivable loans (forgiven after 5 years if primary residence is maintained), and deferred loans (repaid from sale proceeds when property is sold). Eligible repairs include disability accessibility modifications, electrical, energy efficiency, HVAC, lead paint hazard reduction, plumbing, roof, sewer line, water line, and other repairs.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost intake, assessment, and referral services. LIGHT Coordinators connect residents to home repair, energy efficiency, and lead hazard reduction programs. Assistance types include grants, forgivable loans (forgiven after 5 years if primary residence is maintained), and deferred loans (repaid from sale proceeds when property is sold; loans secured by lien on home). Eligible repairs include disability accessibility modifications, electrical, energy efficiency, HVAC, lead paint hazard reduction, plumbing, roof, sewer line, water line, and other repairs. Some programs may have waiting lists.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners and renters needing home safety, health, or comfort improvements, including those with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting residents to home repair programs covering disability accessibility modifications, electrical, energy efficiency, HVAC, lead paint hazard reduction, plumbing, roof, sewer line, water line, and other repairs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Homeowners and renters are both eligible
Applicant must acknowledge information is true and correct to the best of their knowledge
Optional attachments accepted (photos, estimates, violation notices)
Some programs may have waiting lists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Three-stage process: (1) Submit a pre-application online through the Neighborly Software portal (https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD/participant) or by mail to LIGHT Intake and Assessment Unit, 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202, or email dhcd.light@baltimorecity.gov; (2) If pre-application is screened favorably, submit full application with supporting documents; (3) Program review for final determination.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Lead Hazard Reduction Program (LHRP) helps homeowners and landlords identify and address lead hazards in homes built before 1978. The program assesses the presence and location of lead hazards and pays for cost-effective interventions such as window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and structural repairs to make homes safe for children and pregnant women. The program also provides education and temporary relocation referrals as needed.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided as either a grant or a loan depending on the applicant's income and financial status. Homeowners and landlords may apply; landlords are expected to contribute a portion of the cost. Income limits apply and vary based on household size and whether the unit is owner-occupied or renter-occupied (e.g., $104,200 for a 4-person owner-occupied household; $65,150 for a 4-person renter-occupied household).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and landlords of homes built before 1978 where a pregnant woman or a child under age 6 lives (or regularly visits) and who meet income guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction interventions including window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs; education; temporary relocation referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City. Homes must have been built before 1978 within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Home must have been built before 1978
A pregnant woman or child under age 6 must live in the home, or a child must spend at least 3 hours per day on two separate days per week and at least 60 hours per year at the property
Applicants must meet income guidelines based on household size and owner/renter status
Landlords must contribute a portion of the cost of lead hazard reduction services
Lead hazards must be identified by a licensed lead inspector
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Neighborly Software portal or complete a paper pre-application and mail it to LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit, 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. Contact (443) 984-1613 with questions.
attachment_urls: https://s3.amazonaws.com/baltimorecity.gov.if-us-east-1/s3fs-public/2025-12/Lead Hazard Brochure Final Reduced File Address Update 2.pdf

structured_extraction.program_description: The Open Bid Program lets homeowners and small developers purchase and redevelop individual or small bundles of city-owned vacant and abandoned properties in Baltimore City. Applicants search available properties through the BuyIntoBmore portal, submit an application, and go through a background check and feasibility review. The goal is to turn vacant properties into productive uses that raise property values, create community amenities, increase local tax revenue, and attract new residents and businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned vacant and abandoned properties are sold to qualifying homeowners and small developers at bid price. Applicants must demonstrate $90,000 available for rehabilitation per property applied for. After award, the city routes a Land Disposition Agreement (LDA) and conducts lien abatement before settlement. A compliance officer monitors the project until a Use and Occupancy Permit is obtained.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and small developers interested in purchasing and redeveloping city-owned vacant or abandoned properties in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and rehabilitation of city-owned vacant and abandoned properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must have $90,000 available for rehabilitation per property applied for
Must not own vacant building inventory older than two years
Must not own vacant building inventory for less than two years without a recent open/active permit
Must not have open or pending criminal cases that could result in inability to complete the project
Must not have any open federal or state liens
Must not have any open federal or state judgments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Search and apply for available properties through the BuyIntoBmore portal. The application is reviewed for completeness and assigned to a Neighborhood Development Officer. A 2-week competing bid period follows. After the bid period closes, a Real Estate Officer conducts a background check and feasibility review. Successful applicants are notified of award, and a Land Disposition Agreement is routed for approval through the Board of Estimates. After approval, the city conducts lien abatement and the applicant selects a title company for settlement. A compliance officer monitors the project until a Use and Occupancy Permit is obtained.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DHCD Side Yard Program lets property owners adjacent to city-owned vacant lots purchase those lots at a fixed price to expand their property. Owners can use the purchased lots for gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, parking pads, decks, or other property expansion purposes, helping to reduce vacancy and beautify neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners can purchase adjacent city-owned vacant lots at a fixed price. The fixed side yard pricing applies to lots up to 1,500 square feet; lots larger than 1,500 square feet are subject to an additional cost per square foot and additional review. The maximum lot size is 5,000 square feet. Payment must be made by certified check, money order, or cashier's check. Some properties are subject to an ongoing annual ground rent that becomes the buyer's responsibility after settlement. The estimated total process time is approximately 120 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners who own and occupy a residence adjacent to a city-owned vacant lot in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of adjacent vacant city-owned lots for gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, parking pads, decks, or expansion of the existing property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City. Properties must be city-owned vacant lots adjacent to the applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: The side yard property must be vacant and unimproved.
The side yard property must be physically contiguous to the applicant's principal residence.
Priority is given to owner-occupants.
The property must consist of no more than two lots incapable of independent development as determined by local zoning and code enforcement.
The fixed price applies only to lots up to 1,500 SF; larger lots require additional review.
The maximum lot size is 5,000 SF.
The applicant must have a record of responsible property ownership and management.
Intended use must comply with Baltimore City laws and regulations.
Some uses require Zoning Administrator approval; contact (410) 396-4126 for requirements.
Settlement must occur within 60 days of an executed Land Disposition Agreement.
Payment must be submitted as a certified check, money order, or cashier's check in full.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete and submit an application including a disclosure of intended uses through the Buy Into B'More online portal. DHCD reviews the complete offer package and makes an award decision (estimated 30 days), followed by Board of Estimates approval (estimated 45 days), and then settlement (estimated 45 days), for an estimated total process time of 120 days. If approved, the applicant submits full payment by certified check, money order, or cashier's check.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a $10,000 forgivable loan to help people buy and rehabilitate homes that have been vacant for at least one year in Baltimore City, supporting the revitalization of long-vacant properties. No repayment is required if the buyer remains in the home for five years.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000 forgivable loan (no repayment required if the buyer stays in the home for five years). As of April 2026, 86 incentives remain available for the current fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding available through June 30 each fiscal year, on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Home buyers (both first-time and repeat) and developers purchasing or rehabilitating a previously vacant home in Baltimore City that has been subject to a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance and closing cost reduction toward the acquisition and rehabilitation of vacant properties in Baltimore City, including purchase and renovation of vacant homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within Baltimore City and must have had a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year before a developer rehabilitated it or before the new owner bought it to renovate.
requirements_list: Property must have been subject to a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year prior to transaction (developer rehabilitation or sale to home buyer)
Must present a Certificate of Occupancy when applying
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved counseling agency within one year before offer/purchase
Must contribute at least $1,000 of personal funds toward the purchase
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after application submission
Must provide Title Company's EIN in the application portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register and apply through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Registration requires an email and password with email validation via confirmation link. Include Certificate of Occupancy documentation and Title Company EIN. Submit at least 30 days before closing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Weatherization Assistance Program helps low-income households in Baltimore City reduce energy expenses by installing energy conservation materials and products. Free services include energy audits, safety testing and repair of heating and cooling systems, attic insulation, air sealing, LED lighting, carbon monoxide and smoke alarms, and Energy Star appliance replacement when existing appliances are inoperable or inefficient. Assistance may also include grants and forgivable loans (forgiven after 5 years if the property is maintained as primary residence) or deferred loans (due when property is sold). Available for both owner-occupied and tenant-occupied properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free weatherization services including energy audits, heating and cooling system repair and tune-up, insulation, air sealing, LED bulb replacement, low-flow fixtures, carbon monoxide and smoke alarm installation, and Energy Star appliance replacement. Assistance may also include grants and forgivable loans (forgiven after 5 years if the property is maintained as primary residence) or deferred loans (due when property is sold). No cash payment — services are provided directly to eligible households at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners and renters in Baltimore City whose household income falls within HUD FY25 income guidelines (up to 250% of the Federal Level of Poverty, based on household size). The program also considers disability status of household members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation improvements including insulation, air sealing, LED lighting, low-flow fixtures, heating and cooling system maintenance, carbon monoxide and smoke alarm installation, and replacement of inoperable or inefficient appliances with Energy Star-rated models. May also fund disability accessibility modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owner-occupied and tenant-occupied properties in Baltimore City, Maryland. Applications may be submitted online or mailed/delivered to LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit, 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202.
requirements_list: Must be income-eligible per HUD FY25 80%/250% FLP guidelines (e.g., $72,950 for 1-person household, $104,200 for 4-person household)
Owner-occupants must prove ownership via property tax bill, deed, SDAT sheet, property location plot, or mobile home title
Owner-occupants must have deed in own name or co-owned and be current on mortgage, ground rent, and property taxes
Rental properties require landlord/property owner documentation proving ownership and landlord contact information
Landlords must sign a Permission to Enter form and an Owner Agreement form
Lead-based paint screening required for pre-1978 homes with children under 6
Disability accessibility modifications may be assessed as part of repair concerns
Upon completion, each home must pass a Quality Control Inspection by a Weatherization Assistance Program inspector
Must be a low-income household
Some programs may have waiting lists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Neighborly Software portal (https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD/participant) or complete a paper pre-application and mail or deliver it to LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit, 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. The pre-application collects household income, property details, lead-paint history, and repair concerns and is used to determine eligibility for specific programs. Eligible applicants are then invited to submit a full application with supporting documents. Contact (410) 396-3023 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Joint Apprenticeship Program creates a coordinated, citywide apprenticeship ecosystem under the Department of Human Resources. It connects city agencies, contractors, and unions into a single pipeline, aligns capital contracts with apprenticeship goals, and creates entry points through pre-apprenticeship and training programs for young people. The program is made possible through a partnership with the Annie E. Casey Foundation.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A coordinated apprenticeship program connecting young people and job seekers with apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship opportunities across city agencies, contractors, and unions. Made possible through a partnership with the Annie E. Casey Foundation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people and job seekers in Baltimore City looking to enter apprenticeship programs through city agencies, contractors, or unions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce training and apprenticeship placement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Baltimore City Department of Human Resources for information on enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free training program for Baltimore City residents that builds community leadership around urban planning, zoning, and development. Each year, two six-week workshop series are held — one in fall and one in spring — covering zoning principles, the development review process, planning history, neighborhood planning, municipal budget, equitable development, and gentrification. Sessions are offered both in-person and online, and include off-site tours of development projects in the city. No prior planning experience is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six-week cohort-based training (Wednesday evenings, 6–7:30 PM) covering planning history, zoning, development review, neighborhood planning, municipal budget, equitable development, gentrification, and housing finance, plus site visits and specialized topics. Offered twice per year (fall and spring cohorts). Sessions are held in-person and online, with at least one off-site neighborhood tour per cohort. Cohort size is limited to approximately 30 participants to foster interaction and community building.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are currently closed, but will open in Summer of 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents interested in learning about urban planning, zoning, and neighborhood development; community-based project leaders; those seeking involvement in city government or community planning. No prior planning experience required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore City residents only. Preference points are given to residents from disinvested areas as identified by the Housing Market Typology, though this is a preference factor, not a barrier to eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Commitment to attend ALL scheduled meetings (approximately 2.5 hours per week)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted online via https://www.baltimoreplanningacity.com/. Applications are reviewed by a collaborative team from the Department of Planning (DOP) and Planning Academy Alumni, and ranked on responses to four essay questions. Selection criteria include dedication to Baltimore and interest in community support/leadership; preference is given to residents from disinvested areas per the Housing Market Typology. Applications open in Summer 2026 — check the program page or contact Alex Bauer at alex.bauer@baltimorecity.gov for updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: The CLIF Program distributes a portion of Maryland casino gaming revenues to benefit communities in the South Baltimore Gateway area surrounding Horseshoe Casino. The Baltimore City Department of Planning administers these funds, developing annual spending plans with input from the Local Development Council (LDC), city agencies, and community partners. Funding supports infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development (including housing), and other public services in the South Baltimore Gateway area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding allocated through CLIF Spending Plans, guided by the nine goals of the South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan. Specific amounts vary by annual spending plan. Funds may support infrastructure, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development, housing, and other public services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities working to benefit economic and community development in the South Baltimore Gateway area surrounding Horseshoe Casino.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and investments aligned with the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the South Baltimore Gateway area in Baltimore City, centered on Horseshoe Casino.
requirements_list: Projects must benefit the South Baltimore Gateway area
Funding must align with one or more of the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals
Spending plans are developed in consultation with the Local Development Council (LDC), city agencies, community partners, and neighborhood associations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Annual spending plans are developed by the Baltimore City Department of Planning in consultation with the LDC, city agencies, and community partners. Final funding decisions are made as part of the City budget approval by the Mayor and City Council. Contact Chris Firehock for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A neighborhood beautification competition and grant program run by Clean Corps during summer 2026. Residents and community organizations can apply for up to $1,500 in financial support for block-level cleaning and beautification projects such as cleaning streets, alleys, and greenspaces. The program draws inspiration from the AFRO Clean Block competitions of the past and aims to help residents create healthy, beautiful neighborhoods. Up to 20% of funds may be used for refreshments, and funds may be layered with other funding sources. The program includes three winner categories: Youth Power, Small but Mighty, and Best Community Glo-up.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,500 per neighborhood for block-level cleaning and beautification projects. Includes supplies, technical expertise, and organizing support. Up to 20% of funds may be used for refreshments. Funds may be layered with other funding sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, neighborhood associations, faith-based organizations, schools, and community groups who want to beautify their local streets, alleys, or greenspaces; priority given to applications in or near Clean Corps service areas (42 neighborhoods across the city as of 2025); main contact must live in the project neighborhood
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Block-level cleaning and beautification projects including streets, alleys, and greenspaces; must include trash collection or a beautification element (art, plants, lights, seating) and neighborhood resident participation; up to 20% for refreshments; can be layered with other funding sources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City; anyone located in Baltimore City is eligible, but applications located in or near a Clean Corps service area (currently 42 neighborhoods across the city) will be prioritized

Priority given to applications in/near Clean Corps service areas
Projects must include trash collection OR a beautification element (art, plants, lights, seating)
Projects must include neighborhood resident participation
Project site must be accessible and benefit the broader community
Submit final report with before/after photos, trash bag count, participant numbers, and activation count

Current W-9 from fiscal organization (dated and signed in 2026) if using a fiscal sponsor

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the interest form available as a PDF or Word document linked on the program page. Submit by May 15, 2026 along with project site photos and coordinator signature. A fiscal organization W-9 and any required property permission forms must also be included. Participants are notified May 22nd and supplies/money distributed starting June 1st. Projects take place between June and August.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City provides capital funding to nonprofit cultural organizations for physical improvements to their facilities. Every two years, eligible organizations can apply for General Obligation (GO) bonds to fund capital projects such as roof replacements, elevator upgrades, building envelope improvements, plaza upgrades, or museum expansions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1 million per year is available in FY2026 and FY2027, with individual awards capped at $200,000 over a two-year period. Typical awards range from $50,000 to $100,000 over the two-year cycle. Funds are provided through General Obligation bonds for eligible capital improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit museums, galleries, theaters, and other arts and cultural venues located in Baltimore City (including those in designated arts and entertainment districts)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to facilities with a minimum 15-year service life, including building envelope upgrades, roof replacements, elevator replacements, plaza or entrance improvements, museum or exhibit expansions, preliminary studies/surveys, and permanent property improvements. Does not include projects costing less than $50,000, vehicular equipment, routine maintenance items under $100,000, or salaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must have a physical location in Baltimore City and either own the facility or hold a long-term lease with primary responsibility for capital improvements. The facility must be open to the general public. For venues other than museums, galleries, and theaters, the facility must be located within a designated arts and entertainment district.
requirements_list: Must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must have a physical location in Baltimore City
Must own the facility or have a long-term lease of at least 15 years with primary responsibility for capital improvements
Facility must be open to the general public
For venues other than museums, galleries, and theaters, must be located within a designated arts and entertainment district
Eligible projects must cost at least $50,000 and have a minimum 15-year service life
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grant application is released in February. Applicants may attend virtual information sessions in March. Applications are submitted by the April deadline via Microsoft Word document to the contact. Award notifications are sent in June, contingent on capital budget approval. The program operates on a biennial cycle; the FY2026-2027 cycle closed April 30, 2025, with the next cycle (FY2028-2029) expected to open approximately February 2027.

structured_extraction.program_name: Northwest Neighborhood Grants Program (Pimlico Local Impact Aid track)
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds community-led projects in neighborhoods near Pimlico Racecourse in Baltimore City, including operating funds and physical improvements. The program is made possible by Pimlico Local Impact Aid (State video lottery terminal revenue, annually allocated by State statute). In 2025, the program expanded to serve projects in both the Park Heights Master Plan Area and the One Mile Radius around Pimlico.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $500 and $25,000 to support community-led projects including operating funds and physical improvements. Eligible project types include public art, local arts, signage, bicycle amenities, streetscaping, marketing, education, community events, and technical assistance. Previous cycles offered up to $30,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Priority Application Deadline: Friday, March 28, 2025 at 11:59 PM EDT (2025 cycle closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, mission-based organizations with a fiscal sponsor, faith-based organizations (non-religious public-benefit projects), and public schools (community-based projects) in the Park Heights Master Plan Area and the One Mile Radius around Pimlico Racecourse in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: The Pimlico Local Impact Aid program (also called 'slots funding' or 'casino revenue') distributes funding to community partners and agencies for a wide variety of community development projects in the area around Pimlico Racetrack in Baltimore City. Eligible uses include infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development (including housing), and other public services and improvements. The Pimlico Community Development Authority advises the Mayor on priorities, scores applications using a published scoring rubric, and publishes recommendations; final funding decisions are made through the City budget approval process by the Mayor and City Council. The current statute provides for Pimlico Local Impact Aid for 20 years, through fiscal year 2032. Approximately 85% of funds are allocated to projects in the Park Heights Master Plan Area and 15% to the One-Mile Radius Area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to community partners and agencies for community development projects in the eligible funding areas around Pimlico Racetrack (Park Heights Master Plan Area and/or One-Mile Radius Area). Revenue derives from State Video Lottery Terminals (also called 'slots funding' or 'casino revenue'). Approximately 85% of funds are allocated to projects in the Park Heights Master Plan Area and 15% to the One-Mile Radius Area. Starting in FY26, projects must be for at least $25,000. Funding amounts vary by project and are determined through an annual application and review process. The Pimlico Community Development Authority scores applications and advises the Mayor, with final spending plans approved as part of the City budget. The program is authorized through fiscal year 2032.

Authority under State Law § 9-1A-31.

structured_extraction.program_name: B'more Fresh: Online SNAP Produce Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: B'more Fresh is an online and in-store SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) incentive program run by Baltimore City that encourages Baltimore City SNAP participants to buy more fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables. Participants who spend at least $5 per month using their SNAP EBT card at participating retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway) receive a $30 produce incentive each month. At Amazon Fresh, participants receive a $30 produce benefit coupon and a $20 delivery promotion coupon, both credited to the customer's Amazon Benefits Balance after delivery and valid for 60 days. At Giant, a $30 produce voucher is automatically added to the participant's online account. At Safeway, participants receive $30 in digital produce deals (three $10 digital deals) loaded to their Safeway for U account at the start of the following month, plus one free grocery delivery per month. Orders must be placed online for curbside pick-up or delivery in Baltimore City (Amazon Fresh and Giant), or made in-store at a Baltimore City Safeway location. A Prime account is not required for Amazon Fresh. The program is funded by the American Rescue Plan Act and runs through December 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Planning, Food Policy and Planning Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each month, SNAP/EBT cardholders who spend at least $5 on SNAP-eligible items through a participating retailer receive a $30 produce benefit. At Amazon Fresh: a $30 produce voucher and a $20 delivery promotion coupon are credited to the customer's Amazon Benefits Balance after delivery; both are valid for 60 days. At Giant: a $30 produce voucher is automatically added to the participant's online account. At Safeway: $30 in digital produce deals (three $10 digital deals) are loaded to the participant's Safeway for U account at the start of the next month, plus one free grocery delivery per month. Vouchers and deals are redeemable for fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat. The program is funded through December 2026 via the American Rescue Plan Act.

For Amazon Fresh, the participant's Amazon account must have a Baltimore City zip code as the default address. For Safeway, participants must shop at a Safeway location situated in Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application is required. For Amazon Fresh: (1) Create or log in to an Amazon account. (2) Add your SNAP/EBT card to your Amazon Payments Wallet using a Baltimore City address as the default. (3) Spend $5 in SNAP funds at Amazon Fresh. (4) Wait for delivery. (5) Receive the $30 produce benefit coupon and $20 delivery coupon in your Amazon Benefits Balance. (6) Redeem coupons within 60 days. (7) Repeat each month with a qualifying $5 SNAP purchase. For Giant: Shop online using your SNAP/EBT card; after spending $5 on SNAP-eligible items, a $30 produce voucher is automatically added to your online account. For Safeway: (1) Create a free Safeway for U account online or in-store. (2) Shop at a Baltimore City Safeway and spend $5 or more with your SNAP EBT card. (3) Enter your phone number at the pin pad at checkout. (4) Digital produce deals are loaded to your Safeway for U account on the first of the next month. You can also visit amazon.com/bmoresnap or safeway.com for retailer-specific details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Stormwater Fee Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Public Works offers credits and reductions on the stormwater remediation fee for property owners and organizations that take actions to reduce stormwater runoff. Eligible participants include single-family homeowners, businesses, churches, non-profits, industrial properties, faith organizations, and tax-exempt organizations. Eligible activities include installing stormwater best management practices (BMPs) such as rain gardens, rain barrels, and trees; participating in volunteer community cleanup and tree-planting events; and qualifying for special reductions based on property characteristics or organization type. Separate tracks exist for single-family property owners, non-single-family properties, faith organizations, and tax-exempt organizations seeking a hardship exemption through an alternative compliance plan. Faith organizations receive a fee reduction for places of worship and schools. Tax-exempt organizations facing financial hardship may apply for an exemption through an alternative compliance plan demonstrating stormwater runoff reduction practices.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners and organizations receive credits that reduce their stormwater remediation fee. Single-family owners earn credits by volunteering at organized water quality events or installing and maintaining qualifying BMPs. Credit amounts for single-family properties include: $10/year per 4 hours of volunteer participation, $5/year for tree planting, $25 one-time for rain barrels (50 gal+), $8/year for small rain gardens, $16/year for large rain gardens, and up to 45% for other BMP types. Volunteers in community cleanups earn $10 off the stormwater fee per certificate, up to 3 certificates per year (maximum $30/year); the credit is valid for one year. Non-single-family properties (businesses, nonprofits, churches, industries) can receive credits for BMP installation, green space, small development status (up to 820 sq ft impervious area), having less than 50 sq ft of impervious area, holding an NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit (credit valid for five years), maintaining private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor (credit valid for five years), or maintaining cemetery streets open to the public. Faith organizations receive a fee reduction for places of worship and schools. Tax-exempt organizations (IRC §501(c)(3) or (d)) facing hardship can apply for an exemption if their stormwater fee exceeds 0.75% of total annual revenue (capped at $1,000,000/year) and they establish a Green Team of at least 5 members; the exemption must be renewed annually. Credits are reviewed within 30 days of receipt of a complete application and are approved for 1–3 year periods depending on credit type (e.g., five years for NPDES and Harbor Discharger credits).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City property owners and ratepayers including single-family homeowners, businesses, churches, non-profits, industrial properties, faith organizations, and tax-exempt organizations who pay the Baltimore City stormwater remediation fee
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or exemption of the Baltimore City stormwater remediation fee in exchange for installing and maintaining stormwater best management practices (BMPs), volunteering for organized water quality activities, or implementing an alternative compliance plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties located within Baltimore City only. Off-site BMPs must be in the same 8-digit watershed as the property receiving credit. The Direct Harbor Discharge credit is limited to properties draining to Baltimore Harbor via private stormwater systems.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Baltimore City
Single-family owners must volunteer at organized water quality events or install and maintain approved BMPs (e.g., trees, rain gardens, rain barrels)

Non-single-family properties must qualify under one or more credit categories: less than 50 sq ft impervious area, small development up to 820 sq ft impervious area, BMP installation, green space, NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit, private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor, or privately maintained cemetery streets open to the public
Faith organizations must use property as a place of worship or school

Tax-exempt organizations seeking hardship exemption must be organized under IRC §501(c)(3) or (d), have total annual revenue not exceeding $1,000,000, and have a stormwater fee exceeding 0.75% of total annual revenue
Tax-exempt organizations seeking hardship exemption must establish a Green Team of at least 5 members with executive director/congregational leader support
Tax-exempt organizations receiving a hardship exemption must renew the exemption annually, submitting renewal at least 30 days before the end of the exemption period
Tax-exempt organizations must own property or provide current lease showing responsibility for water/sewer charges
Tax-exempt organizations must implement an approved Alternative Compliance Plan (ACP) including at least one BMP installation and at least 3 of 5 outreach/education activities annually
Submit a completed stormwater fee credit application with supporting documentation (photos, sketches, maintenance records, certificates as applicable)
Applications are reviewed within 30 days of receipt of a complete application package
Property owner must maintain active credit status and reapply at end of each credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Single-family owners complete and submit the stormwater fee credit application form with supporting documentation and may download the Single Family Property Guidance Document for instructions. Non-single-family properties and faith organizations should download the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document for detailed instructions and the application form. Tax-exempt organizations seeking a hardship exemption must download and complete the Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program Plan and submit it to DPW. Volunteer community cleanup participants must register their event by calling 311 or via the DPW Volunteer Network (www.bit.ly/volunteerDPW), participate in the registered cleanup, receive a certificate, then submit their certificate and application to DPW. Applications may be submitted by mail to: Bureau of Water and Wastewater, Abel Wolman Municipal Building, 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Attn: Customer Support and Services Division, Baltimore, MD 21202, or by email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov with subject line 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION'. Decisions are issued within 30 days of a complete application; retroactive credit is applied if the Department misses the 30-day window. Denials may be appealed in writing within 30 days to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater. Credits require renewal at the end of each approval period (varies by credit type).

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) provides resources to support community-organized neighborhood cleanups. Two tracks are available: the Pitch-In Dumpster Request provides dumpsters for large-scale cleanups with 20 or more volunteers (up to four dumpsters per neighborhood per year), and the Solid Waste Clean-up Request supports smaller cleanups with fewer than 20 participants by lending tools and supplying gloves, bags, and pickers, then collecting the debris at the end of the event.

For large cleanups (20+ volunteers), neighborhoods may request up to four dumpsters per year. For smaller cleanups (fewer than 20 participants), DPW supplies materials and collects debris at the event's conclusion.

Organizers must provide an event flyer and confirm the date and location. The 311 team reviews requests to ensure the annual allotment is not exceeded. Once approved, DPW finalizes the request and places dumpsters at designated locations. After confirmation, email the event flyer to dpwpitchin@baltimorecity.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: DPW Small Business Development Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Public Works (DPW) offers a Small Business Development (SBD) Training Program — an 11-week intensive training course for small businesses in the construction industry seeking to compete for Baltimore City contracts. The program covers construction management topics including bonding, construction accounting and finance, construction best practices (trenchless sewer repair, site restoration, manhole repair, lateral connections), contract administration, estimating and bidding, M/WBE certification, prequalification for City contracts, OSHA 10-hour safety certification, project scheduling, and marketing. Training modules valued at $1,199 are available for $199 per participant, and scholarships are available for firms experiencing financial hardship. The program is particularly focused on supporting local, minority-, and women-owned small businesses.

Scholarships are also available for firms experiencing financial hardship — applicants must complete the scholarship questions on the application by July 26th to be considered. Training covers project management, scheduling, accounting, construction industry best practices, estimating and bidding, bonding, M/WBE certification, prequalification, OSHA 10-hour safety certification, contract administration, and marketing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Public Works (DPW) reimburses residential customers and property owners for clean-up, disinfection, and disposal costs after sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events (at least ¼ inch of precipitation in 24 hours that causes sewer lines to surcharge or overflow). Reimbursement covers documented expenses up to $5,000 per dwelling unit per event, including any insurance deductible paid that is clearly linked to cleanup or disinfection costs. Insured applicants must first obtain a final written determination from their insurance company before their application can be processed. Applications must be submitted within 90 days of the backup, and final decisions are issued within 60 days of receiving all required documentation. Commercial properties are explicitly excluded. The program is part of Baltimore City's Sanitary Sewer Consent Decree Program and applies to incidents occurring on or after April 6, 2018. The program applies to incidents within Baltimore City's sewage collection system service area, which includes sewersheds such as Jones Falls, High Level, Herring Run, Patapsco, Gwynns Falls, Low Level, Outfall, Dundalk, and Chinquapin Run. The program originated as a three-year pilot under the Modified Consent Decree (entered October 2017), with a planned transition to a long-term program; the current status of the long-term program has not been confirmed in available documentation.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to $5,000 per dwelling unit per qualifying sewage backup event for reasonable, documented clean-up, disinfection, and disposal costs, including any insurance deductible paid that is tied to those costs. Applications must be submitted within 90 days of the backup. If the property has insurance covering backups, a final written insurance determination must be obtained first and may be submitted up to 30 days after receipt. Applications are processed within 60 days of receiving all required documentation. Commercial properties are explicitly excluded.

Applicant must be a Baltimore City residential customer or property owner (homeowner, renter, non-commercial occupant, or tenant) — commercial properties are explicitly excluded
Sewage backup must have occurred on or after April 6, 2018

Application must be received within 90 days after the backup

Submit all documentation provided to and received from your insurance company, including proof of any deductible paid
Tenants must provide a copy of their lease signed by the owner of record
Those filing on behalf of an owner or tenant must provide written proof of power of attorney
Documentation of all cleanup, disinfection, and disposal expenses must be submitted with the application

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Baltimore City DPW website, or submit a completed paper application by email, certified U.S. mail, or equivalent commercial delivery to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater. Residents can call 410-396-3500 to request a mailed application. Notify the City through the 311 system within 24 hours of discovering the backup incident. Submit all required documentation with the application within 90 days of the backup. If the property is insured, you must first obtain a final written determination from your insurer (which may be submitted up to 30 days after receipt). Applications are reviewed within 60 days. If approved, a Release for Signature will be sent; once signed and returned, a reimbursement check is processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hardship Exemption Program (Hardship Water Bill Discount Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Hardship Exemption Program exempts eligible low-income Baltimore City residents from paying the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee on their water/sewer bills. Eligibility is based on the same criteria used by the State's Office of Home Energy Program. Applicants must be City of Baltimore residents who receive a water/sewer bill directly from the City and must be either the property owner-of-record or a tenant with lease responsibility for the water/sewer charges. They must meet at least two of the following criteria: receives energy assistance subsidy; receives public assistance (SSI, food stamps, or medical assistance); receives veterans, Social Security, or Social Security disability benefits; or meets gross income criteria (e.g., max monthly income of $1,770 for a household of 1, increasing by $630 per additional person). Approved customers must reapply each year to maintain the exemption.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved customers are exempted from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee on all future water/sewer bills. The exemption must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners and tenants in Baltimore City who receive a water/sewer bill directly from the City and meet income or public assistance criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee on the applicant's water/sewer bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to City of Baltimore residents who receive a water/sewer bill directly from the City.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Baltimore resident who receives a water/sewer bill directly from the City
Must be the property owner-of-record with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, or provide a lease showing responsibility for paying water/sewer charges at that property

Submit the completed application and supporting documents by email to dpw.billing@baltimorecity.gov, by mail, or in person at 200 Holliday St., Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202. Must reapply annually to maintain the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Medical Exemption Program protects water service for people who are seriously ill or caring for someone who is seriously ill and lives at a Baltimore City address. If shutting off water service would harm the health of the resident or the person they care for, this program prevents water shutoff. Approval is valid for one year and must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved participants receive protection from water service shutoff for one year due to medical necessity. The exemption must be renewed each year by reapplying.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents with delinquent water accounts who have a qualifying serious illness or life-support equipment dependency, including homeowners, renters, or caregivers who pay a city water/sewer bill and whose health — or the health of someone they care for — would be harmed if water service were shut off.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prevents water and sewer service shutoff at a Baltimore City address when shutoff would cause medical harm.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside at a Baltimore City address that receives a water/sewer bill directly from the city.
requirements_list: Must live at the service address
Must provide proof of address (utility bill, credit card statement, bank statement, or lease/mortgage document)
Must receive a water/sewer bill directly from the city for the address

Must provide written certification from a licensed medical doctor on official letterhead stating that water service is medically necessary and that shutoff would cause harm (e.g., serious illness or life-support equipment dependence)
Medical condition must either aggravate an existing serious illness or prevent use of life-support equipment
Applicant and doctor must both sign the application
Caregivers must reside at the same address as the person they care for and must pay the water/sewer bill
If the account is delinquent, the applicant must enter into a payment arrangement and keep the account current
Exemption is valid for one year and must be renewed annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Medical Exemption application form, or call 410-396-5398 to have it mailed to you. Complete and sign the application (both the applicant/caregiver and the doctor must sign). Attach copies of required documents. Submit by email to dpw.billing@baltimorecity.gov, or mail/drop off to Baltimore City DPW - Medical Exemption Program, 200 Holliday St. Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. A decision letter is issued within 5–7 business days of receiving a complete packet.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City Department of Public Works offers flexible, interest-free payment plans to help residents and businesses pay off past-due water and sewer bills. Residential customers can use PromisePay to set up a payment plan for balances of $50 or more, with additional options available for balances between $250 and $5,000. Plans keep water service active and help customers avoid financial consequences. Commercial customers can contact a water customer service analyst directly to arrange a plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free payment plans for past-due water and sewer balances. Residential plans through PromisePay are available for balances of $50 or more, with additional PromisePay options for balances between $250 and $5,000. Plans keep water service active and allow customers to pay off past-due charges over time while avoiding financial consequences. Commercial businesses can also set up payment plans by contacting a water customer service analyst at the Department of Public Works.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential and commercial water and sewer customers with past-due balances. Residential customers with balances of $50 or more can use PromisePay; those with balances between $250 and $5,000 have additional PromisePay options.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying off past-due water and sewer bill balances through a structured, interest-free payment plan while keeping water service active.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Baltimore City water and sewer customers.

Residential customers must have a past-due balance of $50 or more to use PromisePay

Commercial customers can call 410-396-5398 or visit in person at 200 Holliday St., 4th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202 (Monday–Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm).

structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free weekly curbside recycling collection service provided to registered Baltimore City Public Schools at no cost. Schools receive an assigned collection day and a confirmation email within 5–7 business days of registering.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City Public Schools seeking free recycling collection services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recycling collection service for schools — reduces landfill waste, conserves resources, and supports environmental education

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) provides free professional cleaning and disinfection services to residential customers whose property was damaged by a sewage backup caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event (when at least ¼ inch of rain falls within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow). The city contracts with professional cleaning vendors to clean, disinfect, deodorize, remove soiled materials (carpet, flooring, furniture, and other damaged property), and dehumidify affected areas at no cost to the resident. The program is part of the Sanitary Sewer Consent Decree Program and was launched as a 12-month pilot program. Commercial properties are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free professional cleaning, disinfection, disposal, deodorization, and dehumidification services provided at no cost to eligible residential customers. DPW contracts with third-party professional cleaning vendors who perform all work directly at the affected property. Services include cleaning and disinfecting affected areas, removal and disposal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other damaged materials, odor removal, drying, and dehumidification. The on-call cleaning contractor will contact the customer within one hour of notification, and contractors offer cleanup appointments from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. Services are only available for damage caused by capacity-related wet-weather events. Commercial properties are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners, renters, tenants, and property managers) of both single-family and multi-family residential properties whose property suffered sewage backup damage due to a capacity-related wet-weather event. Commercial properties are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional cleanup services including cleaning and disinfection of affected areas, removal and disposal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other damaged materials, odor removal, drying, and dehumidification of areas affected by sewage backup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to owners, residents, and tenants of residential properties (both single-family and multi-family) located within Baltimore City. Commercial properties are explicitly excluded. Does not apply to properties impacted by water main breaks, dry-weather backups, stormwater flooding, or clogs.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner, tenant, or property manager) of a single-family or multi-family residential property.
Sewage backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event (at least ¼ inch of precipitation within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow).
Must report the damage to DPW by calling 311 or visiting the 311-services page online as soon as the backup is discovered.
The City must confirm that the damage was caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event (DPW will send an inspector).
Eligibility is limited to either the SOS Cleanup Program or the Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups — not both.
Does not apply to backups caused by clogs (wet wipes, roots, fats, oil, grease) or maintenance-related issues.
Commercial properties are not eligible.
Does not apply to damage caused by water main breaks.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 311 or visit the Baltimore City 311-services page online (311.baltimorecity.gov) to report the sewage backup damage as soon as it is discovered. DPW will send an inspector to confirm the cause of the backup. If confirmed to be from a capacity-related wet-weather event, DPW will contact the on-call cleaning contractor within one hour of notification. Contractors offer cleanup appointments from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week, scheduled at the customer's convenience. All services are provided at no cost. In the event of an extended period between the backup and the discovery of damage, customers may be able to use DPW's Expedited Reimbursement Program instead. For service complaints or concerns, call 410-396-3500.

structured_extraction.program_description: Eligible tax-exempt organizations in Baltimore City can apply for a hardship exemption from the stormwater fee by submitting an alternative compliance plan. The plan allows these organizations to protect the environment and reduce stormwater runoff and pollution rather than pay the fee. Charitable/nonprofit organizations with §501(c)(3) or (d) IRS exemption qualify for the hardship exemption; veterans organizations with §501(c)(4) or (19) IRS exemption qualify for full exemption. Faith/religious organizations may receive a reduced fee of $1/ERU/month for properties used exclusively for worship or K–12 education. Hardship exemption re-certification is required annually; most stormwater credits are valid for 3 years, while activity-based BMPs are valid for 1 year.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full or partial exemption from the stormwater remediation fee for eligible tax-exempt organizations that submit and implement an alternative compliance plan demonstrating stormwater runoff and pollution reduction practices. Charitable/nonprofit organizations with §501(c)(3) or (d) IRS exemption qualify for the hardship exemption; veterans organizations with §501(c)(4) or (19) IRS exemption qualify for full exemption. Religious nonprofits may receive a reduced fee of $1/ERU/month for properties used exclusively for worship or K–12 education. Hardship exemption re-certification is required annually; most stormwater credits are valid for 3 years, while activity-based BMPs are valid for 1 year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt organizations (including 501(c)(3), 501(c)(d), 501(c)(4), and 501(c)(19) organizations), faith/religious organizations, and other non-single-family property owners in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption or reduction of stormwater fee obligation in exchange for implementing stormwater management practices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City properties only; restricted to non-single-family (non-residential) properties. Off-site treatment BMPs must be located in the same 8-digit watershed as the property to which the credit will be applied. Harbor Discharger Credit requires privately maintained and owned storm drains directly to the Baltimore Harbor.
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt organization (e.g., §501(c)(3), (d), (4), or (19) IRS designation)
Must own or operate a non-single-family property in Baltimore City
For hardship exemption: must submit a written alternative compliance plan and receive Department approval
Hardship exemption requires annual re-certification to maintain exempt status
Faith/religious organizations must apply for the special reduced fee applicable to places of worship and K–12 schools
Most stormwater credits require renewal every 3 years; activity-based BMPs require annual renewal
Renewal application must be received within 30 days before the end of the credit period to ensure credit is reflected on subsequent water bill
Credit applications are reviewed and decided within 30 days of receipt of a complete application package
Off-site treatment BMPs must be in the same 8-digit watershed as the subject property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis year-round. Submit application via the online portal at PublicWorks.Baltimorecity.gov or contact the Customer Support and Services Division by phone at (410) 396-5398. The hardship exemption requires submission of a written alternative compliance plan that must be approved by the Department. Applications are reviewed within 30 days of receipt of a complete package. Annual re-certification is required to maintain the exemption. Download the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document for details on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water and Sewer Adjustment Request (Water Bill Adjustment Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) allows property owners and their authorized representatives to request a review of their water and sewer billing account to determine if they qualify for a bill adjustment due to interior plumbing leaks or underground pipe leaks. Two types of adjustments are available: an interior/situational usage adjustment (credits 50% of excess water usage above average consumption for up to three consecutive months of highest usage, or 100% for customers enrolled in senior or hardship discount programs) and an underground leak adjustment (removes all excess water and sewer volumetric charges caused by an underground leak, provided a licensed plumber repaired it and proof is submitted). Approved adjustments reduce the amount owed on water and sewer charges for the affected billing period and appear on the bill approximately 4 weeks after DPW receives the request. Sewer volumetric charges are included in the adjustment calculation for both adjustment types. Water loss due to theft or vandalism is not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A bill adjustment reduces the water and/or sewer charges on a customer's account. For interior/situational leaks, 50% of excess water usage above average consumption is credited for up to three consecutive months of highest usage (100% for customers enrolled in senior or hardship discount programs). For underground leaks, all excess water and sewer volumetric charges from the leak period are removed. As of modifications effective September 1, 2022, one of each adjustment type (underground and interior/situational) may be granted once every twelve months per property (previously once every 2 years for underground and once every 3 years for interior/situational). Sewer volumetric charges are included in the calculation for both adjustment types. Water loss due to theft or vandalism is not eligible. The adjustment appears on the bill approximately 4 weeks after DPW receives the request form.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 60 days of the bill being issued
structured_extraction.contact_name: DPW Customer Support and Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City water and sewer customers whose bills were unusually high due to a leak or plumbing problem, including property owners and their authorized representatives. Applies to residents who receive bills from the City for water, wastewater, and/or storm water charges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of water and/or sewer volumetric charges on a Baltimore City water bill due to qualifying interior plumbing leaks or underground pipe leaks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners and customers with water or sewer service accounts within Baltimore City served by DPW water and sewer billing. Baltimore County customers are not subject to the 2022 modification directives.
requirements_list: Only the legal property owner or an authorized designee may request an adjustment
Adjustment requests must be submitted within 60 days of the bill being issued
No leak adjustments will be granted if the property has an active leak or the known leak has not been repaired
Repairs must be completed prior to submission
For underground leak adjustments, a receipt from a certified/licensed plumber is required showing the date of repair, type of repair, and confirmation the repair was completed
Water consumption data must support repair receipts if available
Theft or vandalism-related water loss is not eligible
As of September 1, 2022, underground leak adjustments may only be granted once every twelve months per property (previously once every two years)
As of September 1, 2022, interior/situational usage adjustments may only be granted once every twelve months per property (previously once every three years)
Sewer volumetric charges are included in the adjustment calculation for both adjustment types
A standardized request form is required for submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Water and Sewer Adjustment Request form (available online at the Baltimore City website or by download/print) and submit it to DPW Customer Support and Services Division by mail to 200 Holliday St., Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or in person at 200 Holliday St., First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202, or via the Customer Support Page online. If approved, the adjustment will appear on the bill approximately 4 weeks after DPW receives the form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water4All program helps Baltimore City residents pay their water bills. It provides discounts on water and sewer charges based on household income and protects eligible tenants and homeowners from service shut-offs or property liens when they cannot pay their water bill.

Eligible households receive a discount on their water bill. Approval may take up to three months to appear on the bill. Applicants must reapply each year.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City only

Submit proof of income and identification for all household members over 18, along with a copy of the most recent water bill. Applicants can visit a Community Action Partnership center for help completing the application. You will be contacted after submission or if additional information is needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The GROW Center connects Baltimore City residents, communities, and faith-based groups with free and low-cost materials, information, and technical expertise for greening projects. structured_extraction.program_name: BMORE Beautiful Grant Opportunities (Love Your Block, Care-A-Lot, Say YES! Youth Environmental Stewards)
structured_extraction.program_description: BMORE Beautiful offers seasonal grant programs to support community beautification efforts in Baltimore City. Three grant tracks are available: (1) Care-A-Lot Grant – supports organizations that mow and maintain up to 25 vacant lots during the growing season (April–October); (2) Say YES! – Youth Environmental Stewards – supports community-based organizations that engage up to five youth (who must live in the neighborhood where they work) in neighborhood cleaning and beautification, with community leaders providing supervision and mentorship (offered in spring and fall, reopens April 2026); and (3) Love Your Block – micro-grants of up to $1,500 for small block-level projects focused on reducing litter and improving the look and safety of neighborhoods (offered in summer, reopens July 2026). All programs are open to residents, neighborhood groups, and community organizations in Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_description: PARKNPLAY grants support Friends of Parks Groups working to care for public parks, community gardens, and natural areas within the Baltimore City Department of Recreation and Parks.
