structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Transportation (DOT) allows community groups to create art, greenery, signage, parklets, and other creative projects in public spaces like streets, sidewalks, and alleys. Projects can improve neighborhood appearance, calm traffic, and create gathering spaces. The community group applying must fund the project itself. Project types include painted designs in the right-of-way, landscape plantings, planters and barriers for traffic calming, neighborhood signage, parklets (temporary public spaces in parking spots), and special projects like plazas or public art installations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DOT reviews and approves community-led projects in public right-of-way. Applicants receive a written approval agreement outlining what is approved, the project timeline, maintenance responsibilities, and any special conditions. DOT provides guidance on design standards and traffic calming requirements. No financial assistance is provided — the applying group must fund the project itself.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups, neighborhood associations, local businesses, nonprofits, and school parent groups in Baltimore City who want to install creative or beautification projects in public spaces such as streets, sidewalks, and alleys.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — the program provides approval and guidance, not funding. Community groups use their own funds to install painted street art, landscape plantings, planters and barriers, neighborhood signs, parklets, or special projects like plazas or public art in Baltimore City's public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Baltimore City only, in locations maintained by the Baltimore City Department of Transportation.
requirements_list: Applicant must pay for the project
Submit a design rendering
Provide project location(s) and materials list
Obtain letters of support or signed petitions from 60% of adjacent occupants (block for mid-block projects; three properties in each direction for intersections)
Provide proof of property owner support from directly abutting properties
Provide proof that the organization is in good standing with the State of Maryland
Carry commercial liability insurance ($1 million per occurrence, $2 million aggregate) for parklets and special projects
Submit a maintenance plan

All paint must be pre-approved by DOT

Projects must not block walkways or violate ADA requirements, create roadway safety hazards, require unreasonable DOT maintenance, damage public utilities, or include obscene content or harmful plants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project designs and supporting documents through the DOT Community-Led Placemaking Program Application (linked at the end of the program page). If your project includes new traffic calming elements, either submit a 311 traffic calming request first and wait for DOT approval, or hire a contractor with DOT-approved plans. Email DOTcommunityprograms@baltimorecity.gov to confirm location eligibility before hiring a contractor. Once approved, you receive a written agreement with project terms.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Fire Department provides free smoke alarms to Baltimore City residents. structured_extraction.program_description: YH2O is a pre-apprenticeship and mentoring program offered in partnership with the Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW), administered by the Mayor's Office of Employment Development (MOED). structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Works for Wind (MWW) is a workforce development and job training program that prepares residents for careers in the offshore wind industry. The program operates in both Baltimore City (administered by the Mayor's Office of Employment Development) and Baltimore County (administered by the Department of Economic and Workforce Development). Participants earn certifications or complete apprenticeships in welding, electrical, manufacturing, construction, and maritime/transportation/distribution/logistics (MTDL). Career Navigators help match participants with partner organizations—including community colleges, trade unions, and nonprofits—based on career interests. Supportive services are available to address barriers to employment, and may include child-care aid, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire, and transportation assistance.

Baltimore City participants have access to seven training companies; Baltimore County participants are matched with community colleges, trade unions, and nonprofits offering carpentry, CDL, CNC, electrical, welding, heavy equipment operation, and more.

The program also promotes self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs for people experiencing homelessness. This page documents the FY 2023 local competition cycle, which closed on August 21, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 Continuum of Care (CoC) NOFO Program Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) program promotes a community-wide commitment to ending homelessness. It provides federal funding to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to quickly rehouse individuals and families experiencing homelessness while minimizing trauma and dislocation. The program also promotes self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs. Baltimore City's Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) runs a local competition to determine which projects are submitted to HUD for funding. Eligible project types include permanent supportive housing (PSH), rapid re-housing (RRH), transitional housing (TH), supportive services only (SSO), coordinated entry, HMIS, and joint TH-RRH models.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal HUD CoC grants awarded to selected nonprofit providers and city government agencies for projects that rehouse individuals and families experiencing homelessness. Total funding available is approximately $42,797,644, including approximately $31,796,073 in Annual Renewal Demand (ARD), CoC Bonus funding (~$6,359,215), and Domestic Violence Bonus funding (~$3,142,356). Both new/expansion projects and renewal projects are eligible. A 25% match requirement applies (cash or in-kind; in-kind match requires formal MOU or commitment letter). Projects must be executed within 12 months of grant award (24 months for sponsor/project-based rental assistance). Indirect cost rate documentation required if indirect costs are claimed.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rapidly rehousing individuals and families experiencing homelessness via permanent supportive housing (PSH), rapid re-housing (RRH), transitional housing (TH), supportive services only (SSO), coordinated entry (SSO-CE), HMIS, joint TH-RRH, and CoC planning and infrastructure. Budget categories include leasing, rental assistance, supportive services, operations, HMIS, administration, and project staffing.

structured_extraction.program_description: House Baltimore is a property owner engagement initiative that connects Baltimore City landlords and property managers with homeless service providers. Property owners list available units on a dedicated platform (Padmission), lease to people exiting homelessness, and receive financial incentives and ongoing support in return.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a $2,000 incentive payment for each new lease agreement (guaranteed for the first five units leased, with possible additional incentives for flexible screening criteria) and can file claims for damage and vacancy reimbursement of up to $5,000 per unit. Participants also get access to a free listing platform (Padmission) and wraparound support from homeless service agencies. The program is funded through ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and managers in Baltimore City who are willing to rent to people exiting homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentive payments compensate property owners for leasing to people exiting homelessness; damage and vacancy reimbursement covers expenses caused by tenants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must be a property owner or manager in Baltimore City
Must complete the House Baltimore Interest Form
Must complete member onboarding package and training
Must list available units on the Padmission platform
Must execute a lease agreement with a client exiting homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the House Baltimore Interest Form online (bit.ly/HouseBaltimore). 2. Attend an orientation with the House Baltimore support team. 3. Complete the member onboarding package and training. 4. List available properties on the Padmission platform. 5. Receive and review applications from clients exiting homelessness. 6. Execute a lease agreement once the unit is verified to meet the client's needs. 7. Confirm the move-in date with the client and service provider. House Baltimore housing specialists and service providers offer ongoing support to both clients and property owners/managers.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS), in partnership with the Baltimore City Continuum of Care, sought proposals from one qualified applicant to compete for HUD's CoC Builds funding. The program made approximately $175 million available nationally to reduce homelessness by adding new units of permanent supportive housing (PSH) through new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation. Baltimore City was eligible for a portion of the approximately $110 million reserved for CoCs in states with populations over 2.5 million. The selected applicant was expected to provide both supportive services and property management, either through a single organization or via a memorandum of understanding between multiple organizations including a developer, property manager, and service provider.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time HUD CoCBuilds grant award for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of permanent supportive housing units. Approximately $175 million was available nationally, with approximately $110 million reserved for CoCs in states with populations over 2.5 million people, such as Baltimore City (MD-501). Only one application could be submitted per CoC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations (developers, property managers, service providers) qualified to develop and operate permanent supportive housing in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of permanent supportive housing units, plus supportive services and property management
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland (Continuum of Care MD-501)
requirements_list: Must be a qualified applicant capable of providing both supportive services and property management
Proposal must include a developer, property manager, and service provider — either within one organization or through MOU(s) between multiple organizations
Only one application may be submitted per CoC
Application must be submitted via email by October 18, 2024 at 3:00 pm EST
No paper or faxed applications accepted
No late submissions accepted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MOHS released an RFP on August 30, 2024. Applicants submitted written proposals by October 18, 2024. MOHS conducted internal review and scoring, followed by selection panel discussion, Resource Allocation Committee review, and CoC Board approval. MOHS then submitted one CoCBuilds application to HUD via grants.gov by November 21, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: Diversion & Kinship Projects through the Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) is a U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) initiative to help communities prevent and end youth homelessness. Baltimore City received a $3,699,336 YHDP grant to implement a local plan. This specific funding opportunity sought proposals for a Diversion and Kinship program serving unaccompanied youth and young adults experiencing homelessness (no household member older than 24), including pregnant or parenting youth. The selected project was required to coordinate with existing YHDP projects and the Baltimore Continuum of Care.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation and operation of a family-based diversion and kinship program for youth and young adults experiencing homelessness, coordinated with existing YHDP projects and the Baltimore Continuum of Care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must serve unaccompanied youth experiencing homelessness where no household member is older than 24
Must coordinate with existing YHDP projects (Permanent Supportive Housing, Rapid Re-housing, Family-Based Setting Diversion, Transitional Housing)
Must coordinate with the full Baltimore Continuum of Care

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons With AIDS (HOPWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA is the only federal program dedicated to housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS and their families. In the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA), the City of Baltimore receives the annual HOPWA award and contracts with local jurisdictions to deliver services. The Mayor's Office of Human Services (MOHS) administers the program and annually releases a Consolidated Funding Application for new and renewing project sponsors (nonprofits and city agencies) to submit proposals for funding. The program provides safe and sanitary housing, rental and mortgage assistance, and supportive services to help low-income people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) and their families maintain housing stability, access medical care, and improve quality of life. Participating jurisdictions include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County. Carroll County does not provide housing assistance.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Human Services (MOHS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to project sponsors (nonprofits and city agencies) on an annual basis through a Consolidated Funding Application process. At the individual level, provides tenant-based or project-based rental assistance, short-term rent/mortgage/utility payments to prevent homelessness, facility conversion and repair, new construction support, and supportive services including permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, and referrals for health and social services. Annual allocations are distributed to participating jurisdictions within the Baltimore-Towson EMSA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income persons (at or below 80% of area median income) diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and their families residing in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA), as well as nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and city agencies that provide housing and supportive services to PLWHA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing assistance, rental assistance, and supportive services for low-income individuals and families living with HIV/AIDS; tenant-based or project-based rental assistance; short-term rent, mortgage, and utility payments to prevent homelessness; facility conversion, lease, and repair; new construction; permanent housing placement; employment and education services; health and social service referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA): Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County. Baltimore City is the HOPWA grantee for this area.
requirements_list: Must be medically diagnosed with HIV/AIDS
Must have low income at or below 80% of area median income
Family members of eligible persons may also receive assistance
Must reside in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (for individual beneficiaries)
Must be a Non-Profit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or another city agency (for project sponsors)
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland (for project sponsors)
Must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and have an active DUNS number (for project sponsors)
Must submit two years of the most recent A-133 financial audits, or two most recent years of accountant-prepared financial statements for renewal projects without audits (for project sponsors)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Every January, MOHS releases a Consolidated Funding Application for the upcoming City Fiscal Year. New and renewing project sponsors (nonprofits and city agencies) submit project proposals; MOHS reviews applications to verify eligibility requirements before making awards. Individual PLWHA seeking rental assistance and support services should apply through Coordinated Access and contact the HOPWA Program at 410-935-9862 or 410-545-1511. A list of program providers is available on the Baltimore City website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe City Baltimore: Immigrant Education and Defense Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Safe City Baltimore provides education and legal defense services for immigrant communities in Baltimore. The program has three levels: (1) Know Your Rights sessions and Family Safety Plan preparation; (2) immigration screening clinics, coordination with pro bono lawyers, and help with immigration applications; and (3) rapid response deportation defense, legal representation coordination, and case management support for families. The program was originally established in 2017 and revived in early 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three levels of services: community education (Know Your Rights sessions, Family Safety Plans, guidance on ICE arrests); legal assistance (immigration screening clinics, pro bono lawyer coordination, help with immigration applications); and deportation defense (rapid response services, legal representation coordination, case management support, immigration bond assistance). Services are free to eligible immigrants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Immigrant individuals and families in Baltimore City, particularly those facing deportation or seeking to understand their legal rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Know Your Rights education, Family Safety Plan preparation, immigration legal screenings, pro bono legal coordination, immigration applications, deportation defense, and case management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to immigrants residing in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be an immigrant residing in Baltimore City
Must have a viable legal claim to remain in the United States to access Level 2 and Level 3 services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs at mima@baltimorecity.gov to get help through the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) Community Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City established a dedicated Opioid Restitution Fund using $579.9 million (before legal fees and litigation costs) recovered through settlements with pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors. The fund supports programs and interventions to address the opioid and overdose epidemic in Baltimore City. Governed by an Executive Order signed August 2024, the program supports community-based projects related to overdose prevention, harm reduction, treatment access, recovery, and social determinants of health that redress or prevent harms caused by the opioid epidemic. Grants are available in multiple funding tiers (Tier 1: up to $50,000; Tier 2: up to $250,000; Tier 3: up to $500,000), with $2 million available for Round 1 (Fiscal Year 2026); project funding can be spread across a project period of up to two years. The fund is designed to sustain impact for at least 15 years, with annual funding priorities set through Notices of Funding Availability (NOFAs). The Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs (MORP) administers fiscal oversight and contract management for all grantees, while the Mayor's Office of Overdose Response (BCMOOR) sets annual funding priorities in coordination with the Restitution Advisory Board.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs (MORP) and Mayor's Office of Overdose Response (BCMOOR)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded from a trust totaling $579.9 million (before legal fees and litigation costs), designed to sustain impact for at least 15 years, distributed based on annual funding priorities. For Round 1 (FY2026), $2 million is available across three funding tiers: Tier 1 (up to $50,000), Tier 2 (up to $250,000, 2–4 awards), and Tier 3 (up to $500,000, 2–3 awards). Proposed project funding can be spread across a project period of up to two years. The final number of awards depends on the number of approved applications and total available funding; awarded amounts may differ from proposed budgets based on scope of work and available funding. MORP manages and executes grant agreements, reviews expenditures, and monitors compliance with grant terms. Overhead is capped at 15% of the grant award. Future rounds will be shaped by annual budget allocations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals due November 23, 2025 at 11:59 pm EST; Full applications due January 25, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and other eligible entities (including for-profit and government organizations) in Baltimore City working to address the opioid and overdose crisis through overdose prevention, harm reduction, treatment access, recovery programs, and related social determinants of health. Organizations must have an operating location in Baltimore City and experience directly serving people in Baltimore City. Applicants for Tier 2 and Tier 3 must be 501(c)(3) organizations. Priority given to organizations with 5+ years of experience serving populations impacted by the opioid overdose crisis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based projects addressing the opioid and overdose epidemic, including substance use prevention, treatment (including MOUD and behavioral health counseling), recovery support, harm reduction, peer support, case management, housing and transportation assistance, and programs addressing social determinants of health that redress or prevent harms caused by the opioid epidemic. Also allowable: software and evaluation as direct costs, essential staff trainings tied to program delivery, and small-scale improvements supporting service delivery. Unallowable uses include: law enforcement-centered or carceral approaches (police/sheriff/corrections salaries, drug enforcement programs, drug courts, mandated treatment, incarceration-based services), coercive or abstinence-only services, stigmatizing or discriminatory materials, overhead exceeding 15% of grant award, capital/construction/real estate purchases, fundraising/development staff costs, and services that duplicate Statewide Settlement funding. Full list of unallowable uses detailed in Appendix A of the applicant instructions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Funding is intended only for programs operating in and serving residents of Baltimore City. Organizations do not need to be headquartered in Baltimore City but must have an operating location in Baltimore City. Projects must target specific neighborhoods or zip codes within Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City releases Notices of Funding Availability (NOFAs) informed by community engagement and a City-wide Overdose Response Plan. For Round 1, the NOFA was announced October 9, 2025 and the RFP launched October 23, 2025. Applicants must review the Instructions for Proposals for Funding document and appendices, register in the Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs online application portal (Grant Lifecycle Manager), and submit a proposal by the stated deadline. An orientation training session is available on demand. Applications undergo a two-stage process: proposal submission followed by full application for organizations that pass screening. Applications are evaluated based on scoring criteria described in Appendices C and D using a weighted rubric of approximately 100 points plus bonus criteria. Funding recipients were announced in February 2026 for Round 1. MORP serves as the lead contract administrator. Applicants should self-assess eligibility, seek prior approval from relevant parties, submit proposal through the online portal, and provide final reports post-completion. Technical assistance is available via MORP/BCMOOR.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City Farms lets city residents rent garden plots in parks across Baltimore to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers. Beginners are welcome and receive support from experienced gardeners along with educational tools and guides. Gardens are fenced, have water access, and include shared amenities like hoses and wheelbarrows.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gardeners pay a one-time non-refundable $10 application fee (new participants only), sign a City Farms agreement, and pay a $35 rental fee per garden bed based on plot location and size. Two plot sizes are available: a standard bed (10 ft x 15 ft) or a smaller raised bed (9 ft x 6 ft). Amenities include fenced and locked gardens with key access from dawn to dusk, city water (April–October), hoses, wheelbarrows, wood chips, and manure during the growing season.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renting a garden plot to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers in a Baltimore City park.

Sign a City Farms agreement

Planting must begin by May 22 of the program year
Winter clearing deadline of December 4 of the program year

structured_extraction.program_name: TreeBaltimore / TreeNeighborhood (including Yard Tree Adaptation Free Tree Giveaways)
structured_extraction.program_description: TreeBaltimore is a city-wide program led by the Mayor and run by Baltimore City Recreation and Parks (BCRP) Forestry Division. It works to grow and care for trees across Baltimore by maintaining existing trees, supporting natural forest growth, and teaching residents to care for trees in their neighborhoods. The program has several components: (1) The TreeNeighborhood component provides free or discounted trees to Baltimore City residents — residents of designated Healthy Neighborhoods receive free trees, while residents of all other neighborhoods can purchase trees at half price ($10 each). Neighborhoods must order a minimum of ten trees to qualify for free delivery. A neighborhood representative coordinates orders, collects requests from neighbors, and submits a group order form to TreeBaltimore for fall or spring planting. (2) The Yard Tree Adaptation / Free Tree Giveaway component distributes free 1-gallon trees to Baltimore City residents and businesses each spring and fall at farmer's markets, parks, and local community events. (3) The program also organizes community planting events, arranges large-property plantings for schools, businesses, hospitals, and places of worship, and provides Tree Steward training and volunteer opportunities to improve Baltimore's urban tree canopy. (4) A Commemorative Tree Program allows donations of $300 to purchase and install a tree. (5) A Street Tree Request program allows residents to request free street trees planted in the right-of-way.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Recreation and Parks (BCRP) Forestry Division / TreeBaltimore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 1-gallon trees for residents of designated Healthy Neighborhoods and at seasonal giveaway events (held each spring and fall at farmer's markets, parks, and community events); half-price trees ($10 each) for residents of all other Baltimore City neighborhoods. Neighborhoods ordering at least ten trees receive free delivery to a central neighborhood location. Businesses and institutions can contact TreeBaltimore for a site visit and access to discount trees; TreeBaltimore will order and deliver trees to large private and public properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, and places of worship. A Commemorative Tree Program allows a $300 donation to purchase and install a tree. Street tree requests are accepted on a rolling basis; planting occurs 4–10 months after request depending on volume. Tree Steward training is also available for residents. Orders for fall plantings are due in November; orders for spring plantings are due in April. Native species are preferred (at least 50% per project); species must comply with the Baltimore City Approved Tree Species List and ANSI Z60.2 standards.

A neighborhood representative is asked to coordinate group orders for the TreeNeighborhood component. Residents and businesses may also attend seasonal giveaway events to receive free trees. Individuals may request street trees planted in the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on private and public property (residential lawns, yards, large institutional properties, community spaces, street right-of-way), tree maintenance (watering, mulching), urban forestry education and training, and community volunteer planting events. Program targets 40% citywide tree canopy cover.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can receive free trees at seasonal giveaway events (held each spring and fall at farmer's markets, parks, and local events — check the TreeBaltimore calendar for upcoming locations) or request trees using the Tree Neighborhood Individual Order Form. For group orders, a neighborhood representative promotes the program, collects individual tree requests and payments (if applicable) from neighbors, and submits a completed Group Order Form to TreeBaltimore by the appropriate deadline (November for fall, April for spring); TreeBaltimore then delivers trees to a central neighborhood location for a community planting event. For street tree requests, residents submit a signed and dated Street Tree Request and Agreement for Tree Care form via email, mail, or fax to Jahmilla Wilson, Tree Planting Coordinator (jahmilla.wilson@baltimorecity.gov, fax 410-396-6645); the site is then inspected and the request is placed on the planting order for the next season (planting typically occurs 4–10 months after initial request). Community groups can also submit a Street Tree Pit Inventory. Businesses and institutions can contact TreeBaltimore directly for a site visit. For a Commemorative Tree, submit the donation form with a $300 check (payable to Director of Finance) to the mailing address (3001 East Drive, Baltimore, MD 21217). Organizations interested in hosting a giveaway at their event can contact the Forestry Division directly. Volunteers can email staff to get involved.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Digital Equity Fund provides grants to Baltimore-based nonprofit organizations to support community-led digital inclusion projects. Round 2 offers funding across three tiers: digital literacy education and training (Tier 1), advanced digital education and IT fundamentals programming (Tier 2), and digital creatives and virtual makerspaces programming (Tier 3). Each tier offers up to $200,000. The program aims to close the digital divide for Baltimore residents who lack devices, internet access, or digital skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $200,000 per tier. Organizations may apply for each tier separately. Tier 1 supports digital literacy education (older adults and community tech hubs). Tier 2 supports IT fundamentals and certification programs. Tier 3 supports digital creatives and makerspace programming at recreation centers.

Trees are available via preorder or on a first-come, first-served basis at a drive-thru pickup event.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receiving free trees for planting on residential property.

Up to two trees per household

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County Animal Services offers a low-cost spay and neuter surgery package for cats and dogs owned by Baltimore County residents. The package costs $20 and includes the surgery plus rabies vaccine, other vaccines (distemper and Bordetella for dogs), deworming, a County animal license, and a microchip. Appointments are required and services are provided at the Dundalk Spay and Neuter Surgical Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The full spay or neuter surgery package — including surgery, vaccines, deworming, microchip, and a County animal license — is offered for a flat fee of $20, well below the typical market cost. Credit card payment is required at the time of scheduling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who own cats or dogs meeting age, weight, and health eligibility requirements. Rescue and foster groups are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay or neuter surgery for an eligible owned pet, along with required vaccines, deworming, microchip, and County animal license.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of Baltimore County, Maryland, with pets that reside in Baltimore County. Services are provided at the Dundalk Spay and Neuter Surgical Center (7702 Dunmanway, Dundalk, MD 21222).
requirements_list: Pet owner must be a Baltimore County resident and the pet must reside in Baltimore County
Dogs must be between 4 months and 6 years of age, weigh between 5 and 60 lbs (female) or 5 and 80 lbs (male), and have no known illness, injury, or medical condition
Certain dog breeds (boxers, all bulldog breeds, pugs, Shih Tzus) are restricted; other short-faced breeds evaluated case by case
Cats must be between 5 months and 6 years of age, weigh at least 5 lbs, and have no known illness, injury, or medical condition
Hairless, Himalayan, and Persian cats are not eligible
Pets with conditions that increase anesthetic risk (e.g., heart murmurs, kidney disease, seizure disorder, feline leukemia, retained testicles, upper respiratory infections) may be declined
Rescue and foster groups are not currently eligible
Payment is required at the time of scheduling
Pet owners cannot opt out of individual services in the package — all services must be received together
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online appointment request form on the Baltimore County website. If eligible, select the Dundalk facility and proceed to the payment screen — credit card payment is required at time of booking. A confirmation email is sent when the appointment is accepted. On surgery day, arrive at the Dundalk center by 8 a.m. with your pet (cat in a carrier, dog on a non-retractable leash) and any existing medical records. Pets are discharged the same day, no earlier than 3 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a free Trap, Neuter, Return (TNR) program that humanely reduces the number of community (unowned, outdoor) cats. Participants trap feral cats and bring them to the county facility, where each cat receives spay or neuter surgery, rabies and FVRCP vaccines, ear-tipping, tattooing, a microchip, and a vet exam while sedated — all at no charge. After recovery, cats are returned to where they were trapped.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free spay/neuter surgery package for community cats, including rabies vaccine, FVRCP vaccine, ear-tipping, abdominal tattoo, microchip, topical flea treatment, and sedated vet exam. Trap loans (one month) are also available at no cost to eligible property owners. Replacement value for unreturned/damaged equipment: $90/trap, $25/divider.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and community cat caregivers in Baltimore County who care for unowned outdoor cats and want to humanely reduce the feral cat population through sterilization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free veterinary surgery package (spay/neuter, vaccines, ear-tip, tattoo, microchip, flea treatment) for unowned community cats living outdoors within Baltimore County. Free trap loans available for eligible property owners who own the property where trapping will take place.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to community cats living outdoors at addresses within Baltimore County, Maryland. Program is administered at Baltimore County Animal Services, 13800 Manor Road, Baldwin, Maryland 21013. Only outdoor, unowned cats from Baltimore County addresses qualify; pet cats and indoor cats are explicitly excluded.
requirements_list: Complete a Feral Cat Caregiver registration form before scheduling a surgery appointment
Must be registered with Baltimore County Department of Health and comply with TNR Program Guidelines

Adhere to TNR Program guidelines and all 15 caregiver obligations including sterilization, ear-tipping, microchipping, rabies vaccination, humane trapping, record-keeping, food/water management, veterinary care, and complaint resolution
Retrieve the cat the same day as surgery (drop-off 8 a.m., pick-up 3 p.m.)
Return the cat outdoors to where they came from after surgery — cats being removed from the colony are not eligible
Cats must be unowned community cats living outdoors at a Baltimore County address
Cats must arrive in a cat trap or transfer cage, one cat per cage (no carriers or crates)
Cats must be over three months of age AND over three pounds in weight and appear healthy
False information provided by applicant results in permanent program exclusion
If TNR participant does not own the property where trapping will occur, must obtain written permission from the property owner prior to trapping and returning cats

For trap loans: applicant must own the property where trapping will take place, read Humane Trapping Instructions prior to leaving facility, schedule surgery appointments before trapping, monitor trap at all times when set (never leave unattended), maintain humane conditions including temperature control and food/water, and return equipment within 24 hours when requested
For BCAS property entry: property owner or authorized representative must execute Permission for Baltimore County to Enter Property form; valid for up to one year and must be renewed annually
Must be in good standing with Animal Services; rabies booster updates required per COMAR 10.06.02.10
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Feral Cat Caregiver registration form (available in English and Spanish) and submit it before scheduling a surgery appointment. For trap loans, also complete the Permission for Baltimore County to Enter Property form and the Trap Loan Agreement (signed in person at BCAS facility), then email the TNR Coordinator to request a loan. Surgery appointments, trap loan pick-up, and return dates are all scheduled together. Drop cats off at 8 a.m. and pick them up at 3 p.m. on the day of surgery.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant fund that helps Baltimore County residents with mental illness or financial hardship pay for psychiatric medications, eviction prevention, security deposits, and utility arrears, used as a last resort in combination with other resources.

Funds may be used for psychiatric medications, eviction prevention (back rent/eviction notice balance), security deposits for rental housing, and BGE utility arrears (electric/gas). Must be used as a last resort in combination with other community, private, public, and/or family resources. Consumer must have means to meet continued financial obligations. A treatment team member (not the consumer) submits the request on behalf of the consumer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents with mental illness or financial hardship who need assistance with psychiatric medications, eviction prevention, security deposits, or utility arrears while awaiting Medicaid approval or otherwise qualifying.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Psychiatric medications, eviction prevention (back rent or eviction notice balance), security deposits for rental housing, and BGE utility arrears (electric/gas). Maximum $1,000 per fiscal year per consumer. Must be used as a last resort combined with other resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Baltimore County, Maryland. Program administered at 6401 York Road, Third Floor, Baltimore, Maryland 21212.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must have a mental illness diagnosis
Must be waiting for Medicaid (Medical Assistance) approval
Must have a scheduled appointment with a provider that accepts Medicaid
Application must be completed by a treatment team member (not the consumer) on behalf of the consumer
Required documentation: dated invoice/bill within past 30 days with consumer name, address, amount owed, and vendor name/address
W9 required for any vendor not known to the County or for private vendors
Program-specific documents required (e.g., eviction notice, lease, utility bill) depending on assistance type

Allow 7–10 business days for processing.

A member of the individual's treatment team (case manager, therapist, or physician) must complete and submit the application on the applicant's behalf. Applicant must have a treatment team member (case manager, therapist, or physician) who can submit the application on their behalf. Not available for individuals with commercial insurance or for co-pays.

Funds may only be used once per fiscal year and serve as a last resort bridge to Medicaid, MCHP, or other entitlements. Not available for co-pays or individuals with commercial insurance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides psychiatric rehabilitation services to eligible adults with serious and persistent mental illness in a supervised residential setting, helping them build independent living skills and integrate into the community.

Residents contribute to the cost of their care. Applicants must apply through the Core Service Agency (CSA) of their home origin county. A mental health professional completes and submits pages 3–10 of the application to the applicable CSA. Priority is given to in-county residents, though out-of-county placement is possible (max 3 jurisdictions). Placement is not guaranteed; RRP providers interview eligible applicants as vacancies occur.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with serious and persistent mental illness who need psychiatric rehabilitation in a supervised residential setting and are residents of a Maryland county served by a Core Service Agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supervised residential rehabilitation services including daily living assistance, medication monitoring, community integration, and independent living skills development.

Applicants must apply through the CSA of their home origin county (based on current or last known address before hospitalization, incarceration, or homelessness). In-county residents are given high priority; out-of-county referral is possible for up to 3 jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), administered by the Baltimore County Department of Aging, provides free, unbiased, and confidential Medicare counseling to Baltimore County residents year-round. Trained SHIP counselors help Medicare beneficiaries age 65 and older — and those under 65 receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) — understand their coverage options, compare plans, avoid penalties, resolve billing issues, and screen for financial assistance programs that can lower their costs. Year-round one-on-one phone counseling is available, with expanded in-person assistance at senior centers throughout Baltimore County during the annual Medicare Part D Open Enrollment period (October 15 – December 7). During Open Enrollment, counselors help beneficiaries research and compare Prescription Drug Plans based on their specific medications to find the best and least expensive option. Counselors help beneficiaries understand Medicare Parts A, B, C, and D; compare Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans; review Medigap options; file appeals; and screen for and assist with applications to financial assistance programs such as Medicare Savings Programs (including Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) and Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) programs), Extra Help, the Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP), and Medical Assistance — which can reduce or eliminate Medicare premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing for qualifying low-income beneficiaries. Free educational presentations — including a 1.5-hour Medicare Basics session and monthly 30-minute online sessions — are also offered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one Medicare counseling by phone year-round, with expanded in-person counseling sessions at senior center locations throughout Baltimore County during the annual Open Enrollment period (October 15 – December 7). Counselors help beneficiaries understand Medicare Parts A, B, C, and D; compare Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans; review Medigap options; file appeals; evaluate Medicare Part D prescription drug plan options; and screen for and apply to financial assistance programs including Medicare Savings Programs (QMB and SLMB, which reduce or eliminate Medicare premiums, deductibles, and co-payments for qualifying low-income beneficiaries), Extra Help, Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP), and Medical Assistance. Free educational presentations (1.5-hour Medicare Basics and monthly 30-minute online sessions) are also offered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open Enrollment counseling: October 15 to December 7 annually; phone counseling available year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who are Medicare beneficiaries age 65 and older, or under 65 and receiving SSDI, including those seeking help choosing or changing a Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plan, understanding coverage options, comparing plans, or accessing financial assistance programs; also low-income Medicare beneficiaries seeking to reduce their Medicare cost-sharing expenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling to help individuals select Medicare coverage, lower costs, compare Medicare Part D prescription drug plans, and access financial assistance programs such as Extra Help and the Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program — not a cash award. Additionally, screening and application assistance for Medicare Savings Programs that reduce Medicare premiums, deductibles, and co-pays for qualifying low-income beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be age 65 or older, OR under 65 and receiving SSDI
Must be a Medicare beneficiary

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For year-round phone counseling, contact SHIP at 410-887-2059 or medicareinformation@baltimorecountymd.gov to schedule an appointment. For Open Enrollment in-person counseling (October 15 – December 7), schedule an appointment online at the SHIP appointment portal or by calling 410-887-2059 beginning in September each year; appointments are held at senior center locations of the applicant's choice. For Medicare Savings Program screening and application assistance, contact Baltimore County SHIP directly. For educational presentations, register by email or phone.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Aging Caregiver Support Program helps family and informal caregivers who look after Baltimore County residents. The program offers one-on-one consultations with a Caregiver Specialist, financial stipends to cover costs like respite care or medical supplies, outreach and education events, and access to the Trualta online learning platform. Funding comes from the federal National Family Caregivers Support Program (NFCSP) grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides: (1) A one-time, free one-hour private consultation with a Caregiver Specialist who reviews the caregiving situation and suggests resources. (2) A financial stipend that varies by year (waitlist may apply if funds are limited) to cover respite care — such as paying someone to stay at home with the care recipient or a short nursing home stay — or medical supplies like incontinence products not covered by Medicare. The stipend is not available to those in hospice care or already paid by another source such as Medicaid.

Stipend not available if another source such as Medicaid is already paying
One stipend per household for one care recipient
Can apply once per year for up to five years

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County plants 20 to 145 native trees (covering one-tenth to three-fourths of an acre) on residential properties for County residents who do not have a full acre available for the Turf to Trees program. Trees are equipped with deer protection by County-selected contractors. The County covers the cost of trees, labor, tree materials, planting, installation of tree shelters (5' tube + 2"×2"×6' stake), and deer protection. The program is funded through Baltimore County's Waterway Improvement Fund and plantings are credited toward the County's federally mandated Chesapeake Bay Restoration Program as a cost-effective best management practice for urban stormwater runoff management. Property owners are responsible for maintaining the trees, removing stakes and shelters, and reporting their survival to EPS.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Grant Program (Septic System Upgrade Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) Grant Program helps Baltimore County property owners upgrade their septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal, or connect to public sewer. The goal is to reduce nutrients flowing into the Chesapeake Bay. Priority is given to failing systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (CBCA — property within 1,000 feet of mean high tide), but other septic systems may also qualify depending on available funding. Grants cover the full cost and installation of a BAT septic system plus two years of maintenance, or the cost of connecting to public sewer including connection fees and permits. Residential properties with household income under $300,000 per year and all non-profit entities receive 100% funding; non-residential properties receive 50% funding of project cost.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover the cost and installation of a BAT septic system plus two years of maintenance, or the cost of connecting to public sewer including connection fees and permits. Residential properties with household income under $300,000 per year and all non-profit entities receive 100% funding. Non-residential properties receive 50% funding of project cost. Grant funds cannot be used for drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners) or permit/recordation fees for BAT installations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County property owners with septic systems or holding tanks, especially those with failing systems in or near the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area. Includes residential, commercial, and rental property owners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost and installation of a Best Available Technology (BAT) nitrogen-removal septic system plus two years of maintenance; holding tank installation; or connection to public sewer including related fees and permits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County property owners only. Highest priority given to properties within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of mean high tide).

Must provide most recent 1040 federal tax form (pages 1–2, with SSNs blacked out)
Must provide property tax ID
Must allow EPS to conduct an initial site inspection
If approved for BAT installation, property owner must sign an agreement to maintain the BAT system with a qualified operator for as long as the septic system is in use
Property owner must allow the County to conduct periodic onsite inspections
Sites with holding tanks must have a viable soil-based disposal area identified to be considered for a BAT grant
If public sewer is accessible, grant will only be approved for a sewer connection, not a BAT installation

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form from the Baltimore County website. Chesapeake Ave, Room 305, Towson, MD 21204), fax (410-887-4817), or email (groundwater@baltimorecountymd.gov). EPS will review the application, assess public sewer availability, and conduct an initial site inspection if approved. Prioritization is based on CBCA proximity and septic system failure status; award amount is based on taxable income and property type.

structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-funded urban tree planting on managed properties. Projects must include a minimum of 20 trees. Plantings include landscape-style trees and large shade trees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HOAs, apartment complexes, businesses, and property managers in Baltimore County urban areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting trees on managed grounds to increase urban tree canopy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Urban areas of Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Project must include 20 or more trees
Applicant must be an HOA, apartment complex, business, or property manager
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an urban reforestation planting by emailing forestmanagement@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability (DEPS) awards annual grants to local watershed associations and nonprofits to fund staff time for watershed restoration, education, and outreach activities. Grants support projects like tree plantings, stormwater best management practices (BMPs), stream cleanups, rain gardens, and watershed education that help meet water quality goals in Baltimore County's local streams, rivers, reservoirs, and the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $30,000 are available to cover staff salaries for environmental restoration activities and public education. Fringe benefits up to 30% of salary and indirect/overhead costs up to 10% of combined salary and fringe may also be covered. In some cases, grants above $30,000 may be awarded to organizations with at least three years of funding history and an exemplary track record — those organizations may request a meeting with DEPS to discuss a larger award. The grant term runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The minimum ratio of staff hours to grant funds is one hour per $30 requested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit community organizations with active membership in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries and fringe benefits for restoration planning and implementation, and watershed education and outreach. Eligible activities include downspout disconnections, rain gardens, rain barrels, stormwater BMPs, tree plantings, invasive species removal, stream cleanups, and education/outreach. Indirect/overhead costs such as accounting, insurance, and office supplies may also be covered up to 10% of salary and fringe. Materials and equipment are not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All grant-funded activities must be implemented in Baltimore County, including watersheds such as Back River, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, Baltimore Harbor, Liberty Reservoir, Gunpowder Falls, Tidal Gunpowder/Middle River/Bird River, Loch Raven Reservoir, Patapsco River, and Prettyboy. The applying organization must have active membership in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be a locally-based watershed association or community group with membership in Baltimore County
Must be a registered 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or 501(c)(6) organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects
Must have fulfilled all grant requirements on past grants, if previously funded through this program
Minimum ratio of one staff hour per $30 in grant funds requested
All funded activities must be implemented in Baltimore County
Projects must link to approved Watershed Plans and TMDL Implementation Plans
Budget must include fringe benefits (max 30% of salary) and indirect rates (max 10% of salary and fringe)
Volunteer hours must be documented and matched to 'Other Funding Sources' on the AFA form
Financial statements must be submitted (audited, Form 990, unaudited, or treasurer's report)
Officer/board member names must be provided if applicant is a non-individual organization
Related organization disclosures must be provided
Total project cost must match the AFA form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit three components via email to Erin Watts at ewatts@baltimorecountymd.gov by February 6 at 11:59 p.m.: (1) completed DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions, (2) Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance (AFA form), and (3) supporting documents including proof of good standing, a detailed budget proposal, and financial statements. The AFA form requires financial statements, project completion date, in-kind contributions disclosure, officer/board member names, population served, and community benefit narrative. All documents must be submitted as separate PDF files following specified file naming conventions. Use '[Organization Initials] – FY XX Grant Application' as the email subject line.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services to Baltimore County residents between birth and age 21 who have a developmental disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services provided to eligible county residents.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services.

Must be between birth and 21 years of age
Must have a developmental disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Children with Special Healthcare Needs program by phone at 410-887-2720.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community First Choice (CFC) and Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS)
structured_extraction.program_description: Programs that provide home and community-based services and supports as an alternative to institutional placement for Medicaid-eligible individuals who require an institutional level of care. Services include support planning and help with daily tasks such as bathing, dressing, grooming, and toileting, as well as some light household chores related to health and safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home and community-based personal assistance services provided in participants' homes by licensed Residential Service Agencies, monitored by Registered Nurses from the Department. Services include help with daily activities and light household tasks related to the participant's health and safety.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicaid-eligible individuals who have been determined to require an institutional level of care and want to remain in their home or community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal assistance services including bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, light household chores, and other tasks related to health and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Must be Medicaid-eligible
Must have been determined to require an institutional level of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Access Point at 410-887-2594 for more information or to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: An early intervention program that serves families with children under three years of age who have developmental delays or disabilities. Research-based early intervention services are coordinated based on the needs and priorities identified by the family, at no cost to families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free early intervention services coordinated through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) developed based on the family's identified needs and priorities. Services help children develop social-emotional skills, acquire knowledge, and use appropriate behaviors, and help families understand their rights and promote their child's development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under three years of age who have developmental delays or disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services for children with developmental delays or disabilities, including supports and services to promote development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Child must be under three years of age
Child must demonstrate 25% delay in one or more areas of development, atypical development in one or more areas, or a diagnosed condition placing them at risk for developmental delays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Make a referral online at referral.mditp.org or by calling 443-809-2169. Referrals can be made by parents, health care providers, child care providers, social workers, family members, or others familiar with the child's development. The local Infants and Toddlers site will contact the family to schedule an initial evaluation to determine eligibility. If eligible, an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) will be developed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Poisoning Prevention and Asthma Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary home visiting program that provides one to six home visits to eligible families to improve children's health by reducing and eliminating lead, asthma triggers, and other environmental hazards. Includes a free case management service for families of children with lead poisoning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home support visits (one to six visits) provided by community health workers and nurses to reduce lead, asthma triggers, and environmental hazards. Also provides free telephone-based case management, education on reducing lead hazards, cleaning tips, and nutrition guidance for families of children with lead poisoning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County families with children who have elevated blood lead levels or moderate to severe asthma.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home support to reduce lead and asthma triggers; education, cleaning tips, and nutrition guidance for lead poisoning cases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Home visiting eligibility: must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid, be a Baltimore County resident, and be under age 19 and diagnosed with moderate to severe asthma or have an elevated blood lead level (BLL) of 3.5 µg/dL or greater
Case management eligibility: must be a Baltimore County resident, have a BLL of 3.5 µg/dL or greater, and be age 6 or younger
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Lead Poisoning Prevention and Asthma Program by phone at 410-887-4410 or email leadasthma@baltimorecountymd.gov.

Participants learn what opioids are, how to recognize and respond to an overdose, and how to administer naloxone. Attendees receive a completion certificate, a naloxone prescription, and a kit containing the medication.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training sessions held on a recurring schedule throughout 2026. Attendees receive a completion certificate, a prescription for naloxone, and a free naloxone kit distributed one to three days after training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Preregistration required; sessions scheduled through June 17, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals concerned that a loved one is at risk for opioid overdose, and those whose naloxone training certificates will expire within three months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — the program provides free training and a naloxone kit to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serving Baltimore County residents; training is delivered online via Webex.
requirements_list: Preregistration is required before attending a session
Participants who need special accommodations (language interpreter, large print, etc.) should notify the program in advance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the provided Wufoo registration link. A link to the training application will be sent prior to the start of the session. Special accommodation requests can be made by calling 410-887-3072 or emailing hhs@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Links uninsured and underinsured Baltimore County residents to affordable health care coverage and entitlement programs. There is no cost for enrollment, case management, or coordination services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free enrollment assistance, case management, and coordination to connect residents to affordable health coverage or entitlement programs. No cost to participants.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Linkage to affordable health care coverage or government entitlement programs

Income must be below 300% of the federal poverty level
