structured_extraction.program_description: The Administrative Care Coordination/Ombudsman Unit (ACCU) helps Medical Assistance (Medicaid) members and HealthChoice beneficiaries navigate the health care system, access their health care benefits, and connect to local community resources. Services include help understanding benefits, choosing a Managed Care Organization (MCO), finding primary care providers (including prenatal, pediatric, and dental), accessing medical transportation, resolving billing issues and complaints, and navigating appeal and grievance rights. The program provides short-term care coordination for complex medical issues and outreach and education to health care providers and the community. The Ombudsman component helps residents resolve disputes with MCOs through investigation, mediation, and education, and informs clients of their rights and responsibilities. Additional services include Medicaid renewal support, card replacement, and prescription assistance. ACCU programs operate in Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County, each administered by the respective county health department. The program serves children, pregnant and postpartum women, individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, and all Medicaid-eligible residents enrolled in HealthChoice.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Health; Prince George's County Department of Health; Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free care coordination, navigation assistance, and ombudsman services for Medicaid HealthChoice members, including help understanding benefits, choosing an MCO, locating primary care providers (prenatal, pediatric, dental, specialist), accessing medical transportation, Medicaid renewal support, card replacement, prescription assistance, resolving billing issues and complaints, navigating appeal and grievance rights, short-term care coordination for complex medical issues, and connecting to community resources. No cost to participants; no formal application required.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-887-8741 (Baltimore County); 1-800-284-4510 (HealthChoice Help Line); 301-856-9550 (Prince George's County); 240-777-1635 (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medical Assistance (Medicaid) members and HealthChoice beneficiaries in Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County, including children, pregnant and postpartum women, people with disabilities, homeless individuals, and those needing prenatal, primary, dental, or complex care coordination.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigating the managed care system, choosing a Managed Care Organization, finding providers (prenatal, primary care, pediatric, dental, specialist), accessing medical transportation, Medicaid renewal support, card replacement, prescription assistance, billing issue resolution, resolving complaints, understanding appeal and grievance rights, and connecting to community resources — not a cash benefit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County, Maryland. Montgomery County services require Montgomery County residency.
requirements_list: Must be a Medical Assistance (Medicaid) member or beneficiary
Must be enrolled in or eligible for HealthChoice Managed Care
Must be a resident of the county in which services are sought (Montgomery County services require Montgomery County residency)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application required. Baltimore County: Call 410-887-8741 or 1-800-284-4510 at Drumcastle Government Center. Prince George's County: Call 301-856-9403 or 301-856-9607, Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5:00pm, or visit 1801 McCormick Ave, Suite 280, Largo, MD 20774. Montgomery County: Call 240-777-1635, email ACCU@montgomerycountymd.gov, or visit the DHHS office at 1401 Rockville Pike, 2nd floor, suite 2400, Rockville, MD 20850.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-cost or no-cost loans for accessibility modifications to rental homes for renters who hold a Housing Choice Voucher (government rental assistance). Modifications are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and may include wheelchair ramps/lifts, bathroom and kitchen renovations, grab bars, flashing doorbells, and lighting changes. Landlord approval is required prior to modifications.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-cost or no-cost loans to fund accessibility modifications to a rental home for Housing Choice Voucher holders. Modifications are funded on a first-come, first-served basis as long as funding is available. One modification request is permitted per household member, though multiple household members may apply sequentially. Covered modifications include wheelchair ramps/lifts, bathroom and kitchen renovations, grab bars, flashing doorbells, and lighting changes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters who are receiving a Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) in Baltimore County and have a household member with a disability requiring accessibility modifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility modifications to a rental home, including wheelchair ramps/lifts, bathroom and kitchen renovations, grab bars, flashing doorbells, and lighting changes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a renter enrolled in the Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8)
Applicant must have a family member with a disability
Applicant must reside in Baltimore County
A signed lease must be in place
Landlord written approval must be obtained prior to modifications
Modifications are reviewed on a case-by-case basis
Licensed and insured contractor required; tenant selects contractor from county referral list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development, Office of Housing at 410-887-3435 or rar@baltimorecountymd.gov. Complete the CHAMP Renter Application and submit (in person, drop-off, fax, or email) along with landlord written approval to the Reasonable Accommodation Coordinator, who will pre-screen the application and forward to CHAMP for modification execution. Funding is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), HOME Investment Partnerships Program, and Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) — Homeless Services, Public Services, and Capital Projects Grants (FY 2027)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County awards federal HUD funding (CDBG, HOME, and ESG), State of Maryland funds, and Baltimore County General Funds through an annual grants process to nonprofit and government organizations serving County residents. Three funding tracks are available: (1) Homeless Services — projects that prevent homelessness or assist people currently experiencing homelessness; (2) Public Services — projects addressing needs of low-income residents in areas such as employment, crime prevention, child care, health and welfare, drug abuse, education, energy conservation, and recreation; and (3) Capital Projects — projects serving people with disabilities or meeting general community development needs for low- and moderate-income persons. Grants generally range from $15,000 to $200,000 annually. Both new applicants and previous grant recipients are encouraged to apply. Funding recommendations align with priorities in the County's Consolidated Plan, and an Annual Action Plan detailing proposed use of funds is subject to a public comment period. The FY 2027 program year runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants generally range from $15,000 to $200,000 annually, funded through CDBG ($9.18M total for FY 2027 cycle), HOME ($12.8M total), ESG, State of Maryland, and Baltimore County General Funds. Funding is intended to stabilize, enhance, and preserve Baltimore County communities, primarily benefiting low- to moderate-income households. Eligible uses include salaries, fringe benefits, travel, equipment under $500, supplies, indirect costs, rental assistance, operations, and client assistance. Both new applicants and previous grant recipients are encouraged to apply. Grant agreements run twelve months, beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and government organizations serving Baltimore County residents, including those working on homelessness prevention, public services for low-income residents, and capital projects for people with disabilities. Target populations include chronically homeless individuals, families with children, veterans, unaccompanied youth, persons at risk of homelessness, low- and moderate-income persons, persons with disabilities, persons with HIV/AIDS, domestic violence victims, children, elderly persons, and immigrants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homeless services (prevention and assistance for those experiencing homelessness, including Rapid Rehousing with case management, Emergency Solutions Grant activities for unsheltered populations, warming/cooling centers, safe parking with services, storage facilitation, housing navigation); public services for low-income residents (employment, crime prevention, child care, health and welfare, drug abuse, education, energy conservation, recreation); and capital projects serving people with disabilities or addressing general community development needs (construction, rehabilitation, reconstruction, modification, addition, expansion, acquisition, and design/engineering costs in combination with construction). Eligible cost categories include salaries, fringe, travel, equipment under $500, supplies, indirect costs, rental assistance, operations, client assistance, utilities, staffing, storage rental, transportation reimbursement, application/credit check fees, and landlord engagement costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations serving Baltimore County, Maryland residents. All areas in Baltimore County are unincorporated. The program serves countywide low- and moderate-income (LMI) eligible households and Low/Mod Block Group Tracts (overall LMI percentage for Baltimore County: 43.13%). Geographic priority areas include 'Opportunity Areas' in the southwest, northwest-central, and northeast sections of the County. The County coordinates regionally with Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Harford, and Howard Counties on fair housing efforts. Median income for a family of four in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, MD MSA is $130,300 for FY 2025. Applicants must specify the Councilmanic/Legislative District(s) where their project will take place. Grantees may serve either countywide or specific communities within Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit or government organization organized and existing in good standing under the laws of the State of Maryland
Must serve Baltimore County citizens
Projects must fall within one of three categories: Homeless Services, Public Services, or Capital Projects
Projects must primarily benefit low- to moderate-income households
Capital projects must serve people with disabilities or meet general community development needs
Capital projects are limited to nonprofit organizations only
Homeless services projects must prevent homelessness or assist currently homeless individuals
Public services projects must address needs of low-income citizens in eligible categories
Funding recommendations align with priorities in the County's Consolidated Plan
Must submit Corporate Resolution and Board Certification
Must submit Lobbying Certification (federal 1352 compliance)
Must submit Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace Certification
Must submit Non-Discrimination Certification (Title VI, Title I HCD Act)
Must certify no debarment or suspension history
Must certify organization is not a successor or affiliate of a debarred entity
Must comply with minority/women-owned business enterprise (MWBE/WBE) requirements
Must comply with federal audit requirements (2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F) if applicable
Required attachments include: IRS 990, audit/financial review, prior grants/loans list, board roster, org chart, resumes, 501(c)(3) documentation, incorporation/bylaws, and sample client intake form
Must submit one complete Appendix III package per organization with all nine required attachments in specified order
For Homeless Services, prior experience in homeless/housing services is required
Must have board of directors with authority to execute binding legal agreements
Must disclose political contributions as applicable
Must certify compliance with Maryland tax payment requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the applicable grant proposal documents from the Baltimore County website for the relevant funding category (Homeless Services, Public Services, or Capital Projects). RFP materials are made available on or about December 2 each year. A Notice of Public Hearing and Funding Availability is published in the Baltimore Sun (FY 2027: November 25, 2025). A pre-proposal public hearing is held in December (FY 2027: December 10, 2025, 9:30 AM). Staff meetings available through January 20, 2026; questions accepted through January 26, 2026. Requests for FileShare access must be submitted by 4:00 p.m. on January 22, 2026. Proposals are submitted by the February deadline (February 3, 2026 for FY 2027 cycle) at 2:00 p.m. Complete the application forms (Appendix I), budget pages (Appendix II), required attachments (Appendix III), and signature package as directed by the instructions for each category. The Baltimore County Grants Review Committee reviews proposals from February through March. The Annual Action Plan public comment period runs April 15 – May 15, 2026, followed by submission to HUD (May 17, 2026). County Council approval occurs June–August 2026. Grant agreements are executed in August 2026, with the new grant year beginning July 1, 2026. Funding recommendations follow priorities in the County's Consolidated Plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conciliation Housing Accessibility Modification Program (CHAMP – Grant-Based)
structured_extraction.program_description: CHAMP provides grant funding for structural modifications to rental units occupied by Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) holders. The modifications accommodate the disability-related needs of household members with hearing, physical, or vision impairments. There is no cost to eligible tenants or landlords.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding covers the full cost of structural accessibility modifications to rental units (e.g., ramps, grab bars, accessible doorways, ADA toilets, flooring, additional bedroom, live-in aide support). There is no cost to the tenant or landlord. Modifications are completed by licensed contractors selected by the Housing Opportunities and Finance Division, or optionally by the landlord. If the landlord wants modifications removed after the tenant moves out, removal costs can be included in the grant. Additional accommodations may include rental payment standard exceptions, voucher extensions, and accessibility formats (large print, colored paper, interpreters).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) holders or other federally-issued housing voucher holders who have at least one household member with a disability that limits one or more major life activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural modifications to rental units to accommodate disability-related needs (e.g., ramps, grab bars, accessible doorways, ADA toilets, flooring, additional bedroom, live-in aide support). Each request is reviewed case-by-case.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in Baltimore County, MD. No sub-county, municipal, or neighborhood-level restrictions identified.
requirements_list: Head of household must be an active Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) recipient or hold another federally-issued housing voucher
At least one household member must have a disability as defined by the ADA that limits one or more major life activities
Must reside in Baltimore County
Must have a current and signed lease
Landlord must agree to the modification referral
A qualified evaluator (medical provider, social service agency, disability agency, clinic, or professional) must verify the medical need and its direct relationship to the disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application by email to rar@baltimorecountymd.gov, fax to 410-887-8804, by phone at 410-887-3435, or in person at the Office of Housing (6401 York Road, Baltimore, MD 21212). The landlord must approve the referral. The application is then sent to the Housing and Finance Division for processing (initial response approximately 10 business days). Once the scope of work and grant agreement are drafted, both landlord and tenant sign. Modifications are completed by licensed contractors and typically take two to four months after all approvals.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-cost or no-cost loans to pay for accessibility modifications and improvements to a home for households that include a member with a disability. Projects are structural and typically involve construction, modification, or rehabilitation work by an experienced contractor.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-cost or no-cost loans to fund accessibility modifications to a home for households with a disabled member. Eligible modifications include wheelchair ramps/lifts, bathroom renovations, kitchen renovations, grab bars, flashing doorbells, and lighting changes. All work must be done by licensed and insured contractors. Common areas are not included; modifications for renters require landlord approval. Funding is awarded on a first-come, first-served basis as long as funding is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters and homeowners in Baltimore County whose household includes a member with a disability and whose household income is at or below 80 percent of the Area Median Income (ranging from $68,450 for a single-person household to $113,400 for a six-person household).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural modifications and rehabilitation work to improve accessibility in the home, such as wheelchair ramps/lifts, bathroom renovations, kitchen renovations, grab bars, flashing doorbells, and lighting changes. Common areas are not included.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only. Homeowners must own property in Baltimore County; renters must reside in Baltimore County with a rental lease agreement.
requirements_list: Household must include a member with a disability
Household income must be at or below 80% of the Area Median Income for Baltimore County (updated annually)
Open to both renters and homeowners
Renters must have a rental lease agreement and landlord approval for modifications
All work must be performed by licensed and insured contractors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the HAMP Homeowner Application or HAMP Renter Application and submit to the Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development, 105 W. Chesapeake Avenue, Suite 201, Towson, MD 21204. Applicants may also contact the Department of Planning Housing Opportunities at 410-887-6055 or hamp@baltimorecountymd.gov. Funding is awarded on a first-come, first-served basis as long as funding is available.

structured_extraction.program_name: LifeBridge Health Live Near Your Work Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between LifeBridge Health and Baltimore County that provides financial assistance toward down payment or closing costs to LifeBridge Health employees who purchase homes in Baltimore County communities near Northwest and Sinai Hospitals. The benefit amount varies based on which of the designated priority neighborhoods the home is located in.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A combined grant from Baltimore County and LifeBridge Health toward down payment or closing costs: up to $5,000 ($2,500 from Baltimore County + $2,500 from LifeBridge) for homes in four priority neighborhoods near Northwest Hospital; $3,500 ($2,500 from Baltimore County + $1,000 from LifeBridge) for homes in three other priority neighborhoods; $1,000 from LifeBridge for homes in the general area near Northwest and Sinai Hospitals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: LifeBridge Health employees who want to purchase a home near Northwest or Sinai Hospital in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment or closing costs for a home purchase in eligible Baltimore County neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated priority neighborhoods near Northwest and Sinai Hospitals in Baltimore County, defined by mapped boundary zones. Inner zone provides LifeBridge $1,000 only; outer zone provides LifeBridge $1,000 plus Baltimore County $2,500.
requirements_list: Must be a LifeBridge Health employee
Must purchase a home in an eligible Baltimore County community near LifeBridge Health facilities
Buyer must contribute at least $1,000 toward the purchase
Must use the property as principal residence
Household income limits apply for the Baltimore County portion of the funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact LifeBridge Employee Services at 410-601-8000 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) provides gap financing to help developers build or rehabilitate affordable multifamily housing in Baltimore County. Funding may include grants, loans, and bonds. Developers must pursue all available funding sources, as Baltimore County is not a primary or sole funder.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing through a combination of grants, loans, bonds, and Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreements. Loans are structured as cash flow contingent second-lien loans at 3% annual simple interest over a 40-year term, with 75% of annual cash flow applied (capped at 40-year amortization). PILOT agreements are available at $300/unit/year for a 10-year term with a 10-year extension option. Gap financing is limited to 25% of total development cost. Repayment schedules are negotiated between the developer and Baltimore County. Amount depends on project needs and available funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — no fixed deadline; applications reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multifamily affordable housing developers (for-profit and nonprofit), owner-operators of rental properties, and development teams (including consultants, architects, general contractors, and management agents) proposing projects serving low-income households at or below 80% AMI. Bonus consideration for nonprofit organizations (51%+ participation), small, faith-based, BIPOC, or female-led partners, and emerging developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for acquisition, predevelopment, soft costs, construction, rehabilitation, and renovation of affordable multifamily rental housing. Eligible uses include: new construction or rehabilitation of vacant buildings producing units for households at or below 80% AMI; acquisition and rehabilitation of existing occupied housing preserving affordability for low-income tenants at or below 80% AMI; infrastructure (via CDBG); operating reserves (3–6 months projected expenses); reserve for replacements ($300–$350/unit/year depending on project type); loan documentation, settlement, and construction financing costs. HOME funds may be used for acquisition, construction, and rehabilitation of rental/multifamily/special needs housing (50–60% AMI). CDBG funds may be used for infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. VCA (Voluntary Compliance Agreement) eligible areas may receive bonus scoring points; applicants are directed to the Development Guide for a map of VCA eligible census tracts.
requirements_list: Developer must pursue all other available funding sources
Project must comply with HUD and State requirements
Development proposal must meet Baltimore County, State, and Federal regulations
Must comply with requirements outlined in the Attainable Housing Development Guide
Compliance with federal regulations; Federal System for Award Management (SAM) check required
MBE/WBE participation: minimum 15% minority and 2% women-owned business participation
Projects must meet County Prevailing Wage and Local Hiring Law
Developer must disclose concurrent discussions with other lenders affecting County's financial participation, lien position, or documents
Loan-to-value ratio not to exceed 100% of appraised value
Gap financing limited to 25% of total development cost
Post-closing requirements: annual desk audit, site monitoring, on-site inspection, and annual reporting (financial statements and compliance documentation)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Attainable Housing Development Guide and schedule a Pre-Concept Plan Conference (call (410) 887-3335). Complete the Application for Financial Assistance along with supporting documents including Form 202, Project Description and Development Team Narrative, and Application Checklist. Submit completed application and required attachments electronically to dhcdrfa@baltimorecountymd.gov. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis and scored using the Application Scoring System. After review, projects proceed through council approval and closing phases (total process typically 2–36 months from initial contact to closing).

structured_extraction.program_description: SELP provides deferred loans to low and moderate income first-time homebuyers to help pay closing costs when purchasing an existing home within Baltimore County's designated Community Conservation Areas. The loan is forgivable if the homeowner lives in the home as their primary residence for 15 years (the affordability period).
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Deferred loan of up to $10,000 to cover closing costs on the purchase of an existing home in a Community Conservation Area. The loan is forgivable after 15 years if the homeowner occupies the property as their principal residence throughout the affordability period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income first-time homebuyers purchasing homes in Baltimore County Community Conservation Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Closing costs required in the purchase of an existing home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must purchase a home within the designated Community Conservation Areas of Baltimore County. Program is administered from Baltimore County, Maryland (The Jefferson Building, 105 West Chesapeake Avenue, Suite 201, Baltimore, MD 21204).

Must be low to moderate income
Must attend a First Time Homebuyer Two-Part Class and a Workshop
Must complete individual financial counseling with a housing counselor
Must not already have a signed contract to buy a house at time of application
Must occupy the purchased property as principal residence for 15 years to qualify for loan forgiveness

After an initial site visit and meeting, the architect prepares a digital rendering of the building with design recommendations and a rough-cost estimate. The service is free when improvements are certified as complete within six months.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Architectural design services for exterior improvements to commercial properties

requirements_list: Property must be located within a Baltimore County Commercial Revitalization District
Improvements must be certified as complete within six months to receive the service for free
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to meet with staff prior to submitting an application. Contact planningaoc@baltimorecountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Agricultural Land Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Preserves working family farms in Baltimore County by purchasing conservation easements from landowners. The program places voluntary deed restrictions on farmland to prevent conversion to non-agricultural uses, protecting it in perpetuity. Landowners sell their development rights while retaining ownership and agricultural use of the land.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive payment for the sale of a conservation easement on their farmland, based on the County Easement Pricing Formula. The easement price is determined by a formula combining Fair Market Value, soils analysis, farm production status, woodland percentage, and subdivision rights. Maximum compensation is capped at 80% FMV ($10,625/acre) for properties with subdivision rights, or 50% FMV ($6,641/acre) for properties without subdivision rights. The easement restricts more intensive land uses permanently. Applications are reviewed annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of farmland in Baltimore County located within an Agricultural Priority Preservation Area (APPA) with at least 50 acres (or at least 20 acres if contiguous to an existing preserved farm) that meet certain soil criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for the sale of development rights (conservation easement) on qualifying farmland. Easement price is based on the approved Baltimore County Agricultural Easement formula incorporating Fair Market Value, soils, farm production, woodland percentage, and subdivision rights. Landowner must bear costs of required Soil Conservation & Water Quality Plan and Forest Stewardship Plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Baltimore County, Maryland within an Agricultural Priority Preservation Area (APPA). Minimum acreage: 50 acres standalone, or 20 acres if contiguous to an existing easement.
requirements_list: Farm must be at least 50 acres, or at least 20 acres if contiguous to an existing preserved farm
Located within an Agricultural Priority Preservation Area (APPA) in Baltimore County
Must meet certain soil criteria

Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan required (approved by Baltimore County Soil Conservation District), unless property is fully forested; plan must be no more than 10 years old at time of application OR obtained within 1 year of settlement
Forest Stewardship Plan required for forested portions of the property
All property owners must sign the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Baltimore County Agricultural Land Preservation Application. Ensure all owners in title sign the application. Submit to Baltimore County Land Preservation staff. Staff will review whether the property meets program criteria and rank applications. Contact staff before filing to discuss your application.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that benefit the overall Commercial Revitalization District, such as holiday lighting, welcome signs, website development, street trees, security cameras, and farmers markets

Eligible triggers include a transition of farm operation within the family, financial difficulties that jeopardize the farm operation, or imminent development pressure. Applications may be submitted at any time.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications can be made at any time

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Property Tax Credit for Historical Restorations and Rehabilitations
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a property tax credit for qualifying rehabilitation projects on historic residential and commercial properties. Residential owner-occupied homeowners can earn a credit equal to 20% of Qualified Rehabilitation Expenditures (QREs) of at least $1,000, applied against County property taxes over up to 10 years. Commercial and other income-producing property owners receive a credit equal to the increase in assessed value resulting from rehabilitation work, effectively capping their County property tax for 10 years. Credits are fully transferable to new owners for the remaining credit period and may be used alongside State historic tax credits offered through the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT). All rehabilitation work must be pre-approved by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) and must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Planning, Historic Preservation
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential: A fixed tax credit equal to 20% of Qualified Rehabilitation Expenditures (minimum $1,000 in eligible expenses), applied against the annual County property tax bill over up to 10 subsequent tax years. Commercial: A credit equal to the difference between pre- and post-rehabilitation assessed value, functioning as an assessment freeze for 10 years. The credit may not exceed the actual tax levied in any given year. Both credits are fully transferable to new owners and can be used alongside State historic tax credits through the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT). The credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax — other charges on the tax bill are not included.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Part I and Part II applications may be submitted at any time. Part II applications (without State approval) are due two weeks before the next scheduled Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting. Part III is submitted after completion of the rehabilitation work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic residential and commercial properties in Baltimore County — including residential owner-occupants and owners of commercial or income-producing properties — that are listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, contributing resources within a Baltimore County Historic District, or individually listed or contributing resources in a National Register of Historic Places Historic District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and restoration of historic structures, including basement waterproofing (including basement water ejection systems), chimney repair, exterior painting, interior plaster repair, masonry repointing, storm windows, plumbing/electrical/mechanical systems, roof repair and replacement, structural repairs, window restoration, and similar eligible work. Eligible accessory structures (barns, carriage houses, springhouses) may qualify if significance criteria are met. Ineligible uses include new construction, landscaping, architectural consultation, site work, owner labor, new additions, non-attached walls/gates, State/local grant-funded work, new appliances, remodeling projects (e.g. new kitchens/bathrooms), and non-historic outbuildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for properties located in Baltimore County, Maryland. No sub-county geographic restrictions apply; the program is county-wide for eligible historic properties on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, in a Baltimore County Historic District, or in a National Register of Historic Places Historic District.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic: listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, a contributing resource in a Baltimore County Historic District, or individually listed or a contributing resource in a National Register of Historic Places Historic District.
Residential projects must have Qualified Rehabilitation Expenditures of at least $1,000.
Commercial projects generally require rehabilitation work in excess of $50,000 to generate a reassessment.
All work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
Work must be reviewed and approved by the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) or Staff before starting. Work started prior to approval is ineligible.
A Historic Environmental Setting (HES) may be required for Landmarked structures without a National Register designation.
Three-part application: Parts 1 and 2 submitted before work begins; Part 3 submitted after project completion.
Credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax.
Project must rehabilitate the historic structure while preserving significant historic, architectural, or cultural features.

For basement waterproofing systems: applicants must complete a four-item Building Owner's Checklist (gutters, debris removal, downspout extension ≥3 feet, surface grading slope ≥20 feet away from foundation). If water penetration persists, a licensed professional engineer, architect, or landscape architect must submit a report stating surface water management cannot solve the problem and that a basement waterproofing/ejection system is necessary.
Part III (completion) submission must include before/after photographs, itemized cost tally by work item, receipts and cancelled check copies, and all building permits for the project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Parts 1 and 2 of the appropriate application (residential or commercial) before starting work — Part 1 certifies building eligibility; Part 2 certifies the proposed project meets rehabilitation standards. Part 2 applications without State approval are reviewed at the next LPC meeting (submit at least two weeks in advance); those with State approval are reviewed by staff. For basement waterproofing, complete the Building Owner's Checklist and, if needed, obtain a professional engineer/architect report before approval. After completing the project, submit Part 3 to certify the completed work and claimed expenditures, including before/after photographs, itemized costs, receipts, cancelled checks, and building permits. Applications can be submitted by email to histpres@baltimorecountymd.gov or by mail to Baltimore County Department of Planning, Historic Preservation, 105 West Chesapeake Avenue, Suite 101, Towson, MD 21204. Contact Preservation Services at 410-887-3495 for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: CountyRide provides specialized transportation services for eligible Baltimore County residents, including seniors (age 60+), people with disabilities (ages 18–59), and rural residents of all ages. Buses run Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., and are equipped with wheelchair accommodations, low-step entrances, and escorts for riders needing special assistance at no extra charge. The program is funded in part by the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA).
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Public Works and Transportation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free demand-response specialized paratransit transportation service (door-to-door) for eligible residents. Funded primarily by Baltimore County with grants from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA). Medical trips can be scheduled up to 14 days in advance; non-medical trips up to 7 days in advance. All trips are based on availability. Processing of registration takes approximately 30 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County seniors (60+), persons with disabilities (ages 18–59), and rural residents of all ages who cannot use public transportation or live outside the public transit service area. Disabled residents age 60+ do not require a physician statement; those under 60 do.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical and non-medical transportation trips, including appointments and general-purpose travel.

Rural residents: reside within rural boundaries as determined by Baltimore County
All children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult
Children under 8 must have a child safety seat supplied by parent or guardian (unless 4'9" or taller and over 65 lbs)
Persons with disabilities under age 60 must have application completed by both client and physician
Vehicle access to residential address or alternate pickup location required
Household pets must be restrained during pickup

Once approved, contact the office to request a client identification number before service is activated. For hearing or speech disabilities, Maryland Relay 711 is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Boost Fund provides business loans to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Baltimore County. Funded through revenue from Maryland's video lottery terminals directed through the Maryland Department of Commerce, loans range from $50,000 to $250,000 with reduced down payments and interest rates at or below current market rates. Loans have a maximum 20-year term with customized payment plans to help businesses manage cash flow. Businesses must first apply for a bank loan; if the bank cannot cover the full project cost, the County considers a loan application for the funding shortfall. The business must operate in leased, commercially zoned space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $50,000 to $250,000 with reduced down payment requirements and interest rates at or below current market rates. Maximum loan term is 20 years with customized payment plans to help businesses manage cash flow. Funds are provided through the Maryland Department of Commerce via video lottery terminal revenues. Loans are used to fill the gap between what a bank will lend and the total project cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Fair Election Fund provides public matching funds to candidates running for Baltimore County Executive or County Council who qualify by raising a minimum number and dollar amount of small-dollar contributions from County residents. The program is designed to encourage small-donor participation in local elections by amplifying qualifying contributions with public funds on a tiered matching basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public matching funds are provided to certified candidates on a tiered basis. For County Executive candidates, the maximum public contribution is $750,000 per election ($1,500,000 per full election cycle). The matching ratio is 6:1 for the first $50 of a qualifying contribution, 4:1 for $51–$100, 2:1 for $101–$150, and no match for $151–$250. For County Council candidates, the maximum is $80,000 per election ($160,000 per cycle). The matching ratio is 4:1 for the first $50, 3:1 for $51–$100, 2:1 for $101–$150, and no match for $151–$250. Private contributions from any individual are capped at $250 per election cycle (4-year cycle January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026). Qualifying contributions must be between $5 and $250; cash contributions are capped at $100 per cycle. Contributions from PACs, corporations, labor organizations, or party committees are not allowed. The distribution period begins 365 days before the primary election and ends 15 days after the general election.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Receipt submission for General Election through 11/3/2026 at 11:59 PM; qualifying period for primary certification ended 6/23/2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates running for Baltimore County Executive or Baltimore County Council who are County residents and seek public financing for their campaigns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign expenditures for certified candidates in contested primary and general elections. Public funds cannot be used to benefit another candidate.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to candidates who are Baltimore County residents running for County Executive or County Council.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident running for County Executive or County Council
Register a Public Finance Committee with the Maryland Board of Elections Campaign Reporting Information System (MDCRIS)
File a Notice of Intent to Qualify with the State Board of Elections
Open a publicly funded campaign account at a bank
Receive approval of the Public Finance Committee from the State Board
County Executive candidates must collect at least 550 qualifying contributions and $50,000 in aggregate qualifying contributions from County residents
County Council candidates must collect at least 150 qualifying contributions and $15,000 in aggregate qualifying contributions from County residents
Individual private contributions may not exceed $250 per election cycle; qualifying contributions must be between $5 and $250; cash capped at $100 per cycle
No contributions from PACs, corporations, labor organizations, or party central committees
Must be in a contested election to receive matching funds
Qualifying period for primary certification ended 45 calendar days before the primary election (6/23/2025 for the 2026 cycle)
Receipt submission for General Election continues through 11/3/2026 at 11:59 PM
File required periodic campaign finance reports and documentation with the State Board
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a certificate of candidacy with the Baltimore County Board of Elections. Then register a Public Finance Committee in MDCRIS, file a Notice of Intent with the State Board of Elections, open a publicly funded campaign account, receive State Board approval, and raise the required qualifying contributions from County residents. Submit all required campaign finance reports to the State Board. The distribution period begins 365 days before the primary election and ends 15 days after the general election. For the 2026 cycle, the primary election was 2/24/2026 and the general election is 11/3/2026. First disbursements were allowed in June 2025 for the 2026 election cycle. Candidates may also contact the Baltimore County Fair Election Fund Commission at fairelectionfund@baltimorecountymd.gov for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A hardship exemption that removes the Maryland State Bay Restoration Fee from a property owner's real property tax bill for the current fiscal year. Eligible homeowners who meet income or disability criteria can apply annually to have the fee waived.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An approved exemption removes the Bay Restoration Fee from the applicant's current real property tax account for that fiscal year only. The exemption does not carry over — homeowners must reapply each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30 of the fiscal tax year in which the exemption is being sought, by 4 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County homeowners who use the property as their primary residence and currently receive the Homeowners Tax Credit Baltimore County Supplement, the Real Property Tax Exemption for Disabled American Veterans or Surviving Spouse of Disabled American Veterans, or the Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers or Surviving Spouses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the Maryland State Bay Restoration Fee on the applicant's real property tax bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: The property must be the applicant's primary residence.

The applicant must currently receive one of the following: (1) Homeowners Tax Credit Baltimore County Supplement, (2) Real Property Tax Exemption for Disabled American Veterans or Surviving Spouse of Disabled American Veterans, or (3) Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers or Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers.
Application must be received by 4 p.m. on September 30 of the fiscal tax year in which the exemption is sought.
Re-application and re-approval are required each year.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online application form on the Baltimore County website before the September 30 deadline. The county verifies the information provided. If approved, the fee is removed from the current real property tax account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Blind Individual and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state law exempts $15,000 of a property's assessed value from real property tax obligations for blind individuals or their surviving spouses. Baltimore County participates in this statewide program. Blind individuals may also apply for a retroactive refund of property taxes paid in years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, going back up to three years. Applications are filed with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT); refund requests for Baltimore County taxes are submitted to the Baltimore County Council.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exempts $15,000 of a blind individual's (or surviving spouse's) property assessed value from real property tax. Also provides a retroactive refund of property taxes paid in years when the exemption was authorized but not granted, going back up to three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Blind individuals and their surviving spouses who own real property in Maryland. Applicant must be a Maryland resident, the legal owner of the property, and use the property as their principal residence. Medical certification of permanent impairment of both eyes is required from a licensed medical doctor or optometrist, meeting specific visual acuity standards (central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, or a peripheral field defect contracting to 20 degrees or less diameter in the better eye).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in real property tax liability by exempting $15,000 of assessed value; refund of previously paid property taxes for eligible years retroactive up to three years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to property owners in all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. The exemption is authorized by state law and administered by SDAT through 24 county assessment offices statewide. For Baltimore County, refund requests for county taxes are submitted to the Baltimore County Council.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a blind individual or the surviving spouse of a blind individual

Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Applicant must be the legal owner of the property

Medical certification required from a licensed medical doctor or optometrist: permanent impairment of both eyes (central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, OR a field defect where peripheral field contracts to 20 degrees or less in diameter in the better eye)
Must obtain and file an exemption application with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
For a refund, must first receive an approved exemption from SDAT, then submit a copy to the Baltimore County Council with a letter requesting a refund

Medical certification from a licensed medical doctor or optometrist must accompany the application. To request a retroactive refund for Baltimore County taxes, forward a copy of the approved SDAT exemption to the Baltimore County Council at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 205, Towson, Maryland 21204, along with a letter requesting the refund.

structured_extraction.program_name: Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) provides real property tax credits to owners who clean up and redevelop contaminated brownfield sites. Eligible properties must have completed Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and received formal designation as a 'Qualified Brownfields Site' from the Maryland Department of Commerce (formerly Department of Business and Economic Development). After cleanup, qualifying sites receive a tax credit of 50% of the property tax attributable to the increased assessed value. For properties outside Enterprise Zones, the credit lasts five taxable years. An additional 20% credit is available for properties located in an Enterprise Zone or designated commercial revitalization area, and an additional 20% credit is available when voluntary cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000, for a maximum credit of up to 70%. Enterprise Zone properties may also receive the credit for up to 10 years total. Eligible properties include those contaminated by oil or hazardous substances, former industrial/commercial sites in densely populated urban areas that are substantially underutilized, or existing/former industrial sites posing a threat to public health or the environment. The credit is terminated if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval of the Response Action Plan or Certificate of Completion.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit of 50% of the Baltimore County real property tax attributable to the increased assessment after brownfield cleanup. For sites outside Enterprise Zones, the credit lasts five taxable years. An additional 20% credit is available for properties in an Enterprise Zone or designated commercial revitalization area. An additional 20% credit is available when voluntary cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000. Properties in an Enterprise Zone may receive the credit for up to 10 years total. The maximum combined credit is up to 70%. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax portion of the tax bill. Credit is terminated if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval of the Response Action Plan or Certificate of Completion.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Baltimore County real property taxes on the increased assessed value of a cleaned-up brownfield site
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located in Baltimore County, Maryland; additional benefits (extended credit period and higher credit percentage) for properties within one of Baltimore County's three Enterprise Zones or designated commercial revitalization areas
requirements_list: Site must be owned by an inculpable person
Property must have completed MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP)
Property must receive formal designation as a 'Qualified Brownfields Site' from the Maryland Department of Commerce (formerly Department of Business and Economic Development)

Property must meet at least one brownfields criterion: contaminated by oil or hazardous substances; a former industrial or commercial site in a densely populated urban area that is substantially underutilized; or an existing or former industrial site posing a threat to public health or the environment
For the additional 20% Enterprise Zone credit, the site must be located in one of Baltimore County's three Enterprise Zones

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program and obtain formal designation as a Qualified Brownfields Site from the Maryland Department of Commerce. Then download the Brownfields Tax Credit brochure and application form from Baltimore County and submit the completed application with documentation of cleanup costs incurred to the Brownfields Coordinator at 105 West Chesapeake Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Community Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cannabis Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Community Grants Program provides reimbursable grants to community-based nonprofits and private businesses in Baltimore County. Funded through a portion of Maryland's cannabis sales and use tax revenue and administered by the Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance, the program supports initiatives that address the impacts of cannabis criminalization and invest in communities disproportionately affected by the war on drugs and cannabis prohibition enforcement. Priority areas include workforce development, mental health, housing, education, reentry, entrepreneurship, community organization, public health, and justice/equity/diversity.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants ranging from $25,000 to $200,000 per applicant for a one-year project period. A small percentage of funds may be provided upfront. Applicants must provide a 10% monetary or in-kind match. Grant monies may fund no more than 50% of executive/administrative salaries; direct service staff can be fully funded. Indirect costs up to the federal de minimis rate of 15% are allowed. Funding is allocated to Baltimore County based on historical cannabis possession charges relative to statewide totals (July 1, 2002 to January 1, 2023).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofits, private businesses, individuals, and government entities serving low-income Baltimore County residents in Qualified Census Tracts or priority ZIP codes, particularly those impacted by cannabis criminalization and the war on drugs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adult professional development, education and afterschool programs, entrepreneurship and economic development, housing and unhoused prevention services, mental health and harm reduction, nonprofit training for BIPOC community leaders, reentry and reintegration, workforce development and training, community organization, public health, social work, and justice/equity/diversity initiatives. Funds may also support building renovations, capital expenses, facility expansion, and staff professional development when directly tied to eligible CRRF activities. Cannot be used for law enforcement activities or to replace existing local government program funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve Baltimore County residents in priority ZIP codes (21117, 21133, 21136, 21206, 21207, 21208, 21220, 21221, 21222, 21227, 21228, 21234, 21236, 21237, 21244) or in Qualified Census Tracts. Projects outside these ZIP codes may qualify if they serve individuals from or re-entering those areas. Funding allocation is based on the total number of cannabis possession charges in Baltimore County between July 1, 2002 and January 1, 2023, relative to statewide totals.
requirements_list: Must be a community-based private business, nonprofit organization, individual, or government entity
Must be aligned with Baltimore County's CRRF priorities
Must serve or benefit Baltimore County residents
Must serve communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement
Must align with one or more eligible program areas (community organization, education, housing, public health, re-entry services, social work, workforce development, or justice/equity/diversity)
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must provide a 10% monetary or in-kind match
Organizations with budgets over $1 million are encouraged to subcontract with smaller, local organizations
Must score a minimum of 70 out of 100 on the application scoring sheet to be considered for funding
Applications must be emailed with all required forms completed and attached
No bribery convictions (applicant, officers, directors, employees involved in obtaining/performing grants)
No criminal convictions for fraud, embezzlement, theft, forgery, falsification, stolen property, antitrust violations, RICO, mail fraud, MBE law violations, or conspiracy to commit these
Not suspended or debarred by any public entity
All state/county taxes paid
Nondiscrimination in employment compliance
Political contribution disclosure if cumulative contract value is $200,000 or more
SMART goals required (at least 1, up to 3)
Must track number of Baltimore County residents served
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all required application materials including the Community Grant Funding Application, Risk Assessment, Application Scoring Sheet, Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance, Budget Application, Grant Affidavit, Form W-9, financial documents, and an organization chart. Email all completed materials to grsigrants@baltimorecountymd.gov by the April 1 deadline. The county hosted multiple informational webinars (February–March 2026) to walk applicants through the program overview and application process. Applications are scored by an evaluation process and reviewed by the CRRF Commission. Only applications scoring 70 or above out of 100 are considered for funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County provides a real property tax credit to law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who suffered a permanent and total disability while serving the citizens of Baltimore County, as well as to public safety retirees who were disabled due to a line-of-duty injury and retired on a medical disability pension. The credit eliminates 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax on the disabled worker's primary dwelling and renews automatically each year for the lifetime of the disabled person. The credit has been available since July 2009. Eligible retirees who were disabled due to a line-of-duty injury and retired on a medical disability pension and currently reside in Baltimore County may also qualify.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax on the qualifying primary dwelling. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County real property tax — not to other charges on the tax bill. Once approved, the credit continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person without need for further application. The credit began in July 2009. Eligible retirees who were disabled due to a line-of-duty injury and retired on a medical disability pension and currently reside in Baltimore County may also qualify.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who suffered a permanent and total disability during service to Baltimore County residents, as well as Baltimore County public safety retirees who were disabled due to a line-of-duty injury and retired on a medical disability pension and currently reside in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsets the Baltimore County real property tax obligation on the disabled worker's or retiree's primary dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Baltimore County, Maryland. Applicant must currently reside in Baltimore County. Applicant must have been domiciled in Maryland at the time of disability determination. Property must be located in Baltimore County.

Alternatively, send an email with your name, address, and telephone number to financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov or call 410-887-2872 to verify eligibility and request the necessary paperwork.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: Exempts the primary home of a disabled veteran or the surviving spouse of a disabled veteran from all Baltimore County real property taxes. The program also allows eligible individuals to apply for a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years before receiving the exemption. While the exemption application is filed with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), the benefit applies specifically to Baltimore County real property taxes, and refund requests are submitted to the Baltimore County Council.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from all Baltimore County real property taxes on the qualifying home of a disabled veteran or surviving spouse. A retroactive refund of taxes paid for up to three years before the exemption was granted may also be requested by submitting the approved SDAT exemption to the Baltimore County Council.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans and surviving spouses of disabled veterans who own a home in Baltimore County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of Baltimore County real property tax obligation on the applicant's home; refund of previously paid property taxes for up to three years prior to the exemption being granted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Baltimore County, Maryland. The exemption application is filed with SDAT (statewide agency), but the tax relief applies specifically to Baltimore County real property taxes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County real property tax credit for residential property owners who install solar or geothermal energy devices that meet national safety and performance standards to heat, cool, supply electricity, or provide hot water. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation. Due to high demand and an annual budget cap of $1.5 million, approved applications are placed on a waiting list in the order received.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit of 50% of eligible installation costs or $5,000, whichever is less. For a hot water supply system, the credit is $1,500. The credit cannot exceed the property taxes owed in a given year; any excess may be carried forward for up to two additional tax years. Eligible costs include equipment, components, accessories, and reasonable installation costs incurred within 12 months before the initial application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 of the year immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single and multi-family residential property owners in Baltimore County who install solar or geothermal energy devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset Baltimore County Real Property Tax for installation of solar or geothermal devices used to heat, cool, supply electricity, or provide hot water
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Baltimore County, Maryland

Household appliances are explicitly excluded
Costs must be incurred within 12 months before the initial application
Must submit detailed receipts listing amount and dates of payment
Must provide evidence of national safety and performance standards compliance
Must provide the Permit Number for the electrical inspection completed by the Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office
Application must be submitted by June 1 of the year preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
Credit does not transfer with the property; a change of ownership terminates the credit

Gather required documentation (receipts and electrical inspection permit number), then submit the completed application by June 1. structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Hardship Installment Payment Program lets residential property taxpayers who are facing a temporary financial hardship spread out their tax payments over time to avoid having their property sold at the annual tax sale. Eligibility is based on demonstrated hardship, ability to repay, and financial disclosure. Approval is valid only for the fiscal year in which a taxpayer applies, and all future taxes must stay current to keep eligibility.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved taxpayers receive a structured installment payment plan that gives them additional time to pay their property tax liability. Approval is good for one fiscal year at a time.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying overdue residential property taxes on an installment basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a real property tax credit to owners of commercial buildings that achieve at least a silver rating under the LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) Green Building rating system or the American National Standards Institute's National Green Building Standard (NGBS) rating system. The credit percentage and duration vary by rating system, category, and efficiency level achieved. Eligible buildings include commercial properties and income-producing residential buildings with at least 50 units.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

LEED Core and Shell (LEED-CS): Silver=40%, Gold=50%, Platinum=80%, duration 5 years. LEED Existing Buildings (LEED-EB): Silver=10%, Gold=25%, Platinum=50%, duration 3 years. NGBS: Silver=50%, Gold=60%, Emerald=80%, duration 5 years. Only one High Performance Building Credit is allowed per building; the credit runs with the property through ownership changes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County real property tax credit for residential property owners based on the percentage of energy efficiency achieved in the home. The credit applies for a three-year term (or five years if carbon neutral), and the credit percentage corresponds to the energy efficiency level certified by the builder, contractor, rater, or qualified professional. Eligibility pathways include LEED certification (Silver, Gold, or Platinum) for new or renovated residential structures, or achieving at least 30% increased energy efficiency certified by a HERS rater, ASHRAE professional (multifamily), or Passive House consultant. The credit reduces Baltimore County real property taxes and does not apply to other charges or fees on the bill.

The credit term is three years, or five years if the home is carbon neutral. Eligibility pathways include LEED certification (Silver, Gold, or Platinum) for new or renovated residential structures, or achieving at least 30% increased energy efficiency certified by a HERS rater, ASHRAE professional (multifamily), or Passive House consultant. structured_extraction.program_name: Metropolitan Benefit and Construction Loan Deferral
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Budget and Finance offers a deferral program for eligible homeowners age 60 or older who also qualify for the Homeowners Tax Credit. structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County real property tax credit for owners who make qualified physical improvements to a mobile home park, senior housing development, or commercially zoned property. For properties located in one of Baltimore County's 24 designated Commercial Revitalization Districts, a five-year credit is available when physical improvements increase the assessed property value by $100,000 or more, with a 10-year credit available when improvement costs exceed $10 million. The credit reduces the owner's Baltimore County real property tax obligation based on the type and location of the improvement. For senior housing developments in a designated commercial revitalization district, the credit equals 100% of the increase in County taxes resulting from the improvements. For senior housing outside a revitalization district, the credit equals 50% of the tax increase. For other commercial property in a commercially designated district, the credit equals 100% of the County property taxes charged against the property. For mobile home parks, the credit equals 100% of the increase in County taxes resulting from improvements. Properties outside a revitalization district may also be eligible for a reduced credit.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance

For senior housing outside a revitalization district, the credit equals 50% of the tax increase. For other commercial property in a commercially designated district, the credit equals 100% of the County property taxes charged against the property. For mobile home parks, the credit equals 100% of the increase in County taxes resulting from improvements. The credit runs for five years when improvements increase assessed value by $100,000 or more, or 10 years when improvement costs exceed $10 million. Credits are transferable.
