structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a 100% property tax credit on the Baltimore County Real Property Tax to the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) who died in Maryland in the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County. Once approved, the credit continues from year to year without requiring a new application each year. The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 100% of the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation for the surviving spouse's dwelling. It does not apply to other charges on the tax bill. The credit continues automatically from year to year after the initial application is approved. It cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 of the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers, firefighters, EMTs, and volunteer rescue workers employed by Baltimore County who died in Maryland in the course of or as a result of their employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces the surviving spouse's Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation to zero for their dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The decedent must have been employed by Baltimore County and died in the State of Maryland. The dwelling must be located in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: The deceased must have been a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) employed by Baltimore County
Death must have occurred in Maryland in the course of or as a result of employment with Baltimore County
The dwelling is the legal residence of the surviving spouse and is occupied by no more than two families
The surviving spouse has not remarried

The dwelling was owned by the decedent at the time of death, OR the decedent or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland at the time of death and the dwelling was acquired by the surviving spouse within two years of the date of death, OR the dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling
Application must be submitted on or before September 30 of the first taxable year for which the credit is desired
The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Surviving Spouse of a Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker and submit it with a death certificate and eligibility evidence by September 30 of the taxable year for which the credit should begin. Mail or deliver the application to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) Program is a voluntary program that helps Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participants achieve economic independence over a five-year period. Participants work with a case manager to set goals, build skills, and access resources in areas like child care, credit counseling, education, job readiness, and homeownership. As earned income increases, a portion of the rent increase is deposited into an interest-bearing escrow savings account. Participants receive the escrow funds when they complete the program and achieve self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive case management support and access to resources (child care, credit counseling, education, job training, transportation, and more). When a participant's earned income increases, Baltimore County deposits a portion of their rent increase into an escrow savings account. Upon completing the five-year program and achieving self-sufficiency goals, participants receive the accumulated escrow funds plus interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participants whose goal is economic independence. Once the head or co-head of household signs an FSS Contract of Participation, all household members 18 and older are eligible for services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Escrow savings funds can be used upon graduation from the program after achieving self-sufficiency goals. Program resources cover child care, credit counseling, money management, education, career counseling, English as a second language, homeownership, self-esteem, training, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Housing Choice Voucher participants in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be a current Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participant
Goal of economic independence
Head or co-head of household must sign an FSS Contract of Participation
Household members 18 or older become eligible for services once contract is signed
Program lasts up to five years (extendable up to two additional years)
Must complete five goals and achieve self-sufficiency to graduate and receive escrow funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Baltimore County Office of Housing by email at hcvfss@baltimorecountymd.gov for more information or assistance enrolling in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program (formerly Section 8) provides rental assistance subsidies to low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families in Baltimore County. Funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), the program helps eligible families afford decent, safe, and affordable rental housing in the private market. Families on the waiting list receive a voucher subsidy they can use in their current home or in other qualifying rental units that meet housing quality standards and reasonable rent requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance subsidy that covers a portion of the monthly rent for qualifying families. The maximum subsidy paid to landlords is determined by HUD-established Fair Market Rents and Baltimore County payment standards (set at 110% of FY 2026 Fair Market Rents, ranging from $1,498 to $3,733/month for efficiency through 6-bedroom units, effective January 1, 2026). Families pay the difference between their portion and the actual rent. Participants may use the voucher in their current home or move to other qualifying rental housing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No waiting lists open; BCOH will not be accepting any preliminary applications until further notice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families and individuals in Baltimore County whose incomes are below HUD-set income limits. Current voucher holders and active landlords with HCV tenants may also access program services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental assistance for decent, safe, and affordable housing in qualifying private-market rental units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Baltimore County, Maryland. Voucher holders may also port (transfer) their voucher to other jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Income must be below HUD-set income limits for the area
Must provide Social Security numbers for all household members
Must provide documentation of citizenship or immigration status
Must provide detailed income and family information at the time of interview
Rental unit must meet housing quality standards (NSPIRE inspection compliance required)
Rent must be reasonable compared to similar unassisted units in the neighborhood
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants join the waiting list when it is open. Families with the earliest application date and time are served first. When selected from the waiting list and determined eligible, they receive a voucher subsidy. Currently, no waiting lists are open and BCOH is not accepting preliminary applications until further notice. Existing voucher holders have 60 days to find a suitable unit, extendable by two 30-day periods; extension requests must be submitted in writing at least 7 calendar days before voucher expiration. Landlords with HCV tenants may manage HAP payments, inspections, and tax forms through the BCOH landlord portal and may submit rent adjustment requests between 150 and 120 days prior to the anniversary date of their HAP contract.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers grant funding to help neighborhood Citizens on Patrol groups cover startup and operating costs. COP groups are organized volunteers who patrol their neighborhoods to deter crime and report suspicious activity to police.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to supplement Citizens on Patrol groups for startup and operation costs. Grants typically open for applications around April each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community or neighborhood groups forming Citizens on Patrol patrols in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Startup and operation costs for Citizens on Patrol groups
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a community or neighborhood within Baltimore County
requirements_list: Group can have as few as two members
Must be a Baltimore County community or neighborhood
Contact a Community Outreach Officer from the local precinct
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Set up a community meeting, contact a Community Outreach Officer from your local precinct, recruit volunteers, and coordinate a training session. Grants open around April each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week evening program designed to humanize law enforcement by giving community members personal insight into the lives and experiences of individual police officers. The program focuses on open dialogue to build stronger community-police relationships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six evening classes held 6–8 p.m. covering topics such as implicit bias in policing, officer mental health, split-second decisions, and the evolution of policing. Space is limited to 30 participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and community engagement focused on understanding law enforcement officers as individuals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Baltimore County residents
requirements_list: Space is limited to 30 participants
2025 fall program runs October 16 through November 20
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form. The application deadline for the 2025 fall program is October 2, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A seven-week education program for community members, business owners, and religious leaders to learn about police operations, officer training, and the role of law enforcement. The program builds transparency and strong relationships between the police and the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seven Wednesday evening classes (6:30–9:30 p.m.) plus one Saturday class (9 a.m.–3 p.m.) covering police operations, court systems, crime prevention, use of force, and more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members, business owners, and religious leaders in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education about police operations and community-police relations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Baltimore County residents
requirements_list: Applicants are subject to a background check
Exceptions to the application process may be approved by the program coordinator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the provided link. Applicants will undergo a background check. Classes begin April 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) offers a business loan program with flexible lending terms that are more modest and accommodating than traditional lenders. The program is designed to drive job creation and foster sustainable business growth across Baltimore City. It provides working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvements to small and growing businesses. The program prioritizes minority-owned and women-owned businesses to ensure equitable access to capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with flexible terms more accommodating than traditional lenders. Loan types include working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvements. For the Micro Loan track, businesses must have maximum revenue of $5 million. Collateral may be required depending on loan type. Borrowers who own 20% or more of the business may be required to personally guarantee the loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and growing businesses in Baltimore City, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned businesses. Eligible business types include sole proprietors, partnerships, corporations, LLCs, startups, retailers, service providers, and contractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must operate inside Baltimore City boundaries or be in the process of relocating to Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must operate a business inside Baltimore City or be in the process of moving there
Minimum personal credit score of 680
Minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.20x
Owners with 20% or more ownership may be required to personally guarantee the loan
Collateral may be required depending on loan type
Federal, state, and local taxes must be current with no outstanding judgments or liens
Micro Loan track: maximum business revenue of $5 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an intake form online. A BDC team member will follow up after the form is completed. Applicants should be prepared to supply personal and business tax returns, current bank statements, profit and loss sheets or cash flow statements, and any current debt schedules.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally designated area considered outside U.S. Customs territory, allowing companies to hold import/export activities on U.S. soil with cost-saving benefits. Companies can defer import duties, reduce customs processing fees, and streamline logistics for warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing operations. The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) administers FTZ #74 on behalf of Baltimore City and surrounding counties. Because the zone uses the Alternative Site Framework (ASF), companies can complete activation within a few weeks from any property in the designated service area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Companies operating within FTZ #74 benefit from deferred import duties, reduced U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) processing fees, and streamlined logistics. Goods can be stored, processed, or manufactured within the zone with duties assessed only when goods enter U.S. commerce, and no duties owed on goods re-exported.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Companies importing or exporting international goods that use warehouse, distribution, or manufacturing facilities in the Baltimore region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of import duties, reduction of customs processing fees, and operational cost savings for warehousing, distribution, and manufacturing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area covers approximately 1,000 acres of designated industrial and distribution space across Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Harford County, Cecil County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must be located within FTZ #74's designated service area
Must engage in importing or exporting international goods
Must complete the activation process with BDC as FTZ administrator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact FTZ Director Will Cawthern at wcawthern@BaltimoreDevelopment.com to learn about activation. Under the Alternative Site Framework (ASF), activation can be completed within a few weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) that provides funding to small and medium-sized businesses in Baltimore City to help cover utility bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 awarded to eligible small and medium-sized businesses to help pay utility bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and medium-sized businesses in Baltimore City struggling with utility costs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of utility bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City businesses only
requirements_list: Must be a small or medium-sized business
Must be located in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Baltimore Development Corporation website at baltimoredevelopment.com to determine eligibility and apply for funding. Applications open after May 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone and Focus Area Tax Credit Program (Baltimore City)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) manages the State of Maryland Enterprise Zone (EZ) program in Baltimore City. The program provides real property tax credits and state income tax credits to businesses located in a designated Enterprise Zone in exchange for job creation and investment. Businesses in Focus Areas — specific sub-zones within an Enterprise Zone — receive enhanced benefits, including personal property tax credits and higher income tax credits for new hires.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enterprise Zone (EZ) benefits: (1) Real property tax credit on incremental increase in property taxes from real property improvements — 80% credit in years 1–5, decreasing 10% annually in years 6–10, credited to the property owner. (2) Income tax credit of $1,000 per new employee or $6,000 over 3 years per new economically disadvantaged employee; credit may be carried forward 5 years. EZ Focus Area benefits (in addition to EZ benefits): (1) Real property tax credit of 80% on increased assessed value for 10 years. (2) Personal property tax credit of 80% for 10 years on new investment in personal property; credit goes to property owner. (3) Income tax credit of $1,500 per new employee or $9,000 over 3 years per new economically disadvantaged employee; credit may be carried forward 5 years. Businesses must be certified by the local enterprise zone administrator to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in a designated Enterprise Zone or Focus Area in Baltimore City that are creating jobs and making investments in real or personal property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied against real property taxes, personal property taxes, and state income taxes in exchange for job creation and property investment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to businesses located within a designated Enterprise Zone or Focus Area in Baltimore City. Use the Maryland Enterprise Zone Map to verify eligibility by address.
requirements_list: Business must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone or Focus Area in Baltimore City
Business must be certified as eligible by the local enterprise zone administrator (BDC)
Income tax credits require the business to add new employment meeting certain requirements
Not every business in an Enterprise Zone, Sustainable Community, or Opportunity Zone automatically qualifies — certification is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the Maryland Enterprise Zone Map to confirm your address is within an Enterprise Zone or Focus Area. To apply for the property tax credit, use the Baltimore City Property Tax Credits portal. For questions about eligibility and certification, contact BDC at (410) 837-9305 or info@baltimoredevelopment.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Facade Improvement Grant offers matching funds to help business owners and property owners in Baltimore City make exterior building upgrades that improve the look and feel of commercial areas. Eligible properties include commercial buildings, vacant and corner commercial properties, industrial properties, and shopping centers. Grants must be approved before work begins and are reimbursed after the project is complete. Several grant options exist depending on property type.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based matching grant for exterior building improvements. The grant award is a 1:1 match to the owner's investment for most property types; Shopping Center FIG is 10% of total project cost. Grant amounts range from $7,500 to $50,000 depending on property type. Funds are reimbursed after the project is complete — applicants must pay for the entire project before receiving reimbursement. Eligible properties include commercial buildings, vacant and corner commercial properties, industrial properties, and shopping centers. Five FIG options exist depending on property type. Awards depend on available funding and are made at BDC's sole discretion. If final project cost is less than the original estimate, the grant is reduced proportionally to maintain the 1:1 match ratio. Grant recipients must maintain improvements for 5 years post-grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and commercial property owners in Baltimore City seeking to make exterior improvements to commercial and industrial properties. Excludes residential properties, non-profits (except those selling goods/services to the public), new construction built within the last 3 years, and properties actively listed for sale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior building upgrades including storefronts, signage, awnings, facades, exterior paint, windows/doors, lighting, and other improvements that enhance the appearance of commercial and industrial areas. Scope must be pre-approved; work completed before approval is not reimbursable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available citywide in Baltimore City only. Properties in designated Baltimore City CHAP (Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation) Historic Districts must obtain CHAP Authorization to Proceed before commencing work and designs must meet CHAP rules and design guidance. Properties in the following Baltimore City Main Streets Districts may require local Design Review Committee submission (BDC staff will advise): Belair-Edison, Federal Hill, Fells Point, Hamilton-Lauraville, Highlandtown, Pennsylvania Avenue, Pigtown, and Waverly.
requirements_list: Grants must be approved before work begins
Work completed prior to application approval is NOT eligible for reimbursement
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application
Grant award is a 1:1 match to the owner's investment (Shopping Center FIG is 10% of total project cost)
Applicant must provide matching funds
Work cannot begin until the grant is awarded and an agreement letter is signed
Construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter
Applicant must be a business with a signed lease or a commercial property owner located in Baltimore City
Proof of occupancy required (signed lease, letter of intent, or commercial occupancy proof)
Properties in CHAP Historic Districts must obtain Authorization to Proceed before commencing work
Properties in Baltimore City Main Streets Districts may require Design Review Committee submission
Permanently installed, clearly visible commercial signage must be in place before reimbursement
Must have a commercial tenant on the first floor and a complete certificate of occupancy for the building
Residential properties are not eligible
Non-profits are not eligible except those selling goods/services to the public
New construction built within the last 3 years is not eligible
Properties actively listed for sale are not eligible
If final project cost is less than original estimate, grant award will be reduced proportionally
Grant recipients must maintain all improvements for 5 years post-grant
Application requires W-9, two current photos, conceptual drawings, and two contractor estimates
Closeout requires two after photos, all contractor payment receipts/invoices, and a signed Reimbursement Request Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application through the BDC website by entering contact information; the application will be emailed to you. Meet with a BDC economic development officer at the project site prior to submitting the application. Submit the completed application for approval before beginning any work. After project completion, submit documentation (after photos, contractor payment receipts/invoices, and signed Reimbursement Request Form) for reimbursement. For questions, contact the agency by email or phone.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers an 80% personal property tax credit for 10 years to grocery stores that open new locations or make significant renovations in targeted food desert areas of the city. The credit aims to increase access to healthy food and spur economic development in underserved neighborhoods. New stores must meet minimum investment thresholds, and all qualifying stores must dedicate space to fresh produce and other perishable goods.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year, 80% credit against personal property tax (which typically covers furniture, fixtures, and equipment) for qualifying grocery stores. New stores must invest at least $150,000 or $25 per square foot in new personal property. Renovated stores must invest varying minimums based on floor space: at least $5/sq ft for stores 20,000 sq ft or less; at least $8/sq ft for stores between 20,001–45,000 sq ft; and at least $10/sq ft for stores over 45,000 sq ft.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial application must be received by October 1 to be considered for the credit in the tax year beginning January 1 of the next calendar year. Annual continuing eligibility form must be received by November 30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grocery stores locating in or making significant renovations within designated grocery store incentive areas in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit reduces personal property tax owed on furniture, fixtures, and equipment for qualifying grocery stores.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The store must be located within the designated grocery store incentive area in Baltimore City. Applicants can check eligibility by entering an address in the CityView portal at cityview.baltimorecity.gov.
requirements_list: Must be located in the grocery store incentive area
For new stores: must invest at least $150,000 or $25 per square foot in new personal property
For renovated stores with 20,000 sq ft or less: must invest at least $5 per square foot
For renovated stores between 20,001–45,000 sq ft: must invest at least $8 per square foot
For renovated stores over 45,000 sq ft: must invest at least $10 per square foot
Must have at least 500 sq ft dedicated to the sale of fruits and vegetables
Must have at least 500 sq ft dedicated to the sale of other perishable goods including meat, seafood, and dairy products
Must operate produce, meat, seafood, dairy, and canned/packaged goods departments
More than 50% of sales must come from food
More than 50% of floor space must be dedicated to food
Must be in compliance with Baltimore City Health Article, Building and Fire codes
Must be current on all City taxes and fees
Existing stores requesting renovation credit must submit 1-year sales data (food vs. non-food breakdown)
Pre-qualification expires in 24 months from date granted for planned new construction projects, and 180 days from date of issue for all others
Pre-qualification letter and invoices/receipts documenting personal property spending required for initial application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the pre-qualification form (fillable PDF, printed and signed in blue ink, scanned and emailed to info@baltimoredevelopment.com); allow 30 days for processing. Existing stores requesting renovation credit must submit 1-year sales data. 2. Once pre-qualified, proceed with construction or renovation. After completion, submit the initial application form (with pre-qualification letter and invoices/receipts) by October 1 to tax.credits@baltimorecity.gov to request verification; allow 60 days for processing. 3. Each year during the 10-year credit period, submit the continuing eligibility form by November 30 of the prior year to info@baltimoredevelopment.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal capital gains tax incentives are available to private investors who finance real estate, infrastructure, or businesses located in designated Opportunity Zone census tracts. Baltimore City has 42 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts. The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) connects investors and project sponsors with Opportunity Zone resources, co-investors, and state tax credit enhancements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal capital gains tax incentives for investors who place capital gains into Qualified Opportunity Funds that invest in designated Opportunity Zone census tracts. BDC also helps connect investors with co-investors such as the Neighborhood Impact Investment Fund and state-level Opportunity Zone Enhancement Credits from the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private impact investors, Qualified Opportunity Funds, and project sponsors looking to invest in designated Opportunity Zone census tracts in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in real estate, infrastructure, or businesses located in designated Opportunity Zone census tracts in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 42 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Investment must be made through a Qualified Opportunity Fund
Investment must be directed to a designated Opportunity Zone census tract in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BDC at info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com for more information on partnering and accessing Opportunity Zone resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Spaces Grant (OSG), administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC), helps businesses in Baltimore City offset the cost of installing outdoor seating, parklets, landscaping, lighting, and other features that expand a business's use of outdoor space. OSG projects activate public areas, encourage community interaction, and contribute to vibrant street life in Baltimore neighborhoods. The program offers a reimbursement-based grant of up to $5,000; businesses must provide matching funds and pay for the entire project upfront before receiving reimbursement upon proof of completion and payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based matching grant of up to $5,000 to offset costs of outdoor improvements. Applicants must provide matching funds (1:1 match required) and pay all project costs upfront before receiving reimbursement. Eligible applicants include for-profit businesses and nonprofits with signed leases or commercial property ownership, community groups and nonprofits without commercial leases (with a signed MOU from the property owner), and vacant property owners (reimbursement held until a lease is signed, occupancy permit issued, and property is occupied). Award amounts and terms are detailed in the OSG Terms & Conditions (effective June 27, 2025, last updated November 25, 2025). Awards depend on available funding and are made at BDC's sole discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners, property owners, nonprofits, and community groups in Baltimore City seeking to install or expand outdoor spaces for their commercial or community properties. Includes for-profit businesses and nonprofits with signed leases or commercial property ownership, community groups/nonprofits without commercial leases (with MOU), and vacant property owners (conditional). Ineligible: residential properties, new construction (buildings less than 3 years old), properties actively listed for sale, properties that received OSG in the prior 12 months, and applicants not maintaining prior improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outdoor seating (cafe tables and chairs, benches), parklets, curbside facilities, shade structures, outdoor lighting, planters, plants and landscaping (limited to 25% of total grant amount), mobile vending structures, and other features that expand a business's use of outdoor space. Ineligible uses include outdoor heaters, tents/enclosures, barriers, murals, parklet signage, sound amplification equipment (speakers/TVs), roof decks, cable spools, and permit fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available citywide in Baltimore City. Eligible project locations include sidewalk space, adjacent parking spaces, private outdoor seating areas, and community spaces open to the public.
requirements_list: Grants must be approved before work begins
Work completed prior to application approval is NOT eligible for reimbursement
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application
Applicant must provide matching funds (1:1 match required)
Applicant must pay for all project costs before receiving reimbursement
Project construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter
Applicant must be in good legal standing with federal, state, and local authorities
For projects in the public right-of-way, a Curbside Commercial Permit or Minor Privilege Permit is required
For community-led projects, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is required
Applicants must obtain two quotes for work done by third-party contractors
The cost of architectural or design services cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost
The cost of plants and landscaping is limited to 25% of the total grant amount
The grant recipient must maintain the improvements for three years
Vacant property owners must have a lease signed, occupancy permit issued, and property occupied before reimbursement is released
Residential properties are not eligible
Buildings less than 3 years old (new construction) are not eligible
Properties actively listed for sale are not eligible
Properties that received an OSG award within the prior 12 months are not eligible
Applicants who are not maintaining previously funded OSG improvements are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the request form on the BDC website to receive an application (it will be emailed to you). Meet with a BDC representative at the project site. Gather required documents including a W-9 form, a sketch of your project, cost estimates, and any necessary permits or agreements. Submit the complete application package for approval before beginning work. After project completion, submit proof of completion and payment for reimbursement. Applications may be emailed to info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com or mailed to BDC. No application deadline is specified; the program accepts applications on a rolling basis subject to available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Housing Office of Rehabilitation helps low- and moderate-income homeowners with emergency repairs and home improvements. Programs include below-market-rate rehabilitation loans, emergency assistance for homeowners affected by emergency events, exterior facade grants for repairs approved by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation, accessibility-related improvements for seniors, and senior roof repair.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market-rate rehabilitation loans, emergency assistance grants, exterior facade grants, accessibility improvement assistance for seniors, and senior roof repair assistance. Specific amounts and terms are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income homeowners in Baltimore City, including seniors needing accessibility or roof repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency home repairs, below-market-rate rehabilitation, exterior facade repairs approved by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation, accessibility improvements, and roof repair for seniors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Applicant must be low- or moderate-income
Applicant must be a homeowner residing in the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Baltimore Housing Office of Rehabilitation website at baltimorehousing.org/ps_rehab.asp for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary recognition program that encourages businesses and other organizations in Montgomery County to reduce their ecological footprint. Participating businesses earn a Green Business Certification by taking steps to green their operations and transition to a sustainable future. The program is managed by Bethesda Green, a local nonprofit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses that complete the certification process earn Green Business Certification, a public recognition indicating participation in sustainable business practices. The program provides guidance and a certification credential, not direct financial assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations in Montgomery County seeking to reduce their ecological footprint and demonstrate environmental leadership.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a certification/recognition program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and organizations operating in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit Bethesda Green's website at bethesdagreen.org to start the Green Business Certification journey.

structured_extraction.program_description: BioHealth Innovation, Inc. (BHI), in partnership with Montgomery County, Maryland, hires one or more seasoned life sciences professionals as Executives-in-Residence to provide business counseling and technical assistance to local start-up and growth-stage biohealth companies. The role involves helping companies commercialize diagnostics, medical devices, digital health, bioinformatics, AI/machine learning, and therapeutics technologies over a 6–12 month contract period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Contract position (without benefits) for one or more Executives-in-Residence to provide business counseling, technical assistance, customer discovery support, regulatory plan development, market assessment, and non-dilutive funding guidance to Montgomery County biohealth startups. Total contract amount will not exceed $135,000 for all contractors. Contract duration is typically 6–12 months, ideally starting in the last quarter of 2022.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sarah Miller, Vice President of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seasoned life sciences professionals with startup, investing, or fundraising experience interested in a contract role mentoring and advising Montgomery County biohealth companies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) Program attracts private investment into low-income communities by allowing individual and corporate investors to receive a federal income tax credit equal to 39% of their equity investment in certified Community Development Entities (CDEs). CDEs then deploy that capital into businesses and projects in distressed, low-income census tracts. The program aims to break cycles of disinvestment by funding commercial real estate, manufacturing facilities, and access to education and healthcare in underserved areas.
structured_extraction.agency: CDFI Fund (Community Development Financial Institutions Fund)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive a federal income tax credit totaling 39% of their original equity investment in a certified Community Development Entity (CDE), claimed over a seven-year period. CDEs must apply to the CDFI Fund for allocation authority through an annual competition. Businesses and projects in low-income communities access capital by contacting CDEs directly — they do not apply to the CDFI Fund. As of FY 2023, the program has generated $8 in private investment for every $1 of federal funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual CDE allocation competition; investors can claim credit anytime through allocated CDEs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual and corporate investors seeking a federal tax credit, and certified Community Development Entities (CDEs) applying for tax credit allocation authority to channel capital into low-income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investments in Community Development Entities, which then deploy capital into businesses and real estate projects in low-income census tracts — including commercial real estate, manufacturing facilities, education, and healthcare.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Investments must be made in NMTC-eligible low-income census tracts. CDEs may serve communities nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants for allocation authority must be certified as Community Development Entities (CDEs) by the CDFI Fund
Investments must be directed to low-income community census tracts as defined by the IRS
Businesses seeking NMTC-enhanced financing should contact CDEs directly rather than applying to the CDFI Fund
Investors must make qualified equity investments (QEIs) in certified CDEs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Obtain CDE Certification from the CDFI Fund. Step 2: Submit an application during the annual allocation competition (opening date, deadline, and announcement date published each cycle). Step 3: Await award announcement. Step 4: Execute allocation agreement. Step 5: Comply with ongoing reporting requirements. Businesses seeking financing should locate a CDE serving their area using the NMTC Awardee States Served map.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resident Business Percentage Preference Program (RBP3) gives Calvert County-based businesses a competitive advantage when bidding on county procurement contracts. Eligible resident businesses receive a 5% deduction on their bid price for informal solicitations (contracts valued between $10,000 and $29,999.99) and a 5% preference up to a maximum of $25,000 on formal solicitations (contracts valued at $30,000 or more). The program applies to goods and services purchased through formal and informal county solicitation processes. The program is authorized by Maryland state legislation (Ch. 683, HB 835, effective October 1, 2024), which enables Calvert County to adopt a local preference ordinance for resident businesses in procurement competitions. Note: The state legislation is enabling legislation only; the specific preference percentage and implementation details are set by Calvert County ordinance, which the County Commissioners are authorized but not required to enact.
structured_extraction.agency: Calvert County Department of Finance & Budget, Procurement Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible resident businesses receive a percentage bid preference on their quoted price. For informal solicitations ($10,000–$29,999.99), a 5% deduction applies. For formal solicitations ($30,000 and over), the 5% preference is capped at $25,000. If the lowest bidder is a non-resident business and a resident business is also bidding, the resident business may be selected at the lower adjusted price. The specific preference percentage is set by Calvert County ordinance, as authorized by state law (Ch. 683, HB 835, effective October 1, 2024). The program does not apply to federally or state-mandated contracts, cooperative purchasing agreements, or emergency purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with their principal office located in Calvert County that are bidding on Calvert County government procurement contracts for goods and services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bid price reduction/preference when competing for Calvert County government procurement contracts. This is a procurement preference mechanism, not a grant or direct funding program — it provides a competitive bidding advantage rather than distributing funds to applicants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal office located in Calvert County, Maryland. A P.O. box cannot be used to establish a local or principal address. Businesses with their principal office outside Calvert County are classified as nonresident businesses and do not qualify for the preference.
requirements_list: Business must have its principal office located in Calvert County (resident business); a P.O. box cannot be used to establish a local or principal address.
Must submit a responsive bid or offer in the applicable procurement solicitation.
Bid must not exceed the lowest nonresident bid by more than the specified percentage (to be defined by County ordinance).
Program applies to informal solicitations valued between $10,000 and $29,999.99 and formal solicitations valued at $30,000 or more.
Does not apply where federal or state law mandates otherwise (including grants).
Does not apply to contracts awarded through cooperative agreements or emergency purchases.
Does not apply when piggybacking on another jurisdiction's competitively bid contracts.
The program is authorized by state legislation (Ch. 683, HB 835, effective October 1, 2024); the specific preference percentage and implementation details are set by Calvert County ordinance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must participate in the county's standard procurement bidding process (RFI, RFQ, RFP, or ITB). If a resident business is not the lowest bidder, the Procurement Office applies the preference percentage to determine if the resident business can be selected. If the resident business declines the preference award, the contract proceeds to the next eligible bidder.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural Land Preservation Program – Purchase and Retirement (PAR) Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Purchase and Retirement (PAR) Fund allows Agricultural Preservation District (APD) landowners in Calvert County to sell their Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) to the county, which then retires those rights permanently. Unlike a market sale, the TDRs are not reused — they are removed, reducing overall development density. The county uses a competitive ranking process to prioritize applications until available funds are exhausted.
structured_extraction.agency: Calvert County Department of Planning & Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County purchases TDRs from eligible APD owners at $6,230 per TDR. Applications are ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB), and offer letters are sent until funding is exhausted. The purchased TDRs are retired, permanently reducing development density rather than moving it.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2026 deadline was extended to December 12, 2025 at 4:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Agricultural Preservation District (APD) land in Calvert County who want to sell and permanently retire TDRs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds paid to APD landowners in exchange for permanently retiring development rights on their agricultural or forest land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Calvert County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible Agricultural Preservation District (APD) owner
Applications ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB)
Offers made until available funding is exhausted
Applications accepted September through December
Transactions conclude in June
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the PAR application form. Submit between September and December. The APAB reviews applications (December–January), makes offers (January–February), and transactions conclude in June.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural Land Preservation Program – Transferable Development Rights (TDR) Reserve Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The TDR Reserve Program lets landowners sell their Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) to Calvert County and lets developers purchase TDRs from the county, instead of negotiating directly with each other. The county operates it as a revolving fund, buying TDRs from Agricultural Preservation District (APD) owners and selling them to developers. This helps preserve farmland and forests while allowing higher-density development in designated growth areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Calvert County Department of Planning & Zoning
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county purchases TDRs from eligible APD owners at $6,230 per TDR on a first-come, first-served basis. There is an additional 1% administrative fee. Owners of record of TDRs already conveyed from the original APD are also eligible to apply. Developers can also purchase TDRs from the Reserve at the price the county paid plus the 1% administrative fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Agricultural Preservation District (APD) land in Calvert County who want to sell TDRs, and developers who want to purchase TDRs to increase density on receiving-area parcels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from TDR sales go to APD landowners in exchange for permanently restricting development on their land. TDR purchases allow developers to increase density on designated growth-area properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Calvert County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be an owner of an Agricultural Preservation District (APD) to sell TDRs to the Reserve
Owners of record of TDRs already conveyed from the original APD are also eligible to sell
Availability subject to funding and TDR supply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the fillable application form to sell or purchase TDRs. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis as funding and supply allow.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County offers free native trees and planting services to property owners in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area who want to replant trees on their land. The program uses fees collected from landowners who cannot replant forest cover onsite to fund tree planting at approved sites, helping the County maintain 100% of existing forest cover within the Critical Area as required by state mandate. Property owners apply to the Critical Area Reforestation Evaluation (CARE) Committee for free trees and planting assistance. Only species listed on the Calvert County Native Plant List for this program are available, and species availability varies year to year. The program cannot be used to satisfy mitigation requirements for any project, permit, or violation.
structured_extraction.agency: Calvert County Department of Planning & Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free native trees and planting services are provided to eligible property owners in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (land within 1,000 feet of the Mean High Water Line of tidal waters or the landward edge of tidal wetlands). Only species listed on the Calvert County Native Plant List for this program are available, and species availability varies year to year. The program cannot be used to satisfy mitigation requirements for any project, permit, or violation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: CARE meetings are held in January and June
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with land in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area in Calvert County who want to replant trees on their property.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) Grants for Residents
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County's Division of Emergency Management helps eligible homeowners apply for federal Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) grants to reduce risk from natural hazards. Grants cover up to 75% of eligible project costs; homeowners are responsible for the remaining 25% and any cost overruns. Currently, the Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) program is available for flood-related projects. The Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program, which funded cliff house mitigation, was ended by FEMA on April 4, 2025 and is no longer available.
structured_extraction.agency: Calvert County Division of Emergency Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of project costs for eligible hazard mitigation projects. Currently, flood mitigation assistance (elevation of structures above base flood elevation, or acquisition and demolition of flood-prone properties) is available. Cliff house mitigation funding through BRIC is no longer available. Homeowners bear the remaining 25% of costs plus any cost overruns.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: NLT July 1st for pre-screening questionnaire; August 31st for final application materials
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County homeowners with high-hazard properties, particularly those in flood plains with NFIP insurance, and NFIP Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and demolition of high-risk properties (returning land to natural state), or elevation of flood-prone structures above the base flood elevation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be a high-hazard property eligible for hazard mitigation assistance

For acquisition and demolition: property appraisal, plat survey, color photos, and itemized demolition cost estimate required; flood projects also require NFIP insurance copy and documentation of past flood events

For elevation (flood only): plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance policy documentation, documentation of past flood events, elevation certificate, certified structural stability letter from engineer, and itemized elevation cost estimate
Homeowner must contribute 25% of project costs and cover any cost overruns
Applications must be submitted by August 31st deadline; pre-screening questionnaire must be submitted by July 1st
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and submit the Pre-Screening Questionnaire by July 1st at forms.office.com/g/xYtNgB6Ke3. 2. CCDEM contacts the resident with additional information. 3. Submit all application materials to CCDEM by August 31st. 4. CCDEM develops and submits subapplications for initial review in mid-November. 5. Final subapplications submitted to FEMA in late January. 6. FEMA releases funding decisions in late summer. 7. Funding allocated to states and project kicks off in mid-spring.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Calvert County Environmental Commission runs an annual contest that rewards residents who pump out their septic tank or upgrade to a nitrogen-removing tank. Participants who submit a paid receipt by the deadline are entered into a drawing to win a cash reimbursement or other prizes. The contest supports Chesapeake Bay water quality by reducing septic-related pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Winners receive a cash reimbursement or other prizes selected through a drawing held at the January meeting of the Environmental Commission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First Wednesday of January by 4 p.m.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of costs associated with septic tank pump-out or upgrade to a nitrogen-removing tank
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Upgrade to a nitrogen-removing tank with a Bay Restoration Fund Grant, OR hire a company to pump out your septic tank
Submit the online entry form with a copy of the paid bill/receipt
Entries must be received by the Department of Planning & Zoning no later than 4 p.m. on the first Wednesday of January
Consent to release of name if you win
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Pump out your septic tank or upgrade to a nitrogen-removing tank. 2. Submit the online form and upload a copy of your paid receipt. 3. Submit by 4 p.m. on the first Wednesday of January. Winners are selected by drawing at the January Environmental Commission meeting and notified by letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free prescription drug discount card program offered jointly by Calvert County Government and the National Association of Counties (NACo). No enrollment form or membership fee is required, and there are no restrictions on how often the card can be used.

Cardholders pay the negotiated discount price or the pharmacy's retail price, whichever is lower. Discounts may be higher for a three-month supply of some medications via mail service. Pet prescriptions are also eligible at participating retail pharmacies. Only one card per family is needed.

Must show proof of residency
No enrollment form required
No membership fee
No restrictions on frequency of use

structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult family members or informal caregivers age 18+ caring for individuals 60+; caregivers of any age caring for individuals with Alzheimer's disease; grandparents or relatives age 55+ caring for children under 18 or adults 18-59 with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Investment Note® is a fixed-income security issued by Calvert Impact Capital that allows individuals and institutions to invest as little as $20 to finance solutions addressing climate change and inequality. Proceeds are deployed across nine impact sectors — including affordable housing, healthcare, education, clean energy, and small business finance — in the US and over 100 countries. The Note offers fixed interest rates (3.00% for 1-year, 3.50% for 3-year, and 4.50% for 5-year terms) and has a 30-year track record of 100% repayment of principal and interest since 1995. No fees — investor dollars are not used to pay sales commissions or Calvert Impact Capital expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors purchase a fixed-income debt security with a minimum of $20 (online or mail) or $1,000 (brokerage). Current interest rates are 3.00% for 1-year, 3.50% for 3-year, and 4.50% for 5-year terms. No fees — investor dollars are not used to pay sales commissions or Calvert Impact Capital expenses. Available through an online platform, direct mail with check, or through brokerage accounts using CUSIP numbers. Brokerage orders must be placed before CUSIPs trade at Noon EST on 5/29/2026; settlement date is 6/3/2026. As of December 31, 2025, aggregate principal outstanding was $612,299,225 (below the $750M cap at which issuance would pause). Not FDIC or SIPC insured; investment subject to risk of loss.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; brokerage orders must be placed before CUSIPs trade at Noon EST on 5/29/2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: US retail and institutional investors (individuals, nonprofits, and for-profit institutions) seeking fixed-income impact investments starting at $20. Tennessee residents must have gross annual income ≥$70,000 AND net worth ≥$70,000 (or net worth ≥$250,000) and may not invest more than 10% of net worth. Washington residents may not invest more than 10% of joint net worth (excluding primary residence, furnishings, and automobiles). Pennsylvania residents have a two-day right of refusal post-investment. Arkansas residents may only purchase through brokerage accounts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital is invested by Calvert Impact Capital into partners working on affordable housing, community development, education, environmental sustainability, gender equity, health, microfinance, renewable energy, small business, and sustainable agriculture across the US and globally.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to US retail and institutional investors in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and the US Virgin Islands where the Note is authorized for sale. Arkansas residents may only purchase through brokerage accounts. State-specific requirements apply in Tennessee, Washington, and Pennsylvania.
requirements_list: Minimum investment of $20 for online or mail purchase
Minimum investment of $1,000 for brokerage purchase
Must be a US investor in a state where the Note is authorized for sale
Brokerage investors must provide the applicable CUSIP number to their brokerage's fixed income desk
Not FDIC or SIPC insured; investment subject to risk of loss
Tennessee residents: gross annual income ≥$70,000 AND net worth ≥$70,000, OR net worth ≥$250,000; investment may not exceed 10% of personal net worth
Washington residents: investment may not exceed 10% of personal/joint net worth (excluding primary residence, furnishings, and automobiles)
Pennsylvania residents: two-day right of refusal after investing
USA Patriot Act compliance required (name, address, date of birth, SSN verification)
Read prospectus before investing
SSN/TIN must be provided under penalty of perjury (or face 28% backup withholding and account closure)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Online: Create an account at invest.calvertimpactcapital.org, link a bank account, and purchase the Note. By mail: Complete and mail the application form with a check for $20 or more to Calvert Impact Capital, 7550 Wisconsin Avenue, 8th Floor, Bethesda, MD 20814. By brokerage: Provide the applicable CUSIP number to your brokerage's fixed income desk before the listed trading deadline (Noon EST on 5/29/2026); settlement date is 6/3/2026. After brokerage purchase, register your Note with Calvert Impact Capital to receive impact reporting. Payment accepted by check, bank wire, or ACH.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative (group) purchase program that makes it easy for homeowners and small business owners to install rooftop solar systems. By pooling participants, the co-op negotiates group pricing — typically about 20% below the going market rate. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are also available. Joining the contact list does not commit you to purchase; after roof evaluations, each member receives an individual proposal and decides whether to sign a contract.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to residents and small businesses in the Capital Area (Rockville, MD area)

For those not already receiving the state credit, a one-time county form filing is required. Once the county form is filed, no annual re-filing is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program operated by Caroline County Economic Development that provides financing to small businesses located in Caroline County, Maryland. Loans are primarily used for working capital that traditional lenders cannot finance, as well as other business purposes described by the applicant. The maximum loan amount is $20,000, though most loans are for less than $10,000. Interest rate is prime rate plus 1%, at the discretion of the CCED Loan Committee. Loan term is 5–7 years based on risk. Loan amount and repayment term are determined by the application. All funds must be repaid according to agreed terms — this is a loan, not a grant. Loans must be secured by collateral, and repayment is required regardless of business standing, including if the business relocates outside Caroline County. Applicants must have a personal credit score of 600 or above, must be in good standing with Maryland SDAT and the Caroline County Tax Office, and must demonstrate that traditional financing sources were attempted first. Only one active Caroline County Small Business Loan is permitted per business owner. Loans are reviewed by Caroline County Economic Development and Finance Office staff, who make recommendations to the County Commissioners for final approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $20,000 (most loans are for less than $10,000); exceptions may apply for large job-creation projects. Interest rate is prime rate + 1%, at the discretion of the CCED Loan Committee. Loan term is 5–7 years based on risk. Loan amount and repayment term are determined by the application (applicant specifies loan amount and number of months requested). Loan must be secured by collateral. Funds are generally used for working capital that cannot be financed through traditional lenders, or other business purposes as described by the applicant. Cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, or pay delinquent taxes. Resubmitted applications require a $25 application fee. Loan repayment is required regardless of business standing and if the business moves outside Caroline County.

Applicants must have a personal credit score of 600 or above, must be in good standing with Maryland SDAT and the Caroline County Tax Office, and must demonstrate that traditional financing sources were attempted first.

Funds are disbursed after all loan documents are signed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Manufacturing companies in Caroline County can receive a local real property tax credit for expanding or building new facilities. The credit equals 100% of the real property tax attributable to the increased assessable value resulting from facility expansion or new construction, and may be claimed for up to five consecutive years. The business must recertify its eligibility each year between May 1 and October 1. Eligibility requires a minimum $50,000 increase in assessed value from the expansion project and the creation of at least 15 new full-time jobs related to the expansion. New employees must receive at least the federal minimum wage, and the employer must provide a basic employee benefit plan including medical insurance, leave, and a pension. The credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal taxes, and applies to property first placed on the County tax roll on or after July 1, 1990. The program encourages business expansion and development to improve the local economy.

The credit lasts for five consecutive years, with annual recertification required between May 1 and October 1 each year (failure to recertify results in immediate credit cessation). Requires a minimum $50,000 increase in assessed value and the creation of at least 15 new full-time jobs tied to the expansion. The credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal taxes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The North County Enterprise Zone (NCEZ) covers most commercial and industrial property in the towns of Ridgely, Greensboro, and Goldsboro in Caroline County. Eligible businesses can receive two types of tax credits: (1) a one-time $1,000 Maryland income tax credit per new qualified employee (minimum 5 new positions), and (2) a ten-year real property tax credit on the incremental increased assessed value from improvements or expansion (minimum $100,000 investment). The property tax credit is 80% for the first five years, then decreases by 10% each year (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) for the next five years. Applicants can reapply for certification annually.

Minimum $100,000 investment required for the property tax credit; application must be submitted before project completion and before User/Occupancy Permits are issued. Applicants can reapply for certification annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Edge: The Caroline County Business Academy
structured_extraction.program_description: A free 8-week business training and education program for small business owners and entrepreneurs in Caroline County, Maryland. Led by Will Holmes Consulting, the program covers building sustainable organizational infrastructure, leadership and growth planning, marketing and sales (B2G, B2B, B2C), accounting, human resources, legal and tax matters, financial management, and preparing to access capital. Participants meet via Zoom on Tuesday evenings (6–9 p.m.) and work one-on-one with business mentors. Graduates develop financial reports, a growth budget, and a plan to attract clients and access capital, and receive a Certificate of Completion. The program particularly welcomes small, minority, and women-owned businesses. It is funded through a partnership with the Mid-Shore Regional Council (MSRC) using a grant from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF), administered by the Rural Maryland Council (RMC). Space is limited to 15 participants per cohort.

Graduates develop financial reports, a growth budget, and a plan to attract clients and access capital, and receive a Certificate of Completion. Space is limited to 15 participants. structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County offers a Job Creation Tax Credit against County property taxes to encourage businesses to create new jobs. Businesses that construct or expand a facility by at least 5,000 square feet and hire at least 25 new full-time employees within the first 24 months may qualify for the credit. New positions must be new to the state and pay at least 125% of the Average Weekly Wage as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor. The credit amount decreases over six years: 52% of the increased property tax in years one and two, 39% in years three and four, and 26% in years five and six. The credit applies to county property taxes on the business's new or expanded real estate and personal property. The business must be located in a designated Priority Funding Area within Carroll County. The county's economic development team provides guidance on program requirements and assists eligible businesses with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Agricultural Land Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Carroll County Agricultural Land Preservation Program pays landowners who voluntarily place a permanent conservation easement on their property to protect productive agricultural land from non-agricultural development. Landowners retire the non-agricultural development potential of their land while retaining fee simple title and continuing to farm. Easements are legally binding on the land and all future owners in perpetuity. Some easements are also obtained through donation, county code requirements, or transfer of development rights. The program has operated since 1980 and is the most successful in Maryland, having preserved over 81,426 acres across more than 781 farms as of October 2025, with a goal of preserving at least 100,000 acres. The county has invested over $267 million since 1980. The program administers four tracks: the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Program, the Carroll County Easement Purchase Program, the Rural Legacy Program, and the Critical Farms Program (MALPF). Owners apply using a single application that can be considered under multiple program tracks. Payment may be structured as an Installment Purchase Agreement (IPA), which provides interest payments to the landowner over time until maturity. The program also accepts donated easements to conservation organizations or directly to the county. Applications are ranked to prioritize available funding, with properties in the Priority Preservation Area (northwest Carroll County) and Rural Legacy Area ranked higher. Applications are accepted year-round, though they may be held until a new cycle or fiscal year begins. Properties within a Rural Legacy Area may be considered immediately if grant funding is available.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Planning & Land Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Carroll County purchases permanent conservation easements from landowners, compensating them for retiring development rights on their farmland. The county has invested over $267 million since 1980. Payment options include a lump-sum (up to 70% of appraised fair market value) or an Installment Purchase Agreement (IPA, at 40% of appraised fair market value), which provides interest payments to the landowner over time until maturity. The easement is recorded in Carroll County Land Records and restricts development in perpetuity, binding future owners. Multiple program tracks are available: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), Rural Legacy, Carroll County Easement Purchase, and Critical Farms. One application covers all tracks; funding availability and cycle timing may vary by track. The program also accepts donated easements to conservation organizations or directly to the county. Properties within a Rural Legacy Area may be considered immediately if grant funding is available; other applications may be held until a new cycle or fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners and farm owners in Carroll County seeking to preserve productive farmland from non-agricultural development while continuing to farm.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation to landowners for placing a permanent agricultural conservation easement on their property, restricting it to agricultural uses and preventing non-agricultural development in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. Properties must be located outside a Designated Growth Area. Properties within the Priority Preservation Area (northwest Carroll County) or Rural Legacy Area receive higher ranking. Properties within a Rural Legacy Area may be considered immediately if grant funding is available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certification of Local Agricultural Preservation Programs (CLAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County participates in the Certification of Local Agricultural Preservation Programs (CLAPP) process under the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Certified counties retain 75% of their locally generated agricultural transfer tax revenue for farmland preservation, compared to 33% for non-certified counties. To qualify, counties must designate Priority Preservation Areas (PPAs) in their comprehensive plans and focus preservation efforts on large contiguous blocks of agricultural and forested land. Carroll County's certification is renewed every five years.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Planning & Land Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified counties retain 75% of their locally generated agricultural transfer tax revenue for qualifying land preservation expenditures, compared to 33% for non-certified counties. Retained revenue must be spent or encumbered within three years of collection or it reverts to MALPF.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments seeking certification to retain a larger share of agricultural transfer tax revenue for local farmland preservation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualifying land preservation expenditures, focused on preserving large contiguous blocks of agricultural and forested land within designated Priority Preservation Areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. The CLAPP framework applies to charter counties statewide; counties must designate Priority Preservation Areas meeting criteria under Agriculture Article § 2-518, with at least 80% of remaining undeveloped land within the PPA.

County must manage PPAs according to criteria set by the Agricultural Stewardship Act of 2006

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A county may apply to the Maryland Department of Planning and the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation jointly for certification of its Priority Preservation Area. The county must have an agricultural preservation advisory board and governing body approval. The Department and Foundation jointly certify PPAs and report on the certification program annually by January 15. Contact Carroll County Ag Pres Program staff for more information.

The county matches both volunteer labor hours and cash contributions from the requesting organization.

County funding is capped at 85% of projects up to $25,000; costs above $25,000 are the requesting organization's responsibility. All funds are administered through the Department of Recreation and Parks.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County's Division of Aging & Disabilities administers three Medicaid-funded programs — Community Options Waiver (CO), Community First Choice (CFC), and Community Personal Assistance Service (CPAS) — that help eligible individuals with disabilities or chronic conditions live in the community rather than a nursing facility. Services include personal assistance, nurse monitoring, assistive technology, home-delivered meals, environmental accessibility adaptations, and more.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded community-based services provided to eligible individuals in lieu of nursing facility care. Services vary by program: CO Waiver covers assisted living (Level 2 or 3), personal assistance, nurse monitoring, support planning, environmental adaptations, assistive technology, behavior consultation, respite care, personal emergency response system, home-delivered meals, family/consumer training, medical adult daycare, senior center plus, and transition services. CFC covers personal assistance, nurse monitoring, support planning, environmental assessment, environmental accessibility adaptations, assistive technology, home-delivered meals, and personal emergency response system. CPAS covers personal assistance services, nurse monitoring, and support planning services.
