structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County's Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program provides rental assistance to income-eligible households, helping them afford safe, decent housing in the private rental market. Eligible families and individuals with household incomes meeting HUD federal guidelines can apply to be placed on a waiting list. When selected, participants find housing that meets HUD's Housing Quality Standards, and the Housing Agency pays a portion of the rent directly to the landlord while the tenant pays the difference. Participants choose their own rental unit and may use portability options to move within or outside Carroll County or Maryland where an HCV Program exists. Current wait time is approximately 30–36 months for county residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Division of Housing & Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance vouchers that cover the difference between the tenant's required contribution and the actual rent. The Housing Agency enters into a contract with the landlord on behalf of the family. FY26 Payment Standards (effective November 1, 2025) range from $1,362 for an efficiency unit to $3,394 for a 6-bedroom unit. Eligibility is based on HUD income limits; extremely low, very low, and low income thresholds apply based on family size. Median Area Income is $130,300 (effective May 1, 2025). Under the portability option, families may use the voucher within or outside Maryland where an HCV Program exists.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible families and individuals (extremely low, very low, or low income) seeking affordable rental housing. Preference given to Carroll County residents and workers, then Maryland residents, then all others. Households experiencing homelessness must have been a resident in Carroll County for six months prior to becoming homeless.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance — voucher covers a portion of monthly rent for a privately-owned rental unit that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to households in Carroll County, Maryland. Preference given to those who reside or work in Carroll County, then Maryland residents, then all others. Portability allows use of voucher in other jurisdictions after requirements are met — contact a Housing Specialist for details.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a preliminary application online at waitlistcheck.com, in person, or by downloading and mailing the application to 10 Distillery Drive, Suite 101, Westminster, MD 21157 to be placed on the waiting list. structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County offers a tax credit to encourage property owners along the Finksburg MD 140 commercial corridor to visually enhance and redevelop their properties. The credit is intended to catalyze revitalization of this commercial area. For existing buildings, the credit is 75% if improvement costs exceed 25% of the assessed property value, or 50% if costs are 25% or less. For new construction, the credit is 50% if improvement costs for the building's exterior exceed 50% of the property's assessed value. The total credit cannot exceed the total cost of improvements, and credits may be available for up to five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit available for up to five years based on the percentage of improvement cost compared to the current assessed value of the property. For existing buildings, the credit is 75% if improvement costs exceed 25% of the assessed property value, or 50% if costs are 25% or less. For new construction, the credit is 50% if improvement costs for the building's exterior exceed 50% of the property's assessed value. The total credit cannot exceed the total cost of improvements. Only improvements that significantly improve the overall appearance of the property are eligible, including exterior façade, landscaping, signage, lighting, sidewalks, pedestrian plazas, and other exterior site improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial or industrial properties located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor in Finksburg, from the Carroll County line to Sandymount Road.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improvements to exterior façade (e.g., new windows, paint, new roof), landscaping, signage, lighting, sidewalks, pedestrian plazas, and other exterior site improvements that visually enhance the appearance of properties along the Maryland 140 commercial corridor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties zoned commercial or industrial located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor in Finksburg, from the Carroll County line to Sandymount Road, including properties that front MD 140 or are directly adjacent to a property that does.
requirements_list: Property must be used for business, commercial, or industrial purposes
Property must be located within a C-1, C-2, C-3, I-1, or I-2 commercial or industrial zone
Property must be located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor from the Carroll County line to Sandymount Road
Improvements must significantly improve the overall appearance of the property
Qualified improvements include exterior façade, landscaping, signage, lighting, sidewalks, and pedestrian plazas
You must apply before starting the improvement project
Application must be submitted on or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain the application form from the Department of the Comptroller. Complete and sign the application, including a tax map, property photos, a detailed description of planned improvements with drawings, and a summary of costs. Submit the complete application before beginning any work and by the May 1 deadline. Contact Paige Sunderland, Deputy Director / Business Development, at (410) 386-2314 or psunderland@carrollcountymd.gov for more information. Additional information and the governing ordinance are available at carrollbiz.org/financing-incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County's Broadband Grant Program provides matching reimbursement grants to internet service providers (ISPs) and Carroll County businesses that need broadband service in unserved or underserved areas of the county. The program supports expansion of the Carroll Broadband fiber optic network to reach more commercial and industrial customers, funded through the county's Fiber Network Enterprise Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% matching reimbursement of qualified project expenses, capped at $25,000 per approved project. A cap of $100,000 per entity or service provider per fiscal year applies, subject to allocations approved by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve unserved areas (below 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload) or underserved areas (below 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload from two or more providers) within Carroll County, MD.
requirements_list: Applicant must be in good business standing with federal, state, and local government authorities
ISPs must have legal authority to provide, construct, operate, and maintain proposed facilities or services
Business applicants must be based in Carroll County
Project must serve an unserved or underserved area of Carroll County, or provide internet redundancy for business continuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Carroll Broadband Grant Application and submit to the county along with the Project Detail form. A county committee reviews the application and applicants will be notified in writing of the approval or denial within two weeks of receipt. If approved, the applicant and the county will execute a Carroll Broadband Grant Agreement outlining the terms. Reimbursement requires invoices, vendor references, and check copies; project costs must be paid no later than 30 days after the project period ends. Contact Jay Uebel, Broadband Project Manager, at juebel@carrollcountymd.gov or 410-386-2309 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Finksburg Facade Improvement Program (FIP) provides matching grant funds to eligible property and business owners in the Finksburg Designated Sustainable Community to improve the appearance of building facades and signs. Goals include encouraging facade renovation, improving the appearance of the Finksburg Corridor, leveraging private investment, and preserving the economic vitality of commercial services. Funded by Maryland DHCD's Community Legacy Program and administered by Carroll County Government's Comprehensive Planning Division. Grants cover up to 80% of total facade renovation costs, with property owners contributing at least 20%. A greening incentive offers up to 100% reimbursement for projects that include approved greening or landscaping improvements visible from MD 140. Minimum grant is $500; maximum grant is $10,000. Grants are awarded on a rolling basis as funding permits, with remaining funding of $39,148. Work completed before the grant award is not eligible.

Grant awards depend on available funds, number of qualified applicants, and evaluation criteria. Work completed before the award is not eligible. This is a reimbursement program offered on a rolling basis as funding permits. Remaining funding: $39,148.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Portability program allows current HCV participants to transfer their housing rental subsidy when moving to a different area outside of Carroll County Housing's jurisdiction. Vouchers are valid anywhere in the U.S. or U.S. territories that has a Public Housing Authority (PHA) with an HCV program. The page explains how to port out of Carroll County to another PHA and how to port into Carroll County from another PHA.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A housing rental subsidy that can be transferred ('ported') to a new jurisdiction. The subsidy amount varies by Housing Authority based on payment standards, income limits, and bedroom size determinations. Assistance cannot begin in a new unit until the unit passes a HUD Housing Quality Standards inspection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Housing Choice Voucher participants who want to move into or out of Carroll County's jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing rental subsidy to help pay for an approved rental unit that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards.

requirements_list: Must be a current Housing Choice Voucher participant
To port out: rent portion and utilities must be up to date
If you do not live in Carroll County when issued your voucher, you must lease up in Carroll County for one year before porting out
Any money owed to a Housing Authority must be paid in full before using portability
Must continue to comply with current lease and provide required notice to landlord before moving
Must attend an eligibility meeting and voucher briefing at Carroll County Housing when porting in
Must submit a completed Request for Tenancy Approval from a landlord before the voucher expires
Selected unit must pass a HUD Housing Quality Standards inspection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To port out: Ask your Housing Specialist for a Request to Transfer form. To port in: Notify your current Housing Authority of your intent to port to Carroll County. Your current Housing Authority will process the required paperwork. Once approved, attend an eligibility meeting and voucher briefing at Carroll County Housing, submit a Request for Tenancy Approval completed by your new landlord, and wait for an inspection of the unit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chronic Disease Self-Management / Living Well Health Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: A series of free six-week workshops offered by Cecil County Department of Community Services in partnership with the Cecil County Health Department, designed to help adults with chronic health conditions and their caregivers manage their health. Programs meet once per week (approximately 2–2.5 hours per session) at community locations throughout Cecil County such as senior centers, churches, libraries, and hospitals. Workshop topics include managing fatigue, frustration, and pain; appropriate exercise; correct medication use; understanding the pain and symptom cycle; coping with difficult emotions; healthy eating; and working effectively with a healthcare team. The suite of programs — collectively known as 'Living Well' and based on Stanford University research — includes Living Well with Chronic Conditions (CDSMP), Living Well with Diabetes, Living Well with Chronic Pain, Living Well with Cancer: Thriving and Surviving, and a Hypertension program. Each participant in the CDSMP track receives a copy of 'Living a Healthy Life with Chronic Conditions' and a relaxation CD ('Relaxation for Mind and Body'). All programs are free of charge.

structured_extraction.program_name: Living Well Health Programs: Diabetes Self-Management (Cecil County & Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Free six-week workshop series programs offered by county health and community services departments for people with type 2 diabetes, pre-diabetes, or a diabetes diagnosis, and their family members, caregivers, and friends. The Cecil County program is offered by the Cecil County Department of Community Services in partnership with the Cecil County Health Department and is held in-person at community settings such as senior centers, churches, libraries, hospitals, and community centers throughout Cecil County. The Prince George's County program is offered online (virtually, Mondays 4:00 p.m.–6:30 p.m.) by the Prince George's County Department of Health. Both programs are based on Stanford University research. Weekly sessions (2.5 hours each) cover stress management, strength and endurance activities, communication and decision-making skills, healthy lifestyle development, nutrition, managing fatigue, pain, emotional challenges, medication use, and problem-solving with a health care team. Each participant receives a copy of 'Living a Healthy Life with Chronic Conditions.' Cecil County participants also receive a relaxation CD/audio tape ('Relaxation for Mind and Body'). Workshops are led by two trained volunteer leaders, often people living with the condition themselves. The Cecil County program is part of a broader Living Well Health Programs suite that also includes tracks for chronic conditions, chronic pain, cancer, and hypertension.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Department of Community Services / Prince George's County Department of Health
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free six-week self-management training program (once per week, 2.5 hours per session) provided at no cost to participants. structured_extraction.program_name: Route 40 Business Revitalization Program (including Special Blight Removal Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that helps businesses and organizations along the Route 40/Pulaski Highway corridor in Cecil County improve their exterior appearance and function. Funded by Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) revenues from Hollywood Casino in Perryville, the program offers two funding tracks: (1) a standard revitalization grant that reimburses eligible exterior improvement costs up to $25,000 per applicant, with a dollar-for-dollar match required; and (2) a special blight removal grant of up to $50,000 for projects that demolish or remove vacant, dilapidated, or blighted structures along the corridor, with no matching requirement. Both tracks disburse funds on a reimbursement basis after project completion. Up to 20% of standard grant funds may be used for related interior improvements with prior approval. Blight is defined as a vacant or dilapidated building that poses a safety or health risk to the community and likely requires demolition.

Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis after project completion. Up to 20% of standard grant funds may be used for related interior improvements with prior approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Elderly/Disabled Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil County's Elderly/Disabled Tax Deferral program allows eligible residential property owners who are elderly or permanently disabled to postpone payment of a portion of their annual County property taxes. Instead of paying the full amount, qualified homeowners defer the year-over-year increase in county taxes — the amount deferred equals the difference between the current year's County property taxes and the prior year's County property taxes, calculated after any Homestead Credit or Homeowner's Tax Credit is deducted. The total cumulative deferral may not exceed 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of initial application. No interest is charged on deferred amounts. The deferral applies only to the County portion of property taxes, not the state or municipal portions. Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property and must be repaid upon sale, change of ownership, death of the eligible owner (without an eligible surviving co-owner), tax sale, failure to reapply, loss of eligibility, or if income exceeds $60,000. Applicants must reapply each year to continue receiving the deferral. The program strongly encourages applicants to apply for the Homeowner's Tax Credit before applying for the deferral.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each year, the program defers the annual increase in Cecil County property taxes — specifically, the amount by which the current year's County taxes exceed the prior year's County taxes, calculated after any Homestead or Homeowner's Tax Credits are applied. The total cumulative deferral may not exceed 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of initial application. No interest is charged on deferred amounts. Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property and must be repaid upon sale, change of ownership, death of the owner (without an eligible surviving co-owner), tax sale, failure to reapply, loss of eligibility, income exceeding $60,000, or moving out. Applicants must continue to pay base property taxes to avoid tax sale. The deferral applies only to the County portion of property taxes, not state or municipal portions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applicants: September 1. Returning applicants: application by May 1 and signed Deferral Agreement by June 1 (to be included in July tax bill); in all cases no later than September 1.

Taxes are postponed, not forgiven, and must eventually be repaid. Applies only to the County portion of property taxes, not state or town portions, allowing qualifying homeowners to remain in their homes without paying the full tax increase each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil County offers real property tax credits for three distinct groups of qualifying residents: (1) Veteran homeowners — including active, retired, honorably discharged, or disabled veterans and surviving spouses — who own their primary residence in Cecil County, receiving a 20% credit on county property taxes applied to the first $400,000 of assessed value for dwellings valued at $800,000 or less with adjusted gross income under $150,000; (2) Sworn law enforcement officers employed by Cecil County who own and occupy their principal residence in Cecil County, receiving a property tax credit applied to the first $400,000 of assessed value for dwellings valued at $800,000 or less with annual household income under $150,000; and (3) Senior citizen homeowners in Cecil County who are 65 or older, meet income requirements (adjusted gross income under $150,000), have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 10 years, and own a dwelling assessed at $500,000 or less, receiving a 20% credit on county property taxes. Applications for all three programs are due by September 1 each year.

For senior citizens: a 20% credit on Cecil County property taxes for homeowners who are 65 or older, have adjusted gross income under $150,000, own a dwelling assessed at $500,000 or less, and have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 10 years. structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program – Section 8 (Cecil County)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program, also known as Section 8, is the federal government's main program to help very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities afford safe and decent housing in the private market. Administered by the Cecil County Housing Agency (Cecil County Division of Housing and Community Development), participants find their own housing — including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments — and the program pays a portion of their monthly rent directly to the landlord. Participating landlords receive monthly Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) directly from Cecil County, covering the difference between the tenant's share of rent and the agreed contract rent, up to the area's fair market rent. There is currently a multi-year waiting list (approximately 3 years for Cecil County residents).
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Housing Agency / Cecil County Division of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A rental subsidy paid on behalf of eligible families to private landlords. The subsidy covers a portion of the monthly rent; the family pays the remainder. Landlords receive monthly Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) directly from Cecil County, covering the difference between the tenant's share of rent and the agreed contract rent, up to the area's fair market rent. There is currently a multi-year waiting list (approximately 3 years for Cecil County residents).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities in Cecil County who need help affording rental housing in the private market; also rental property owners in Cecil County who want to rent to Housing Choice Voucher holders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidizes a portion of monthly rent for qualified housing units that meet HUD Housing Quality Standards and allowable rent limits. Monthly rental subsidy payments are also made to participating landlords on behalf of voucher-holding tenants, covering the difference between the tenant's share of rent and the agreed contract rent, up to the area's fair market rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Cecil County, Maryland residents. Preference is given first to Cecil County residents, then Maryland residents, then all others. Portability options allow voucher holders to move within or outside Maryland where HCV programs exist. Rental properties must be located in Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must meet federal income guidelines (very low income)
Must complete a preliminary application to be placed on the waiting list
Must find housing within 120 days that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards and allowable rent limits
Housing unit must pass agency inspection and lease must meet Voucher Program standards
Property must pass Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection
Property must meet all state and county codes, including health and safety requirements
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors must be present
Any household appliances present must be functional
Landlord must comply with Maryland Department of the Environment lead certification requirements
Rent must not exceed comparable units in the area (rent reasonableness test)
A Request for Lease Approval form must be submitted by the prospective tenant before inspection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For tenants: 1. Complete the preliminary application (download PDF, have it mailed, or drop it off at the County Administration Building). 2. Application is placed on the waiting list by date and time received. 3. When your name reaches the top of the list, an enrollment interview is scheduled to determine eligibility. 4. If eligible, attend a briefing session about how the program works. 5. Find qualifying housing within 120 days. 6. Negotiate lease terms with the landlord. 7. Housing Agency inspects the unit and reviews the lease. 8. Upon approval, the Housing Agency and landlord enter into a contract on behalf of the family. For landlords: List your property on AffordableHousing.com and contact the Housing office to notify them of the vacancy. A voucher holder will submit a Request for Lease Approval form. The Housing office will conduct an HQS inspection and negotiate rent if needed. Upon passing inspection, the Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contract is finalized and a lease is signed with the tenant.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Cecil Catalyst is a low-interest loan program operated by the Cecil County Office of Economic Development that provides funding to creditworthy small businesses and individuals in Cecil County who have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional lenders due to limited equity, insufficient collateral, or marginal cash flow. The program aims to promote job growth, new investment, business retention, and job creation, and supports both start-up and existing small businesses in Cecil County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $5,000 to $75,000 (the maximum may be increased by the Loan Review Committee with County Executive approval). The interest rate is the Prime Rate (as published in the Wall Street Journal on the date of application) plus 2%, fixed for up to 5 years. For loans exceeding 5 years, the rate resets on day one of month 61 (adjusting at month 59 based on the Prime Rate at that time plus 2%), starting with the 61st payment. Repayment terms vary by use: real estate (up to 10-year max with 20-year amortization and balloon payment at month 120), equipment (3–10 years depending on useful life), working capital (1 year interest-only with balloon payment at month 12, extendable up to 2 additional 1-year periods at committee discretion), and physical improvements to real property (up to 5 years). Loans may be secured or unsecured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion; a personal guaranty from all business principal(s)/owner(s) is required (except limited partners in a limited liability partnership). A one-time non-refundable $100 application fee is due at submission, plus all customary closing costs at settlement. Loan requests exceeding $75,000 must demonstrate a level of capitalization meeting loan underwriting standards for the type of loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (including start-ups), individuals, new investors, and existing businesses seeking retention support in Cecil County who cannot obtain traditional financing due to limited equity, collateral requirements, or marginal cash flow.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leasehold improvements, acquisition of real property (borrower must occupy at least 51% of improvements on the subject parcel), construction, renovation and rehabilitation, machinery and equipment, working capital (may include loan fees imposed by third-party lenders), business investment, expansion, retention, and job creation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and individuals operating in Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must demonstrate creditworthiness
Applicant must demonstrate an acceptable debt-to-income ratio showing ability to repay the loan in full
Applications reviewed by a qualified underwriter selected by the Loan Review Committee
Personal guaranty required from all business principal(s)/owner(s), except limited partners in a limited liability partnership
Loans may be unsecured or secured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion
Real property acquisitions require applicant to occupy at least 51% of improvements on the subject parcel
Loan requests exceeding $75,000 must demonstrate a level of capitalization meeting loan underwriting standards for the type of loan
$100 non-refundable application fee due at submission
All applicable closing costs due at settlement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact the Office of Economic Development at 410-996-6292 or by email to discuss your project. Step 2: Complete the application form (PDF) and submit it with required supporting documents by email to the Economic Development Manager. Step 3: The Loan Review Committee reviews the application package and underwriting decision, then approves or denies the loan. If approved, settlement is scheduled and repayment terms are set based on the approved use of funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Enterprise Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Enterprise Zone program provides real property tax credits and state income tax credits to businesses located within a designated Enterprise Zone in exchange for job creation and capital investment. Cecil County has Enterprise Zones covering 4,389 acres across nine business parks, with 17 designated zones shown on the program map. Businesses that locate or expand in a Cecil County Enterprise Zone may qualify for a 10-year real property tax credit on improvements and a one-time income tax credit per new employee hired.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tax credit types are available. (1) Real Property Tax Credit: a 10-year credit against local real property taxes on improvements. The credit is 80% in years one through five, then decreases by 10% per year, reaching 30% in year ten. (2) Income Tax Credit: a one-time $1,000 credit per new employee hired. For economically disadvantaged employees, the credit is $6,000 per employee paid over three years. Businesses must apply to the Office of Economic Development before completing construction or expansion — property tax credits are not granted retroactively.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating or expanding within a designated Cecil County Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied against local real property taxes on improvements and against state income tax liability for each new hire, tied to job creation and capital investments within Enterprise Zone boundaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within a designated Cecil County Enterprise Zone. The county has 17 enterprise zones covering 4,389 acres across nine business parks.
requirements_list: Business must be located within a designated Cecil County Enterprise Zone
Must create new jobs and/or make qualifying capital investments
Property tax credit application must be submitted before completing construction or expansion
Property tax credits are not granted retroactively
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email the Cecil County Office of Economic Development before completing any construction or expansion project to apply for the property tax credit. Complete the Enterprise Zone Certification Application (PDF available on the program page).

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program provides small grants to support the growth, diversification, and long-term sustainability of existing agricultural businesses in Cecil County, Maryland. Funding supports capital improvements, value-added production, agritourism infrastructure, strategic marketing, technology adoption, research, and other investments that strengthen the local agricultural economy. Grants are offered in three tiers: Seed Grants (up to $2,500), Growth Grants (up to $5,000), and Impact Grants ($7,500–$10,000). Total available funding is $74,666, provided through a partnership between the Upper Shore Regional Council and Cecil County Office of Economic Development. All awards are cost-reimbursable — awardees pay project expenses upfront and then submit receipts for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-reimbursable grants in three tiers: Seed Grants up to $2,500, Growth Grants up to $5,000, and Impact Grants from $7,500 to $10,000. Total available funding is $74,666. Awardees must pay project costs upfront and submit receipts and documentation by June 15, 2026 for reimbursement. All projects must be completed by May 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing agricultural businesses physically located in Cecil County, Maryland, including farms, producers, and agricultural enterprises engaged in crop production, livestock, greenhouse/nursery operations, value-added food production, agritourism, aquaculture, or timber/forestry operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production equipment and capital improvements, value-added processing and product development, agritourism and farm experience infrastructure, strategic marketing and market development (branding, packaging, websites, advertising), technology innovation and implementation, research and pilot projects, climate resiliency and conservation improvements, animal welfare improvements, and business diversification. Funds may not be used for debt repayment, general operating expenses, existing staff salaries, vehicles/trailers (unless permanently mounted equipment), land or real estate purchases, or expenses outside the approved project period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland. Projects must operate within Cecil County.
requirements_list: Operate an existing agricultural business (not a conceptual or idea-stage project)
Be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland
Be actively producing agricultural goods or services
Be able to cover project costs upfront and request reimbursement
Be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal by the stated deadline
Submit a detailed project budget including vendor information, cost estimates, and quotes or screenshots for major purchases
Certify eligibility through mandatory attestations in the application
All funded projects must be fully completed by May 30, 2026
Submit reimbursement requests with all receipts and documentation no later than June 15, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application through Cecil County's OpenGov portal at https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/cecil by February 27, 2026 at 12 p.m. Applications must include a detailed project budget with vendor information and cost estimates. Collaborative projects must include letters of support from confirmed partners. Applications are reviewed by Cecil County Office of Economic Development staff and external reviewers using a standardized scoring rubric covering eligibility, project impact, feasibility, budget clarity, and overall quality.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Charles County Economic Development Department (EDD) supports small, locally-based for-profit businesses through the Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) Program by certifying them and encouraging participation in county contracts and procurement opportunities. Certified SLBE firms receive exclusive access to informal procurements under $50,000 reserved for qualifying businesses when at least three certified firms are available, competitive bid preferences and evaluation advantages on formal solicitations between $50,000 and $500,000, and increased visibility through inclusion on the official County SLBE Vendor List used by departments seeking qualified local firms. For formal procurements valued $50,000–$500,000, certified firms receive a bid preference of up to 10% cost above the lowest bid on Invitations to Bid and Requests for Quotation, and up to 10 evaluation points on Requests for Proposals, prorated based on SLBE participation. Firms graduate from the program after receiving more than $3 million in SLBE awards within any 60-month period, exceeding Maryland SBR size thresholds, or relocating outside Charles County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and textbook costs for credit courses that are job-related or part of a degree related to the employee's current job or a County position the employee may reasonably expect to advance into.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Charles County Government.
requirements_list: Must be a full-time or full-time reduced hour (grandfathered) employee
Must have been employed with the County for a minimum of 1 year
Must be a non-probationary employee
Courses must be credit courses and job-related or part of a degree related to the employee's current or expected County position
Undergraduates must earn a grade of C or better; graduate students must earn a B or better
Employees must submit final grade report and textbook receipts to receive reimbursement

Additional details are in Chapter 21 of the Charles County Government Personnel Policies and Procedures Manual.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) is a Maryland state initiative established under the Cannabis Reform Act of 2023 following the legalization of adult-use recreational cannabis. The fund allocates a portion of cannabis sales tax revenue to local jurisdictions to support community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities and those disproportionately affected by past cannabis prohibition enforcement. In Charles County, FY2026 funds ($811,000) are split between grants to local non-profits (via Charles County Charitable Trust) and essential services for seniors (via the Aging Division), focused on the Waldorf region. In Harford County, funds serve low-income communities and areas with higher rates of cannabis prohibition enforcement, with priority ZIP codes 21001 (Aberdeen), 21009 (Abingdon), and 21040 (Edgewood) identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity; a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) has been published for FY2027. In Talbot County, competitive grants are administered by the Talbot County Reinvestment and Repair Commission and Talbot Family Network, with priority area ZIP code 21601 (Easton) identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity; an inaugural funding round was released January 27, 2026. Two grant pathways are available in Talbot County: Small Community Grants (up to $10,000; total $50,000 available) and Community Impact Grants (minimum $25,000; total $150,000 available), with an application deadline of March 27, 2026 and an anticipated award period of May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.agency: Charles County Government; Harford County Office of Drug Control Policy; Talbot County Reinvestment and Repair Commission / Talbot Family Network
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding distributed to community-based organizations and local initiatives serving low-income communities and areas with historically high cannabis prohibition enforcement. In Charles County, FY2026 budget of $811,000 is split: $411,000 to Charles County Charitable Trust for grants to local non-profits serving the Waldorf region, and $400,000 to the Department of Community Services-Aging Division for senior services including Meals-on-Wheels. In Harford County, priority ZIP codes are 21001, 21009, and 21040. In Talbot County, competitive grants are available through two pathways: Small Community Grants (up to $10,000; total $50,000 available) and Community Impact Grants (minimum $25,000; total $150,000 available); priority ZIP code is 21601 (Easton). The inaugural Talbot County funding round had an application deadline of March 27, 2026, with an anticipated award period of May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Law enforcement agencies and activities are explicitly prohibited from receiving CRRF funds; funds may not supplant existing local government program budgets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income communities, individuals and communities disproportionately affected by past cannabis prohibition enforcement, local non-profits, for-profit community-based organizations, seniors, and government entities in Charles County (Waldorf region), Harford County (Aberdeen, Abingdon, and Edgewood), and Talbot County (ZIP code 21601, Easton). In Talbot County, nonprofit and for-profit community-based organizations are the primary applicants (not individuals).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants to local non-profits and community-based organizations supporting low-income and disproportionately impacted communities; essential services for seniors including Meals-on-Wheels and other senior assistance programs; community-based services and supports; reentry, legal, and stabilization supports; economic opportunity and workforce development; and other initiatives that benefit disproportionately impacted and low-income communities affected by past cannabis enforcement and related social and economic disparities. Explicitly prohibited: law enforcement agencies or activities; supplanting existing local government program budgets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County (focused on the Waldorf region), Harford County (priority ZIP codes: 21001 Aberdeen, 21009 Abingdon, 21040 Edgewood), and Talbot County (priority ZIP code: 21601, Easton), Maryland. Projects in Talbot County outside Easton must demonstrate they address similar disproportionately impacted communities of focus.
requirements_list: Applicants must serve low-income or disproportionately impacted communities
Non-profit organizations in Charles County apply through the Charles County Charitable Trust grant program
Must serve communities in the Waldorf region of Charles County (Charles County applicants)
Must serve low-income communities or communities with higher rates of cannabis prohibition enforcement in Harford County
Priority areas in Harford County are ZIP codes 21001, 21009, and 21040
Applicants in Talbot County must be nonprofit or for-profit organizations (not individuals)
Applicants in Talbot County must review the Notice of Funding Opportunity before applying
Application and budget form must be submitted electronically via the submission link in the NOFO (Talbot County)
Projects must benefit disproportionately impacted or low-income communities in Talbot County
Small Community Grant pathway (Talbot County): application max 5 pages, award up to $10,000
Community Impact Grant pathway (Talbot County): application max 11 pages, award minimum $25,000
Applicants must demonstrate ability to execute within the grant period
Applicants must articulate intended outcomes and success measures
Applicants must commit to data collection including participation/service data and demographics by race/ethnicity
Applicants must comply with background checks and applicable state/federal law
Law enforcement agencies and activities are not eligible for CRRF funds
Funds may not supplant existing local government program budgets
Program operates in alignment with the State of Maryland's CRRF under oversight of the Maryland Office of Social Equity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Charles County, non-profit organizations may apply for grants through the Charles County Charitable Trust grant program; senior services funding is allocated directly to the Department of Community Services-Aging Division. In Harford County, a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) has been published for FY2027; public input was gathered through a county survey and virtual town halls. In Talbot County, select one of two grant pathways (Small Community Grant or Community Impact Grant), review the Notice of Funding Opportunity, then complete and submit the application form and budget form electronically via the submission link provided in the NOFO. A pre-application meeting slide deck and recording are available for reference. Contact Nancy Andrew at director@talbotfamilynetwork.org or 410-200-5532 for Talbot County information; contact the respective county office for other counties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Grant Program (Charles County Septic)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) is a state-supported grant program locally administered by the Charles County Health Department. It provides funding to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units, fund sewer connections to public sewer for existing dwellings, or — for low-income households — replace a failing septic system. The program's goal is to reduce harmful nutrients, especially nitrogen, that septic systems discharge into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to cover the cost of replacing a conventional septic system with a nitrogen-reducing unit, connecting an existing dwelling to public sewer, or (for low-income households) replacing a failing septic system. Specific grant amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County property owners with conventional septic systems; low-income households with failing septic systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of conventional septic tank with a nitrogen-reducing unit; connection to public sewer; replacement of a failing septic system for low-income households; installation of nitrogen removal units on residential on-site septic systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Charles County, Maryland; eligibility may vary based on Priority Funding Area (PFA) status
requirements_list: Must be a Charles County resident
Must have an on-site septic system eligible for a nitrogen removal unit upgrade
Low-income status required for failing septic system replacement
Must apply through the Charles County Health Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Charles County Health Department at 301-609-6792. Download the Bay Restoration Fund Application and applicable checklist (PFA or non-PFA) from the Charles County website and submit to the Health Department.

structured_extraction.program_name: First Time Home Buyers Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct financial assistance of up to $6,000 for settlement expenses to qualified low- and moderate-income first-time homebuyers in Charles County. The loan is secured by a second mortgage with repayment deferred until the property is sold, transferred, refinanced, or the buyer stops using it as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Deferred second mortgage loan of up to $6,000 to cover settlement/closing costs for first-time homebuyers. Repayment is deferred until the property is sold, transferred, refinanced, or the buyer no longer occupies the home as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income first-time homebuyers in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Settlement/closing expenses for the purchase of a home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer
Must meet low- to moderate-income eligibility criteria
Property must be used as principal residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Charles County Housing Authority for application details. Program guidelines are available for download.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Housing Initiative and Indoor Plumbing Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income homeowners in Charles County obtain indoor plumbing and/or potable water for their principal residence. The program is administered by the Charles County Housing Authority. Household income limits apply based on household size, ranging from $74,800 for a 1-person household to $141,000 for an 8-person household. A pre-qualification form is available online for residents to check their eligibility before applying.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for low-income homeowners to install or repair indoor plumbing and/or obtain potable water for their primary residence. Household income limits apply based on household size, ranging from $74,800 for a 1-person household to $141,000 for an 8-person household.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in Charles County who lack indoor plumbing or potable water at their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or repair of indoor plumbing and/or potable water systems at the applicant's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Must be a low-income homeowner
Household income must fall within program income limits based on household size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Plumbing Program Pre-Qualification Form available on the Charles County website to check eligibility. Then contact the Housing Authority to obtain a full application package, submit a completed Pre-application form, and the Housing Authority will follow up after receiving it.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Façade Improvement Program provides matching grants to owners of commercial buildings within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County to upgrade the visible, corridor-facing components of their properties. The program covers eligible exterior improvements such as windows, awnings, signage, lighting, roofs, and storefronts. Priority is given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.
structured_extraction.agency: Charles County Planning and Growth Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 50% matching grant reimbursement. The applicant pays 50% of the total approved façade improvement cost, and Charles County reimburses the remaining 50%. Payment is made within 30 days after the applicant provides proof of payment. Incremental draws may be available depending on the award amount. Construction must be completed within 90 days of the award letter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial buildings located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: External building façade improvements including: exterior wall materials, façade color, balconies, roof treatments, storefronts, entries and doorways, windows, awnings and canopies, lighting, signage, porches, chimneys, and related permits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County, MD. Priority is given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.
requirements_list: Application must be for a commercial building within the WURC boundary.
Application must be received by the designated deadline (August 1, 2025 at 4:30 pm).
Projects must be for external building façade improvements only.
Work cannot begin prior to receiving a commitment letter from Charles County.
All scope of work changes must be approved by staff before work is done.
Applicant must agree to maintain all improvements in their finished state.
Applicant must pay all project costs in full before receiving reimbursement.
Construction must be completed within 90 days of the award letter.
Only commercial businesses are eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the application form on the program's webpage. Applicants selected to receive funding will be notified by early fall 2025. After approval, the applicant completes the construction within 90 days and pays all costs in full. The applicant then provides proof of payment (canceled checks or other verification) to receive the 50% grant reimbursement within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County provides free wood chip mulch to residents through its yard waste and Christmas tree recycling programs. Residents can pick up mulch at designated facilities while supplies last. Self-loading is available; county operators can also load vehicles, but residents assume responsibility for any vehicle damage.
structured_extraction.agency: Charles County Public Works - Environmental Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free wood chip mulch is available to Charles County residents while supplies last. Mulch is available for self-service loading (residents must bring a pitchfork or shovel) or operator-assisted loading at participating facilities. Commercial vehicles are prohibited.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mulch for use in planting beds or lawn areas
