Commercial vehicles are prohibited (no business signage, over 10,000 lbs, stake/utility body, box/cargo body, uniformed crew, or lawn equipment)
Residents must bring a pitchfork or shovel for self-loading
Available Saturdays 7:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. only for all vehicle types
Supplies available while they last
Load must be secured before leaving the facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required. Visit the Piney Church Road Mulch Facility or other participating recycling centers on Saturdays from 7:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. Bring a shovel or pitchfork to load mulch yourself, or request operator loading (at your own risk).

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County offers qualifying water and sewer customers either a one-week payment extension or a deferred payment plan to avoid water disconnection when they need extra time to pay their bill. A payment extension extends the disconnect date by one week. A deferred payment plan allows scheduled payments to be received up to one week prior to the next quarterly bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Customers may request a one-week extension on their water/sewer disconnect date, or set up a deferred payment plan with scheduled payments (minimum $50 per payment for bills over $250) spread out until one week before the next quarterly bill. Note: late payment charges of 10% on unpaid balance and 3% interest on arrears still apply.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be submitted prior to the scheduled disconnect date, no later than the prior business day
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County water and sewer customers who need extra time to pay their bill due to unusual circumstances
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extending the time to pay a past-due water/sewer bill and avoiding water service disconnection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Charles County water and sewer customers
requirements_list: Request must be submitted before the scheduled disconnect date, preferably before the bill due date
Customer payment history is reviewed for eligibility
Tenants must have a renter's form on file from their landlord; landlord must send written approval directly to the billing office for each deferred payment plan request
Cannot request both an extension and a deferred payment plan
For deferred payment plans: first payment of at least $50 must be made before or immediately after the request
Last deferred payment must be received one week before the next billing date
Deferred payments cannot be more than one month apart
Minimum payment of $50 per month for invoices over $250
Any request received on the scheduled disconnect date may be denied
If water is disconnected, full payment is required before reconnection
Defaulting on a plan may result in denial of future arrangements for up to one year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request online using the Payment Extension form or Deferred Payment Plan Request form before the scheduled disconnect date. An email confirmation will be sent within 24 business hours indicating approval, denial, or required changes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charlotte Hall Veterans Home is an assisted living and skilled nursing facility for eligible Maryland veterans and certain qualifying spouses. Located on 126 acres in St. Mary's County, the home provides comfortable, high-quality care including assisted living, skilled nursing, and memory care. Residents receive a range of on-site services including medical, dental, therapy, pharmacy, and recreational amenities. The cost of care is subsidized by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) per diem payments and, for assisted living, by the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans receive a VA per diem subsidy to reduce their cost of care. As of October 1, 2025, the VA per diem rates are $148.71 per day ($4,535.66/month) for nursing home care and $64.19 per day ($1,957.80/month) for assisted living. Veterans rated 70% or greater service-connected disability (VP1) may be entitled to the full cost of nursing home care covered. For assisted living, veterans pay 90% of their monthly net income (up to the full monthly cost), and the State of Maryland subsidizes the balance after the VA per diem credit is applied. Non-veteran spouses must pay the full cost of care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veterans who served on full-time active duty and were discharged under honorable conditions, certain reserve component members, and certain non-veteran spouses of eligible veterans. Applicants must be Maryland residents aged 62 or older, or deemed disabled by SSA or the VA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential assisted living or skilled nursing facility care, including room and board, medical services, therapy, pharmacy, and other on-site amenities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland veteran who served on full-time active duty (not active duty for training) in the U.S. Armed Forces and was discharged or released under honorable conditions
Certain reserve component members who meet legal residence requirements are also eligible
Certain non-veteran spouses of eligible veterans may be admitted to the assisted living program
Must be a Maryland resident aged at least 62 years old, or deemed disabled by the Social Security Administration or the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Make an appointment with the Veterans Service Officer (VSO) by calling 301-884-8171 Ext. 5112. 2. Complete the application form (PDF available at charhall.org). 3. Send the completed application to Amanda Hanbury via email or mail to Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, Attn: Admissions, 29449 Charlotte Hall Road, Charlotte Hall, Maryland 20622.

structured_extraction.program_name: 22Beacon Charter School Facility Financing (Direct Loans, Guarantees, and Credit Enhancement)
structured_extraction.program_description: 22Beacon (formerly Charter Schools Development Corporation / CSDC) is a certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) that provides financing solutions for charter school facilities nationwide. The program offers direct loans, lease and loan guarantees (credit enhancement), and financial support to help charter schools acquire, construct, or renovate educational facilities. It serves schools at all stages, with a particular focus on new and early-stage schools serving under-resourced communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 22Beacon provides direct loans, lease and loan guarantees (credit enhancement), loan loss reserves, debt service reserve funds, and additional collateral support. The program also offers leasehold and tenant improvement loans, debt refinancing, and climate-focused/green lending. Schools must complete an application to be considered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charter schools of all types and stages, with a focus on new and early-stage schools serving under-resourced and economically disadvantaged communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, or renovation of educational facilities; leasehold and tenant improvements; debt refinancing; green/climate-focused facility improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 30 states and Washington, D.C., including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a charter school
Must complete an application to be considered for financing services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 22Beacon to learn more about financing services and begin the application process. A prospective school must complete an application to be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Building Block Fund™ provides credit enhancement support to charter schools seeking to secure facility loans or leases. It focuses on helping schools obtain safe, modern, economical, and efficient facilities, with the goal of 100% financed facilities at an affordable cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides partial and limited lease and loan guarantees, additional collateral, loan loss reserves, and debt service reserve funds to help charter schools secure facility financing. Aims for excellent leverage resulting in 100% financed facilities at an affordable cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charter schools seeking to secure facility loans or leases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit enhancement to support facility loans or leases for safe, modern, economical, and efficient school facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program; available where 22Beacon operates, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a charter school seeking a facility loan or lease
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 22Beacon and complete the financing application to be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Chesapeake Bay Foundation initiative that provides free plant material, implementation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Also supports livestock producers with conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, and connects farmers to grazing mentors and technical assistance through the CBF-led Maryland Grazers Network, including support on farm economics and marketing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free plant material, implementation services, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Livestock producers can receive funding for conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, plus grazing mentors and technical assistance on farm economics and marketing through the Maryland Grazers Network.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and rural landowners in Maryland, particularly those interested in streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, or rotational grazing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, and related technical assistance on farm economics and marketing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Rob Schnabel at rschnabel@cbf.org or 443-482-2175 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Community Tree Planting Mini Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Anne Arundel County Forestry Board, City of Annapolis, and the Chesapeake Bay Trust that provides small community-based grants up to $5,000 to help communities and organizations increase the number of trees and tree canopy in neighborhoods, parks, and communities throughout Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small community-based grants up to $5,000 for tree planting and canopy expansion projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, organizations, neighborhoods, and groups seeking to plant trees and increase tree canopy in Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting trees and increasing tree canopy in neighborhoods, parks, and communities; raising public awareness about tree canopy health, watersheds, air quality, and water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at the linked URL.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration and Forestry Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership grant program between the Chesapeake Bay Trust, Anne Arundel County Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration, and the City of Annapolis that funds on-the-ground watershed restoration projects to reduce pollutants in local waterways. Projects must reduce stormwater runoff from impervious surfaces and treat or filter pollutants entering local waterways, helping the County and City meet water quality goals under their Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit. Grants can fund both design and construction/implementation of stormwater treatment facilities. Design grants may fund engineering work, public outreach meetings, and gathering of maintenance agreements. Construction grants require public bidding and deliver as-built plans to the City. The program also supports reforestation and greening efforts and the protection of forested land to improve water and air quality, increase habitat and tree cover, and reduce flooding and erosion. Two project categories exist: Category 1 (small-scale, disturbance footprint under 5,000 sq ft or less than 100 cubic yards of earth) and Category 2 (large-scale, disturbance footprint over 5,000 sq ft or more than 100 cubic yards of earth).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $300,000 are available per project, with approximately $1,000,000 available for Anne Arundel County projects and $300,000 for City of Annapolis projects per cycle. Requests larger than $300,000 require prior approval from the Trust's Senior Program Officer. Matching funds are not required but are viewed favorably. Grants may fund design of stormwater treatment facilities (engineering, public outreach, maintenance agreement preparation) and/or construction/implementation of stormwater improvement projects (requiring public bidding and delivery of as-built plans), as well as reforestation and greening efforts and protection of forested land.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: RFPs open annually in the Fall and close in the Spring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified 501(c) nonprofit organizations based in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis), such as local watershed groups, community and homeowner associations, service and civic groups, and faith-based organizations, as well as property owners, local governments, and communities seeking to improve water quality, increase tree canopy, reduce flooding and erosion, and implement watershed restoration practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-ground watershed restoration practices that reduce stormwater runoff volume and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces entering local streams and waterways; design of stormwater treatment facilities (engineering, public outreach, maintenance agreement preparation); construction/implementation of stormwater improvement projects including stream restoration (prevented sediment, instream denitrification, floodplain reconnection, ephemeral channel retrofits), shoreline stabilization/living shorelines; reforestation and greening efforts; protection of forested land to improve water and air quality, increase habitat and tree cover, and reduce flooding and erosion. Project budgets should account for extra discretionary funds to cover fees and bonds associated with any permits. Projects may be located on non-profit property, private property, City of Annapolis-owned property, or public school properties with landowner approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located throughout Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a certified 501(c) nonprofit organization
At least one partner must represent a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis)
Project must be located in Anne Arundel County or City of Annapolis
Project must treat stormwater runoff from impervious surfaces or demonstrate measurable water quality improvement
Applicants must provide sound technical designs and project budgets
Project budgets must account for extra discretionary funds to cover fees/bonds associated with any permits
Landowner support must be documented when projects are on private or non-profit-owned property
Construction projects must be publicly bid
As-built plans must be delivered to the City upon project completion
Long-term maintenance agreements with Anne Arundel County DPW may be required
Site evaluation framework (Easy Sites / Complicated Sites / Poor Sites) used in project selection
Partnerships with experienced partners recommended for complex projects
BMP metrics, as-builts/design plans/reports, BEHI data (where applicable), GIS shapefiles, drainage area maps, Storm ID assignment, and project contact coordination required for documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: RFPs are solicited annually by the Chesapeake Bay Trust, typically opening in the Fall and closing in the Spring. Visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust application page at https://cbtrust.org/grants/anne-arundel-county-watershed-restoration/ to access the current RFP and apply. Applicants may also contact the Chesapeake Bay Trust or Anne Arundel County Watershed Protection and Restoration Program staff for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust - Chesapeake Conservation Climate Corps
structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long service program where young adults (ages 18-25) are placed as Climate Coordinators at host organizations across Maryland to support environmental and climate resilience projects. The City of Annapolis Resilience and Sustainability Division is one such host organization, seeking a coordinator to help implement its Climate Action Plan, conduct research on climate legislation and policy, and assist with community engagement activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A stipend-supported year of service paying $33,280 annually, disbursed bimonthly. Also includes health care coverage for those without private insurance, 15 professional development trainings, 4 all-cohort project days, 4-10 networking visits, 1 capstone project, 1 grant opportunity, and funding to attend a regional professional conference. Program runs August 19, 2026 to August 19, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18-25 who are U.S. citizens, permanent resident aliens, or have documentation to work in the U.S., interested in climate resilience and environmental work across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend to support a year of service focused on climate adaptation, community resilience, grant identification, research, and community engagement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Placed at host organizations across the state of Maryland. Applicants interested in working with the City of Annapolis should indicate this during the application process.
requirements_list: Age 18-25 at the start of the program
Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, or have documentation confirming permission to work in the U.S. during the year-long term of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. Applicants interested in being placed with the City of Annapolis should indicate that preference during the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Montgomery Watershed Restoration and Outreach Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds public outreach, stewardship, and community-based restoration projects that reduce pollutants and improve water quality in Montgomery County's local streams and waterways. Projects should educate and engage residents in watershed improvement while achieving measurable impacts and sustainable behavior change. Eligible project types include community-based restoration, litter reduction, public outreach and stewardship, and water quality monitoring.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards to nonprofit organizations for water quality improvement projects. Award amounts are set each year based on available funds. Match is encouraged but not required; preference is given to projects with match and/or in-kind services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically, the fall of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations such as local watershed groups, community associations, service and civic groups, and faith-based organizations. At least one partner must represent a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public outreach and stewardship projects, community-based restoration projects (e.g. designs for construction-ready in-the-ground stormwater projects on nonprofit-owned property), litter reduction efforts, and water quality monitoring initiatives that educate and engage residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must serve Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland
Projects must reduce pollutants and improve water quality in Montgomery County's local streams and waterways
Match is encouraged but not required; projects with match or in-kind services receive preference
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Chesapeake Bay Trust's online application system at cbtrust.org/grants/cleanwatermontgomery/. All proposals are evaluated by a Technical Review Committee prior to award. Applications are typically due in the fall of each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Forestry Catalyst Fund (CF2) provides grants to support tree planting projects and build the capacity of organizations to scale up tree planting and maintenance in overburdened, underserved communities across Maryland. Funded by Inflation Reduction Act Urban and Community Forestry funding from the USDA Forest Service and administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust in partnership with the Maryland Forest Service, the program aims to reduce barriers to tree planting and give local partners flexible access to funds that can be leveraged to secure additional resources without requiring matching funds. Three funding tracks are available: Track A (Site Readiness — stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal to enable new plantings); Track B (Implementation — direct tree planting projects requiring pre-application technical assistance from the Maryland Forest Service or an authorized representative from a 5 Million Trees for Maryland partnership agency); and Track C (Capacity Building — staff or contractual support, workforce development, and new or expanded pilot programming related to tree planting and maintenance). Tracks A and B may be combined in a single application, but Track C must be submitted separately. All projects must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities as identified in the IRA Disadvantaged Communities Map (Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from $5,000 to $50,000 per project for Tracks A and B (Site Readiness and Implementation), and $5,000 to $250,000 per year for Track C (Capacity Building). No matching funds are required; the match waiver must be passed on to any sub-awardees. Funded by Inflation Reduction Act Urban and Community Forestry funding from the USDA Forest Service. Payments are phased with a 10% holdback until final report submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, September 15, 2025 at 11:59 PM EST (FY26 cycle; application period is currently closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, federally recognized tribes and tribal organizations, non-profit organizations, public and state-controlled institutions of higher education, and community-based organizations working in overburdened or underserved communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Track A: site readiness activities such as stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal leading to replacement tree planting. Track B: direct tree planting implementation projects. Track C: staff or contractual support, workforce development, and expansion or creation of new pilot programming related to tree planting and maintenance. All work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All projects must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities in Maryland as identified in the Inflation Reduction Act Disadvantaged Communities Map (Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool). 100% of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities.
requirements_list: Projects must directly or indirectly result in trees being planted in overburdened, underserved communities
Project location must be identified in the IRA Disadvantaged Communities Map
100% of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities
Track B projects require pre-application technical assistance from the Maryland Forest Service or an authorized representative from a 5 Million Trees for Maryland partnership agency
Track A and B applications may be submitted together, but Track C may not be combined with another track in the same application
No matching funds required; match waiver must be passed on to any sub-awardees
Two separate individuals required: Executive Officer (decision-making authority) and Project Leader (primary contact); neither can be contractors
Project Leader's email must match the submission email address or application will be rejected
Applicants may not be awarded grants in consecutive grantmaking cycles
Two-year maintenance plan required as part of proposal (watering, mulching, pruning, pest monitoring, invasives management, leaf removal, mowing integration)
Final reports with receipts, invoices, and timesheets required before subsequent funding disbursement
Organizations with outstanding reports are ineligible for future grants
10% payment holdback until final report is submitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online system managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust at cbtrust.org/grants/community-forestry/. The online application form includes multiple tabs: Eligibility Quiz, Applicant Information, Project Information, Timeline, Deliverables, Volunteers, Project Partnerships, Narrative & Supporting Documents, Budget, Terms and Conditions, Demographics, and Survey. A two-year maintenance plan (per Appendix A forestry maintenance requirements) and partner letters of commitment are required. Budget must be submitted using the Chesapeake Bay Trust's Financial Management Spreadsheet template. Contact CBT Program Officer Samara Pyfrom at 410-974-2941 ext. 147 or spyfrom@cbtrust.org with questions about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Chesapeake Bay Trust, in partnership with the City of Rockville, administers grants to nonprofit organizations for projects within Rockville city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources. Eligible projects include permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for projects within Rockville city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources. Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with projects in Rockville, MD that address stormwater pollution, natural resource protection, or environmental sustainability, particularly projects that benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Project must be located within Rockville city limits
Project must reduce stormwater pollution or protect natural resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at cbtrust.org/grants/outreach-and-restoration/.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program (PGCSSGP), managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT) in cooperation with Prince George's County, funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve communities and water quality. The program also engages County residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. Eligible activities include water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed. Award history shows 12 projects and $675,000 granted in FY22.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants for on-the-ground restoration and program activities. Match (cash or in-kind) is not required but is considered favorably in the review process. Grant amounts are not specified on this page. Award history shows 12 projects and $675,000 granted in FY22.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt or 501(c) nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners, and businesses located in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water quality improvement projects, citizen awareness and engagement activities, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed. All programs must be implemented in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County, Maryland, targeting the Anacostia watershed.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a tax-exempt or 501(c) nonprofit organization, municipality, faith-based organization, educational institution, community association, civic group, homeowner, or business
Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County
Activities must target the Anacostia watershed
Applications are evaluated on quality and consistency with the RFP, justification and need, appropriate partners, cost-effectiveness, likelihood of success, sustainability, and demonstration value
Match (cash or in-kind) is not required but preferred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed and implemented by the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT). The process is competitive; all applications are evaluated by funding partners and an external Technical Review Committee on criteria including likelihood of success, cost-effectiveness, consistency with the RFP, sustainability, justification and need, partnerships, and demonstration value. For application details, visit cbtrust.org or https://cbtrust.org/prince-georges-stormwater-stewardship-2/.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rockville residents and eligible property owners can receive rebates for installing small-scale stormwater management projects on their property. Projects reduce polluted runoff, help prevent flooding, improve water quality, provide cooling, and create wildlife habitat. Eligible projects include conservation landscaping, rain gardens, pavement removal, rain barrels, cisterns, native tree planting, permeable paver retrofits, and green roofs. The program is administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust in partnership with the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates up to a lifetime maximum of $5,000 per property. Rebate rates vary by project type: Conservation Landscaping — $6/sq ft with soil improvement, $5/sq ft without; Rain Garden — $10/sq ft; Pavement Removal — $6/sq ft if replacing with conservation landscaping, $3/sq ft if replacing with sod; Rain Barrel — $1/gallon; Cistern — $1/gallon; Tree Canopy — $150/tree; Permeable Paver Retrofit — $14/sq ft; Green Roof — $9/sq ft.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family and townhome residents, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits with eligible properties in the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management projects including conservation landscaping, rain gardens, pavement removal, rain barrels, cisterns, native tree planting, permeable paver retrofits, green roofs, rainwater collection systems, outlet protection, swales, pervious hardscapes, and ground covers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the City of Rockville, Maryland. Relevant watersheds include Rock Creek Watershed, Watts Branch Watershed, Upper/Lower Rock Creek, and Cabin John Creek — all tied to Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Rockville
Eligible property types include single-family residences, townhomes, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits
Must install qualifying sustainable landscaping practices
Lifetime maximum rebate of $5,000 per property
Licensed professional recommended or required for retaining walls over 3 feet (engineer-designed and permit required)
Building permits required for many projects
Contact the City for permitting assistance and proper specifications before replacing impermeable surfaces with permeable pavers
Rain garden installations require infiltration testing and a 10-foot setback from house and 40-foot setback from septic systems
Obtain all necessary permits prior to project installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. The Trust reviews and processes applications, performs site visits, and is available to answer questions. Applicants may also contact the City of Rockville for rebate eligibility guidance and permitting assistance. Free educational workshops and on-site stormwater runoff evaluations are available. More information available at www.rockvillemd.gov/rainscapes or www.rockvillemd.gov/environment.

Planning projects include watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, and financing plans. Design assistance covers non-point source best management practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical planning and design assistance provided through preferred contractors for watershed protection and restoration projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations working on water quality protection and restoration in the Chesapeake Bay watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, and design of non-point source best management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or non-profit organization
Project must lead to improved water quality in the Maryland Chesapeake Bay watershed or Maryland Coastal Bays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a proposal to the Watershed Assistance Collaborative. See the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for details and a list of preferred contractors.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Assistance – Two-Year Milestone Support Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration programs and projects that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Planning and design grants are provided through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (lead partner), with additional financing strategy and stakeholder development support via the University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center, and technical assistance from 5 regional watershed restoration specialists. The Stormwater Financing and Outreach Unit (SFOU) works with up to 2 Maryland communities per year and offers workshops for municipal stormwater managers. The program has awarded over $8.1 million to date.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for water quality improvement projects. Planning and design grants are provided through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (lead partner). Additional support includes financing strategy and stakeholder development via the University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center, and technical assistance from 5 regional watershed restoration specialists assigned by region. The Stormwater Financing and Outreach Unit (SFOU) works with up to 2 Maryland communities per year and offers workshops for municipal stormwater managers. The Watershed Assistance Grant Program has awarded over $8.1 million to date. Full terms and amounts are described in the Request for Proposals document.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local communities, local governments, businesses, and citizens seeking to undertake comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration programs and projects that improve water quality. Eligible uses include non-point source restoration, wetland/forest restoration, stormwater management, and infrastructure planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include local governments, businesses, and citizens
Projects must be located within the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, or the Maryland Coastal Bays
Projects must support protection and/or restoration activities that lead to improved water quality
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Request for Resources & Services Form. Planning and design grants are provided through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (lead partner); refer to cbtrust.org for grant information. Financing strategy and stakeholder development assistance is available through the University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center. Technical assistance is provided by 5 regional watershed restoration specialists assigned by region. The Stormwater Financing and Outreach Unit (SFOU) works with up to 2 Maryland communities per year and holds workshops for municipal stormwater managers. See the Request for Proposals document for full application details. Contact Carrie Decker at the Chesapeake & Coastal Service for more information.

Funded projects must increase citizen awareness of water quality issues, provide education opportunities for Howard County residents, or implement restoration projects.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds are awarded to local non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations for water quality education and restoration projects in Howard County. Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations in Howard County interested in water quality education or restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increasing citizen awareness and participation in water quality issues, providing education opportunities for Howard County residents, and/or implementing restoration projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to non-profit organizations operating in Howard County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization
Project must address water quality in Howard County's lakes, rivers, or streams

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Rain Check Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Chesapeake Bay Trust and Prince George's County Department of the Environment that offers rebates to property owners who install approved stormwater management practices on their properties. The program helps Prince George's County meet its Clean Water Act obligations to reduce stormwater pollution in rivers and streams by improving runoff quantity and quality. Eligible practices include cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy plantings. The program also reimburses residents and businesses for the purchase price of trees planted on residential or commercial properties, up to $150 per tree. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis up to a lifetime ceiling per property.
structured_extraction.agency: Chesapeake Bay Trust / Prince George's County Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are provided based on the type of practice installed. Rates include: cisterns at $2/gallon stored (250-gallon minimum); conservation landscaping at $5/sq ft (250 sq ft minimum); green roofs at $10–$20/sq ft depending on planting depth (minimum 1/4 roof retrofit); pavement removal at $6/sq ft (no minimum for residential; 400 sq ft minimum for commercial/organizational applicants); permeable pavement at $12/sq ft (no minimum for residential; 400 sq ft minimum for commercial/HOA/civic/multi-family/nonprofit applicants); rain barrels at $2/gallon stored (minimum 50 gallons for residential; minimum 100 gallons for commercial/associations/nonprofits); rain gardens at $10/sq ft (100 sq ft minimum); and urban tree canopy at $150/tree (minimum 5-foot height, minimum 5 trees). Maximum lifetime rebate per property is $6,000 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial, multi-family, HOA, condo association, civic association, nonprofit, and not-for-profit properties. Rebate amounts cannot exceed total project cost. The program also reimburses the purchase price of trees up to $150 per tree planted on residential or commercial properties. Trees must be native species (ash/Fraxinus species not recommended due to emerald ash borer), planted between October 1 and May 1, on private property only (not public right-of-way).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners, commercial property owners, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwelling owners, nonprofit and not-for-profit organizations, and public property owners in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved stormwater management practices: cisterns (rainwater collection for non-potable outdoor uses such as landscape irrigation and car washing), conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal and replacement with permeable surfaces or vegetation, permeable pavement (interlocking pavers, porous asphalt, pervious concrete, grass pavers), rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy plantings on residential, commercial, or public properties; also purchase and installation of native trees for residential or commercial properties in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Prince George's County, Maryland. Residents of the City of Bowie are not eligible. Residents of the Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park are only eligible for cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden projects.
requirements_list: Applicant must own the property, or be a nonprofit with an agreement to complete a project on private or public land
Property must be located in Prince George's County
Must install eligible stormwater management practices
Projects must be completed within 12 months of receiving pre-approval from the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT)
CBT must pre-approve all applications prior to implementation, except rain barrel projects
CBT must inspect the completed project and confirm it complies with the approved application and County best practice guidelines
If the property is part of an HOA, applicant must provide documentation of HOA approval
Projects associated with permit approval for new building construction, additions, or renovations are not eligible
All applicants must sign a property owner agreement; commercial or public project applicants must also sign an operations and maintenance agreement
Property must not be located within a municipality that has a similar stormwater management rebate program
Tree must be planted on a residential or commercial property in Prince George's County

Green roof projects must replace existing roof area (not expand footprint); structural load analysis report from licensed structural engineer required; must be installed by certified green roof contractor (certified by national organization such as NRCA or Green Roofs for Healthy Cities; DIY not eligible); minimum 1/4 of roof area must be remodeled
Cistern must capture at least 250 gallons of rainwater during a storm; must be placed at least 10 feet from existing trees; level terrain or concrete platform required for above-ground systems

Rain barrel minimum: 50 gallons (residential); 100 gallons (commercial/institutional); property must have downspouts discharging to paved surfaces or steep slopes; system must include hose connection, filter trap, and overflow outlet

Permeable pavement: no minimum area for residential; 400 sq ft minimum for commercial/HOA/civic/multi-family/nonprofit applicants; site slope must be less than 5%; installation must be by licensed, bonded contractor; permit required if project exceeds 5,000 sq ft and/or 100 cubic yards earth disturbance; cannot be used on high-load traffic areas or high-pollutant zones

Pavement removal: no minimum for residential; 400 sq ft minimum for commercial/organizational applicants; utilities must be identified before work (Miss Utility at 811 or 1-800-257-7777); permit required for work in public right-of-way; permit required if project exceeds 5,000 sq ft or 100 cubic yards earth-moving disturbance

Rain garden soil must drain in 24–36 hours; minimum distance 10 feet from home/neighbor homes (downhill), 25 feet from septic field or well head; 2-foot clearance above bedrock/groundwater; full or partial sun exposure; native plants required; minimum 100 sq ft

Urban tree canopy: trees must be native species (ash/Fraxinus not recommended due to emerald ash borer), minimum 5 feet tall, minimum 1/2-inch caliper, planted in biodegradable 5-gallon container or balled/burlapped; planted on private property only (not public right-of-way); planting window October 1 – May 1; minimum 5 trees; spacing at least 3 ft from underground utilities/fences/driveways, 7 ft from small trees/shrubs, 10 ft from aerial utilities/large trees, 15 ft from structures; no permit required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT) website at cbtrust.org/grants/prince-georges-county-rain-check-rebate/. CBT handles application review, processing, and pre- and post-inspections. All applications except rain barrels must receive CBT pre-approval before starting the project. For pavement removal: (1) Identify impervious pavement on property; (2) Observe rainwater flow during rain; (3) Measure pavement area and confirm it meets minimum threshold; (4) Contact program for rebate qualification process. Rain barrel projects are self-installation and do not require pre-approval or a contractor. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Contractors who complete the Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course are listed on the Contractor Training Completion List and can install qualifying practices. For permit questions related to projects exceeding 5,000 sq ft or 100 cubic yards of earth disturbance, contact the County Department of Permitting, Inspections & Enforcement (call 311).

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank provides commercial loans for affordable housing projects, including Naturally Occurring Affordable Housing (NOAH), that ensure long-term affordability for low-, moderate-, and middle-income households up to 120% of Median Family Income (MFI). The program offers loan products including Acquisition, Construction-to-Permanent, Bridge, and Unitranche loans up to $21,000,000. It partners with minority-led developers and community-based investors to expand housing access and promote economic stability in underserved neighborhoods.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commercial loans up to $21,000,000 for affordable housing development and preservation projects, including NOAH properties serving households up to 120% of Median Family Income. Loan products include Acquisition, Construction-to-Permanent, Bridge, and Unitranche loans. LTV/LTC ranges from 50%–90% depending on loan product and property type. Terms up to 7 years for acquisition/construction; up to 24 months for bridge loans (longer for LIHTC). Rates based on CFB Cost of Funds plus spread. City First Bank partners with minority-led developers and community-based investors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-led developers, community-based investors, and for-profit and nonprofit organizations developing or preserving affordable housing for low-, moderate-, and middle-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing development and preservation, including acquisition, rehabilitation, construction, and short-term bridge financing with takeout identified, for Naturally Occurring Affordable Housing (NOAH) projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves DC, Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California; primarily focused on underserved neighborhoods in the Washington DC metro area
requirements_list: Project must ensure long-term affordability for low-, moderate-, or middle-income households
Households served must be at or below 120% of Median Family Income (MFI)
DSCR must be at or above 1.20x at stabilization
Owner personal guarantee required for owners with 20% or greater ownership interest
LTV/LTC ceilings vary by loan product and property type: raw land 50%, improved/multifamily up to 80%, construction-to-permanent up to 85% LTC, with LTV/LTC up to 90% for certain products
Origination fee 1%–2%; settlement costs and due diligence fees covered by borrower
1st lien collateral required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact City First Bank at 888.351.3280 to discuss loan terms and initiate an application. Speak with a banker or schedule an appointment at the Washington DC branch to discuss loan options.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank offers tailored commercial lending products for businesses, including financing for commercial real estate purchases, equipment, and working capital. The program is designed to help companies with revenues under $25 million become or remain owner-occupants of their business premises, supporting long-term growth and stability. Products include Working Capital Lines of Credit, Term Loans, Owner Occupied Real Estate loans, SBA 504 loans, and other SBA products (7(a), Express, Veterans Advantage).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tailored commercial loans available in multiple product types: Working Capital Lines of Credit (cash flow, receivables, general operating expenses); Term Loans (vehicles, equipment, supplies, leasehold improvements, working capital for expansion/growth); Owner Occupied Real Estate loans (purchase/refinance of real estate for borrower's business use); SBA 504 (long-term fixed asset loans for expansion, renovation, new construction, land/building purchase, leasehold improvements, working capital); and other SBA products (7(a), Express, Veterans Advantage) for expansion, renovation, new construction, land/building purchase, leasehold improvements, and working capital. Most products require minimum 3 years of operations. Any owner with ≥20% ownership interest must provide a guarantee. SBA 504 requires net worth <$15M and income <$5M. Available to businesses with revenues under $25 million. Note: This is not a commitment to lend. Loan terms may vary depending on the purpose of the loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses with annual revenues under $25 million seeking to purchase or retain ownership of commercial real estate or finance equipment and working capital. Most products require at least 3 years of operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial real estate purchases or refinancing, equipment financing, vehicles, supplies, leasehold improvements, working capital (including lines of credit and expansion financing), and long-term fixed asset investments via SBA products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City First Bank operates in the Washington, DC area and Baltimore, Maryland, and also serves Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California.
requirements_list: Business revenues under $25 million
Minimum 3 years of operations (required for most products)
Any owner with 20% or more ownership interest must provide a personal guarantee
SBA 504 applicants must have net worth under $15 million and net income under $5 million
Must meet SBA size standards for SBA loan products
Real estate loans require owner-occupancy of the financed property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact City First Bank at 888.351.3280 to speak with a banker or schedule an appointment. You may also visit the City First Bank website to connect with a representative at the Washington DC location. Note: This is not a commitment to lend. Loan terms may vary depending on the purpose of the loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank provides commercial real estate loans, term loans, and lines of credit to nonprofit organizations to support the development and expansion of owner-occupied facilities that serve low-income and minority-majority urban communities. Eligible projects include health care centers, charter schools, arts organizations, and social services facilities. Loan products include revolving lines of credit (up to $5M, ~3-year term) and term loans (up to $21M, up to 10-year term). Funds may be used for working capital, receivables financing, operating expenses, vehicles, equipment, supplies, leasehold improvements, expansion capital, and facility acquisition, finance, or refinance. Loan terms include up to 75% LTV, minimum 1.2x DSCR, and 1–2% origination fee. Personal/organizational guaranty typically not required. The program serves the Washington D.C. metro area and surrounding regions including Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City First Bank offers revolving lines of credit (up to $5M, ~3-year term) and term loans (up to $21M, up to 10-year term) to nonprofit organizations. Rates are Cost of Funds + Spread. Funds can be used for working capital, receivables financing, operating expenses, vehicles, equipment, supplies, leasehold improvements, expansion capital, and facility acquisition/finance/refinance. Loan terms include up to 75% LTV, minimum 1.2x DSCR, up to 25-year amortization for term loans, and 1–2% origination fee. Personal/organizational guaranty typically not required. This is not a commitment to lend; loan terms may vary depending on the purpose of the loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-funded tree planting program that restores Annapolis's urban forest canopy by planting trees at homes, congregations, businesses, and schools. Now in its fourth year of planting projects, the program has planted 380 trees from September 2023 to December 2025. Volunteer community leaders called 'Tree Troopers' are trained through a free program (4 virtual sessions plus one in-person planting event) to identify planting sites and oversee projects. The program is administered in partnership with the Anne Arundel Watershed Stewards Academy.

The program is city-funded and administered in partnership with the Anne Arundel Watershed Stewards Academy.

The program supports compliance with Annapolis's ordinance requiring all leaf blowers used within city limits to be electric-powered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis MPDU Program (also called 'Annapolis Houses') requires private developers to include affordable housing units in new residential subdivisions of 10 or more units, with 15% of homes for sale or rent priced below market rate for households at or below 100% of the Baltimore MSA area median income. Income-eligible city residents, city employees, and qualifying workers can apply for a Certificate of Eligibility to purchase or rent one of these below-market-rate units. For-sale prices are determined by the Department of Planning and Zoning based on HUD median family income data; rental prices are set at 80–100% of HUD Fair Market Rents depending on whether the landlord pays utilities. Units are subject to resale restrictions and owner-occupancy requirements for 30 years (for-sale) or 99 years (rental). Up to $10,000 in settlement expense assistance (down payment and closing costs) may also be available to eligible Certificate holders, and below-market mortgage financing may be available through the Maryland Mortgage Program. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis in person, by mail, or electronically.

Below-market mortgage financing may also be available through the Maryland Mortgage Program. Both rental and for-sale units are available in new residential developments subject to MPDU requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis MPDU Program requires private developers and builders of new residential developments with 10 or more units to set aside 15% of units as Moderately Priced Dwelling Units (MPDUs) — housing priced and rented below market rate for income-eligible households. Moderate-income households can apply for a Certificate of Eligibility to purchase or rent these below-market homes. The city sets sales prices based on HUD median family income data and rental rates at 80–100% of HUD Fair Market Rents depending on whether the landlord pays utilities. Units are subject to resale restrictions and owner-occupancy requirements for 30 years (for-sale) or 99 years (rental). Both minimum and maximum income thresholds apply. Applications from households are accepted on a rolling basis in person, by mail, or electronically. For developers, the program establishes the agreements, procedures, and forms required to satisfy inclusionary housing obligations and make MPDUs available to eligible certificate holders.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Transit Fare Program for Persons With Disabilities, Seniors and Students
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified individuals — including people with disabilities, seniors age 60 and older, Medicare cardholders, and students — can ride Annapolis Transit fixed-route buses for one-half the regular fare. Eligible riders pay $1 per one-way cash fare instead of the standard $2 base fare. Reduced fares also apply to day, weekly, monthly, and annual passes. K–12 students who live within the City of Annapolis ride free during school months. Students at private schools, colleges, and the Naval Academy who live outside the city but within the Annapolis Transit service area are eligible for the half-fare. Reduced fare does not apply to curb-to-curb ADA Complementary Paratransit service.

Reduced fare does not apply to curb-to-curb ADA Complementary Paratransit service.

Repayment is due upon sale or transfer of the property, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property via a Deed of Trust. The homebuyer must contribute a minimum of 1% of the sales price from their own funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Office of Community Services provides operating and/or capital grants to non-profit organizations to strengthen community services. Operating grants support day-to-day costs of running a non-profit; capital grants support property purchases, facility construction or remodeling/expansion, or equipment purchases. Funding is prioritized for organizations that sustain and empower youth, families, and individuals toward self-sufficiency; preserve and enhance community character; contribute to a vibrant local economy; or promote community revitalization, economic development, and environmental sustainability. Final funding decisions are made by the Annapolis City Council as part of the FY 2027 City Budget process.

FY 2027 funding is structured to prioritize organizations demonstrating strong community impact, collaboration, and diverse funding sources. Final funding decisions are made by the Annapolis City Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Annapolis Children and Families Success Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Office of Community Services (OCS) provides grants to community-based organizations to open, expand, or enhance child care and youth development programs. Funded programs must promote healthy child development, foster community resilience, and reduce opportunity gaps for Annapolis families. Programs must offer structured, adult-supervised activities for youth at a physical location within Annapolis. Eligible activities include recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, education, enrichment, life skills, and wellness. Priority is given to programs serving low-income youth, especially those running between 2pm and 7pm during school year and summer months, and programs emphasizing equity, diversity, and inclusion. Total program funding is $50,000 per fiscal year, with individual grants awarded at $2,500, $5,000, or $10,000. At least five organizations are funded per cycle. The funding period covers Fiscal Year 2026 (July 2025 – June 2026).
structured_extraction.agency: City of Annapolis Office of Community Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $2,500, $5,000, or $10,000 per proposal, with a total program budget of $50,000 per fiscal year. At least five organizations will be funded per cycle. The first 75% of funds are disbursed during the week of August 25th after a signed contract is returned. Grantees must submit a mid-program and final report and attend three meetings with OCS staff. Funding period covers Fiscal Year 2026 (July 2025 – June 2026).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and businesses that provide child care and youth development programs serving low-income youth in Annapolis, including 501(c)(3) organizations and businesses providing free or scholarship-based youth programming within the City of Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding must be used for implementing the proposed youth program, including providing scholarships to participants or developing structured, adult-supervised activities offered at no cost. Eligible uses include after-school and summer programming, recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, education, enrichment, life skills, wellness, child development, literacy, and athletics. Not intended to cover general organizational operational expenses beyond what is necessary for successful project implementation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers a rental assistance program to help low- and moderate-income households pay rent, security deposits, and/or utility bills. Its goals are to stabilize housing situations, prevent eviction, prevent utility shutoffs, and provide security deposit assistance for families who need housing. The city sends payment directly to the property manager or utility company on the applicant's behalf. Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year and is not guaranteed. Application processing can take up to 4–6 weeks.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Annapolis Office of Community Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance paid directly to the landlord or utility company on behalf of approved applicants. The approved funding amount is based on the applicant's qualifications. Payments are made by check, which can take 4–6 weeks to be received. Applicants receive a promissory letter during the processing period. Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year; approvals are not guaranteed. Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due. Payments can only be made to rental properties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program – Single-Family Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis administers federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds to support low- and moderate-income individuals and households. The program funds capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction within Annapolis, as well as home repairs and rehabilitation for low-income homeowners, and social services provided by organizations serving low-income populations. The Single-Family Rehabilitation component provides assistance to low- and moderate-income homeowners to ensure their homes are safe, healthy, and habitable. Each year, the city invites applications from eligible organizations and homeowners through an annual application process that includes required public hearings. Public service projects through the capital project track are no longer funded.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Annapolis, Community Development Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are awarded for two primary purposes: (1) capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction that benefit low- and moderate-income individuals and households, and (2) home repairs and rehabilitation for low-income homeowners (to ensure homes are safe, healthy, and habitable) and social service programs run by organizations serving low-income populations in Annapolis. The City of Annapolis anticipates receiving approximately $278,182 in CDBG funds for fiscal year 2027 (beginning July 1, 2026). The City runs an annual application process for these funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income homeowners, community organizations, and social service agencies serving low-income residents in Annapolis seeking funding for capital projects, home repair/rehabilitation, or social service programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction that benefit low- and moderate-income persons; home rehabilitation and repairs for low-income homeowners to ensure homes are safe, healthy, and habitable; social services provided by organizations serving low-income populations. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City holds two required public hearings as part of the annual CDBG application process. Interested parties may submit written comments or register to speak at public hearings. Submit a completed CDBG application to the Planning and Zoning Department by the stated deadline. The City Affordable Housing and Community Equity Development Commission reviews applications and recommends funding to the City Council, which approves all CDBG-funded projects. For the Single-Family Rehabilitation component, contact the Office of Community Development for application details. Contact the Community Development Division for all program inquiries.

structured_extraction.program_name: Port of Baltimore Business Wage Subsidy Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Baltimore created a Wage Subsidy Program to help Port-impacted small businesses retain incumbent workers following the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. The program provides wage subsidies so that workers remain attached to their employers and maintain health benefits during the port closure. The City provided an initial $1 million in total funding and was examining adding an additional $1 million. Eligible businesses receive $7,500 per worker for up to 3 workers, for a maximum of $22,500 per business (3 months of assistance per worker). Workers supported must be Baltimore City residents and existing employees of the applicant business.

SBA Disaster Recovery Centers (open Monday–Friday 8am–6pm, Saturday 10am–2pm) have representatives from the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Employment Development on site to provide additional support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tree Frederick is a City of Frederick program that supports residential tree planting by offering a 50/50 cost share on containerized trees each spring. City residents can order up to five native trees at a discounted price and pick them up at a scheduled spring event. The program also includes an HOA FILO (Financial Incentives for Low-Income Outreach) Planting initiative for homeowner associations. The program aims to increase the city's tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and help residents reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City covers 50% of the cost of containerized trees. Residents pay the remaining 50% at the time of purchase through the Tree Frederick online storefront. Each resident may purchase up to five trees per year in a single transaction. An HOA FILO (Financial Incentives for Low-Income Outreach) Planting initiative is also available for homeowner associations targeting low-income communities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open from February 1st until all trees sell out

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Tree Frederick online storefront (open February 1 until sold out), enter your address to verify city residency, select and pre-order trees, pay at checkout (price already reflects the 50% discount), then pick up trees at the scheduled spring pickup event at Harry Grove Stadium. HOAs interested in the FILO Planting initiative should complete the HOA FILO Planting Application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free weatherization services for low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties. The program improves home energy efficiency through air sealing, insulation, heating and cooling system upgrades, energy-efficient lighting, thermostat installation, and health and safety improvements. Eligible households can save $372 or more per year on energy bills. The program includes two tracks: (1) Whole Home Energy Efficiency — a full home energy audit followed by a range of weatherization upgrades; and (2) Crisis Program — emergency HVAC repair or replacement for households currently without a working heating or cooling system, with heating funding available in winter and cooling funding in summer. Applicants may also qualify based on participation in programs such as Energy Assistance (OHEP), SSI, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, or the DHCD Rehab Program.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Frederick Housing and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All weatherization work is provided free of charge, funded by federal and state grants. The program covers air sealing, insulation, HVAC upgrades, lighting replacement, thermostat installation, and health and safety improvements. Households save an average of $372 or more per year on energy bills. For renters, the landlord must sign a building owner agreement. Apartment buildings with up to 4 units are eligible for state weatherization funds; buildings with more than 4 units are reviewed case by case.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties, including City of Frederick residents. Nonprofits and social service organizations can refer eligible clients. Landlords of residential properties (up to 4 units) may also participate if their tenants income-qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Air sealing, insulation improvements, heating and cooling system upgrades and repairs, energy-efficient lighting, programmable or smart thermostat installation, mechanical ventilation, and health and safety measures (smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, combustion appliance venting).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland, including the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Applicant must live in Frederick, Carroll, or Washington County (including the City of Frederick)
Household income must be at or below the program income thresholds (e.g., $68,500 for a household of 1; $97,800 for a household of 4; up to $129,100 for a household of 8)
Renters are eligible but landlord must sign a building owner agreement and provide proof of ownership
Apartment buildings must have 4 or fewer units to qualify for state weatherization funds (larger buildings reviewed case by case)
Landlords of commercial spaces are NOT eligible
Clients already enrolled in qualifying income-eligible programs (e.g., SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, SSI, Energy Assistance/OHEP, DHCD Rehab Program) may use an abbreviated application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the program's application form on the City of Frederick website, providing name, address, email, phone number, and information about qualifying assistance programs received. Choose the Whole Home Energy Efficiency application for a full range of weatherization services, or the Crisis Program application if your heating or cooling system is currently not working. After approval, a qualified professional audits your home to determine which improvements will save the most energy.
