structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department offers a 50% discount on all youth programs for eligible residents under age 18. Qualifying households must show proof of City residency and meet one of three eligibility criteria: participation in the free/reduced-price lunch program through Frederick County Public Schools, receipt of Food Supplement Program (FSP) or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) benefits, or residency in a City of Frederick public housing community (Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village).
structured_extraction.agency: City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible youth under age 18 receive 50% off all youth programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth under age 18 who are City of Frederick residents and meet income-based or housing-based eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: 50% discount on youth recreation program registration fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Youth must be under age 18
Must provide proof of City of Frederick residency (driver's license or MVA-issued ID, water bill, or electric bill)

Must meet one of the following: eligible for free/reduced-price lunch through Frederick County Public Schools (FCPS) with a letter from FCPS; OR live in a household receiving Food Supplement Program (FSP) or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) benefits and provide an orange Independence Card from Frederick County Department of Social Services; OR live in Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village public housing communities owned by the Housing Authority of the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain eligibility approval by visiting the Wm. Talley Recreation Center Registration Desk at 121 North Bentz Street, Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 6:30 pm, with required proof documents. Once approved, register for programs online, in person, or by phone — the RRP discount will apply automatically.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Frederick Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A City of Frederick property tax credit for rehabilitation work on the exterior of commercial or residential buildings located within the Historic District Overlay (Historic Preservation Overlay Zone), whether individually designated or within a district. Work must total at least $500, have prior Historic Preservation Commission (HPC) approval (unless eligible under the Minor Rehabilitation List), and labor costs are only eligible if completed by licensed contractors. Property owners can apply for a reduction in their property tax liability based on approved historic preservation rehabilitation work reviewed by the Historic Preservation Commission. Provides a 25% credit on eligible exterior expenditures, up to a maximum of $7,500.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A City property tax credit equal to 25% of eligible exterior rehabilitation expenses on qualifying historic properties located in the City of Frederick's Historic Preservation Overlay Zone, up to a maximum of $7,500. Details on credit amounts and terms are provided in the City Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit Guide.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1st following the calendar year in which the expenditures were incurred (e.g., April 1, 2026 for 2025 expenditures)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and residential historic properties in the City of Frederick's Historic Preservation Overlay Zone — individually designated or within a district — undertaking qualifying exterior rehabilitation work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for eligible exterior expenditures on approved historic preservation rehabilitation work within the Historic Preservation Overlay Zone. Labor costs are eligible only if performed by licensed contractors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the City of Frederick's Historic District Overlay (Historic Preservation Overlay Zone), Maryland — individually designated or as part of a historic district under the Historic Preservation Commission's jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City of Frederick's Historic Preservation Overlay Zone (individually designated or as part of a district)
Rehabilitation work must total at least $500
Expenditures must be eligible exterior expenditures
Project must have prior HPC approval unless eligible under the Minor Rehabilitation List
Labor costs are only eligible when completed by licensed contractors
Keep copies of receipts as they are required with the application
Application must be submitted to the Planning Department by April 1st following the calendar year in which the expenditures were incurred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Historic Preservation Tax Credit Application online via the 'Apply Online' tab on the City of Frederick website, or submit the application with copies of receipts for eligible work, by April 1st following the calendar year in which the expenditures were incurred. Contact Christina Martinkosky, Division Manager of Historic Preservation, at CMartinkosky@CityofFrederickMD.gov or 301-600-1831 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Promotion Grant Program, administered by the City of Frederick Office of the Mayor, awards competitive grants annually to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to supplement existing funds that either create or enhance services that positively impact the greatest number of City of Frederick residents. Applicants can submit applications through the Foundant online portal. Separate applications are recommended for each specific type of promotion activity. Funds are available after July 1 of the funding year and are distributed after a letter of agreement is completed between the City and the recipient organization. The City may award partial amounts, and scorecards are available for review. Recent grant totals have ranged from approximately $315,000 to $385,000 distributed across 30–41 organizations per cycle, with individual awards typically ranging from $2,000 to $28,000.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Frederick, Office of the Mayor
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations. Funding is distributed after July 1 of each fiscal year following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the recipient organization. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. A separate application is recommended for each specific type of promotion activity. Recent grant totals have ranged from approximately $315,000 to $385,000 distributed across 30–41 organizations per cycle, with individual awards typically ranging from $2,000 to $28,000. Scorecards used in evaluation are available for review.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; FY2027 funding cycle opened November 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit charitable and civic organizations serving residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating or enhancing services that positively impact City of Frederick residents; separate applications are recommended for each specific type of promotion activity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations serving residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit charitable and/or civic organization
Submit a separate application for each specific type of community promotion activity
Must attend one of two required virtual information sessions
All previous grant reporting must be up to date before applying
Must complete online application via Foundant portal
Complete a letter of agreement with the City before funds are distributed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Program Overview (PDF). 2. Ensure all prior grant reporting is up to date. 3. Attend one of two required virtual information sessions. 4. Complete and submit the online application through the Foundant portal at grantinterface.com. Funds are distributed after a letter of agreement is completed between the City and the organization.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frostburg Main Street Structural Stabilization Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial support for structural repairs on historic and commercial buildings along Frostburg's Main Street corridor. The program aims to address the most critical and expensive barriers to redevelopment — such as foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, and roof work — so that property owners can move forward with rehabilitation and return buildings to active use.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Frostburg and Allegany County Economic and Community Development (ACECD)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by $250,000 in state funds from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Strategic Demolition Fund (FY 2025). Grants cover structural repair costs including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, and roofing. Exact award amounts per applicant are not yet specified. Funding is expected to be competitive.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, tax-paying property owners of commercial or mixed-use buildings within Frostburg's Main Street district who need structural stabilization work before rehabilitation can begin.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural repairs including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, roofing, and other work that makes up the structural integrity of the building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district in Frostburg, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district
Property must be commercial or mixed-use (e.g., first-floor storefront with residential units above)
Property must be owned by a for-profit, tax-paying entity
Owner must be in good standing with the city, county, and state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: City staff manage applications and intake; county staff oversee fund distribution and compliance. A review committee evaluates applications based on a project rubric. Applications were expected to open in summer 2025. Interested property owners are urged to gather information about their properties' structural needs and project timelines before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown allocated $600,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds for eligible nonprofit organizations to apply for project funding. Projects must address one or more of these categories: Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 per category are available to eligible nonprofit organizations for projects addressing defined community needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status serving Hagerstown residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status
Submit IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter
Submit Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland SDAT (dated within past 30 days or dated screenshot showing current status)
Submit Project Budget including all current and anticipated funding sources
Submit evidence of active SAM.gov registration showing the Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Project must fall under at least one eligible category
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed application and all required supporting documents by 4:00 p.m. on September 1, 2023 to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org. Questions must be submitted by 4:00 p.m. August 25, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Admissions & Amusement Tax Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Visual and performing arts enterprises located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District are exempt from the State of Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax. Businesses must qualify for the exemption and notify the Maryland State Comptroller's Office, which eliminates the obligation to collect and remit this state tax. Registration is completed using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from the State of Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax for qualifying visual or performing arts enterprises located within the Hagerstown Arts & Entertainment District, eliminating the obligation to collect and remit this tax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Visual and performing arts enterprises located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from collecting and remitting the State of Maryland Admissions and Amusement Tax.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to enterprises within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District.
requirements_list: Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District
Must qualify for the exemption and notify the Maryland State Comptroller's Office
Must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Owners of properties in Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District can receive a 50% property tax credit for 10 years on the increase in assessed value resulting from a renovation that creates artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises. Both the City of Hagerstown and Washington County provide the credit. The credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by a qualifying artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. Properties already using the Enterprise Zone property tax credit are not eligible.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50% property tax credit on the increase in assessed value from a qualifying renovation, applied for 10 years. Applies only to the portion of the building occupied by the qualifying artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. Both the City of Hagerstown and Washington County provide the credit. Cannot be combined with the Enterprise Zone property tax credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District who renovate to create artist housing or arts and entertainment enterprise space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability on the increased assessed value resulting from qualifying renovation projects within the Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Hagerstown's designated Arts and Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District
Renovation must create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises
Credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
Property must not be utilizing the Enterprise Zone property tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department to apply for the property tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides matching grants to businesses and property owners in Hagerstown's City Center to improve storefront designs, façade elements, and commercial signage. The goal is to enhance building presentations, boost brand visibility, and increase customer awareness. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability. All projects must involve commercial or mixed-use buildings. Two tracks are available: a Commercial Sign grant (up to $1,500) and a Façade grant (up to $7,500), each requiring a 1:1 match from the applicant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% matching (1:1) reimbursement grant. Commercial Sign grants range from $250 to $1,500 (requiring a $250–$1,500 applicant match for a total project cost of $500–$3,000). Façade grants range from $2,500 to $7,500 (requiring a $2,500–$7,500 applicant match for a total project cost of $5,000–$15,000). Grants are subject to funding availability and awarded first-come, first-served.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Subject to funding availability; first-come, first-served
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners in Hagerstown's City Center with commercial or mixed-use buildings seeking to improve signage or building façades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving storefront designs, façade elements, and commercial signage on commercial or mixed-use buildings in the City Center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City Center area of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must pertain to a commercial or mixed-use building
Applicant must provide a 1:1 matching investment equal to the grant amount
Projects are subject to funding availability
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis
Full program guidelines apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the full program guidelines and complete the application form (both linked on the program page). Submit to the DCED team at DCED@Hagerstownmd.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund (HRLF) provides low-interest loans to small businesses and developers in Hagerstown, Maryland. Funds can be used for growth and expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, and façade enhancement, including land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery and equipment, working capital, and micro-enterprise activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate loans at PRIME plus 1% (minimum 3%). Loans range from $5,000 to $200,000 (or 80% of total project cost, whichever is less). Working capital loans are capped at $30,000; micro-enterprise loans up to $5,000. Loan term may not exceed 7 years (5 years for working capital). Borrowers must provide a minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less). Repayment begins within one month of construction completion or taking possession of purchased equipment. A non-refundable application fee based on the requested loan amount is required, along with a credit check.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and developers organized as a proprietorship, partnership, LLC, or corporation with annual sales under $5,000,000 for each of the last two years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growth and expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, façade enhancement, land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery and equipment purchase (with a useful life of at least 5 years), building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and developers located in Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a small business or developer organized as a proprietorship, partnership, LLC, or corporation
Annual business sales must be less than $5,000,000 for each of the last two years
Minimum loan amount is $5,000
Minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less)
Loan term may not exceed 7 years (5 years for working capital)
Repayment begins within one month of construction completion or taking possession of purchased equipment
Lease term must equal or exceed the loan term for leasehold improvements, and the City must secure a lien on the land or building
Credit check required
Non-refundable application fee required based on requested loan amount

Funds may not be used by non-profit institutions, gambling organizations, lending or investment organizations, or for land speculation, debt repayment/consolidation, management fees, franchise fees, refinancing, moving costs, or illegal activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Program Guidelines and Application from the City of Hagerstown website. Submit with required application fee and credit check authorization. A credit check will be conducted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partners in Economic Progress (PEP) Program offers incentives to building owners to renovate properties within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center, and assists with attracting businesses to renovated buildings. Incentives include an annual grant equal to City property tax for 5 years, utility benefits, parking benefits, rent assistance for new tenants, waiver of development fees, expedited permitting review, code flexibility, and consultation on historic tax credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Incentives include: (1) Annual grant equal to City property tax for 5 years; (2) 2 free equivalent dwelling units (EDUs) for utilities valued at $13,800; (3) 1 year free parking and 50% discount for 4 additional years; (4) Rent assistance up to $30,000 paid to property owner for first 2-3 years of a tenant business's operation; (5) Waiver of development fees including building permits, plan review, occupancy, and zoning fees; (6) Expedited review through Planning Department and Historic District Commission; (7) Code flexibility using Maryland Building Rehabilitation Code; (8) 2 hours of consultation on historic tax credits paid for by the City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and businesses seeking to renovate or lease space within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and improvement of commercial, residential, or mixed-use properties within the PEP Zone; attracting and supporting new or expanding businesses in PEP-eligible buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center of Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Project must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center
Minimum investment of $250,000 for commercial, $100,000 for residential, or $200,000 for mixed-use projects (excluding property acquisition costs)
Commercial projects must participate in the Enterprise Zone Program
Applicant must not be delinquent on any City or County taxes or other financial obligations to the City
Building and all core systems must meet all City of Hagerstown Code requirements
Residential and artist live-work spaces must meet minimum square footage requirements
Prior renovation projects completed after January 1, 2007 are eligible
For rent assistance, businesses must be new or existing businesses relocating to or expanding within the PEP Zone
Business must occupy first-floor retail, restaurant, or non-storefront commercial space in PEP approved buildings
Business must maintain a lease and operate for a minimum of 4 years

Eligible business types include: business/professional/cultural/medical offices, professional schools, educational services, medical and diagnostic laboratories, motion picture and sound recording, photo finishing, radio and television broadcasting, telecommunications, visual and performing arts studios and galleries, light manufacturing, artist live-work units, and fitness centers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply and receive approval from the PEP Committee. Approved developers must submit progress reports every 6 months, report square footage by use type upon completion of construction, and submit annual Enterprise Zone Tax Credit reports if applicable. Changes to approved development plans must be resubmitted for PEP Committee review.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sale of City-Owned Properties – Competitive Negotiated Sale Process
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown makes city-owned real estate available for purchase through a Competitive Negotiated Sale Process. Applications are evaluated based on the applicant's vision and plan for the property combined with an offer price. The goal is to return properties to the private sector for their highest and best use. Properties currently listed for sale include 14 N. Potomac St., Central Parking Lot, and 441 S. Potomac St.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned real estate is sold through a competitive negotiated process. Buyers submit an application describing their vision and plan for the property along with a purchase price offer. Properties currently listed for sale include 14 N. Potomac St., Central Parking Lot, and 441 S. Potomac St.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, individuals, developers, and nonprofits interested in purchasing city-owned real estate in Hagerstown for redevelopment or reuse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of city-owned property for redevelopment or private-sector use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties are located within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must submit a vision and plan for the property
Applicants must submit a purchase price offer
Applications are evaluated competitively on plan quality and offer price
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City's Department of Community and Economic Development or download the Program Guidelines and Competitive Negotiated Sale Application Form (PDF) from the city website. Submit the completed application with your development vision and offer price.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers grants to help revitalize vacant first-floor commercial storefronts in Hagerstown's Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area. The goal is to bring commercial spaces up to current code standards, reduce blight, preserve buildings, and create employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Hagerstown Department of Community & Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants have no minimum amount but a maximum of $50,000. Funds are disbursed only after all renovation work has been completed, verified by staff, and all required site inspection approvals and final receipts have been provided. Approved applicants receive a Letter of Commitment from the City of Hagerstown that can be used to assist in financing the project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or developers seeking to revitalize vacant first-floor commercial storefronts in Hagerstown's Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation of vacant first-floor commercial spaces to bring them up to current code standards, including rectifying code violations and completing improvements outlined in the development plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District in Hagerstown, MD, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area. Priority is given to projects on Main Street near Public Square.
requirements_list: Project must be located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District
Application must include a development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components
All work must comply with federal, State, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
All upgrades must be performed to City Code and regulated through the City's Planning and Code Administration Department
Funds disbursed only after staff verify all work is completed to Code, all required site inspections are approved, and final receipts are provided

Grant eligibility criteria include: economic impact, proximity to Public Square, renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition and code violation rectification, and length of prior vacancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form along with a development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components. The cross-department Review Committee evaluates applications based on eligibility criteria. Approved projects receive a Letter of Commitment from the City. Funds are disbursed after all work is completed and verified by staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown's Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Microenterprise Grant Program provides reimbursable grants of $2,500 to $5,000 to small, for-profit businesses with five or fewer employees (including owners) located in or primarily operating within Hagerstown. The program aims to expand employment opportunities for low-to-moderate income residents, support job creation and retention, revitalize vacant commercial spaces, and promote business growth and stabilization. Owner(s) must meet HUD low-to-moderate income limits to qualify. Funding is administered on a rolling basis as reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Hagerstown Department of Community and Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from $2,500 to $5,000 with no private match required. Funding is administered as a reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts after eligible expenses are incurred. The program operates on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline. Prior awardees must wait three years before reapplying, and no more than two grants may be awarded per household. Applications received after all funding is expended are placed on a waitlist. Funding cannot be used for real property improvements or rehabilitation, rent/mortgage or utility payments for home-based business occupancies, repayment of existing debt, or reimbursement of costs incurred before grant approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit microenterprise business owners (5 or fewer employees including owner) located in or primarily operating within Hagerstown whose household income is at or below HUD low-to-moderate income limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of business equipment, purchase of inventory, necessary fixed assets (machinery, IT equipment, vehicles), professional services including marketing and business promotion, technological infrastructure and upgrades, entrepreneurial training, and operational expenses including payroll, utilities, and rent/mortgage for commercial locations. Cannot be used for real property improvements or rehabilitation, political or sectarian activities, home-based business utilities/rent, repayment of existing debt, or reimbursement of costs incurred before grant approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown or conduct at least two-thirds of its business within the City of Hagerstown. Mobile (roving) businesses must document that at least two-thirds of their business activity occurs within city limits and must have been operating for at least six months. Must meet Federal CDBG income guidelines.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the City of Hagerstown or conduct at least two-thirds of its business within the City of Hagerstown (roving businesses must show at least two-thirds of activity within city limits and have at least 6 months of operating history)
Business must have five or fewer total employees including owner(s)
Business must be a private, for-profit entity
Business and owner(s) must be in good standing with the City and State of Maryland
Business and owner(s) must comply with all applicable City of Hagerstown regulations including the Land Management Code

Business must be established and operating for at least 12 months at time of application (newer businesses operating less than 12 months must submit a business plan and documentation of consultation with a business counseling service)
Owner's household income must be at or below HUD low-to-moderate income limits (e.g., $52,500 for 1-person household, $74,950 for 4-person household, up to $98,950 for 8-person household)
Ineligible businesses: those restricting access to minors (18+), rental or property investment businesses, and cannabis-based businesses
Previous awardees must wait three years before reapplying; maximum of two grants per household
Cannot use funds for real property improvements or rehabilitation
Cannot use funds for rent/mortgage or utility payments for home-based business occupancies
Cannot use funds to repay existing debt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online pre-screening questionnaire on the City website. City staff will confirm receipt and provide a full application. Submit the completed application with all required documents including tax returns, bank statements, profit and loss statement/business financials, lease agreement or home business permit, and income verification documents. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The prescreen does not guarantee funding and is the first step in determining eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each year, the City of Hagerstown makes Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds available to local non-profit organizations through a competitive grant program. Grants fund activities that provide decent housing, a sustainable living environment, or expanded economic opportunities for low- and moderate-income residents. The public service portion is typically about 15% of the City's overall CDBG entitlement grant. Applications are accepted for approximately one month, typically opening in mid-December and closing in mid-January. Applications are reviewed by City staff and the CDBG Citizen Advisory Committee, a draft Annual Action Plan is put on public display in April/May, and awards are announced by the Mayor and City Council in May or June following the application cycle.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Hagerstown Department of Community and Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public service grants funded by CDBG dollars. A portion (typically about 15%) of the City's total annual CDBG entitlement grant is made available to non-profit organizations through a competitive application process. Specific award amounts vary by year and are determined through the competitive review process. Awards are announced in May or June following the application cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY28 will open in late 2026; FY27 application is closed (FY27 deadline was January 9, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit 501(c)3 organizations located in or primarily serving low- and moderate-income residents of the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities that provide decent housing, a sustainable living environment, or expanded economic opportunities for low- and moderate-income persons. Must be a new or expanded level of public service. Activities must primarily benefit low- and moderate-income persons meeting Federal CDBG income limits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must be located in the City of Hagerstown or offer a service that primarily benefits residents of the City of Hagerstown. Activities must benefit low- and moderate-income persons meeting Federal CDBG income limits.
requirements_list: Must be a registered 501(c)3 non-profit
Must be located in the City of Hagerstown or offer a service that primarily benefits City of Hagerstown residents
Must meet a CDBG program national objective
Must provide an activity that is either new or an expanded level of public service
Activities must primarily benefit low- and moderate-income residents
Must meet Federal CDBG income guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open application period (typically mid-December to mid-January, approximately one month). Applications are reviewed by City staff and the CDBG Citizen Advisory Committee in late January/early February. A draft Annual Action Plan with funding recommendations is put on public display in April/May, the CDBG budget is approved by the Mayor and City Council in May/June, and official award notifications are sent in May/June.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center and City-Wide Redevelopment Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Two-track redevelopment grant program for projects in Hagerstown. The City Center track provides grants of $150,000–$250,000 for larger redevelopment projects in the city center, requiring a minimum 2:1 developer match (total project cost $450,000–$750,000+). The City-Wide track provides grants of $5,000–$25,000 for smaller redevelopment projects anywhere in the city, also requiring a minimum 2:1 developer match (total project cost $15,000–$75,000+). Both tracks are part of the City's Invest Hagerstown program.

City-Wide track: grants of $5,000–$25,000 with a minimum 2:1 developer match required (total project cost $15,000–$75,000+). Complete program guidelines apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Fire Suppression System Grant Program helps property owners install or upgrade National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)-compliant fire suppression systems by lowering the financial barriers associated with installing water service lines, fire lines, meter vaults, water meters, and related public utility infrastructure. Grants range from $7,500 to $50,000 and require a 1:1 match from the applicant, resulting in total project costs ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. The program operates on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to funding availability, and applies to residential, commercial, professional office, retail, and mixed-use buildings located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Hagerstown Department of Community and Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $50,000. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to the grant amount (1:1 match), resulting in total project costs ranging from $15,000 (minimum) to $100,000 (maximum). Eligible expenses include installation of automatic sprinkler systems, water service/fire line upgrades, installation or upgrade of meter vaults, and replacement of outdated sprinkler heads, piping, mains, and backflow devices. Fire suppression project water service installations must use service meters that are four inches or larger.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use buildings located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area seeking to install or upgrade NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of automatic sprinkler systems; water service/fire line upgrades; installation or upgrade of meter vaults; installation, upgrade, or replacement of sprinkler heads and piping; replacement of mains and backflow devices.

requirements_list: Project must involve a fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use building.
Project must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
Fire suppression system must be NFPA-compliant and meet current code standards.
Applicant must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown.
Total project cost must demonstrate a minimum 1:1 match (minimum total project cost is $15,000, including $7,500 grant and $7,500 match).
Fire suppression project water service installations must use service meters that are four inches or larger.
Application must align with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision for the city.
Program is subject to funding availability and operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Fire Suppression System Grant Application (linked on the program page) and review the full program guidelines. Submit the completed application to the City's Department of Community and Economic Development. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to funding availability. Contact dped@hagerstownmd.org with questions or requests for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants of up to $15,000 and low-interest loans to income-qualified homeowners in the City of Hagerstown for emergency repairs — defined as situations that are life-threatening or that prevent someone from living in decent, safe, and sanitary conditions. Eligible repairs may include items like roofs, furnaces, and porches. Funded through the City's Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) entitlement, with federal CDBG income requirements (FY2025-2026 limits set by HUD) applying. A low-interest loan option is also available for comprehensive property improvements beyond the emergency repair grant.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative (HHI) provides up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost assistance to reduce barriers to homeownership within the City of Hagerstown. The assistance is structured as a forgivable loan-to-grant, meaning no repayment is required if the recipient meets the program conditions. The program aims to reduce vacant homes and increase homeownership across city neighborhoods. Priority is given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown purchases vacant properties within city limits, renovates them, and sells them at the current appraised value to income-qualified individuals and families. The program is funded by the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and aims to create affordable homeownership opportunities. Applicants must be pre-qualified for a mortgage loan and have household income below the program limits. The program may be combined with other mortgage assistance programs such as the Maryland Mortgage Program, including down payment and closing cost assistance. The city pays a 2.5% realtor commission if a buyer uses a realtor and successfully completes the purchase.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown Department of Parks & Engineering allows residents to memorialize a special person or life event by donating a tree or bench placed in one of the City's parks. Donors can honor occasions such as births, deaths, weddings, anniversaries, and graduations. A $500 donation funds planting of a tree with an engraved tag; a $1,500 donation funds installation of an engraved metal bench with a plaque.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: For a $500 donation, the City supplies and plants a 6-foot conifer or 2-inch caliper deciduous tree in a City park with an engraved tag and acknowledgement letter. For a $1,500 donation, the City provides and installs a 6-foot powder-coated metal bench with an engraved plaque in a City park. All donations are tax deductible. Trees that die within the first three years are replaced by the City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form, then return it to the City of Hagerstown Department of Parks & Engineering at 1 East Franklin Street, Hagerstown, MD 21740. structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides free bicycle racks to businesses, property owners, and non-profits near their storefronts. The city purchases and installs inverted-U style bike racks either in public rights-of-way or on private property (with a signed agreement). Racks are distributed on a first come, first served basis and are meant for public use, available to anyone at any time. Business owners or property managers who lack bicycle parking near their shop or office may apply to receive a rack provided and installed at no cost.

Racks are distributed on a first come, first served basis. Racks require a 72" x 24" parking space and must allow at least a five-foot clear walkway if placed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path. Racks placed on private property require a signed agreement with the city.

Customers using SNAP/EBT or Farmers Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) checks receive a 1:1 match in tokens to spend on locally grown fruits, vegetables, meat, cheese, and dairy at the market.

Must shop at the Rockville Farmers Market
Matching funds are provided once per customer per market visit

For FMNP-WIC: Use your FMNP-WIC checks to buy produce from a vendor, get a receipt, and bring it to the information tent to receive free matching MMM tokens.
