structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents seeking free trees for their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on residential or eligible properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents within the City of Rockville, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the Environment and Sustainability Newsletter for updates on upcoming giveaway dates and registration details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides matching reimbursement funds to Rockville residents and property owners who have made improvements to their properties to reduce future flood damage. The program covers up to 50% of approved project costs, up to a maximum of $5,000, distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. The program is administered in partnership between the City of Rockville and the Chesapeake Bay Trust.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to 50% of the total costs for approved flood mitigation improvements, with a maximum reimbursement of $5,000 per homeowner. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applications are reviewed and processed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Only approved measures are eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents and single-family property owners who have made or plan to make approved improvements to their properties to mitigate future flood damage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds:
Reimbursement for approved property improvements that reduce future flood damage, including: structural modifications (flood vents, drain tiles, sump pumps and battery backups, floodgates/panels, interior walls); window and door protection (custom window wells, watertight covers, permanent glass protection, floodgates, basement window protection); equipment and materials (sandless sandbags, flood socks, Quick Dams
def, sandbags, interior concrete sealers and waterproof paints, flood-resistant building materials, portable submersible pumps and hoses, utility covers); landscape and drainage improvements (surface grading, earthen berms, protective flood walls, impermeable/water-resistant material around foundations, French drain systems, disconnect/plug internal floor drains); utility elevation and protection (HVAC, appliances, electrical outlets/breakers, generator quick-connect systems); and flood alert systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and property owners within the City of Rockville, Maryland only. Property-level eligibility may depend on location within Rockville flood zones.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident or property owner
Property must be a single-family home or residential property
Improvements must be approved flood mitigation measures listed under FMAP-approved practices
Must have made or plan to make eligible improvements to the property to mitigate future flood damage
Funds distributed on a first-come, first-served basis
Only approved measures will be reimbursed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust application portal at rockvillemd.gov/services/apply-for-flood-mitigation-assistance. The Chesapeake Bay Trust will review and process applications and is available to answer questions at rockvillefloodmitigation@cbtrust.org or 410-974-2941 ext. 131. Additional information including eligibility criteria and a list of approved flood-proofing measures is available at rockvillemd.gov/floodassistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Latino Youth Development Program promotes positive, team-oriented activities and physical exercise for Latino male students in Rockville middle and high schools. Students participate in soccer leagues, field trips, summer camp, life skills workshops, academic guidance, and college tours. Case management is also provided to students' families. Students earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours through community service activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program providing soccer league registration, summer camp (five weeks in July), weekly study hall and academic support, life skills workshops, field trips, college tours, and case management for families. Transportation is provided to all students at stops within the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Latino male students in grades 6–12 enrolled in the Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARMS) program and attending Earle B. Wood or Julius West middle schools, or Richard Montgomery or Rockville high schools in Rockville, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Soccer league participation, summer camp activities, field trips, academic tutoring and guidance, life skills workshops, college tours, SSL hours, and family case management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must attend an eligible Rockville-area middle or high school (Earle B. Wood, Julius West, Richard Montgomery, or Rockville High School) and reside within or near the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in the Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARMS) program
Must attend a qualifying Rockville middle or high school (grades 6–12)
Must attend weekly after-school meetings
Must attend weekly practices
Must attend all weekend games
Must attend all field trips
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students may be referred by school counselors or administrators, or may self-refer using the Student Referral Form available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based program at Maryvale Elementary School in Rockville that provides accessible services to at-risk children and their families to improve school adjustment and performance. Services include health and mental health support, social services, educational support, after-school and summer programming, parenting workshops, and help with food, utility, and housing problems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free school-based services including individual, family, and group counseling; after-school and summer programming (academic mentoring, therapeutic recreation, enrichment); parenting and nutrition workshops; assistance with food, utility, and housing problems; help completing financial and medical assistance forms; and community outreach and prevention programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk children and their families in the Maryvale Elementary School community in Rockville, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to improve children's well-being and academic success, including mental health counseling, educational support, and assistance accessing social services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Maryvale Elementary School, 1010 First St., Rockville, MD 20850
requirements_list: Must be a student or family associated with Maryvale Elementary School
Children must be at-risk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Fadeke Adepoju at the Housing and Community Development Department, Community Services Division by phone or email during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.).

structured_extraction.program_name: Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires most private development projects in the City of Rockville to include spending on a publicly accessible art project, based on an annually adjusted fee schedule. The ordinance encourages the use and incorporation of public art in private development to enrich community character, improve quality of life, and foster economic vitality.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private development projects must include an expenditure for a publicly accessible art project. Contribution amounts are determined by an annually adjusted fee schedule based on the Builder's Cost Index. The 2025-2026 fee schedule is effective February 2025 through June 30, 2026. Developers may fulfill the requirement through one or more of six options: installing art on site, presenting art on site, making a monetary contribution to the City's Art in Public Places Program, providing an arts space, providing arts-based infrastructure, or a combination of options. Fees are calculated by project type (residential units, commercial square footage, or industrial square footage) using tiered per-unit/per-sq-ft rates. Eligible costs include consultant and artist fees, freight, shipping, fabrication, installation, purchase of arts-based infrastructure, and the percent of construction costs associated with an arts space; consultant fees are capped at 10% of the required contribution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers undertaking residential, commercial, or industrial construction or redevelopment projects in the City of Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding a publicly accessible art project as part of a private development. Acceptable uses include: installation or commissioning of visual, literary, or performing artworks on-site; building and outfitting arts spaces (studios, theaters, offices); purchase, delivery, and installation of arts-based infrastructure (audio/visual equipment); monetary donations to the City's Art in Public Places Program for a future public artwork in the planning area of the project; and monetary contributions to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit arts and culture organizations. Consultant and artist fees, freight, shipping, fabrication, and installation are all eligible costs, with consultant fees capped at 10% of the required contribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland only. Contributions to the Art in Public Places Program are designated for a future public artwork installed in the planning area of the project.
requirements_list: Must be a private development project located within the City of Rockville
Project must not be exempt under the ordinance (Chapter 4, Article IV of the Rockville City Code, ordinance 3-04)
Must include an expenditure for a publicly accessible art project based on the annually adjusted fee schedule
Contribution amount is calculated by project type: residential (per unit), commercial (per square foot), or industrial (per square foot) using tiered rates
Maximum 10% of required contribution may be applied to consultant fees
If contributing to an arts organization, the organization must be an eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit arts and culture organization meeting program criteria
Compliance must be achieved before permit issuance and project completion before Certificate of Occupancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Development Review Committee identifies AIPD applicability and issues comment letter. 2. Developer meets with Arts and Culture Program staff to discuss compliance options. 3. Complete the AIPD Application form, entering unit counts and/or commercial/industrial square footage and calculating the total required contribution using the tiered fee schedule. 4. Select one or more of the six contribution options (install art on site, present art on site, monetary contribution, provide arts space, provide arts-based infrastructure, or a combination). 5. Attach required documentation per the AIPD Implementation Manual. 6. Submit the completed form and attachments to the assigned planner and Anne O'Dell. Approval must be obtained before permit issuance and completion must occur before Certificate of Occupancy. Arts and Culture Program staff will collaborate with developers to resolve circumstances that might prevent project completion after an artist contract is signed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resources for Federal Employees and Contractors
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides services and delayed payment options for federal employees and contractors who live in Rockville and are affected by a federal government shutdown. Eligible residents may qualify for delayed payments with no penalties on city services including child care, water and sewer utilities, pet licenses, and residential parking permit fee waivers. Landlords and tenants can also seek rent negotiation assistance to prevent eviction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Delayed payment options with no penalties on child care, water and sewer utility bills, pet license fees, and food services. Residential parking permit fee waivers. Rent negotiation assistance to prevent eviction. Applicants must provide proof of Rockville residency and federal employment or federal contractor status (e.g., federal employee/contractor ID badge or employer letter).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Federal employees and contractors who live within the City of Rockville and are impacted by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferred payment of city-provided child care, water and sewer utilities, pet licenses, and food assistance. Residential parking permit fee waivers. Rent negotiation support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must reside within the City of Rockville
Must be a federal employee or federal contractor
Must provide proof of Rockville residency
Must provide proof of federal employment or contractor status (e.g., federal employee/contractor ID badge or employer letter)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the relevant city department for each service (child care, utility billing, rent assistance, pet licenses, parking permits). Provide proof of Rockville residency and federal employment or contractor status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program (City of Rockville)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program is a federal grant program administered by the City of Rockville for housing and community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods. Funded projects may include home repair, facility upgrades, and supportive housing improvements. Public services are explicitly excluded from FY 2027 funding.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are awarded as grants to eligible organizations for housing and community development capital and physical improvement projects. In FY 2025, $263,000 was allocated in total across multiple projects. FY 2027 grants will fund projects for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Public services are not eligible for FY 2027 funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations and government/quasi-government entities seeking funding for housing and community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods in Rockville, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing rehabilitation, facility upgrades, safety improvements, supportive housing maintenance, and other capital and physical community development projects benefiting low- and moderate-income households. Public services are not an eligible use in FY 2027.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations serving the City of Rockville, Maryland. County-level review is required but funding is limited to the City of Rockville service area. Administering office: 111 Maryland Avenue, Second Floor, Rockville MD 20850.
requirements_list: Projects must benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods
Primary applicants must be 501(c)(3) non-profit or government/quasi-government agencies
Applicants must complete the Eligibility Form in the online grant portal to determine qualification
Applications must be submitted by October 17, 2025 at 5:00 P.M.
Applicants are encouraged to attend a virtual technical session and the public hearing at Rockville City Hall
Public services are not eligible for FY 2027 funding — only capital and physical improvements are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and review the FY 2027 guidelines. 2. Attend one of two virtual technical sessions (Aug. 21 or Sept. 16, 2025). 3. Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com, complete the Eligibility Form, and submit the application by October 17, 2025 at 5:00 P.M. 4. Optionally attend the public hearing at Rockville City Hall on Sept. 8, 2025. 5. Mayor & Council approvals expected by December 31, 2025; County review January/February 2026; funds available after October 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Empowerment Matching Grant Program helps neighbors and community groups work together on projects that support the health, vitality, and inclusivity of their neighborhood. The City of Rockville offers competitive grants ranging from $500 to $1,000 to groups that match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours. Projects must benefit residents within Rockville city limits and address at least one of three objectives: building community, community improvement projects, or livability initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants typically ranging from $500 to $1,000. Applicants must match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours (volunteer hours valued at $29.95/hour). Total cash matching funds and in-kind donations must match or exceed the amount requested. All funds provided are subject to taxes. Funds must be used by Dec. 14, 2026, and any unused funds must be returned to the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighbors, neighborhood associations, civic associations, homeowners associations, community groups, and student groups within Rockville city limits who want to collaborate on community-building projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs or projects that promote neighborhood association development, community inclusion and diversity, enhancement of shared spaces, strengthening community identity, or livability initiatives such as safety improvements, serving low-income residents, or welcoming newcomers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must benefit residents living within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: At least three members in the applying group
Designate one individual to manage grant contracts and funds
Provide documentation of authorization if applying on behalf of an established organization
Match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours; total cash matching funds and in-kind donations must match or exceed the amount requested
Volunteer hours are valued at $29.95/hour for matching purposes
Submit project documentation (receipts, two visual items, brief report) by Dec. 18, 2026
Return any unused funds by Dec. 18, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and complete the budget worksheet to estimate costs and matching funds. 2. Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com and complete the Eligibility Form and full application by 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 5, 2025. 3. Receive award notification by Feb. 13, 2026. 4. Complete project and submit documentation (receipts, visuals, report) through the online portal by Dec. 18, 2026. 5. Return any unused funds to the City of Rockville by Dec. 18, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) (City of Rockville)
structured_extraction.program_description: HEAP provides one-time financial assistance of up to $1,000 to eligible City of Rockville residents living in housing with documented energy inefficiencies. The program helps residents access weatherization services, home energy assessments, and comprehensive energy audits, and supplements the cost of utility efficiency retrofits. A community services referral coordinator connects residents to additional public and private resources as needed.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance of up to $1,000 to cover eligible energy-efficient upgrades such as insulation, air sealing, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace repairs, and health and safety items (e.g. mold remediation, lead hazard removal, radon mitigation). Funds are issued as a check to the utility or contractor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income City of Rockville residents (at or below 60% Area Median Income) who are PEPCO, BGE, or Potomac Edison customers and have already been approved for MEAP, EmPOWER Maryland LIEEP, Weatherization Assistance Program, or Enhanced Weatherization Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient home upgrades including attic/floor/wall insulation, blower door air sealing, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items such as mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke/carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, lead hazard removal, and approved electrical repairs. Cannot be used for past-due utility bills or non-energy-efficient household repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside within the corporate city limits of Rockville, MD for at least six months (180+ days) prior to applying.
requirements_list: Must reside within Rockville city limits at the time of application and for at least six months (180+ days) prior
Must meet 60% Area Median Income (AMI) guidelines (2018 thresholds: 1-person $24,280 up to 5-person $58,840 plus $8,640 per additional person)
Must be a previous or new recipient of Rockville's Emergency Assistance Program
Must use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating
Must be a PEPCO, BGE, or Potomac Edison customer
Must have already been approved for MEAP, EmPOWER Maryland LIEEP, Weatherization Assistance Program, or Enhanced Weatherization Program
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills before the retrofit
Must provide documentation of a comprehensive home energy audit
Renters must provide landlord or property manager approval for energy-efficient retrofits
Must agree to reside at the retrofitted property for one year after the retrofit is completed
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills after the retrofit
Property must be the applicant's primary residence
Must demonstrate prior rent payments have been made for the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the eligibility criteria and eligible/ineligible expenses on the program page. Download and complete the application form. Submit the completed application to the Community Services Division by email at hcd@rockvillemd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville requires some for-sale properties to be offered to eligible buyers at below-market prices through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program. First-time homebuyers who meet income and eligibility requirements can purchase an affordable, income-restricted home in Rockville at prices set at 50%, 60%, or 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Buyers are placed on a waiting list and contacted when MPDU homes become available. Non-U.S. citizens may also apply. After the 30-year control period expires, the owner may rent out, sell at market price, or keep as primary residence, but must pay the City 50% of excess appreciation on the first post-control sale.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible first-time homebuyers can purchase a for-sale home at a below-market, affordable price set by the city. Homes are priced at 50%, 60%, or 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) depending on the unit. Buyers must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000, commit to owner-occupancy for a full 30-year MPDU control period, and follow city guidelines if selling before that period ends. After the 30-year control period expires, the owner may rent out, sell at market price, or keep as primary residence, but must pay the City 50% of excess appreciation on the first post-control sale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers, including non-U.S. citizens, who are Rockville residents or workers and meet household income limits based on AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of an affordable for-sale home in Rockville at a below-market price. Home must be used as a primary residence throughout the 30-year control period. During the control period, permanent improvements to the unit are allowed (up to 10% of the owner's initial purchase price) and may be credited toward the resale price; eligible costs include materials, professional fees, contractor costs, and permit fees. Accessibility upgrades are not subject to the 10% cap. Owner labor, tools/equipment, and cosmetic/routine maintenance items are not eligible improvement costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to buyers who currently live or work in the City of Rockville, Maryland. Priority on the waiting list is given to current Rockville residents or workers, households with members over 55, and larger households.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (no home ownership by any household member in the past 5 years)
Must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000
Home must be the buyer's primary residence for the full 30-year MPDU control period
Home may not be rented to others without written City permission
Must qualify for bank financing
Pre-qualification letter must be notarized, on lender letterhead, and renewed annually if not yet purchased
Full disclosure of verified household income from all sources required; non-disclosure results in rejection
Credit check and asset verification required
All household members over 18 must submit proof of income
Household gross income must fall within the applicable AMI limit at time of signing a sales agreement
Cannot own a second home during the 30-year control period
Can only sell through the MPDU program at a City-determined price during the control period
Refinancing requires City approval
Must commit to owning the home for 30 years; if selling earlier, must follow city resale guidelines, including 50% profit-sharing with the City on first post-control sale
Non-U.S. citizens may apply
Must receive copy of recorded MPDU covenants and City Code Chapter 13.5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Attend a six-hour First-Time Homebuyer Class through Montgomery County's Housing Initiative Partnership or any HUD-approved counseling agency and obtain a completion certificate. 2. Obtain a mortgage pre-qualification letter (notarized, on lender letterhead) from a bank lender using the city's sample lender letter; the letter is valid for one year and must be renewed if it expires before purchase. 3. Complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online (or request a PDF by emailing rockvillempdu@rockvillemd.gov). The application must be renewed every two years. Once approved, an MPDU certificate is emailed within 3–4 weeks and the household is placed on the waiting list. For resale or refinance requests, submit the applicable request form with HUD-1 settlement sheet and original improvement documentation (receipts).

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers emergency financial assistance to eligible Rockville residents facing temporary financial crises. The program helps cover evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs. Referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial counseling, and employment services are also available.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency financial assistance for expenses such as rent/eviction prevention, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental bills, and food. Referrals for food, clothing, financial counseling, and employment services are also provided. Residents over 60 needing prescription cost help under $200 should contact the department directly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible City of Rockville residents experiencing financial emergencies, including furloughed federal employees and residents over 60 needing prescription assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eviction prevention (rent arrears), utility shut-off prevention or reconnection, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be current residents of the City of Rockville for a minimum of six months.
requirements_list: Must be a current Rockville city resident for at least six months

Rent assistance requires a current eviction notice from the court (e.g., Summons to Appear for Failure to Pay Rent, Writ or Warrant of Restitution, or Final Eviction Notice from the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office)
Utility assistance requires a current shut-off notice or already-disconnected service
Must demonstrate financial need due to job loss, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of a family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or other financial emergency
Must first apply for emergency assistance through Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) before receiving City of Rockville assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Apply for emergency assistance through Montgomery County DHHS first. 2. Montgomery County DHHS submits a referral to the City of Rockville on behalf of eligible residents. 3. Once you receive a referral, call 240-314-8300 to schedule an appointment with the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funded by the federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program, this initiative helps eligible low-to-moderate income Rockville homeowners pay for home repairs and improvements. It covers code deficiencies such as roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation. Lead-based paint testing and remediation may also be covered. The program prioritizes repairs based on severity of need.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home improvement work is performed at no upfront cost to the homeowner, up to a maximum of $25,000 per household. The assistance is structured as a no-interest forgivable loan secured by a lien on the property. No monetary loan is issued directly. The lien is forgiven at 20% per year over five years. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within five years of work completion, the homeowner must repay a percentage of the contract price corresponding to the remaining unforgiven balance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income Rockville homeowners (owner-occupants only) who meet income and asset eligibility requirements and need repairs to correct code deficiencies in their primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, and lead-based paint remediation. Work must address code deficiencies, not general property improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to homeowners within the City of Rockville, Maryland. Applicants who do not live within City of Rockville city limits are not eligible.
requirements_list: The home must be the owner's primary residence.
The owner must not own another home or condominium.
The owner must not owe more than the home's assessed value.
Total assets must not exceed $150,000.
Property taxes must be current.
Household income must not exceed the program's gross income limits based on family size (e.g., $68,500 for a one-person household; $97,800 for a four-person household, effective May 2024).
If the home was built before 1978, lead testing is required.
Applicant must live within the City of Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Mail a completed eligibility assessment application to the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department. 2. After the assessment is accepted, a rehabilitation specialist will contact you to complete a full eligibility review — submit tax returns, income statements, insurance policy, mortgage statements, and bank statements. 3. Materials are reviewed and work is prioritized by the rehabilitation specialist; review takes 7–10 business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Safe Waters: Swim Scholarship Program for Youth with Autism
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program established in memory of Ace Alexander that provides financial support for inclusive swim lessons at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The program aims to create a safe, inclusive swim instruction environment that promotes water safety, physical development, and family engagement.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships covering swim lesson fees for up to 10 children per cycle. Scholarship covers registration for one class season (single course) of inclusive swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for one child. Specific dollar amounts are not stated; see the scholarship application for details.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until the 10 scholarships are awarded
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 3–10 with a confirmed ASD diagnosis who are residents of the City of Rockville and meet financial eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One class season of inclusive swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for one child, held in person.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville to be eligible for scholarship consideration. Lessons held in-person at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center (Rockville, MD).
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3–10 with a confirmed ASD diagnosis
Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Commitment to attend in-person swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
Youth must be ready to engage in group swim lessons
Adult must be present at facility during lessons
Proof of residency required (current City of Rockville water/sewage bill, property tax bill, or state-issued ID with Rockville address)

Must meet at least one financial requirement: TCA/SNAP/TEMHA/WPA award letter, medical assistance, rental assistance, shelter residency, SSI, MCPS FARMS, Care for Kids, MEAP, Montgomery County HHS Rental Assistance, Maryland unemployment benefits, or WIC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Scholarship Application. Email the completed form to programaccess@rockvillemd.gov. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis by the Rockville Safe Waters Committee until 10 scholarships are awarded. Contact 240-314-8611 or programaccess@rockvillemd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that helps Rockville residents ages 60 and older pay for senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships. Administered by the City of Rockville Department of Recreation and Parks, Senior Social Services.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participant pays 50% of the actual cost of the program or membership. The fund subsidizes up to $50.00 per quarter. Assistance can be used for trips, classes, and memberships.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 60 and older who need financial assistance to participate in senior recreation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships. Subsidy capped at $50.00 per quarter; participant covers 50% of actual cost.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must be age 60 or older

Income verification required with supporting documentation (accepted forms: W-2, Social Security/VA/pension letters, Medicaid/Food Stamps/SSI documentation, pay stubs, family support letter, tax form, or other)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8810 for additional information and to apply. A downloadable application form is available at https://www.rockvillemd.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Senior-Assistance-Fund-Application.pdf. The application requires name, address, phone, date of birth, income amount and source, and proof of income documentation. Applicant and staff signatures with dates are required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Support Services – Community Resources and Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville Senior Center provides personalized services to seniors and residents in need, including resource referrals, emergency financial information, home and hospital visits, counseling resources, notary services, and financial aid to qualified candidates for recreational classes and membership.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers personalized resource referrals, emergency financial information, home and hospital visits, counseling resources, notary services, and financial aid for qualified candidates to attend recreational classes and obtain memberships. Spanish-speaking staff available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville senior residents and those in need of community resource referrals or financial assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Resource referrals, emergency financial information, counseling, notary services, and financial aid for recreational classes and memberships
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville residents
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must qualify for financial aid (for recreational class/membership assistance)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8816 or 240-314-8817 for more information. A Spanish speaker is available if needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Support Services – Transportation Subsidy (City of Rockville)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville Senior Center provides free bus-shuttle service and taxi subsidies to eligible seniors. The shuttle serves all Rockville residents age 60 and older, while bus and taxi subsidies are available to seniors living within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
