structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville residents age 60 and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from destinations via city bus-shuttle service or subsidized bus and taxi fares
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a City of Rockville resident; bus and taxi subsidies limited to those living within Rockville city limits
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older
Must be a City of Rockville resident
Reservation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8810 to make a reservation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The TERRIFIC Bicycle Award is a character-building program for Rockville students in grades 1–5. Children complete 6 out of 16 good deeds — such as volunteering, helping neighbors, or keeping a clean school environment — to demonstrate Trustworthiness, Earnestness, Respect, Responsibility, Involvement, Fairness, Industriousness, and Care. Students who complete the challenge are invited to a special event where they receive a free refurbished bicycle and helmet and are recognized by the Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible students receive a free refurbished bicycle and helmet upon completing the program's good-deed challenges. The program is limited to 80 participants per cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in grades 1–5 who live in or attend school in Rockville, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free refurbished bicycle and helmet awarded to students who complete the character-building challenge.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a student in grades 1–5
Must register during the open registration window (limited to 80 participants)
Must complete 6 out of 16 designated good deeds
Must submit completed form postmarked by April 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online during the registration window (January 20 – February 14, 2026). Selected participants are notified in late February and begin completing good deeds on March 1. Participants submit their completed form by April 30. Awardees receive bikes at a special event on May 16, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that helps Rockville residents ages 18 and younger pay for City of Rockville recreation and childcare program fees. The fund covers most of the program fee after the participant pays a $15 contribution, up to set maximums per session and per family.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships cover program fees beyond a $15 participant co-pay. Up to $100 per person per session (fall, winter, spring, summer) and $1,000 maximum per family. For summer camp, up to $175 per youth per camp session and $1,000 maximum per child. Any remaining balance must be paid by the participant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 18 and younger who need financial assistance to participate in recreation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation and childcare program fees for City of Rockville programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must be age 18 or younger
Participant must pay $15 toward each program fee
Limited number of scholarships available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8620 or email registration@rockvillemd.gov to apply or learn more.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides school- and community-based mental health counseling for Rockville residents who are uninsured or unable to access counseling on their own. The program focuses on early intervention and prevention for school-age children (ages 4–18), using a short-term model of up to 12 sessions. Services include individual and group counseling for anger management, managing emotions, social skills, and school transitions.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Rockville, Community Services Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized short-term counseling of up to 12 sessions, provided by licensed professional counselors, licensed master's-level social workers, or supervised clinical interns. Both individual and group sessions are available, with guardian participation strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or underserved school-age children (ages 4–18) who live in or attend school in Rockville, MD, and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health counseling covering anger management, managing emotions, social skills development, and transitions to middle or high school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in or attend school within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Must be between 4 and 18 years old
Must live in or attend school in Rockville
Must be uninsured or unable to access mental health services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Services Division by phone at 240-314-8306 or email at counseling@rockvillemd.gov to request an appointment and complete eligibility screening.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax benefits available to qualifying artists and arts and entertainment enterprises located within the Salisbury Arts & Entertainment (A&E) District. Benefits include a real property tax credit for renovation or new construction, an income tax subtraction modification for income from artistic work sold by qualifying resident artists (eliminating state and local income tax on that income), and an exemption from the Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges by qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises or resident artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tax benefits are available: (1) A real property tax credit for renovation of existing buildings or construction of new buildings for use by qualifying residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises. The City of Salisbury offers this credit for 6 years, up to the percentage set by local legislation, applied to the increased assessed value from qualifying renovations. (2) An income tax subtraction modification allowing qualifying residing artists to deduct income from artistic work created and sold within the district before state and local income taxes are calculated — effectively eliminating state and local income tax on that qualifying income. (3) An exemption from Maryland's Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges by qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises or qualifying residing artists in the district.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Bob Young, Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying residing artists and arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit or nonprofit entities dedicated to visual or performing arts) located within the Salisbury Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits and exemptions reduce property tax liability on renovated or newly constructed arts-related buildings, eliminate state and local income tax on qualifying artistic income, and exempt gross receipts from admission or amusement charges from the Admission and Amusement Tax.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the designated Salisbury Arts & Entertainment District in Salisbury, Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise as defined under Maryland law.
Property must be located within the Salisbury A&E District.
For property tax credit: building must be renovated or newly constructed for use by a qualifying residing artist or A&E enterprise; renovation must require a building permit.
For income tax subtraction: artist must reside and sell artistic work within the district; single-member LLCs may qualify as individuals.
For Admission and Amusement Tax exemption: entity must be a qualifying A&E enterprise or qualifying residing artist charging admissions or amusement fees within the district.
The Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation determines on a case-by-case basis whether an establishment qualifies as an A&E enterprise.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualifying artists and venues should contact the Office of the Maryland Comptroller for the income tax subtraction and Admission and Amusement Tax exemption. For the property tax credit, contact the local office of the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Complete the applicable state tax forms (e.g., Maryland Form 502AE for the income tax subtraction modification).

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy A Home, Build A Business
structured_extraction.program_description: A City of Salisbury program that encourages people to buy a home and build a business in Salisbury. The program offers down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchase (up to $5,000 as a 5-year forgivable lien) and up to $500 toward business expenses, administered through Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (SNHS). Local businesses have added additional incentives for qualifying participants, such as a $1,000 gift certificate from Outten Brothers of Salisbury toward new furniture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Down payment and closing cost assistance up to $5,000 (5-year forgivable lien, owner-occupied, borrower contributes minimum $1,000); up to $500 toward business expenses for qualifying participants who also complete the home purchase component; plus additional incentives from local partner businesses including a $1,000 gift certificate toward new furniture from Outten Brothers of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College juniors, seniors, and recent graduates (within past 5 years of program application); young entrepreneurs with business ideas; and potential homebuyers looking to buy a home and build a business within the City of Salisbury, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home purchase down payment and closing costs (up to $5,000); business expenses (up to $500); partner incentives can be used toward new furniture and potentially other goods/services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Both home purchase and business establishment must be within the City Limits of Salisbury, Maryland (Wicomico County).
requirements_list: Must qualify for the Buy A Home, Build A Business program
Home must be owner-occupied within City Limits of Salisbury
Down payment/closing cost assistance up to $5,000 with a 5-year forgivable lien
SNHS Homebuyer Education class required prior to settlement
Income restrictions apply
Compatible with FHA loans
Borrower must contribute a minimum of $1,000
Ratified sales contract required
$60 recording fee not included in assistance
Build A Business component (up to $500) is contingent on qualifying for the Buy A House component
Must have a business plan to qualify for business assistance
Business must be established within City Limits of Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (SNHS) directly for information. SNHS is located at 540 Riverside Drive, Suite #18, Salisbury, MD 21801 (www.salisburynhs.org). A program flyer is available for download.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to help businesses located within the Main Street District recover from the economic impacts of COVID-19. Each eligible business can receive up to $20,000 as a one-time, no-repayment grant. Funds can be used for payroll, sick leave, rent or mortgage payments, supply chain costs, PPE, safety improvements, and other COVID-related business needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of up to $20,000 per business entity. No repayment required. Due to funding constraints, not all eligible applications may be fully funded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury, MD that have been negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees; maintaining payroll and retaining employees; meeting increased costs due to supply chain disruptions; past-due or future rent or mortgage payments; repaying past-due or future obligations; purchasing PPE or spending on safety measures; building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread; business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19; other COVID-related recovery uses with justification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area.
requirements_list: Must have a physical location in the designated Main Street area
Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgments prior to March 5
Home-based businesses are not eligible
Churches are not eligible
Banks and financial institutions are not eligible
Investment real-estate entities are not eligible (unless applying for payments for a business in the Main Street area or COVID-related investments on a property in the area)
Food trucks are not eligible
Government agencies are not eligible
Contractors/construction/service repair-based businesses are not eligible (unless applying for COVID-related investments on a property in the Main Street area)
Employees receiving sick leave or payroll support must spend over 50% of their time working in the Main Street area
Limited to one award per business entity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open application period. Applications are graded by a committee based on: the degree the business was negatively impacted by COVID, how funds would help recovery, and the business's contribution to the Main Street area vitality. Applicants are notified of award decisions around March 5. Funded businesses must later submit proof of receipts and a use-of-funds narrative.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time micro-grant program funded by donations from Delmarva Power and the City of Salisbury's Revolving Loan Fund to help small businesses in Salisbury that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and related Maryland State Executive Orders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 with no repayment required, limited to one award per business entity. Awards are distributed via a lottery system among eligible applicants. Tier 1 applicants (mandated to fully close) receive priority; remaining funds are then lotteried among Tier 2 applicants (mandated to partially close).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small for-profit businesses with a physical location in the City of Salisbury that were impacted by COVID-19 and related state executive orders, with no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees affected by COVID-19; payroll maintenance and employee retention; increased costs from supply chain disruptions; rent or mortgage payments; repaying obligations due to revenue losses; purchasing PPE or spending on safety measures to reduce COVID-19 spread.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury. Businesses within the Revolving Loan Boundary area are eligible for the full program; businesses outside that boundary but meeting other criteria are eligible for the Delmarva Power-funded lottery portion.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and the City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury
Must have no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020
Must be engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland's State of Emergency with a relevant license/permit showing mandated partial or full closure
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgments prior to March 5, 2020

Home-based businesses, churches, medical service providers, non-profits, banks and financial institutions, investment real estate entities, food trucks, national franchises, government agencies, and contractors/construction/service repair businesses are NOT eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or by email to businessdevelopment@salisbury.md. Applications are reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness. Approved applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated full closure) or Tier 2 (mandated partial closure) and entered into a lottery. Awardees are selected at random and receive the grant check by mail. Awardees must complete a disbursement form and provide receipts within 60 days of City approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Summer Youth Employment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid 8-week summer employment program for local high school students in the City of Salisbury. Participants work in various City departments to gain workforce readiness and career-specific skills. The program is operated by the City of Salisbury in partnership with Junior Achievement of the Eastern Shore and the Wicomico County Board of Education. It includes structured learning, mentoring, resume writing guidance, and soft skills development. Participants may work up to 28 hours per week over the 8-week period. Applications open annually in January for the following summer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid employment for up to 28 hours per week over an 8-week period (June 22 – August 14). Participants also receive mentoring, resume writing guidance, soft skills development, and access to local business resources through Junior Achievement of the Eastern Shore and the Wicomico County Board of Education.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Summer 2026 are now closed; Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students entering 10th–12th grade for the 2026/2027 academic year who are enrolled in the Wicomico County school district. City of Salisbury residents are preferred but not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive paid wages for work performed in City of Salisbury departments, along with workforce readiness training, resume development, and career skill-building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be enrolled in the Wicomico County school district. Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required.
requirements_list: Must be entering 10th–12th grade for the 2026/2027 academic year
Must be currently enrolled in the Wicomico County school district
Must provide a work permit no later than June 22, 2026
Must provide 2 forms of updated identification (birth certificate, social security card, current student ID, or state-issued ID)
Must have consistent, reliable transportation to and from work
Must be able to work up to 28 hours per week for the 8-week period (June 22 – August 14, 2026)
City of Salisbury residency preferred but not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open in January each year for the following summer program. Submit an application during the open application window. An application for 2025 was available at https://salisbury.md/summer-youth-employment-program-application-2025. Contact the Community Relations Division at 410-341-9550 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury offers free copper and lead water testing for eligible residents. The city drops off a testing bottle at your home, picks it up after testing, and delivers results within 30 days.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home water testing for lead and copper. The city delivers a testing bottle, collects it after use, and provides results within 30 days at no cost to the resident.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Salisbury residents in single-family homes built before 1988 that are serviced by City water.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water testing for lead and copper presence in the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a single-family home serviced by City of Salisbury water.
requirements_list: Home must be serviced by City water
Home must be a single-family home (no multi-unit dwellings)
Home must have been built prior to 1988
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online form on the program page. The city will drop off a testing bottle. After testing is complete, the city picks the bottle back up. Results are provided within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury to help cover the cost of connecting their buildings to Maryland Broadband's high-speed fiber optic network running along Main Street. Grants reimburse eligible construction costs for bringing fiber into a private property up to the modem termination point.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $2,500 per application, awarded on a reimbursement basis only (costs must be incurred before reimbursement). Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget is exhausted. Applicants may not pass construction costs on to end users of the service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Until funds run out for the Fiscal Year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury who want to connect their building to the high-speed fiber network installed along Main Street.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs of bringing fiber from the existing Main Street conduit into the private property, ending at the modem termination point. Costs cannot include sidewalk excavation or alteration of the Main Street construction improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury and must be abutted by existing conduits installed as part of the Main Street project.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury using conduits abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project
Application must be made by the legal property owner or by a tenant with written approval from the property owner
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to perform the work
Must obtain approval from the Historic District if applicable
The City will not approve digging up sidewalks or work that alters the Main Street construction improvements
Grants are reimbursement-based only — construction costs must not be passed on to end users of the service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application form with project description, photograph of the building façade showing the planned fiber entry point, anticipated cost, and amount requested (up to $2,500). If the project is already complete, include copies of all receipts or paid invoices. Tenants must include a letter of approval from the property owner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Safety Officer Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for eligible public safety officers — including full-time and volunteer firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, and police officers employed by the City of Salisbury — who own and reside in the property to which the credit is applied. The credit reduces the City's real property tax owed on the officer's primary residence and must be renewed each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit of up to $2,500 applied to the City of Salisbury real property tax for the applicant's primary residence. The credit may not exceed the total real property tax imposed on the dwelling. The credit is valid for one taxable year and must be renewed annually. Application must be filed on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applying to the next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time Salisbury Fire Department firefighters/EMTs/paramedics and Police Officers with at least one year of full-time employment; active volunteer Salisbury Fire Department members meeting service requirements; officers who retired in good standing; officers with service-related disabilities; and volunteer members with 20+ years of active service (Lifetime members).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of City of Salisbury real property taxes on the eligible officer's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and reside in property located within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current full-time employee or qualifying volunteer/retired/disabled public safety officer of the City of Salisbury Fire Department or Police Department
Full-time employees must have completed at least one year of full-time employment
Must own the property to which the credit will be applied
Property must be the applicant's primary residence
Must not have received a real property tax credit under Title 9 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland for the same property
Must submit supporting documentation (e.g., current paystub, retirement/separation letter, volunteer status letter)
Application must be filed on or before April 1 before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Credit terminates if officer is no longer employed full-time (for reasons other than retirement or disability) or no longer resides in the dwelling
Must notify the City of Salisbury Finance Department if eligibility requirements are no longer met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form at salisbury.md/public-safety-tax-credit-application, providing property parcel number, fiscal year, applicant and owner names, address, contact information, qualifying officer designation, and supporting documentation. Both the applicant and co-applicant (if applicable) must sign electronically. Submit before April 1 of the year preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury offers a revolving loan fund to support new businesses opening in Salisbury or existing businesses expanding or renovating within eligible areas of the city. Administered by the Arts, Business & Culture department, applicants can request up to $100,000 to fund business projects located within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area, including the Historic District. The program is reviewed by the Revolving Loan Advisory Committee and requires applicants to complete a loan application and personal financial statement along with supporting documentation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $100,000 are available for new or expanding businesses located within the Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury. The interest rate is set at the U.S. Treasury less than 10-year long-term composite rate published daily plus 1%, fixed for the loan term (3, 5, or 7-year terms available). Collateral may be up to 100% loan-to-value; the City is willing to take a subordinate position and can lien other applicant assets. Funds can be used for professional engineering and architectural assistance, renovation of building exteriors and interiors, and purchase or renovation of equipment or machinery. Ineligible uses include start-up costs, working capital, refinancing fees, access streets/roads, parking areas, utility/service extensions, and activities violating local ordinances or historic district guidelines. Applicants must provide personal investment and other committed financing. Priority is given to projects that create jobs, provide needed goods/services, and generate additional tax revenue. The loan is administered by the City of Salisbury Arts, Business & Culture department and reviewed by the Revolving Loan Advisory Committee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New businesses opening in Salisbury and existing businesses seeking to expand or renovate within the city's designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area, including qualified property owners and qualified commercial tenants with written property owner approval.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional engineering and architectural assistance; renovation of exteriors and interiors of buildings; purchase or renovation of equipment or machinery within the target area. Ineligible uses include start-up costs, working capital, refinancing fees, access streets/roads, parking areas, utility/service extensions, and activities violating local ordinances or historic district guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in the City of Salisbury, Maryland. A map of eligible areas is available from the program. Projects in the Historic District require approval from the Salisbury Historic District Commission.
requirements_list: Must be located within the Revolving Loan Fund boundary map area in Salisbury
Must be located in a designated Revolving Loan eligible area within Salisbury
Must submit a completed Revolving Loan Application
Must submit a Personal Financial Statement
Business plan with three-year pro forma projections (for startups)
Personal and company tax returns for the past two years
Evidence of personal financial investment in the project
Conceptual design illustration and detailed project description
Project timeline
Three written cost estimates for proposed project costs
Copy of lease and written approval from landlord
Evidence of Historic District Commission concept plan approval (if applicable)
Articles of incorporation
Credit report dated no more than one month prior to application submission
Approval from City Infrastructure & Development department
Must complete the Revolving Loan Fund Application and Personal Financial Statement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the fillable Revolving Loan Fund Application and Personal Financial Statement forms (including required schedules for cash, life insurance, stocks/bonds, real estate, notes payable, charge accounts, and endorsed loans). Gather all required documents from the checklist (business plan, tax returns, cost estimates, lease, approvals, articles of incorporation, credit report, and personal financial statement) and submit along with supporting materials to the Director of Business Development at 110 N Division Street, Salisbury, MD 21801. Applications are reviewed by the Revolving Loan Advisory Committee. Note: once available funds have been fully loaned, applications will be held on file without evaluation until funds become available. The program goal is to take action upon each application within 45 days after receipt of all required information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program that recognizes businesses in Salisbury, Maryland that adopt environmentally friendly practices. Businesses complete a checklist of sustainable actions — such as using compostable or non-plastic utensils, energy-efficient lighting, recycling, sourcing local food, using clean energy, and managing stormwater — and earn points for each practice. Points determine a tiered certification level: bronze (10–14 points), silver (15–19 points), or gold (20+ points). Businesses may also propose their own green practices for 1–3 points. A designated 'Green Advocate' within the organization is worth 3 points and must attend the City's Sustainability Advisory Committee (Green Team) once a year. Certified businesses receive a certification sticker to display at their entry point, a photo with the Mayor shared on social media, and logo placement on the City's website under the green business section.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified businesses receive a tiered certification (bronze: 10–14 points, silver: 15–19 points, or gold: 20+ points) based on a scored checklist of environmentally sustainable practices worth 1, 2, or 3 points each. Benefits include a certification sticker to display at their entry point, a photo with the Mayor shared on social media, and logo placement on the City's website under the green business section.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in Salisbury, MD that are willing to adopt and document environmentally sustainable practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a certification program, not a cash assistance program. Recognition and promotional benefits are provided to certified businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses operating within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Salisbury, MD
Must earn a minimum of 10 points from the green practice checklist to qualify for bronze certification

Points are assigned based on criteria such as using compostable utensils, non-plastic straws, energy-efficient bulbs, recycling, local food purchasing, clean energy use, stormwater management, and more
Businesses may also propose their own green practice for 1–3 points
A designated 'Green Advocate' within the organization is worth 3 points and must attend the City's Sustainability Advisory Committee (Green Team) once a year
Applicant must provide accurate information and digital signature
Certifications between 2019 and 2022 received a COVID-19 extension of 3 total years from initial date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online registration form at salisbury.md/green-business-certification-application by providing business information, indicating which green practices your business currently uses, and calculating your total points. The Green Team will verify the checklist. Certified businesses are recognized with a certification sticker, mayoral photo, and website listing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual public art competition open to Maryland residents and organizations. Selected artists receive a cash award and materials stipend to design and install a public artwork at a designated City of Salisbury location. The competition runs in two rounds: an initial application review where the top three candidates each receive $500 to develop an extended proposal, followed by an in-person or virtual presentation to the Public Art Committee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The winning artist or team receives a $10,000 cash award plus a reimbursable materials stipend of up to $5,000. The top three finalists in Round 1 each receive $500 to develop an extended proposal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 30, 2026 – competition submissions due by 11:59 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland artists, architects, engineers, and creative teams aged 18 or older; Salisbury and local-based artists are strongly encouraged to apply
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and installation of a public artwork at a designated City of Salisbury location; materials and supplies for the winning proposal (up to $5,000 reimbursable)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Maryland residents and organizations; local Salisbury-area artists are strongly encouraged to apply
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or organization
Must be 18 years of age or older
All designs must be original art — no trademarked, copyrighted, or AI-generated imagery
No copies of existing photos or images created by others
Designs must be appropriate for broad public audiences of all ages — no religious, political, or sexual content; no corporate logos or advertising
The winning design becomes the property of the City of Salisbury
Winner is solely responsible for all applicable taxes on their award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Round 1: Submit an initial application using the online form. The Public Art Committee reviews all submissions and selects the top three proposals. Round 2: Top three finalists receive $500 each and present an extended proposal in-person or virtually to the Public Art Committee. The winning artist is notified in late April, an agreement is signed, and funds are encumbered by the City. Installation commences in June and must be completed within six months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Enterprise Zone program offers tax credits to businesses, property owners, and developers that locate, expand, or improve commercial properties within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone in Wicomico County. Two types of credits are available: (1) a Real Property Tax Credit — a 10-year credit against local property taxes equal to 80% of the increase in assessed value from capital improvements of $50,000 or more, with the credit at 80% for years 1–5, then declining by 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) over years 6–10; and (2) a State Income Tax Credit based on new employees hired — $1,000 one-time per non-economically-disadvantaged employee, or up to $3,000 in year one, $2,000 in year two, and $1,000 in year three for economically disadvantaged employees. The Business Development Specialist at the City of Salisbury provides information and assistance with applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tax credits are available: (1) Real Property Tax Credit — a 10-year credit against local property taxes equal to 80% of the increase in assessed value from capital improvements of $50,000 or more. The credit is 80% for the first five years, then declines by 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) over the final five years. (2) State Income Tax Credit — a credit based on new employees hired: $1,000 one-time per non-economically-disadvantaged employee; up to $3,000 in year one, $2,000 in year two, and $1,000 in year three for economically disadvantaged employees. Requires hiring two or more qualifying new employees working at least 35 hours per week for at least six months at 150% of federal minimum wage. A Personal Property Tax Credit may also be available in Focus Area Zones.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For Real Property Tax Credit, the Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31 of the preceding calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, property owners, and developers located within or planning to locate in the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone in Wicomico County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real Property Tax Credit applies to capital improvements on commercial properties. State Income Tax Credit applies to new employees hired within the Enterprise Zone. Tax credit to offset costs of business location or expansion within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone boundary in Wicomico County. Email the Business Development Specialist or review the eligible area map to confirm eligibility. The zone was established in 1982; the map document notes an expiration date of December 14, 2022.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone
Business must locate or expand within the Salisbury Wicomico designated Enterprise Zone

Real Property Credit: capital investment of $50,000 or more in commercial property; application must be submitted before project completion and issuance of occupancy permits; only commercial properties are eligible

State Income Tax Credit: must hire two or more qualifying new employees; employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least six months; employees must be paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage; employees must spend at least half their working hours in the Enterprise Zone
New employees must be filling a new position or replacing a previously certified economically disadvantaged employee
Must submit application to the Business Development Specialist prior to project completion
Must apply and receive approval
Workers must be eligible under program rules
Must complete the Enterprise Zone Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Enterprise Zone application (available online or as a printable PDF) and submit to the Business Development Specialist. 2. The Zone Administrator reviews the application and forwards it to the appropriate State entities for approval. 3. If eligible, you receive a certification letter from the City of Salisbury. 4. For Real Property Tax Credit, the credit is automatically reflected in property taxes. For State Income Tax Credit, claim the credit when filing business entity tax returns. Application sections include: Section A (Applicant Information), Section B (Enterprise Zone Property Information), Section C (Property Improvements Information, if applying for property tax credit), and Section D (Employment Tax Credit Information, if applying for employment tax credit).

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury's Stormwater Utility allows property owners to apply for a credit against their annual stormwater utility fee, which is billed as part of the property tax bill. Property owners may also apply for a hardship exemption or appeal their fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can apply for a credit against their annual stormwater utility fee. A hardship exemption form and a fee appeal form are also available for eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners within the City of Salisbury who are subject to the annual stormwater utility fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or exemption of the annual stormwater utility fee billed as part of the property tax bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Stormwater Utility Credit Application or Stormwater Hardship Exemption Form from the City of Salisbury website and submit as directed. A fee appeal form is also available for those wishing to contest their fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury invites artists, designers, and creatives to submit proposals for a temporary painted design of three crosswalks at the intersection of South Division St. and West/East Market St. The selected design should reflect the city's character, history, and artistic vibrancy using abstract patterns, geometric shapes, or elements inspired by natural or architectural features, while prioritizing pedestrian safety and visibility. The selected artist receives a $3,000 stipend to design and implement the artwork, which will be displayed for up to two years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $3,000 stipend is awarded to the selected artist for designing and painting three crosswalks. Painting must be completed by September 14, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Incentive Program (WIN) helps income-eligible households in Salisbury pay their water and/or sewer bills. Eligible households can receive up to $2,000 per year toward their water and/or sewer bill (or up to $1,000 if the property has a leak). Applicants who already receive certain state assistance programs (such as SNAP, SSI, TCA, TDAP, ERAP, LIHEAP, or energy assistance through OHEP) are automatically eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households may receive one payment per year of up to $2,000 applied toward their water and/or sewer bills issued by the City of Salisbury (for properties with no leaks), or up to $1,000 per year for properties with a detected leak. Assistance is limited to actual charges appearing on the water/sewer bill and is capped at one payment per household per year. Income thresholds are based on 60% of State Median Income, scaled by household size ($3,574–$9,414/month for 1–8 members; +$205/month per additional member), effective October 1, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents (both tenants and homeowners) who are responsible for paying a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury and whose total household income does not exceed 60% of the State Median Income, or who are currently receiving qualifying assistance programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward water and/or sewer bills issued by the City of Salisbury. Assistance is limited to actual charges on the water/sewer bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live at the property receiving assistance and the property must be served by the City of Salisbury water/wastewater system.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be responsible for paying a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury
Must live at the property for which assistance is requested

Total household income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income (scaled by household size) OR applicant must be currently receiving OHEP/LIHEAP energy assistance, TCA/TANF, TDAP, SNAP, SSI, ERAP, or Veterans benefits (MTVB)
Must provide government-issued photo ID, proof of residence (water/sewer bill), Social Security cards for all household members, and proof of all gross income for the last 30 days
If rental property, both tenant and owner must apply
One application per household per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at salisbury.md/win or download the printable application at salisbury.md/win-application. You may also apply in-person at Wicomico County Social Services (201 Baptist St., Ste. 27, Salisbury, MD 21801) or at Salisbury Public Utilities billing division (125 N. Division St., Room 103). Upload or submit required documentation including government-issued ID, proof of residence (water/sewer bill), Social Security cards for all household members, and proof of gross income for the last 30 days. If applicable, attach award letters for other assistance programs received. Sign and submit the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Manufacturing and Research & Development Machinery and Equipment Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption on personal property (tools, machinery, and equipment) used for manufacturing or research and development operations in Salisbury. Eligible businesses can receive an exemption for up to 5 years on qualifying equipment purchased in a specific calendar year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An exemption on personal property taxes for machinery and equipment used in manufacturing or research and development. The exemption applies to the specific year the equipment was purchased and can last up to 5 years. To qualify for the maximum 5-year term, the application must be submitted within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased. A separate application is required for each year of equipment acquisition. Once granted, a copy of the personal property tax return must be submitted annually for each year of the exemption. All exemptions require approval by the City of Salisbury City Council.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sandra Green (Director of Finance); Phillip Menzel (Assistant Director Finance - Accounting)

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax exemption on personal property taxes for tools, machinery, and equipment used in manufacturing or research and development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must operate a manufacturing or research and development facility in the City of Salisbury, Maryland.

Application must be received within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased to qualify for the maximum 5-year exemption term.
A separate application must be made for each calendar year of equipment acquisition.

Must attach a copy of the Maryland State Personal Property Return for the year of acquisition.

All exemptions require approval by the City of Salisbury Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury partners with two non-profits — Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County and Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services — to fund critical repairs on owner-occupied single-family homes within Salisbury city limits. The program is funded through Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) dollars and helps low-to-moderate income homeowners bring their homes up to City code.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Salisbury Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $20,000 per property for eligible home repairs. A 5-year lien is placed on the property after the grant is received. Extenuating circumstances may allow amounts above $20,000. Recipients are not eligible for another grant until the 5-year lien term expires.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income owner-occupants of single-family homes within the City of Salisbury city limits whose household income is below 80% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repairs to bring homes into compliance with City codes, including: repair or replacement of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; building components such as roofs, foundations, floors, doors, and windows; energy conservation improvements; lead paint hazard reduction; and accessibility modifications for disabled persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury corporate limits.
requirements_list: Total gross household income before taxes must be below 80% of Area Median Income (limits range from $52,500 for a 1-person household to $98,950 for an 8-person household)
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by entireties (no tenants in common)
At least one owner on the deed must reside in the property
Applicant must have legal capacity to incur obligations under the program
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous 3 months
Applicant must be free of any tax lien or judgment
Bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of 2 years
All property taxes and City-issued invoices attached to the parcel must be current
Property must have clear title
Property must be free of all judgments including IRS liens
Applicant must insure the property for the entire lien term; flood insurance required for properties in the 100-year floodplain
Properties in a floodway are not eligible
Owner-occupant must not own any other house and must not have substantial assets enabling them to secure rehabilitation funds elsewhere
A 5-year Notice of Lien must be signed and recorded in Land Records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility criteria on the program page, then contact one of the two subrecipient agencies — Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County (410-546-1551) or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (410-543-4626) — for further information and to apply. Basic qualification does not guarantee funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Tax Abatement Program (Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling Incentive)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury offers a property tax abatement program for individuals who purchase a rental property and convert it into their primary owner-occupied, single-family residence within the City of Salisbury. City property taxes are fully abated (100%) for the first five years of participation, then phased in at 20% per year over years six through nine (20% in year six, 40% in year seven, 60% in year eight, 80% in year nine), with full property taxes due in year ten at the then-prevailing tax rate. The program is designed to increase owner-occupied housing in the city while helping homeowners save on property taxes during the transition period. Eligibility is determined on a property-by-property basis through the Housing and Community Development department.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Salisbury Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City property taxes are fully abated (100%) for the first five years of participation. Taxes are then gradually phased in at 20% per year over years six through nine (20% in year six, 40% in year seven, 60% in year eight, 80% in year nine), with full property taxes due in year ten at the then-prevailing tax rate. Eligibility is determined on a property-by-property basis through the Housing and Community Development department. Continuing participants must certify qualification by April 1 each year. Participation ends if the property ceases to be owner-occupied or is conveyed to a new owner. Applicants should review the Participation Form and FAQ for full details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals purchasing a rental property and converting it into their primary owner-occupied, single-family residence within the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of City property taxes for owners converting rental properties to owner-occupied, single-family primary residences. The abatement is a direct tax reduction — no monetary funds are disbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the corporate limits of the City of Salisbury, Maryland only. No county-wide or regional component applies.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the corporate limits of the City of Salisbury
Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least three consecutive years prior to conversion, or must have been rehabilitated after rental use for 3 consecutive years
Property must be converted to an owner-occupied, single-family detached dwelling
Owner must intend to occupy the home within one year of the date of closing
Owner must submit annual certification of qualification by April 1 each year for continued participation (recertification required for nine years)
Property must qualify as determined by Housing and Community Development
Must purchase a rental property
Must convert the property to an owner-occupied primary residence
Participation ends if the property ceases to be owner-occupied or is conveyed to a new owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Salisbury Housing and Community Development department to determine if your property qualifies. Complete and submit the Participation Form. Apply in person at the City Finance Office, 125 N Division St., Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801, or download the application from the City of Salisbury's website. Continuing participants must recertify eligibility by April 1 each year. See the FAQ for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program – City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.program_description: The CDBG Program provides annual formula-based grants to the City of Salisbury to fund a wide variety of community and economic development activities. Eligible activities include neighborhood revitalization, economic development, public services, housing rehabilitation, historic preservation, lead paint hazard reduction, improved community facilities and services, and assistance to nonprofits and micro-enterprises. The City of Salisbury administers its own CDBG funds locally, selecting activities based on local needs and priorities. Each funded activity must meet at least one national objective: benefit low- and moderate-income persons, prevent or eliminate slums and blight, or address urgent community development needs. The City awards subgrants to eligible organizations on a competitive basis. All funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis.
structured_extraction.agency: City of Salisbury – Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based federal grant funds allocated to the City of Salisbury and distributed to subrecipients for eligible community and economic development activities. For program year 2021 (7/1/2021–6/30/2022), total CDBG funds are $399,903, with $329,903 available for program/project activities and up to $59,985 for public service projects. The maximum any single applicant (subrecipient) may request in a competitive funding round is $150,000. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis — recipients must spend their own funds first, then submit documentation (paid invoices, cancelled checks) for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, businesses, and government entities seeking funding for community development, neighborhood revitalization, economic development, or public services activities in Salisbury that benefit low- and moderate-income residents or meet other national CDBG objectives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition/disposition and clearance of real property; public improvements and facilities (e.g., senior centers, day care centers); public services (e.g., child care, health care, job training, homeless services); relocation assistance; rehabilitation of residential, commercial, industrial, or nonprofit-owned buildings; historic preservation; lead-based paint hazard evaluation and reduction; code enforcement; assistance to micro-enterprises; homeownership assistance; technical assistance to nonprofits; neighborhood revitalization; economic development; and other eligible community development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Subrecipients must be registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations (for nonprofit applicants) and must provide documentation confirming this status.
Activities must meet at least one national objective: benefit to low- and moderate-income persons, prevention/elimination of slums and blight, or urgent community development need.
Activity must be eligible under CDBG rules.
Capital projects on property not owned by the subrecipient must include written approval from the property owner.
Subrecipients requesting public service funds must be developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in an existing service.
All funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis — applicants must have sufficient operating funds to cover expenses before reimbursement.
Maximum request per competitive funding round is $150,000.
No more than 20% of the grant may be spent on planning and administrative costs.
No more than 15% of the grant may be spent on public service activities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible organizations apply as subrecipients in a competitive funding round, submitting a proposal for either a public service or capital grant. Prospective subrecipients should review the CDBG Program Guidelines document for details on program administration and how to apply. After award, subrecipients expend their own funds on eligible project expenses, then submit paid invoices, cancelled checks, and other requested documentation to the City for reimbursement.

Must live in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: Comcast Internet Essentials offers low-cost home internet service at $9.95 per month for qualified households. The program provides fast, reliable, and affordable broadband access for eligible new and existing Comcast (Xfinity) customers in the Calvert County area. The program also includes a broadband infrastructure buildout initiative to expand fiber/internet service to underserved addresses in Calvert County, funded through ARPA ($4.7M), FY2022 Franchise Fee allocation ($1.6M), and Maryland DHCD Home Stretch DSP ($1.65M state + $550K county match), with $1.968 million remaining after state grant reduction. As of August 2025, 643 of 735 addresses have been completed with 92 remaining.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified households can receive home internet service for $9.95 per month through the Internet Essentials program. Available to eligible new and existing Comcast customers. Additionally, a broadband infrastructure buildout is underway targeting underserved and difficult-to-serve properties in Calvert County across three phases (Phase I & II: 325 addresses completed; Phase III: 388 addresses with 70 remaining; DSP grant: 22 addresses remaining). Total project funding is $7.95 million; $1.968 million remains. As of August 2025, 643 of 735 addresses completed with 92 remaining.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence
structured_extraction.program_description: Since 1987, the Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence, administered by the Committee on Hate and Violence (COHV) under the Montgomery County Office of Human Rights, provides partial financial compensation to victims of hate-motivated acts in Montgomery County. The program reimburses individuals and private institutions for property damage or medical expenses resulting from hate or violence acts targeting people on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability. It aims to demonstrate community support for victims and ease the financial burden caused by such acts. Reimbursement for property damage is up to $2,000 per hate/violence act, and up to $4,000 for medical expenses from physical injury, with total compensation capped at $8,000 to any one victim within a 12-month period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Guaranteed Basic Income (GBI) Pilot Program – Phase Two
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that provides monthly financial assistance to low- to moderate-income families with children in Howard County. Phase Two gives each participating family $500 per month in direct income support plus $500 per month deposited into a savings account held at SECU (a nonprofit financial institution). Participants also receive wrap-around services, monthly check-ins with Community Action Council (CAC) staff, and are required to complete a financial literacy program. The program aims to help families achieve economic self-sufficiency and build a household contingency/reserve fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Action Council of Howard County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive $500 per month in direct income payments plus $500 per month deposited into a savings account at SECU, for 12 months. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Household needs such as rent, debt paydown, utilities, food, transportation, and other essential expenses to improve economic stability.

Must have at least one child 17 years old or younger living in the household

structured_extraction.program_description: A food assistance program that lets eligible Howard County residents shop for groceries at no cost, similar to a regular grocery store. Participants can choose from fresh produce and dairy, frozen meats, breads, shelf-stable foods, hygiene products, diapers and baby supplies, and allergy-friendly foods. The program also provides access to SNAP application assistance and connects residents to energy, housing, and early childhood education services.

Items available include fresh produce and dairy, frozen meats, breads, canned and boxed foods, hygiene products, diapers, baby formula and food, and allergy-friendly options. Availability depends on donations and may vary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Howard County residents who need food assistance and can provide required eligibility documentation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Groceries and household essentials including produce, dairy, meat, bread, canned goods, hygiene products, diapers, and baby supplies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Equity and Emergency Distribution Grant Program (FEED)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Frederick County FEED Grant Program is a targeted initiative to support local nonprofits, food banks, pantries, religious entities, and other organizations responding to increased food needs among county residents, particularly those affected by federal government shutdown delays in SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits. The program provides grant funding to help organizations continue or expand food-related services, including purchasing food and essential food service equipment. It is administered in partnership with the Community Foundation of Frederick County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total available funding is $1,000,000 split into two rounds of $500,000 each. Grants are disbursed as a one-time payment. Eligible uses include food distribution and meal programs, general operating support for food-related initiatives, administrative overhead directly tied to food service delivery, and capital purchases such as refrigerators, freezers, and food storage (vehicles are not eligible). Grant funds must be used between June 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local nonprofits (501(c)(3)), food banks, food pantries, and religious organizations that provide food assistance to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food distribution and meal programs; general operating support for food-related initiatives; administrative overhead directly tied to food service delivery; capital purchases (e.g., refrigerators, freezers, food storage). Vehicles are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve Frederick County residents; at least 51% of program participants must reside in Frederick County.
requirements_list: Be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) in good standing, an existing food bank or pantry, or a religious organization
Provide food commodities, bagged groceries, backpack food programs, or hot meals to residents
Demonstrate a need for funding and submit a project description, budget, and organizational documentation
Serve Frederick County residents (at least 51% of program participants must reside in Frederick County)
Be in compliance with Maryland Secretary of State's Charitable Division requirements
Be in compliance with Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation requirements
Be in compliance with IRS requirements (verified via GuideStar Charity Check)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Community Foundation of Frederick County at FrederickCountyGives.org/Grants. Applicants must submit a project description, budget, and organizational documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Foundation of Howard County Annual Community Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual competitive grants program through which the Community Foundation of Howard County (CFHC) partners with donors to award grants to registered nonprofit organizations working to improve the lives of Howard County residents. Nonprofits may apply for operational support (organizational costs) or support for a specific program or special project. Grants support a wide range of sectors including human services, arts and culture, education, health, the environment, and other community improvement initiatives. Applications are reviewed based on community impact, sustainability, and alignment with the Foundation's mission of improving quality of life for all county residents. The program is highly competitive and receives dozens of applications each cycle. Each grant cycle has unique eligibility and application requirements outlined in the annual guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive operational grants awarded to qualified registered nonprofits (501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations, or organizations with fiscal sponsors meeting 501(c)(3) requirements) for flexible unrestricted operational support. Grant amounts vary by cycle and organization budget size. In the 2025 cycle: up to $37,500 for organizations with budgets above $100,000, and up to $10,000 for smaller organizations. In the 2024 cycle: up to $10,000 for organizations with budgets over $100,000, and up to $5,000 for organizations with budgets under $100,000. Grantees must fulfill all reporting and accountability requirements, including a grant report with financial and narrative information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations (or nonprofits with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor) of all sizes and sectors serving Howard County, Maryland — from grassroots community groups to established institutions — seeking to improve quality of life for county residents across human services, arts and culture, education, health, environment, and community affairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flexible unrestricted operational and organizational support for mission-aligned activities, or support for a specific program or special project, including community improvement initiatives across human services, arts and culture, education, health, environment, and other sectors as outlined in the annual grant guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland. Applicants must deliver services to Howard County residents and provide services in Howard County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization, or a nonprofit with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor
Must deliver services to Howard County residents
Must provide services in Howard County
Must operate in at least one of the following areas: human services, arts and culture, education, health, environment, or community affairs
Proposal must demonstrate future community impact
Proposal must demonstrate sustainability of proposed work
Proposal must align with the Foundation's mission of improving quality of life for all residents
Each program cycle has unique eligibility requirements outlined in the annual guidelines
Award recipients must fulfill all reporting and accountability requirements, including a grant report with financial and narrative information, as outlined by the Foundation
Sign up for the Foundation's email list to receive alerts about new grant applications and deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Foundation's grants management system (grantinterface.com / Foundant GLM). Applicants must create an account to apply. The application window opens in October (e.g., October 20 in 2025) and closes at midnight on the published deadline (e.g., November 14 in 2025). Applicants can attend an optional virtual information session held in October (e.g., October 28, 2025) and/or schedule a one-on-one appointment with Foundation staff (contact Dee Athey at dathey@cfhoco.org). An online applicant tutorial is available to help with account creation and submission. Sign up for the Foundation's email list to receive alerts about new grant applications and deadlines. Applications are reviewed after the deadline and recipients are announced.

structured_extraction.program_description: Endow Maryland is a Maryland state tax credit program that rewards donors who make new contributions to build permanent, endowed charitable funds at community foundations across the state. Donors who contribute $500 or more to qualifying permanent endowment funds may receive a 25% state tax credit against Maryland corporate income tax, personal income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax. Credits are limited and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Only new contributions qualify — grants from donor-advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers are not eligible. Contributions may be made by personal check, charge, online payment, or publicly traded securities. The maximum annual donation eligible is $200,000, yielding a maximum credit of $50,000 per year, and unused credits may carry forward up to 5 years. At the Community Foundation of Howard County, qualifying funds include the Fund for the Common Good, the Next 50 Campaign, and the Next 50 Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 25% Maryland state tax credit is available for new donations of $500 or more made to a qualified permanent endowment fund (QPEF) at an eligible community foundation. The maximum annual donation eligible is $200,000, yielding a maximum credit of $50,000 per year. Unused credits may carry forward up to 5 years after earned. The credit can be applied against Maryland corporate income tax, personal income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax. Credits are limited and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Contributions must be new gifts made by personal check, charge, online payment, or publicly traded securities; grants from donor-advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits available on a first-come, first-served basis for the current calendar year while supplies last
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland individual and business taxpayers who make charitable contributions of $500 or more to qualified permanent endowment funds at eligible community foundations across the state.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Donations must go to a qualified permanent endowment fund (QPEF) at an eligible community foundation. At the Community Foundation of Howard County, qualifying funds include the Fund for the Common Good, the Next 50 Campaign, and the Next 50 Fund, supporting permanent endowed charitable purposes for local communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland taxpayers statewide through eligible community foundations across Maryland. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD); the Community Foundation of Howard County is one participating eligible foundation supporting Howard County community needs.
requirements_list: Minimum donation of $500 to a qualified permanent endowment fund (QPEF)

Contributions must be new gifts (not from a donor-advised fund or IRA charitable rollover)

Must complete and submit the Endow Maryland Certification of Contribution Form for each contribution

Must complete and submit the Donor and Foundation Acknowledgment Form (also referred to as the Endow Maryland Waiver of Information Form) annually; Foundation must submit form to Department annually for each donor
Taxpayer must apply to Maryland DHCD for certification in each year of a multi-year pledge, as long as funding remains in the tax credit pool for that calendar year
Unused credits may carry forward up to 5 years after earned
Tax credit is non-refundable; excess carryover expires 5 years after earned
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Dan Flynn, Director of Development at the Community Foundation of Howard County (dflynn@cfhoco.org or 410-730-7840), to verify that credits are still available for the current calendar year and to confirm which funds qualify. Download, complete, and return the Endow Maryland Certification of Contribution Form (required for each contribution) and the Endow Maryland Waiver of Information Form/Donor and Foundation Acknowledgment Form (required annually) by email, in person, by mail, or by fax to 410.997.6021 to the Community Foundation of Howard County. The certification form is attached to Form 502CR on the donor's state tax return. You may also contact Maryland DHCD Division of Neighborhood Revitalization at 410-209-5800 or endowmaryland.nr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: HoCo EXCEL is Howard County's Nonprofit Excelerator Program, launched in February 2024, that provides training, coaching, and funding to help Howard County nonprofits build their capacity to become high-performing organizations. The program has two components: (1) a sector-wide Training Program with interactive, experiential sessions open to all Howard County nonprofits, and (2) a Capacity-Building Cohort that offers intensive, multi-year support including annual operating grants, organizational assessments, customized action plans, one-on-one coaching, and other individualized resources. A cohort of up to five nonprofits is selected annually. The program is a partnership between Howard County government and the Community Foundation of Howard County, with the County investing $340,000 in kickoff funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Capacity-Building Cohort is a 3-year initiative in which up to five nonprofits are selected annually and receive customized coaching, training, and annual operating grant funding: $20,000 in Year 1, $20,000 in Year 2, and $15,000 in Year 3. The sector-wide Training Program component provides interactive, experiential training sessions open to all nonprofit organizations in Howard County. The County invested $340,000 in kickoff funding for the program.
