structured_extraction.program_description: A $50 million multi-year fund managed by FSC First on behalf of Prince George's County, administered through the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive and supported by the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation (EDC). The fund stimulates economic growth by providing loans and, in exceptional cases, grants to businesses and development projects to support business retention, expansion, and attraction. Goals include broadening the commercial tax base, retaining and creating jobs, supporting key industry sectors—including federal government contractors, hospitals and health services, information technology services, and research-intensive technologies—and supporting small, local, and minority enterprises. Interest rates are set on a case-by-case basis at competitive market rates or slightly below (the Prince George's prime rate is 4%). Approximately $7 million to $11 million is available each fiscal year, with approximately 65% of committed funds revolving back into the fund for future investment. A $1 million set-aside supports small businesses in obtaining lines of credit from traditional banks. Projects located in the county's developed tier, transit-oriented development areas, Transforming Neighborhoods Initiative areas, and other focus areas receive special priority. Eligible uses include land and building acquisition, building construction and improvement, equipment acquisition, and working capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Minimum loan of $250,000. Loan term up to 10 years with amortization not to exceed 25 years. Interest rates set on a case-by-case basis at competitive market rates or slightly below (Prince George's prime rate is 4%); interest rate is finalized at the time of underwriting. Application fee is 1% of the loan amount: $2,500 upfront for loans up to $1,000,000; $5,000 upfront for loans above $1,000,000 with the balance due at closing; a portion of the fee may be financed as part of the total loan amount. Approximately $7 million to $11 million available each fiscal year from a $50 million total multi-year commitment, with approximately 65% of committed funds revolving back into the fund for future investment. A $1 million set-aside supports small businesses in obtaining lines of credit from traditional banks. Most awards are loans to small and medium-sized businesses. Grants may be considered in extraordinary circumstances involving large numbers of jobs. Nonprofits may receive funding for projects that grow the commercial tax base and create jobs, but not for operational expenses. All awardees must provide collateral (business and personal assets) and personal guarantees. The application and approval process takes approximately 90 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and developers seeking to locate, expand, or be retained in Prince George's County that will broaden the commercial tax base and create or retain jobs, with a focus on small, local, and minority businesses and key industry sectors including federal government contractors, hospitals and health services, information technology services, and research-intensive technologies. Nonprofits are eligible for projects resulting in commercial tax base growth and new jobs, but not for operational expenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business retention, expansion, and attraction; new project development; business acquisition; capital investment; land and building acquisitions; building construction and improvement; equipment acquisition; working capital; relocation; transit-oriented development; small and local enterprise support; projects that expand the county's commercial tax base and create or retain jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Projects in the county's developed tier, transit-oriented development areas, Transforming Neighborhoods Initiative areas, and other focus areas receive special priority. Projects must align with the County's revitalization goals.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application from the EDI Fund website (edif.princegeorgescountymd.gov) or from fscfirst.com, fill out an online application at https://pgfscfirst.tfaforms.net/6, or pick one up from the office. structured_extraction.program_description: A Pepco/Exelon-sponsored loan program administered by FSC First (a U.S. Treasury-certified Community Development Financial Institution and Prince George's County Green Bank manager) that advances public and private investment in clean energy and innovative green technologies in Prince George's County. The program provides loan guarantees, loans, and loan loss reserves to participating lenders and borrowers to finance sustainable energy projects including commercial building energy efficiency improvements, energy conservation, renewable energy measures, energy storage, community solar, distributed energy generation, microgrids, clean transportation, and resiliency measures. Priority is given to diverse and minority-owned businesses and lenders implementing projects.

Ongoing servicing/guaranty fee of 20 basis points on outstanding principal balance annually. Minimum 10% cash equity injection required. An energy audit or feasibility study is required. Diverse and minority-owned businesses and lenders are required to implement the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA 504 Long Term Fixed Assets (Commercial Real Estate and Equipment Loan Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The SBA 504 program provides loans guaranteed by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to help established business owners purchase owner-occupied commercial real estate or long-life equipment. FSC First, an SBA-certified development company (CDC), finances up to 40% of eligible project costs through a second-trust mortgage, while a participating bank finances up to 50%, and the business provides at least 10% in owner's equity — allowing up to 90% financing for expansion projects, preserving capital for cash flow. Eligible fixed assets include commercial real estate acquisition (accommodations, warehouses, retail centers, office buildings, and public/private venues), construction, machinery, and equipment with a useful life of at least 10 years. Loan terms are 20–25 years for real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment. FSC First is authorized to serve as the CDC for any commercial real estate or equipment loan transaction in the State of Maryland. The Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation also facilitates access to this program for businesses in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $5.5 million (CDC portion up to 40% of eligible project costs via second-trust mortgage). Fixed interest rate determined at underwriting. Loan terms are 20–25 years for real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment with straight amortization. Requires a minimum 10% cash down payment from the borrower (15% if the business is a startup or has less than 3 years of profitable operating history, or involves a limited-use facility). Personal guaranties required.

Loan proceeds can be used for general working capital, leasehold improvements, inventory, equipment purchases, smaller real estate acquisitions, and human capital increases.

FSC First may require controlled disbursements via joint payee checks to vendor and borrower.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that reimburses individuals for funeral expenses incurred for deaths attributed to COVID-19. Applicants can receive reimbursement for costs such as caskets, burial plots, cremation, funeral home services, and other eligible expenses related to COVID-19 deaths occurring on or after January 20, 2020.

Eligible expenses include transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy services, funeral ceremony arrangements, funeral home equipment or staff, cremation or interment costs, costs for producing and certifying multiple death certificates, and additional expenses required by local or state law. Amounts already reimbursed by other sources cannot be claimed again.

Documentation must include the applicant's name as responsible party, decedent's name, and amount of expenses
Applicant cannot claim expenses already reimbursed by other government agencies, voluntary agencies, non-profits, or burial/funeral insurance
Multiple contributors to expenses should register under a single application as applicant and co-applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the FEMA COVID-19 Funeral Assistance Line at 844-684-6333 (TTY: 800-462-7585), Monday–Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. CT. Gather required documents including a copy of the death certificate and proof of funeral expenses before calling. If multiple people contributed to funeral expenses, they should apply together under one application as applicant and co-applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: FEMA Community Rating System (CRS) Flood Insurance Discount
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County participates in FEMA's Community Rating System (CRS) Program. Because the county meets CRS requirements — including floodplain protection activities, public education, and flood data management — residents who own property with structures in the 100-year floodplain receive a 10% discount on their flood insurance premiums when they start or renew a National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) policy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10% discount on National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) flood insurance premiums for property owners with structures in the 100-year floodplain in Calvert County. The discount applies when initiating or renewing a flood insurance policy (effective May 1, 2015).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Calvert County whose structures are located within the 100-year floodplain.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of flood insurance premium costs under the NFIP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Calvert County, Maryland with structures in the 100-year floodplain.
requirements_list: Property must have a structure located within the 100-year floodplain in Calvert County
Must initiate or renew an NFIP flood insurance policy to receive the discount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Discount is automatically applied when initiating or renewing a National Flood Insurance Program policy for a qualifying property in Calvert County. Contact FEMA or your insurance agent for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individual Assistance Program (Individuals and Households Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Following a Presidentially declared disaster, the Individual Assistance (IA) Program provides grants to eligible households experiencing difficulties after a disaster. The Individuals and Households Program (IHP) component provides Housing Assistance (HA) and Other Needs Assistance (ONA) when households are denied low-interest Small Business Administration loans and their homeowners or flood insurance does not cover sufficient costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to eligible households for Housing Assistance (temporary housing rental money, home repair, home replacement, or semi-permanent/permanent housing construction) and Other Needs Assistance (medical, dental, funeral, clothing, household items, tools, educational materials, clean-up items, vehicle repair or transportation, moving and storage, and other necessary expenses). Available only after a Presidentially declared disaster. FEMA may provide up to the IHP maximum for repair or replacement; applicants may then apply to the SBA for additional assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households affected by a Presidentially declared disaster who have been denied SBA low-interest disaster loans and whose homeowners or flood insurance does not provide sufficient coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary housing, home repair, home replacement, semi-permanent or permanent housing construction, medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, clothing, household items, tools, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel, vehicle repair or transportation, moving and storage, flood insurance premiums, and other necessary disaster-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in areas covered by a Presidential disaster declaration.
requirements_list: Must be in an area covered by a Presidential disaster declaration
Must have been denied a low-interest SBA disaster loan
Homeowners/flood insurance must not provide sufficient payout
Repair and replacement assistance requires flood insurance compliance if home is in a Special Flood Hazard Area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through FEMA's Individual Assistance Program. See FEMA's website at https://www.fema.gov/assistance/individual for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation awards one-time, project-oriented grants to non-profit organizations primarily in the greater Baltimore area and Maryland. The Foundation focuses on capital projects, equipment, and technology in areas including housing, health, education, economic mobility, arts, environment, historic preservation, and community development. The Foundation prioritizes shovel-ready projects rather than pre-development or early capital, and favors requests with defined beginnings and endings rather than ongoing operational support. For 2025-2026, the Foundation has also launched the Meet the Moment Fund, a one-year grantmaking strategy responding to impacts of recent public policy changes on Baltimore residents, neighborhoods, and nonprofits, alongside its traditional grantmaking. Projects involving new construction or renovation must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time, project-oriented grants for capital projects (approximately 60%), equipment (approximately 30%), and nonprofit capacity building and other one-time needs (approximately 20%). For requests under $50,000, decisions are made on a rolling monthly basis. For requests over $50,000, four LOI closing dates are offered each year with grant decisions issued approximately two months after proposals are submitted. The Foundation does not fund individuals, special events, deficit financing, political activities, or general operating/annual giving. Construction or renovation projects must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling for under $50,000; next LOI closing date May 29, 2026 for over $50,000
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations holding 501(c)(3) status (or with a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent) located primarily in the greater Baltimore area and Maryland, seeking funding for capital projects, equipment, and technology improvements. Organizations must have a Board with a president, secretary, and treasurer, with at least 51% unrelated voting board members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time, project-oriented capital projects (brick and mortar), equipment, and nonprofit capacity building with defined beginnings and endings. Shovel-ready projects are prioritized. Construction or renovation projects must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation. Environmental and historic preservation projects may be funded throughout Maryland. The Foundation does not fund general operating costs, annual giving, special events, deficit financing, political activities, or grants to individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily within the greater Baltimore area and the greater Baltimore region (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Howard, Carroll, and Harford counties); concentration within the State of Maryland. Primary focus on greater Baltimore area (Baltimore City and Baltimore County), where approximately 90% of recent grants are concentrated. Environmental and historic preservation projects are eligible throughout the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)(3) status or have a fiscal sponsor with 501(c)(3) status
Must have a Board with a president, secretary, and treasurer, with at least 51% unrelated voting board members
Must have financial stability to sustain the project
Must demonstrate adequate administrative capacity and program effectiveness
Must be able to describe evaluation criteria, methods, and expected outcomes
Requests should be one-time and project-oriented with defined beginnings and endings
Construction/renovation projects must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation
Submit a 1–3 page Letter of Inquiry (LOI) on official letterhead signed by CEO/Executive Director

LOI must include legal organization name, mailing address, tax ID, contact information, organization description, project description, total project cost, funds already committed, fundraising gap, amount requested, and project timeline
If multiple project components, include all in a single LOI submission
Organizations must complete a two-year waiting period from the final payment date of a previous grant before submitting a new request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Application FAQs and the Foundation's grantmaking process page before applying. 2. Submit a 1–3 page Letter of Inquiry (LOI) via the online portal (create or log in to an account at bbgm-apply.yourcausegrants.com). 3. Foundation staff acknowledge receipt within 24 hours. 4. If invited, submit a full proposal within approximately one month of invitation. 5. A program officer reviews the proposal, often with a site visit. 6. Grants Committee reviews requests; requests over $50,000 go to the Board of Directors, which meets four times per year. 7. Grantees sign a grant agreement; payments are made within one month of signed agreements. Total timeline is approximately 3–5 months.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation's Meet the Moment Fund is a one-year grantmaking initiative for fiscal year 2025–2026 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) providing short-term financial support to eligible Baltimore-area nonprofits facing disruptions caused by changes in public policy or federal funding cuts. The fund offers one-time operating grants in two categories: gap support for nonprofits with a sustainability plan awaiting withheld or restructured resources, and strategic response support for nonprofits or collaborative groups addressing organizational or sector-level changes. Focus areas include health, housing, safety, education, and environmental protection. Up to 40% of the Foundation's annual distribution is allocated to this fund, and an expedited review process is used to accelerate grant decisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time operating grants for gap support or strategic response. Includes bridge funding for organizations awaiting withheld or restructured resources, costs related to service discontinuation or workforce reductions, transitioning clients to new providers, and costs related to organizational collaborations, restructurings, consolidations, mergers, or shared services. Up to 40% of the Foundation's annual distribution is allocated to this fund. Specific grant amounts are not stated. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis once a month using an expedited review process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, decided once a month; fund runs through fiscal year 2025–2026 (June 30, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prior France-Merrick Foundation grantees and nonprofits (or collaborative groups of nonprofits) serving Baltimore residents, neighborhoods, or nonprofits in the Baltimore area, whose organizations or vital services face risks and losses due to changes in public policy or federal funding cuts, and that have a plan for operational sustainability. Focus areas include health, housing, safety, education, and environmental protection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding while awaiting new, withheld, or restructured resources; costs related to service discontinuation, workforce reductions, or client transitions; costs for organizational collaborations, restructurings, consolidations, wind-downs, or mergers; capacity building, pooled or aligned funds, cohorts for planning, and shared services; strategic response support for nonprofits or collaborative groups addressing dramatic organizational or sector-level changes caused by public policy changes and funding cuts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve Baltimore residents, neighborhoods, or nonprofits in the Baltimore area.
requirements_list: Must be a prior France-Merrick Foundation grantee, OR be part of a collaborative group of nonprofits responding to the Foundation's areas of focus
Must serve the Baltimore area
Must advance France-Merrick Foundation priorities
Organization or services must face risks and losses due to changes in public policy or funding
Must have a plan for operational sustainability (fund is not intended to sustain organizations without such a plan)

Must be advancing one or more of the fund's focus areas: preventing disruptions to essential community services, supporting strategic responses to sustain organizations or vital services, or investing in collaborative structures to meet complex needs with reduced resources
Must be a 501(c)(3) organization or have a fiscal sponsor
Request must be 2–3 pages on official letterhead, signed by the CEO or Executive Director
Must include legal organization name, mailing address, and 501(c)(3) Tax ID

Must include brief description of organization including mission, population served, scope of activities, current budget, and finances/work at risk

Must include narrative describing funding loss or policy change impact and pathway to sustainability including funds committed, the gap, and outstanding requests
Must include timeline over which funding is needed and overall project timeline
Must attach list of board of directors with professional affiliations, percent giving, and amount contributed in the last year
Must attach current organizational operating budget (12 months)
Must attach latest audit, if applicable
Must attach IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Organizations are encouraged to contact a program officer to discuss their idea before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a program officer to discuss your idea before applying. Then submit a 2–3 page request via the Foundation's online portal (https://bbgm-apply.yourcausegrants.com/apply/programs/0f1329f7-18d9-45fc-9382-7d47e2099928). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed once a month using an expedited review process. Additional information may be requested during review. The fund runs through fiscal year 2025–2026 (June 30, 2026).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Partners Incentive Program (CPIP) helps income-eligible first-time homebuyers purchase a home in the City of Frederick. Eligible buyers can receive up to $5,000 in loan assistance — up to $2,500 from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and up to $2,500 from the City of Frederick. The program is part of a statewide Maryland DHCD initiative in which the City of Frederick participates as a local partner.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Medbank Program helps low- to moderate-income, uninsured, or underinsured people in Frederick County obtain free or low-cost prescription medications through patient assistance programs run by pharmaceutical companies. A Medbank Case Manager identifies available programs, completes applications, and coordinates with physicians to obtain medications for qualifying residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost prescription medications obtained through pharmaceutical company patient assistance programs. Most drug companies ship a 90-day supply of medications to the patient's physician's office.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income, uninsured, or underinsured Frederick County residents who need prescription medications for longer-term conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prescription medications for medical or psychiatric conditions requiring at least several months of treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Must meet financial guidelines set by the pharmaceutical companies
Must have no other prescription drug coverage or insurance
Must not be enrolled in or eligible for Medical Assistance, Primary Adult Care Program, or Medicare Part D
Medications must be for longer-term conditions requiring three months or more of treatment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application, then fax it to 301-600-6098 or submit online. Applicants must provide proof of income for all household members, a list of medications with dosage and prescribing physician, and a completed Patient Questionnaire and release of information forms. The Medbank Case Manager then identifies patient assistance programs, completes applications, and coordinates with physicians.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rehabilitated Vacant Commercial Structures Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit that creates an incentive for the rehabilitation of vacant commercial structures and capital investment in existing infrastructure in Frederick County. Eligible properties must have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months, must be used for non-residential purposes in an area permitting commercial or industrial use, and must have been constructed prior to the year 2000. The credit reduces property tax liability for qualifying owners who take action to rehabilitate or reoccupy the property. Applications must be submitted by April 30 annually for the tax credit to be applied on the following fiscal year's tax bill (mailed July 1).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit on rehabilitated vacant commercial structures. The credit is calculated based on the increase in assessment attributable to reconstruction and improvements. Eligible properties must have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months prior to lease or sale and must have been actively listed for sale or lease, must be used for non-residential purposes in an area permitting commercial or industrial use, and must have been constructed prior to the year 2000. Applications must be submitted by April 30 annually for the tax credit to be applied on the following fiscal year's tax bill (mailed July 1). Completed applications must be submitted to the State Department of Assessment & Taxation, 5310 Spectrum Drive, Frederick, MD 21703.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of vacant commercial structures in Frederick County and the City of Frederick seeking to rehabilitate or reoccupy their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability following rehabilitation or reoccupation of qualifying vacant commercial structures. Credit is based on the increase in assessment attributable to reconstruction and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County and the City of Frederick, Maryland. Property must be located in an area permitting commercial or industrial use.
requirements_list: Property must have been vacant for a period not less than 18 of the previous 24 months prior to the lease or sale of the property
Property must have been actively listed for sale or lease during the vacancy period
Property must be used for non-residential purposes
Property must be located in an area permitting commercial or industrial use
Structure must have been constructed prior to the year 2000
Application and all backup documentation must be submitted before April 30 for the tax credit to be applied on the following fiscal year's tax bill
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Vacant Commercial Tax Credit Application or the Rehabilitated Vacant Commercial Structures Tax Credit information sheet from the Frederick County Economic Development website. Submit the completed application and all backup documentation to the State Department of Assessment & Taxation, 5310 Spectrum Drive, Frederick, MD 21703 before April 30 for the tax credit to be applied on the following fiscal year's tax bill (mailed July 1). structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income seniors in Frederick County remain in their homes through community-based service coordination. Service Coordinators, registered nurses, and Community Health Workers work with seniors over time to assess their needs, develop service plans, connect them to community-based services, and advocate on their behalf so they can age in place with dignity and self-determination.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Service coordination provided by trained staff, including registered nurses and Community Health Workers. Services include needs assessment, service plan development, referrals to community resources, help accessing services, advocacy with service providers, and ongoing monitoring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income seniors in Frederick County who wish to remain in their homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service coordination to help seniors remain at home, including needs assessments, service plans, referrals, and advocacy

Must be low-income

Must wish to remain in their home (owned or rented)

structured_extraction.program_description: The Creek ReLeaf program increases forested area within Frederick County by planting native trees and shrubs on eligible privately owned and public lands. Participating property owners receive a land assessment, a forest plan, installation of native trees and shrubs, five years of mowing and tree maintenance, and payment for a permanent conservation easement placed on the planted parcel. The program helps reduce landowner maintenance burdens such as mowing, invasive species control, and managing slopes, drainage, or erosion issues. After five years of county-supported maintenance, the property reverts to owner management, with county staff available for additional resources and site inspections every three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides a land assessment, forest plan, installation of native trees and shrubs, five years of mowing and tree maintenance, and payment to the property owner for a permanent conservation easement. The easement is permanent and runs with the land even if sold. Properties must be at least 2 acres (or multiple adjacent properties combined to reach 2 acres). Sites must be outside certain municipal boundaries: Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick City, Middletown, Mount Airy, Myersville, Thurmont, and Walkersville.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual application period open from October through December
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners and public property owners in Frederick County who want to reforest at least 2 acres of land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land assessment, forest plan, installation of native trees and shrubs, five years of mowing and maintenance, and payment for a conservation easement on the reforested parcel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland. Sites must be outside the municipal boundaries of Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick City, Middletown, Mount Airy, Myersville, Thurmont, and Walkersville.
requirements_list: Proposed reforestation area must be at least 2 acres (multiple property owners may combine adjacent parcels)
Property must be outside specified municipal boundaries
No existing easements such as water, sewer, or power lines on the parcel
No existing or proposed septic fields on the parcel
No existing agricultural easements where conflict may occur
No wells or septic fields in the reforestation area
Must agree to a permanent conservation easement
Property owner must review the proposed Permanent Conservation Easement prior to applying
Apply during annual application window (October through December)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted annually from October through December. Interested property owners should review the Permanent Conservation Easement document, identify the area to be reforested, check for existing easements, and contact the program office. Applying does not guarantee acceptance or obligate participation. County staff rank and prioritize proposals using scoring criteria including parcel size, proximity to streams, potential to connect existing forests, access to site, and nearby restoration efforts.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County's Green Homes Program offers a $75 rebate every five years to households that have their septic tank pumped out by a licensed hauler. The program aims to encourage regular tank maintenance to reduce pollution in local waterways used for drinking, recreation, and fishing. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $75 rebate is provided once every five years to households that have their septic tank pumped out by a licensed hauler. Applications are first-come, first-served and subject to funding availability. Pump-outs that occurred before January 1, 2025, are no longer eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County homeowners with septic systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rebate for the cost of having a septic tank pumped out by a licensed hauler
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to households in Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must use a licensed pumping company from the list of Frederick County permitted haulers
Pump-out must have occurred on or after January 1, 2025
Properties are eligible for a rebate only once every five years
Must submit an invoice from a licensed pumping company and proof of payment (signed invoice, credit card receipt, or canceled check)
Application must include all required documentation; if missing information is not provided within 60 days, the application will not be processed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Use a licensed pumping company from the permitted haulers list. 2. Check eligibility using the Pump-Out Eligibility Calculator if you have previously received a rebate. 3. Review the application instructions. 4. Complete the online application (preferred) or download and mail/email a printable application. 5. Include required documentation: invoice from licensed pumping company and proof of payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Meals on Wheels & Home Delivered Meals
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County's Division of Aging and Independence provides daily meal delivery to homebound older adults and adults with disabilities. Meals on Wheels delivers two meals per day (one hot, one cold) to eligible residents age 60 or older, or adults of any age with a chronic health condition or disability who are homebound and unable to prepare their own food. Home Delivered Meals are available to homebound adults age 60 or older who live within the service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, and Urbana. Meals meet Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults and are available in several special diet formats. The program also provides regular wellness checks and referrals to other services.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Aging and Independence
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive two meals per day (one hot midday meal and one cold meal) delivered to their home. Voluntary contributions are accepted but not required. Participants, family, and friends may also purchase meals or make donations via the county's online store.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebound adults age 60 or older, or adults of any age with a chronic health condition or disability, who live in Frederick County and are unable to prepare their own meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily meal delivery to eligible homebound residents to support nutritional health and independent living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, with Home Delivered Meals specifically available in the service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, and Urbana.
requirements_list: Must be homebound due to illness or physical limitations
Must be age 60 or older, OR be an adult of any age with a chronic health condition or disability
Must be unable to prepare meals independently
Must have no caregiver to assist with food shopping and preparation, or cannot safely prepare food due to physical, mental, or emotional impairment
Must live in Frederick County (Meals on Wheels) or within the service area of a qualifying senior center (Home Delivered Meals)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Eligibility Guidelines and call 301-600-1234 to begin the screening process.

The program also offers education and training, information and referrals, resource materials, caregiver support groups, and access to programs like Powerful Tools for Caregivers (a six-week skills program), Dementia Live training, Memory Cafes, and Partners in the Arts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers of adults age 60 or older; caregivers of any age person with Alzheimer's disease or related disorder; grandparents or relative caregivers age 55+ caring for children age 18 or under or adult children with disabilities ages 19–59.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care costs (up to $800/year); education and training; information, assistance, and referrals to local services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to caregivers in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: No income requirements
Caregiver must be caring for someone age 60 or older, or a person of any age with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder; OR
Caregiver must be age 55 or older and caring for a child age 18 or under or an adult child with a disability ages 19–59, and cannot be the child's natural or adoptive parent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate respite application (Caregiver Respite Application or Grandparent/Relative Respite Application) and submit along with a W-9 form. Contact the Caregiver Program Coordinators at 301-600-6022 or caregiversupport@frederickcountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Care and Personal Care Programs (Frederick County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides in-home support services to frail, health-impaired older adults in Frederick County. A case manager evaluates needs in the home, arranges appropriate services including in-home aide services for activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, meal preparation, chores, and homemaking), and may provide gap-filling service dollars for those who meet financial and other eligibility criteria, all at no cost to the individual. The program helps older adults continue living at home and in the community rather than in an institutional setting.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Aging and Independence
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost in-home needs assessment and case management. In-home aide services covering activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, meal preparation) as well as chore and homemaker services. Eligible individuals may also receive gap-filling service dollars to cover needed care services if they meet financial and other eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents age 60 or older who require assistance with activities of daily living. The Senior Care component additionally targets those age 65 or older who are medically at risk of institutionalization and moderately or severely disabled.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home aide services for activities of daily living including bathing, dressing, meal preparation, chores, and homemaking; case management; and gap-filling service dollars for eligible individuals to cover needed care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Age 60 or older (Personal Care Program); age 65 or older (Senior Care Program)
Requires assistance with activities of daily living
Medically at risk of institutionalization (Senior Care component)
Moderately or severely disabled (Senior Care component)
Resident of Frederick County
Needs assistance with several daily activities such as bathing or meal preparation

A qualified staff person or team will conduct an in-home evaluation of needs. After services are identified, a case manager arranges the appropriate services. Gap-filling service dollars are available for those who meet financial and other eligibility criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that helps households in Frederick County learn eco-friendly actions, track progress toward going green, and earn certifications for their efforts. Participants choose from a variety of sustainability steps — covering energy efficiency, green lifestyle changes, and renewable energy — and earn points toward three certifications: Power Saver, Green Leader, and Renewable Star. The program is open to homeowners and renters alike.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Energy and Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online platform (frederickgreenchallenge.org) that guides participants through eco-friendly actions, tracks their environmental impact, and awards certifications (Power Saver, Green Leader, Renewable Star) upon reaching point thresholds. No direct financial payment — the program provides information, tracking tools, and recognition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and renters in Frederick County, Maryland who want to reduce their environmental impact and save money through sustainable home practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Guidance and certification for energy efficiency improvements, green lifestyle changes, and adoption of renewable energy (solar, wind, geothermal, sustainable biomass) for home power, heating, cooling, and hot water.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to households in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Open to any household — homeowners or renters, rural or urban
Register at frederickgreenchallenge.org to track actions and earn points
Choose actions across one or more of three challenge tracks: Power Saver, Green Leader, Renewable Star
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit frederickgreenchallenge.org to create an account, browse available eco-friendly actions, log completed actions to earn points, and work toward one or more certifications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Green Homes Program – Green Compass Community Navigator & Green Homes Challenge
structured_extraction.program_description: The Green Homes Program helps Frederick County residents create more sustainable households. It is administered by the Frederick County Division of Energy and Environment and includes three main components: Green Compass (Community Navigators who provide free one-on-one guidance to help residents identify and access local, state, and federal sustainability and energy efficiency programs and incentives, assist with applications, and offer referrals to partner organizations); the Green Homes Challenge (a free online platform at frederickgreenchallenge.org that guides participants through eco-friendly actions, tracks their environmental impact, and awards certifications — Power Saver, Green Leader, and Renewable Star — upon reaching point thresholds, open to homeowners and renters alike); and Green Incentives (financial assistance for home improvements, including Power Saver Retrofits for low- to moderate-income households and Septic Rebates open to any household with a septic system). Navigators also conduct outreach to neighborhood groups, churches, HOAs, and clubs. The program especially focuses on reaching residents who may not have considered sustainability before, including those facing energy cost burdens, climate risks, or other barriers. In late 2024, the program received a $997,266 EPA Environmental Justice grant, though federal funding was subsequently frozen in early 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Energy and Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one guidance from a Community Navigator who helps residents find and apply for energy efficiency and sustainability programs, including incentives for energy-efficient appliances, solar panels, electric vehicles and chargers, and home improvements. Financial incentives include Power Saver Retrofits (available to low- to moderate-income households) and Septic Rebates (open to any household with a septic system). The interactive Green Homes Challenge (frederickgreenchallenge.org) provides an online platform to track eco-friendly actions, log completed steps across Power Saver, Green Leader, and Renewable Star tracks, and earn certifications — no direct financial payment, but provides information, tracking tools, and recognition. Navigator services and the Green Homes Challenge platform are free to participants. In late 2024, the program received a $997,266 EPA Environmental Justice grant, though federal funding was subsequently frozen in early 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Frederick County residents — homeowners and renters, rural or urban — with special focus on low- to moderate-income households, minority, elderly, disabled, and other underserved populations who face greater climate risks or barriers to sustainable living, as well as residents seeking guidance on sustainability programs, energy efficiency improvements, and available incentives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy improvements, reduced energy costs, septic system upgrades, sustainable living support, and access to programs covering energy-efficient appliances, renewable energy (solar, wind, geothermal, sustainable biomass), and electric vehicles. Navigator services and the Green Homes Challenge platform are free to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Frederick County, Maryland
Open to all Frederick County residents — homeowners or renters, rural or urban
Power Saver Retrofit program limited to low- to moderate-income households
Septic Rebate program requires a septic system
Register at frederickgreenchallenge.org to track actions and earn points
Choose actions across one or more of three challenge tracks: Power Saver, Green Leader, Renewable Star
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Navigator by email at GreenHomes@FrederickCountyMD.gov or by phone at 301-600-1416 to schedule a consultation, or contact the same email to schedule a program for a group, neighborhood, or business. For the Green Homes Challenge, visit frederickgreenchallenge.org to create an account, browse available eco-friendly actions, log completed actions to earn points, and work toward one or more certifications. Follow @SustainableFCMD on Facebook and Instagram for event updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free home energy audits and no-cost energy-saving improvements for low- to moderate-income households in Frederick County. A certified contractor assesses the home's energy use, then approved improvements are made at no cost to the occupant or owner.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Energy and Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home energy audit by a certified contractor followed by no-cost energy-saving improvements including air sealing, insulation, caulking, duct sealing, lighting upgrades, water heater replacements, HVAC tune-ups or upgrades, and up to $1,500 for health and safety repairs related to implementing improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and occupants in Frederick County whose gross household income is below 85% of the county's median income based on family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Air sealing and insulation (attics and basements), window and door caulking and weather-stripping, duct sealing and insulation, energy-efficient lighting upgrades, heat pump water heater replacements, HVAC tune-ups or upgrades to Energy Star models, and up to $1,500 for health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Frederick County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Must be a registered participant in Frederick County's Green Homes Challenge
Gross household income must be less than 85% of Frederick County median income based on family size (e.g., $68,500 for 1 person, $97,800 for 4 people, $129,100 for 8 people)
Condominium, mobile home, and rental property residents should contact the PSR Coordinator to discuss eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application at the county website (preferred) or request a print application by calling 301-600-1416 or emailing PSR@FrederickCountyMD.gov. Applications are reviewed for eligibility. If approved, a certified contractor schedules a home energy audit. A list of projects is reviewed and approved by county staff and the homeowner before work begins.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County awards competitive grants to eligible nonprofit 501(c)(3) community organizations that provide and deliver services to Frederick County residents. The program supports four priority areas: addressing homelessness and housing solutions, quality of life initiatives, public health programs, and supporting the arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to eligible nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations serving Frederick County residents. One application per organization. Grantees must meet accountability standards. Specific award amounts are not stated on the program page; prior award lists are available for reference.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations that have been in operation for at least 3 years and provide a majority of direct services to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services targeting: homelessness and housing solutions (housing insecurity, affordable housing, financial literacy, aging in place); quality of life (childcare, senior support, youth empowerment, community inclusion, transportation); public health (food insecurity, mental health, behavioral health, substance use disorder, intimate partner violence, health equity, maternal health); and supporting the arts (cultural enrichment, placemaking, community arts programming).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must provide a majority of direct services to residents living within Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) organization (excluding churches, fraternal/civic organizations, homeowner associations, labor unions, cemeteries, volunteer fire departments, and private, political, or public foundations)
Must have been in operation for a minimum of 3 consecutive years with generating revenues and operating/administrative expense activities
Must provide a majority of direct services to Frederick County residents
Must be in good standing with the IRS, the Maryland Secretary of State's Charitable Division, and the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT)
Limit of one application per organization
Must meet accountability standards if awarded a grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open December 2, 2025, with an in-person information session held December 2 at 1:30 p.m. at Winchester Hall, 12 East Church Street, Frederick. Applications close January 20, 2026 at 4:00pm via the Foundant online grant portal. Technical assistance Q&A sessions are offered throughout the application period. The County Executive presents proposed awardees in April 2026, the County Council finalizes awards in May 2026, and the grant period of performance begins July 2026. Visit www.FrederickCountyMD.gov/CPG or email CPG@FrederickCountyMD.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County Government owns and operates Bell Court Apartments in Woodsboro, Maryland, providing affordable rental housing for low-income elderly residents. Tenants must be 62 years of age or older and have an annual income at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI), with some sources indicating eligibility at or below 30% AMI. There are typically no more than 1-2 vacancies per year, and the waiting list is currently closed.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Bell Court Apartments located in Woodsboro, Frederick County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and/or closing cost assistance for purchasing a home

Application submitted by the first mortgage lender

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Historic District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year decreasing property tax credit for owners of qualifying historic properties within the Frederick County historic district. The credit offsets property tax increases resulting from restoration or improvement work on existing residential and commercial structures. It provides a 100% credit on the increase in assessed value for the first two taxable years following qualifying work, then phases down over the remaining three years, for a total of five years of property tax relief. The program was enacted in 1975 and revised in 1990.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Planning and Permitting
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% credit on the increase in assessed property value in the first two taxable years following qualifying restoration or improvement work, phasing down over the remaining three years, for a total of five years of property tax relief on qualifying historic properties within the Frederick County historic district. Enacted in 1975 and revised in 1990.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of existing structures within the Frederick County historic district seeking to offset property tax increases resulting from restoration or improvement work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability resulting from increases in assessed value due to restoration or improvement work on qualifying historic district structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Structures within the Frederick County historic district, Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be an existing structure within the Frederick County historic district
Restoration or improvement work must result in an increase in assessed value as determined by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Improvements must be made to the existing structure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the Historic District Tax Credit document available on the Frederick County website at https://www.frederickcountymd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/10454. An information sheet is also available from the Frederick County Economic Development website at https://www.discoverfrederickmd.com/DocumentCenter/View/101/Frederick-County-Historic-District-Tax-Credit-PDF.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 25% credit on eligible exterior expenditures for locally designated historic properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties locally designated as historic by Frederick County, the City of Frederick, or the Town of New Market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible exterior expenditures on locally designated historic properties.

requirements_list: Property must be locally designated as historic by Frederick County, the City of Frederick, or the Town of New Market
Expenditures must be exterior and eligible under the program

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County offers competitive grants to eligible owners of historic properties in unincorporated areas of the county. Grant funds support exterior work to stabilize, rehabilitate, restore, or preserve historic buildings. Projects must meet the U.S. Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties. The program is administered by the Frederick County Division of Planning and Permitting and is designed to preserve, protect, and enhance rural historic properties. Properties must be designated on the County Register of Historic Places or be contributing resources in a County-designated Historic District.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Planning and Permitting
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $50,000 per applicant for exterior work to stabilize, rehabilitate, restore, or preserve historic buildings in unincorporated Frederick County. Grants will not be awarded for work already underway or completed, new construction, landscaping, or projects that do not meet the U.S. Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties located in unincorporated areas of Frederick County that are listed on the County Register of Historic Places or are contributing resources within a County-designated Historic District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior work to stabilize, rehabilitate, restore, or preserve historic buildings. Must meet the U.S. Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties. Funds may not be used for work already underway or completed, new construction, or landscaping.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in the unincorporated (rural) areas of Frederick County, Maryland, and must be designated on the County Register of Historic Places or be contributing resources in a County-designated Historic District.
requirements_list: Property must be located in an unincorporated area of Frederick County
Property must be designated on the County Register of Historic Places or be a contributing resource in a County-designated Historic District
Property must be in good standing with the County

If the property or district is not currently designated, a determination of eligibility must be made by the Historic Preservation Commission prior to applying, and the letter of determination must be included with the application
Projects must meet the U.S. Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties
Attendance at one informational workshop is required (registration required; virtual option available)
Grants will not cover work already underway or completed, new construction, or landscaping
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The grant cycle opens September 1, 2025 and closes November 30, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. Applicants must attend one informational workshop before applying (registration required at www.FrederickCountyMD.gov/HPGrant; virtual and in-person options available). Download and complete the Grant Application and review the Application Instructions from the program website. Submit application by the November 30, 2025 deadline. Award notifications take place in early Spring 2026. Contact staff with questions if unable to attend a workshop.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Capacity Fees for LEED-Certified Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County offers reduced water and sewer capacity fees for buildings and properties that earn LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification for water efficiency. The program assumes that LEED-certified buildings require less system capacity than comparable non-certified buildings, resulting in lower capacity fee charges. Established by Frederick County Resolution #12-14 on August 16, 2012.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduced water and sewer capacity fees for buildings and properties that obtain LEED certification for water efficiency. The reduction reflects the lower demand that LEED-certified buildings place on the county's water and sewer system. Established by Frederick County Resolution #12-14 on August 16, 2012.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers seeking building permits for properties that will pursue LEED certification for water efficiency within Frederick County's water and sewer service area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in water and sewer capacity fees owed to Frederick County at time of building permit issuance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Frederick County, Maryland, for properties served by the Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities. Applicable to building permits issued on or after August 16, 2012.
requirements_list: Building must obtain LEED certification for water efficiency
A Notice of Intent must be filed prior to issuance of the building permit (for permits issued on or after August 16, 2012)
Must execute a LEED Reduced Capacity Fee Agreement with the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Notice of Intent to Obtain LEED Certification before the building permit is issued. Upon achieving LEED certification for water efficiency, execute the LEED Reduced Capacity Fee Agreement with Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water and Sewer Capacity Fee Payment Plan Fund (PPF) for Small Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County offers a Payment Plan Fund (PPF) that provides loans to commercial water and/or wastewater customers — including small businesses — to help finance water and sewer capacity fees over time, rather than paying the full amount upfront. The program covers capacity fees required for new construction or expansion of existing facilities connected to the county's water and sewer system. Certain manufacturing companies may also be eligible for water and sewer lease opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to commercial water and/or wastewater customers to purchase water and sewer capacity fees in installments rather than as a lump sum. Covers new construction or expansion of existing facilities. Certain manufacturing companies may also be eligible for water and sewer lease opportunities. Specific loan terms and conditions are available in program documents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and commercial water and/or wastewater customers seeking to connect to, expand, or construct new facilities served by Frederick County's water and sewer system, including certain manufacturing companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of water and/or sewer capacity fees required for new construction or expansion of existing facilities connecting to Frederick County's water and sewer system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Frederick County, Maryland, for properties served by the Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a small business or commercial water and/or wastewater customer
Must have water and/or sewer capacity fees due to Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities
New construction or expansion of existing facilities required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Frederick County Division of Water and Sewer Utilities Accounting and Finance office at WaterSewerBilling@frederickcountymd.gov or 301-600-2354. Review the sample loan agreement and terms and conditions documents available on the website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Family Partnership is a family support center in Frederick County that provides free programs to help children, youth, and families build strong foundations. Using science-based approaches and protective factors, the center offers early childhood development services, parent education groups, and youth programs. All services are provided at no cost to eligible participants.

Youth ages 16–24 (youth program)

structured_extraction.program_description: The Career Explorer Program is a Frederick County Government initiative for high school students, college students, and individuals interested in skilled trades apprenticeships who want to explore careers in local government. The program provides guided, hands-on work experiences with mentorship from experienced public sector professionals. Participants gain career readiness skills, explore diverse roles across county departments, and develop a deeper understanding of local government.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on work experience placements across Frederick County Government departments, including mentorship, professional feedback, skill-building, and structured exploration of public sector career paths. Available tracks include Aging & Independence, Agriculture, Animal Control, County Council, Energy & Environment, Family Services, Fire & Rescue, Human Resources, Park & Recreation, Planning & Permitting, Public Works, Solid Waste & Recycling, and Water & Sewer Utilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Helping Empower Area Resources Together (HEART) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The HEART grant program provides one-time emergency grants of up to $50,000 to eligible nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in Frederick County that were impacted by the federal government shutdown. Grants are intended to help nonprofits cover operational expenses due to revenue gaps, increased costs, or expanded service demand resulting from the shutdown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 (capped at 10% of the organization's approved annual operating budget for fiscal year 2026) are awarded as a lump sum after the grant agreement is executed. Total program funding is approximately $1,500,000. Grant period runs from agreement execution through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in Frederick County that provide direct services to residents and were impacted by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational expenses resulting from revenue gaps or shortfalls; operational expenses from increased service demand; expansion of essential direct services to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must have a physical location in Frederick County and serve a majority (over 51%) of Frederick County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must have a physical location/address in Frederick County and serve over 51% of Frederick County residents
Must be in good standing with the IRS, Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and Frederick County Government
Must have been established prior to July 1, 2022, and plan to continue operating through at least June 30, 2026
Demonstrated impact from the federal government shutdown (e.g., decreased revenue, increased costs, financial insecurity)
Organizations under an umbrella or fiscal sponsor are not eligible

Ineligible organizations include: churches and religious organizations, fraternal/civic organizations, homeowner's associations, labor unions, private/political/public foundations, cemeteries, and volunteer fire departments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Frederick County online grant portal (Foundant). New users must create an account. Required attachments include: finalized budget with actuals for the last two fiscal years and year-to-date current fiscal year, good standing confirmation from Maryland SDAT, IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter, financial statements for the past year, and most recent IRS Form 990 or E-Postcard. Applications are reviewed by the Grant Management Department, which makes award recommendations to the County Executive for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program (LHRGLP)

Eligible activities include door and window treatment, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning. Funds are issued as a grant or loan depending on the applicant's ability to repay.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are provided as either a grant or a loan based on the applicant's ability to repay. The maximum loan term is 20 years. There are no income limits for the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners occupying their primary residence in Frederick County, landlords with rental properties, and licensed childcare facilities seeking to reduce lead-based paint hazards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door and window treatment, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning to reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Frederick County, Maryland. Units must be in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant.
requirements_list: Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead reduction work
Units must be located in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant
Rental properties built prior to 1950 must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Applicants must be Maryland residents of an owner-occupied property used as the principal residence (rental properties and licensed childcare facilities are also eligible)

structured_extraction.program_description: The STAR Program preserves and improves single-family properties by rehabilitating them to applicable building codes. STAR loans may also be used to build replacement houses under certain conditions. The program is funded with federal HOME funds, and HUD requirements apply. Grants may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fully deferred loans at zero percent interest. The maximum loan is generally 110 percent of the after-rehabilitation value of the property (exceptions considered case by case). Grants may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Loans are generally secured by a Deed of Trust.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with incomes at or below 30% of the Washington, D.C. MSA median income. Consideration may also be given to families with incomes at or below 55% of the statewide median income with a poor credit rating. In exceptional cases, borrowers with incomes up to 80% of the HUD-defined median may be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of single-family homes to applicable building codes, or construction of replacement houses under certain conditions. Property must meet HUD's definition of 'modest housing.'
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be owner-occupant of a single-family home

Income at or below 30% of the Washington, D.C. MSA median income (primary eligibility), OR at or below 55% of the statewide median income with a poor credit rating, OR up to 80% of HUD-defined median in exceptional cases
Property must meet HUD's definition of 'modest housing'
Loan generally secured by a Deed of Trust
Funded with federal HOME funds; HUD requirements apply

structured_extraction.program_description: The Agricultural Innovation Grant is a competitive grant program that helps improve the economic viability of Frederick County's agriculture industry by encouraging agricultural producers to expand, diversify, and innovate their business operations. Grants of $5,000 or more are available to a wide range of agricultural businesses including crop and livestock producers, value-added producers, seafood processors, timber product processors, and agricultural cooperatives. Funding may be used for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, equipment, and processing facilities. Applications are reviewed by a committee of banking, economic development, and agriculture representatives, who recommend award recipients to the County Executive for final approval. Projects are scored on a 100-point rubric covering project description, budget, innovation, economic impact, and business plan quality; businesses that have never received a Frederick County Agricultural Innovation Grant receive bonus points.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of $5,000 or more awarded to eligible agricultural producers in Frederick County. Funds can be used for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, equipment, and processing facilities. Applicants are scored on a 100-point rubric; businesses that have never received a Frederick County Agricultural Innovation Grant receive bonus points. A review committee recommends award recipients to the County Executive for final approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Next cycle opens October 1, 2026; March 31 (March 2026 cycle)

Applications must be well-documented proposals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Develop a business plan using available resources (University of Minnesota, Maryland SBDC, Maryland Women's Business Center). 2. Contact the Frederick County Zoning Office to confirm the project is an allowed use. 3. If the project involves additional waste discharge, contact the Frederick County Health Department. 4. If the property is in a Land Preservation Easement, contact Shannon O'Neil. 5. Prepare a detailed budget broken down by category and list other funding sources. 6. Prepare a 'Capital Needed' description. 7. Write an Economic Impact Description. 8. Submit the completed application online at the Frederick County Agricultural Innovation Grant webpage when the grant cycle opens. A review committee recommends award recipients to the County Executive for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Installment Purchase Program and Forest Resource Ordinance Collaboration
structured_extraction.program_description: The Frederick County Office of Agriculture and Division of Planning and Permitting offer a combined easement program that helps preserve farmland and protect natural resources. Eligible farmers and landowners can place a combined Installment Purchase Program (IPP) and Forest Resource Ordinance (FRO) easement on their land. The IPP purchases agricultural preservation easements to permanently restrict development on farmland and woodland, paying the landowner tax-free interest over a 10- to 20-year term with a balloon lump sum principal payment at the end. Eligible applicants who receive an IPP easement offer may also elect an optional FRO easement, which uses fee-in-lieu funds to provide an upfront lump sum payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Installment Purchase Program pays landowners tax-free interest over a 10- to 20-year term with a balloon lump sum principal payment at the end of the term, in exchange for permanently restricting development on farmland and woodland. Eligible applicants may also opt into the Forest Resource Ordinance easement, which provides an upfront lump sum payment using fee-in-lieu funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners in Frederick County seeking to preserve farmland and protect natural resources through combined easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation of farmland and woodland through agricultural preservation easements; protection of forest resources through Forest Resource Ordinance easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must submit application by September 2, 2025
Requirements detailed on the Office of Agriculture website at www.FrederickCountyMD.gov/IPP

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Commercial & Industrial Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a 10-year real property tax credit for businesses conducting manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations in Frederick County. Qualifying businesses must make a total new investment of at least $5 million and create at least 25 new permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The credit reduces the amount of property tax owed on the value of new improvements resulting from building or expanding a facility. If the average credit over the 10 years exceeds 60% of the new tax amount, County Council approval is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit for businesses that construct or expand facilities in a Priority Funding Area within Frederick County and create a significant number of new full-time jobs. To qualify, businesses must construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet and create at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years of expansion. The standard credit is applied over six years on the increased assessed value of the expanded property: 52% for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, and 26% for years five and six. An Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is available for larger expansions of at least 250,000 square feet, providing a 12-year credit equal to 58.5% of the property tax imposed on the increase in assessment of the new or expanded premises and any substantially renovated adjoining property (where renovation covers at least 50% of each building). The Enhanced credit requires creation of at least 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, or alternatively at least 2,500 full-time jobs with 500 additional positions, all paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. Available for new construction only.
