The business must be located in a Frederick County Priority Funding Area, and may be an existing county business or one relocating from outside Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County's Parks and Recreation Commission (FCPRC) awards grants to eligible non-profit community organizations that provide recreation opportunities for county residents. Grants fund improvements to existing recreation facilities or construction of new ones on land owned or used by the applicant organization.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to a share of a $50,000 annual budget are awarded to eligible organizations. Funds are provided before project construction and can be applied toward materials, equipment, and contracted labor. Construction labor may be volunteer or paid contractor. Grants are not awarded for routine maintenance. Projects must be completed within two years of July 1 of the funding year.

Funds may not be used for routine maintenance or for projects on land owned by federal, state, municipal, or Frederick County governments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Taxi Access Program (TAP) is a supplemental transportation service for eligible Transit Plus participants in Frederick County. Eligible users receive a monthly allotment of taxi funds loaded onto a reloadable swipe card with photo ID. The county subsidizes a portion of each fare, and participants pay a zip code-based co-pay. Up to three months of funds can be stored on the card.

Participating taxi companies swipe the card to pay the fare.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County Transit Services offers the Vanpool Incentive Program (VIP) to help new vanpools get started in Frederick County. The program provides a financial subsidy to cover the cost of empty seats during the first year of operation, helping new vanpools become self-sustaining by offsetting operating costs while the vanpool builds its rider base. As more riders join, the subsidy decreases. The program is particularly targeted at employees and commuters who travel 30 or more miles. Eligible operating expenses include lease cost and gasoline. Maximum monthly subsidy amounts vary by vehicle size: months 1–6 range from $263 (7-passenger) to $500 (15-passenger); months 7–12 range from $158 (7-passenger) to $300 (15-passenger).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible vanpools receive a monthly financial subsidy for empty seats during the first 12 months of operation. The subsidy is calculated per unfilled seat based on total eligible operating expenses (lease cost and gasoline) divided by available seating positions (excluding the driver). As more riders join, the subsidy decreases. Maximum monthly amounts vary by vehicle size: months 1–6 range from $263 (7-passenger) to $500 (15-passenger); months 7–12 range from $158 (7-passenger) to $300 (15-passenger). The program is targeted at commuters traveling 30 or more miles.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of empty seats in a new vanpool during the first 12 months of operation, based on lease costs and gasoline expenses, while the vanpool grows to full capacity.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Garrett County Commissioners Scholarship Program provides Garrett County high school graduates with equal access to post-secondary education at Garrett College. Established in 2006, the program aims to build an educated, skilled workforce and support the county's economic development by investing in its young people. The program includes both an academic scholarship (GCAS) for credit degree or certificate programs and an occupational scholarship (GCOS) for workforce training and industry certification programs. It is the first program of its kind in Maryland, making post-secondary education financially and geographically accessible for local youth.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Board of County Commissioners
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two scholarship components: (1) Garrett County Academic Scholarship (GCAS) covers tuition and combined fees for credit degree or certificate programs at Garrett College, up to 64 credit hours maximum plus required developmental studies courses; full-time enrollment (12+ credits/semester) required; does not cover repeated courses; (2) Garrett County Occupational Scholarship (GCOS) covers tuition/course fees, course materials, and industry certification testing fees for occupational training programs (e.g., Welding, CNA, CNC Machining, Medical Coding, Truck Driving, Underground Mining, Veterinary Assistant); maximum annual GCOS amount equals average GCAS awards from prior fiscal year. Both scholarships are combined with external financial aid to cover costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Garrett County high school graduates (public school including Northern Garrett HS and Southern Garrett HS, homeschooled, state-approved non-public schools such as Salem School, and GED recipients) seeking post-secondary education or occupational/workforce training at Garrett College; dual-enrolled high school students and ECAP participants are also eligible
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: (1) Academic track: tuition and combined fees for credit degree or certificate programs at Garrett College, up to 64 credit hours plus required developmental studies courses; (2) Occupational track: tuition, course fees, course materials, and industry certification testing fees for occupational training programs leading to industry-recognized certifications
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett County, Maryland residents who have been legally documented residents of Garrett County for 2 full years prior to graduation or GED completion; students in State custody must have been documented as placed in Garrett County
requirements_list: Must be a Garrett County high school graduate (public school including Northern Garrett HS and Southern Garrett HS, homeschooled, state-approved non-public school, or GED recipient)
Must have been a legally documented resident of Garrett County for 2 full years prior to graduation or GED completion
Must enroll at Garrett College

Academic scholarship (GCAS): must enroll in credit degree or certificate program; required developmental studies courses covered (with exception for dual-enrolled students); does not cover repeated courses; maximum 64 credit hours; full-time enrollment (12+ credits/semester) required
Occupational scholarship (GCOS): must enroll in qualifying occupational training program leading to industry-recognized certification; does not cover repeated courses
Dual-enrolled high school students charged 50% tuition
Enrollment must begin in the fall semester immediately following high school graduation (NHS or SHS), with limited exceptions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Policies and procedures are detailed in the program document developed in coordination with the Board of Education and Garrett College. The governing document was effective July 1, 2010 and approved by the Board of County Commissioners on July 2, 2010. No specific application deadline or submission window is described in available documentation; contact the Garrett County Commissioners office at 301-334-8970 or commissioners@garrettcountymd.gov for current application procedures. Note: available program documentation dates from 2014; current program status should be verified directly with Garrett County or Garrett College.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to for-profit restaurant and bar businesses in Garrett County to help fund outdoor dining infrastructure such as heaters, outdoor furniture, patio fencing, umbrellas, and lighting. Grants cover up to 90% of eligible project costs, up to $5,000, and are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted. Applicants must contribute at least 10% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $5,000, covering up to 90% of eligible project costs. The applicant must contribute at least 10% of the total project cost. Funds are limited each fiscal year and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Eligible costs include portable electric heaters, portable outdoor gas-fired heating appliances, outdoor furniture (tables and chairs), patio fencing or physical barriers, folding umbrellas, and lighting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit restaurants and bars with a fixed physical location in Garrett County that are currently in operation and open to the general public. Private clubs and member-only organizations are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Portable electric heaters, portable outdoor gas-fired heating appliances, outdoor furniture (tables and chairs), patio fencing or physical barriers to delineate outdoor seating space, folding umbrellas for tables, and lighting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant business must have a fixed physical location in Garrett County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit business offering restaurant and/or bar service
Must be currently in operation and open to the general public
Must have a fixed physical location in Garrett County
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Garrett County Government
Must hold a current Garrett County Business License, if required by law
Must submit the grant application and receive written notice of grant approval before incurring any expenses
Must contribute at least 10% of total project costs
Not eligible for multiple awards during the same fiscal year
Private clubs and member-only organizations are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application and await written notice of grant approval before incurring any expenses. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted. Contact Kim Durst for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Business Property Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County offers a property tax credit to new and expanding businesses that make improvements to business property. The improvement must increase the tax assessment by at least $100,000 to qualify. The credit applies to the county's portion of real property tax on the new improvements for five years, starting at 50% in year one and decreasing by 10 percentage points each year (40%, 30%, 20%) to 10% in year five. Eligible projects include new construction, expanding, renovating, or making capital improvements to a business property. Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A five-year tax credit against the county's portion of real property tax on new business property improvements. The credit starts at 50% of the assessed value of the new improvements in year one and decreases by 10 percentage points each year (40%, 30%, 20%), reaching 10% in year five. The improvement must increase the tax assessment by at least $100,000 to qualify. Eligible uses include new construction, renovations, and purchase of real property improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding commercial or industrial businesses in Garrett County that make qualifying improvements to business property, including corporations, LLCs, partnerships, sole proprietorships, non-profits, ESOPs, and other business entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property tax on assessed value of new improvements to business property. Eligible projects include new construction, renovations, or purchase of real property improvements to a business property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses in Garrett County, Maryland, for improvements reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007.
requirements_list: New improvement must increase the tax assessment on the property improvements by at least $100,000
Must be a new or expanding business in Garrett County
Complete and submit the application to the Department of Economic Development
Must notify the Department immediately upon completion of any expansion, renovation, or capital improvement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, notify the Garrett County Department of Economic Development of intent to apply, ideally right after completing any property expansion, renovation, or improvement. Then complete the Business Property Tax Incentive Application and submit it to the department. If the business qualifies, the department issues a certificate of eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Agriculture Marketing Grant Program provides grants to aid in the promotion and marketing of agriculture-based businesses located in Garrett County, Maryland. The program helps local farms, farm businesses, farm-related businesses, and farm-related organizations or associations fund marketing and promotional efforts to improve visibility, attract new customers, and grow their operations. Grants are awarded as reimbursements after approved purchases are made. FY 2025 Agriculture Marketing Grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 (up to 90% of total project cost) for eligible marketing expenses. Applicants must provide a minimum 10% match of total project cost. Funds are disbursed as reimbursement only after purchases are made and documentation is submitted. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability. Grant awards are taxable income and recipients receive a 1099. FY 2025 Agriculture Marketing Grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY 2026 are now closed (original deadline: May 15, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farms, farm businesses, farm-related businesses, and farm-related organizations or associations based in Garrett County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible marketing expenses include: website development or redesign (including e-commerce), digital marketing (social media ads, Google ads), print advertising, radio or television advertising, graphic design for branding or promotions, signage and banners, and farmers market display items (canopies, tables, tablecloths).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Garrett County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farm, farm business, farm-related business, or farm-related organization or association based in Garrett County, Maryland
Must be a registered business in good standing with the State of Maryland and Garrett County Government, if required by law
Must hold a current business license if one is required for the business type
Must submit a completed application including a signed IRS W-9 form and vendor information request form before making any purchases
Must have at least 10% matching funds
All approved purchases must be completed within 30 days of written grant approval
Proof of purchases and payments must be submitted within 30 days of written grant approval
FY 2025 Agriculture Marketing Grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026
Applicant is not eligible for multiple awards in any given fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a completed application with cost estimates or vendor quotes, proof of 10% matching funds, business license (if required), verification of good standing, signed IRS W-9 form, and completed Vendor Information Request form. 2. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; applicants are notified in writing of approval status. 3. Make approved purchases within 30 days of written grant approval. 4. Submit proof of purchases (itemized invoices/receipts) and payments within 30 days of written grant approval. 5. Receive reimbursement for approved expenses up to 90% of $1,000.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Business Marketing Grant Program helps small for-profit, non-agricultural businesses in Garrett County fund marketing and promotional efforts to improve visibility, attract new customers, and grow business operations. Two tiers are available based on employee size: one for businesses with 1 to 25 employees and one for businesses with 26 to 75 employees. Grants are awarded as reimbursements of up to $1,000 (covering up to 90% of eligible marketing expenses) after approved purchases are made. Applicants must provide a minimum 10% match of total project cost. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to available funds. FY 2025 grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 (covering up to 90% of eligible marketing expenses). Two employee-size tiers: 1–25 employees and 26–75 employees. Applicants must provide a minimum 10% match of total project cost. Purchases must be made after written grant approval and within 30 days of approval. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to available funds. Grant awards are taxable income and recipients receive a 1099. FY 2025 grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY 2026 are now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small for-profit, non-agricultural businesses with a physical location in Garrett County, Maryland, with 1 to 75 employees (two tiers: 1–25 employees and 26–75 employees).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible marketing expenses include: website development or redesign, digital marketing (social media ads, Google ads), print advertising, radio or television advertising, graphic design for branding or promotions, and signage or promotional materials.

Must have between 1 and 75 employees (two tiers: 1–25 and 26–75 employees)
Must be a registered business in good standing with the State of Maryland and Garrett County Government
Must hold a current business license if required for the business type
Home-based businesses, independent contractors, national franchises/chains (unless locally owned and operated), non-profits, religious organizations, and agriculture-based businesses are ineligible
FY 2025 Small Business Marketing Grant recipients are not eligible to apply in FY 2026
Must submit completed application including IRS W-9 form and vendor information request form before making any purchases
All approved purchases must be completed within 30 days of written grant approval
Proof of purchases and payments must be submitted within 30 days of written grant approval
Minimum 10% matching funds required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application (including IRS W-9 form and vendor information request form) with cost estimates or vendor quotes, documentation of at least 10% matching funds, employee details, business license, and verification of good standing. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. After written approval, make purchases within 30 days, then submit proof of purchases and payments for reimbursement. The FY 2026 application deadline was May 15, 2026; applications are now closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County Government subsidizes the cost of connecting difficult-to-serve addresses to broadband internet service. When a resident receives a quote from an internet service provider (ISP) that is too expensive to afford, the program can cover some or all of the required customer contribution, paying the ISP directly to extend service to the home or business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county pays subsidies directly to internet service providers to cover the cost of extending broadband service to a difficult-to-serve address. The customer may be asked to contribute up to 10% of the requested subsidy amount if possible. Funding per project and total program funding are both limited. ISPs must also contribute to each project and must participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP, if funded) to qualify. Only expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service are eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Garrett County residents who have been quoted a price to bring broadband service to their home that is unaffordable or partially unaffordable
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering the cost of extending broadband internet infrastructure to a difficult-to-serve residential or business address. Payments go directly to the internet service provider.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to addresses in Garrett County, Maryland that cannot be served by an existing broadband provider (minimum 100 Mbps download / 20 Mbps upload).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Garrett County resident who has been quoted a price for broadband service that is out of their budget
Address must not already be served by a provider offering at least 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload
Address must not be reachable by another provider without a subsidy
The internet service provider must also contribute to the project
The internet service provider must participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP), if that program is funded
Customer may be asked to contribute up to 10% of the subsidy amount if possible
All payments are made directly to the internet service provider — no direct customer expenses can be reimbursed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The customer contacts an ISP requesting service; the ISP assesses the project and provides a cost estimate. If the cost is unaffordable, the customer can ask the ISP to request a subsidy, or the customer can contact Cheryl DeBerry directly at broadband@garrettcountymd.gov or 301-914-1543. If the subsidy is approved, the ISP begins the project (permits, easements, or other legal requirements may delay the actual connection).

structured_extraction.program_name: Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County's Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area program allows property owners within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area to sell a perpetual conservation easement to the County using available Rural Legacy funds. The program protects over 31,000 acres of the Bear Creek watershed, preserving productive agricultural land, forests, view sheds, natural habitats, and waterways.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Planning & Land Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area may sell a perpetual conservation easement to Garrett County using available Maryland Rural Legacy Program funds. The easement permanently restricts development on the land.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area in northern Garrett County who want to sell a perpetual conservation easement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of perpetual conservation easements to protect agricultural land, forests, view sheds, natural habitats, and waterways within the Bear Creek watershed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area in the northern part of Garrett County, Maryland, near reference points including US 219, MD 42, MD 495 and towns such as Hoyes, Accident, McHenry, and Friendsville.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Garrett County Planning & Land Management Division for information about selling a conservation easement within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area.

structured_extraction.program_name: Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program helps preserve agricultural land by allowing eligible landowners to enroll their farmland in a preservation district. Enrolled properties may qualify for a property tax credit and may become eligible to sell a conservation easement to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Properties within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area may also be eligible to sell an agricultural preservation easement to the County. Neighboring landowners with smaller parcels may form a collective to meet acreage requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Planning & Land Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved Agricultural Preservation District or easement properties receive a tax credit on all agricultural lands and woodlands. The property tax on all real estate is 100% rebated under the Tax Credit Program. Taxes continue to be assessed on residential and agricultural structures. If the district is terminated, the landowner must repay all back property taxes plus interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with agricultural land and woodlands in Garrett County, including owner-operated and tenant-operated farms. Properties in the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area may also offer to sell an agricultural preservation easement to the County. Neighboring landowners with smaller parcels may form a collective to meet acreage requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief on agricultural lands and woodlands enrolled in a preservation district or easement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett County, Maryland. Land within the boundaries of a 10-year water and sewer service area plan is generally not eligible unless it has extraordinary productive capability and is of significant size. Properties within the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area may be eligible to sell an agricultural preservation easement to the County.
requirements_list: Minimum 50 contiguous acres (smaller parcels may qualify if adjoining an existing district or having extraordinary agricultural capability)
Land must meet soil productivity criteria (Class I, II, or III soils; or Groups 1 or 2)
Land must not be within the 10-year water and sewer service area plan unless it has extraordinary productive capability and is of significant size
Minimum 3-year commitment to agricultural use
Must sign and notarize the Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Agreement
No subdivision or development for residential, commercial, or industrial use unless approved by the County
Property must be approved by the Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, the Planning Commission, and the Board of Garrett County Commissioners
Landowner must complete the District Property Description form
Property must be approved as an Agricultural Preservation District or easement property
Property must meet soil productivity requirements as determined by the Garrett Soil Conservation District
A Soil and Water Conservation Plan revised within the last 10 years is required
A tax map outlining property boundaries must be submitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Planning & Land Management staff to obtain required forms. Complete the District Property Description form with assistance from the Garrett Soil Conservation District (301-334-6951) to confirm the property meets soil productivity requirements. The application is reviewed by the Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board and the Garrett County Planning Commission, and must be approved by the Board of Garrett County Commissioners. Sign and notarize the Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Agreement upon approval.

structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Planning & Land Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: POS funding is used to purchase parks, conservation areas, and recreational facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and conservation entities seeking to acquire parkland and open space in Garrett County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of ballfields, playgrounds, tennis courts, boating facilities, swimming pools, fishing sites, hunting areas, forests, golf courses, hiking trails, greenways, wildlife areas, historic sites, and other natural community resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free or low-cost English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) classes offered by the Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center for immigrants and non-native English speakers in Montgomery County. Classes are offered in person and online via Zoom at multiple levels (Basic through Level 4) and meet for 8 weeks per session. Related services offered by the center include Basic Computer Skills, English Conversation, and Citizenship Preparation.

Online Saturday classes are free. Online evening classes require a $35 textbook fee. Placement is determined by an online placement test taken during registration. In-person locations: Wheaton (11002 Veirs Mill Rd, Suite 506, Wheaton, MD 20902) and Gaithersburg Library, 2nd floor (18330 Montgomery Village Ave, Gaithersburg, MD 20879). Online classes available via Zoom (evenings and Saturdays).
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident
Must be age 18 or older
Online registration required
Online placement test required to determine class level
Classes meet for 8 weeks with regular attendance required
Students may not register for both Evening and Saturday classes
Space is limited — registration is first-come, first-served
Completing the registration form does not guarantee a spot

Test results determine class level placement. If no space is available, the program will help connect applicants to alternative providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free in-person and online classes that prepare permanent residents and immigrants to apply for U.S. citizenship. Classes cover U.S. history, civics, and English reading, writing, and speaking skills needed for the naturalization interview and test. In-person classes are held on Saturdays at the Gaithersburg Library; online classes are held on Tuesdays and are accessible via smartphone, tablet, or computer. Classes run approximately 10 weeks per session on a seasonal schedule.
structured_extraction.agency: Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center, Montgomery County Community Engagement Cluster
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free citizenship preparation classes offered in-person on Saturdays at the Gaithersburg Library and online on Tuesdays. Classes run approximately 10 weeks per session on a seasonal schedule (spring, summer, fall, winter). Students may only register for one class per session. Covers U.S. history, civics, and English language skills to help applicants prepare for the naturalization interview and exam. One-on-one tutoring, exam prep, application assistance, and childcare support may also be available. Classes offered in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for WINTER 2026 classes is now closed. Check again later for information about our Spring session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County, MD residents aged 18 or older who are permanent residents (green card holders) for at least four years, or two years if married to a U.S. citizen, with at least basic English skills; immigrants and lawful permanent residents interested in applying for U.S. citizenship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparation for the U.S. naturalization test and citizenship interview, including civics, U.S. history, and English language skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, MD resident. In-person classes held at the Gaithersburg Library. Some partner providers in the broader DC metro area may also serve residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, MD resident
Must be 18 years or older
Must have been a permanent resident (green card holder) for at least four years, or two years if married to a U.S. citizen
Must have at least basic English skills
Students may only register for ONE class per session
Interested in applying for or preparing for U.S. citizenship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online using the registration form linked on the program page. Classes fill up quickly; if full, applicants are directed to other providers. Find additional resources and class information through the Montgomery County Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Management Assistance Grants provide funds for nonprofit organizations to hire consulting expertise to support initiatives such as strategic planning, program evaluation, merger exploration, fund development, and sustainability planning. The program targets smaller, well-established nonprofits primarily operating in metropolitan Baltimore, with most recipients having operating budgets of less than $2 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund consulting services for nonprofit capacity-building activities. Amount is not specified. A cash match is required: at least 50% of the grant for organizations with budgets of $250,000 or more, or at least 25% for organizations with budgets under $250,000. Applications are accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis, with board funding decisions made approximately once per quarter. Applicants must contact the Foundation's program officer before submitting to confirm eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Smaller, well-established nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations carrying out their work principally in metropolitan Baltimore, primarily Baltimore City. Most recipients have operating budgets of less than $2 million. Organizations must have completed at least two full budget years and be able to demonstrate program outcomes already achieved. Not intended as start-up support for new nonprofits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engagement of qualified consulting expertise for strategic planning, fund development, financial management, program evaluation, IT assessment, board development, service delivery systems, and merger/partnership exploration. Not for hardware or software purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must carry on their work principally in metropolitan Baltimore, primarily Baltimore City. Preference is given to organizations with programs in the Foundation's interest areas (community development and education), but applications from any organization not conflicting with grantmaking policies will be considered.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization under IRS Section 501(c)(3) and 509(a)
Must operate principally in metropolitan Baltimore, primarily Baltimore City
Must be a smaller, well-established nonprofit; most recipients have operating budgets of less than $2 million
Must have completed at least two full budget years
Must be able to demonstrate program outcomes already achieved
Not intended as start-up support for new nonprofits
Must not discriminate on the basis of race, creed, color, physical handicap, or gender
Must contact Foundation program officer Annie Milli for a mandatory pre-application meeting before submitting an application
Applications submitted without prior approval will not be considered
Cash match required: at least 50% of grant for organizations with budgets of $250,000 or more, or at least 25% for organizations with budgets under $250,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Email Annie Milli (Program Officer) to request an interview and discuss your initiative. 2) Participate in an interview to confirm eligibility. 3) Prepare a detailed proposal with the assistance of the Foundation's review committee. 4) Submit the detailed proposal with required attachments. 5) Foundation staff review materials and notify applicants; requests are considered at one of four quarterly board meetings. Applicants are notified in writing after each meeting. Grantees must submit progress reports at 6 and 12 months after grant award.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Adult Day Reporting Center (DRCE) program enables local jurisdictions in Maryland to implement a Day Reporting Center that provides community-based services and treatment to individuals under parole, probation, or pretrial supervision. The goal is to reduce recidivism, jail and prison populations, and corrections-related costs. Centers are highly structured, non-residential programs offering counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, drug treatment, educational remediation, job training, and intense supervision. Participants live at home and report to the center regularly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Body Armor for Local Law Enforcement (BARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: BARM is a state-funded reimbursement grant to non-state local law enforcement agencies. It reimburses 50% of the cost of bullet-resistant body armor vests purchased for sworn law enforcement officers in any Maryland county, incorporated city or town, including Baltimore City. State agencies are not eligible. A 50% cash match is required from local government funds or agency/county budgets (not state or federal grant funds, except Federal Bulletproof Vest Program funds are allowable for match). Reimbursement is made on a quarterly basis following timely submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP/BSCI)
structured_extraction.program_description: Authorized by the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (BSCA) of 2022, the Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP/BSCI) provides states with funding to implement firearm violence reduction strategies at the intersections of behavioral health and domestic violence. This includes funding for extreme risk protection order (ERPO) programs that temporarily remove guns from individuals who pose a threat to themselves or others, mental health courts, drug courts, veteran treatment courts, behavioral health deflection programs, and law enforcement gun storage initiatives. In Maryland, the program is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) as the State Administering Agency. The SFY 2026 NOFA is titled BEACON (Building Engagement Around Crisis, Outreach, and Navigation).

Authorized under the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act of 2022. Up to 30 awards anticipated; funding range starts at $50,000. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement of expenditures basis and may cover personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other costs. The SFY 2026 NOFA is titled BEACON (Building Engagement Around Crisis, Outreach, and Navigation). The anticipated period of performance for SFY2026 awards is October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026. Individuals and for-profit entities are not eligible.

Individuals and for-profit entities are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: ERPO programs; training for ERPO implementers; communication and public awareness initiatives; specialized court-based programs (drug, mental health, veterans treatment courts); behavioral health deflection programs; law enforcement gun storage and tracking; and other crisis intervention strategies including violence reduction. Allowable cost categories include personnel, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, and equipment. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, lobbying, and promotional trinkets.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Advocacy Center Services (CACS) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The CACS grant program funds Child Advocacy Centers (CACs) across Maryland. CACs bring together professionals from law enforcement, child protective services, and social work into multi-disciplinary teams to coordinate investigative and intervention services for child abuse and sexual crime cases. CACs assist in responding to and investigating allegations of sexual crimes against children and child abuse, and provide care meeting accreditation standards under the Maryland Statewide Organization for Child Advocacy Centers. The goal is to create a child-focused approach to child abuse investigations so that child victims are not re-traumatized by the systems meant to protect them. CACs must meet accreditation standards under the Maryland Statewide Organization for Child Advocacy Centers and be recognized under Maryland State Statute §11-928. Funding was established by a 2010 state law requiring annual budget appropriations to supplement (not replace) existing program funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State budget funds are awarded on an annual grant cycle (SFY 2027 cycle currently open) to designated Child Advocacy Centers and the Maryland Children's Alliance. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursable, quarterly basis and may be used for personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other allowable categories. Allowable costs include salaries and fringe benefits (up to 30%), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications, office/project supplies), travel (mileage, lodging, meals per Maryland state rates), contractual services (consultant training/evaluation; max $81.25/hour or $650/day without preapproval), equipment (≥$10,000 useful life ≥1 year), and indirect costs (up to 15% de minimis or negotiated NICRA). Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction/capital expenses, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), prior debt, and trinkets. Grants supplement but do not supplant existing funding from other sources.

Eligible entities include 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) nonprofits, units of local government, state agencies, and institutions of higher learning that operate qualifying CACs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (salaries, fringe benefits up to 30%), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications, office/project supplies), travel (mileage, lodging, meals per Maryland state rates), contractual services (consultant training, evaluation; max $81.25/hour or $650/day without preapproval), equipment (≥$10,000 useful life, ≥1 year), and other costs including registration fees, program supplies, and indirect costs (up to 15% de minimis or negotiated NICRA). Budget line items must be tied to specific Goals and Objectives outlined in the application narrative. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction/capital expenses, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), prior debt, and trinkets.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act Regional Navigator Program (RGNV)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Regional Navigator Program Grant (RNPG) funds community-based nonprofit organizations, Designated Child Advocacy Centers, and Rape Crisis Centers to provide screening and services for child sex trafficking victims under the Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act of 2019. The program places Regional Navigators in jurisdictions across Maryland to connect children identified as potential trafficking victims with needed services, helping them achieve self-sufficiency and safety. The program began as a pilot in 3 jurisdictions in FY2020, expanded to 10 jurisdictions, and has since expanded to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions using ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) funds. Grant funding is disbursed on a quarterly reimbursable basis, and the program operates on an annual NOFA cycle.

Grants are disbursed on a quarterly reimbursable basis. The SFY2026 cycle (RNPG) is continuation funding for previously funded Regional Navigator Programs serving all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. The SFY2024 cycle anticipated up to eight awards with up to $1,750,000 total available. Specific award amounts per organization are not stated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Children's Justice Act Committee (CJAC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The CJAC Grant Program provides federal grants under the Children's Justice Act (originally established by Congress in 1986) and the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act (CAPTA) to support the prevention, assessment, investigation, prosecution, and judicial handling of cases of child abuse and neglect, with a particular focus on child sexual abuse and exploitation. The program aims to limit additional trauma to child victims while improving outcomes for children. The Children's Justice Act Committee reviews grant applications and makes funding recommendations. Eligible organizations may use funds to develop, establish, and operate programs addressing child abuse and neglect cases across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding to develop, establish, and operate programs addressing child abuse and neglect cases. Approximately $282,000 total available; 5-7 sub-awards ranging $50,000–$75,000 each. Funded cost categories include personnel (salary, fringe, MDT members, child abuse investigators), contractual services, equipment ($10,000+ per unit), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage), travel (per State of Maryland and GSA rates), and other related costs. Consultant rate cap is $81.25/hr or $650/day; fringe benefits may not exceed 30% of salary costs without prior approval. Reimbursement is on a quarterly basis. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), previous debt, and trinkets.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Grant Program Fund helps local law enforcement agencies establish community programs and helps local government agencies establish violence intervention programs. Eligible programs must provide recreational or athletic opportunities, improve relations between citizens and law enforcement, otherwise benefit or improve the community, or establish violence intervention programs supported by local law enforcement or another local government agency. Up to $500,000 in total grant funding is available for SFY 2027, with individual awards ranging from $5,000 to $50,000 (up to 25 awards). Awards are reimbursed on a quarterly basis with a period of performance from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: COAP (also known as COSSUP — Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Use Program) provides funding to states, tribes, territories, and local governments to respond to illicit substance use and misuse, reduce overdose deaths, promote public safety, and support access to prevention, harm-reduction, treatment, and recovery services. In Maryland, the program supports community-based programs, diversion from the criminal justice system through law enforcement and other first responder-based responses, court-based programs, and programming in jails and prisons to improve access to care. Funded activities include expanding medication-assisted treatment, advancing racial equity, enhancing harm reduction efforts, supporting youth prevention programs, expanding the addiction workforce, and expanding recovery support services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (BJAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Byrne Justice Assistance Grants (BJAG) support a broad range of state and local criminal justice initiatives critical to Maryland's goal of reducing crime and improving public safety. Funds are designed to reduce gaps in service that affect violent crime, crime victims, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, rehabilitation, courts, crime prevention, corrections, and drug treatment. The program also supports improving sentencing and correction policies, protecting victims, tracking DNA, training local law enforcement, providing technology to law enforcement, firearm violence prevention, behavioral health diversion, reentry and workforce integration, data and technology infrastructure, and victim services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal formula grant funding supporting a broad range of criminal justice activities statewide in Maryland. Eligible costs include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to criminal justice programs addressing violent crime, crime victims, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, rehabilitation, courts, crime prevention, corrections, and drug treatment. Specific award amounts are not stated. Funds are disbursed on a quarterly reimbursable basis. The standard annual timeline begins in spring with a review of crime data and legislative priorities; the NOFA is released in summer (typically August), with applications due in early fall (typically September); awards are issued in early fall for a performance period beginning October 1. Federal funds may not supplant state/local funds and must supplement existing program funding. Equipment is defined as items with unit cost over $10,000 and useful life over one year. Indirect cost rate must be current/unexpired federally approved OR eligible for 15% de minimis rate per 2 CFR 200.414(f). Single audit required if subrecipient expends $1M+ in federal funds annually per 2 CFR §200.514.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program makes temporary shelter environments and supportive services available through a network of local domestic violence services programs. These programs provide comprehensive services to meet the specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families. Providing these services locally increases the likelihood that victims will benefit from them and that there shall be appropriate linkages to other community-based services as needed. FVPS supports the establishment, maintenance, and expansion of programs to prevent family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence; provide immediate shelter and supportive services for victims and their dependents; and provide specialized services for children exposed to violence, underserved populations, and racial/ethnic minority victims. Provision of services fosters a coordinated community approach to serving domestic violence victims that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other related support agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funds assist law enforcement agencies and prosecutors that have a demonstrated need and a viable plan to address firearms-related violence in their jurisdictions. The program was established under the Responsible Gun Safety Act of 2000, which created the Maryland Cease Fire Council, and is administered in conjunction with that council. Funds may support personnel, equipment, contractual services, travel, and other costs related to reducing firearms-related violence. Total funding available for the SFY 2027 cycle is $926,940, distributed across tiers based on jurisdictional firearm-crime volume: Low-Impact (up to 100 crimes/year), Moderate-Impact (101–500 crimes/year), and High-Impact (500+ crimes/year). Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis. Up to 25 awards ranging from $15,000 to $100,000 are anticipated for SFY 2027.

Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, and meals (except pre-approved client food). Applicants must also complete the Organizational Capacity Questionnaire (OCQ) via Qualtrics as a mandatory condition of a complete application. Multiple supporting documents must be uploaded to GMS. NOFAs are typically released at the beginning of each calendar year with applications due in April. The SFY 2027 application deadline was April 3, 2026. Post-award, grantees submit quarterly progress reports through GMS. Technical assistance inquiries can be directed to dlmsac.gocpyvs@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Law Enforcement Training Scholarship Program (LETS) provides scholarships of up to $5,000 per recipient to support specialized law enforcement training. Grant funds may be used for non-degree courses and related expenses such as travel, lodging, registration fees, and training materials. In some cases, funds may also be used to bring trainers directly to a law enforcement agency. The program is open to all eligible state and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland, including prosecuting agencies such as State's Attorney's Offices and the Maryland Attorney General's Office. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but must be submitted at least 30 business days before the training start date. All projects must end on or before September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships of up to $5,000 per individual per course. Up to 20 awards anticipated, with $75,000 total funding anticipated. No matching funds are required. Funds may cover non-degree training courses, registration fees, training materials, travel (airfare, mileage at $0.70/mile, parking, ground transportation), lodging, per diem for meals, or the cost of bringing a certified trainer to the agency. Grant funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis. All projects must end on or before September 30, 2026. Funding is federal pass-through via Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (ALN 16.738).

structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland, including prosecuting agencies such as State's Attorney's Offices and the Maryland Attorney General's Office.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-degree training courses and related expenses including registration fees, training materials, travel (airfare, mileage, parking, ground transportation), lodging, and per diem for meals. May also fund bringing a certified trainer to a law enforcement agency. Allowable costs include consultant services, equipment, registration fees, program/office supplies, and indirect costs via NICRA or de minimis rate. Personnel costs (salary + fringe) capped at 30%.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Services for Crime Victims Fund (LSCV)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Legal Services for Crime Victims (LSCV) Fund provides annual grants to ensure that money obtained from unclaimed restitution is used to provide legal representation for crime victims in Maryland courts. The fund is administered by the State Board of Victim Services and supports legal counsel for victims of crime and delinquent acts to protect their rights under law. Funding levels fluctuate annually based on unclaimed restitution collection. Funding is authorized under MD Criminal Procedure Article §11-614(b) and is contingent upon final approval of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's budget during Maryland's legislative session.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants funded by unclaimed restitution proceeds under MD Criminal Procedure Article §11-614(b). Grant funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to providing legal counsel to crime victims. Eligible personnel include Staff Attorneys and Directors of Legal Services. Allowable costs include personnel (salaries, fringe benefits ≤30%), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel (mileage at 72.5¢/mile, lodging, meals per State of Maryland rates), contractual services (consultants capped at $81.25/hr or $650/day unless pre-approved), equipment (≥$10,000 useful life), and other (registration fees, program/office supplies, indirect costs). Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction/capital expenses, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, and lobbying. The total funding amount changes each year based on how much unclaimed restitution is collected. Funding is contingent upon final approval of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's budget during Maryland's legislative session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (including faith-based and community organizations) and local and state government agencies that provide statewide legal services to crime victims in Maryland. Applicants must provide legal advice, consultation, or representation by a licensed attorney to victims of crimes and delinquent acts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing legal counsel to victims of crime and delinquent acts, including legal advice, consultation, or representation provided by a licensed attorney. Allowable costs include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel (e.g., Staff Attorney, Director of Legal Services), and travel. Subrecipients must also provide services to Limited English Proficient (LEP) individuals per DOJ Title VI guidance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations serving Maryland crime victims across all 24 jurisdictions. Applicants must provide statewide legal counsel; project design must address the legal needs of victims in every Maryland jurisdiction including Baltimore City.

Post-award reporting is quarterly on a reimbursement basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Warrant Apprehension & Absconding Grant Program (WAAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The WAAG program provides grants to law enforcement agencies across Maryland to reduce the number of open warrants — especially for violent crimes — and to apprehend individuals who have absconded from court-ordered drug or alcohol treatment facilities. Established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2022 through Senate Bill 585, the program aims to decrease open warrants and reduce crime in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to local government and law enforcement agencies covering contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, other costs, personnel, and travel. Eligible applicants include police departments of county or municipal corporations in Maryland and offices of the sheriff that provide law enforcement functions. Each applicant entity may submit no more than one application per cycle. Grants are reimbursed on a quarterly basis. The FY2026 award period of performance ran July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, other costs, personnel, and travel related to warrant apprehension and absconding reduction efforts. Funds must be used to reduce open warrants (especially for violent crimes) or apprehend individuals absconding from court-ordered drug or alcohol treatment facilities. Includes overtime for law enforcement officers to serve warrants, analysts to identify wanted/absconded individuals, program administration, and warrant-related supplies/equipment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Markell Hendricks Youth Crime Prevention and Diversion Parole Grant Program (YCPD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance to local law enforcement agencies and eligible entities for diversion programs or youth engagement programs in high-crime areas. The program aligns with Maryland's Comprehensive State Crime Control and Prevention Plan, with priority given to jurisdictions with the highest number of offenders (individuals on parole or under mandatory supervision). The Office anticipates making one award per SFY cycle with intent for two additional years of level funding contingent on good standing and positive outcomes.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis following submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports. Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) is encouraged. Eligible costs include equipment (items $10,000+ per unit require a Property Inventory Report Form), operating expenses, personnel (fringe benefits capped at 30% of salary unless pre-approved), travel (mileage reimbursed at $0.70/mile effective 1/1/25), consultant services (maximum $81.25/hour or $650/day), and other costs related to diversion programs or youth engagement programs in high-crime areas. Indirect costs may be charged at a de minimis rate of 15% of Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC) or at an approved rate. Only one application per agency or organization is permitted per cycle. Funding is contingent upon final approval of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's budget during Maryland's Legislative Session. Funds cannot be extended beyond June 30, 2026 for the SFY 2026 cycle.

Priority jurisdictions include Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, consultant services, indirect costs, and other costs related to diversion programs or youth engagement programs in high-crime areas. Supported outcomes include family engagement, educational opportunities, victim services, interagency coordination, and data-driven criminal justice initiatives. Funds may not supplant existing state or local funds; must increase available funding for program activities.

Priority is given to jurisdictions with the highest number of offenders (individuals on parole or under mandatory supervision), including Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Criminal Intelligence Network (MCIN) program is a coalition of criminal justice agencies that collaborates and coordinates tactics, resources, and intelligence through data sharing, cross-jurisdictional partnerships, and supporting technologies. MCIN focuses on identifying, disrupting, and dismantling gangs and violent criminal networks involved in drug distribution, firearms violence, human trafficking, and other violent criminal enterprises. Funding is used to improve intelligence infrastructure, support information-collection strategies, employ subject matter experts, and pay for expert prosecutors to handle cases at the federal and state levels.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other costs related to improving criminal intelligence infrastructure and supporting investigations and prosecutions targeting violent criminal networks. Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis. The SFY 2027 funding opportunity (MCIN-ODAC) had an application deadline of May 15, 2026, with a period of performance of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Total funding available is $6,623,865 (contingent on Governor's Office budget approval). MCIN awards range from $100,000–$700,000 (up to 14 awards); ODAC positions range from $40,000–$110,000 (up to 25 positions). All funding is contingent upon the final approval of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's budget during Maryland's 2026 Legislative Session of the General Assembly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorney's Offices in Maryland, as well as the Washington/Baltimore High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (W/B HIDTA). Program is invite-only; only designated MCIN and ODAC jurisdictions may apply, with a maximum of one application per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving intelligence infrastructure, collecting information leading to investigations, employing subject matter experts trained to investigate criminal networks, and paying expert prosecutors to prosecute cases at the federal and state levels. Eligible cost categories include contractual services, equipment, personnel (salaries for coordinators, analysts, prosecutors, overtime), travel (conferences, training on guns/gangs/drugs/human trafficking, substance use prevention), and other costs. Explicitly excludes alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction, and corporate expenses. Consultant rate capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day; mileage at 72.5 cents/mile.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates statewide with coordination across Maryland jurisdictions. MCIN component jurisdictions include: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Washington, and Wicomico. ODAC component jurisdictions include: Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington/Baltimore HIDTA, Wicomico, and Worcester. Jurisdictions marked as currently funded for ODAC must submit a combined MCIN application only; separate ODAC applications are rejected. Applicants are expected to coordinate with the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC) and Washington/Baltimore HIDTA.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Training/Technical Assistance call was held on April 21, 2026. structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program that funds a network of local domestic violence service programs to provide temporary shelter and comprehensive supportive services to domestic violence victims and their families. The program promotes a coordinated community approach that links victims with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, social services, and other community agencies. The program aims to prevent incidents of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and to meet the needs of all victims and their dependents, including those in underserved communities.

Total funding available for the FY2024 cycle was $2,089,779 across 19 awards, with a maximum award of $116,099 per jurisdiction. Grant cycles are 12 months in length. Indirect costs are permitted under a negotiated rate or 10% de minimis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Victims of Crime Fund (MVOC) provides grants for advocacy and support services to victims of crime in Maryland. Administered by the State Board of Victim Services under the authority of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, the fund supports new programs and enhances existing ones across the state. It funds implementation of crime victims' rights under the Maryland Constitution and federal guidelines for the treatment of and assistance to crime victims and witnesses. For the SFY2027 cycle, 8–10 awards are anticipated with an award range of $50,000–$75,000 per award and a total anticipated availability of $524,836, covering a period of performance of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Entertainment District Security Grant (EDSG) provides funding to community organizations, nonprofit organizations, and local governments to support security operations in entertainment districts that experience high pedestrian traffic and above-average calls for police assistance. The program aims to reduce criminal activity, improve crowd management, and enhance public safety through collaborative efforts among local governments, community organizations, and law enforcement. Established in 2024 under §§4–1701 through 4–1703 of the Public Safety Article of the Maryland Code.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of $20,000–$50,000 per award (up to $50,000 for local governments; up to $30,000 for community organizations and nonprofits) covers security operations during peak pedestrian activity in entertainment districts. Funding is disbursed on a quarterly reimbursement basis (monthly reimbursement available for nonprofits with awards >$50,000). Eligible costs include: security and law enforcement overtime, procurement of security equipment (surveillance cameras, enhanced lighting, communication tools, reflective vests), hiring security officers and administrators, emergency response training (de-escalation, crowd management), lighting improvements in public areas, public safety signage, and public safety awareness initiatives. Allowable cost categories include personnel (salaries, fringe benefits up to 30%), operating expenses, travel (Maryland state rate 72.5¢/mile effective 1/1/26; federal GSA per diem rates), contractual services (consultant max $81.25/hr or $650/day unless pre-approved), equipment (≥$10,000 useful life), and indirect costs (15% de minimis or negotiated NICRA). Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction/capital, fundraising, lobbying, and most meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4)), officially recognized neighborhood associations, county government agencies, local government agencies, and local law enforcement agencies operating in or serving entertainment districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Security and law enforcement overtime, procurement of security equipment (surveillance cameras, enhanced lighting, communication tools, reflective vests), hiring security officers and administrators, emergency response training (de-escalation and crowd management), lighting improvements in public areas, public safety signage, and public safety awareness initiatives during peak pedestrian activity in entertainment districts. Personnel, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, and travel are all allowable cost categories.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Eligible entertainment districts are defined as areas up to a half-square-mile with a high concentration of establishments serving alcohol or onsite consumption, hookah bars, or establishments that regularly host live entertainment. Districts must experience higher than average calls for police assistance in response to reported crimes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Performance Incentive Grant Fund (PIGF) provides grants funded by savings from Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act (JRA) reforms. The program supports evidence-based strategies to safely reduce the prison population, improve reentry outcomes, reduce recidivism, support victims of crime, and connect nonviolent offenders with behavioral health treatment and community support. structured_extraction.program_name: Police Recruitment and Retention Grant Program (PRAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local and state law enforcement agencies to recruit and retain qualified sworn police officers. Funding may be used for hiring bonuses, retention incentives, tuition reimbursement, health incentives, contractual services, equipment, personnel costs, and travel. Anticipated availability of $1,300,000 with up to 40 awards ranging from $10,000 to $150,000. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for local and state law enforcement agencies to support police recruitment and retention efforts. Anticipated availability of $1,300,000 with up to 40 awards ranging from $10,000 to $150,000 (tiered by sworn officer count). Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Period of performance: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Eligible expenses include contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other costs such as hiring bonuses (e.g., bilingual $2K, veteran hire $2K, degree $2K new hire/$1K existing, referral $1K), retention incentives, tuition reimbursement, and health incentives. structured_extraction.program_name: Program for Preventing Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection for Rape Victims
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies for providing a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care to rape and sexual assault victims at risk of HIV infection. The program is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy and funded through the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund. As of October 1, 2019, state law requires that the State pay for a full course of nPEP medication and no survivor may be denied access based on cost.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement for the full course of nPEP treatment, medication, and follow-up care for sexual assault victims at risk of HIV infection. Total reimbursements may not exceed $750,000 annually. Follow-up care within 180 days of the sexual assault is eligible for reimbursement. Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. As of October 1, 2019, state law requires that the State pay for a full course of nPEP medication and no survivor may be denied access based on cost. Survivors may opt out of insurance use for privacy; manufacturer assistance programs are also available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service
structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies that provide nPEP treatment and follow-up care to rape and sexual assault victims in Maryland. The clinical benefit is directed to survivors of rape and sexual assault deemed at risk for HIV.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for nPEP medication, treatment, and follow-up care provided to sexual assault victims at risk of contracting HIV. Covered services include medical screening, forensic exams, labs (STI, toxicology, pregnancy, HIV), medications (antibiotics, emergency contraception, nPEP), vaccines, radiology, and surgical consults. Reimbursement is also available for SAFE (Sexual Assault Forensic Exam) services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. No county or municipal exclusions. Program directs survivors to local Rape Crisis Centers statewide via 211 or mcasa.org. Administrative address: 100 Community Place, Crownsville, MD 21032.

Victim must be at risk for contracting HIV as a result of the sexual assault
Medication regimen must begin within 72 hours of the sexual assault
Follow-up care must occur at four to six weeks, three months, and six months post-assault
Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service
The nPEP Reimbursement Form must be completed in its entirety
Follow-up care within 180 days of the sexual assault is eligible for reimbursement for nPEP services

Reimbursement subject to SARU regulations and guidelines

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must complete the nPEP Reimbursement Form and submit it to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy within 90 days of the date of service. The SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF) must be used separately for sexual assault forensic exams (SAFE) and related follow-up care, submitted with an itemized bill and UB-04, CMS-1450, or OMB-0938-1197 1500 form to the SARU within 90 days of the exam. Survivors access nPEP through Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) providers; no competitive application cycle exists for victims.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Safe Neighborhoods grants develop, implement, and support anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies in Maryland. Funds support dedicated partnerships forming a PSN task force aimed at creating safer neighborhoods through a sustained reduction in violent crime, including addressing criminal gangs and the felonious possession and use of firearms. The program combines targeted law enforcement efforts with community engagement, prevention, and reentry efforts. Grant funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis, and organizations expending $1,000,000 or more in federal awards during a fiscal year are subject to Single Audit requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs associated with anti-gang and violent crime enforcement task forces and PSN partnerships. Funding supports implementation of violent crime reduction strategies through collaborative PSN task forces emphasizing four core elements: Community Engagement/Partnerships, Prevention and Intervention, Focused and Strategic Enforcement, and Accountability. Grant funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis following submission of fiscal and programmatic reports. Organizations expending $1,000,000 or more in federal awards during a fiscal year are subject to Single Audit requirements. Specific award amounts are not stated on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Protecting Against Hate Crimes (PAHC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Protecting Against Hate Crimes (PAHC) Grant Program provides support to nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations, whose facilities and membership can be targeted for hate crimes. Grants fund security enhancements and support collaboration between law enforcement, victim services, and communities targeted for hate crimes.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other expenses related to security enhancements for eligible nonprofit and faith-based organizations that may be targeted for hate crimes. Funding is tiered by organizational budget: up to $50,000 for organizations with annual budgets under $500,000, and up to $100,000 for organizations with annual budgets between $500,000 and $5,000,000. Funding is reimbursable quarterly.

Explicitly excludes: alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction/capital improvements, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, most meals, prior debt, firearms, ammunition, vehicles, administrative/indirect costs, pre-award or post-closeout costs.
