structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Substance Abuse Treatment (RSAT) for State Prisoners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps state, local, and tribal governments develop and implement substance abuse treatment programs in correctional and detention facilities. It also funds community reintegration services for people after they are released from incarceration. The goal is to break the cycle of drugs and violence by reducing demand for and use of illegal drugs. Funds support three types of programs: residential treatment, jail-based treatment, and aftercare. Applications that partner with community-based substance abuse treatment programs receive priority consideration. The program is administered through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP), with eligible applicants including local detention centers, the Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS). The program serves pre-trial defendants, individuals in correctional facilities, and citizens in need of post-incarceration treatment and community reintegration.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funds distributed by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to eligible applicants for developing and implementing residential substance abuse treatment, jail-based treatment, and aftercare/reentry programs in correctional facilities. For the SFY 2026 cycle, total available funding was $559,505 with up to 3 anticipated awards; minimum request $50,000, maximum request $225,000. Eligible cost categories include personnel, fringe benefits, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other expenses. Consultant rate cap: $81.25/hour or $650/day. Travel reimbursement: $0.70/mile (effective 1/1/25). Indirect costs: de minimis rate 15% of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) or negotiated federally-approved rate. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), prior debt, UAS/UAVs, vehicles, prizes/entertainment, and supplanting state/local funds. Grants are reimbursed quarterly. Specific award amounts and terms vary by funding cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local detention centers, Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS); serves pre-trial defendants, individuals in correctional facilities, and citizens in need of post-incarceration treatment and community reintegration
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and implementation of residential substance abuse treatment programs, jail-based treatment programs, and aftercare/community reintegration services for incarcerated individuals or those recently released. Funds cover personnel, fringe benefits, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other costs. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses/commissions, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), prior debt, UAS/UAVs, vehicles, prizes/entertainment, and supplanting state/local funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible government correctional agencies. Eligible applicants are state and local governmental agencies in Maryland (DPSCS, DJS, local detention centers). Applications must define and provide zip codes for service sites and catchment areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: STOP (Services * Training * Officers * Prosecutors) Violence Against Women Formula Grant Program (STOP VAWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The STOP VAWA Program, administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy under the authority of the Department of Justice, encourages the development and strengthening of effective, victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, and court strategies to combat violent crimes against women in Maryland. Funding is distributed among law enforcement (25%), prosecution (25%), nonprofit victim service providers (30%), and court entities (5%), with up to 15% at the State's discretion. At least 10% of the victim service allocation must go to linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations, and 20% of total funds must meaningfully address sexual assault, including stranger rape, acquaintance rape, alcohol or drug-facilitated rape, and rape within intimate partner relationships.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal formula-based grant funding distributed to law enforcement agencies, prosecution offices, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers. Funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to victim-centered strategies addressing violent crimes against women, including training, specialized units, coordinated community response infrastructure, victim services (hotline, counseling, legal representation, housing, transportation), and technology/databases. Allocations are set by statute: 25% law enforcement, 25% prosecution, 30% nonprofit victim services, 5% courts, up to 15% at State discretion. The FFY24 continuation funding cycle made $3,018,680 available for the award period October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, court strategies, and nonprofit victim services addressing violent crimes against women. Eligible uses include: law enforcement specialized training, DV fatality review teams, lethality assessment programs, sexual assault response teams, and trauma-informed responses; prosecution U/T Visa training, domestic violence and sexual assault units, victim support, and case coordination; victim services including 24/7 hotlines, crisis intervention, legal representation, housing, counseling, and culturally sensitive services; court victim advocates, interpreter services, databases, and judicial training; and discretionary uses such as capacity building, coordinating councils, and family justice centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations throughout all jurisdictions in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sex Offender and Compliance Enforcement in Maryland (SOCM)

Funds support sex offender registration, compliance verification, and enforcement activities across all 24 designated Maryland local law enforcement agencies, one per jurisdiction across all Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

Funding is disbursed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Allowable costs include personnel salaries (with time/effort documentation), supplies and equipment, partnerships and technology, and project activities aligned to Goals and Objectives. Budget categories include: Personnel (salaries, fringe benefits, timesheets required), Operating Expenses (rental, printing, communications), Travel (mileage, lodging, meals per State reimbursement rates), Contractual Services (consultant agreements, max $81.25/hour or $650/day), Equipment ($10,000+ per unit; includes tax, delivery, installation), and Other (registration, supplies, indirect costs up to 15% de minimis or negotiated NICRA).

structured_extraction.program_name: Sexual Assault Kit Testing Grant Program (SAKT)
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to support capacity expansion and testing of sexual assault evidence collection kits (SAKs) by forensic laboratories; also supports victim notification hotlines, advocacy, law enforcement investigations, and peer-to-peer telehealth providers. Administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, the program provides funding to the Maryland State Police and local law enforcement agencies to pay for the testing of sexual assault evidence collection kits (SAKs). Funding covers in-house personnel and supplies for testing, outsourcing of testing to forensic labs, and equipment purchases or upgrades for agencies with in-house labs. Funding is limited to testing of SAKs collected since May 1, 2018. Up to $3,500,000 in total grant funding is available for SFY2027 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $3,500,000 in total grant funding is available for SFY2027 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027). Funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to SAK testing. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis. Equipment threshold is $10,000 or more per unit. Consultant rate cap is $81.25/hr or $650/day (pre-approval required above cap). Fringe benefits capped at 30% of salary unless pre-approved. Funds cannot be extended beyond June 30, 2027. Applications must be submitted through the Grants Management System (GMS); use Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome for best performance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimburses physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and laboratories for the physical examination, collection of evidence, and emergency treatment of individuals who are victims of alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. The program aims to prevent re-victimization by handling medical-forensic claims processing directly with providers so victims and families can focus on healing.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursements are paid directly to physicians (up to $80 for examination and evidence collection, or up to $80/hour for up to 5 hours for child sexual abuse cases), hospitals (at rates set by the Health Services Cost Review Commission), laboratories, and pharmacies for covered services provided to sexual assault victims. Covered services include emergency room and in-hospital treatment, SAFE exams, medical-only exams, follow-up testing within 90 days, pregnancy and STI screening, diagnostic and toxicology tests (including drug-facilitated sexual assault toxicology), postcoital and prophylactic medications, nPEP/HIV prophylaxis, radiology, and any injury directly associated with the assault. For drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA), blood samples must be collected within 24 hours and urine samples within 120 hours of suspected ingestion, and specimens must be submitted to an MDH-licensed forensic toxicology laboratory. Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Providers must establish a pay-to account with the Maryland Comptroller.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 90 days from the date of service
structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and laboratories that provide medical-forensic services to victims of rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse in Maryland, including SAFE programs, urgent cares, individual physicians, and telehealth providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement to medical providers for forensic medical examinations (SAFE exams and medical-only exams), evidence collection, emergency treatment, follow-up care within 90 days, laboratory tests, STI testing, toxicology screening (including DFSA), radiology, and medications (emergency contraception, antibiotics, vaccines, nPEP/HIV prophylaxis) related to sexual assault
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Medical providers must be licensed to practice in Maryland. Reimburses for care provided within Maryland, even if the assault occurred in another state.
requirements_list: A police complaint number must be documented for victims who report to police; for non-reporting victims, a property held number, Jane Doe number, CPS/CHESSIE number, or similar case identifier is required

Signed SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF, formerly Form #2923) or Form #4456 for child cases, signed by a physician and forensic nurse examiner (or physician assistant/nurse practitioner if necessary)
Payment sheet (CMS Form #1450, CMS Form #1500, UB-04, or self-designed form) with vendor name, address, federal tax ID, patient name, patient date of birth, date of service, and amount due
Itemized bill including documentation of laboratory/diagnostic tests and medications ordered
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service
Programs must use updated reimbursement forms (effective January 1, 2025)

Providers must establish a pay-to account with the Maryland Comptroller

For DFSA claims, invoice must include itemized charges, hospital/lab name, billing address, federal tax ID, patient info, and lab codes
DFSA box on SSRF should only be checked if outsourced testing or in-house screening beyond 12-panel standard is performed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF) along with a payment sheet (UB-04, CMS-1450, or CMS-1500) and itemized bill to the SARU within 90 days of the date of service. Providers must have a pay-to account established with the Maryland Comptroller. Contact saru.claims@maryland.gov for billing questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sexual Assault Services Program (SASP) provides intervention, advocacy, accompaniment (accompanying victims to court, medical facilities, police departments, etc.), support services, and related assistance for adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault, as well as family and household members of victims and those collaterally affected by sexual assault. It is the first federal funding stream solely dedicated to direct intervention and related assistance for victims of sexual assault, created under the Violence Against Women and Department of Justice Reauthorization Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. §14043g). Grants are awarded to rape crisis centers in Maryland — specifically the 18 local full-service rape crisis centers identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA) and MCASA itself — to cover contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to providing these services across all 24 Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding (disbursed on a reimbursement basis, quarterly) for rape crisis centers and qualifying organizations to cover contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to providing intervention, advocacy, accompaniment, and support services to adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault, their family and household members, and those collaterally affected by sexual assault. structured_extraction.program_name: State Aid for Police Protection Fund (SAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A formula-driven funding program that supplements resources for police protection in local communities. State funds provide additional revenue to support the operational costs of local and county police agencies. Fund distributions are calculated based on a formula using a jurisdiction's population, number of police officers, and total jurisdictional taxable income. Annual distributions are calculated according to the previous year's operations costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based annual fund distributions to local and county police agencies. Distribution amounts are calculated using each jurisdiction's population, number of sworn police officers, and total taxable income, with annual amounts based on the previous year's operations costs. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis unless otherwise stated in the NOFA.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland, including all 24 counties and qualifying municipalities. Eligible entities must be incorporated and submit only one application per agency. Minimum thresholds: either at least $5,000 annual police protection expenditure plus at least 1 qualified full-time officer, or at least $80,000 police protection expenditure plus at least 2 qualified part-time officers (county/sheriff department only).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance to counties and qualifying municipalities to help offset the costs associated with local law enforcement services. Funds shall be used exclusively to provide adequate police protection. Allowable uses include: salaries and wages for sworn officers devoted entirely to police protection; full-time civilian police department employee costs; capital outlay (equipment, vehicles, radios, investigation equipment); debt service (interest and principal directly tied to police activities); communications (telegraph, radio, telephone, postage); travel (in-state and out-of-state for police training, seminars, conferences); fuel and utilities (identifiable portion if shared facility); contractual services (labor plus equipment or labor plus materials); supplies and materials (office, medical, vocational, clothing, ordnance, photographic, K-9, riot supplies); fixed charges (rent, workers' compensation insurance, public employment insurance); motor vehicle operations and maintenance; contributions; miscellaneous; traffic control; central alarm system; and other operating expenses. SAPP recipients are required to track and report on expenses and efforts related to violent crime reduction. Funds may not be used for supplanting — they must increase the amounts of state/local funds available for program activities. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, commissions, construction/capital expenses/land acquisition, corporate formation costs, fundraising, honoraria, and lobbying.

structured_extraction.program_name: State's Attorney's Office Case Automation System Enhancement Grant Program (SACM)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps State's Attorney Offices (SAOs) in Maryland establish or upgrade automated case management systems. Funding supports modernizing case tracking technology, improving data accuracy and transparency, tracking key data on defendants and victims, and training staff on new systems. The program assists SAOs in capturing comprehensive case information including charges at arrest, filed charges, final dispositions, law enforcement and prosecution details, plea offers, reasons for dismissal or declination, and defendant and victim characteristics (race/ethnicity, age, gender, zip code). Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grant funding for contractual services, equipment, personnel, operating expenses, and other costs related to establishing or enhancing automated case management systems in State's Attorney Offices. Allowable costs include salaries, fringe benefits, materials, supplies, services, travel, equipment (under $5,000), and indirect costs. Grants are reimbursed on a quarterly basis; programmatic reports are due within 15 calendar days of quarter-end and financial reports within 30 calendar days.

Also covers staff training on new systems. Allowable cost categories include salaries, fringe benefits, materials, supplies, services, travel, equipment under $5,000, and indirect costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Survivors of Homicide Victims Grant Program (SOHG)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps establish and expand statewide programs that serve survivors of homicide victims across Maryland. It funds victim assistance, advocacy, support services, and coordinated justice system responses so that survivors of homicide victims can exercise their legal rights. Eligible applicants include nonprofit, faith-based, and eligible government organizations, with priority for programs that expand services to rural and underserved areas.

Eligible cost categories include personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other costs. Reimbursement is issued quarterly (or monthly for nonprofits with awards over $50,000). Projects may not exceed twelve months unless explicitly stated in the NOFA. structured_extraction.program_name: Title II Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention Formula Grant (JJAC)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Title II Formula (JJAC) grant funds reform in Maryland's juvenile justice system. It supports initiatives and strategies aligned with a Developmental Approach to Juvenile Justice Reform, including accountability without criminalization, alternatives to justice system involvement, individualized responses based on needs and risk assessments, limiting confinement to public safety needs, fairness, reducing disparate treatment, and family engagement. The program aims to improve outcomes for children and youth by strengthening programs in aftercare and reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation. It is authorized under Sections 221–223 of the Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 1974, as amended.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based grant funding distributed to eligible applicants for juvenile justice reform initiatives. Total SFY2027 funding is up to $745,000, consisting of up to 6 continuation awards totaling $585,700 and 1 competitive sub-award up to $200,000. Funds are reimbursed quarterly (or monthly for nonprofits with awards over $50,000). A 10% match requirement applies. Allowable costs include personnel (salary and fringe benefits up to 30%), contractual services (consultants max $81.25/hr or $650/day without preapproval), equipment (≥$10,000 with useful life >1 year), operating expenses (rent, communications, postage, printing), travel (in-state at MD rates: 72.5¢/mile as of 1/1/26), and other approved categories. Explicitly unallowable: alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, lobbying, trinkets, previous debt. Period of performance: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) program improves the treatment of crime victims by providing assistance and services to aid their recovery after a violent criminal act and support them through the criminal justice process. Services include crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation to court, temporary housing, and criminal justice support and advocacy. The program establishes or expands the availability of direct services to crime victims and their families, and ensures victims receive information about and assistance in filing for Crime Victim Compensation. Funding comes from the federal Crime Victims Fund, which is supported by fines and fees collected from people convicted of federal crimes.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants available for SFY 2027 (period of performance: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027). Funding combines federal VOCA (Victims of Crime Act) and state VOCG (Victims of Crime Grant) through a single combined application. Grants are reimbursed on a quarterly basis. Funds may cover contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to victim services programs, including crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation to court, temporary housing, and criminal justice support and advocacy. Federal VOCA awards require a 20% cost-share; a waiver is available. Approximately 150 awards are anticipated. All funding is contingent upon final approval of GOCPP's budget during Maryland's 2026 Legislative Session and upon receipt of federal funds from the Office for Victims of Crime.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies, local law enforcement agencies, and nonprofit victim service organizations providing services to crime victims in Maryland, including Certified Rape Crisis Centers, Designated Comprehensive Domestic Violence programs, Designated Child Advocacy Centers, and State-recognized Victim Service Coalitions and Alliances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel costs (direct victim services personnel; administrative personnel capped at 30% of salary/fringe), travel, and other expenses related to providing victim assistance services such as crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation, temporary housing, and criminal justice advocacy. Funds support both brief/intermediate and extended direct services to primary victims (directly harmed) and secondary victims (indirectly affected). Direct services include immediate crisis intervention, emotional/psychological/physical health services, personal advocacy and emotional support, case management, mental health counseling/outpatient therapy, peer support groups, criminal justice participation facilitation, legal assistance, forensic medical evidence collection exams, forensic interviews, transportation to services and proceedings, public awareness and education (capped at 30% of request or $50,000, whichever is lower), and transitional housing. Match may be satisfied with non-federal funds or volunteer time valued at industry-standard rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Only victims who live, work, or were victimized in the state of Maryland are eligible for services under this funding. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions apply. Applicants serving ENOUGH-eligible communities (27 designated communities with high levels of concentrated child poverty) may receive bonus scoring in the competitive review process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Violence Intervention and Prevention Program (VIPP) supports effective violence reduction strategies, specifically gun violence, through evidence-based and/or evidence-informed public health programs. Funded programs may include hospital-based violence intervention programs that provide intensive counseling, case management, and social services to individuals recovering from injuries resulting from violence. Program models may include Hospital-based Violence Intervention Programs (HVIPs), Street Outreach, Cognitive Behavioral Theory (CBT), Group Violence Intervention (GVI), Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED), adapted versions of existing models, or locally developed approaches informed by research, best practices, and community experience.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants to support evidence-based and evidence-informed public health programs that reduce gun violence. Total funding available for SFY2027 is $2,600,000, with up to 20 awards and individual awards not to exceed $300,000. Grants are funded on a reimbursable basis with quarterly disbursements. A 33% cash or in-kind cost share requirement applies. Eligible cost categories include personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other expenses. Applications for continuation funding from programs operational for 1 or 2 years receive priority consideration. All funding is contingent upon final approval of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's budget during Maryland's Legislative Session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (including faith-based and community-based organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status), local and state government agencies, local health departments, local hospitals, law enforcement agencies, State's Attorney's Offices, and institutions of higher learning seeking to implement evidence-based or evidence-informed gun violence prevention and intervention programs in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (salaries and fringe benefits up to 30%), contractual services (consultant max $81.25/hr or $650/day), equipment (items $10,000 or more), operating expenses (rental, printing, communications), travel (mileage, lodging, meals per MD state rates), and other costs related to evidence-based or evidence-informed gun violence prevention and intervention programs. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), retirement of previous debt, and trinkets.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) provides financial assistance to innocent victims of crime in Maryland who suffer physical or psychological injury, when no other resources are available. Eligible individuals can receive reimbursement for medical expenses related to physical injuries, psychological injury costs (including counseling and lost wages from psychological harm), lost earnings due to inability to work after a crime, bereavement leave, disability compensation, funeral expenses in homicide cases, and loss of financial support for dependents of homicide victims. CICB is the payer of last resort — all other available reimbursements must be exhausted first. Emergency and supplemental awards are also available. In homicide cases, may also cover funeral expenses and loss of financial support for dependents of the victim.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial compensation for unreimbursed medical expenses related to physical injuries, psychological injury costs (counseling, lost wages), lost earnings (minimum two continuous weeks or less if combined with $100+ in other unreimbursed costs), bereavement leave up to two weeks or $2,000, total or partial permanent or temporary disability, funeral expenses in homicide cases, loss of support when a homicide victim was the claimant's primary provider, up to 30 days of lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by a crime, crime scene cleanup, and other Board-approved expenses. Emergency and supplemental awards are also available. Minimum unreimbursed costs of $100 required. Available when no other financial resources are available. CICB is the payer of last resort — all other available reimbursements must be used first.

Small Business Webinar Series offers free monthly training to help small, minority, women, and veteran-owned firms compete in state contracting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ready, Set, GROW! Procurement Connections Workshops
structured_extraction.program_description: A series of free in-person workshops and events run by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs (OSBA) that connect small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses to Maryland state government procurement opportunities. The program runs five outreach event types: (1) Procurement Connections Workshops — broad workshops on the state procurement process, tools, and buyer introductions; (2) Open Houses — focused sessions with specific state agencies; (3) State Agency–Prime Contractor Matchmaking — connecting businesses with prime contractor opportunities; (4) Prime Contractor–Subcontractor Matchmaking — connecting subcontractors with active prime contractors; and (5) Regional Opportunities Workshops — events focused on regional industries and needs across six OSBA regions covering all Maryland counties. Participants learn how Maryland's small, minority, women, and veteran procurement programs work, identify which state agencies buy their products or services, and network with procurement officers, program liaisons, and local partners. Workshops also cover Maryland's three socioeconomic procurement certification programs: Small Business Reserve (SBR), Veteran Small Business Enterprise (VSBE), and Minority Business Enterprise (MBE). A T.I.P.S. (Techniques, Insights, & Practices for Procurement Success) webinar series offers 2 free webinars every month on topics such as navigating eMMA, MBE compliance, and VSBE/SBR certifications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program / Small Business Preference (SBP) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's prime contracting programs for Certified Small Businesses (CSBs). The SBR Program creates a dedicated set-aside marketplace where certified small businesses compete only against other small businesses for state contracts — on average, over 20% of all open state-funded solicitations on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) are designated as SBR, providing access to nearly $500 million in state-funded contracting opportunities. When a procurement is designated as SBR, only CSBs can win the award, meaning they do not compete against larger established companies, and certified firms can receive direct payments from the state as prime contractors. The companion Small Business Preference (SBP) Program gives CSBs a price preference of up to 5% of total contract value (7% for veteran-owned, 8% for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses) when competing on non-reserved solicitations. To participate, businesses must first obtain free CSB certification through eMMA by self-attesting to size and revenue eligibility standards. Certifications are valid for three years (beginning August 29, 2025). Same-day certification is available for qualified vendors already registered in eMMA.

A price preference of up to 5% (7% for veteran-owned, 8% for disabled-veteran-owned) applies on the Small Business Preference (SBP) track for non-designated procurements. There is no direct financial payment for certification itself — the benefit is preferential access to state contracts. structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary crime-prevention training program operated by the Hagerstown Police Department for owners and managers of rental properties — including larger apartment complexes and multiple housing units — within the City of Hagerstown. The program trains participants on crime prevention best practices, physical security (CPTED), lease management, eviction procedures, and community awareness to reduce crime, drugs, and gang activity on rental properties. The full multi-housing program consists of three phases: Phase I is an 8-hour management training class taught by police covering crime prevention, lease agreements, eviction, and security management; Phase II is a CPTED (Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design) survey and inspection conducted by police; and Phase III requires an annual crime prevention social event hosted by property management and police. Properties completing all three phases receive a gold certification valid for one year and the right to display official Crime Free Multi-Housing signage. A basic 4-hour Crime-Free Housing course is also available, introducing landlords, property owners, and managers to best practices for achieving a crime-free property. Some property owners/managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city under Chapter 95 and Chapter 197 of the City Code.

structured_extraction.program_name: CDBG/HOME Nonprofit Subrecipient Grants (Community Development Block Grant & HOME Investment Partnerships Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County Community Development subgrants its federal HUD entitlement funds — Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) — to partner nonprofit and, in some cases, for-profit organizations and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) serving low- to moderate-income residents. The CDBG program provides funds to support projects that offer decent affordable housing, a suitable living environment, and expanded economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons. Activities must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low-to-moderate-income persons, address slum and blight, or respond to an urgent need. HOME funds support affordable housing activities including rental housing development, rehabilitation, new construction, refinancing, and supportive housing, and also build the capacity of nonprofit housing developers. HUD requires a 25% non-federal match for each eligible HOME activity, and properties assisted with HOME funds must remain affordable for 15–20 years depending on the amount and type of activity. Harford County submits an Annual Consolidated Action Plan to HUD describing how funds will be used. Funds are disbursed annually through a competitive application process, typically in January and February each year. Harford County retains the right to accept, reject, or reduce funding requests, and funds are not available directly to individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual entitlement and formula grant funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), allocated to Harford County and dispersed as subgrants to eligible nonprofit organizations, for-profit developers, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and partner organizations for qualifying projects. Funding amounts vary by project. Eligible uses include public facility improvements, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, low-to-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, critical repairs, capital projects for decent affordable housing, suitable living environments, economic opportunity expansion, and reduction of slum and blight. HUD requires a 25% non-federal match for each eligible HOME activity. Properties assisted with HOME funds must maintain affordability restrictions: 15 years for projects using $15,000–$40,000; 20 years for new construction of rental housing; 15 years for refinancing of rental housing. Harford County retains the right to accept, reject, or reduce funding requests. Funds are not available directly to individuals.

Eligible activities include festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming that promote cultural, historical, agricultural, eco-tourism, sports tourism, or heritage-focused experiences. In FY 2024, nearly $645,000 was awarded to 15 nonprofits. The FY 2027 cycle has an application deadline of May 8, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Agricultural Land Preservation Program (HALPP) / Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) and Agricultural Preservation District Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Harford County Agricultural Land Preservation Program protects productive agricultural land and woodland in Harford County to support the continued production of food and fiber and the vital role of agriculture in the county economy. Harford County has preserved more than 64,000 acres since 1977. The program operates on two tracks: (1) a permanent Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) track, in which landowners voluntarily sell a permanent conservation easement on their agricultural or forest land on a competitive basis, giving up certain development rights in exchange for payment via a permanent deed of easement that extinguishes all pre-existing development potential and prohibits future commercial or residential subdivision (with only very limited rights reserved for the original grantor and immediate family), while retaining full fee simple ownership subject to the easement. The program works alongside the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) and other state and federal partners. (2) A temporary Agricultural Preservation District track, in which a property owner commits to limiting subdivision of their parcel for a minimum of five years in return for a property tax credit — after the five-year term, the agreement and tax credit remain in effect until the owner requests termination, at which point all accrued tax credits must be refunded to Harford County. The district program can also serve as a precursor to permanent preservation. Program updates were made in 2024.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Department of Planning and Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two forms of assistance are available. (1) PDR/Permanent Easement (Competitive): Landowners receive payment for permanently selling and extinguishing their development rights to the state or county via a permanent conservation easement deed. Applications are reviewed on a competitive basis by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board, which provides recommendations to the Department of Planning and Zoning. Once development rights are purchased, the farm is subject to a permanent easement that prohibits future non-agricultural development. Property must have at least one extra development right available and must meet minimum soil productivity standards as determined by the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. (2) Agricultural Preservation District (Temporary 5-Year Track): Property owners receive a tax credit of $50 per acre, offsetting up to 50% of the parcel's Harford County real property tax (whichever is less), in exchange for a five-year commitment limiting subdivision. After the five-year term, the agreement and tax credit remain in effect until the owner requests termination, at which point all accrued tax credits must be refunded to Harford County. The agricultural district program requires a minimum of 50 acres.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program, also known as Section 8, is a federally funded rent subsidy program providing housing assistance to eligible low-income families, the elderly, and people with disabilities in Harford County. Eligible participants receive a Housing Choice Voucher to help pay for privately owned rental housing. Harford County Housing and Community Services (HCHCS) makes monthly rental subsidy payments directly to participating landlords on behalf of tenants, while tenants pay the remaining balance. HCHCS determines the subsidy amount based on income and rent reasonableness surveys; a unit will not be approved if rent exceeds 40% of the tenant's income. Payments are made via direct deposit by the first of each month. Applicants are placed on a waiting list; when selected, they must complete a formal application, attend a required briefing on rules, regulations, and family obligations, and then receive their voucher. Rental units are inspected before a contract is signed and at least annually thereafter to ensure they meet HUD Housing Quality Standards. Families can remain on the program as long as they remain eligible and comply with family obligations, provided continued funding exists. The waiting list periodically opens for new applications during defined windows. Residents within the municipal limits of Bel Air, Havre de Grace, or Aberdeen should contact their local government.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers that subsidize monthly rent payments for eligible low-income individuals and families. The subsidy is paid directly to the landlord on behalf of participating families via direct deposit by the first of each month. HCHCS determines the subsidy amount based on income and rent reasonableness surveys; a unit will not be approved if rent exceeds 40% of the tenant's income. Voucher payment standards (effective November 1, 2025) range from $1,379/month for a studio to $3,703/month for a 6-bedroom unit. Families are responsible for finding housing within 60 days that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards and allowable rent limits. Rental units are inspected before a contract is signed and at least annually thereafter. Participants are placed on a waiting list; voucher receipt may take several years depending on application date, preferences, and available funding. Families can remain on the program as long as they are eligible and comply with family obligations, provided continued program funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income single individuals, families, the elderly, and people with disabilities in Harford County who meet federal income limit guidelines (at or below 50% of area median income). Priority preferences are given to families who live or work in Harford County and fall into categories such as families with dependent children, working families, elderly families, disabled families, veterans or surviving spouses of veterans, and the homeless. Landlords in Harford County who wish to participate by renting to voucher holders are also served by the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance — the voucher subsidizes monthly rent payments for eligible participants renting decent, safe, and sanitary privately owned housing units in the private market that meet HUD Housing Quality Standards and Harford County health and safety standards (Livability Code).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of or workers in Harford County, Maryland. Housing units must be located within Harford County. Priority preferences given to applicants who live or work in Harford County. Residents within the municipal limits of Bel Air, Havre de Grace, or Aberdeen should contact their local government.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Apply online during the open application window (e.g., December 8–12, 2025). After applying, receive a confirmation number and check status at www.waitlistcheck.com or by calling 1-877-204-9098. 2. Wait to be contacted by mail when your name reaches the top of the waiting list. 3. When selected, complete a formal application and attend an enrollment interview for eligibility determination. 4. If eligible, attend a required briefing session on rules, regulations, and family obligations. 5. Receive the Housing Choice Voucher at the briefing. 6. Find housing within 60 days that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards and rent limits, and negotiate lease terms with the landlord. Submit a Request for Tenancy Approval form with the landlord. 7. Harford County Housing & Community Services reviews the lease and inspects the unit. 8. Upon approval, Harford County and the landlord enter into a Housing Assistance Payment Contract on behalf of the family. Payments are then made monthly via direct deposit. For general inquiries, call the Harford County Housing Agency at 410-638-3045.

structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County's Grant-in-Aid program allocates more than $1 million each year to support local nonprofits that deliver human services to Harford County residents. The program is designed to enhance the capacity of public and private sector organizations to address emergency and daily needs, including housing and homeless prevention services, particularly for low- to moderate-income individuals. New applicants can receive up to $5,000 in starter funds to help growing service providers get started. Recipients enter into an agreement with the county and must comply with financial and programmatic procedures. The program is offered on a competitive basis; applicants must meet specific eligibility criteria and submit requests by a predetermined deadline using a county-provided application form. Harford County also offers competitive grant funding through the Criminal Justice Coordinating Council (CJCC) to eligible nonprofit and government organizations in Harford County for criminal justice coordination purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Landmark Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County offers property tax credits to owners of properties designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks who rehabilitate or restore their historic properties. Credits reduce county real property taxes based on two mechanisms: (1) the increased assessed value resulting from rehabilitation or restoration work, and (2) a percentage of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses. Since 2002, the program has saved Harford County Historic Landmark owners $40,000 in property taxes.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Planning and Zoning Department
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Owners of Harford County Historic Landmarks may reduce their county real property taxes through two mechanisms: (1) a credit based on the amount their property assessment increased due to rehabilitation or restoration work, and (2) a credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses (QREs) up to $7,500 (based on QREs of $75,000; QREs may exceed $75,000 but the 10% credit is capped at $7,500). A previous tax credit must be fully exhausted before a new credit can be granted. Since 2002, the program has saved Harford County Historic Landmark owners $40,000 in property taxes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation funds capital, program, and operating grants to support affordable housing and homelessness services in its priority communities. The program has three focus areas: (1) Housing With Supportive Services — funding nonprofit housing developments that produce affordable housing integrated with wraparound services for people exiting homelessness; (2) Community-Led Development — supporting innovative, community-driven efforts such as community land trusts and community ownership models that preserve affordable housing and prevent displacement; and (3) Coordinated Responses to Homelessness — improving collaboration across public systems and organizations serving people without housing or at risk of homelessness. A key initiative focuses on building nonprofit housing developer capacity through predevelopment grants and support for nonprofit loan funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation Small Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation's Small Grants Program awards funding to smaller nonprofit organizations in Maryland and Northeastern Pennsylvania that provide direct services for poor and vulnerable populations. Grants of up to $50,000 per year for two years (up to $100,000 total) may be used for operating, program, or capital expenses in the areas of health, housing, jobs, education, and aging. Organizations must have an annual budget of $1 million or less to be eligible. There is no deadline for grant requests and no Letter of Inquiry is required, unlike the Foundation's standard grantmaking process. After two years of funding, organizations must take a year off before being eligible for an additional two years; after four total years of Small Grants funding, organizations must shift to the regular grant process.

Loan funds may also be available for those who qualify. The program targets low- and moderate-income homeowners in eligible Healthy Neighborhoods located within approved Disadvantaged Zip Codes in Baltimore City.

Additional benefits include a free residential energy audit, direct homeowner education, technical assistance, and a post-project homeownership guide. Eligible costs include audits, design, engineering, and construction soft costs. Funded through the EPA Thriving Communities Program. Funds are limited.

structured_extraction.program_description: A below-market interest rate loan for owner-occupant homeowners living within a designated Healthy Neighborhood area in Baltimore City. Borrowers can use the funds for home renovation projects including exterior improvements (e.g., a new porch), permanent interior upgrades (e.g., energy-efficient appliances), kitchen upgrades, bathroom remodels, window replacements, and mechanical system improvements. Funds must be used for work completed after loan settlement and cannot be used to pay off existing debt. The loan is underwritten and approved by M&T Bank; borrowers must meet standard underwriting guidelines including a minimum credit score of 700 and total long-term debt at or below 43% of income. Upon closing, up to 20% of the renovation cost or $8,000 is advanced; the remainder is held for bank disbursement upon satisfactory inspection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans between $5,000 and $20,000 at 1% below market interest rate, with a 10-year permanent term (following a short-term construction phase of up to 12 months). Two-close structure: short-term construction loan that refinances to a permanent second mortgage. Underwritten and approved by M&T Bank; borrower must meet standard underwriting guidelines including a minimum credit score of 700 (exceptions possible) and total long-term debt ≤43% of income. Upon closing, up to 20% of renovation cost or $8,000 is advanced; the remainder is held for bank disbursement upon satisfactory inspection. Funds must be used for home improvements made after loan settlement, not for pre-completed work or debt payoff. No prior Healthy Neighborhoods loans may exist on any property.

Cannot be used for already-completed work or debt repayment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home purchase and renovation loan for eligible borrowers buying a home within a designated Healthy Neighborhood area. Borrowers must use the loan to make improvements to the property at the time of purchase. The loan offers a fixed interest rate 1% below market, requires no private mortgage insurance, and allows borrowers to finance up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value. Borrowers must contribute 3% of the purchase price from their own funds. Design assistance from an architectural firm is also available to help buyers plan improvements and review contractor proposals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate mortgage loan priced 1% below market rate. Structured as a two-close loan: a short-term construction loan refinanced into a 30-year permanent mortgage. Borrower contributes 3% of the purchase price from their own funds (gifts allowed; grants and settlement expense loans do not count) and may borrow the balance needed to purchase and renovate the home, up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value, with a maximum loan amount of $375,000. No private mortgage insurance required. Design assistance from an architectural firm is available to help plan improvements and review contractor proposals. M&T Bank serves as the underwriting and originating lender.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prospective homebuyers and owner-occupants purchasing a home in a designated Healthy Neighborhoods community who plan to make improvements to the property at the time of purchase.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and renovation of a home within a designated Healthy Neighborhood. Purchase financing covers home acquisition in eligible areas; sales prices/mortgage balances up to $170,000 (habitable condition), greater than $170,000 (habitable or non-habitable depending on repair commitment), or non-habitable properties requiring code remediation. Rehabilitation financing covers owner-occupant improvements including exterior work, with minimum spend requirements: at least $5,000 for acquisitions at or below $170,000; at least 10% of acquisition price for acquisitions between $170,000–$200,000; at least $20,000 for acquisitions at or above $200,000; and full code remediation for non-habitable properties. Eligible costs include licensed contractor labor and materials, or borrower/subcontractor materials reimbursed as materials-in-place with receipts. Settlement expense loans, government/philanthropic grants, and private mortgage insurance do not count toward the 3% down-payment requirement. Applies to 1–4 unit residential properties.

See https://healthyneighborhoods.org/neighborhoods/ for the full list of eligible locations. Must be purchasing a home within a designated Healthy Neighborhood in Baltimore City or other eligible areas.

For select properties located in a Vacancy Reduction Priority Geography zone, an optional Interest Rate Reduction (IRR) Grant buys down mortgage discount points on behalf of the borrower, reducing the interest rate to 3.5%.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program allows low-income families to rent quality housing in the private market using federal funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The Housing Authority of Calvert County (HACC) pays a portion of eligible families' monthly rent directly to the property owner or manager each month. Families can use their vouchers to rent a house or apartment from private landlords throughout Calvert County. The program helps families transition from subsidized to non-subsidized housing. As of September 2024, there is a 5-year waitlist for this program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) maintains a separate waiting list for current HAPGC program participants, residents, and applicants who need an accessible housing unit due to a disability. Eligible individuals can apply at any time to be placed on this list for Project-Based Voucher units that meet their accessibility needs. The subsidy stays with the building (not transferable if the household moves), and rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income. Units may include single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments in privately owned/managed properties. Priority is assigned through a four-tier system based on wheelchair/scooter use and current housing status; within each tier, applications are processed first-in, first-out by application date.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides access to accessible housing units through the Project-Based Voucher (PBV) program for persons with disabilities. The subsidy stays with the building (not transferable if the household moves), and rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income. Units may include single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments in privately owned/managed properties. Only the Head of Household may apply. The waiting list is not open to the general public; only current HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher, Public Housing, Project Based Voucher, and Moderate Rehabilitation program participants/residents, as well as current applicants on any HAPGC waiting list, may apply. Priority is assigned through a four-tier system based on wheelchair/scooter use and current housing status; within each tier, applications are processed first-in, first-out by application date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher participants, Public Housing residents, Project Based Voucher participants, Moderate Rehabilitation participants, and current applicants on any HAPGC waiting list who need an accessible unit due to a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessible rental housing units (single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments) that meet the applicant's disability-related accessibility needs, including physical modifications, auxiliary aids, and alternative formats for reasonable accommodations. Rental subsidy covers the portion of rent above approximately 30% of the household's adjusted gross income. The subsidy is project-based and remains with the building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to current participants and applicants of HAPGC programs in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current participant of the HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher Program, OR a current resident of the HAPGC Public Housing Program, OR a current participant of the HAPGC Project Based Voucher Program, OR a current participant of the HAPGC Moderate Rehabilitation Program, OR a current applicant on an HAPGC waiting list
Must have a disability requiring an accessible unit
Only the Head of Household is eligible to apply — other household members cannot apply separately
Priority is assigned by a four-tier system based on wheelchair/scooter use and current housing status; within each tier, applications are ordered by date received (FIFO)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed PBVAWL application to the 504 Coordinator at HAPGC's office (9200 Basil Court, Rm 500, Largo, MD 20774) by mail or in person. Applications are available at HAPGC's office (9200 Basil Ct., Suite 107, Largo, MD 20744) or online. The application form includes a checklist for specific accessibility needs (e.g., wheelchair access, single-level units, grab bars, visual/hearing aids, live-in attendant bedrooms). Applications are dated and time-stamped upon receipt for priority placement within each tier.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) provides tax-exempt bond financing that also generates 4% Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) for multifamily rental housing projects. The program supports new construction, adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings, and preservation of existing housing units to promote affordable rental housing for low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and seniors throughout Prince George's County. Bond authority is allocated on a first-come-first-served basis from HAPGC's annual allocation of tax-exempt bond authority. Income restrictions require 20% of units at or below 50% AMI or 40% of units at or below 60% AMI, with maximum rents set at 30% of AMI. Minimum project size is 5 units.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bond financing that also generates 'as-of-right' 4% Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) for multifamily rental housing projects. Flexible financing supports new construction, adaptive reuse, and preservation projects. Developer's fee limits apply: 15% on first $10M of development costs and 10% on excess. Builder's fees are 15% (new construction, large projects) or 17% (rehabilitation, large projects). Deed restrictions required for a minimum of 15 years. Income restrictions require 20% of units at or below 50% AMI or 40% of units at or below 60% AMI, with maximum rents set at 30% of AMI. Minimum project size is 5 units. Underwriting standards include minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.15 stabilized/1.00 through year 15, minimum 5% vacancy underwriting, operating expenses of $4,000–$7,000/unit/year, replacement reserves of at least $300/unit/year, and operating reserves of 3–6 months of expenses.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings, and preservation/acquisition with substantial rehabilitation of existing affordable multifamily rental housing units (minimum 5 units).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Prince George's County, Maryland, with priority given to projects located in: Inner Beltway Communities (incorporated and unincorporated areas between DC and I-495); Regional Transit Districts (areas around Metro stops at Largo Town Center, New Carrollton, Prince George's Plaza, Branch Avenue, and Suitland); Opportunity Zones (census tracts designated as Opportunity Zones); and Designated Development Areas (e.g., Westphalia). Projects to preserve existing affordable housing are also a county-wide priority. New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas (Smart Growth). Projects outside designated priority areas may also be eligible where the applicant demonstrates to HAPGC's satisfaction that there is a need for affordable rental housing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program for Housing Choice Voucher and Public Housing participants administered by the Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC). Participants sign a 5-year contract with the Housing Authority and receive supportive services — including education, job training, career development, behavioral health, health and fitness, and employment assistance — to help them become economically independent and reduce dependency on welfare assistance and rental subsidies. As household income rises and rent increases, the difference between the old and new rent is deposited into an escrow savings account for the family. Services are provided at no cost to residents.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program – Landlord Partnership and Recruitment
structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) administers the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program (also known as Section 8), which provides tenant-based rental assistance to eligible low-income households and recruits private landlords to participate in the program. On the tenant side, eligible low-income applicants join a waiting list through a lottery process; a lottery randomly selects up to 5,000 applicants from those who apply during the open application window, and selected participants receive vouchers to help pay for housing in the private market. Families may choose any housing unit that meets program requirements, including units with rent above the payment standard if the family pays the difference (up to 40% of adjusted income). Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) program participants are automatically added to the waitlist. On the landlord side, HAPGC recruits and partners with private landlords to rent their units to voucher holders. HAPGC pays the difference between what the tenant can afford (no more than 30% of their adjusted monthly income for rent and utilities) and the lower of the payment standard or the unit's gross rent, with guaranteed monthly rental assistance payments made directly to the landlord's bank account. All rents are subject to a comparability study of similar unassisted properties in the area. HAPGC is especially seeking landlords willing to make properties accessible for voucher holders with disabilities. Landlords must meet county licensing and property standards requirements and attend a landlord briefing to participate. Payment standards cover 40+ Prince George's County zip codes in the 20601–20912 range; landlords in zip codes 20607, 20720, 20623, 20715, 20716, 20721, 20722, 20735, 20772, and 20774 are especially encouraged to participate.

Selected participants receive vouchers to help pay rent to private landlords in the private market.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Project Based Voucher (PBV) Program provides affordable rental housing assistance at specific privately owned properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers, PBV assistance is attached to designated units at approved properties — if a family moves out, the rental assistance stays with the unit, not the family. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and administered locally by the Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC).

structured_extraction.program_description: SHIP provides free, unbiased Medicare counseling and education to Medicare beneficiaries in Howard County. Trained staff and Certified Medicare Counselors help with questions about what Medicare covers, prescription drug plans, Medicare Advantage and health plans, Medigap policies, billing, claims, denials, and appeals, as well as programs that can help lower Medicare costs. SHIP also includes a Senior Medicare Patrol (SMP) component that helps beneficiaries prevent, detect, and report health care fraud and billing errors. The program also provides Medicare enrollment guidance, Medigap counseling, appeals assistance, and prescription drug cost assistance screening.

SHIP also directs beneficiaries to external resources including Medicare.gov, SSA.gov, and the Maryland Insurance Administration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Work Green Howard Business Recycling Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Work Green Howard is Howard County's certification, recognition, and technical assistance program that helps businesses, apartments, condominiums, and office buildings reduce waste, improve recycling practices, and adopt greener operations. Businesses submit an annual recycling report detailing their activities—including single stream, cardboard, organics, and other materials—and upon completion receive a signed certificate and window cling/decal to display in the community. Certified businesses are also eligible to apply for the county's annual Green Awards, including the Business Recycling & Waste Reduction Award and the Green Community Leadership Award. The program provides technical assistance and guidance to businesses seeking to improve their environmental performance and sustainability practices, including a step-by-step framework for establishing or improving a workplace recycling program (waste audit, employee education, container labeling, measurement, and maintenance guidance). The program is open to Howard County businesses of all types, including offices, restaurants, car washes, and other commercial operations, as well as apartment/condominium properties and office buildings. Office buildings of 150,000 sq ft or greater are required by state law and Howard County Code to submit a recycling plan and annual report. Apartment/condominium properties with 10 or more units must also submit a recycling plan and annual report.
structured_extraction.agency: Howard County Bureau of Environmental Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses that complete and submit the annual recycling report receive Work Green Howard certification, a signed certificate, and a window cling/decal to display in the community. The program also provides technical assistance and guidance on recycling and sustainability practices, including a step-by-step framework for establishing or improving a workplace recycling program (waste audit, employee education, container labeling, measurement, and maintenance guidance). Small businesses may also use the drop-off recycling service at Alpha Ridge Landfill for Howard County-generated recyclables (no permit required). Certified businesses are eligible to apply for the annual Green Awards program, including the Business Recycling & Waste Reduction Award and Green Community Leadership Award. There is no monetary award associated with certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County offers loans to property owners to help cover the cost of connecting their existing septic systems to the public sanitary sewer system (or both public water and sewer). The program aims to reduce reliance on septic systems, protect groundwater, improve environmental infrastructure, and protect the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The program does not apply to water-only connections. It is authorized under Howard County Code Title 20, Subtitle 7 (Water/Sewer Connection Financing Program, Section 20.700). Properties in the eastern area of the county served by the public water and sewer system, within the Planned Service Area of the Howard County Master Plan for water and sewerage, are eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are available to finance all or part of the costs of switching an existing septic system connection to the public water and sewerage systems. The program applies to sewer-only connections or combined water and sewer connections — not water-only connections. Authorized under Howard County Code, Title 20, Subtitle 7, Section 20.700. Specific loan amounts, interest rates, and terms are detailed in the Water & Sewer Financing Program Fact Sheet available for download.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs of connecting an existing septic system to the public sanitary sewer system, or to both public water and sewer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland — properties in the eastern area of the county served by the public water and sewer system, within the Planned Service Area of the Howard County Master Plan for water and sewerage, where access to existing sewer lines is available. structured_extraction.program_name: Aging in Place Property Tax Credit (CB 23-2021)
structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County provides a property tax credit for senior homeowners and certain military veterans to help them remain in their homes. Available since 2017 and extended in 2025 from a maximum of eight years to 10 years (per CB 60-2025), the credit has three eligibility tracks: (A) Longevity — applicant must be 65 or older and have owned and resided in the dwelling for 30 or more years; (B) Retired Service Member or surviving spouse — 65 or older with 20 or more years of active-duty service; (C) Disabled Service Member or surviving spouse — active, retired, or honorably discharged with a 75–99% service-connected VA disability rating. The 2025 extension (CB 60-2025) also expanded eligibility to include the Disabled Service Member track. The credit equals 20% of the net County property tax on assessed value up to $650,000, applied after all other eligible credits, and may be granted for a total of 10 years. Applicants cannot receive this credit in the same tax year as the Senior Tax Credit or the Public Safety Officer Tax Credit. The program also covers homeowners making qualifying modifications to their homes to support aging in place, as established under CB 23-2021. Established under County Bill CB 23-2021 and amended by CB 60-2025, the credit helps older and veteran residents afford to stay in their homes by reducing their property tax bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit equals 20% of the net County property tax on assessed value up to $650,000, after all other eligible credits have been applied. Cannot be combined with the Senior Tax Credit or Public Safety Officer Tax Credit in the same tax year. Credit may be granted for a total of 10 years (extended from 8 years by CB 60-2025). After the initial application is approved, an annual attestation (Statement of Eligibility) is required each spring for up to 9 additional years. Renewal is available upon submitting verification of continued eligibility. Does not automatically renew without attestation. Application deadline is October 1, 2026 for tax year 2026 (annually September 30; new applicants affected by CB 60-2025 had 30 days from December 9, 2025). The program also applies to qualifying aging-in-place home modifications per CB 23-2021.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1, 2026 (annually September 30; new applicants affected by CB 60-2025 had 30 days from December 9, 2025)

Also applicable to homeowners making qualifying home modifications to support aging in place.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County property tax liability on the principal residence, helping homeowners afford to remain in their home. Also applies to qualifying aging-in-place home modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Howard County, Maryland. Dwelling must be located in Howard County and must be the applicant's only principal residence.

Eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months before applying, and the application must include a certificate from the County's Department of Inspections, Licenses, and Permits verifying the device is a geothermal energy device and has been properly installed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County's Livable Homes Tax Credit provides a one-time credit against County property taxes for the cost of certain accessibility features installed in a homeowner's principal residence in Howard County. Eligible features include no-step entrances, widened doorways, grab bar reinforcements, elevators, lifts, accessible bathrooms, slip-resistant flooring, lever handles, and similar age-friendly modifications. The credit is intended to help homeowners make their homes more accessible for aging or disabled residents, supporting aging in place. Costs incurred within 12 months before applying are eligible, must exceed $500, and must be paid by the applicant and not reimbursed by another entity. The credit also covers the cost of an age-friendly assessment by a certified aging in place specialist (up to $100). If the credit exceeds the County property tax owed, the unused amount carries over to future tax years until the full amount is received. This credit cannot be renewed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time property tax credit equal to 100% of the eligible cost of qualifying accessibility features, up to $2,500, against County property taxes. Eligible costs must exceed $500, must have been incurred within 12 months before applying, and must be paid by the applicant and not reimbursed by another entity. Costs must be for authorized accessibility features (including reasonable installation costs) installed on an existing principal residence, or for an age-friendly assessment by a certified aging in place specialist (up to $100). If the credit exceeds the County property tax owed, the unused amount carries over to future tax years until the full amount is received. This credit cannot be renewed.

A separate track exists for permanently and totally disabled public safety officers or judicial officers, and for surviving spouses or cohabitants of fallen public safety or judicial officers. The credit does not automatically renew and cannot be combined with the Aging in Place or Senior Tax Credit in the same year. Annual renewal via a Statement of Eligibility is required for the disabled/fallen officer track.

Does not automatically renew; annual Statement of Eligibility required by September 30 for the disabled/fallen track. Cannot be combined with the Aging in Place, Public Safety Officer, or Senior Tax Credit in the same year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Trash, Bay, and Watershed Protection Fee Hardship Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County offers an income-based hardship tax credit and fee exemption for low-income homeowners and renters. Eligible homeowners receive a 60 percent credit against the County Trash Fee and Watershed Protection Fee, plus a 100 percent exemption from the Bay Restoration Charge (Bay Fee), which is $15.00 per quarter for residential properties. Renters who pay their own water and sewer bill directly for the property they are leasing may also qualify for the Bay Fee exemption only. Homeowners can apply for both the Bay Fee Hardship Exemption and the Trash Fee Credit using a single application form, since the eligibility requirements are the same for both. Residents who receive the Senior Tax Credit automatically receive this hardship credit if eligibility requirements are met. A separate renter application is available for low-income renters seeking only the Bay Fee exemption. Combined household income must be at or below 250% of the Federal poverty level (e.g., $39,900 for a household of 1; $54,100 for a household of 2; up to $80,375 for a family of four for tax year 2025). The credit does not automatically renew and must be reapplied for each year.
