structured_extraction.program_name: Chestertown Arts & Entertainment District Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: The Chestertown Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District offers place-based tax benefits for artists, entrepreneurs, property owners, and nonprofits to support a vibrant cultural life in downtown Chestertown. The District covers 51 acres of Chestertown's historic downtown area. Benefits include: (1) an income-tax subtraction for qualifying artists who create and sell their creative works within the District; (2) property tax credits for property owners who build or renovate structures for qualified arts purposes; and (3) an admission and amusement tax exemption for qualifying arts and entertainment activities. The program is administered in coordination with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the State Comptroller's Office.

State and local tax abatements are available for qualified artists and property owners.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on income, property, and admissions/amusement taxes for arts and entertainment activities in downtown Chestertown, including tax abatements on income from creative work sold within the District and on property improvements for qualified arts purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the 51-acre Chestertown Arts and Entertainment District in historic downtown Chestertown, Kent County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: hotDesks is a coworking office space and business incubator network operated by Kent County Economic and Tourism Development in Chestertown, Maryland. Members get access to shared workspace, gigabit broadband internet, mentors and coaches, entrepreneur and innovation training, access to capital connections, and services for project acceleration, prototyping, and commercialization. structured_extraction.program_description: Entrepreneur Training for Success (ETS) is a free, intensive 3- to 4-month training program (60 hours) in business, financial literacy, and leadership skills for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs. The curriculum covers micro-entrepreneurship fundamentals including time management, marketing, sales, branding, communications, accounting, budgeting, pricing, business registration, financing, and investor pitching. The program has been offered in multiple cohorts and formats — including in-person and online sessions — targeting women with early-stage business ideas or startups operating less than one year, Spanish-speaking participants (including Washington, D.C. residents), and participants in the Montgomery County, MD; Baltimore Metropolitan Area (including West Baltimore and Baltimore City); and Arlington County, VA regions. Classes are held on weekday evenings, with cohorts of up to 12 participants supported by a lead trainer, volunteer mentors, and guest speakers. There is no cost to accepted participants thanks to program sponsors and donors. A Baltimore City cohort offered a $1,000 stipend upon completion. The Spring 2025 cohort is sponsored by Montgomery County, MD and Arlington County, VA, with the program starting April 21, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: First-Time Homebuyer Counseling, Education, and Housing Classes (Talleres de Vivienda, including Spanish 6-Hour Seminar for Montgomery & Prince George's Counties)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) provides comprehensive first-time homebuyer counseling and education services for residents of the District of Columbia, Maryland (Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Baltimore), and Northern Virginia/Virginia. Services include group homebuyer education courses ranging from 2-hour introductory sessions to 8-hour in-person certificate classes (in-person and virtual), one-on-one counseling sessions with HUD-Certified Housing Counselors, and group seminars — offered in both English and Spanish. Topics covered include the home-buying process, mortgage loans, credit history, budgeting, personal finances, local assistance programs, energy efficiency rebates, Inclusionary Zoning/Affordable Dwelling Unit (ADU) opportunities, and closing on a home. Counselors also assist clients in applying for down payment assistance programs. Certificate classes qualify participants for certain homeownership programs (e.g., DC Inclusionary Zoning/ADU). LEDC additionally offers a 6-hour homebuyer education seminar (available in both English and Spanish) via Zoom (two 3-hour sessions) specifically for prospective buyers in Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, Maryland, featuring experts including a loan officer, home inspector, real estate agent, and insurance agent. Completing the seminar and an individual counseling appointment satisfies lender and government first-time homebuyer training requirements and leads to a HUD counseling certificate. The Energy Efficiency and Electrification workshop is explicitly free. Spanish-language classes (Talleres de Vivienda) are offered specifically to serve Spanish-speaking prospective homebuyers across these service areas.

Topics include the homebuying process, budgeting, mortgages, closing costs, local assistance programs, energy efficiency, Inclusionary Zoning/Affordable Dwelling Unit (ADU) opportunities, and closing. Counselors assist clients in applying for down payment assistance programs. A two-part, 6-hour virtual homebuyer education seminar (offered in both English and Spanish) is available for Montgomery and Prince George's County residents; upon completing both sessions and an individual counseling appointment, participants receive a HUD certificate required for first-time homebuyer assistance programs. Spanish-language Talleres de Vivienda workshops are available covering the full range of homebuying topics. The Energy Efficiency and Electrification workshop is explicitly free.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 based on the small business's revenues. Funds cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by other federal, state, or local disaster relief programs.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority given to businesses in southeast Baltimore County, southeast Baltimore City, and northern Anne Arundel County. Businesses in other parts of Maryland must demonstrate severe impact from the bridge collapse.

Services include evaluating business ideas, developing business plans and financial projections, online and social media marketing strategy, navigating licensing and permitting, improving credit, bookkeeping (including QuickBooks), company formation, food service certifications, DC Great Streets grant application assistance, pricing, and industry-specific guidance in sectors such as construction, cleaning, daycare, and retail. Advisors have decades of experience across a wide range of industries. Business financing through LEDC loan officers (loans up to $250,000) is also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost one-on-one business coaching and group training workshops covering business planning and strategy, financial projections and management, web and social media presence, bookkeeping tools (including QuickBooks), company formation, food service certifications, licensing and permitting, DC Great Streets grant application assistance, marketing and advertising, access to capital, pricing, and industry-specific topics including construction, cleaning, daycare, and retail. Business financing through LEDC loan officers (loans up to $250,000) is also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aspiring entrepreneurs and current small business owners seeking practical guidance to start or grow a business, across all industries.

structured_extraction.program_name: LEDC CrediFirst and Resilience Loan (Credit Builder Loans)
structured_extraction.program_description: Two credit-building loan products offered by the Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) for individuals who want to build or repair their credit score. The CrediFirst loan ($500–$1,000) helps individuals with no credit history establish a positive credit history, while the Resilience Loan (up to $2,500) helps borrowers improve existing credit by paying off high-interest debt, collections, or past-due obligations. Both loans carry a 4.5% fixed APR with no minimum credit score required. Repayment activity is reported to all three major credit bureaus. The program includes personalized one-on-one credit counseling and access to free financial coaching. A $32 nonrefundable credit report fee is required to process the application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CrediFirst: loans of $500–$1,000 at 4.5% fixed APR, up to 12-month term, no collateral or closing fee. Resilience Loan: up to $2,500 at 4.5% fixed APR, up to 36-month term, no collateral or closing fee. No minimum credit score required. A $32 nonrefundable credit report fee is required. If approved, loan funds are used to pay off debt (collections up to $2,000 or high-interest debt) to improve credit score; any remaining funds are deposited into the borrower's account. Repayment reported to all three major credit bureaus.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DC, Maryland, and Virginia residents aged 18 or older — including employed individuals and business owners — who want to establish or improve their credit history, including those with no credit history (invisible credit) or those seeking to repair existing credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit building, reducing credit card debt, paying off collections (up to $2,000) or high-interest debt, and paying past-due obligations to improve credit score; any remaining loan funds are deposited to the borrower's account.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Washington DC, Maryland, or Virginia. LEDC serves the Washington DC metro area and Maryland, including Montgomery, Prince George's, Frederick, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older
Must be a DC, MD, or VA resident
Must be employed or able to demonstrate ability to repay the loan (proof of income required)
Personal bank statements for last 3 months
2 months of personal pay stubs (CrediFirst only)
Completed LEDC application form
No past-due accounts exceeding $2,500, tax liens, court judgments, or child support
If recently filed for bankruptcy, must wait at least one year before applying
Applicants with recent missed payments or collections exceeding the loan amount must meet with a financial coach before proceeding
$32 nonrefundable credit report fee required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an interest form online at the LEDC website (or via Airtable form). If eligible, LEDC sends an email with a link to the full application. Pay the $32 nonrefundable credit report fee via the Xpress Pay link sent by email/text. An underwriter reviews the file (1–7 days on average) and may request additional information. Credit counseling may be required. Loan decision is communicated via email.

structured_extraction.program_name: LEDC NextGen Impact Fund – Contractor Network

Approved contractors gain access to a broader customer base, sales growth support, training, and co-marketing opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: LEDC, a certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI), offers alternative small business loans to help entrepreneurs launch and grow local businesses. The program serves startups and existing small businesses that have difficulty obtaining credit from traditional banks, including those without a Social Security number (ITIN accepted), with no minimum credit score required, and for businesses that have not yet started operations. Loan officers assess each application beyond standard credit guidelines, focusing on the character of the entrepreneur and the potential of their idea. Three primary business loan products are available: the Growth Loan for established businesses with 2+ years in operation (up to $250,000, up to 10 years, 3% closing fee); the Startup Loan for businesses under 2 years old (up to $20,000, up to 60 months, 3% closing fee); and the SEED Loan for very early-stage startups under 1 year or planning to launch within 3 months (up to $5,000, up to 36 months, 1% closing fee, no collateral required). Additionally, credit-building loan products are available for individuals: CrediFirst ($500–$1,000) and the Resilience Loan (up to $2,500), both at 4.5% APR. Rates for business loans start at 6.5% fixed APR. Loans over $10,000 require collateral or a co-signer. Approval takes approximately 2 weeks for loans under $50,000 and up to 4 weeks for larger amounts. No hidden fees; free business advice and training are included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Business loans ranging from $500 to $250,000 at fixed APRs starting at 6.5%, with terms from 6 to 120 months depending on loan product. Three business loan tiers: Growth Loan (up to $250,000, up to 10-year term, 3% closing fee, for established businesses with 2+ years in operation); Startup Loan (up to $20,000, up to 60-month term, 3% closing fee, for businesses under 2 years old); SEED Loan (up to $5,000, up to 36-month term, 1% closing fee, no collateral required, for businesses under 1 year or pre-launch). Credit-building products for individuals include CrediFirst ($500–$1,000) and the Resilience Loan (up to $2,500), both at 4.5% APR. Requirements vary by loan amount: loans up to $2,500 require 3 months of bank statements; up to $5,000 require 3 months of bank statements and last year's tax return; up to $10,000 require 6 months of bank statements and two years of personal tax returns; up to $250,000 require 6 months of bank statements, two years of personal tax returns, collateral worth at least 25% of the loan and/or a co-signer, and financial statements or a business plan. No minimum credit score required; ITIN accepted. Uses include vehicles and equipment, working capital, inventory, renovation or business expansion, bridge financing for government grants and contracts, expansion to new locations, hiring additional personnel, and business acquisition. No hidden fees; free business advice and training included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and entrepreneurs at any stage, including startups and established businesses, as well as individuals seeking to build credit. Designed to serve underbanked and underserved communities, including those without a Social Security number (ITIN accepted), those with limited or poor credit history, and those in low- and moderate-income or minority communities in Maryland, Virginia, DC, or Puerto Rico.

structured_extraction.program_description: LEDC's Down Payment Assistance Program provides first-time homebuyers with $10,000 for down payment or closing costs, along with homebuyer education and one-on-one counseling, to help working families achieve homeownership and build long-term financial stability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $10,000 in grant funds for down payment and/or closing costs for eligible first-time homebuyers purchasing a primary residence. Funds are limited and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Recipients must contribute a minimum of $1,000 of their own funds. Applicant liquid assets must be less than 20% of the purchase price. Property must be a single-unit (single-family home, townhouse, condominium, or modular/manufactured home); cannot be used for investment property or second homes. Pro-rated repayment required if property is sold within 3 years of purchase; full amount due if property ceases to be owner-occupied during the 3-year compliance period; no monthly payments or accruing interest. Funds are considered taxable income (1099-MISC issued). Program also includes homebuyer seminar, one-on-one counseling, and post-purchase counseling.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Casino Business Investment Fund (MCBIF) is managed by MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.) and provides affordable, flexible, and patient capital to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. The fund receives a portion (1.5% of gross video lottery terminal revenue) of proceeds from Maryland casino facilities, channeled through the State's Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce. At least 50% of funds must go to businesses in communities surrounding a video lottery terminal (casino) facility, including locations in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Worcester County, and Prince George's County; the remaining 50% can go to any Maryland business. Since inception, MCBIF has deployed over $108.9 million across more than 1,067 settled transactions to small businesses. The fund offers loans ranging from $500 to $250,000 (varying by fund manager), equity investment products (convertible subordinated notes, preferred stock, common stock, and warrants), and surety bonding (bid, payment, and performance bonds). Multiple fund managers participate including Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Baltimore County DEWD, Howard County EDA, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Prince George's FSC First, Montgomery County MCEDC, and Tri-County Council for Western Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $500 to $250,000 (varies by fund manager), including term loans (interest rates 5%–12%), lines of credit, professional/technical assistance loans, demand loans, and letters of credit. Terms typically up to 10 years. Equity products include convertible subordinated notes, preferred stock, common stock, and warrants. Surety bonding includes bid, payment, and performance bonds. Non-refundable application fee of $250; commitment fee of $500–$3,500 if approved. At least 50% of investment funds must go to businesses in designated Target Areas near Maryland casinos (Baltimore City, Cecil County, Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Worcester County, and Prince George's County); the remaining 50% can go to any Maryland business. Multiple fund managers participate (Anne Arundel EDC, Baltimore County DEWD, Howard County EDA, Maryland Capital Enterprises, FSC First, Montgomery County MCEDC, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland). Eligible uses include acquisition of businesses, equipment, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, working capital, marketing, staffing, inventory, professional consulting, franchise fees, startup costs, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances.

Counties served include Wicomico, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Frederick, Howard, Washington, Cecil, Harford, Somerset, Dorchester, Worcester, Caroline, Queen Anne's, Charles, and others.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) – Guaranty Fund Program (GFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Guaranty Fund Program (GFP) provides financial assistance to eligible small businesses in Maryland through loan guaranties and interest rate subsidies for loans made by financial institutions such as banks, finance companies, and leasing companies. A loan guaranty cannot exceed the lesser of 80% of the loan or $2,000,000, with terms not exceeding 10 years. The program can also subsidize up to 4 percentage points of the interest charged by the lending institution, subject to annual review. By reducing lender risk, the program helps small businesses that cannot access adequate financing through normal lending channels, particularly those owned by individuals from historically underserved groups.
structured_extraction.agency: MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.), managing the MSBDFA on behalf of the Maryland Department of Commerce
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan guaranties up to the lesser of 80% of the loan or $2,000,000, with terms not exceeding 10 years. Interest rates generally range from prime rate to prime rate plus 2%. Guarantee fees range from 0.75% to 1.5% of the loan amount. The program can also subsidize up to 4 percentage points of the lender's interest rate, subject to annual review. Repayment terms for the subsidy are negotiated directly with the borrower.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Easement Purchase Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) was established by the Maryland General Assembly in 1977 and is administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture to preserve productive agricultural land and woodland for continued food and fiber production. The program purchases permanent agricultural preservation easements (purchase of development rights) on eligible farmland and woodland. By selling the development rights to their property, landowners permanently restrict the land to agricultural use while retaining private ownership and the right to continue farming. The Foundation pays for the easement and monitors the property to ensure compliance in perpetuity. Payment is the lesser of: the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value of the land, or 75% of the appraised fair market value. Recent offers have ranged from approximately $600 to over $10,000 per acre (with some areas such as Caroline County ranging between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre in recent years; Worcester County FY25/26 average was $3,123/acre with a range of $2,200–$3,123/acre). Landowners who sell an easement below the full appraised value of the restrictions may also qualify for certain tax benefits. Properties are ranked and selected based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas. The program has preserved over 350,000 acres in all 23 Maryland counties, representing a public investment of over $900 million. Participation is completely voluntary. The program helps curb random urban development and sprawl, protects open space and wildlife habitat, and enhances Chesapeake Bay and Coastal Bays water quality. Worcester County has been state-certified since FY04, allowing it to retain 75% of the agricultural transfer tax collected for farmland protection and to receive additional state funds. The program is administered at the county level through a Program Administrator and the local Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board. Talbot County administers the local application process through the Talbot County Planning and Zoning Office, with a local deadline of April 1, 2026. FY27 applications to sell an easement to MALPF are accepted from January to May 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) / Maryland Department of Agriculture
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MALPF pays landowners for agricultural preservation easements that permanently restrict development on their farmland and woodland. Payment is the lesser of: the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value of the land, or 75% of the appraised fair market value. In recent years, the Foundation has paid between approximately $600 and over $10,000 per acre (in Caroline County, between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre in recent years; Worcester County FY25/26 average: $3,123/acre, range $2,200–$3,123/acre). Properties are ranked annually and easements are purchased competitively each cycle year. Easement restrictions are permanent (in perpetuity), and a preservation agreement is recorded in Maryland Land Records. Landowners who sell an easement below the full appraised value of the restrictions may also qualify for certain tax benefits. Worcester County retains 75% of the agricultural transfer tax collected under its state-certified program to fund local farmland protection efforts.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural landowners with eligible prime farmland or woodland in Maryland who are willing to voluntarily sell a permanent easement restricting development on their property. The program is administered at the county level through local Program Administrators and Agricultural Preservation Advisory Boards. In Talbot County, owners of eligible farmland and/or woodland who want to permanently protect their land for agricultural use may apply through the Talbot County Planning and Zoning Office. In Worcester County, contact Katherine Munson (MALPF Program Administrator) or Lily Wagner (Environmental Planner II).

Landowners may use easement proceeds for any purpose, including purchasing farm or additional farmland, retirement, estate planning, improving farming operations, investing in new farm products, restoring a historic home, or paying off debt.

Caroline County landowners contact Caroline County Planning; Washington County landowners apply through the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning; Cecil County landowners apply through the Cecil County Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board; Charles County landowners contact Charles County Planning Staff at the Department of Planning and Growth Management; Worcester County landowners contact the Worcester County Department of the Environment (Katherine Munson, kmunson@worcestermd.gov, 410-632-1220 ext 1302); Talbot County landowners apply through the Talbot County Planning and Zoning Office at 215 Bay Street, Suite 2, Easton, MD 21601.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Easement Purchase Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) was established by the Maryland General Assembly in 1977 and is administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture to preserve productive agricultural land and woodland for continued food and fiber production. The program purchases permanent agricultural preservation easements (purchase of development rights) on eligible farmland and woodland. By selling the development rights to their property, landowners permanently restrict the land to agricultural use while retaining private ownership and the right to continue farming. The Foundation pays for the easement and monitors the property to ensure compliance in perpetuity. Payment is the lesser of: the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value of the land, or 75% of the appraised fair market value. Recent offers have ranged from approximately $600 to over $10,000 per acre (with some areas such as Caroline County ranging between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre in recent years; Worcester County FY25/26 average was $3,123/acre with a range of $2,200–$3,123/acre; some counties have seen recent offers from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre). Landowners who sell an easement below the full appraised value of the restrictions may also qualify for certain tax benefits. Properties are ranked and selected based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas. The program has preserved over 350,000 acres in all 23 Maryland counties, representing a public investment of over $900 million. Participation is completely voluntary. The program helps curb random urban development and sprawl, protects open space and wildlife habitat, and enhances Chesapeake Bay and Coastal Bays water quality. Worcester County has been state-certified since FY04, allowing it to retain 75% of the agricultural transfer tax collected for farmland protection and to receive additional state funds. The program is administered at the county level through a Program Administrator and the local Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board. Talbot County administers the local application process through the Talbot County Planning and Zoning Office, with a local deadline of April 1, 2026. FY27 applications to sell an easement to MALPF are accepted from January to May 2026, with the county-level application emailed to the MALPF Administrator by July 1st of the application year. Note: The State of Maryland has diverted $25 million a year through FY29 from land conservation programs including MALPF, and funding for land conservation will continue to be at risk in coming years.

Payment is the lesser of: the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value of the land, the county cap, or 75% of the appraised fair market value (per Md. Agric. Art. §2-510). In recent years, the Foundation has paid between approximately $600 and over $10,000 per acre statewide (in Caroline County, between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre in recent years; Worcester County FY25/26 average: $3,123/acre, range $2,200–$3,123/acre; some counties have seen recent offers from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre). Properties are ranked annually and easements are purchased competitively each cycle year. Easement restrictions are permanent (in perpetuity), and a preservation agreement is recorded in Maryland Land Records. Landowners who sell an easement below the full appraised value of the restrictions may also qualify for certain tax benefits. Worcester County retains 75% of the agricultural transfer tax collected under its state-certified program to fund local farmland protection efforts. The state has invested over $900 million in this program. Note: The State of Maryland has diverted $25 million a year through FY29 from land conservation programs including MALPF, creating funding risk in coming years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program

The program is designed to attract and retain large animal veterinarians in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation

Loan terms vary by amount: 3.5 years ($25,000–$39,999), 4 years ($40,000–$59,999), 4.5 years ($60,000–$79,999), or 5 years ($80,000–$100,000). Up to 6-month interest-only repayment period available. Loan origination fee is 0.25%. Collateral security may not exceed 95% of fair market value. Borrower must contribute at least 10% of the cost of purchased items. Personal guarantee required for business entity borrowers. Minimum credit score of 620.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled and agree to have a majority of their large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term.

Reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled
Agree to have a majority of large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers loans to help start up or expand small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facilities in Maryland. The program supports processing of meat, poultry, and blue catfish. It can provide standalone financing or work alongside commercial lenders. Loan proceeds come from the USDA Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program Grant, with matching funds from MARBIDCO. MARBIDCO also provides an equity grant matching the borrower's contribution dollar-for-dollar up to 10% of project costs (capped at $250,000).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $250,000 to $2,500,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.00% (or 3.75% with Home Town Hero veteran discount), with a 0.25% loan origination fee (up to $5,000). Loan terms correspond to the useful life of financed assets, following an initial interest-only period of up to 12 months. Borrowers must provide at least 7.5% equity. MARBIDCO matches the equity contribution dollar-for-dollar up to 10% of project costs, capped at a $250,000 equity grant. New facility applicants must show working capital of at least 10% of project cost. Personal guarantees are required but waived if the borrower provides a 20% equity contribution including MARBIDCO's grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small- and medium-sized livestock processing businesses seeking to start up or expand USDA-inspected slaughter facilities in Maryland. Individual owners and guarantors in the meat and poultry processing sector. Large meat and poultry processing companies (those holding a top-four market share in the sector) are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase real estate, construct a new or expand an existing livestock processing facility, and purchase livestock processing equipment. Priority is given to construction of new facilities, especially in underserved parts of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Priority given to the construction of new facilities in underserved parts of Maryland. No specific county or municipal exclusions.

Recipient/business must self-certify it does not hold a top-four market share in the meat and poultry processing sector
Borrower must provide at least 7.5% of total project cost as equity
Applicants constructing a new facility must demonstrate working capital of at least 10% of project cost (cash or bank line of credit)
Personal guarantees required from all owners of the business entity (waived if borrower provides 20% equity including MARBIDCO equity grant)
All projects must be submitted to USDA for approval before MARBIDCO can disburse funds

structured_extraction.program_name: Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund

It provides financing for equipment purchases and working capital to businesses that cannot obtain commercial financing from traditional lenders such as banks or farm credit associations. Loan origination fee: 1% of the loan amount. Typically 10% equity contribution required. Personal guarantee required from all business owners.

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Agricultural, Rural Business, and Loan Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) offers low-cost loans and competitive grants to support Maryland's agricultural, forestry, and seafood industries. Programs are available for new and existing businesses, young and beginning farmers, watermen, commercial fishermen, landowners, and agribusiness owners. Grant programs help farmers, agribusiness owners, and local governments obtain commercial financing and qualify for federal, state, or county government grant opportunities, with a focus on innovation, diversification, and emerging market opportunities in food and fiber production and rural agritourism. Loan programs are designed to meet financing needs for agricultural, forestry, and seafood businesses, with loans available for land purchases, construction or renovation of facilities, equipment acquisition, and working capital. Specific financing areas include livestock processing, vineyards and orchards, seafood, aquaculture, urban farming, farmland purchase, working capital, commercial fishing boats, crop support, agricultural equipment, equine, dairy, forestry equipment, produce, and veterinarian truck/equipment. Specialty programs include the Maryland Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Fund Program and the Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund. Some programs have regional restrictions: the Southern Maryland Agricultural Revolving Loan Fund is limited to Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's Counties; the Upper Shore Regional Council Farm Incentive Fund is limited to Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties. MARBIDCO works cooperatively with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA Farm Service Agency, and other partners to deliver financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO offers a range of low-cost loans and competitive grants to Maryland agribusinesses. Interest rates range from 3.00%–6.75% and loan amounts range from $10,000 to $2.5 million depending on the program, with most programs requiring full collateralization. Loan programs cover areas such as farmland purchase, livestock processing, vineyards, hopyards, orchards, seafood, aquaculture, working capital, commercial fishing boats, agricultural equipment, equine operations, dairy, and forestry equipment. Grant programs include agriculture added-value grants, urban farming grants, produce grants, and grants supporting innovation and diversification in food and fiber production and rural agritourism. Competitive grants are awarded by a Grant Review Committee, with ranking factors including the significance of the enterprise for economic development and the business's potential economic viability. Specialty programs include the Maryland Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Fund Program and the Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund. MARBIDCO works with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA Farm Service Agency, and other partners to deliver financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established by MARBIDCO to help finance eligible seafood processing projects, including historic oyster shucking facilities. The program supports renovation, construction, or expansion of oyster processing facilities and purchase of processing equipment, while facilitating the return of oyster shells to the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $25,000 to $250,000 at a fixed interest rate of 3.25%, with no origination fee. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund (Nursery Operations)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides affordable loans to commercial watermen who want to start or expand shellfish remote-setting (nursery) aquaculture operations in Maryland. Borrowers who stay current on payments and meet production plan requirements receive partial loan forgiveness in the final year, effectively turning part of the loan into a grant. The University of Maryland Extension also provides training and business planning assistance to participants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $5,000 to $30,000. Loans of $5,000–$15,000 have a 5-year term; loans of $15,001–$30,000 have a 6-year term. The first year requires interest-only payments at a 5.25% interest rate. Borrowers who remain in good standing and meet their production plans have the final year of loan repayments forgiven, effectively providing a grant equal to 22%–27% of the principal. No application fee. Borrowers must contribute at least 10% of the loan amount as a cash equity contribution. A credit score of at least 620 is required (or a qualifying co-signer). The University of Maryland Extension provides training and business planning assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are processed in the order received (rolling basis).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and supplies for commercial remote-setting aquaculture projects with approved business plans, including seed (larvae), shell (substrate), tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, and tank heaters for raising oysters or clams in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MRBIFF Loan Program provides low-interest loans to agricultural and resource-based industry (RBI) enterprises in Maryland. It is available as either a Direct Lending program or a Participation Loan program. Both options help businesses purchase land and capital equipment for production and processing activities. Under the Direct Loan structure, MARBIDCO provides supplemental loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing needed in partnership with a commercial bank. Under the Participation Loan structure, MARBIDCO's share is 30% to 49% while the lead lender holds 51% to 70%. Both options require involvement of a commercial or public sector lender. An additional equity incentive matching fund is available for borrowers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through the Upper Shore Regional Council.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans available in two structures: (1) Direct Loan — MARBIDCO lends 20%–40% of total project cost alongside a commercial bank; interest rate is 4.75% for years 1–3, 5.25% for years 4–6, and 5.75% for remaining term; 1% origination fee; term of 5–7 years for equipment, 10–30 years for land. Maximum amounts: $600,000 for real estate/poultry house construction, $300,000 for equipment/fixed assets, $1,000,000 for large-scale food/fiber processing (capped at 25% of project cost). (2) Participation Loan — MARBIDCO holds 30%–49% share alongside a lead lender (currently Horizon Farm Credit or Colonial Farm Credit); interest rate of 4.25% (with veteran reduction of −0.25% available) plus up to 0.75% lender servicing fee (max blended 5.00%); amortization up to 30 years with a mandatory MARBIDCO balloon payment after 15 years; interest-only period up to 2 years permitted; repayment frequency may be monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, or annual. Maximum amounts: $700,000 for real estate/poultry house construction, $350,000 for equipment/fixed assets, $1,000,000 for large-scale food/fiber processing (capped at 25% of project cost). Typically requires 10% equity contribution from borrower. Commercial lender and/or public instrumentality must have at least equal financial commitment to the project. An Equity Incentive Grant of up to 5% (max $15,000) is available for borrowers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties.

Young and beginning farmers may qualify for reduced equity requirements. Veterans may qualify for a reduced interest rate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of land, poultry house construction, capital equipment and fixed assets for production, building construction, working capital, renewable energy projects, on-farm value-added processing, and large-scale food or fiber processing projects.

requirements_list: Must be an agricultural or resource-based industry enterprise (eligible sectors include agricultural production, aquaculture/fishing/seafood, forestry/timber, wood processing, value-added farm food processing, agri-tourism with farm production requirement, biomass/energy production, equine, horticulture, and environmental/water quality improvement)
Must involve a commercial or public sector lender
A commercial bank or Farm Credit Association loan officer must develop and submit the application on behalf of the applicant

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund – Commercial Oyster Harvester Disaster Relief Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO (Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation) operates this zero-interest, no-collateral disaster relief loan program to support eligible commercial oyster harvesters across Maryland. The Maryland General Assembly approved $2 million in the FY 2027 state budget for this program, and MARBIDCO is temporarily contributing an additional $1 million, bringing total available funding to $3 million. The program helps watermen manage personal and business expenses tied to oyster harvesting following a difficult season marked by poor market conditions, bad weather, and environmental calamities. All qualified applicants receive the same prorated loan amount based on total available funding divided by the number of qualified applications received by the deadline, up to a maximum of $10,000 per borrower. Repayment begins February 1, 2027, with equal quarterly principal payments over 10 quarters (2.5 years). Borrowers who remain current on all payments may qualify for partial loan forgiveness equal to the final two quarterly payments. Borrowers more than 90 days late on any quarterly payment forfeit the forgiveness opportunity and owe the full remaining principal, plus any late fees and default interest.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR), offers subsidized loan financing to commercial watermen and entrepreneurs who want to start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations in Maryland's Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. The program provides low-interest loans with principal forgiveness provisions to new and existing shellfish aquaculture businesses. The University of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Agriculture also contribute training and business planning assistance to current and prospective shellfish growers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $5,000 to $100,000 at a MARBIDCO interest rate of 5.25% (maximum; can be as low as 3.00% during the initial interest-only period). No loan origination fee. At least 10% equity contribution required. Repayment terms vary by purchase type: substrate and seed up to 5 years (1–3 years interest-only, then 2 years principal and interest); capital equipment up to 7 years (1–3 years interest-only, then 4 years P&I); blended purchases up to 6 years. First-time borrowers receive 40% principal forgiveness (up to $100,000). Existing borrowers in good standing receive 25% principal forgiveness on amounts between $100,001 and $300,000. Grant funds from NRCS EQIP or Chesapeake Bay Watershed Initiative can be assigned to MARBIDCO to reduce loan interest and principal; applicants cannot receive both MARBIDCO principal forgiveness and NRCS grant for the same project activity. Business planning assistance and training are also available through the University of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis — applications processed in order received
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial watermen and entrepreneurs holding or having applied for a Maryland DNR shellfish aquaculture lease who wish to start or expand shellfish operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of substrate (e.g., shell), seed or larvae, and capital equipment with a 15-year life expectancy. On-bottom and water column aquaculture projects (cages or floats) are eligible. Eligible expenses also include advertising, workboat expenses, vehicle expenses, labor, insurance, equipment, repairs, freight, utilities, consultants, consumable equipment, storage, and spat & shell costs. Motor vehicles including boats and trucks are NOT eligible for capital equipment financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland (Chesapeake and Coastal Bays); applicants must hold or have applied for a State submerged land or water column aquaculture lease from DNR
requirements_list: Must hold a shellfish aquaculture lease from DNR or have applied for one
Must demonstrate that proposed shellfish aquaculture production will begin within 12 months of lease approval
Must have a production and business plan demonstrating financial feasibility
Credit bureau score of at least 620; no bankruptcy within the last seven years (a qualifying co-signer required if score is below 620)
At least 10% equity contribution of the loan amount required
Must indicate where shell or substrate will be purchased
Priority given to applicants who have received less than $100,000 in prior MARBIDCO shellfish funding
Cannot 'double-dip' — cannot receive both MARBIDCO principal forgiveness grant AND NRCS grant for the same project activity
Project must be completed before NRCS grant funds are received by borrower
Persons holding State water column leases are also eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form (available on the MARBIDCO website). Submit a completed and signed original application with all required attachments — including the project financing submission checklist — to MARBIDCO Loan Programs Office, Attn: Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email to brawlings@marbidco.org. Loans are processed in the order received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps beginning urban farmers access financing to develop their urban agricultural enterprises. MARBIDCO provides a grant incentive to applicants who have secured a commercial loan, covering up to 25% of total project costs and no more than 33% of the approved commercial loan amount. The program is administered by MARBIDCO in partnership with Horizon Farm Credit, and operates on an ongoing basis to support urban agriculture commercial activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $1,000 to $15,000 for equipment and working capital, or up to $35,000 for real property purchase. The grant cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost or 33% of the approved commercial loan. A commercial lender must have already approved a loan for the project before a grant is awarded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Beginning urban farmers — individuals or incorporated businesses whose principal operator(s) have 10 or fewer years of commercial farming experience or limited financial resources (net worth under $300,000), operating a commercial food/fiber growing operation in an urban area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of real estate, agricultural inputs and supplies (seeds, fertilizer, compost, baskets), farm tools and equipment, greenhouses, high tunnels, refrigeration, irrigation systems, and hired labor (up to 20% of total eligible project cost).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farming operation must be located in an urban area as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Principal operator must have 10 or fewer years of commercial farming experience or net worth under $300,000
Must operate a commercial food/fiber growing operation in an urban area or incorporated municipality in Maryland
Must have an approved commercial loan or Farm Service Agency loan for the proposed project before a grant is awarded
Grant amount cannot exceed 25% of total project cost
Grant amount cannot exceed 33% of the approved commercial loan
Minimum commercial loan of $3,000 required (to support the minimum $1,000 grant)

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO offers affordable loans to help Maryland landowners establish or expand vineyards, orchards, and hop yards. The program aims to increase the acreage of viable commercial vineyards, orchards, and hop yards in Maryland. MARBIDCO provides low-cost financing in conjunction with a private commercial lender. Interest-only payment options are available for the first two to three years depending on the rate option selected.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $15,000 to $100,000 (minimum updated from application form). Maximum loan term of 10 years. Two interest rate options: (1) Adjustable rate at 5.00% for the first three years, then 6.25% for the remainder; or (2) Fixed rate at 6.25% with the option to make interest-only payments for the first three years. A 0.25% interest rate reduction (Home Town Heroes incentive) is available for U.S. military veterans who hold at least 50% ownership and management control. Loan origination fee is 1% of the loan amount. Equity requirement is typically 10% of total project cost (grant funds may qualify). A commercial lender must participate by providing a letter of referral. Personal guarantees are required from owners. MARBIDCO makes and services all loans, which must be fully collateralized.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland rural landowners and business entities (including proprietorships) seeking to establish or expand commercial vineyards, hop yards, or tree fruit orchards, including those wanting to develop wineries. U.S. military veterans with at least 50% ownership and management control are eligible for an interest rate reduction incentive.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preparation for plant installation, purchase of vines or trees, and related equipment and supplies for new vineyard, tree fruit orchard, or hop yard installation. Tractors, pickup trucks, and winemaking equipment are not eligible under this program (refer to MRBIFF or the Agribusiness Equipment & Working Capital Loan Fund instead).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. An additional equity incentive grant is available for farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through a partnership with the Upper Shore Regional Council.
requirements_list: Must be establishing or expanding a vineyard, orchard, or hop yard in Maryland
A commercial lender must participate and provide a letter of referral
Equity contribution of typically 10% of total project cost (grant funds may qualify)
Loan must be fully collateralized
Personal guarantees required from owners of the business entity
Eligible expenses must relate to installation of new vineyards, tree fruit orchards, or hop yards
Applicants must complete detailed financial disclosure including income, expenses, and debt schedules as part of the loan application
Maximum loan term is 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The applicant must originate all applications. Cooperative extension agents, Maryland Forest Service, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may assist with the application. Applicants must complete detailed financial disclosure forms including farm/business income, expenses, and existing debt schedules. Submit completed applications to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or by email to info@marbidco.org. Applications are reviewed as received and typically take 3–4 weeks to process. Each application is reviewed for financial viability by a panel of agricultural lenders and for operational and viticultural viability by wine/grape industry experts.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO's Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program provides low-interest, unsecured microloans to licensed commercial watermen (both generational and beginner) and seafood processing businesses in Maryland to help them purchase necessary equipment, commercial fishing boats, or seafood processing equipment. The program includes a loan forgiveness component for borrowers who make all payments on time. Purchased equipment must have a useful life of at least 7 years. Beginning July 1, 2025, Beginner Watermen and seafood processors are also eligible in addition to Generational Watermen.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, unsecured microloans at a fixed 3.00% interest rate. Equipment loans range from $7,000 to $20,000; workboat loans up to $30,000; combined workboat and equipment loans up to $40,000. The lifetime aggregate limit is $40,000. Repayments include at least a 6-month interest-only period followed by quarterly amortizing payments over 4–6 years depending on loan amount. Partial loan forgiveness (approximately the final 25% of payments, estimated at $1,871–$10,964 depending on loan size) is available to borrowers who make all payments on time. No collateral required. Commercial watermen may purchase boats, motors, harvesting tools, or other equipment; seafood processors may only purchase seafood processing machinery. All purchased equipment must have a useful life of at least 7 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed commercial watermen (Generational and Beginner categories) who are Maryland residents, and seafood processing businesses holding appropriate licenses from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources or the Potomac River Fisheries Commission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of tangible equipment (boats, motors, harvesting gear) for commercial watermen, or seafood processing machinery for seafood processors. Equipment must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of Maryland. Applicants must hold either a Tidal Fishing License (TFL) issued by the Department of Natural Resources or a commercial license to catch finfish, crabs, clams, and oysters issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions beyond state residency. Program is available statewide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides down-payment funding assistance to young, beginning, or first-time farmers purchasing agricultural farmland. MARBIDCO serves as a conduit financing agent, working cooperatively with commercial or farm credit lenders and county farmland conservation programs. MARBIDCO provides down payment assistance equal to 51% of the land-only fair market value appraisal of the farm property (capped at $500,000). During the purchase process, development rights on the acquired farmland are temporarily extinguished, with the goal of permanent land preservation. After settlement, buyers must enroll in the applicable County Agricultural District and actively pursue a permanent easement within seven years; if no permanent easement is obtained, MARBIDCO places a permanent easement on the property. Applications are reviewed on a competitive basis by a Review Committee that makes recommendations to the MARBIDCO Board of Directors. The program is administered statewide, with Washington County applications processed through the County's Land Preservation Office. In Washington County, properties must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Acreage Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (SANG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The SANG Program helps qualified beginning or first-time farmers purchase small farmland properties between 10 and 49 acres. MARBIDCO provides 30% to 60% of the Fair Market Value (land only) in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement, and those funds are used as a down payment to purchase the farmland. The program addresses barriers to entering agriculture, including high farmland costs and limited access to financial capital. The property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of settlement — there is no separate seven-year easement pursuit requirement. The program is designed to fill a gap left by the original Next Gen Program, which typically requires properties of at least 50 acres or contiguous with preserved property. MARBIDCO serves as a conduit financing agent working with other State and local government agencies and/or private land trust organizations. A commercial or farm credit lender must also be involved in the transaction, and most approved purchases are completed in 6 to 8 months. Applications are reviewed on a competitive basis. In Washington County, properties qualifying for the County Agricultural District program are permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of settlement. Properties in designated Priority Preservation Areas or Rural Legacy Areas receive bonus points in competitive scoring. The program will continue to be offered as long as available funding permits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Revolving Loan Fund for Agricultural & Shellfish Aquaculture Producers
structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized low-cost loan program for farmers and shellfish aquaculture producers in Southern Maryland. Designed to help applicants with projects that may not qualify for traditional commercial financing, the program supports livestock, shellfish aquaculture, small fruits and hops production, produce safety upgrades, equine farm development, and on-farm value-added production. Borrowers in good standing receive a partial loan forgiveness of approximately 20–25% at the end of the loan term by having the final one-quarter of amortizing loan payments forgiven.

Personal guarantee required for business entity borrowers. Minimum credit score of 620. Borrowers in good standing have approximately 20–25% of the loan amount forgiven at the end of the term.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) provides free assistive technology (AT) services to help people with disabilities live, work, and learn more independently. Services include: (1) Consultations — in-person or virtual meetings with staff to discuss needs and explore AT options; (2) Demonstrations — hands-on or virtual trials of equipment so consumers can compare devices and find what works best for them; and (3) Device Loans — borrow AT devices free of charge for up to 4 weeks, available for pickup or shipped directly with virtual setup and instructional support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Auto Program (CAP) is Maryland's Adapted Vehicle Access Pilot Program, operating from October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2030. CAP facilitates the donation of working, adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities who need adapted vehicles but do not qualify for other programs or financing to purchase them. The program also covers vehicle modification and adaptation services as needed.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: CAP facilitates the donation of working, adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities. Recipients receive a donated adapted vehicle at no cost. The program also covers vehicle modification and adaptation services as needed. Funding sources include vehicle donations, vehicle modification and adaptation services funds, and federal grants.

requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability who uses a mobility aid
Must be the vehicle's primary driver
Must possess a valid driver's license with appropriate adaptation restrictions OR a current (within last 12 months) prescription for vehicle modifications
Must not qualify for other existing Department adapted vehicle programs

Must have been turned down for a financial loan through the AT Financial Loan Program within the MD Department of Disabilities, OR voluntarily self-disqualify by not applying to the AT Financial Loan Program
Priority given to individuals residing in areas with limited access to public transportation

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) offers free one-on-one consulting services to prospective and current business owners, as well as new and aspiring entrepreneurs. A business consultant assesses the client's needs, helps develop a business plan, assists with marketing plan development, financial projections, legal structure guidance, credit and collateral review, and loan application assistance, and helps secure additional support needed to start or grow a business. Sessions cover business idea assessment, feasibility review, business plan development, marketing plan assistance, financial projections, legal structure guidance, credit and collateral review, and small business loan application assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one consulting sessions covering business start-up and expansion topics including needs assessment, business plan development, marketing plan assistance, financial projections, credit and collateral review, legal structure guidance, and small business loan application guidance. Consultants also help clients secure additional assistance needed to start or grow a business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prospective business owners, current business owners looking to expand, and new and aspiring entrepreneurs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a free consulting service, not a cash award. Services include business plan development, needs assessment, marketing planning, financial projections, legal structure guidance, and securing additional assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland entrepreneurs statewide, with particular emphasis on Eastern Shore counties including Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Caroline, Queen Anne's, Kent, and Cecil.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Capital Enterprises to schedule a one-on-one consulting session. Call MCE to make an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides small business loans to for-profit business owners located in MCE's service area. Loans range from $5,000 to $50,000 and can be used for business expansion needs such as opening a new location, purchasing equipment, buying vehicles, or covering working capital. Borrowers must demonstrate the ability to repay and have reasonable credit history.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $5,000 to $50,000 with repayment terms up to 10 years. Interest rates range from 6% to 12%. Fees include a 1% closing fee, a legal reserve fee ($250–$1,500), a $100 non-refundable application fee, and a $25 credit report fee per applicant. No prepayment penalties. Security (collateral) may be required up to the full loan amount. Collateral types accepted include business assets, personal guarantees, equipment, vehicles, real estate, or life insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small business owners with 10 or fewer employees located in MCE's service area (Maryland's Eastern Shore counties of Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Caroline, Queen Anne's, and Kent, plus Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Harford, and Calvert counties) who have been turned down by traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Opening a new business location, purchasing machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies/materials/inventory, working capital, or buying a vehicle for the business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses in MCE's service area: Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Caroline, Queen Anne's, and Kent counties (Eastern Shore), plus Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Harford, and Calvert counties.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit business with 10 or fewer employees
Must have attempted to obtain a loan from a traditional lender or bank
Must be located within MCE's service area
Must have a clearly established business idea and business plan
Must demonstrate the ability to create full-time and/or part-time employment for low-to-moderate income residents
Must be a U.S. citizen or legal alien
Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Must have reasonable credit history and payment records
Must be 2+ years in business (with 2 years of tax returns) to qualify for higher loan amounts
Business entity must be a sole proprietor, partnership, corporation, or LLC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule an appointment with an MCE Loan Officer before submitting an application. The Loan Officer will review required paperwork, help prepare the Loan Application Packet, and present it to the Loan Committee for approval. The Loan Committee meets on a scheduled basis and issues decisions on the meeting day. Closing takes place 2–4 weeks after approval once all liens and title searches are completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides small business microloans ranging from $500 to $5,000 to micro businesses and entrepreneurs in select Maryland counties. The program helps small businesses avoid high-interest credit cards for business expenses and improve their credit rating by offering affordable financing to businesses that have been unable to obtain financing through traditional lenders or banks. Loans are typically unsecured and can be used for machinery, equipment, inventory, working capital, and other business needs. The program includes mandatory financial counseling and periodic site visits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $500 to $2,500 carry a 12–18 month term; loans from $2,501 to $5,000 carry a 12–36 month term. Interest rates vary based on risk and loan amount. Fees include a $50 non-refundable application fee, a $25 non-refundable credit report fee per applicant, and a $50 closing/underwriting fee. Collateral may be required up to the full loan amount. Automatic monthly debit is required; opting out results in a 2% higher interest rate. MCE conducts semi-annual site visits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Micro businesses with 10 or fewer employees organized as for-profit entities (sole proprietorships, partnerships, or corporations), located in Maryland's Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester) or Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County, that have tried but been unable to obtain financing from a traditional lender or bank.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies, materials and inventory, working capital, and vehicle (truck or car) purchases for the business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses in the 8 counties of Maryland's Eastern Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester) as well as Baltimore County, Baltimore City, and Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a legally organized for-profit entity (sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation)
Must be a micro business with 10 or fewer employees
Must have tried to obtain a loan through a traditional lender or bank
Must be located in the 8 Eastern Shore counties or Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County
Must create full-time or part-time employment for low-to-moderate income residents
Must be a U.S. citizen or legal alien
Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan with documentable income
Must have a reasonable credit history and payment track record (positive history of 12 months or longer may be required)
Must agree to financial business counseling before and after loan closing
Must agree to periodic staff visits to assess business function and progress
Must agree to periodic credit checks at MCE's expense
All contractors used with loan funds must be licensed
Must provide a voided business check for loan approval
Must provide collateral sufficient to support the loan amount
$50 non-refundable application fee required
$25 non-refundable credit report fee per applicant
$50 closing fee for underwriting
Borrower must specify intended use of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online loan application with general business and personal information, employment details, a description of the use of loan proceeds, and business references. Provide required documentation including photo ID, voided business check, and collateral information. A $50 non-refundable application fee and $25 non-refundable credit report fee are required. Applications are reviewed by the Loan Committee on a case-by-case basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides small business loans (microloans) to for-profit micro businesses on Maryland's Eastern Shore and in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, and Anne Arundel County. Loans range from $5,000 to $100,000 and can be used for equipment, supplies, inventory, working capital, and vehicle purchases. Borrowers receive business counseling before and after loan closing and are subject to periodic site visits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $5,000–$35,000 (new businesses) or $35,001–$100,000 (expansion), with terms up to 10 years and interest rates starting at 6% (set by loan committee based on business plan, credit history, and collateral). Upfront costs include a $100 application fee and $25 credit report fee. Closing fees include a 1% underwriting fee and a legal reserve fee ranging from $250 to $1,500 depending on loan amount. Automatic monthly debit is required; opting out adds 2% to the interest rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit micro businesses with 10 or fewer employees located in Maryland's Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester) or in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County that have tried and been unable to obtain financing from a traditional lender or bank.

Must be a micro business with 10 or fewer employees
Must have tried to obtain a loan through a traditional lender or bank and been unable to do so
Must be located in one of the eligible Maryland counties
Must create full-time or part-time employment for low-to-moderate income residents

Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan with documentable income

Must agree to periodic staff visits to assess business function and progress
Must agree to periodic credit checks at MCE's expense
Must provide a voided business check for loan approval
All contractors used with loan funds must be licensed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online loan application with required documents including a business plan, cash flow projections for 2 years, personal federal tax returns for 2 years, and other financial documents. Pay the $100 application fee and $25 credit report fee. The Loan Committee reviews the application and may adjust terms or amounts. Upon approval, borrowers receive a detailed list of closing fees and must sign a loan agreement with personal guarantee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Capital Enterprises Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides micro-loans and small business loans to entrepreneurs and small business owners in Maryland who cannot access traditional lending sources. MCE offers micro-loans up to $35,000 and small business loans up to $50,000 to help start or expand small and micro businesses. MCE also offers Credit Builder and Emergency Loans for individuals needing to build credit or address urgent financial needs. MCE is a nonprofit micro-lender certified as an SBA, USDA, and CDFI Intermediary Lender. Applications are reviewed in-house and may include credit counseling if needed. MCE also provides counseling and training support alongside lending. MCE has a historical focus on the Eastern Shore region but serves Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Micro-loans up to $35,000 and small business loans up to $50,000 are available to eligible entrepreneurs and small business owners. MCE also offers Credit Builder and Emergency Loans for individuals needing to build credit or address urgent financial needs. Loans are targeted at businesses with fewer than 10 employees that lack access to traditional credit. Applicants must provide a full loan packet including a business plan, cash flow projections, tax returns, bank statements, and proof of denial from a traditional lender (for business loans). A non-refundable application fee is required. Loans are reviewed in-house for approval or denial; applicants may receive credit counseling if needed. MCE also provides counseling and training support alongside lending.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed individuals, low-income entrepreneurs, start-ups, and small business owners who have been denied traditional financing or lack collateral and credit history, as well as individuals seeking credit-building or emergency loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing equipment, working capital, business expansion, starting a new business, credit building, or emergency financial needs. May also cover startup costs, inventory, and personnel costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a historical focus on the Eastern Shore region including Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Caroline, Queen Anne's, Kent, and Cecil counties.

Provide 3 months of business bank statements (existing businesses)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Client Intake Form online, then assemble and submit the full loan application packet including all required documents such as business plan, tax returns, cash flow projections (years 1–3), personal financial statement, legal documents/licenses, and supporting materials. Contact Maryland Capital Enterprises to inquire about loan eligibility and application steps, or call MCE to make an appointment. The application is reviewed in-house; a credit report may be ordered. Applicants may receive credit counseling if needed. Approval or denial is determined by MCE.
