structured_extraction.program_description: The Bridge Finance Facility (BFF) is a short-term bridge loan program administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA). It provides financing to solar developers and project owners to cover pre-construction and early-construction costs for community solar and affordable multifamily solar projects that benefit low- and moderate-income (LMI) households across Maryland. The program addresses critical financing gaps for early-stage costs that commercial lenders typically will not finance — such as interconnection applications and deposits, engineering and design, permitting, and equipment deposits. It focuses on community solar projects (front of the meter, up to 2 MW AC) and affordable multifamily housing projects (behind the meter), with solar-plus-storage projects also eligible. At least 51% of project benefits must serve households at or below 150% of the Area Median Income, and projects must deliver more than 50% of total benefits directly to LMI households to reduce their energy burdens by at least 20%, consistent with SEIF requirements. The program is funded by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term bridge loans ranging from $500,000 to $1,000,000 (preference), with a maximum of $1,500,000 per developer across all accepted projects. Maximum initial interest rate of 7%, with the final rate fixed at approval based on SOFR plus a risk/impact spread. No additional origination or legal fees. Repayment is interest-only during the term with principal due at maturity. Preferred loan term is 12 months with an optional 6-month extension. Loans are disbursed in a single draw based on approved uses, documentation, and project milestones. Collateral includes a first-priority UCC lien and/or guaranty. Loans must be repaid before construction financing or any other capital that would require a lien on the same project assets. Eligible borrowers include corporate entities, special purpose entities (SPEs), nonprofits, and multifamily housing cooperatives that own or control Maryland-sited solar PV project assets.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 13, 2026 (Round 1 intake period: February 3–13, 2026; the first round has ended)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private and nonprofit solar developers, project special purpose entities (SPEs), affordable housing owners or affiliates, and mission-driven organizations developing Maryland-sited solar or solar-plus-storage projects that serve low- and moderate-income households. Out-of-state developers are eligible if the project is located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include utility interconnection application fees, studies, and deposits; engineering and system design; permitting and related fees; equipment deposits and procurement; EPC contractor mobilization; site preparation; and initial construction and commissioning-related costs, including early equipment procurement once construction financing is identified. Loan proceeds may not be used for long-term operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Solar PV projects must be sited in Maryland. Applicants may be based outside Maryland. All 24 Maryland jurisdictions (all 23 counties and Baltimore City) are covered under the statewide program.
requirements_list: Project must be a solar PV project sited in Maryland
Project size must be up to 2 MW AC (community solar) or behind the meter (affordable multifamily housing)
Project must be a community solar project (front of the meter) or affordable multifamily housing solar installation (rooftop or carport, behind the meter)
Solar-plus-storage projects are eligible; battery storage is not required
At least 51% of project energy or financial benefits must serve households at or below 150% of the applicable Area Median Income
Project must deliver more than 50% of total benefits directly to LMI households to reduce their energy burdens by at least 20%, consistent with SEIF requirements
Applicant must demonstrate site control or a credible path to site control (lease, option, or letter of intent)
Applicant must demonstrate a credible path to takeout financing (grants, construction financing, permanent debt, tax equity, sponsor equity, or other capital) to repay the BFF loan
Projects must be approved by the MCEC Board of Directors
Applicants with multiple projects must submit one application per project
If multiple projects from one sponsor are accepted, MCEC will consolidate into a single BFF loan
Each project SPE should apply separately; the borrowing entity should be the one that will assume the BFF loan
Organizations applying via project SPE must provide controlling entity's audited financials and tax returns
All required documents must be uploaded to OneHub after submitting the intake application
Borrowers must provide quarterly reporting during the loan term and a final Project Closeout report upon repayment
Must be a solar photovoltaic project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the BFF Intake online application during the open intake window (Round 1: February 3–13, 2026). 2. Upon successful submission, MCEC sends a link to upload required attachments to OneHub. Required documents include site control documentation, interconnection status evidence, project site map, construction timeline, subscriber acquisition plan (community solar only), evidence of affordable housing status (multifamily), two years of business tax returns, three years of financial statements, preliminary EPC budget, project-level pro forma, borrower financial projections, capital stack summary, sources and uses, and corporate documents. 3. MCEC conducts eligibility and risk/impact screening, and may request additional information. 4. Selected projects undergo due diligence and underwriting. 5. Projects proceed through review and approval, including MCEC Board of Directors approval. 6. Legal documentation is finalized and executed. 7. Following closing, borrowers request funds via an agreed draw structure. 8. Borrowers repay principal and interest per agreed terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: C3 Climate Catalytic Capital Fund – Investment Window 3 (IW3): Project Feasibility Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Investment Window 3 (IW3) provides grant funding for early-stage pre-development work that turns a clean energy concept into a financeable project. Many clean energy projects never reach the financing stage because feasibility analysis, engineering studies, design, financial modeling, and permitting are too costly to fund out of pocket. IW3 fills that gap by funding work that produces a clear answer about whether and how a project will move forward.

The program is designed to make energy upgrades more accessible for Maryland households by combining flexible loan terms with utility rebate programs, helping homeowners reduce energy bills and improve home comfort.

structured_extraction.program_description: The C3 Fund (Climate Catalytic Capital Fund) is a dedicated investment fund administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) that provides financing and grants to support clean energy technology development and deployment across Maryland. Established under the Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022 with a $15 million allocation over three fiscal years beginning in FY24 (with an additional $23.75M approved for future cycles), the fund aims to leverage private capital, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and advance energy equity. At least 40% of fund awards each fiscal year must benefit low-to-moderate income communities. The fund operates through three investment windows: (1) IW1 – short-term bridge loans for geothermal, community solar, and resiliency hub project developers; (2) IW2 – revolving lines of credit for solar developers and installers; and (3) IW3 – project feasibility grants for nonprofits, community organizations, municipalities, affordable multifamily housing owners/developers, and other underserved market actors. All funding decisions are made by the C3 Fund Investment Oversight Committee (IOC). No more than 5% of the fund balance may be used for administrative purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three investment windows are available: IW1 provides short-term bridge loans up to $3,000,000 per developer (up to 12-month term, with possible 6-month extension) for early-stage geothermal, community solar, and resiliency hub projects at a maximum initial interest rate of 7%, with no origination or legal fees. IW2 provides revolving lines of credit up to $1,500,000 per developer (up to 24-month term) for solar developers and installers, also at a maximum initial rate of 7%. IW3 provides project feasibility grants typically ranging from $100,000–$300,000 to nonprofits, community organizations, municipalities, public housing authorities, school districts, affordable multifamily housing owners/developers, and other public/quasi-public entities for early-stage clean energy project work. The fund also supports equity investment through an Equity Investment Fund and capacity building grants through a Capacity Building Program. At least 40% of fund investments must assist low-to-moderate income households and communities. The fund has $15M committed over three fiscal years beginning FY24, with an additional $23.75M approved for future cycles. Funds may not be used to install new fossil fuel equipment or improve efficiency of existing fossil fuel equipment. No more than 5% of the fund balance may be used for administrative purposes.

IW3 feasibility grants: early-stage project development work (feasibility studies, planning) that turns a clean energy concept into a financeable project; not for construction, equipment, or installation costs. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling monthly basis, due by the 15th of each month for an award to be made approximately 60 days thereafter. structured_extraction.program_description: C-PACE provides commercial property owners and nonprofits with up to 100% up-front financing to implement building upgrades that save energy, lower operating costs, and support clean energy goals. Eligible projects include energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy systems (solar, geothermal, wind), water conservation, environmental remediation (indoor air/water quality, asbestos, lead paint, mold), and resiliency projects (flood mitigation, stormwater management, fire/wind resistance, EV charging, energy storage). The loan is repaid over up to 20 years through a long-term surcharge on the state property tax bill that transfers with the sale of the property. Projects can be cash flow positive from day one and add value to the commercial asset.

structured_extraction.program_description:
MEIA is a multi-phase clean energy and climate technology startup accelerator operated by the Maryland Clean Energy Center, implemented in partnership with the NSF Mid-Atlantic Hub I-Corps team at the University of Maryland. It supports and funds inventors, scientists, and startup founders who are building climate technologies with the potential to help Maryland meet its climate goals and grow a new clean energy industry. The program accelerates the commercialization of advanced energy and climate technologies from Maryland's businesses, universities, and labs by connecting climate tech startups with experts, investors, and resources, helping early-stage energy technology founders and inventors become investment-ready.

The program includes multiple phases that participants can join individually or in sequence:

- Pre-Accelerator (Phase 0): A 2-month, part-time training and commercialization readiness program for very early-stage climate-tech researchers, inventors, and entrepreneurs at TRL 1–3 with no prior investment and minimal commercial engagement. Participants work through small workshops covering the entrepreneurial journey, customer discovery, business model development, financing, and commercialization, plus advisory support from a chosen mentor. The program runs virtually with weekly mentor sessions or workshops, plus an in-person graduation ceremony. The Winter 2026 cohort runs January 13 through March 24, 2026.

- Launchpad (Phase 1): Targets technologies at TRL 3–5, providing $10,000 in funding with an opportunity to apply for an additional $5,000, plus hands-on MEIA support, Energy Executive in Residence (EEIR) engagement, and services support over a 6-month timeline. Over 4–6 months, startup teams conduct customer discovery, develop a business model canvas, and create a commercialization plan and investor-ready pitch deck. MEIA recruits two Energy Executives per team to lead commercialization planning.

- Manufacturing Accelerator (Phase 2): Drives growth and scalability for startups at TRL 4–6, providing a $30,000 budget to advance prototyping and manufacturing activities, hands-on direct support from MEIA staff, introductions to funders, assistance obtaining seed or Series A funding, and connections to Maryland's innovation ecosystem. MEIA helps startups build credibility with third-party investors, identify strategic partners, develop a product roadmap, and connect to other Maryland state services.

- Climate Technology Founders Fund (Phase 3): Specifically focuses on empowering Minority, Women, and Veteran-Owned Business (MWVOB) entrepreneurs with critical investments to advance clean energy and decarbonization solutions.

Overall, MEIA runs cohort-based programs and has facilitated over $90 million in funding for 120+ participants and helped create 175+ jobs. A Climate Technology Fund to Support Diverse Founders was also launched in early 2025. Financial support is subject to fund availability and approval by a Fund Oversight Committee; funding is limited and not guaranteed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) operates this initiative to expand the use of woody biomass — organic material from trees such as branches, wood chips, and logging residues — as a renewable thermal energy source in Maryland. Through partnerships with the U.S. Forest Service (via the Wood Innovations Grant), the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service, and the Maryland Wood Energy Team, MCEC identifies facilities that depend heavily on heating oil and are located near forested land suited for active management. The program helps facilities switch from fossil fuels to woody biomass heating systems by providing engineering and analysis services from the USFS Wood Education and Resource Center (WERC), bid-ready designs, wood supply chain development, IMPLAN economic impact analyses, connections to economic development funding programs, and community education and outreach materials. The initiative also conducts educational tours, publishes research reports, assists prospective users with grant applications, and supports education, outreach, and advocacy to raise public awareness about the benefits of biomass energy. The Wood Energy Initiative supply chain analysis covers all Maryland counties across four regions: Central, Eastern, Southern, and Western, with the broader analysis also including adjacent counties in Pennsylvania, Delaware, Virginia, and West Virginia.

The initiative also provides grants and educational resources supporting wood energy systems and economic development. Funding is sourced from the USDA Wood Innovations Grant, the Rural Maryland Council, and the U.S. Forest Service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE / MD-PACE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) program provides commercial property owners, businesses, and nonprofits with 100% up-front private financing to fund energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, resiliency, and environmental remediation improvements with no upfront cost. The loan is structured as a voluntary lien / property tax assessment tied to the property itself, not the owner, and is repaid through annual or semi-annual surcharges on the property tax bill over typical terms of 10 to 30+ years. Because the assessment stays with the property, it transfers to new owners upon sale. Financing is underwritten based on the underlying building rather than the owner's credit rating, making it accessible to property owners with non-investment-grade credit. Projects can be cash flow positive from day one and add value to the commercial asset. Eligible improvements include HVAC systems, water heaters, building envelope upgrades, solar, geothermal, wind, environmental remediation, and resiliency measures, as well as solar energy equipment, geothermal energy devices, wind energy systems, water conservation devices, high efficiency lighting and building systems, high efficiency boilers and furnaces, high efficiency hot water heating systems, combustion and burner upgrades, fuel switching, heat recovery and steam traps, fenestration improvements, and building energy management systems and process equipment upgrades. Eligible property types include office, retail, hospitality, multifamily, senior housing, assisted living, healthcare, faith-based, agricultural, industrial, warehouse, self-storage, nonprofit, and specialty use. Nineteen Maryland counties have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own programs independently — Prince George's County is served by FSC First as Fund Manager (financing limited to up to 20% of appraised property value), while Frederick County, Garrett County, Charles County, and all other eligible counties are served through MD-PACE, managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. In Frederick County, the program is also supported by the Frederick County Office of Economic Development. In Charles County, the program is supported by the Charles County Economic Development Department. Repayment can also be passed through to tenants in applicable buildings.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Clean Energy Center (MD-PACE) / FSC First (Prince George's County) / Frederick County Office of Economic Development / Charles County Economic Development Department
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: C-PACE provides 100% private financing covering eligible project costs with no upfront payment to the property owner. Repayment is made through annual or semi-annual surcharges added to the property's tax bill over typical terms of 10 to 30+ years. Projects typically start at a minimum of $50,000 and commonly range up to $100,000 or more. Financing in Prince George's County is limited to up to 20% of the appraised value of the commercial property. Financing is underwritten based on the underlying building, not the owner's credit rating, and is funded through private capital at no cost to taxpayers. The outstanding assessment balance transfers with property ownership upon sale. Owners may also pass financing costs to tenants where tenants pay the energy bill. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own programs independently; all other eligible Maryland counties (including Garrett County, Frederick County, and Charles County) are served through MD-PACE, managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Loan administration procedures vary by county based on local enabling ordinances.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial, industrial, and nonprofit property owners, builders, businesses, contractors, capital providers, and local governments in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation (including Frederick County, Garrett County, and Charles County), seeking to invest in energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, environmental remediation, or resiliency projects. In Prince George's County, applicants must be 100% legal owner as recorded on title; government-owned properties are not eligible under that county's program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades (lighting, HVAC, chillers, boilers, building envelope, fenestration, energy management systems); renewable energy systems (solar PV, wind, geothermal); environmental remediation (asbestos, mold, lead paint and pipe replacement, indoor air/water quality); water efficiency and conservation improvements (including water conservation devices not required by law); resiliency measures (stormwater management, flood mitigation, hurricane shutters, fire/wind resistance, EV charging stations, energy storage); construction, renovation, or retrofitting to reduce energy consumption; process equipment upgrades; fuel switching; heat recovery and steam traps; combustion and burner upgrades; capital-intensive building retrofit and new construction improvements; and all associated project costs including audits, design, installation, and loan closing costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in the 19 Maryland counties that have adopted C-PACE enabling legislation through an ordinance. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own programs independently. Prince George's County is served by FSC First as Fund Manager, with financing limited to up to 20% of the appraised value of the commercial property. Frederick County, Garrett County, Charles County, and all other eligible counties are served through MD-PACE, managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center, which requires counties to sign a Locality Agreement. In Frederick County, the program is additionally supported by the Frederick County Office of Economic Development. In Charles County, the program is supported by the Charles County Economic Development Department. Procedures vary by participating county based on local enabling ordinances.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners work with private capital providers to arrange C-PACE financing; the county collects repayment through surcharges on the property's tax bill. Property owners in Prince George's County apply through FSC First via the online application portal or by downloading the application, checklist, and program overview document at https://fscfirst.com/learn/programs/commercial-property-assessment-for-clean-energy. Property owners in Frederick County may contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development at 301-600-1058, or apply through MD-PACE at the Maryland Clean Energy Center website. Property owners in Charles County may contact the Charles County Economic Development Department at 301-885-1344 or explore eligibility at md-pace.com. Jurisdictions must first adopt enabling legislation and sign a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center before C-PACE can be used in that area. structured_extraction.program_name: Climate Technology Founders Fund (CTFF) — MEIA Phase 3
structured_extraction.program_description: The Climate Technology Founders Fund (CTFF), established under Maryland Senate Bill 0960 as Phase 3 of the Maryland Energy Innovation Accelerator (MEIA), is an equity investment fund launched by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. It invests directly into Maryland-based climate tech startup teams that have proven their technology and are ready to raise capital. The fund provides direct equity investment of $50,000–$100,000 per team and can lead investment rounds for other investors by setting deal documents and conducting due diligence. A matching requirement applies — founders must raise external capital or invest personal funds. The fund supports a diverse range of founders and prioritizes small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses whose core mission is developing solutions to combat climate change, including the development and deployment of emission-reducing technology projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) Annual Request for Applications (RFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) awards competitive grants approximately once a year through an annual Request for Applications (RFA) / Call for Proposals process. Grants expand access to affordable, high-quality health care services in underserved areas of Maryland. The FY 2026 round makes $7 million available. Applicants must address one or both of two strategic priorities: (1) advancing health equity by addressing health disparities and social determinants of health such as food security, transportation, and health insurance coverage through innovative community partnerships; and (2) supporting safety net providers and community-based organizations to align with state initiatives like the ENOUGH initiative and the AHEAD model to reduce avoidable emergency department visits, hospital admissions, and readmissions. Funding is available across six areas of focus: hospital-community partnerships; support for medically vulnerable populations including older adults and people with disabilities; chronic disease prevention and management; maternal and child health; dental health; and behavioral health for adults including mental health and substance use disorder services. Grants also support programs that expand primary care access, reduce infant mortality, increase dental care access, integrate behavioral health treatment, and help safety net providers adopt health information technology. Grant proposals are evaluated by independent subject matter experts on criteria including use of evidence-based practices, ability to collect and report outcomes data, demonstration of community need, program sustainability, and likelihood of overall program success. Since inception, the CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling over $396 million. The program was re-authorized by the Maryland General Assembly in 2024 until June 2035. Award decisions for FY 2026 are expected in late June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded through an annual Request for Applications (RFA) / Call for Proposals process. The FY 2026 round makes $7 million available statewide. Anticipated award range is $300,000–$750,000 total per grant, for up to three years (minimum requests below $300,000 are also allowed). Applicants submit a Letter of Intent followed by a full application package via Smartsheet. Award decisions for FY 2026 are expected in late June 2026. Since inception, the CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling over $396 million. Grant amounts and priority areas vary by cycle and are determined by CHRC Commissioners. Grants support programs serving underserved communities across all Maryland jurisdictions. Indirect costs are capped at 15% of direct costs; personnel/fringe benefits capped at 25%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Full proposals due April 23, 2026 by 3:00 pm EDT; issued approximately once a year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, community-based organizations, safety net providers, health care providers, local health departments, FQHCs, FQHC look-alikes, school-based health centers, outpatient mental health clinics, hospitals, substance use treatment providers, home health agencies, residential service agencies, for-profit entities, and government entities seeking to address health care access barriers and health disparities in underserved areas of Maryland, including those focused on primary care, dental care, behavioral health, infant mortality reduction, and health information technology adoption.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports community health programs addressing health disparities and social determinants of health (food security, transportation, health insurance coverage), safety net provider capacity building, hospital-community partnerships, chronic disease prevention and management, maternal and child health, dental health, behavioral health services including mental health and substance use disorder, primary care expansion, infant mortality reduction, reduction of avoidable emergency department visits and hospital admissions, and health information technology adoption among safety net providers. Eligible costs include personnel (W-2 salaries), fringe benefits (up to 25%), supplies, travel, trainings, contractual services, furniture, IT/telecom, minor infrastructure, marketing, and indirect costs (up to 15% of direct costs). Funds may not be used for major equipment purchase/lease, construction, clinical trials, non-FDA-approved medical devices/drugs, lobbying, political activity, or activities duplicating other funded sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland jurisdictions, with priority given to underserved areas of the state. Applicants must offer services primarily to Maryland residents from service sites located in Maryland. Applicants serving census tracts eligible under the ENOUGH initiative receive 5 additional scoring points. Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore are noted as priority areas for oral health workforce needs. The ENOUGH initiative targets 116 high-need census tracts across the state.
requirements_list: Must address at least one of the two strategic priorities (health equity/SDOH or safety net capacity building)
Must apply in one or more of the six areas of focus
Letter of Intent required by March 30, 2026 at 3:00 PM EDT via Smartsheet
Applicants must be notified of eligibility by CHRC staff after LOI submission
Full application due April 23, 2026 by 3:00 pm EDT via Smartsheet

Must submit mandatory documents: Transmittal Letter, Grant Application Cover Sheet, Executive Summary and Full Project Proposal, Contractual Obligations/Assurances/Certifications, IRS Form W-9, Legal and Financial Disclosure, Budget Form Template, Budget Narrative Template, and required appendices

Required appendices include: list of officers/board, organizational chart, overall organization budget, resumes of key personnel, letters of commitment from collaborators or MOUs, logic model, and workplan template
Must provide most recent IRS Form 990 or Business Tax Return
Must provide audited financial statements or most recent financial audit
Must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation dated within one year of submission due date
Must qualify as a 'community health resource' per COMAR 10.45.05
Must maintain a sliding fee scale or offer free services per COMAR 10.45.05.05
Organization must have existed prior to LOI submission and sliding fee scale must be posted publicly
Applicants must propose use of evidence-based practices
Program must be able to collect and report outcomes data
Proposal must demonstrate a community need
Program must demonstrate a plan for sustainability after initial grant funds are used
Proposal must show likelihood of overall program success
Must disclose all other funding sources (state, federal, local, private grants; Medicaid, Medicare, HSCRC)
CHRC funds must supplement, not supplant, other funding sources
Must comply with non-discrimination requirements (race, creed, color, sex, national origin, and other protected classes per state/federal law)
Must comply with ADA requirements
Must certify compliance with Environmental Tobacco Smoke requirements (Pro-Children Act of 1994, P.L. 103-227)
Must be in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have no overdue debts, liabilities, claims, judgments, or penalties
Must comply with Maryland Solicitations Act (Business Regulation Article, Title 6)
If charitable organization, must be registered with Maryland Secretary of State per §6-401 and §6-408
All application materials become Commission property upon submission
All information submitted must be true, correct, and not misleading
Must disclose outstanding and settled litigation, judgments, and regulatory compliance status
Must disclose state/federal tax liabilities and other financial liabilities

Work plan must include measurable goals (1–5 years), objectives, key activities/action steps, expected outcomes (targets), data evaluation and measurement methods, baseline data/data sources, responsible persons/groups, timetable for achievement, and alignment with CHRC priorities
Must track and report unduplicated individuals served using standard metrics
Multiple proposals permitted if projects are wholly different
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The CHRC issues an annual Request for Applications (RFA) / Call for Proposals approximately once a year. For the FY 2026 round: review RFA documents and key dates, then attend the FAQ webinar held March 19, 2026. Submit a Letter of Intent by March 30, 2026 at 3:00 PM EDT via Smartsheet. Receive eligibility confirmation from CHRC staff. Submit a full application package including all mandatory documents by April 23, 2026 at 3:00 pm EDT via the Smartsheet portal. Proposals are evaluated competitively by independent subject matter experts using criteria outlined in each Call for Proposals (100-point scale: strategic priorities 15 pts, project feasibility 20 pts, budget reasonableness 5 pts, community need & partnerships 20 pts, plus 5 bonus points for proposals serving ENOUGH initiative census tracts). Priority areas and review criteria are set by CHRC Commissioners. Applicants are notified about the status of their grant applications in early June 2026. Award decisions are expected in late June 2026. Prospective applicants can join the CHRC mailing list to receive updates on new Calls for Proposals. Full information is available on the CHRC notices page. Contact Mark Luckner (mark.luckner@maryland.gov) or Jen Clatterbuck (jen.clatterbuck@maryland.gov) with questions. CHRC mailing address: 45 Calvert Street, Room 336, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Health Equity Resource Communities (HERC) program provides grant funding and state resources to local community organizations to address health disparities, improve health outcomes, expand access to primary care and prevention services, and help reduce health care costs. Established under the Maryland Health Equity Resource Act (2021) and implemented by the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC), the program awards 5-year grants to organizations implementing clinical interventions and social determinants of health (SDOH) support for marginalized populations. Twelve grantees are currently implementing programs over the period July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2029, with a total funding pool of $41,550,000 across 12 awards. Focus areas include cardiovascular disease, diabetes, mental health, social isolation, maternal and child health, substance use disorder, obesity, childhood vaccination, and elder care. Programs are currently open for enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-year (5-year) grants awarded to community organizations to implement programs addressing health disparities. The current implementation period runs from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2029. Twelve grantees were awarded in the most recent cycle with a total funding pool of $41,550,000 (grant amounts vary by recipient; e.g., one grantee received $5 million). Programs provide free clinical services and social services support (transportation, food assistance, housing, etc.). All 12 sub-programs state 'no one will be turned away' (universal access). Grantees serve specific Maryland regions including Baltimore City, St. Mary's County, Wicomico County, Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, Somerset County, Talbot County, Allegany and Garrett Counties, and Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, faith-based organizations, academic institutions, hospital systems, federally qualified health centers, county health departments, and health care organizations serving marginalized populations in Maryland, including low-income residents, racial/ethnic minorities, and homeless populations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clinical interventions and social determinants of health support for marginalized populations; includes free clinical services, care coordination, health screening, chronic disease management, maternal/infant health, mental health/substance use services, and SDOH support (transportation, food assistance, housing); focus areas include cardiovascular disease, diabetes, mental health, social isolation, maternal and child health, substance use disorder, obesity, childhood vaccination, and elder care
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Current grantees serve specific regions: Baltimore City (University of Maryland School of Nursing serving West Baltimore and North Avenue corridors; Greater Baltimore Medical Center; Health Care for the Homeless focusing on Black/African American and Latina/Latinx women experiencing homelessness; MedStar Harbor Hospital serving South Baltimore); St. Mary's County/Southern Maryland (St. Mary's County Health Department); Wicomico County/Lower Eastern Shore (TidalHealth REACH serving African American and Haitian communities); Montgomery and Prince George's Counties (Interfaith Works; Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine/Sickle Cell); Somerset County/Lower Eastern Shore (Somerset County Health Department); Talbot County/Eastern Shore (Talbot County Health Department & EMS serving rural Hispanic women, children, and older Black adults); Allegany and Garrett Counties/Western Maryland (AHEC West serving rural/remote communities); Washington County (Community Free Clinic). Programs collectively address Maryland residents statewide across urban, rural, and Eastern Shore locations.
requirements_list: Must serve marginalized populations experiencing health disparities
Programs must address health disparities and improve health outcomes
Must provide clinical interventions and/or social determinants of health (SDOH) support
Organizations must focus on clinical interventions and/or social determinants of health (SDOH) support for marginalized populations
No one will be turned away (universal access language applies to all 12 sub-programs)

Eligible organization types include community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, academic institutions, hospital systems, federally qualified health centers, and county health departments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed and awarded by the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) with assistance from the HERC Advisory Committee, the Maryland Department of Health's Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, and CRISP. The CHRC Commissioners approved twelve HERC grant awards for the 2024–2029 cycle totaling $41,550,000. Contact the CHRC or visit the program page for enrollment information. A PDF with enrollment information and program service descriptions is available via the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland residents who are 65 or older, or totally disabled (or whose spouse is totally disabled), may subtract a portion of their taxable pension and retirement annuity income from their federal adjusted gross income when calculating Maryland state taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible taxpayers may subtract qualifying pension and retirement annuity income from their federal adjusted gross income before calculating Maryland income tax. The exclusion amount and instructions are described in Instruction 13 of the Maryland resident tax booklet. Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs, Keogh Plans, and ineligible deferred compensation plans do not qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 65 or older, or totally disabled individuals (or those with a totally disabled spouse), who receive pension or retirement annuity income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability by excluding qualifying pension and retirement annuity income from federal adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents filing state income taxes.
requirements_list: Must be 65 or older OR totally disabled, OR have a spouse who is totally disabled, on the last day of the tax year
Must have included on your federal return income received as a pension, annuity, or endowment from an employee retirement system
Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs, Keogh Plans, and ineligible deferred compensation plans do not qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Follow Instruction 13 in the Maryland resident tax booklet when filing Maryland state taxes to claim the pension exclusion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Military Retirement Pay Income Tax Deduction
structured_extraction.program_description: Veterans and spouses of military retirees can subtract a portion of their military retirement income from their federal adjusted gross income when calculating Maryland state taxes. Taxpayers aged 55 or older may subtract up to $20,000; taxpayers under 55 may subtract up to $12,500.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible taxpayers may subtract up to $20,000 (age 55+) or $12,500 (under 55) of military retirement income from their federal adjusted gross income before calculating Maryland income tax. The deduction is claimed on Maryland Form 502, Line 13.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans and spouses of military retirees who receive military retirement income and file Maryland state taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability by subtracting qualifying military retirement income from federal adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents filing state income taxes.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran or spouse of a military retiree receiving military retirement income

Retirement income must result from service in the U.S. Armed Forces (active or reserve component), the Maryland National Guard, or separated active-duty employment with the Public Health Service, NOAA, or the Coast and Geodetic Survey
Taxpayers 55 or older may subtract up to $20,000; taxpayers under 55 may subtract up to $12,500
Deduction is claimed on Maryland Form 502, Line 13
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Maryland Form 502 and follow the instructions in the Maryland resident tax booklet for Line 13 to subtract military retirement income.

structured_extraction.program_name: Admissions and Amusement Tax Exemption Program (A&E District)
structured_extraction.program_description: Visual and performing arts enterprises located within a designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District are exempt from collecting the State of Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying arts enterprises are fully exempt from collecting the State of Maryland Admissions and Amusement Tax. Businesses must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA) to be eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Visual and performing arts enterprises located within a designated A&E District in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from collecting the State of Maryland Admissions and Amusement Tax on qualifying events and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within a designated Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Business must be located within an A&E District
Must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA) to qualify for the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: Artists who create and sell work within a designated Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District in Maryland can subtract income derived from art and art enterprises from their Maryland state income taxes. This is an income tax subtraction modification, not a tax credit — qualifying art income is simply not taxed at the state level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying artists subtract art-derived income from Maryland state taxable income by filing Form 502AE with their state income tax return. Federal income taxes still apply in full.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists who own or rent residential property in Maryland, create work in any A&E District, and earn income from the sale or performance of art within any A&E District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability on income derived from art and art enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to artists who create and sell work within any designated Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District in Maryland.
requirements_list: Own or rent residential property within Maryland
Create artistic work in any A&E District
Have generated income from the sale or performance of art within any A&E District
File Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with state income tax return
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Maryland State Tax Form 502AE when filing your state income tax return. Direct questions about eligibility to the Comptroller of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Housing/Healthy Aging Program (formerly Congregate Housing Services Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging contracts with housing and senior service provider organizations — such as local housing authorities, nonprofits, and housing management companies — to operate a Community Housing/Healthy Aging program for eligible residents of designated buildings. The program provides services that help residents live as independently as possible, including meals, housekeeping, medication management, and limited personal assistance with activities like bathing, dressing, and laundry.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Aging awards grants to organizations that operate the program. In FY26, over $1.9 million was awarded to 10 organizations across the state. Grant-funded services are then provided to eligible residents (those aged 62 or older with low or no income who need help with one or more activities of daily living) at no or reduced cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local housing authorities, and housing management companies that serve low-income seniors aged 62 and older in designated housing buildings across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support delivery of supportive services to eligible residents, including meals, housekeeping, medication management, and personal assistance with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, and laundry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Current program sites are located in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Garrett counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a housing authority, nonprofit organization, or housing management company
Program must serve residents of designated buildings
Resident beneficiaries must be at least 62 years of age
Resident beneficiaries must have low or no income
Resident beneficiaries must need assistance with one or more activities of daily living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Aging or your local Maryland Access Point for information on applying. Call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465).

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program operated by the Maryland Department of Aging that collects gently-used durable medical equipment (DME) through donations, sanitizes and refurbishes each item, and provides it at no cost to Maryland residents with any illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age or insurance coverage. The program covers both basic DME (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails) and complex DME (manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, trapeze bars, and other advanced equipment). Equipment is permanently transferred to the recipient, and residents can also donate unused DME back to the program when no longer needed. The program is intended for individuals who have exhausted all other means of obtaining DME, including insurance coverage. For complex equipment, requests must be initiated by a licensed healthcare professional (PT, OT, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP); requests for power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only. A formal prescription is not required — only the completed request form. Equipment is available while supplies last and must be picked up by appointment only at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD (11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623) or at satellite locations statewide including Aberdeen, Baltimore, Cambridge, Centreville, Columbia, Elkton, Hagerstown, Odenton, Rockville, Silver Spring, Towson, Westminster, and Worcester; no delivery is available. Cell phone or tablet photos of forms are not accepted. Healthcare providers may also initiate requests on behalf of patients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free refurbished durable medical equipment provided at no cost to eligible Maryland residents. Basic DME includes canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails. Complex DME includes manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars. Requests for basic DME do not require a formal prescription but must include a section completed by a licensed healthcare professional. Complex DME requests must be initiated by a licensed healthcare professional (PT, OT, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP); requests for power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only. Recipients may keep the equipment as long as needed. Equipment is available while supplies last and must be picked up at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD or at satellite locations statewide; no delivery is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of any age (including children) with any illness, injury, or disability who need durable medical equipment (basic or complex) and have exhausted all other means of obtaining it, including through Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance. No age or insurance requirement. Healthcare providers may also initiate requests on behalf of patients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of durable medical equipment — including mobility aids (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, power chair rollators), bathroom safety equipment (shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails), hospital beds, mechanical lifts, manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars — at no cost to eligible Maryland residents for personal use to support mobility, safety, and independence at home and in their communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Program is available statewide. Equipment pickup at Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD (11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623) or satellite distribution sites including Aberdeen, Baltimore, Cambridge, Centreville, Columbia, Elkton, Hagerstown, Odenton, Rockville, Silver Spring, Towson, Westminster, and Worcester. Baltimore City also operates two donation collection sites at the Northwest Transfer Station (5030 Reisterstown Rd) and the Quarantine Road Landfill (6100 Quarantine Rd).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have an illness, injury, or disability
No age requirement
No insurance requirement
Must have exhausted all other means of obtaining DME, including through Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance (applies to complex DME requests)
For basic DME: complete the Basic DME Request Form; Part C must be completed by a treating healthcare professional (Physician, PT, OT, PA, or CRNP); no formal prescription required
For complex DME: requestor completes Part A of the Complex Request Form; a licensed healthcare professional (Physician, PA, CRNP, PT, or OT) must complete Parts B and C
Requests for power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only
A formal prescription is not required — only the completed request form
Requestor signs a Liability Waiver and Release agreement
Completed request form (all required parts) must be submitted by mail, email (scanned copy), fax, or online via Maryland OneStop
Cell phone or tablet photos of forms are not accepted
Equipment must be picked up by the beneficiary or a designated trusted individual — no delivery available
Equipment pickup is by appointment only and subject to availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Basic DME — Option 1: Apply online via Maryland OneStop (create an account, verify email, and submit the form). Option 2: Download the Basic DME Request Form, complete all required fields in blue or black ink, and submit by mail to Maryland DME Re-Use, 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623, or by scanning and emailing to DME.MDOA@maryland.gov. For Complex DME — Option 1 (Online): Complete the Complex Request Form via Maryland OneStop. Create an account, verify your email, and fill out Part A. The healthcare provider completes Parts B and C either online or via printed hard copy uploaded to OneStop. Option 2 (Hard Copy): Download and print the Complex Request Form. Complete Part A, then pass to a healthcare professional to complete Parts B and C. Submit the completed form by mail, email (scanned), or fax. For all requests: the program contacts the requestor by phone to confirm equipment availability and, if equipment is in stock, schedules a pick-up appointment. To donate equipment, drop off at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham (Mon–Fri, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.) or at Baltimore City collection sites (Northwest Transfer Station or Quarantine Road Landfill, Mon–Sat). You may also contact the Maryland Department of Aging by phone at 240-230-8000 or email at DME.MDOA@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia (ADRD) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging awards grants to non-profit organizations to support home- and community-based services for people living with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and their caregivers. Funded activities include day programs, caregiver training, transportation, companionship services, and intergenerational programming.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nearly $134,000 was awarded in FY24 to six non-profit organizations, with individual grants ranging from approximately $11,500 to $27,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations providing services to individuals with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias and their caregivers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of home- and community-based supportive services, improving coordination of care, and expanding social support opportunities for people with ADRD and their caregivers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization
Programs must support individuals with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and/or their caregivers

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Access Point (MAP) is Maryland's No Wrong Door Aging and Disability Resource Center and a statewide network of local sites that serves as the single entry point for older adults and people with disabilities who need help with long-term care planning and independent living. MAP specialists help individuals, caregivers, and professionals identify, plan, and access public and private resources including health care, transportation, income assistance, financial aid, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, volunteer opportunities, and more. Services include information and assistance, referrals, application assistance, Options Counseling (a free person-centered service where trained counselors work one-on-one to match needs, preferences, and values with community services and develop a personalized action plan), level one screening for waiver programs to evaluate risk of institutionalization, and nursing facility transition counseling. MAP operates through 20 local sites—one in each county and Baltimore City—run by Area Agencies on Aging and Centers for Independent Living.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free information, referrals, application assistance, and options counseling provided by trained specialists at 20 local MAP sites across all Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Services include person-centered Options Counseling to develop personalized care plans, a level one screen to evaluate risk of institutionalization and connect individuals to waiver programs, and nursing facility transition counseling. Specialists connect individuals to long-term services and supports including health care, transportation, income support, financial aid, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, senior and community centers, and volunteer opportunities. Accessible by calling 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465) or visiting marylandaccesspoint.info.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults, people with disabilities, individuals with long-term care needs, caregivers, and professionals seeking long-term care planning and community support resources in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides free counseling, referrals, application assistance, and support navigating community services rather than direct financial assistance. Assistance covers access to health care, transportation, income support, financial aid, senior and community centers, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, volunteer opportunities, and other long-term services and supports.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (all counties and Baltimore City) through local MAP offices operated by Area Agencies on Aging and Centers for Independent Living.
requirements_list: Must be an older adult, person with a disability, individual with long-term care needs, caregiver, or professional seeking long-term care planning or community support resources
Must be located in or seeking services in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465), visit marylandaccesspoint.info, or contact your local county MAP office directly. A 211 Maryland information and referral specialist will assess your needs, identify local resources, and connect individuals with complex needs to their local MAP office for further assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Family Caregiver Support Program (also known as the National Family Caregiver Support Program) provides services and supports to family and informal caregivers who assist older adults and individuals with disabilities living in the community. Administered by the Maryland Department of Aging through local Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) with federal funding from the Administration for Community Living (ACL), the program operates through two categories: Caregivers of Older Adults (for those caring for people 60+ or individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders) and Older Relative Caregivers (for relatives 55+ caring for children under 18 or adults 18-59 with disabilities). Assistance includes information and referral, education, training, respite care, and supplemental services. The program works alongside state and community-based services to reduce caregiver depression, anxiety, and stress, and to help caregivers provide care at home for as long as possible — avoiding or delaying the need for costly institutional care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Support services are delivered locally through Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) and Maryland Access Point offices. Eligible caregivers can access up to five types of caregiver support, including information and referral, education, training, respite care, and supplemental services to reduce caregiver stress, depression, and anxiety and help sustain their caregiving role at home for as long as possible. Specific services vary by local AAA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family members and informal caregivers age 18 and older caring for adults 60+ or individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders; grandparents and other relatives (not parents) age 55+ caring for children under 18 or adults age 18-59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and referral, education, training, respite care, and supplemental services to reduce caregiver stress, depression, and anxiety, and help caregivers sustain their caregiving role and care for loved ones at home for as long as possible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Area Agencies on Aging and Maryland Access Point offices.
requirements_list: Must be an adult family member or informal caregiver age 18 or older caring for an individual age 60 or older
OR an adult family member or informal caregiver age 18 or older caring for an individual of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders
OR a grandparent or other relative (not a parent) age 55 or older caring for a child under age 18
OR a grandparent or other relative (not a parent) age 55 or older caring for an adult age 18-59 with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Access Point (MAP) at marylandaccesspoint.211md.org, call 1-844-MAP-LINK (TTY #711), or reach out to your local Area Agency on Aging (AAA) to access program services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program advocates for the health, safety, well-being, and rights of residents in assisted living and nursing homes. Working at the direction of the resident and only with their consent, Ombudsman services are free and confidential. Ombudsmen investigate complaints, educate residents and staff about resident rights, support resident and family councils, and advocate for policies that protect resident rights and improve quality of life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential advocacy and complaint investigation services for residents of assisted living facilities and nursing homes statewide, delivered through local ombudsman offices in every Maryland county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of assisted living facilities and nursing homes in Maryland, and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Complaint investigation and resolution, resident rights education, advocacy, and support for resident and family councils.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties through local ombudsman offices.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of a licensed assisted living or nursing home in Maryland
Services provided at the direction and with the consent of the resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local county ombudsman office directly by phone. Phone numbers for each county are listed on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded by the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA) to community-based organizations serving naturally occurring retirement communities (NORCs) — neighborhoods or housing developments where a large percentage of residents have aged in place. The program funds programming, service coordination, and community support for low-income older adults facing declining health, isolation, financial hardship, and language barriers. It encompasses three project types: Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, and Traditional NORC (aging-in-place services). In FY26, MDOA awarded $1.3 million to 7 organizations, with individual awards ranging from $75,000 to $325,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded grants to community-based organizations. In FY26, MDOA awarded $1.3 million to 7 organizations. Individual awards ranged from $75,000 to $325,000 across three project tracks: Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, and Traditional NORC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations serving concentrated areas where low-income older adults face declining health, isolation, financial hardship, and language barriers anywhere in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programming, service coordination, and community support for low-income older adults, including elder abuse prevention, support for Holocaust survivors, and aging-in-place services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations serving older adults anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community-based organization
Must serve concentrated areas where low-income older adults face declining health, isolation, financial hardship, or language barriers
Must serve a NORC or address one of three program areas: Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, or Traditional NORC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Grant Availability page at aging.maryland.gov/Pages/Grants.aspx for information on current funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Assisted Living Subsidy Program helps low- to moderate-income adults age 62 and older pay for assisted living in Maryland. The subsidy can cover the cost of services such as meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision for residents who need help living independently.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The subsidy covers the difference between the resident's net monthly income (after a $130/month personal allowance deduction) and the approved monthly assisted living fee. To be financially eligible, an applicant's net monthly income must be no higher than 60% of the state median income, with assets no greater than $20,064 for singles or $26,400 for couples.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income adults age 62 and older who are residents of or approved for entry into a participating assisted living community in Maryland and need financial assistance to afford care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of assisted living services including meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Area Agencies on Aging.
requirements_list: Must be age 62 or older
Must be a resident of or approved for entrance into a participating assisted living community
Must have entered into a service agreement with an Area Agency on Aging
Must be physically or mentally impaired and need assistance with activities of daily living
Net monthly income must not exceed 60% of the state median income
Assets must be no greater than $20,064 for singles or $26,400 for couples
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging or Maryland Access Point office to apply. Counselors are available to provide free information and assistance with eligibility and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Call Check and Social Connections
structured_extraction.program_description: Senior Call Check and Social Connections is a free daily check-in service for Maryland residents age 60 and older. Each day, the program sends an automated phone call or text message to enrolled participants during a pre-selected one-hour window between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. If the participant does not respond after three attempts, an alternate contact chosen by the participant is notified. If neither the participant nor the alternate can be reached, local non-emergency service providers are asked to conduct a welfare check. TTY is available. The program is available every day of the year except six holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas). In addition to the automated daily check-in, the program offers an optional weekly live check-in called Senior Call Check Live, where a trained representative provides additional social connection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free daily automated phone call or text message check-in service. Participants select a preferred one-hour call window between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. If unanswered after three attempts, an alternate contact is notified; if still unreachable, local non-emergency services are contacted to conduct a welfare check. TTY is available. An optional weekly live check-in (Senior Call Check Live) with a trained representative is also offered for additional social connection. No cost to participants. Program operates every day except New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 60 or older with a landline or cell phone who wish to have a daily wellness check-in service and optional weekly live social connection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily automated wellness check-in calls or texts to help ensure the safety and well-being of older adults; alternate contact notification if no response; welfare check coordination with local non-emergency services; optional weekly live social connection call (Senior Call Check Live).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents age 60 and older.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be 60 years of age or older
Must have a landline or cell phone (TTY available)
Must enroll personally — cannot be enrolled by another person
Must not have call blocking features that would prevent automated or live calls (or disable call blocking for this program)
Must notify alternates and household members of participation
Must provide accurate information and update the program promptly if changes occur
Alternates must be reliable adults who agree to participate and have a reliable phone connection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There are three ways to apply: (1) Complete the online application via the Google Forms link on the program page; (2) Download, print, and mail the paper enrollment form to Senior Call Check and Social Connections, 4 N. Park Drive, Suite 202, Hunt Valley, Maryland 21030; (3) Call toll-free 1-866-50-CHECK (1-866-502-0560) to request a paper application by mail. After submitting, allow up to 10 days for a program administrator to contact you to verify information and conduct a test call. A Welcome Packet with start date will be mailed once all information is validated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Care (Maryland Department of Aging, State-Level)
structured_extraction.program_description: Senior Care provides case management and support services for people aged 65 and older who are at risk of nursing home placement. The program offers screening, assessment, and case management through local aging, health, and social services agencies. Gap-filling funds may also be available to help cover personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, and emergency response systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management services are provided in-kind by local agencies. Gap-filling funds are also available for eligible individuals to cover costs such as personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, and emergency response systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 65 or older who are at risk of nursing home placement and are severely or moderately disabled.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, and emergency response systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local aging, health, and social services agencies. Applicants must live in the county where services are to be received.
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years of age
Must be severely or moderately disabled
Must live in the county where services are to be received (for case management)
Must meet case management and income criteria (for gap-filling funds)
Assets must not exceed established resource limits (for gap-filling funds)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Access Point (MAP) Information and Assistance Office or call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465). The process includes screening to determine eligibility, a face-to-face assessment, and development of a person-centered care plan with a Case Manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging allocates more than $750,000 in annual state funds to support innovative programs and critical operating needs for senior centers across Maryland. Funding is distributed to each county by formula based on the population of residents aged 60 and older, with $100,000 allocated on a competitive basis. All counties are eligible to apply for formula funding, and select counties can compete for additional funds to run innovative programs serving historically underserved communities. In FY25, competitive supplemental grants were awarded to Caroline, Cecil, Harford, and Worcester counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: More than $750,000 in annual state grants distributed statewide. Most funding is allocated by formula based on each county's population of residents aged 60 and older; $100,000 is allocated competitively. In FY25, competitive supplemental grants were awarded to Caroline, Cecil, Harford, and Worcester counties for innovative programs serving historically underserved communities. All counties are eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior centers, Area Agencies on Aging, and local governments across all Maryland counties seeking funding to support senior center operations and programs for older adults aged 60 and older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Senior center operations and innovative programming for older adults, including programs serving historically underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties; competitive portion open to all counties with qualifying proposals.
requirements_list: Must be a senior center or organization operating senior center services
Competitive funding requires programs that serve historically underserved communities
Formula allocation is based on the county population of residents aged 60 and older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging for information about applying for funding or starting a senior center in your community.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free legal advice, counseling, and representation to Maryland residents aged 60 and older. Area Agencies on Aging contract with local attorneys and law centers to deliver services. Priority issues include income maintenance, nutrition, public and disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination, civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons. The program also supports local Ombudsmen, Health Insurance Counselors, and Public Guardianship managers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal advice, counseling, and representation on priority issues. No cost for services on priority issues. Preference is given to older adults with the greatest economic or social need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 60 and older, and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal advice, counseling, and representation on issues including income maintenance, nutrition, public/disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination, civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Area Agencies on Aging.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident aged 60 or older, or a caregiver of such a person
Priority given to those with the greatest economic or social need

Priority given to cases involving income maintenance, nutrition, public/disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination/civil rights, or advocacy for institutionalized persons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging's Maryland Access Point (MAP) to seek assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Medicare Patrol (SMP) Program empowers and assists Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, their families, and caregivers to detect, prevent, and report healthcare fraud, errors, and abuse through outreach, counseling, and education. SMP helps Marylanders spot, stop, and report Medicare and Medicaid fraud, scams, and billing errors through free, unbiased counseling and education. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Aging through 19 local offices across Maryland, including the Baltimore City Department of Aging and the Queen Anne's County Area Agency on Aging.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, unbiased outreach, counseling, and education to help Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, their families, and caregivers recognize, prevent, detect, and report healthcare fraud, billing errors, and program abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, their families, and caregivers who want to protect themselves from scams, fraud, and billing errors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Detecting, preventing, and reporting Medicare and Medicaid fraud, scams, and billing errors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through 19 local offices across Maryland, including Baltimore City and Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must be a Medicare or Medicaid beneficiary, family member, or caregiver
