structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local SHIP or Senior Medicare Patrol office by phone for free, confidential assistance. In Baltimore City, call 410-396-CARE (2273). In Queen Anne's County, call 410-758-0848. To find your local SMP office, visit the Maryland Department of Aging website.

structured_extraction.program_description: SOAR supports healthy aging, caregiving, housing stability, and social connections for older Marylanders who do not qualify for Medicaid or are on lengthy Medicaid waitlists. The program provides case management, home and community-based supports, and partial financial assistance for assisted living fees. In 2026, three existing state-funded programs were consolidated into SOAR to modernize supports for a growing older adult population.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management services; home and community-based supports that may include personal care, homemaker/chore services, meals, transportation, safety-related minor home repairs/modifications, adult day care, medical supplies, emergency response systems, and respite care; partial financial support for assisted living monthly fees. Services are subject to annual funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders age 62 or older who make less than 60% of the median state income, have assets below eligibility thresholds, need help with activities of daily living, and do not qualify for Medicaid or are on lengthy Medicaid waitlists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management; personal care; homemaker/chore services; meals; transportation; minor home repairs and modifications; adult day care; medical supplies; emergency response systems; respite care; partial assisted living fee assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be age 62 or older
Must make less than 60% of the median state income
Must have assets below eligibility thresholds
Must need help with activities of daily living
Must not qualify for Medicaid, or must be on a lengthy Medicaid waitlist
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Connect with Maryland Access Point (MAP) at marylandaccesspoint.211md.org or contact your local Area Agency on Aging to determine eligibility and begin the process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supportive Communities Capacity Building Grants (Aging-in-Place Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA) awards annual competitive grants to local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, community-based organizations, and nonprofit organizations to increase their capacity to provide high-quality services and supports, develop social connections, and foster community engagement for older Marylanders and their caregivers. The program helps low-income older adults maintain independence at home and participate in their communities safely. It supports transportation, care coordination, home accessibility modifications, and other services that help older adults age in place and remain socially connected in their own homes and communities. In FY26, MDOA awarded $261,173 to 11 organizations across Maryland, with individual awards ranging from approximately $9,500 to $45,000. The FY27 Notice of Funding Opportunity is currently open, with applications due June 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded to eligible organizations. In FY26, MDOA awarded $261,173 to 11 organizations, with individual awards ranging from approximately $9,500 to $45,000. For FY27, funding supports community-based organizations and Area Agencies on Aging to provide programming, service coordination, and support enabling low-income older Marylanders to live independently at home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, community-based organizations, and nonprofit organizations serving low-income older Marylanders and their caregivers in high-need areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation and social programs, social connection networks, mobile food delivery, care coordination, nonprofit capacity planning, master aging plans, financial and housing counseling, caregiver support, volunteer network development, online caregiver resources, home accessibility modifications, essential programming, and other services that help older adults age in place and remain socially connected and independent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations serving older adults anywhere in Maryland; all Maryland counties are eligible. High-need areas are prioritized.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local Area Agency on Aging, Senior Village, community-based organization, or nonprofit organization
Must serve older Marylanders and/or their caregivers
Must serve low-income older Marylanders
Must provide programming or services in high-need areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity and supporting documents at aging.maryland.gov/grants. Attend the information session (April 23, 2026). Submit questions by May 25, 2026. Complete and submit the Proposal Application via Smartsheet by June 1, 2026 at 5:00pm EST. Contact the Maryland Department of Aging for additional application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Animal Waste Technology Fund (AWTF) provides grants to individuals, vendors, and businesses to demonstrate proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste from Maryland livestock operations. Eligible technologies may reduce nutrient levels in animal waste, convert it to alternative products, generate energy, or create marketable products from waste. Projects in the research and development stage are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $750,000 is available per fiscal year cycle. Grants fund the implementation of proven, innovative animal waste management technologies. Funding is supported by the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due October 17, 2025; full proposal due December 23, 2025 (2026 application window is now closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, vendors, and businesses with proven technologies for managing animal waste from Maryland livestock operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demonstration of innovative animal waste management technologies, including alternative product development, manure-to-energy projects, nutrient reduction technologies, and projects that generate energy or marketable products from animal waste.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must involve Maryland livestock or animal production processes.
requirements_list: Animal waste must be generated by on-farm animals or through an animal production process involving Maryland livestock
Projects must demonstrate potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being, offer alternative waste management solutions, and have a positive economic development impact
Projects in the research and development stage are ineligible
Must submit a Letter of Intent before being invited to submit a full grant proposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants first submit a Letter of Intent by the stated deadline. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the department in consultation with the Animal Waste Technology Evaluation Committee. High-ranking projects are then invited to submit a full grant proposal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Certified Local Farm and Fish Program certifies Maryland farms and seafood dealers so that state agencies and public four-year universities can purchase food from them to meet a goal of 20% local procurement. Farms with a nutrient management plan and licensed seafood dealers can register to be listed in an online directory used by state agencies and institutions seeking to buy local food and Chesapeake invasive species products.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification and listing in the Maryland Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory, which connects certified farms and seafood dealers to state agency procurement contracts. There is no cost to become certified. Certified businesses gain visibility to state agencies required to meet a 20% local procurement goal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farms with a nutrient management plan and licensed seafood dealers (Tidal Fish Dealers) seeking to sell to state agencies and universities; also state agencies and public four-year universities required to meet a 20% local food procurement goal
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification and directory listing to facilitate sales to Maryland state agencies and public universities pursuing a 20% local food procurement goal
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farms and seafood dealers operating in Maryland; statewide scope with no county-by-county restrictions. State encourages searching the entire state of Maryland for certified local providers.
requirements_list: Farms must have a nutrient management plan on file with the Maryland Department of Agriculture, or meet nutrient management requirements (e.g., apiarists, aquaculturists)
Seafood dealers must be licensed as a Tidal Fish Dealer with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Chesapeake Certified Invasive Species Providers may also apply
Must register via the online application on Maryland OneStop (https://onestop.md.gov/)
Must update directory information annually (renewal reminders sent at 90 days, 7 days, and on final day before expiration)
State agencies and public four-year universities must submit annual reports and waiver requests to MDA by September 30 of each year
State agencies and universities must structure food procurement to achieve an overall goal of 20% local food procurement
Contracts signed before March 14, 2021 (law effective date) are exempt from reporting requirements
Non-compliance is reported to the Board of Public Works
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register using the online application on Maryland OneStop (https://onestop.md.gov/). 2. MDA verifies the nutrient management plan or Tidal Fish Dealer license. 3. Upon verification, MDA certifies the farm or dealer and lists their contact information, products, and certification number in the online directory. 4. Certified businesses must update their directory information once a year; renewal reminders are sent at 90 days and 7 days before expiration and on the final day. For state agencies and universities: submit annual reports and waiver requests to MDA at local.food@maryland.gov by September 30 each year; MDA compiles an annual report for the General Assembly by December 31.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Equipment Tax Break (Maryland Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Conservation Equipment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive that helps farmers offset the cost of buying certain types of conservation equipment to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, and protect local water quality. Farmers can subtract eligible conservation equipment purchases from taxable income on Maryland individual (Form 502) and corporate (Form 500) tax returns. The subtraction is 100% of cost for most eligible equipment types (no-till planters/drills, manure injectors/spreaders, installation costs, deep no-till rippers, GPS devices, optical sensing and nutrient application systems) and 50% for vertical tillage equipment used for manure incorporation. Unused deductions may be carried over for up to five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows farmers to subtract eligible conservation equipment purchases from taxable income on Maryland individual (Form 502) and corporate (Form 500) tax returns. Subtraction is 100% of cost for most eligible equipment types (no-till planters/drills, manure injectors/spreaders, installation costs, deep no-till rippers, GPS devices, optical sensing and nutrient application systems) and 50% for vertical tillage equipment used for manure incorporation. Unused deductions may be carried over for up to five years. Equipment must have been purchased within the last five years and have a minimum useful life of four years. Statutory basis: Md. Code Ann., Tax - General, § 10-208.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers in Maryland (individual and corporate taxpayers) who purchase conservation equipment to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, and protect local water quality
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of conservation equipment used in agricultural production to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, and protect local water quality, including: No-Till Planter or Drill (purchased after 12/31/85, 100% subtraction), Liquid Manure Injection Equipment (after 12/31/89, 100% subtraction), Poultry or Livestock Manure Spreading Equipment (100% subtraction), deep no-till rippers (100%), GPS devices (100%), optical sensing and nutrient application systems (100%), and vertical tillage equipment used for manure incorporation (50% subtraction)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; no county exclusions. Applicants submit certification form to their local soil conservation district, which verifies eligibility by county and forwards to MDA for final approval.
requirements_list: Must purchase eligible types of conservation equipment used in agricultural production
Equipment must be used for controlling soil erosion, managing nutrients, or protecting water quality
Equipment must have been purchased within the last five years
Equipment must have a minimum useful life of four years
Serial numbers required for new and trade-in equipment
Equipment must be certified by local soil conservation district and approved by MDA
Individual taxpayers must provide Social Security Number or Federal ID Number on application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the certification form (Tax-Subtraction-Application) along with a signed, dated equipment receipt to your local soil conservation district. The district verifies eligibility and forwards to MDA for final approval. Serial numbers are required for new and trade-in equipment. Upon approval, applicant receives two copies of the certificate (one for filing with the tax return, one for records). On the Maryland tax return, enter the subtraction under the designated line (Form 502 for individuals; Form 500 for corporations). Unused deductions may be carried over for up to five succeeding tax years. This is a continuous/rolling program with no stated application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) is a voluntary state-federal partnership that pays landowners and farmers annual rental income and incentive payments to protect environmentally sensitive areas. Since 1997, the program has helped thousands of Maryland landowners plant streamside buffers, establish wetlands, protect highly erodible land, and create wildlife habitat. Farmers and rural landowners who remove environmentally sensitive agricultural land from production for 10–15 year contract terms receive attractive annual land rental rate payments. Newly enrolled farmers who plant riparian forest buffers next to streams receive a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre (through 2031) on top of annual rental payments. The program also provides cost-share assistance for streamside buffers, wetlands, livestock fencing, watering systems, and related conservation practices. Landowners also have the option of selling a permanent easement on their land to the State of Maryland. CREP buffers meet all Maryland stream setback requirements and can help finance required stream protection practices for livestock operations. Sign-up is ongoing until acreage goals are met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides attractive annual land rental rate payments for removing environmentally sensitive agricultural land from production for 10–15 year contract terms, plus a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre (through 2031) for newly enrolled farmers who plant riparian forest buffers next to streams. Cost-share assistance (up to 87.5%) is also available for installing streamside buffers, wetlands, livestock fencing, watering systems, and related conservation practices. Practice incentive payments and maintenance payments are also offered. Maryland also offers a $100/acre sign-up bonus for re-enrolled contracts and $200/acre for CRP-to-CREP conversions. Landowners may also sell a permanent easement to the State of Maryland. Sign-up is ongoing until acreage goals are met.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing until acreage goals are met
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners and farmers with environmentally sensitive lands, particularly those near streams, with highly erodible soils, wetland potential, streamside property, or other qualifying conservation areas. Landowners/producers must have owned or operated the farm/ranch for 12 months prior to enrollment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removing environmentally sensitive agricultural land from production; planting streamside buffers, riparian forest buffers, and wetlands; protecting highly erodible land; creating wildlife habitat; installing livestock fencing and watering systems; wetland restoration; and meeting Maryland stream setback requirements. Annual rental payments compensate landowners for taking land out of agricultural production for 10–15 years. Eligible land types include cropland next to streams, highly erodible land within 1,000 feet of a stream, and marginal pastureland adjacent to streams.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties/soil conservation districts. Farmers should contact their local soil conservation district or county Farm Service Agency (FSA) office to sign up. Program is particularly focused on the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
requirements_list: Participation is completely voluntary
Must be a farmer or rural landowner in Maryland
Land must include environmentally sensitive areas such as streamside buffers, wetlands, or highly erodible land
Must plant riparian forest buffers next to streams to receive the signing bonus (available through 2031)
New enrollments of riparian forest buffers qualify for the signing bonus (through 2031)
Commit to removing land from production for 10 to 15 years (10 years for highly erodible land and shallow water practices; 10–15 years for all other practices)
Install approved conservation practices
Must meet Maryland setback requirements where applicable
Landowner/producer must have owned or operated the farm/ranch for 12 months prior to enrollment
Eligible land types include: cropland next to streams, highly erodible land within 1,000 feet of a stream, and marginal pastureland adjacent to streams
Apply through the local soil conservation district or county USDA Farm Service Agency office
For re-enrollment of expired CREP contracts: existing practices must be re-enrolled no later than June 1 of the year after the expiration date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign-up is ongoing until acreage goals are met. Interested farmers and landowners should contact their local USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) office or local soil conservation district for free help from experts in meeting conservation needs. Contracts begin the 1st day of the month following the FSA County Committee's approval; applicants may defer the contract start date for up to six months. You may also contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources or Maryland Department of Agriculture for enrollment information. Landowners may also review the 'CREP in Maryland: Start to Finish' guide for enrollment details. See program brochures and FAQs linked on the program page for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cover Crop Plus offers higher incentive payments to Maryland farmers who plant enhanced cover crop mixes to improve soil health and water quality. Farmers sign a 3-year contract to grow multispecies cover crop mixes on the same fields, maintain a living root system year-round, and use no-till or conservation tillage. Base payment is $125 per acre per year, with optional add-on practices that can increase the rate up to $180 per acre.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Base payment of $125 per acre per year for a 3-year contract to grow multispecies cover crops. Optional add-on practices (e.g., residue management, biodiversity enhancements) can increase the per-acre payment up to $180 per year. Enrollment is capped at 500 acres per farmer.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2024-2025 Enrollment Period has ended. Fall cover crop planting deadline is October 15.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers (agricultural operations) who want to earn higher incentives for planting enhanced cover crop mixes to improve soil health and water quality.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentive payments for planting multispecies cover crop mixes on enrolled fields for 3 consecutive years using no-till or conservation tillage, maintaining living roots and residue management targets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farmers throughout Maryland who meet the state's definition of an agricultural operation.
requirements_list: Must meet Maryland's definition of an 'agricultural operation'
If leasing land, must confirm enrolled acres will be under your care for the full 3-year contract term

Must be in good standing with the Maryland Nutrient Management Program, the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program, the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation Program, and other MDA conservation grant programs
Must submit a current Nutrient Management Plan Certification with your application
Must sign a 3-year contract to grow cover crop mixes on the same fields
May enroll up to 500 acres
Must maintain a living root system on enrolled fields throughout the year and manage cover crops to achieve 30% residue
Fall cover crops must be planted within 10 days of harvesting or terminating the previous crop, or planted green into a standing crop; planting deadline is October 15
Must plant multispecies cover crops with cereal grain or ryegrass making up at least 50% of the mix and a legume making up at least 25%
Only no-till or conservation tillage may be used throughout the 3-year contract
Optional add-on practices must be new practices not used in the previous 3 years on an enrolled field
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district for assistance with applications and claim for payment forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Cover Crop Program provides cost-share grants to help farmers plant cold-hardy cereal grains, legumes, brassicas, and other fall cover crops following the harvest of spring and summer crops. Cover crops recycle unused plant nutrients, prevent erosion, improve soil health, remove carbon dioxide from the air, and protect farm fields from extreme weather events. The program is funded by the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund and the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share grants that help pay for seed and planting costs for eligible fall cover crop species. Cost-share rates vary from year to year. Additional incentives are available for early planting (by October 10th) or for using rye, triticale, or a multi-species cover crop mix. Cost-share is also available for seed testing (seed sample testing fee is $30.00 per sample). There is a 10-acre minimum; no acreage caps.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual enrollment window, usually late June and early July. 2026-2027 sign-up opens June 22, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and farm operators/landowners seeking to plant fall cover crops following spring and summer crop harvests.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed and planting costs for eligible fall cover crop species, including cereal grains, brassicas (when planted in a mix with a cereal grain), and legumes (when planted in a mix with a cereal grain). Also covers seed testing costs ($30.00 per sample submitted to the MD Seed Lab).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties. Applications are submitted through the applicant's local soil conservation district.
requirements_list: Minimum of 10 acres enrolled (no acreage cap).
Cover crops must follow corn, soybeans, sorghum, tobacco, vegetables, hemp, sunflowers, sod, or millet.
Eligible planting methods: no-till, conventional till, broadcast/light tillage, broadcast/stalk chopping, and aerial seeding.
Must comply with Maryland Seed Law and Regulations if using homegrown seed.
Must be in good standing with the Conservation Grants and Nutrient Management programs.
Cover crop must be planted by early November to qualify for payment.
Must certify planted acres with your local soil conservation district within one week of planting and after kill down or suppression.
Bring a completed Nutrient Management Plan Certification and IRS Form W-9 when applying.
NMP must cover the time period of the cost-share practice(s) and must be certified by a certified NMP preparer (or certified farm operator) per COMAR 15.20.07.
NMP Certification Form must be submitted to the local Soil Conservation District (SCD) office.
Seed samples for seed testing must be at least 2 lbs (lunch bag or quart-jar size); treated samples must state the treatment name; $30.00 fee per sample.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local soil conservation district during the annual enrollment window (typically late June to early July). Bring a completed Nutrient Management Plan Certification (certifying compliance with current NMP per COMAR 15.20.07) and IRS Form W-9. After planting, certify planted acres with your local soil conservation district within one week of planting and again after kill down or suppression. For seed testing, submit a seed sample of at least 2 lbs to the MD Seed Lab (50 Harry S Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401) with a completed Seed Sample Testing Form and $30.00 fee; results are mailed the same day completed and bills are mailed end-of-month.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ecosystem Incentives Program – Tree Planting Incentives
structured_extraction.program_description: A component of Maryland's Ecosystem Incentives Program, the Tree Planting Incentives provide a bonus payment to farmers and landowners who install qualifying conservation practices financed through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program. Eligible participants receive $2 for each new tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice, paid in addition to the regular MACS cost-share rate (up to 100% for most practices, up to 87.5% for Silvopasture). Qualifying tree-planting practices include Windbreak Establishment, Silvopasture, Riparian Forest Buffer, Hedgerow Planting, and Tree and Shrub Establishment. The broader Ecosystem Incentives Program also includes conservation buffer incentives, CREP bonus payments, Cover Crop Plus grants, tax incentives for conservation equipment, and low-interest loans (LILAC) for agricultural conservation projects. The Maryland Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Conservation Equipment allows eligible farmers to subtract 100% of the cost of qualifying conservation equipment (50% for vertical tillage equipment) from their Maryland income tax return; qualifying equipment includes no-till planters/drills, manure spreaders/injectors, GPS systems, optical sensing systems, vertical tillage equipment, and installation costs. Equipment must have a useful life of at least 4 years and must have been purchased within the last five years for certification eligibility. All incentives aim to promote clean water, healthy soils, and climate solutions across Maryland, and support the state's tree-planting goal to capture greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentives including: $2 per new tree planted as part of an approved MACS conservation practice (in addition to the regular MACS cost-share rate, up to 100% for most practices, up to 87.5% for Silvopasture); grants (Cover Crop Plus); low-interest loans (LILAC) for agricultural conservation projects; tax incentives including the Maryland Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Conservation Equipment (100% subtraction for qualifying conservation equipment, 50% for vertical tillage equipment); and CREP bonus payments. Qualifying conservation equipment includes no-till planters/drills, manure spreaders/injectors, GPS systems, optical sensing systems, vertical tillage equipment, deep no-till rippers, and installation costs. Equipment must have a useful life of at least 4 years and must have been purchased within the last five years for certification eligibility. Equipment purchase date thresholds vary by type (1985–2012).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and landowners (individual and for-profit) seeking conservation incentives for clean water, healthy soils, and climate solutions, including those participating in the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program and those seeking income tax subtractions for conservation equipment purchases
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting as part of approved conservation practices (Windbreak Establishment, Silvopasture, Riparian Forest Buffer, Hedgerow Planting, Tree and Shrub Establishment), conservation buffers, cover crops, agricultural conservation projects using low-interest loans, and conservation equipment (no-till planters/drills, manure spreaders/injectors, GPS systems, optical sensing systems, vertical tillage equipment, deep no-till rippers, and installation costs)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; no county, municipal, or regional restrictions. Program is administered through the local soil conservation district network statewide.
requirements_list: Must install qualifying conservation practices financed through the MACS Program
Trees must be planted as part of an approved conservation practice
For tax subtraction: equipment must have a useful life of at least 4 years
For tax subtraction: equipment must have been purchased within the last five years for certification eligibility
For tax subtraction: nutrient management plan preparer certification and soil conservation district certification required
For tax subtraction: equipment must be used for soil erosion control, nutrient management, or water quality protection (e.g., livestock/poultry manure management, no-till crop production)

For tax subtraction: equipment purchase date thresholds vary by type (e.g., no-till planting equipment after 12/31/1985, liquid manure injection and poultry/livestock manure spreading equipment after 12/31/1989, certain other equipment after 12/31/2012)
For tax subtraction: complete Certificate of Conservation form and submit with equipment receipt to local soil conservation district
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district for free help from experts in meeting your conservation needs. For the income tax subtraction, submit a completed Certificate of Conservation form along with equipment receipt to your local soil conservation district. The equipment must have been purchased within the last five years. The district will certify and forward to Maryland Department of Agriculture, Conservation Grants, 50 Harry S. Truman Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21401. Visit the Ecosystem Incentives Program link for full details on all available incentives and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free on-farm readiness reviews help Maryland farmers understand and meet the requirements of the federal Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Produce Safety Rule. A reviewer visits the farm to assess compliance readiness and provide guidance before formal inspections occur. Reviews are conducted by MDA, University of Maryland (UMD), and University of Maryland Extension (UME) teams. Farmers receive a pre-review manual, an on-farm walkthrough, and post-review written feedback on compliance status and areas for improvement. Follow-up assistance is also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost, confidential, non-regulatory on-farm readiness reviews to help farmers assess compliance with the FSMA Produce Safety Rule. Reviews are conducted by MDA, University of Maryland (UMD), and University of Maryland Extension (UME) teams. Farmers receive a pre-review manual, an on-farm walkthrough, and post-review written feedback on compliance status and areas for improvement. Follow-up assistance is also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers required or eligible to comply with the FSMA Produce Safety Rule, including farms with covered activities (growing, harvesting, packing, or holding covered produce) across financial categories: Large (>$500K), Small ($250K–$500K), Very Small ($25K–$250K), and Exempt (<$25K)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-farm assessment and technical guidance to help farmers meet FSMA Produce Safety Rule requirements, including pre-review preparation, on-farm walkthrough, and post-review recommendations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farms located in Maryland; no county or regional restrictions
requirements_list: Farm must be potentially subject to or eligible to comply with the FSMA Produce Safety Rule
Farm must engage in covered activities: growing, harvesting, packing, or holding covered produce
Farmer must submit a completed On Farm Readiness Review Request Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the On Farm Readiness Review Request Form (available as PDF or Word document) and submit via email to produce.safety@maryland.gov, fax to 410-841-2750, or mail to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. MDA will contact the farm after receiving the form to gather details, personalize the review, and schedule a date and time. The on-farm visit is conducted by an MDA/UMD/UME team with a walkthrough and observation. Post-review notes detailing compliant and improvement-needed areas are provided, and follow-up assistance is available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Good Agricultural Practices / Good Handling Practices (GAP/GHP) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) Food Quality Assurance Program offers GAP/GHP training, one-on-one assistance, and certification for Maryland fruit and vegetable producers and handlers. MDA helps producers develop, write, and implement food safety programs addressing water quality, manure and compost use, worker health and hygiene, and contamination prevention. The program includes a State GAP/GHP certification for direct marketers and first-time participants, as well as USDA/AMS audits conducted through a cooperative agreement with USDA that provide national recognition. USDA Specialty Crop grant funds are also available to help Maryland producers offset the cost of USDA audit fees. Program requirements are updated annually to meet current buyer and regulatory requirements. Training and one-on-one assistance are also available in cooperation with the University of Maryland, with regional training sessions offered January through March each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA provides GAP/GHP food safety training and direct one-on-one assistance to help producers develop, write, and implement food safety programs at no stated cost. MDA conducts State GAP/GHP certification inspections—producers who pass receive a GAP/GHP certificate—and USDA-recognized audits through a cooperative agreement with USDA/AMS that determine compliance with USDA GAP/GHP and Pre/Post Harvest Harmonized standards. USDA Specialty Crop grant funds are available to help eligible Maryland producers offset the cost of USDA audit fees. MDA and the University of Maryland offer producer training sessions regionally January through March each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland fruit and vegetable producers, direct marketers, and handlers seeking GAP/GHP food safety training, certification, or USDA audit cost assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food safety training, development and implementation of food safety plans, GAP/GHP certification inspections, USDA audit verification, and offsetting costs of USDA audit fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any Maryland producer or handler of fruits and vegetables; statewide scope with no county or regional restrictions
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland producer or handler of fruits and vegetables
Must implement food safety practices related to water quality, manure and compost use, worker health and hygiene, and contamination prevention
State GAP/GHP certification is targeted at direct marketers and producers that have never had a GAP/GHP inspection or audit
For USDA audit: must comply with USDA GAP/GHP standards and Pre/Post Harvest Harmonized standards
Must complete approved GAP/GHP training
Must complete a self-assessment of current food safety practices
Must develop a written food safety plan
Must undergo an MDA inspection; if deficiencies are found, corrective actions and reinspection may be required
Inspection is voluntary and free of charge
If certified, farm/packer is declared compliant with MDA GAP program standards
Secretary of Agriculture retains authority to quarantine crops showing gross contamination presenting an immediate public health risk; quarantine decision may be appealed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Producers can request an MDA GAP/GHP inspection using the MDA GAP/GHP Inspection Request Form, or request a USDA GAP/GHP audit using the USDA GAP Audit Request Form and Participant Agreement. Upon submission of the inspection request form, an MDA auditor will contact the applicant to schedule the inspection. Training and one-on-one assistance are available in cooperation with the University of Maryland, with regional training sessions offered January through March each year. Contact Molly Gillingham at 410-841-5769 or Molly.Gillingham@maryland.gov for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) International Marketing Program helps Maryland agricultural producers and suppliers export their products overseas. MDA advises on foreign markets, organizes trade missions and trade shows abroad, assists with export logistics (overseas shipping, labeling, import restrictions, language, and financial transfer), and connects Maryland businesses with overseas buyers, importers, and distributors. MDA works with USDA embassies and organizations like the Southern U.S. Trade Association (SUSTA) and US Livestock & Genetics Export Association to facilitate exports to more than 35 countries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA provides technical export assistance, trade mission organization, trade show support, market research, buyer introductions, export training seminars, and access to funding programs such as SUSTA's Market Access Program (MAP), which allocates funding directly to Maryland companies for their own export promotions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland agricultural producers and food/agricultural suppliers seeking to enter or expand in overseas markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Export promotion, trade missions, trade shows, market research, buyer connections, export logistics assistance, and training seminars for international trade.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland-based agricultural businesses statewide. The program supports companies seeking to export globally, with applicants indicating their current and desired export markets by country.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland producer or supplier seeking to export agricultural or food products
Complete and submit the International Marketing Assistance Form to MDA's International Marketing Director
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and return the International Marketing Assistance Form to MDA's International Marketing Director Stone Slade at [email protected]. No review timeline, approval process, or next steps post-submission are specified.

structured_extraction.program_description: LEEF is a statewide agricultural certification program established by the Chesapeake Bay Legacy Act (effective July 1, 2025) and administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). The program is designed to recognize and incentivize farms that adopt conservation practices (such as cover crops, nutrient reductions, and pollinator habitats) and community practices (such as research participation, mentorship, and food bank service). Farms earn points for qualifying practices and achieve tiered certification levels (Certified, Silver, Gold, Platinum), with higher tiers unlocking greater incentives such as priority access to equipment funding, grants, tax incentives, and lower loan rates. The program framework is voluntary, dynamic, and subject to annual review. Financial incentives are being developed in partnership with entities such as MARBIDCO and Horizon Farm Credit. The program is currently in development and is expected to launch in Spring 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn points by implementing conservation and community practices on their farms. Higher point totals unlock higher certification tiers (Certified 40-49, Silver 50-59, Gold 60-79, Platinum 80+). Incentives include prioritization for equipment funding or contracts with vendors; future incentives may include priority access to programs and grants, tax incentives, lower loan rates, infrastructure grants, processing plant development funding, permit/license streamlining, consumer marketing support, and field trial participation. Financial incentives are being developed in partnership with entities such as MARBIDCO and Horizon Farm Credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Launching Spring 2026; not yet accepting applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers seeking to enhance environmental stewardship and earn recognition and incentives for conservation and community practices, including beginning/new farmers and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentives for implementing conservation practices (cover crops, nutrient reductions, buffers, renewable energy, carbon sequestration, conservation tillage, natural filters, wildlife/pollinator habitats, healthy soils) and community practices (research, mentorship, food bank service, participation in nutrition programs, farmers market nutrition program, certified local farm participation, service leadership, beginning farmer mentorship, food system resiliency initiatives).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; practice weights may be prioritized based on location within critical areas or other priority areas, including Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Southern Maryland also referenced for certain partner incentive programs.
requirements_list: Must be a farm operator in Maryland
Implementation must include both conservation and community practices
Farms earn points for qualifying practices to reach certification tiers: Certified (40-49 points), Silver (50-59), Gold (60-79), Platinum (80+)
MDA will verify practices through field assessment staff and data
Program framework is voluntary and dynamic, subject to annual review
Both conservation practices and community best practices must be adopted to qualify for tiered certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is not yet accepting applications as of early 2026. Interested farmers can join the LEEF mailing list to receive updates. Partners and interested parties can contact LEEF.MDA@maryland.gov. MDA is hosting feedback sessions and gathering input through an open survey during the development process. Future meetings will consider administrative decisions such as prioritization, verification of practices, and program incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps farmers and registered manure brokers cover the cost of transporting manure to farms with low phosphorus fields or to alternative use facilities. Two options are available for poultry manure: a standard grant application and a 'Haul Now, Apply Later FastTrack' option where hauling happens first and cost-share reimbursement is applied for afterward. A simplified process is also available for dairy and non-poultry livestock manure transport.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For poultry manure: payments of up to $28 per ton (at rates of $0.14–$0.16 per ton per mile, with higher rates of $0.16/ton-mile for Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties) to transport poultry litter. Up to $40 cost-share per manure analysis test. For dairy and livestock manure: cost-share grants pay up to 87.5 percent of all eligible costs, with payment rates based on transport distance and manure type (liquid or solid). Funding is capped at $15,000 per season and $30,000 per year. Injection grants are available up to $45 per acre. Payment is the lesser of the calculated rate or actual invoiced hauling cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible farmers, businesses receiving manure, and registered manure brokers who need to transport poultry, dairy, or livestock manure to low-phosphorus fields or alternative use facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering the cost of transporting manure from the sending farm to receiving farm fields with low phosphorus levels or to approved alternative use facilities. Manure analysis testing costs (up to $40 per test for poultry manure). Manure injection equipment and labor (up to $45 per acre).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The sending farm must be located in Maryland. For poultry manure, the sending farm must raise broiler chickens for a participating Delmarva poultry company (Amick, Mountaire, Perdue, or Tyson). Poultry litter must be transported more than 7 miles from the sending farm. Dairy and livestock manure must be transported more than 1 mile from the sending source. Higher reimbursement rates ($0.16/ton-mile) apply for farms in Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: For poultry manure: sending farm must be in Maryland and raise broiler chickens for a participating Delmarva poultry company (Amick, Mountaire, Perdue, or Tyson)
Poultry litter must be transported more than 7 miles from the sending farm
Receiving fields with a phosphorus Fertility Index Value greater than 150 are not eligible for Standard option; FastTrack requires P-FIV ≤ 100
Transported poultry litter must be land applied as a nutrient source for an agricultural crop OR sent to an approved alternative use facility
Either the farmer or the manure broker (not both) may apply for cost-share reimbursement for a given load
Applicant must submit a current nutrient management plan (NMP Certification Form must be submitted to local Soil Conservation District; may be submitted at claim stage for Manure Transport projects)
Soil test must be no older than 3 years
Manure analysis must be no older than 2 years
Claim for Payment must be submitted within 40 days from last date of transport
For dairy and livestock manure: receiving farm fields must have a Maryland soil phosphorus Fertility Index Value below 101
Dairy and livestock manure must be transported more than 1 mile from the sending source
Only operations receiving dairy or livestock manure may apply for transport grants
Manure must be applied to crops or hay fields containing less than 25 percent legumes
Maximum application rates: 6,000 gallons per acre for liquid/slurry or 10 tons per acre for solid/semi-solid manure
Grants are available for spring or fall-planted crops; work may begin March 1
Compliance with COMAR 15.20.07 required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For poultry manure (standard option): farmers apply through the local soil conservation district; registered manure brokers apply directly to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. For poultry manure (FastTrack option): download and complete the FastTrack application and claim form, haul the manure, then apply for reimbursement within 40 days of last transport date. For dairy and livestock manure: use the Non-Poultry Manure FastTrack Application and Claim Form; contact local soil conservation district or download application from mda.maryland.gov/manure. Mail completed forms to Maryland Department of Agriculture, Conservation Grants, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Room 207, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_description: ACReS is Maryland's official USDA-certified agricultural mediation program. It provides voluntary, confidential mediation services to help farmers, agricultural lenders, agencies, families, and members of the public resolve disputes outside of court. Disputes can include USDA agency decisions, farm credit issues, land or equipment leasing conflicts, neighbor disputes, and family farm planning or transition concerns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: ACReS provides free initial consultation and a first mediation session at no cost. If additional sessions are needed, nominal costs are shared among participants. Full or partial fee waivers may be available based on income. The program assigns a neutral mediator to help parties reach a mutually acceptable resolution. A toll-free line (800-492-5590) is also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural lenders, agencies, families, and members of the public with disputes related to agricultural operations in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mediation services to resolve agricultural disputes including USDA agency decisions, credit issues, land and equipment leasing, neighbor conflicts, and family farm planning or succession.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Agricultural operations include aquaculture, tree farms, beekeeping, horticulture, and urban farming.
requirements_list: Must have a dispute related to agricultural production or an agricultural operation
All participants must agree to participate voluntarily
Participants must agree to confidentiality of the mediation process
Parties must waive right to civil action against the State of Maryland and MDA to participate
Complete the ACReS Mediation Intake Form to request services
Good-faith participation and complete and honest disclosure of relevant information required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed intake form with description of conflict, prior resolution attempts, and party contact information. Staff will confirm willingness of all parties to participate and gather background information. A mediator is assigned and all parties are notified of the date, time, and location of the session. Information marked confidential.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The MACS Program provides farmers, agricultural landowners, and small-scale equine and livestock operations with cost-share grants to cover up to 100 percent of the cost to install conservation measures known as best management practices (BMPs) on their farms. These practices prevent soil erosion, manage nutrients, and safeguard water quality in streams, rivers, and the Chesapeake Bay. More than 40 eligible BMPs include grassed waterways, streamside buffers of grasses and trees, animal manure management systems, animal waste storage facilities, spring developments, cover crops, stream protection practices, conservation cover, nutrient management services, and many other practices. Farmers can also receive cost-share assistance to transport excess poultry litter off the farm. The program supports tree-planting conservation practices including riparian forest buffers, hedgerow plantings, silvopasture, tree and shrub establishment, and windbreak establishment, with up to 100% cost-share (87.5% for silvopasture) plus $2 per tree planted. The program also supports livestock farmers through stream protection practices, including livestock watering facilities (frost-free waterers, spring developments), livestock exclusion fencing, stream crossings, and riparian forest buffers, helping farmers comply with Nutrient Management Program livestock setback requirements. A 2024 expansion made farms with at least 1,000 pounds of live animal weight eligible, covering small-scale equine and livestock operations and qualifying practices such as watering facilities, pasture management, animal waste storage structures, heavy use area protection, roof runoff structures, stream exclusion fencing, and interior pasture fencing. Cost-share rates range from 50% to 100% depending on the practice. Priority watersheds are identified for targeting funds. The Maryland Department of Agriculture's Office of Resource Conservation works closely with Maryland farmers and soil conservation districts to plan and implement these conservation practices and programs that balance crop and livestock production with environmental protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share grants covering up to 100% of the cost to install eligible best management practices (BMPs) on farms; rates vary by practice (50%–100%) as detailed in the MACS Manual. For tree-planting practices: riparian forest buffers (up to 100% + $2/tree), hedgerow planting (up to 100% + $2/tree), silvopasture (up to 87.5% + $2/tree), tree and shrub establishment (up to 100% + $2/tree), and windbreak establishment (up to 100% + $2/tree). For stream protection practices: livestock watering facilities, livestock exclusion fencing, and stream crossings (up to 87.5%); riparian forest buffers (up to 100% + $2/tree). For small equine and livestock operations: watering facilities, pasture management, animal waste storage structures, heavy use area protection, and roof runoff structures (up to 87.5%); stream exclusion fencing (up to 100%); interior pasture fencing (up to 50%). Single non-waste project maximum: $150,000 (no pooling) or $200,000 (with pooling). Animal waste storage/treatment maximum: $200,000 per project; $450,000 per person across all such projects. Nutrient management plans: up to 87.5% of eligible costs. Minimum eligible state cost-share: $200. Farms must have at least 1,000 pounds of live animal weight to qualify under the 2024 expansion for equine and livestock operations. Also provides cost-share assistance to transport excess poultry litter off the farm. Assistance is provided on a reimbursement model — applicant pays upfront and receives reimbursement upon project completion and certification. Funding sources include state bond funds (requiring State Board of Public Works approval) and federal/other grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural landowners, livestock farmers, horse owners, small-scale equine and livestock operations, and other individuals, partnerships, corporations, trusts, or businesses operating a Maryland farm with existing or potentially critical conditions causing soil, nutrients, or pollutants to enter state waters, seeking to install conservation practices that protect water quality, manage nutrients, plant trees and shrubs for conservation purposes, and improve soil health and wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of conservation best management practices (BMPs) such as grassed waterways, streamside buffers of grasses and trees, animal manure management systems, animal waste storage facilities, livestock watering facilities (frost-free waterers, spring developments), livestock exclusion fencing, stream crossings, riparian forest buffers, hedgerow planting, silvopasture, tree and shrub establishment, windbreak establishment, pasture management measures, animal waste storage structures, heavy use area protection, roof runoff structures, interior pasture fencing, cover crops, conservation cover, nutrient management services, rainwater harvesting systems, well protection, windbreaks for poultry houses, contour farming, conservation drainage, critical area planting, subsurface denitrifying bioreactors, saturated buffers, integrated pest management, pollinator habitat, wetland restoration, and more than 40 other eligible practices to prevent soil erosion, manage nutrients, protect water quality, and improve herd health. Also covers transport of excess poultry litter off the farm. Free Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans (SCWQPs) are also available through local soil conservation districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through local soil conservation districts; priority watersheds are identified for targeting funds, including Lower Susquehanna (Baltimore, Harford), Pocomoke (Somerset, Worcester, Wicomico), Nanticoke/Wicomico (Somerset, Wicomico, Caroline, Dorchester), Choptank (Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Queen Anne's), Chester River (Talbot, Queen Anne's, Kent), Sassafras River (Kent), Reservoirs (Baltimore, Carroll, Howard, Montgomery), Patapsco River (Carroll, Howard), Patuxent (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Howard), Washington Metro (Montgomery), Middle Potomac (Frederick, Washington, Carroll, Montgomery), and Upper Potomac (Washington). Available to all farms located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a farmer or agricultural landowner
Applicant must be an individual, partnership, corporation, trust, or other business operating a Maryland farm
Must have an existing or potentially critical condition on agricultural land causing soil, nutrients, or other pollutants to enter state waters
Project must involve installation of an eligible best management practice (BMP)
Proposed project must improve water quality
Proposed project must meet MACS eligibility criteria and cost-effectiveness requirements
Nutrient Management Plan may be required for certain practices; nutrient management compliance required as condition of eligibility (MD Agric. Code Ann. §§8-801–8-806, COMAR 15.20.06-08)
Various practice-specific eligibility criteria and provisions apply as detailed in the MACS Manual
Applicants seeking stream protection practices must have livestock and pastureland bordering a stream
Must work with a local soil conservation district to identify suitable practices and apply for grants
For small equine and livestock operations: must have at least 1,000 pounds of live animal weight
For animal waste facility projects: minimum 15 animal units qualify for full flat rates; 1–14 animal units subject to reduced cost-share
Project must benefit land devoted to agricultural activity and reduce pollutants to waters of the State (surface or groundwater)
For sediment control: maximum cost-effectiveness threshold of $55/ton of soil saved
Project must be completed within one year of Agreement execution; one 6-month extension allowed with written justification
Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan required for Sediment Control Ponds
Entire project must be maintained for the longest maintenance life of all BMPs (typically 5–15 years)
Signed NRCS designated technician and SCD Chairman/Designee authorization required; Operation and Maintenance Plan mandatory

Property deed documentation required (Maryland Property View Account ID, Liber and Folio numbers, and recorded deed copy); corporations, trusts, and partnerships must provide Certificate of Resolution
USDA NRCS standards and local soil conservation district approval required
Annual compliance monitoring: SCDs inspect up to 10% of BMPs randomly selected
Failure to maintain BMPs triggers full repayment liability

Property transfer requires written notice to MACS; agreement transfers to new owner; non-transfer in ≤30 days allows pro-rated repayment; 31–90 days requires full repayment; >90 days triggers enforced collection plus 17% fee
Participants must alert MACS in writing of operation changes or property transfers
Must keep Waste Management System Plan and Nutrient Management Plan updated throughout maintenance life (for animal waste projects)
Confined Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) must obtain farm plans as part of Maryland Department of Environment permitting
Subsurface denitrifying bioreactors must achieve ≥30% annual nitrate-nitrogen load reduction
Saturated buffers must intercept subsurface drain from ≥15 acres
Extended Buffer Worksheet required if riparian buffer width exceeds MACS guidelines
Contact local soil conservation district to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program manager or your local Soil Conservation District (or the USDA Service Center located in each county) for free technical assistance to identify suitable practices. Complete the Water Quality Project Application Form (Excel) and required attachments as specified in the MACS Manual. District staff will help you plan conservation practices and submit the cost-share application. Within 30 days of receipt of a complete application, MACS will notify the SCD of preliminary eligibility. Upon determination of preliminary eligibility, the SCD, applicant, and all landowners sign the MACS Agreement and return it within 30 days. Submit forms and supporting documentation per practice-specific guidelines, including deed documentation, Operation and Maintenance Plan, and NRCS technician sign-off. You may also contact the Maryland Department of Agriculture Office of Resource Conservation directly at (410) 841-5864 or visit mda.maryland.gov/conservation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Century Farms Program honors farm families whose farms have been in the same family for at least 100 years and continue to be productive. Established in 1994, the program recognizes Century Farm honorees for their contributions to agriculture and farmland preservation in Maryland. Benefits are non-monetary and include a Governor and Secretary of Agriculture signed certificate, plaque listing, farm sign, and invitation to an annual awards ceremony.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recognition/certification award for farm families whose land has remained in the same family for at least 100 years and continues to operate productively. Benefits are non-monetary: a Governor and Secretary of Agriculture signed certificate, plaque listing, farm sign, and invitation to an annual awards ceremony. Families apply for official designation as a Maryland Century Farm.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open year-round; no fixed deadline. A family may apply at any time throughout the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farm families in Maryland whose farm has been in continuous family ownership for at least 100 years, retains at least 10 acres of the original holding, generates at least $2,500 annually from farm product sales, and remains productive.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition and certification only; no funding disbursed. Benefits include a Governor and Secretary of Agriculture signed certificate, plaque listing, farm sign, and invitation to an annual awards ceremony.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties; no county or regional restrictions.
requirements_list: Farm must have been in the same family for at least 100 consecutive years to the date of application
Farm must retain at least 10 acres of the original holding
Farm must generate at least $2,500 annually from farm product sales
Farm must continue to be productive
Applicant must be a descendant of the original owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available via MDA contact or www.mda.maryland.gov and may be submitted at any time throughout the year. Download and submit the Century Farm application form available on the Maryland Department of Agriculture website. Submit completed application by mail to: Maryland Department of Agriculture, Attn: Century Farm Program, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401. The Century Farm Committee reviews applications and the Secretary of Agriculture certifies approved applications. Families are recognized annually at an awards ceremony. Applications are retained by MDA for future research.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEQAP is a voluntary program that helps egg producers and processors reduce the risk of Salmonella enteritidis (SE) contamination in shell eggs. Participants commit to management and monitoring practices proven to prevent SE contamination. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) provides oversight, technical advice, and compliance inspections. Eggs produced and processed under MEQAP standards may be labeled with the Maryland's Best logo.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA provides technical advice and compliance inspections at no cost to participants. The egg industry covers the costs of testing, monitoring, training, and quarterly MDA plant visits. Participants gain the right to label qualifying eggs with the Maryland's Best logo.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Egg producers and processors in Maryland seeking to demonstrate Salmonella enteritidis prevention practices and market eggs under the Maryland's Best label.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical oversight and advice for implementing SE prevention practices including chick placement, rodent control, cleaning, environmental monitoring, egg washing, refrigeration, labeling, and quality control.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any poultry producer or shell egg processor located in Maryland. Participation of flocks or processing of eggs from outside Maryland is at the discretion of the Maryland Department of Agriculture, based on flock status in a program equivalent to MEQAP.
requirements_list: Place SE-clean chicks
Implement rodent control
Clean and disinfect between flocks
Conduct environmental monitoring of pullet and layer houses
Continuously test eggs from environmentally positive houses
Handle eggs properly on farm
Divert SE-positive eggs for pasteurization
Follow MEQAP washing, refrigeration, labeling, and quality control guidelines for processing
Maintain records proving eggs sourced from Maryland MEQAP-registered flocks (for packers)
Monitor and record wash water temperature (min. 90°F, 20°F above egg temperature) and pH (min. 10) every 2 hours with corrective actions documented
Maintain approved rodent control program
Use only new cartons or new fiber filler flats for Maryland's Best eggs
Maintain plant sanitation records
Cooperate with MDA monitoring and prevention procedures
Participate in training on quality control and recordkeeping
Pay for training, monitoring, and quarterly MDA plant visits
Maintain MDA-approved monitoring logs
Adopt MDA Standard Operating Procedures for sanitation and egg quality
Obliterate MDA logo from non-compliant cartons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participation is voluntary and ongoing with no announced end date. Producers and processors apply separately using the MEQAP Producer Application or MEQAP Processor Application (PDF forms available on the program page). Applicants complete and sign the participation agreement form and submit to the Maryland Department of Agriculture, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401. Contact Molly Gillingham at (410) 841-5769 for more information. Independent random inspections by the Department verify ongoing compliance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Food Donation Program provides Maryland income tax credits to farmers who donate eligible food products to certified food banks and food pantries. The credit is based on the value of the donated food, as determined using USDA wholesale price listings. This was a pilot program for tax years 2017, 2018, and 2019 only and has since expired. Credits equal 50% of the wholesale value of eligible donations (75% for certified organic produce), with a per-farm annual cap of $5,000 (up to $10,000 with Secretary of Agriculture approval) and an aggregate annual cap of $200,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers may receive a Maryland income tax credit of 50% of the wholesale value of eligible food donations (75% for certified organic produce), up to $5,000 per farm per year. The Maryland Secretary of Agriculture may approve an increase allowing up to $10,000 in total credits per year. An aggregate annual cap of $200,000 applies to total credits issued per fiscal year. Credits were available only for tax years 2017, 2018, and 2019.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program expired December 31, 2019 (pilot for tax years 2017–2019 only)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who donate eligible food products to certified food banks and food pantries in Maryland. Secondary audience: Tax Credit Certificate Administrators (TCCAs), which must be 501(c)(3) organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against Maryland state income tax for farms donating fresh farm products for human consumption to MDA-certified food banks and food pantries. Credit equals 50% of the wholesale value of eligible donations, or 75% for certified organic produce donations. Annual per-farm cap of $5,000 (up to $10,000 with Secretary approval); aggregate annual cap of $200,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to qualified farms that donate eligible fresh farm products for human consumption to MDA-certified food banks and food pantries.
requirements_list: Donor must be a qualified farm.
Donated products must be eligible food products (fresh farm products for human consumption).
Food must be donated to a food bank or food pantry certified by MDA.
The receiving organization must be a Tax Credit Certificate Administrator (TCCA) and a 501(c)(3) organization.
TCCA must submit a Producer Donation Form to MDA for each eligible donation.
Tax credits could only be claimed for tax years 2017, 2018, and 2019.
A TCCA may not issue a tax credit certificate after December 31, 2019.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-profit organizations or charities wishing to accept donations under this program must first become a Tax Credit Certificate Administrator (TCCA) by completing an Application for TCCA and submitting it to MDA. Once approved, the TCCA can submit eligible food donations from qualified farms using the Producer Donation Form, sent to the MDA Marketing Office by mail or email. Note: This program has expired and no new tax credit certificates may be issued after December 31, 2019.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Food and Agricultural Resiliency Mechanism Grant Program (MFARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: The MFARM grant program helps food-insecure Marylanders access nutritious food while creating a market for local farmers and seafood providers. It provides grants to Maryland food banks, charitable emergency food providers, and nonprofits to purchase agricultural and seafood products from the Certified Local Farm and Chesapeake Invasive Species Provider Directory and deliver them to families in need. Grant funds can also cover transportation and distribution of agricultural and seafood products, as well as staff and supplies up to 20% of the grant amount.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $5,000 to a maximum of $40,000. Total funding availability is $200,000. At least 80% of funds must go toward food costs; up to 20% may be used for transportation, distribution, staff, and supplies. Payment structure: 80% upfront once the grant agreement is signed, 20% disbursed based on final program and financial report. No match requirement. Applicants must be registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and registered as a charity with the Maryland Secretary of State. A signed W-9 (signed within the past 2 years, address must match applicant org address) is required, and applicants with established producer relationships must provide a signed Letter of Support from those producers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland food banks, charitable emergency food providers, and nonprofits (including faith-based/bona fide religious organizations) focused on food insecurity and food access
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of agricultural and seafood products from the Certified Local Farm and Fish (CLFF) Directory for distribution to food-insecure Maryland residents; transportation and distribution of those products; staff and supplies (up to 20% of grant). Organizations may spend more than 80% on food. Transportation costs for product pickup are reimbursable. Grant period: July 1, 2026 – November 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be registered in Maryland; products must be sourced from the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program directory; food must be distributed to Maryland residents (not the greater DC area).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland food bank, charitable emergency food provider, or nonprofit focused on food insecurity/food access
Must be registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Nonprofits must be registered as a charity with the Maryland Secretary of State; faith-based/bona fide religious organizations must provide SoS registration status or an exemption letter on letterhead
Must submit a signed W-9 form (signed within past 2 years; address must match applicant organization address)
If applicable, must provide a signed Letter of Support from producers/seafood providers listed in the Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory demonstrating an established relationship
At least 80% of grant funds must be used for food costs; no more than 20% for transportation, distribution, staff, and supplies
Partner farm(s) must be registered in the CLFF directory and have a nutrient management plan
Food must serve Maryland residents
Must demonstrate infrastructure to support fresh, local food
Must provide quantifiable, measurable impacts with specific reach numbers
Must submit a program and financial report (sample report format available on OneStop public profile)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the OnestopMD portal at the link provided on the program page. Required documents include a signed W-9 (within past 2 years, address matching org address), Letters of Support from CLFF-registered producers, and proof of Maryland Secretary of State charity registration (or exemption letter for faith-based organizations). 80% of awarded funds are disbursed upfront upon signing the grant agreement; the remaining 20% is released after submission of a final program and financial report.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hemp Farming and Research Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A registration and licensing program operated by the Maryland Department of Agriculture for growers interested in growing industrial hemp for commercial purposes or for research. The commercial farming track registers industrial hemp growing sites and facilitates the commercial production of industrial hemp as an agricultural commodity. The research pilot track registers growers partnering with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture to conduct research into any aspect of growing, cultivating, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transporting, marketing, or selling industrial hemp. License fee is $550/site (Hemp Farming Program) or $250/site (Hemp Research Pilot Program). Licenses are issued on a calendar-year basis, valid through December 31 of the year issued. Products must comply with state and federal law; THC must remain at or below 0.3% or crop must be destroyed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides registration and licensing of industrial hemp growing sites for either commercial production or research purposes. License fee is $550/site (Hemp Farming Program) or $250/site (Hemp Research Pilot Program). Licenses are issued on a calendar-year basis, valid through December 31 of the year issued. Commercial applicants apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal. Research applicants must complete a PDF application and mail it with supporting documents to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Program provides a regulatory licensing pathway, not a grant or direct funding program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications due December 1 annually; initial applications may be submitted at any time during a calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland growers interested in growing hemp for commercial purposes, and growers interested in researching industrial hemp in partnership with a higher education institution or the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, have no felony conviction in the past 10 years, and have landowner permission if they do not own the growing site.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration of sites for growing, cultivating, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transporting, marketing, or selling industrial hemp for commercial, agricultural, industrial, or research purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions. Outdoor production sites must be located at least 1,000 feet from a school or public recreation area. All growing sites must be located in Maryland; applicants must provide GPS coordinates and county for each site.
requirements_list: Must be growing hemp for commercial purposes (commercial track) or partnering with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture for research purposes (research track)
Must be at least 18 years old
Must have no felony conviction in the past 10 years
Must obtain landowner permission if applicant does not own the growing site
Must register industrial hemp growing sites with the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Must comply with Maryland Hemp Farming Program regulations and 2018 U.S. Farm Bill provisions
Must submit FBI Criminal Background Check (report no more than 60 days old)
Must provide GPS coordinates, site map, and legal land rights documentation
Must submit Annual Production Report by December 1 each year (including acreage, planting/harvest dates, varieties, weight/type harvested, and storage location)
