Must submit Geospatial reporting to USDA Farm Service Agency
Must report any drug felony conviction to the Department within 15 days
Must maintain records for 3 years
THC testing required; crop must test at or below 0.3% delta-9 THC on a dry weight basis
Must cooperate with annual regulatory inspections
Must submit Pre-Harvest Report at least 5 days before harvest
Noncompliant hemp must be disposed of under supervision of a Department representative
Site modification applications must be submitted at least 15 days before the proposed modification
Must comply with Nutrient Management and Pesticide Regulations
Commercial applicants must apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal
Research applicants must complete a PDF application and mail it with supporting documents to the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Must partner with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture (research track)
Must obtain partnering institution signature if applicable
Must pay a $250 registration fee per site (research track) or $550 per site (commercial track)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Initial applications may be submitted at any time during a calendar year. Steps include: (1) determine hemp type (commercial or research); (2) identify research partnership with a Maryland higher education institution if applicable; (3) develop crop plan; (4) select and confirm site eligibility; (5) obtain FBI Criminal Background Check; (6) submit MDA site registration application — commercial track: apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal at onestop.md.gov; research track: complete the PDF application and mail the completed application and supporting documents to the Maryland Department of Agriculture at 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401; (7) submit background check; (8) develop nutrient management and pesticide compliance plan. Department reviews application and provides opportunity to amend insufficient submissions. Renewal applications must be submitted by December 1 to maintain continuity into the following year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A registration program for growers interested in partnering with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture to grow industrial hemp under a research program. The program facilitates research into any aspect of growing, cultivating, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transporting, marketing, or selling industrial hemp.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides registration of industrial hemp growing sites for research purposes in partnership with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture. A $250 registration fee per site is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Growers interested in researching industrial hemp in partnership with a higher education institution or the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research into growing, cultivating, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transporting, marketing, or selling industrial hemp for agricultural, industrial, or commercial purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All growing sites must be located in Maryland; applicants must provide GPS coordinates and county for each site.
requirements_list: Must partner with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Must complete a PDF application and mail it with supporting documents to the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Must submit FBI criminal history check
Must provide maps with GPS coordinates for each growing site
Must obtain partnering institution signature if applicable
Must obtain landowner signature if applicant is not the landowner
Must pay a $250 registration fee per site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the PDF application and mail the completed application and supporting documents (including FBI criminal history check and maps with GPS coordinates) along with the $250 registration fee per site to the Maryland Department of Agriculture at 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401. No online or email submission is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports Maryland's horse industry. The board promotes horse-related activities and recreation. It also supports educational projects, job training, and planning for facilities to help the local horse economy grow. The board advises the Secretary of Agriculture and licenses stables in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The board supports the horse industry through promotional activities, educational and research projects, and development efforts like job training and facilities planning. The website's navigation indicates that grants are available, but this page does not provide specific details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People and businesses in Maryland's horse industry, including horse owners and stable operators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Organic Certification Program (MOCP) is operated by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA), which is USDA-accredited as a certifying agent for farm operations in Maryland under National Organic Program (NOP) standards. Producers who grow and/or process foods sold or labeled as organic must be certified. MDA certifies under four scopes: Crops, Livestock, Wild Crops, and Handling/Processing (small-scale, on-farm only). New applicants develop an Organic System Plan (OSP), submit application forms, a $500 fee, and undergo an on-site inspection by MDA; certified producers must submit an annual OSP update and $500 renewal fee by April 1 each year. Producers grossing $5,000 or less in organic sales annually are exempt from certification but may optionally register as an exempt operation with MDA for a $30 fee; annual filing is required to maintain listing on MDA's website and in the MDA Brochure. The program also administers the Organic Certification Cost Share Program (OCCSP), which reimburses producers and handlers 75% of certification fees, up to $750 per scope, subject to available annual USDA funding. As of August 2025, USDA had not yet announced OCCSP funding for 2025. Certification provides assurance to consumers that organic products were grown according to USDA NOP standards. MOCP does not certify farms outside of Maryland, nor does it certify standalone organic processing/handling operations such as food processors, brokers, or importers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA reviews an applicant's Organic System Plan (OSP), conducts an on-site inspection, and issues an official USDA organic certificate to operations that meet National Organic Program standards under four scopes: Crops, Livestock, Wild Crops, and on-farm Handling/Processing. New applicants pay a $500 application fee; renewal/annual update fee is $500 due April 1 each year. An optional Organic Exempt Registration is available for producers grossing $5,000 or less annually for a $30 fee; annual filing is required to maintain listing on MDA's website and in the MDA Brochure. Additionally, the Organic Certification Cost Share Program (OCCSP) reimburses 75% of organic certification fees, up to a maximum of $750 per scope. Cost-share funding is subject to annual USDA appropriations; as of August 2025, USDA had not yet announced OCCSP funding for 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: New applicants may apply at any time; renewal updates due April 1 annually; cost-share applications subject to USDA funding availability annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farm operations that grow and/or process organic products and wish to sell, label, or represent their products as organic, as well as certified producers and handlers seeking cost-share reimbursement for certification fees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organic certification of farm operations under NOP standards for Crops, Livestock, Wild Crops, and on-farm Handling/Processing; reimbursement of organic certification fees paid to USDA-accredited certifiers through the OCCSP cost-share program; allows operations to market and sell products as certified organic under USDA NOP standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farm operations located in Maryland only. MOCP does not certify farms outside of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farm operation that grows and/or processes foods sold, labeled, or represented as organic
Must be located in Maryland
Must develop an Organic System Plan (OSP) in accordance with NOP standards
New applicants submit completed application forms and $500 fee
Operation must appear to be in compliance with the National Organic Program upon review of the OSP
MDA reviews the OSP for compliance with the National Organic Program
Operation must pass an on-site inspection by MDA
Certified producers must submit an annual OSP update and $500 renewal fee by April 1 each year
Operations grossing $5,000 or less in organic sales annually are exempt from certification but must still follow NOP regulations including recordkeeping
Exempt producers may optionally register with MDA for a $30 fee; annual filing required to maintain listing on MDA's website and in MDA Brochure
For cost-share (OCCSP): must be a crop or livestock operation in Maryland certified by a USDA-accredited certifier
For cost-share: must submit Cost Share Application to MDA Organic Certification Program after receiving certificate
Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer is issued a certificate
Non-MDA certified producers must be located in Maryland and submit a copy of their certification fees invoice with the cost share application
MOCP does not certify individual organic processing/handling operations (e.g., food processors, brokers, importers)
Cost-share funding is subject to annual USDA appropriations

All seed inoculants, pesticides, and other material inputs must be pre-approved by MOCP via submission of Crop Appendix B: Material Inputs List; use of prohibited materials triggers 36-month transition period
Exempt producers must maintain 3-year field history, prohibited substance documentation, recordkeeping (5 years), soil testing, and input tracking per NOP
Three-year transition period (36 months no prohibited substances) required for land compliance with NOP standards
Documented search for certified organic seed required (minimum 3 seed supplier contacts)
Recordkeeping must be maintained for 5 years per NOP §205.103
Gross agricultural income from organic sales must be $5,000 or less annually to qualify for exempt registration (NOP §205.101(a))
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For certification: (1) Complete all applicable forms in the relevant application packet (Crop and Pasture, Livestock, or On-Farm Processor/Handler), develop an Organic System Plan (OSP), and submit forms along with the $500 application fee to MDA. (2) MDA reviews the OSP for compliance with the National Organic Program. (3) If the OSP appears compliant, MDA schedules an on-site inspection. (4) MDA reviews the application and inspection report. (5) If all requirements are met, MDA issues an organic certificate. For renewals: submit the annual update packet and $500 fee by April 1 each year. For exempt producers: submit the Organic Exempt Application with a $30 fee; must be filed annually to maintain listing on MDA's website and in MDA Brochure. For cost-share reimbursement (OCCSP): after receiving your certificate, submit the Cost Share Application to the MDA Organic Certification Program. Application forms for cost-share are posted when USDA announces OCCSP funding. Contact MDA at organic.certification@maryland.gov or (410) 841-5769, 50 Harry S Truman Parkway, Annapolis MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Postharvest Infrastructure Grant Program (PHI) provides funding to establish cold storage infrastructure in Maryland rural communities to expand food aggregation and distribution capacities. Administered through the federally funded Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), the program supports local food producers and distributors handling fresh produce, dairy, grains, meat, poultry, herbs, and Maryland seafood, with the goal of improving access to nutritious, locally sourced food for rural Marylanders. Grants start at a minimum of $30,000, with total program funding of $1.6 million, and may be used for cold storage infrastructure, transportation and fleet upgrades, distribution logistics and technology, handling and loading infrastructure, and food safety modernization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available with a minimum award of $30,000 and total program funding of $1.6 million. Funds may be used for cold storage infrastructure, transportation and fleet upgrades, distribution logistics and technology, handling and loading infrastructure, and food safety modernization. Equipment purchases of $10,000 or more per unit with a useful life greater than one year are eligible, as are supplies under $5,000 per unit such as packaging, labeling, and storage materials. Agricultural producers and seafood processors are listed as priority applicants. Grantees will be notified by August 2026 (subject to CMS approval), with funds to be spent by September 30, 2027 and a project end date of June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, seafood processors, nonprofit organizations, local government entities, and institutions in Maryland rural communities seeking to improve cold storage and food distribution infrastructure. Agricultural producers and seafood processors are a priority category.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage infrastructure, transportation and fleet upgrades, distribution logistics and technology, handling and loading infrastructure, and food safety modernization. Eligible costs include equipment ($10,000 or more per unit with useful life over one year) and supplies (under $5,000 per unit) such as packaging, labeling, and storage materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to applicants operating in and serving designated Maryland rural counties: Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. All funded activities must operate in and serve a Maryland rural county.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include agricultural producers or seafood processors (priority), nonprofit organizations, local government entities, and institutions.
Minimum grant request is $30,000.
Projects must support cold chain or distribution improvements for local food products including fresh produce, dairy, grains, meat, poultry, herbs, or Maryland seafood.
All funded activities must operate in and serve a designated Maryland rural county.
Food banks interested in cold storage should contact the Maryland Food Bank directly rather than applying through this program.
Agricultural producers and seafood processors are a priority category.
Applications must be complete; incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

Projects will be evaluated and scored based on feasibility and impact on the health of rural Marylanders, including a 10-point criterion for whether the project clearly takes place in or directly serves a designated rural area.
Funds must be spent by September 30, 2027; project end date is June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the GrantInterface portal. Download and review the Request for Proposals (RFP). A virtual information session was held on May 27, 2026 from 2–3 p.m. EST. Submit application by June 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Grantees will be notified by August 2026 (subject to CMS approval).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Spay and Neuter Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Established by Maryland Senate Bill 820 in 2013, the Maryland Spay and Neuter Grant Program is a competitive grant program that reduces the number of animals surrendered to and euthanized in shelters by funding free spay and neuter surgeries for dogs and cats. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) provides grants to local animal welfare organizations and government entities statewide, which administer the services directly to eligible recipients. Two grant tracks are offered: (1) a Pet Focused Grant for owned-pet services targeting low-income families seeking free spay/neuter for their cats or dogs, and (2) a Feral Cat Focused Grant providing free spay/neuter for free-roaming, unowned, and feral cats. Organizations may apply for one or both tracks per cycle. Surgeries may also include a free rabies vaccine. Funding comes entirely from fees paid by pet food manufacturers who sell products in Maryland — not from taxpayer dollars. In FY26, 38 projects received a total of $1,001,665 to fund 14,444 spay and neuter surgeries. The FY27 cycle had an estimated total funding of approximately $850,000, with individual awards ranging from $5,000 to $75,000. The grant application window for organizations typically opens in early January and closes in early April each year (the FY27 window opened January 16, 2026 and closed April 17, 2026; the FY28 RFP is expected late December 2026 with the window opening January 2027). MDA does not provide funding directly to individuals. In Queen Anne's County, the program is administered through Queen Anne's County Animal Services (phone: 410-827-7178), which requires an annual household income under $60,000 and submission of an application with required documents. Note: The enabling legislation (SB 820) included a sunset clause; text in the bill contains apparent redline marks indicating either a 6- or 9-year term (sunset Sept 30, 2019 or Sept 30, 2022). The program appears to have continued operating beyond that date based on documented FY26 and FY27 grant cycles, suggesting reauthorization or continuation occurred.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually to local governments and qualifying nonprofit animal welfare organizations. Two grant tracks are available: a Pet Focused Grant for spay/neuter services (and sometimes rabies vaccines) for pets of low-income Marylanders (household income under $60,000), and a Feral Cat Focused Grant for programs serving unowned or free-roaming community cats. In the FY26 cycle, 38 projects received a total of $1,001,665 to fund 14,444 spay and neuter surgeries. The FY27 cycle had an estimated total funding of approximately $850,000, with individual awards ranging from $5,000 to $75,000. Funding is disbursed in two allocations: the first (50% of surgery funding plus 100% of rabies vaccine and other applicable funding) arrives in mid-to-late December; the second (remaining 50% of surgery funding) is released once the grantee has spent 35% of their budget. Grant projects typically run from January 1 through December 31 of the grant year, or until funding is exhausted. This is a supplemental grant and not intended to be the sole or primary funding source. The grant application window typically opens in early January and closes in early April each year. Low-income pet owners access free spay/neuter surgery (and sometimes a free rabies vaccine) by contacting a local MDA-funded organization directly. In Queen Anne's County, residents with annual household income under $60,000 may apply directly through Queen Anne's County Animal Services by downloading and submitting the Spay Neuter Grant application form.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 application window opened January 16, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST and closed April 17, 2026 at 5:01 PM EST; FY27 RFP was posted December 18, 2025. FY28 cycle expected to open in January 2027. Individual services are active as long as grant funds allow.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government animal shelters and 501(c)3 nonprofit animal welfare organizations in Maryland seeking to provide free spay and neuter services for low-income pet owners or for unowned/feral cats; also low-income pet owners and residents (household income under $60,000) who can access services through participating local organizations, including Queen Anne's County residents who may apply directly through Queen Anne's County Animal Services (410-827-7178).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free spay and neuter surgeries (all-inclusive: materials, veterinary services, pre/post-operative care) for pets of low-income Marylanders or unowned free-roaming community cats; rabies vaccines; transportation assistance for pet owners/caretakers; outreach and education materials; equipment (durable goods, up to $5,000 cumulative per application); emergency medical expenses (max 5% of grant budget, coordinator-approved). Prohibited uses include overhead, office equipment, uniforms, capital campaigns, large construction projects, and promotional giveaways (except pamphlets and educational materials).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland where active MDA-funded projects exist. Applying organizations and veterinary clinics do not need to be based in Maryland, but all animals and owners receiving services must reside in Maryland. Active projects cover Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties, among others. Community cat projects are currently active in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Projects may cover specific areas or zip codes within those counties. In Queen Anne's County, residents must live within Queen Anne's County and may apply directly through Queen Anne's County Animal Services.
requirements_list: Applicant organization must be a local government or a qualifying 501(c)3 nonprofit animal welfare organization
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Nonprofit applicants that fundraise in Maryland must have a current Maryland Charitable Solicitation Permit
Applicants with animal shelters in Maryland must comply with the Maryland Animal Shelter Standards of Care
Must submit a signed W-9 dated within six months of the application date
Program must facilitate and promote spay and neuter services for cats or dogs
Must serve either low-income pet owners (owned pets track) or unowned/feral cats (feral cat track)
Must comply with COMAR 15.01.10 regulations for the Spay/Neuter Grant Program
Services must be provided to pets of low-income Marylanders (Pet Focused) or unowned free-roaming cats (Feral Cat Focused) — not to shelter or rescue animals prior to placement
Only one application per grant type (Pet Focused or Feral Cat Focused) per organization per cycle
This is a supplemental grant and not intended to be the sole or primary funding source
Grantees must submit Quarterly Grant Progress Reports and a Final Report if funded
Program does not fund individuals directly — eligible residents must contact a participating local organization
Services for owned pets may be limited to specific areas or zip codes within listed counties
Funding is limited and projects are active only as long as funds allow
Pet owner must be low-income (income eligibility verified by the participating organization)
Annual household income under $60,000 (for individual pet owners accessing services, including in Queen Anne's County)
Services available for owned cats and/or dogs (one project is dogs only)
Projects cover specific areas or zip codes — not all of a county may be covered
Queen Anne's County residents may apply directly to Queen Anne's County Animal Services using the Spay Neuter Grant application form available on the Animal Services Forms page
Must reside in Queen Anne's County to apply through Queen Anne's County Animal Services
Must submit the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application and required documents (for Queen Anne's County applicants)
Applications are competitive and reviewed by the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board
No co-pays permitted for recipients; sterilization cost must be all-inclusive
Equipment requests capped at $5,000 cumulative unless justification provided
Outreach expenses over $1,000 must be well-justified; price quotes required for items $500 or more
Emergency medical expenses capped at 5% of budget; must be submitted within 60 days of service
Veterinarian/clinic must be in good standing with the state veterinary board
Feral cat projects must comply with local jurisdiction laws regarding feral cat colonies and TNR (trap-neuter-return) best management practices
Ear-tipping or microchipping of altered cats required for feral cat projects
Coordination with local animal control and shelters required for feral cat projects
Must contact a participating local organization to verify eligibility and availability
Community cat services are limited to free-roaming, unowned, or feral cats
Funding is not available directly to individual pet owners
Mandatory 3-year shelter intake/euthanasia data for target area required for organizational applicants
Must provide Point of Contact with public-facing contact info
Must include detailed target area map(s) with notations
Must provide letters of support from local animal control/shelters
Applicants must demonstrate net increase in surgeries over baseline for prior grantees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Request for Proposals (RFP) is posted in mid-to-late December each year. For the FY27 cycle, the RFP was posted December 18, 2025, and the application window opened January 16, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST and closed April 17, 2026 at 5:01 PM EST. For organizations: Read the Guidelines and Instructions documents carefully before applying. Gather required documentation including a signed W-9, SDAT good standing confirmation, charitable registration permit (if applicable), and shelter statistics. Submit the application during the open window. After submission, no changes or resubmissions are allowed. The Program Coordinator conducts due diligence (April–May), the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board (SNAB) reviews and scores applications (May–July), and meets in August to make funding recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture. Applicants are notified in August–September, and grant contracts are signed in September–October. MDA sends grant agreements to recipients usually within 30 days following approval. For individuals seeking free services: Check the list of active MDA-funded projects on the program page to find a participating organization in your county and contact them directly to confirm availability and eligibility. Queen Anne's County residents with household income under $60,000 may download and complete the Spay Neuter Grant application form from the Animal Services Forms page (https://www.qac.org/1436/Forms) and submit it to Queen Anne's County Animal Services (410-827-7178) to be contacted for scheduling. If no project covers your area, contact your local animal shelter or nonprofit animal welfare organization for other low-cost options. Contact Jen Swanson at jen.swanson@maryland.gov or (410) 841-5766 with any questions before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Specialty Crop Block Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) awards competitive grants to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops, including fruits and vegetables, culinary herbs and spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees, and nursery crops. Projects must demonstrate broader industry impact beyond a single organization or producer. MDA administers funding received from the USDA Specialty Crop Block Grant Program (SCBGP) and conducts an annual competitive review process guided by industry, nonprofit, and government stakeholders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funded by the USDA Specialty Crop Block Grant Program. Approximately $400,000 in funding is anticipated to be available. Grant funds must comply with USDA General Terms and Conditions (effective December 31, 2025). Projects must benefit a broader group of producers or an industry segment, not just a single entity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Specialty crop producers, nonprofits, government entities, and others working to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops including fruits, vegetables, herbs, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees, and nursery crops.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops and benefit a broader group of similar producers or an industry segment. Allowable costs include supplies and materials (including computing devices under $5,000), training required to meet project objectives, and domestic and foreign travel (when in approved budget or with prior written approval, within GSA Federal Travel Regulation rates if no formal org policy exists). Allowable and unallowable costs are defined in program documents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate broader impact for a group of similar producers or an industry segment — not just a single organization, business, institution, or individual
Proposals by individual producers must show potential impact beyond the single producer
Grant awardees are subject to USDA General Terms and Conditions (effective December 31, 2025)
Applicants are strongly encouraged to review USDA General Terms and Conditions before applying
Must complete SCBGP Project Profile Template in full (mandatory for grant funding consideration)
If approved for State Plan, template forwarded to USDA for final review
All required fields (marked with red asterisks) must be completed before submission

Travel costs must either be in approved budget or have prior written approval; must align with legislated program purpose; non-profit orgs with formal travel policies may use those; for-profits and orgs without policies capped at GSA rates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov/). Register, search for 'Maryland Specialty Crop Block Grant Application,' complete the 4-page form, upload the required SCBGP Project Profile Template, submit, and receive confirmation. Applicants can save drafts and revise before final submission. A Financial Capability Questionnaire is also required. Grant reports are due November 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland WIC Farmers' Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) and Fruit and Vegetable Benefits (FVB) Authorization
structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA-funded nutrition subsidy program jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in partnership with the Maryland Department of Aging. The program provides annual benefits to Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) recipients and low-resource seniors to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers markets and farm stands. WIC FMNP provides $30 per participant per market season; WIC Fruit and Vegetable Benefits (FVB) provide monthly benefits of $26 for children, $47 for pregnant women, and $52 for breastfeeding mothers. Senior FMNP participants receive $35 annually. Benefits are redeemable between June 1 and November 30. Farmers and farmers markets can apply to become authorized vendors to accept these benefits. FMNP benefits are processed through the Healthy Together app; FVBs are processed through the free S3 Merchant Link app (no setup, transaction, or cancellation fees and no additional equipment required). An alternative processor (TotilPay) is also accepted at no charge. Authorized farmers receive an FMNP Farmer Handbook, FMNP posters, pricing signs, and 'Maryland WIC Accepted Here' signage. The program is available statewide at 100+ authorized farmers markets throughout Maryland across all 24 counties. Farmers who are already FMNP-authorized can apply to also accept WIC FVBs as electronic benefits using the S3 Merchant Link app.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorized farmers can redeem WIC participant benefits for fresh fruits and vegetables sold at farmers' markets and farm stands. FMNP benefits provide $30 per WIC participant per market season (redeemable through November 30). Senior FMNP participants receive $35 annually. FVBs provide monthly benefits of $26 (children), $47 (pregnant women), or $52 (breastfeeding mothers). Farmers use the Healthy Together app to process FMNP benefits and the free S3 Merchant Link app to process electronic WIC (eWIC) FVBs — no setup, transaction, or cancellation fees and no additional equipment required. An alternative processor (TotilPay) is also accepted at no charge. Participants can present a phone barcode or printed 30-day barcode; the farmer scans it with the app. Payments to farmers are made via ACH deposit 2 business days after settlement. There is no cost or deadline for farmers to participate. Authorized farmers receive an FMNP Farmer Handbook, FMNP posters, pricing signs, and 'Maryland WIC Accepted Here' signage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline to participate; 2026 senior application opens June 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: WIC recipients (children, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers), low-resource seniors, and Maryland farmers/farmers markets interested in becoming authorized vendors to accept FMNP and WIC FVB benefits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and redemption of WIC and senior participant benefits for fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers markets and farm stands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland at 100+ authorized farmers markets across all 24 counties, including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying WIC participant or low-resource senior to receive benefits
Farmers must be authorized by the Maryland State Department of Agriculture to accept FMNP benefits before applying to accept WIC FVBs
Farmers must attend a Maryland Department of Agriculture training session
Farmers must complete the farmer application on Maryland's One Stop (MDOneStop)
Farmers must sign the Farmer Agreement electronically once approved
Farmers must download the Healthy Together app to accept FMNP benefits
Farmers must download and use the S3 Merchant Link app to process WIC FVBs
Farmers must contact Andrea Tompkins at andrea.tompkins@maryland.gov to sign up for the S3 Merchant Link app to accept WIC FVBs
Farmers must have a smartphone or tablet with Android v5.0+ or iOS v14.0+ and a cellular data connection
No separate POS machine needed; app has a built-in barcode scanner
Farmers must have an ACH banking account for payments
WIC participants sign up during clinic appointments
Seniors can apply online starting June 1 or connect with their local Area Agency on Aging
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers: (1) Attend a Maryland Department of Agriculture training session (sign up via MDOneStop). (2) Complete the Farmer Application Package on Maryland's One Stop portal. (3) Once reviewed and approved, sign the Farmer Agreement electronically via Maryland's One Stop. (4) Download the Healthy Together app to accept FMNP benefits. (5) To also accept WIC FVBs, contact Andrea Tompkins (andrea.tompkins@maryland.gov); she will forward your information to Solutran (S3 Merchant Link provider), and you will receive an email invitation to sign up via the S3 Merchant Link app (free, no deadline). Seniors: Apply online at mda.maryland.gov starting June 1 or contact local Area Agency on Aging. WIC participants: Sign up during clinic appointments beginning in June.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland farmers and agricultural producers find and create profitable markets for their products. It supports them in selling locally, nationally, and internationally.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides marketing services to connect consumers with local Maryland products. It helps farmers find new buyers and provides information on federal resources and agricultural policies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers can use this program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides farmers and landowners with incentive payments to plant streamside buffers on farmland to improve the health of local streams and the Chesapeake Bay. Three types of buffers are eligible: forest buffers planted next to waterways, grass buffers planted next to waterways or field ditches, and watercourse access control areas adjacent to pastures. New riparian forest buffers qualify for a one-time bonus payment per acre. Contracts run for 5 or 10 years. Local soil conservation districts provide free technical assistance. Applications are accepted during an annual open enrollment period (November 1 through April 30).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of the project cost up front and 25% after verification of planting. A one-time bonus payment of $1,000 per acre is available for enrolled forest buffers, plus up to $330 per acre per year for maintenance during the first five years of the contract. Local soil conservation districts provide free technical assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual open enrollment period: November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners responsible for the management of eligible agricultural lands adjacent to streams, ditches, or floodplains in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and maintenance of streamside grass buffers, riparian forest buffers, and watercourse access control areas on eligible farmland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, available through local soil conservation districts. Eligible land must be cropland or pasture next to a stream or ditch, or areas adjacent to watercourses with highly erodible or hydric soils as determined by the local soil conservation district.
requirements_list: Farmers and landowners who are responsible for the management of eligible lands may apply.
Must be a farmer or rural landowner in Maryland.
Farmers who lease land must certify an active lease for the term of the buffer or provide an agreement from the landowner.
Farmers and landowners must be in good standing with USDA and state cost-share programs.
A current Nutrient Management Plan Certification is required and must be submitted with the application.
Eligible land must have an established cropping history in pasture, commodity crops, or hay.
Existing buffers or agricultural lands actively enrolled in state (MACS) or federal programs (CRP, CREP, EQIP, etc.) or mandated by an easement are not eligible.
Field ditches are not eligible for woody (tree/shrub) conservation buffers.
Planting must occur within 1 year of the signed agreement.
Must apply during the annual open enrollment period (November 1 through April 30).
Contact local soil conservation district to apply.
All landowners on property deed(s) must sign agreement.
Signed W-9 form required (legal name and address must match application).
Color map and acreage/location documentation with roads and waterbodies marked required.
Authorization documents (Certificate of Resolution, Power of Attorney, Certificate of Sole Proprietor, or Trust Agreement as applicable) required where relevant.
Agricultural operation must follow a current Nutrient Management Plan to the extent required by COMAR 15.20.07.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district during the annual open enrollment period (November 1 through April 30) to apply. Download and complete the application form, and submit it along with a map showing the location and acreage of the buffer, a signed Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form, and a signed IRS Form W-9. Applications are accepted on a first come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that supports Maryland farmers and organizations working with farmers to implement innovative soil health conservation practices. Grants fund projects that minimize soil disturbance, maximize soil cover, enhance biodiversity, and increase living roots. Eligible practices include cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture planting, prescribed grazing, nutrient management, and agroforestry practices such as silvopasture, windbreak establishment, alley cropping, and critical area plantings to improve soil health and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $50,000 per selected applicant to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices. Up to 30% of funds are disbursed upfront after agreement signing; the remainder is distributed annually in spring upon verification of progress (4 total payments). Funds may be used for implementation of conservation practices, equipment purchases (rental or used preferred), project staff time directly related to project implementation, and research costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application period for the 2025-2026 Program ran November 3, 2025 – January 9, 2026 (mailed applications postmarked by January 6, 2026) and is now closed. Grant award recipients will be contacted on or around March 30, 2026. Open enrollment typically begins in November/January and runs for approximately 8 weeks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers (individuals or groups) and individuals or organizations that work with Maryland farmers to implement conservation practices and improve soil health and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of soil health conservation practices including cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture and hay planting, adaptive/prescribed grazing, nutrient management, agroforestry practices (silvopasture, windbreak establishment, alley cropping, critical area plantings), woody plant establishment (trees and shrubs), grass and forb establishment, equipment purchases (rental or used preferred), project staff time directly related to project implementation, and research costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural operations must be operating in Maryland. Program is available statewide to all Maryland counties. No county exclusions. No minimum or maximum acreage requirements.
requirements_list: No minimum or maximum acreage requirements
Open to individual farmers, groups of farmers, or individuals/organizations working with Maryland farmers

Agricultural operation must have gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more in donated agricultural products for non-profits) and/or manage 8 or more animal units (8,000 pounds of live animal weight)
Applicants must submit a Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form showing compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements at time of application
Must apply during the annual open enrollment period (typically beginning in November/January, approximately 8 weeks)
Application is competitive
Program has been operating since its inception in 2023; has funded 53 projects across the state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the application and required forms during the annual open enrollment period. Applications may be submitted via email (as Word or PDF attachment) or by mail. Required documents include the Project Narrative, Project Budget, and any applicable practice templates (Cover Crop, Grazing, Tree & Shrub Planting, Grass & Forb Planting). Download all documents to your device before completing. Grant awards are announced on or around March 30 following the application period.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture and University of Maryland Extension offer a statewide schedule of nutrient management training courses, seminars, voucher training, certification exams, and online webinars for farmers, consultants, and natural resource personnel. Training covers agricultural and turfgrass nutrient management, soil science, nutrient management planning software, and Maryland nutrient management regulations. Participants can earn continuing education units (CEUs) and prepare for the Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Examination. The program also supports Professional Fertilizer Applicator (PFA) certification and recertification through exams and recorded webinars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost in-person classes, workshops, and recorded webinars covering nutrient management planning, soil science, and state regulations. The Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Examination is offered for a $50 fee (government personnel exempt). The Professional Fertilizer Applicator (PFA) Certification Exam is offered for a $100 fee and consists of a 50-question multiple-choice exam with a 70% pass threshold; applicants may attempt the exam up to three times or within 3 months, whichever comes first. A review session is offered prior to the exam. Participants can earn CEUs and PFA credits toward certification renewal. Training is available in-person and virtually throughout the year. Recorded webinars offer 1–2 PFA continuing education credits upon quiz completion and submission within 3 business days of viewing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Various dates through December 3, 2026; PFA exam applications accepted on a rolling basis before any announced examination
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural consultants, turfgrass professionals, natural resource personnel, Professional Fertilizer Applicators (PFA), landscaping/lawn care business employees, government agency employees, and anyone seeking Maryland Nutrient Management or Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certification
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in nutrient management planning, soil science, Maryland nutrient management regulations, and Professional Fertilizer Applicator (PFA) certification and recertification
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — sessions held at various Maryland locations including Annapolis, Derwood, Boonsboro, Salisbury, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Washington County, and Easton; some sessions available virtually
requirements_list: Farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres must complete a 2-hour voucher training every three years
Nutrient Management Certification exam requires a $50 fee (government personnel exempt with a Government Sales and Use Tax Exempt certificate)

Professional Fertilizer Applicator (PFA) Certification Exam requires a $100 fee plus a completed PFA certification application form and Fertilizer Application Business License (MDA-F) number or business license application ($50) and photo ID
PFA exam: 50-question multiple-choice format with a 70% pass threshold; maximum 3 attempts or within 3 months, whichever comes first
PFA certification and business licenses expire December 31 of each year — annual renewal required
Participants in software update sessions must be familiar with a keyboard and computer
Fundamentals of Nutrient Management Training is recommended for those planning to take the certification exam
For recorded webinar PFA credits: must answer all quiz items correctly and submit within 3 business days of viewing
Webinar quiz submissions must include: printed name, PFA number (as shown on certificate), signature, date completed, and contact information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for individual sessions via the links provided on the page (Eventbrite, Google Forms, or UME Extension website). For the Nutrient Management Certification exam, complete the online registration form. For the Professional Fertilizer Applicator (PFA) Certification Exam, submit a completed PFA certification application form with the $100 exam fee, your Fertilizer Application Business License (MDA-F) number or a business license application ($50), and a photo ID to MDA before any announced examination date. For recorded webinars, access them directly online, complete the associated quiz correctly, and mail the signed form to Maryland Department of Agriculture, Nutrient Management Program, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Room 201, Annapolis, MD 21401 within 3 business days of viewing to earn PFA continuing education credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service for current or retired farmers and producers in Maryland to safely dispose of unwanted or unusable pesticides. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) collects any EPA- or USDA-registered pesticide product and unknown materials (which are sampled and tested first), then arranges for a licensed hazardous waste hauler to transport materials from the farm to an EPA-approved disposal facility (incinerator or hazardous waste landfill). Commercial businesses may also be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free pesticide collection and disposal service. MDA inspectors conduct a site visit to verify inventory, then contract a licensed hazardous waste hauler to pick up pesticide materials directly from the storage site and transport them to an EPA-approved disposal facility (incinerator or hazardous waste landfill). Program is funded by licensing, certification, and registration fees collected from pesticide businesses, certified applicators, and manufacturers. Commercial businesses may be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost. Homeowners and commercial dealers are excluded (dealers directed to contact the section for case-by-case review).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or retired farmers and producers, including orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers; individuals who purchased farms with legacy pesticides; commercial businesses may also be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost. Homeowners and commercial dealers are excluded.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of unwanted, unused, banned, or expired pesticide materials stored on farm or production sites, at no cost to participants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, covering all 23 counties and Baltimore City; registration does not guarantee pick-up as MDA reviews registrations and determines which areas will be serviced based on regional capacity
requirements_list: Must be a current or retired farmer or producer (including orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, Christmas tree growers)
Individuals who purchased farms with legacy pesticides may also be eligible
Homeowners and commercial dealers are excluded
Pesticide must have an EPA or USDA registration number, or be identifiable as a pesticide
Unknown materials will be sampled and tested by MDA before collection
Must complete and submit a registration form to MDA's Pesticide Regulation Section
An MDA inspector will conduct a site visit to verify information
Commercial businesses may be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost
Program is strictly voluntary with no regulatory impacts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the fillable PDF registration form. Submit by email to rob.hofstetter@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Agriculture, Pesticide Regulation Section, 50 Harry S Truman Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21401. An MDA inspector will then schedule a site visit to verify pesticide inventory before collection is arranged. Operations not chosen for the current program cycle will be notified and placed on a waiting list.

structured_extraction.program_name: Poultry and Rabbit On-Farm Processing Certification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary statewide certification program for Maryland producers who slaughter and process poultry and rabbits on their farm. Certified producers are recognized as an approved source by the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, allowing them to sell whole and cut poultry and rabbit directly to consumers, restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets anywhere in Maryland (intrastate). Participation requires attending MDA training, following basic program requirements, and allowing MDA to conduct inspections. Eligible species include chickens, turkeys, domestic duck, domestic geese, other poultry, and rabbits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification program that grants approved-source status to qualified on-farm poultry and rabbit producers. Includes mandatory online self-paced training (~6 hours, pass open-book exam ≥80%) offered through University of Maryland Extension and MDA, periodic MDA inspections, and a certification credential that expands legal sales channels statewide. An annual fee of $75.00 is required. Eligible species include chickens, turkeys, domestic duck, domestic geese, other poultry, and rabbits. If exam score is below 80%, applicant must attend a review session before certification is issued.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; course is self-paced and offered continuously
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and producers who slaughter and process poultry (up to 20,000 birds annually) or rabbits of their own production and wish to sell beyond the farm gate to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification allows producers to sell poultry and rabbit products (whole and parts, not ground) to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets anywhere in Maryland (intrastate sales only).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to producers throughout Maryland for intrastate sales only. No county or regional restrictions; applicant county is a required field on the application form. Program administered under the Annotated Code of Maryland, Agriculture Article §§10-601 et seq.
requirements_list: At least one person from each facility must attend MDA training (online self-paced course, approximately 6 hours)
Pass open-book exam with a score of at least 80%; if below 80%, must attend review session before certification is issued
Submit certification application with a $75.00 annual fee and a sample label for approval
Follow basic program requirements including written GMP, SSOP, and HACCP plans
Allow MDA access to conduct inspections
Slaughter/process no more than 20,000 poultry of own production annually (federal FSIS exemption threshold); intrastate sales only
Meat cannot be ground
Health and biosecurity standards: no sick animals, rodent and contamination control
Potable water only; annual water testing required
Adequate lighting for night/enclosed operations
Personnel hygiene and health restrictions
Food-grade packaging and labeling required (name, address, Maryland number, net weight, 'Exempt PL-90-492', slaughter date, safe handling instructions)
Offal and wastewater disposal controls
Recordkeeping: slaughter dates, animal counts, sick animals, sales records and invoices
Intrastate sales only (Maryland)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the On-Farm Rabbit/Poultry Processing Application and pay the $75.00 annual fee. Register for and complete the required online self-paced training course (offered through University of Maryland Extension and MDA; no registration deadline — course is offered continuously). Pass the open-book exam with at least 80% (if below 80%, attend a review session before certification is issued). Submit a sample label for approval. MDA will conduct inspections to verify compliance. Renewals require submission of the On-Farm Rabbit/Poultry Renewal Application annually (renewal deadline has historically been June 30). Mail applications to: Food Quality Assurance Program, Maryland Department of Agriculture, P.O. Box 17304, Baltimore, MD 21297-1304. Office address: 50 Harry S. Truman Pkwy, Suite 449, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_name: Registration of Service Agencies and Service Technicians
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture registers service agencies and service technicians who install, service, or repair commercial weighing and measuring devices. Registration allows technicians and agencies to legally place commercial devices into service and appear on a published list available to businesses that use commercial weighing or measuring equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Service agencies pay a biennial registration fee of $250 and service technicians pay a biennial registration fee of $75. Applicants can attend in-person Meters or Scales classes ($25 fee) at MDA headquarters in Annapolis, or take NCWM Registered Service Agent exams (proctored in-person at MDA for $25, or virtually for $20; NCWM member exam fee is $50, non-member is $100). Upon passing the qualifying exam and completing registration, applicants receive a registration number and certificate (agencies) or wallet-size ID registration (technicians).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and individuals who install, service, or repair commercial weighing and measuring devices, such as gasoline stations, grocery stores, meat markets, and other commercial operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to legally install, service, or repair commercial weighing and measuring devices and appear on the Department's published list of registered agencies and technicians.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Classes held at MDA headquarters, 50 Harry S. Truman Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21401.
requirements_list: Complete and submit the appropriate application form (New Service Agency or New Service Technician)
Service agencies must provide a copy of their test/service report forms

Service agencies must provide a copy of ALL current certifications of traceable standards approved by the Maryland Weights and Measures Laboratory, NIST, or other NIST-approved state metrology laboratory
Service technicians must work for a registered Service Agency
Applicants must pass a qualifying examination (State of Maryland RSA class/test or NCWM RSA exam)
Pay biennial registration fee: $250 for service agencies, $75 for service technicians
Agencies must renew registration on a biennial basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the applicable application form (New Service Agency or New Service Technician) and email it to the MDA Weights and Measures office. Submit required certificates and supporting documents including copy of ALL current certifications of traceable standards from a NIST-approved state lab. State Weights and Measures personnel will review the materials and notify applicants of any deficiencies. Attend and pass the qualifying exam (in-person class or NCWM online exam at https://www.ncwm.com/rsa-program). Pay the biennial registration fee. Upon approval, receive a registration number and certificate or ID card.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilient Food Systems Infrastructure (RFSI) Program builds resilience in the middle of the food supply chain by supporting aggregation, processing, storage, transportation, wholesaling, and distribution of local food products. The program aims to provide better markets for small farms and food businesses, support value-added product development, encourage fair prices and wages, and create safe job opportunities. Maryland's Department of Agriculture administers $3.8 million in federal USDA funding as subawards to eligible applicants across the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant tracks are available: (1) Infrastructure Equipment Grants ranging from $100,000 to $3 million per award, and (2) Simplified Equipment-Only Grants ranging from $10,000 to $100,000. Projects run for three years. Applicants must provide a 50% match of the total proposed project cost. Historically underserved farmers and ranchers and qualifying small businesses (small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and veteran-owned small businesses) need only a 25% match. Grants are reimbursement-based; funds awarded no earlier than August 1, 2024. Infrastructure funding period ends May 1, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food businesses, farms, agricultural producers and processors, cooperatives, nonprofits, local governments, tribal governments, and institutions (schools, universities, hospitals) involved in the aggregation, processing, storage, transportation, wholesaling, and distribution of local food products including specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, and aquaculture. Historically underserved farmers and ranchers and qualifying small businesses receive reduced match requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage equipment; expanding capacity for processing, aggregation, and distribution; construction of new facilities; employee training; modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and information technology systems; special-purpose equipment (minimum $5,000); installation and shipping costs; facility construction/renovation; refrigerated vehicles (farm-to-processor only). Funds may not be used for meat and poultry processing, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, fiber, landscaping, tobacco, or dietary supplements. Not allowable: land/building acquisition, employee housing, general-purpose equipment, vehicles for general use, or projects already funded by other federal awards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants' facilities must be physically located within Maryland. All applicant businesses and organizations must be domestically owned. Applicants doing business along the Maryland border should only apply in one state to avoid duplication of federal funds. No specific county, municipality, or regional restrictions apply; the entire state of Maryland is eligible.
requirements_list: Projects must relate to aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, or distribution of local food products

Eligible products include specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, aquaculture, and other food products (excluding meat and poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, fiber, landscaping, tobacco, and dietary supplements)
Infrastructure Grant minimum award request: $100,000; maximum award request: $3 million
Equipment-Only Grant minimum award request: $10,000; maximum award request: $100,000
Applicants must provide a 50% cost match (reduced to 25% for historically underserved farmers/ranchers and qualifying SBA small businesses)
Projects are for a three-year period
Applicants' facilities must be physically located within Maryland
All applicant businesses and organizations must be domestically owned
Must include a completed USDA AMS Applicant Environmental Questionnaire with application
Agricultural producers applying for Infrastructure Grant must have a Maryland nutrient management plan
Applicants must obtain a UEI (Unique Entity Identifier) from SAM.gov prior to completing their application (no cost)
Must be in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
Letters of support from producers required (three letters recommended for individual applicants)
Current MDA licenses required for Maryland producers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either the Infrastructure Equipment Grant application or the Equipment Grant Only application along with required documents: USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire, Match Verification Template Letter, Evidence of Critical Resources and Infrastructure Template Letter, and RFSI Budget-Match Worksheet. Also required: W9, three letters of support, Good Standing screenshot, and construction documents if applicable. See the RFSI RFP (updated 1/22/24) for full instructions. Applications were submitted via email to RFSI.MDA@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Farmers' Market Nutrition Program (SFMNP) provides coupons or benefit cards to eligible low-income older adults (age 60 and over) to purchase locally grown fresh vegetables, fruits, honey, and cut herbs at authorized farmers' markets, roadside stands, and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) programs. The program promotes healthy eating, supports local farmers, and increases awareness and use of Maryland farmers' markets. It is administered statewide through county-level Area Agencies on Aging and other partners, with coordination by the Maryland Department of Agriculture. In Anne Arundel County, the program is managed by the Department of Aging and Disabilities, with coupons distributed on a first-come, first-served basis and electronic payments available through the Healthy Together app. In Montgomery County, the program is administered through the Office of Food Systems Resilience, with applications opening June 1, 2026 for the 2026 season. In Baltimore City, eligible older adults receive a $35 benefit card (treated as cash) redeemable at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers throughout Maryland, distributed on a first-come, first-served basis at senior centers during scheduled distribution dates (June 2 – July 2, 2026 for the 2026 season); cards are valid July 1 – November 30, 2026. In Howard County, approved participants receive a card loaded with $50 to purchase fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, herbs, and honey at authorized farmers' markets and roadside stands, with benefits usable between June 1 and November 30.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Coupons or benefit cards are issued to eligible seniors aged 60 and over to purchase locally grown fresh vegetables, fruits, honey, and cut herbs at authorized farmers' markets, roadside stands, and CSA programs. The standard benefit is $50 per eligible person per year (one card per person per year), valid July 1 through June 30 of the following year in Anne Arundel County. In Anne Arundel County, coupons are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis; applicants are notified within 15 business days of submission, and electronic payment options may be available via the Healthy Together app. In Montgomery County, applications open June 1, 2026 for the 2026 season. In Baltimore City, eligible older adults receive a $35 card (treated as cash, one-time use) distributed in person at participating senior centers on a first-come, first-served basis during scheduled distribution dates (June 2 – July 2, 2026); cards are valid July 1 – November 30, 2026 at designated farmers' markets and approved farm stands throughout Maryland; a proxy designee may obtain cards for an eligible older adult (limit of 2 cards per proxy, Baltimore City); cards cannot be replaced if lost. In Howard County, approved participants receive a card loaded with $50; benefits can be used between June 1 and November 30 and do not roll over.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Anne Arundel County: apply online beginning May 15th; Montgomery County: applications open June 1, 2026; Baltimore City: cards distributed June 2 – July 2, 2026, while supplies last (first-come, first-served); 2026 cards valid July 1 – November 30, 2026; Howard County: apply starting May 19, 2025, supplies are limited, apply early; Anne Arundel County 2025 benefit cards valid July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income older adults age 60 and over in Maryland, including residents of Anne Arundel County, Montgomery County, Baltimore City, and Howard County (household income at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of locally grown fresh fruits, vegetables, honey, cut herbs, and other eligible food items at authorized farmers' markets, roadside stands, CSA programs, and approved farm stands throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Area Agencies on Aging; specifically documented in Anne Arundel County, Montgomery County, Baltimore City, and Howard County, and across all 24 Maryland counties. Baltimore City applicants must be Baltimore City residents; Howard County applicants must be current Howard County residents. Cards can be used at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers/farm stands throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older (proof of age required)
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be low-income: household income at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines
Must meet eligibility criteria established by the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Coupons/benefit cards available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last
Must use coupons/benefit cards at participating/authorized farmers' markets, roadside stands, or CSA programs
One card per person per year maximum (prior year card holders must surrender existing card if applicable)
Baltimore City applicants must be Baltimore City residents (proof of residence required)
Howard County applicants must be current residents of Howard County
Proxy designee may obtain cards on behalf of an eligible older adult (limit of 2 cards per proxy, Baltimore City)
Cards cannot be replaced if lost (Baltimore City)
Online applicants (Baltimore City) must still pick up their card at a designated senior center site
Howard County benefits do not roll over and must be used between June 1 and November 30
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Statewide applicants may apply through their local Area Agency on Aging or at mda.maryland.gov. In Anne Arundel County, complete the application (available in English, Spanish, and Korean) and submit by visiting a local Senior Activity Center, emailing senior_nutrition@aacounty.org, or mailing to the Senior Nutrition Program at 7320 Ritchie HWY, Glen Burnie, MD 21061; accepted applicants are notified within 15 business days. In Montgomery County, eligible adults aged 60 and over can apply beginning June 1, 2026 by visiting the Maryland Department of Agriculture website or contacting ofsr@montgomerycountymd.gov. In Baltimore City, apply online or in person at a participating senior center during scheduled distribution dates (June 2 – July 2, 2026); online applicants must still pick up their card at a senior center; no membership in a senior center is required. In Howard County, apply online at mda.maryland.gov starting May 19, 2025; paper and translated applications (Korean, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Vietnamese) are available at local 50+ Centers; applying online is recommended as spaces are limited; if benefits are exhausted, applicants can join a waitlist.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to urban and small-scale producers who want to plant cover crops but do not qualify for traditional cover crop grant programs designed for larger farm operations. Growers planting fewer than 10 acres of cover crops can apply for reimbursement of up to $1,500 per year based on paid receipts for eligible costs including seed purchases, labor, equipment rental, and custom services directly related to cover crop planting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant of up to $1,500 per grower per year based on paid receipts for eligible costs including cover crop seed (including shipping), labor (capped at $15/hour), equipment rental, and custom services directly related to cover crop planting. Eligible species include single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes. Crops may be planted in open plots/fields, raised beds, or high tunnels. Two implementation periods: summer (3/1 – 8/31) and winter (8/1 – 11/15). All documentation must be submitted to the Department by December 31, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 16 through April 24, 2026; documentation submission deadline December 31, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Urban and small-scale agricultural producers planting fewer than 10 acres of cover crops in Maryland, including individual growers, for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations with at least $1,000 in annual farm product sales or donations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed costs (including shipping), labor (capped at $15/hour), equipment rental, and custom services directly related to cover crop planting. Eligible seed includes single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes for planting in open plots/fields, raised beds, or high tunnels.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland. Program is statewide with no county or regional exclusions.
requirements_list: Must plant fewer than 10 acres of cover crops
Operation must generate a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually from a farm product
Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland
Must comply with all local, state, and federal regulations and obtain required permits
Must follow cover crop planting recommendations from the seed manufacturer or University of Maryland Extension
Must have a current nutrient management plan or conditional exception
Must have a soil and water conservation plan (if available)
Must provide a location map (aerial photo or hand-drawn sketch)
Must have control of land for duration of agreement
Cover crops must be implemented during fallow periods
Winter cover crops must be terminated in spring after March 1, 2027 (or February 15, 2027 for early-season vegetables)
All documentation must be submitted to the Department by December 31, 2027
Must comply with MDA spot-check verification

Eligible operations include agricultural, horticultural, vegetable, or fruit products; livestock, meats, marine food products, poultry, eggs, or dairy products; equine operations; wool, hides, feathers, or honey; or any product of farm, forest, orchard, garden, or water
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the 2026 Small Acreage Cover Crop Program Application form (PDF) and the Requirements and Agreement form. Submit by postal mail or email during the enrollment period (March 16 – April 24, 2026). Growers are reimbursed based on paid receipts after planting. All documentation must be submitted to the Department by December 31, 2027. Contact Bill Tharpe at bill.tharpe@maryland.gov or 410-841-5869 for questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program provides financial assistance to small-scale agricultural operations in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas. The program helps farmers adopt Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices to improve natural resource management and increase community access to healthy foods. It offers Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants and Urban Agriculture Water and Power Grants, with additional grant programs under development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are offered in two tracks: Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants (available in spring and fall) and Water and Power Grants for qualifying urban operations. The program is funded by the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations operating small-scale farms in Maryland that generate at least $1,000 in annual sales or donations from farm products.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adoption of Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices, including cover crop establishment and water and power infrastructure for urban agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm products must be grown or raised in Maryland. Operations may be located in urban, peri-urban, rural, or suburban areas. Water and Power Grants are limited to operations in urban areas.
requirements_list: Must produce a farm product generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland
Grantee is responsible for all applicable local, state, and federal regulations and permits
Eligible products include crops, livestock, marine food products, poultry, eggs, dairy, equine operations, wool, hides, feathers, honey, and other farm or garden products
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two grant tracks are available: Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants (offered in spring and fall) and Water and Power Grants for urban operations. See individual grant program pages for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Turfgrass Nutrient Management Program – Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Turfgrass Nutrient Management Program administers the state's lawn fertilizer law, which regulates how lawn fertilizer may be applied to protect the Chesapeake Bay from excess nutrients. The program certifies and licenses lawn care professionals who apply fertilizer commercially, sets application rules for homeowners and professionals, and enforces compliance. Lawn care professionals must be certified by MDA or work under direct supervision of a certified individual. The program offers training exams throughout the year, annual certificate renewal, and business licensing for individuals and companies that fertilize turf commercially.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides fertilizer applicator training, certification exams throughout the year, and business licensing. Lawn care professionals must pass a certification exam (50 multiple-choice questions, 70% passing score) administered by MDA. Exam fee is $100; government agency employees pay $0. Applicants have up to three attempts to pass. Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certificates are valid through December 31 each year and may be renewed annually for a $100 fee with verification of recertification training. The department offers in-person exams and recertification classes and webinars. Business licenses (MDA-F) are required for individuals and companies that fertilize turf commercially and expire December 31 each year; fee is $50 (waived for government agencies). License holders must file an Annual Fertilizer Application Report (AFAR) by March 1 each year.
