Employees working under a certified applicator must complete MDA Fertilizer Applicator Training within 30 days of employment and register with a $15 fee (waived for public agencies), with registration renewable annually by December 31. 2026 exam dates include Boonsboro (June 8), Salisbury (August 19), and Annapolis (December 3).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Certificates and business licenses expire December 31 of each year; AFAR due March 1 each year; exams offered throughout the year (remaining 2026 dates: June 8 in Boonsboro, August 19 in Salisbury, December 3 in Annapolis)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lawn care professionals, turf managers at golf courses, parks, airports, athletic fields, businesses, cemeteries, and other non-agricultural properties who apply fertilizer for hire; also homeowners who apply fertilizer to their own lawns; and employees of licensed fertilizer applicator businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification and licensing to legally apply lawn fertilizer commercially in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide – available to all lawn care professionals and applicable businesses operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be certified by MDA or work under direct supervision of a certified individual to apply fertilizer for hire
Certification requires passing a department exam (50 multiple-choice questions, 70% passing score); up to three attempts allowed
Exam fee is $100; government agency employees pay $0
Certificates are valid through December 31 and must be renewed annually for a $100 fee with recertification training verification
Business licenses (MDA-F) required for individuals and businesses that fertilize turf commercially; fee is $50 (waived for government agencies); expire December 31 each year
Business must employ at least one Maryland Certified Professional Fertilizer Applicator
Business license holders must maintain 3-year application records and display MDA-F license number (2-inch lettering on both sides of vehicles)
License holders must file an Annual Fertilizer Application Report (AFAR) by March 1 each year covering the prior year; penalties may be incurred for late submissions

Employees working under a certified applicator must complete MDA Fertilizer Applicator Training within 30 days of employment and register with a $15 fee (waived for public agencies); registration expires December 31 each year
Must follow University of Maryland fertilizer recommendations and all fertilizer application rules under Maryland law
Fertilizer blackout dates: no nitrogen or phosphorus applications between November 16 and March 1
A single application may not exceed 0.9 lb total N per 1,000 sq ft (no more than 0.7 lb soluble N)
Phosphorus may only be applied when a soil test indicates need or when establishing, patching, or renovating a lawn
Do not fertilize if heavy rain is predicted or the ground is frozen
Keep fertilizer 10-15 feet from waterways
Regulatory basis: COMAR 15.20.10; Agriculture Article Section 8-806 (Fertilizer Use Act of 2011)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective lawn care professionals register for a certification exam using the exam schedule and application form (see the 2026 exam schedule). Applications must be completely filled out and accompanied by the fee before any announced examination date. After passing the exam, they apply for a business license using the Fertilizer Applicator Business License Application form. Annual renewal requires recertification training and a $100 fee by December 31. Employees working under a certified applicator must complete MDA training within 30 days of employment and submit a Trained Employee Registration Form with a $15 fee. Annual Fertilizer Application Reports (AFARs) can be filed electronically at Maryland OneStop or by paper form by March 1 each year to MDA Nutrient Management Program, 50 Harry S Truman Parkway, Suite 201, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_name: Urban Agriculture Water & Power Infrastructure Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program provides grants to urban farms and community gardens to purchase and install equipment needed to access water and electricity. The program helps operations sustain themselves by funding infrastructure such as water meters, pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, and electrical lines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 87.5% of total project costs for eligible water and power infrastructure. Each application has a maximum funding limit of $75,000. The program has up to $500,000 in annual funding through Fiscal Year 2027. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis as long as funds remain available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing basis as long as funds remain available, through Fiscal Year 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Urban farms and community gardens located in urban areas as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of water and power infrastructure, including water meters, water pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, electrical lines, and other department-authorized equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible operations must be located in urban areas as defined by the United States Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must produce a farm product generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Must comply with all local, state, and federal regulations and secure required project permits
Operation must be located in an urban area as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or an incorporated municipality recognized by Maryland
Applicant must have controlled the land for at least 5 years through ownership or leasing
Bids required from authorized contractors for work on public roads, sidewalks, water mains, and transformers, and from private contractors for on-site installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the interactive map to confirm your property meets the location criteria. If eligible, download and complete the application and instruction packet. Submit the completed application to the program. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as long as funds remain available.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture's Value-Added Agricultural Specialist provides technical guidance and support to Maryland farmers and agricultural stakeholders interested in value-added agriculture — activities that alter or enhance raw agricultural products to increase their worth and generate more revenue. The Specialist helps navigate regulatory frameworks including local zoning/permitting, MDH licensing (Cottage, On-Farm Home, or Commercial), FDA compliance (FSMA, acidified foods, dairy), and USDA requirements (meat/poultry), and offers information to support new or expanded agricultural businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state-employed specialist provides one-on-one technical guidance, regulatory navigation support, and informational resources to farmers, producers, processors, and other agricultural stakeholders pursuing value-added agriculture activities. The Specialist helps businesses navigate local, state, and federal regulatory pathways including zoning/permitting, MDH licensing (Cottage, On-Farm Home, or Commercial), FDA compliance (FSMA, acidified foods, dairy), and USDA requirements (meat/poultry). No financial award is involved — the assistance is advisory and educational. Eligible activities include on-farm processing, agritourism (farm stays, event barns, pick-your-own produce, farm stands, corn mazes), craft beverages, dairy products, farm-raised meat sales, and direct-to-consumer sales.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers, agricultural producers, processors, agribusiness owners, and agritourism operators interested in value-added agriculture or expanding an existing agricultural business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical guidance on regulatory requirements (local zoning/permitting, state licensing, federal compliance), business considerations, and value-added agricultural product development including on-farm processing, agritourism, food service, and direct-to-consumer sales.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to agricultural stakeholders across all 24 Maryland counties, including Baltimore City. 13 counties have designated County-level Agricultural Specialists for additional local coordination.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland farmer, producer, processor, or agricultural stakeholder
Must be interested in value-added agriculture or expanding an existing agricultural business

Product-specific regulatory requirements may apply, including local zoning and permitting, MDH licensing (Cottage, On-Farm Home, or Commercial Food Processing), FDA compliance (FSMA, acidified foods, dairy), and USDA requirements (meat and poultry)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Value-Added Agricultural Specialist directly by phone at (443) 924-0329 or by email at martin.proulx@maryland.gov. The process is advisory rather than a formal application: (1) consult County Agricultural/Economic Development professionals; (2) determine product type, location, and scale using 'Getting Started' questions; (3) navigate the local → state → federal regulatory pathway with guidance from the VA Specialist and referenced resources such as the UMD ALEI Decision Tree and MDA Office of Food Protection.

structured_extraction.program_name: Soil Conservation Districts Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's 23 Soil Conservation Districts (SCDs), supported by the Maryland Department of Agriculture's Office of Resource Conservation, provide free technical and engineering assistance to landowners, farmers, and horse owners. District staff — including engineering technicians and field specialists — help design and install best management practices (BMPs) on farms and land to protect natural resources, improve soil and water quality, and comply with environmental regulations. Districts support the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Implementation Plan and help landowners comply with environmental laws. District staff also develop Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans required by many federal and state conservation programs. Assistance includes help identifying permit and authorization requirements, design services for BMPs, assistance applying for cost-share funding, and navigation of federal and state cost-share programs including the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Agriculture, Office of Resource Conservation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical and engineering assistance provided by local soil conservation district staff — including engineering technicians and field specialists — to design and install best management practices on farms and land to protect natural resources and improve soil and water quality. Staff also develop Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans required by many federal and state conservation programs, and assist with compliance with environmental laws. Includes help identifying permit and authorization requirements, design services for BMPs, assistance applying for cost-share funding, and navigation of federal and state cost-share programs including the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program. The MACS Program can cover up to 100% of eligible BMP installation costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, landowners, and horse owners seeking free technical or engineering assistance to design and install best management practices, protect natural resources, comply with environmental laws, and navigate federal and state cost-share programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and installation of agricultural best management practices; development of Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans; natural resource protection and water quality improvement; compliance with environmental regulations; help identifying permit/authorization requirements for stream, floodplain, and wetland work; navigation of federal and state cost-share funding programs; permit identification and application support for stream, floodplain, and wetland projects; engineering design and best management practice installation assistance; free field consultations and site assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local soil conservation districts across all Maryland counties, serving farms in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, coastal zone, and western regions. Conservation plans are required for farmland in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area (the 1,000 ft. strip along those shorelines) and for highly erodible lands under the Federal Food Security Act.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner, farmer, or horse owner in Maryland
Land must be located within Maryland
Some livestock and poultry farms must obtain farm plans as part of CAFO permitting
Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans are required by many federal and state conservation programs
Plans are required for farmland in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area
Plans are required for highly erodible lands under the Federal Food Security Act
Plans are required for farms enrolled in the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program
Plans are required by MDE for certain livestock and poultry farmers
Plans should be updated every 10 years minimum
Prior permits/authorizations are required for work in streams, floodplains, and wetlands before work begins
Contact your local Soil Conservation District to initiate assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district directly by phone or through their website to request free technical or engineering assistance. A local district conservation planner will conduct a farm visit — no formal application required. The planner will perform a resource assessment and develop a custom conservation plan; the farmer then selects BMPs to implement. District contact information is available on the program page for all Maryland counties. Central contact: District Operations, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401 | 410-841-5952 | mda.maryland.gov/conservation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law allows land that is actively used for farm or agricultural purposes to be assessed at its agricultural use value rather than its market value, significantly reducing property taxes. The assessment is administered by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and applies statewide to farmland, woodland associated with farms, and woodland under an approved forest management plan. Woodland tracts can qualify when the owner obtains an approved forest management plan prepared by a registered forester and meets minimum acreage and compliance requirements. Two types of plans qualify: a Forest Conservation Management Agreement through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or a forest stewardship plan recognized by DNR.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Land that qualifies is assessed at a preferential agricultural use value of $500 per acre (instead of market value), substantially reducing annual property tax bills. Woodland under a Forest Conservation Management Agreement is assessed at $125 per acre; woodland under a forest stewardship plan is assessed at $187.50 per acre, rather than at market value. As an example, a 100-acre parcel with a market value of $3,000/acre would be assessed at $50,000 under the agricultural use assessment rather than $300,000 at market value, saving approximately $2,780 in annual taxes using a combined rate of $1.112 per $100.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners whose property is actively devoted to farm or agricultural use, including farming operations and woodland under approved forest management plans, as well as owners of woodland tracts of at least 5 acres who have or are willing to obtain an approved forest management plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax assessment and tax liability on qualifying agricultural and forested land, including woodland parcels under approved forest management plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available in all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Note: a few counties also impose a County Agricultural Transfer Tax in addition to the State tax; property owners should contact the Finance or Treasurer's Office for the county in which the property is located to determine if any additional local tax applies.
requirements_list: Land must be actively and primarily used for a continuing farm or agricultural purpose.
Parcel must meet minimum size thresholds (generally at least 3 acres; parcels under 3 acres must meet special conditions).
Land zoned to a more intensive use at the owner's request is not eligible.
Homesites on the farm are not eligible and are assessed at market value.
Parcels less than 20 acres but at least 5 acres may need to meet a $2,500 gross income test from agricultural activity.
The $2,500 gross income test must be applied when at least 3 but less than 5 acres are actually devoted to an approved agricultural activity.
Woodland must be part of a farm or covered by an approved forest management plan prepared by a registered professional forester; minimum 5 acres required for standalone woodland parcels.
Maximum of 5 parcels under 10 acres in the same county may qualify under platted subdivision lots; no more than 2 parcels under 3 acres statewide under the same ownership.
Woodland parcel must be at least 5 acres (excluding homesite); parcels under 5 acres are not eligible.
Parcels may not be combined to meet the 5-acre minimum.
Forest management plan must be prepared by a professionally registered forester.
Plan must be either a Forest Conservation Management Agreement from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources or a forest stewardship plan recognized by DNR.
Owner must submit compliance documentation with the plan to the Department at required intervals.
Purchaser of qualifying property may file a Declaration of Intent to maintain agricultural use for 5 consecutive years to waive the Agricultural Transfer Tax.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners should contact their local SDAT assessment office. The Department determines eligibility based on the nature and extent of agricultural use. Owners may be required to provide evidence of gross income (sales receipts, invoices, lease agreements, Schedule F tax filings, etc.). Woodland owners must obtain a qualifying forest management plan from a registered forester or through the Maryland DNR Forest Conservation Management Agreement program, then submit the plan and required compliance documentation to the local SDAT assessment office. More information is available on the Maryland DNR website. Questions regarding Agricultural Transfer Tax exemptions should also be directed to the local Assessment Office. Purchasers are encouraged to contact the local Assessment Office for the county in which the property is located.

structured_extraction.program_name: Improvement Required for Health or Medical Condition Real Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax assessment exemption for new improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings that are necessitated by the health or medical condition of a resident. The exemption prevents medically necessary home modifications from increasing the property's taxable assessed value. The exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value (assessment) of the real property. The exemption applies for the current tax year in which the application is received and is removed for the next full tax year after a transfer or after notification that the individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building. Statutory basis: Tax Property Article Section 8-233 (Maryland).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The value added to a residential property by medically necessary improvements is excluded from the taxable assessment. The exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value of the property. Exemption applies for the current tax year in which the application is received. The exemption is removed for the next full tax year after a transfer or notification that the individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building. Statutory basis: Tax Property Article Section 8-233 (Maryland).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners and resident homeowners who have made or need to make improvements to their home necessitated by the health or medical condition of a resident. Property must be the permanent residence of the individual with the medical condition.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prevention of increased real property tax assessment resulting from medically necessary home improvements to a permanent residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties. Application must be submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located. All assessment offices are open Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, except Baltimore City which is open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
requirements_list: Improvement must be a new improvement, change, or addition to a residential building
Improvement must be necessitated by the health or medical condition of a resident
Sufficient evidence of medical necessity must be presented with the application
Application must be prepared by the physician of the property owner
Application must include physician signature attesting to the medical necessity of the improvement
Medical condition may be permanent or temporary; applicant designates condition type and expected duration if temporary
Property must be the permanent residence of the individual with the medical condition
Exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value (assessment) of the real property
Improvements that do not add value to the property are not eligible
Improvement must be required for the health or medical condition of the resident

Submit the completed application with supporting documentation of medical necessity to the local county assessment office where the property is located. No stated application deadline; applications are submitted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Manufacturing and Research and Development Personal Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: State law authorizes local governments in Maryland to exempt from taxation personal property used in manufacturing, including research and development activities. Qualifying businesses can apply annually for an exemption on personal property assets used in manufacturing or R&D operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local governments may exempt personal property used in manufacturing or research and development from personal property taxation. The exemption applies to assets used directly in the manufacturing or R&D process. Applicants must itemize assets and describe how each is used in the qualifying process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 or within 6 months after the date of the first assessment for the taxable year that includes the manufacturing/research & development property
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing businesses and businesses engaged in research and development activities in Maryland seeking an exemption from personal property taxation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from local personal property taxes on equipment and assets used in manufacturing or research and development processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; local governments determine whether to grant the exemption.
requirements_list: Explain the manufacturing or research and development process in detail
Supply an itemized list of assets for which the exemption is claimed
Describe how each asset is used in the manufacturing or R&D process
Answer all application questions completely
Provide a categorized detailed depreciation schedule
Provide a legible depreciation schedule with original cost, year of acquisition, and use description for each asset
Explain the use of all manufacturing/R&D equipment
Supply lease schedules for any leased equipment
Report all expenses and fully depreciated property
Submit Form 1120 Schedule L or balance sheet (IRS-filed)
Identify asset type (MFG, R/D, QC, FPT)
For manufacturing requests: explain raw material transformation, primary customer type, and provide major raw materials list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form (14 questions, a leased property schedule, and an optional flowchart). Submit by September 1 or within 6 months after the date of the first assessment for the taxable year that includes the manufacturing/research & development property. Email submission preferred to sdat.ppaudit@maryland.gov; alternative mail submission to SDAT Personal Property Division, 700 E. Pratt Street, 2nd Floor, Baltimore MD. Supporting documents such as photos, flowcharts, technical brochures, and product catalogs are optional but helpful. Contact the Personal Property Division at (410) 767-1170 or toll free 1-888-246-5941 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State of Maryland, through the Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), provides property tax relief to eligible renters who pay high monthly rent relative to their total income. Based on the principle that renters indirectly pay property taxes as part of their rent, the program is modeled after the Homeowners' Tax Credit (Circuit Breaker) Program and is designed to give renters similar protection against high property tax burdens. Eligible renters receive a direct check from the State Treasury for the difference between 15% of their annual occupancy rent (excluding utilities) and their calculated tax limit based on income. If utilities such as heat and electricity are included in rent, the eligible credit amount is reduced (e.g., -18% if heat and electricity are included). The maximum credit is $1,000 per year. Credits are calculated based on total combined gross household income from all sources (including Social Security and retirement benefits) and rent paid. In 2022, 6,004 renters received an average of $450 in relief. Eligible applicants include those age 60 or older, 100% disabled, or under age 60 with at least one dependent under age 18 meeting separate income guidelines (under $31,200 for a family of four), with a combined net worth under $200,000. Applicants must have lived in their primary residence in Maryland for at least six months and must not receive federal or state housing subsidies or reside in public housing. The program is administered statewide by SDAT, with local application assistance available (e.g., through senior activity centers in St. Mary's County and the Carroll County Division of Aging & Disabilities).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct check payment from the State Treasury of up to $1,000 per year issued to eligible renters to offset the portion of rent attributable to property taxes paid indirectly. The credit equals the difference between 15% of annual occupancy rent (excluding utilities) and the calculated tax limit based on household income. If utilities such as heat and electricity are included in rent, the eligible credit amount is reduced (e.g., -18% if heat and electricity are included). Benefit amount is calculated based on total combined gross household income from all sources (including Social Security and retirement benefits) in relation to rent charged. In 2022, 6,004 renters received an average of $450 in relief.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the year in which the credit is sought (Carroll County guidance notes September 1 as a local assistance deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland renters who are age 60 or older, 100% disabled, or under age 60 with at least one dependent under age 18 meeting separate income guidelines (under $31,200 for a family of four), with a combined net worth under $200,000, who pay high rent relative to their income and do not receive federal or state housing subsidies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct cash payment to offset high rent costs relative to income; reduction of tax burden attributable to property taxes included in rent payments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to qualifying renters throughout Maryland who have resided in their rented dwelling in Maryland as their principal residence for at least 6 months of the calendar year. Credits are only available for rent paid in Maryland. Local application assistance available at senior activity centers in St. Mary's County and through the Carroll County Division of Aging & Disabilities.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland renter paying rent toward a primary residence
Rented dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence in Maryland for at least 6 months in the calendar year
Must have been a Maryland renter for at least 6 months of the previous year
Applicant must have a bona fide leasehold interest and be legally responsible for the rent
Rented dwelling must not be exempt from property taxation (not owned by a tax-exempt or charitable organization)
Must qualify based on gross household income in relationship to a fixed amount of rent charged
Monthly rent must be high relative to total income
Combined net worth of applicant, spouse, and/or co-tenant must be less than $200,000 as of December 31
Age 60+ or 100% disabled: income and rent must meet Chart 1 thresholds

Under age 60: must have at least one dependent under age 18 living with applicant, must not receive federal or state housing subsidies or reside in public housing, and combined household income must be below Chart 2 limits (under $31,200 for a family of four)
Must not receive federal or state housing subsidies
Must not reside in public housing
Must apply by October 1 of the applicable year
Utilities included in rent reduce the eligible credit amount (e.g., -18% if heat and electricity are included)
A new application must be filed every year if applicant wishes to be considered for a tax credit
All household income sources must be reported (taxable, non-taxable, Social Security, worker's compensation, deferred compensation, inheritance, gifts over $300)
Business or rental losses cannot reduce reported gross income
Non-dependent household occupants not paying room and board must report prior-year gross income
Federal tax return for the applicable tax year required (with all schedules and forms)
If income from partnership or corporation: Form 1065 (Schedule K-1) and/or Form 1120/1120S (Schedule K-1) required
Original documents should not be sent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal (www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov) or download and mail the paper application (Form RTC-1) to the Renters' Tax Credit Program, P.O. Box 49006, Baltimore, MD 21297. Online applications are processed faster. In-person appointments can be scheduled at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202. Applications must be submitted by October 1 of the applicable year. Do not email applications containing personal information such as Social Security numbers or tax returns. Required documents include copies of all 1099 forms, rent receipts from January through December, a copy of the lease or rental agreement, and a copy of the federal income tax return if one was filed. Application assistance is also available at all senior activity centers in St. Mary's County and through the Carroll County Division of Aging & Disabilities at 410-386-3800.

structured_extraction.program_name: Personal Property Tax Exemption for Home-based Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Small home-based sole proprietorships may be exempt from personal property tax on business equipment and inventory. Eligible businesses that initially file a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2) and meet the criteria receive a one-time approval and do not need to file further returns as long as they remain eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personal property owned by a qualifying home-based sole proprietorship is exempt from personal property taxation. To qualify, the total original cost of all business personal property (including average inventory, excluding exempt vehicles) must be less than $10,000. Eligible businesses file once, receive a one-time approval email, and do not need to file again as long as criteria continue to be met.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual sole proprietors who operate a home-based business where the home is both the principal residence and principal place of business, and whose total business personal property is valued under $10,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from personal property tax on business equipment and inventory used in a home-based sole proprietorship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Personal property must be owned by an individual used in a sole proprietorship (corporations, LLCs, LPs, and LLPs are not eligible).
The personal property must be located at the individual's principal residence, which must also be the principal place of business.
Total original cost of all business personal property, including average inventory and excluding exempt vehicles, must be less than $10,000.
Eligible businesses must initially file a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2).
Businesses needing a Trader's License should submit a Declaration of Inventory form to the Clerk of the Court with the license application instead of filing a personal property return.
Amended returns for prior years must be filed within 3 years from the April 15th due date of the original report.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2) initially. If eligibility criteria are met, a one-time approval email will be sent near the beginning of the following calendar year. No further returns are required as long as criteria continue to be met. Prior-year exemptions can be claimed via an amended return filed within 3 years of the original due date.

Dwelling must be owned by the surviving spouse

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Real Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a real property tax exemption on the principal residence of the surviving spouse of a veteran who had a 100% service-connected permanent and total disability rating. The exemption continues after the veteran's death and may follow the surviving spouse to a subsequently acquired dwelling.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from real property taxes on the surviving spouse's principal residence. For subsequently acquired dwellings, the exemption amount equals the exemption allowed on the prior dwelling. Refunds of previously paid taxes may also be available starting with the 2018-2019 tax year within a 3-year window from the calendar year the surviving spouse first became eligible. Remarriage forfeits the exemption, but an annulment voiding the subsequent marriage allows reinstatement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unmarried surviving spouses of veterans who had a 100% service-connected permanent and total disability rating, who own and reside in a Maryland dwelling as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability on the surviving spouse's principal residence. Applicants may also request a refund of prior property taxes under Tax Property Article 7-208.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Application must be submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located. 24 county-level Supervisor of Assessments offices accept applications.
requirements_list: Disabled veteran must have had a 100% service-connected permanent and total disability rating (not from misconduct) prior to or after death
Disabled veteran must have been a Maryland resident at the time of death
Disabled veteran must have owned the dwelling at time of death (or veteran must have resided and died in Maryland if the dwelling was not owned by the veteran)
Surviving spouse must own and reside in the dwelling as their principal residence
Surviving spouse must be a Maryland resident
Surviving spouse must not have remarried (remarriage forfeits exemption; reinstatement possible after annulment voiding the subsequent marriage)
Required documentation: copy of veteran's Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214
Required documentation: copy of veteran's most recent V.A. rating notification showing 100% permanent/total or 100% permanently unemployable disability rating (with effective date and decision date)
Required documentation: proof of applicant Maryland residency (current MD driver's license, voter registration, or redacted prior-year MD income taxes)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Exemption Application and file with the local County Supervisor of Assessments office where the property is located. Required attachments include: (1) copy of veteran's Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214; (2) copy of veteran's most recent V.A. rating notification showing 100% permanent/total or 100% permanently unemployable disability rating with effective and decision dates; (3) proof of applicant Maryland residency (current MD driver's license, voter registration card, or redacted prior-year MD income taxes). The assessment office will approve or disapprove the application. Applicants may also request a refund of prior property taxes under Tax Property Article 7-208.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BRAC Zone program directs growth from military base realignment into designated growth areas and provides local governments with financial assistance for public infrastructure. Participating local jurisdictions in BRAC Zones receive payments based on real property tax increments on qualified properties, which can be used to repay bonds issued for infrastructure improvements, including Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds. Projects in BRAC Zones may also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies. The program is designed to support areas absorbing population growth resulting from U.S. military base realignment under the BRAC 2005 federal law. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local jurisdictions receive: (1) payment equal to 100% of the state real property tax increment on qualified properties, and (2) payment equal to 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property. Funds must be used for infrastructure improvements, including repayment of Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds issued for infrastructure. Projects may also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in designated BRAC Zones in Prince George's County seeking financial assistance for public infrastructure improvements related to military base realignment and population growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure improvements; repayment of bonds including Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds issued for infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in areas within Prince George's County designated as BRAC Zones under the BRAC 2005 federal law.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction located within a designated BRAC Zone
Funds must be used for infrastructure improvements
Benefits are available for 10 years from the date the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist, or visit the Maryland Department of Commerce website for more details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Biotechnology Investment Incentive Tax Credit (BIITC) provides a Maryland income tax credit to qualified investors who invest in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBCs). The credit equals 33% of an eligible investment up to $250,000, or 50% up to $500,000 for investments in QMBCs located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. Enhanced credits are available for investors in QMBCs located in Opportunity Zones (65% up to $575,000 for Level 1; 75% up to $750,000 for Level 2) and RISE Zones (50% up to $500,000). Credits are issued on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget is exhausted. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability.

Opportunity Zone Level 2 enhancement: 75% up to $750,000. RISE Zone enhancement: 50% up to $500,000. Minimum investment of $25,000 required. Credits are refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. Total credits issued are capped at the annual program budget and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) promotes economic development and environmental improvement, especially in distressed urban areas, by identifying and redeploying underutilized properties contaminated by hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants (brownfields). It supports Maryland's Smart Growth efforts by providing financial incentives—including grants, loans, and a real property tax credit—to qualifying property owners and developers in participating local jurisdictions following site cleanup. Eligible sites must have completed Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, received a Maryland Department of Commerce designation as a qualified brownfields site, and be located within a jurisdiction that has enacted local BRIP legislation. The tax credit applies to the increase in the assessed value of the remediated site: a base credit of 50% with an optional additional 20% credit granted by the local jurisdiction. Properties in Enterprise Zones may receive the credit for up to 10 years; all other properties receive it for five years. Grants and loans are available through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) to support organizing, assessing, and cleaning up brownfield properties. Eligible jurisdictions include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester counties, as well as the municipalities of Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BRIP provides grants and loans through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) to support organizing, assessing, and cleaning up brownfield properties, as well as a real property tax credit. The tax credit equals 50% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value of a cleaned-up brownfield site (difference between pre- and post-remediation assessments), with an optional additional 20% credit granted by the local jurisdiction. The base credit is 50%; combined credits may not exceed 70%. The credit applies for 5 taxable years after site cleanup. If the site is located in a designated Enterprise Zone or Opportunity Zone, the tax credit period may extend up to 10 years. The taxing jurisdiction is also required to contribute 30% of the same property tax amount to the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. Combined with other real property tax credits, the credit may not exceed 100% of the tax on the increased value of the site.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and local governments seeking to redevelop brownfield properties in participating Maryland jurisdictions. Applicants must be inculpable persons enrolled in the Maryland Department of the Environment's Voluntary Cleanup Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups; real property tax credit applied to property taxes on the increased assessed value of a remediated brownfield site, including improvements added within 5 years after reassessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only sites located in a participating jurisdiction that has enacted local BRIP legislation are eligible. Any Maryland taxing jurisdiction may elect to participate. Participating counties include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester. Participating municipalities include Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown (as of 12/31/2022). Expanded incentives apply in designated Enterprise Zones or Opportunity Zones.

Site must be owned or operated by an inculpable person.

Property must have received a Maryland Department of Commerce designation as a qualified brownfields site.

Recipient cannot withdraw from the Voluntary Cleanup Program; credit terminates if VCP approval is withdrawn.
The local jurisdiction must either approve property tax credits pursuant to State statute or maintain a list of priority brownfields sites.
Applicant must submit a completed General Application and the BRIP addendum.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, then submit a completed General Application and BRIP addendum along with required MDE documentation and building permit to the Maryland Department of Commerce. If the site qualifies, Commerce issues a designation letter that the property owner takes to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit. For grant and loan inquiries, contact the Maryland Department of Commerce Office of Finance Programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) / Brownfields Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) promotes economic development and environmental improvement, especially in distressed urban areas, by identifying and redeploying underutilized properties contaminated by hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants (brownfields). BRIP supports Maryland's Smart Growth efforts by providing financial incentives—including grants, loans, and a real property tax credit—to eligible brownfield sites that have completed the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and received a Maryland Department of Commerce designation as a qualified brownfields site. The property must also be located within a jurisdiction that has enacted local BRIP legislation. Eligible sites receive a 50% to 70% property tax credit on the increase in county and/or municipal real property tax assessment after remediation. An additional optional 20% credit may be granted by the local jurisdiction, and an additional 20% credit is available when voluntary cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000. Brownfields in Enterprise Zones may receive the credit for up to 10 years; properties outside these zones receive it for five taxable years. Credit is terminated if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval of the Response Action Plan or Certificate of Completion. Grants and loans are available through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) to support organizing, assessing, and cleaning up brownfield properties. Baltimore County offers its own BRIP tax credit application process through the Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development (administered via the Office of Budget and Finance) for qualifying properties—providing a 50% credit on the increased County real property tax liability, with an additional 20% for Enterprise Zone or commercial revitalization area sites and an additional 20% where cleanup costs exceed $1 million (10-year credit period for Enterprise Zone sites, 5 years for others). Frederick County and the City of Frederick also administer a local brownfields property tax credit for qualifying previously developed or contaminated sites that have undergone environmental cleanup, providing a 50%–70% credit on the increased assessed value for five years after cleanup. Participating counties include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester, as well as the municipalities of Baltimore City, Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BRIP offers grants and loans through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) to support economic development activities such as organizing, assessing, and cleaning up brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups. It also provides a real property tax credit of 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in the assessed value of a cleaned-up brownfield site. The base credit is 50%; an optional additional 20% credit may be granted by the local jurisdiction; and an additional 20% credit is available when voluntary cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000. The credit applies for 5 taxable years after site cleanup. If the site is located in a designated Enterprise Zone, the tax credit period may extend up to 10 years total. Combined with other real property tax credits, the credit may not exceed 100% of the tax on the increased value of the site. Credit is terminated if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval of the Response Action Plan or Certificate of Completion. The taxing jurisdiction is also required to contribute 30% of the same property tax amount to the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. Baltimore County administers its own Brownfields Tax Credit through the Department of Economic and Workforce Development / Office of Budget and Finance for qualifying properties within the county, providing a 50% credit on the increased County real property tax liability, with an additional 20% for Enterprise Zone or designated commercial revitalization area sites and an additional 20% where cleanup costs exceed $1 million (10-year credit period for Enterprise Zone sites, 5 years for others). In Frederick County and the City of Frederick, a local brownfields property tax credit of 50%–70% of the increased assessed value is available for five years after cleanup, reducing property tax liability for qualifying brownfields properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and local governments seeking to redevelop brownfield sites located in participating Maryland jurisdictions, including inculpable persons enrolled in the Maryland Department of the Environment's Voluntary Cleanup Program. In Baltimore County, owners of properties designated as Qualified Brownfields Sites under the Maryland Voluntary Cleanup Program are also eligible. In Frederick County, property owners remediating or redeveloping brownfields sites who have completed environmental cleanup of a brownfield site are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credit applied to property taxes on the increased assessed value of a remediated brownfield site, including improvements added within 5 years after reassessment; grants and loans for organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups. In Baltimore County, the credit reduces the County real property tax on brownfield properties that have been cleaned up. In Frederick County, the credit reduces property tax liability for qualifying brownfields properties following cleanup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Brownfield property must be located within a participating Maryland jurisdiction that has enacted BRIP legislation. Participating counties include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester. Participating municipalities include Baltimore City, Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown (as of 12/31/2022). Additional benefits available for properties within Enterprise Zones or designated commercial revitalization areas. Baltimore County and Frederick County/City of Frederick have their own local application processes for properties within those jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, then apply for a qualified brownfields site designation through the Maryland Department of Commerce by submitting a completed General Application and BRIP addendum along with required MDE documentation and building permit. For grant and loan inquiries, contact the Maryland Department of Commerce Office of Finance Programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program provides matching grants to support innovation infrastructure projects in Maryland's strategic technology sectors. Operated by the Maryland Department of Commerce, the program funds the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, installation, improvement, or equipping of innovation infrastructure — such as wet laboratories, cyber ranges, prototype manufacturing centers, and specialized workforce training spaces. The program targets sectors including advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, blue technology, cybersecurity, defense, energy and sustainability, life sciences, quantum, and sensors and robotics. The program is a pilot established by House Bill 552 (Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023) and is scheduled to run through June 30, 2027, at which point it will be abrogated with no further action required by the General Assembly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $2 million per entity per fiscal year. For grants up to $1 million, the applicant must provide matching funds of at least 200% of the grant amount. For grants exceeding $1 million and up to $2 million, the applicant must provide matching funds of at least 400% of the grant amount. The program is funded at $7 million for FY26. No more than 50% of the annual appropriation may be awarded to colleges and universities. Fifty percent of the grant award is delivered upon execution of a grant agreement; the remaining 50% is reimbursed upon project completion and documentation of expenditures. Grant funds must be expended within two years of executing the grant agreement, and the project must be fully operational within two years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY2026 Phase 1 deadline was September 26, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EDT (passed). Applications are not being accepted for the remainder of FY2026. No FY2027 deadline has been announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private companies (including publicly held companies), nonprofit entities, local governments, colleges and universities, and foundations affiliated with eligible colleges and universities in Maryland operating innovation infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip an eligible innovation infrastructure project — including real property, buildings, infrastructure, machinery and equipment, leasehold improvements, and furniture and fixtures. Funds may NOT be used for soft or indirect costs such as operating costs, management fees, consulting fees, administrative fees, curriculum development, or salaries of new positions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in the State of Maryland. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions apply.

Applicants must show they can pay for their share of the project costs.
There is only one opportunity to submit applications each fiscal year.
The program is a pilot with a legislatively mandated sunset of June 30, 2027; funding in future years is subject to Governor and General Assembly appropriation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has two phases. Phase 1 is an open call for proposals requiring a project outline and narrative describing how the project qualifies and supports the program goals, including location, size, function, technology sector, sources and uses of funds, and transformational aspects. Applications are submitted by email to buildourfuture.commerce@maryland.gov. Commerce reviews Phase 1 applications and invites a limited number of applicants to submit a more detailed Phase 2 application covering project scope, transformative nature, community impact, sustainability, and a detailed budget. Grant awards are then made to successful Phase 2 applicants in the spring following the Phase 1 submission. There is only one application opportunity per fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Telework Assistance Grant Program helps businesses and non-profits retain and create jobs across Maryland by expanding telework capabilities. Grants of up to $25,000 help applicants purchase hardware, software, and technical services needed to develop and implement telework policies for employees. The program was funded with $1 million from the FY2023 state budget.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Buy Maryland Cybersecurity (BMC) Tax Credit encourages small Maryland businesses to purchase cybersecurity technologies and services from certified Maryland cybersecurity companies. Buyers can claim a tax credit equal to 50% of the net purchase price of eligible cybersecurity purchases against their Maryland state income tax liability. Sellers can apply to be certified as Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Sellers so their products and services are eligible for the credit. The program is designed to incentivize Maryland businesses to strengthen their cybersecurity posture while supporting Maryland-based cybersecurity firms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified Maryland Companies (buyers with fewer than 50 Maryland employees that file Maryland income tax returns) may claim a tax credit equal to 50% of the net purchase price of cybersecurity technologies or services purchased from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. The maximum tax credit per buyer is $50,000 per tax year (based on up to $100,000 in purchases). Credits are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The Department of Commerce has $4.0 million available per tax year: $3.0 million for technology purchases and $1.0 million for service purchases. A single seller's sales may generate no more than $400,000 in total tax credits per year ($200,000 each for technology and services). The credit must be claimed for the tax year in which the purchase was made. Note: the program's statutory authorization expired June 30, 2023; reauthorization would be required for the program to continue.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; applications accepted on a rolling basis subject to available funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small Maryland businesses (fewer than 50 Maryland employees) purchasing cybersecurity technologies or services, and Maryland cybersecurity companies seeking certification as Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Sellers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit to offset Maryland income tax liability for purchases of eligible cybersecurity technologies and services from certified Maryland cybersecurity sellers. Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. Services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies required to file a Maryland income tax return and having fewer than 50 employees in Maryland. Sellers must be headquartered and based in Maryland.

Buyers submit an online application through the Commerce portal after making qualifying purchases. Before applying, contact Cindy Zeng at cindy.zeng@maryland.gov, as some sellers may have reached their funding cap for the current tax year. Approved buyers receive a Certificate of Approval from Commerce, which must be attached to their Maryland income tax return filed with the Comptroller of Maryland. No paper applications are accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Cannabis Business Assistance Loan/Grant Fund (CBAF) is a financing resource operated by the Maryland Department of Commerce. It provides grants and loans to small businesses — including small, minority-owned, and small women-owned businesses — entering the adult-use cannabis industry. CBAF also provides grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) for cannabis-related programs and to business development organizations, including incubators, to train and assist small businesses, minority and women business owners, and entrepreneurs seeking to become licensed in the adult-use cannabis industry. The current active funding opportunity is the Social Equity Conditional Licensee Grant, which delivers milestone-based grant disbursements in four tranches to Social Equity Applicants awarded a conditional Maryland Cannabis License. Maximum grant amounts vary by license type: Dispensary (Standard up to $131,250; Micro up to $43,750), Processor (Standard up to $183,750; Micro up to $61,250), Grower/Cultivator (Standard up to $525,000; Micro up to $175,000).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans are available. The current Social Equity Conditional Licensee Grant disburses funds in four milestone-based tranches. Maximum grant amounts per license type: Dispensary Standard up to $131,250, Dispensary Micro up to $43,750; Processor Standard up to $183,750, Processor Micro up to $61,250; Grower/Cultivator Standard up to $525,000, Grower/Cultivator Micro up to $175,000. Partial disbursements may be approved if some but not all milestone requirements are met for a tranche. Grants are taxable. No fees to apply. Eligible expenses include rent, payroll, utilities, professional services, training, equipment, build-out, and insurance/bonding. Ineligible expenses include tax payments, licensing fees, marketing, zoning/permitting fees, litigation costs, and expenses claimed in prior CBAF rounds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No stated deadline; application portal opened June 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Social Equity Cannabis License holders in Maryland; small businesses (0–50 employees per license), small minority-owned businesses, small women-owned businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry; HBCUs for cannabis-related programs; business development organizations and incubators that train and assist small, minority, and women business owners seeking cannabis licensure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: License application assistance for adult-use cannabis industry participation; operating or capital expenses of a cannabis business (including rent, payroll, utilities, professional services, training, equipment, build-out, insurance/bonding); targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry; cannabis-related programs at HBCUs; training and assistance by business development organizations and incubators for prospective cannabis licensees. Ineligible uses include tax payments, licensing fees, marketing, zoning/permitting fees, litigation costs, and expenses claimed in prior CBAF rounds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program incentivizes data center investment and job creation in Maryland. Data centers that locate or expand in Maryland and create new full-time positions may receive an exemption from Maryland sales and use tax on the purchase of qualified data center personal property, including servers, equipment, and related infrastructure. Eligible projects that meet investment and job creation requirements may receive this benefit for up to 20 years. To qualify, businesses must be certified as a Qualified Data Center, meet investment thresholds (which vary by location tier), and create at least 5 new full-time positions. Tier 1 Areas have a lower investment threshold of $2 million, while all other areas require at least $5 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying data centers receive a sales and use tax exemption on purchases of qualified data center personal property (including servers, equipment, and related infrastructure). The benefit period is 10 consecutive years (subject to annual renewal) for businesses that within 3 years invest at least $2 million (Tier 1 Areas) or $5 million (all other areas) in qualified data center personal property and create at least 5 qualified positions. The benefit period expands to 20 consecutive years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first 10 years after submitting an application. Tier 1 Areas include Baltimore City, Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, as well as Opportunity Zones in any Maryland county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Data centers (individuals or corporations) locating or expanding in Maryland that create new full-time positions and make minimum qualified investments in data center personal property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sales and use tax exemption on the purchase of qualified data center personal property, including servers, equipment, and related data center infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Tier 1 Areas (Baltimore City, Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, plus Opportunity Zones in any Maryland county) have lower investment minimums ($2 million vs. $5 million).

Business must create at least 5 qualified positions within 3 years of submitting an application.

Qualified positions must be full-time, pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage, be newly created (net new to Maryland), not moved or transferred from another Maryland facility, and be filled for at least 12 months.
Business must maintain at least 5 qualified positions for the duration of the 10- or 20-year benefit period.
Certificate of eligibility is subject to annual renewal.
For the 20-year benefit period, the business must invest at least $250 million in qualified data center personal property within the first 10 years after submitting an application.
Annual reporting required for the duration of the benefit period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Security Clearance Costs (ESCC) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: The ESCC Tax Credit provides Maryland income tax credits to businesses for three types of expenses: (1) administrative costs of obtaining federal security clearances for employees, (2) construction or renovation of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) in Maryland, and (3) first-year lease payments for space used to perform security-based contracting work (available only to qualified small businesses). The total credit is capped at $2 million per calendar year across all applicants; if applications exceed the cap, credits are prorated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three credit tracks: (1) Security Clearance Administrative Expenses — up to $200,000 per taxable year for qualifying clearance processing, computer system, and training costs; (2) SCIF Construction/Renovation — 50% of costs up to $200,000 for a single SCIF, or total costs up to $500,000 for multiple SCIFs; (3) First-Year Leasing Costs for qualified small businesses — up to $200,000 for first-year rental payments. All credits combined are capped at $2 million per calendar year. Excess credit may be carried forward. Credits apply against Maryland state income tax only (not county income tax).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 15 following the tax year in which expenses were incurred
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses (500 or fewer employees) that incur federal security clearance administrative expenses, construct or renovate SCIFs in Maryland, or lease space to perform security-based contracting work. The leasing credit is limited to qualified small businesses with 25 or fewer employees that are independently owned and not dominant in their field.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit to offset Maryland state income tax liability for: processing federal security clearance applications; maintaining, upgrading, or installing computer systems required for federal security clearances; training employees to administer the clearance process; constructing or renovating SCIFs in Maryland; and first-year lease payments for space used for security-based contracting (small businesses only).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must operate in Maryland. Security clearance administrative expenses must be for processing, computer systems, and employee training in the State. SCIFs and leased spaces must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must apply to and be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce

Eligible expenses must be for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022 and before January 1, 2028
Applications must be submitted by September 15 following the tax year in which expenses were incurred
