Commerce will certify the approved credit amount by December 15 of that year. The business then files an amended Maryland income tax return using Form 500CR, attaching the Commerce certification to claim the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Enterprise Zone (EZ) Tax Credit program provides real property tax credits and state income tax credits to businesses located within a designated Maryland Enterprise Zone in exchange for job creation and capital investment. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Commerce, with local administration handled by county economic development offices. Designated Enterprise Zones exist across 20 Maryland jurisdictions, including in Baltimore County (North Point/Chesapeake, Southwest, and Federal Center at Woodlawn), Cecil County (17 enterprise zones covering 4,389 acres across nine business parks), and Garrett County (Southern Garrett Enterprise Zone and Northern Garrett Enterprise Zone). Businesses in designated Focus Areas may also qualify for personal property tax credits on new investment and enhanced income tax credits for creating new jobs. The program aims to encourage investment in distressed areas across Maryland by incentivizing job creation and capital investment, promoting use of empty or underused properties, and supporting efforts to improve older office and industrial areas. In Cecil County, businesses must apply to the Office of Economic Development before completing construction or expansion, as property tax credits are not granted retroactively. Enterprise zone designations require the area to be located entirely within a State Priority Funding Area and meet at least one of four socioeconomic criteria. Zone applications are accepted on April 15 and October 15 each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of income tax credits are available: (1) General Income Tax Credit — a one-time $1,000 credit per qualified new employee in an enterprise zone, or $1,500 per qualified new employee in a focus area; (2) Income Tax Credit for Economically Disadvantaged Employees — a three-year credit per qualified new economically disadvantaged employee ($3,000/$4,500 year 1, $2,000/$3,000 year 2, $1,000/$1,500 year 3 for zone/focus area respectively; totaling $6,000 over three years for economically disadvantaged employees in standard zones). Property Tax Credits include: Real Property Tax Credit — a 10-year credit against local real property taxes on eligible expansion, renovation, or capital improvement (80% of eligible assessment for first 5 years, then decreasing 10% annually for the next 5 years in standard zones, reaching 30% in year 10; 80% for all 10 years in focus areas). Focus areas also offer a Personal Property Tax Credit — a 10-year credit at 80% of eligible assessment on new investment in personal property. Unused credits may carry forward up to five tax years. Both county and state tax credits are available in all designated Enterprise Zones statewide. In Cecil County, property tax credit applications must be submitted before completing construction or expansion — credits are not granted retroactively. Baltimore County businesses in the Chesapeake, Southwest, or Woodlawn zones may also qualify for BGE Rider 7 electricity price reduction for load increases of 200kW or more with at least 10 new FTE hires.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15 and October 15 each year (zone designation applications); December 31 (Baltimore County property tax credit)
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and individuals located in or relocating to a designated Maryland Enterprise Zone or Enterprise Zone Focus Area that create new jobs or make capital investments, including businesses in Baltimore County's designated enterprise zones (Chesapeake/North Point, Southwest, Federal Center at Woodlawn), Cecil County's enterprise zones, and Garrett County's Southern and Northern Garrett Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits reduce state income tax liability for job creation and local property tax liability for real and personal property investment in enterprise zones. Reduces both county and state tax obligations for qualifying businesses that invest in Enterprise Zone areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in one of the designated Enterprise Zones or Focus Areas across 20 Maryland jurisdictions. All designated zones must be located entirely within a State Priority Funding Area. In Baltimore County, qualifying zones are the Chesapeake Zone (formerly North Point), Southwest Enterprise Zone, and Federal Center at Woodlawn. In Cecil County, enterprise zones cover 4,389 acres across nine business parks (17 zones shown on the program map). In Garrett County, the two designated zones are the Southern Garrett Enterprise Zone (Southern Garrett Industrial Park and Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park) and the Northern Garrett Enterprise Zone (Northern Garrett Industrial Park). Enterprise Zones are also located in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. A full list and an interactive map are available on the program website.
requirements_list: Business must be certified by the local enterprise zone administrator as eligible for the credit.
Business must be located within a designated Maryland Enterprise Zone or Enterprise Zone Focus Area.
The enterprise zone must be located entirely within a State Priority Funding Area (PFA).

The zone area must meet at least one of four socioeconomic criteria: (1) unemployment rate ≥150% of state or US average (18-month average); (2) poverty rate ≥125% of national average; (3) ≥70% of families earn <80% of median family income; or (4) ≥10% population decline (2000–2010 census) plus property abandonment or tax arrearages over 3 years.
Focus Areas must meet ≥3 of 5 additional criteria (unemployment 150%, poverty 150%, crime rate 150%, substandard housing 200%, commercial vacancy ≥20%).
Business must expand operations or add employees to qualify.
Must create jobs and/or make qualifying investments.
For income tax credits: employee must be hired after the business located in the zone or after zone designation.
Employee must be employed at least 35 hours per week for six months (or 12 months in a Focus Area) before or during the taxable year the credit is claimed.
Employee must spend at least 50% of work time in the enterprise zone or in activities resulting from its location there.
Employee must fill a newly created position (total full-time positions must increase by number of credits taken).
Employee must earn at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
For economically disadvantaged employee credit: business must obtain certification from the Maryland Department of Labor; employee must remain in position for three years to receive full credit.
For property tax credits: business must make an investment in capital improvements or hire new employees and meet all state and local eligibility requirements.
Real property credit requires major capital improvements.
Income credit requires creation of new jobs.
In Cecil County, property tax credit application must be submitted before completing construction or expansion — credits are not granted retroactively.
Most businesses are eligible, but retail businesses are generally excluded from some local zone designations.
Application to the Baltimore County Department of Economic Development must be submitted by December 31 to receive a property tax credit on the next tax bill.
For Real Property Tax Credit in Baltimore County, application must be submitted prior to project completion and User/Occupancy Permit issuance.
Local eligibility requirements vary by enterprise zone.

Zone designation applications (submitted by political subdivisions) must be received on April 15 or October 15 each year; late applications cannot be accepted. Data submission required at least 60 days before submission date.
Annual reporting by April 15 is required for political subdivisions receiving designations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Business must apply to the local enterprise zone administrator for certification. In Baltimore County, download the eligibility application for County and Maryland Tax Credits (available at https://resources.baltimorecountymd.gov/Documents/EconomicDevel/Enterprise/ezqualificationapp.pdf) and send the completed application to the Enterprise Zone Coordinator, Baltimore County Department of Economic Development, Historic Courthouse, Suite 100, 400 Washington Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204 by December 31. After review, you will receive a letter confirming eligibility. For the property tax credit, the county will automatically notify the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. For BGE Rider 7 electricity rate reduction, contact BGE directly. In Cecil County, email EconomicDevelopment@cecilcountymd.gov before completing any construction or expansion project; also complete the Enterprise Zone Certification Application (PDF available at https://www.cecilcountymd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/334/Enterprise-Zone-Certification-Application-PDF). In Garrett County, visit the Maryland Department of Commerce Enterprise Zone Program page at commerce.maryland.gov for application details. Verify address eligibility using the interactive map. To claim the income tax credit, complete Maryland Tax Form 500CR and include it in the state tax return. If hiring a disadvantaged employee for a higher credit, obtain certification for that employee from the Maryland Department of Labor. For zone designation applications (submitted by political subdivisions), applications must be received on April 15 or October 15 each year; late applications cannot be accepted. The Secretary may designate zones within 60 days of each submission date.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ExportMD Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce, helps Maryland small businesses offset the costs of international marketing by providing reimbursement grants of up to $5,000, covering 50% of eligible expenses. The program helps businesses enter or expand into global markets by making international marketing initiatives more financially accessible. Eligible expenses include international travel, trade show registration and fees, website development, translation of marketing materials, and other international marketing costs. The program is funded in part through a Cooperative Agreement with the U.S. Small Business Administration. Applications are accepted on a rolling monthly basis, with deadlines on the 1st of each month.

Applications are accepted monthly, with deadlines on the 1st of each month.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a Maryland State income tax credit to qualifying small businesses for hiring qualified veterans, based on wages paid to those veteran employees during their first year of employment. The program covers tax years 2017 through 2020. For positions created in tax year 2021 and later, businesses should refer to the Job Creation Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee during their first year of employment (tax years 2017–2020). Maximum credit is $1,800 per qualified veteran employee. Employers may claim up to 5 qualified veteran employees per taxable year. Total credits available per year are capped at $500,000 on a first-come, first-served basis. The credit is not refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time employees that hire qualified veterans who were hired on or after January 1, 2017 and meet federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit veteran criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland State income tax liability based on wages paid to qualified veteran employees in their first year of employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland employers statewide.
requirements_list: Employer must be a small business (50 or fewer full-time employees) operated as an individual, partnership, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, LLC, or corporation.
Veteran employee must have been hired on or after January 1, 2017.
Veteran must have served in the active U.S. Armed Forces and been discharged under honorable circumstances.

Veteran must have served on active duty for more than 180 days OR been discharged for a service-connected disability, AND must not have a period of active duty of more than 90 days that ended during the 60-day period ending on the hiring date.

Veteran must qualify under the Federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit as a veteran who: (a) is a member of a family that received SNAP benefits for at least 3 months in the 15-month period before hiring; OR (b) is a disabled veteran hired within 1 year of discharge or unemployed for 6+ months in the year before hiring; OR (c) has been unemployed for at least 4 weeks in the year before hiring.
Credit applies only to wages paid in the veteran's first year of employment.
Maximum of 5 qualified veteran employees may be claimed per taxable year.
Program covers tax years 2017 through 2020 only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Application Forms A & B, Qualified Veteran Employee's Self-Certification Form(s), copies of W-2s and/or paystubs, and copies of DD214 or equivalent discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce. Commerce will certify or deny the application within 45 days of receiving a complete application. After certification, file Maryland Tax Form 500CR electronically with the Comptroller of Maryland along with a copy of the certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Job Creation Tax Credit (JCTC) provides a Maryland state income tax credit to eligible businesses that locate or expand in Maryland and create a minimum number of net new full-time positions. The credit is $3,000 per new job (or $5,000 if in a revitalization area such as an enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). Enhanced credits are available for jobs filled by qualified veteran employees: $4,000 per veteran-filled job ($6,000 in a revitalization area). Small businesses that hire at least one qualified veteran employee for a net new full-time position can receive a $2,500 credit per qualified veteran employee (up to five per credit year) without meeting a minimum job threshold. Eligible businesses that establish or expand a Maryland facility primarily engaged in warehousing and distribution within a Priority Funding Area may also receive a credit equal to the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of one year's wages for each new employee in a qualified position. The program is capped at $4 million in tax credits per calendar year, certified on a first-come, first-served basis. The program remains in effect until January 1, 2027, subject to extension by the Maryland General Assembly. The program is available statewide, including to companies newly locating to or expanding in Anne Arundel County.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit of $3,000 per new qualified full-time job created, increasing to $5,000 per job if the business is located in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). Enhanced credits of $4,000 per job filled by a qualified veteran employee, or $6,000 per veteran-filled job in a revitalization area. Small businesses hiring qualified veteran employees receive $2,500 per qualifying veteran hire (up to five per credit year). For warehousing and distribution facilities in a Priority Funding Area, the credit equals the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of one year's wages for each new employee in a qualified position (e.g., creating 80 qualified positions within a 2-year period could yield approximately $80,000 in credits). Credits are non-refundable and may be carried forward for five taxable years. A business may not earn more than $1 million in credits per year. The program is capped at $4 million in tax credits per calendar year. Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program remains in effect until Jan. 1, 2027, subject to extension by the Maryland General Assembly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible businesses (for-profit and non-profit with taxable income) that locate or expand in Maryland and create net new full-time jobs, including companies newly locating to or expanding in Anne Arundel County; small businesses hiring qualified veteran employees; and companies establishing or expanding warehousing and distribution facilities within a Priority Funding Area. Caroline County businesses must add at least 10 qualifying full-time positions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability for job creation through new location or expansion of business operations. Unused credits may be carried forward up to five taxable years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, including Anne Arundel County. Minimum job creation thresholds vary: 60 net new full-time jobs statewide; 25 jobs in a Priority Funding Area; or 10 jobs in qualifying lower-income/lower-employment counties (including Caroline County). Higher credit amounts available in revitalization areas including Tier 1 Counties: Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, and Wicomico. Warehousing and distribution facilities must be located within a Priority Funding Area as defined by the Job Creation Tax Credit statute.
requirements_list: Businesses must file a Declaration of Intent with Commerce before hiring qualified employees (not required for small businesses hiring veteran employees).
Business must obtain preliminary and final certification from Maryland Department of Commerce.
Minimum job creation: 60 net new full-time jobs statewide; 25 jobs in a Priority Funding Area; or 10 jobs in qualifying lower-income/lower-employment counties (including Caroline County).
Jobs must be created within a 24-month period.
Positions must be filled for at least 12 months before applying for final certification.

For positions filled on or after Oct. 1, 2021: must pay prevailing wage rate or 150% of state minimum wage; provide career advancement training; allow collective bargaining; provide paid leave; be covered employment for unemployment insurance; entitle employee to workers' compensation; offer employer-provided health insurance with premiums not exceeding 8.5% of net monthly earnings; and offer retirement benefits.
For positions filled before Oct. 1, 2021: must pay at least 120% of state minimum wage.
Facility must be primarily engaged in a qualifying industry.
Jobs must remain filled for at least three years following the credit year or credits must be repaid; recapture triggered if positions fall more than 5% below average or fall below minimum threshold.
Business may not claim both the One Maryland Tax Credit and JCTC in the same tax year.
Small businesses must employ 50 or fewer total full-time employees to qualify for the veteran hire credit track.

Qualified veteran employee must be honorably discharged and qualify as a 'qualified veteran' under the Federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit; must have served 180+ days active duty with honorable discharge, OR discharge for service-connected disability, OR no active duty >90 days ending in 60 days before hire; and must be a SNAP recipient for 3+ months in prior 15 months, OR have a service-connected disability with discharge  fffd1 year before hire, OR have 4+ weeks unemployment in prior year.
Veterans must provide official discharge documentation (DD-214) and supporting government-issued documents.
Applications certified on a first-come, first-served basis up to the $4 million annual cap.
Must be a newly locating or expanding company (Anne Arundel County applicants may contact AAEDC for assistance).
For warehousing and distribution track: facility must be primarily engaged in warehousing and distribution and located within a Priority Funding Area.

Applicants must complete and sign Employment Affidavit reporting full-time employees at intent date, one year prior, and two years prior; employment numbers for prior years will be averaged to establish base employment.
Annual reporting required for 3 years after credit year; Year 3 report requires CPA statement.
Temporary vacancies permitted if filled within 4 months and less than 10% of positions vacant at any time.
Recapture provisions may be extended for labor actions or force majeure events.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Notice of Intent to Commerce (taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov) before creating new qualified jobs (not required for small businesses hiring veterans). 2. Optionally submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit to determine preliminary qualification. 3. After positions have been filled for at least 12 months, submit a Final Application along with a List of Qualified Employees Form. 4. Commerce certifies eligibility and calculates the credit amount on a first-come, first-served basis (preliminary certificate in ~30 days; final certificate in ~60 days). 5. Claim the credit on Maryland Tax Form 500CR with a copy of the Final Certificate of Eligibility attached. 6. Submit Annual Report for three years post-certification to confirm retained positions. Applications can be submitted through the online portal at programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcredits. For the veteran hire track, employee completes self-certification form and provides DD-214 or discharge papers; employer submits application with employee certification. Anne Arundel County businesses may also contact AAEDC for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that promote Maryland breweries, distilleries, and wineries and their products through research, promotion, and agricultural business development. The program aims to reinforce Maryland as a world-class producer of craft beverages and a desirable destination for craft beverage visitors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded by the Secretary of Commerce based on recommendations from the Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion. Eligible activities include investing in creation and expansion of breweries, distilleries, and wineries; attracting new visitors; creating incentives for special events; educating the public about alcohol manufacturing history; conducting research and promoting growth of Maryland agricultural products used in craft beverages; and supporting expansion of minority ownership in state breweries, distilleries, and wineries.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Grant Application Period Open through Wednesday, November 19, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6)) and state or local government units seeking to promote Maryland's craft beverage industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Promoting Maryland breweries, distilleries, and wineries; attracting visitors; hosting special events; public education about alcohol manufacturing history; research and promotion of Maryland agricultural ingredients; supporting minority ownership in craft beverage operations; project deliverables including reports, workshops, advertising campaigns, and publications; marketing and promotion platforms such as flyers, posters, radio, TV, website, and social media.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible applicants promoting Maryland breweries, distilleries, and wineries.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization under 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code, or a state or local government unit
Applications must be submitted by the deadline (November 19, 2025 for FY26)
Applications must be submitted in the format stipulated by the Department of Commerce
Applications must be submitted online
If awarded, a Final Report must be submitted within 60 days after the grant term ends covering project accomplishments, financial expenditures, and impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review Tips & Hints document before applying. Prepare a deliverables list, detailed timeline with milestones, itemized budget, and project narrative with outcomes and success metrics. Submit application online by the deadline. Applications are reviewed by the Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion, which evaluates alignment with eligible activities and makes recommendations to the Secretary of Commerce for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Capital Access Program (MD CAP) helps small businesses get financing. It creates a Loan Reserve Program to encourage banks to lend to businesses that might otherwise have trouble getting a loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program helps lenders cover losses if a small business defaults on a loan. It can cover up to 100% of losses for participating lenders. The maximum loan amount that can be enrolled is $250,000. Loans can have a term up to ten years. The lender, borrower, and the MD CAP program all contribute to a reserve account to cover potential losses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses and non-profit organizations with fewer than 50 employees. Businesses must meet SBA size standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for start-up costs, business expansion, or working capital. The program does not fund passive real estate investments, residential living facilities, certain adult entertainment businesses, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Loan term may not exceed ten years
Loan amount may not exceed $250,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a small business applies for a loan directly with a participating lender. The lender determines if the loan qualifies for the program. If it does, the lender enrolls the loan. The lender, the borrower, and the MD CAP program all contribute to a reserve fund. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form to the Maryland Capital Access Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Capital Access Program (MD CAP) is a loan loss reserve / credit enhancement program that helps small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Maryland access financing they might not otherwise qualify for. Administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce, MD CAP encourages banks, credit unions, and community development financial institutions (CDFIs) to make loans to small businesses by establishing a loan loss reserve fund. The lender, borrower, and MD CAP each contribute to a reserve account — typically 2% from the lender, 1% from the borrower, and a 3% match from MD CAP, totaling 6% of the original loan amount. In the event of default, the lender can file a claim against the reserve account. Borrowers may receive more favorable loan terms because lenders have added protection against default losses. The program is particularly focused on businesses located in Maryland Priority Funding Areas, though it is available statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MD CAP establishes a Loan Loss Reserve Program to help small businesses obtain loans up to $250,000 from participating lenders. The lender, borrower, and MD CAP each contribute to a reserve account (typically 2% from the lender, 1% from the borrower, and a 3% match from MD CAP — totaling 6% of the original loan amount). MD CAP may provide up to 100% coverage to participating lenders on losses from certain loan defaults. Loans may be short or long term, fixed or variable rate, secured or unsecured, and have a term not exceeding ten years. In the event of default and after normal collection efforts, the lender files a one-page claim form to draw on the reserve account.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (including nonprofits) with fewer than 50 employees that have difficulty obtaining traditional business financing, particularly those located in Maryland Priority Funding Areas. Also available to participating lenders (banks, credit unions, financial institutions, and CDFIs) enrolled in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business start-up costs, expansion, working capital, or other business financing through lines of credit or term loans. Loans for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, community halls, hospitals, colleges, adult entertainment, gambling, check cashing, liquor stores, pawn/gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland small businesses statewide. Businesses located in Maryland Priority Funding Areas (as approved by the Maryland Department of Planning under the Smart Growth Act of 1997) are specifically noted as eligible.
requirements_list: Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Business must be located in Maryland
Borrower must apply to a participating MD CAP lender
Lender must be a credit union, financial institution, or CDFI
Lender must complete the MD CAP application and be certified by Commerce as a participating lender
Qualifying loans must not exceed $250,000
Loan term must not exceed ten years
Lender must enroll a qualifying loan within 30 days of first disbursement

Loans for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, community halls, hospitals, colleges, adult entertainment, gambling, check cashing, liquor stores, pawn/gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction are not eligible
Business must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area

Loan proceeds cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, community halls, hospitals, colleges, adult entertainment, gambling, or sectarian religious instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Lenders apply for registration using the MD CAP Lender Application form and must be certified by Commerce as a participating lender. Once registered, a small business applies to a participating lender for a qualifying loan. The lender underwrites and enrolls the loan (or a portion of it) in MD CAP. The lender, borrower, and MD CAP each deposit contributions into a reserve account. A one-page loan enrollment form with summary information is submitted to MD CAP by the lender. In the event of default and after normal collection efforts, the lender files a one-page claim form to draw on the reserve account. Current participating lenders have included BB&T and PNC Bank.

structured_extraction.program_description: An online mapping tool that helps child care providers and other businesses assess demand in their area, find locations where services are most needed, and connect to financing options and business support resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online tool that shows where families need child care the most, helping businesses validate location, expansion, or capacity decisions. Also connects users to additional financing options and business support resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and child care providers evaluating location, expansion, or financing decisions in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tool used for planning and demand assessment; not a direct funding program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the tool directly at compass.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DefTech Center helps entrepreneurs, technology companies, and DoD lab personnel commercialize defense technologies developed at Department of Defense labs in Maryland (NSA/Fort Meade, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Ft. Detrick, and others). It provides information, networking, education, and one-on-one mentoring to help clients navigate the Technology Transfer (T2) process, license DoD-developed technology, and develop commercialization plans. Established in 2018 as a pilot program in the APG community with DoD Office of Economic Adjustment funding, it expanded statewide in 2019 with U.S. Department of Commerce Economic Development Administration funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance including: guidance on navigating the DoD Technology Transfer (T2) process; networking with T2 staff, scientists, and engineers; education on topics such as IP and patent law, market-oriented product development, and customer discovery; and one-on-one mentoring for licensing DoD technologies, market analysis, and commercialization planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs looking to commercialize DoD-developed technology, technology companies seeking to establish a presence in Maryland, and scientists or engineers working at DoD research labs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides free technical assistance services, not direct funding. Services include information, networking, education, mentoring, one-on-one technical assistance for licensing technology from federal labs, market analysis, and commercialization planning support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, focused on DoD labs in Maryland including NSA/Fort Meade, Aberdeen Proving Ground, and Ft. Detrick.
requirements_list: Must be an entrepreneur, technology company, or DoD lab personnel in Maryland
Interest in licensing or commercializing technology developed at a DoD research lab in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application process. Contact the DefTech team for more information or to arrange a meeting: visit www.deftechmd.com or email info@deftechmd.com. Alternatively, contact Jill Porter, Business Development Director, by phone or email to learn more about Fort Meade technology transfer opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland E-Nnovation Initiative Fund (MEIF) offers a state match to private funds raised to support endowed research chairs at Maryland's nonprofit higher education institutions. The Governor appropriates $8.5 million annually, and investment earnings from the endowments are used to support basic and applied research in scientific and technical fields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state provides matching funds to private donations raised for endowed research chairs. The Governor appropriates $8.5 million per year for the program (FY 2027 allocation: $8,500,000 available for award after administrative costs). Investment earnings on the endowments fund basic and applied research. A minimum qualified donation threshold of $500,000 applies, and greater-than-1:1 match ratios are prioritized. Awards have ranged from $200,000 to over $3 million per institution per year. Authority issues notice of approval or rejection within 60 days after the application is deemed complete.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit institutions of higher education (NPIHEs) in Maryland seeking to establish research endowments through state-matched private donations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing research endowments to fund basic and applied research in scientific and technical fields, including endowed chairs at Maryland higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonprofit institutions of higher education located in Maryland that receive State funds in the annual operating budget. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions apply beyond the statewide Maryland requirement.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit institution of higher education located in Maryland
Institution must receive State funds in the annual operating budget
Institution must secure matching private donations (minimum qualified donation: $500,000)
Applications must be submitted on the Authority-provided form as a single PDF document
Application must include: research endowment plan, institution legal name, addresses, contact person, federal EIN, president certification, and other requested information
Application must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. on the applicable submission date (Round 1: June 1; Round 2: November 1)
Deficient applications may be cured within a 5-business-day cure period
Post-award: annual reporting required by November 15 each year for the 12-month period ending June 30
Post-award: five-year comprehensive impact report required after endowment installation
Post-award: Authority inquiries must be responded to within 45 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There are two submission dates per fiscal year: Round 1 on June 1 (before the fiscal year begins) and Round 2 on November 1 (during the fiscal year). First-round submissions have priority for fund allocation. Submit a completed application (single PDF document) by email to sarah.sheppard1@maryland.gov by 5:00 p.m. on the applicable submission date. The Authority must publish evaluation criteria at least 90 days before the first submission date. The Authority has 5 business days to notify applicants of deficiencies (cure period applies) and 60 days from application completion to issue notice of approval or rejection. Application form and instructions are available on the program page. Annual Reports for existing award holders should be emailed to Sarah Sheppard.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAF provides loans of up to $150,000 for small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees. The program helps small businesses upgrade or modernize operations, develop or expand commercial applications for technology, or enter new markets. Eligible businesses include manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, technology firms, service companies, and skilled trades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $150,000 for small businesses with fewer than 50 employees. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, and site improvements. Applicants must demonstrate creditworthiness, ability to repay, and inability to qualify for loans from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees that cannot qualify for loans from traditional lending sources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, and site improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses in all regions of Maryland

Demonstrate creditworthiness and ability to repay
Unable to qualify for loans from traditional lending sources
Submit a business plan with 3-year projections, cost budget, and sources and uses of funds
Provide a current personal financial statement
Provide a listing of all owners and percentages of ownership
Provide resume of principal owner(s)
Provide personal federal tax returns with all schedules for the most recent two years
Provide business federal tax returns with all schedules for the most recent two years
Explain the amount of personal or business funds to be contributed to the project
Explain the type of collateral to be provided to secure the loan

Submit the completed application along with required documents (business plan, financial statements, tax returns, ownership listing, resume, collateral information) to the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) / Advantage Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: Advantage Maryland (also known as MEDAAF — Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund) is a flexible, broad-based program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that provides conditional grants, loans, and investments to support economic development. It funds business attraction and retention, infrastructure support, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare/child care, revolving loan funds, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste initiatives, and local strategic planning. Awards are made on a competitive basis and projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas. The program offers six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities — loans up to $10 million or 20% of fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity — loans up to $5 million, conditional loans and grants up to $2 million; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO — up to $3 million for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, feasibility studies, and economic development plans; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund — grants of $250,000 annually to capitalize local revolving loan funds; (5) Special Purposes Loan — targeting specific state priorities including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care; (6) Sunny Day Fund — promotes extraordinary economic development opportunities in Priority Funding Areas. Assistance is provided to both businesses and political jurisdictions, and generally cannot exceed 70% of total project costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive conditional grants, loans, and equity investments awarded through six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities — loans up to $10 million or 20% of fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity — loans up to $5 million, conditional loans and grants up to $2 million; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO — up to $3 million for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, feasibility studies, and economic development plans; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund — grants of $250,000 annually to capitalize local revolving loan funds; (5) Special Purposes Loan — targets Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care; (6) Sunny Day Fund — promotes extraordinary economic development opportunities in Priority Funding Areas. Assistance generally cannot exceed 70% of total project costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in eligible industry sectors and local jurisdictions seeking to attract or retain businesses, support infrastructure, redevelop brownfields, establish revolving loan funds, or conduct local strategic planning within Maryland Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business attraction and retention, infrastructure improvements, land acquisition, fixed asset acquisition, leasehold improvements, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, child care/daycare, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste initiatives, revolving loan funds, feasibility studies, and local strategic planning within Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland Priority Funding Areas. Assistance generally cannot exceed 70% of total project costs.
requirements_list: Project must be within a Priority Funding Area
Project must include a County Resolution
Project must support significant economic development initiatives

Business must operate in an eligible industry sector (Aerospace/UAS, Agriculture/Forestry/Resource-Based Industries, Biotechnology/Health Care Technology/Pharmaceuticals, Businesses with U.S. or regional headquarters in Maryland, Distribution/Warehousing/Transportation/Logistics, Environmental Technology/Renewable Energy/Energy Production, Financial Services, Technology and Cybersecurity, or Manufacturing)
Assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs (with some exceptions)
Sunny Day Fund applicants must have a strong balance sheet and be credit worthy
Sunny Day Fund projects must be consistent with the State's strategic economic development plan
Sunny Day Fund participants must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of the Sunny Day assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the business development representative in your region for more information. Contact information for regional representatives is available on the Maryland Department of Commerce website at commerce.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for Foreign Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: A business incubation and market-entry program that helps international companies—particularly Korean businesses—test and establish a presence in the U.S. market at low cost. Through a network of partner organizations statewide (including the Innovation Station Business Incubator in Prince George's County), participants receive subsidized office space, a $10,000 Maryland Global Gateway Grant, one-on-one mentoring, business development support, assistance with business registration, immigration, and accounting, recruitment help, training workshops, customer introductions, and access to public and private funding tools and tax incentives—all for up to six months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 6 months of subsidized office space, a $10,000 Maryland Global Gateway Grant, private or collaborative workspaces, one-on-one mentoring and business development support, assistance with business registration, immigration, and accounting, recruitment help, training workshops, and customer introductions, plus access to public and private funding tools and tax incentives. Additional resources available through Prince George's County partners include the EDI Fund ($50 million available), ExportMD grant program (up to $5,000 plus up to 40 hours of Commerce foreign trade representative services), and state tax credits and incentives (job creation, facility, equipment). Funding can also be used for physical, programmatic, and other costs related to entering the U.S. market.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foreign companies, particularly Korean businesses, that want to explore entering or establishing operations in the U.S. market, including through the Innovation Station Business Incubator in Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Office space costs, business registration, immigration and accounting assistance, business development, training, market entry support, and other costs related to entering the U.S. market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide through a network of partner organizations. Companies must physically locate in Maryland within six months of the application round. One key partner site is the Innovation Station Business Incubator in Prince George's County, which is located within a foreign-trade zone.
requirements_list: Must be legally registered as a business in its home country for at least one year.
Must have at least five full-time equivalent employees.
Must have at least $500,000 USD in sales revenue and/or external investment in a single year (2023 or 2024).
Must be able to locate physically in Maryland within six months of the application round.
Applicant must be an international company (particularly Korean businesses are targeted).
Must participate through a Maryland Global Gateway partner organization.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online portal at commerce.maryland.gov/softlanding. The Department of Commerce will help you find a partner organization. To receive funds, you must sign an agreement with a Global Gateway partner. For more information, contact global.gateway@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects by issuing taxable and tax-exempt private activity revenue bonds and providing credit insurance (loan guarantees) to reduce lender risk. The program expands capital access for small and medium-sized businesses, historically disadvantaged businesses, manufacturers, nonprofit organizations, and businesses in rural areas. Programs include taxable and tax-exempt industrial revenue bonds and conventional, bond, and linked deposit credit insurance programs. Eligible uses include land acquisition, building acquisition, construction, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, certain soft costs, energy-related projects, and working capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA issues private activity revenue bonds (taxable and tax-exempt) and provides credit insurance in the form of loan guarantees. Taxable bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds are available to 501(c)(3) nonprofits, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects. The Conventional Credit Insurance Program insures up to 80% (not to exceed $2.5 million) of a lender transaction; export transactions may be insured up to 90%. The Bond Program insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million. Linked Deposits provide below-market-rate loans to eligible small businesses in qualifying rural high-unemployment areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and medium-sized commercial and industrial businesses located in Priority Funding Areas (excluding retail), manufacturers, nonprofit organizations, and day care providers. Also includes businesses seeking long-term capital or credit enhancement for economic development projects, as well as historically disadvantaged businesses and businesses in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, building acquisition, construction costs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, certain eligible soft costs, energy-related projects, working capital, and fixed asset financing. Credit enhancement for lenders financing economic development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must generally be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area. Manufacturers, nonprofits, and day care providers may also be eligible. Linked Deposits are available only in qualifying rural high-unemployment areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a commercial or industrial business in a Priority Funding Area (retail excluded), a manufacturer, a not-for-profit entity, or a day care provider
Tax-exempt bonds are limited to 501(c)(3) nonprofits, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects
Linked Deposits available only in qualifying rural high-unemployment areas
Additional federal tax law limitations apply to specific transaction types
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Bruce Alderman, Finance Specialist at the Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs, for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: IITC fosters growth in Maryland's technology sectors by incentivizing investment in early-stage companies. It provides a refundable income tax credit to qualified investors who invest in Qualified Maryland Technology Companies (QMTCs) — for-profit companies headquartered in Maryland that are developing innovative technology in eligible sectors. NOTE: This program has sunset and is no longer operational.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refundable income tax credit equal to 33% of an eligible investment in a Qualified Maryland Technology Company (QMTC), up to $250,000 in tax credits. Increases to 50% of an eligible investment, up to $500,000, if the QMTC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. Enhanced credits are available for Opportunity Zone fund investors (up to $300,000 at 33% or up to $500,000 at 50%) and for investors in QMTCs located in RISE Zones (50%, up to $500,000). The minimum investment is $25,000. Credits are issued on a first-come, first-served basis up to the annual budget. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program has sunset and is no longer operational
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified investors (individuals or entities investing at least $25,000 in a QMTC) and Qualified Maryland Technology Companies (QMTCs) in eligible technology sectors including advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, artificial intelligence, blue technology, cybersecurity, education, energy and sustainability, financial, life sciences, quantum, and sensors and robotics.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit for investors in early-stage Maryland technology companies. Credits reduce or eliminate Maryland income tax liability, with any excess refunded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: QMTCs must be headquartered and based in Maryland. Enhanced credits available for QMTCs in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset counties, as well as QMTCs located in Opportunity Zones or RISE Zones.
requirements_list: Investor must invest at least $25,000 in a single QMTC transaction
Investor must file an income tax return in any jurisdiction
QMTC must be organized for profit and engaged in research, development, or commercialization of innovative proprietary technology in an eligible sector
QMTC must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland
QMTC must own or have licensed its proprietary technology
QMTC must have aggregate capitalization of at least $100,000
QMTC must have fewer than 50 full-time employees
QMTC must not have participated in IITC for more than three prior fiscal years
QMTC must not have publicly traded securities
QMTC must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and current on all tax obligations
Founders, current employees of the QMTC, and their spouses/minor children are ineligible as investors
Pension plans, IRAs, and similar retirement accounts are ineligible as investors
Companies certified as qualified Maryland biotechnology companies under the Biotechnology Investment Incentive Tax Credit Program are ineligible as QMTCs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. QMTC submits Form B application through Commerce's online system. 2. Investor submits Form A application through Commerce's online system before the deadline. 3. Timely investors receive a username and reference number. 4. Investors use the username and reference number to register in the Online Electronic Queue on the registration date, which determines first-come, first-served order. 5. Commerce reviews applications in submission order. 6. Approved investors receive an Initial Certificate of Approval and must invest within 30 days. 7. Investor provides proof of investment within 10 days of investing. 8. Commerce issues a Final Certificate of Approval awarding the tax credit. NOTE: Program has sunset and is no longer accepting applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland MADE (Manufacturing Assets Deployed for Energy) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland MADE grant program provides grants to small Maryland manufacturers to invest in the adoption and deployment of smart manufacturing and high-performance manufacturing technologies that will increase energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and enable lasting improvements. Awards are up to $15,000 and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until all funds are disbursed. Funded by the Maryland Department of Commerce with support from the U.S. Department of Energy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $15,000 are available to eligible small manufacturers with 3 to 75 full-time employees. Funds are disbursed as 100% reimbursement upon completion of the project or installation of equipment with proof of paid expenses. Applicants must carry the $15,000 expenditure through the project and then request reimbursement from Commerce. Projects must be completed within 4 months of the executed agreement. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, limited to available funds. The application period is open for 60 days or until fully funded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open for 60 days or until fully funded; FY2025 cycle opened January 12, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small Maryland manufacturers with 3 to 75 full-time employees engaged in manufacturing (NAICS codes 31-33) seeking to adopt smart or high-performance manufacturing technologies to improve energy efficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expenses for support devices, machinery, and equipment related to advanced manufacturing technologies such as smart thermostats, variable frequency drives, energy meters, compressed air system upgrades, high-efficiency motors, power factor correction devices, and other approved smart manufacturing technologies (e.g., digital twins, industrial IoT, additive manufacturing, robotics, AI/machine learning).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must take place at a Maryland manufacturing facility.
requirements_list: Proposed project must involve Advanced Manufacturing Technologies as described
Proposed project must take place at a Maryland manufacturing facility
Be an existing business in good standing with the State of Maryland
Applicant must not have an open Manufacturing 4.0 grant project
Have between 3 and 75 total full-time employees (defined as working at least 1,800 hours in a 12-month period)
Have a two-digit NAICS code prefix of 31-33
Be in good standing with federal OSHA and Maryland OSHA regulations
Have completed a Maryland MADE technology initial assessment review through Maryland MEP (contact skeith@mdmep.org)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a Maryland MADE technology initial assessment review through Maryland MEP. Submit an application by email to m4grant.commerce@maryland.gov during an open application period. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants are contacted within 2-3 weeks of submission and notified of selection or non-selection.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Manufacturing 4.0 (M4.0) Grant Program provides grants to small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers to invest in Industry 4.0-related technologies, machinery, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and digital business practices to remain competitive and drive growth. Grants range from $25,000 to $500,000, covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3–50 employees) and up to 50% for mid-sized manufacturers (51–250 employees). Twenty percent of available funds are reserved for small manufacturers with 3–50 employees. The program is legislatively mandated with funding through FY2028.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from $25,000 to $500,000. Small manufacturers (3–50 employees) receive grants covering up to 75% of project costs, requiring a 25% match. Mid-sized manufacturers (51–250 employees) receive grants covering up to 50% of project costs, requiring a 50% match. Funds are disbursed as 50% at notice of award and 50% upon project completion with proof of expenses. Applicants located in ENOUGH Act eligible census tracts receive a +5 point scoring bonus.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for the 2026 program closed on August 29, 2025 at 5PM.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers with 3–250 full-time employees, in business at least 2 years, with a two-digit NAICS code of 31–33.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Industry 4.0 technologies and investments including advanced sensors, AI, big data and analytics, cloud computing and cybersecurity, embedded software, ERP and data analytics software, robots and autonomous equipment, systems integration projects, automation, robotics, SCADA systems, CNC equipment, real-time data integration, equipment, infrastructure/facilities improvements, consulting, training, and employee training or consulting costs related to implementation of new systems, technologies, or equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be an existing business in good standing with the State of Maryland with a physical location in Maryland. Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants in ENOUGH Act eligible census tracts receive a +5 point scoring bonus.
requirements_list: Must be an existing business in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must have a physical location in Maryland
Must have between 3 and 250 total full-time employees (working at least 1,800 hours in a 12-month period)
Must have a two-digit NAICS code of 31–33 (manufacturing)
Must have been established for a minimum of 2 years
Must be in good standing with federal OSHA and Maryland OSHA regulations (no unresolved violations in past 5 years)
Must demonstrate ability to successfully implement the proposed project
Must demonstrate an overall commitment to or strategy for Industry 4.0 adoption
Must demonstrate ability to provide matching funds (25% for 3–50 employees; 50% for 51–250 employees)
Must complete the CESMII Technology Assessment offered through Maryland MEP
Recipients of FY2023 and FY2024 M4.0 grants may reapply only if their previous grants are completed
Must provide affidavit attestations (no convictions, bankruptcy, pending litigation, delinquent taxes, outstanding judgments)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a competitive application during the open application window via an online portal. Applications are evaluated on technical capability, operational experience, financial capacity, and overall project impact to the company and the State of Maryland. Larger grant requests require more detailed proposals. Pre-qualification screening is part of the process. Applications for the FY26 program were accepted from August 1, 2025 to August 29, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and Funds - Nonprofit, Interest-Free Micro Bridge Loan Account (NIMBL)
structured_extraction.program_description: NIMBL is an interest-free micro bridge loan program that provides short-term financing to small nonprofit organizations between the date a government grant or contract is awarded and when the funds are actually received. Loans of up to $25,000 cover operating expenses only and must be repaid no later than the date of the final government grant or contract payment to the nonprofit. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce and applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Eligible nonprofits must have annual revenues not greater than $750,000, have been in existence for no more than 10 years, and principally provide health, education, environmental, agricultural, or social services through community-based programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free micro bridge loans up to $25,000 to cover operating expenses while the nonprofit awaits receipt of an awarded government grant or contract. Loan repayment must be made no later than the date of the final grant or contract payment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. FY 2026 appropriation is $1,000,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small nonprofits (annual revenues under $750,000, in existence 10 years or less) that provide health, education, environmental, agricultural, or social services through community-based programs and have been awarded government grants or contracts but have not yet received the funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, bridging the gap between the award date of a government grant or contract and actual receipt of those funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nonprofit must be located in the State of Maryland and be recognized as tax-exempt under IRS Section 501(c)(3), (4), or (6).
requirements_list: Annual revenues not greater than $750,000
In existence for not more than 10 years
Principal purpose is providing health, education, environmental, agricultural, or social services through community-based programs
Located in Maryland
IRS tax-exempt status under Section 501(c)(3), (4), or (6)
Must have written confirmation of a government grant or contract award but not yet received the funds
Loans cannot exceed $25,000
Loan repayment must be made no later than the date of the final grant or contract payment
Must be a nonprofit organization
Must have a government grant or contract in place to repay the bridge loan
Must be registered with the Maryland Secretary of State
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request for an application by email to nimbl.loanfund@maryland.gov or through Commerce's online portal. A Commerce team member will respond with application materials. The full application must include: IRS Determination Letter, Good Standing Certificate from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and Maryland Secretary of State, Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws, written confirmation of government funding award, current and previous fiscal year budget documents, most recent annual report and financial statements, and a fully executed copy of the government grant or contract. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and processed within approximately 30 calendar days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_description: Overview page listing financial incentive programs available to startups in Maryland, operated by the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The page is an overview/hub page listing multiple startup funding programs. Specific program details are not described on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Startup businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Varies by individual program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Venture Fund provides equity investment capital to early-stage and growth-stage companies in Maryland. It supports innovation and entrepreneurship by investing in high-potential startups and emerging businesses across the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investment capital provided to eligible Maryland companies. Specific investment amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage and growth-stage for-profit companies in Maryland seeking equity investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth, innovation, and development activities for qualifying Maryland companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The page references TEDCO (http://tedco.md/) as a related resource but does not provide detailed application steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit for qualified capital expenses incurred to start, improve, or expand a winery or vineyard in Maryland. The credit equals 25% of qualifying capital expenses, with a maximum of $500,000 in total credits per tax year. If total applications exceed $500,000, credits are prorated among qualified applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses to start, improve, or expand a Maryland winery or vineyard. Maximum $500,000 in total credits per tax year; prorated if total applications exceed the cap.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland winery or vineyard owners starting, improving, or expanding their operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State income tax credit on qualified capital expenses for winery or vineyard start-up, improvement, or expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must incur qualified capital expenses for starting, improving, or expanding a Maryland winery or vineyard
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit choosemaryland.org for full details and to apply, or contact CCED for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Military Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business Loan Program (MPVOLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MPVOLP provides no-interest loans to businesses owned by military veterans, reservists, and National Guard personnel, as well as small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ or are owned by such persons. For reservists or National Guard members called to active duty, funds cover identifiable business costs resulting from the call to active duty. For service-disabled veterans and businesses that employ them, funds help cover costs of making a home, motor vehicle, or workplace accessible to individuals with disabilities and other necessary expenses. Loan amounts range from $1,000 to $100,000 with terms of one to eight years at zero interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest loans ranging from $1,000 to $100,000. Loan maturity is one to eight years. The repayment period generally does not exceed the useful life of the equipment purchased.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: New applications are being accepted from July 1, 2025 through August 29, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veteran-owned small businesses, businesses owned by military reservists and National Guard members called to active duty, and small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ such persons, including service-disabled veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business expenses resulting from a call to active duty; costs of making a home, motor vehicle, or workplace accessible for service-disabled veterans; and other necessary expenses for eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran-owned small business, a business owned by a military reservist or National Guard member called to active duty, or a small business with 50 or fewer employees that employs such persons.

For reservists/National Guard: funds must be used for identifiable business costs resulting from the call to active duty; loan may be made from the date of call through six months after end of active duty.
Business Plan with 3-year projections, cost budget, and sources and uses of funds.
Current Personal Financial Statement.
Listing of all owners and percentages of ownership.
Resume of principal owner(s).
Personal Federal Tax Returns with all schedules (most recent two years).
Business Federal Tax Returns with all schedules (most recent two years).
Explanation of personal or business funds to be contributed to the project.
Explanation of collateral to be provided to secure the loan.
Terms of 1 to 8 years.
0% interest rate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce (Commerce). Commerce coordinates with the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families (DVMF) for an eligibility review. Once DVMF confirms basic eligibility, Commerce conducts a financial review and underwriting using standard commercial credit criteria. Send inquiries to veteran.mpvoloanfund@maryland.gov to obtain an application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The More Jobs for Marylanders program promotes growth of the manufacturing sector in Maryland by providing tax incentives for job creation, encouraging investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation, and funding job training and apprenticeship programs. Manufacturers that locate or expand in Maryland and create new jobs may qualify for income tax credits, property tax credits, sales and use tax refunds, and fee waivers for up to a 10-year benefit period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible manufacturers in Prince George's County (a Tier 1 jurisdiction) may receive: (1) a refundable credit against State income tax; (2) a credit against the State's portion of property tax; (3) a refund of sales and use tax; and (4) a waiver of fees charged by SDAT. These benefits are available for a 10-year period. Existing manufacturers qualify for a refundable income tax credit only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing manufacturers that locate or expand in Prince George's County, Maryland and create new manufacturing jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives for manufacturing job creation, investment in new equipment, and job training and apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to manufacturers locating or expanding in Prince George's County, Maryland (designated as a Tier 1 jurisdiction under the program).
requirements_list: Must be a manufacturer primarily engaged in NAICS Sector 31, 32, or 33 (excluding refiners).
Must offer ongoing job training or a postsecondary education program (e.g., tuition reimbursement).
New manufacturers must provide Notice of Intent to the Maryland Department of Commerce before establishing a facility in Maryland.
Existing manufacturers must provide Notice of Intent to the Maryland Department of Commerce before creating new jobs.
Must create at least 5 new qualified jobs (full-time, paying at least 120% of State minimum wage, filled for 12 months).
Must begin hiring within 12 months of Notice of Intent and add 5 new qualified positions within 12 months of the first new hire.
Existing manufacturers that relocate from one Maryland county to another after June 1, 2017 are not eligible.
Must be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce as a Qualified Business Entity.
Enrollment and certification must occur before June 1, 2020.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Intent to the Maryland Department of Commerce before establishing a facility (new manufacturers) or before creating new jobs (existing manufacturers). Then apply for certification as a Qualified Business Entity. Contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation or visit the Maryland Department of Commerce website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs for Marylanders Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The More Jobs for Marylanders (MJM) program promotes manufacturing job creation and business growth in Maryland by providing refundable income tax credits to eligible manufacturers and non-manufacturers that locate or expand in the state. Non-manufacturers must be located in an Opportunity Zone. The program sunsetted on June 1, 2024 — no new enrollments are accepted, but businesses that received an Enrollment Certificate before that date can still participate during their benefit period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a refundable income tax credit equal to 4.75% of wages paid for each qualified full-time position. For businesses enrolled on or after June 1, 2022, the credit is available for a 5-year consecutive benefit period (Tier 2 Areas) or 10-year consecutive benefit period (Tier 1 Areas). Additional benefits include a state real property tax credit (for new manufacturers in Tier 1 Areas that own their facility) and a sales and use tax refund for manufacturers. Total income tax credits are capped annually and issued based on priority rules.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program sunsetted on June 1, 2024; no new Enrollment Applications or Notices of Intent are being accepted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing businesses (NAICS sectors 31–33, excluding refiners) that locate or expand in Maryland, and non-manufacturing businesses that locate or expand in Maryland Opportunity Zones, that were enrolled in the program before June 1, 2024
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refundable income tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax for each qualified full-time position created; also includes state real property tax credits and sales and use tax refunds for qualifying manufacturers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Tier 1 Areas (Baltimore City and Allegany, Baltimore, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince George's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, plus all Opportunity Zones statewide) receive a 10-year benefit period. Tier 2 Areas (all other Maryland areas) receive a 5-year benefit period.
requirements_list: Business must have received an Enrollment Certificate prior to June 1, 2024 to participate
Manufacturers must be primarily engaged in NAICS Sector 31, 32, or 33 activities (excluding refiners)
Manufacturers must offer ongoing job training or a post-secondary education program (e.g., tuition reimbursement)
Manufacturers in Tier 1 Areas must create at least 10 new qualified positions; Tier 2 Areas require at least 20
Non-manufacturers must be located in an Opportunity Zone and create at least 10 qualified positions
Qualified positions must be full-time, pay at least 150% of state minimum wage (manufacturers) or at least $50,000/year (non-manufacturers), and be filled for 12 months
Business must begin hiring within 12 months of its Notice of Intent to Commerce
Existing businesses that moved their facility from one Maryland county to another after June 1, 2017 are not eligible
If the number of qualified positions falls below the level established in the first benefit year, the business is removed from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses already enrolled must submit an Initial Tax Credit Application each year (during an application period established after July 1) to reserve income tax credits, then submit a Final Tax Credit Application once jobs have been filled for 12 months. Applications are submitted through Commerce's online portal. Commerce is no longer accepting new Notices of Intent or Enrollment Applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The One Maryland Tax Credit is a Maryland state income tax credit for businesses that invest in an economic development project in a Tier 1 County (distressed county) by acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, or equipping a facility in a Priority Funding Area (or qualified opportunity zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties), or by relocating to Maryland and furnishing or equipping a new location.
