The credit rewards businesses that incur significant eligible project costs and create a minimum number of new, full-time qualified jobs within 24 months. Credit amounts are tiered by investment level and number of new jobs created: up to $1 million for 10–24 new qualified positions (minimum $500,000 in eligible project costs), up to $2.5 million for 25–49 positions (minimum $2.5 million in eligible project costs), and up to $5 million for 50 or more positions (minimum $5 million in eligible project costs). The credit can be applied against Maryland state income tax (or insurance premiums tax for insurance companies) and carried forward for up to 10 years after the certified credit year. Beginning in the fourth year after the credit year, the business may apply the credit against its state income tax liability and request a refund, limited annually to payroll withholding attributable to qualified positions.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit of up to $5 million based on job creation and eligible project costs. Credit tiers: up to $1 million for 10–24 new qualified positions (minimum $500,000 in eligible project costs); up to $2.5 million for 25–49 positions (minimum $2.5 million in eligible project costs); up to $5 million for 50 or more positions (minimum $5 million in eligible project costs). The credit may be carried forward for up to 10 years after the certified credit year. Beginning in the fourth year after the credit year, the business may apply the credit against its state income tax liability and request a refund, limited annually to payroll withholding attributable to qualified positions. Insurance companies may apply the credit against their insurance premium tax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and nonprofit corporations that locate or expand operations in a Priority Funding Area (or qualified opportunity zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties) within a Tier 1 (economically distressed) Maryland county and create at least 10 new full-time jobs paying at least 120% of the state minimum wage. Also includes businesses in eligible industries relocating to Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax (or insurance premiums tax for insurance companies). Eligible project costs include acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, or equipping a business facility; costs related to relocating a business from outside Maryland and furnishing or equipping the new location; land acquisition, utility installation, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunications equipment, and office furniture.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must locate or expand in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or qualified opportunity zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties, within a Tier 1 County. As of December 2025, Tier 1 counties are: Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, and Wicomico. Worcester County remains eligible under the 24-month look-back provision through September 2026. Tier 1 status is reviewed monthly.
requirements_list: Business must submit a written Declaration of Intent to Maryland Commerce before incurring eligible costs or creating new qualified jobs.
Business must be certified as a qualified business entity by Commerce (Preliminary and Final Certification required); certifications must be issued after June 30, 2019 to qualify under HB 1295 rules.
Business must create at least 10 new full-time qualified positions at the project within 24 months.

Qualified positions must be full-time (at least 840 hours during at least 24 weeks in a 6-month period), pay at least 120% of the state minimum wage ($18.00/hour as of January 1, 2024), be filled for 12 months, and be net new jobs to Maryland.
Business must incur at least $500,000 in eligible project costs (higher tiers require $2.5 million+ or $5 million+ in costs and 25+ or 50+ new jobs respectively).
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or qualified opportunity zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties, within a Tier 1 County.

Business must be engaged in an eligible activity (manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, agriculture, forestry, fishing, public utility, research/development/testing, biotechnology, business services, warehousing, filmmaking, resort and recreation, computer programming/data processing, central financial/real estate/insurance services, company headquarters, or cannabis operations as of July 1, 2023).
Business may not claim both the One Maryland Tax Credit and the Job Creation Tax Credit in the same tax year.
Business must submit an annual report to Commerce by April 1 of each year after the year the eligible project is placed in service, during the carry-forward period.
Business must maintain records of costs, employment, and withholding information.
Construction must begin within 12 months of notification or application submission, and the project must be completed within 3 years of construction start.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a written Notice of Intent to Maryland Commerce (taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov) before incurring eligible costs or creating new jobs. 2. Register for an account at the Commerce online portal (https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcreditsregister). 3. Log in and submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit with projected job and wage data. 4. Commerce reviews and issues a Preliminary Certificate of Eligibility (estimated 30–60 days). 5. Once eligible project costs are incurred and at least 10 qualified jobs have been filled for 12 months, submit a Final Application with documentation of costs and qualified positions. 6. Commerce reviews and issues a Final Certificate of Eligibility (estimated 120 days), which the business attaches to its tax return. Annual reports must be submitted by April 1 of each year after the project is placed in service for as long as the credit is being claimed.

structured_extraction.program_description: PWQ is a matching training grant program that helps small and mid-sized manufacturing and technology companies in Maryland improve the skills of their existing workers. The program reimburses up to 50% of qualified training costs for formal classroom and on-the-job training in new technologies and production processes. It is designed to improve employee productivity, increase employment stability, and strengthen the competitive position of Maryland businesses. The program also provides support services to help companies identify and address workforce needs. At least 60% of available funds must be awarded to employers with 150 or fewer employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grant that reimburses up to 50% of qualified direct training costs. Minimum grant award is $5,000 (requiring a minimum total training project cost of $10,000). By statute, an employer may not receive more than $200,000 per year from the program. At least 60% of available funds must be awarded to employers with 150 or fewer employees in Maryland. Grants may also be awarded to community colleges, private career schools, State-accredited training agencies, trade associations, and union-sponsored training programs. Funds may not be used for capital equipment or trainee wages.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturing and technology companies seeking to train existing or newly hired workers in job-specific skills and new technologies. Prioritizes businesses with 150 or fewer employees; encourages participation of small and minority-owned businesses. Grants may also be awarded to community colleges, private career schools, State-accredited training agencies, trade associations, and union-sponsored training programs acting on behalf of employers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimburse costs of worker training projects including curriculum development, course books and materials, and instructor salary and expenses. Training must be formal, third-party, classroom, and/or on-the-job training that increases business efficiency and competitive advantages. Funds may also support training for new technologies and production processes, improving productivity, and increasing employment stability. Funds may NOT be used for capital equipment or trainee wages.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a Maryland employer with operations in Maryland. Priority is given to manufacturing and technology companies and employers threatened by foreign or domestic competition; other regionally important industries may qualify with justification.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland employer located in the State
Minimum of ten full-time employees
Must not be in arrears with any State taxing agency
Must not be in default with any Maryland Commerce program
At least 60% of available funds are reserved for employers with 150 or fewer employees in the State
Priority given to manufacturers and employers threatened by foreign or domestic competition; other industries may qualify with regional justification
Small and minority-owned businesses encouraged to apply
Training assistance provided only at the specific request of an employer or group of employers
Funds may not be used for capital equipment or trainee wages
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Commerce regional representative who covers the county or region where your business is located to apply for PWQ funding. Applications can also be initiated through the Maryland Department of Commerce website. The program operates on a request basis — assistance is provided at the specific request of an employer or group of employers. For questions about existing applications, email pwq.grantfund@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Port of Baltimore Emergency Business Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides emergency grant funding to for-profit businesses that have been financially harmed by the disruption to Port of Baltimore operations following the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Eligible businesses can receive grants to offset lost revenue or increased operating costs caused by reduced port operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 per business to offset lost revenue or increased operating costs resulting from reduced Port of Baltimore operations. Funds may be used for general operating expenses including rent, utilities, maintenance, fuel, supplies, insurance premiums, employee payroll, and loan repayments. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Grant funds may not be used for repayment of other government disaster relief assistance or to cover costs already paid by other sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with operations or shipments primarily reliant on the Port of Baltimore that have suffered economic injury from the disruption to port operations after March 26, 2024, and have between 2 and 499 full-time equivalent W-2 employees in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating expenses including rent, utilities, maintenance, fuel, supplies, insurance premiums, employee payroll, and loan repayments (principal and interest). Funds may not be used to repay other government disaster relief assistance or to cover costs already paid by other assistance sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have principal operations located in Maryland or use program funds for operations within Maryland.
requirements_list: Operations or shipments are primarily reliant on the use of or access to the Port of Baltimore
Business operations or shipments have been hindered or halted due to reduced Port of Baltimore operations
Principal business operations are located in Maryland or funds will be used for Maryland operations
Business has at least 2 full-time equivalent W-2 employees but fewer than 500 full-time or equivalent workers in Maryland
Must provide evidence of Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must submit a completed W-9 form
Must submit filed U.S. Corporate or Partnership Federal Tax Return for 2023 (or most recently available)
Must provide a narrative describing how the bridge collapse affected operations
Must provide documentation demonstrating increased costs or decreased net revenue
Must disclose business insurance status and deductibles
Must disclose status and amount of other state and federal disaster assistance applications
Must attest to intent to continue operations at the Port of Baltimore upon resumption of full operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the online portal (currently closed). Applicants must gather required documents before entering the portal: SDAT Good Standing evidence, completed W-9, 2023 federal tax return, narrative about bridge collapse impact, supporting financial documentation, and insurance information. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: This page serves as a hub for Maryland Department of Commerce programs available to lending institutions. The page does not describe any individual program in depth.

Maryland's Research and Development (R&D) Tax Credit provides state income tax credits to businesses that incur qualified R&D expenses in Maryland. The credit equals 10% of eligible R&D expenses that exceed the Maryland Base Amount for the taxable year. The total annual cap is $12 million, with a $3.5 million set-aside for small businesses and $8.5 million for other applicants. A single applicant may not receive more than $250,000. Small businesses with net book value assets under $5 million may receive a refundable credit if the credit exceeds their income tax liability. Unused credits may be carried forward for up to 7 tax years. The program is in effect through June 30, 2027 per Chapter 114 of 2021.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 10% of Maryland qualified R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year in excess of the Maryland Base Amount. Total statutory cap is $12 million per year ($3.5 million set-aside for small businesses; $8.5 million for other applicants). Maximum credit per applicant is $250,000. Credits for small businesses (net book value assets under $5 million) certified after December 15, 2012 are refundable to the extent they exceed the business's income tax liability. Unused credits may be carried forward for up to 7 tax years. Program is in effect through June 30, 2027 per Chapter 114 of 2021.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which expenses were incurred; for Tax Year 2025, the application window is June 1, 2026 through November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and individuals that incur qualified research and development expenses in Maryland, including corporations, LLCs, partnerships, and sole proprietorships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland income tax liability for qualified R&D expenses conducted in Maryland, as defined under § 41(b) and § 41(d) of the Internal Revenue Code.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: R&D activities must be conducted in Maryland (in this State). The Maryland Department of Commerce and Comptroller jointly adopt regulations to determine when research or development is considered conducted in the State, considering: location where services are performed, residence/business location of persons performing services, location where supplies used in R&D are consumed, and other factors deemed relevant. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions apply — statewide program.
requirements_list: Must incur Qualified Research and Development Expenses as defined by § 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code in Maryland.
Must submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by November 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which expenses were incurred.
Small businesses must have net book value assets of less than $5 million at the beginning or end of the taxable year.
Small businesses must submit balance sheet documentation confirming asset levels.
Parent company must apply on behalf of subsidiaries; credits are allocated among subsidiaries proportionally.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online portal at rdtaxcredit.commerce.maryland.gov by November 15. Commerce will certify the approved credit amount by February 15 of the following year. After receiving certification, the business may file an amended tax return for the certified year or claim the credit on a return filed for any of the following 7 tax years. A copy of Commerce's certification must be attached to the tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funds for infrastructure projects that support economic development, stimulate private investment, and create jobs in rural Maryland counties. Projects are proposed by the state's five tri-county regional councils in coordination with local jurisdictions. Regional projects fostering collaboration between multiple counties are encouraged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds up to $10,000,000 with no matching requirement, distributed through the state's five tri-county regional councils for public infrastructure projects, commercial/industrial property acquisition, workforce development, entrepreneurship and innovation, and planning and feasibility studies. Capital and operational expenses are eligible. Administrative costs capped at 3% of total award. All funds must be expended within 24 months of award. Interim reports required at 6 and 18 months; final report at 24 months. Direct private sector incentives, subsidies, grants, loans, and residential/housing projects are ineligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31 (hard deadline set by the Maryland Department of Commerce)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural Maryland counties and regional tri-county councils seeking to fund infrastructure and economic development projects; eligible applicants include local government entities, institutions of higher education, workforce development organizations, and not-for-profit entities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure (utilities, transportation, broadband); industry-sector infrastructure (manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, cybersecurity, agribusiness); commercial/industrial property acquisition for business parks; workforce development; entrepreneurship and innovation; planning and feasibility studies; capital and operational expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in rural counties served by Maryland's five tri-county regional councils. Eligible counties include Allegany, Garrett, and Washington County among others. Regional projects fostering collaboration between multiple counties are encouraged. Regional councils coordinate with local jurisdictions within their regions.
requirements_list: Projects must be proposed by one of the state's five tri-county regional councils
Projects must support economic development, stimulate private investment, or grow jobs
Eligible uses limited to public infrastructure, property acquisition, workforce development, or planning studies
Direct private sector incentives, subsidies, grants, loans, and residential/housing projects are ineligible
Granting land or buildings purchased with these funds to private sector entities is prohibited (sale or lease is permitted)
Regional projects which foster collaboration between multiple counties are encouraged
All funds must be expended within 24 months of award
Interim reports required at 6-month and 18-month points; final report at 24 months
Demographic/MBE information collection from contractors/vendors (voluntary response)
Administrative costs capped at 3% of total award
Clawback provisions apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Multi-stage annual process: (1) June 30 – Projects solicited from County; (2) July 26 – Projects submitted to County; (3) August 10 – Projects received by Tri-County Council (TCC); (4) August 17 – TCC identifies projects for funding and requests full applications; (5) August 26 – Full applications due (applicants must complete a form including project summary ≤250 words, budget with funding sources/amounts/uses, and economic development impact narrative); (6) August 31 – TCC and project applications submitted to Maryland Department of Commerce (hard deadline, no extensions). Proposals and questions may be submitted via email to grantmgmt@washco-md.net.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable tax credit for small businesses in Maryland that provide their employees with paid sick and safe leave, as required or beyond what is required under the Maryland Healthy Working Families Act. Businesses can claim up to $500 per qualifying employee, up to a maximum of $7,000 per business per tax year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refundable tax credit of up to $500 per qualifying employee, with a maximum of $7,000 per small business per tax year. The credit is taken against Maryland State income tax only (not against the county income tax add-on). If the credit exceeds the business's tax liability, the business receives a refund for the difference. Credits are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to annual appropriation ($5 million available for tax year 2022). After Commerce certifies the credit, the business files Maryland Tax Form 500CR electronically with the Comptroller of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program is closed; Commerce is not accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 14 or fewer employees whose primary work location is in Maryland that provide paid sick and safe leave to qualifying employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit to offset the cost of providing paid sick and safe leave to employees earning up to 250% of the federal poverty guideline for a single-person household.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Employees' primary work location must be in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must employ 14 or fewer employees whose primary work location is in Maryland
Business must provide paid sick and safe leave in accordance with the Maryland Healthy Working Families Act
Qualifying employees must earn wages equal to or less than 250% of the annual federal poverty guideline for a single-person household (e.g., $36,450/year or $17.52/hour for Tax Year 2023)
Business must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Business must be current with all Maryland tax obligations (Good Standing Certificate from the Comptroller required)
Application must include copies of employees' W-2 forms or pay stubs and a statement of accrued paid sick and safe leave for each employee claimed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce along with copies of each qualifying employee's W-2 or pay stubs and a statement of accrued paid sick and safe leave. Commerce reviews and certifies or denies the application within 45 days of receiving a complete application. After certification, the business files Maryland Tax Form 500CR electronically with the Comptroller of Maryland to claim the credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account – Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) Fund / State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) Fund — also referred to as the State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Fund — uses 1.5% of video lottery terminal proceeds from the state's six casinos to provide below-market-rate loans to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. At least 50% of funds are prioritized for businesses within targeted areas near the six casinos: Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County. The remaining 50% is available to qualifying businesses statewide. The Maryland Department of Commerce oversees the program, and regional fund managers distribute allocations. In Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties), the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (TCCWMD) manages funds through its Summit Financing Solutions lending program — all three counties are recognized as a targeted area for TCCWMD's use of SLoT funds. Cecil County businesses near Hollywood Casino may also access this resource through the Cecil County Office of Economic Development. Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000, with interest tied to the prime rate (currently prime plus 1%), maximum terms of 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market-rate loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000, distributed through regional fund managers including FSC First, Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Meridian Management Group, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Baltimore County Economic Development, City of Baltimore Development Corp., Howard County Economic Development Authority, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Summit Financing Solutions), and Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation. Interest rate is tied to the prime rate, currently prime plus 1%. Maximum loan terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Application fee is $250 (non-refundable); loans between $10,000–$25,000 require a $25 application fee. Approved borrowers pay a 1% loan origination fee at closing. At least 50% of funds go to businesses in targeted areas near Maryland's six casinos; the remaining 50% is available to eligible small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses throughout Maryland. Eligible uses include business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, leasehold improvements, equipment, start-up costs, working capital, professional/technical assistance, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland, with priority for businesses in targeted areas surrounding Maryland's six casinos (Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County). In Western Maryland, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland administers the fund for Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties (all recognized as a targeted area). Cecil County businesses near Hollywood Casino may contact the Cecil County Office of Economic Development for local assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing including commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment purchase, vehicles, furniture/fixtures, start-up costs, working capital, inventory, franchise fees, professional/technical assistance, marketing, personnel costs, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances, for small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: At least 50% of funds are prioritized for businesses within targeted areas near Maryland's six casinos (Cecil, Worcester, Anne Arundel, Allegany, Prince George's Counties, and Baltimore City); the remaining 50% is available to qualifying businesses statewide throughout Maryland. In Western Maryland, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland administers the fund for Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties, all of which are recognized as a targeted area.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women, or veteran-owned business
Must be located in Maryland
Businesses seeking priority funding must be located in targeted areas near one of Maryland's six casinos
Personal credit score of 650 generally required (lower scores considered)
Personal guaranties required from all owners with 20% or greater ownership interest
Minimum 10% equity injection required for start-up businesses
A business plan is required

Must meet standard underwriting criteria including repayment capacity, debt service coverage, financial strength of company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral protection
Collateral required: deeds of trust, machinery and equipment liens, personal guaranties, and key man life insurance
Application fee of $250 (non-refundable); $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000
Approved borrowers must pay a 1% loan origination fee at closing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the fund manager in your region to apply. Regional fund managers include FSC First, Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Meridian Management Group, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Baltimore County Economic Development, City of Baltimore Development Corp., Howard County Economic Development Authority, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Summit Financing Solutions), and Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation. Western Maryland businesses (Allegany, Garrett, Washington counties) may submit an inquiry form through Summit Financing Solutions at tccwmd.org; a business plan is required and standard underwriting practices apply. Cecil County businesses near Hollywood Casino in Perryville may contact the Cecil County Office of Economic Development at 410-996-8465. For program overview, visit the Maryland Department of Commerce VLT page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Soft Landing Exchange for Maryland Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland companies test expansion into new international markets affordably. It provides access to facilities, resources, and networking through a global network of partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible companies can receive a grant of up to $10,000. This money helps pay for program costs and travel expenses like flights, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies that want to expand into new international markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can cover participation costs charged by the partner program, as well as travel, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to companies located anywhere in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, click the 'Apply Now' button on the program webpage to access the online grant application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable Maryland state income tax credit equal to 25% of qualified production costs incurred in Maryland by eligible theatrical production companies. The production must be a for-profit National Touring Production or Pre-Broadway Production live stage theatrical production. Minimum qualifying production costs must exceed $100,000, and the maximum credit per production is $2 million. The credit is refundable, meaning the company can receive a payment even if it owes no state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refundable credit of 25% against Maryland state income tax on qualified direct production costs (e.g., set design, special effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, lodging, vehicle leasing) incurred in Maryland. Minimum qualifying spend is $100,000 in estimated direct costs. Maximum credit is $2 million per production. Credit is claimed via Form 500CR on an electronically filed Maryland income tax return. No compensation costs are eligible for individuals earning more than $100,000 per week in personal services. All costs must be pro-rated to time/use in Maryland. For items over $1,000, the net cost (purchase price minus resale value) applies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY2023 tax credits were accepted through June 1, 2023. Applications must also be submitted before beginning any work on the theatrical production in the State.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit theatrical production companies operating National Touring Productions or Pre-Broadway Productions that incur qualifying costs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset Maryland state income tax liability based on qualified direct production costs incurred in Maryland, including set construction and operation, special effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, facility rental, vehicle leasing, food and lodging, travel expenses, salaries for work performed in Maryland, and advertising costs within Maryland. Qualified vendors must maintain a physical location in Maryland from which goods and services are provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Production costs must be incurred within the State of Maryland. Qualified vendors must maintain a physical location in Maryland from which employees are based and goods/services are generated, unless via online order. All costs must be pro-rated based upon the time personnel or materials are in Maryland. Travel, shipping, and lodging must be into or within Maryland only. Legal, CPA, and independent auditor fees require Maryland licensure. No county, municipality, or regional sub-limitations apply.
requirements_list: Production must be a for-profit National Touring Production or Pre-Broadway Production performed live in a qualified theatrical production facility in Maryland.
Estimated total direct production costs incurred in Maryland must exceed $100,000.
National Touring Productions must have at least two public performances and afterward be performed for a total of four weeks or more in at least four cities outside Maryland.

Pre-Broadway Productions must have at least eight public performances, must be in original or adaptive form not widely performed in the past five years, and must be prepared exclusively at a qualified facility for Broadway presentation within 12 months of the final performance in Maryland.
Application for Qualification must be submitted and approved BEFORE beginning any production work in Maryland.
Application Addendum must be submitted BEFORE the first rehearsal.
Non-resident companies must register to do business in Maryland and obtain a Certificate of Status.
Production company must hold insurance: General Liability, Excess Liability/Umbrella, All Risk/Property, and Worker's Compensation.
Must provide Unemployment Insurance Account Number.
Theatrical Production entity must demonstrate financing.
Productions with total authorized direct costs greater than $250,000 must include an independent third-party auditor's report (Agreed Upon Procedures) prepared by a Maryland-licensed CPA.
Applicant must certify no outstanding amounts owed to Maryland vendors before a Tax Credit Certificate is issued.
No compensation costs are eligible for individuals earning more than $100,000 per week in personal services.
Writers, theater/stage directors, and producers cannot have salaries/wages counted (except for strictly technical roles such as Lighting Director, Casting Director, or Art Director).
Productions must contact at least three qualified vendors before using a non-qualified vendor, and submit a Due Diligence Form with closing documentation.
All costs must be pro-rated to time/use in Maryland; for items over $1,000, net cost equals purchase price minus resale value upon completion.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Before starting any production work in Maryland, submit a complete Application for Qualification (with all required attachments, proof of financing, script, and production budget) to the Department via email. 2. The Department reviews complete applications in order received and issues a Letter of Qualification within 30 days confirming eligibility and maximum credit amount. 3. Before the first rehearsal, submit the Application Addendum (including insurance documentation, unemployment insurance account number, and accountant/payroll contacts). 4. Within 180 days after the production completion date, submit the Application for Tax Credit Certificate along with all required final documentation, receipts, expenditure report, and (if applicable) an independent Maryland-licensed auditor's Agreed Upon Procedures report. 5. The Department reviews the final application and issues a Tax Credit Certificate. 6. Claim the credit on the Maryland state income tax return using Form 500CR, attaching the Tax Credit Certificate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program provides financial assistance to individuals and corporations to establish a new winery or vineyard in Maryland, or to complete capital improvements at an existing winery or vineyard. The program provides a grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses, which include equipment and agricultural materials used in wine production (such as barrels, tanks, tractors, irrigation equipment, and fruit plants), but do not include construction costs or labor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses incurred for establishing or improving a winery or vineyard in Maryland. Qualified expenses include equipment and agricultural materials (e.g., barrels, tanks, tractors, irrigation equipment, fruit plants) but exclude construction, labor, utilities, repairs, office supplies, marketing, and maintenance costs. Leasing costs are only eligible for leases of 3 or more years. If total applications exceed the annual appropriation, grants are approved on a pro-rata basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and corporations operating or establishing a licensed winery (Class 3 or Class 4) or vineyard (at least 1 contiguous acre growing grapes for wine production) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of equipment or agricultural materials used in wine production or vineyard operations. Eligible items include barrels, bins, bottling equipment, tanks, tractors, irrigation equipment, fruit plants, fermentation devices, pruning equipment, refrigeration equipment, and similar items. Leasing costs are eligible only for leases of 3 or more years. Construction costs, labor, utilities, repairs, office supplies, and marketing costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Maryland. Vineyard must consist of at least one contiguous acre of agricultural land in Maryland used to grow grapes for wine production.
requirements_list: Winery must be licensed by the Maryland Comptroller as a Class 3 or Class 4 winery
Vineyard must consist of at least 1 contiguous acre in Maryland growing grapes for wine production
Qualified capital expenses must relate to establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one
Applicant must submit a detailed Report of Expenses with supporting documentation (receipts and invoices)
Business must be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce as a qualified business entity
Application must be submitted to Commerce by January 16, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the WVEDG Online Application portal at https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/winecreditwelcome on the Maryland Department of Commerce website. Include a completed Report of Expenses with supporting documentation (receipts and invoices). Commerce will review the application and certify the grant amount. If total approved grants exceed the annual appropriation, awards are made on a pro-rata basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable income tax credit for film production entities that incur qualifying direct costs in Maryland to carry out a film production activity in the state. Eligible entities can receive a credit of up to 28% (or 30% for a series) of total authorized direct costs, with a maximum of $10,000,000 per project. A separate Maryland Small Film track is available for smaller, independently owned and operated film production entities, offering up to 28% of authorized direct costs with a maximum of $125,000 per project.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Maryland Film Office
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refundable income tax credit of up to 28% of total authorized direct costs of a film production activity (or 30% for a series), with a maximum credit of $10,000,000 per project. Maryland Small Films may receive up to 28% of authorized direct costs with a maximum of $125,000 per project. The Department is limited to certifying $12 million in total tax credits for FY 2026 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026). Credits are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. If the credit exceeds the film production entity's total tax owed, the excess is refundable.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 2026 (July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026), first come first serve basis until $12 million cap is reached
structured_extraction.program_audience: Film production entities (including Maryland Small Films) incurring qualifying direct costs in Maryland for film production activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refundable tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax for authorized direct costs incurred in Maryland in connection with a qualified film production activity, including salaries (up to $500,000 per individual), equipment rentals, labor, materials, travel into Maryland, location fees, post-production costs, and other qualifying expenditures. Individuals earning over $500,000 in total compensation are excluded. Materials/goods with initial cost over $1,000 must be depreciated (initial cost minus resale value). All costs must be pro-rated for time/use in Maryland only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 50% of principal photography must occur in Maryland. Direct costs must be incurred in Maryland only. Filming in Washington DC does not qualify.
requirements_list: All statutory requirements must be met
Application for Qualification must be complete and signed
Film production entity must demonstrate financing
Film production entity must provide acceptable evidence of national distribution
50% of principal photography must occur in Maryland
Principal photography must be scheduled to begin within 120 days of receiving the Letter of Qualification
Total authorized direct costs projected to be incurred in Maryland must exceed $250,000 (or $25,000 for Maryland Small Films)
Application for Qualification must be submitted before beginning any work on the film production activity in Maryland
Application for Final Tax Credit Certification must be submitted no later than 180 days after the completion date

For Maryland Small Films: entity must have been organized in Maryland for at least 3 months prior to application, be independently owned and operated, not be a subsidiary of another entity, not be dominant in its field, and not employ more than 25 full-time employees

All goods and services must be provided by a qualified vendor (registered in MD, with physical location in state, historic ordinary course of business); exceptions available for specialized/technical goods via Non-Qualified Vendor Due Diligence Form requiring contact with at least 3 qualified vendors
Film production entity must certify no outstanding amounts owed to Maryland vendors at time of final certification
If organized outside Maryland: must register to do business in Maryland before production begins
All taxes and fees must be current; no State/local contract defaults

Before principal photography begins, submit Form for Additional Documentation and Information including Good Standing Certificate, insurance certificates (General Liability, Excess/Umbrella, All Risk/Property, Worker's Compensation), Unemployment Insurance Account Number, and key accountant/payroll/CPA contacts

Independent CPA (Maryland-licensed) auditor's Agreed Upon Procedures report required for productions with costs over $250,000; draft engagement letter must be approved by Department before principal photography completion

Final certification submission must include complete payroll/earnings report, general ledger, vendor/accounts payable list, list of Maryland residents employed, list of Maryland businesses providing goods/services, list of all Loan Out Companies/Personal Service Corps, completed Production Expenditure Form, final production schedule, final crew list, call sheets, and SAG Minority Breakdown
Either relocation fee OR housing may be claimed, not both
No entertainment or gift costs qualify
Travel costs to Maryland must end-point in Maryland; round-trip travel divided in half
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before beginning any work in Maryland, submit an Application for Qualification (or Maryland Small Film – Application for Qualification) along with all required attachments to the Maryland Film Office by email to Josh.Slates@maryland.gov or by mail/in person to Josh Slates, Maryland Film Office, 401 East Pratt Street, 14th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202. Applications are reviewed in order received on a first-come, first-served basis; incomplete applications will not be considered. The Department will issue a Letter of Qualification or denial within 30 days of receiving a complete application. Before principal photography begins, submit the Form for Additional Documentation and Information (including Good Standing Certificate, insurance certificates, unemployment insurance account number, and key contacts). After completing production, submit an Application for Final Tax Credit Certification (along with required documentation including complete payroll/earnings report, general ledger, vendor lists, receipts, and for productions with costs over $250,000, an independent Maryland-licensed CPA's Agreed Upon Procedures report) no later than 180 days after the completion date. The Department will then issue a Final Tax Credit Certificate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland provides enhanced versions of several state economic development tax credit programs for businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. Eligible businesses can apply for Level 1 or Level 2 enhancements to the following credits: Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, More Jobs for Marylanders Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Focus Area Income Tax Credit, and Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit (BIITC). The enhanced credit amounts replace — not supplement — the standard credit amounts under each program. To receive these benefits, a business must first qualify for one of the underlying state economic development tax credit programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses in Maryland Opportunity Zones can receive enhanced tax credits under six programs. Level 1 and Level 2 enhancements provide higher credit amounts than the standard programs. Examples: Job Creation Tax Credit — Level 1: $3,075/qualified position ($5,125 in revitalization area); Level 2: $3,300 ($5,500 in revitalization area). One Maryland Tax Credit — Level 1: up to $5,125,000; Level 2: up to $5,500,000. More Jobs for Marylanders — Level 1: 6% of wages; Level 2: 6.25%. Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit — Level 1: $1,025/new job standard; Level 2: $1,200/new job standard. Enterprise Zone Focus Area — Level 1: $1,540/new job standard; Level 2: $1,750/new job standard. BIITC — Level 1: 65% of investment up to $575,000; Level 2: 75% up to $750,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and investors located in Maryland Opportunity Zones that are Qualified Opportunity Zone Businesses (as defined in IRC § 1400Z-2) and have received investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund, or Qualified Opportunity Funds investing in qualifying Maryland biotechnology or technology companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced tax credits to reduce state tax liability for businesses operating in Opportunity Zones. Credits are tied to job creation, wages paid, or investment amounts depending on the underlying credit program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in a Maryland Opportunity Zone (as designated under federal IRC § 1400Z-2).
requirements_list: Must first meet all eligibility requirements of the underlying tax credit program being enhanced

Must be a Qualified Opportunity Zone Business (IRC § 1400Z-2) and have received investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund (for Job Creation, One Maryland, More Jobs for Marylanders, Enterprise Zone, and Enterprise Zone Focus Area credits)
For BIITC: the investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund and the company receiving investment must be in an Opportunity Zone

Level 1: Submit Opportunity Zone Enhancement application (Addendum A) with date and amount of Qualified Opportunity Fund investment, total project/business investment including leverage, address and census tract, NAICS code, an impact report with qualitative and quantitative data, and other information required by Commerce

Level 2 (in addition to Level 1): Provide community representation evidence (board members who are community residents OR a community benefits agreement); Provide a resolution or letter from the municipality or county approving the enhanced credits; and other information required by Commerce
For investment-based credits like the BIITC or IITC, the investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attach the Opportunity Zone Enhancement Tax Credit Application (Addendum A) to the application for the specific underlying tax credit program. Submit all required documentation for the desired enhancement level (Level 1 or Level 2). To submit an application, email taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Access Maryland provides capital budget funds to bring state-owned facilities into compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, ADA Accessible Design Standards of 2010, and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. The program covers state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks. State agencies submit requests for accessibility modification projects, which are reviewed and prioritized by the Maryland Commission on Disabilities. The Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) then recommends approved projects to the Department of Budget and Management for inclusion in the Capital Budget, after which the Department of General Services provides technical assistance for design and procurement. MDOD also provides oversight through design and construction phases. MDOD notifies agencies to submit requests in January/February each year, with a standard deadline of March 1st. Approved projects receive funds beginning July 1 of the applicable fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital budget funding for physical accessibility modifications and barrier removal at state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks. Projects must be valued at $1,000 or more, cannot be part of a larger renovation or the agency's five-year capital improvement plan, and cannot be located in auxiliary facilities or relate solely to a reasonable accommodation for an employee. USM and higher education campuses must expend 30% of institutional funds on each project. Approved projects are eligible for funding for two years; if design is not completed and approved within two years, the project becomes permanently ineligible unless an extension is granted. The Department of General Services provides technical assistance for design and procurement. Funds are available beginning July 1 of the approved fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st annually (agencies submit completed applications; funds available July 1 of the approved fiscal year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state agencies, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks seeking to make facilities accessible to persons with disabilities through ADA-compliant modifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical barrier removal and accessibility upgrades at state-owned facilities, parks, and University System of Maryland campuses to comply with ADA and Section 504 requirements, including ramps, accessible paths, and other accessibility modifications. Covers both design and construction phases for ADA accessibility modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for state-owned facilities, state-owned parks, and University System of Maryland campuses.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland state agency, University System of Maryland campus, or state-owned park
Project must be located in a state-owned facility
Project must address physical accessibility barriers consistent with ADA Accessible Design Standards of 2010
Project value must be at least $1,000
Project cannot be part of a larger renovation
Project cannot be part of the agency's five-year capital improvement plan
Project cannot be located within auxiliary facilities
Project cannot relate solely to a reasonable accommodation for an employee
Request forms must be signed by the ADA coordinator designated by the agency or campus head
Agencies should have an ADA Transition Plan in place
Frequent public use of the facility enhances probability of approval
USM and higher education campuses must expend 30% of institutional funds on each project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MDOD notifies agencies to submit requests in January/February each year. Agencies have 4–6 weeks to submit applications following the January solicitation, with a standard deadline of March 1st. State agencies submit project requests signed by their designated ADA coordinator to MDOD. MDOD forwards requests to the Maryland Commission on Disabilities for review and prioritization. MDOD then recommends prioritized projects to the Department of Budget and Management for inclusion in the Capital Budget during the legislative session (January–April). After legislative approval, approved projects receive funds beginning July 1 of the applicable fiscal year. The Department of General Services provides technical assistance for design and procurement. MDOD provides oversight through design and construction phases. A Policies and Procedures document outlines the full application process, review process, and project and funding timeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Attendant Care Program provides financial reimbursement to help adults with severe chronic or permanent physical disabilities pay for attendant care services. Participants direct their own care and select their own service providers. Reimbursement may cover attendant care services provided at home, school, the workplace, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for attendant care services used in the home, school, workplace, or other community settings. Applicants are placed on a waiting list and contacted as space becomes available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 to 64 with severe chronic or permanent physical disabilities who need attendant care services to live, work, or study in the community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attendant care services provided at home, school, workplace, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 to 64
Must have a severe chronic or permanent physical disability

Must meet at least one of the following: (1) be self-employed or competitively employed with compensation; (2) be actively seeking employment; (3) be attending a post-secondary, higher education, or apprenticeship training program; (4) be a resident of a nursing facility seeking to transition into the community; or (5) be at risk of placement in a nursing home as certified by the attending physician if attendant care services are not received in the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a OneStop account at onestop.md.gov by providing your name and a verifiable email address. After creating an account, select 'Maryland Department of Disabilities' from the home screen and complete the short application to be placed on the registry. When space becomes available on the waiting list, you will receive an email link to complete the full application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Centers for Independent Living Technical Assistance (CIL-TA) Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance project coordinated by the Maryland Department of Disabilities in partnership with the MD Department of Aging to benefit Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living (CILs). The project, funded by a grant from the Administration for Community Living, aims to enhance the state's Aging and Disability Resource Centers (ADRCs) — one-stop shops where older adults and people with disabilities can find long-term services and supports. A consultant from the Maryland Center for Developmental Disabilities at Kennedy Krieger Institute provides technical assistance and training to CILs on improving operational infrastructure and program sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and training provided to Maryland's Centers for Independent Living on enhancing operational infrastructure and program sustainability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living (CILs) that serve as designated disability partners within the state's Aging and Disability Resource Center network.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing operational infrastructure and program sustainability of Centers for Independent Living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be one of Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living

structured_extraction.program_name: Community First Choice Self-Direction (CFC SD) Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A training program for Community First Choice (CFC) participants who are interested in self-directing their personal assistance services. Offers individual and small group training in the participant's home or at an accessible community location. Topics include how to recruit, interview, hire, supervise, and dismiss personal assistance providers, being an effective employer, emergency preparedness, and creating a back-up plan. Participants are referred through their Supports Planner.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual and small group training sessions held in the participant's home or at an accessible community location covering self-direction of personal assistance services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities participating in Community First Choice (CFC) who want to self-direct their personal assistance services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on self-directing personal assistance services, including recruiting, hiring, supervising, and dismissing providers, emergency preparedness, and back-up planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Community First Choice (CFC) participant
Must be interested in self-directing personal assistance services
Referral through a Supports Planner required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred to the program through their Supports Planner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ethan Saylor Alliance for Self-Advocates as Educators Community Impact Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for Maryland nonprofit organizations that propose creative and innovative ways to improve relationships between people with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities (I/DD) and law enforcement and/or other first responders. The program was created in honor of Ethan Saylor, a young man with Down Syndrome who died during a law enforcement encounter in 2013.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $1,000 to $5,000 awarded to eligible nonprofits. Funds must be used for programming, community events, and activities that build connections between people with I/DD and law enforcement or other first responders. Activities must be completed by December 31, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland 501(c)(3) nonprofits that support people with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Joint trainings, inclusive community events (e.g. Be Safe events, ride-alongs, bowling, pool parties, fitness events), disability awareness kits for officers, role-playing exercises, or compensating self-advocates/individuals with I/DD for training roles. Preference given to direct programming over administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland eligibility; no county or municipality restrictions mentioned. Must be a nonprofit supporting people with I/DD in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization supporting people with I/DD in Maryland
Must be in good standing with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must submit a budget and narrative explaining how funds will be spent
Activities must be completed by December 31, 2023
Must credit The Ethan Saylor Alliance for Self-Advocates as Educators within the MD Department of Disabilities in all project communications
Must submit a brief programmatic and financial report within 30 calendar days of the event/activity/program and no later than January 31, 2024
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically by 5pm on March 6, 2023. Applications are reviewed first by MDOD staff for eligibility and then by the Alliance's Steering Committee for final approval. Awards announced via email no later than March 31, 2023. Checks mailed the week of April 3, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Partnership for Affordable Housing (MPAH) — The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation's Affordable Rental Housing Opportunities Initiative for Persons with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and the State of Maryland that provides affordable rental housing for non-elderly, very low-income persons with disabilities. The initiative uses $7 million in capital grants from the Weinberg Foundation combined with Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Multifamily Rental Housing Program and Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) financing to create 'Weinberg Apartments' — units designated by owners of eligible rental housing developments (with non-profit involvement) for non-elderly, disabled persons earning 10–30% of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI). The Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) qualifies eligible households and refers potential tenants to property managers. Eligible tenants pay 30% of their income toward rent and utilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants totaling $7 million from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation are awarded to owners of eligible rental housing developments (with non-profit involvement) to designate affordable 'Weinberg Apartment' units for very low-income persons with disabilities. Financing is also provided through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Multifamily Rental Housing Program and the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program. Eligible tenants pay 30% of their income toward rent and utilities, with units reserved for households earning 10–30% of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-elderly persons with disabilities (ages 18–62) who receive SSI or SSDI and have a gross household income at 10–30% of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI) in the Maryland county where they wish to reside.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing — subsidized rental units for very low-income non-elderly persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Units are located in multiple Maryland counties. As of February 2020, Weinberg Apartments exist in Dorchester, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, and Wicomico counties, with additional units under development or in the pipeline in Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Howard County, and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be between the ages of 18 and 62
Must be disabled and receiving SSI or SSDI income
Must have a gross household income at 10–30% of AGMI in the Maryland county of desired residence
Must not have a criminal background that includes a lifetime sex offender registry requirement
Must not have a criminal background that includes a conviction for production of methamphetamines in federally assisted property
Must be referred by a case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community services, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must be referred by their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community services, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application. MDOD qualifies eligible households and refers potential tenants to property managers. Applicants are drawn from a waiting list as suitable units that meet their needs become available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Choice Homes (CCH) provides affordable rental housing in Montgomery County for adults with disabilities who have extremely low income. Participants pay 30% of their monthly household adjusted income for rent and utilities while living in one of 30 Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC)-owned rental units. The program is a partnership between HOC and the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and runs for a 15-year period.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) / Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County (HOC)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 30% of their monthly household adjusted income for rent and utilities in one of 30 HOC-owned affordable rental units. The subsidy is project-based and tied to the specific unit — it does not move with the participant if they leave.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with disabilities aged 18–62 at time of leasing who have extremely low income (at or below 30% of area median income), receive SSI or SSDI, and live or work in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing — participants pay reduced rent (30% of adjusted household income) for an HOC-owned unit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must live or work in Montgomery County at time of referral, or have lived/worked there within the past 5 years and currently reside in an institution or group living setting.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 30% of area median income (AMI); priority given to incomes between 10–30% AMI
Income must include cash payment from SSI or SSDI at time of initial eligibility determination (applicants with suspended SSI eligibility also eligible)
Adults aged 18–62 at time of leasing (may continue in program after age 62)
Must be registered on the HOC Housing Path Waitlist
Must live or work in Montgomery County at time of referral, or have done so within 5 years and currently live in an institution or group living setting

Criminal background must not include a lifetime sex offender registry requirement or conviction for production of methamphetamine in federally assisted housing, and must meet other HOC eligibility requirements

Must comply with program requirements: maintaining eligibility for permanent housing assistance, applying for rent subsidies as offered by HOC, completing tenant training, making timely rent and utility payments, and adhering to all lease requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Persons with a disability seeking assistance should contact their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application. Interested persons must be added to the Weinberg Apartment waitlist by their case manager via www.Socialserve.com, and must also enroll on the HOC Housing Path waitlist.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Loan Program (ATLP) helps Maryland residents with disabilities and their families qualify for low-interest loans to purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles, and home and vehicle accessibility modifications to support independent living, working, and learning. Loans range from $500 to $70,000 depending on loan type: unsecured AT loans up to $10,000; unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000; non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000; and adapted vehicles up to $70,000. All loans carry below-market, fixed interest rates that vary based on creditworthiness and are disclosed at the time of application processing. Approval criteria are less stringent than traditional banks, considering income-to-debt ratio, residential and employment stability, payment history, and ability to repay. A 90-day default clause and 17% collection fee apply; a loan guarantee may be required for some applicants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Disabilities Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $500 to $70,000. Unsecured AT loans up to $10,000; unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000; non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000; adapted vehicles up to $70,000. All loans carry below-market, fixed interest rates with extended repayment terms. Rates vary based on creditworthiness and are disclosed at the time of application processing. Approval criteria are less stringent than traditional banks — the program considers income-to-debt ratio, residential and employment stability, payment history, and ability to repay. A 90-day default clause and 17% collection fee apply; a loan guarantee may be required for some applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities, as well as family members, friends, or anyone purchasing assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability who needs financing for assistive technology equipment, home/vehicle accessibility modifications, or vehicle purchases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology devices and equipment that help a person with a disability live more independently, including home modifications, adapted and non-adapted vehicles, scooters, wheelchairs, hearing aids, computers and iDevices, smart home technology, Braille equipment, vision aids, augmentative communication devices, environmental control units, adaptive peripherals, and other eligible assistive technology devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents with disabilities. Applicants must provide a Maryland state-issued ID and Maryland address. No county-specific or regional restrictions apply.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident with a disability, or a family member/friend purchasing assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability.
Must provide a Maryland state-issued ID and Maryland address.
Must need financing for assistive technology equipment, home/vehicle accessibility modifications, or vehicle purchase.
Program evaluates income compared to debt, stability in residence and employment, payment history with existing creditors, and financial ability to repay the loan.
Income documentation required: pay stubs within last 30 days, SSI/SSDI award letters, pension statements, or tax forms as applicable.
Not all applicants will be approved; some may be declined based on financial review.
A credit check will be conducted; a loan guarantee may be required for some applicants.
Co-applicant option available; co-applicant may be required by the Board.
Automatic debit payments may be mandated.
Decision promised within 30 days of application; appeal process available with a 7-day decision window.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online via the Maryland OneStop portal, or download the fillable ATLP application form (updated February 2025) and email the completed application with supporting documents to mdtap.atlp@maryland.gov. Call 1-800-832-4827 (toll-free), 410-554-9230 (local/711 Relay), or fax 410-554-9237 for more information. Financial counseling and coaching is available through a partnership with the CASH Campaign of Maryland. Mailing address: 2301 Argonne Drive, Rm T-42, Baltimore, MD 21218.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center accepts donations of assistive technology (AT) devices, cleans, refurbishes, and repairs them, then donates them free of charge to Marylanders with disabilities who are in need. Available devices include CCTVs, video magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer keyboards and mice, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, eye-gaze systems, and amplified telephones. Training and support are also provided to help users integrate the technology into daily life. Availability of specific devices depends on what has been donated and refurbished.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Disabilities Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free donation of refurbished high-tech assistive technology devices to Marylanders with disabilities, along with training and support to help integrate them into daily life. Devices are not sold; they are given at no cost. Availability depends on what has been donated and refurbished. Devices include CCTVs, video magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer keyboards and mice, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, eye-gaze systems, and amplified telephones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities who need high-tech assistive technology devices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recipients receive refurbished assistive technology devices such as CCTVs, video magnifiers, speech communication devices, adapted input devices, eye-gaze systems, amplified telephones, and more, along with training and support to integrate the technology into daily life.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to residents of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a disability
Must complete the MATR Application online
Consultation and/or device pickup may be coordinated after application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MATR Application online at https://forms.gle/KzaXyWM3yVMaCbrk9. Staff will follow up to coordinate a consultation and/or device pickup. You can also schedule a consultation or pickup by contacting Shawn Bateman at 410-554-9232 or MDTAP.AT-Reuse@maryland.gov. For more information about available products and pickup location, visit the MATR Center page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term loans of portable ramps to Maryland residents who need temporary solutions for getting in and out of their homes. Ramps are loaned for up to 120 days (4 months) and are fully ADA-compliant. The program is a partnership between the Maryland Department of Disabilities' Assistive Technology Program and centers for independent living across the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Disabilities Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Portable ADA-compliant ramps loaned for up to 120 days at no cost through local Centers for Independent Living. Borrowers must arrange pickup and return of the ramp.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland consumers who need a short-term portable ramp solution for home access.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing a portable ramp for temporary home accessibility needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Centers for Independent Living.
requirements_list: Must need a short-term portable ramp solution
Must arrange pickup and return of ramp from local Center for Independent Living
Loan period is up to 120 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find your local Center for Independent Living using the ILRU directory and contact them to inquire about borrowing a portable ramp. Visit the Statewide Portable Ramp Loan Program page for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDTAP 3D Printed Assistive Technology / AT Fabrication Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP), operated under the Maryland Department of Disabilities, runs a small 3D printing lab that fabricates low-tech assistive devices for Marylanders with disabilities at no cost. Devices can be selected from a 3D AT Catalogue of standard items, custom-printed to meet individual needs, or modified to better fit a particular person. MDTAP also partners with the UMBC 3D Printing lab on device fabrication and training, and works closely with recipients to customize devices to best suit their needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Disabilities – Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free fabrication and delivery of low-tech assistive devices using 3D printing technology.
