Recipients can browse a 3D AT Catalogue and submit a request form online (available via Google Forms) for standard catalog items, or contact MDTAP directly for custom-printed devices not in the catalogue or modifications to existing devices tailored to individual needs. MDTAP partners with the UMBC 3D Printing lab on fabrication and training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who need low-tech assistive devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fabrication and delivery of free 3D-printed low-tech assistive devices for daily living, including standard catalog items, custom-printed devices, and modifications to existing devices tailored to the individual needs of people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a disability
Must need a low-tech assistive device
Must submit a request via the 3D AT Catalogue and Request Form or contact MDTAP directly
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Browse the 3D AT Catalogue and submit a request form online (available via Google Forms), or contact MDTAP directly by phone at 1-800-832-4827 or by email at mdtap@maryland.gov with questions, customization requests, or to inquire about the most recent catalog.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide partnership program that helps Maryland K-12 school systems improve their cybersecurity resilience. The program provides planning support (cybersecurity maturity assessments, emergency operations plan reviews, resource allocation analysis, training program setup), implementation assistance (remediation recommendations, cyber incident response plan development, disaster recovery and continuity of operations planning, training and exercises), and ongoing support (funding notifications, network access for continuous help and resources).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance and training delivered through a partnership of state agencies (MDEM, DoIT, MCSS) and MABE. Services include cybersecurity assessments, emergency and cyber response plan reviews, remediation recommendations, incident response plan development, disaster recovery and COOP planning, cybersecurity training sessions and exercises, and ongoing support and funding notifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland K-12 school systems (Local Education Agencies)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity assessments, response plan development, disaster recovery and continuity of operations planning, staff training and exercises, and access to ongoing cybersecurity support resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to K-12 school systems throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland K-12 Local Education Agency (LEA) or school system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online request form linked on the program page to request support in one or more of the listed assistance areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program run by FEMA and administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). It provides funding to nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist or extremist attacks to improve physical security and integrate their preparedness activities with state and local efforts. Funds support facility hardening, security system installation, and other physical security enhancements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive annual grants for physical security enhancements. Applicants may apply for up to $200,000 per location, with a maximum of six locations per organization and no more than $600,000 total per state. No cost-share requirement. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis. For FY2025, FEMA allocated $274,500,000 nationally toward the program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Currently closed; check back later for updates
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3)) in Maryland at high risk of terrorist or extremist attacks, including private institutions of higher learning. Organizations in Montgomery or Prince George's County must apply through the National Capital Region via the District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical security enhancements and other security-related activities at nonprofit facilities, such as facility hardening and security system installation. Funds may also cover management and administration costs if approved. Grant operates on a reimbursement basis only — no advance funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland except Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, which must apply through the National Capital Region via the District of Columbia. Maryland jurisdictions are divided into State Area, Baltimore Urban Area, and National Capital Region Urban Area funding tracks.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be at high risk of a terrorist or other extremist attack
Must submit an Investment Justification (IJ) form
Must submit a vulnerability assessment conducted at the facility within the last two years (self-assessment allowed for houses of worship only)
Must submit organization's mission statement on letterhead
Must submit short bios and resumes of organizational leadership and board members including names and addresses
Must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) through SAM.gov prior to receiving an award
Must declare whether work or mission involves supporting aliens and whether the organization has DEI practices
Must not include foreign nationals unless properly vetted and compliant with all government statutes
Must attend mandatory Subrecipient Grant Award Briefing if awarded
Must submit quarterly status reports throughout the period of performance
Must complete Environmental and Historic Preservation (EHP) screening before starting any work (with limited exceptions)
Must comply with federal procurement requirements including Build America, Buy America Act
Purchasing prohibited from Hytera Communications, Hangzhou Hikvision, Dahua Technology, and their subsidiaries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application packet as a single email to nsgp.mdem@maryland.gov. The packet must include: (1) a completed Investment Justification form (downloaded and opened from your computer, not a browser), (2) a vulnerability assessment from the past two years, (3) your organization's mission statement on letterhead, and (4) short bios and resumes of leadership and board members. All documents must be submitted as PDFs. Do not submit applications directly to FEMA or grants.gov — MDEM is the State Administrative Agency responsible for all submissions to FEMA.

structured_extraction.program_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP) provides federal funding to help states, local governments, rural areas, and territories address cybersecurity risks and threats to information systems. In Maryland, the program is administered by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) as the state's lead agency, with the Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT) providing technical guidance. Funding supports strategic investments to enhance the cybersecurity posture of government agencies, protect critical infrastructure, and build long-term cybersecurity capacity. The FFY2023 cycle has a 48-month period of performance (December 1, 2023 – November 30, 2027). Funding is also available in FFY2024 and FFY2025, each with its own funding notice and application period. Maryland ensures that 80% of SLCGP funds are passed down to local jurisdictions, and rural applications receive score multipliers (FEMA Rural x1.5, Maryland Rural x1.0).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based federal subgrant program. Subrecipients must submit reimbursement requests for approved project-related expenses within 90 days of expenditure. FY22 and FY23 funding cycles are currently active. FY23 second-round applications are being accepted on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. FY24 and FY25 each have their own funding notice and application period. All FY2023 projects must be completed by September 30, 2027, with a full period of performance running December 1, 2023 through November 30, 2027. Maryland will ensure that 80% of SLCGP funds are passed down to local jurisdictions. Rural applications receive score multipliers (FEMA Rural x1.5, Maryland Rural x1.0). Total FFY2023 allocation for Maryland: $6,514,533.00.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling (first-come, first-served); projects must be completed by 30 September 2027; FY2024 and FY2025 each have their own funding notice and application period
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, school boards/systems, special districts, councils of governments, regional/interstate government entities, and rural communities in Maryland seeking to improve cybersecurity posture and resilience
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity projects that address cybersecurity risks and threats to information systems, strengthen protection of critical infrastructure, and build long-term cybersecurity capacity. Eligible uses include adoption and enhancement of priority cybersecurity best practices. All projects must align with Maryland's Cybersecurity Plan and the state's cybersecurity priorities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (counties, cities, towns). Eligible entities include counties, municipalities, cities, towns, townships, local public authorities, school districts, special districts, intrastate districts, councils of governments, regional/interstate government entities, and agencies or instrumentalities of local government. FEMA-designated rural counties (population <50,000, not designated urbanized area): Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, and Worcester. Additional Maryland-defined rural communities may qualify by providing evidence of rural status such as planning and zoning designation or mapping.
requirements_list: Must be a state agency or local government (county, municipality, city, town, township, local public authority, school district, special district, intrastate district, council of governments, regional/interstate government entity, or agency/instrumentality of local government)
Must register in SAM.gov (System for Award Management) with a current Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Municipalities and local health departments must submit a completed W-9 form
Must register for CISA Cyber Hygiene (CyHy) service and send acceptance email to MDEM
Must complete the Nationwide Cybersecurity Review (NCSR) annually (first year and each subsequent year)
Must complete Cybersecurity Capabilities Assessment (Appendix A)
Must establish Measurable Milestones (Appendix E)
Must submit Quarterly Status Reports (QSRs) until project is complete
Must retain records for 3 years after end of project period
Must have a signed Subrecipient Agreement (SRA) in place before starting any project
Must submit reimbursement requests within 90 days of expenditure
Must provide itemized vendor quotes if using contractors
Must certify no suspension/exclusion from federal programs
Must affirm fiscal responsibility and proper accounting for federal awards
FY2022 projects must be completed by September 30, 2026
FY2023 projects must be completed by September 30, 2027; full period of performance is December 1, 2023 – November 30, 2027
Do not submit applications to FEMA or grants.gov — MDEM submits on behalf of the State
Letters of Intent to Accept or Reject Funding must be submitted within 30 days of award notification
Subject to monitoring and site visits by FEMA and MDEM
Noncompliance may result in termination of award
Must comply with Section 504 (Rehabilitation Act) accessibility requirements
Must participate in CISA Web Application Scanning and Vulnerability Scanning services
Must submit final closeout Quarterly Status Report upon project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the FFY2023 application documents (Project Proposal Application, Additional Application Documents Packet including Budget Narrative and Budget Justification, Cybersecurity Capabilities Assessment, and Measurable Milestones, and Form W-9 if applicable). Email completed forms to slcgp.grant@maryland.gov with the required subject line format. Applications are accepted on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. The Planning Committee submits proposals to FEMA, which approves or rejects projects. If approved, MDEM issues the subaward agreement and applicants must submit a Letter of Intent within 30 days. Each subsequent FFY cycle (FFY2024, FFY2025) will have its own funding notice and application period.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Disaster Recovery Fund (SDRF) provides disaster-related financial assistance to communities affected by disasters. It has three main objectives: (1) Assistance to Individuals and Households — financial support to local jurisdictions for immediate needs and short-term recovery of affected residents; (2) Small Business Loans — financial assistance to small businesses for economic recovery; and (3) Assistance to Local Governments — financial assistance to local governments for eligible disaster response and recovery costs, with priority given to debris cleanup. SDRF is a last-resort fund and may not supplant other funding sources, though it may be used as matching funds after a federal disaster declaration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided through three tracks: (1) grants to local jurisdictions for individual/household assistance covering immediate needs, clean-up, health/medical, utilities, personal items, transportation, temporary storage, and legal fees; (2) loans to small businesses for economic recovery; and (3) grants to local governments for disaster response and recovery costs, including infrastructure repair. Administrative costs are capped at 5% of the total award. Unused funds must be returned. Award period of performance is 365 days post-approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: SDRF activation request must be submitted within 14 days of the end of the incident period response
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county and municipal jurisdictions), small businesses, and individuals/households in Maryland affected by disasters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Immediate and critical needs, clean-up, health and medical expenses, utility assistance, personal items, dependent care, transportation, temporary storage, legal assistance, debris cleanup, infrastructure repair, small business recovery, and other disaster-related costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland jurisdictions affected by a declared State of Emergency
requirements_list: A local or state State of Emergency must be declared by the highest elected official in the applying jurisdiction
The specific jurisdiction must be included in any state-level declaration
Activation request must be submitted within 14 days of the end of the incident period response via email to recovery.mdem@maryland.gov
Request must be submitted by the emergency management director or designee

Request must include: type of assistance requested, estimated costs by category, administration plan, statement of impact, confirmation that the incident exceeds local recovery capabilities, and a description of all other funding sources secured or being pursued
No other forms of funding, resources, or support must be available to meet the need
SDRF funds may not supplant other available funding sources
Amendment requests are due within 30 days post-approval, if applicable
Small businesses must meet Maryland State Finance and Procurement Code § 14-501 definition
Disaster must exceed local capacity; emergency operations plan must be implemented
Damage assessments are required (conducted using MDEM Survey123 tool)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. A local or state State of Emergency is declared. 2. Local jurisdiction assesses and documents damage using MDEM Survey123 tool and prepares application during days 1–14. 3. Submit SDRF activation request by Day 14 via email to recovery.mdem@maryland.gov. 4. MDEM and the SDRF Committee review and approve or deny the request. 5. If approved, amendment requests (if needed) are due within 30 days. 6. Award period of performance runs 365 days post-approval. Unused funds must be returned. Jurisdictions may request case management services; a blended funding approach with state/NGO support is available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Accredited Community Health Worker Training Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health accredits Community Health Worker (CHW) training programs offered by various organizations across Maryland. These accredited programs provide training and certification for individuals seeking to become Community Health Workers. Multiple programs are listed with varying locations, language options, and specialty focuses such as peer recovery and perinatal health. Some programs offer grants, scholarships, or stipends for eligible students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accredited CHW training programs are offered at various locations throughout Maryland. Individual programs may offer grants, scholarships, or stipends to qualifying students. Programs provide certification training for Community Health Workers, with some specializing in areas such as peer recovery or perinatal health.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to become certified Community Health Workers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification as a Community Health Worker
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; programs are located in various counties including Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Howard County, Washington County, Wicomico County, Cecil County, and others.
requirements_list: Applicants must contact individual accredited programs for specific eligibility requirements
Some programs offer language options including Spanish, Arabic, Korean, and Amharic
Some programs have specialty focuses such as peer recovery or perinatal health
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact individual accredited training programs directly to inquire about enrollment, eligibility, and any available scholarships or funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: AERS is a state-mandated Maryland program based in local health departments that provides assistance to frail, aged, and disabled adults and children who are at risk of entering institutional care. Licensed Registered Nurses and social workers conduct a comprehensive, person-centered, no-cost on-site in-home evaluation to assess individual needs, develop a personalized care plan, and connect clients to home and community-based services to promote independence and prevent unnecessary placement in a nursing home or other residential care facility. Services include connection to Community First Choice (CFC) and Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS) for help with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, meal preparation, light chores, and community access. Case management is also available to coordinate and monitor public services. Interpretation and translation services are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost on-site in-home assessment by a licensed Registered Nurse or social worker, individualized care plan development, and case management services to coordinate and monitor public services. Connects individuals to community support services including Community First Choice (CFC) and Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS) for assistance with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, meal preparation, light chores, and community access. Individuals must meet specific medical and financial criteria (such as Medicaid eligibility) for certain support programs. Case management is available for eligible older adults. Interpretation and translation services are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frail, aged, and disabled adults and children who are at risk of placement in a care facility, have chronic medical conditions, or need help with activities of daily living and want to remain living safely in the community. Includes older adults aged 65 and older needing case management services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home assessment and care planning; case management; connection to community support services such as CFC and CPAS for assistance with activities of daily living including bathing, dressing, meal preparation, light chores, and community access; home and community-based services to help individuals remain safely at home and maintain independence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local health departments. The referral form on the Maryland Department of Health page is exclusively for Queen Anne's County residents; residents of other counties should contact their local health department. Baltimore County residents may contact the Baltimore County Department of Health at 410-887-2754.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at risk of placement in a care facility, entering institutional care, or facing a change in normal living situation
Must have chronic medical conditions or need help with activities of daily living
Must meet specific medical and financial criteria (such as Medicaid eligibility) for certain support programs like CFC and CPAS
Case management is available for individuals aged 65 and older
Voluntary program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone can make a referral. For Queen Anne's County residents: submit the AERS Referral Form, apply by phone through Maryland Access Point (MAP) at 844-627-5465, or contact the local Queen Anne's County MAP Coordinator at 410-758-0848. For Baltimore County residents: call 410-887-2754. Residents of other counties should contact their local health department or MAP Coordinator directly. A nurse or social worker completes an assessment at the individual's current location, followed by an individualized care plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: ACIS is a Medicaid program operating under Maryland's Medicaid 1115 Health Choice Waiver that provides housing-related case management services and wrap-around supports to people who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless, including those at risk of institutional placement. The program targets high-risk, high-utilizing Medicaid enrollees who cycle in and out of multiple systems with chronic health conditions, mental illness, addictions, and a history of incarceration and/or homelessness. A case manager works with participants to create a supportive housing plan and helps connect them with needed services so they can live safely and independently in their home and community. The program aims to provide low- or no-barrier stable housing and well-integrated medical care with wrap-around support services. In Prince George's County, the program also includes stable housing placement and integrated medical care coordination. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs in standard case management. Available in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive housing-related case management services including community integration assessments, person-centered community integration planning, help connecting with social services, assistance communicating with landlords or property managers, and connection to training and resource support for managing their home. In Prince George's County, the program also provides stable housing placement and integrated medical care coordination with wrap-around support services. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs in standard case management, but housing placement support may be provided through participating entities and community partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid enrollees who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, at risk of institutional placement, or have two or more chronic conditions or frequent emergency room/hospital use. Served in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County. Prince George's County specifically targets high-risk, high-utilizing individuals with chronic health conditions, mental illness, substance use disorders, or a history of incarceration or homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing-related case management services including needs assessments, person-centered community integration planning, social service connections, landlord/property manager communication, home management training and resources, stable housing placement, and integrated medical care with wrap-around support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Have Medicaid in Maryland
Have two or more chronic conditions (long-term illness) OR use the emergency room or be hospitalized more than four times per year
Be experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, or facing institutional placement
Choose to participate in the ACIS program
Live in a current ACIS service area: Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, or Prince George's County

Must meet at least one housing criterion: facing homelessness upon release from a health-care, mental health, substance abuse, foster care, or correctional facility, OR currently homeless and at imminent risk of institutionalization

Must meet at least one health criterion: repeated ED use (more than 4 visits per year) or hospital admissions, OR two or more chronic conditions as defined in Section 1945(h)(2) of the Social Security Act (Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the county office for your area to get more information and start the process. Baltimore City: email mmcp.acis@maryland.gov. Prince George's County: call 301-883-3413 to request a Referral Form and a Release of Information form; self-referrals and referrals on behalf of another person are accepted. You can also email acis@maryland.gov. Cecil County and Montgomery County contacts are listed on the Maryland Department of Health ACIS page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assistance in Community Integration Services (ACIS) Program – Provider Solicitation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Assistance in Community Integration Services (ACIS) Program delivers housing and tenancy-based services to eligible individuals who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless. The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) invites local health departments and county governments to apply to become ACIS providers and deliver these services within their jurisdictions. MDH awards participant spaces to new and existing providers and lead entities, with 1,520 spaces available in the 2026 solicitation and a total program capacity of 2,140 participant spaces statewide. Providers receive monthly reimbursement through Maryland Medicaid for delivering a minimum of three ACIS services per month per member. The program has been in effect since July 1, 2017 and was approved by CMS on January 12, 2025 to expand statewide. It operates under a Maryland Medicaid §1115 Demonstration Waiver effective January 13, 2025 through December 31, 2026, with an extension application submitted for January 2027–December 2031.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH awards participant spaces (1,520 spaces available in the 2026 solicitation; total program capacity is 2,140 spaces statewide) to qualifying local health departments and county government agencies. Providers receive monthly reimbursement through Maryland Medicaid at $725 per member per month for delivering a minimum of three ACIS services per month per member, plus $100 per member per year for Lead Entity compliance activities (W9910-ACIS code). Funding is split 50% State General Funds and 50% Federal Funds. Providers must be enrolled Maryland Medicaid providers (Provider Type GH) to bill for services. Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. Multiple claim submission pathways are available: EDI (837 batch via MMEE), eMedicaid (web-based CMS 1500), or paper CMS 1500 (paper processing up to 90 days).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments, county government entities, and consortiums of such entities (including consortiums of local health departments from multiple counties) seeking to become ACIS Lead Entities and deliver housing and tenancy-based services to Medicaid members experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Participating Entities (subcontractors such as 501(c)(3) nonprofits, private for-profit entities legally authorized in Maryland, health services agencies, mental health agencies, housing authorities, criminal justice/probation entities, and human services agencies) may deliver services under a Lead Entity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of housing and tenancy-based services to eligible Medicaid members who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless, including tenancy-based case management, housing case management, and housing supports/subsidies coordination. Lead Entity compliance and Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) completion activities are also reimbursable. Services are billable up to 3 instances per calendar month per participant; compliance/HSCP activities are reimbursed at $100/member/year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; providers deliver services within their local jurisdiction. The program operates under a Maryland Medicaid §1115 Demonstration Waiver effective January 13, 2025 through December 31, 2026, with an extension application submitted for January 2027–December 2031. Currently approved Lead Entities include Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services, Cecil County Health Department, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, and Prince George's County Health Department, with expansion to all Maryland jurisdictions authorized.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local health department, county government entity, or consortium of such entities serving one or more Maryland counties
Must be an enrolled Maryland Medicaid provider (Provider Type GH) to deliver and bill for ACIS services
Lead Entity representative must attest as a Local Health Department or County Government
Must be a member of their local Continuum of Care (CoC) Program
Must submit a mandatory letter of intent (LOI) prior to submitting application
Must submit the Request for Responses/Application by the deadline
Must provide a minimum of three ACIS services per month per member to receive monthly reimbursement
Must conduct monthly attestation of exclusion database checks (OIG, SAM)
Must comply with HIPAA requirements
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service
Must conduct Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) reviews at least every 12 months
Participating Entities (subcontractors) must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits or private for-profit entities legally authorized in Maryland, and may not bill Medicaid directly
Medicaid enrollment required for eligible program participants (Fee-for-Service Medicaid participants meeting health and housing criteria)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Email [email protected] to request the mandatory LOI template and instructions. 2. Submit the LOI by March 13 at 5 p.m. 3. Submit the Request for Responses/Application by April 6 at 5 p.m. MDH will conduct a review period (April 6–24), send award notifications on May 1, and begin program onboarding on May 18. An appeal process is available within 7 calendar days of notification. Should participant spaces remain available after the initial solicitation, a subsequent solicitation is anticipated, likely within the following year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT) Program, established in 1992, provides breast cancer and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment services to eligible Maryland residents. The program reimburses a range of participating health care providers — including hospitals, physicians, pharmacies, medical laboratories, and other health care professionals — throughout the state to deliver diagnosis and treatment services to program participants. Patients receive covered diagnosis and treatment services at no cost through participating providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses eligible health care providers for breast and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment services provided to program participants. Patients receive covered diagnosis and treatment services at no cost through participating providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are eligible for breast and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment services, as well as health care providers — including hospitals, physicians, pharmacies, medical laboratories, and others — seeking to participate in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Breast cancer and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must meet program eligibility criteria as defined under COMAR 10.14.02
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Patients, navigators, and coordinators submit applications along with all supporting documents via fax at (410) 333-7279 or secure email at [email protected]. Providers submit provider applications and revalidations via fax or email at [email protected]. Claim status is available through the provider portal at https://phpa-bccdtp.my.site.com/bccdtproviderportal/s/ or via fax and secure email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health partners with health centers, providers, and community groups. The center helps ensure newly arrived humanitarian immigrants get health assessments, follow-up care, and education. The program also helps migrant and seasonal farm workers access healthcare, including immunizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive health assessments, follow-up care, care coordination, referrals, and health education for humanitarian immigrants. It also offers technical assistance, resources, and training to healthcare and community associations that work with these populations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves newly arrived humanitarian immigrants, including refugees and asylees, as well as migrant, seasonal, and agricultural workers. It also supports health centers, health providers, and community organizations that work with these groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides services. Key activities include: Identifying and addressing public health conditions through health assessments and treatment. Connecting immigrants to culturally-informed healthcare. Providing health education about the U.S. healthcare system. Offering technical assistance and training to partner organizations. Developing and sharing health education materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Children's Medical Services (CMS) Program helps low-income, uninsured, or underinsured Marylanders ages 0–21 who need specialty care for a chronic illness or disability. CMS pays for pre-authorized services such as specialist visits, hospitalizations, surgeries, medications, therapies, lab work, x-rays, and medical equipment and supplies. Routine check-ups, immunizations, sick visits, emergency services, routine dental care, mental health services, and transportation are not covered. All services must be pre-authorized at least 10 business days before the service is provided. Applications must be submitted through the Salesforce Patient Portal; old application forms are no longer accepted as of June 16, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CMS pays for pre-authorized specialty medical services for eligible children and young adults (ages 0–21), including specialist visits, hospitalizations, surgeries, medications, therapies, lab work, x-rays, and medical equipment and supplies. Routine check-ups, immunizations, sick visits, emergency services, routine dental care, mental health services, and transportation are not covered. All services must be pre-authorized at least 10 business days before the service is provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured or underinsured Marylanders ages 0–21 with a chronic illness or disability who need specialty care. Both patients/families and providers interact with the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for pre-authorized specialty medical services including specialist visits, hospitalizations, surgeries, medications, therapies, lab work, x-rays, and medical equipment and supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be low-income
Must be uninsured or underinsured
Must be ages 0–21 years
Must need specialty care for a chronic illness or disability
All services must be pre-authorized; CMS requires a minimum of 10 business days to process pre-authorization before the service is provided
Applications must be submitted through the Salesforce Patient Portal (https://phpa.my.site.com/patientportal/s/); old application forms are no longer accepted as of June 16, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Salesforce Patient Portal at https://phpa.my.site.com/patientportal/s/ (old application forms no longer accepted as of June 16, 2025). Providers must submit applications and pre-authorizations through the Salesforce Provider Portal at https://phpa.my.site.com/providerportal/s/ (effective June 16, 2025 for applications and June 30, 2025 for pre-authorizations). All services require pre-authorization before they are rendered. For assistance, contact CMS staff by phone at 410-767-5588 (new applications) or 410-767-5298 (renewal applications), or by email at mdh.childrensmedicalservices@maryland.gov or crmsd@mdthink.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cigarette Restitution Fund Program (Direct Services/Cessation Counseling)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cigarette Restitution Fund Program offers smoking cessation counseling and free Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) patches to Queen Anne's County residents. It also provides education on tobacco use prevention and cessation assistance to community groups, school groups, and businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) patches are provided to eligible Queen Anne's County residents. Smoking cessation counseling and tobacco use prevention education are also available to individuals, community groups, school groups, and businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Queen Anne's County residents seeking smoking cessation support; community groups, school groups, and businesses seeking tobacco use prevention and cessation education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoking cessation counseling, free nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) patches, and tobacco use prevention education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Queen Anne's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Queen Anne's County resident (for free NRT patches)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-758-1306 to schedule an appointment or get more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) is an evidence-based, patient-centered care model that integrates behavioral health services into primary care settings. Primary care provider (PCP)-led teams — including a behavioral health care manager and a psychiatric consultant — can receive Medicaid reimbursement for care coordination, systematic monitoring using validated clinical rating scales, and psychiatric or substance use disorder (SUD) caseload consultation. Services do not require prior authorization and apply to both HealthChoice and Fee-For-Service Medicaid programs. Eligible provider types include Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Rural Health Clinics (RHCs), Behavioral Health Administrative Services Organizations (BHASOs), and primary care providers (physicians, advance practice nurses, physician assistants, pediatricians, OB/GYN practitioners). Effective October 1, 2023.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid reimbursement for Collaborative Care Model services billed under the primary care provider's name and provider number. No prior authorization is required. Covers care coordination, clinical monitoring, and psychiatric/SUD caseload review and consultation for HealthChoice and Fee-For-Service Medicaid patients. Eligible provider types include Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Rural Health Clinics (RHCs), Behavioral Health Administrative Services Organizations (BHASOs), and primary care providers (physicians, advance practice nurses, physician assistants, pediatricians, OB/GYN practitioners). Effective October 1, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary care providers (PCPs) and their care teams — including behavioral health care managers and psychiatric consultants — as well as MCOs, FQHCs, RHCs, and BHASOs participating in Maryland Medicaid (HealthChoice or Fee-For-Service). Ultimately serves Medicaid beneficiaries with behavioral health needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing Collaborative Care Model services including care coordination and management, systematic monitoring using validated clinical rating scales, and psychiatric/SUD caseload reviews and consultation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Maryland Medicaid providers across all counties. Applies to both HealthChoice MCO and Fee-For-Service Medicaid participants statewide. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions.
requirements_list: Care team must include a primary care provider (PCP), a behavioral health care manager, and a psychiatric consultant.
Services must be billed under the PCP's name and provider number.
No prior authorization required for CoCM services.
Applicable under both HealthChoice and Fee-For-Service Medicaid programs.
Eligible provider types include MCOs, FQHCs, RHCs, BHASOs, physicians, advance practice nurses, physician assistants, pediatricians, and OB/GYN practitioners.
Provider enrollment via ePREP is required to participate in Maryland Medicaid.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers should enroll with Maryland Medicaid via ePREP (ongoing enrollment, not time-gated). For guidance on reimbursement, coding, and provider participation, refer to Provider Transmittal PT 71-24 (April 19, 2024), effective October 1, 2023. Contact the Provider Enrollment Helpline at 1-844-463-7768 or email [email protected] for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Health Worker Certification Training Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Health accreditation program for organizations that want to offer Community Health Worker (CHW) certification training. Under the Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR 10.68.02), all CHW certification training programs must be accredited by the Maryland Department of Health before they can operate. Accreditations are issued for 3-year terms and are subject to renewal indefinitely. The Department acts within 60 calendar days after all requirements are met. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations receive official accreditation from the Maryland Department of Health to operate Community Health Worker certification training programs. The CHW team provides assistance to applicants during the accreditation process. Accreditations are issued for 3-year terms and are subject to renewal indefinitely per COMAR 10.68.02. The Department acts within 60 calendar days after all requirements are met. A fee set by the Department applies for accreditation and renewal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to offer Community Health Worker certification training programs in Maryland, including non-profits, for-profits, government entities, and higher education institutions that wish to train and certify Community Health Workers under COMAR 10.68.02
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation to legally operate a CHW certification training program in Maryland; does not involve grant funding — this is a regulatory approval/certification process
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to organizations in Maryland. No county, regional, or municipality restrictions apply.
requirements_list: Must review all information and documents on the program page before completing an application
Must comply with COMAR 10.68.02 (Community Health Worker Certification Training Programs)
Accreditation must be issued before an organization may offer a CHW certification training program
Accreditation is valid for 3-year terms and must be renewed to continue operating
Applications are accepted in accordance with a schedule established by the Department and made publicly available
A fee set by the Department is required for accreditation and renewal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review all information and documents on the program page, then complete and submit an accreditation application. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis in accordance with a schedule established by the Department. The Department acts within 60 calendar days after all requirements are met. Contact the CHW team at [email protected] or 410-767-5971 for assistance. For renewal inquiries, contact [email protected].

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps individuals with disabilities or functional limitations live independently in their own homes and communities. Provides personal assistance services for activities of daily living, supports planning, and nurse monitoring. Eligibility is based on both medical and financial criteria for community Medicaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded personal assistance services including help with bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, and light chores; supports planning; and nurse monitoring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who live in the community and require assistance with daily activities at home, and who meet medical and financial eligibility for community Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal assistance with activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, light chores), supports planning, and nurse monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in the community (not in an institution) in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must live in the community (not in an institution)
Must require assistance with daily activities at home
Must meet both medical and financial eligibility for community Medicaid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Health for application information. Eligibility is determined based on medical and financial criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Core Funding program provides state funding to Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City to support core public health functions and staff. Established under Health-General Article §2–301–2–305, it distributes funding based on a state-driven formula to help local health departments deliver the ten essential public health services, including infectious disease prevention and treatment, environmental health, family planning, maternal and child health, wellness promotion, adult and geriatric health services, protective equipment for health care personnel, communicable disease emergency preparedness, and administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual state funding distributed to Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City based on a state-driven formula. The budget is approved annually through the Governor's Budget and updated monthly with actual and projected expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments in Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infectious disease prevention and treatment, environmental health services, family planning, maternal and child health, wellness promotion, adult and geriatric health services, protective equipment for health care personnel, communicable disease emergency preparedness, and administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a local health department in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funding is distributed through the state-driven formula as part of the annual Governor's Budget process. The budget is updated monthly with actual and projected expenditures. Contact dhmh.phscorefunding@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program authorizes staff of youth camps, food service facilities, and institutions of higher education to obtain and administer auto-injectable epinephrine to individuals experiencing severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) when a physician or emergency medical services are not immediately available. Participants must complete an approved training course and receive a certificate from the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) before obtaining epinephrine from a pharmacy. Certificates are issued to individuals (not facilities) upon successful completion of an approved training course and submission of the required application form and written policy. Eligible instructors (physicians, registered nurses, or certified nurse practitioners) may also apply to have training courses approved by submitting their training materials for review.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues certificates to individuals who complete an approved epinephrine training course, authorizing them to obtain and administer auto-injectable epinephrine at their facility. The certificate allows the holder to purchase auto-injectable epinephrine from a pharmacy for emergency use. Participants submit form MDH 4783 along with a written policy to receive a certificate from the Maryland Department of Health. To have a new training course approved, facilities submit form MDH 4782 along with the training manual, handouts, presentations, exams, and sample completion certificate. Eligible instructors (physicians, registered nurses, or certified nurse practitioners) may apply to have training courses approved per COMAR 10.16.07.15D.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Brian Flynn (youth camps); mdh.envhealth@maryland.gov (food service/higher education)
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (410) 767-8417; Toll Free 1-877-463-3464 ext. 78417; Environmental Health Bureau (866) 703-3266
structured_extraction.program_audience: Staff employed by youth camps, food service facilities, and institutions of higher education in Maryland who need authorization to administer epinephrine in emergencies; also trainers/instructors (physicians, registered nurses, certified nurse practitioners) seeking to offer approved emergency epinephrine training courses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining a certificate that authorizes the holder to purchase and administer auto-injectable epinephrine to individuals experiencing anaphylaxis at their facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for qualifying facilities and camps. Eligible facility types are youth camps (COMAR 10.16.07), food service facilities, and institutions of higher education (COMAR 10.13.04). No county-level or municipal restrictions apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be employed by a participating youth camp, food service facility, or institution of higher education
Applicant must be at least 18 years of age
Applicant must complete an MDH-approved epinephrine training course and attach the completion certificate
Applicant must submit the certificate holder application form (MDH 4783)

A written facility policy must be submitted along with the application form, addressing designated agents, storage, parental notification, security, reporting, annual training, and 3-year documentation retention
Facilities or camps seeking course approval must submit the training program application form (MDH 4782)
Course instructors must hold a license as a Physician, Registered Nurse, or Certified Nurse Practitioner
Course approval applicants must submit training manual, handouts, presentations, exams, and completion certificate for review per COMAR 10.16.07.15D
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Verify eligibility under the relevant statute and regulations (COMAR 10.16.07 for youth camps; COMAR 10.13.04 for food service facilities and institutions of higher education). 2. Complete an approved training course (a list of pre-approved courses for youth camps is available on the program page; contact mdh.envhealth@maryland.gov or (866) 703-3266 for food service or higher education courses). 3. Submit the certificate holder application form (MDH 4783) along with a written policy to the Maryland Department of Health to receive a certificate. To have a new course approved, submit the training program application form (MDH 4782) along with the training manual, handouts, presentations, exams, and sample completion certificate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The EID Program is a Medicaid buy-in program for working people with disabilities who would otherwise be ineligible for Medicaid because of their earnings. Eligible participants pay a monthly premium on a sliding scale based on their income, ranging from $0 (for those with income below $15,960/year) up to 7.5% of monthly countable income (for those with income above $95,760/year), and receive full Medicaid health coverage in return. A hardship exemption is available for those temporarily unable to pay their premium — the exemption can waive the monthly enrollment fee for up to 6 months for those whose payment would compromise their ability to obtain basic food, shelter, or clothing. Premium amounts are updated periodically; the current schedule is effective January 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive full Medicaid health coverage by paying a monthly premium on a sliding scale. Premiums range from $0 (for individuals earning less than $15,960/year) up to 7.5% of monthly countable income (for individuals earning over $95,760/year). A Hardship Exemption is available for those temporarily unable to pay their premium — the exemption can waive the monthly enrollment fee for up to 6 months for those whose payment would compromise their ability to obtain basic food, shelter, or clothing. Premium amounts are updated periodically; the current schedule is effective January 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents ages 16–64 who are employed or self-employed, have a disability meeting Social Security medical criteria, and would otherwise be ineligible for Medicaid due to their earnings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicaid health insurance coverage (health insurance subsidy) for eligible working individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Maryland. No county-level or regional restrictions; program is statewide. Homeless applicants must designate their state and county.
requirements_list: Be at least 16 years old but not yet 65 years old
Be working for pay (employed or self-employed, with earnings subject to taxes — no 'under the table' work)
Have a disability that meets Social Security's medical criteria
Be a U.S. Citizen or a qualified non-citizen
Live in Maryland
Meet the $10,000 asset limit ($10,000 for individual; joint assets and individually owned assets count, but spouse-only resources do not)
Provide identification documents (birth verification, SSN card, marriage/divorce certificates, Medicare card, citizenship/immigration papers if applicable)
Provide four consecutive weeks of pay stubs or an employer earnings statement; self-employed applicants must provide most recent tax return and earnings records
Provide documentation of other income (Social Security, disability benefits, pensions, unemployment, veterans benefits, insurance payments, rental income, trust fund income, etc.)
Provide resource documentation (bank accounts, savings bonds, CDs, stocks, vehicles, property, trusts)
Provide health insurance identification card for applicant and household members
Application must be signed and dated to be accepted
Report changes affecting eligibility or benefit amount within 10 days
Provide truthful information; false statements may result in fraud penalties
Must cooperate with Department to secure payments from third-party insurance
Must allow home visits and document inspection by Department staff

For hardship exemption: financial hardship must be so severe that payment of the premium would compromise ability to obtain basic food, shelter, and clothing for self or dependents (maximum 6-month exemption)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the EID Program application (all sections including demographics, citizenship, income, assets, medical expenses, and insurance). Sign and date the application — unsigned applications will not be accepted. Enclose all required supporting documents and mail the package to: Eligibility Determination Division, EID Program, Maryland Department of Health, 6 St. Paul Street, 4th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202. An interview (in person, by phone, or via authorized representative) may be required. A fillable PDF is available at https://mmcp.health.maryland.gov/eid/pages/home.aspx. Disability agencies or Centers for Independent Living in Maryland may assist with the application. For the Hardship Exemption, request form DHMH EID 2A from your caseworker, complete it with income, expense, and resource documentation, and mail it to the Eligibility Determination Division; MDH will notify you of its decision within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Healthiest Maryland Businesses (HMB) is a statewide collaborative of Maryland businesses with a shared mission to build and promote a culture of health in the workplace. Participating businesses receive accredited workplace wellness resources, individualized technical assistance, training, and peer support to develop comprehensive wellness strategies. Members in good standing can display the HMB logo on their website, email signatures, or in their workplace to show their commitment to employee wellbeing. Businesses can also earn recognition for their commitment to workplace wellness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating businesses receive accredited workplace wellness resources, individualized technical assistance, training, and peer support to develop comprehensive wellness strategies. Members in good standing may display the HMB logo on their website, email signatures, or in their workplace to demonstrate their commitment to employee wellbeing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses committed to building and promoting a culture of health in the workplace and seeking workplace wellness resources, training, and peer support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workplace wellness programming, resources, training, and peer support to improve employee health and business outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland businesses.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland business
Must join HMB and remain in good standing to display the HMB logo
Must be in good standing with the HMB collaborative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses can join HMB by visiting the 'How to Join' page on the HMB website at https://health.maryland.gov/phpa/ccdpc/HMB/Pages/HMB.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Babies - Pregnancy and Postpartum Coverage
structured_extraction.program_description: Healthy Babies provides free Medicaid health coverage to pregnant people who live in Maryland and meet income limits, including those who are not U.S. citizens. Coverage begins as soon as the person applies during pregnancy and can continue up to four months after the baby is born. The program pays for prenatal visits, doctor visits, hospital care (including delivery), dental care, lab work, prescription drugs, mental health care, behavioral health services, and non-emergency medical transportation to medical appointments. Medicaid may also retroactively help pay for health care received in the three months before the application date.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Medicaid health coverage that pays for prenatal visits, doctor visits, hospital stays (including delivery), dental care, lab work, prescription drugs, mental health care, behavioral health services, and non-emergency medical transportation. Coverage lasts through pregnancy and up to four months postpartum. Medicaid may also retroactively cover health care costs from up to three months before the application date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals living in Maryland who meet income limits, including non-U.S. citizens, who cannot afford health care. Coverage extends through approximately four months postpartum.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care coverage including prenatal visits, doctor visits, hospital care, dental care, lab work, prescription drugs, mental health care, behavioral health services, and non-emergency medical transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Maryland. Program is available statewide with no county-level or regional restrictions. Applications can be submitted online, by phone, or in person at local Health Departments or Health and Human Services offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be pregnant
Must live in Maryland
Must meet the Medicaid income limit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through Maryland Health Connection online at marylandhealthconnection.gov, by phone at 1-855-642-8572, TTY users call 711 (Maryland Relay), via mobile app, or in person at a local Health Department or Department of Social Services/Health and Human Services office. Sign up as soon as you know you are pregnant. Enrollment is ongoing with no fixed application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free removal of lead hazards and in-home case management services to reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers for Maryland families with a child who has been exposed to lead. The program covers the full cost of lead hazard remediation at no cost to the family from homes, apartments, or day care facilities where the child spends time. Additionally, the program provides in-home visits from local health department staff to help reduce environmental hazards in the home. Lead hazard removal is available statewide, while in-home case management services are available in participating counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Lead hazards are removed from the home, apartment, or day care at no cost to the family. Additionally, in-home visits and case management services are provided to help reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers for children, delivered through local health departments in participating counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico). No dollar amount is specified for the remediation services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families with a child (age 18 or younger) who has elevated blood lead levels (5 micrograms per deciliter or higher) or moderate to severe asthma, and is enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP/MCHP. Lead hazard remediation is available statewide; in-home case management is available for children with elevated blood lead levels or moderate to severe asthma in participating counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal of lead hazards from the place where the child was exposed (home, apartment, or day care), and in-home services to reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers in the child's home environment, including case management support for affected children and families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Lead hazard remediation is available statewide in Maryland. In-home case management services are available in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Child is 18 years old or younger and lives in Maryland
Child has a recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher, OR moderate to severe asthma (frequent attacks or on daily long-term controller medication)
Child is enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP/MCHP
Child spends 10 or more hours per week at the location where lead exposure occurred (for lead hazard remediation)
Child must reside in one of the participating counties (for in-home case management services)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Environmental Health Help Line toll-free at 1-866-703-3266 or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov to find out more and begin the process. For in-home case management services, contact the local health department in the county where the child lives.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland initiative operated by the Maryland Department of Health that provides free removal of lead hazards from homes, apartments, or day care settings for families with a child who has been exposed to lead, as well as in-home case management services to reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers. The program covers the full cost of lead hazard remediation — including lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in homes built before 1978 — at no cost to the family or property owner. In-home visits are delivered through local health departments in participating counties. The program targets children 18 years old or younger who have elevated blood lead levels and live in Maryland, and are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP. Lead hazard removal is available statewide, while in-home case management services are available in participating counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free lead hazard removal and minor home repairs to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in the home, apartment, or day care setting where the child was exposed, at no cost to the family or property owner. Includes homes built before 1978. Additionally, in-home visits and case management services are provided through local health departments in participating counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico) to help reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers for children. No specific dollar amount is stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families with a child (age 18 or younger) who has been exposed to lead, has a blood lead level of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher (or moderate to severe asthma), is enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP (MCHIP), and spends 10 or more hours per week at the location where lead exposure occurred (home, apartment, or day care). In-home case management services are available to families in participating counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal of lead hazards and minor home repairs to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed at the place where the child was exposed (home, apartment, or day care), including homes built before 1978, as well as in-home services and case management support to reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers in the child's home environment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The lead hazard remediation component is available statewide in Maryland. In-home case management services are delivered through local health departments in participating counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Child must be 18 years old or younger and live in Maryland.

Child must have a recent blood lead test of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher (lead hazard remediation) or 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher (home visiting services), OR moderate to severe asthma — defined as frequent attacks or daily use of long-term controller medication (home visiting services).
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHIP/CHIP).
Child must spend 10 or more hours per week at the location where lead exposure occurred (home, apartment, or day care) for lead hazard remediation eligibility.
Child must reside in a participating county for in-home case management services.
Property where lead exposure occurred must have been built before 1978 (for home repair component).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Environmental Health Help Line toll-free at 1-866-703-3266 or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov to find out more and begin the process. Families may also contact the local health department in the county where the child lives. Additional information is available on the Maryland Department of Health's Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Visiting Services for Children with Asthma (Case Management Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland counties offer in-home services to help families reduce asthma triggers and improve health outcomes for children with moderate to severe asthma who are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP. Families receive home visits and case management from county health staff who assess the home environment and provide support to manage the child's asthma. Services are available through local county health departments in participating counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home case management and home visiting services by county health staff to assess and address asthma triggers and lead hazards in the home environment for children 18 years old or younger with moderate to severe asthma or lead poisoning who are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP. Home visits address environmental triggers including dust, pests, mold, pets, and smoke.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with a child (18 years old or younger) who has moderate to severe asthma, lead poisoning, or both, and is enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP, residing in eligible Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home environmental health visits and case management to identify and address asthma triggers and lead hazards, and improve asthma management and living conditions for children with moderate to severe asthma or lead poisoning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Child must be 18 years old or younger and live in Maryland in an eligible county
Child must have moderate to severe asthma (frequent asthma attacks or on a daily long-term controller medication), lead poisoning, or both
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local county health department directly using county-specific contact information, or call the Environmental Health Help Line toll-free at 1-866-703-3266 or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov to get more information or to refer a child for home visiting services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community-Based Options Waiver (Community Options Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Home and Community-Based Options Waiver (also known as the Community Options Waiver) provides Medicaid-funded services to adults 18 and older with physical disabilities or aging-related care needs who would otherwise require nursing home placement, enabling them to live at home or in an assisted living facility instead. The federal government waives certain Medicaid requirements — such as the requirement that services be provided in a nursing facility — so the state can pay for covered services that allow eligible clients to remain in the community. Services include personal care, assisted living support (including room and board costs for eligible assisted living residents), behavior consultation, case management, dietitian and nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, respite care, home-delivered meals, environmental assessments and adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, and all standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice for those living at home. The program is statewide and locally administered through county departments of aging and disabilities, including in Anne Arundel, Charles, Howard, and Prince George's counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid waiver services provided in the home or community setting rather than a nursing facility, including personal care, assisted living support (including room and board costs for eligible assisted living residents), behavior consultation, case management, dietitian/nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, respite care, home-delivered meals, environmental assessments and adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, and all other standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice for those living at home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents 18 and older, including older adults and individuals with physical disabilities, whose advanced age or disability would otherwise require nursing home placement and who meet Medicaid income and asset guidelines. The program is locally administered in Anne Arundel County through the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities, in Charles County through the Charles County Department of Aging and Senior Services, in Howard County through the Howard County Office on Aging and Independence (Maryland Access Point at (410)313-1234), and in Prince George's County through the Aging and Disabilities Services Division (301-265-8450).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers services that allow eligible adults to live in their own home or an assisted living facility instead of a nursing home, including personal care, assisted living support (including room and board costs for eligible assisted living residents), behavior consultation, case management, dietitian/nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, respite care, home-delivered meals, environmental adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, and other community-based long-term care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents who meet eligibility requirements. Locally administered in Anne Arundel County through the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities, in Charles County through the Charles County Department of Aging and Senior Services, in Howard County through the Howard County Office on Aging and Independence, and in Prince George's County through the Aging and Disabilities Services Division.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be a Maryland resident
Must meet Medicaid long-term care admission criteria (medical and functional criteria for nursing facility level of care)
Must meet Medicaid financial eligibility criteria (income and assets reviewed)
Monthly income not to exceed $2,199
Assets not to exceed $2,000–$2,500
Must be eligible for Medicaid Community Options Waiver
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 1-844-627-5465 (toll free) for more information or to apply. An assessment is conducted to determine if the required level of care for nursing facility services is met. Anne Arundel County residents may also contact the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities. Charles County residents may also contact the Charles County Department of Aging and Senior Services. Howard County residents may call Maryland Access Point (MAP) at (410)313-1234 (voice/relay) for more information. Prince George's County residents may contact the Aging and Disabilities Services Division at 301-265-8450. Additional information is available through the Maryland Department of Health waiver programs page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Interim Care program provides short-term medical evaluation and treatment services to residents of Queen Anne's County who do not have a primary care provider. The program manages conditions such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cholesterol, and helps patients transition to a permanent primary care provider. Interpretation and translation services are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term medical care for high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and/or high cholesterol; assistance finding and transferring to a permanent primary care provider; connection to community resources. Interpretation and translation services are available.
