structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 and older who are residents of Queen Anne's County, do not have a primary care provider, and have a known or suspected diagnosis of high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and/or high cholesterol.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term medical evaluation and treatment for high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and/or high cholesterol; care coordination and referral to a permanent primary care provider; connection to community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Queen Anne's County only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Queen Anne's County
Must be 18 years of age or older
Must not currently have a primary care provider
Must have a known or suspected diagnosis of high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and/or high cholesterol
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Interim Care Referral Form (available on the program page at https://click.pattrac.net/dWa5x4). Self-referrals, family referrals, and patient referrals by providers are all accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program aims to improve the oral health of Maryland residents through various public health projects and interventions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants, technical assistance, and information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for county governments, non-profit organizations, and state colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support public oral health initiatives and interventions.

structured_extraction.program_description: MADAP ensures that people living with HIV in Maryland have access to the HIV and related medications they need to stay healthy. The program pays for medications for eligible clients with no insurance and helps clients who have insurance by covering eligible co-pay and deductible costs. The MADAP formulary includes all FDA-approved anti-retroviral therapies to treat HIV, as well as medications for opportunistic infections, complications of HIV, and non-HIV related conditions. Clients can fill prescriptions at approximately 1,432 pharmacies that accept Maryland Medicaid. MADAP Plus, a companion component, pays health insurance premiums for eligible clients whose plan includes prescription coverage meeting minimum formulary and coverage standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MADAP covers the cost of HIV and related medications for uninsured eligible clients, and pays co-pays and deductibles for insured clients. MADAP Plus pays health insurance premiums for plans with prescription drug coverage that meet minimum standards (formulary comparable to MADAP's and coverage cap greater than $2,500). Clients approved for MADAP must reapply annually. Income eligibility thresholds (effective 02/01/2026): annual gross household income must fall within a minimum–maximum range (e.g., $22,025–$79,800 for household of 1, scaling to $76,894–$270,750 for household of 8+). Hepatitis C medications require prior authorization; preauthorization review takes 1–3 business days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No fixed deadline; continuous intake with annual renewal required
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents living with HIV who have household income at or below 500% of the federal poverty level and are not eligible for Medicaid. Also serves HIV/HCV co-infected clients for hepatitis C medication coverage. Unhoused applicants may provide a letter stating they are without a home, verified by a case manager or agency staff receiving Ryan White support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for HIV anti-retroviral therapies, medications for opportunistic infections and HIV complications, non-HIV related medications on the MADAP formulary, hepatitis C medications (with prior authorization), and health insurance premiums (MADAP Plus).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Maryland. Acceptable residency documentation includes a valid Maryland driver's license or Maryland ID card, current Medicaid notice of decision, lease, utility bill, or similar documents. Unhoused applicants may provide a letter verifying lack of permanent address. Program is statewide with no county-level or municipal restrictions.
requirements_list: Diagnosed with HIV
Household income at or below 500% of the current federal poverty level for household size
Annual gross household income must fall within program minimum–maximum thresholds (e.g., $22,025–$79,800 for household of 1; scales to $76,894–$270,750 for household of 8+; effective 02/01/2026)
Maryland resident (acceptable documentation includes valid Maryland driver's license/ID, current Medicaid notice of decision, lease, utility bill, or similar)
Not eligible for Maryland Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
Proof of insurance or documentation of why applicant lacks coverage
Authorization for information exchange with providers and insurers
Non-compliance with continued eligibility verification results in suspension/termination
For MADAP Plus: responsible for paying 50% or more of health insurance premium
For MADAP Plus: health insurance must have a formulary comparable to MADAP's and a coverage cap greater than $2,500
For HCV medications: patient must have sufficient eligibility period to cover full prescribed treatment course; TAP (Temporary Assistance Program) clients awaiting Medicaid are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a MADAP Client Enrollment Application (most recent version: July 2025) with required documentation including proof of HIV diagnosis, Maryland residency, income documentation, and insurance information. Submit by mail, email, or fax. Eligibility determinations for complete applications are made within 10 business days of receipt. Approved clients must reapply annually; annual eligibility recertification form is due by the end of the 11th month of the enrollment period and must be completed by the end of the 12th month. For MADAP Plus, complete the insurance section of the enrollment application and include a copy of the current insurance premium bill. For hepatitis C medications, prior authorization is required and is reviewed within 1–3 business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (BCCP) – Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland BCCP provides free breast and cervical cancer screenings to eligible women on the Eastern Shore who face financial or insurance barriers. Services are provided through local doctors, clinics, and hospitals and include clinical breast exams, mammograms, Pap and HPV tests, and follow-up testing and support for eligible women with limited income and no or inadequate health insurance coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost breast and cervical cancer screenings including clinical breast exams, mammograms, Pap and HPV tests, and follow-up testing and support, provided through local doctors, clinics, and hospitals to eligible women with limited income and no or inadequate health insurance.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-778-7970 (Upper Shore: Kent, Queen Anne's, Cecil); 410-479-8080 (Mid-Shore: Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot); 410-548-5175 (Lower Shore: Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women aged 40–64 (or over 65 without Medicare Part B) living on Maryland's Eastern Shore who have limited income and no insurance or insurance that does not fully cover breast and cervical cancer screenings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Breast and Cervical Cancer Screening Program (BCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Breast and Cervical Cancer Screening Program (BCCP) is funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Maryland Cigarette Restitution Fund. It operates on two levels: (1) providing grants to local health departments and health systems to deliver breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic, patient navigation, outreach, and education services; and (2) providing free or low-cost breast and cervical cancer screening and diagnostic services directly to eligible low-income, uninsured, or underinsured women across the state. Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms (screening and diagnostic), breast ultrasound, surgical consultation, breast biopsy, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, and cervical biopsy, as well as patient navigation support including help scheduling appointments, finding transportation, accessing interpretation services, and linkage to treatment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants to local health departments and hospitals to support breast and cervical cancer screenings, outreach, education, patient navigation, and follow-up services, including hiring community health outreach workers and contracting with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories. Additionally, free or low-cost screening and diagnostic services are provided directly to eligible women, including clinical breast exams, mammograms (screening and diagnostic), breast ultrasound, surgical consultation, breast biopsy, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, and cervical biopsy, along with patient navigation services such as appointment scheduling, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and linkage to treatment.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Center for Cancer Prevention and Control
structured_extraction.program_audience: Two audiences: (1) Local health departments and hospitals in Maryland seeking grants to provide cancer screening services; and (2) Women in Maryland ages 18–64 (or 65+ without Medicare Part B) with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level who are uninsured, underinsured, or need help accessing screening services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support the provision of breast and cervical cancer screenings, outreach, education, patient navigation, and follow-up services, including hiring community health outreach workers and contracting with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories. Direct services include clinical breast exams, mammograms (screening and diagnostic), breast ultrasound, Pap tests, HPV tests, diagnostic procedures, surgical consultations, breast biopsy, colposcopy, and cervical biopsy, as well as patient navigation including appointment scheduling, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and linkage to treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must live in Maryland
Ages 18–39 for diagnostics if symptomatic or screening if at increased risk

Ages 21–64 for cervical cancer screening
Age 65+ and do not have Medicare Part B
Income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
No health insurance, or health insurance that does not fully cover needed services
Individuals with insurance who need help getting screened or obtaining follow-up testing are also eligible
Eligible organizational applicants include county/local health departments and non-profit health systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals: Call 1-800-477-9774 or use the online county finder tool on the program website to find the nearest service location. Organizations seeking grants: Application deadlines vary; typically in late spring. Contact the Center for Cancer Prevention and Control at mdh.cancer@maryland.gov or 410-767-5281 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Cancer Prevention, Education, Screening and Treatment (CPEST) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cancer Prevention, Education, Screening, and Treatment (CPEST) Program provides and administers grants to local health departments and academic centers to reduce cancer mortality and cancer disparities in Maryland. Funded through the Maryland Cigarette Restitution Fund (CRF), the program coordinates statewide public health initiatives targeting seven cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), and oral cancers. Grants fund prevention, education, screening, diagnostics, and treatment services for uninsured and underinsured low-income individuals. The program aims to reduce mortality and morbidity rates for cancer and tobacco-related diseases across all Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project grants are provided to local health departments and academic centers to fund prevention, education, early detection, screening, and treatment services for seven targeted cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), and oral cancers. Services primarily target uninsured and underinsured low-income individuals.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Center for Cancer Prevention and Control
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments and academic centers in Maryland seeking funding to reduce cancer mortality and disparities among uninsured and underinsured low-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cancer prevention, education, screening, diagnostics, and treatment services for the seven targeted cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), and oral cancers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available across all Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local health department, academic center, or non-profit organization
Services must address one or more of the seven targeted cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), or oral cancers
Activities must align with the goal of reducing cancer mortality and morbidity in Maryland
Applicants must form a Community Health Coalition
Applicants must create and submit a cancer control plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Health Coalitions create a cancer control plan and submit it to the Maryland Department of Health as part of their application for funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Certified Community Health Worker (CCHW) Certificate Renewal
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's statewide renewal process for Certified Community Health Workers (CCHWs). A CCHW certificate is valid for two years from the date of issue. Certified workers must complete 20 hours of professional development activities and submit a renewal application to maintain their certification at no cost. Applications can be submitted up to 120 days before and up to two years after the certificate expiration date. The department confirms completeness within 30 calendar days and issues a determination within 1–90 calendar days. Applications may be submitted online through the Maryland OneStop portal or by requesting a paper application from the MDH CHW team. State certification and renewal program for Community Health Workers operating under Md. Health-General Art. § 13-37 and COMAR 10.68.01.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certificate renewal for Certified Community Health Workers (CCHWs). No fee is charged. The renewed certificate is valid for two years from the date issued. Renewal requires completing 20 hours of professional development activities (courses, webinars, conferences, workshops, trainings, lectures, or readings). Applications may be submitted up to 120 days before and up to two years after the certificate expiration date. The department confirms application completeness within 30 calendar days and issues a determination within 1–90 calendar days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; applications accepted up to 120 days before and up to two years after certificate expiration date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Community Health Workers (CCHWs) in Maryland holding active or recently expired (within 2 years) certificates who are eligible for renewal; certification is voluntary and open to individuals age 18+ who have completed an accredited CHW training program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renewal of a Certified Community Health Worker professional certificate; no monetary funds disbursed. The program provides a credential renewal pathway at no cost to the applicant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Certified Community Health Workers throughout Maryland statewide; no county, municipal, or regional restrictions
requirements_list: Hold a current or recently expired (within 2 years) Maryland CCHW certificate
Be at least 18 years of age
Hold a high school diploma or GED
Have completed an MDH-accredited CHW training program
Submit a Certificate Renewal Application through the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov) or contact the CHW team to request a paper application
Complete 20 hours of professional development activities (courses, webinars, conferences, workshops, trainings, lectures, or readings)

Document each professional development activity with: activity title, date, hours, sponsor, location, written explanation of acquired knowledge and/or skill application, and associated CHW core competency or health principle
Provide seven required elements per activity: title, sponsor, location, date(s), hours, associated CHW core competency or health principle, and brief description of knowledge or skills acquired
Activities must align with at least one of Maryland's nine CHW Core Competencies or health principles
Only educational/instructional hours count (exclude travel time, breaks, meals, social media time, and non-educational components)
Apply no earlier than 120 days before and no later than 2 years after the certificate expiration date
Renewal applications received less than 30 calendar days before the certificate expiration date may not be processed before the expiration date
Notify the Maryland Department of Health if name or contact information changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov) or contact the CHW team at 410-767-5971 or [email protected] to request a paper application (available in multiple languages). Log professional development activities directly in the application using the Professional Development Activities Tracking Sheet and upload required documents. Use Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, or Safari for best results. The application can be started up to 120 days before expiration and submitted up to two years after expiration. The application remains in Draft mode until submitted and can be updated at any time. The department will confirm completeness within 30 calendar days and issue a determination within 1–90 calendar days. Renewal notification is sent 90–120 days before each individual certificate's expiration date. Allow approximately 30 days for processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health certifies Community Health Workers (CHWs) who have completed a Maryland Department of Health-accredited CHW training program. Certification is valid for two years and is issued free of charge, with no fee for initial certification or renewal. Applicants apply through the Maryland OneStop portal by submitting proof of age and documentation of completing an accredited CHW training program. Applications are reviewed within 30 days for completeness and a final determination is made within 1–90 calendar days after a complete application is submitted. Paper applications are available in English and other languages (including Spanish) by contacting the CHW Team. A Spanish-language version of the program page is also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A no-fee, two-year CHW certification is issued to qualifying applicants who have completed a Maryland Department of Health-accredited CHW training program. Certification is renewed every two years at no cost (must be renewed within 30 days of certificate expiration). Applications are submitted online through the Maryland OneStop portal or via paper application (available in English and other languages including Spanish). Applications are reviewed within 30 days for completeness and a final determination is made within 1–90 calendar days after a complete application is submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — no deadline; applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals aged 18 or older who have completed a Maryland Department of Health-accredited Community Health Worker training program and hold a high school diploma or GED equivalent. Spanish-language materials and assistance are available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional certification as a Community Health Worker in Maryland; not a funding program. Obtaining a two-year Community Health Worker certification recognized by the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions stated; all Maryland residents or workers who meet individual eligibility requirements may apply.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years of age or older
Must have a high school diploma or GED equivalent
Must have successfully completed a CHW training program accredited by the Maryland Department of Health
Must submit official documentation from the accredited training program including: program name, program address, program accreditation number, date of completion, and an authorizing signature

Must provide documentation of training completion (official certificate, letter, or document including training program name, address, accreditation number, date of completion, and authorizing signature)
Must submit a CHW Certification Application with supporting identity and training completion verification documents
Must read, agree to, sign, and date the attestation on the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov/forms/chw-certification-application-5d6ebfe095ea3d00feed6f9c) including age verification and documentation of successful completion of an accredited CHW training program. Steps: (1) Complete an MDH-accredited CHW training program; (2) Visit the MDH CHW webpage and confirm eligibility; (3) Register with Maryland OneStop and complete the online application, or request a physical application by contacting the CHW program; (4) Upload required identity verification and training completion documents; (5) Review uploaded documents for legibility and accuracy; (6) Read, agree to, sign, and date the attestation; (7) Submit online or via physical mail. Paper applications in English, Spanish, or other languages are available by contacting the CHW Team at 410-767-5971 or MDH.CHWApplications@maryland.gov. Use Google Chrome, Firefox, or Safari for the best online experience. Applications are reviewed within 30 days for completeness, and a final determination is made within 1–90 calendar days of submitting a complete application. Certificates are valid for two years and must be renewed within 30 days of the certificate expiration date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Harm Reduction Training and Technical Assistance: ROR Training Series, Bold Initiative, and Wound Care Training
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health provides a suite of harm reduction training and technical assistance programs to support the harm reduction workforce, reduce stigma, and improve care for people who use drugs across Maryland. Programs include: (1) The Regrounding Our Response (ROR) Training Series, a workforce development program that reduces stigma, increases understanding of trauma and trauma-informed approaches, and supports linkages to behavioral health and quality care. It trains Master Presenters to disseminate information to the broader community and federally qualified health centers, and measures stigma using the Shatterproof Addiction Stigma Index (SASI). Free, on-demand courses are available online covering Adverse Childhood Experiences, Medications for Addiction Treatment, Comprehensive Care Framework for People Who Use Drugs, Social Determinants of Health, and Stages of Change. (2) The Wound Care and Comprehensive Care Training, co-created by MDH and the Maryland Harm Reduction Training Institute (MaHRTI), provides free in-person or virtual wound care training for clinical staff and basic first aid and medical training for non-clinical staff. It includes video resources in English and Spanish covering wound care basics, dressing changes, xylazine-associated wounds, and related health topics. (3) The Bold Initiative, a trauma-informed training series for outreach workers and providers that supports overdose prevention, leadership development for people who use drugs, and addresses overdose variances in communities throughout Maryland. It includes Peer Leadership Development Training, Youth Peer Prevention Curriculum, Maternal Health Curriculum, and Overdose Prevention for Seniors Curriculum. Technical assistance is available via email for all programs. Training resources include on-demand online courses, in-person and virtual workshops, curated educational materials, and master presenter development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-demand online training through the ROR series covering Adverse Childhood Experiences, Medications for Addiction Treatment, Comprehensive Care Framework for People Who Use Drugs, Social Determinants of Health, and Stages of Change, accessible at ror-mdhealth.thinkific.com. Free in-person or virtual wound care training for clinical staff and basic first aid and medical training for non-clinical staff, with video playlists in English and Spanish covering wound care basics, dressing changes, xylazine-associated wounds, and related health topics. The Bold Initiative provides a trauma-informed training series for outreach workers and providers including Peer Leadership Development Training, Youth Peer Prevention Curriculum, Maternal Health Curriculum, and Overdose Prevention for Seniors Curriculum. Formats include courses, curricula, videos, and master presenter development. Technical assistance is available via email for all programs. No funds are distributed to applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Clinical and non-clinical staff, outreach workers, health care providers, behavioral health staff, federally qualified health center staff, harm reduction workers, people who use drugs, and communities affected by overdose across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free training and technical assistance covering workforce development, stigma reduction, trauma-informed care, overdose prevention, behavioral health linkages, wound care, first aid skills, leadership development, and innovative curricula for diverse populations including youth, seniors, and maternal health — no funds are distributed to applicants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access free on-demand ROR training at ror-mdhealth.thinkific.com. For ROR technical assistance, email mdh.ror@maryland.gov. For Bold Initiative information or technical assistance, email mdh.bold@maryland.gov. For wound care training information or technical assistance, email mdh.woundcare@maryland.gov. Additional contact: ingrid.mcdowell@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program (MHSDP) provides dental care to eligible Medicaid members at no cost. The program covers a wide range of dental services with no premiums, deductibles, copays, or annual benefit maximum. A benefits management company (SKYGEN) administers the program on behalf of Maryland Medicaid. Eligible populations include children under age 21, former foster care members through age 25, pregnant and postpartum adults over age 21, adults over age 21 receiving full Medicaid benefits, special needs populations, HIV/AIDS patients, homeless individuals, and low-income uninsured individuals (sliding fee scale available at select providers).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free dental coverage for eligible Medicaid members with no premiums, deductibles, copays, or annual benefit maximum. Covered services include anesthesia, crowns, fillings, fluoride treatments, extractions, regular checkups, root canals, teeth cleaning, and x-rays. Children under 21 also receive fluoride varnish, orthodontics, and sealants. Adults receive denture adjustments. Cosmetic procedures, dentures for adults 21+, and experimental procedures are not covered. Sliding fee scales available at select providers for uninsured/underinsured individuals. Translation and transportation services available at select providers. Wheelchair accessible facilities available at many providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents eligible for full Medicaid coverage, including: children under age 21; former foster care members through age 25; pregnant and postpartum adults over age 21; adults over age 21 receiving full Medicaid benefits; special needs populations (physically, mentally, or developmentally disabled); HIV/AIDS patients; homeless individuals; LGBTIQ community; seniors (55+); and low-income uninsured individuals (sliding fee scale available at select providers).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental care services including routine checkups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions, x-rays, fluoride treatments, anesthesia, and additional services for children under 21 (orthodontics, sealants, fluoride varnish) and adults (denture adjustments). Also covers preventive, restorative, prosthetic, pediatric, emergency, endodontic, periodontal, geriatric, and oral surgery services depending on provider.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all eligible Maryland Medicaid members. All 24 Maryland counties are covered. Some providers are designated statewide service providers (no geographic restrictions); others serve county-specific residents. Resources in Delaware and Washington D.C. are also listed in the Maryland Oral Health Resource Guide for reference.
requirements_list: Must have full Medicaid coverage
Must have a red and white Medicaid card
County residency requirements vary by individual provider
Proof of income required for sliding fee scale at select providers
HIV case management or Ryan White Regional Services Network enrollment required for HIV/AIDS specialty services at select providers
Maryland residency required
Must keep scheduled appointments (some programs)
Cannot reapply if treatment has already been provided (some programs)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit member.mdhealthysmiles.com to find a Medicaid dentist near you. Call 855-934-9812 or email outreachcoordinator@skygenusa.com for assistance. No formal application is required beyond having full Medicaid coverage. Patients call individual provider clinics directly to schedule an appointment. For Office of Oral Health general inquiries, call 410-767-7915. TTY users may use Maryland Relay 711.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Income Tax Credit for Preceptors in Areas with Health Care Workforce Shortages (Maryland Preceptor Tax Credit Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a credit against Maryland State income tax to licensed health professionals who voluntarily serve as uncompensated preceptors (clinical supervisors) for medical, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, registered nurse, or licensed practical nurse students in community-based clinical rotations at qualifying underserved or rural practice sites in Maryland. Credits of $1,000 per qualifying rotation are issued on a first-come, first-served basis up to $10,000 per individual preceptor per tax year, subject to annual funding availability. Eligible preceptors apply during a designated application window each year, with a complete four-part application submitted to the Maryland Department of Health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit certificates of $1,000 per qualifying rotation are issued by the Maryland Department of Health, capped at $10,000 per individual preceptor per tax year. Credits are applied against Maryland State income tax liability for the tax year in which the preceptor served qualifying rotations. Credits are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to annual funding availability and are not guaranteed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application cycle opens December 1, 2026; deadline January 5, 2027 at 11:59 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed health professionals (physicians/MDs/DOs, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, certified nurse midwives, clinical nurse specialists, certified registered nurse anesthetists, registered nurses, and licensed practical nurses) who serve as uncompensated preceptors for eligible students at qualifying underserved or rural practice sites in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland State income tax liability for the tax year in which the preceptor served qualifying rotations, at a rate of $1,000 per qualifying rotation up to $10,000 per tax year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Practice site must be located in a Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA), Federally Qualified Health Center, Medically Underserved Area (MUA), Medically Underserved Population (MUP), federal designated rural area, or state designated rural area in Maryland. Program is available statewide.

Must serve as a preceptor without compensation
Must precept an eligible student type enrolled in a recognized preceptorship program
Must complete a minimum of three distinct rotations per tax year
Rotations for medical and PA students must be at least 100 hours each; rotations for NP, RN, or LPN students must be at least 90 hours each

Practice site must be located in a qualifying shortage or rural area (HPSA, Federally Qualified Health Center, MUA, MUP, or designated rural area)
Must hold a professional license (provided by applicant as Part 4 of application)
Must provide proof of student attendance (Part 2, submitted by the educational institution)
Must provide proof of preceptorship (Part 3 of application)
Complete application must be received between December 1, 2026 and January 5, 2027 (11:59 PM)
Applications received prior to December 1, 2026 will be discarded
All four parts of the application must be submitted; only complete applications will be considered
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability
Credits are subject to available annual funding and are not guaranteed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit all four parts of the application to mdh.preceptortaxcredit@maryland.gov between December 1, 2026 and January 5, 2027 (11:59 PM). Part 1 is the application and attestation. Part 2 (proof of student attendance) must be submitted by the educational institution. Part 3 is proof of preceptorship. Part 4 is the applicant's professional license. Applications are reviewed and tax credit certificates are issued on a first-come, first-served basis as funding allows. Sign up for the MDH Workforce Listserv to receive updates about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Medicaid Doula Program connects eligible Medicaid members who are pregnant or recently pregnant with a trained doula (birth worker) who provides physical, emotional, and informational support before, during, and after birth. The program serves multiple audiences: (1) eligible Maryland Medicaid members who receive free doula services including prenatal visits, attendance at birth, and postpartum visits delivered in a person-centered, culturally respectful way; (2) certified doulas seeking to participate as Medicaid providers; and (3) doula training organizations seeking to become MDH-approved certification organizations. Doulas must be certified through an MDH-approved certification organization and enrolled as Medicaid providers to receive reimbursement for services rendered to eligible members. Services are provided at no cost to eligible members through their HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free doula services for eligible Medicaid members (prenatal visits, attendance at birth, postpartum visits, labor support, breastfeeding guidance, self-advocacy coaching, and connection to community resources) delivered through HealthChoice Managed Care Organizations at no cost to eligible members. Medicaid reimbursement is also available to certified doulas enrolled as Medicaid providers. Organizations that train doulas may apply to become MDH-approved certification organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid members who are currently pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days; certified doulas seeking to become Medicaid providers; and organizations that train doulas seeking to become MDH-approved certification organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Doula services including prenatal and postpartum home visits, attendance at birth, labor support, comfort measures, breastfeeding guidance, mental health support, self-advocacy coaching, and connection to community resources for Medicaid members; reimbursement for doulas providing those services to Medicaid-covered individuals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Medicaid members and Medicaid-enrolled doulas
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member (to receive services)
Must be pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days (to receive services)
Must be enrolled in a HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) to be connected with a doula (for members)
Must be certified through an MDH-approved doula certification organization (for doula providers)
Must enroll as a Medicaid provider (for doula providers)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Medicaid members: Contact your HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) directly; the MCO will help connect you to a doula as soon as one is available and provide more information about available services. Alternatively, talk to your health care provider or call your health insurance provider for more information. For doulas: Obtain certification from an MDH-approved certification organization, then enroll as a Medicaid provider through the provider enrollment process. For organizations seeking to become approved certification organizations: Apply during open application periods; interested organizations can email their contact information to mdh.medicaidmch@maryland.gov to be notified of future application periods.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Maternal Opioid Misuse (MOM) Case Management Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The MOM Program provides free enhanced case management services to pregnant and postpartum Maryland Medicaid members diagnosed with or who have a history of opioid use disorder (OUD). A dedicated case manager meets with participants at least monthly to develop a personalized care plan covering mental and physical health needs, opioid treatment (including medication-assisted treatment), overdose prevention, and connections to local community resources. Services include screenings for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health, as well as coordination of prenatal and postpartum healthcare visits and linkage to behavioral health treatment. Care plans are shared through CRISP, Maryland's statewide health information exchange. Services are available during pregnancy and up to one year after delivery, delivered through Maryland's nine Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free enhanced case management services provided through Medicaid managed care organizations. A case manager meets with participants at least monthly to develop a personalized care plan, coordinate prenatal and postpartum healthcare visits, connect participants to opioid treatment (including medication-assisted treatment), screen for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health, and link participants to behavioral health treatment and local community resources. Care plans are shared via CRISP, the statewide health information exchange. Services continue during pregnancy and up to one year after delivery.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced case management services to coordinate prenatal and postpartum care, opioid use disorder treatment, mental health support, overdose prevention, health screenings, care planning, and connections to local community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid members.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in Maryland Medicaid
Must be pregnant or postpartum (services available up to one year after delivery)
Must be diagnosed with or have a history of opioid use disorder (OUD)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll online at https://health.maryland.gov/EnrollMOM or contact your health care provider or health care plan for help getting started. For questions, email MDH.MOMModel@maryland.gov.
