structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Refugee Mental Health Program connects humanitarian immigrants — including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking — with culturally and linguistically appropriate mental health services. The program recognizes that many of these individuals have experienced trauma such as war, torture, or prolonged family separation, and helps them access care suited to their language and cultural background.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Referral and connection to culturally and linguistically appropriate mental health services for eligible humanitarian immigrants in Maryland, including those who have experienced trauma such as war, torture, and prolonged family separation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Humanitarian immigrants in Maryland, including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking, who need mental health support and have resettled in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to mental health services that are culturally and linguistically appropriate, tailored to the cultural and linguistic needs of humanitarian immigrants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a humanitarian immigrant (refugee, asylee, parolee, or victim of trafficking) residing or resettled in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland School-Based Health Center Program supports comprehensive primary, acute, and preventative health services — including chronic condition management, mental health services, and other health care — for students, families, and communities through clinics physically located on or near school campuses. There are currently 91 active school-based health centers across 16 jurisdictions in Maryland. The program helps organizations open and operate school-based health centers (SBHCs), with a focus on increasing health access in underserved communities and improving student health and educational outcomes. Authorization to operate a school-based health center on a school campus in Maryland is granted upon acceptance into the program. Tailored support is provided to applicants throughout the application and startup process, with applications typically accepted in July and November.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding and tailored support and guidance to organizations interested in opening and operating school-based health centers. Authorization to operate a school-based health center on a school campus in Maryland is granted upon acceptance into the program. Staff offer email-based support to help applicants navigate the process, which varies depending on the type of organization, extent of collaboration with local stakeholders, and the building structure of the desired site. Specific grant award amounts and terms are not publicly described. Applications for new SBHCs are typically accepted in July and November.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for new SBHCs are typically accepted in July and November.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations interested in opening or operating school-based health centers in Maryland, particularly in underserved communities, including nonprofits, for-profits, government entities, and higher education institutions, serving students, families, and communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and operating school-based health centers on or near school campuses to deliver primary, acute, preventative, and mental health services to students, families, and communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; currently 91 active school-based health centers across 16 jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be interested in opening a new school-based health center on a school campus
Must be an organization capable of operating a school-based health center
Site must be physically located on or near a school campus
Must collaborate with local school and community stakeholders
Must have a suitable school campus site
Application requirements vary based on organization type, collaboration with local stakeholders, and building structure of the desired site
Process varies depending on organization type, extent of collaboration with local stakeholders, and building structure of desired site
Applications are typically accepted in July and November
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email [email protected] for further information and tailored support. Applications for new SBHCs are typically accepted in July and November.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tobacco Quitline is a free, confidential phone, web, and text message service available to all Maryland residents age 13 and older to help them quit any form of tobacco, including cigarettes and vaping. Trained quit coaches are available 24/7 to work with participants one-on-one to create a personalized quit plan, manage cravings, identify barriers to quitting, and provide ongoing follow-up support. The program provides free nicotine replacement therapy (NRT such as patches and gum) while supplies last, printed and web-based self-help materials, text messaging support, and referrals to local cessation resources. Specialized intensive multi-call programs are available for youth (ages 13–17) and pregnant women. A teen-specific program, Live Vape Free, is also available online and via text for ages 13–17, featuring podcasts, videos, and live coach chats focused on vaping cessation. A dedicated New and Expectant Parents Program is available for pregnant Marylanders and new parents who use tobacco; these participants receive free coaching sessions (typically 15–25 minutes each), medication guidance with doctor approval, free tailored booklets, and may enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation while supplies last. Healthcare providers can refer patients through a Fax to Assist program and receive HIPAA-compliant outcome reports. Services are available in English, Spanish, and other languages. The program is also open to non-smokers seeking to help a family member, friend, patient, or client quit tobacco.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential one-on-one quit coaching from trained cessation counselors available 24/7 via phone (1-800-QUIT-NOW), web, and text message (text READY to 34191). Services include a personalized quit plan, craving management and barrier identification support, follow-up counseling, printed and web-based self-help materials, and free nicotine replacement therapy (patches and/or gum) while supplies last. Intensive multi-call programs are available for youth (ages 13–17) and pregnant women. Teens can also access the Live Vape Free program online at livevapefree.com or by texting VAPEFREE to 873-373. For expectant and new parents, coaching sessions are typically 15–25 minutes each and include medication guidance (with doctor approval), free tailored booklets, and referrals to local programs; pregnant participants may receive gift cards for participation while supplies last. Healthcare providers can refer patients through a Fax to Assist program and receive HIPAA-compliant outcome reports. Coaches speak English, Spanish, and other languages.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 13 and older who want to quit any form of tobacco, including cigarettes and vaping, including youth, pregnant women, new parents, and adults in recovery from substance use; also available to non-smokers seeking to help a family member, friend, patient, or client quit tobacco. Healthcare providers can enroll as Fax to Assist referral partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation support including quit coaching, personalized quit planning, nicotine replacement therapy (patches and gum), self-help materials, text messaging support, referrals to local cessation resources, medication guidance, and gift card incentives for pregnant participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents age 13 and older, or those seeking services in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or seeking services in Maryland
Must be age 13 or older
Must want to quit tobacco use in any form (cigarettes, vaping, etc.)
For the New and Expectant Parents Program: must be pregnant or expectant
For the New and Expectant Parents Program: must enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline
Must register for the incentive program during enrollment to receive gift cards (while supplies last)
Teens (ages 13–17) can enroll online in the Live Vape Free program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669), enroll online at smokingstopshere.com or quitnow.net/maryland, or text READY to 34191. Teens can text VAPEFREE to 873-373 or enroll at livevapefree.com to access the Live Vape Free program. Pregnant and expectant parents should enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline and register for the incentive program at the time of enrollment to be eligible for gift cards. Coaches are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Healthcare providers can refer patients via the Fax to Assist program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tobacco Quitline – New and Expectant Parents Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Free tobacco cessation support program for pregnant and new parents in Maryland. Participants work with quit coaches available 24/7 who help create a quit plan, discuss health benefits of quitting, provide medication guidance (with doctor approval), and offer ongoing support in English, Spanish, and other languages. Services are available by phone, web, and text message. Pregnant participants may also enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation while supplies last. Free booklets tailored to expectant and new parents and referrals to local programs are also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free quit coaching calls (15–25 minutes each) by phone, web, or text message, available 24/7. Coaches speak English, Spanish, and other languages. Pregnant participants may receive gift cards for participation in the incentive program while supplies last. Free booklets tailored to expectant and new parents and referrals to local programs are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and expectant Marylanders and new parents who use tobacco and want to quit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation support including coaching, quit planning, medication guidance, educational materials, and gift card incentives for pregnant participants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Marylanders
requirements_list: Must be pregnant, expectant, or a new parent in Maryland
Must enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline
Pregnant participants must register for the incentive program during enrollment to receive gift cards (while supplies last)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline by phone, web, or text message. Pregnant participants should register for the incentive program at the time of enrollment to be eligible for gift cards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland WIC is a federal nutrition assistance program (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children) administered by the Maryland Department of Health. It provides supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and healthcare and social services referrals to eligible low-income pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding mothers, infants, and children under age five who meet income guidelines and are at nutritional risk as determined by a health professional. Participants receive food benefits—including fruits, vegetables, whole grains, dairy products, infant formula, and other WIC-approved nutritious items—loaded onto an electronic benefits transfer (EBT/eWIC) card or smartphone app for purchase at participating authorized retailers, with benefits provided monthly based on participant category. More than half of all infants born in the United States participate in WIC. Individuals enrolled in Foster Care, Medical Assistance, SNAP, or TCA may qualify automatically. Local WIC agencies serve all 24 jurisdictions (all counties and Baltimore City) statewide. Program information and app resources are available in multiple languages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides supplemental nutritious foods accessed via an electronic benefits transfer (EBT/eWIC) card or smartphone app at participating authorized stores, along with nutrition education, breastfeeding support services, and referrals to healthcare and social programs for eligible participants. Food benefits are provided monthly based on participant category and include WIC-approved items such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, dairy products, and infant formula. Benefits are available to pregnant women, new moms (up to six months postpartum), breastfeeding moms (up to one year postpartum), infants, and children under age five. Benefits are delivered through local WIC agencies in each county and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income pregnant women, new mothers (up to 6 months postpartum), breastfeeding mothers (up to 1 year postpartum), fathers and caregivers of children under age 5, infants, and children under age 5 who live in Maryland and meet income and nutritional need guidelines. Also includes individuals enrolled in Foster Care, Medical Assistance, SNAP, or TCA programs who may qualify automatically.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplemental healthy foods including fruits, vegetables, whole grains, dairy products, infant formula, and other WIC-approved nutritious items purchased at participating authorized stores; nutrition education; breastfeeding support services; and referrals to other health and social programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Maryland. Local WIC agencies are available in every county and Baltimore City, serving all 24 jurisdictions statewide.
requirements_list: Must reside in Maryland
Must be pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months after delivery), breastfeeding (up to 1 year after delivery), a father or caregiver of a child under age 5, an infant, or a child under age 5

Must meet income guidelines (low-income) — income threshold varies by family size (e.g., family of 1: ≤$28,953 annual; family of 2: ≤$39,128 annual; family of 8: ≤$100,178 annual); additional family members add $10,175 to income cap per member; based on 130% of federal poverty level; income numbers can change every year — call WIC to confirm current thresholds
Automatic eligibility if enrolled in Foster Care, Medical Assistance, SNAP, or TCA
Must have a nutritional need as determined by a health professional

Must bring proof of household income (pay stubs, SSI/Social Security/unemployment benefit letter, Medical Assistance/Medicaid card, Independence/SNAP/EBT card with recent receipt, tax return, or prior year W-2)
Must bring proof of identity for each person applying (birth certificate, driver's license/state ID, social security card, or government/school/employment photo ID)
Must bring proof of address (driver's license/state ID, official bill or statement, or rental/lease agreement)
Must attend first appointment in person with all individuals applying for benefits
If applicable: proof of pregnancy, immunization record for infant or child, or WIC referral form
Documentation required at application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check eligibility and schedule an appointment with a local WIC office by calling the county WIC office, calling 1-800-242-4942, or using the online Client Portal at wicclientportal.health.maryland.gov. Bring all persons applying for benefits to the first appointment in person, along with required documents (proof of income, proof of identity for each applicant, and proof of address). A health professional will assess nutritional risk and income eligibility. You may also contact Maryland WIC by email or through the Maryland WIC app (available on iOS and Android). Program information is available in multiple languages. Income guidelines are updated periodically — call WIC to confirm current income thresholds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maternal, Infant and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides voluntary, evidence-based home visiting services for expectant parents, young children, and their families. Trained professionals visit families at home to offer support. The program helps families strengthen bonds, promote child development and safety, and reduce the risk of child abuse.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides federal grant funding to states, territories, and tribal entities. The funds support the implementation of evidence-based, voluntary family support programs that meet the needs of their communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves expectant parents, young children, and their families, particularly those in at-risk communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support evidence-based home visiting programs. These programs aim to improve parenting skills, promote healthy child development, ensure child safety, and strengthen family bonds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates statewide but prioritizes funding for communities identified as having the highest risk based on a statewide needs assessment.
requirements_list: Grants may only support evidence-based home visiting programs that meet specific federal criteria.
Up to 25% of funding can be allocated for 'promising' home visiting models, which must be rigorously evaluated.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid provides an enhanced payment to qualified CenteringPregnancy prenatal care practices. Eligible practices can bill for a higher reimbursement rate for group prenatal care services delivered through the CenteringPregnancy model, effective January 1, 2023. Starting January 2024, practices must be accredited or pending accreditation by the Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI) to qualify for reimbursement. FQHCs are not eligible for the enhanced payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enhanced Medicaid reimbursement of $50 per participant per visit (CPT code 99078 with modifier -TH), for up to 10 group prenatal care visits per pregnancy, for qualified CenteringPregnancy practices enrolled in Maryland Medicaid. Only CenteringPregnancy is covered (not CenteringParenting). Practices must be accredited or pending accreditation by the Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI). FQHCs under the Prospective Payment System are not eligible for the enhanced payment. Accreditation status is reviewed annually to maintain eligibility. Practices must complete provider enrollment steps before billing. Guidance is published in the Professional Services Provider Manual.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Healthcare providers and group practices (OB/GYN, Family Medicine, Nurse Practitioners, Nurse Midwives) that deliver CenteringPregnancy group prenatal care services and participate in Maryland Medicaid. FQHCs under the Prospective Payment System are excluded from the enhanced payment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced payment for delivering CenteringPregnancy group prenatal care services to Medicaid enrollees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualified CenteringPregnancy practices operating in Maryland that are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid.
requirements_list: Practice must be enrolled as a group practice type with Maryland Medicaid
Practice must be accredited or pending accreditation by the Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI) (required as of January 1, 2024)
Both the group and each rendering provider must submit supplemental applications in ePREP
Group must submit: supplemental application, CHI approval letter, and CenteringPregnancy Addendum
Each rendering provider must submit: supplemental addendum with group's accreditation attached
Accreditation status is reviewed annually to maintain enhanced reimbursement eligibility
FQHCs under the Prospective Payment System are not eligible to bill for the enhanced payment
Must follow guidance in the Professional Services Provider Manual
Must properly document group visit times and topics
Only CenteringPregnancy qualifies (not CenteringParenting)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must complete enrollment through the ePREP (Electronic Provider Revalidation and Enrollment Portal) by submitting supplemental applications. Both the group practice and each individual rendering provider must submit supplemental applications in ePREP. The group must attach a CHI approval letter and the CenteringPregnancy Addendum. Each rendering provider must submit a supplemental addendum with the group's accreditation attached. For account updates, log into ePREP, go to the 'Accounts' tab, select the orange 'Update Account' action icon, complete the Supplemental Application form, and sign and submit using the last four digits of your SSN. For enrollment questions, contact mdh.providerenrollment@maryland.gov. For program questions, contact mdh.medicaidmch@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: CenteringPregnancy is a group-based prenatal and postnatal care program for Maryland Medicaid members who are pregnant. Participants meet with a provider for individual health checks and then join a group of about 8–10 people who share similar due dates. Group sessions last 90 minutes to two hours and cover topics such as pregnancy side effects, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy eating. Each visit combines individual provider health exams with group education and peer support before and after birth. Research links this model to higher birth weights, higher breastfeeding rates, lower rates of preterm birth, and better management of conditions like gestational diabetes. The program is free for eligible Medicaid members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group-based prenatal and postnatal care for eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Participants receive individual health exams with a provider, group education sessions covering pregnancy health, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and nutrition, and peer support — all at no cost through the Medicaid program. Sessions run 90 minutes to two hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals who are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid (HealthChoice managed care).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Group-based prenatal and postnatal care including individual provider health exams, health education on pregnancy, labor, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and nutrition, and peer support sessions before and after birth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid members. Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) to find a participating provider.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) — the number is on your insurance card — and ask them to help you find a CenteringPregnancy provider near you.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Medicaid Family Planning Program is a free, income-based, limited-benefits Medicaid plan for Maryland residents who are not eligible for full Medicaid coverage. The program provides family planning services including birth control, STI and HIV screenings, hepatitis screening, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, HPV vaccination, and sterilization (for those at least 21 years old). It is not full health care coverage and does not cover prenatal care or infertility services. Coverage can start immediately upon approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free family planning services with no premiums, deductibles, or copays. Coverage includes exams and advice about birth control, prescription and over-the-counter birth control, IUDs, implants, emergency contraception, STI/hepatitis/HIV screenings, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, HPV vaccine, and sterilization (tubal ligation or vasectomy) for those at least 21 years old. Does not cover prenatal care or infertility services. Coverage can start immediately upon approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of all ages who are not eligible for full Medicaid, Medicare, or another Medicaid program, who meet the income limit for family planning services, and who are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens. Must not be pregnant or already sterilized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family planning services including birth control (prescription, over-the-counter, IUD, implant, and emergency), STI/HIV/hepatitis screening, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, HPV vaccination, sterilization (tubal ligation or vasectomy for those at least 21 years old), and related exams and advice. Does not cover prenatal care or infertility services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen
Must meet the income limit for Family Planning
Must not have or be eligible for full Medicaid coverage or another Medicaid program
Must not have Medicare
Must not have already been sterilized (tubes tied or vasectomy)
Must not be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at any time online or by calling Maryland Health Connection at 1-855-642-8572. Applications can also be submitted through Maryland Health Connection. If eligible, coverage can start right away.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid's HealthySteps program integrates child development specialists into pediatric primary care to support healthy growth and development during the first three years of life. For eligible Maryland Medicaid families with children under age four, a HealthySteps Specialist joins the pediatric care team to provide developmental screenings, parenting resources, breastfeeding support, mental health support, and connections to community resources such as housing and transportation — at no cost to participants. For providers, qualified HealthySteps pediatric practices (including FQHCs) may bill Maryland Medicaid for an enhanced payment rate for delivering HealthySteps services, effective January 1, 2023. Eligible provider types include PT 20 (Physicians), PT 23 (Nurse Practitioners), and PT 80 (Physician Assistants). FQHCs have additional guidance published November 2023; note that FQHCs are not eligible to bill for the enhanced payment component due to the Prospective Payment System, but may implement HealthySteps. Specific payment amounts are detailed in the Professional Services Provider Manual, and practices must complete enrollment steps including submission of a supplemental application through the ePREP portal before billing for the enhanced payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For eligible Medicaid families: free child development support services through a HealthySteps Specialist embedded in the pediatric care team, providing developmental screenings, parenting guidance, breastfeeding support, mental health support, and community resource referrals at no cost. For qualified provider practices: an enhanced (higher) Medicaid reimbursement rate for delivering HealthySteps services using billing code H0025 for HealthySteps services in pediatric E&M and well-child visits, effective January 1, 2023. Eligible provider types include PT 20 (Physicians), PT 23 (Nurse Practitioners), and PT 80 (Physician Assistants). Practices must complete required enrollment steps, including a supplemental application through the ePREP portal, and must have completed HealthySteps Addenda (Group and Individual) plus an active site confirmation letter. FQHCs have additional guidance (published November 2023) but are not eligible to bill for the enhanced payment component due to the Prospective Payment System. Specific payment amounts are detailed in the Professional Services Provider Manual.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Two audiences: (1) Maryland Medicaid members with children from newborn to their 4th birthday; (2) Maryland Medicaid-enrolled pediatric primary care practices (including physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants; and FQHCs for implementation purposes) participating in the HealthySteps model and delivering HealthySteps services to pediatric patients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For families: child development screenings, parenting support, breastfeeding guidance, mental health and stress management support, and referrals to community resources such as housing and transportation. For providers: enhanced Medicaid reimbursement for delivering HealthySteps integrated child development services within primary care settings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid members and Maryland Medicaid-enrolled providers.
requirements_list: Child must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Child must be newborn through age 3 (under 4th birthday)
Practice must be a qualified HealthySteps practice
Must complete provider enrollment steps via ePREP supplemental application before billing for the enhanced payment
Eligible provider types: PT 20 (Physicians), PT 23 (Nurse Practitioners), PT 80 (Physician Assistants)
Must have completed HealthySteps Addenda (Group and Individual) and have an active site confirmation letter for all new and existing provider enrollments
Must follow guidance in the Professional Services Provider Manual
FQHCs may implement HealthySteps but are not eligible to bill for the enhanced payment component due to the Prospective Payment System

Required documents for enrollment include: DEA registration, state licenses, IRS letter, SDAT documentation, lab permits/CLIA (if applicable), NPI documentation, HealthySteps Addenda (individual and group), and active site confirmation letter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For families: Call your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) — the number is on your insurance card — or talk to your pediatrician. The MCO will help you find a HealthySteps provider. For providers: Submit a supplemental application through the ePREP portal. For post-enrollment account updates, providers use the ePREP Portal Accounts tab → Supplemental Application → select update type → Start updates → generate application → Sign and Submit with last four SSN. Resources including a step-by-step guide, recorded webinar (5/14/25), and guidance from the Professional Services Provider Manual are available on the program page. Contact the ePREP Call Center at 1-844-463-7768 (M–F, 9am–5pm EST) for enrollment questions, or [email protected] for claims/billing questions, or [email protected] for enrollment process questions, or [email protected] for general MCH program questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Home Visiting Services provide support and teach parenting skills to pregnant people and new parents before and after birth. Specially trained professionals or nurses visit the home to help families have a healthy pregnancy and raise healthy children. Services cover baby development and learning, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, mental health and stress management, and future planning. Maryland currently offers two evidence-based models: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership. Services continue until the child's second or third birthday, depending on the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home Visiting Services are free for eligible Maryland Medicaid members who are pregnant or have recently given birth. A specially trained professional or nurse visits the home to provide parenting support, child development education, self-care guidance, connection to community resources, diet and nutrition counseling, mental health support, and future planning. Services continue until the child is 2 or 3 years old depending on the program model (Healthy Families America or Nurse Family Partnership).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant Maryland Medicaid members or those who have delivered a child within the past three months
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home support services covering baby development and learning, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, mental health and stress management, and future planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Medicaid members statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant or have delivered a child within the past three months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Managed Care Organization (MCO) or health care provider to get connected to the right home visiting program. Your health plan can also help find the appropriate program for you.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to licensed medical day care centers. The centers use the funds to offer health, social, and support services to functionally disabled adults. This helps individuals stay in their homes and communities instead of moving to a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides contracts to licensed adult day care providers. The state sets the payment rates for these services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Day care centers are under contract 7/1/16 - 6/30/21.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the delivery of health, social, and related support services in a structured group setting for functionally disabled adults.
requirements_list: Providers must be licensed under COMAR 10.12.04, Day Care for Elderly and Adults with a Medical Disability.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Health Departments submit yearly budgets. Day care centers operate under contract with the state.

structured_extraction.program_description: This office works to end health differences among population groups. It uses state resources, offers expert advice on health fairness, and helps shape policies and communications to improve health for all.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The office provides project grants and technical assistance. Specific grant programs include the Minority Outreach and Technical Assistance (MOTA) and Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and individuals working to reduce health disparities in Maryland. This includes government bodies, non-profits, for-profits, and higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that address social factors affecting health and aim to eliminate health disparities among different population groups.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should call the office for information on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Money Follows the Person (MFP) is a Medicaid program that helps eligible individuals who live in a nursing home or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities move into a community setting — such as a home, apartment, or group home with four or fewer residents. A support team, including a peer mentor, helps participants find housing, care, and services needed to live independently in the community. Medicaid long-term care coverage transitions with the individual from the facility into the community setting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides Medicaid-funded long-term care services and supports that follow the individual into a community setting (home, apartment, or group home with four or fewer people). A support team and peer mentor assist with finding housing, care, and services needed to transition out of an institution and live independently. Medicaid coverage transitions with the person from the facility to the community setting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicaid-eligible individuals currently living in a nursing home or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities who wish to move into a community setting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Long-term care services and supports to help eligible individuals move from institutional settings into homes, apartments, or small group homes in the community and live independently.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible Maryland Medicaid recipients.
requirements_list: Must have lived at least 60 days in a nursing home or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities
Must have at least one day of Medicaid eligibility during the qualifying facility stay
Must sign an MFP Consent Form (can be completed independently or with help from a local Area Agency on Aging or peer mentor)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MFP Consent Form online (via the Cognito Forms link provided) either independently or with assistance from a local Area Agency on Aging (AAA) or peer mentor. Contact the MFP Program at 410-767-4915 or mdh.mfp@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free transportation to non-emergency medical appointments for Carroll County residents who qualify for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) and have no other means of transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free transportation to non-emergency medical appointments for eligible Carroll County residents enrolled in Medical Assistance (Medicaid).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County residents enrolled in Medical Assistance (Medicaid) who have no other means of transportation to medical appointments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to non-emergency medical appointments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Carroll County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must live in Carroll County
Must have Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
Must have no other means of transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Department of Health's Division of Community Support Services page for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nursing Facility Pay For Performance (P4P) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Pay-For-Performance (P4P) program awards Maryland Medicaid nursing facilities that perform highly on certain quality indicators. Each year, one percent of the program's nursing facility budget is distributed as awards. Facilities with the highest scores receive 85 percent of the total award pool, while facilities that showed improvement from the prior year receive the remaining 15 percent. Performance is measured across staffing levels, staff stability, MDS quality indicators, family satisfaction survey results, and staff immunization rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A total of one percent of the Maryland Medicaid nursing facility budget is awarded annually. Facilities with the highest scores share 85 percent of the pool; facilities showing the most improvement from the previous year share 15 percent of the pool. Awards are paid on a per Medicaid day (MA Day) basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid-participating nursing facilities with 45 or more beds that are not continuing care retirement centers and have not had recent federal quality enforcement actions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Performance-based financial awards for nursing facilities achieving high quality indicator scores or demonstrating improvement over the prior year. Awards are paid per Medicaid day (MA Day) and are tied to performance on staffing levels, staff stability, resident satisfaction surveys, MDS outcomes, and staff immunization metrics. No restrictions on use of funds are specified.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying nursing facilities participating in Maryland Medicaid statewide. No county-level or regional restrictions apply.
requirements_list: Must have 45 or more beds
Must not be a continuing care retirement center (CCRC)
In the previous year ending March 31, must not have been identified as a federally-designated 'special focus facility'
In the previous year ending March 31, must not have had a denial of payment for new admissions (DPNA) by CMS
In the previous year ending March 31, must not have been determined to have provided 'substandard quality of care' as defined in federal Medicaid regulations
Must participate in Maryland Medicaid
Must report payroll data
Must participate in the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) family satisfaction survey
Must submit MDS data to CMS
Must complete the MHCC staff immunization survey
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Performance scores are calculated by the Maryland Department of Health based on submitted and available data including staffing levels, staff stability surveys, MDS quality indicators, the Maryland Health Care Commission Family Satisfaction Survey, and staff immunization rates. No separate application process is described. Facilities must ensure required data submissions (payroll data, MDS data, MHCC surveys) are completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Health Internship Program (PHIP) is a paid internship run by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) that introduces undergraduate and graduate students to public health careers. Interns gain hands-on experience in subject areas such as epidemiology, health policy, biostatistics, community health, and more, supplementing their academic training and preparing them for the public health workforce. The program complements students' academic studies and provides practical experience across a wide range of public health disciplines including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship positions: undergraduate students earn $17.15/hour and graduate students earn $20.15/hour. The Summer 2026 cohort runs June 3 – August 11, 2026. Interns gain hands-on experience across a range of public health tracks including epidemiology, health policy, biostatistics, community health, health education, health informatics, healthcare administration, infectious disease, and more. Role-specific skills include data management, statistical analysis in SAS and Tableau, data visualization, policy research and analysis, legislative tracking, healthcare fraud auditing, accounting, regulatory board operations, and program development. Some positions (notably certain health policy and health education tracks) may be unpaid or experience-based; compensation details vary by role.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate students (who have completed at least 60 credit hours) and graduate students enrolled at an accredited college or university in good academic standing. Recent graduates of undergraduate or graduate programs may also be accepted. Some tracks specifically target current Public Health or Epidemiology graduate students or recent college graduates with interest in public health.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid work experience at the Maryland Department of Health in public health subject areas including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications. Interns build resume experience, program and data management skills, statistical skills (SAS and Tableau), data visualization, policy analysis, legislative affairs, healthcare fraud investigation, accounting, program evaluation, and regulatory/licensing board operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is operated statewide by the Maryland Department of Health; most internship positions are located in Baltimore City, MD, with some positions in Carroll County (Sykesville) and coordination with Prince George's County. Applicants must be enrolled at or recent graduates of an accredited college or university.
requirements_list: Must be an undergraduate student who has completed at least 60 credit hours, OR a graduate student, OR a recent graduate of an undergraduate or graduate program
Must be enrolled at an accredited college or university
Must be in good academic standing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the JobAps cloud portal linked on the program page (https://www.jobapscloud.com/MD/sup/bulpreview.asp?b=&R1=26&R2=008998&R3=0006). The application deadline for Summer 2026 is March 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rare and Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The REM Program provides medical case management and other services for Maryland Medicaid (HealthChoice) enrollees who have specific rare and expensive medical conditions. It is a voluntary program. Participants receive a dedicated REM case manager who conducts needs assessments, develops care plans, helps apply for and coordinate services, monitors services, and provides education. In addition to standard Medicaid benefits, the program offers supplemental services such as private duty nursing, certified nursing assistant care, chiropractic services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, home health aide services, and more. Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a healthcare provider; some require preauthorization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive all standard Medicaid covered services plus additional REM-specific services including case management, certified nursing assistant services, chiropractic services, home health aide services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and private duty nursing. A dedicated REM case manager conducts a needs assessment, develops a care plan, helps apply for services, monitors services, and provides education. Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a healthcare provider; some require preauthorization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid (HealthChoice) enrollees who have at least one qualifying rare and expensive medical condition and choose to participate voluntarily.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical case management, care planning, coordination of services, and supplemental healthcare services including nursing, therapy, nutrition counseling and supplements, and home health aide services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to individuals enrolled in the HealthChoice Medicaid managed care program.
requirements_list: Must be eligible for Maryland's HealthChoice managed care (Medicaid) program
Must have at least one qualifying rare and expensive condition for your age group as defined in COMAR 10.09.69
Must voluntarily choose to enroll in the REM program
Must have a valid Medical Assistance (MA) number
Must have a qualifying ICD-10 diagnosis on the REM disease list; age limits vary by diagnosis (generally 0–20 or 0–64 years)
History and physical must be completed within the past 12 months
Specialist consultation note or laboratory/imaging studies required per diagnosis guidelines
Physician signature required on referral form
Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a healthcare provider; some require preauthorization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone can refer an individual to the program. A licensed healthcare provider must complete the REM Intake and Referral Form with patient demographics, diagnoses (ICD-10), and required clinical documentation, then sign and date it. The completed form can be submitted via fax (410-333-5426), email to mdh.remreferralfax@maryland.gov, or mailed to REM Intake Unit, Maryland Department of Health, 201 W. Preston Street, Room 208, Baltimore, MD 21201-2399. The REM Intake Unit screens for eligibility and issues an approval or denial decision.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health's Sickle Cell Disease Follow-Up Program follows newborns, children, and young adults with sickle cell disease (SCD) up to age 18. It provides families with information about SCD and other hemoglobin disorders, guidance on what to expect from doctors and specialists, guides for living with SCD, and resources related to daycare, school, sports, transitioning to adult care, and community organizations.

Families with children born in other states may also enroll. A self-referral form is available online, and program staff will follow up with enrolled families.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides information, education, and resources to families managing sickle cell disease — not a funding program.

Child must be age 18 or younger
Children born in other states may also enroll
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can self-refer by completing the online self-referral form at cognitoforms.com/MDH3/scdselfreferralform. Program staff will contact the family after the form is submitted.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) and Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians (MLARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health administers two linked loan repayment programs for health care providers. The State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) is a federal program that requires a 1:1 match with the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MLARP), a state program. Both provide educational loan repayment funds to physicians, physician assistants, and medical residents who commit to a 2-year service obligation in a Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) or Medically Underserved Area (MUA). SLRP covers primary care or mental health practice; MLARP also covers state-designated shortage areas and extends eligibility to medical residents within their last year of residency. Awards are up to $50,000 per year for a 2-year obligation, with a maximum total award of $200,000 across multiple obligation periods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 per year for a 2-year service obligation (up to $100,000 per obligation period). Recipients may reapply after completing the first two-year obligation; total award cannot exceed $200,000 (two 2-year obligations at $50,000 per year). Funds are used for repayment of eligible higher education (student) loans. Recipients must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreeing to serve full-time at an eligible practice site per program guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible physicians, physician assistants, and medical residents (within their last year of residency) who have existing higher education loan debt and are willing to serve in a Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) or Medically Underserved Area (MUA) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of eligible higher education (student) loans for qualifying physicians, physician assistants, and medical residents serving in health professional shortage areas or medically underserved areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must practice at an eligible practice site located in a federally or state-designated Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA), Medically Underserved Area (MUA), or state-designated health professional shortage area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a United States citizen or U.S. National
Must have a medical degree and a valid unrestricted license to practice medicine in Maryland when the service obligation begins
Must have no existing or un-served service obligation with any other loan repayment program
Must have existing higher education loan debt and not be in default on any eligible higher education loan
Must never have violated court-ordered child support or been delinquent in child support payments
Must practice at an eligible practice site
Must meet other requirements as outlined in the eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application enrollment opens March 1. Complete and file an application available from the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). Application materials are available at https://pophealth.health.maryland.gov/Pages/State-Loan-Repayment-Program.aspx. The application deadline is April 15. For more information, call (410) 767-6123 or contact MDH.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides health care coverage through Medicaid — including vision, dental, behavioral health, substance use treatment, prescription drugs, and other services — to individuals who qualify under the Walter Lomax Act (Maryland SB0014, 2021) for at least five years. structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health licenses and regulates all youth camps in Maryland to protect the health and safety of children. Camp operators apply for certification by submitting documentation demonstrating compliance with state regulations covering personnel background checks, health services, supervision ratios, safety procedures, and facility maintenance. Both day camps and residential camps must obtain a certificate before operating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH issues certificates of compliance to youth camp operators who meet minimum state standards. New day camps pay $190 and new residential camps pay $500 at the time of application, with any balance owed paid at the end of camp. The certification allows camps to legally operate in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Operators of youth day camps and residential camps in Maryland serving children ages 3.5 to 18.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to legally operate a youth camp in Maryland, demonstrating compliance with health and safety regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties.

Day camps must include three recreation activities or one specialized activity
Day camps must have seven or more campers unrelated to the director
Day camps must be primarily recreational or at least 25% outside recreational activity
Residential camps must have campers stay away from parents for five days (four nights)
Residential camps must have seven or more campers unrelated to the director
Residential camps must be primarily recreational or at least 25% outside recreational activity
Complete a pre-application and current application in the MDH Youth Camp Portal
Upload required compliance documentation (building, water, sewage, health program, emergency procedures, child abuse prevention, background checks)
Pay applicable application fee

Receive email from MDH with instructions to create a password for the MDH Youth Camp Portal. 3. Log into the Portal to complete the current application, upload required compliance documentation, and pay the application fee. Operators with multiple locations must submit separate applications for each camp.

structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)
structured_extraction.program_description: WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) is a federally funded nutrition assistance program that provides healthy foods and nutrition counseling to pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under five years old. Participants receive nutrition education, referrals to health and social services, breastfeeding support, and checks (vouchers) to purchase approved foods at grocery stores including milk, 100% juice, peanut butter, cheese, eggs, dried beans and peas, cereal, whole grain breads, and fresh fruits and vegetables. The program serves Queen Anne's County (Centreville office) and Kent County (Chestertown office) on the Upper Eastern Shore of Maryland. Mobile WIC services are available at rotating sites throughout the service area including Galena, Sudlersville, Rock Hall, and Queenstown.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive vouchers/checks to purchase approved nutritious foods (milk, 100% juice, peanut butter, cheese, eggs, dried beans and peas, cereal, whole grain breads, and fresh fruits and vegetables) at grocery stores. Nutrition counseling, breastfeeding support, and referrals to other health and social services are also provided. Mobile WIC services are available at rotating sites throughout the service area, operating 9am–3:30pm.

Mobile clinic visits are available at 5 rotating sites on a monthly schedule; all sites operate 9am–3:30pm. Please call the office to verify mobile WIC schedule prior to appointment. Mobile site closures follow QACPS (Queen Anne's County Public Schools) weather-related closure policies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland WIC Program offers training classes for authorized WIC vendors to help them successfully participate in the program. Classes are designed to help stores understand and comply with WIC program policies, procedures, authorized foods, and transaction requirements, including changes to the Authorized Foods List. Maryland WIC regulations require authorized vendors to accept training from the WIC Program, with at least one representative attending an interactive training session each calendar year. Each vendor must designate at least one person as a designated WIC trainer, who is responsible for training all cashiers and other staff involved with WIC transactions on program policies, procedures, and any changes to the Authorized Foods List.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Medical Day Care Services Waiver (MDCSW) is a home and community-based services (HCBS) Medicaid waiver that helps eligible individuals receive medical care and support in their home and community instead of in a nursing institution. It provides full Medicaid covered services plus additional waiver services centered on medical day care, delivered by licensed medical day care providers. Services include skilled nursing and nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, social work, activity programs, daily living skills training, transportation, therapy, personal care, and nutrition services, provided at least four hours a day up to seven days a week. The program supports eligible Maryland residents who would otherwise require nursing facility-level care.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health Medicaid Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded waiver covering full standard Medicaid-covered services and benefits plus waiver services including medical day care (at least four hours a day, up to seven days a week), activity programs, meals, medication monitoring, nutrition services, skilled nursing and nursing assessments, social work services, daily living skills training, therapy, personal care, and transportation. Services are delivered by licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 16 or older who have full Medicaid coverage (red and white card), require nursing facility level of care, have a medical order for medical day care services, and are not enrolled in another home and community-based waiver program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical day care services provided at least four hours a day up to seven days a week, including skilled nursing and nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, social work, activity programs, daily living skills training, transportation, therapy, personal care, and nutrition services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible Medicaid recipients. Applicants must reside in Maryland and can contact their local health department or Maryland Access Point to apply.

Must have full Medicaid (red and white card)

Must require nursing facility level of care (medical eligibility)
Must have a medical order for medical day care
Cannot be enrolled in another home and community-based waiver program at the same time
Cost of community-based services must not exceed the cost of institutional care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request a medical assessment to determine if you meet the level of care requirement by calling your local health department or by calling Maryland Access Point at 1-844-627-5465 (toll free). You may also contact the Maryland Department of Health at 410-767-1444 or 1-800-535-0182 (toll free) to inquire about eligibility and apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hospital Preparedness Program (HPP) supports and enhances the ability of hospitals and health care systems to provide effective care during emergencies and disasters. The Maryland Department of Health receives federal funding annually from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR), then awards these funds as grants to health care system partners statewide. Partners use the funds to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters. The program also invests in four regional health care coalitions that bring together hospitals, local health departments, emergency medical services, and other partners to improve coordinated preparedness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health Office of Preparedness and Response
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds awarded as grants to health care system partners including hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services agencies, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing health care system preparedness, response, and recovery capabilities for emergencies and disasters, including joint training and exercises, shared assets and equipment, and coordinated preparedness planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Four regional health care coalitions serve: (1) Western Maryland — Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties; (2) Central Maryland — Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Harford, and Howard counties; (3) Eastern Shore — Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties; (4) Southern Maryland and National Capital Region — Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties.
requirements_list: Must be a health care system partner such as a hospital, free-standing emergency department, community health center, state-managed facility, poison control center, emergency medical service, home care agency, hospice agency, or regional health care preparedness coalition.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Medicare Savings Programs (also called Medicare Buy-In Programs) help low-income Medicare beneficiaries pay the costs of Medicare coverage, including out-of-pocket cost sharing such as premiums, deductibles, and co-payments. The programs include four tiers: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), Qualifying Individual (QI), and Qualifying Disabled & Working Individuals (QDWI). QMB pays Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles, and Part B co-insurance (the 20%) for individuals with income at or below 100% of the federal poverty level (FPL); income limits are approximately $1,350/month (single) or $1,824/month (married), with asset limits of $9,950 (single) or $14,910 (married) — primary residence and vehicle excluded. SLMB pays only the Medicare Part B premium for those with income between 100% and 120% of FPL; income limits are approximately $1,816/month (single) or $2,455/month (married), with the same asset limits. QI and QDWI provide additional tiers of assistance based on income and disability status. All four programs are administered through Maryland Medicaid. Eligibility workers determine which program an applicant qualifies for based on income and assets. Trained counselors through the Maryland Department of Aging's SHIP offices (19 local offices statewide) help Marylanders identify and enroll in these programs, which can save thousands of dollars a year on Medicare premiums, cost-sharing, and medications. Applicants must be Maryland residents and U.S. citizens or lawfully admitted aliens enrolled in Medicare Part A and/or Part B.

SLMB: Pays only the Part B premium for those with income between 100%–120% FPL (income limits: ~$1,816/month single, ~$2,455/month married; same asset limits). QI and QDWI provide additional assistance at higher income thresholds. Primary residence and vehicle are excluded from asset calculations. Income and asset limits are subject to annual change. Free, unbiased counseling is also available through 19 local SHIP offices statewide to help eligible Marylanders enroll in the appropriate program tier and reduce prescription drug costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Vaccines for Children (VFC) Program provides free childhood immunizations to eligible children ages 18 and younger. Enrolled physicians and healthcare providers across Maryland can receive all routinely recommended vaccines at no cost through federally-supplied vaccines, removing cost as a barrier to vaccination. Eligible children include those who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, Native American or Alaskan Native, or underinsured (health insurance does not cover immunization). Enrolled providers receive training on safe storage and handling, updates on immunization issues, and guidance on federal documentation requirements. In Montgomery County, the program is administered through Department of Health and Human Services clinics at four locations (Silver Spring, Germantown, Rockville), offering free or low-cost vaccinations on a sliding fee scale based on family size and income. A child will not be denied vaccination based on inability to pay the administration fee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Public Health Core Tobacco Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health's Center for Tobacco Prevention and Control (CTPC) provides grants and technical support to all 24 local health departments in Maryland to support comprehensive tobacco control and prevention efforts. The program includes three components: Community Initiatives (coalition building, tobacco-free education, and policy interventions); School-Based Initiatives (tobacco prevention education for K-12 students in partnership with school systems); and Tobacco Treatment and Cessation Initiatives (behavior change programs, free cessation aids, and Maryland Quitline referrals for adults and youth). Award amounts are determined by a formula based on population size and tobacco use rates per jurisdiction, as outlined in the CRF statute, with a base amount provided to each health department. The program promotes integration at the local health department level to address the combined impact of tobacco use, chronic disease, and related risk factors using a 'whole health' approach, and emphasizes health equity to address disparities related to tobacco use and chronic disease.

Technical assistance is also provided by the state health department. structured_extraction.program_name: Community Options Waiver and Community First Choice Program (Home and Community-Based Options Waiver / HCBOW)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid-funded program that provides essential home and community-based services to enable older adults and individuals with physical disabilities or functional limitations (age 18+) to live independently in their own homes or in assisted living facilities, rather than in an institutional or nursing facility setting. The federal government waives certain Medicaid requirements — such as the requirement that services be provided in a nursing facility — so the state can pay for covered services that allow eligible clients to remain in the community. The program serves individuals who require a nursing home or institutional level of care but wish to remain safely in the community. Services include personal assistance with daily living activities (bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, light chores), supports planning, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, assistive technology, home environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, consumer training, transition services, home-delivered meals, assisted living (including assistance with room and board costs for eligible assisted living residents), case management, assistive devices, behavior consultation, medical adult day services, Senior Center Plus services, medical equipment, diet and nutritional services, dietitian/nutritionist services, assistance with transitional costs, respite care, and personal care services. For those living at home, all standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice are also available. Participants must meet an institutional level of care and be financially and medically eligible for community Medicaid (monthly income not to exceed $2,199; assets not to exceed $2,000–$2,500). The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Health, with local access available through county offices including Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities, the St. Mary's County Department of Aging & Human Services (MAP Coordinator at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1057), Charles County Department of Aging and Senior Services, Prince George's County Aging and Disabilities Services Division, Howard County Office on Aging and Independence, Montgomery County DHHS Disability Services, and Baltimore County Department of Health. In Baltimore County, the waiver is not currently accepting new community applicants; a Service Registry exists for interested individuals.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP) uses federal and state funds to ensure all Maryland children have medical insurance. It provides free or low-cost full health benefits for eligible uninsured children under 19 and pregnant women of any age who meet income guidelines, delivered through HealthChoice Managed Care Organizations (MCOs). Children whose families earn too much to qualify for Medicaid but cannot afford private health insurance may qualify. Coverage is available at no cost for those at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL), or with a premium for those up to 300% FPL. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Health, Medical Care Programs Administration, with local eligibility determination and application assistance available through county health departments and local departments of social services. Enrolled individuals receive full Medicaid-equivalent benefits including dental care, doctor visits, hospital care, immunizations, lab work, mental health services, prescription medicine, substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, and vision care. The program also covers adults up to age 64 in some contexts, and related populations including parents, children 19–21, new adults, family planning recipients, aged/blind/disabled individuals, refugees, and Medicare Savings Program enrollees. Note: One MCO (Jai Medical Systems) is closed to new enrollments as of February 2026; all other MCOs remain open.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Medical Care Programs Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full health benefits provided through HealthChoice Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) for eligible children and pregnant women, and adults up to age 64 in some county programs. Covers children under 19 whose countable income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL) at no cost, or up to 300% FPL with a monthly premium. MCHP income thresholds range from 123–300% FPL depending on category. Also covers pregnant women of any age and adults up to age 64 meeting income guidelines. Benefits include dental care (free for children, pregnant women, and adults enrolled in Medicaid/MCHP), doctor visits, hospital care, immunizations, lab work, mental health services, prescription medicine (no copays for children under 21 or pregnant women), substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, and vision care. Coverage is delivered through one of Maryland's nine HealthChoice managed care organizations of the family's choosing. There are no fees or payments required for those at or below 200% FPL. Asset limits apply for certain categories (e.g., Medicare Savings Program, Employed Individuals with Disabilities): $4,000–$15,000 per person/couple depending on category.

Also covers pregnant women of any age and adults up to age 64 meeting income guidelines, as well as families, caretaker relatives, parents, children 19–21, new adults, family planning recipients, aged/blind/disabled individuals, refugees, and Medicare Savings Program enrollees. Residents can receive application assistance at county health departments and local departments of social services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health's Office of Harm Reduction (OHR), within the Behavioral Health Administration, provides grants to local organizations to implement harm reduction programs statewide. The ACCESS program — Advancing Cross-Cutting Engagement and Service Strategies for People Who Use Drugs — currently funds 50 organizations (28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments) to conduct activities aimed at reducing substance-related illness and death among people who use drugs by optimizing services and ensuring statewide access to naloxone and related harm reduction resources.

OHR currently funds 50 organizations (28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments). Applications for new funding are closed at this time. Current grantees submit monthly, quarterly, and expenditure reports via online webforms. Specific award amounts are not publicly stated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) - Nurses and Nursing Support Staff
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) provides loan repayment assistance to nurses and nursing support staff who agree to work at approved practice sites in Maryland that serve underserved populations. Eligible disciplines include Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (Nurse Practitioners, Certified Nurse-Midwives, Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists, Clinical Nurse Specialists), Registered Nurses, Licensed Practical Nurses, and nursing support staff such as Certified Medication Technicians, Certified Medicine Aides, Certified Nursing Assistants, and Geriatric Nursing Assistants. The program repays qualifying education loans (for undergraduate or graduate study leading to licensure/certification) directly to the loan holder on behalf of participants who fulfill a service obligation at an approved site.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MLRP pays qualifying education loan debt directly to the verified loan holder on behalf of the participant. Loan repayment covers loans obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses for undergraduate or graduate study leading to licensure or certification as a nurse or nursing support staff. Participants may work part-time (20–39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week) at an approved eligible practice site. Service obligations begin July 1 following the application cycle. Award amounts are not specified on the program page.
