structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Repayment Programs (MLRP) help recruit and retain health professionals in areas of Maryland experiencing health professional shortages. In exchange for working at an eligible practice site for a set service obligation, participants receive educational loan repayment assistance. Awards are based on applicant eligibility, technical scoring aligned with State and Federal priorities, and availability of funding; the application process is competitive. The MLRP includes three components: the State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP, federally funded), the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians and Physician Assistants (MLARP PPA, state-funded), and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff (MLARP NNSS, state-funded). The SLRP provides educational loan repayment funds to physicians and physician assistants who serve a 2-year obligation in a health professional shortage area (HPSA) or medically underserved area (MUA) in primary care or mental health; SLRP requires a 1:1 match with MLARP. Eligible professionals include physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants, final-year medical residents specializing in primary care, nurses (APRN, RN, LPN), and nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA). Award amounts vary by credential: Physicians (MD/DO) and Physician Assistants — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for a 2-year service obligation; Final-year medical residents — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for a 3-year obligation; APRNs — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for 2 years; RNs and LPNs — up to $50,000 full time or $25,000 part time for 2 years; Nursing support staff — up to $5,000 full time or $2,500 part time for 1 year. Total award cannot exceed $200,000 across multiple obligation periods (up to two MLRP service obligations per lifetime). Loan repayment funds are paid directly to verified education loan holders on behalf of awarded participants. Eligible practice sites must be physically located in Maryland, serve patients regardless of ability to pay, utilize sliding fee scales or discounts for low-income patients, and accept Medicare/Medicaid/CHIP. As a condition of participation, MLRP participants and their practice sites are required to complete cultural competency training, including implicit bias training. The program also requires incorporation of National CLAS Standards (culturally and linguistically appropriate services) and serves culturally and linguistically diverse communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MLRP pays qualifying education loan repayment funds directly to verified education loan holders on behalf of awarded participants. Two full payments are made over the course of the service obligation, once during the first service obligation year and once during the second service obligation year. Participants commit to a service obligation at an approved eligible practice site in Maryland. Award amounts by credential: Physicians (MD/DO) and Physician Assistants — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for a 2-year service obligation. Final-year medical residents — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for a 3-year obligation (1 year during residency + 2 years post-residency). APRNs (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) — up to $100,000 full time or $50,000 part time for 2 years. RNs and LPNs — up to $50,000 full time or $25,000 part time for 2 years. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) — up to $5,000 full time or $2,500 part time for 1 year. Full time is defined as 40+ hours per week; part time is 20–39 hours per week. At least 80% of work hours must be dedicated to direct patient care (OB/GYN physicians: at least 50% in ambulatory care). Recipients may reapply after completing the first two-year obligation; total award cannot exceed $200,000 (up to two MLRP service obligations per lifetime). Awards are competitive and based on applicant eligibility, technical scoring aligned with State and Federal priorities, and available funding. Cultural competency training resources are also provided to MLRP participants and practice sites to meet program requirements, including HHS physician training, TRAIN Maryland courses, and MDH Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities implicit bias training materials.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual application cycle runs March 1 through April 15; the 2026 cycle deadline was April 15, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.

Practice sites must have contracts with at least one Maryland Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO). National Health Service Corps-approved sites are also eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during the annual application cycle, which runs March 1 through April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST). Complete Part I online via CognitoForms (applicant information). After Part I is submitted, the employer receives a link to complete Part II (practice site confirmation). Submit Part III (site eligibility), Part IV (cultural competency requirements), and Part V (experience, impact, and retention data). All components are due by April 15 at 11:59 p.m. Two professional references are also required. Applicants must verify eligibility in three areas — discipline, participant, and practice site — and demonstrate compliance throughout the service obligation. Applicants are reviewed for eligibility, then technically scored based on discipline, specialty, geographic location, practice type, and nonprofit/for-profit status, with priority tier assignment and cascading fund distribution. Final-year medical residents follow a specific application process described in Section IV.A.5 of program materials. Awards are effective July 1 following the application cycle; award recipients are generally notified of application status by July 1 of the application year. Award recipients must complete offer acceptance documentation (promissory note, service obligation agreement, lender verification form, certification regarding lobbying, and debarment affirmation). Year 2 renewal requires submission of employment verification, impact data collection, cultural competency training documentation, and lender verification. At mid-term of each participant's service obligation, proof of cultural competency continuing education and practice site CLAS assessment must be submitted. Applicants and employers can attend informational sessions or watch recorded sessions for guidance. Cultural competency training resources and requirements are available at http://health.maryland.gov/pophealth/Pages/MLRP-Cultural-Competency.aspx. Review program guidelines and required documents at https://health.maryland.gov/pophealth/Pages/State-Loan-Repayment-Program.aspx. Contact the MLRP office at (410) 767-6123 or mdh.loanrepaymentprograms@maryland.gov for technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities (MHHD) offers internship opportunities to build the capacity of the public health workforce to advance health equity. Interns work on projects related to their subject area, such as grant management, health equity conference planning, vaccine distribution planning, grant writing training, data analysis, and data chartbook updates. The program is run in partnership with the MDH Public Health Workforce Development Internship Program. It is typically three months in duration with a minimum of 10 hours per week, and requires a hybrid work arrangement with occasional in-person visits to the office at 201 West Preston Street, Baltimore, MD 21201.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Minority Outreach and Technical Assistance (MOTA) program is a chronic disease prevention and health disparities reduction program operated by the Maryland Department of Health's Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities (MHHD). It provides competitive grant funding to community-based organizations to conduct outreach, technical assistance, education, and linkage-to-care services in racial and ethnic minority and underserved communities across Maryland. The program aims to ensure minority community participation in publicly funded state health programs and to reduce racial and ethnic health disparities. Health focus areas include asthma, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, obesity, diabetes/prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, mental health, tobacco, and infant mortality. The program uses community engagement, partnerships, outreach, and ongoing intervention strategies. Grantees selected in FY27 may be considered for a non-competitive continuation grant renewal into FY28 based on year-one performance. Grantees are monitored through narrative reports and performance measures throughout the funding period.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities (MHHD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded to organizations providing chronic disease prevention, education, outreach, and linkage-to-care services in minority and underserved communities. Awards range from a minimum of $25,000 to a maximum of $75,000 each; organizations in jurisdictions with 20,000 or fewer minorities are eligible for up to $25,000, and organizations in jurisdictions with more than 20,000 minorities are eligible for up to $75,000. Up to 18 awards anticipated. The FY27 grant period runs July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Grantees selected in FY27 may be considered for a non-competitive continuation grant renewal into FY28 based on year-one performance. In FY 2021, 18 community-based organizations in 12 jurisdictions received MOTA grants. MHHD monitors grantee activities through narrative reports and performance measures throughout the funding period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations — including non-profit community-based, faith-based, hospital-based, and grassroots groups, as well as for-profit entities, government agencies, and higher education institutions — providing chronic disease prevention, education, outreach, and linkage-to-care services in Maryland communities, particularly those serving racial and ethnic minority and underserved populations (African Americans, Pacific Islanders, Asian Americans, Hispanics/Latinos, and American Indians). Applicants must maintain an operational office within the proposed jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prevention, education, outreach, and linkage-to-care programs targeting chronic diseases and health disparities including asthma, cardiovascular disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes/prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, mental health, tobacco, and infant mortality; community engagement, partnerships, technical assistance, and ongoing intervention; ensuring minority community participation in publicly funded state health programs. Allowable budget categories include personnel (salary and fringe), consultants, travel, contractual, supplies, operating costs, and other project-related costs. Funds may not be used for clinical trials, direct service payments (except reimbursable expenses), legal services, vehicle costs, land/building improvements (except minor remodeling), property taxes, capital projects, personnel cost supplantation, or lobbying.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Dent-Care Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MDC-LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MDC-LARP provides student loan repayment assistance to licensed dentists and dental hygienists who treat Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP/Medicaid) recipients. The program aims to increase access to oral health care for Maryland's most vulnerable populations by incentivizing providers to serve Medicaid patients. Full-time dentists can receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment (up to $150,000 total); full-time dental hygienists can receive up to $10,000 per year for a two-year commitment (up to $20,000 total). Part-time dentists (20–39 hours per week with at least 80% clinical hours) can receive up to $25,000 per year for three years; part-time dental hygienists up to $5,000 per year for two years. Dentists may renew for up to two additional years after the initial year (3 years total); dental hygienists may renew for one additional year (2 years total). The number of recipients per award cycle is determined based on available funding. The program is a collaboration between the Maryland Department of Health Office of Oral Health (OOH) and the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) Office of Student Financial Assistance, which distributes offer letters and loan repayment checks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Oral Health
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual loan repayment checks disbursed through the Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Assistance. Full-time dentists: up to $50,000/year for 3 years (total up to $150,000). Full-time dental hygienists: up to $10,000/year for 2 years (total up to $20,000). Part-time dentists (20–39 hours/week with at least 80% clinical hours): up to $25,000/year for 3 years. Part-time dental hygienists: up to $5,000/year for 2 years. Dentists may renew for up to two additional years; dental hygienists for one additional year. Participating providers must treat a minimum of 30% MMAP (Medicaid) recipients as a portion of their total patient population per year, enroll in Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental program, and submit monthly reports to the Maryland Department of Health Office of Oral Health. Number of recipients per award cycle is determined based on available funding. Recommended only for applicants with higher education debt exceeding the full award amount ($150,000 for dentists; $20,000 for dental hygienists) due to competitive nature.

Applicants must have graduated from an accredited dental or dental hygiene school in Maryland, hold a valid unrestricted Maryland license, and be currently repaying student loan debt. Applicants are recommended to have higher education debt exceeding the full award amount ($150,000 for dentists, $20,000 for dental hygienists) due to the competitive nature of the award. structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) authorizes organizations to operate OADPOPs (formerly known as Syringe Services Programs or SSPs) statewide. Authorized programs provide infectious disease prevention, overdose prevention, harm reduction services, and support to people who use drugs. Services include sterile needle/syringe distribution and collection, substance use disorder counseling, HIV/HCV/STD testing, naloxone, fentanyl and xylazine test strips, wound care, overdose prevention education, reproductive health services, and referrals to treatment and recovery services. The MDH Office of Overdose Prevention & Education (OPE) reviews new applications, manages program reporting, issues guidance, and provides technical assistance to approved programs. Authorized programs must comply with MD Health-General §24-901 through 909 and COMAR 10.52.01.01-10.52.01.09. There are currently 30 authorized OADPOPs operating in 21 Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Overdose Prevention & Education (OPE)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH reviews and approves applications for organizations seeking to operate an OADPOP, granting them legal authorization to distribute sterile injection supplies and provide harm reduction services. Approved programs receive authorization to legally operate under MD Health-General §24-901 through 909 and COMAR 10.52.01.01-10.52.01.09, along with program guidance, reporting support, technical assistance, and ongoing support from the MDH Office of Overdose Prevention & Education. MDH responds in writing within 60 days of receipt of a complete application with approval or disapproval. Disapproved applicants may appeal to the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services within 30 calendar days. Approved organizations can distribute syringes, provide harm reduction services, and offer a range of health services to people who use drugs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments and community-based organizations (CBOs) — including public or private organizations representative of a community that provide educational, health, or social services — seeking authorization to operate an Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP) in Maryland.

No cost to participants for needles, syringes, or preventive supplies. Programs must submit quarterly data reports on participants served, demographics, needles/syringes distributed/collected, and referrals made.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Health Worker (CHW) Specialty Training Modules
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health's Community Health Worker (CHW) Program, housed in the Office of Population Health Improvement (OPHI), offers free specialty training modules to CHW training entities. The modules cover five health focus areas: Behavioral Health, Chronic Disease-Asthma, Infectious Disease, Maternal and Child Health, and Older Adults and Aging. Each module includes a PowerPoint presentation, Student Guide, Facilitator Guide, handouts, activities, and a knowledge assessment. Materials are available in English and Spanish, are editable and customizable, and can be used in whole or in part. Training hours earned through these modules count toward the 20 hours required to renew a CHW certificate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is a federally funded cooperative agreement authorized by H.R. 1 (Section 71401 of Public Law 119-21) with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) that empowers states to strengthen rural communities by improving healthcare access, quality, and outcomes. Maryland received $168,180,837.61 in federal funding (100% funded by CMS/HHS) in December 2025 to modernize health care across 18 state-designated rural areas, renewable over five years (Budget Period 1: December 29, 2025 – October 30, 2026; Budget Periods 2–5 run October 31 through October 30 annually through 2030). All unexpended or unobligated funds must be returned to the U.S. Treasury by October 1, 2032. The program is organized around three pillars: (1) Transform the Rural Health Workforce — expanding apprenticeships, training, and recruitment for healthcare professionals; (2) Promote Sustainable Access and Innovative Care — expanding primary care, telehealth, school-based health centers, behavioral health, and mobile health services; and (3) Empower Rural Marylanders to Eat for Health — investing in post-harvest cold storage infrastructure for agricultural producers, small grocery support, food system aggregation, and local foods purchasing strategies. Funding is distributed through subawards and competitive procurement processes (RFAs and RFPs) administered by Maryland state agency partners including the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Rural Maryland Council (RMC). Specific funding opportunities include: Apprenticeship and RAMP Allied Health Expansion ($3.5M), Workforce Pipeline and Provider Training ($15M), Primary Care Practice Creation and Expansion ($6.3M), Service Expansion/HIT Advances/Behavioral Health/Innovative Care ($73M), School-Based Health Center Capacity ($6.7M), Mobile Health Expansion ($23M), Post Harvest Cold Storage Infrastructure ($3.7M), NourishMD Expansion for Small Grocers and Mobile Markets ($1.6M), and Food Aggregation and Local Foods Purchasing ($4.7M administered by RMC as part of $6,047,464 FY2027 allocation). Budget Period 1 includes subawards totaling $163.7 million, of which $134.8 million will be available through competitive procurement. Budget Period 1 funds must be obligated by October 30, 2026 and spent by September 30, 2027. The Local Food Systems grant component uses a two-phase application process with a Letter of Intent and full application. Additional competitive bid processes are anticipated for Workforce Data Clearinghouse, Telehealth Needs Assessment, and Efficiency of Local Agency Operations. Partners and subawardees must comply with RHTP terms and conditions, CMS NOFO requirements (NOFO citation: CMS-RHT-26-001), and Maryland Notice of Award Terms and Conditions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) provides funding to Community Development Organizations to support strategic investment in local housing and businesses, aiming to create healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and improved quality of life. The program targets areas where modest, coordinated investment will have a meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact in Baltimore City and parts of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Community Areas within the BRNI boundary.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is available for eligible projects located in Sustainable Community Areas within the BRNI boundary. Projects may include down payment assistance, property acquisition and rehabilitation, energy efficiency improvements, mixed-use development, open space or public infrastructure, workforce development, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects. Assistance may take the form of grants or loans; technical assistance and information may also be provided.

To verify address eligibility, use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper or contact your Regional Project Manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reinvest Baltimore is a coordinated state, city, nonprofit, and for-profit effort to eliminate concentrations of vacant properties, revitalize neighborhoods, and improve quality of life in Baltimore City. Governor Moore's executive order established the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Council (BVRC) to leverage targeted investments and move at least 5,000 vacant properties into homeownership or other positive outcomes — such as demolition and stabilization — between Fiscal Year 2025 and Fiscal Year 2029. The initiative includes a Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Dashboard to track progress and the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI), which provides grant funding to public and nonprofit partners for acquisition, stabilization, demolition, and other pre-development activities, clearing the way for new green space, affordable housing, or mixed-use developments. Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City, with special consideration given to projects within the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geography.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Home Loan Program provides unsecured financing to Maryland homeowners to improve the energy efficiency and comfort of their homes. Eligible improvements include insulation, air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, hot water heaters, appliances, windows, doors, lighting, thermostats, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic systems (up to 50% of total loan), and health and safety costs related to energy improvements such as mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of loan). Projects must be performed by a licensed and insured Maryland contractor and must not already be purchased or completed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan at 6.99% APR. Minimum loan amount is $5,000; maximum is $30,000. Loan terms up to 10 years (flexible, less than 10 years also allowed). Financing for solar photovoltaic installation is capped at a 1:1 match to the cost of energy efficiency measures (up to 50% of total loan). Up to 25% of the cost of energy measures can be used for health and safety improvements (including mold/radon remediation) necessary for the energy work. Funds are disbursed via two-party check (or one-party for retail purchases): 30% down payment at project start, 70% upon completion. Cannot finance projects or upgrades already purchased or completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners with mortgages seeking to improve home comfort and energy efficiency. No income limits documented. Rebate and savings opportunities vary by utility service territory (BGE, PEPCO, Delmarva Power, Potomac Edison, SMECO).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including insulation, air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, hot water heating equipment, Energy Star appliances, windows, doors, lighting and controls, smart thermostats, ceiling and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, and solar photovoltaic systems (up to 50% of total loan). Health and safety costs related to energy improvements such as mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of energy measures cost) are also eligible. Non-energy projects such as kitchen/bath remodeling, roofing, or other non-energy improvements are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland homeowners statewide. Contractors must be licensed and insured in Maryland. Rebate and savings opportunities vary by utility service territory (BGE, PEPCO, Delmarva Power, Potomac Edison, SMECO coverage areas).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland homeowner with a mortgage
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio must not exceed 50%
Project must not be already purchased or completed; work and purchases are prohibited until funding is received
Current employment information (employer name, address, and contact phone number)
Work history for at least 2 years, or previous employer contact information if at current job less than 2 years
Contractor details including name, address, email, and phone number
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland
Recent mortgage statement required
Pay stubs (30 days) and income documentation required
Driver's license required
Credit report required
Solar financing capped at 50% of total loan
Mold/radon mitigation capped at 25% of total loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the online BeSMART Loan Application at https://dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/mds9vfn1awvtrf. Have employment history and contractor details ready before starting. 2. Provide required income documentation: driver's license, 30 days of pay stubs, and recent mortgage statement. Sign DocuSign consent for SSN/credit check provided by DHCD. 3. Submit contractor or retailer estimate and project specifications including scope of work and ENERGY STAR equipment specifications. 4. Sign loan documents via DocuSign once the specific project is approved. 5. Begin the project with an initial draw of 30% of funds via two-party check (or one-party check for retail purchases). 6. Confirm work completion with your contractor, submit photos, and both sign a Certificate of Completion for the final draw of the remaining 70%. Borrower repayment begins after final disbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant Program is offered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program. It provides direct microgrants of $20,000 to $50,000 to eligible small business owners located in designated Sustainable Communities that need capital for growth or expansion opportunities. The Department has offered up to $2 million total per funding round. Priority is given to home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside the home, businesses designated as Minority Business Enterprises, and businesses that support minority- and women-owned enterprises, drive innovation or technology advancements, grow new industries, leverage existing regional strengths, or leverage partnerships with school districts or other education institutions in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal block grant program that helps strengthen Maryland communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods, and improving the overall quality of life. The program provides grants to non-entitlement local governments who then carry out eligible projects benefiting low- and moderate-income persons, eliminating slum and blight, or meeting urgent community needs. Maryland administers the federal funds received from HUD through two funding categories: a competitive Community Development category and a Special Projects category for planning and economic development. Eligible activities include economic development, housing rehabilitation, public facilities, and infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are awarded to eligible non-entitlement local governments through two categories. The Community Development category is competitive and accepts applications once per year, with a maximum funding amount of $800,000 for SFY 2026. The Special Projects category for planning, economic development, and special criteria projects accepts applications at any time after written approval, also capped at $800,000 (Planning capped at $50,000). Sub-recipients (public or private entities) may receive funds through eligible local governments. Grant periods are 24 months standard; 12 months for planning grants. Over any three-year period, the state must use at least 70% of its allocation to benefit low- and moderate-income persons. Housing rehabilitation grants are capped at $40,000 per single family house.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications due by Friday, October 24th by 2:00 p.m. (SFY 2026 competitive round); Special Projects can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-entitlement counties with populations under 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns under 50,000 population. Entitlement communities (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's counties and the cities of Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury) are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible activities include housing projects (acquisition, construction, renovation of single-family and multi-family rental housing; housing rehabilitation up to $40,000 per unit), public facilities (water/sewer, streets, childcare/senior/community centers, shelters, homeless/domestic violence shelters), economic development projects, infrastructure improvements, planning studies, and demolition of blighted buildings. Projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low- and moderate-income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent community need. Excludes new construction in special flood hazard areas, 100-year floodplains, regulatory floodways, and coastal high hazard areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to non-entitlement counties under 200,000 population and non-entitlement cities and towns under 50,000 population in Maryland. Entitlement communities are not eligible to apply to the State program. Anne Arundel, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties are entitlement counties and are not eligible. Projects must generally be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (except for public services, single family housing rehabilitation, acquisition/renovation/sale of existing houses, and downpayment assistance).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a unit of general local government in a non-entitlement county (population under 200,000) or a non-entitlement city or town (population under 50,000)
Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply
Other public or private entities may participate as sub-recipients through the eligible local government
Projects must meet at least one of three national objectives: benefit low- and moderate-income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin
For Special Projects, written approval must be received before submitting an application

Applicant must meet minimum scoring threshold of 105 points (70%) for funding consideration on 150-point scale (Public Purpose 45 pts, Project Impact 25 pts, Project Management 55 pts, Local criteria remaining)
Performance threshold review must be completed by October 17 (7 days before application deadline) for Community Development category

Build America, Buy America (BABA) domestic procurement compliance required for projects funded after July 1, 2023 (waived for projects $250,000 or less total cost or housing rehab $250,000 or less per unit); BABA manufactured products expansion applies for projects funded after July 1, 2025
Section 3 requirements apply to construction projects with HUD funding over $200,000 (25% labor hours by Section 3 workers; minimum 5% by Targeted Section 3 Workers)

Competitive procurement required for all federally funded activities; full and open competition standards apply; firm fixed contracts only (time-and-material, cost-plus, and percentage contracts prohibited)
Minimum 2-week bid window; at least 2 bids required; bonds required (5% bid bond for projects >$100K; 100% payment and performance bonds for contracts >$100K)
Conflict of interest policy compliance required (2 CFR Part 200); written Conflict of Interest Policy required
MBE/WBE outreach and documentation required for each procurement
Radon testing required for CDBG grants funded after July 1, 2024
Citizen Participation Plan and Anti-Displacement Plan required (valid for five-year period)
Public hearing must be held prior to submission of application
Environmental Review Record (ERR) must be completed within 75 days of award or 2% penalty applies; Release of Funds required before activity initiation
For job creation/retention projects: 51% of jobs/employees must be LMI; jobs must be permanent, full-time; cost per job ceiling of $20,000 (max consideration at $10,000 or below)
LMI benefit verification required: area benefit (51%+ LMI population), limited clientele, or direct housing benefit; Part 5 income calculation method
Single Audit threshold: $750,000 federal funds per fiscal year
Debarment checks required for all contractors
Generators required for multi-family rental and government-owned facilities (lighting capacity minimum)
Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity compliance; non-discrimination requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Community Development projects, submit a competitive application once per year when the State notifies eligible localities of fund availability; applications are due by Friday, October 24th by 2:00 p.m. Submit one original plus three copies by physical mail or delivery to DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. A performance threshold review must be completed by October 17 (5:00 p.m.), one week before the application deadline. Awards are expected to be announced within approximately 90 days of the application submission deadline. Three-step evaluation process: threshold review, project evaluation, funding recommendations. For Special Projects and Planning, submit an application at any time throughout the year on a first-come, first-serve basis after receiving written approval. Application checklist includes: public hearing notice, statement of assurances and certifications, support letters, and original application with copies. Visit the Maryland DHCD CDBG program page at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Communities/Pages/programs/CDBG.aspx for full application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Investment Tax Credits (CITC) program supports 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of Maryland State tax credits. Nonprofits use these allocations as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses for local projects and services. Donors who give $500 or more to an approved nonprofit project earn a tax credit equal to 50% of the value of money, goods, or real property contributed — a dollar-for-dollar reduction of Maryland state income taxes owed, on top of standard deductions. Tax credits must be used against taxes owed in the year the contribution was made and cannot be applied retroactively. Awardee nonprofits must generate at least 2× the tax credit allocation amount in donations within the 24-month contract period, with a maximum award of $50,000 per applicant per cycle. The program has leveraged nearly $27 million in charitable contributions to approximately 700 projects statewide. Donors connect with approved nonprofits through the GIVE Maryland platform, and claim the credit using Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (businesses/banks) along with the Tax Credit Certificate issued by DHCD.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofits receive allocations of Maryland State tax credits equal to 50% of qualifying donations, with a maximum award of $50,000 per applicant per cycle. Donors who contribute $500 or more in money, goods, or real property to an approved nonprofit project receive a Maryland state income tax credit equal to 50% of the contribution value — a dollar-for-dollar reduction of taxes owed. Awardees must raise donations equal to double the tax credits requested within the 24-month contract period. Credits are claimed at filing using Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (businesses/banks) and must be applied against taxes owed in the year the contribution was made; they cannot be used retroactively. The donor makes a gift, the organization certifies the donation to DHCD, and DHCD sends a Tax Credit Certificate to the donor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations supporting projects in or serving residents of Priority Funding Areas; individual and business donors, financial institutions, and fiduciaries who owe Maryland state income tax and contribute $500 or more to approved nonprofit projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For nonprofits: capital and/or operating projects including education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, neighborhood and business district enhancement, arts and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. For donors: tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability at filing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Capital projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Maryland. Operating projects must serve residents of a Priority Funding Area. Priority consideration given to projects in ENOUGH-designated areas and Just Communities. Tax credits are available to Maryland state income taxpayers statewide.
requirements_list: Nonprofit applicant must be an IRS-designated 501(c)(3) organization
Must provide IRS determination letter; religious organizations with tax exemption and affiliates of umbrella organizations accepted with appropriate documentation
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Awardees must generate at least 2× the tax credit allocation amount in donations within the 24-month contract period
Donors must contribute at least $500 in money, goods, or real property
Donors must owe Maryland state income tax
Donors must obtain and complete a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
Donors wishing to contribute real property must contact the nonprofit prior to making the donation
Tax credits must be used against taxes owed in the year of contribution; cannot be applied retroactively
Business donors must conduct a trade or business in Maryland and be subject to Maryland income tax, franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax
Individual donors must be a natural person or fiduciary with personal tax liability in Maryland
Donation must be certified by the nonprofit to DHCD, which then issues a Tax Credit Certificate to the donor
Attach the Tax Credit Certificate to tax return and claim credit on Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (businesses/banks)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofits apply competitively each year through the DHCD Application Portal via an annual Fiscal Year application round. Applicants must register through the portal by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration form (registration approval can take up to 72 hours). The FY26 application round opened May 19, 2025 and closed June 19, 2025; award announcements are expected in Fall 2025. The FY2026 award agreement contract period runs January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027. Once approved, nonprofits list available tax credits through the GIVE Maryland platform. Donors connect with approved nonprofits, make a qualifying gift of $500 or more, and complete the Donor Form. The nonprofit certifies the donation to DHCD, which sends a Tax Credit Certificate to the donor for use at tax filing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Schools Rental Assistance Program (CSRAP) provides emergency financial assistance to families and students enrolled in community schools who are facing eviction, housing instability, or homelessness. Eligible households can receive help paying past-due rent and utilities, moving costs and deposits for a new rental home, and future rent or utility assistance related to current housing instability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CSRAP provides emergency financial assistance to eligible households. Assistance can cover past-due rent and utility bills (including water, late fees, and court fees related to eviction), moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home (security deposit, application fees, first month's rent, utility deposit), and future rent and/or utility payments related to current housing instability. Maximum assistance is up to 15 months per eligible household (no limit on number of applications, but total capped at 15 months). No required match for administering organizations; indirect cost rate up to 15%; administrative set-aside capped at 10% of total award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in a Maryland community school (including Judy Center program families) who rent their home and are experiencing housing instability, at risk of eviction, or experiencing homelessness. Administering organizations must be nonprofits, local government agencies, or quasi public-private organizations in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past-due rent and utility bills (including water) including late fees and court fees; moving costs and deposits for a new rental home (security deposit, application fees, first month's rent, utility deposit); future rent and/or utility assistance related to current housing instability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in eight Maryland jurisdictions: Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Must have at least one student currently enrolled in a Community School (or Judy Center program) in the jurisdiction where applying, living in the household.
The student must be enrolled in a school in one of the participating jurisdictions.
Must be renting your home or trying to rent a new home (homeowners are not eligible).
Must be experiencing housing instability such as homelessness, at risk of eviction, utility shut-off, or behind on rent or utilities.
Residency must be documented via lease, rental agreement, or proof of rent payment history.
Administering organizations must be nonprofits, local government agencies, or quasi public-private organizations in Good Standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
Nonprofit administering organizations must have active, compliant charity registration with Maryland Secretary of State.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the local participating organization in your jurisdiction. Applications may be submitted online or on paper; required documents include proof of community school enrollment, rental agreement, and invoice/proof of missed payments. Contact the organization listed for your county on the program webpage or email homelessness.dhcd@maryland.gov. Administering organizations submit monthly invoices, data reports, and transaction summaries via the grants management system.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program supports a range of direct services designed to help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency. Funds are distributed through a statewide network of seventeen designated Community Action Agencies (CAAs) in Maryland, which serve all twenty-three counties and Baltimore City. The state also administers a discretionary component (up to 5% of the federal allocation) available to CAAs, non-profits, and local government units to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization, including training and technical assistance. Services address needs in employment, education, better use of available income, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 90% of the federal CSBG allocation (93% of the CSBG award, approximately $9,786,612 per year) goes directly to Maryland's seventeen designated Community Action Agencies. Up to 5% is available as discretionary funding for CAAs, non-profits, and local government units to support programs and services addressing poverty, self-sufficiency, and community revitalization, as well as training and technical assistance. A separate T/TA budget of $210,464 per year supports coordination and capacity building among eligible entities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's seventeen designated Community Action Agencies (for the 90% allocation); Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units serving individuals and families at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines (for discretionary funding). Eligible populations include low-income families and individuals, homeless families, migrant/seasonal farmworkers, and elderly low-income individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct services to help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency; programs to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization; training and technical assistance; coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies. Eligible service areas include employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health. Also covers emergency food and nutrition services, utility assistance, eviction prevention, affordable housing, youth entrepreneurship, elder transportation, and case management. Multi-agency coordination with LIHEAP, Weatherization, TANF, Head Start, Health, Education, WIOA, SNAP, Child Welfare, and Housing offices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — all twenty-three Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Seventeen Community Action Agencies serve every jurisdiction in Maryland, including single-county entities (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Somerset, Talbot, Washington) and multi-county/regional entities (Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Dorchester/Delmarva region, Caroline/Cecil/Kent, Prince George's, Somerset/Queen Anne's/Wicomico/Worcester, Calvert/Charles/St. Mary's).
requirements_list: Applicants for the 90% allocation must be one of Maryland's seventeen formally designated Community Action Agencies

CAA boards must have at least one-third elected public officials (or designees), at least one-third representatives of low-income persons, and the remainder from business, industry, labor, religion, welfare, education, or other community interests
Discretionary applicants (CAAs, non-profits, local government units) must serve individuals and families at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines
Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines
Proposed programs must demonstrate measurable outcomes that help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency
Eligible entities must annually submit a Community Action Plan (CAP) including a community-needs assessment
Eligible entities must participate in ROMA (Results Oriented Management and Accountability) or an approved alternate performance measurement system
Drug-free workplace certification required
Tripartite board with low-income representation required; petition procedures must be in place
Debarment and environmental tobacco smoke compliance certifications required
Anti-lobbying certification required
State CSBG statute amended in 2024 to align board composition requirements with the federal CSBG Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The FY25 discretionary application round is closed. Monitor the CSBG program page for announcements about future funding rounds. Individuals seeking services should contact the Community Action Agency serving their county. The 90% formula allocation is distributed directly to the seventeen designated eligible entities; a competitive application process applies to the discretionary component. Eligible entities must annually submit a Community Action Plan (CAP) by the established state deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Low Income Energy Efficiency Program – Network Partner Participation
structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD recruits and contracts with local service providers (network partners) to deliver energy efficiency services to low-income households across Maryland. Nonprofits and local governments apply through a Request for Applications (RFA) in conjunction with the DOE Weatherization Assistance Program, while for-profit home improvement contractors apply through a Request for Proposals (RFP). Competitive rounds are held at least every three years, or more frequently, to ensure statewide coverage. The program operates on multi-year cycles (e.g., 2024–2026) and includes programs such as Whole Home Efficiency, MEEHA, Base Efficiency, and MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up). MEET is intended to extend the life of installed energy measures for participants and increase long-term energy savings via ongoing client engagement and maintenance of installed equipment; it is offered to customers who completed a project in the Whole Home Efficiency, Base Efficiency, or MEEHA program, one year after their initial project, and MEET clients can participate every three years. Active procurement opportunities are posted on the DHCD webpage and the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) system. Legislation enacted in 2023 set statewide limited-income household electric savings goals of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026. DHCD has served the limited-income population with weatherization services for four decades and has implemented the EmPOWER Limited Income Programs for twelve years; the program originated as LIEEP in 2012 and has been DHCD's comprehensive energy program for individual households since then. DHCD assigns an average of 980 income-qualified applications per month to its Network Partners on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations selected as network partners receive contracts and funding to deliver energy efficiency services to low-income households. The program operates on multi-year cycles (e.g., 2024–2026), with competitive procurement rounds held at least every three years. Eligible measures include insulation, weatherization, HVAC, heat pump water heaters, lighting, windows, doors, and smart thermostats. Nonprofits and local governments respond to an RFA; for-profit home improvement contractors respond to an RFP. Active opportunities are posted on the DHCD webpage and the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) system. Incentive amounts vary by utility territory (BGE, Delmarva, PE, Pepco, SMECO, WGL). Health & Safety (H&S) measures are capped at $1,000 per job (EmPOWER) or 20% average (MEAP-Wx); MEAP-C H&S can reach 50% of HVAC system replacement cost when H&S measures enable the replacement. Incidental repairs are capped at 20% of total job cost (EmPOWER); up to 30% for Whole Home Efficiency. Job cost cap for Whole Home Efficiency is $16,000 per job total. Measure pricing is subject to approved price lists with not-to-exceed values and will be updated at the conclusion of the next procurement. MEET clients can participate every three years. Landlord contribution of 15% is required if appliances/systems are not owned by the tenant. Subgrantees may also receive training and technical assistance (T&TA) reimbursements and program operations funding. DHCD assigns an average of 980 income-qualified applications per month to its Network Partners on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Posted when an active RFP or RFA is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors interested in delivering low-income energy efficiency services statewide as Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs), Statewide Weatherization Contractors (SWCs), or MEEHA Qualified Energy Auditors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of energy efficiency services to low-income households across Maryland as a contracted network partner. Mandatory measures across all building types include: Health & Safety (per DOE plan), LED lighting replacement, air sealing, duct sealing & insulation, attic/ceiling insulation, wall insulation (mandatory for >10% uninsulated exterior wall area in multifamily), and floor insulation. Optional measures (priority 9–12 depending on building type) include smart thermostats and water efficiency (faucet aerators, showerheads, tank/pipe insulation). Additional eligible measures include weatherization, HVAC, heat pump water heaters, windows, doors. Measures fall into three categories: Energy Conservation Measures (ECM), Health & Safety measures, and Incidental Repairs. DOE and MEAP-Wx require a Savings-to-Investment Ratio (SIR) of at least 1.0 (air sealing excepted); MEAP-C has no SIR requirement. Natural gas domestic hot water replacements and gas-fired heating system replacements are allowable only in BGE or WGL territory. No oil or propane system replacements are permitted. Funding sources include DOE WAP, BIL, MEAP, MEAP-C, EmPOWER, and Base Efficiency programs. Allowable costs also include training and technical assistance (T&TA), administrative/program operations expenses subject to procurement thresholds ($3,000 micropurchase, $150,000 simplified acquisition), transportation, vehicle maintenance, liability insurance, and financial audit costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, covering all 23 counties and Baltimore City. Participants must have an active utility account with BGE, Delmarva, PE, Pepco, SMECO, or WGL. Homes without qualifying utility accounts may be transferred to the DOE Weatherization Assistance Program. Program serves both single-family and multifamily buildings, including mobile/manufactured homes. Incentive allocations are made per utility territory. Outreach targets underserved areas throughout the state. Washington Gas (WGL) account verification is specifically required for clients in Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties. Natural gas system replacements (furnaces, boilers, DHW) are allowable only in BGE or WGL territory. No oil or propane system replacements are permitted. Applicants may also qualify via the MDEE J Map if their address falls within an area with a Final EJ Score Percentile at or above 90 (covering approximately 444,478 people / ~169,648 geographically eligible households). Geographic coverage depends on Network Partner availability across utility service territories. Leads are assigned by territory and jurisdiction, with consideration for the Network Partner's contract rank, availability of funds, capacity, performance, and proximity to the client's home. Attic insulation in western Allegany and Garrett County is to R-60 (vs. R-49 elsewhere in Maryland). Gas duct sealing/insulation is allowed only in BGE or WGL territory; smart thermostats in BGE, Pepco, and Delmarva territories must use a model compatible with the thermostat optimization program. Historic property review is mandatory if a property is more than 45 years old or listed in the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties and the work scope includes specified measures.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) website to be notified of open procurements. Monitor the DHCD webpage for active RFPs or RFAs and submit a response when one is posted. Contact Seth Fawcett to be added to the vendor notification email list. structured_extraction.program_description: The Homelessness Solutions Program (HSP) helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing technical support and funding to lead agencies for Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs).
