DHCD provides federal and state funding to local CoCs, consolidating funds previously managed through the Emergency Solutions Grant, Rental Allowance Program, Emergency and Transitional Housing and Services, Homeless Women's Crisis Shelter Homes, Service-Linked Housing, and the Housing Navigator and Aftercare Program. DHCD distributes over $15 million in annual state funding to Maryland's 16 CoCs and LHCs for a range of homelessness services, including homeless prevention, emergency shelter, street outreach, rapid re-housing, permanent supportive housing case management, and HMIS. The program emphasizes Housing First principles, low-barrier access, and equitable service delivery.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides grants, rental assistance, and technical support to lead agencies for Maryland's 16 Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. Funds support eight eligible activities: (1) Homeless Prevention/Shelter Diversion, (2) Emergency Shelter, (3) Street Outreach, (4) Rapid Re-Housing, (5) Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) Case Management, (6) Homeless Management Information System (HMIS), (7) Special Events (Homeless Resource Day, Point-in-Time support), and (8) Administration. Eligible costs include rental assistance (short/medium-term, arrears), security deposits, application fees, utility deposits/payments, moving costs, case management, legal services, credit repair, housing search and placement, and landlord incentives. All CoCs must provide matching funds of at least 25% of the total grant (waived for ESG-CV). Administrative costs are capped at 10%. Rental assistance is limited to up to 24 months per 3-year period for RRH. The program distributes over $15 million in annual state funding (SFY2026 total anticipated funding: $15,200,000 comprising $14M state HSP + $1.2M federal ESG). Maryland DHCD processes payments within 30 days. All records must be retained for 5 years after grant closeout. The SFY2026 grant performance period runs July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lead agencies for Maryland's 16 Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs), including nonprofit providers and local/state governments, applying on behalf of homeless services providers in their communities. Ultimate beneficiaries include individuals and households experiencing homelessness or at imminent risk, including unaccompanied youth under 25, veterans, survivors of domestic violence/dating violence/sexual assault/stalking, individuals with disabilities, and people living with HIV/AIDS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street Outreach, Emergency Shelter, Rapid Re-Housing, Homeless Prevention/Shelter Diversion, PSH Case Management, HMIS, Special Events (Homeless Resource Days, Point-in-Time Counts), rental assistance (short/medium-term and arrears), security deposits, application fees, utility deposits and payments, moving costs, furniture (State funds only), discretionary assistance (State funds only), case management, legal services, credit repair, landlord-tenant mediation, housing search and placement, landlord incentives (signing bonuses up to 2 months rent, security deposits up to 3 months rent), hazard pay for direct care staff, volunteer incentives, lived experience stipends, coordinated entry systems, pilot interventions (e.g., shelter-to-PSH conversion, workforce development, medical respite, direct cash transfer), and Administrative Costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 23 counties of Maryland and the City of Baltimore, administered through the 16 Continuums of Care regions. Eligible local governments include all counties of the State, the City of Baltimore, and municipal corporations subject to Maryland Constitution Article XI-E. The CoC must ensure the system is accessible throughout its geographic area, with multiple access points permitted for larger areas and specialized access points for specific populations such as youth or victims of domestic violence.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care (CoC) OR a DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition (LHC).
Applications must be submitted on behalf of homeless services providers in the community; lead agencies may subgrant to government agencies or nonprofit organizations.
Applications from independent parties or non-affiliated organizations will not be accepted.
Shelter providers serving unaccompanied minors must register with DHCD (effective July 1, 2020).
Must be part of a local Continuum of Care.
Must enroll in local HMIS or a comparable database approved by DHCD (victim services providers may use an approved comparable database instead).
Must comply with HUD participation, data collection, and reporting standards.
Current/previously funded grantees must be in full HMIS compliance at time of application; new subgrantees must be in full HMIS compliance at time of grant agreement signature.
Must participate in Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW); data must meet all quality standards or funding may be reduced.
Victim services providers must document confidentiality and safety procedures.
Must comply with Housing First principles and low-barrier shelter practices.
Must comply with VAWA protections, reasonable accommodations for disabilities, affirmative outreach, and fair housing requirements (Title VIII, ADA, Equal Access Rule, Gender Identity Rule).
Criminal background check policies for staff working with minors required (subject to CoC Lead Agency approval).
Family non-separation required; no mandatory faith-based activities.
Must develop written confidentiality procedures per HUD regulations; staff confidentiality statements and secure record storage required.
Written grievance procedures for termination/denial required; termination notice must include 14-day minimum window to request informal hearing; hearing decision must be issued within 30 days.

Income eligibility: Street Outreach and Emergency Shelter have no income limits; Rapid Re-Housing requires ≤30% AMI at intake with redetermination at 12 months and annually; Homelessness Prevention (State HSP) requires ≤30% AMI with redetermination every 3 months; Homelessness Prevention (ESG-CV) requires ≤50% AMI with redetermination every 3 months.
Rental unit must meet Fair Market Rent limits and rent reasonableness standards (ESG-CV waives FMR but not rent reasonableness).
Income documentation must be dated within 30 days or within 12 months if reflecting current benefits.
All CoCs must provide matching funds of at least 25% of the total grant (waived for ESG-CV).
Administrative costs capped at 10% of total grant.
All records pertaining to each fiscal year of funding must be retained for 5 years after the closeout of the grant.
Monthly invoicing required within 15th–30th window; W9 collection required.
Procurement standards must be followed per federal and state requirements.
Coordinated Entry participation required across all programs.
Equity analysis required (racial, gender, age, disability, ethnicity disparities).
Lived experience incorporation in governance required; CoCs must have at least one person with lived experience on board.
Subgrantee monitoring and compliance documentation required.
Stella Performance Module (Stella P) report submission required (except Balance of State).
2024 System Performance Measures report submission required (except Balance of State).
Housing First approach implementation mandatory for all applicants.

Habitability standards required for rental units: structural soundness, access, fire safety, sanitary facilities, thermal environment, lead-based paint compliance; annual on-site inspections required.
Lease requirements and rental assistance agreement with owner required; documentation of comparable rents required.
Duplication-of-benefits screening required.
Limited English Proficiency services required.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the Application Guidance carefully before downloading and completing the forms. 2. Attend or review training materials (training session held March 3, 2025 for SFY2026 cycle). 3. Submit Organization Profile by the stated deadline (March 21, 2025 for SFY2026). 4. Submit the full application narrative and budget online via the Project Portal at projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us by the application deadline (April 25, 2025 for SFY2026). 5. Review the application training slides for guidance. 6. Contact your project manager with any questions. For general inquiries, contact the local Continuum of Care or visit the program page for details. Award notifications are issued approximately 5–6 weeks after the deadline (June 2, 2025 for SFY2026), with grant periods beginning July 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Grant is a limited program that helps eligible Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Created under Section 3206 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, it provides grants to fund critical home repairs to primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. The program processes applications on a first-come, first-served basis and is available statewide across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Standard grant of up to $10,000 for critical home repairs. Up to $15,000 may be granted for extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Assistance is one-time per household (non-repayable, no lien recorded). Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications Closed: April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to COVID-19 who need critical home repairs in their primary residence to prevent displacement; applicants must have experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020, with income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI), and must reside in and be named on the deed of their primary residence. Renters and tenants are ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs including non-functioning heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, roof repair/replacement, mold/mildew remediation, lead paint/asbestos removal, and structural and maintenance issues that could prevent homeowner displacement. Remodeling is ineligible; no reimbursement for prior payments or deposits. Maximum $10,000 per application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland homeowner residing in their primary residence; program is available statewide across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Income limits are set by County Area Median Income (AMI) and vary by county.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020 (includes hardships that began before January 21, 2020 but continued after that date)
Income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI)
Must be a Maryland homeowner and owner-occupant
Must reside in the primary residence
Must be named on the deed of trust
Provide a work proposal for the critical repair from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor, with photos or drawings
Work proposal must be dated within the last 60 days
Contractor bid must not exceed $10,000 total
Contractor must provide MHIC/trade license and certificate of insurance (minimum $1M coverage)
Critical repair must present risk of involuntary displacement if unaddressed
Assistance is limited to one-time per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD recommends starting with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify needed improvements and enroll in appropriate programs. To apply, submit a completed application with supporting documentation (income verification, home ownership proof, contractor bids with required licenses/insurance) via email or mail. Application must include one work proposal estimate dated within the last 60 days from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with photos. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible families or individuals to help pay for housing. The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) funds local public housing agencies — typically a county or municipal authority — to administer the program. In Maryland, the state Department of Housing and Community Development directly administers the program for several Eastern Shore counties and the City of Elkton.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental vouchers (subsidies) that eligible families or individuals can use toward housing payments. The voucher covers the gap between what the household can afford and the actual rent. Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) are made directly to landlords/owners on behalf of eligible families for units leased and occupied by eligible families, with payment calculations based on Payment Standard (90–110% of HUD Fair Market Rent) and rent reasonableness determinations. Vacancy payments to owners are available up to a maximum of two full months of monthly rent to owner. Funds support existing, newly constructed, or rehabilitated Project-Based Voucher (PBV) housing. Special-purpose vouchers are available for specific populations including Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Mainstream, and Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2) categories. Local public housing agencies manage eligibility, applications, waitlists, and verification. The Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program offers escrow accounts and supportive services to help participants achieve economic self-sufficiency. A homeownership option is also available for eligible long-term voucher participants, covering down payment, principal and interest on initial mortgage, mortgage insurance premium, real estate taxes, homeowner's insurance, and maintenance expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM (for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton waitlist openings)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families and individuals seeking rental assistance. Eligible populations include: very low-income families (at or below 50% of Area Median Income), extremely low-income households (at or below 30% AMI), and low-income households (below 80% AMI). Special priority is given to elderly families (age 62+), near-elderly persons, persons with disabilities, families with children, single persons, displaced persons, and racial/ethnic groups with disproportionate housing needs. Mixed families (at least one member with eligible citizenship/immigration status) are also eligible. Domestic violence survivors and crime victims are protected under VAWA provisions. Special-purpose vouchers target veterans (VASH), families needing family unification (FUP), non-elderly disabled persons (NED2), and mainstream populations. Families may access a homeownership option after completing at least 2 years of continuous voucher assistance. Elderly and disabled families receive exemptions from certain employment and income verification requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental payments for housing through Section 8 tenant-based assistance vouchers for private-market rental units, including Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) to owners on behalf of eligible families for units leased and occupied by eligible families, and utility allowances for tenant-paid utilities. Vacancy payments to owners of up to two full months of monthly rent are also supported. Funds may also support: existing, newly constructed, or rehabilitated project-based vouchers (PBV) attached to specific properties; special-purpose vouchers (VASH for veterans, FUP for family unification, Mainstream, Non-Elderly Disabled); Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program escrow accounts and supportive services including employment counseling and asset development; homeownership assistance (down payment, mortgage principal and interest, mortgage insurance premium, real estate taxes, homeowner's insurance, and maintenance expenses for eligible long-term participants); housing search services via MDhousingsearch.org; mobility counseling and fair housing outreach; and housing inspections and quality assurance. Mixed-finance development partnerships and Section 8 replacement housing resources are also supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local public housing agencies. DHCD directly administers the program through regional offices including an Eastern Shore Regional Office (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties), Allegany County, Frederick County, and Garrett County offices, as well as the City of Elkton. All other jurisdictions have their own local programs. Waiting list status varies by jurisdiction: some county lists are currently open (e.g., City of Cumberland, Allegany County, Garrett County) while others have been closed for extended periods (e.g., Frederick County for 10+ years). Several jurisdictions plan to reopen waiting lists during FY2027 (beginning July 1, 2026), including Caroline, Dorchester, Elkton, Kent, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Portability to other jurisdictions is permitted if the receiving jurisdiction operates a compatible program.
requirements_list: Eligibility criteria are set by the local public housing agency for each jurisdiction
Applicants must apply through the public housing agency serving their area
Waitlist placement is determined by lottery; submitting an application does not guarantee a waitlist spot

Income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI); priority is given to extremely low-income households at or below 30% AMI; standard eligibility threshold is very low-income (at or below 50% AMI); minimum 75% of new admissions must be extremely low-income
Head of household or spouse must be at least 18 years old or an emancipated minor
At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; eligible immigrants must be verified via INS/SAVE system; non-citizen students on Student Visas are ineligible
All household members must have valid Social Security Numbers (with exception for undocumented non-applicants)
Eligible populations include elderly families (62+), near-elderly persons, families with disabilities, and families with children
Applicants with disabilities may request reasonable accommodations to complete the application or briefing process
Specific categories of families may be admitted to waiting lists even when lists are generally closed (e.g., emergency or priority categories)
Voucher units must pass HQS (Housing Quality Standards) inspection before lease commencement
No family member may be engaged in drug-related or violent criminal activity within the last 3 years
No family member may be registered in a state or federal sex offender registry
No prior termination from Section 8 assistance within the past 5 years
No eviction from federally assisted housing within the past 5 years
Family share of rent must not exceed 40% of monthly adjusted income when gross rent exceeds Payment Standard
Applicant cannot be concurrently receiving other federal, state, or local housing subsidies
Family must obtain DHCD approval before new household members occupy unit (except births, adoptions, court-awarded custody)

For homeownership option: participants must have completed initial lease term and second annual recertification (or 2+ years continuous assistance); minimum annual income equals federal minimum hourly wage times 2,000 hours; disabled and elderly families may receive waivers from employment requirements
Families with outstanding debt to DHCD or another housing agency are ineligible for the homeownership option

PBV site selection and environmental review requirements must be satisfied for project-based voucher housing; de-concentration of poverty, civil rights compliance, and HQS site/neighborhood standards required
Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) protections apply; certification required
Fair Housing compliance (Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing) required
Section 504 accessibility compliance required for applicable housing
Lead certification and property registration required prior to lease signing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local public housing agency for your jurisdiction to apply. For DHCD-administered areas (Eastern Shore counties and City of Elkton), submit a preliminary application online at waitlistcheck.com/MD1645 or check waitlist status at waitlistcheck.com. In-person assistance is available for those who need support. Waiting list status varies by county — several county lists are currently closed but multiple jurisdictions plan to reopen during FY2027 (starting July 1, 2026), including Caroline, Dorchester, Elkton, Kent, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. The City of Cumberland, Allegany County, and Garrett County waiting lists are currently open. Applications are accepted as a written pre-application when a specific waiting list is open; a full application is completed at an eligibility appointment. All adult members are required to attend; applicants have 14 calendar days to supply requested documentation. Verification of disability and citizenship/immigration status is required. Once eligibility is determined, applicants attend a mandatory initial briefing (group or individual) before voucher issuance. Vouchers are valid for 60 days from issuance, with one 30-day extension available; additional extensions possible with justification. Households with disabilities may request a 30-day extension as a reasonable accommodation. After receiving a voucher, families search for a qualifying unit, which must pass an HQS inspection before the lease begins. Housing search assistance is available at MDhousingsearch.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Innovation Pilot Program (HIPP) provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers through the Housing Innovation Fund. Funds can also be used for projects where a county, in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer, purchases existing privately owned housing. The program aims to increase the volume of housing production and reward counties pursuing innovative solutions to housing scarcity. $5 million total is available for FY 2026, and DHCD may only select one project per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to eligible applicants for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing. Short-term loans are 3–5 years at approximately 3% interest; longer-term loans are 7–10 years at approximately 5.5% interest. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing where at least 20% of units are set aside for households at or below 50% of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households at or below 60% of area median income. $5 million total is available for FY 2026. DHCD may only select one project per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities, county governments partnering with housing developers, and counties partnering with local housing authorities or housing developers to purchase existing privately owned housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing (including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities), or acquisition of existing privately owned housing to create public housing opportunities. Rehabilitation includes both major renovation and no major renovation scenarios. Energy efficiency improvements (minimum 15% savings required) apply where applicable. All new construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA); rehabilitation projects are not subject to this geographic restriction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Proposed projects must be in Maryland. All new construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA); rehabilitation projects are not subject to this requirement. DHCD may only select one project per jurisdiction. Scoring bonuses (not eligibility requirements) are awarded for projects within 3/4 mile of a rail station, within ENOUGH Act approved award locations, Just Communities designations, and Communities of Opportunity.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority, a county government partnering with a housing developer, or a county in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
All new construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Projects must have projected closing dates within two (2) years of the award date to receive funding
Site control must be maintained for at least 180 days from the application deadline date
Applicant must submit a Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package with required forms (Form 202, Form 203, Form 209) and application fee of $2,500
Applicant must demonstrate organizational experience and track record
Projects must comply with State of Maryland Fair Housing requirements
Applicant must submit debarment affidavits and previous project performance documentation

Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (AFHMP) using HUD Form 935.2A required, including prohibitions on income requirements for voucher holders, elimination of local residency preferences, accessibility provisions, flexible application hours, credit flexibility for special needs populations, coordination with housing authorities/voucher programs, annual certification of voucher acceptance, and targeted marketing to underrepresented applicants; AFHMP must be reviewed and updated at minimum every 5 years

Development team (developer, sponsor/owner, general contractor, architect, management agent) must demonstrate prior experience with similar project type, scale, and complexity; scattered-site experience required if applicable
All development team members and ownership interests (except limited partners/non-managing members) must provide debarment affidavits certifying no HUD debarment, suspension, or voluntary exclusion
General Contractor must provide AIA Document A305 and supplemental certification
Architect must provide AIA Document B305; Design Architect must provide direct construction administration
Management Agent must provide Form 209 and minimum 3 references
Building accessibility consultant engagement required
RESNET Certified HERS Rater or BPI Certified Professional certification required
Comprehensive energy audit within 90 days of reservation letter issuance; minimum 15% energy savings over pre-rehabilitation condition required
Affordability maintenance period of 15, 30, 40, or 99 years required
3 prior fiscal years and interim financial statements (GAAP-audited or reviewed/compiled by CPA) required
Credit references from at least 3 previous lenders required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package (due May 18, 2026 by 12 PM) along with required forms (Form 202 Instructions, Multifamily Form 203, Form 209) and a $2,500 application fee. A pre-application meeting request may be submitted. Applications are evaluated using a scoring rubric that includes organizational experience and track record (1–4 points), location factors (transit proximity, ENOUGH Act census tracts, Just Communities designation, Community of Opportunity), and project readiness. Waiver request forms are also available if needed. An information session was held on March 11, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state tax credit administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) for residents who make accessibility renovations to their own home, a family member's home, or a rental property. Applicants can receive up to 50% of qualifying renovation costs back, up to a maximum of $5,000 per applicant. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in total credits per year; if demand exceeds this cap, individual credits may be reduced proportionally. Applicants submit an online or paper application with supporting documentation (receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos) by June 1. DHCD reviews submissions by August 31 and notifies approved applicants with a tax credit certificate. Approved applicants then file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD certification attached.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% of qualifying accessibility renovation costs, with a maximum credit of $5,000 per applicant. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in total credits per year; if demand exceeds this cap, individual credits may be reduced proportionally. Applicants must submit receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos. If approved, they receive a tax credit certificate from DHCD and must file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X) with the certification attached to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed accessibility renovations to their own home, a family member's home, or a rental property during the previous tax year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset the cost of home accessibility renovations such as no-step entrances, grab bars, widened doorways, chairlifts, roll-in showers, accessible parking, and other features that improve mobility and access within a home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident filing Maryland taxes for the year the renovations were completed. The renovated home must be located in Maryland. Available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must file Maryland taxes for the same calendar year the renovations were completed
Accessibility/visitability renovations must have been completed in the applicable tax year
Applicant must have paid for the renovations
Must have proof of payment (receipts, invoices) and before-and-after photos of the accessibility renovations
Must provide permits as applicable
Certification that accessibility features were paid by applicant and completed in applicable tax year
No duplicate funding from other sources for the same renovation costs
Must submit a completed application to DHCD by June 1st of the current calendar year
Eligibility requirements detailed on the Independent Living Tax Credit main page
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the accessibility renovations and file your Maryland taxes for that tax year. 2. Submit the completed application and supporting documentation (receipts, invoices, before-and-after photos, permits) to DHCD by June 1st of the current calendar year — either online via dhcd.wufoo.com or by downloading the paper application and submitting by email or mail. 3. DHCD reviews applications and notifies approved applicants by August 31st. 4. If approved, file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certification attached.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners and rental property owners to install or repair indoor plumbing in residential properties. Covered improvements include wells, septic systems, piping, plumbing fixtures, connections to public water or sewer systems, and replacement of lead pipes inside the home.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Deferred loans are available for health, safety, or accessibility improvements, including replacement of lead pipes inside the home. Deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for households with incomes below 30% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties with income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, including homeowners who need to replace lead pipes or make indoor plumbing improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic systems, connections to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment (including handicapped fixtures), additions and modifications to provide toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative septic and water systems, and replacement of lead pipes inside the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Loans are processed by local governments and administered through county housing offices, nonprofits, and local banks. Income limits vary by region, with higher thresholds for the DC PMSA region (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) compared to the rest of the state.
requirements_list: Owner-occupants must have income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Rental property residents must also be income eligible at or below 80% of median income
Single-family homes must be owner-occupied with inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Properties must be structurally sound
Must be an individual with limited income.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants contact their local housing office (listed on the DHCD website by county) or DHCD Special Loan Programs directly at 301-429-7409 or 877-218-8101. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed through DHCD's network of local administering agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Indoor Plumbing Program (IPP) is a loan program administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners and rental property owners to install or repair indoor plumbing in residential properties. In Frederick County, the program is locally administered by Frederick County Housing. Eligible properties include single-family owner-occupied homes and rental properties with one to twenty units. Covered improvements include wells, septic systems, piping, plumbing fixtures, connections to public water or sewer systems, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative septic and water systems, and replacement of lead pipes inside the home. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay, and deferred loans are available for qualifying low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay. Interest rate tiers are tied to AMI thresholds (e.g., 4.5%–6.0% and 0%–4.5% depending on income at 80%, 60%, 50%, or 30% of AMI). Maximum loan term is 30 years (up to 20 years in Frederick County). Loan amounts up to 95% of the property's value (accounting for any superior mortgage). Deferred loans are available for health, safety, or accessibility improvements. Deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for households with incomes below 30% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. In Frederick County, deferred payments are available only to owner-occupants at or below 50% of the applicable MSA median income — not available to landlords. Eligible uses include replacement of lead pipes and all indoor plumbing repairs and improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties (one to twenty units) with income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, as well as homeowners needing to replace lead pipes or make indoor plumbing improvements. In rental properties, all tenants must have income at or below 80% of the applicable MSA median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic systems, connections to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment (including handicapped-accessible fixtures), additions and modifications to provide toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative and innovative septic and water systems, connection fees and assessments, and replacement of lead pipes inside the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Loans are processed by local governments and administered through county housing offices, nonprofits, and local banks. In Frederick County, the program is administered by Frederick County Housing. Income limits are based on the statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income depending on property location, with higher thresholds for the DC PMSA region (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) compared to the rest of the state. Income limit tables are effective 7/1/2025.
requirements_list: Owner-occupants must have income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income

structured_extraction.program_description: The Just Communities Designation identifies 419 Maryland communities historically affected by exclusionary and discriminatory policies such as redlining and intentional disinvestment. Authorized by HB 241 and SB 308 passed in the 2024 legislative session, the designation targets census tracts with a Just Community Score of 13.5 or higher based on equity indicators including redlining history, homeownership rates, property value trends, vacancy rates, lead paint exposure, proximity to Superfund sites, asthma rates, and incarceration rates. Applicants for eligible Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) funding programs who are located in a designated Just Community receive prioritized consideration for state investment. The designation itself lasts five years and is not a standalone funding program but a priority-access designation that elevates applications from eligible communities across a range of existing DHCD grant, loan, and tax credit programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants located within one of 419 designated Just Communities receive prioritized consideration when applying for eligible DHCD funding programs, including energy efficiency grants, home repair loans, business loans, neighborhood revitalization grants, and tax credits. The designation does not provide direct funding itself but improves access to existing DHCD assistance programs. Each designation lasts five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, nonprofits, and other entities located within one of 419 designated Just Communities in Maryland that are applying for eligible DHCD funding programs. The designation is intended to serve marginalized, underserved, overburdened, socioeconomically marginalized and minoritized communities historically impacted by redlining, urban renewal, highway projects, high imprisonment rates, and unequal environmental and health hazard exposure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Priority access to DHCD funding programs covering energy efficiency, home repair, business development, neighborhood revitalization, housing counseling, and related community investment activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within the 419 census tracts across Maryland designated as Just Communities (score ≥ 13.5) based on indicators such as redlining history, homeownership rates, property value trends, vacancy rates, lead paint exposure, proximity to Superfund sites, asthma rates, and incarceration rates. Designation is limited to areas within Priority Funding Areas (MD MDP 2019 definition).
requirements_list: Applicant or project must be located within a designated Just Community (census tract with Just Community Score ≥ 13.5)
Must be applying for an eligible DHCD funding program
Designation is based on geographic location as determined by the Just Communities Geographic Viewer
Just Communities are identified via state-driven geospatial criteria analysis; areas are designated by the Governor based on DHCD Secretary recommendation
Designation lasts five years

Eligible communities must demonstrate past or current economic and housing need, including criteria such as legal racial segregation (redlining, urban renewal, highway projects), high state imprisonment rates, and unequal environmental/health hazard exposure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designation is administrative — areas are identified via geospatial criteria analysis and designated by the Governor based on DHCD Secretary recommendation. Individuals and organizations do not apply to become a Just Community. When applying for eligible DHCD funding programs, applicants are asked whether they are located in a designated Just Community. If yes, their application is prioritized for state investment. Use the Just Communities Geographic Viewer interactive map to check if a location qualifies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that helps Maryland homeowners and landlords reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards in residential and childcare properties. Financial assistance is provided as a grant or loan depending on the applicant's ability to repay and location. Grants are available in certain target areas (units must be in a targeted census tract); elsewhere the income limit is 80% of Area Median Income (AMI), with no income limits in targeted areas. The program also includes a HUD-funded component: a $4 million award from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes providing grants of up to $25,000 per eligible property owner for lead abatement services statewide (except Baltimore City), with funding available until April 1, 2029. Eligible property types include owner-occupied single-family homes, residential rental properties (including multi-family), and licensed residential childcare facilities. Frederick County administers the program locally, with the maximum loan term of 20 years and units required to be in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided as a grant or loan based on the applicant's ability to repay and location. Grants are available up to $25,000 per unit ($100,000 annual maximum for sponsors) in certain targeted census tracts with no income limits; a 20% match is required for for-profit sponsors and 10% for nonprofits/owner-occupants above 80% median income. Amortizing loans are available at 0%–7% interest with a 20-year term up to $25,000 per unit. Deferred loans at 0% interest are also available with a 20-year term up to $25,000 per unit; forgiveness is possible if no equity is available after resale, transfer, or 20 years. Income limits vary by tier (30%, 50%, 60%, 80% of AMI), with separate thresholds for the Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) and the rest of the state. Additionally, a HUD-funded grant component provides up to $25,000 per eligible property owner for lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor (available statewide except Baltimore City, with funding through April 1, 2029). Eligible costs include door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, and innovative lead hazard reduction methods approved by the department.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: HUD-funded grant component: funding available until April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners (owner-occupants), residential rental property owners (single-family and multi-family), licensed residential childcare facilities, for-profit and non-profit sponsors, and licensed day care centers seeking to reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards. The HUD-funded grant component is not available in the City of Baltimore. Frederick County residents may also apply through Frederick County Housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, innovative lead hazard reduction methods approved by the department, and lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Acquisition costs are not financeable with program funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The HUD-funded grant component is available in all counties except Baltimore City. Units must be in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant, unless the property utilizes innovative lead hazard reduction treatment. Income limits are tiered separately for the Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) and the rest of the state.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident if an owner-occupant and must own and occupy the dwelling as a principal residence.
Rental properties must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program (rental properties built prior to 1950 must be registered with MDE).
Property must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity.
Property must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity.
Units must be located in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant (alternative: properties utilizing innovative lead hazard reduction treatment may also qualify).
Income limit of 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) applies outside targeted areas; no income limits in targeted areas. Income tiers of 30%, 50%, 60%, and 80% AMI determine interest rates and terms.
Licensed residential childcare facilities and licensed day care centers may also be eligible.
For-profit sponsors must provide a 20% match; nonprofits and owner-occupants above 80% median income must provide a 10% match.
Clearance testing is required upon completion of work.
Underwriting affordability assessment and debt-to-value limits apply.
For the HUD-funded grant component: work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor.
For the HUD-funded grant component: property must not be located in the City of Baltimore.
Maximum loan term is 20 years.

Sponsor applicants must submit organizational documents including Articles of Incorporation, By-Laws, Partnership Agreement, and verification of 501(c)(3) status (if applicable), along with deed, mortgages, insurance, financials, zoning evidence, lead testing results, contractor proposal, and MDE registration proof.

Income limits are tiered by household size and AMI percentage (80%, 60%, 50%, 30%) with separate thresholds for Washington DC PMSA counties (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's) and the rest of the state.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Special Loan Programs office at DHCD (toll-free: 877-218-8101, direct: 301-429-7409, email: DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov, address: 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706) or a local Special Loan Program partner (such as Frederick County Housing) for program and application information. Submit a completed Application Form (for owner-occupants) or Sponsor Application Form (for sponsors/landlords) along with a 17-item checklist of supporting documents. Forms are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program, created by the Tax Reform Act of 1986, encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. States receive an annual tax credit allocation based on population. Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) awards tax credits competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible rental housing projects, guided by the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for credits outside the competitive process. The tax credit equals the applicable IRS-determined percentage of the qualified basis of each qualifying low-income rental building, and is claimed on the federal income tax return by project sponsors or their investor partners. Ten percent of Maryland's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Projects must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal tax credits awarded annually to eligible rental housing project sponsors. The tax credit equals the applicable IRS-determined percentage of the qualified basis of each qualifying low-income rental building. Credits are claimed on the federal income tax return by project sponsors or their investor partners. Ten percent of Maryland's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for credits outside the competitive process. Projects must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit sponsors, county governments, and municipalities involved in low-income rental housing projects in Maryland; also LIHTC project owners and management agents with projects in the Extended Use Period (post-Year 15)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or rehabilitation of residential rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Buildings must be placed in service within two years of the allocation year. At least 20% of units must serve households at or below 50% of area median income, or at least 40% of units must serve households at or below 60% of area median income. Buildings must maintain compliance with tenant income limits, maximum rent levels, and low-income occupancy requirements for a minimum of 40 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Income and rent limits vary by county/HMFA: Baltimore-Towson HMFA (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Harford, Howard, Queen Anne's Counties); Cumberland MSA (Allegany County); Hagerstown HMFA (Washington County); Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington MSA (Cecil County); Salisbury HMFA (Wicomico County); Washington-Arlington-Alexandria HMFA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's Counties); and individual county areas including Caroline, Garrett, Dorchester, Somerset, Kent, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a for-profit or nonprofit sponsor of a residential rental housing project
Building must be placed in service within two years of the year the allocation is made
Project must provide at least partial low-income occupancy
Must rent either 20% of units to households at 50% or less of area median income, OR 40% of units to households at 60% or less of area median income
Must comply with tenant income limits, maximum rent levels, and minimum low-income occupancy percentages
Building must remain in compliance and is subject to a covenant for a minimum of 40 years
Awards are based on criteria in Maryland's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP)
Ten percent of the annual allocation is set aside for nonprofit sponsors
Income and rent limits apply only to properties with a Placed in Service (PIS) Date of May 15, 2023 or later (per FY 2024 limits effective April 1, 2025)

Existing LIHTC property owners in the Extended Use Period (post-Year 15) are subject to ongoing compliance monitoring by DHCD's Division of Credit Assurance, including on-site physical inspections at least once every five years

Utility allowances for LIHTC projects must be reviewed and updated at least once during each calendar year; submissions are generally due end of February for the prior compliance year ending December 31st

Licensed Engineer or Qualified Professional signatures required for utility allowance attestations; engineer must be on DHCD's approved listing and qualified per HUD Utility Schedule Model and/or Energy Consumption Model
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sponsors apply competitively for tax credit allocations based on criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for credits outside the competitive process. For current QAP, program guides, and the Multifamily Document Library, visit the DHCD website. Existing property owners seeking a Qualified Contract may apply through DHCD's Community Development Administration (Tax Credit Administrator, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706) beginning with the first day of the 15th year of the Compliance Period; an administrative fee of $3,000 (Part I) and a $30,000 deposit for third-party expenses (Part II) are required. Appraisals and market studies must be performed within 6 months of the date of the Qualified Contract request. Property owners in the Extended Use Period should direct compliance inquiries to the Division of Credit Assurance at dca_mf.dhcd@maryland.gov (Attn: Extended Use Tax Credit Compliance), 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Main Street Improvement Program (MIP) Grant provides operating assistance funding to designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods. The program helps these communities build capacity to achieve community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout Maryland. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other projects identified in the applicant's work plans as key to its Main Street efforts.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are allocated based on accreditation status: fully accredited Designated Main Street Maryland Communities receive approximately $33,000 each; affiliate-accredited Designated Main Street Maryland Communities receive approximately $25,000 each; and Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Final amounts are contingent upon approval by the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session. No funding match is required. Funds are restricted to operating expenses only, not capital projects.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, staff and consultant services, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program that are identified in the applicant's work plans. Capital project costs are not eligible. All activities must be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods located in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a designated or aspiring Main Street Maryland community
Must be a local government or non-profit organization located in Maryland

Organization profile in the Project Portal must include all required documents before submitting

New applicants must contact the project manager for eligibility verification. Ensure the organization profile includes all required documents before submitting. A virtual Application Training was scheduled for March 3, 2026, and individual technical assistance sessions are available via Calendly. For application dates, visit the MIP program page on the DHCD website. Late applications will not be accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Main Street Maryland supports community development and revitalization in Maryland's historic downtowns. The program began in 1998 and now supports over 50 communities statewide. It offers a tiered membership approach — Designated Main Streets, Aspiring Main Streets, and Connected Main Streets — based on each community's readiness and capacity. Communities receive training, technical assistance, and access to the National Main Street Center network to support long-term downtown revitalization using the Main Street Approach, which focuses on economic vitality, design, promotion, organization, and clean/safe/green practices.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Communities receive technical assistance, training, and access to the National Main Street Center network. The program offers a tiered approach: Designated Main Streets receive full program support and national accreditation; Aspiring Main Streets complete a two-year training program to build a foundation toward accreditation; Connected Main Streets can use select pillars of the Main Street Approach to improve their local economy. In 2024, the program supported 200 new businesses, 3,030 existing business expansions, 428 property improvements, 505 full-time and 327 part-time jobs created, 45,848 volunteer hours, and $75.2 million in total public and private investment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application process will reopen in May 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Historic downtown commercial districts, neighborhood commercial districts, and local community organizations seeking to revitalize their business districts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting new and existing businesses, property redevelopment, enhancing physical and visual features of commercial districts, promoting downtown identity, building community partnerships, and improving neighborhood sustainability and safety
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to communities across Maryland. Eligible communities must have a population of at least 1,000 (most recent U.S. Census), hold Sustainable Community designation from the State of Maryland, have a defined central business district with significant historic commercial buildings, and have boundaries falling within a Priority Funding Area (PFA) as determined by the Maryland Department of Planning.

The application process to MD DHCD can take 6 months to a year, after which newly designated communities pursue 1–2 years toward National Main Street Center accreditation standards. The application process is scheduled to reopen in May 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Affordable Housing Trust (MAHT) promotes affordable housing for households earning less than 50% of area or statewide median income. Created by the Maryland General Assembly in 1992 and governed by a Board of Trustees, it is managed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. MAHT funds capital costs of rental and ownership housing, provides financial assistance for nonprofit-developer capacity building, funds supportive services for occupants of affordable housing, and covers operating expenses of affordable housing developments. Funding is sourced from interest generated by title company escrow accounts.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for project-specific capacity building, operating expenses, and support services is generally provided as grants. Funding for capital costs is offered as deferred-payment loans or recoverable grants, repayable if the project is sold or ceases to be used for low-income occupancy. Pre-development awards are generally repayable. The Trust reserves the right to make funding available as interest-bearing loans. Loan guarantees and other financial assistance may also be available.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs of rental and ownership housing including acquisition, pre-development costs, construction, and rehabilitation; nonprofit-developer capacity building related to a specific housing development; supportive services for occupants of affordable housing; operating expenses of affordable housing developments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MD-DIG program, administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) through the Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB), provides competitive grants to expand digital inclusion across Maryland. Funding supports the development of digital inclusion plans and the implementation of programs that expand access to high-speed internet, digital literacy training, and public computing centers, with priority given to underserved populations such as low-income households, aging individuals, people with disabilities, non-English speakers, racial and ethnic minorities, and rural residents.

Individual grant amounts may be reduced based on competition and applicant's ability to deploy funds. Applications are competitive.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Facade Improvement Program provides funding to improve the exteriors of businesses located in Maryland Sustainable Communities. Eligible applicants (local governments and community development organizations) apply to capitalize a local grants fund, then develop their own application process for businesses to improve their building facades. Individual business grants must be between $1,000 and $50,000 per cycle. Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities and should help achieve the local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding to capitalize a local grants fund that businesses can then draw on to cover capital costs for improving exterior building facades. Individual business grants must be between $1,000 and $50,000 per cycle. The applicant (local government or community development organization) administers the grant fund and develops a local application process for businesses. Technical assistance and information are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, groups of local governments, and community development organizations (such as community development corporations, main street organizations, and downtown partnerships) seeking to fund business facade improvements in designated Sustainable Communities. At the local level, commercial business owners and operators in communities with commercial corridors may apply to the locally-administered grants fund.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to commercial property exteriors within designated Sustainable Communities, including signage, painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, lighting, windows and doors, masonry, murals, and roofing. Ineligible uses include interior work, solar panels, EV charging stations, improvements under $1,000 or over $50,000 per cycle, predevelopment costs, and operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within designated Maryland Sustainable Communities — geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Eligibility can be verified using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, a group of local governments, or a community development organization
Project must be located within a designated Sustainable Community
Project should help achieve the local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Applicant must capitalize a grants fund and develop an application process for businesses to improve facades
Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants
Compliance with local building codes required
Properties over 50 years old are subject to Federal Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation
All capital improvements subject to Preservation Officer review and Maryland Historical Trust review if necessary
Work completed before applying is ineligible
Business applicants must provide evidence of site control (deed, purchase contract, or lease)
Existing condition photographs required
Written consent from landlord and lessee (as applicable) required
Project description and two cost estimates with sketches required
Screenshot from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (Business Express Entity Search) showing business in good standing required
Completion timeline must be less than 120 days from award date
Must provide evidence of expenditures (receipts, canceled checks)
Valid insurance coverage required
Must maintain property/improvements and remove graffiti promptly
Pro-rated grant repayment required if improvement is removed within two years
Historic windows and doors should be preserved or restored; replacement only if truly deteriorated beyond repair
Original features should match in material, size, and style when replaced
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage for information on how to apply. Program guidelines and a sample application are available for download on the program page. Applicants apply to create a grants fund and must develop their own application process for local businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Counseling Fund (MHCF) provides annual competitive grants to non-profit organizations and local government agencies that offer housing counseling services and free or low-cost legal assistance. Supported activities include homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching, and legal services for homeowners facing foreclosure or renters facing eviction. HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff receive priority funding consideration.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive grants providing operating support for housing counseling programs and non-profit legal services providers. Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports by the 15th of the month following each quarter of the grant term. Priority funding consideration is given to HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for housing counseling programs (homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching) and legal services for homeowners facing foreclosure or renters facing eviction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Housing Fund Mortgage Insurance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps develop affordable single-family and multi-family housing across Maryland. It also supports economic growth in priority funding areas. The program protects lenders from financial loss by insuring mortgage loans if a borrower defaults.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides insurance for mortgage loans. This protects lenders against financial losses if a borrower defaults on their loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lenders, housing developers, and government entities that develop affordable housing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available statewide, with an emphasis on projects located in Priority Funding Areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP) provides rehabilitation loans and grants for single-family, owner-occupied homes and one-to-four unit rental properties across Maryland. The program helps bring properties up to applicable building codes by addressing exterior and interior deficiencies, including major systems (heat, electrical, plumbing), accessibility improvements, health or safety violations, energy conservation measures, and elimination of lead-based paint hazards. Administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), the program is also delivered locally through entities such as Baltimore County, the City of Hagerstown Department of Housing & Community Development, and Frederick County Housing. Loans up to $50,000 are available through the Hagerstown local program. Loan interest rates are based on the borrower's percent of median income and ability to repay, and can be as low as 0% and generally no higher than 4% statewide (up to 6% in Baltimore County and Hagerstown). Maximum secured debt including the loan is generally 110% of the after-rehab property value with a maximum term of 20 years statewide (up to 30 years through Hagerstown). Deferred payment loans may be available for very low-income households at or below 50% of the applicable median income; in exceptional cases up to 80% of median may qualify statewide. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. There is no application fee for the statewide program; administrative, closing, and recording costs may be included in the Baltimore County loan. The program helps lower monthly utility bills and improve quality of life for homeowners and rental tenants across Maryland. Household income may not exceed 80% of the Adjusted Median Income published annually by DHCD. Assistance amounts depend on the type of work needed, household income, and ability to repay.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and low-interest loans for home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, and rehabilitation to meet building codes and standards. Loans up to $50,000 available through the Hagerstown local program. Interest rates are based on the borrower's percent of median income and ability to repay; rates can be as low as 0% and no higher than 4% statewide (up to 6% in Baltimore County and Hagerstown). Maximum secured debt including the loan generally cannot exceed 110% of the after-rehab property value with a maximum term of 20 years statewide (up to 30 years in Hagerstown). Deferred payment loans may be available for households at or below 50% of applicable median income (in exceptional cases up to 80% may qualify statewide). Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. Administrative, closing, and recording costs may be included in the loan (Baltimore County). Loan must be repaid upon discontinuance of owner occupancy or sale of the home. No application fee for the statewide program. Amounts based on type of work, household income, and ability to repay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible owner-occupants of single-family homes who use the property as their permanent, year-round residence, and owners of one-to-four unit rental properties whose tenants have incomes at or below 80% of the applicable area median income. Available to Maryland homeowners seeking affordable home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, accessibility upgrades, or rehabilitation to meet building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of residential properties to meet applicable building codes, including exterior and interior repairs, major systems (heat, electrical, plumbing), accessibility improvements, health or safety violation corrections (mold remediation, gas leak repairs, asbestos/vermiculite/lead abatement, radon mitigation, electrical hazards), energy conservation measures, elimination of lead-based paint hazards, modifications for persons with disabilities (ramps, grab bars, chair lifts), roof and gutter repair, plumbing, water, septic and sewer repairs, windows and doors (health & safety, water intrusion, and security only), structural repair, and some general improvements. Also covers energy efficiency improvements (Energy Star appliances, air quality, lighting, insulation, air sealing, HVAC systems).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Also administered locally through Baltimore County, the City of Hagerstown Department of Housing & Community Development (14 N. Potomac St., Suite 200A, Hagerstown, MD 21740), and Frederick County Housing. Income limits in Frederick County are based on the Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) median income depending on property location. In Baltimore County, property must be a single-family owner-occupied dwelling or multi-family property with up to four rental units. The Hagerstown local program serves properties within the City of Hagerstown.

Owner-occupants must occupy the home as their permanent, year-round residence
All residents of rental housing must have income at or below 80% of the applicable area median income

Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans

All persons listed on the Deed must agree to loan terms and sign closing documents
Mortgage and property tax payments must be current
Title to property must be clear of liens and judgments
Property must be insured to cover all indebtedness
Repairs must be made by a licensed, insured contractor
Must provide a contractor and scope of work/work proposal (Hagerstown)
Must meet program eligibility criteria (details available by contacting the administering agency)
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home or one-to-four unit rental property

For Frederick County, contact Frederick County Housing.
