structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that reduces interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) and small businesses. Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on loans obtained from participating banks. The program uses State funds deposited with participating banks to subsidize the interest rate reduction, making capital more affordable for small and minority-owned businesses to grow and expand.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible borrowers receive up to a 2% interest rate reduction on qualifying term loans from participating banks. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office deposits funds equal to the loan amount with the lending bank at a reduced interest rate, allowing the bank to offer a lower rate to the borrower. The rate reduction applies for the full term of the loan (up to 10 years), as long as the borrower remains in good standing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, and small businesses in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, seeking affordable loans for Maryland-based projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds must be used for projects or activities located in Maryland. Funds cannot be used for sectarian or religious purposes. Loans are term loans only with fixed rates and one disbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects or activities must be located in Maryland. Participating lenders are located across multiple Maryland regions including Anne Arundel County (Annapolis), Montgomery County (Silver Spring), Washington County (Hagerstown), and Howard/Prince George's Counties (Columbia/Greenbelt).
requirements_list: Borrower must be a certified Minority Business Enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, OR a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Loan purpose must be for a project or activity located in Maryland
Borrower must apply to DHCD to be eligible
Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years
Points charged by lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
Funds cannot be used for sectarian or religious purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The eligible applicant or a participating lender submits a brief application (online or paper form) to the Linked Deposit Program at DHCD. DHCD verifies eligibility and forwards the application to enrolled banks. The borrower then contacts participating banks to complete their full loan application. The bank underwrites the loan at a rate up to 2% below their standard rate and enrolls the approved loan in the program. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office then deposits funds equal to the loan amount with the bank.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Microenterprise Loan Program (MLP) expands opportunities for microenterprise development and supports small business start-ups and expansions. It provides flexible financing to entrepreneurs for starting up or expanding small (micro) businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas across Maryland, while also sustaining local economies through direct lending to local Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs). The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (MD DHCD) partners with community-based microlenders (Intermediaries) that originate and administer the loans, giving micro-entrepreneurs easier access to capital, training, and technical assistance. Intermediary partners include Baltimore Community Lending, Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc., Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center, and Prince George's Financial Service Corporation (FSC First), each serving defined geographic areas. FSC First serves as a designated Fund Manager for Prince George's County and administers loans to small businesses in Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas. Eligible businesses must have no more than 5 employees and annual revenue under $500,000. The program supports both established businesses and feasible start-ups with financing for working capital, equipment purchases, leasehold improvements, and human capital increases. In Prince George's County, the program is administered through the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation in partnership with FSC First.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 per project, with interest rates up to 12% (rate determined at underwriting). Loan terms of 2 to 5 years (cannot exceed 5 years). Collateral is required and may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, pledges of accounts, and personal assets. No prepayment penalties. Additional funds may potentially be added by the Intermediary lender. Funds can be used for leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital. Home-based businesses may be eligible subject to FSC First approval when applying through that intermediary. The program also provides loans directly to local CDFIs, which then lend to small businesses and microenterprises.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Microenterprise owners and entrepreneurs with businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities or Priority Funding Areas in Maryland, with no more than 5 employees and annual revenue under $500,000, seeking to start or expand a microenterprise. Open to both established small businesses and feasible startups. Also targets Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) in Maryland. In Prince George's County, start-up and expanding small businesses in Priority Funding Areas may apply through FSC First or the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payment, minor renovations, leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment purchases, human capital increases, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. CDFIs use loan funds to provide financing to small businesses and microenterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in designated Sustainable Community areas and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. Specific Intermediary partners serve defined geographic areas including Baltimore City, various counties, Eastern Shore counties (served by Maryland Capital Enterprises and Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center), and Prince George's County (served by FSC First in partnership with the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation).

Eligible business types: retail, manufacturing, goods and services
No home-based businesses (except home-based businesses may be eligible through FSC First subject to their approval)

Ineligible businesses include residential/transient living, multifamily or single-family housing developments, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, crisis care centers, group homes, transitional housing, homeless shelters, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment/adult bookstores, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors
In Prince George's County, business must be located in a Priority Funding Area designated by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the Intermediary Microloan Partners directly to receive an application. Partners are assigned by county or region and include Baltimore Community Lending, Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc. (Salisbury, 410-546-1900, www.marylandcapital.org), Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center (Easton, 410-770-9330, info@ventureahead.org), and Prince George's Financial Service Corporation (FSC First, apply online via fscfirst.com/learn/programs/micro-enterprise-loan-program-md-dhcd). The program accepts applications on a rolling basis. In Prince George's County, applicants may also contact the EDC's Financial Services Manager (Andre Plummer, applummer@co.pg.md.us, 301-583-4635) for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Opportunity Zone program is a nationwide initiative created under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and administered by the U.S. Treasury and IRS. It provides federal tax incentives to encourage investors to reinvest unrealized capital gains into Qualified Opportunity Funds dedicated to investing in low-income or underserved communities. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts statewide, administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with support from the Maryland Department of Commerce. Baltimore City has 42 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts; the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) connects investors and project sponsors with Opportunity Zone resources, co-investors, and state tax credit enhancements. Anne Arundel County has four federally designated Opportunity Zone tracts — one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park — promoted locally by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC). Washington County's Department of Business and Economic Development promotes the program locally, including designated Opportunity Zones within the City of Hagerstown. Garrett County also has designated Opportunity Zone census tracts. Caroline County has Opportunity Zones in Denton and Federalsburg. The City of Frederick in Frederick County also has designated Opportunity Zones. The program offers three tax incentives: (1) temporary deferral of capital gains taxes reinvested into a Qualified Opportunity Fund until the earlier of disposal or December 31, 2026; (2) a step-up in basis of 10% if held at least 5 years and an additional 5% if held at least 7 years (up to 15% of original gain excluded); and (3) permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains accrued on the opportunity zone investment if held for at least 10 years. There is no cap on the amount of capital that can flow through Opportunity Zone investments, and the program allows various types of investments including small businesses and real estate. Eligible uses include economic development, workforce and affordable housing, infrastructure, start-up businesses, and capital improvements to underutilized assets. BDC also helps connect Baltimore City investors with co-investors such as the Neighborhood Impact Investment Fund and state-level Opportunity Zone Enhancement Credits from the Maryland Department of Commerce. The program is available through year 2027.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive three types of federal tax incentives for investing through a Qualified Opportunity Fund: (1) Temporary deferral of capital gains taxes reinvested into a Qualified Opportunity Fund until December 31, 2026 or earlier disposition; (2) Step-up in basis of 10% if held at least 5 years and an additional 5% if held at least 7 years (up to 15% of original gain excluded from taxation); (3) Permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains accrued on an Opportunity Fund investment if held at least 10 years. There is no authorized cap on the amount of capital that can be invested. Qualifying investments must be made in designated Opportunity Zone tracts through a Qualified Opportunity Fund (a partnership or corporation), and can include investments in small businesses and real estate within designated zones. The Qualified Opportunity Fund must invest at least 90% of its assets into Opportunity Zone property. The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) also provides technical assistance, connecting investors with co-investors such as the Neighborhood Impact Investment Fund and state-level Opportunity Zone Enhancement Credits from the Maryland Department of Commerce. The program is available through year 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with unrealized capital gains seeking to deploy into distressed, low-income, or underserved communities designated as Opportunity Zones in Maryland, including 42 designated tracts in Baltimore City, four designated tracts in Anne Arundel County (Odenton and Brooklyn Park), designated Opportunity Zones in Hagerstown and Washington County, Garrett County, Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County, the City of Frederick in Frederick County, and 149 designated census tracts statewide. Also includes private impact investors, Qualified Opportunity Funds, and project sponsors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in eligible property located in designated Opportunity Zones through a Qualified Opportunity Fund, including investments in small businesses, real estate, and infrastructure within economically distressed, low-income, or underserved Opportunity Zone communities throughout Maryland. The Qualified Opportunity Fund must invest at least 90% of its assets into Opportunity Zone property. Eligible uses include economic development, workforce and affordable housing, infrastructure, start-up businesses, and capital improvements to underutilized assets. Funds support federal capital gains tax deferral, reduction, and permanent exclusion for qualifying investments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 149 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts throughout Maryland (at least one per county), including 42 tracts in Baltimore City, four tracts in Anne Arundel County (one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park), designated Opportunity Zones in the City of Hagerstown and Washington County, designated Opportunity Zone census tracts in Garrett County, Opportunity Zones in Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County, and designated Opportunity Zones in the City of Frederick in Frederick County. Program is national but Maryland-specific administration is handled by DHCD, with local support from BDC in Baltimore City and AAEDC in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Investment must be made through a Qualified Opportunity Fund (a partnership or corporation)
Qualified Opportunity Fund must invest at least 90% of its assets into eligible Opportunity Zone property
Investor must have unrealized capital gains from a prior investment to fund the Opportunity Fund
Capital gains must be reinvested within 180 days of realization
Deferred gain must be recognized by December 31, 2026 or when the investment is sold, whichever is earlier
To receive 10% basis step-up, investment must be held at least 5 years
To receive additional 5% basis step-up, investment must be held at least 7 years
Permanent exclusion of accrued gains requires holding the investment for at least 10 years
Must invest in a qualified Opportunity Zone business or property
Must be located in a designated Opportunity Zone census tract
Qualified Opportunity Fund must self-certify by submitting IRS Form 8996
Investors should consult accountants and/or attorneys for guidance
Program available through year 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors reinvest capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund within 180 days of realization. The fund self-certifies as a Qualified Opportunity Fund by submitting IRS Form 8996 (no state application process required). The fund then invests in designated Opportunity Zone tracts, ensuring at least 90% of assets are invested in Opportunity Zone property. Guidance on fund formation is available from the U.S. Treasury and IRS (see IRS Form 8996 and IRS Opportunity Zone FAQs). Visit the Maryland DHCD Opportunity Zones page for details on eligible zones and investment requirements. Contact DHCD for information on Maryland-specific programs that can complement Opportunity Zone investments: Frank Dickson at frank.dickson1@maryland.gov or 301-429-7408. Washington County's Department of Business and Economic Development can be contacted at 240-313-2280 for local assistance. Anne Arundel County investors may contact AAEDC for local assistance with commercial revitalization and reinvestment opportunities. Baltimore City investors and project sponsors can contact BDC at info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com or (410) 837-9305 for more information on partnering and accessing Opportunity Zone resources. Investors in Frederick may also contact the City of Frederick Department of Economic Development for local guidance. Caroline County investors may contact Caroline County Economic Development for local guidance. Garrett County investors may visit the Garrett County business incentives page for local guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's SSBCI program provides loans and equity investments to support small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses with limited opportunities for growth. The program targets communities and areas with a high concentration of small, micro, and SEDI businesses across Maryland. Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), the program also offers technical assistance including financial advisory consulting, webinars, workshops, loan packaging assistance, and tailored mentorship and network connections through partner organizations. TEDCO allocates up to $50 million in federal SSBCI funding across four programs — the Venture Equity Fund, Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, Seed Funds Equity program, and Social Impact Funds — to support technology-based small businesses and entrepreneurs in Maryland. The DHCD Direct Loan Program offers flexible direct loans with terms up to 30 years, minimum $500,000 and maximum $5 million, requiring a 1:1 private capital match. Technical assistance is also available through the MD Business Opportunity Center (financial advisory consulting, webinars, workshops, loan packaging) and F3Tech's SEDI Program (mentorship and network connections). Note: SSBCI does not offer grants — funds are issued as loans or equity investments only.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans and equity investments (no grants) are available through DHCD lending partners including Lendistry, City First Enterprises, FSC First, and Community Development Fund. The DHCD Direct Loan Program offers flexible direct loans (senior or subordinated positions) with terms up to 30 years, loan amounts from $500,000 to $5 million, interest rates determined by underwriting, and a required 1:1 private capital match. Fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. Personal guarantees from owners with >20% equity are required, along with adequate collateral and total project costs ≤$20 million. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center (financial advisory consulting, webinars, workshops, loan packaging) and F3Tech's SEDI Program (mentorship and network connections). TEDCO separately allocates up to $50 million in SSBCI funds through four equity investment programs: (1) Venture Equity Fund, (2) Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, (3) Seed Funds Equity program, and (4) Social Impact Funds — all targeting technology-based small businesses and entrepreneurs in Maryland. The Social Impact Funds track targets entrepreneurs who demonstrate multiple disadvantages.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis. Contact program managers for additional details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (fewer than 500 employees), micro businesses, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI)-owned businesses in Maryland with limited growth opportunities, including technology-based startups and entrepreneurs. The Social Impact Funds track targets entrepreneurs who demonstrate multiple disadvantages.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and capital access for small and SEDI businesses. Funds are deployed as loans or equity investments through lending partners. Direct loan use of funds includes: machinery, equipment, and working capital; owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (≥51% owner-occupied for renovation; ≥60% for new construction); mixed-use projects (if not 100% residential); passive real estate investment; tenant improvements; and debt refinancing (with restrictions). Excludes: back taxes (without payment plan), lobbying, equity purchases (except ESOPs/worker co-ops), refinancing existing debt with same lender, stock purchases, federal loan collateral enhancement, and conflicts of interest. TEDCO equity investments support technology-based startups and small businesses in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Program helps small town and city governments build their administrative capacity by providing grants to hire professional staff to work as a 'circuit rider' — a shared employee serving multiple towns — to assist with specific municipal functions and activities. The program operates on a competitive annual basis, with funding levels determined by the Maryland General Assembly appropriation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded through a competitive process each year. The annual funding amount is determined by the Maryland General Assembly appropriation. Grant funds may only be used to pay salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two-year period. Technical assistance is also available for interested governments and sponsors.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually; eligible governments are notified when applications are due each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small municipalities with populations of 5,000 or less, and eligible circuit sponsors including municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations serving two or more municipalities in reasonable proximity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider professional staff over a two-year period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Small municipalities in Maryland with populations of 5,000 or less.
requirements_list: Municipalities must have a population of 5,000 or less
Circuit sponsors must organize a circuit of two or more municipalities
Municipalities in the circuit must be within reasonable proximity to each other
Circuit sponsors may be municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations
Applications are evaluated on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment and support
Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance

Eligible governments are notified at the opening of the competition and when applications are due. Applications are evaluated on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment and support. Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides flexible financing to help start up, rehabilitate, or expand small businesses and nonprofits that offer healthy food options in underserved areas. The program focuses on increasing access to fresh food in designated Food Desert Areas and Sustainable Communities, with priority given to businesses sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers. Financing is delivered through community-based lending intermediaries (CDFIs, local governments, or quasi-public agencies) that originate and administer loans and provide technical assistance to borrowers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible loans for the start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of food-related businesses and nonprofits located in designated Food Desert Areas or Sustainable Communities. Loans are originated and administered by selected community-based lending intermediaries. Technical assistance is also provided to borrowers by those intermediaries.

Also eligible as intermediaries: CDFIs, local governments, and quasi-public agencies working in Maryland communities.

Intermediary lenders must be CDFIs, local governments, or quasi-public agencies currently working in Maryland communities

Entities seeking to become an intermediary must submit a separate application to DHCD. Priority for intermediary status is given to applicants focused on jurisdictions with active food desert initiatives.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Multifamily Bond Program increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. It provides tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing, and leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (4% LIHTC). Projects must contain at least five complete independent dwelling units and comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years with interest rates based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate, and a first lien position is generally required. Six product types are available: Risk Sharing (HRB), GNMA Long Term (HRB), GNMA Tax/TE (Standalone), Freddie Tel (Standalone), Fannie Mae M.TEB (Standalone), and Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Credit Enhanced Funds (Standalone).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other acceptable credit enhancement. Projects may also leverage federal 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTCs). Refinancing of existing high-interest private loans is allowed when combined with rehabilitation. Six product types are available: Risk Sharing (HRB), GNMA Long Term (HRB), GNMA Tax/TE (Standalone), Freddie Tel (Standalone), Fannie Mae M.TEB (Standalone), and Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Credit Enhanced Funds (Standalone).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers of multifamily rental housing serving households with limited incomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing with a minimum of five units. Loans may also refinance existing high-interest private loans when combined with rehabilitation. Typical construction period is 20–24 months.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must contain a minimum of five units
Projects must contain complete independent dwelling units
Sponsor must make either 20% of units available to households at 50% or less of area median income, or 40% of units available to households at 60% or less of area median income
First lien position generally required for all bond loans

Projects using tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
All loans must comply with federal requirements for tax-exempt revenue bonds
Housing must be for families with limited incomes
Subject to Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP) for LIHTC and Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program accepts applications on a rolling basis. Contact Housing Development Programs by email or phone for more information. A TEFRA Form is available for download on the program page. A variety of financing structures are accepted; see the Multifamily Program Financing Option Comparison document for details on structures, indicative interest rates, fees, and costs. Applicants should check with CDA Loan Underwriters regarding currently available financing options.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The MEEHA program promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. It provides grants and loans to fund energy efficiency improvements, greenhouse gas reduction measures, and electrification upgrades. Funding is available through two sub-programs: EmPOWER (reduces electric or gas consumption) and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP, which replaces fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided through two sub-programs: (1) EmPOWER — grants or loans (0% interest, deferred payments) totaling $134.9 million for calendar years 2024–2026, used to reduce electric or gas consumption; gas-reducing measures are allowed only in BGE or WGL utility territories. (2) GHGRP — grants only, $8.75 million in FY2024 and $5 million each in FY2025 and FY2026, used to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions by replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment. Funds are released after equipment is installed and inspected. An MBE participation goal of 29% applies to applicable DHCD-funded projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing and Building Energy Programs, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments seeking to improve energy efficiency or reduce greenhouse gas emissions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements (reducing electric or gas consumption), greenhouse gas reduction measures (replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment), building energy conservation, alternative energy generating systems, solar PV, EV charging, BEPS Roadmap program opt-in, HVAC replacement/upgrade, insulation, lighting, duct sealing, thermostats, VFDs, electrification costs, energy audits, new construction certifications (Energy Star, DOE Efficient, Passive House), and limited health and safety or incidental repairs incidental to qualifying measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Gas-reducing measures under EmPOWER are limited to buildings in the BGE or WGL utility service territory. GHGRP is limited to existing buildings with 35,000 gross square feet or more (excluding parking garages).
requirements_list: EmPOWER: minimum 20% of households at 80% AMI or less for at least 5 years (up to 15 years for some funds)
GHGRP: minimum 51% of households at 80% AMI or less for at least 15 years
GHGRP projects must be in existing buildings with 35,000+ gross sq ft of floor area (excluding parking garages)
A Qualified Energy Professional must conduct an energy audit (rehabilitation) or energy certification review (new construction) and submit the Funding Request to DHCD
Gas-reducing measures under EmPOWER only funded in BGE or WGL utility territories
MBE participation goal of 29% on applicable DHCD-funded projects; only MDOT MBE-certified firms count toward goal
MBE firms must hold applicable NAICS code and perform a commercially useful function (CUF)
Monthly MBE subcontractor payment reports due by the 15th of each month to ofpnpcompliance.dhcd@maryland.gov
Account holder consent required to release energy use data (24-month lookback and 24-month post-completion)
Projects must use the January 1, 2026 Program Guidance for applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026
Qualified Energy Professionals must complete at least 1 project per program year or face removal from the qualified list
Energy Star Portfolio Manager tracking required for GHGRP projects (2-year utility data retention post-completion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner submits MEEHA Application (or 202 Application if also applying for Rental Lending) to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. 2. Owner commissions a Qualified Energy Professional to complete an energy audit (rehab) or energy certification review (new construction). 3. Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD within 10 business days of request. 4. DHCD reviews the Funding Request and sends a scope confirmation. 5. Owner accepts scope and executes funding agreement (OAG grant/loan agreement drafted). 6. Project kickoff meeting held. 7. Project installs funded measures. 8. Project team submits requisitions with supporting documentation. 9. DHCD inspects installed measures and processes payment (typically 4–5 weeks). 10. Project enters affordability period after construction is complete.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan to Lender Program provides capital loans to Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) for re-lending to small businesses throughout Maryland. It focuses on businesses owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), Very Small Businesses (VSBs, fewer than 10 employees), and those in CDFI Investment Areas. Loan sizes range from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity, with SSBCI funding capped at $5,000,000 per CDFI and total financing less than $20,000,000. Targeted end loans to small businesses are up to $350,000. CDFIs must have 20% at risk, and a private capital match is required (4:1 for non-SEDI businesses with 10 or more employees; 2.3:1 for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees). At least 34.46% of Maryland SSBCI funds must reach very small businesses and SEDI-owned businesses combined. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Part of Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).

SSBCI funding capped at $5,000,000 per CDFI; total financing must be less than $20,000,000. Loan sizes range from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity. Targeted end loans to small businesses of up to $350,000. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. Private capital match required: 4:1 for non-SEDI businesses with 10 or more employees; 2.3:1 for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees. Assistance may take the form of loans, investments, or other credit/equity support.

SEDI-owned business eligibility includes enterprises operating in CDFI Investment Areas, U.S. territories, rural communities, and communities undergoing economic transitions (including net-zero economy transitions or deindustrialization). Applicant CDFIs self-designate the Maryland counties/cities they serve.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: CDFIs complete and submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application (Appendix A form). Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Step 2: DHCD reviews the application and, upon approval, issues a commitment letter specifying the loan amount, private capital match requirement, and funding timetable. Step 3: SSBCI loans are closed per terms and conditions established by the Maryland Office of Attorney General. Step 4: Lender outlines its proposed SBL program with specific geographic, demographic, and industry focus goals, SBL products, and underwriting requirements. Contact dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov or 866-226-3559 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Venture Funds Program provides venture debt financing to early-stage businesses in Maryland with high job-growth potential. It supports companies that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking bridge financing to reach the next equity raise milestone. Venture debt is provided as repayable principal and interest or convertible notes. Part of Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).

Aggregate funding round must be under $20,000,000. SSBCI funds must be on at least a pari passu (equal standing) basis with the private capital match. Private capital match required: minimum 1:1, with target exceeding 2:1. Typical bridge rounds exceed $2,000,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) provides competitive grants to support commercial and residential revitalization activities in targeted areas of Prince George's County and Montgomery County. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy can have a meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact. Eligible projects must align with a Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funds for commercial and residential development projects in targeted revitalization areas of Prince George's County and Montgomery County. The program also provides technical assistance/information. Specific award amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities/towns, and community development organizations (non-profits) in eligible areas of Prince George's County and Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers; acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties; improvement of existing residential and business properties; energy efficiency weatherization and retrofits; development of affordable housing; development of mixed-use projects; development or enhancement of community open space or public infrastructure; strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County projects must be located at least in part within the boundary of Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia. Montgomery County projects must be within an Enterprise Zone or within the boundary defined by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495, and the District of Columbia. Projects must be within a designated Sustainable Community.

Project must be located in an eligible Sustainable Community in Prince George's County or Montgomery County
Project must support goals and objectives in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information and how to apply, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage at dhcd.maryland.gov. Contact the relevant Regional Project Manager for questions about specific address eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: The National Housing Trust Fund (HTF) is a federal program administered in Maryland by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to help create and preserve affordable rental housing for households with the lowest incomes. DHCD uses HTF funds to support extremely low-income households earning 30% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI). HTF funds are often combined with other federal, state, and local housing resources to help make affordable housing projects financially feasible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds are awarded competitively and on a first-ready, first-served basis depending on fund availability. Maryland will receive $3,000,000 in HTF funds from HUD for FFY 2025 (October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026). Funds may be used for construction or rehabilitation, property acquisition, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. HTF funds cannot be used to refinance existing debt. If selected, recipients receive a Notice of Award stating DHCD's intent to provide HTF funds. The affordability period is 40 years beginning at project completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, for-profit developers, and other qualified housing development entities seeking to develop or preserve affordable multifamily rental housing for extremely low-income households in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or rehabilitation of affordable rental housing, property acquisition, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. Cannot be used for refinancing existing debt. HTF subsidy may be layered with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and other housing funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative, which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City, with exceptions for areas annexed after 1/1/1997), areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits, areas between the Washington DC beltway and DC boundary, Sustainable Communities, federal and state enterprise zones, and county-designated PFAs including rural villages. Projects must also be located in either a Qualified Census Tract (QCT) or Difficult Development Area (DDA) contributing to a concerted community revitalization plan, or family projects must have reasonable access to jobs, quality schools, and other economic and social benefits (measured by location in a Community of Opportunity per Maryland QAP Comprehensive Opportunity Maps). Rural areas include any area eligible under USDA Rural Development programs, or any area in Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, or Worcester Counties (if not otherwise CDBG entitlement communities or HOME Participating Jurisdictions). Rural projects and family projects in Communities of Opportunity receive scoring priority. Geographic diversity priorities include Baltimore City (Thompson v. HUD census tracts) and Baltimore County (116 census tracts per HUD Conciliation Agreement).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan Participation Program provides below-market-rate loans to small businesses in Maryland for working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation. It is part of Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) and targets businesses in CDFI Investment Areas, with priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) who own or operate Maryland-based small businesses.

Application fee of $250 and closing fee of $250. Private capital match required: 4:1 for non-SEDI/VSB, 2.3:1 for SEDI/VSB, minimum 1:1.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) loan program offers flexible financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Maryland. Loans support a wide range of commercial purposes including construction, equipment, working capital, and real estate acquisition, with the goal of supporting commercial district or town center revitalization. Projects must be located in designated targeted geographies such as Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in select counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. Interest rate is based on underwriting analysis and creditworthiness. Eligible applicants include Maryland-based small businesses (as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration), local development corporations, and nonprofit organizations whose activities contribute to broader revitalization efforts. Requires 10% applicant cash contribution, personal guarantees, sufficient collateral, and positive net operating income. Fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment/origination fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications to date exceed total funds available until July 2026; operates on first-come, first-serve basis with a wait list available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses (500 or fewer employees), local development corporations, and nonprofit organizations seeking financing for commercial projects in targeted geographies including Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, or other construction; leasehold improvements; machinery and equipment; working capital; market/planning/feasibility studies; starting or expanding small businesses; and promoting investment in commercial districts or town centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico County, a Transit-Oriented Development area designated by MDOT, or a BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone. Local governments are not eligible applicants.

For an initial consultation, complete the Pre-Application Consultation Form on the DHCD website. Submit a complete NBW loan application with all items listed in the application checklist.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions and their ISP partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The local jurisdiction serves as the applicant and fiscal agent. The program is now closed and no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of between $50,000 and $500,000 covering 70% to 90% of capital construction costs. Cash or in-kind match of 10% to 30% required. Local jurisdiction or ISP may own funded assets. This program is closed and not accepting applications.

Match of 10% to 30% of capital construction costs required
Areas having received prior state grant funding are ineligible
All federal rules of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closed. Contact the Office of Statewide Broadband for information on past awards.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides matching grants to support the operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations. These nonprofits partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, and local governments to stabilize and improve housing markets in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. NHS corporations use the funds to provide homeownership opportunities, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community-organizing activities. The Department currently supports three NHS corporations operating in targeted neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 per eligible NHS corporation, not to exceed one-third of the corporation's annual operating budget. NHS umbrella corporations may apply for a separate grant of up to $50,000 for each program under their supervision, also not to exceed one-third of that program's annual operating budget. State grants must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions. Technical assistance and information may also be available.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Neighborhood Revitalization
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations approved by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation (NeighborWorks America)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of NHS corporations, including homeownership programs, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves low- and moderate-income neighborhoods in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Salisbury, Maryland, through certified NHS corporations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation (dba NeighborWorks America).
A local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local NHS corporation and participate on its board of directors.
Grant amount must not exceed $50,000 and must not exceed one-third of the corporation's annual operating budget.
State grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible NHS corporations apply directly to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Contact the Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Net Zero Loan Program (Energy-Efficient Homes Construction Loan Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest construction loans and loan enhancements to support the construction of Net Zero homes in Maryland. Net Zero homes produce as much or more energy than they use, featuring advanced energy-efficient design, renewable energy resources, and a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower. The program also offers loan enhancements for applicants seeking financing through a private lender.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest construction loans are available with interest rates based on HERS score and income served: HERS 0–15 at 3% (market rate) or 2% (if 50%+ of units serve households at or below 60% AMI); HERS 16–35 at 4% or 3%; HERS 36–50 at 5% or 4%. Loan-to-value (LTV) up to 90%. Loan terms include a 12-month construction period and 12-month repayment period for for-sale projects. Closing fees include a 1% administration fee, ~$290 appraisal fee, and title fees. Loan enhancements are also available for applicants seeking financing through a private lender.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Accepting applications until available funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, and investors constructing or deeply retrofitting homes to Net Zero energy standards; eligible entity types include for-profit corporations, non-profit corporations, limited general partnerships, limited liability companies, sole proprietorships, and other organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a HERS rating of 50 or lower and are properly zoned for residential use, built in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be qualified to do business in Maryland
Must have legal capacity and all necessary authorization to incur the loan obligation
Must demonstrate credit worthiness and repayment ability acceptable to the department
Must demonstrate the ability to complete the project
Project must achieve a HERS rating of 50 or lower
Must be new construction or a deep energy retrofit of an existing home
Property must be properly zoned for residential use
Must be constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable Local, State, and Federal building codes

Financial Statements

Insurance: Property/Builder's Risk Insurance (ACORD), Borrower's Liability Insurance (ACORD), Flood Insurance with specified endorsement requirements
Construction Documents: Plans, Specifications, Budget, Draw Schedule, Construction Schedule, General Contractor certifications, Building Permits, HERS Rating
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan (Net Zero) Program paper application form. 2. Review the list of required documentation. 3. Submit the completed application by email to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov with a CC to Thomas.Walz@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NourishMD Grant Program (a pilot program) provides direct grants to eligible food retailers to expand access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity. Grants range from $25,000 to $150,000, with up to $2 million in total funding available. Eligible retailers include grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores serving communities with limited healthy food access.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $25,000 to $150,000 per project (up to $2 million total available). A $250 processing fee is deducted from the award amount. Funds can be used for equipment purchases, facility upgrades, inventory expansion, working capital, and infrastructure for SNAP/EBT access. An optional supplemental loan may also be available via Neighborhood BusinessWorks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit food retailers — including grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores — serving communities with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible; however, businesses can be added by emailing compass@maryland.gov. Exceptions to the geographic eligibility requirement may be granted on an individual basis.
requirements_list: Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Operate at least 5 days per week, year round (farmers markets and on-farm markets are exempt from the 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
A $250 processing fee is sourced from the award amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted through an online portal. The portal opened January 20, 2026 and closed February 20, 2026. Applications are currently under review. The agency reviews applications in February and March and finalizes recommendations in April 2026. Award notifications occur in May 2026, followed by Board of Public Works approval and disbursements in June 2026. Applicants can schedule an initial consultation or email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov for questions. The program follows an annual cycle: December (NOFA release) → January 20 (portal opens) → February 20 (portal closes) → February–March (review) → April (recommendations) → May (announcements) → June (BPW approval and disbursement). Note: This program is designated a pilot program; long-term recurrence beyond the current cycle has not been confirmed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax incentive designed to drive long-term private investment into distressed communities. Investors who place capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund can defer and potentially reduce their federal tax liability on the sale of assets. Funds pool capital to support investments in small businesses and real estate within designated Opportunity Zones to improve communities and quality of life for residents. There is no cap on the amount of capital that can be made available through Opportunity Zone investments, and the program allows various types of investments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors can defer and reduce federal tax liability on capital gains by investing those gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund. The fund pools capital for investment in small businesses and real estate within designated Opportunity Zones. There is no authorized cap on the amount of capital that can be invested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors seeking to defer or reduce federal capital gains taxes by investing in distressed communities in Hagerstown's designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in small businesses and real estate within designated Opportunity Zones.

Investments must be located within a designated Opportunity Zone
Investments must be made in small businesses or real estate within designated Opportunity Zones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors place gains into an Opportunity Fund. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers the program with support from the Maryland Department of Commerce. See dhcd.maryland.gov for details. IRS Form 8996 is required for Opportunity Zone Fund certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Own Your Future provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy or renovate commercial real estate they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program offers flexible loans funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) for property acquisition or renovation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $500,000 to $5 million with terms up to 30 years. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Senior or subordinate loan positions are available. Borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Personal guarantees are required from all owners with more than 20% equity. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million.

Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion; new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership Rental Housing Program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households. Projects typically involve a partnership between state and local governments. A 2006 statutory change also allows non-governmental entities to use program funds to create housing for households that include one or more individuals with disabilities or special needs, integrating affordable units within traditional rental housing developments. Loans are provided for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are provided for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million (without a per-unit cap) for small projects (defined as 40 units or fewer). Repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rent it to income-eligible households. Any profits from the sale of the project must be used for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities partially owned by a local government or housing authority, and non-governmental entities serving individuals with disabilities or special needs. Resident households must have gross income at or below 50% of statewide median income (or 30% of Area Median Income for disability/special needs units).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing, including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located in priority funding areas.
requirements_list: Local governments must contribute land or an equivalent contribution from non-state resources.
The local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it.
Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50% of statewide median income adjusted for family size.
Resident households in disability/special needs units must have gross income not exceeding 30% of Area Median Income adjusted for household size.
Residents must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds, or neighborhood (Tenant Contributed Services), except occupants of disability/special needs units.
Non-governmental entities are eligible only for units serving individuals with disabilities or special needs.
If other department funds are requested alongside Partnership Rental Housing Program funds, the application requirements and deadlines of those other funds must be met.
Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis and evaluated based on meeting the program's purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library. Contact Housing Development Programs by email or phone to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Restore provides grant funding to new or expanding businesses that open or expand into previously vacant retail and commercial properties in Maryland. The program offers two types of grants: a Rental Assistance Grant of up to $30,000 to cover rent for one year for small businesses with 50 or fewer employees, and a Business Operations Grant of up to $250,000 per year (for one or two years) based on sales and use tax generated by the business. Businesses in designated Tier 1 areas (including Washington County) or Opportunity Zones are eligible for up to two years of Business Operations Grant funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

Funds may be used for staff costs, capital improvements, marketing, inventory and supplies, and utilities, but not executive salaries or bonuses. Businesses in Tier 1 areas (including Baltimore City and Washington County) or Opportunity Zones are eligible for two years; all other counties are eligible for one year.

State funds may be combined with federal HOME funds, low-income housing tax credits, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, and other public or private funds. Funding is awarded through a competitive process held one or two times a year, with priority given to projects that restrict units to low-income tenants, provide tenant services, and leverage non-State funds.

Funds may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs (including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, and legal fees).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to housing development.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works (RHW) provides subordinate gap financing (loans) to support the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing in Maryland. It works alongside the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program to fill financing gaps. The program is designed to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy.

Loans have a 40-year term, carry 2% simple interest, and are due on sale, refinancing, or transfer. Payments are limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans must be used in conjunction with DHCD's tax-exempt bonds and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for creation and preservation of affordable rental housing projects financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits; must conform to RHW funding limitations and IRC Section 42
