structured_extraction.program_description: The Section 811 Project Rental Assistance (PRA) Program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by making rental units in the community affordable. Funded by HUD and managed jointly by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD), the program operates as a project-based rental assistance subsidy. DHCD awards rental assistance to approved rental housing projects — not directly to individuals — while MDOD refers eligible tenants and provides supportive services. Participating properties receive project-based rental assistance subsidizing the contract rent for eligible tenants. Tenants pay 30% of their income toward rent and utilities, and the program pays the remaining rent directly to the landlord. The initial lease term is one year, and rent does not change unless the participant's income changes. Eligible residents are non-elderly adults (ages 18 to under 62) with disabilities who receive Medicaid and have very low income (at or below 30% of AMI). The program is operated through a partnership with MDOD and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), links affordable housing with services and supports, promotes independent living, and provides tenants with resources such as personalized tenant training, transition planning, money management assistance, and access to voluntary support services. Administrative costs are capped at 8% of the annual award. Individual tenant assistance periods are up to 5 years. Cooperative Agreements have a minimum term of 20 years. Maryland received a $9,808,054 grant for 150 units under the FY2013 funding cycle. Multiple funding rounds have been awarded including FY2012, FY2013, and FY2019.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. Tenants pay 30% of their income toward rent and utilities; the program pays the remaining rent directly to the landlord. Assistance is not provided directly to individuals but to housing projects through DHCD's existing financing programs (Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds). The initial lease term is one year, and rent does not change unless the participant's income changes. Administrative costs are capped at 8% of the annual award. Individual tenant assistance periods are up to 5 years. Cooperative Agreements have a minimum term of 20 years, with initial funding for the first five years and subsequent funding renewal subject to appropriations. After the initial five years, grantees receive a single year's worth of funding each year as long as Congress appropriates the funding. Maryland received a $9,808,054 grant for 150 units under the FY2013 funding cycle. FY2013 funding was anticipated to serve the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metro areas (75%) and Eastern Shore and Western Maryland (25%).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis for eligible applicants in priority categories; as of March 1, 2017, the Waitlist Registry is closed to new applicants who do not meet a priority category
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing developers and property owners with projects financed through DHCD that serve low-income adults with disabilities; and eligible individual tenants aged 18 to under 62 who have a qualifying disability, receive Medicaid, have household income at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI), and are referred by MDOD. Priority is given to institutionalized individuals or those at risk of institutionalization, DD/BHA program participants, and homeless persons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidize the contract rent of eligible units occupied by low-income adults with disabilities in approved rental housing projects. Covers the portion of rent above 30% of the tenant's income, paid directly to the landlord. Funds may also be used for planning and infrastructure/technology costs and administrative costs (capped at 8% of award amount). Supportive services including case management, waivers, psychiatric rehabilitation, and attendant care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in participating rental units. FY2013 funding was anticipated to serve the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metro areas (75%) and Eastern Shore and Western Maryland (25%). Projects must be located in priority funding areas.
requirements_list: Project must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds
Project must receive financing from DHCD
Eligible residents must be between ages 18 and 61 (non-elderly, under age 62 at time of leasing)
Must have a qualifying disability
Must be a Medicaid recipient
Must have household income at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI)
Eligible residents must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
Eligible multifamily properties must have at least 5 units (duplexes excluded)

No more than 25% of total units in an eligible multifamily property may receive rental assistance (total of 811 PRA units plus tenants admitted under occupancy preference for persons with disabilities may not exceed 25% of total units in building)
Properties must comply with Fair Housing Act, Title VI Civil Rights Act 1964, Section 504 Rehabilitation Act 1973, and Title II ADA
Grantee must execute Cooperative Agreement (HUD-93205-PRA)
Compliance with affirmative outreach, effective communication for persons with disabilities, and accessible units requirements
Davis-Bacon wage standards apply for construction
Energy Star compliance required for new construction or substantial rehabilitation
Properties must have a Use Agreement with a minimum 30-year term
Rental Assistance Contract (RAC) term is a minimum of 20 years
Applicants with prior lease terminated by eviction are subject to a 6-month waiting period
Two prior lease terminations result in permanent ineligibility unless reasonable accommodation is granted
Background check (criminal and credit) required for tenant applicants
As of March 1, 2017, the Waitlist Registry is closed to new applicants who do not meet a priority category
SAM.gov registration required for organizational applicants
Medical/disability documentation must be on official letterhead with contact information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For housing developers/property owners: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee (including MDOD and MDH representatives) to review and select eligible projects. Once selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming eligibility for unit subsidies. Organizational applicants must submit applications electronically via Grants.gov and must be registered in SAM.gov. For individual tenants: Contact your case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application on your behalf. Eligible residents are referred by MDOD rather than applying directly. New applications receive a date/time stamp. The Waitlist Manager refers 2-3 applicants for each available unit within one month after notification of unit availability. Participants are offered up to 3 units matching their needs and preferences and must accept or decline within 5 business days. Non-selected applicants may re-apply at any time. As of March 1, 2017, the Waitlist Registry is closed to new applicants who do not meet a priority category. A decision to close the PRA Waitlist may be made by MDOD, in consultation with MDH and DHCD, and will be posted on MDOD and DHCD's websites.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions — colleges, universities, and qualifying hospitals in Maryland — for capital improvement projects located in Sustainable Communities or other underinvested areas of the state. Projects must generate jobs, strengthen ties between anchor institutions and surrounding communities, and contribute to safer, healthier, and more attractive neighborhoods. Recipients must provide a 1:1 match of funds received.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans for capital improvement projects. Recipients must provide matching funds equal to the amount received (1:1 match). Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Institutions of higher education and qualifying hospital institutions in Maryland, including their departments, foundations, and affiliated entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects located in Sustainable Communities or other underinvested areas of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities or other underinvested areas of Maryland. Geographic eligibility can be checked using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland institution of higher education or a qualifying Maryland hospital institution (or their departments, foundations, or other affiliated entities).
Qualifying hospital must have a group of at least five physicians organized as a medical staff.
Qualifying hospital must maintain facilities to provide diagnostic and treatment services for two or more unrelated individuals under medical staff supervision.
Qualifying hospital must admit or retain individuals for overnight care.
Project must be located in a Sustainable Community or an underinvested area of the state.
Applicant must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage on the DHCD website for application information and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to nonprofit organizations and local governments to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters, with the goal of reducing homelessness in Maryland. Eligible uses include new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelter facilities that include supportive services for residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Generally, grants may cover up to 50% of total project costs, but under certain conditions may cover up to 75%. Sponsors must maintain the project as transitional housing or an emergency shelter for 15 years; if use is discontinued before 15 years, the grant must be repaid. Eligible uses include alteration, addition/expansion, conversion, relocation, renovation, replacement, restoration, site development, utilities, and certain equipment/furnishings. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, furnishing replacements, operating assistance, feasibility studies, and maintenance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments seeking to provide transitional housing or emergency shelters for homeless or at-risk-of-homelessness individuals and households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters that include supportive services for residents. Eligible project types include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family homes, single-room occupancy, and group/shared housing. Eligible uses include alteration, addition/expansion, conversion, relocation, renovation, replacement, restoration, site development, utilities, and certain equipment/furnishings. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, furnishing replacements, operating assistance, feasibility studies, and maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City), areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits, areas between the Washington DC beltway and DC boundary, areas designated as Sustainable Communities, federal and state enterprise zones, county-designated PFAs (including rural villages in county comprehensive plans as of July 1, 1998), and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Acquisition and rehabilitation projects have no stated geographic restriction. Local government letters of support are required for all projects.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or a local government
Housing must serve homeless individuals and households, or those in danger of becoming homeless
Project must include supportive services for residents
A local government letter of support is required for all projects
Sponsor must maintain the project as transitional housing or an emergency shelter for at least 15 years
If use is discontinued before 15 years, the grant must be repaid
Grant funds generally may not exceed 50% of total project costs (up to 75% under certain conditions)
Applicant must demonstrate evidence of site control
Project must demonstrate readiness to use funds within 12 to 18 months of the grant application
New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted any time of the year and processed on a first-come, first-served basis, pursuant to program funding availability and project readiness. Process includes: (1) Threshold review (Section 6.1) confirming nonprofit/local government status, capital assistance within limits, funds for eligible uses, and site control; (2) Viability review (Section 6.5) in which sponsors submit detailed construction and underwriting documents and the Department issues a viability report with pro-forma and term sheet; (3) Commitment review (Section 6.6) in which final documents are submitted and the Department prepares a commitment report — a commitment letter is issued within 70 calendar days of commitment package submission. A fast-track option combining viability and commitment packages is available at the Department's discretion. Kick-off meetings set specific milestone dates conforming to the Department's submission kit process. Architectural standards follow the AIA Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice.

structured_extraction.program_description: An income-targeted financing program designed to bring properties up to applicable building codes and standards. Provides loans for rehabilitation and renovation of single-family homes to meet building codes and standards for income-eligible Maryland homeowners.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income-targeted financing for rehabilitation and renovation of single-family homes to meet building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible Maryland homeowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and renovation of single-family homes to meet building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD recommends starting with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify needed improvements and enroll in appropriate programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State Revitalization Programs (SRP) offer a range of grant funding to support community revitalization goals across Maryland. Funding is primarily used for capital projects — physical improvements with at least a 15-year useful life — located within designated Sustainable Communities. Common projects include upper-story residential redevelopment in historic business districts, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, and acquisition/rehabilitation of vacant residential properties. The SRP umbrella includes several sub-programs: Community Legacy, Maryland Facade Improvement Program, Strategic Demolition Fund, Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (formerly Project C.O.R.E.), Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative, National Capital Strategic Economic Development Program, and Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant and loan (including recoverable grant) funding for capital and, in select sub-programs, operating revitalization projects located within Sustainable Community boundaries. Award amounts range from approximately $20,000 to $20,000,000 depending on sub-program. A 4% Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee applies to capital awards beginning FY26 (except Maryland Façade Improvement Program). Awards have a 2-year term; 50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by the first anniversary date. Funding is requested by the Governor and subject to General Assembly approval, so a round is not guaranteed every year. Capital-only programs: Community Legacy, Strategic Demolition Fund, SEED, Maryland Façade Improvement Program. Capital and operating programs: Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI), National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 application period closed July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit community development organizations, local governments, higher education institutions (SEED only), small businesses, and other eligible entities located within or serving Maryland Sustainable Communities seeking funding for capital revitalization projects. Priority investment areas include ENOUGH areas, Just Communities, transit-oriented development sites, and historic Main Streets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects such as upper-story residential redevelopment, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, community open space enhancements, acquisition/rehabilitation of vacant residential properties, streetscaping, demolition, building stabilization, environmental remediation, predevelopment, and architectural/engineering design. Select sub-programs (BRNI, NED) also allow operating expenses up to 15% indirect costs. Prohibited uses include pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, massage parlors, adult entertainment, check cashing, gambling, tattoo parlors, liquor stores, and religious practice projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a designated Sustainable Community and support the outcomes in that community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Projects must also be located within Priority Funding Areas (PFAs). Nearly 130 designated Sustainable Community Areas exist across the state, with at least one in each county. Boundaries can be verified using the DHCD Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper 4.0. Select programs have additional geographic requirements (e.g., Opportunity Zones for certain Community Legacy projects in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset counties; Baltimore City/inner-beltway for BRNI).

Project must connect to the community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Project address must be within a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Organizations must register in the Project Portal before applying
New organization registration must be completed by the cutoff date (typically two weeks before application deadline)

Required organizational documents (Certificate of Good Standing, Corporate Resolution, SDAT Good Standing, Articles of Incorporation, By Laws, Board certifications, IRS Determination Letter, MD Charitable Registration Letter) must be uploaded to the organization's profile before submitting
Applications missing required documents may be disqualified

4% Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee applies to capital awards (except Maryland Façade Improvement Program)
50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by first anniversary date of award; 100% by completion date
Quarterly progress reports required (due Oct 1, Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1) and final report due within 45 days of project completion
MBE/WBE plan, MHT determination, Sustainable Communities check, and site control verification required for award management
Conflict of interest policies: board members with owned properties/interests must recuse from decision-making
Records retention: minimum 3 years after close of award; for loans/loan combinations, duration of loan term plus 3 years
Payment requests must meet minimum $3,000 guideline and require supporting documentation (invoices, receipts, contracts, canceled checks)
Award execution requires 60-day turnaround for signed agreement and special condition documentation
Organizations that have previous year funding are required to be up to date before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register in the Project Portal at projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us (select 'New User?' and complete the registration request form; approval takes up to 72 hours; new user account requests must be submitted by approximately two weeks before the application deadline). Upload required organizational documents to your profile. Review program guidelines for your chosen sub-program. Submit application online through the DHCD Project Portal (no paper submissions accepted) by the deadline. Applications are scored on five criteria totaling 100 points: community need & input (20), project scope clarity (20), readiness & timeline (15), financing & leverage (25), and sponsor/partner capacity (20). After award: award agreements drafted and executed within 60 days; four-stage management cycle: Award Approval → Agreement Execution → Award Management → Award Close Out. Contact your regional project manager or Larry Brown, Jr. (larry.brownjr@maryland.gov, 410-209-5819) with questions. Portal support: nrsystemsupport.dhcd@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund seeks to catalyze activities that accelerate economic development and job production in existing Maryland communities. The Fund aims to improve the economic viability of 'grey field' redevelopment — development on previously used land that often faces more barriers than sprawling 'green field' development. Since funds are limited, awards focus on those projects that can have a high economic and revitalization impact in their existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards are provided for eligible projects outside Baltimore City. The program focuses funding on projects with high economic and revitalization impact. Assistance may include project grants and loans, as well as technical assistance and information. Specific award amounts are not publicly stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City whose projects are located in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of derelict non-contributing structures; site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels; site development; construction-level architectural and engineering designs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible applicants whose projects are located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City, or Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. A separate program, the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative, covers Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Lead applicants must be local governments or nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City
Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City, or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico Counties
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage for more information and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program provides funding to nonprofit organizations and local governments to support operating costs related to local housing, community, and economic revitalization projects or initiatives. Grants help cover salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, consultant contracts, and other administrative expenses tied to community and economic revitalization activities. Projects must be located in or serve designated Priority Funding Areas, Sustainable Community areas, or communities supported through the ENOUGH Act or Just Communities designations. Capital project costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 (minimum $1,000 per request for payment) for operating costs related to community revitalization efforts. No funding match is required. All projects or activities must be completed within one year from award agreement signature. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis, with up to 25% of award available as an advance (proof of spend required in next payment request). Capital project costs are not supported through TAG.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit organizations involved in community and economic revitalization activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, consultant contracts, staff salary, studies and analyses, and other related administrative expenses as outlined in grant agreement Exhibit B. Excludes alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal items, fines, unauthorized travel companions, and capital project costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area. Bonus points awarded for projects in designated ENOUGH areas (up to 10 points) and designated Just Communities (10 points). Transit-Oriented Development sites, historic Main Streets and business districts, and Baltimore City vacant property elimination are also noted as priorities.

Applicant must be involved in community and economic revitalization activities
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Projects or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans, or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies
All projects or activities must be completed within one year from award agreement signature
Capital project costs are not supported through TAG

Final report due by expiration date or within 30 days after

3-year record retention required
Conflict of interest disclosure required
Awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within the grant term
Minimum $1,000 per Request for Payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the DHCD Project Portal (projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us) selecting 'Community Development and Services Application FY2026'. New users must register first by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form — approval may take up to 72 hours. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting, as incomplete applications may be disqualified. Visit the TAG program page on the DHCD website for current application dates. Late applications will not be accepted.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT aims to increase property values and create wealth-building homeownership opportunities by accelerating the development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. The program closes the 'appraisal gap' — the difference between what it costs to build or renovate a home and what the home can sell for on the open market — which is especially common in communities historically affected by redlining and disinvestment. The State covers the appraisal gap through UPLIFT funding, enabling qualified development teams to acquire, develop, build, and sell affordable homes in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing. Development loans are structured as 2nd lien position, 0% interest during the construction period; homeowner promissory notes for appraisal gap financing use a 5-year declining balance, 0% interest, with automatic forgiveness at 20% per year. The program also couples its development loans with a commitment from DHCD to offer grants and loans to nearby 'Legacy Homeowners,' often living in energy inefficient and deteriorated housing. Projects in ENOUGH Initiative or Just Communities census tracts receive enhanced flexibility. Applicants use an electronic submission request form to obtain a Dropbox folder for application packages, final underwriting, closing, draws/requisitions, and close-out submissions. Initial deployment focused on the City of Baltimore and City of Cambridge, with anticipated expansion to other neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: UPLIFT covers the appraisal gap — the difference between the total eligible cost to develop a property and the price it can sell for on the market — through direct program funding. Development loans are structured in a 2nd lien position at 0% interest during the construction period. Homeowner promissory notes for appraisal gap financing use a 5-year declining balance at 0% interest with automatic forgiveness at 20% per year. A non-refundable $1,000 application fee per project is required at submission, plus a 1% origination fee on the loan amount due at initial closing. Payment must be made via ACH or check. Applications are accepted on a rolling, first-come first-served basis as long as funding is available, with changes announced at pre-round information sessions and posted to DHCD's website at least 30 calendar days before the application deadline. Total program resources referenced at approximately $20M (original $10M pilot plus $10M FY'24 allocation). Each project must sell 25% of its units to households earning at or below 80% AMI.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, as long as funding is available; specific deadlines announced at least 30 calendar days in advance via DHCD website
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers, builders, community-based organizations, Public Housing Authorities (PHAs), and local small businesses engaged in housing development in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities in Maryland. All Primary Development Team members (developer, builder/GC, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, marketing/sales entity) must have experience building/renovating at least 3 units of comparable type within the last 5 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in targeted low-income and historically redlined neighborhoods. Funds cover the appraisal gap between development costs and market sale prices. Eligible costs include project acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, pre-development and operational costs, professional fees, developer fees, neighborhood engagement activities, infrastructure improvements within ¼ mile of project area, and environmental remediation. Additional grants and loans may be available to Legacy Homeowners in nearby areas. New construction projects are excluded from FEMA Flood Zone Areas (with limited waivers for Zones C and X).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in both a low-income census tract (50% of households below 60% AMI or poverty rate ≥25%) AND a designated Maryland Sustainable Community. Projects in ENOUGH Initiative or Just Communities census tracts receive enhanced flexibility. Initial deployment in the City of Baltimore and City of Cambridge, with anticipated expansion to other neighborhoods. A Qualified Areas Map is available on the program page.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a UPLIFT qualified area — both a low-income census tract and a designated Sustainable Community
Applicant must be a qualified development team (nonprofit or for-profit developer/builder, PHA, or local small business)
All Primary Development Team members must have experience building/renovating at least 3 units of comparable type within the last 5 years as of application date
Disqualifying factors include unpaid state/federal obligations
Must complete a pre-application meeting with DHCD before submitting a full application
Must submit required documentation at least two business days before the pre-application meeting
Must pay a $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project at time of submission (ACH or check only)
Must pay a 1% origination fee on the loan amount due at initial closing
Must submit both an electronic copy (via Dropbox) and a hard copy of the application
Hard copy must be delivered to DHCD's Lanham, MD office and must match the electronic version
New construction projects may not be located in FEMA Flood Zone Areas (limited waivers available for Zones C and X)

Waiver requests for Threshold or Evaluative Scoring Criteria must be submitted in writing to the Director of the Community Development Administration using a Waiver Request Form; DHCD responds within 15 calendar days; Secretary of DHCD approval required for certain waivers
Projects reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis as long as funding is available
25% of units must be sold to households earning at or below 80% AMI
Site control of at least 70% vacant properties required (waiver eligible)
Minimum project size of 8 units (waiver eligible)
Must comply with fair housing requirements and Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Marketing Plan (AFHMP)
Must meet URA relocation requirements where applicable
Must meet all UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review the program guide and all application materials; prepare project details including scope, development plan, and financials; schedule a pre-application meeting and submit required documentation at least two business days before the meeting. Step 1: After the pre-application meeting, submit the Electronic Application Submission Request Form (hosted at dhcd.wufoo.com); DHCD will send a private Dropbox link for submitting application documents. Step 2: Download the Application Documents Package, complete all sections using the UPLIFT Detailed Application Instructions, and prepare two copies (one electronic, one hard copy). Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable application fee and upload proof of payment (ACH or check). Step 4: Upload all files to Dropbox, sign and upload the Final Submission Checklist, and deliver the hard copy to DHCD's Lanham, MD office. Step 5: DHCD conducts a threshold review and scores eligible projects using criteria including Development Team Capacity (40 pts), Project Impact (50 pts), Leveraging & Cost Effectiveness (30 pts), and Readiness to Proceed (30 pts). Step 6: If approved, receive a commitment/reservation letter. A 1% origination fee on the loan amount is due at initial closing. Post-award steps include a Project Kick-off Meeting (generally 45–60 days after complete application submission), Final Underwriting Submission, Secretary determination, Initial Financing Closing, and Construction Kick-off Meeting. Waiver requests must be submitted in writing to the Director of the Community Development Administration prior to application submission. If unfunded in a round, applicants may reapply when applications are next being accepted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Weatherization Assistance Program – Local Weatherization Agency (Subgrantee) Participation
structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD recruits nonprofit organizations, Community Action Agencies (CAAs), and local government agencies to serve as Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs) that deliver federally funded weatherization services to low-income households. Requests for Applications are conducted at least every three years or more frequently to ensure statewide coverage. Maryland has administered the DOE WAP program since 1987 and operates through a network of skilled subgrantees providing services in each of the state's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected subgrantees receive federal Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) funds to deliver weatherization services to eligible low-income households in their service area. Subgrantees also procure local contractors to perform the weatherization work. Funds support energy efficiency retrofits (air sealing, insulation, hot water tank wraps, window/door repair/replacement), health and safety hazard elimination, furnace repair/replacement, energy audits, client education, training and technical assistance for staff, and incidental repairs necessary to make weatherization materials effective. Administrative costs up to 7.5% of the grant are also allowable. EmPOWER soft cap is $7,500 per funding source (hard cap $12,500); DOE WAP tied to approved average cost per unit; incidental repair spending cap cannot exceed 20% of total job cost; H&S spending NTE $1,000 across programs. BIL (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law) funds are tracked separately and are available until expended (award period 07/01/2022–06/30/2027). Work on multifamily buildings with 5 or more units will not be serviced with BIL funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Posted when an active RFA is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Action Agencies, other nonprofit organizations, and local government agencies interested in becoming a Local Weatherization Agency subgrantee
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of federally funded weatherization services to low-income households as a subgrantee. Eligible uses include: air sealing; cellulose/fiberglass insulation (attic, rim/band areas, floor, rim joist, exterior wall, knee wall, attic access, roof, mobile home belly/roof); hot water tank wraps and pipe insulation; window/door repair/replacement with insulated materials; furnace/boiler/heat pump/HVAC repair or replacement (BGE/WGL territory for gas; all EmPowerMaryland territories for electric); duct sealing and insulation; smart thermostats; LED lighting; faucet aerators and low-flow showerheads; water heater replacement/repair; appliance replacement (refrigerators/freezers meeting efficiency standards, max $850/unit); energy audits; client education on energy management; health and safety hazard abatement including combustion gases testing and remediation, electrical repairs and hazard mitigation, combustion safety corrections, asbestos testing and encapsulation, biological/unsanitary condition remediation, mold/moisture remediation, lead-safe work practices, air conditioning/heating system repair or replacement for at-risk occupants, radon precautions, pest exclusion, smoke alarm installation, CO detector installation, fire extinguishers (only when solid fuels present), vapor retarder installation, mechanical ventilation systems; minor structural repairs; roof repair; exterior/interior structural repair; foundation or subspace repair; exterior drainage repairs; plumbing repair; electrical repair; incidental repairs (capped at 20% of total job cost); Weatherization Readiness Fund (WRF) for pre-weatherization deferral conditions (average cost cap $15,000); direct-install measures; crisis intervention measures; client education materials; training and technical assistance for state and local weatherization staff (up to 10% of project ECM package); administrative costs; and program operations costs. Health & Safety (H&S) costs for occupant and worker protection during weatherization activities are budgeted separately from energy efficiency measures and are allowable only where direct weatherization occurs; H&S expenditure limit is 20% of per-unit average cost (DHCD policy).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. The dwelling must have a physical address in Maryland. Subgrantees are organized by county with primary and secondary agencies designated per county where feasible. No exclusion of specific counties or municipalities. Three counties (Anne Arundel, Carroll, Harford) currently do not have a designated Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) and may be serviced by existing LWAs. Network Partners are assigned leads based on jurisdiction and/or lead distribution guidelines with consideration for proximity to the client's home. For gas utility data verification, targeted outreach is conducted in Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties (Washington Gas service territory). Natural gas domestic hot water and gas heating/boiler system replacement is limited to BGE/WGL territories; electric systems are eligible in all EmPowerMaryland territories.
requirements_list: Must be a Community Action Agency (CAA), or other public or nonprofit entity recognized by federal and state law
Nonprofit organizations must have an active board of directors and be organized under Maryland law
Must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) before submitting an application
Must provide a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number
Must maintain active SAM registration throughout the period of any federal award
Energy efficiency improvement projects must meet an SIR of 1.0 or greater (with exception for air sealing)
Individual measures must meet SIR ≥1.0 (DOE WAP) or SIR ≥1.1 (EmPOWER); total job package must meet SIR ≥1.0
Health and safety measures must be installed per plan; can only be skipped if physically impossible
Historic preservation compliance required for projects affecting properties on the National Register or state historic inventory (Maryland Historical Trust Act)
Subgrantees must maintain a waiting list of applicants that have contacted the agency to apply for assistance
Subgrantees must complete annual re-verification of client eligibility (no application older than one year)
Subgrantees must maintain active certifications for staff including HEP QC Inspector and Energy Auditor credentials
Annual State Plan must be submitted to DOE for approval each fiscal year as part of the state's application for federal WAP funds
Auditors, assessors, and inspectors must have knowledge of radon (occurrence, factors, precautionary measures) and training in proper vapor retarder installation
ASHRAE 62.2-2016 compliance required for mechanical ventilation systems
OSHA standards compliance required; Hazard Communication Plan (HCP) required, specific to workplace/materials, shared with workers via training, reviewed and updated annually
Informed consent form must be signed by client prior to work
Medical documentation required (no older than 180 days) for air conditioning eligibility for at-risk occupants

Staff certifications required include BPI HEP Energy Auditor, HEP Retrofit Installation Technician (RIT), HEP Crew Leader, and HEP Quality Control Inspector (QCI); EPA LRRP training and OSHA 10-hour Construction Safety card also required
New staff must obtain required certifications within 60 days of hire
Subgrantees must maintain insured bank accounts (FDIC or NCUA-insured) for federal fund advances; interest-bearing accounts required with interest >$500/year remitted quarterly to DHCD
Submit Program Income budget for approval at beginning of annual period; minimum 80% of Program Income funds must be used for labor, materials, and program support
Maintain client files with DOE-required documentation (application, proof of ownership, eligibility notice, historic preservation letter if applicable)
Maintain records for minimum 3 years following close of associated federal grant
50% or more of prior-year expenditures must be in eligible program costs (per budget compliance requirements)
Job cost soft cap: $7,500 (DOE/EmPOWER per funding source); hard cap $16,000 (EmPOWER) or $12,500 (EmPOWER per source)
H&S expenditure limit: 20% of per-unit average cost (DHCD policy)
Obtain DHCD Quality Assurance Inspector approval before deferral
Document deferral decisions with signed forms, photos, cost estimates in Hancock Energy Software
Notify clients in writing within 7 calendar days of deferral decision with appeal rights
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: When an active RFA is posted on the DHCD webpage, eligible organizations submit an application demonstrating they meet minimum qualifications. Maryland conducts a Request for Applications process to solicit new DOE WAP subgrantees; selected applications receive an award for the applicable period of performance. Contact Saniya Mosley to be added to the vendor notification list. The WAP State Plan is developed annually by HBEP staff as part of the state's application for federal WAP funds; subgrantee network is organized by county with primary and secondary agencies designated per county where feasible. Client case management is handled via Hancock Energy Software for client prioritization. Income verification for end-user clients is conducted via OHEP (175% FPL auto-eligible; 175–250% FPL screened as 'OHEP leads') or direct application to DHCD/LWA; written notification of eligibility/ineligibility provided within 30 days; appeal process available for ineligibility determination.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The EmPOWER Maryland Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP), administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), provides free energy efficiency improvements and weatherization services to eligible low-income and limited-income households at no cost. Eligible homeowners, renters, and mobile home owners receive a home energy audit and contractor services, with upgrades that may include attic, floor, and wall insulation; air sealing; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning and repairs; refrigerator retrofits; and health and safety items. The program is designed to reduce energy use, lower monthly utility bills, improve home comfort, and may improve air quality and family health. Applicants must meet household income limits and have a utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas. May also cover critical home repairs including heating, cooling, water heating systems, and structural, electrical, water leak, lead, and asbestos remediation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of energy efficiency improvements and weatherization services at no charge to eligible limited-income households. Improvements may include attic, floor, and wall insulation; air sealing; hot water system upgrades; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofits; and health and safety items. A home energy audit is also provided at no cost. May also cover critical home repairs including heating, cooling, water heating systems, and structural/electrical/water leak/lead/asbestos remediation, with contractor bids required and assistance capped at $50,000. Loan financing is also available for homeowners needing critical repairs to their primary residence (maximum loan amount $50,000; maximum initial deposit 33% of total project cost).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income Maryland homeowners, renters, and mobile home owners who are customers of participating utilities (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas) and meet household income limits. Priority given to seniors (60+), young children (0–5), persons with disabilities, critically ill persons, and families with medical need for heating/cooling/water heating systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy efficiency upgrades and weatherization services including insulation, air sealing, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items. May also cover critical home repairs including heating, cooling, water heating systems, and structural/electrical/water leak/lead/asbestos remediation. Repair funding capped at $50,000 per application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must have a utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas, and must be located within EmPOWER utility service territories.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income or limited-income Maryland homeowner, renter, or mobile home owner (with ownership proof)
Household income must fall below program limits based on household size (e.g., $72,950 for a household of 1, up to 250% of the Federal Poverty Level for larger households)
Must have a utility account with one of the six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas
Must be located within an EmPOWER utility service territory

Automatic income eligibility for participants in OHEP Utility Bill Pay Assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Income documentation, utility bill, and benefit documentation required for application
Income verification documentation including recent pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, and Social Security/disability/public assistance letters
Proof of home ownership (deed, current mortgage statement, or property tax bill) required for homeowners
Current homeowners insurance and flood insurance (if applicable) required for home repair assistance
Medical documentation available for expedited processing if applicant has a documented medical condition requiring functioning HVAC or water heating systems

For home repair assistance: contractor bids required (quote no more than 60 days old; total bids capped at $50,000); contractor must be Maryland-licensed (MHIC/electrical/plumbing/HVAC), insured (COI ≥$1M per occurrence), in good standing, and provide W-9
Bid cover sheet with photographs of critical repairs required for home repair applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an online pre-application or submit a paper application (available in English and Spanish) with required documents to the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or apply for Energy Assistance through the Department of Human Services to be screened for the program. Two application tracks are available: a 'Quick application' for energy efficiency improvements only, and a full application for home repair assistance. Applicants already approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services may call the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Once eligibility is confirmed, a local agency will schedule a home energy audit, discuss results, and arrange for a contractor to complete recommended upgrades. After upgrades are completed, the local agency conducts a follow-up evaluation. Visit https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Energy-Home-Repair/Pages/Homeowner-Grants/EmPOWER.aspx for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) is a federal program that supports affordable housing by providing funding to state and local governments. Maryland's program is administered by the Community Development Administration (CDA) Development. Funds can be used in conjunction with existing CDA programs to build, buy, or rehabilitate rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Community Development Administration
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are typically provided as zero-interest deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years. In some cases, funds may be provided as grants or regular amortized loans. If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with CDA. The maximum assistance amount generally will not exceed what is needed to make the project financially viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. State government agencies are automatically eligible and receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater. As of 2024, maximum subsidy limits range from approximately $181,488 to $359,263 depending on unit bedroom count. Funds are allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis for the HOME Special Reserve Fund. Maryland received $7,319,907 in federal HOME funds for FFY 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, and nonprofit organizations developing or rehabilitating affordable housing in Maryland. Program primarily targets Non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland counties and municipalities except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County (except Annapolis), Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County). Residents of funded units must have household incomes at or below 50% of area median income (rental) or 55% of area median income (owner-occupied).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, purchasing, or rehabilitating rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes for low-income residents. Funds may also be used through the HOME Special Reserve Fund, which replaced the former HOME Initiative Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. HOME funds will be used primarily in Non-Participating Jurisdictions, which include the entire state except for Baltimore City and Anne Arundel County (except for the City of Annapolis), Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's Counties. Income and rent limits are set by HUD on a metropolitan statistical area (MSA) and county basis, covering areas including the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson MSA, California-Lexington Park MSA, Cumberland MD-WV MSA, Hagerstown MD HUD Metro FMR Area, Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington PA-NJ-DE-MD MSA, Salisbury MD HUD Metro FMR Area, Washington-Arlington-Alexandria DC-VA-MD HUD Metro FMR Area, and individual counties including Somerset, Worcester, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, and Talbot.
requirements_list: For rental housing, resident household income must be 50% or less of area median income (set annually by HUD based on household size).
For owner-occupied housing, owner household income must be 55% or less of area median income (set annually by HUD based on household size).
If HOME funds are used with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME federal requirements.

Number of income-restricted units is generally calculated by dividing HOME funds by total project cost, multiplied by total units; CDA may allow fewer income-restricted units if needed for financial viability.
If property is sold or ceases use as low-income housing, borrower must share equity gain with CDA.

Program primarily serves Non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland areas except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County (except Annapolis), Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County).
HOME Special Reserve Fund allocates funds on a first-come, first-serve basis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants include state government agencies (automatically eligible), local governments, local housing agencies, and nonprofit organizations. Projects using HOME funds alongside other CDA programs must meet both CDA and federal HOME eligibility requirements. HOME funds are primarily directed to Non-Participating Jurisdictions. The HOME Special Reserve Fund allocates funds on a first-come, first-serve basis. Contact the program manager for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration (CDA), part of the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance public infrastructure projects. The CDA then loans the bond proceeds to local governments at interest rates based on market conditions at the time of sale. The program pools local demand to reduce issuance costs and provides bond counsel and financial advisory expertise to help local governments manage the bond financing process. Technical assistance is also available to help local governments navigate the application and financing process.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds are issued by the Community Development Administration and the proceeds are loaned to local governments. Loan amounts range from $150,000 to $10 million or more. The interest rate is based on market conditions at the time of the pooled bond sale. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Borrowers repay the debt and pay their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs, and must pledge their full faith and credit as security for repayment. Technical assistance is also available to help local governments complete the application and navigate the bond financing process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need long-term capital financing for public infrastructure projects but do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to initiate financing on their own.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure projects including street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks, and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage, and distribution systems; stormwater control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance, and other service-related facilities; and refinancing of existing eligible debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties, municipalities, and their instrumentalities statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or agency thereof
Must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared State revenues
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government or its agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments complete an application that elicits information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. Timing of bond issuance is influenced by the volume and frequency of local government participation. Those seeking technical assistance can submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Sustainable Communities (SC) Designation is a place-based geographic designation program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), Division of Neighborhood Revitalization, that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability in older communities statewide. Created by the State of Maryland, the designation concentrates state resources to support coordinated revitalization efforts. Jurisdictions submit an action plan identifying specific geographic areas and revitalization goals covering housing, transportation, economic development, and neighborhood revitalization. Once a jurisdiction receives the SC designation, organizations and property owners with projects located within the designated area become eligible to apply for state grants, tax credits, and other resources — including Community Legacy grants, Neighborhood BusinessWorks loans, the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund, Low Income Housing Tax Credits, Job Creation Tax Credits, Small Commercial Tax Credits (Historic Preservation), the Sustainable Communities Tax Credit, the Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program, Maryland Bikeways grants, Sidewalk Retrofit, Community Safety and Enhancement, and Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing programs. The designation is valid for five years (renewable) once approved and must be within a Priority Funding Area. Baltimore City received its SC designation on November 26, 2012. Designated areas in Howard County include Ellicott City, North Laurel-Savage, Long Reach Village, and others; in Anne Arundel County these include Brooklyn Park and Glen Burnie (approved 2013) and Odenton/Severn (approved 2014). Boundary amendments may be submitted on a rolling basis and are reviewed by DHCD twice a year. Past awards to Howard County communities have ranged from $25,000 to $5,000,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Division of Neighborhood Revitalization
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD awards a Sustainable Communities designation to qualifying local government areas. The designation is valid for five years (renewable) and unlocks eligibility for multiple state funding programs including Community Legacy grants, Neighborhood BusinessWorks loans, the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund, Low Income Housing Tax Credits, Job Creation Tax Credits, Small Commercial Tax Credits (Historic Preservation), the Sustainable Communities Tax Credit, the Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program, Maryland Bikeways grants, Sidewalk Retrofit, Community Safety and Enhancement, and Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing programs. Organizations and property owners whose projects are located within a designated Sustainable Community area gain priority or enhanced access to these state funding programs. Past awards to Howard County communities have ranged from $25,000 to $5,000,000. Heritage Area designation provides access to state funding up to $100,000 in capital and $50,000 in project grants, as well as mini grants and emergency grants for governments and nonprofits. Boundary amendments may be submitted on a rolling basis and are reviewed by DHCD twice a year. An interagency panel reviews designation applications and the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet gives final approval. Renewal applications must be submitted on or before the expiration date of the Sustainable Communities designation. Eligible applicants for renewal are local governments or local government consortiums with an existing SC designation. Renewal cycles occur on a five-year basis (e.g., 2017 renewal to 2022 renewal for Ellicott City).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted on or before the expiration date of the Sustainable Communities designation; amendments reviewed twice a year on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal and county governments seeking a Sustainable Community designation to access state revitalization resources, as well as nonprofits, businesses, individuals, developers, property owners, anchor institutions (higher education institutions, hospitals), local development agencies, and community development organizations located within designated Sustainable Community areas — including Baltimore City, Howard County, and Anne Arundel County — seeking reinvestment and revitalization support through state incentive programs. Also relevant to older communities statewide seeking reinvestment and revitalization support. Local governments with an existing SC designation are eligible to submit renewal applications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation, housing and economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, green development, affordable housing, community revitalization, commercial corridor investment, transit-oriented development, anchor institution investment, rehabilitation and revitalization of properties in designated Sustainable Communities areas, facade improvements, building rehabilitation, demolition and predevelopment, bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure, commercial kitchen development, small business support, flood mitigation, stormwater management, workforce development, community facilities, emergency services, food access, business retention and attraction, homeownership encouragement, mixed-use development, streetscape improvements, land assembly, environmental remediation, water quality improvements, tree planting and riparian buffers, complete streets and trail improvements, MARC connectivity, and unlocking eligibility for state programs focused on community reinvestment and revitalization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The proposed designation area must be within a Priority Funding Area and within or near a town center or transportation center, and must show a financial need for local revitalization. Projects must be located within a designated Sustainable Communities boundary to access state programs. Baltimore City's SC designation was approved November 26, 2012. Designated areas in Howard County include Ellicott City (approximately 350 acres including the Historic District, Main Street corridor, and West End), North Laurel-Savage, and Long Reach Village; in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park and Glen Burnie (approved 2013), and Odenton/Severn (approved 2014). Any organization or resident may submit a request to amend (expand) the SC boundary.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For designation: 1. Email Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov to request an application template, including the community name and sponsoring jurisdiction in the subject line. New designation applicants must schedule a meeting with program staff before applying. 2. Submit an application including a defined geographic area, a Sustainable Community Action Plan, and a local government resolution. 3. An interagency panel led by DHCD reviews the application. 4. The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 5. Once approved, the designation is valid for five years and must be renewed. For renewal: submit a renewal application to DHCD on or before the expiration date of the existing designation; the renewal includes an updated Sustainable Community Action Plan and report of accomplishments under the prior designation period. Renewal applications include multiple sections (Sections A–F) with checklist, attachments, GIS shapefiles, photos, action plan matrix, workgroup roster, and signature letter from the authorized local government official. For boundary amendments in Baltimore City: submit a request to the Baltimore City Planning Department at plan@baltimorecity.gov with the address of the area to be included and bullet points explaining alignment with the SC Action Plan. The Planning Department reviews the request in collaboration with other city agencies, and final approval is made by the State DHCD internal review committee. The requester receives a letter informing them of the decision. For Anne Arundel County information, contact Lynn Miller at 410-222-7431 at the Anne Arundel County Office of Planning and Zoning. For Howard County-specific information, visit https://www.howardcountymd.gov/planning-zoning/sustainable-communities. Once an area is designated, eligible organizations can apply to individual state programs (such as Community Legacy, Neighborhood BusinessWorks, or Strategic Demolition Fund) through DHCD. Designations are renewed every five years.
