structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) is the largest residential energy conservation program in the country. It helps income-eligible homeowners and renters reduce heating and cooling costs by an average of 30 to 35% through free installation of energy conservation measures, while also addressing health and safety issues in their homes. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Office of Energy Efficiency through local weatherization agencies across all Maryland counties. An energy auditor evaluates the home to identify areas of heat loss and air infiltration, then installs measures such as blower door air infiltration reduction, attic, floor, wall, basement, and crawl space insulation, caulking and air sealing around windows, doors, and crawl spaces, hot water system improvements including wrapping of hot water heaters and pipes, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning, tuning, or replacement, moisture control, HVAC and ductwork upgrades, and health and safety repairs. No lien or claim is filed against the home. Services are delivered at no cost to eligible households after an energy audit inspection. Low-income households that apply for energy assistance through the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) are automatically referred to WAP unless they opt out on their application; qualified applicants are then contacted by the WAP office before receiving benefits. Program funding comes through grants from the Maryland State Department of Housing and Community Development, with federal funding from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) WAP and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL), as well as EmPOWER Maryland funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Office of Energy Efficiency
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free weatherization services provided to income-eligible households, including blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation (attic, floors, walls, basement, crawl space), caulking and air sealing, hot water system improvements (including wrapping of hot water heaters and pipes), lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning/tuning/replacement, moisture control, HVAC and ductwork upgrades, and health and safety repairs. Services are delivered through local weatherization agencies after an energy audit inspection at no cost to the eligible household. No lien or claim is filed against the home. Program funding comes through grants from the Maryland State Department of Housing and Community Development, with federal funding from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) WAP and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL), as well as EmPOWER Maryland funds. Low-income OHEP energy assistance applicants are automatically referred to WAP and contacted by the WAP office prior to receiving benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible Maryland homeowners and renters statewide, including low-income households applying for energy assistance through OHEP, with priority given to households with members over age 60, those with disabilities, families with children under 5, and households with high energy usage or energy burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home weatherization improvements including air sealing, insulation (attic, floors, walls, basement, crawl space), hot water system upgrades and pipe wrapping, lighting retrofits, furnace repairs or replacement, caulking, moisture control, HVAC and ductwork upgrades, and health and safety items to reduce heating and cooling costs and improve energy efficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local weatherization agencies in each Maryland county. All 23 counties and Baltimore City are covered through the subgrantee network, though some counties (Anne Arundel, Carroll, Harford) are noted as currently lacking designated LWAs and are served by existing agencies. Previously administered locally in some counties (e.g., Prince George's County); all applications are now handled by the MD Office of Energy Efficiency.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a homeowner or renter in Maryland
Must meet household income limits: 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher
Households currently receiving SSI, TANF, SNAP, utility bill pay assistance through OHEP, or HUD housing assistance are automatically income-eligible
Priority given to households with members over age 60, persons with disabilities, families with children under 5, and high energy burden households
An application must be submitted to apply for services
Prove homeownership (if applying as homeowner)
Have not previously received weatherization services through the program
Home must be structurally sound
Must qualify through the OHEP energy assistance application (for OHEP referral pathway)
OHEP energy assistance applicants are automatically referred to WAP unless they opt out on their application
WAP office will contact qualified applicants prior to providing benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local weatherization agency (LWA) or submit an application to the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development by calling 1-855-583-8976. You may also apply for Energy Assistance through the Department of Human Services (OHEP) at 1-800-332-6347 to be screened and automatically referred to WAP unless you opt out. In Prince George's County, the program is no longer administered locally; call the MD Office of Energy Efficiency at 844-400-3423 or 1-800-756-0119 to apply. Once eligibility is determined, the LWA will schedule an energy audit inspection. If the home's condition permits, weatherization services are then provided at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_name: Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) — Prince George's County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) helps income-eligible households lower their energy costs by an average of 30 to 35% through free installation of energy conservation measures. An energy auditor evaluates the home to identify areas of heat loss and air infiltration, then installs measures such as attic, floor, wall, basement, and crawl space insulation; caulking and air sealing around windows, doors, and crawl spaces; and wrapping hot water heaters and pipes. No lien or claim is filed against the home.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Office of Energy Efficiency
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of energy conservation measures for income-eligible homeowners. No cost to eligible residents. Program is funded through a grant from the Maryland State Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners in Prince George's County who are elderly (60+), disabled, have children under 5, or have excessive energy consumption.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy conservation measures including insulation, air sealing, caulking, and wrapping of hot water heaters and pipes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland residents who are eligible homeowners.
requirements_list: Meet minimum income requirements (call Office of Energy Efficiency for details)
Prove homeownership
Be elderly (60+), disabled, have a family with children under 5 years old, and/or have excessive energy consumption
Have not previously received weatherization services through Prince George's County WAP or the MD Office of Energy Efficiency
Home must be structurally sound
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Maryland Office of Energy Efficiency at 844-400-3423 or 1-800-756-0119 to apply or get more information. The program is no longer administered by Prince George's County; all applications are now handled by the MD Office of Energy Efficiency.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MD-GAPS Connected Communities Grant Program provides grants to local governments, nonprofits, anchor institutions, and community-based organizations to build, upgrade, operate, or maintain community broadband gap networks. The goal is to provide low-cost or no-cost internet access to low- and moderate-income households and other underserved populations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Office of Statewide Broadband
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants ranging from $25,000 to $250,000. Grants may cover up to 100% of costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based broadband gap networks. Individual grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the intended population and the applicant's ability to deploy funds responsibly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), nonprofits (501(c) organizations), community-based anchor institutions, and other community-based organizations serving low- to moderate-income and other underserved populations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, networking hardware and software, and digital network technology to deliver broadband at 100 Mbps down/up to covered populations at low or no cost. Eligible activities include building new gap/community networks, upgrading or expanding existing networks, and operating and maintaining new or existing networks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must provide services within the State of Maryland and be registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, a 501(c) nonprofit, a community-based anchor institution, or another community-based organization
Must provide services within the State of Maryland
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Projects must reliably provide a minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up (with exceptions noted in the application guide)
Application must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding
Submit completed and signed application form, project summary, IRS determination letter (if nonprofit), Certificate of Good Standing, IRS W-9, and DUNS number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and all required attachments via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov. The application includes a project summary covering executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides limited financial help with funeral expenses when a deceased person was receiving Public Assistance or met eligibility requirements for a program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, and their family cannot afford funeral costs. A cash benefit is paid directly to the funeral director to cover eligible funeral expenses. Qualifying programs include Foster Care, Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Medical Assistance (MA), and Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Newborn children not receiving TCA may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A cash benefit paid directly to the funeral director to cover eligible funeral expenses. Burial plots, vaults, grave digging, and burial clothing are excluded from covered expenses. Funds cannot be used to reimburse expenses already paid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of deceased individuals who were receiving or eligible for Maryland Public Assistance programs, including Foster Care, Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Medical Assistance (MA), or Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Newborn children not receiving TCA may also be eligible. Family must be unable to afford funeral costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible funeral expenses for a deceased recipient of a qualifying Public Assistance program. Excludes burial plots, vaults, grave digging, and burial clothing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Deceased individual must have been receiving or eligible for a qualifying DHS-administered assistance program (Foster Care, PAA, TCA, TDAP, Medical Assistance, or SSI)
Family must be unable to afford funeral costs
Verification of assets, death, and funeral arrangements required
Funds cannot be used to reimburse expenses already paid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-800-332-6347 or fill out the contact form on the DHS website to apply for Burial Assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds services for families. These services include mediation, counseling, and parent education. It also helps develop parenting plans, enforce visitation, and create guidelines for visitation and custody.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to organizations. These organizations then offer services like mediation, counseling, parent education, and help with creating parenting plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments and non-profit organizations that provide family services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support services for families, including: mediation, counseling, parent education, developing parenting plans, enforcing visitation, and creating visitation guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must respond to a Request for Proposals (RFP) through the eMMA system.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) / My Groceries To Go!
structured_extraction.program_description: My Groceries To Go! (also known as CSFP) reduces food insecurity for low-income seniors by providing monthly food packages valued at approximately $50. The USDA funds the food packages, which are distributed through local agencies. Seniors can pick up their package at a food bank or local sponsor, have an authorized person pick it up, or in some communities receive home delivery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly food package valued at approximately $50, funded by the USDA and distributed through local partner agencies (Salvation Army, Capital Area Food Bank, and Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission). Packages are distributed via self pick-up, group pick-up, or home delivery. Participant or authorized proxy must sign food issuance document before receiving package.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income seniors age 60 or older with household income at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level living in eligible Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly food packages (contents set by FNS guidelines) to supplement the diets of eligible low-income seniors. Administrative funds cover payroll, mileage and allowable expenses, data management systems, capital expenditures, and management studies. Local agencies are responsible for ordering, shipping, collecting, packaging, and distributing monthly food packages; certification of participants; nutrition education; training; and monitoring distribution sites. Local agencies must maintain warehouseman's legal liability insurance covering spoilage, loss, and failure to rotate stock. USDA FNS approval is required prior to data system purchases, capital expenditures over $5,000, and outside consultant contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Allegany County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Queen Anne's County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years of age or older
Household income at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level
Must reside in an eligible Maryland county (Allegany, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Queen Anne's, Montgomery, or Prince George's County)

Identity verification required during application and box pickup processes using government-issued ID (may be expired) showing name and age/date of birth (e.g., driver's license, state ID, passport, alien registration, SSN card)
Participants may not receive benefits at more than one distribution site simultaneously
Participants may not be served more than once per month
Full certification required every 3 years; simplified re-certification every 12 months
Applicants will be notified of eligibility/ineligibility within 10 days of the date of application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of Maryland's CSFP providers to apply: the Salvation Army, Capital Area Food Bank, or Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission. Applicants must complete a state-developed certification form. Eligibility verification requires a government-issued ID showing name and age/date of birth (expired IDs acceptable); income must be certified at or below 150% of the federal poverty line for applicants age 60 or older; and household size must be identified. ID verification procedures are used during both the application and box pickup processes. Participant or authorized proxy must sign a food issuance document before receiving each package. This appears to be a continuous-intake program; deadlines, if any, are managed locally by the distributing agency.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland residents who have had SNAP, cash assistance, or Pandemic-EBT (P-EBT) benefits stolen from their EBT card can apply to have 100% of those stolen benefits replaced. The program covers theft going back to January 1, 2021, and replacement benefits are issued within 10 business days of claim approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHS replaces 100% of confirmed stolen EBT benefits (SNAP, cash assistance, or P-EBT). Replacement benefits are loaded onto the cardholder's EBT card within 10 business days of claim approval. Benefits stolen as far back as January 1, 2021 are eligible for replacement. Claims must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who receive SNAP, cash assistance, or P-EBT benefits on an EBT card and have had those benefits stolen without their permission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of stolen SNAP food benefits, cash assistance benefits, or Pandemic-EBT (P-EBT) benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current or former recipient of SNAP, cash assistance, or P-EBT benefits on an EBT card
Benefits must have been stolen (used without the cardholder's permission)
Must submit an EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim form
Claim must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft
Replacement is not available if the cardholder willingly gave their card and PIN to the person who stole the benefits
Theft must have occurred on or after January 1, 2021
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form online at marylandbenefits.gov, in person at a Local Department of Social Services office, or by mail. Community partner organizations are available to assist with completing the form by phone. DHS will make an eligibility decision within 10 business days and notify the claimant. Approved replacement benefits are loaded onto the claimant's EBT card.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland ETV program provides funds on a first-come, first-served basis to students currently in foster care and former foster care youth to help pay for education-related expenses, including tuition, books, fees, and other costs associated with college or vocational programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 per eligible student for education-related expenses, awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Maryland's student Financial Aid deadline is March 1st every year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current and former foster care youth seeking to pay for college or vocational education expenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education-related expenses including tuition, books, fees, and other costs associated with college or vocational programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to foster youth in Maryland attending eligible institutions.
requirements_list: Currently in foster care or a former foster care youth
Must submit the FAFSA by the March 1st state financial aid deadline each year
Funds awarded on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FAFSA online at studentaid.gov by the March 1st deadline each year. Contact your case worker for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Assistance to Families with Children (EAFC)
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency Assistance to Families with Children (EAFC) provides emergency cash assistance to families who need help paying rent or utilities or for other urgent needs. Funds are available through the local Department of Social Services once every two years, when funds are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency cash assistance available once every two years per family, when funds are available. Funds can be used for rent, utilities, or other qualifying emergencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with one or more children under age 21 who are facing an emergency such as eviction or utility shut-off.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent, utilities, or other qualifying emergencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services.
requirements_list: Must have one or more children under age 21 living in the household
Must present proof of an emergency not caused by a family member voluntarily quitting a job
Must present an eviction notice, utility cut-off notice, or other proof of emergency
Must provide identification
Must provide proof of address
Must provide proof of income for the past two months
Must provide Social Security numbers for all household members receiving services
Must provide proof of other cash or non-cash resources
Must provide proof of household expenses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local Department of Social Services, or submit an application by mail, fax, or other electronic means. You can also apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homelessness Prevention Program (HPP) helps individuals and families facing a housing crisis. It provides small, one-time crisis grants paid to landlords to prevent eviction, along with case management, counseling, budgeting and life skills training, tenant rights education, and landlord-tenant mediation. Households must have a lease in their name, demonstrate an ability to pay rent going forward, and comply with a documented case plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time direct grants paid to landlords to prevent eviction of qualifying households. Case management, budgeting and life skills training, tenant rights education, and landlord-tenant mediation are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families facing a housing crisis or risk of eviction who have a lease in their name and the ability to pay rent going forward.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants are paid to landlords to prevent eviction. Additional support covers case management, budgeting and life skills training, education on tenant rights and responsibilities, and mediation between landlord and tenant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services (DSS) in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a lease in their name
Must demonstrate the ability to pay rent going forward
The local DSS or service provider must determine the household can remain in or move to permanent housing
Must comply with a documented case plan
All policies applied consistently and in accordance with COMAR
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services (DSS) for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Human Services offers high school students in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County paid internships in the human services field. Participants receive mentorship from experienced professionals, real-world experience in areas like social work and child welfare, priority consideration for employment and scholarships covering up to 100% tuition, and a $500 stipend if hired after completing the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship with mentorship, real-world experience, priority hiring consideration, priority consideration for a scholarship covering up to 100% tuition, and a $500 employment stipend upon being hired after the program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will open for school year 2027-2028 in March 2027; closed for 2026-2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County with an interest in public service and human services fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid internship, mentorship, tuition scholarship consideration, and employment stipend for participants pursuing careers in human services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to high school students residing in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current high school student
Must be enrolled in a school in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, or Prince George's County
Must have a strong interest in public service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted via an online form on the DHS website. The application for school year 2027-2028 will open in March 2027. Contact DHShscpp.internship@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot scholarship program operated by the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) that provides 100% tuition and mandatory fees assistance to Maryland high school seniors and current higher education students who are pursuing credentials or degrees needed to fill high-demand DHS positions. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation working in eligible county jurisdictions after completing their education. The program targets specific positions including Child Support Specialist, Family Investment Specialist, Family Support Worker, Family Services Caseworker, and Social Worker series.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% of tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible Maryland public institution per Maryland Code, Education § 18-3902. Scholarships are automatically renewed each year as long as the recipient remains qualified (minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale). Recipients must fulfill a service obligation of 15 months per academic year funded through the scholarship, working in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents or graduates of Maryland high schools who are rising high school seniors or current higher education students seeking credentials or degrees to work in DHS-targeted positions (Child Support Specialist, Family Investment Specialist, Family Support Worker, Family Services Caseworker, or Social Worker series).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible Maryland public institution for a credential or degree program that qualifies the recipient for a targeted DHS position.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or graduates of a Maryland high school and must be accepted or enrolled at a public higher education institution in Maryland. Service obligation must be fulfilled in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or a graduate of a Maryland high school
Must be accepted for admission to, or currently enrolled in, a program leading to a credential or degree necessary to work in one of the five targeted DHS positions
Degree program must be at a public institution within Maryland
Must enter into an agreement with MHEC (Maryland Higher Education Commission) to fulfill a service obligation of 15 months per academic year funded
Service obligation must be fulfilled in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Prince George's County within 8 years of initial award
Must maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale to retain the scholarship
Must meet eligibility requirements as outlined in the Eligibility Requirements for the Human Services Scholarship Program document
Must be pursuing one of the targeted positions listed in the Targeted Positions, Salaries, and Qualifications document
Child Support Specialist Series: HS to AA degree; 0–5 years experience depending on grade
Family Investment Specialist Series: HS to BA degree; 1–4 years experience
Family Support Worker Series: HS diploma; 1–3 years support services experience
Family Services Caseworker Series: BA degree; 0–3 years casework experience
Social Worker Series: MSW plus license; 0–3 years child welfare/adult services experience
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application via the online Google Form linked on the program page. DHS human resources staff review applications based on statutory requirements and departmental priorities. Scholarship determinations are made within 30 days of the application deadline. Scholarships renew automatically each year if the recipient remains eligible. Additional details are available in the program documents including the Scholarship Flyer and Eligibility Requirements PDF. Contact dhs.hscscholarship@maryland.gov or call (410) 767-3300 for questions.
attachment_urls: https://dhs.maryland.gov/documents/Initiatives/The Human Services Careers Scholarship/Eligibility Requirements for the Human Services Scholarship Program.pdf
https://dhs.maryland.gov/documents/Initiatives/The Human Services Careers Scholarship/Targeted Positions, Salaries, and Qualifications.pdf

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides in-home aide services to adults with functional disabilities to help them remain living at home and avoid placement in nursing homes or other facilities. Services include personal care (dressing, bathing, grooming, eating), chores (cooking, laundry, cleaning, shopping), and other activities of daily living. Ongoing case management is also provided to help plan and explore other needed services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides in-home aide services on a subsidized basis. A sliding-scale fee may apply based on the applicant's income and family size. The fee, if any, is paid to the local Department of Social Services. The number of individuals served statewide depends on available funding, and a ranking scale prioritizes those with the greatest need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Maryland who have functional disabilities and need help with personal care, chores, or activities of daily living to remain in their own homes. Priority is given to vulnerable adults with no available caregiver, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home aide services covering personal care, household chores, and activities of daily living to support independent living at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of all counties and cities in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must reside in Maryland
Must have a functional disability
Must need assistance with personal care, chores, and/or activities of daily living to remain at home
Priority given to those with no willing or capable caregiver, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the local Department of Social Services in the county or city where the applicant lives. A local department representative will arrange a home visit to interview the applicant and assess their specific needs. A ranking scale is used to prioritize those with the greatest need based on available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Long Term Care Medical Assistance covers the cost of nursing home care and waiver-based community care for low-income individuals who meet eligibility requirements, including a look-back review of the applicant's resources for the five years prior to application. Applicants must meet income and asset eligibility criteria to qualify. The program is jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services and the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Applications may be submitted online, by mail to a local health department or local department of social services, or through the Office of Long Term Care at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD 21228, which handles applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers the cost of nursing home care and waiver-based community long-term care services for eligible low-income individuals who meet income and asset requirements, including a five-year look-back review of resources prior to application. Covered expenses may include long-term care facility costs, Medicare premiums (Parts A, B, C, D), other health insurance premiums, non-covered medical expenses (dentistry, audiology, vision), and shelter expenses for a spouse remaining in the community (rent, mortgage, utilities, taxes, insurance, condo fees).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals who require nursing home or waiver-based long-term care services and meet financial eligibility requirements, including income and asset criteria. Applicants with spouses and dependents are also considered. Eligible individuals include disabled persons, veterans, and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of nursing home care costs and waiver-based community long-term care services, including Medicare premiums (Parts A, B, C, D), other health insurance premiums, non-covered medical expenses (dentistry, audiology, vision), and shelter expenses for a spouse remaining in the community (rent, mortgage, utilities, taxes, insurance, condo fees).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Maryland residency is required. The Office of Long Term Care at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD 21228 handles applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a U.S. citizen or lawful immigrant
Must be a low-income individual requiring nursing home or waiver-based long-term care services
Must meet eligibility requirements including income and asset criteria
Subject to a look-back review of resources for the five years prior to application (or 12 months for annual redetermination)
Must provide true, correct, and complete financial information
Must disclose all asset transfers within the 60-month (5-year) period prior to month of application
Must report changes within 10 days
Must provide Social Security number(s)
If approved, the Department may recover from the estate of a deceased recipient age 55 or older if no surviving spouse, child under 21, or blind/disabled child exists
Federal law requires the Department to be named as primary remainder beneficiary in applicant's annuity as a condition of receiving LTC services
Failure to complete redetermination will result in cancellation of Medical Assistance coverage
Application requires 5 years of tax returns, bank statements, and asset verification documentation
Application requires unpaid medical bills from prior 3 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://marylandbenefits.gov, or mail the application (DHS/FIA 9709) to your local health department or local department of social services. Applications for Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County are handled by the Office of Long Term Care, 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD 21228. Do not wait to apply. Extensive supporting documentation is required, including 5 years of tax returns, bank statements, asset statements, income verification, property deeds, and medical insurance cards. Existing recipients must complete periodic redetermination (DHS/FIA 9709R) to maintain eligibility.
