structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) is a tax benefit for working people with low to moderate income. If you qualify for the federal EITC and claim it on your federal tax return, you may be entitled to a Maryland EITC on your state return equal to 50% of the federal tax credit. The credit will reduce or eliminate the amount of state and local income tax you owe. Free tax preparation help is available through the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program, and electronic filing with direct deposit into up to 3 separate bank accounts is also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Maryland state tax credit equal to 50% of the federal EITC. The credit reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed. Free tax preparation help is available through the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program for people earning $67,000 or less (2024 tax year), persons with disabilities, and limited English speakers. IRS-certified volunteers e-file returns and arrange direct deposit of refunds into up to 3 separate bank accounts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and working individuals and families with low to moderate income (under $67,000 in 2024) who qualify for the federal EITC, including persons with disabilities and limited English speakers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces or eliminates Maryland state and local income tax liability. Free tax preparation services, electronic filing, and direct deposit of refunds into up to 3 separate bank accounts are also available through the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with free tax preparation centers serving all counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, and Wicomico.
requirements_list: Must qualify for and claim the federal Earned Income Tax Credit on your federal tax return
Must have earned income under $67,000 (2024 tax year)
Social Security card or ITIN for all family members and photo ID for each taxpayer
W-2 forms for all jobs worked during the tax year
Form 1099-G if unemployment was received (if applicable)
Child care provider letter with address, Tax ID, child name, and amount paid (if applicable)
Banking information for direct deposit of refund
Prior year tax return
Form 1095-A if received
All adults must sign in person at the tax preparation site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the Maryland EITC on your Maryland state income tax return after claiming the federal EITC. Free tax preparation is available through VITA/CASH sites across Maryland. Call 800-492-0618 or visit cashmd.org to find local tax prep centers. Bring required documents to a free tax site where IRS-certified volunteers will e-file your return and arrange direct deposit of your refund. Use the IRS EITC Assistant online to check eligibility and estimate your credit amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland SUN Bucks (also known as Summer EBT) helps families with school-aged children who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals buy groceries during summer break when school meals are unavailable. Eligible children receive $40 per month for June, July, and August ($120 total per child) loaded onto an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card. The program is run in partnership with the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS), the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), and the USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible children receive $40 per month loaded onto an EBT card for June, July, and August, totaling $120 per child. Benefits are added to an existing SNAP EBT card if the household has one, or issued on a new white Maryland SUN Bucks card. Benefits expire 122 days after issuance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted year-round; FARMS determination must occur before August 31, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-aged children (ages 5–18) enrolled in Maryland schools that participate in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and who meet income eligibility guidelines for free or reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase eligible food items at stores and vendors that accept EBT, including most large grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and some authorized online retailers. Cannot be used for alcohol, tobacco, non-food items, or hot/prepared food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Children must be enrolled in a Maryland school (public, charter, or private) that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP). Virtual schools and homeschools do not qualify.
requirements_list: Child must be enrolled in a Maryland school participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP)
Child must be between ages 5 and 18

Child must meet one of the following: applied for and received free or reduced-price meals at school in the prior school year; is part of a household receiving SNAP, TCA, or Medicaid/Medical Assistance; is in foster care; is homeless, migrant, or runaway; OR applies and is determined eligible for FARMS before August 31, 2025
Family must meet Maryland SUN Bucks income guidelines (based on NSLP income eligibility guidelines)
All immigration statuses are eligible — participation does not affect immigration status
EBT card PIN must be 4 digits
PIN cannot include common PINs, two repeating digits, or two consecutive digits (e.g., 1234, 1111)
PIN must be kept private and never shared
Have Maryland SUN Bucks Card and date of birth of cardholder ready before calling activation line
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Most eligible students are automatically enrolled — no action needed if the child received free or reduced-price meals last school year, is in a SNAP/TCA/Medicaid household, or is in foster care. Households not automatically enrolled (e.g., children in Community Eligibility Provision schools not receiving SNAP/TCA/Medicaid and not in foster care) must apply online at marylandbenefits.gov or submit a paper application. Applications are accepted year-round. Call 1-800-332-6347 and select the Maryland SUN Bucks option for assistance. To activate a new SUN Bucks card and set a PIN, call 800-997-2222, follow the voice prompts, enter your card number and date of birth (enter 0000 when prompted for SSN last 4 digits), then select and confirm a 4-digit PIN. Upon successful PIN selection, you will receive a confirmation message: 'You have successfully selected your PIN. Your card is ready to use.'

structured_extraction.program_description: Medical Assistance (also called Medicaid) is a state and federally funded health coverage program that pays medical bills and provides free or low-cost health insurance for eligible low-income and needy Maryland residents. Covered populations include individuals who are aged, blind, disabled, living in a nursing home, or otherwise medically needy, as well as low-income families with dependent children, children under 21, pregnant women, and adults under 65. A key component, Medical Assistance for Families, provides free and full health care coverage to low-income families with dependent children whose annual household income does not exceed 116% of the federal poverty level, an eligibility expansion in effect since July 2008. Covered services include inpatient and outpatient hospital care, physician and doctor visits, pharmacy and prescription costs, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, dental, vision, preventive care, pregnancy care, family planning, lab tests, immunizations, Medicare premium payments, and other health services. No fees or payments are required from recipients; managed care organization (MCO) plans are available. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through 24 local departments of social services, with local assistance also available through the Howard County Health Department, Carroll County Health Department, and the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost health insurance coverage for eligible low-income individuals and families, paying medical bills including inpatient and outpatient hospital care, physician care, pharmacy and prescription costs, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, doctor visits, exams, dental (via Maryland Healthy Smiles), vision, preventive care, pregnancy and prenatal care, family planning, lab tests, immunizations, Medicare premium payments, and other health services, using federal and state funds. For families with dependent children, full health care coverage is available at no cost when household income does not exceed 116% of the federal poverty level. No fees or payments are required from recipients; managed care organization (MCO) plans are available (including Aetna Better Health of Maryland, AMERIGROUP Community Care, Jai Medical Systems, Kaiser Permanente, Maryland Physicians Care, MedStar Family Choice, Priority Partners, UnitedHealthcare, and CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield Community Health Plan of Maryland as of 2022). Local resources are available through 24 county departments of social services statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income and needy Maryland residents who meet income and eligibility requirements, including individuals who are aged, blind, disabled, living in a nursing home, or otherwise medically needy, as well as low-income families with dependent children whose annual household income does not exceed 116% of the federal poverty level (FPL), children under 19 (MCHP) or under 21 (Medicaid), pregnant women, and adults under 65.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of medical bills and health care costs including inpatient and outpatient hospital care, physician care, pharmacy and prescription costs, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, doctor visits, exams, dental (via Maryland Healthy Smiles), vision, preventive care, pregnancy and prenatal care, family planning, lab tests, immunizations, Medicare premium payments, and other health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through DHS's 24 local departments of social services. Howard County residents can contact the Howard County Health Department at 8930 Stanford Blvd, Columbia, MD 21045 or call 410-313-5845. Carroll County residents can contact the Carroll County Health Department for local assistance (410-876-4811). Montgomery County residents can access information and resources through the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services at regional offices in Silver Spring, Rockville, and Germantown.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a low-income or needy individual or family
Must meet income and need guidelines for low-income individuals

Must be aged, blind, disabled, living in a nursing home, or medically needy (for individual/general Medicaid eligibility), or qualify under another coverage group such as families, children under 21, or pregnant women
Annual household income must not exceed 116% of the federal poverty level (FPL) for families with dependent children
Must be a U.S. citizen, legal permanent resident, or qualified alien (including refugees and asylees)
Family must have dependent children (for Medical Assistance for Families eligibility)
Must meet program eligibility criteria determined by a case manager
Proof of income required (tax return or two recent pay stubs)
Proof of identity required (driver's license or photo ID)
Proof of citizenship required (birth certificate or passport)
Social Security number required
Pregnant women may qualify under the Healthy Babies Equity Act (regardless of immigration status) or Full Medicaid (U.S. citizens and lawfully present individuals)
SSI recipients should contact their local office to apply
Must report life and income changes to maintain eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at mymdthink.maryland.gov, marylandhealthconnection.gov, or marylandbenefits.gov; call the Maryland Health Connection Call Center at 1-855-642-8572 or DHS at 1-800-332-6347; use the Enroll MHC mobile app; submit by mail; or visit one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services in person. Carroll County residents can contact the Carroll County Health Department by phone at 410-876-4811 or by email during office hours (Monday–Friday, 8am–5pm). Howard County residents can contact the Howard County Health Department at 410-313-5845 or in person at 8930 Stanford Blvd., Columbia, MD 21045 (Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). Montgomery County residents may visit the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services at regional offices in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown; applications are processed in approximately 10 days. Upon enrollment, applicants choose or are auto-assigned an MCO; insurance card is typically received within 14 days. Interpreter services are available for non-English speakers, and relay service is available for deaf/hard of hearing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mobile Point of Sale Equipment Program (MPOSEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MPOSEP provides grants to Farmers Markets and individual farmers or vendors to purchase mobile point of sale (mPOS) equipment for processing Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) / SNAP transactions. The program aims to help Maryland farmers access the SNAP recipient market, which represents over $1.1 billion in food assistance issued annually by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Grants of up to $600 are available and remain open until all grant funds have been exhausted within the fiscal year cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $600 are provided to cover the purchase of mobile point of sale (mPOS) equipment and associated app services used to process EBT/SNAP transactions at farmers markets. Applications remain open until all grant funds have been exhausted within the fiscal year cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open until all grant funds have been exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers Markets and individual farmers or vendors who sell at Maryland Farmers Markets and are authorized or seeking authorization as SNAP retailers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of mobile point of sale (mPOS) devices and application (app) services to process EBT/SNAP transactions at farmers markets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must participate in a Farmers Market that meets the state definition and appears in the Maryland Farmers Market Directory.
requirements_list: Must be a Farmers Market or a dedicated vendor in at least one Maryland Farmers Market that meets the state definition
Complete USDA eAuthentication Account Registration
Apply and become authorized as a SNAP-authorized retailer with the USDA
Provide proof of Farmers Market vendor membership and authorized FNS number
Vendor applicants must indicate vendor category (Farmer Vendor, Value Added Vendor, or Prepared Food Vendor) and provide relevant permits and/or certifications
Choose an mPOS device/application service
Submit all requested documentation with the grant application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete USDA eAuthentication registration, obtain SNAP retailer authorization, gather proof of farmers market participation and FNS authorization number, then apply for an MPOSEP grant and submit all required documentation to DHS. Applications are open until all grant funds have been exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Home, also known as the C.A.R.E. (Certified Adult Residential Environment) Program, is a supportive housing program for adults with mental illness or other disabilities. It uses an adult foster family model of care, placing residents in a stable, family-like living arrangement in the community as a less costly alternative to nursing homes, psychiatric hospitals, or other institutional settings. Residents receive opportunities for growth and independent living skills development. Case management services connect residents to community activities and supports. Certified care providers open their homes to residents and provide room, board, daily living assistance, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and transportation to medical appointments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents receive financial assistance for room and board in a certified adult foster family home. Care providers are reimbursed at rates based on resident needs and level-of-care system for room, board, supervision, and assistance provided to residents. Residents may also access Public Assistance to Adults and Medical Assistance for cost-sharing. Providers must demonstrate they have sufficient independent income to meet their own needs. Service plans are reassessed at least every 6 months or as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 or older with a mental, developmental, or physical disability, including elderly adults unable to live alone, who are willing and able to live in a family setting. Also targets individuals age 21 or older who can serve as certified care providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Room, board, supervision, assistance with activities of daily living, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and transportation to medical appointments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; administered through local Departments of Social Services offices in all 24 Maryland counties: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older
Must have a documented mental, developmental, or physical disability
Must be willing and able to live in a family setting
Documentation of disability, income, and functional capability required
Residents who take medication must be able to self-medicate or learn to self-medicate with cuing and coaching
Must be able to access community resources and maintain or develop independent living skills
Care providers must be age 21 or older and reside in the home
Care providers must be recruited, screened, and certified
Providers must work with the local DSS case manager and resident to develop and implement a treatment plan
Providers must participate in training provided by the local DSS
Providers must demonstrate an attitude of acceptance towards others
Providers must demonstrate they have sufficient independent income to meet their own needs without relying on Program Home reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Please apply at your local Department of Social Services. Care providers are recruited, screened, and certified to open their homes. Residents apply and must provide documentation of disability, income, and functional capability. Applications are accepted at all 24 county/local DSS offices statewide. Service plans are reassessed at least every 6 months or as needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Assistance to Adults program pays for the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for individuals who live in assisted living facilities licensed by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and in Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (also known as Project Home). PAA also pays only the personal needs allowance to people in MDH Rehabilitative Residences. Recipients are also eligible for Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PAA pays for the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for eligible individuals in licensed assisted living facilities or Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home). For individuals in MDH Rehabilitative Residences, PAA pays only the personal needs allowance. Recipients are also eligible for Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults in licensed assisted living facilities, Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home), or MDH Rehabilitative Residences who meet technical and financial eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of care in eligible residential settings and a personal needs allowance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must meet technical and financial eligibility criteria
Must apply for Social Security Administration (SSA) benefits as a condition of eligibility
Cost of care must be greater than the applicant's countable income
Assets must not exceed the allowable limit
The assistance unit is always one person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/).

structured_extraction.program_description: PA2E offers entrepreneurship training classes for Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) customers who receive public assistance and want to start a small business. The program runs for approximately 6 weeks, covering 8 courses that include Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Creating a Business Plan, Credit Restoration, A to Z Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Classes meet 1-2 times per week (approximately 2 hours each) and are offered virtually and/or in a classroom setting in spring and fall sessions. DHS partners with Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) across the state to deliver the program, including dedicated presences in Anne Arundel County and Howard County. Participants also receive access to SBDC business consultants and earn a Workforce Development Training Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately 6-week training program consisting of 8 courses (1-2 sessions per week, ~2 hours each) covering Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Creating a Business Plan, Credit Restoration, A to Z Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Classes are offered virtually and/or in a classroom setting in spring and fall sessions. Participants also receive access to SBDC business consultants and earn a Workforce Development Training Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland DHS customers including SNAP recipients, Temporary Cash Assistance recipients, non-custodial parents, foster youth, and veterans receiving assistance who want to start a small business. Anne Arundel County residents who receive public assistance through DHS are also eligible. Howard County residents may contact Howard County Department of Social Services at howco.dss@maryland.gov or 410-872-8700.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Entrepreneurship training and business start-up education to help participants start a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through regional SBDC partnerships, including dedicated programs in Anne Arundel County and Howard County.
requirements_list: Must be a current Maryland Department of Human Services customer (public assistance recipient)
Eligible groups include SNAP recipients, Temporary Cash Assistance recipients, non-custodial parents, foster youth, and veterans receiving assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the Google Form linked on the program page at dhs.maryland.gov/workforce-development/public-assistance-entrepreneurship-pa2e. Anne Arundel County residents may also visit the PA2E program page at https://www.aacounty.org/workforce-development/public-assistance-entrepreneurship-pa2e/ for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial reimbursement to informal family caregivers for short-term, temporary (periodic) care of individuals with developmental or functional disabilities. The program gives caregivers a period of rest and renewal by temporarily relieving them of caregiving responsibilities. Respite care can be provided at planned intervals, in a time of crisis, or on an as-needed basis. Family caregivers are responsible for identifying a care provider. The program serves children and adults with developmental disabilities and adults with functional disabilities and their families. It is funded by the Department of Human Services (DHS) and administered by agencies throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement to informal family caregivers for short-term, temporary (periodic) respite care costs. An informal family caregiver is an unpaid individual who routinely cares for someone with a developmental or functional disability without compensation. Family caregivers are responsible for identifying the care provider.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Informal family caregivers who routinely and without compensation care for a child or adult with a developmental disability, or an adult with a functional disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term, temporary (periodic) care for individuals with developmental or functional disabilities to provide the family caregiver a period of rest and relief from caregiving responsibilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services and agencies contracted throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an informal family caregiver — an individual who routinely cares for someone with a developmental or functional disability without compensation.
The care recipient must have a developmental disability (children or adults) or a functional disability (adults).
Caregiver must not be compensated for the care provided.
Family caregiver must identify the care provider.
Applicant must contact their local Department of Social Services or contracted agency to apply.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services or the local agency that covers your area via DHS's website and speak with a caseworker, who will assess your unique needs and walk you through next steps. You can also call DHS's Constituent Services Unit at 1-800-332-6347 or TTY 1-800-925-4434. Find your local office at dhs.maryland.gov/local-offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) allows elderly (age 60 or older), disabled, and homeless SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) recipients in Maryland to use their EBT (Electronic Benefit Transfer) card to purchase prepared or hot food from participating restaurants and delis. The program does not provide additional benefit funds — it expands where existing SNAP benefits can be spent. Eligible SNAP households experiencing homelessness may also purchase meals at a concessional (discounted) price from restaurants that have contracted with the federal government to participate. Participating restaurants are not permitted to charge sales tax under the program. Restaurants interested in participating must apply to the USDA for authorization to accept EBT payments and sign a Memorandum of Understanding with MD DHS. The program is available statewide in Maryland and is currently piloting in select counties with plans to expand to additional jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible SNAP recipients (elderly age 60+, disabled, or homeless) can use their existing SNAP EBT benefits to purchase prepared or hot meals at participating restaurants and delis. The program does not change the recipient's benefit amount — it expands where benefits can be spent. Homeless SNAP households may purchase meals at a concessional (discounted) price from federally contracted restaurants. Participating restaurants are not allowed to charge sales tax under the program. Restaurants must apply to USDA using the FNS 252-2 form and sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MD DHS to participate. MD DHS collects all required documentation and submits the package to USDA Food and Nutrition Service. USDA has 45 days to make an authorization decision. After authorization, restaurants must set up Point of Sale (POS) equipment to accept EBT payments. Note: The FNS-252-2 application form on file carries an OMB expiration date of 01/31/2024; applicants should confirm the current form version with MD DHS.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly (age 60+), disabled, and homeless SNAP recipients in Maryland; restaurants and delis (including drug/alcohol treatment programs, meal delivery services, communal dining facilities, homeless meal providers, shelters for battered women and children, group living arrangements, and senior citizens centers) interested in accepting EBT as payment for prepared or hot meals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of prepared or hot meals at participating restaurants and delis using existing SNAP EBT benefits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; currently piloting in select counties with plans to expand to additional jurisdictions. Recipients may also use benefits at RMP-participating restaurants in other states that run the program (e.g., Virginia).
requirements_list: Recipient must be an active SNAP participant in Maryland

Recipient must meet at least one qualifying criterion: experiencing homelessness, age 60 or older (includes qualifying spouse), or disabled (includes spouse if they are the only two members on the SNAP case)
Eligibility is reviewed at every SNAP recertification/redetermination
Restaurants must apply to USDA using the FNS 252-2 Application Form for Meal Services and be authorized to accept EBT payments
Restaurants must be private, for-profit establishments where 50% or more of gross sales are in prepared foods where meals are sold or served
Restaurants must sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MD DHS

Restaurants must provide required documentation including government-issued photo ID, Social Security Number verification for all owners/partners/officers, and a valid business license or health permit for each location
A business cannot be both a licensed food retailer/grocery store and a restaurant under the program — one authorization only

Eligible meal service providers also include drug/alcohol treatment programs, meal delivery services, communal dining facilities, homeless meal providers, shelters for battered women and children, group living arrangements, and senior citizens centers (public/private nonprofit or publicly operated as applicable)
Owner/principal must certify truthfulness of application and accepts responsibility for staff compliance with SNAP rules; sanctions/disqualification possible for violations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Recipients: Use your existing EBT card at participating restaurants — no separate application required, though eligibility is confirmed automatically at SNAP recertification. Restaurants: (1) Reach out to Annette Jones-Wilson at annette.jones-wilson@maryland.gov to obtain and sign a Memorandum of Understanding with MD DHS. (2) Complete the USDA FNS 252-2 Application Form for Meal Services (confirm current form version with MD DHS as the previously linked form carried a 01/31/2024 OMB expiration). (3) Gather required documentation (government-issued photo ID, Social Security Number verification for all owners/partners/officers, valid business license or health permit). (4) Submit the complete application package to MD DHS, which forwards it to USDA Food and Nutrition Service. USDA has 45 days to make an authorization decision. (5) After authorization, set up Point of Sale (POS) equipment to accept EBT payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's SNAP Outreach Program works with community-based organizations to inform and educate the public about Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. The program helps eligible individuals and families learn about SNAP, addresses misinformation and stigma around receiving benefits, and connects people with organizations that can help them apply. It is funded through federal funds and private contributions from program partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program connects residents with community-based organizations that can help them apply for SNAP benefits. Organizations provide outreach, education, and application assistance to eligible individuals and families. The program is funded through federal funds and private contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who may be eligible for SNAP benefits but are unaware of or need help applying for the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach, education, and application assistance for SNAP benefits to help individuals and families purchase healthy food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident who may qualify for SNAP benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the SNAP Outreach Community Based Organizations page and contact the organization closest to your address. If no organization serves your area, contact any statewide organization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Social Services to Adults (SSTA) program is the Maryland Department of Human Services' core case management program for vulnerable adults. It helps adults with limited capacities remain or become self-supporting and self-sufficient, prevents abuse, neglect, or exploitation, and reduces unnecessary institutionalization or secures appropriate institutional care when needed. The program builds on the adult's existing community and family support systems rather than replacing them. Services include information and referral, crisis intervention (up to 60 days of intensive help and guidance), and ongoing case management delivered by a social worker with an individualized plan of service. The program is provided free of charge through local departments of social services in each Maryland county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free case management services provided through local departments of social services. Services include: Information and Referral (connecting adults to other agencies best suited to meet their needs); Crisis Intervention (up to 60 days of intensive help and guidance for adults facing a crisis or major life change); and Case Management (comprehensive needs assessment and individualized plan of service developed with a Social Worker to support independent living in the community or secure appropriate institutional care when necessary).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vulnerable adults with functional disabilities — adults age 65 and older (regardless of income) or adults under age 65 with disabilities whose income does not exceed 80% of the State median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and referral, crisis intervention (up to 60 days), and ongoing case management services to support adults in maintaining independence in the community, preventing abuse/neglect/exploitation, and securing appropriate institutional care when necessary.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services in each Maryland county.
requirements_list: Must be an adult with functional disabilities
Adults aged 65 or older are eligible regardless of income
Adults under age 65 with disabilities must have income that does not exceed 80% of the State median income
Must apply through the local department of social services in your county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the local department of social services in your county. Services are provided free of charge.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) / Food Supplement Program (FSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), known in Maryland as the Food Supplement Program (FSP), is the largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation. It helps low-income households buy food they need for good health. In Maryland, eligible households receive monthly food benefits loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card called the Independence Card, which works like a debit card at authorized retailers. Benefits can be used to purchase groceries in store, shop online at participating retailers (including Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, and Safeway), or dine at participating restaurants through the Restaurant Meals Program. SNAP benefits cannot be used to pay for shipping or delivery fees. Benefit amounts are based on the USDA Thrifty Food Plan (updated annually) and depend on household size and net monthly income after allowable deductions, including a standard deduction, 20% of earned income, dependent care costs, child support payments, shelter and utility expenses, and medical expenses over $35/month for members age 60+ or disabled, all calibrated to the USDA Maximum Allotment adjusted annually for food prices. Gross monthly income must be under 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL); net income must be under 100% FPL; categorical eligibility is available at 200% FPL. Benefit amounts range from $298 to $1,789 per month for households of 1–8 members; additional persons add proportionally. Standard benefits are issued within 30 days of application. Expedited SNAP benefits may be available within 7 days for very low-income households with little or no money, requiring only an interview and identity verification. Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) ages 18–64 must work, join a SNAP Employment & Training program, or volunteer at least 80 hours per month to maintain benefits, starting November 1, 2025, with a 3-month grace period available between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026. In Maryland, the program is administered by the Department of Human Services through local Departments of Social Services across all counties. Everyone has the right to apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly food benefits loaded onto an EBT card (Independence Card) to help eligible households purchase food and groceries at authorized retailers, including online grocery shopping at participating retailers (Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, Safeway) and, in some cases, at participating restaurants through the Restaurant Meals Program. SNAP benefits cannot be used to pay for shipping or delivery fees. Benefit amounts are based on household size and remaining monthly income after allowable deductions (standard deduction, 20% of earned income, dependent care costs, child support payments, shelter and utility expenses, and medical expenses over $35/month for members age 60+ or disabled), calibrated to the USDA Maximum Allotment (Thrifty Food Plan) adjusted annually for food prices. Income guidelines effective 10/01/2025 (revised 08/2025). Gross monthly income must not exceed 130% FPL; net income must not exceed 100% FPL; categorical eligibility available at 200% FPL. Benefit amounts range from $298 to $1,789 per month for households of 1–8 members. Standard benefits are issued within 30 days of application; expedited benefits may be available within 7 days for qualifying very low-income households. ABAWDs ages 18–64 must work, join a SNAP Employment & Training program, or volunteer at least 80 hours per month to maintain benefits starting November 1, 2025; a 3-month grace period is available between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and households in Maryland with gross monthly income under 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) and net income under 100% FPL (or categorical eligibility at 200% FPL), including working low-wage earners, unemployed or part-time workers, recipients of public assistance, elderly or disabled individuals on small incomes, homeless persons, U.S. citizens, and certain eligible non-citizens such as refugees, asylees, and lawful permanent residents with 'qualified immigrant' status. Also includes Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) ages 18–64 who must meet work requirements starting November 1, 2025. Special populations served through the E&T partner network include veterans, at-risk youth, ex-offenders, opportunity youth, foster care youth, underemployed individuals, single parents, and low-income residents. Household members must purchase and prepare food together and meet income and citizenship/immigration eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible food items and groceries at authorized retailers to prepare nutritious meals for the household, including online grocery shopping at participating retailers (Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, Safeway). Benefits can also be used at participating restaurants through the Restaurant Meals Program. SNAP benefits cannot be used to pay for shipping or delivery fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Departments of Social Services. Apply at your local Department of Social Services (including regional offices in Montgomery County: MidCounty, Silver Spring, UpCounty, or the TESS Center; and Prince George's County service centers), by mail, by fax, or online at MarylandBenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov). Carroll County residents may also contact the Division of Aging & Disabilities at 410-386-3800 for application assistance. Interpretation services are available free of charge for limited English proficiency customers.
requirements_list: Must file a signed application (DHS/FIA Form 9701, Application for Assistance, revised 07/2024)
Must complete an interview with a case manager (phone or in-person)
Must meet all financial and technical eligibility factors including income limits (see Income Guidelines effective 10/01/2025, revised 08/2025)
Gross monthly income must be under 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)
Net monthly income must be under 100% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)
Categorical eligibility available at 200% FPL per SNAP Manual Section 115
Must work for low wages, be unemployed or part-time, receive public assistance, be elderly or disabled on a small income, or be homeless
Household members must live together and buy and prepare food together

Must meet citizenship or eligible immigrant status requirements (U.S. citizens required; non-citizens with 'qualified immigrant' status such as refugees, asylees, and lawful permanent residents may also qualify)
Must provide a Social Security number for each household member (except undocumented immigrants applying on behalf of others)
Must provide proof of identity, Social Security number, proof of residence, proof of income, and proof of citizenship or immigration status (for non-U.S. born applicants)
Must provide verification of income, legal immigrant status (if applicable), child support payments, and medical expenses for members age 60+ or disabled
Must answer all application questions completely and honestly
Able-bodied adults ages 16–60 must generally register for work, accept suitable work offers, and participate in employment and training when referred

Most college students ages 18–49 enrolled at least half-time are ineligible unless they meet specific exceptions (e.g., work 20+ hours/week, receive TCA cash assistance, participate in work-study, care for a child under 6, or have a disability)

For Expedited SNAP: must have little or no money (household income under $150/month and cash/savings at or below $100; or shelter costs exceed income and resources; or migrant/seasonal farm worker status); only an interview and identity verification required — benefits may be issued within 7 days
ABAWDs ages 18–64 must work, join a SNAP Employment & Training program, or volunteer at least 80 hours per month to maintain benefits starting November 1, 2025

Exemptions from ABAWD work requirements apply for individuals under 18 or 65+, caregivers of children under 6 or dependent adults, those already working 30+ hours/week or earning $217.50+/week, unemployment benefit recipients, certain Native American individuals, those with physical or mental health limitations, half-time students, TANF work-rule compliant individuals, and those living with a household member under age 14
A 3-month grace period for ABAWDs is available between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026
Households applying for or receiving SSI may apply at their Social Security district office
Must report changes in household circumstances within 10 days
Must report lottery/gambling winnings of $3,500 or more within 10 days
False statements, benefit trading, and unauthorized EBT card use are prohibited; penalties include disqualification, fines up to $250,000, and imprisonment up to 20 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov), in person at a local Department of Social Services or local service center, by phone at 1-800-332-6347, by mail, by fax, or by downloading and submitting the DHS/FIA Form 9701 (Application for Assistance, revised 07/2024). Applications can also be submitted at Montgomery County regional offices (MidCounty, Silver Spring, UpCounty) or the TESS Center on a walk-in basis or by appointment, or at Prince George's County service centers. Carroll County residents may contact the Division of Aging & Disabilities at 410-386-3800 for help starting the application. SNAP benefit eligibility is based on the date you sign the application and give it to the Department of Social Services; the office accepts signed applications the same day they are received. Applicants must complete an application, attend an interview with a case manager (in most cases by telephone), and provide required documentation (proof of income, Social Security numbers, immigration status if applicable, and other verification documents) within the timeframe specified at interview. After the interview, a notice is sent explaining eligibility and benefit amount. Benefits are issued within 30 days; expedited benefits within 7 days for qualifying households with little or no money. Language interpreter services are available free of charge for applicants with limited English proficiency. This is a rolling/continuous intake program with no application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's SNAP E&T program connects residents who receive SNAP (food supplement) benefits to free, job-driven training programs. Programs typically run an average of 12 to 16 weeks and train participants for employment in in-demand industries such as welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and information technology/computer technology. All programs also offer job placement, retention, and support services to help graduates find and keep employment. Participants have access to a personal career navigator and success coach, as well as assistance resolving employment barriers such as criminal records, driver's licenses, work clothing, and tools. Participants not yet receiving SNAP can apply for benefits at marylandbenefits.gov or at a local DSS office.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job-driven training programs lasting an average of 12 to 16 weeks. Programs provide hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers (such as criminal records, driver's licenses, work clothing, and tools/supplies), and access to support services. A personal career navigator and success coach are also available. No formal application is required; participants enroll through local Departments of Social Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 16 and older who currently receive SNAP (food supplement) benefits, do not receive Cash Assistance/TANF, and are able to work upon completion of the program. Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) who want to maintain full SNAP benefits beyond three months must work or enroll in an employment and training program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free job-driven occupational training and employment support services including job placement and retention services, transportation, work clothing and supplies, industry-recognized certifications, referrals to community services, career navigation, and assistance resolving employment barriers such as criminal records, limited job experience, or transportation challenges.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Departments of Social Services and third-party training providers.
requirements_list: Must be age 16 or older
Must currently receive SNAP (food supplement) benefits
Must not receive Cash Assistance/TANF
Must be able to work upon completion of the program
Individual training programs may have additional eligibility requirements
Participation is voluntary for most SNAP recipients
Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) must work or enroll in an employment and training program to maintain full SNAP benefits beyond three months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application is required. Interested individuals should contact their local Department of Social Services (DSS) or call the DHS helpline at 1-800-332-6347 to learn about and find available programs in their area. Those not yet receiving SNAP can apply for benefits at marylandbenefits.gov or at a local DSS office. A directory of SNAP E&T training providers is available on the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) is Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) program. It provides cash assistance to families with dependent children when their available resources do not fully cover the family's needs. The program also helps participants prepare for financial independence through work activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash assistance payments for families with dependent children whose earned and unearned income does not exceed the benefit level for their household size. Benefits can be received via direct deposit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with dependent children who have limited financial resources and need temporary cash support while working toward employment and self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance for general family needs when available resources are insufficient.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Family must cooperate with child support
Must participate in work activities
Must comply with substance abuse provisions
Must meet financial and technical eligibility requirements
Earned and unearned income cannot exceed the benefit level paid for the assistance unit size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov, or apply in person at a Local Department of Social Services office. Applications can also be submitted by mail, fax, or other electronic means, or dropped off by another person on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP) provides cash benefits to low-income, disabled Marylanders during a period of short-term disability or while they await approval of federal disability support. The program is state-funded and available to individuals without dependent children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash benefits for up to 12 months out of any 36-month period. Recipients disabled for 12 months or more must also apply for federal Supplemental Security Income (SSI).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income disabled Marylanders without dependent children who are experiencing short-term disability or awaiting federal disability (SSI) approval.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance to cover living expenses during a period of disability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income Maryland resident
Must have a qualifying disability verified by a licensed medical practitioner (medical report required)
Must not have dependent children
Applicants disabled for 12 months or more must apply for Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Benefits limited to 12 months out of any 36-month period unless pursuing SSI
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local Department of Social Services office. You may also apply by mail, fax, or other electronic means, or have someone drop off an application on your behalf. Online applications are available at MarylandBenefits.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEFAP is a federally funded program created in 1983 that provides USDA-purchased foods to low-income individuals and families through a network of soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters. The Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) administers TEFAP in Maryland by contracting with the Maryland Food Bank and the Capital Area Food Bank to receive, store, and distribute USDA foods across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. The program also offers technical assistance and information to eligible agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEFAP distributes USDA-purchased foods (such as canned fruits and vegetables, meat, dairy, grains, and dried goods) and federal administrative funds to eligible agencies (soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters). Each state receives an allocation based on population, poverty, and unemployment rates. Administrative funds reimburse ordering, receiving, tracking, storing, and distributing costs. The program also provides technical assistance and information to participating organizations. FFY26 income eligibility thresholds are active (2026 guidelines for households at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters (Emergency Recipient Agencies/Emergency Feeding Organizations) serving low-income individuals and families across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. End beneficiaries must meet at least one eligibility category: SNAP, Medical Assistance, TANF, Unemployment, or Energy Assistance recipients, or have household income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (2026 income thresholds active for FFY26).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of USDA-purchased food commodities to low-income residents through local food assistance agencies. Administrative funds reimburse costs of ordering, receiving, tracking, storing, and distributing USDA foods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Maryland Food Bank serves all areas except Montgomery and Prince George's counties; Capital Area Food Bank serves Montgomery and Prince George's counties.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible agency such as a soup kitchen, food pantry, or shelter (ERA or EFO designation)
Must have current Tax-Exempt/501(c)(3) status
Must comply with non-discrimination policies and complete annual Civil Rights training
Must operate in one of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions
Must conduct at least one food distribution per month
Must comply with food safety, temperature monitoring, and inventory requirements (refrigerated foods ≤40°F, frozen foods ≤0°F; stored 6 inches off floor)
Must submit monthly reports and comply with 7 CFR 251 and 7 CFR 250
Must maintain records and report monthly to TEFAP Sponsoring Agency
Must post USDA non-discrimination posters and complaint forms
Must attend annual Civil Rights, Customer Service, Conflict Resolution, and Food Safety training
USDA foods cannot be sold, traded, bartered, or exchanged for cash donations
Confidentiality of client information must be maintained

End beneficiaries must complete a self-disclosure form (available in English and Spanish) confirming eligibility: receipt of SNAP, Medical Assistance, TANF, Unemployment, or Energy Assistance benefits, or household income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines
End beneficiaries must meet 2026 income thresholds by household size (1–8+ members) as specified in FFY26 Self-Disclosure form
DHS, in collaboration with Sponsoring Agencies, maintains the right to limit the number of new ERAs in jurisdictions with a saturation of providers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible agencies work with the Maryland Food Bank (for most of Maryland) or the Capital Area Food Bank (for Montgomery and Prince George's counties) to receive USDA foods. New ERAs/EFOs undergo an onboarding process vetted by DHS and Sponsoring Agencies before distributing. A Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with a 3-year term is executed between eligible recipient agencies and sponsoring agencies. Individuals seeking food assistance complete a self-disclosure (SDI) form at the distribution site and can use food bank locator tools at mdfoodbank.org or capitalareafoodbank.org by entering their zip code.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Transportation Assistance Program (TAP) provides reliable used vehicles to eligible low-income families — primarily recipients of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) — to help them find and keep employment and move toward financial independence. Vehicles are provided for two years or 24,000 miles (whichever comes first) through a statewide network of partners across Maryland, including local departments of social services and the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change. The program aims to increase mobility, reduce commute times, make higher-paying jobs or shifts more accessible, support medical and family transportation needs, and improve overall quality of life for families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families and low-income individuals receive a reliable used vehicle to use for two years or 24,000 miles (whichever comes first) at no stated cost to the recipient. Vehicles are distributed through a statewide network of partners, including the statewide TAP partner Vehicles for Change, and can be used for commuting, medical appointments, grocery shopping, and other family needs. Participants apply through their local department of social services TAP Coordinator or through Vehicles for Change.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and low-income individuals in Maryland, especially those receiving Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), who face transportation barriers to finding and maintaining employment and need a reliable vehicle to support employment access and family well-being.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of a reliable used vehicle to eligible families and individuals to support transportation to and from employment, reduce commute time, make higher-paying jobs or shifts more accessible, and support medical appointments, grocery shopping, and other family needs, improving overall quality of life.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services and the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change.
requirements_list: Must be a recipient of or eligible for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) or similar assistance, or otherwise be low-income
Must need transportation assistance to access employment
Must inquire through local department of social services TAP Coordinator or contact Vehicles for Change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Potential participants should contact their local department of social services TAP Coordinator or reach out to the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change, at vehiclesforchange.org to find out if you qualify.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents Program (STEP Up!)
structured_extraction.program_description: STEP Up is a free, job-driven pilot program for noncustodial parents who have a Baltimore City child support case. It provides free job training and comprehensive support services to help parents overcome employment barriers and build careers in industries such as welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, and biotechnology. Training is delivered through partners including Baltimore City Community College, Humanim, and CivicWorks, and covers hard skills, soft skills, job readiness, job placement, industry-recognized certifications, and work experience. Support services include transportation assistance, a personal career navigator, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (criminal record, legal issues, license suspension), and work clothing, tools, and textbooks. Participants who successfully complete the program can earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services – Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job training in high-demand industries including healthcare, construction, welding, green construction, machining, hospitality, warehousing, and biotechnology. Training programs include hard skills, soft skills, job readiness, job placement, industry-recognized certifications, and work experience. Additional support includes transportation assistance, a personal career navigator, referrals to community services (including legal help and driver's license reinstatement), help resolving barriers to employment (criminal record, legal issues, license suspension), work clothing, tools, and textbooks. Participants who successfully complete the program may receive forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents who have a Baltimore City child support case and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, and other in-demand fields. Assistance may also cover transportation, work clothing, tools, textbooks, and referrals to community services including legal help and driver's license reinstatement. Successful completion can lead to forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to noncustodial parties who have a Baltimore City child support case. Initial enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent with a Baltimore City child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must have a child support obligation
Must commit to working upon program completion
Must be a noncustodial parent living in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 844-7001 x 7144 to schedule an enrollment session. Initial enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645. After enrollment, participants join a training program offered by one of the STEP Up employment partners (Baltimore City Community College, Humanim, or CivicWorks). You may also contact your local Department of Social Services or the DHS workforce development office for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: CAPE is a free job-training and employment support program for non-custodial parents who owe child support in Washington County, Maryland. It helps unemployed or underemployed parents overcome barriers to employment and build careers in industries such as welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost job training and support services including hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (e.g., criminal record, legal services, driver's license suspension), access to work-related items (clothing, tools, textbooks), and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants who complete the program may also receive forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents who have a child support case in Washington County, Maryland and are unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, career development, and employment support services to help participants gain employment and make consistent child support payments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to non-custodial parties with a child support case in Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a non-custodial party with a child support case in Washington County

Must complete an employability assessment covering current employment status, employment-related skills and abilities, employment history, education, literacy levels, communication skills, and career interests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Program Coordinator Bobbie Nave to begin enrollment. Once enrolled, participants join a training program offered by one of the CAPE participating partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: Re-Engaging Individuals through Successful Employment (RISE) is a no-cost employment training and placement program for noncustodial parents (parents who owe child support) who are unemployed or underemployed and live in the Mid-Shore region of Maryland. The program connects participants with job training, industry certifications, job placement, and support services to help them find and keep employment so they can support their families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free employment training and placement program that provides: hard and soft skills training in in-demand industries, industry-recognized certifications (e.g., forklift, CDL, HVAC, welding, ServSafe, security), job readiness coaching, job search and placement support, transportation assistance, work clothing and tools, referrals to legal and other community services, and ongoing support from a personal career navigator and success coach.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Damien Ransome (Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's Counties); Louis Nichols (Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot Counties); Kameka Sampson / Jada Johnson (Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset Counties)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents (individuals who owe child support) who are unemployed or underemployed and have a child support case in the Mid-Shore region of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training, industry certifications, job placement, transportation assistance, work clothing, tools, and removal of barriers to employment such as legal services or addressing license suspensions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the nine-county Mid-Shore region of Maryland: Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial party (owe child support)
Must have a Mid-Shore child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a program coordinator for your county to enroll. During an enrollment session, inform the intake coordinator of any specific training programs of interest. Call the DHS help-line at (800) 332-6347 for additional assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NETWorks Program helps noncustodial parents (parents who owe child support) overcome barriers to employment so they can better support themselves and their families. It supplements the state's Tri Pep Program, which serves Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. NETWorks provides one-time financial support for work-related expenses, connects participants with training and education, helps address transportation barriers, and works to reduce recidivism — including potentially expunging criminal records.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial support for identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation costs related to job interviews. Case managers help remove employment barriers including criminal record expungement. Training options include GED and Driver Improvement courses, regional flagger certifications, work experience placements, and CDL (Commercial Driver's License) courses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who owe child support and reside in Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Work-related expenses (ID, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, transportation); GED and driver improvement courses; flagger certifications; CDL training; criminal record expungement assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to noncustodial parties served by the Somerset County, Wicomico County, or Worcester County Office of Child Support
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial party owing child support
Must have a direct connection to IVA services or a court-ordered referral for employment services through the Tri Pep Program
Must agree to stipulations set by program administrators
Must reside in Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester County
Applications reviewed on merits and financial aid dependencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact program staff directly — Diana Columna at 410-713-3147 or diana.columna@maryland.gov, or Torrez Wise at 410-219-5712 or torrez.wise@maryland.gov. You can also call the DHS helpline at 800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Payment Incentive Program encourages noncustodial parents (NCPs) to make consistent child support payments by reducing or eliminating state-owed child support arrears. If an NCP makes full child support payments for 12 consecutive months, the state-owed arrears balance is cut in half (50% reduction). If full payments continue for 24 consecutive months, the remaining balance owed to the state is eliminated entirely. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made immediately before joining the program, and consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work or no-fault job termination.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces state-owed child support arrears by 50% after 12 consecutive months of full, on-time payments. Eliminates the remaining state-owed arrears balance after 24 consecutive months of full payments. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made immediately before joining the program. Consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work or no-fault job termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not affected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents (NCPs) in Maryland who owe state-owed child support arrears, have a Maryland court order, and have gross income below 225% of the federal poverty level (household size considered).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of state-owed child support arrears balances for qualifying noncustodial parents who make consistent full child support payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester). Applicant must have a Maryland court order. Central office: Child Support Administration, 25 S. Charles Street, Baltimore, MD 21201.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent with a Maryland court order with an arrears balance owed to the State because the custodial party received public assistance.
Must have a Maryland court order.
Gross income must be less than 225% of the federal poverty level (household size is considered).
Must not have been terminated from this program three or more times.
A separate application must be completed for each case.
Must pay child support as ordered for 12 or 24 consecutive months to receive the arrears reduction.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and print the Payment Incentive Program application or submit an application online through the program's website. Applications may also be submitted in-person, by email, by mail, or by scan to a local child support agency. A separate application must be completed for each case. Contact the Maryland Child Support Administration at 1-800-332-6347 for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Services Helping the Involvement of Non-Custodial Parents and Employment (SHINE)
structured_extraction.program_description: SHINE is a free, 12-month case management program for noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support. The program helps participants overcome barriers to employment, achieve financial stability, and strengthen their relationships with their children. Participants receive job readiness support, skills training, legal and documentation assistance, parenting resources, and referrals for basic needs such as housing, transportation, and health services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 12-month case management program providing employment readiness activities, job placement support, resume and interview skills training, access to vocational and GED training, assistance obtaining vital documents, legal aid referrals, parenting resources, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing and transportation assistance, and help applying for state benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support and seeking stable employment, typically referred by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing or by the Child Support Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services, skills training, legal and documentation assistance, parenting support, and referrals for basic needs such as housing, transportation, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to noncustodial parents in Allegany County, Maryland. Intake appointments are held at the Allegany County Department of Social Services office at 1 Frederick Street, Cumberland, MD 21502.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent obligated to pay child support
Must be referred by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing for outstanding child support arrearages, or referred by the Child Support Administration
Must not have known physical or mental disabilities that prevent working
Must consistently report weekly job search activities, current employment status and income, child support payment history, and any changes in address, phone number, or employment status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Once referred by a court or the Child Support Administration, contact the Allegany County DSS office to schedule an intake appointment. At the appointment, a Noncustodial Parent Employment Program (NPEP) Specialist conducts a strengths and needs assessment — collecting demographic, financial, employment history, living situation, legal history, and service-planning information — and reviews program compliance policies. Case management continues over 12 months with regular meetings to monitor progress.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Support Pass Through program sends a portion of child support payments to families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA). When a noncustodial parent (NCP) pays current child support in a given month, the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) passes some of that payment directly to the custodial party. Child support payments are assigned to DHS while the family receives TCA. The pass-through amount depends on the number of children in the TCA household and the amount of current support paid in the prior calendar month: up to $100 per month for one child, or up to $200 per month for two or more children, or the court-ordered support amount, whichever is less. Payments on past-due support (arrears) do not qualify. Active SNAP case alone does not qualify — the family must have an active cash assistance (TCA) case. Once the TCA case closes, the custodial party receives the full child support payment directly, though one additional pass-through payment may arrive the month after closure if support was paid before case closure.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Food Program (MEFP) provides annual grants to nonprofit feeding organizations — such as soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs — to purchase food and distribute groceries and meals at no charge to individuals and families in emergency need. Grants are awarded based on available funding and demographic indicators of need, including population size, poverty levels, unemployment rates, and SNAP enrollment. Funds are allocated across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Currently, 104 programs around the state receive MEFP funding.
