The FY2026 award period is July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026. Grantees must expend all funds by June 1, 2026; any unexpended funds must be returned by June 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA) helps low-income Maryland households pay off outstanding electric and gas utility bill debt (arrearages). Eligible customers can receive a grant of up to $2,000 toward their overdue balance, paid directly to the utility company. Customers must have a past-due balance of $300 or more and must be eligible for EUSP (Electric Universal Service Program) to qualify. Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limitation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) / Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) / Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), helps low-income households with home energy costs. Programs include: (1) The Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), which provides a one-time grant per heating season paid directly to the household's heating supplier to offset home heating costs (grant amount based on fuel type, household income relative to household size, and location within Maryland), as well as repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost to eligible households (maximum repair funding: $50,000; homeowners only for repair program; licensed Maryland contractors required); (2) The Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), a one-time-per-program-year electric assistance grant to help low-income customers afford their electric bills (grant amount based on average kilowatt-hour cost in Maryland, household primary heat source, household income relative to household size, and prior 12 months of kilowatt usage), with optional budget billing enrollment available through the utility company that spreads annual utility costs into even monthly payments to avoid seasonal spikes; (3) Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA for gas, EARA for electric), which provides grants of up to $2,000 toward past-due electric bills and up to $1,000 toward past-due gas bills for customers with a past-due balance of $300 or more (available once every five years with exceptions for vulnerable households; arrearage grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit); (4) the Utility Service Protection Program (USPP), which protects eligible households from utility shut-offs through an equal monthly payment plan and can place a 55-day hold on accounts threatened with termination while an application is pending; and (5) general OHEP utility and heating bill assistance for electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, kerosene, and other home energy costs. Income limits are up to 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $2,608/month for a household of 1 up to $10,859/month for a household of 10 for FY26). Residents do not need a turn-off notice to qualify. Energy assistance is supplemental and will not cover the entire bill. The current program cycle is effective July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026; OHEP is a year-round program and applicants can apply at any time. Programs operate year-round on a rolling basis; FY2025 applications began July 1, 2024. In St. Mary's County, the program is administered locally by the Tri-County Community Action Committee, with applications accepted at any senior activity center between July and May each year. Special flood assistance is available for households in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. Dedicated specialists at local offices guide applicants through the energy assistance application process. A Critical Medical Needs Program component is also available through OHEP, with applications processed by trained navigators who are bound by confidentiality agreements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Office of Home Energy Programs / Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEAP (heating bill assistance): A one-time grant per heating season paid directly to the applicant's heating supplier to offset home heating costs; grant amount based on fuel type, household income relative to household size, and location within Maryland. MEAP (system repair/replacement): Eligible homeowners receive repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems at no cost; maximum repair funding is $50,000; work is determined through a home assessment and depends on funding availability; licensed Maryland contractors required; mobile home applicants must provide title or bill of sale; applicants may be placed on a waitlist due to limited funding and high demand; renters and mobile homeowners do not qualify for repair program funding. EUSP: A one-time-per-program-year electric assistance grant paid directly to the applicant's electric company to help low-income customers afford their electric bills; grant amount based on average kilowatt-hour cost in Maryland, household primary heat source, household income relative to household size, and prior 12 months of kilowatt usage; optional budget billing enrollment available through the utility company that spreads annual utility costs into even monthly payments to avoid seasonal spikes. Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA/EARA): Up to $2,000 toward past-due electric bills and up to $1,000 toward past-due gas bills for customers with a past-due balance of $300 or more; may only be received once every five years with exceptions for vulnerable households; arrearage grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit. USPP: Protects eligible households from utility shut-offs through an equal monthly payment plan; OHEP can place a 55-day hold on accounts threatened with termination while an application is pending. General OHEP: Income-based grants to help low-income households pay home energy (utility) bills including electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, and kerosene; applicants do not need a turn-off notice to qualify. Energy assistance is supplemental and will not cover the entire bill. Benefits can be received once per fiscal year (July–June); applicants must reapply each year. Assistance is delivered through local Home Energy Program offices in each Maryland county and Baltimore City. Eligibility is income-based using FY26 monthly income limits (e.g., $2,608/month for a household of 1, up to $10,859/month for a household of 10). Current program cycle: effective July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round / rolling basis; benefits must be applied for each fiscal year (July–June). Current cycle: July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026. EUSP available once per program year (July–June); St. Mary's County applications accepted between July and May each year. MEAP waitlist in effect due to limited funding. Applicants can apply at any time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland households — including homeowners, renters, public housing residents, sub-metered homes, roomers/boarders — who pay for home energy costs and are struggling to afford them. Income limit is up to 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FY26 monthly limits: $2,608/month for a household of 1, up to $10,859/month for a household of 10). MEAP targets those needing help paying home heating bills or with non-functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (homeowners only for system repair/replacement). EUSP targets low-income households struggling to pay electric utility bills. Arrearage Retirement Assistance targets those with large past-due electric or gas balances. Households receiving SNAP or TCA are categorically eligible. Residents do not need a turn-off notice to qualify. A Critical Medical Needs Program component is available for households with serious illness or life-support equipment dependency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of home heating bills directly to fuel supplier or utility company (MEAP heating assistance); repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems for eligible homeowners (MEAP system assistance, up to $50,000); payment of electric utility bills directly to the electric company (EUSP); payment of electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, or kerosene bills (OHEP); payment toward past-due electric and gas bills (Arrearage Retirement Assistance/GARA/EARA); protection from utility shut-offs (USPP); heating expenses paid directly to heating supplier (St. Mary's County). Assistance cannot be applied to security deposits or property damage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with local offices in every jurisdiction. Applications must be processed by the local OHEP office in the applicant's jurisdiction. Baltimore City residents apply through local CAP Centers. In St. Mary's County, applications are accepted at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee. Special flood assistance is also available for households in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. DHCD mailing address for system repair program: 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income household (homeowner, renter, public housing resident, sub-metered home, roomer/boarder)

Must meet income eligibility requirements: household income cannot exceed up to 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FY26 monthly limits: $2,608 for 1 person, $3,525 for 2 people, up to $10,859 for 10 people)
Must be a Maryland resident
Must provide government-issued photo identification
Must provide proof of primary residency
Must provide Social Security cards or equivalent federal documents for all household members
Must provide documentation of all household gross income for the last 30 days (paystubs, Social Security award letters, pension statements, etc.)
Must provide most recent utility and/or heating fuel bill or receipt (and termination notice if applicable); clear photos of documents are acceptable

Self-employed applicants must provide most recent Schedule SE tax form (if taxes filed) or weekly/monthly/quarterly books, ledgers, sales slips, cancelled checks, invoices, and bank statements for the last 30 days (if taxes not filed), and complete an Income Verification of Self-Employment Form (DHS-FIA-808)

Household members 18+ with zero income must complete a Declaration of Zero Income form (DHS-FIA-806); zero income definition includes wages, self-employment, Social Security, TCA/TDAP, Unemployment, monetary gifts and loans
Households receiving SNAP or TCA in Maryland are categorically eligible and do not need to complete a separate application
Participants in OHEP utility bill pay assistance, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs are automatically considered income-eligible for MEAP
Categorical eligibility also applies to recipients of TDAP, SSI, or VA benefits

Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, MEEHA, and geographic eligibility for certain areas are NOT accepted as proof of income eligibility for MEAP
Must have home heating costs (MEAP heating bill assistance)

Must have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system (MEAP system repair/replacement); homeowners only — renters and mobile homeowners do not qualify for repair program funding; mobile home applicants must provide title or bill of sale; licensed Maryland contractors required; maximum repair funding $50,000
Applicants do not need a turn-off notice to qualify for OHEP
EUSP is available once per program year (July–June); grant amount based on household income and electric use over the past 12 months

For Arrearage Retirement Assistance: must have a past-due bill balance of $300 or more; arrearage benefit may only be received once every five years (with exceptions for vulnerable households); arrearage grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit
Benefits limited to once per fiscal year; must reapply annually
Required documents can be submitted as clear photos, scans, or originals
Must apply through the local Home Energy Program Office for the county where you reside
Grant amount varies by fuel type, household income, and location in the state
Applicants with alimony or child support income must provide verification via DHS-FIA-803 form

Applicants with no household income in last 30 days must complete Household Worksheet (DHS-FIA-807) documenting basic needs (Shelter, Food, Utility); if non-government third party assists with basic needs, that provider must complete a Resource Provider Statement (DHS-FIA-813)

Applicants with safety concerns may waive address requirement on applications with third-party verification (domestic violence service providers, legal representatives, medical/social service providers, or law enforcement) using DHS-FIA-804 form

Crisis Season Declaration (DHS-FIA-805) is only for use during crisis season (November 1 – March 31); applicants receiving crisis benefits must provide documentation within 15 days or repay the benefit
Proxy applicants must complete a Proxy Authorization Form (DHS-FIA-811)

For utility service protection based on medical need: physician, certified nurse practitioner, or physician assistant certification required; within 30 days of submitting certification, applicant must enter into a payment agreement with utility
When applicants cannot provide sufficient pay stubs, employer wage verification may be required (DHS-FIA-814 Wage Verification Form completed by employer)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by phone at 1-800-332-6347, by mail, in person at a local OHEP office, or by dropping a completed paper application and required documents in a secure drop box at a local office. A paper application (including fillable version) can be downloaded from the DHS website, filled out, and mailed in or dropped off. Baltimore City residents can drop applications at the nearest CAP Center. Home visits are available for seniors and those with special medical needs. All required documents must be submitted with the application to avoid delays; applications are reviewed within 14 days of receiving a complete application packet and a final determination is made within 45 days; allow 15 days from submission for the application status to be displayed online at myohepstatus.org. Required documents can be submitted as clear photos, scans, or originals. For MEAP system repair/replacement: complete the program application and submit all required documents to the DHCD office (7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706); if currently approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services, call 1-800-332-6347. Once eligibility is confirmed, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment, after which a licensed Maryland contractor will complete the recommended work. Once approved and processed for MEAP heating bill assistance, the grant is sent directly to your heating supplier. For EUSP, the grant is sent directly to your electric company upon approval. Local specialists will guide applicants through the process. In St. Mary's County: apply at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee between July and May each year. Energy assistance is a year-round, rolling program (current cycle: July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026); applicants may apply at any time but must reapply each fiscal year. Navigators processing Critical Medical Needs Program applications must sign a confidentiality agreement (Confidentiality Form) before handling applicant information. When pay stubs are insufficient, applicants may need to have their employer complete a Wage Verification Form (DHS-FIA-814).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of home heating bills directly to fuel supplier or utility company (MEAP heating assistance); repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems for eligible homeowners (MEAP system assistance, up to $50,000); payment of electric utility bills directly to the electric company (EUSP); payment toward electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, or kerosene bills (OHEP); payment toward past-due electric and gas bills (Arrearage Retirement Assistance/GARA/EARA); protection from utility shut-offs (USPP). Assistance cannot be applied to security deposits or property damage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with local offices in every jurisdiction. Applications must be processed by the local OHEP office in the applicant's jurisdiction. Baltimore City residents apply through local CAP Centers. In Washington County, administered by the Washington County Community Action Council (301-797-4161; WashingtonCountyOHEP@wccac.org), located at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740. In Carroll County, local assistance is provided through the Carroll County Division of Aging & Disabilities (410-386-3800). In St. Mary's County, applications are accepted at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee. Special flood assistance is available for households in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. DHCD mailing address for system repair program: 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a low-income household (homeowner, renter, public housing resident, sub-metered home, roomer/boarder)

Must meet income eligibility requirements: household income cannot exceed up to 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FY26 monthly limits: $2,608 for 1 person, $3,525 for 2 people, up to $10,859 for 10 people)
Assets are not counted for eligibility
Must have home heating or energy costs
Turn-off notice is not required to qualify
Must apply through the local Home Energy Program Office for the county where you reside
Must provide government-issued photo ID
Must provide proof of primary residency
Must provide Social Security cards or equivalent federal documents for all household members
Must provide a copy of utility and/or heating bill
Must provide documentation of all household gross income for the last 30 days (paystubs, Social Security award letters, pension statements, etc.)
Must provide a copy of most recent heating fuel bill or receipt if applicable
Must provide a copy of termination notice if applicable

Self-employed applicants must provide most recent Schedule SE tax form (if taxes filed) or weekly/monthly/quarterly books, ledgers, sales slips, cancelled checks, invoices, and bank statements for the last 30 days (if taxes not filed), and complete an Income Verification of Self-Employment Form (DHS-FIA-808)

Household members 18+ with zero income must complete a Declaration of Zero Income form (DHS-FIA-806); zero income definition includes wages, self-employment, Social Security, TCA/TDAP, Unemployment, monetary gifts and loans

Participants in OHEP utility bill pay assistance, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs are automatically considered income-eligible for MEAP
Categorical eligibility also applies to recipients of TDAP, SSI, or VA benefits

Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, MEEHA, and geographic eligibility for certain areas are NOT accepted as proof of income eligibility for MEAP

Must have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system for MEAP system repair/replacement; homeowners only — renters and mobile homeowners do not qualify for repair program funding; mobile home applicants must provide title or bill of sale; licensed Maryland contractors required; maximum repair funding $50,000
EUSP is available once per program year (July–June); grant amount based on household income and electric use over the past 12 months

For Arrearage Retirement Assistance: must have a past-due bill balance of $300 or more; arrearage benefit may only be received once every five years (with exceptions for vulnerable households); arrearage grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit
Benefits limited to once per fiscal year; must reapply annually
Grant amount varies by fuel type, household income, and location in the state
Required documents can be submitted as clear photos, scans, or originals
Applicants with alimony or child support income must provide verification via DHS-FIA-803 form

Applicants with no household income in last 30 days must complete Household Worksheet (DHS-FIA-807) documenting basic needs (Shelter, Food, Utility); if non-government third party assists with basic needs, that provider must complete a Resource Provider Statement (DHS-FIA-813)

Applicants with safety concerns may waive address requirement on applications with third-party verification (domestic violence service providers, legal representatives, medical/social service providers, or law enforcement) using DHS-FIA-804 form
Crisis Season Declaration (DHS-FIA-805) is only for use during crisis season (November 1–March 31); applicants receiving crisis benefits must provide documentation within 15 days or repay the benefit
Proxy applicants must complete a Proxy Authorization Form (DHS-FIA-811)

For utility service protection based on medical need: physician, certified nurse practitioner, or physician assistant certification required; within 30 days of submitting certification, applicant must enter into a payment agreement with utility
When applicants cannot provide sufficient pay stubs, employer wage verification may be required (DHS-FIA-814 Wage Verification Form completed by employer)

MEAP and EUSP benefits may not be applied to security deposits or retained for dwelling damage costs; landlords receiving direct payments must reduce tenant rent or utility charge by the full benefit amount and return unused funds if tenant moves
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by phone at 1-800-332-6347 (TTY: 1-800-735-2258), by mail, in person at a local OHEP office, or by dropping a completed paper application (DHS-FIA-9780) and required documents in a secure drop box at a local office. A paper application (including fillable version) can be downloaded from the DHS website, filled out, and mailed in or dropped off. Baltimore City residents can drop applications at the nearest CAP Center. Home visits are available for seniors and those with special medical needs. All required documents must be submitted with the application to avoid delays; applications are reviewed within 14 days of receiving a complete application packet and a final determination is made within 45 days; allow 15 days from submission for the application status to be displayed online at myohepstatus.org. Required documents can be submitted as clear photos, scans, or originals. For MEAP system repair/replacement: complete the program application and submit all required documents to the DHCD office (7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; phone: 855-583-8976); if currently approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services, call 1-800-332-6347. Once eligibility is confirmed, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment, after which a licensed Maryland contractor will complete the recommended work. Once approved and processed for MEAP heating bill assistance, the grant is sent directly to your heating supplier. For EUSP, the grant is sent directly to your electric company upon approval. In Washington County, apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740. In St. Mary's County, apply at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee between July and May each year. In Carroll County, contact Carroll County Information & Assistance at 410-386-3800 to schedule an appointment. Gather required documents (government-issued photo ID, proof of residency, Social Security cards, income documentation, utility bills) and submit with the application. You can apply at any time during the year but must reapply each fiscal year (July–June). Local specialists will guide applicants through the process. Navigators processing Critical Medical Needs Program applications must sign a confidentiality agreement before handling applicant information. Proxy applicants may designate an 18+ representative to apply in person at a local OHEP agency using the Proxy Authorization Form (DHS-FIA-811).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Adult High School Program helps adults 21 and older who did not graduate from high school earn a Maryland High School Diploma. The program offers academic coursework aligned to Maryland graduation requirements, along with postsecondary education opportunities, industry-recognized credentials, and wraparound support services. Previous high school credits may be applied toward the diploma.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants complete coursework aligned to Maryland High School Graduation Requirements and, upon successful completion, earn a Maryland High School Diploma. Program may also include industry-recognized credentialing and postsecondary coursework. Currently offered at two locations in Baltimore City: South Baltimore Adult High School (operated by Elev8 Baltimore) and The Excel Center (operated by Goodwill Industries of the Chesapeake).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Earning a Maryland High School Diploma through academic coursework, with opportunities for postsecondary education, industry certifications, and wraparound support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in the State of Maryland. Current program locations are in Baltimore City.

Must reside in the State of Maryland
Must not already have a Maryland High School Diploma
Must not have already completed high school graduation requirements through the GED Test or the National External Diploma Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact South Baltimore Adult High School or The Excel Center directly for enrollment information. For South Baltimore Adult High School, contact Sharée Turner at 443-682-9403. For The Excel Center, contact Sherry DeFrancisci at 443-870-5050.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance to employers impacted by COVID-19 to help them recruit, train, and retain employees. Employers can use funds to establish Employee Support Programs (covering transportation, housing, and child/dependent care assistance) and/or Payroll Incentives (such as signing bonuses, retention bonuses, and wages during training).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to employers to fund Employee Support Programs and/or Payroll Incentives for their workforce. Employee Support Programs can cover transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, and child/dependent care costs. Payroll Incentives can cover signing bonuses, retention bonuses, and wages during training. The program is funded by a federal award from the U.S. Department of the Treasury to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No longer accepting applications as of October 14, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers impacted by COVID-19 who want to improve employee recruitment, training, and retention
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee Support Programs (transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, child and dependent care assistance) and Payroll Incentives (signing bonuses, retention bonuses, wages during training or professional development)

Proposed program must include elements of Employee Support Programs and/or Payroll Incentives

Eligible applicants who hold a valid license in good standing in another state can receive their Maryland license within 60 days of submitting a completed application with all supporting documentation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Expedited processing of occupational and professional license applications for eligible military veterans, active service members, and their spouses or surviving spouses. Licenses are issued within 60 days of receiving a completed application with all supporting documentation. Applicants must hold a valid license in good standing in another state.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expedited issuance of Maryland occupational and professional licenses across a wide range of fields including architecture, barbering, cosmetology, electricians, HVACR, real estate, engineering, plumbing, and more.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Division of Unemployment Insurance provides temporary financial assistance to eligible workers who become unemployed through no fault of their own. Eligible claimants can receive weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 for up to 26 weeks (approximately 6 months) while they search for new employment. The exact benefit amount depends on prior wages and other factors such as severance received. Federal employees, military members, and federal contractors may also be eligible. The program also establishes rates and collects taxes from Maryland employers to finance benefits, and conducts appeals for claimants and employers when disputes arise.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 for up to 26 weeks (approximately 6 months). The exact amount depends on prior wages and other factors such as severance received. Claimants must complete weekly certification and document at least 3 job search activities per week to continue receiving benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland workers and residents who have lost their jobs through no fault of their own, including former federal civilian employees, military members, federal employees on furlough, and federal contractors whose last official duty station was in Maryland or who are Maryland residents separated from federal employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary income replacement while unemployed and actively searching for new employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Federal employees whose last official duty station was in Maryland, or who are Maryland residents separated from federal employment, may also apply.
requirements_list: Must be unemployed through no fault of your own
Must be ready and able to work normal hours as soon as possible, without restrictions
Must have earned at least $1,176.01 in one quarter and at least $1,800 total over at least two quarters of the 18-month base period
Must register on the Maryland Workforce Exchange
Must actively search for work each week and document at least 3 job search activities
Must complete weekly certification each week to continue receiving benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Determine eligibility. Step 2: Gather required information including Social Security number, employment history for the last 18 months, and dependent information if applicable. Step 3: File a claim online via the BEACON portal (beacon.labor.maryland.gov) or by phone at 667-207-6520. Step 4: Register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange System and document weekly job search activities. Step 5: Complete weekly certification each Sunday via BEACON, the mobile app, or the automated phone line to continue receiving benefits.

Adults who did not finish high school can also earn a Maryland High School Diploma through GED® testing, the National External Diploma Program (NEDP®), or the Adult High School Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: EARN Maryland (Employment Advancement Right Now) is a statewide, state-funded, competitive workforce development grant program that is industry-led and regional in focus. It invests in strategic industry partnerships from key economic sectors across Maryland regions, coordinating education, workforce, and economic development efforts to train and place workers in skilled jobs. The program supports both incumbent workers seeking new credentials and unemployed individuals seeking employment, including hard-to-serve jobseekers. It addresses employer workforce needs, creates career paths to good jobs, reduces barriers to employment, and provides job readiness training, GED preparation, occupational skills development, literacy advancement, and help with transportation and child care. Current industry training tracks include Automotive, Biotechnology, Childcare, Construction/Skilled Trades, Cyber/IT, Green, Healthcare, Hospitality, Manufacturing, Residential Leasing, and Transportation/Logistics. As of October 2024, more than 25,000 Marylanders have been positively impacted, over 15,000 incumbent workers have received training and credentials, and nearly 11,000 individuals have obtained employment through the program. For every $1 of state funding invested, an additional $18.16 in economic impact is created.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive state grants fund strategic industry partnerships to deliver industry-specific workforce training programs across sectors including automotive, biotechnology, childcare, construction/skilled trades, cyber/IT, green industries, healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing, residential leasing, and transportation/logistics. Partnerships coordinate across education, workforce, and economic development initiatives to address employer training needs and place workers in skilled employment. For every $1 of state funding invested, an additional $18.16 in economic impact is created.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Strategic industry partnerships from key economic sectors, employers, incumbent workers seeking new credentials, unemployed individuals, hard-to-serve jobseekers, and job seekers in Maryland who want to receive industry-specific career training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce training and education including job readiness training, GED preparation, occupational skills development, literacy advancement, credential and certification attainment, career training in targeted industries, and support for transportation and child care barriers.

requirements_list: Applicants must be industry-led partnerships
Partnerships must focus on a specific industry sector
Partnerships must cover a regional area of Maryland
Plans must address training and placement of workers in meaningful employment
Individual job seekers must select an industry track
Must locate and enroll in a designated program in area of residence
Must meet individual program enrollment requirements (varies by program)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For partnerships: Competitive grant application process — visit the EARN Maryland website to learn about partnership opportunities. For job seekers: 1. Review available industries and select the field matching your interests. 2. Find the designated program in your area of residence. 3. Review the training flyer for the selected program. 4. Contact the website or representative listed on the jobseeker flyer for upcoming training dates and enrollment requirements. 5. Complete the enrollment process and begin training.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland employers and registered apprenticeship sponsors offset the cost of training registered apprentices. Employers can receive up to $3,000 per newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 per newly registered high school level apprentice to cover eligible training expenses. Established under the Registered Apprenticeship Investment for a Stronger Economy (RAISE) Act (SB 431, Chapter 2, 2025).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $3,000 per newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 per newly registered high school level (HSLRA) apprentice to offset eligible training expenses including tuition, fees, books, materials, mentorship costs, on-the-job learning expenses, apprentice recruitment expenses, disability accommodation costs, and supportive services. Applications must be submitted within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with MD Labor (30 days before or after registration date). A one-time blanket exception to the 30-day application window is active for FY 2026 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) for apprentices registered since July 1, 2025. Standard limit of 10 awards per employer/sponsor per calendar year for adult apprentices; unlimited awards for HSLRA apprentices.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling (within 30 days of apprentice registration); FY2026 one-time exception: retroactive to July 1, 2025, expires June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Christopher MacLarion, Director, Office of Apprenticeship
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Registered Apprenticeship Program Sponsors (group or individual, joint or non-joint) and Registered Apprenticeship Employers of any size, industry, or location in Maryland who are in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and hire new registered apprentices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional expenses (tuition, fees, books, materials), mentorship and on-the-job learning expenses, apprentice recruitment expenses, costs for disability accommodations, and supportive services for apprentices

Incumbent workers are eligible if they were not previously registered apprentices with that sponsor/employer
Sponsors and employers must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation

Once approved, submit invoice for reimbursement in a timely manner following the apprentice's seven months of employment. structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Business Works is a workforce training program operated by the Maryland Department of Labor that provides funds to help Maryland businesses train their employees. MOED partners with the Maryland Department of Labor to provide training funds to businesses focused on employee retention, growth, and layoff prevention. The program targets small businesses with in-demand occupations. It offers a dollar-for-dollar match requirement with a maximum of $4,500 per trainee per project and up to $40,000 annually per business. Note: the program may not be accepting new applications when all budgeted funding for a fiscal year has been obligated.

Maximum funding per trainee is $4,500 per project or series of projects. Maximum annual request per business cannot exceed $40,000. Funds cover classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skill-upgrade opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Professional Outplacement Assistance Center (POAC) is a workforce development program operated by the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning that provides free career transition and job search assistance to professional, technical, managerial, executive, and scientific workers who are unemployed or transitioning careers. Services include a one-day JumpStart training program on job acquisition strategies, a Computer Resource Lab for resume writing and software skills development, and ongoing Value Added Sessions (seminars, workshops, and simulations) on topics such as interviewing, networking, compensation negotiation, and social media. POAC also provides individualized career guidance, written publications and resource materials, free copying, networking events, career management information, and job postings. These services are available at no cost to Maryland residents and are comparable to private outplacement services that typically cost thousands of dollars.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (Maryland Forest Service) and the Potomac Watershed Partnership offer free native tree and shrub seedlings to homeowners and property owners who have a waterway on or adjacent to their property. The program provides a 'buffer in a bag' containing 20–30 native tree and shrub bare-root seedlings (approximately 1–2 feet tall), along with fact sheets on species, planting techniques, and maintenance, to help property owners create a streamside riparian forest buffer. This buffer improves water quality by reducing sediment, fertilizer, and pollutant runoff, stabilizes streambanks, and creates wildlife habitat. A limited number of bags are available each year on a first-come, first-served basis through county coordinators, with reservations typically taken in March and pickup at designated local sites in time for spring planting. Specific coordinators are listed for Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Carroll, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.

Bags are distributed at no cost on a first-come, first-served basis through county coordinators each spring. A limited number of bags are available each year, with reservations typically taken in March and pickup at a designated local site before the spring planting season.

structured_extraction.program_description: Becoming an Outdoors-Woman (BOW) offers outdoor skills workshops for women 18 and older. Weekend workshops feature over 30 classes plus evening programs (game feasts, nature presentations, crafts, and night hikes). Beyond BOW events are shorter, more focused one- to three-day workshops on specific activities such as fishing clinics, backpacking, goose hunting, and outdoor survival skills. The goal is to help women learn outdoor recreational skills in a supportive, hands-on environment. The 2026 Weekend Workshop is scheduled for August 7-9, 2026.

Some classes provide materials or equipment (e.g., Chainsaw provides all equipment; Leather Craft and Woodcarving provide tools/materials; Outdoor Cooking provides recipes). structured_extraction.program_description: A state-established public donation fund that accepts contributions to support largemouth bass and smallmouth bass conservation in Maryland. structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund (Trust Fund) funds non-point source pollution control projects to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays. It targets financial resources toward the most efficient and cost-effective projects to reduce nutrient and sediment pollution, restore streams and floodplains, enhance riparian buffers and forests, improve wetland ecosystems, and manage stormwater. The program also builds local capacity through technical assistance and advances restoration science through innovative technology and project monitoring. State agencies work with local partners to leverage funds, target geographic areas, engage communities, and ensure accountability. The program has received continuous annual appropriations since FY09 and is anticipated to receive $50M annually on an ongoing basis. A Whole Watershed Act component (five-year pilot, enacted 2024) targets five Maryland watersheds with $5M annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Trust Fund provides grants for nonpoint source pollution control projects targeting water quality improvements, including stream and floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, and innovative restoration technologies. Co-benefits supported include aquatic resource restoration (submerged aquatic vegetation, oyster reefs, marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, shoreline stabilization), climate resilience, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, fish passage restoration, local employment, recreational opportunities, and environmental justice benefits. Technical assistance is also provided to local governments and non-governmental organizations to meet local water quality goals through the Watershed Assistance Collaborative and Habitat Restoration and Conservation programs. Funds are targeted geographically to maximize pollution reduction impact. Annual allocations are determined through a collaborative process involving Maryland's Chesapeake Bay Council agencies and a Scientific Advisory Panel.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-governmental organizations, state colleges and universities, and other partners working on water quality restoration and non-point source pollution reduction in the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stream and floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, innovative restoration technology, aquatic resource restoration (submerged aquatic vegetation, oyster reefs, marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, shoreline stabilization), fish passage restoration (dam/culvert removal, stream daylighting), wildlife habitat creation, climate resilience, carbon sequestration, local employment, recreational opportunities, environmental justice benefits, and local water quality planning and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with geographic targeting toward areas where funding will most efficiently reduce non-point source pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay mainstem. The Trust Fund Targeting Map (interactive map with 21 layers and sublayers) is used to identify priority project locations.
requirements_list: Projects must address non-point source pollution reduction
Projects must be cost-effective and efficient
Funding is geographically targeted based on the Trust Fund Targeting Map
Applicants must complete the 'Co-Benefits' section of the Common Application
Applicants must utilize the Trust Fund Targeting Map to spatially document project benefits
Projects located within the Climate Ready Action Boundary (CRAB) subject to Coast Smart Construction Program must complete a project screening form and attach it with required project documents
Applicants are encouraged to coordinate with local floodplain manager for projects in regulated floodplain areas
Applicants may upload additional data layers or provide links to supplementary datasets for reviewer assessment of co-benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Grants Gateway at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/ccs/Pages/funding/grantsgateway.aspx. Applicants must: (1) complete the 'Co-Benefits' section of the Common Application; (2) utilize the Trust Fund Targeting Map to spatially document project benefits; (3) optionally upload additional data layers or provide links to supplementary datasets for reviewers. Projects in the Climate Ready Action Boundary (CRAB) may be required to complete a Coast Smart Project Screening Form (see https://dnr.maryland.gov/ccs/Pages/CoastSmart-Council.aspx). Coordination with local floodplain manager is encouraged for stream/wetland projects in regulated floodplain areas. The annual allocation process targets funds to the most cost-effective locations and practices, leverages funds to the greatest extent achievable, and engages community stakeholders.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Marina Partner Designation for Smaller Facilities

structured_extraction.program_description: The Coastal Resilience Program, housed within DNR's Center for Coastal and Ocean Planning, helps Maryland's coastal communities address short- and long-term coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. The program connects local government staff and partners to financial assistance, technical assistance, training opportunities, and supportive information, tools, visualizations, resources, and networks to build community resilience and foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies resilient to coastal hazards. Technical assistance includes sea level rise planning guidance and nuisance flood plan compliance support under Maryland HB 1427 (2019). Multiple recurring grant programs are available through partner agencies and the Chesapeake & Coastal Grants Gateway.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance through Outcome 2 of the Chesapeake & Coastal Grants Gateway (typically opens July, applications due December), technical assistance to local communities, and training opportunities for local practitioners. Also links to supportive information, federal and state resources, tools, visualizations, and networks. Multiple recurring grant programs are available including BRIC/FMA (opens October, due February), Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program (opens December, closes end of January), PROTECT Program (typically opens April, closes August), Chesapeake Bay Trust Watershed Assistance Grant Program (opens September, closes December), and Small Watershed Grant Projects (opens February, closes April). Technical assistance includes sea level rise planning guidance and nuisance flood plan compliance support under Maryland HB 1427 (2019).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government staff and partners in Maryland coastal communities facing coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise, including counties and municipalities required to develop Nuisance Flood Plans under Maryland HB 1427 (2019).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies resilient to coastal hazards including flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. Also supports development and updating of Nuisance Flood Plans as required by state statute.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland coastal communities along the Chesapeake Bay, Coastal Bays, and Atlantic Ocean. The Nuisance Flood Plan requirement applies to the Maryland Coastal Zone, which extends 3 miles into the Atlantic Ocean to the inland boundaries of 16 counties and Baltimore City bordering the Atlantic Ocean, Chesapeake Bay, and Potomac River to DC.
requirements_list: Applicants must be local governments or community partners in Maryland coastal areas.

Nuisance Flood Plans must be updated every five years; second cycle plans were due October 2025, next cycle due October 2030.
Nuisance Flood Plans must be posted on the jurisdiction's website and submitted as PDF to the Maryland Department of Planning.

For the 2025-2030 cycle, jurisdictions must submit a nuisance flood plan (new or updated) along with a cover letter and 1-2 page explanation to the Maryland Department of Planning at deborah.herrcornwell@maryland.gov.

Contact the program office for technical assistance and training opportunities. Technical assistance and financial assistance may be available through Maryland DNR to help communities meet the Nuisance Flood Plan requirement — contact Sasha Land at Sasha.Land@maryland.gov or (410) 260-8718, or review the list of funding opportunities in Appendix B of the NFP Guidance document.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program — Permanent Easement (CREP-PE)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Conservation Reserve Enhancement Permanent Easement Program (CREP) allows agricultural landowners in Maryland with an existing federal CREP or Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) contract to place a permanent conservation easement on their land. The State of Maryland acquires a permanent interest in the land to ensure conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources are maintained in perpetuity. Landowners must have already installed the required conservation practices under their federal contract. After the federal contract expires, the landowner agrees to keep the land in an approved conservation practice — such as a riparian buffer or other prescribed vegetation — forever, as defined in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan. Landowners may also add up to ten times their CREP Contract acreage to the easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. The easement is a legal agreement filed with county land records and held by a government agency or qualified nonprofit conservation organization, binding on current and all future landowners permanently. No structures may be built on enrolled lands. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, with Washington County participation through the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A permanent conservation easement is placed on eligible agricultural land. The State of Maryland acquires a permanent interest in the land in exchange for compensation to the landowner based on an easement valuation system. The exact amount is tailored to each property. Landowners with an existing FSA CREP Contract may also add up to ten times the CREP Contract acreage to their easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. No structures may be built on enrolled lands, and the land must be maintained in the vegetation type specified in the conservation plan or forest stewardship plan. The easement is filed with county land records and conveyed to a government agency or nonprofit conservation organization qualified to hold and enforce easements. Easement restrictions are permanent and apply to all future landowners. Annual monitoring of enrolled lands is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Maryland who have an existing federal CREP or Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) contract and have already installed the prescribed conservation practices on their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintaining land in approved conservation practices (e.g., riparian buffers, prescribed vegetation) as specified in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan, permanently protecting water quality and natural resources. Landowners may also add up to ten times their CREP Contract acreage to maximize land preservation and easement value.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. As of January 2024, all landowners in every county are eligible. Washington County landowners may apply through the Washington County Land Preservation Office.

Must have already installed the prescribed CREP or CRP conservation practice(s)
After the federal contract expires, must agree to keep land in an approved conservation practice as defined in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan permanently
Land use restrictions are specified in the easement; no structures may be built on enrolled lands
Land must be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan
Landowner may add up to ten times CREP Contract acreage to the easement
Easement remains effective in perpetuity and applies to all future landowners
Annual monitoring of enrolled lands is required
Landowner retains ownership but all restrictions pass to future owners
Must notify easement holder of proposed changes to the property
Must allow annual monitoring visits
Must notify easement holder when selling or transferring the property
Must comply with all easement restrictions

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with an existing federal CREP or CRP contract should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to inquire about enrolling in a permanent easement after their federal contract expires. A conservation easement is then tailored to the specific property and situation of the landowner, filed with county land records, and conveyed to a government agency or qualified nonprofit conservation organization. Washington County landowners may also apply through the Washington County Land Preservation Office. Contact information for local sponsors is available via the DNR contact list.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) offers paid and volunteer internships to high school and college students across a wide range of environmental, scientific, natural resources, and administrative fields. Interns gain hands-on experience working within DNR units including Chesapeake and Coastal Service, Fishing and Boating Services, Maryland Park Service, Natural Resources Police, and more. Interns apply classroom learning to real-world practice, build professional skills under experienced mentors, and can earn academic credit. Positions span areas such as environmental planning, fisheries biology, coastal restoration, outdoor recreation, graphic design, natural resources monitoring, grant program support, water quality monitoring, and law enforcement community outreach. Enrichment activities such as a welcome lunch, career panel, and field trips are also included. Internships run for approximately 10–12 weeks in summer (June–August) or fall (October–December).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full and part-time paid and volunteer internships lasting approximately 10–12 weeks. Summer internships run June–August and open for applications in February; fall internships run October–December and open for applications in July. Interns may earn academic credit and receive a stipend for paid positions. Enrichment activities including a welcome lunch, career panel, and field trips are included. Positions cover fields such as environmental planning, fisheries biology, coastal restoration, outdoor recreation, graphic design, water quality monitoring, grant program support, and natural resources law enforcement outreach.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Summer internships open for applications in February; fall internships open for applications in July.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school and college students, or recent graduates within one year of the internship start date, interested in environmental, natural resources, outdoor recreation, or related careers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intern stipend or volunteer experience; academic credit available. Positions cover areas including grant program support, coastal restoration, fisheries surveys, outdoor recreation outreach, law enforcement community outreach, graphic design, and water quality monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Most internships are based in Annapolis, MD, but positions may be located across Maryland depending on agency needs.

Completed state application
Resume
Two letters of recommendation (not from relatives)
Unofficial transcript with minimum 2.5 GPA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: When available, internships are posted on the State of Maryland Job Openings webpage at jobapscloud.com/MD. Applicants can also submit an Internship Interest Form to be notified when future internships open. Applications must include a state application, resume, two letters of recommendation, and an unofficial transcript.

structured_extraction.program_name: Elk Neck State Forest Fuelwood Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Elk Neck State Forest Fuelwood Program allows members of the public to obtain firewood (downed, damaged, or standing dead trees) from designated trail areas within Elk Neck State Forest for personal use only. Permits are issued on a daily basis at $10 per permit, with operations progressing eastward through the forest along main driving trails. Permittees may collect up to one standard pickup load per day and no more than 5 loads per calendar year. No resale of collected wood is permitted. Operations are restricted to the Trails Area within 200 linear feet of main driving trails (excluding Trail 2 south of Plum Creek and areas near Irishtown Road) and are prohibited from September 1 through January 31.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Daily permits are issued for $10.00 each, allowing permit holders to collect up to one standard pickup load of firewood per day (not exceeding one cord and not exceeding cab height of the pickup truck). Permittees are limited to no more than 5 standard loads per calendar year and no more than 3 permittees are allowed per day. Operations are prohibited from September 1 through January 31 each year, and no weekend or after-hours operations are permitted. Dump trucks and other heavy service vehicles are prohibited. Splitting of material on Elk Neck State Forest is prohibited. All material is for personal use only — resale is prohibited.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal firewood collection from downed, damaged, or standing dead trees within designated trail areas of Elk Neck State Forest. No resale permitted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Elk Neck State Forest in Cecil County, Maryland. Operations cover the Trails Area within 200 linear feet of main driving trails (excluding Trail 2 south of Plum Creek and areas near Irishtown Road).

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Conservation Act Qualified Professional Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Conservation Act (FCA) Qualified Professional (QP) program certifies individuals to prepare Forest Stand Delineations (FSDs) and Forest Conservation Plans (FCPs) required during land development in Maryland. Applicants must meet education and experience requirements and complete a DNR-approved 40-hour forest conservation training course before applying for QP status.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants must complete a 40-hour DNR-approved forest conservation course (offered as noncredit professional training through Anne Arundel Community College or Carroll Community College) and then submit a Qualified Professional Application to DNR along with resume, transcripts, and a supervisor reference. Upon approval by the State Forest Conservation Manager, the applicant receives Qualified Professional status allowing them to legally prepare Forest Stand Delineations and Forest Conservation Plans under the FCA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed foresters, licensed landscape architects, and other professionals with degrees or experience in natural resource sciences, management, landscape planning, or environmental planning who want to prepare Forest Stand Delineations and Forest Conservation Plans in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to legally prepare Forest Stand Delineations (FSDs) and Forest Conservation Plans (FCPs) under the Maryland Forest Conservation Act.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Certification applies to work performed anywhere in Maryland. The application form lists all 24 Maryland counties; applicants may self-select the counties or regions where they advertise their services, but program eligibility is not restricted by county.
requirements_list: Bachelor's or graduate degree in Natural Resource Sciences or Management, or Landscape or Environmental Planning; OR four years of relevant professional experience in those fields; OR a graduate degree in natural resources plus at least one year of relevant experience
Satisfactory completion of a DNR-approved forest conservation training program (currently offered as a 40-hour course through Anne Arundel Community College or Carroll Community College)
Submission of completed Qualified Professional Application with transcripts and resume
Supervisor reference/sign-off required
Proof of forest conservation training certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Meet the education or experience eligibility requirements. 2. Complete the DNR-approved 40-hour forest conservation course at Anne Arundel Community College or Carroll Community College. 3. Download the Qualified Professional Application from the DNR website. 4. Submit the completed application, resume, transcripts, forest conservation training certificate, and supervisor reference to FCA.DNR@maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland DNR Forest Service, Tawes State Office Building E-1, 580 Taylor Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401. 5. The State Forest Conservation Manager reviews and grants final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides funds to eligible applicants to cover the cost of obtaining up to two independent appraisals for properties proposed for acquisition under the Greenspace Equity Program. Funded through the state share of Program Open Space subject to annual budget actions, the program targets overburdened and underserved communities as identified by the MDEnviroScreen tool. Approved applicants must complete appraisals in time to submit a property acquisition application in the upcoming FY 2028 Greenspace Equity Program Grant round.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable competitive grant funding to cover costs for up to two independent appraisals obtained from certified general real estate appraisers for properties proposed for acquisition under the Greenspace Equity Program. Narrative reports must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) standards. Funded through the state share of Program Open Space subject to annual budget actions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land trusts (qualifying under IRC §170(H)(3), MET cooperative agreement, or Affordable Housing Land Trust designation), county governments, and municipal governments in overburdened and underserved communities seeking to acquire greenspace who need appraisal funding before submitting a full acquisition application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may only be used to obtain independent appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers with qualifications consistent with industry standards and all applicable Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations. Narrative reports must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; proposed property must be located in an overburdened or underserved community (or adjacent census tract) as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool, and must be located in Maryland with a MD Legislative District number.
requirements_list: Property proposed for acquisition must meet the general requirements of the Greenspace Equity Program
Property must be located in an overburdened or underserved community as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool
Applicants may request funding for up to two independent appraisals

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide outreach program run by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to introduce novice hunters and shooters to hunting and shooting sports. The program offers free or low-cost mini-workshops, mentored hunts, and other hands-on events in partnership with shooting ranges, nonprofits, and government agencies. Events cover topics such as waterfowl hunting basics, rifle handling, and managed deer hunts, and include both classroom instruction and live-fire range time. The program aims to give participants enough knowledge and connections to continue pursuing hunting and shooting sports on their own. Equipment such as shotguns, ammunition, and safety gear is provided at no cost for qualifying events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost hands-on workshops, mentored hunts, and events. Most events are free to participants; some partner events may charge a fee (e.g., $100 for certain rifle workshops). Shotguns, ammunition, and safety equipment are provided at no cost for qualifying events. Participants are selected by application or lottery depending on the event.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by event; registration closes before each individual event
structured_extraction.program_audience: Novice hunters and shooters, youth (ages 14–17 for some events), women, active military, military veterans, and lapsed or intermediate hunters ages 18 and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in hunting and shooting sports workshops, mentored hunts, managed deer hunts, and shooting sports events including classroom instruction and live-fire range time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; specific events held at various locations including Seneca Creek State Park and shooting ranges across the state; some events give preference to residents of specific counties (e.g., Dorchester County for the Grand National Waterfowl Association Youth Hunt)

Some events require Hunter Education certification and a current hunting license

Dorchester County youth residents receive preference for the youth waterfowl hunt
Applications reviewed for acceptance; space is limited and some events use lottery selection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online via Google Forms links provided for each individual event on the program page. Accepted participants are notified by email by specified dates before the event. Contact the event coordinator with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides interest-free loans to local land trusts. The loans help them buy land and conservation easements for preservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers interest-free loans to help with the purchase of conservation lands and easements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually Rolling applications. Deadlines are set by real estate settlement dates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local land trusts and individuals who want to purchase conservation lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase conservation lands and easements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure Program (FY 2022–2023 Capital Budget)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded through the FY 2022 and FY 2023 Maryland capital budgets (HB590 and SB291) that provides grants primarily to local governments for park and recreation projects. Administered similarly to Program Open Space local grants for acquisition and development projects, with the matching requirement waived. Funds may not be used for projects inaccessible to the general public, that require memberships, exclude the public due to high use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants for park and recreation acquisition and development projects. Matching requirement is waived. Specific dollar amounts not stated. Funded through FY 2022 and FY 2023 state capital budgets. Funds cannot support projects that are inaccessible to the general public, require memberships, exclude the public due to higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities. Reimbursement-based: grantees submit reimbursement requests after expenditures are incurred.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties, municipalities, and Baltimore City) and certain nonprofit organizations in Maryland involved in park and recreation projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land for local parks and playgrounds (including incidental costs such as appraisals, surveys, title work, legal fees, and settlement fees); design, construction, and capital equipping of indoor and outdoor park infrastructure and other capital-eligible projects that enhance recreational amenities. Funds may not be used for projects that require memberships, exclude the public because of higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to local governments (counties, municipalities, and Baltimore City) across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) reimburses marinas for the purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities. Funding is also available for pumpout operations, maintenance, upgrades, and replacements of existing sewage pumpout stations. Annual grants are also available to cover operations and maintenance costs of existing stations. The program gives boaters a proper method of disposing of sewage, contributing to cleaner Maryland waters. It is funded 75% by the federal Clean Vessel Act and 25% by the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund. Marinas must pay for equipment upfront and then submit paperwork for reimbursement. Some county permit fees for first-time installations are also reimbursable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants for marinas. New installations: up to $20,000; replacements/upgrades: up to $18,000 (case-by-case exceptions available). Annual operations and maintenance (O&M) grants are also available, capped at $5,000 per marina per boating season. The 2026 O&M grant covers the boating season from April 15, 2026 to November 15, 2026, with reimbursement submitted between November 15, 2026 and January 15, 2027. Marinas must pay for equipment upfront and then submit paperwork for reimbursement. Some county permit fees for first-time installations are also reimbursable. Grants are available for up to one year after the date they are approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing for installation grants (no fixed deadline stated); O&M applications for 2026 season were due prior to April 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private marinas in Maryland seeking to install, upgrade, or maintain marine sewage pumpout facilities, including marinas with existing sewage pumpout stations seeking operations and maintenance support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities; pumpout operations and maintenance; pumpout upgrades and replacement; permit fees for first-time installations; annual operations and maintenance of existing pumpout stations. O&M eligible expenses include staff labor ($3.75/pumpout, repair labor) and pumpout logs tracking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to marinas throughout Maryland. Projects may be located in any Maryland county. Local health department and MDE approval required for sewage disposal method. Contractors must be licensed to do business in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For installation grants: 1) Download and complete the DNR Maryland Pumpout Grant Application (or call 410-260-8772). 2) Submit the completed application with a project proposal, equipment quotes, at least three competitive bids from Maryland-licensed contractors, and a site drawing. 3) Complete Part I of the Coordinated Environmental Review Form and send to DNR; DNR will coordinate with the local health department and MDE. Obtain any required local permits and forward copies to DNR. 4) Complete the Watershed and Climate Services Risk Assessment Form. 5) Once all approvals and permits are in hand, DNR will approve the application.
