Applications must be submitted and approved prior to the start of the boating season (April 15). Reimbursement invoices are submitted between November 15 and January 15 following the boating season. Contact pumpouts.dnr@maryland.gov or 410-260-8772 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Abandoned Boat and Debris Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) provides reimbursable grants and technical expertise to help authorized public agencies remove abandoned boats and hazardous debris from Maryland state waterways. Abandoned vessels and debris can pose navigation hazards and environmental risks. Grants cover up to 100% of removal and disposal costs, up to $25,000 per project, and are reimbursable after completion of work and compliance with all grant terms and conditions. Each grant project period does not exceed one year. Funding comes from the state Waterway Improvement Fund, which is generated from a one-time 5% excise tax paid when a boat is purchased and titled in Maryland. The program aims to keep state waterways safe for navigation and protect the environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% reimbursable grants of up to $25,000 per project and technical expertise for the removal and disposal of abandoned vessels and hazardous debris from Maryland state waters. Eligible costs include labor, equipment, and contractor services. Reimbursement is provided after the work is completed and all grant terms and conditions are met. Applications are accepted in July and funds are obligated immediately upon approval. Each grant project period does not exceed one year. Funded by the Waterway Improvement Fund (a one-time 5% excise tax on boat purchases titled in Maryland).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Authorized public entities in Maryland — including local governments and municipalities — that have ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where an abandoned vessel or hazardous debris is located.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal and disposal of abandoned vessels and hazardous debris from Maryland state waters, including vessels proven abandoned under Natural Resources Article §8-721 and debris that poses a hazard to navigation or limits access to a public boating facility or shipping channel. Eligible costs include labor, equipment, and contractor services including contractor services, supplies, materials, equipment rental, and in-house labor/equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for public entities with jurisdiction over the waterway location of the abandoned vessel or debris. Eligible sites must be in state waters under the jurisdiction of the applying public entity.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an authorized public entity (e.g., local government or municipality) with ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where the vessel or debris is located.
Abandoned boats must be proven abandoned in accordance with Natural Resources Article §8-721.
Debris must pose a hazard to navigation or limit access to a public boating access facility or shipping channel to be eligible for removal.
Reimbursement is contingent upon compliance with all terms and conditions of the grant.
Applications are accepted in July.
Removal must be from state waters in Maryland.
Project must involve removal of abandoned boats or debris from Maryland state waters.
Invoices/requisitions with proof of payment (canceled checks or EFT printouts) must be submitted with reimbursement request.
Before and after photos of debris/boat removal must be provided.
Contractor must be selected via public bidding (lowest bidder) or existing Blanket Purchase Order.
For abandoned vessels: proof of abandonment and compliance with Natural Resource Article §8-721, including NRP-419 report or owner notice, must be provided.
Subcontractor contracts must be retained for 3 years post-reimbursement.
All registered Maryland boaters must have equal access to the improved public boating facility.
Project period may not exceed one year per grant.
All necessary Federal, State, and local permits must be secured before construction.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the grant application (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF on the program page) during the July application window. Funds are obligated immediately upon approval. After completing the removal work, submit the reimbursement form (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF) to DNR Boating Services Unit, 303 Marine Academy Drive, Stevensville, MD 21666 along with documentation showing compliance with all grant terms and conditions. Allow one month from receipt for reimbursement processing. Visit https://dnr.maryland.gov/Boating/Pages/abandonedboats.aspx for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) Training and Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers training and professional certification in stream sampling protocols and taxonomic standards used by the Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS). Summer training is held over 4 days in-person at Bowie State University, covering classroom instruction, laboratory work, and field protocol demonstrations. Six certifications are available: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. These certifications are required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for biomonitoring and stream monitoring work to be considered consistent with MBSS protocols. Certifications are valid for one to three years depending on type, except mussel taxonomy which is valid indefinitely with annual documentation. Only individuals can be certified — not firms, organizations, or agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Four-day in-person summer training held May 26–29, 2026 at Bowie State University, with classroom/laboratory instruction and field protocol demonstrations. Participants may register for 1–2 days at $75 per day, or 3 or more days for $200 total. Six certifications are available upon passing written tests, field audits, and other quality assurance procedures. Certification fees vary by type and payment is not accepted until written tests are passed. Benthic macroinvertebrate sampling certification costs $750 plus annual spring training registration; lab processing/subsampling certification costs $425; fish crew leader and fish taxonomy certifications cost $300 each ($400 combined); mussel taxonomy certification costs $50; physical habitat assessment certification fee not specified. Benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, lab processing/subsampling, fish crew leader, and fish taxonomy certifications are valid for 3 years; physical habitat assessment certification is valid for 1 year from date of issue; freshwater mussel taxonomy certification is valid indefinitely with annual documentation of minimum experience. Only individuals can be certified — not firms, organizations, or agencies. Fish taxonomy certification requires correctly identifying all fish from an electrofishing pass with ≥15 species richness, with ≤1 misidentification allowed. Fish crew leader certification requires successfully sampling own site in adherence to MBSS protocols. Mussel taxonomy certification requires ≥90% on mussel taxonomy test and 100% on state-listed species identification test. Physical Habitat Assessment certification is only offered during MBSS summer training (policy effective 2024).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Summer training May 26–29, 2026; registration open now; field audits for fish certifications must be scheduled before June 15 annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Environmental professionals, consultants, individuals, and agency staff (non-profit, for-profit, and government) who conduct or are required to conduct stream biomonitoring using MBSS protocols, including those working for counties or state agencies and those needing MBSS certification for stream sampling, fish surveys, mussel surveys, or physical habitat assessments in Maryland. Open to both professionals and non-professionals. Only individuals can be certified (not firms, organizations, or agencies).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training and certification program, not a funding program. Registration fees ($75–$200) are paid by participants to attend training. Certifications demonstrate competency in benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, fish sampling, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment using MBSS protocols.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Training is held at Bowie State University (benthic lab certification at DNR Annapolis office). Certifications are required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for MBSS-consistent biomonitoring work.
requirements_list: Attend MBSS spring or summer training (required for 5 of 6 certifications; annual attendance at MBSS summer trainings required to maintain fish certifications)

Pass written tests administered at training (≥90% passing score required for fish taxonomy and mussel taxonomy certifications; 100% on state-listed species identification test for mussel taxonomy; pass for fish crew leader)

Pass field audits conducted by a DNR Quality Control Officer (required in Year 1 for most certifications; field audit for fish certifications must be scheduled before June 15 annually; benthic sampling field audit must be scheduled before March 15; BIBI score difference ≤1.0 acceptable for benthic sampling audit)

For fish taxonomy field audit: correctly identify all fish from electrofishing pass with ≥15 species richness; ≤1 misidentification allowed; bring fish ID keys, formalin, voucher jars/containers, labels, digital camera, species lists, and decontamination solution
For fish crew leader field audit: successfully sample own site in adherence to MBSS protocols; bring required electrofishing equipment
Pass laboratory audit and written test for benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling certification (completed same day at DNR Annapolis office)
For benthic macroinvertebrate taxonomy: hold SFS Group 2 (EPT genera) and Group 3 (Chironomidae genera) certifications

For benthic macroinvertebrate sampling field audit: bring required equipment including D-net ≤600 micron, waders without felt soles, 95% ethanol, and sample containers; must correctly execute sampling protocol across five habitat types (Riffle, Rootward/Woody Debris, Leaf Pack, Macrophytes, Undercut Banks); nine essential elements must be passed or certification is disqualified; D-net/sieve inspection, proper preservation ratio, correct labeling, disinfection technique, and non-felt waders are among essential elements

Provide documentation of adequate prior experience with regional mussel survey protocols for mussel taxonomy certification (≥20 surveys within last 10 years OR ≥10 surveys within last 5 years plus two letters of reference)
For mussel taxonomy certification: score ≥90% on mussel taxonomy test and 100% on state-listed species identification test; no misidentification of non-listed species as threatened/endangered
Certification fees must be submitted after passing written tests (payment not accepted before then); payment due one week after field audit for fish certifications
Obtain appropriate state and/or federal permits prior to conducting mussel survey work
To maintain benthic macroinvertebrate sampling certification: attend spring training each year during the 3-year certification term
To maintain fish crew leader certification: attend fish sampling protocol portion of summer training each year during the 3-year certification term

To maintain mussel taxonomy certification: provide annual documentation of minimum experience (handle ≥5 individuals of each threatened/endangered species per year in field, or 0.5 hours per species in museum reference collection) and report prior-year experience to DNR by February 15 annually; maintain running 2-year average; certification lapses if requirements unmet
Physical Habitat Assessment certification is only offered during MBSS summer training (policy effective 2024); certification is valid for one year from date of issue
For Physical Habitat Assessment certification: attend presentations and field demonstration at MBSS summer training, pass written test, and undergo field audit during MBSS summer training
No walk-ins accepted; online registration required in advance; registrations are first-come-first-served; refunds considered on a case-by-case basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for summer training using the Google Forms link on the program page. Pay registration fees ($75–$200) through the DNR Outdoor Store (credit card). Attend in-person training at Bowie State University. Pass required written tests at training, then submit certification fees and complete required field or laboratory audits to obtain certification. For fish certifications, schedule field audit before June 15; payment due one week after audit; name then posted to MBSS Certification Registry. Field audits are conducted by MBSS Auditors using standardized checklists. For benthic macroinvertebrate lab certification, training, written test, and proficiency demonstration are completed same day at DNR Annapolis office. For mussel taxonomy certification, submit prior experience documentation for review after passing tests; DNR then initiates certification payment process. Contact william.harbold@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Marina Initiative is a voluntary certification program operated by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that recognizes and promotes marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs demonstrating environmentally responsible practices. Facilities that meet legal requirements and voluntarily adopt pollution prevention practices can earn certification as a Clean Marina or Clean Marina Partner. The program provides a guidebook with best management practices, a self-evaluation checklist, staff assistance, workshop opportunities, and an optional informal site visit to help facilities meet certification requirements. Certified marinas receive the right to use the Clean Marina logo in advertising, an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, a large aluminum sign, a free online business listing, acknowledgment in Clean Marina publications, promotional advertisements in regional boating publications, and a DNR-issued news release recognizing the facility. Certified facilities must annually sign an Affirmation of Good Standing and undergo a reaffirmation visit at least every three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Facilities receive certification as a Clean Marina or Clean Marina Partner designation. The program provides a guidebook with best management practices, a self-evaluation checklist, staff assistance, and workshop opportunities to help facilities meet certification requirements. Certified marinas receive the right to use the Clean Marina logo in advertising, an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, a large aluminum sign, a free online business listing, acknowledgment in Clean Marina publications, and promotional advertisements in regional boating publications. DNR also issues a news release recognizing certified facilities. No direct financial assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs of any size operating in Maryland waters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification support, pollution prevention best practices, and recognition and marketing benefits for marine facilities that meet environmental stewardship standards for protecting Maryland waterways
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs throughout Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Meet legal requirements for marina operations
Voluntarily adopt pollution prevention practices
Sign the Clean Marina Pledge committing to keep Maryland waterways clean and send a photocopy to DNR
Assess facility using the Clean Marina Award Checklist and Guidebook

Meet minimum passing scores on the Award Checklist: Vessel Maintenance & Repair (85%), Petroleum Control (80%), Emergency Planning (80%), Sewage Handling (80%), Waste Containment & Disposal (85%), Marina Management (80%), Stormwater Management (75%), Marina Design & Maintenance (70%)
Pass a confirmation site visit by Clean Marina staff and a certified Clean Marina operator
Receive approval from the Clean Marina advisory committee
Annually sign and return the Affirmation of Good Standing
Undergo reaffirmation visit at least every three years
Implement appropriate pollution prevention practices within one year of signing the Clean Marina Pledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Obtain program materials by attending a workshop, downloading documents from the DNR website, or contacting the Clean Marina office. (2) Sign the Clean Marina Pledge and send a photocopy to DNR. (3) Assess your facility using the Clean Marina Award Checklist and Guidebook, optionally requesting an informal site visit from Clean Marina staff. (4) Implement recommended changes at your own pace (within one year of signing the pledge). (5) When ready, call the Clean Marina office to schedule a confirmation visit. (6) After the visit, Clean Marina staff share results with the advisory committee, which reviews and approves certification. Contact Donna Morrow at donna.morrow@maryland.gov or 410-260-8773 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Conservation Corps (MCC) is an award-winning AmeriCorps-style conservation service program managed by the Maryland Park Service and operated by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. It engages young adults ages 18–24 in natural resource management and park conservation projects across Maryland's state parks, public lands, forests, watersheds, and communities. Members serve on crews of 5–7 people performing hands-on conservation tasks including planting trees and native plants, building and maintaining trails, restoring wildlife habitat, removing invasive species, chainsaw operation, hemlock treatments, land stewardship, educational programming, and supporting the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. Service runs from mid-September through late June. Members receive a living stipend, low-cost state park housing averaging $150/month including utilities, health insurance through Cigna Healthcare (premium paid by the program, covering medical, prescription, AD&D, vision, and dental), a $200 boot reimbursement, a $150 pant reimbursement, uniforms, personal protective equipment, a $6,000 completion award, and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate. Training includes First Aid/CPR/AED, 40-hour Wildland Fire Fighting certification, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Chainsaw Skills and Safety, Leave No Trace ethics, trail maintenance and construction, Canoe Trip Leading, and Foundation for Search Operations. Since 2025, the program partners with DSCI's Maryland Corps/Service Year Option and is designed to prepare participants for careers in conservation, park operations, and land management. Shadow/volunteer opportunities are available from October through early June for prospective applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members receive a living stipend, low-cost state park housing averaging $150/month including utilities, health insurance through Cigna Healthcare (premium paid by the program, covering medical, prescription, AD&D, vision, and dental), a $200 boot reimbursement, a $150 pant reimbursement, uniforms, all personal protective equipment, a $6,000 completion award, and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate upon finishing the program. Training certifications include First Aid/CPR/AED, 40-hour Wildland Fire Fighting, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Chainsaw Skills and Safety, Leave No Trace ethics, trail maintenance and construction, Canoe Trip Leading, and Foundation for Search Operations. Service runs mid-September through late June. Projects are supervised by experienced DNR staff. Shadow/volunteer opportunities are available October through early June for prospective applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18–24 who are U.S. citizens, Maryland residents at the time of application, with a high school diploma or GED (or who will acquire one), who are interested in natural resource conservation, park operations, and environmental community service in Maryland, seeking careers in conservation, park operations, and land management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in conservation and park improvement projects across Maryland state parks, forests, public lands, watersheds, and the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays, including trail building, habitat restoration, invasive species removal, hemlock treatments, tree planting, educational programming, and chainsaw operation. Member benefits include housing, health insurance, gear reimbursements, uniforms, a living stipend, a $6,000 completion award, professional training certifications, and career development support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — projects and crew placements take place across Maryland's state parks, forests, public lands, watersheds, communities, and along the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. Must be a Maryland resident at the time of application.
requirements_list: Must be 18–24 years of age
Must be a Maryland resident at the time of application
Must be a United States citizen
Must have or acquire a high school diploma or GED
Must demonstrate dedication and commitment to service
Must have a desire to work in conservation
Must be willing to work in all kinds of outdoor conditions
Must be willing to camp for up to a week at a time
Must be able to work in a team-based crew environment
Must be a team player and have a positive attitude
Personal or public transportation to a designated job site is required
Projects are supervised by experienced DNR staff
Submit an online application through the Department of Service and Civic Innovation website at dsci.maryland.gov (via the BuildWithin portal)
Application includes: outdoor interest, preferred geographic location(s), and specific MCC interest
AI pre-screening questionnaire completed through the BuildWithin portal
Virtual interview with MCC staff, scheduled beginning in May
Hiring target is by August 19th with a program start date of September 9th
Application is reviewed by the Conservation Corps Program Officer
Prospective members can shadow a crew for a day (available October through early June) before applying by signing up through a Google Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the BuildWithin portal via the Department of Service and Civic Innovation website at dsci.maryland.gov, or see the 'How to Apply' page at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Pages/mcc_application.aspx for application details. Steps include: (1) Create an account on the BuildWithin portal; (2) Submit an application including outdoor interest, preferred geographic location(s), and specific interest in MCC; (3) Complete an AI pre-screening questionnaire; (4) Participate in a virtual interview with MCC staff. Interviews are scheduled beginning in May, with hiring completed by August 19th and a program start date of September 9th. Applicants can register for an informational webinar to learn more. Housing is assigned on a first-come, first-served basis with preference given to out-of-area members. Prospective members can shadow a crew for a day (available October through early June) before applying by signing up through a Google Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week, non-residential summer program operated by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) in partnership with community youth organizations. Participants join a crew to work on hands-on outdoor conservation projects in Maryland State Parks — building bridges and trails, making rain barrels, and interacting with wildlife — while also enjoying outdoor recreation activities such as climbing walls and wildlife encounters. The program aims to give youth the skills needed to prepare for career opportunities and a lifetime of outdoor engagement, providing paid summer employment, conservation skills, environmental stewardship experience, and career readiness training. Note: The program is currently on hiatus while undergoing organizational restructuring.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants join a crew for five to six weeks during the summer to work on outdoor conservation projects in Maryland State Parks. The program is non-residential and includes both hands-on work projects (bridge and trail building, rain barrel construction, habitat restoration, invasive species removal, tree planting, waterway cleanup, park facility repairs) and outdoor recreational activities (climbing walls, wildlife encounters, archery, kayaking, fishing, stream surveys, camping). Participants receive paid summer employment, gain conservation skills, environmental stewardship experience, and career readiness training. In 2018, total program value was approximately $2,755,000, employing 465 youth across 133 projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disadvantaged youth ages 14–19 in Maryland, particularly those from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, and Anne Arundel County, seeking hands-on outdoor conservation work experience and paid summer employment in Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid summer employment wages; conservation and restoration work in Maryland State Parks including trail and bridge building, rain barrel construction, habitat restoration, invasive plant removal, invasive species removal, tree planting, waterway cleanup, and park facility repairs; skills training in outdoor recreation (archery, kayaking, fishing, stream surveys, wildlife identification, camping, canoeing, hiking), power tools, knot-tying, woodworking, and career readiness; uniforms, safety equipment, transportation, and meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates at Maryland State Parks and other public lands statewide, with a mission focus on the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Historically served participants primarily from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, and Anne Arundel County. Parks served have included Assateague State Park, Gunpowder Falls State Park, Gwynns Falls Trail, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad State Park, Lake Clifton Park, Merkle Wildlife Sanctuary, Patapsco Valley State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, Rocks State Park, Rocky Gap State Park, Rosaryville State Park, Sandy Point State Park, Seneca Creek State Park, Susquehanna State Park, Smallwood State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapman State Park, Cunningham Falls State Park, Patuxent River State Park, Monocacy Natural Resource Management Area, Tuckahoe State Park, Cylburn Arboretum, Tawes Garden, and Southern Maryland Recreational Complex, as well as nearby city and county parks.
requirements_list: Must be ages 14–19
Must be a youth participant affiliated with a community youth organization or referred through a partner organization
Participation is through partnership with community youth organizations, local government agencies, and nonprofits
Program is a summer seasonal opportunity
Priority recruitment targets first-time workers ages 14–15; returning corps members ages 16–17
Must commit to attending the full summer employment period (five days per week)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth are recruited through partner organizations including local government agencies (e.g., Mayor's Office for Employment Development/Youthworks in Baltimore City, county Departments of Social Services, county Departments of Recreation) and nonprofits (e.g., Civicworks, Telamon Services, Worcester County Board of Education, Chesapeake Research Consortium). Check the Maryland DNR website for updates on opportunities to join a future iteration of the program. You may also contact the CJC program via the Contact Us page on the DNR website or by calling 1-800-830-3974.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, fully in-person, multi-day hunter safety education course that provides the Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license. The course is taught by state-certified Hunter Safety Education Instructors and covers firearm safety, hunting skills, wildlife conservation, ethics, and Maryland-specific regulations. Students must pass a 50-question written test (80% passing score required) and a Trail Walk practical skills evaluation to receive their certificate. The course runs 12–16 hours and includes classroom instruction, a Trail Walk evaluation, and a live-fire range session. Pre-registration is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, multi-day classroom training course (12–16 hours) covering firearm safety, hunting skills, wildlife conservation, ethics, and Maryland-specific hunting regulations. Includes classroom sessions, a 50-question multiple choice test (80% passing score required), a Trail Walk practical skills evaluation, and a live-fire range session. Pre-registration is required. Successful completers receive a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who wish to obtain a Maryland hunting license and need the required Certificate of Competency in hunter safety, especially new and younger hunters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunter safety education and certification required to purchase a Maryland hunting license — no funds are disbursed to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; classes are scheduled independently by training teams throughout the state.
requirements_list: Pre-registration required
Must pass a 50-question multiple choice test with a score of 80% or higher
Must pass the Trail Walk practical skills evaluation
Must demonstrate ability to behave in a mature and safe manner
Must wear proper clothing for outdoor sessions
Check individual class descriptions for any special requirements or live-fire waivers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online for a scheduled Classroom Course through the DNR registration portal at register-ed.com/programs/maryland/88-maryland-hunter-education-classroom-course. Check the DNR website for currently scheduled classes near you and note any special instructions for the specific class location before registering.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Mentored Hunt Program pairs first-time and lapsed hunters (mentees) with experienced veteran hunters (mentors) to teach hunting skills. The program includes technical lectures on firearm safety, hunting techniques, and strategies, as well as hands-on range time. Mentors and mentees communicate directly throughout the program, and staff and partner organizations contribute resources and knowledge to prepare mentees for hunting. The program is free to participate in and is open to first-time hunters, apprentice license holders, junior hunters, and lapsed hunters of all ages across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mentored hunting education program that pairs new or lapsed hunters with experienced mentor hunters. Includes structured technical lectures on firearm safety, hunting techniques, and strategies, hands-on range time, and one-on-one mentorship. No cost to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time hunters, apprentice license holders, junior/youth hunters, and lapsed hunters (those who held a Maryland hunting license in the past but have not purchased one recently) of all ages in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunting education, firearm safety training, hunting techniques and strategies, mentorship, and hands-on hunting experience through mentored instruction and range time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a first-time hunter, apprentice license holder, junior hunter, or lapsed hunter
Lapsed hunter defined as having held a MD hunting license in the past but not purchased one recently
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through learnhunting.org to become a mentor or mentee. Contact Torey Vayer at torey.vayer@maryland.gov with questions about the program. For technical issues with the learnhunting.org website, contact the web administrators at learnhunting.org/contact-us/.

structured_extraction.program_description: Virginia-licensed charter boat operators can apply for a Maryland Provisional Charter Boat Permit, which allows them to operate charter fishing trips in Maryland's tidal Chesapeake Bay waters without needing a Maryland commercial fishing guide license. The permit is free and non-transferable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free, non-transferable permit allowing Virginia-licensed charter boat captains to operate in Maryland tidal Chesapeake Bay waters. Applicants must submit a completed application form, proof of Virginia Charter Boat licensure in 2001 and 2002, a current Coast Guard license, and a current Virginia Charter Boat license. Processing takes at least one week. Applicants must reapply each year. Applications may be submitted by mail to Tawes State Office Bldg. B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401 or by fax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Virginia-licensed charter boat operators who wish to conduct charter fishing trips in Maryland tidal Chesapeake Bay waters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to operate a charter fishing vessel in Maryland tidal waters without a Maryland commercial fishing guide license
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for charter fishing trips originating from Virginia tidal waters and operating in the tidal Chesapeake Bay in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be licensed by Virginia to operate a charter boat in its jurisdictional tidal waters
Must hold a current Virginia Class A Fishing Guide License
Must provide documentation of fishing activity for 2001 and 2002 based on Virginia Marine Resources Commission licensing and reporting requirements
Must submit a completed application form
Must provide proof of Virginia Charter Boat licensure in 2001 and 2002
Must provide a copy of current Coast Guard license
Must provide a copy of current Virginia Charter Boat license
Must comply with the reciprocity agreement (effective January 1, 2009)
Permit is valid only for charter fishing trips originating from Virginia tidal waters
Permit is non-transferable
Must reapply each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Fishing Guide Reciprocity Application along with required documentation (proof of 2001 and 2002 Virginia Charter Boat licensure, current Coast Guard license, and current Virginia Charter Boat license) to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources by mail to Tawes State Office Bldg. B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401 or by fax to (410) 260-8279. Allow at least one week for processing. Permits cannot be processed at licensing service centers. Applicants must reapply each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free nature and parks education program for senior citizens age 55 and older. Participants attend six weekly sessions led by rangers, historians, naturalists, and other Maryland Department of Natural Resources experts. Topics include plants, animals, conservation, history, and stewardship. Sessions include exercise, expert-led talks, fellowship, games, and hikes. Programs are offered in spring and fall at multiple state parks across Maryland. Participants who complete all sessions earn a certified Senior Ranger designation. 2026 sessions are scheduled at Seneca Creek State Park, Bohemia River State Park, Elk Neck State Park, Patapsco Valley State Park, Calvert Cliffs/Merkle NRMA, Southern Maryland Recreational Complex, Tuckahoe/Martinak/Sassafras/Wye Island parks complex, and Janes Island State Park.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six weekly group sessions (roughly 1.5–2 hours each) held at participating Maryland state parks, led by rangers, naturalists, historians, and other experts. Sessions are offered in spring and fall. Participants who complete all sessions earn a Senior Ranger certification. A program fee of $40 applies (with a $10 discount for Golden Age Passholders). 2026 sessions are scheduled at Seneca Creek State Park, Bohemia River State Park (sessions May 6–June 17, 2026; meets 10 AM–12 Noon; 4030 Augustine Herman Hwy, Chesapeake City, MD), Elk Neck State Park (sessions May 13–June 17, 2026; meets 10 AM–12 Noon; North East, MD), Patapsco Valley State Park, Calvert Cliffs/Merkle NRMA, Southern Maryland Recreational Complex, Tuckahoe/Martinak/Sassafras/Wye Island parks complex (sessions Apr 28–May 26, 2026; meets Tuesdays 1–2:30 PM — cycle now concluded), and Janes Island State Park. Space is limited; registration is required through each park. Fall 2026 sessions are scheduled for September–November 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by park and session; registration opens April 1, 2026 for some locations; no explicit close date stated; fall sessions scheduled for September–November 2026; space is limited so contact your park to check availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 and older who want to learn about nature, state parks, and conservation while getting active and connecting with others. Golden Age Passholders are eligible for a $10 discount on the program fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides structured outdoor education, nature programming, physical activity, social engagement, and Senior Ranger certification to senior participants. A $40 program fee applies ($30 for Golden Age Passholders at some locations).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple Maryland state parks in the Central, Southern, Eastern, and (coming soon) Western regions, including Seneca Creek State Park, Bohemia River State Park (Chesapeake City, MD), Elk Neck State Park (North East, MD), Patapsco Valley State Park, Calvert Cliffs/Merkle NRMA, Tuckahoe/Martinak/Sassafras/Wye Island, and Janes Island State Park.
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older
Must register in advance through the specific park offering the program
Space is limited — availability varies by location and session
A program fee of $40 applies; Golden Age Passholders receive a $10 discount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact or register through the individual park hosting the session. Registration for some locations opens April 1, 2026. Some parks use an online Google Form registration; others ask you to email the listed park contact. Check the program page or the park's own website for current session dates and availability. Registration links and contact emails are listed for each park location on the program page. Contact examples: Bohemia River State Park — bohemiariver.statepark@maryland.gov; Elk Neck State Park — William Gibb, william.gibb@maryland.gov; Tuckahoe Complex — Erin Gale, erin.gale@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary statewide program that encourages Maryland residents to create backyard wildlife habitat. The program provides fact sheets, landscaping guides, identification resources, and a quarterly newsletter (HabiChat) to help landowners enhance their yards, schoolyards, or developments to provide food, water, shelter, and nesting areas for wildlife.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational resources including wildlife and plant fact sheets, landscaping guides, identification guides, nest box plans, and a quarterly newsletter to help residents create and improve backyard wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents, homeowners, and school communities interested in creating or improving wildlife habitat on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating backyard wildlife habitat by providing food, water, shelter, and nesting resources for wildlife through landscaping and habitat enhancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Participants must comply with local or county laws, homeowners' agreements, and other covenants.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application required. Access fact sheets, guides, and newsletters directly on the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Waterfront property owners grow young oysters (called spat) in cages suspended from their private piers for approximately 9–10 months, protecting the vulnerable young oysters from silt and predators during their first year of life. After the grow-out period, participants return the oysters for planting on local sanctuaries to enrich the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem and support large-scale native oyster restoration in Maryland. There is no cost to participants. The program began in the Tred Avon River in 2008 and has since expanded to 32 tributaries throughout Maryland. Community associations, non-profit organizations, RiverKeeper groups, local government, and public schools may serve as tributary sponsors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive up to four oyster cages stocked with up to 500 oyster spat per cage at no charge. Participants care for and maintain the cages for approximately 9–10 months, keeping oysters fully submerged at all times, then program staff collect the grown oysters for planting on local oyster sanctuaries. Participants retain the cages and may continue in the program each year by receiving new spat after collection. Community associations, non-profits, RiverKeeper groups, local government, and public schools may serve as tributary sponsors, supporting a minimum of 100 cages per tributary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Waterfront property owners with a pier or wharf in one of the 32 program tributaries (rivers, creeks, and coves) in Maryland who want to help restore the Chesapeake Bay oyster population and support Bay stewardship. Community associations, non-profits, RiverKeeper groups, local government, and public schools may serve as tributary sponsors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing and protecting young oysters in cages suspended from private piers for eventual planting on local oyster sanctuaries to enhance the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem and native oyster population.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in one of the 32 selected tributaries (rivers, creeks, and coves) participating in the program throughout Maryland. The pier or wharf must have at least four feet of water at low tide. Tributary selection is salinity-dependent. The program began in the Tred Avon River in 2008 and has since expanded to 32 tributaries statewide.
requirements_list: Must have an existing pier or wharf with at least four feet of water at low tide
Pier or wharf must be located in one of the 32 tributaries selected for the program
Must be willing to provide maintenance for up to four cages for up to 10 months
Must keep oysters fully submerged at all times
Must have an interest in Chesapeake Bay and oyster stewardship
Tributary sponsors must be able to support a minimum of 100 cages per tributary
Do not consume oysters raised at private piers due to unmonitored water quality and pathogen risk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the application package by March 31 annually via mail, email, or fax to DNR (580 Taylor Avenue, Annapolis MD 21401; eric.campbell@maryland.gov; fax 410-260-8279). Register online via the Oyster Gardening Registration link on the program page. If your tributary is not yet in the program, your group can apply to join using the How Your Tributary Can Join the Program application form. Once enrolled, participants receive notification from the local sponsor when cages are ready for pickup, along with a briefing and care instructions/information package.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Marylanders Plant Trees program is a statewide coupon program launched in 2009 that encourages Maryland residents and organizations to plant native trees. Participants receive a $25 coupon toward the purchase of one qualifying tree (retail value of at least $50) from participating retail nurseries and garden centers across Maryland. The discount is applied at the register at the time of sale. Coupons are valid for trees on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List. The program aims to help plant 150,000 new trees in Maryland and is funded through a Clean Air Act settlement with a major power generator, in partnership with the Office of the Attorney General and participating tree vendors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $25 coupon discount off the purchase of one qualifying tree (retail value of $50 or more) at participating retail nurseries and garden centers. The discount is applied at the register at the time of sale. One coupon is required per tree purchased. Trees must appear on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List. Retail sales only — wholesale tree sales do not qualify. The $25 cost is funded through a Clean Air Act violation settlement from a major power generator, in partnership with the Office of the Attorney General and participating tree vendors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and organizations purchasing native trees from participating retail nurseries and garden centers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of native or recommended trees listed on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List from a participating retail nursery or garden center
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating retail nurseries and garden centers located across Maryland
requirements_list: Tree must have a retail value of $50 or more
Tree must be on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List
Coupon must be filled in completely and signed by the customer
One coupon per tree purchased
Retail sales only; wholesale purchases do not qualify
Must use the coupon at a participating Marylanders Plant Trees (MPT) nursery or garden center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Print the $25 coupon from the program website. Step 2: Fill in the coupon completely and sign it. Step 3: Find a participating nursery in your area and present it at the register at the time of purchase of one qualifying native tree.

structured_extraction.program_description: A seven-day residential camp for high school students interested in careers in natural resources. The camp covers traditional forestry, GIS and GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology. Natural resource professionals deliver the curriculum, and students have the opportunity to develop contacts for future employment. County-level Forest Conservancy District Boards recruit two students per county, conduct interviews, and provide partial scholarships to attend. Students who are at least 16 years old by the first day of camp may earn two transferable college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by attending the full week and completing an exam.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-level Forest Conservancy District Boards recruit two students per county, conduct interviews, and provide partial scholarships to attend the seven-day residential camp. Students aged 16 or older by the first day of camp may also earn two transferable college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by attending the full week and completing an exam.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for NRCC 2025 are now being accepted (camp runs July 20–26, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in careers in natural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attendance at the seven-day Natural Resources Career Camp, including access to curriculum delivered by industry professionals, camp activities, and optional transferable college credit from Allegany College of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — students are recruited through county-level Forest Conservancy District Boards across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Must be recruited and interviewed by a local county Forest Conservancy District Board
Must be at least 16 years old by the first day of camp to be eligible for college credit
Must attend the full week and complete an exam to earn two transferable college credits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Forestry Foundation website (marylandforestryfoundation.org), linked from the DNR page. Local Forest Conservancy District Boards recruit and interview applicants from their counties and provide partial scholarships to selected students.

structured_extraction.program_name: New or Replacement Pumpout Installation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Installation grants for marinas to purchase and install new or replacement boat sewage pumpout systems. Funded under the federal Clean Vessel Act and the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant covering the purchase and installation of a new or replacement sewage pumpout system at a marina. Specific dollar amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas seeking to install new or replacement boat sewage pumpout systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of a new or replacement pumpout system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to marinas located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a marina seeking to install a new or replacement pumpout system.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Pumpout Grant Application and Agreement form. Review the 'How to Apply for a Grant for a New Pumpout' page for detailed instructions. Contact pumpouts.dnr@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports costs associated with providing outdoor learning field investigations away from school campuses for students in pre-Kindergarten through grade 12, as part of comprehensive Meaningful Watershed Educational Experiences (MWEEs) that contribute to school environmental literacy programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants available through the Department of Natural Resources Grants Gateway to support outdoor learning field investigations for K-12 students as part of Meaningful Watershed Educational Experiences (MWEEs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: School systems (districts), higher education institutions, and local and state agencies working in partnership with schools serving pre-K through grade 12 students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with providing outdoor learning field investigations away from school campuses for students in pre-K through grade 12.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a school system (district), higher education institution, or local/state agency working in partnership with schools
Activities must support outdoor learning field investigations away from school campuses
Must be part of comprehensive Meaningful Watershed Educational Experiences (MWEEs)
Must contribute to school environmental literacy programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Department of Natural Resources Grants Gateway.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership Program (ORLP) provides competitive matching grants for park projects in underserved communities. It operates under the rules of the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) with additional eligibility requirements focused on population size and underserved community status. Projects must be located in a community with a population of 25,000 or more (per the 2020 Census) and must be determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation. Grants are competitive at the federal level and administered through the National Park Service (NPS), with coordination required from Maryland's Department of Natural Resources (DNR). Two application rounds are offered each year: a Spring Round and a Fall Round. Anticipated awards: 25–40 per calendar year, ranging from $300,000 to $15,000,000 per project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants for park projects in underserved communities. Award range: $300,000–$15,000,000 per project; anticipated 25–40 awards per calendar year. Requires a minimum 50% non-federal cost share (1:1 match); insular areas may receive 100% federal assistance. Grants are competitive at the federal level through the National Park Service (NPS). Applicants submit a pre-application to DNR, then a full application to NPS, and if selected, a final application package to NPS within one year of the NPS selection notification. Applications are accepted in two annual rounds: a Spring Round (pre-applications due April 15 to DNR, full applications due June 1 to NPS) and a Fall Round (pre-applications due September 15 to DNR, full applications due November 1 to NPS). Successful applicants are notified by September 1 (Spring Round) or February 1 (Fall Round). Agreement term is 1–3 years, negotiated per project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring Round: pre-applications due April 15 to DNR, full applications due June 1 to NPS (11:59 PM Eastern); Fall Round: pre-applications due September 15 to DNR, full applications due November 1 to NPS (11:59 PM Eastern). Recurring semi-annual deadlines through at least November 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and eligible organizations in underserved communities with a population of 25,000 or more seeking to develop or improve parks and outdoor recreation facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land for public outdoor recreation and development or rehabilitation of outdoor recreation facilities in urban underserved communities, subject to Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) rules and regulations. Eligible uses include green infrastructure, ecosystem restoration, disaster resilience, and native landscape restoration. Infrastructure projects must comply with American iron, steel, and domestic materials standards (2 CFR 184).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a Maryland community with a population of 25,000 or more per the 2020 Census and must be in a community determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation. A half-mile buffer is acceptable for Census/CEJST/EJScreen boundary definitions.

Must submit a full application to NPS by the applicable deadline (June 1 or November 1) if selected

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact Molly Pickel at DNR to discuss potential projects. 2. Submit a pre-application to DNR by April 15 (Spring Round) or September 15 (Fall Round). DNR reviews materials for eligibility and completeness. 3. Submit a full application to NPS via Grants.gov by June 1 (Spring Round) or November 1 (Fall Round) at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Applications undergo an Initial Review screening for eligibility and completeness, followed by a Comprehensive Merit Review scored on a 0–10 scale across 5 criteria (weights: Criterion 1: 20%, Criterion 2: 30%, Criterion 3: 10%, Criterion 4: 20%, Criterion 5: 20%). 4. The National Park Service selects applicants and notifies successful applicants by September 1 (Spring Round) or February 1 (Fall Round) that they may proceed to a final application package to NPS within one year. For technical support, contact ORLP_Inquiries@nps.gov or Grants.gov Customer Support at 1-800-518-4726.

structured_extraction.program_name: Play Area Accessibility – Recreation Communication Boards Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot grant program created by Maryland HB 420 (Chapter 568, signed May 9, 2024) that funds the purchase and installation of communication boards in public play areas at state and local parks. Communication boards display photos, symbols, or illustrations to help individuals with limited language skills communicate, improving play area accessibility. The program runs from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2028, subject to funding availability. Total funding is capped at $100,000; grants are available until funds are exhausted. Grants are capped at $3,000 per communication board.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based grants to eligible local governing bodies for the purchase and installation of communication boards in public play areas at state and local parks. Maximum of $3,000 per communication board. Total program funding is $100,000; grants are available on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted. Program is effective July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2028. Applicants submit a Request for Final Reimbursement form upon project completion with invoices, proof of payment, and labor/equipment documentation if applicable.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Effective July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2028, subject to funding availability; grants available until funds are exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governing bodies — the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission and the governing body of any county or Baltimore City. Municipal governments are excluded.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of communication boards (devices displaying photos, symbols, illustrations, words, and braille) in public play areas at state and local parks to improve accessibility for individuals with limited language skills. Eligible costs include supplies, materials, services, equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to local governing bodies in Maryland — the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission and the governing body of any county or Baltimore City.

Upon project completion, submit the Request for Final Reimbursement form with required documentation (invoices, proof of payment, and labor/equipment records if applicable) to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space (POS) Stateside, established in 1969, preserves natural areas across Maryland for public recreation, watershed protection, and wildlife protection. The program acquires land through fee simple purchases and conservation easements. Fee simple properties are managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as State Parks, Forests, and Wildlife and Fisheries Management Areas. The program also funds permanent Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) easements, making permanent conservation practices from 10- to 15-year CREP contracts. Funding is generated primarily from a 0.5 percent State property transfer tax. Properties are evaluated on two equally weighted categories: Land (ecological value, wildlife habitat connectivity, rare or endangered species, aquatic life support, forest water quality, location in Targeted Ecological Areas, restoration opportunity, climate adaptation) and People (new public access, water access, trail connections, capacity relief for existing units, coastal resilience, educational or historical value).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds acquisition of land (fee simple) and conservation easements for public recreation, watershed protection, wildlife habitat, and climate resilience. Properties are evaluated on two equally weighted categories: Land (ecological value, wildlife habitat connectivity, presence of rare or endangered species, support of aquatic life, forests important for water quality, location within Targeted Ecological Areas, restoration opportunity, and climate change adaptation) and People (new public access, public beach or water access in access-limited areas, critical trail connections, expansion of existing recreation opportunities, capacity relief for existing land units, coastal community resilience, and educational, cultural, or historical value). Funding also supports permanent CREP easements. Funded by a 0.5 percent State property transfer tax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners and entities (including individuals, non-profits, for-profits, and government bodies) with land that has ecological or recreational value in Maryland, including those whose properties could become State Parks, Forests, Wildlife and Fisheries Management Areas, or conservation easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of fee simple land and conservation easements for public recreation, wildlife habitat protection, watershed protection, climate resilience, and permanent conservation of ecologically valuable lands. Also funds permanent CREP easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, covering all 23 counties and Baltimore City including Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Carroll, Cecil, Baltimore, Harford, Frederick, Baltimore City, Kent, Howard, Queen Anne's, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Caroline, Prince George's, Talbot, Calvert, Charles, Dorchester, Wicomico, Worcester, St. Mary's, and Somerset.
requirements_list: Property is evaluated based on Land criteria: wildlife habitat connectivity, presence of rare or endangered species, support of aquatic life, forests important for water quality, location within Targeted Ecological Areas, restoration opportunity, and climate change adaptation.

Property is evaluated based on People criteria: provides high-value resource-based recreation, new public access, public beach or water access in access-limited areas, critical trail connections, expansion of existing recreation opportunities, addresses long-term management concerns for existing land units, buffers existing lands, contributes to large landscape protection, conserves natural features, enhances coastal community resilience, and has educational, cultural, or historical value.
Land and People evaluation components are equally weighted in acquisition decisions.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the DNR Real Property office using the Program Open Space Stateside Contacts page to inquire about and initiate discussion about a potential land acquisition. The department evaluates candidates through a review process balancing conservation attributes and public recreation needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual grant providing reimbursement to approved marinas for operations and maintenance costs of existing boat sewage pumpout stations during the boating season (April 15 – November 15). Funded under the federal Clean Vessel Act (CFDA 15.616) and the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund. Reimbursement covers eligible O&M expenses up to $5,000 per marina per season, minus pumpout revenue collected.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant up to $5,000 per marina per boating season for eligible operations and maintenance expenses of pumpout stations. Eligible expenses include: $100 for usage log tracking; $3.75 per pumpout (up to $2,000) for paid staff conducting pumpouts; $25/hour up to $625 (25 hours) for paid staff repairs/maintenance; licensed plumber/electrician fees; replacement parts/equipment from factory-authorized dealers; sewage hauler payments; and winterization costs. Reimbursement equals eligible O&M expenses minus pumpout revenue. The 2026 boating season runs April 15 – November 15, 2026, with reimbursement submissions accepted November 15, 2026 – January 15, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to April 15, 2026 (applications must be approved prior to marina participation)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas with existing sewage pumpout stations seeking reimbursement funding for operations and maintenance costs during the boating season.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operations and maintenance of existing boat sewage pumpout stations, including usage log tracking, paid staff conducting pumpouts, staff repairs and maintenance, licensed plumber/electrician fees, replacement parts and equipment from factory-authorized dealers, sewage hauler payments, and winterization.

Contact pumpouts.dnr@maryland.gov or 410-260-8772 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resiliency Through Restoration Initiative – Grants Gateway Outcome 3
structured_extraction.program_description: The Resiliency Through Restoration Initiative provides financial and technical assistance to local governments and non-profit organizations for living shorelines and other nature-based restoration projects that protect communities from erosion, flooding, and storm and climate change impacts. The program funds design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of nature-based living shoreline restoration or stormwater projects that address flooding and/or erosion. Eligible project types include living shorelines, tidal marsh restoration, dune restoration, rain gardens, bioswales, beneficial use of dredged material, and other nature-based practices that provide community and ecosystem benefits. Projects must provide community-wide coastal protection benefits to community infrastructure or assets on public, private, or community property, be nature-based, and consider climate change data and address future conditions. Both public and private lands are eligible, but projects on private lands must demonstrate a community-wide benefit and require a landowner agreement. Community public property is prioritized; funding on private residential properties can be difficult to obtain. Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded, and permitting fees are not eligible costs. For the CY2026/FY2027 cycle, construction projects are not eligible due to funding limitations, and funding is available July 1, 2026 – October 1, 2026 depending on fund source and approvals. Design and permit projects typically cost between $30,000 and $100,000. Up to 1:1 matching funds are encouraged but not required. Funding comes from a combination of State of Maryland funds and a federal NOAA Maryland Coastal Zone Management Award from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial and technical assistance for the design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of nature-based living shoreline restoration or stormwater projects that address flooding and/or erosion. Design and permit projects typically cost between $30,000 and $100,000. For the CY2026/FY2027 cycle, construction is not eligible due to funding limitations; funding is available July 1, 2026 – October 1, 2026 depending on fund source and approvals. Up to 1:1 matching funds are encouraged but not required. Permitting fees are not eligible costs. Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded. Community public property is prioritized; funding on private residential properties can be difficult to obtain. Specific funding amounts and availability for each phase are described in the current Grants Gateway solicitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations seeking to implement living shorelines or other nature-based shoreline restoration or stormwater projects that provide community-wide coastal protection benefits to community infrastructure or assets on public, private, or community property, reducing flood risk and erosion in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of nature-based living shoreline restoration or stormwater projects that address flooding and/or erosion. Eligible project types include shoreline restoration, beneficial use of dredged material, tidal marsh restoration, dune restoration, rain gardens, bioswales, and other green stormwater and nature-based practices. Projects must benefit a community and address climate change impacts. Permit fees are not eligible. Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded. Construction is not eligible for the current CY2026/FY2027 cycle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects can be located throughout Maryland (statewide). Both public and private lands are eligible, but projects on private lands must demonstrate a community-wide benefit. Community public property is prioritized.

Templates for several attachments are available on the Grants Gateway site. Applications for CY2026/FY2027 are for design and permitting proposals only. See the most recent Grants Gateway solicitation for current funding availability and application details for each phase.

structured_extraction.program_description: Roots for Resilience is an initiative designed to help Maryland's lower Eastern Shore adapt to climate change by enhancing nature's ability to store carbon and buffer climate impacts. The initiative funds tree planting, coastal habitat restoration, living shorelines, and community engagement to strengthen natural defenses and reduce carbon emissions. Activities include wetland restoration, tidal reconnection, urban forestry expansion, improved forestry management, and outreach to private landowners and communities. The program unites existing relationships and initiatives on the Lower Shore to build a healthier, more resilient landscape. Funding is provided in part by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The initiative funds wetland restoration activities, living shorelines, enhanced forestry management, afforestation projects, coastal resilience management plans, and community outreach. An open Request for Proposals (RFP) is available for Living Shoreline projects in Dorchester, Somerset, and Wicomico counties. Enhanced Forestry Management and Afforestation projects are available in Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Coastal Resilience Management Plans cover Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. A new RFP was opened in January 2026 for additional Roots for Resilience projects. Specific grant amounts are not stated. Funding is provided in part by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners, nonprofits, local governments, organizations, and communities on Maryland's lower Eastern Shore interested in climate resilience, forest management, wetland restoration, living shoreline projects, tree planting, and coastal habitat restoration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting, wetland and tidal marsh restoration, living shoreline implementation, enhanced forestry management, afforestation, coastal resilience planning, coastal habitat restoration, and community outreach and engagement that build climate resilience and reduce carbon emissions on the Lower Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in select counties on Maryland's lower Eastern Shore: Living Shoreline projects in Dorchester, Somerset, and Wicomico; Enhanced Forestry Management and Afforestation in Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester; Coastal Resilience Management Plans in Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester. Additional counties including Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's may also be eligible for certain project types.

An RFP for Living Shoreline Solicitation is available at the linked solicitations page, and a new RFP was opened in January 2026. Contact dnr.rootsresilience@maryland.gov for questions or additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Roots for Resilience Living Shoreline Solicitation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) issues a Request for Proposals (RFP) to fund construction, design/build, and design proposals for living shoreline projects in the Chesapeake Bay portions of Dorchester, Wicomico, and Somerset Counties. The goal is to award large-scale living shoreline restoration projects that collectively protect a total of 400 acres of adjacent high-quality tidal marsh habitat. A total of $17 million in grant funding is available, funded 100% by the EPA Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG), with a minimum project request of $1 million (design-only exceptions possible with DNR approval). No match is required. Awards are reimbursed on a monthly invoicing basis and all construction must be completed by July 1, 2029. Additional solicitations may be held in future years depending on funding availability and progress toward marsh protection acreage goals.

Proposals may cover construction, design/build, or design of large-scale projects that collectively protect 400 acres of adjacent high-quality tidal marsh habitat. No match required. Funded 100% by federal EPA Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG). Awards reimbursed on a monthly invoicing basis. All construction must be completed by July 1, 2029.

Projects must protect adjacent high-quality tidal marsh habitat in the Chesapeake Bay portions of Dorchester, Wicomico, and Somerset Counties.
