structured_extraction.program_description: The Rural Legacy Program is a Maryland state program created in 1997 and administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to protect large, contiguous tracts of Maryland's most valuable agricultural, natural, forestry, and cultural resource lands from sprawl development while enhancing natural resources, agricultural, forestry, and environmental protection and supporting a sustainable land base for natural resource-based industries. The program creates public-private partnerships and encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas (RLAs) — delineated areas within a county that include both working farms and ecologically significant landscapes — and competitively apply for funds to protect land, complement existing land conservation efforts, or create new ones. Grants are awarded to local government and nonprofit land trust sponsors (counties, municipalities, land trusts, and conservation organizations) to purchase conservation easements and fee-simple land acquisitions in designated Rural Legacy Areas across Maryland, safeguarding working farms, forests, wetlands, wildlife habitat, historic sites, water quality resources, scenic landscapes, and recreation and tourism resources. A key component of the program is stream buffer protection, with participants required to maintain 100-foot grass and/or forest buffers around streams, as well as impervious surface limits, Forest Stewardship Plans, and Soil and Water Quality Conservation Plans. Funding comes from Maryland Program Open Space dollars and general obligation bonds from the state's capital budget; county governments may also contribute matching funds, and grants may be leveraged with other federal and state land preservation programs such as the U.S. Navy's Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program. Individual landowners within designated RLAs may also receive payment for voluntarily relinquishing development rights through a permanent conservation easement, based on an Easement Valuation System (EVS) formula that awards points for development potential, presence of agriculture and woodland resources, and natural resource protection. Recent offers ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre with cash at settlement. Landowners retain ownership and may continue to farm or otherwise use the land. The program has conserved more than 130,668 acres on over 1,000 easements statewide across 36 designated Rural Legacy Areas, with at least one Rural Legacy Area in every county of the state and total designated acreage across all Rural Legacy Areas exceeding 1.38 million acres. Since 1997, the program has awarded over $479.5 million in grants across 27 application cycles. Note: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025 diverts $25 million per year from Rural Legacy Program funding for FY 2026 through FY 2029, reducing but not eliminating program funding. New area applicants must read the Rural Legacy Program Grants Manual and meet with a program administrator before applying. New areas submit a Full Application; established areas use an Abbreviated Application for grant renewals or boundary changes. The program follows an annual grant cycle with GIS data due January 15, sponsor applications due on the second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m., individual landowner applications due December 1, state agency review in spring (February through April), Rural Legacy Advisory Committee and Board review from April through July, and Board of Public Works approval of grants in August–September.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides two forms of assistance: (1) Annual competitive grants awarded to local government and nonprofit land trust sponsors (counties, municipalities, land trusts, and conservation organizations) to fund the purchase of conservation easements and fee-simple land acquisitions protecting rural and agricultural lands within designated Rural Legacy Areas, as well as planning activities. Funding comes from Maryland Program Open Space dollars and general obligation bonds from the state's capital budget; county governments may also contribute matching funds, and grants may be leveraged with other federal and state programs such as the U.S. Navy's REPI Program. New areas apply with a Full Application; established areas use an Abbreviated Application for grant renewals or boundary changes. Grant amounts are determined through the annual review and approval process involving the Rural Legacy Advisory Committee, Rural Legacy Board, and the Maryland Board of Public Works. The FY 2025 budget appropriation was $15,329,028, with demand exceeding $104 million (approximately 7:1 demand-to-funding ratio). Since 1997, the program has awarded over $479.5 million in grants across 27 application cycles. Note: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025 diverts $25 million per year from Rural Legacy Program funding for FY 2026 through FY 2029, reducing but not eliminating program funding. (2) Direct payment to individual landowners for purchase of development rights (easements) based on an Easement Valuation System (EVS) formula that awards points for development potential, presence of agriculture and woodland resources, and natural resource protection, with a focus on stream buffer areas requiring 100-foot grass and/or forest buffers. Recent offers to landowners ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre with cash at settlement. Landowners retain ownership and may continue to farm or use the land after permanently extinguishing development rights.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15 (GIS data submission); second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m. (sponsor grant applications); December 1 (individual landowner applications); annual application cycle
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies, land trusts, and conservation organizations (sponsors) operating within or seeking to establish approved Rural Legacy Areas in Maryland who seek competitive grant funding to purchase conservation easements and fee-simple acquisitions of farmland, forests, and natural resource lands; as well as individual landowners with large, contiguous tracts of land within designated Rural Legacy Areas who wish to voluntarily relinquish development rights, particularly those with stream buffer areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For sponsors: purchase of conservation easements and fee-simple land acquisitions on privately owned land within approved Rural Legacy Areas to protect farmland, forests, wetlands, wildlife habitat, water quality, historic sites, scenic resources, and recreation and tourism resources from development, as well as planning activities. For landowners: compensates landowners for voluntarily relinquishing development rights on their land through a permanent easement to preserve natural, agricultural, and forestry resources, with an emphasis on stream buffer protection. Conservation efforts must target ecologically valuable properties that impact Chesapeake Bay and local waterway health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland within designated Rural Legacy Areas; there are 36 designated Rural Legacy Areas with at least one in every county of the state, spanning all 24 jurisdictions including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Total designated acreage across all Rural Legacy Areas exceeds 1.38 million acres.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an approved Rural Legacy Area sponsor — a local government (county government), land trust, or conservation organization
Sponsor must identify a Rural Legacy Area within a county that includes working farms and ecologically significant landscapes
Land must be located within a designated Rural Legacy Area
New area applicants must read the Rural Legacy Program Grants Manual and meet with a program administrator before applying
New area applicants must complete a Full Application and follow GIS Submittal Guidelines
Established area sponsors must use the Abbreviated Application form and Property List Form for renewals or boundary changes
GIS data submission is due January 15 each year (if that date falls on a weekend, holiday, or day state offices are closed, the next business day applies)
Sponsor applications are due in the Rural Legacy Office on the second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m.
Individual landowner applications are due December 1 each year
Sponsors must apply annually to the Rural Legacy Board for participation and funding

Applications are reviewed by the Rural Legacy Advisory Committee (eleven volunteers appointed by the Governor), then forwarded to the Rural Legacy Board (comprised of Secretaries of DNR, Agriculture, and Planning), and finally approved by the Maryland Board of Public Works (Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer)
Application must be approved by the Board of Public Works before a Grant Agreement is executed; Grant Agreement is executed between the Rural Legacy Board and the Sponsor
Conservation efforts must target ecologically valuable properties that impact Chesapeake Bay and local waterway health
Projects must complement existing land conservation efforts or develop new ones
Easements or purchases must be from willing landowners
Property must be located within a designated Rural Legacy Area (for individual landowners seeking easement payment)
Rural Legacy Areas must include both working farms and ecologically significant landscapes
Conservation easements must permanently extinguish development rights
Easements must include required stream buffers, impervious surface limits, Forest Stewardship Plans, and Soil and Water Quality Conservation Plans
Participants are required to maintain 100-foot grass and/or forest buffers around streams
Land conservation investments are targeted to the most ecologically valuable properties with direct impact on Chesapeake Bay and local waterway health
Easement monitoring is required at minimum once every 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the Rural Legacy Program Grants Manual (available on the Download page). 2. Meet with the appropriate RLP Program Administrator to discuss the proposal. 3. Submit GIS data by January 15 (or next business day if that date falls on a weekend, holiday, or day state offices are closed). 4. Complete and submit the Full Application (new areas) or Abbreviated Application (established areas), following GIS Submittal Guidelines. Sponsor applications are due in the Rural Legacy Office by the second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m. Individual landowner applications are due December 1. 5. State agencies review sponsor applications February through April. The Rural Legacy Advisory Committee reviews applications and makes recommendations to the Rural Legacy Board, which reviews applications April through July and makes final recommendations to the Governor and Board of Public Works. 6. The Board of Public Works approves grants in August through September; upon approval, receive and execute a Grant Agreement (September through October). 7. Proceed with individual land acquisitions as defined in project agreements. For individual landowners: Contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for information on applying. See the 'How to Apply' and 'Rural Legacy Documents & Forms' pages for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Schoolyard Forests Program helps public schools create outdoor spaces that support student well-being, enrich learning, and strengthen connections to the natural world. It provides campus planning, technical support, hands-on training, educational opportunities, community engagement events, youth career exploration experiences, and microgrants to help schools transform their grounds into healthier, more inviting environments — increasing shade and comfort, integrating nature-based learning, and advancing toward Maryland Green School certification. The program is offered in partnership with the Maryland Association of Environmental & Outdoor Education and aims to increase tree canopy cover, create nature discovery pathways, and support climate resiliency. The program also supports schools working toward Maryland Green School certification. Public schools are prioritized, though privately funded schools may also participate. Program resources are directed first toward public schools and communities with the greatest need.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools may receive campus planning and technical support, hands-on training and assistance for staff, educational and student-centered learning opportunities, community engagement and celebration events, youth career exploration experiences, microgrants, and classroom support materials. Free professional services include teacher workshops, landscape stewardship manuals, specimen tree inventory and mapping, arbor day and earth day activities, forest health assessments, professional development and continuing education, hazard tree evaluation and removal, native tree planting, edible food plots, and summer tree maintenance. Program resources are directed first toward public schools and communities with the greatest need; privately funded schools may participate but receive resources after public schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools of all types and sizes, district-level facility teams, and community partners working directly with school campuses. Priority is given to schools and communities with the greatest need. Privately funded schools may also participate. Students of all backgrounds and educators are also served.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving school outdoor spaces, including tree planting and stewardship, native plantings, campus planning and mapping, outdoor learning integration, heat and comfort improvements, seed collection, environmental literacy projects, and advancing toward Maryland Green School certification. Services also include teacher workshops, landscape stewardship manuals, specimen tree inventory and mapping, arbor day and earth day activities, forest health assessments, professional development and continuing education, hazard tree evaluation and removal, edible food plots, and summer tree maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools throughout Maryland, with priority given to schools and communities with the greatest need.
requirements_list: Open to Maryland public schools of all types and sizes
District-level facility teams and community partners working directly with school campuses are also eligible
Private schools may participate but receive resources after public schools
Priority given to schools and communities with the greatest need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An online application is available on the program page. A formal application process is also being developed and will be linked from the program page once available. Schools may also contact the program administrator directly to discuss interest and initial questions. Eligibility for free services is determined through direct outreach and engagement with the program team.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers free 'do-it-yourself' hunts for stocked pheasants on public lands across Maryland. Eligible hunters enter a lottery to participate in hunts on designated Wildlife Management Areas (WMAs) and state forests. Selected participants receive a permit letter and map showing the specific release and hunting area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free access to stocked pheasant hunts on public lands. Selected participants receive a permit letter and map showing hunt area. Friends, family, or mentors may accompany the selected participant, but only the lottery winner may carry and use a firearm. No cost to apply or participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth (junior) hunters, apprentice hunters, first-time full season license buyers, and lapsed hunters who have held a MD hunting license in the past but have not purchased one for any three of the last five years
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participating in stocked pheasant hunts on public lands in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public lands (Wildlife Management Areas and state forests) across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a youth (junior) hunter, apprentice hunter, first-time full season license buyer, or lapsed hunter
Lapsed hunter: held a MD hunting license in the past but not purchased one for any three of the last five years
Must have an MD Outdoors account to apply
Must possess required hunting license to participate
Can only apply for one day (not both hunt days)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in to your MD Outdoors account and enter the lottery (free to create account, free to apply). Select first, second, and third choice for hunt area and one preferred day. Applications accepted July 1 – October 3, 2025. Winners selected at random and listed on the webpage by October 24, 2025; winners receive email by October 31, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Sunfish and Students is an aquatic resources education program run by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers raise hatchery-bred Bluegill Sunfish in classroom aquariums from October through May, conduct related lessons, and then release the fish at approved sites. DNR provides aquarium starter and replacement kits (approx. $300 value per set), hatchery-raised fish and fish food, a teacher's manual, data sheets, and lesson plans at no cost. Equipment is loaned for the school year and must be returned if the participant is not continuing. Participants also receive reimbursement for fish release trip costs (50% of bus costs up to 3 buses, 100% of substitute teacher costs up to 3 substitutes). The program is supported by a Federal grant; budget fluctuates annually and space is limited on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR provides free aquarium starter and replacement kits (approx. $300 value per set), hatchery-raised Bluegill Sunfish, fish food, a teacher's manual, data sheets, and lesson plans at no cost. Equipment is loaned for the school year and must be returned if the participant is not continuing. Participants also receive reimbursement for fish release trip costs: 50% of total bus costs (maximum 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (maximum 3 substitutes). Reimbursement packages must be submitted by June 30th. Program is supported by a Federal grant; budget fluctuates annually and space is limited on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, non-formal educators, environmental education centers, and nature centers in Maryland; program is available to a limited number of schools per year
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquarium supplies and equipment (loaned), live fish and fish food, educational materials, and reimbursement for bus and substitute teacher costs associated with fish release field trips
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland

Must register annually by May 15th (both new and returning participants); registration opens January 1st
New participants must attend the Teacher Training Workshop; returning participants must attend every 3 years
The September 12, 2026 training workshop is mandatory for all participants
Fish must be picked up on one of the two designated pick-up days in October (or an approved alternate)
Must raise fish and conduct lessons October through May
Fish must be released at an approved site no later than June 30th

Inventory aquarium materials upon receipt and report missing or broken items immediately
Return all equipment if not continuing the program the following school year
Submit required demographic Google Form — mandatory for eligibility in following year

Water must be dechlorinated before use
Daily, weekly, and monthly aquarium maintenance schedule required; bluegills measured biweekly

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online using the Google registration form starting January 1st (deadline May 15th). New participants must attend the mandatory Teacher Training Workshop (September 12, 2026 for the 2026-2027 school year); returning participants must attend every 3 years. Pick up fish and aquarium supplies in October at one of the designated locations. Raise fish and conduct lessons from October through May. Release fish at an approved site by June 30th. Submit reimbursement package (with itemized expenses and receipts) by June 30th and complete the online ARE reporting form by July 31st. To request DNR staff assistance for the release event, provide at least 2 weeks advance notice; complex event planning assistance should be requested over the winter. Confirm event logistics including participant counts, location, parking, restrooms, water access, and any user agreements or fees in advance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers free fishing gear for loan at various locations throughout the state, including state parks, public libraries, and nature centers. The program helps new anglers and their families build confidence and skills while enjoying Maryland's outdoors. Individuals, families, and groups can borrow a rod and reel setup at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of fishing gear (spincast rod and reel with bobber, split shot sinker, swivel, and hook) at participating sites. Individual loans are available at libraries and some parks; group programs are available at select state parks by reservation. Some sites allow multi-day loans and off-site use; others are on-site only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, families, and groups who want to try recreational fishing, especially new anglers and children. Kids under 16 do not need a fishing license to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing fishing equipment for recreational fishing at or near participating loaner sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at participating sites across Maryland, including locations in Anne Arundel, Allegany, Baltimore, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Complete a borrower form before picking up gear
Contact the loaner site directly to confirm availability and policies
Return gear by the agreed return date
Group programs require advance reservations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find a nearby loaner site, complete the online borrower form, visit the site to check out gear, go fishing, and return the equipment on the agreed date. Call ahead to confirm availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Trout in the Classroom is an aquatic resources education program for classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers serving grades 3–12. Participating schools raise rainbow trout from eggs to fingerlings in classroom aquariums, conduct science lessons tied to state and national standards, and then release the fish at an approved site. Maryland DNR provides financial aid for equipment (starter kits and chillers for new schools, replacement kits for returning schools), hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs, fish food, lesson plans, and reimbursement for fish release field trip costs. The program is managed in Maryland by Trout Unlimited's Mid-Atlantic chapter in partnership with DNR.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR provides financial aid to participating schools as the budget allows: one starter kit (approximately $700, not including a chiller) and one chiller per new school; one replacement kit (approximately $220) for returning schools. DNR also provides hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs and fish food, plus reimbursement for fish release trips — 50% of total bus costs (maximum 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (maximum 3 substitutes). Teacher training workshops are hosted in the fall by Trout Unlimited volunteer coordinators with DNR participation (first-year teachers must attend a one-day session on October 24, 2026). Schools/centers not pre-cycling their tank by November 12, 2026 will be dropped from the program. Reimbursement packages are due June 30th and reporting forms are due July 31st.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens January 1st; deadline March 15th. Invoice packages due June 30th. Reporting form due July 31st.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers serving grades 3–12 in Maryland and Washington D.C.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Starter kits and chillers for new schools, replacement kits for returning schools, hatchery-raised trout eggs and fish food, reimbursement for bus and substitute costs for fish release field trips.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools and education centers throughout Maryland and Washington D.C. (statewide). Fish must be released at a DNR-approved stream, river, or pond.

Program is designed for grades 3–12
Both new and returning participants must register every year beginning January 1st
Must submit a signed Memorandum of Intent (MOI) with registration

Must release fish at an approved release site

Schools/centers not pre-cycling their tank by November 12, 2026 will be dropped from the TIC program

School principal certification and signature required on reimbursement invoice

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register using the online registration form starting January 1st (deadline March 15th). 2. Submit a signed Memorandum of Intent (MOI) with the registration. 3. Attend teacher training workshop in the fall hosted by Trout Unlimited (first-year teachers must attend the October 24, 2026 session). 4. Pre-cycle tank by November 12, 2026 or risk being dropped from the program. 5. Receive fish eggs in early December from the Albert Powell Fish Hatchery. 6. Raise fish and conduct lessons October–May. 7. Release fish at an approved DNR site in April/May. 8. Submit reimbursement package (invoice, proof of purchase, and W-9) by June 30th. 9. Complete the online reporting form by July 31st.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides money to marinas and local governments. They can use the funds to build temporary boat slips for recreational boats that are longer than 26 feet.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas and local or state government bodies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the construction of boat slips for temporary use by recreational boats over 26 feet long.
requirements_list: Projects must be for recreational vessels over 26 feet in length.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Universal Disability Pass (UDP) is a free, lifetime, non-renewable pass issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) for individuals with qualifying disabilities, as defined under §504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. It provides free entrance for the pass holder and one companion to day-use facilities at Maryland State Parks, Forests, and Wildlife Management Areas where entrance fees apply. Eligible applicants include individuals with a qualifying disability documented by a Veterans Affairs disability determination letter, an MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification by a licensed health care professional (physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner). The pass does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping, boat launch, rentals, bus parking, concessions, or other special charges. Additionally, eligible holders with a qualifying mobility impairment and a valid Maryland hunting license may hunt from a vehicle at designated public lands under the ADA/504 program, including State Parks, State Forests, and Wildlife Management Areas. Special vehicle access roads and accessible hunting structures at certain Wildlife Management Areas are available exclusively to UDP holders. A physician must certify the permit application for the hunting-from-vehicle privilege. Non-profit groups serving people with disabilities may also apply via a separate application form. Applications can be submitted to service centers by mail, email, or in-person appointment (service centers are open by appointment only).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free, lifetime, non-renewable pass granting the pass holder and one companion free entrance to day-use facilities at Maryland State Parks, Forests, and Wildlife Management Areas managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources where entrance fees apply. Does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping, boat launch, rentals, bus parking, concessions, or other special charges. Additionally provides a special permit allowing hunters with qualifying mobility impairments and a valid Maryland hunting license to hunt from a vehicle at designated public lands under the ADA/504 program, with access to special vehicle access roads and accessible hunting structures at certain Wildlife Management Areas. A physician must certify the application for the hunting-from-vehicle privilege. A non-profit group application option is also available. Service centers are open by appointment only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such impairment, or who are regarded as having such an impairment, as defined under the ADA and §504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. Eligible documentation includes a Veterans Affairs disability determination letter, an MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification by a licensed health care professional (physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner). Also includes those with qualifying mobility impairments who hold a valid Maryland hunting license and wish to hunt from a vehicle. Non-profit groups serving people with disabilities may also apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free lifetime entrance to DNR-managed public lands (state parks, state forests, wildlife management areas) for the pass holder and one companion. Also permits hunting from a vehicle under the ADA/504 program for eligible holders with a valid Maryland hunting license and qualifying mobility impairment; grants access to designated special vehicle access roads and accessible hunting structures at Wildlife Management Areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at all Maryland State Parks, State Forests, and Wildlife Management Areas managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Applications can be submitted by mail, email, or in-person appointment (by appointment only) at any Maryland DNR Regional Service Center, including locations in Annapolis, Bel Air, Centreville, Frederick, Salisbury, Solomons, and Cumberland. Applications are also available from Wildlife & Heritage Service Offices.
requirements_list: Applicant must have a disability as defined under §504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 or the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such impairment, or being regarded as having such an impairment)
Register and obtain a DNRid number through the MD Outdoors licensing website (mdoutdoors.maryland.gov)
Complete the Application for Universal Disability Pass with name, DNRid#, phone number, signature, and date

Licensed health care provider certification must indicate whether the condition is permanent or temporary (if temporary, specify anticipated duration) and must include the provider's medical license number and expiration date
Submit the completed application in person, by mail, or by email at any Maryland DNR Regional Service Center location (open by appointment only)
Must present identification when using the pass
Pass is non-transferable
Pass does not cover automated gate systems, camping, boat launches, rentals, bus parking, concessions, or other special charges

For non-profit group applications: evidence of current non-profit status required; certified disability documentation from licensed health care provider (including medical license number and expiration date) required
For vehicle hunting: must possess a valid Maryland hunting license and have a disability that impairs mobility
Physician must certify the permit application for the hunting-from-vehicle privilege
Pass must be in possession while hunting from a vehicle
Vehicle must be at a complete stop with motor off while shooting, aiming, or firing
All weapons must be unloaded while the vehicle is in motion
Cannot shoot or have a loaded weapon while on a public roadway or shoulder

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register at mdoutdoors.maryland.gov to obtain a DNRid number. 2) Obtain the application form online (individual application: http://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Documents/UDisabilityPass.pdf; non-profit group application: http://dnr.maryland.gov/Documents/UDP-NonProfit-Application.pdf) or from any Maryland DNR Regional Service Center or Wildlife & Heritage Service Office. 3) Complete the Application for Universal Disability Pass and attach one of three supporting disability verification documents: VA disability determination letter, MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification from a licensed health care provider (physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner) including the provider's medical license number and expiration date, and indicating whether the condition is permanent or temporary. For the hunting-from-vehicle privilege, a physician must certify the application before submission. Non-profit group applicants must also provide evidence of current non-profit status and certification of clients' disabilities from a licensed health care provider. 4) Submit the completed application and supporting documentation to any Maryland DNR Regional Service Center location by mail, email, or in-person appointment (service centers are open by appointment only; all offices reachable at 866-344-8889).

structured_extraction.program_name: Vessel Excise Tax Exemption for Active Duty Military
structured_extraction.program_description: Active duty armed services members stationed in Maryland are exempt from the 5% vessel excise tax for one year on vessels currently registered elsewhere and brought into Maryland due to a duty transfer. New vessel purchases are not exempt under this exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Active duty armed services members serving in Maryland are exempt from the 5% vessel excise tax for one year. The exemption applies only to vessels already registered elsewhere that are brought into Maryland because of a duty transfer. New vessel purchases are not exempt.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the 5% vessel excise tax for one year on qualifying vessels.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Active duty military members serving in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an active duty armed services member serving in Maryland
Vessel must currently be registered elsewhere
Vessel must be brought to Maryland due to a duty transfer
New vessel purchases are not exempt
Exemption is valid for one year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for details on boat registration and how to apply for the vessel excise tax exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Veterans Conservation Corps (VCC) is a full-time, paid, year-round program operated by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that places U.S. military veterans in conservation service roles at Maryland State Parks. Members work on trail building and maintenance, habitat restoration, facilities improvement, environmental education, and other large-scale conservation projects. The program provides veterans with professional development, certifications, and hands-on work experience to help them pursue careers in natural resource management, conservation, and park operations. Positions are based primarily at Merkle Natural Resources Management Area in Prince George's County and operate within the Southern Maryland Regional Complex, including Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapel Point State Park, Chapman State Park, Hallowing Point Waterfront Recreation Area, Rosaryville State Park, and Smallwood State Park.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time paid positions with competitive wages, health insurance (through the Student Conservation Association), professional training and certifications (including Emergency Medical Responder, Wildland Fire Fighter, Chainsaw Use and Care, trail construction, and more), a $200 boot reimbursement, uniforms, and personal protective equipment. Positions are one year in length with the possibility of contract renewal.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ranger Sara Marcinak, Director of Conservation Corps
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. military veterans interested in conservation, natural resource management, park operations, and outdoor recreation careers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages, health insurance, training, certifications, uniforms, personal protective equipment, and networking and career development opportunities for veterans serving in conservation roles at Maryland State Parks, including trail maintenance, habitat restoration, environmental education, park operations, and large-scale conservation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is based at Merkle Natural Resources Management Area in Prince George's County (Upper Marlboro) and operates within the Southern Maryland Regional Complex, including Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapel Point State Park, Chapman State Park, Hallowing Point Waterfront Recreation Area, Rosaryville State Park, and Smallwood State Park.
requirements_list: Prior service in the U.S. Armed Forces
Education or experience in park operations, recreation, education, business, administration, forestry, social sciences, or a natural resources related field preferred
Ability to lift up to 50 lbs repeatedly and use hand tools including heavy tools such as pulaskis, sledge hammers, and chainsaws
Ability to travel to and from park locations and various work sites
Commit to a one-year service term with possible renewal
Ability to attend mandatory overnight trainings and projects for up to one week at a time
Availability to work certain weekends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Director of Conservation Corps, Ranger Sara Marcinak, at sara.marcinak@maryland.gov or 443-370-8246 for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Whole Watershed Program (WWP) is a five-year pilot program established by Maryland's Whole Watershed Act (SB 969/HB 1165) in April 2024. It provides collaborative, science-based grants and technical support to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. The program selects up to five watersheds every five years via a Request for Proposals (RFP) and funds project sponsors to implement a diverse mix of environmental actions including pollution reduction, habitat creation, aquatic resource improvements, equitable public access, carbon sequestration, public health enhancements, and community outreach. A State Management Team (SMT) comprised of multiple Maryland agencies (DNR, MDE, MDA) oversees the program, selects watersheds, awards implementation grants and operations grants, coordinates permitting, and funds watershed monitoring. The Whole Watershed Fund covers up to 50% of project implementation costs, with project sponsors required to provide a 50% match from outside sources. Five watersheds were selected in March 2025 for the first five-year pilot period (FY 2026–2030): Antietam Creek, Baltimore Harbor, Upper Choptank River, Newport Bay, and Severn River. Total FY26 investment is approximately $22.25 million ($11.25 million state funds plus $11 million leveraged funds). The program and its enabling subtitle terminate on June 30, 2029 per the sunset clause in the legislation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards Implementation Grants covering up to 50% of project implementation costs (with the project sponsor required to provide 50% matching funds from non-Whole Watershed Fund sources). For FY 2026, up to $2 million per watershed was available for implementation and operations grants (including $20,000 for operational expenses), plus $250,000 per watershed for water quality monitoring grants ($1.25 million total). Total FY26 investment is approximately $22.25 million ($11,248,876 state funds + $11,007,788 leveraged = $22,256,644 total). Additional agricultural project support is provided through the Maryland Agricultural Cost Share Program (MACS) and Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). The State Management Team also provides coordinated state permitting support and technical assistance. Funds are distributed to a single Project Sponsor per watershed on a quarterly reimbursement basis; pay-for-performance contract and upfront lump sum options are also available depending on fund source. The Project Sponsor may sub-award funds to partner entities. In each fiscal year from 2026 through 2030, up to $100,000 from the Fund shall be used to fund operations grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Original RFP due December 3, 2024 (11:59 pm); next RFP to be released on or before October 1, 2029
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sarah Lane (Chair, State Management Team); Shelly Baird (Whole Watershed Coordinator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal, county, and regional agencies; nonprofit organizations; faith-based groups; homeowners associations; land trusts; conservation districts; and soil and water conservation districts seeking to lead watershed restoration projects in Maryland. A single project sponsor must be identified to administer each project, but sponsors can form partnerships and sub-award funds to other entities. Priority given to projects engaging overburdened, underserved, and BIPOC communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project implementation costs for watershed restoration and conservation actions including pollution reduction best management practices (BMPs), habitat creation, stream and wetland restoration, stormwater management, riparian buffers, living shorelines, agricultural conservation practices, green infrastructure, flood risk reduction, recreational access improvements, community outreach, and watershed monitoring. The Whole Watershed Fund covers up to 50% of implementation costs; the remaining 50% must come from outside sources not associated with the six Whole Watershed Fund programs. Administrative/operational costs up to $20,000 per watershed per year are also covered. Non-point source pollution control projects and best management practices on farms to prevent soil erosion, manage nutrients, and safeguard water quality are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located within a Maryland 8-digit watershed. Five watersheds were selected in March 2025 for the first five-year pilot period (FY 2026–2030): Antietam Creek (Washington County), Baltimore Harbor (Baltimore City), Upper Choptank River, Newport Bay, and Severn River. Selected watersheds must meet required designations including one urban, one suburban, two agricultural, one adjoining another state, and two with overburdened or underserved communities. The program and its enabling subtitle terminate on June 30, 2029. The next RFP for new watershed selections will be issued on or before October 1, 2029.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a municipal, county, or regional agency; nonprofit organization; faith-based group; homeowners association; or soil/water conservation district
A single project sponsor must be identified to administer the project and be accountable for funds
Project must be located within a Maryland 8-digit watershed
Project must be endorsed by each county and municipal corporation in which the project will occur
Project sponsor must provide 50% matching funds (1:1 cash match) from sources not associated with the six Whole Watershed Fund programs
Matching funds must be spent after July 1, 2025; only new implementation projects beginning after July 1, 2025 are eligible as match
Project sponsor must hold at least 4 community meetings per year that include local government representation
Project sponsor must provide opportunity for public comment on preliminary designs of major or large-scale actions
Watersheds must meet required designations: one urban, one suburban, two agricultural, one with an adjoining state, and two with opportunities to engage overburdened or underserved communities

Projects evaluated on water quality improvement, habitat restoration, cost-effectiveness, local land use support, environmental justice opportunities, innovation, and multiple co-benefits including wildlife habitat, carbon sequestration, climate resilience, employment, public health, and recreational access
Watershed must demonstrate potential for water quality improvement, habitat creation, environmental justice, and climate resiliency
Best management practices must deliver at least 5 of 7 prioritized benefits
Letters of support from partners, local government(s), and affected landowners required
Community engagement plan required
Monitoring plan required
Environmental justice/DEIJ focus required
Program and enabling subtitle terminate June 30, 2029 per sunset clause in legislation (Section 2 of Ch. 559, 2024 Laws of Maryland)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State Management Team issues a Request for Proposals (RFP) on or before October 1 every five years (first RFP issued October 1, 2024; next RFP due on or before October 1, 2029). Eligible organizations submit a proposal through an online application (with an upload feature for additional details and required budget tables per the RFP guidelines) by the stated deadline (December 3, 2024 at 11:59 pm for the first cycle). The SMT evaluates proposals based on watershed selection criteria including water quality benefits, cost-effectiveness, partnerships, environmental justice, and multiple co-benefits. Up to five watersheds are selected on or before March 1 following each RFP cycle (first selection announced March 2025). After selection, the SMT works with the Project Sponsor to develop an Implementation and Financing Plan. Funds are distributed via quarterly reimbursement requests, with pay-for-performance contract and lump sum options also available. The State Management Team reports annually to the General Assembly on or before November 1 each year on the status of each approved project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free, hands-on wildlife education trunks available to Maryland educators for 1-2 week loan periods. Each trunk contains an educator guide with lesson plans and K-12 activities, plus physical materials such as furs, replica skulls, track molds, puppets, books, DVDs, and activity supplies. Trunk themes include White-tailed Deer, Black Bear, Furbearer, Wild Turkey, Growing Up WILD, Project EduBat, and Aquatic Invasive Species. Trunks are loaned at no cost and are available for pickup at nine locations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of wildlife education trunks for 1-2 week periods depending on availability. Educators pick up and drop off trunks at one of nine locations across Maryland. Each trunk includes an educator guide with lesson plans and hands-on materials such as furs, skulls, track molds, puppets, books, and DVDs. An online reservation system is available for some trunks (e.g., deer trunk).
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 educators and students in Maryland, including classroom teachers at all grade levels (K-12). Activities are grade-leveled for K-2, K-3, K-5, 2-3, 3-5, 4-12, 5-8, 7-12, and 9-12 audiences.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on classroom instruction and student learning about Maryland wildlife, including white-tailed deer, black bears, furbearers, wild turkeys, bats, and aquatic invasive species.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to educators throughout Maryland at nine pickup locations statewide. Curriculum content references wildlife found across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be an educator in Maryland
Responsible for picking up and dropping off the trunk at the designated location
Trunks available for 1-2 week loan periods depending on availability
Must reserve in advance by contacting the nearest location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the trunk location nearest you to reserve a trunk. An online reservation system is available for some trunks (e.g., deer trunk) at http://dnr.maryland.gov/wildlife/Pages/Education/education_trunks.aspx. Pick up and return the trunk yourself at that location.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland requires anyone who wants to care for and rehabilitate orphaned, sick, or injured wildlife — with the goal of releasing them back to the wild — to obtain a Wildlife Rehabilitator Permit/License from the Department of Natural Resources. The permit is renewed every two years and specifies the species and number of animals the holder may keep at one time. Applicants must show adequate training in wildlife capture, handling, and care, and must have suitable facilities. New applicants start at the Apprentice level and can progress to Master level. Continuing education credits are required to maintain the permit. There is no fee for the permit application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues a permit/license authorizing the holder to legally possess and rehabilitate wildlife in Maryland. New applicants apply for an Apprentice Wildlife Rehabilitation Permit; those who meet further criteria can progress to the Master level. The permit is renewed on a two-year cycle and requires continuing education credits for renewal. There is no fee for the permit application.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Permits Coordinator, Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals in Maryland who want to provide care and treatment for the rehabilitation and release of orphaned, sick, or injured wildlife.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this program provides a permit/license, not financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions apply.

Suitable facilities (owned or leased) of sufficient size and design to maintain permitted wildlife in captivity
Completed Application for Apprentice Wildlife Rehabilitation Permit (new applicants)
Statement of Veterinary Support (new applicants) — veterinarian signs statement of availability (non-binding)
Apprenticeship Agreement (new applicants)
Sponsorship by a Master Rehabilitator (for apprentice applicants) — master rehabilitator must co-sign
Workers' compensation insurance or self-employment exemption

Veterinarian consultant arrangement

Compliance with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations (including COMAR 08.03.12)
Description of experience/skills handling wild animals
Competencies across categories: raptors, waterfowl, songbirds, mammals, herpetiles

Training in: identification, first aid, disease/parasites, release criteria, facilities, euthanasia/necropsy, species ID, natural history, diet, capture/handling, restraint, bandaging, splinting, hand-feeding, oral dosing, wound management, record keeping, tubing, injections, drug dosage calculations
Knowledge of Wildlife Rehabilitator's Code of Ethics (NWRA/IWRC), state/federal regulations, humane wildlife prevention methods, and public contact protocols
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants must submit the Application for Apprentice Wildlife Rehabilitation Permit, Statement of Veterinary Support, and Apprenticeship Agreement. To progress to the Master level, applicants must also submit an Availability Questionnaire and Sponsor's Checklist. Applications can be submitted by email or mail to the Permits Coordinator, Wildlife and Heritage Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis, MD 21401. There is no application fee. The program operates on a rolling basis with no fixed application cycle. Office visits require a confirmed appointment; walk-in customers are not accepted. Contact wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or call 410-260-8540 to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Wounded Warrior and Veteran Outreach Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Department of Natural Resources offers recreational opportunities for wounded warriors, veterans, and their families across Maryland's 72 State Parks. Activities include hiking, biking, boating, fishing, swimming, horseback riding, team-building ropes courses, hunting, and camping. The program also provides opportunities to work, learn, and volunteer in Maryland's natural habitats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides recreational, volunteer, and employment opportunities for wounded warriors, veterans, and their families at Maryland State Parks. Activities are designed to support mental and physical well-being.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wounded warriors, veterans, and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation, volunteering, work, and learning opportunities in Maryland State Parks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Maryland State Parks statewide, from Western Maryland to the Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Wounded Warrior and Veteran Outreach Program website at the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Purchases permanent conservation easements from willing landowners in designated Rural Legacy Areas around select Washington County towns and rural villages to protect natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural resources from sprawl development. Easement restrictions are permanent (in perpetuity).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) / Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning

Properties are ranked based on size, development rights, proximity to other easements, agricultural, historic, and environmental characteristics. Applications are accepted prior to February 1st of each cycle year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of permanent conservation easements to protect rural landscapes from sprawl development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Rural Legacy Areas in Washington County, MD, surrounding the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, Boonsboro and Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville, and Gapland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a designated Rural Legacy Area
Application must be submitted prior to February 1st of each cycle year
Properties ranked on size, development rights, proximity to other easements, agricultural, historic, and environmental characteristics

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Conservation and Management Program (FCMP) – Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Conservation and Management Program (FCMP) gives private landowners a financial incentive to conserve and responsibly manage their forestland. By enrolling in a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, landowners receive a reduced and stabilized property tax assessment — generally at the agricultural rate — frozen for the life of the agreement (minimum 15 years). A professional forester prepares a forest management plan for the landowner at no cost, and the landowner must follow that plan throughout the agreement term. The program recognizes that private forests provide broad public benefits — including water quality protection, wildlife habitat, carbon storage, air quality improvement, and support for rural economies — and creates a partnership between landowners and the State to sustain those benefits long-term. Open land recently planted with tree seedlings can be included after one completed growing season. If the agreement is broken, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the start of the agreement. Non-forest areas such as house sites, crop land, and other non-forest open spaces are not eligible. The program also works to minimize the loss of Maryland's forest resources during land development by making identification and protection of forests and other sensitive areas part of the site planning process.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A professional forester prepares a forest management plan for the landowner at no cost. Enrolled forestland receives a reduced property tax assessment — generally at the agricultural rate — which is frozen for the entire term of the Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA), with a minimum term of 15 years. Open land recently planted with tree seedlings can be included after one completed growing season. The agreement is recorded in county land records. If the agreement is broken, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the start of the agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners who are Maryland residents with five or more contiguous acres of forestland who want to conserve their forest, reduce their property tax burden, and manage their land under a DNR-approved forest management plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management planning (free forest management plan prepared by a professional forester) and property tax relief (reduced, stabilized property tax assessment) for maintaining forested land under a legally binding agreement for a minimum of 15 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to any eligible landowner with five or more contiguous acres of forestland. Applications are processed through local Maryland Forest Service offices.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must own five or more contiguous acres of forestland
Eligible land includes forested tracts, newly reforested land (after one completed growing season), and Christmas tree plantations harvested at maturity
Non-forest areas such as house sites, crop fields, and other non-forest open spaces are not eligible
Must enter into a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) recorded in county land records
Must have a forest management plan prepared specifically for the property
Must agree to manage land according to a DNR-approved management plan
Minimum agreement term is 15 years
Must follow the forest management plan throughout the agreement term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office to determine eligibility and begin enrollment. Forestry staff will answer questions, explain program requirements, prepare or review a forest management plan, and guide landowners through the agreement process. The agreement is recorded in county land records. You may also apply through the Maryland Forest Service's Forest Conservation and Management Program page at dnr.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Forest Service administers the Roadside Tree Program, a regulatory system that protects trees growing within public road rights-of-way. Anyone who wants to plant, prune, or remove trees in a public road right-of-way must first obtain a Roadside Tree Permit. Two permit types are available: Project Permits for individual tree work and Blanket Permits for entities with routine or recurring maintenance needs across multiple sites. Permits are valid for one year from issuance. The program also authorizes individuals to become Roadside Tree Experts by passing the Roadside Tree Care Expert (RSTCE) Examination (140 questions, 70% passing threshold), submitting a signed Roadside Tree Expert Agreement, and optionally completing a training course. Roadside Tree Experts are qualified to apply for and oversee permitted tree care along public roads. The Forest Service conducts one preparatory course for examinees in each region each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues Roadside Tree Permits authorizing tree planting, pruning, removal, clearance from utilities, root protection, pesticide use, and other tree care activities within public road rights-of-way. Two permit types are available: Project Permits for individual tree work and Blanket Permits for entities with routine or recurring maintenance needs across multiple sites. Permits are valid for one year; a new application and inspection are required if work is not completed within that period. A $25.00 fee is required for non-public-agency applicants. The program also authorizes individuals to become Roadside Tree Experts by passing the RSTCE Examination (140 questions, 70% passing threshold) and submitting a signed Roadside Tree Expert Agreement. The Forest Service conducts one preparatory course per region per year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, municipalities, utilities, and contractors who need to perform tree work (planting, pruning, or removal) in a public road right-of-way in Maryland; also individuals and public agency employees seeking authorization as Roadside Tree Experts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining authorization to plant, prune, or remove roadside trees within public road rights-of-way; becoming authorized as a Roadside Tree Expert. Blanket Permits cover ongoing maintenance across multiple sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Montgomery County residents must contact the Montgomery County Permits Office at (240) 777-6335 for the county's own roadside tree permit instead.
requirements_list: Any individual, business, municipality, or utility must obtain a Roadside Tree Permit before performing tree work in a public road right-of-way.

Project Permit applications must include: precise tree location, property owner name and address, description of the tree care activity, and a site plan if work is associated with construction or development.
If a tree is on a boundary between two properties, written consent from both property owners is required.
Blanket Permits require applicants to define the geographic scope, type of work, and notification/reporting procedures.
All commercial roadside tree work must be conducted under the direction of a Licensed Tree Expert (LTE).
Applicant must contact the roadway-maintaining agency before work commences.
If work is within 10 feet of overhead utilities, applicant must coordinate with the applicable utility.
If ground disturbance occurs, applicant must contact Miss Utility for underground utility location.
To become a Roadside Tree Expert, applicants must pass the Roadside Tree Care Expert (RSTCE) Examination (140 questions, 70% passing threshold) and submit a signed Roadside Tree Expert Agreement.
Attendance at a MD DNR Forest Service RSTCE preparatory class is referenced as a prerequisite or preference for the exam.
Permits are valid for one year; a new application and inspection are required if work is not completed within that period.
A copy of the permit must be kept on site during all tree work.
Compliance with Annotated Code of Maryland Natural Resources Article 5-401 et seq. and COMAR 08.07.02 et seq. is required.
A $25.00 fee is required for non-public-agency applicants.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The online application portal is temporarily unavailable. Applicants should complete the paper application form and mail or deliver it with payment to their local DNR Forest Service office. Once received, a Forest Ranger conducts an on-site inspection and may request additional information. If approved, a permit is issued by mail or email. If denied, a written denial notice is sent with reasons and appeal instructions. Appeals must be submitted in writing within 10 working days of denial. To become a Roadside Tree Expert, contact roadsidetrees.DNR@maryland.gov to request the exam or register for the optional training course. The Forest Service conducts one preparatory course per region per year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Greenspace Equity Program, established in 2023, provides competitive grant funding to eligible applicants to preserve, create, and enhance public greenspace in overburdened and underserved communities across Maryland, with the goal of enhancing public health and livability. Funded projects can include land acquisition (fee simple or perpetual conservation easement) and stewardship activities such as developing community gardens, parks, trails, urban farms, community woodlands, and gathering spaces. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) through Program Open Space (POS) Local. Funding is authorized annually through the state share of Program Open Space, subject to annual budget actions. The FY 2025 round distributed $4.3 million. The FY 2027 round has closed; FY 2028 application materials will be posted when available. Funding must be distributed with geographic diversity across the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Land Acquisition and Planning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable competitive grant with no established minimum or maximum award amount (up to 100% of project cost). Grant funds cover land acquisition costs (including appraisals, environmental assessments, surveys, title work), site clearing and development for community greenspace, administrative costs up to 3% of the grant amount, and easement monitoring compliance costs up to 1.5% of the grant amount (placed in a long-term managed investment account). Recipients pay costs upfront and are reimbursed; partial reimbursements and advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis after Maryland Board of Public Works approval. No contingency costs may be included in budget estimates. Maintenance and operating costs are not eligible. Projects must be approved by the Maryland Board of Public Works before funds are encumbered. Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity; developed land must be maintained for public use for at least 15 years after project completion. The FY 2025 round distributed $4.3 million. FY 2028 application materials will be posted when available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 2027 round deadline was January 14, 2026 by 3:00 p.m. (closed); FY 2028 application materials will be posted when available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land trusts, nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), county governments, and municipal governments located in or working in overburdened or underserved communities in Maryland, as well as other eligible applicants seeking to preserve, create, or improve public greenspace in these communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land in fee simple or perpetual conservation easement; site clearing and development for community greenspace (community gardens, parks, trails, urban farms, community woodlands, gathering spaces, green networks); related due diligence expenses (appraisals, environmental assessments, surveys, title work); playground surfacing (with strict environmental/lead/PFAS restrictions); public access improvements; administrative costs (up to 3% of grant); easement monitoring compliance costs (up to 1.5% of grant, placed in a long-term managed investment account). Maintenance and operating costs are not eligible. No contingency costs may be included in budget estimates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects must be located in or adjacent to a census tract designated as an overburdened community or underserved community in Maryland as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool and as defined under Maryland Environment Article §1-701. Overburdened communities are census tracts where three or more environmental health indicators are above the 75th percentile statewide. Underserved communities are census tracts meeting one or more socioeconomic indicators per the U.S. Census Bureau. Funding must be distributed with geographic diversity across the state.

Applicant must be a land trust, nongovernmental organization (NGO), county government, or municipal government located in or working in an overburdened or underserved community where the project will be implemented

NGOs that are not eligible land trusts may not acquire real property with program funds
Land trusts and NGOs must be in good standing

Land acquisition must be supported by two independent appraisals; purchase price funded up to the average of the two appraisals
Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity
Land developed or improved must be maintained for public use for at least 15 years after project completion

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Grant Application and Project Agreement Word document, save to desktop, fill all required fields, and submit with all necessary attachments including a succinct response to each question, a detailed itemized cost estimate, and supporting documentation as listed on the Accompanying Document Checklist (including evidence of community support and collaboration). Applications must be emailed to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov by the stated deadline. The Greenspace Equity Program Administrator prepares and distributes application materials to local governments and interested parties. Grant writing workshops may be conducted to assist applicants. After selection, projects proceed through State Clearinghouse review and Board of Public Works approval before funds are encumbered. Costs are reimbursed after project completion; partial reimbursements are permitted. Application materials for the FY 2028 round will be posted on the program page when available. Contact Stephanie Benavides (stephanie.benavides1@maryland.gov, 443-510-4572) or laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space (POS) Local is a nationally recognized program established in 1969 that provides financial and technical assistance to Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City for planning, acquiring, and developing public recreation land and open space. Administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, the program draws on funds from the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969 and the Land and Water Conservation Fund of the National Park Service to conserve natural resources and provide outdoor recreation opportunities. Funds are allocated annually by formula to the 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City; counties may share allocations with municipal governments. Eligible project types include land acquisition (maintained in perpetuity), land development for public recreation or open space (minimum 20-year lifespan), and completion of the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP). Funded facilities include ballfields, playgrounds, trails, wildlife areas, historic sites, greenways, tennis courts, boating facilities, swimming pools, fishing sites, hunting areas, forests, and golf courses. Development projects require a 10% or 25% local match depending on the county's LPPRP results, while acquisition and planning projects do not require a local match. The program operates on a reimbursable basis; partial reimbursements are permitted and advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Each year, participating local jurisdictions submit an annual program of proposed projects to the Maryland Department of Planning for review and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for approval. Once approved by the Board of Public Works, allocated funds are encumbered. Technical assistance, including grant writing workshops and application review, is also available from Local Grants Administrators. In Allegany County, public comments on proposed funding are accepted and recommendations are submitted to the County Commissioners for review and approval. In Garrett County, the program is administered locally through the Planning & Land Management Division.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Land Acquisition and Planning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable, formula-based grants allocated annually to Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City for acquisition or development of public recreation land and open space. Municipalities may receive allocations through their county. Acquisition and planning projects require no local match. Development projects require a 10% or 25% local match depending on the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP) results. Baltimore County provides 100% funding reimbursement for park acquisition projects (up to average of two appraisals or purchase price, whichever is lower) and 75% reimbursement for park development, enhancement, or rehabilitation project costs. Partial reimbursements are permitted; advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Funds are encumbered upon approval by DNR and the Board of Public Works. Planning grants are limited to $25,000 annually. No specific maximum dollar amount is stated for acquisition or development grants. Technical assistance is also available, including grant writing workshops and guidance from Local Grants Administrators. Reimbursement requests are submitted by email to the Local Grants Administrator for the county, with invoices, canceled checks or proof of payment, cost summary, and final photos.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 1 each year; public comment accepted through October 16 for FY26 funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland — particularly Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City — seeking funding for land acquisition, park development, and open space planning projects. Local government subdivisions within individual counties (e.g., Allegany County) may also participate. Municipal governments may receive allocations through their county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land for public recreation or open space; development of public recreation facilities or open space including ballfields, playgrounds, tennis courts, boating facilities, swimming pools, fishing sites, hunting areas, forests, golf courses, hiking trails, greenways, wildlife areas, and historic sites; recreational facilities on lands owned by third parties (via joint use agreement); completion of the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP); planning grants (up to $25,000 annually); major capital rehabilitation projects; LED lighting retrofits; court renovations; playground replacement; trail construction; shade structures; pedestrian bridge replacement; pathway access/connectivity improvements; park facility development including parking, pavilions, roof replacement, lighting, dugouts, and walking trails; equipment and vehicle replacement; urban forestry and green infrastructure acquisition; pool facility modernization; athletic field and court rehabilitation; park planning and design; ADA compliance improvements; stormwater management; bioretention facilities; boathouse replacement; dog park improvements; boardwalk and pilings repair; land preservation planning; urban forest demonstration projects; flood control and habitat preservation; comfort station/restroom facility construction; basketball court rehabilitation; multi-use playing fields; kayak/canoe launches; exercise amenities; paddleball and racquetball courts; field lighting; fencing; park infrastructure renovation; museum facilities; pool renovation; conservation area development; preliminary site planning; construction and site preparation; equipment for initial facility operation (not maintenance equipment); materials and supplies; informational and interpretive signage/facilities; force account personnel costs; project planning costs (site investigation, feasibility studies, preliminary design, cost estimates); contract costs; direct purchases; force account/in-house labor and equipment usage for parks and playgrounds projects; ADA-compliant overlooks and picnic areas; pavilion construction and trail enhancements; amphitheater sealing; parking kiosks; accessible pathways and wayfinding; outdoor gathering spaces; pickleball courts; park systemic improvements; dredging; engineering/design work; demonstration urban forest projects; stormwater management and flood control land acquisition; habitat preservation and green infrastructure. In Washington County, municipalities including Funkstown, Hagerstown, Williamsport, Boonsboro, Clear Spring, Smithsburg, Hancock, Keedysville, Sharpsburg, and Edgemont may participate. In Carroll County, municipalities including Westminster, New Windsor, Union Bridge, and Taneytown may participate on a rotating basis. In Somerset County, the program is administered locally through the Recreation, Parks & Tourism Division. In Talbot County, projects are submitted to the Talbot County Parks Advisory Board and approved by the Talbot County Council. In Queen Anne's County, the Department of Parks and Recreation submits an annual acquisition and development summary. In Wicomico County, municipalities submit project lists to local recreation councils. In Worcester County, projects are selected by the Recreation & Parks Advisory Committee and approved by County Commissioners.
