structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Local Grants Administrator for your area before submitting. Local grants staff prepare and distribute application materials to local governments and may conduct grant writing workshops. Applicants submit a project application including a detailed cost estimate (using the official Acquisition, Development and Capital Renewal, or Planning Grant Application and Project Agreement forms) to the Maryland Department of Planning for review and to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for approval by July 1 each year. The Local Grants Administrator reviews the application for completeness and consistency with program requirements. The application is then submitted to the State Clearinghouse and other DNR units for review. After reviews are complete, the project is scheduled on the next available Board of Public Works (BPW) agenda. BPW approval is required before funds can be encumbered. The full process typically takes 2–3 months. For acquisition applications, applicants must prepare required attachments including a city/county road map (8.5x11, location marked in red), acquisition line map (parcels outlined in red), local/regional planning agency approval and infrastructure review letter, project photographs, two independent appraisal reports with photographs, copy of deed showing current owner, retention of rights explanation (if applicable), and funding authorization signed by the County Liaison Officer; contact the POS Program Administrator for a site inspection and application review before submitting. For development and capital renewal applications, applicants must prepare attachments including site plan, road map, planning approval, photographs, deed/lease documentation (minimum 20-year remaining term if not fee-simple), reforestation law compliance certification if applicable, and funding authorization; contact the POS Program Administrator for a site inspection and application review. For planning grant applications, complete the Planning Grant Application form with project information, location, description tied to LPPRP objectives, funding details, and applicant/coordinator authorization. For reimbursement, submit the completed reimbursement request form with invoices/requisitions in chronological order, proof of payment (canceled checks or payment evidence), cost summary, for in-house labor: payroll/accounting records with job function, dates, hours, and rates; for equipment: usage logs with dates, hours, and rates from county/town schedules; final photos, and acknowledgment sign documentation by email to the Local Grants Administrator for your county. The Project Coordinator or Fiscal Authority must certify compliance with local/state/federal procurement rules on the Payment Certification. In Allegany County, public comments on proposed Program Open Space funding are accepted via email to Andrew Cowan (publicworks@alleganygov.org), and funding recommendations are submitted to the County Commissioners for review and approval. In Garrett County, contact the Planning & Land Management Division (Siera Wigfield, Senior Planner, 301-334-7477) for local application guidance. In Carroll County, proposed capital project requests are developed annually; projects are evaluated by the Recreation and Parks Advisory Board and approved by the County Commissioners. In Calvert County, projects are submitted directly from the LPPRP, by the Board of County Commissioners, or by municipalities, screened by an in-house Open Space Committee, and presented to the Planning Commission and Board for action. In Kent County, projects are submitted by the Parks & Recreation Advisory Board and approved by the County Commissioners before fiscal budget implementation. In St. Mary's County, projects are reviewed by staff, recommended by the Recreation and Parks Citizen Advisory Board, reviewed by the Planning Commission, and adopted by the County Commissioners. In Talbot County, projects are submitted to the Talbot County Parks Advisory Board for approval before being presented to the Talbot County Council for final approval. In Washington County, municipalities submit projects through the county Division of Public Works; the annual program is reviewed by the Recreation & Parks Board and approved by the Board of County Commissioners before submission to DNR. In Wicomico County, municipalities submit project lists to local recreation councils; the Wicomico County Recreation Commission recommends projects; the County Executive approves; and the program is submitted to the state with budget documentation. In Worcester County, projects are selected by the Recreation & Parks Advisory Committee and approved by County Administration and Commissioners. In Harford County, recreation council presidents review and rank requests each September; projects are developed by the Department of Parks and Recreation and submitted annually. In Caroline County, projects must align with the 2022 Caroline County LPPRP and conform to National Playground Safety Standards and ADA requirements. In Queen Anne's County, the Department of Parks and Recreation submits an annual acquisition and development summary reflecting projects seeking POS assistance. In Charles County, projects are prepared and updated annually through a five-year plan process by the Department of Recreation, Parks and Tourism. In Montgomery County, the M-NCPPC and incorporated municipalities including Gaithersburg and Takoma Park submit annual development and acquisition project plans. In Prince George's County, M-NCPPC and municipalities including District Heights, Berwyn Heights, Greenbelt, Laurel, and College Park submit annual program summaries to DNR. In Somerset County, projects are submitted through the Recreation, Parks & Tourism Division. For federally funded (L&WCF) components, the project sponsor submits to the State Liaison Officer, who then submits to the NPS Regional Director for federal review and approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Forest Lands Hunting Tract Lottery
structured_extraction.program_description: Hunt clubs can enter a lottery to obtain a 10-year hunting lease agreement on available Chesapeake Forest Lands tracts. Selected clubs are awarded a lease on one of the non-leased tracts available for Hunt Club leasing. There is no fee to enter the lottery.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 10-year hunting lease agreements on Chesapeake Forest Lands tracts at a per-acre rate (e.g. $14–$16 per acre per year). For example, Tract S13 (Hradowsky Complex, 76 acres) is available at $14.00/acre ($1,064.00 total), and Tract W20 (Dr. Phillips Complex, 79 acres) is available at $16.00/acre ($1,264.00 total). Lessees may also camp on the tract with a permit ($50 for deer season, $25 for turkey season). There is no fee to enter the lottery.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunt clubs (minimum two members licensed to hunt in Maryland, with a designated club president) interested in obtaining a hunting lease on Chesapeake Forest Lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunting lease on state forest lands providing exclusive hunting rights on the leased tract (fishing and trapping explicitly excluded), with permission to camp on the tract with a permit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available on specific Chesapeake Forest Lands tracts in Somerset and Wicomico counties, Maryland. The Chesapeake Forest Office is located at 6572 Snow Hill Road, Snow Hill, Maryland 21863.
requirements_list: Only hunt club members at least 18 years of age can participate in the lottery
A hunt club must have at least two members licensed to hunt in Maryland
One person must be designated as the club president
Each member may submit one lottery entry; only one submittal per person will be placed in the lottery
Hunt clubs must carry a Commercial General Liability Insurance Policy with $1 million per occurrence and $2 million annual aggregate
Proof of insurance is required upon payment
Hunt clubs are expected to help maintain access roads, gates, and signs on the leased property
Lessee must not interfere with Lessor's (Maryland DNR) land management, silviculture, timber operations, fire prevention, public access, or utilities
Lessee is liable for damage caused by negligence and subject to road damage assessment
Lessee cannot assign or sublet the lease
Lessee cannot record the lease in county land records
Lessee must comply with Maryland Building Performance Standards, ADA, and OSHA
Political contribution disclosure required if cumulative contract value is $100,000 or more
No advertising on premises permitted
No profit or income production from the leased tract permitted
No discrimination in operations permitted
No contingent fee arrangements permitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Lottery Entry Form before the deadline (August 21, 2025 at 11:59 pm). A random automated online drawing is held the following day. Winners are contacted by phone or email within 2 business days. Payment and required paperwork must be submitted by the payment deadline (September 10, 2025 at 4:00 pm).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Park Service Youth Group Pass
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Park Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources) offers a biennial (two-year) pass to non-commercial youth organizations such as scout troops, schools, churches, religious groups, and other affiliated tax-exempt youth organizations. The pass provides free day-use entry into Maryland state parks (excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day) and allows youth groups to reserve and camp in designated youth group camping areas, subject to site availability and a valid reservation. The pass is valid for two years, requires a new application each time (no renewals), is non-transferable, and must be physically received and presented upon arrival. Service charges for special facilities such as shelters, boat concessions, and special events, as well as reservation transaction fees, are not covered by the pass. Applications must be submitted by mail and cannot be processed by phone, email, or fax.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Maryland Park Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free biennial (two-year) pass that entitles qualifying non-commercial youth organizations to free day-use entry into Maryland state parks (excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day) and the ability to reserve and camp in designated youth group camping areas, subject to site availability and a valid reservation. Reservation transaction fees still apply. Service charges for special facilities such as shelters, boat concessions, and special events are not covered. The pass is non-transferable and must be physically received before use and presented upon arrival. Passes are issued in the order applications are received and cannot be expedited.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating Maryland state parks and forests. Designated youth group camping areas are located across the Eastern, Central, Southern, and Western regions of Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Youth Group Pass Application (available at https://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/documents/YGPass.pdf). Mail the completed application along with two supporting documents — (1) proof of current tax-exempt status and (2) documentation confirming your organization is a valid, current youth group — to: Maryland Park Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Avenue, E-3, Annapolis MD 21401, Attention: Youth Group Coordinator. Passes are issued in the order applications are received and the process cannot be expedited; allow sufficient time to apply before your current pass expires. Once issued, make camping reservations by calling 1-888-432-2267, booking online at parkreservations.maryland.gov, or calling the specific state park office directly. For Assateague State Park group camping, send a roster prior to arrival to assateague.statepark@maryland.gov and check in during ranger station office hours.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Resident Curatorship Program allows individuals or non-profit organizations to live in and restore historically significant structures located on Maryland State Park lands and natural resource areas. In exchange for a lifetime residential lease at no rent, curators are responsible for funding and completing the restoration of the historic property, maintaining it in good condition, covering all utilities and taxes, and opening the property to the public 3–5 times per year (or providing equivalent public access such as a blog or virtual tour). Curators typically invest $150,000–$300,000 in restoration over five to seven years, with a minimum of $150,000 in restoration and initial improvements of $200,000–$250,000 depending on the property. All work must comply with the Secretary of Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation. The program has been in operation since 1982 and has nearly 50 curatorships across Maryland, from Western Maryland to Assateague Island. The Department of Natural Resources insures the structure against fire, flood, and similar damage via a self-insurance trust fund, coordinates permitting and review, and provides technical guidance on historic preservation compliance. Non-profit organizations are given preference when their mission aligns with the land unit where the property is located. All improvements become property of the State of Maryland. Curators must also represent the Department of Natural Resources professionally and pass lead paint testing before taking up residence. Selected applicants receive a Right of Entry while the final Curatorship Agreement is drafted and approved by the Board of Public Works.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Maryland Park Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Curators receive a lifetime residential lease on a historic property located on state parkland at no rent (a Curatorship Agreement), with annual rent set at $1.00/year. The state provides the property; curators fund all restoration (typically $150,000–$300,000 over up to seven years, with a minimum of $150,000 and initial improvements of $200,000–$250,000) and ongoing maintenance, utilities, and taxes. No direct financial payment is made to curators — the subsidy is the rent-free use of a historic home on state parkland. The Department of Natural Resources insures the structure against fire, flood, and similar damage via a self-insurance trust fund, coordinates permitting and review, and provides technical guidance on historic preservation compliance. Curators must carry comprehensive personal liability insurance naming the State as co-insured; contractors must carry $1M/$2M CGL insurance. A Right of Entry is granted to selected applicants while the final Curatorship Agreement is drafted and approved by the Board of Public Works. The lease becomes effective only upon execution by both parties and approval by the State of Maryland Board of Public Works. All improvements become property of the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and non-profit organizations committed to historic preservation who wish to live in and restore a historic structure on Maryland State Park land or natural resource area. Non-profits with missions aligned with the Land Unit (State Park, Forest, Wildlife Management Area, etc.) receive preference.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration, ongoing maintenance, and operation of a historic property on State Park land, including improvements compliant with the Secretary of Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation, labor, materials, and sweat equity, as well as modern upgrades (kitchens, bathrooms, HVAC), electrical, plumbing, heating, hazardous material remediation, utilities, taxes, and all associated fees. Tenant must complete all restoration work within seven years of the lease commencement date. Additions and alterations to historic fabric are discouraged. No state funds are provided to curators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland — properties are located within Maryland State Parks and natural resource areas, from Western Maryland to Assateague Island.
requirements_list: Must be committed to historic preservation
Must want to live in a historic house on State natural resource land
Must restore the historic property to good condition meeting current building codes
Must maintain the property and grounds in good condition

Must obtain prior department approval for any material changes to the building or land
All plans and renovations must comply with building, safety, and environmental codes
All plumbing, structural, and electrical work must be performed by a licensed and insured professional (master electricians and plumbers required)

All proposed work must undergo departmental review (approximately 30 days for minor alterations; up to 60 days for environmental review)
Written permission required for any work outside the original proposal

Exterior appearance of the building must remain substantially the same

No hunting, pesticide use, or timber cutting without written approval
No domestic animals or livestock without written permission

Must provide a Schedule of Restoration with task-by-task breakdown, cost estimates, and yearly phases (not to exceed 7 years)

May be required to submit a current credit report

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review program policies and frequently asked questions on the DNR website. Interested parties are encouraged to call the Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources to discuss the proposal process before submitting. When properties become available, submit a cover letter and detailed proposal (electronically or by mail; faxed proposals not accepted) to the Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources, including a restoration and management plan (Schedule of Restoration with task-by-task breakdown, cost estimates, and yearly phases not to exceed 7 years), resume(s), and a Personal Financial Statement. All planned work undergoes an environmental and historic preservation review process coordinated by the Program Manager. Proposals are reviewed and scored by an interagency panel including the area park manager, DNR regional engineer, a Maryland Historical Trust representative, and the Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources (initial review takes approximately three months). After a winning proposal is selected, the process from proposal to final approval by the Maryland Board of Public Works (Governor, State Comptroller, and State Treasurer) takes approximately six months. Successful applicants receive a Right of Entry to the premises while the final Curatorship Agreement is drafted. Contact the Maryland Park Service Resident Curatorship office at curatorships.dnr@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Solar Generation Facilities - Pollinator-Friendly Designation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program for commercial ground-mounted solar facilities in Maryland to receive an official pollinator-friendly designation from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR). Solar developers follow a defined process — including submitting an application, a pollinator habitat management plan, using DNR-approved seed mixes, and passing a site inspection — to earn a two-year certification. The solar facility must be ground-mounted, use photovoltaic cells for electricity generation, and be at least 1 acre in size. The certification is valid for two years and can be renewed every two years by contacting the Power Plant Research Program within 90 days of expiration. No direct financial assistance is provided; the program confers an official designation from DNR recognizing facilities that have established and manage pollinator-friendly habitat.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Power Plant Research Program
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-year pollinator-friendly certification (designation) for qualifying commercial ground-mounted solar facilities that are at least 1 acre in size. The certification is valid for two years and is renewable by contacting PPRP within 90 days of expiration. No direct financial assistance is provided; the program confers an official designation from DNR recognizing facilities that have established and manage pollinator-friendly habitat.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial ground-mounted solar facility developers and operators in Maryland seeking an official pollinator-friendly site designation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a certification/designation program, not a funding program. The designation recognizes solar facilities that have established and manage pollinator-friendly habitat.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for commercial ground-mounted solar facilities that are ground-mounted, use photovoltaic cells for electricity generation, and are at least 1 acre in size.
requirements_list: Submit an application to pprp@maryland.gov including facility name, location, tax map information, acreage, contact information, and a short description of the facility
Indicate whether the facility is proposed or existing
Include a pollinator habitat management plan with the application

Use a seed mix appropriate for the Maryland region as specified by DNR

Submit any additional information requested by the Department within 30 days of the request; failure to do so results in termination of the application
For renewal, contact PPRP within 90 days of the expiration of the two-year certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application (available from PPRP) and pollinator habitat management plan to pprp@maryland.gov. DNR may request additional information; the applicant has 30 days to comply or the application is terminated. Use a DNR-approved seed mix and arrange a site inspection by a DNR-approved inspector. After the inspection, submit the completed Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning and Assessment Scorecard, final habitat plan, and inspector's letter to DNR within 30 days. DNR reviews the materials and issues the certification upon approval. To renew, contact PPRP within 90 days of the certification's expiration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland DNR's Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway (also known as the Grants Gateway) is a single point of entry providing financial and technical assistance for projects that restore local waterways, increase resilience to climate impacts, strengthen local economies, and develop the next generation of environmental stewards. Grants and loans are funded through the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, the Coastal Resiliency Program, the Waterway Improvement Fund, the Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Fund, NOAA, and the EPA Chesapeake Bay Program. The program supports projects achieving at least one of five defined outcomes related to Chesapeake Bay restoration and community resilience, with a focus on Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bay communities statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Watershed & Climate Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants, loans, and technical assistance are available through a single portal. Funding sources include the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, the Coastal Resiliency Program, the Waterway Improvement Fund, the Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Fund, NOAA, and EPA's Chesapeake Bay Program. The Shore Erosion Loan Program offers a sliding-scale administrative fee (10–3%) with 5–20 year terms, limited to living shoreline projects (bulkheads and stone revetments are ineligible). Landowner agreements are structured in two tracks: Form A (in perpetuity) for stream restorations, tidal wetlands, living shorelines, and stream-wetland complexes; Form B (15-year term) for tree plantings, non-tidal wetlands, meadows, and bioretentions. Shoreline Erosion Loan Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Technical assistance and site visits are available during the application period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2028 Request for Solicitation will open in July 2026; FY2027 deadlines have passed (Outcome 5: September 18, 2025; Outcomes 1-4 and Shoreline Loan: December 12, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities and organizations — including nonprofits, government entities, for-profits, individuals, and HOAs/community groups — seeking to restore local waterways, address climate impacts, strengthen local economies, or develop environmental stewards in Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bay communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waterway restoration, shoreline erosion control (living shorelines only for loan track), climate resilience projects, local economic strengthening, environmental stewardship development and education, flood mitigation, stormwater management, coastal hazard adaptation, habitat restoration, carbon sequestration, and watershed implementation planning. Projects with co-benefits including aquatic resource restoration, climate resilience, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, local employment, recreational opportunities, and environmental justice benefits are prioritized.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bay communities. Sea level rise guidance applies to Maryland's coastal zone with reference to seven NOAA tide gauge locations (Annapolis, Baltimore, Cambridge, Ocean City, Solomons Island, Tolchester Beach MD, and Washington DC). Coastal resilience co-benefits are mapped across 16 coastal counties and Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register on the Grants Gateway Portal (https://webportalapp.com/sp/grants_gateway) and submit the online application by the applicable deadline. Outcome 1 and Outcome 3 follow a two-step submission process (Common Application then Site/Task Details); Outcome 2 follows a three-step process (Common Application, Site/Task Details, Budget with template). Technical assistance and site visits are available upon request during the application period. Budget templates and common application questions are available on the program page. Applicants should use the Trust Fund Targeting Map and Co-Benefits section of the Common Application to document project co-benefits and spatial alignment with program priorities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Innovative Technology Fund, administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources' Watershed & Climate Services in partnership with the University of Maryland's Maryland Industrial Partnership Program (MIPS) and Mtech Ventures, provides capital funding to Maryland companies, organizations, and University of Maryland System personnel developing innovative technologies to accelerate Chesapeake Bay restoration. The program funds projects focused on reducing non-point source nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus), sediment, and other pollutants in the Chesapeake Bay, including carbon mitigation, biofuel, and wastewater treatment technologies, as well as green job creation. The program operates two tracks: (1) the Seed Capital track, administered through the Mtech Ventures Chesapeake Bay Seed Capital Program at the University of Maryland, awards between $50,000 and $450,000 to eligible Maryland companies for research, development, and commercialization of Bay restoration technologies; and (2) the Research and Development track, administered through MIPS, provides grants of $30,000 to $100,000 to students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System, as well as other organizations and businesses, to develop innovative environmental technologies. Total program funding is approximately $1 million per year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Watershed & Climate Services / University of Maryland Industrial Partnership (MIPS) / Mtech Ventures

Total program funding is approximately $1 million per year.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The Seed Capital track requires applicants to be Maryland-based companies or organizations. The R&D track requires applicants to be affiliated with the University of Maryland System.

structured_extraction.program_description: Flying WILD is a bird education and conservation program for educators. Participants attend a 3- to 6-hour workshop led by certified trainers, where they try out various Flying WILD activities and receive a free copy of 'Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds' upon completion. Two training partners operate in Maryland: the Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury and Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds. The educator activity guide can also be purchased separately from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies.

Alternatively, the guide can be purchased directly from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educator professional development in bird education and conservation; participation in training workshops on bird-related activities; receiving the Flying WILD activity guide

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the training partner nearest you — Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury or Jen Scully at Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds — to inquire about upcoming training opportunities. Check the Maryland DNR professional development page for scheduled events.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay and Endangered Species Fund Tax Checkoff
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland taxpayers can donate to the Chesapeake Bay and Endangered Species Fund by entering an amount on line 35 of their state income tax Form 502. Donations are split evenly between Bay restoration grants administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust and rare species programs run by the Wildlife and Heritage Service at the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Donations support habitat research, stream cleanups, tree plantings, monitoring, and protection of rare, threatened, and endangered species and plants. Donations are 100% tax deductible the following year.

Donations are 100% tax-deductible the following year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Fishing and Boating Services partners with local community organizations to host youth fishing rodeos across the state. The program introduces children ages 3–15 to fishing in a safe, controlled environment, teaches basic angling skills, and fosters stewardship of natural resources. The department supports sponsoring organizations by providing fish stocking (trout or hybrid sunfish, limited supply), permits, technical advice, event listing on the department's website, and assistance locating commercial fish sources. Community and non-profit organizations can apply for department support to sponsor and run their own rodeo events held between March and November throughout Maryland. Approximately 7,000 children participate annually in up to 70 events statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Fishing and Boating Services

Organizations must submit a Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Application by January 15 each year (applications accepted after September 1 of the prior year) and a post-event report from a prior event to receive a rodeo permit or fish the following year. Additional support may include fishing gear and/or bait, fishing tips and assistance, food, and prizes.

The body of water must be a lake, pond, or stream (not to exceed 10 acres surface area for events held on private property). No county-by-county restrictions apply.

Applications are accepted starting September 1 of the prior year. Requests are prioritized based on information quality and the date received (rolling review). After hosting an event, coordinators must submit a post-event evaluation report within 30 days to remain eligible for a permit and fish allocation the following year. Post-event reports can be submitted by mail, fax (301-791-4672), or via the online form at the DNR website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Cost Share Assistance Programs (EQIP, WIP, CREP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service (MDNR-FS) and the USDA Farm Services Agency (FSA) offer cost share assistance programs to private landowners to help cover the cost of forest improvement practices. Three programs are available: the Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP), the Woodland Incentive Program (WIP), and the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP). Cost share assistance typically reimburses 50% to 75% of the total cost of approved forestry practices. Eligibility depends on property size and fund availability. A forest stewardship management plan is usually required before applying. Funding must be allocated before any work begins. Technical assistance, vendor referrals, and contract crews may also be available through the county forester.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost share assistance reimburses landowners for 50% to 75% of the total cost of recommended forestry improvement practices. Funding must be allocated before any work begins. Three programs are available: EQIP, WIP, and CREP, each targeted at different landowner goals and property objectives. Technical assistance, vendor referrals, and contract crews may also be available through the county forester.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering a portion of the cost of recommended forest improvement and stewardship practices as outlined in a forest stewardship management plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible landowners. Eligibility depends on property size and availability of funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Forest Service offers technical and financial assistance programs to help landowners establish, protect, plan, and manage their forests. Services are organized by region, with specific programs and fees outlined in regional brochures available for each of the four service areas: Central, Eastern, Southern, and Western Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Regional technical and financial assistance programs covering forest establishment, protection, planning, and management. Specific services and any associated fees vary by region and are detailed in regional brochures available as downloadable PDFs. Cost-share programs include the Woodland Incentive Program (WIP, 65% funding), EQIP (variable, up to 90% combined with WIP), and CRP/CREP. Tax incentive programs include the Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA, minimum 5 acres, 15-year minimum term), Woodland Assessment, Maryland Income Tax Modification (3–1,000 acres), and Public Law 96-451 federal reforestation tax credit. Tree seedlings are available through the John S. Ayton State Forest Tree Nursery (four to five million pine, hardwood, and shrub seedlings annually) on a first-come, first-served basis beginning in the fall for spring shipment. Fee schedule (subject to change): Timber Stand Improvement Marking $12/acre; Forestry Services Coordination $4/acre; Planting Site Examinations $40 flat fee (with $10 seedling credit if order placed within 4 months); FCMA inspections $100 per inspection (every 5 years); Woodland Assessment forester letter $50–$100 (every 3 years).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private non-industrial landowners in Maryland seeking assistance with forest establishment, protection, planning, and management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest establishment, protection, planning, and management, including: Forest Stewardship Plan preparation (long-range management recommendations for wildlife, forestry, recreation, soil and water management); reforestation and site preparation; timber stand improvement (marking trees for firewood, pulpwood, seed tree designation, and routine thinnings); tree and shrub planting; planting site examinations and coordination of plantings; forestry equipment rental; wildlife enhancement activities; vegetative buffers along waterways; cover on highly erodible lands; aerial spraying (non-commercial); and tax incentives for qualifying woodland management practices. Note: Fees charged by the Maryland Forest Service for plan development and some technical services may not be cost-sharable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties, organized into four regional service areas: Central (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Harford, Howard, Montgomery), Eastern (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington). Western Region services also available to Delaware citizens for John S. Ayton Nursery seedlings.

Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) requires 5–1,000 acres of private non-industrial forestland

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the relevant regional Forest Service office for your county. Apply through your local Maryland Forest Service office or local NRCS office (for EQIP) or local Farm Services Agency (FSA) office (for CRP/CREP) depending on the program. Tree seedling orders are taken beginning in the fall for seedlings shipped in the spring on a first-come, first-served basis. Regional service brochures outlining available services and associated fees are available as downloadable PDFs on the program page. Central Regional Office: (410) 836-4551; toll-free: 1-877-620-8DNR ext. 8531.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Modification Program for Reforestation & Timber Stand Improvement
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a financial incentive for forest landowners to manage their forest land by allowing them to deduct double the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices from their federal adjusted gross income for Maryland income tax purposes. The deduction is reduced by any cost-share assistance received through other programs. The modification applies to forest management practices installed on 3 to 1,000 acres in any one year. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years and are subject to periodic inspections. If practices are not maintained, the tax savings must be repaid. Christmas tree and ornamental tree operations are not eligible. Eligible costs include direct costs for certified reforestation and timber stand improvement practices such as tools, machinery and depreciation, labor, consultant fees, chemicals (herbicides, insecticides, rodenticides, animal repellents, fertilizer), seed and seedlings. Both initial and supplemental follow-up practice costs are eligible, with supplemental costs counted at a 2× multiplier in the final calculation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible participants may deduct double the cost of qualifying reforestation and timber stand improvement practices — minus any cost-share assistance received through other programs — as a subtraction from federal adjusted gross income on their Maryland state tax return. The modification applies to forest management practices installed on 3 to 1,000 acres of eligible forest land in any one year. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years. Eligible costs include direct costs for certified reforestation and timber stand improvement practices such as tools, machinery and depreciation, labor, consultant fees, chemicals (herbicides, insecticides, rodenticides, animal repellents, fertilizer), seed and seedlings. Both initial and supplemental follow-up practice costs are eligible, with supplemental costs counted at a 2× multiplier in the final calculation. Final Cost = Initial Cost Subject to Modification + (2 × Supplemental Cost Subject to Modification).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest landowners who own or lease between 3 and 1,000 acres of forest land capable of growing more than 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year, available primarily for growing and harvesting trees. Christmas tree and ornamental tree operations are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation and timber stand improvement practices on eligible forest land. Eligible costs include: direct costs for certified reforestation and timber stand improvement practices (both initial and supplemental follow-up practices), tools and machinery (including depreciation), labor, consultant fees, chemicals (herbicides, insecticides, rodenticides, animal repellents, fertilizer), seed and seedlings. Net costs after subtracting any cost-share assistance received are eligible for the tax modification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible forest landowners. Forestland must be located in Maryland and must be capable of growing more than 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year. No county-level or regional restrictions apply. Acreage eligibility: 3 to 1,000 acres.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland DNR forester or Dan Rider at the Maryland DNR Forest Service. Complete DNR Form 393 (DNR-393) and have a Maryland-licensed Registered Professional Forester certify successful implementation and affix their professional seal. Four copies of the form must be produced and distributed to: the taxpayer (for tax return attachment and personal copy), the professional forester, and the Maryland Forest Service Supervisor. Submit one copy of the completed form to the Supervisor, Forest Stewardship, Maryland Forest Service, Tawes State Office Building E-1, Annapolis, MD 21401. Report the subtraction from federal adjusted gross income on the Maryland state tax return. Guidelines and instructions are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) provides financial cost-share assistance to private, non-industrial woodland owners who manage their forest land in Maryland. The program reimburses landowners for up to 65% of eligible practice costs (not to exceed $5,000 per year or $15,000 per 3-year period) after practices are completed and inspected and approved by a local forester. Eligible practices include preparation of forest stewardship plans, reforestation of open land (including abandoned farm fields and cutover woodlands), tree planting, site preparation, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, and planting of seedlings. Landowners must agree to maintain the forestry practice for 15 years. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75–100 landowners for management practices on 1,500–2,000 acres. The program is administered by the Maryland Forest Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources) and is available statewide. Technical assistance is also available through the Maryland DNR and USDA NRCS.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share financial assistance reimbursing up to 65% of eligible practice costs, not to exceed $5,000 per year (or $15,000 per 3-year period). Landowners complete the practices, pay for goods and services, and then receive a reimbursement check after a forester inspects and approves the work. Eligible practices include preparation of forest stewardship plans, reforestation of open land (including abandoned farm fields and cutover woodlands), thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, site preparation, herbicide treatments, and planting of seedlings. Landowners must agree to maintain the forestry practice for 15 years. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75–100 landowners for management practices on 1,500–2,000 acres. Technical assistance is also available through the Maryland DNR and USDA NRCS.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparation of forest stewardship plans, reforestation of open land (abandoned farm fields and cutover woodlands), tree planting, site preparation, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, and planting of seedlings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland on eligible non-industrial private forestland. Program is served through four regional offices (Western, Eastern, Central, Southern Maryland).
