structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible landowners apply through their local Maryland DNR department forester or the Maryland Forest Service using the fillable PDF application form. The Consulting Forester or DNR Forester reviews and signs the application (electronic or physical signature accepted) and submits it to Headquarters via email (woodlandincentiveprogram.dnr@maryland.gov) with the Regional Forester copied. The application is assigned a number, entered into the system, and a confirmation is sent to the submitting forester; a letter with application copy is sent to the landowner. If approved, landowners complete the practices and pay for goods and services. The local forester inspects the practice, and upon approval, the landowner submits payment forms with supporting paperwork (bills, receipts) to receive a reimbursement check for up to 65% of eligible costs, not to exceed $5,000 per year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Golden Age Pass is a lifetime pass for Maryland residents aged 62 and older that provides free day-use entry to all state parks that charge service fees, half-price camping at campsites and mini-cabins (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays), and waived boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks. The pass costs a one-time $10 processing fee and is non-transferable. Per-vehicle free entry applies when the cardholder is present. A supplementary magnetic swipe card is available at no extra charge for parks with automated gate systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources – Maryland Park Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $10 one-time processing fee grants a lifetime pass providing: free day-use entry to all Maryland state parks that charge service fees (per-vehicle fee waived when cardholder is present); half-price camping at campsites and mini-cabins Sunday through Thursday (excluding holidays); and waived boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks. The pass is non-transferable and the passholder must be present during use. A supplementary magnetic swipe card is available at no extra charge for parks with automated gate systems. Available for purchase online at shopdnr.com or in person at designated state parks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 62 or older who wish to access state parks at reduced or no cost.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free day-use entry to state parks, half-price camping at campsites and mini-cabins (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays), and waived boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Valid at Maryland State Parks statewide.
requirements_list: Must be 62 years of age or older
Must provide valid proof of age (U.S. Passport, Birth Certificate, Driver's License, or State-Issued ID)
$10 processing service fee required
Pass is non-transferable; must present original pass at check-in
Passholder must be present at check-in and remain with the camping party for the entire stay when using the camping discount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Purchase the pass online at shopdnr.com or in person at a designated state park (call ahead to confirm availability). Online purchasers must upload a valid age-verification document. If unable to upload, mail a copy of the document along with the purchase confirmation to the Maryland Park Service in Annapolis. The physical pass is mailed within 7–10 days and must be in hand before use. For parks with automated gates, contact the relevant park office after receiving the pass to arrange a supplementary magnetic swipe card.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Shore Erosion Control (SEC) Program provides technical and financial assistance to landowners, communities, local governments, and businesses for completing structural and non-structural shore erosion control projects along the Chesapeake Bay, coastal bays, and their tributaries. The program funds vegetative (living shoreline) and structural erosion control projects to prevent sediment loss, reduce pollution, and protect shorelines. Matching grants are available for private landowners (45/55 match, where the program pays 45%) and public land protection projects (75/25 match, where the program pays 75%). Financial assistance for non-structural projects on private and public lands using State special funds may also be structured as 75% interest-free loans. Property owners typically form a Special Taxing District to access program benefits; future maintenance is the responsibility of the property owner(s). Technical assistance includes site evaluations, problem assessments, and recommended solutions. In St. Mary's County, the program is coordinated through the Department of Public Works, and at least 75% of affected property owners must confirm the petition before the County proceeds to a public hearing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Boating Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 45/55 matching grants for private landowners (property owner pays 55%, program pays 45%) and 75/25 grants for eligible public land protection projects (program pays 75%, public entity pays 25%). Financial assistance for non-structural projects on private and public lands using State special funds may be structured as 75% interest-free loans. Grants and loans fund design and construction of shoreline erosion control projects. Costs may be shared via special benefit assessments levied on participating property owners annually. Technical assistance includes site evaluations, problem assessments, and recommended solutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private property owners, communities, local governments, and businesses experiencing shoreline or streambank erosion problems along the Chesapeake Bay, coastal bays, and their tributaries in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, management, and financing of vegetative (living shoreline) and structural shore erosion control projects, including sand fill placement and marsh grass planting, as well as streambank or shoreline erosion control on public and private lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners abutting a body of water in Maryland, including the Chesapeake and coastal bays and their tributaries. In St. Mary's County, coordinated through the Department of Public Works.
requirements_list: Applicant must own property abutting a body of water in Maryland
Must file an application requesting assistance
Submit a Letter of Interest (petition) and an Exhibit showing the boundary of the proposed Shore Erosion Control District
Exhibit must show a bold boundary around the lots to be included in the proposed District
For non-structural/living shoreline projects, follow DNR Step-by-Step Procedure for Establishment of Non-Structural, Living Shoreline Projects
Structural assistance limited to protection of public lands and facilities (e.g., roadways) and private property (reinstated 2002)
Applicants must be co-owners capable of forming a special taxing district
At least 75% of affected property owners must confirm the petition before the County proceeds to public hearing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The owner of any property abutting a body of water in Maryland may file an application requesting assistance with design, construction, management, and financing of a shoreline or streambank erosion control project. Applicants submit a Letter of Interest (petition) and an Exhibit to establish a Shore Erosion Control Taxing District. DNR conducts a feasibility study. In St. Mary's County, the County confirms the petition with a 75% threshold of participating property owners, followed by a Public Hearing to establish the District. Construction planning, bidding, and construction follow. Annual assessments are levied on participating property owners. Refer to the Procedures for Establishing a Shore Erosion Control Taxing District document. Contact the Department of Public Works or DNR for further steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program established under the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 that provides financial assistance to Maryland to administer and implement its Coastal Zone Management Program. Maryland receives approximately $2.5 million annually from NOAA's Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management (OCRM). Grants are 18 months in duration and subdivided into three sections: Section 306 (program administration and implementation, requires 1:1 non-federal match), Section 306A (land acquisition, low-cost construction such as public access improvements, and habitat restoration projects, requires 1:1 non-federal match), and Section 309 (coastal zone enhancement projects in areas such as wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, and aquaculture — no match required). Each 18-month grant cycle totals $4.5 to $4.7 million including federal funds and non-federal match. Funded projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed under individual contracts typically 12 months in duration.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake & Coastal Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland receives approximately $2.5 million annually from NOAA. Each 18-month grant cycle totals $4.5 to $4.7 million including federal funds and non-federal match. Section 306 and 306A funding must be matched 1:1 by non-federal sources. Section 309 funding does not require a match. Funded projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed under individual contracts typically 12 months in duration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government partners working to administer and implement Maryland's Coastal Zone Management Program, including developing programs, plans, and strategies to address coastal zone management issues, as well as acquisition, construction, and coastal zone enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administration and implementation of Maryland's Coastal Zone Management Program (Section 306); acquisition of land interests, easements, low-cost construction projects such as public access improvements, and habitat restoration (Section 306A); coastal zone enhancement projects addressing wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, and aquaculture (Section 309).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland coastal zone, defined by the state's tidal shoreline and coastal population areas, available statewide.
requirements_list: Section 306 and 306A funding must be matched 1:1 by non-federal fund sources
Section 306A projects require additional documentation approval from NOAA before projects can be approved
Section 309 funding does not require a match

Section 309 projects must address one of nine identified enhancement areas: wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, or aquaculture
Projects are reimbursed after work is completed under individual contracts typically 12 months in duration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Maryland receives funds based on the size of its coastal population and the length of its tidal shoreline. Contact the Chesapeake & Coastal Service at the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for information on funding opportunities and application procedures. Funded projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed under individual contracts.

structured_extraction.program_name: Living Shorelines Program (Maryland Chesapeake and Coastal Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) offers funding and project management assistance to homeowners experiencing shoreline erosion. The program helps with funding, design, and construction of non-structural 'living shorelines,' which use stone structures, sand, and marsh grasses to protect property and restore habitat, as required by the Living Shoreline Protection Act of 2008.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake and Coastal Program
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding, design, and construction assistance for living shoreline projects. Specific funding amounts are not detailed on this page; visit DNR's website for specifics.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners experiencing shoreline erosion on their property in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of non-structural living shoreline projects including stone structures, sand fill, and marsh grass planting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners along tidal shorelines in Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must have shoreline erosion
Property must be along a tidal shoreline
Living Shoreline Protection Act of 2008 encourages living shorelines over hard structures such as bulkheads and revetments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Bhaskar Subramanian, Program Manager for Habitat Restoration and Conservation, via phone at 443-454-1638 or email at bhaskar.subramanian@maryland.gov, or visit DNR's website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants authorized under Section 117(e)(1)(A) of the Clean Water Act to help Maryland achieve the goals of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement. Funding supports implementation of the Agreement's management strategies, with particular focus on reducing nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution to improve water quality. Funds also support Sustainable Fisheries, Vital Habitats, Toxic Contaminants, Healthy Watersheds, Stewardship, Land Conservation, Environmental Literacy, and Climate Resiliency goals. Maryland's Chesapeake and Coastal Service administers the funds, which leverage state and federal investments with regional and local implementation programs. Grants require a 1:1 non-federal match.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake and Coastal Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funds requiring a 1:1 non-federal match. Funding supports state agencies, the University of Maryland system, local governments, and non-profit organizations working to implement Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement management strategies. The matching model is designed to leverage state and federal investments with regional and local implementation programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, University of Maryland system institutions, local governments, and non-profit organizations working to advance Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement goals in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement's management strategies, including projects that reduce nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution and support Water Quality, Sustainable Fisheries, Vital Habitats, Toxic Contaminants, Healthy Watersheds, Stewardship, Land Conservation, Environmental Literacy, and Climate Resiliency goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, as one of the signatory jurisdictions of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement.
requirements_list: Must be a state agency, University of Maryland system entity, local government, or non-profit organization
Projects must support implementation of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement management strategies
Requires a 1:1 non-federal match
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Cory Russell at coryc.russell@maryland.gov or 410-260-8799 for more information. Maryland's CBIG program is administered by the Chesapeake and Coastal Service in coordination with EPA Region 3 and the Chesapeake Bay Program Office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant (CBIG) – Outcome 4: Environmental Education and Stewardship
structured_extraction.program_description: The Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant (CBIG), funded by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake and Coastal Service, provides annual grant funding for environmental education and stewardship projects in Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Outcome 4 aims to improve student and community ability to take action benefiting Chesapeake and coastal ecosystems through two tracks: Track One serves formal K-12 education systems and Track Two serves communities or public education. Both tracks focus on local watershed and land-use issues, environmental stewardship, professional development, outdoor learning, curriculum expansion, and civic engagement, and support hands-on, learner-led educational experiences leading to stewardship action. Track 1 proposals must connect to curriculum standards such as NGSS, Maryland Environmental Literacy Standards, and/or Meaningful Watershed Educational Experiences, while Track 2 proposals must connect to environmental or stewardship best practices. Projects should result from collaborative student/community-stakeholder planning oriented toward capacity building and civic engagement. Funding levels vary year to year based on annual federal allocation from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake and Coastal Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $75,000 per applicant (maximum request). Up to $100,000 total in CBIG funds available for Outcome 4 per solicitation cycle; proposals above that threshold should be discussed with the outcome contact before submission. Funding becomes available September 1, 2026. Funds vary year to year based on annual federal allocation from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Applications are submitted through the Grants Gateway system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-governmental organizations and non-profits, local and state agencies, schools and school systems, and higher education institutions working on environmental education and stewardship within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation and facility fees for student, teacher, or community access to natural areas; environmental engagement or stewardship activities for students or community members; environmental educator professional development and training; community environmental education programs and training; and supply costs for environmental investigations, field equipment, and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Eligible project sites include public lands, schoolyards, community property, and private property.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local non-governmental organization, non-profit, local or state agency, school, school system, or higher education institution
Projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed
Proposals must be submitted through Grants Gateway under Outcome 4

Track 1 (School Systems) requires: transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive, letter(s) of support from school system leadership, letters of support from partners/impacted community members, and Environmental Literacy Plan or evidence of environmental literacy programming
Track 1 proposals must connect to curriculum standards such as NGSS, Maryland Environmental Literacy Standards, and/or Meaningful Watershed Educational Experiences

Track 2 (Community Organizations) requires: transmittal letter with signature of authority, letter(s) of support from school administration or other partners, and outline or documentation of environmental education curriculum or programming plan
Track 2 proposals must connect to environmental or stewardship best practices
Proposals must include collaborative student/community-stakeholder planning oriented toward capacity building, civic engagement, and stewardship
Proposals should detail how they support local communities, enhance outreach to groups demonstrating need, and involve communities in programming
Projects should be based on sound environmental education principles
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Grants Gateway portal, selecting Outcome 4. Submit all required attachments specific to the applicable track (Track 1 for school systems or Track 2 for community/partner organizations). Contact Jen Wolfe at jen.wolfe@maryland.gov to discuss project ideas, eligibility, or application questions before applying. Submit required attachments with your proposal by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Director of Fishing and Boating Services annually rewards efforts to protect black bass resources by supporting tournament directors who promote bass conservation and watercraft safety among young anglers. Winners receive supplies (up to $500 value) and a plaque to help run youth-focused bass fishing tournaments using best conservation practices.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Fishing and Boating Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Winners receive a small plaque and supplies valued up to $500, purchased by the department on the winner's behalf. Up to two awards are given per year, depending on funding. Participants who complete the online Bass Class receive a Certificate of Completion. Supply purchases begin July 1 and winners receive their certificate and awarded supplies by August 1 of the award cycle year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 1 (annual; most recent cycle was May 1, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tournament directors or co-directors who are Maryland residents running small bass fishing tournaments with at least 50% youth participants (ages 16–25).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tournament supplies such as release chutes, bump tanks, mesh bags, rulers, cull clips, barbless tackle, thermometers, life jackets, aerators, ice, rubber nets, shade canopies, or weigh-in systems that promote bass survival.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Director or co-director applicant must be a Maryland resident. Tournament participants must hold a Maryland fishing license if required by law.
requirements_list: Director or co-director applicant must be a Maryland resident
Tournament participants must have a Maryland fishing license if required by law
Tournament must have at most 49 boats
At least 50% of angler participants must be between 16 and 25 years old
Applicant must identify at least one best management practice when obtaining a tournament permit
All tournament participants must complete Fishing and Boating Services' online Bass Class
Applicant must submit a brief narrative (500 words or less) describing supply needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Electronically submit the application to Ryan Gary at ryan.gary@maryland.gov by May 1 of the applicable year. Applicants will be notified of their standing by June 1. Supply purchases will be made by the department beginning July 1, and winners receive their certificate and awarded supplies by August 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law that requires replacement of forests cleared during state-funded highway construction. When a highway project using $1 or more of state funds cuts or clears forested land, the constructing agency (usually the State Highway Administration) must replant on a one-to-one (acre-for-acre) basis on public land within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. If replanting is not feasible, the agency may purchase credits from a forest mitigation bank or deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund at $0.10 per square foot ($4,356 per acre), which the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Forest Service then uses to plant replacement trees on public lands statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Constructing agencies must submit construction plans and a completed Reforestation Site Review Form (UF920) to the appropriate regional DNR Forest Service office during the initial design stage and prior to construction start. DNR completes a field review within 20 working days of request receipt. Mitigation options include: (1) replanting on public land acre-for-acre within the same county or watershed within two years or three growing seasons of project completion; (2) purchasing credits in a forest mitigation bank; or (3) depositing into the Reforestation Fund at $0.10 per square foot ($4,356 per acre) of cleared area, which DNR uses to plant replacement trees on public lands statewide. A fund-transfer option is available with DNR approval if on-site planting is impossible.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniel Coy, Urban & Community Forestry Supervisor
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government constructing agencies and contractors (typically the State Highway Administration) undertaking projects that use $1 or more in state funds and involve cutting or clearing of one or more acres of forested land, and who are required to mitigate forest clearing under Maryland law.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation Fund deposits are used by DNR to plant replacement trees on designated public lands statewide to offset forests cleared during state-funded highway construction; funds may also be used for forest pest damage recovery and forest health emergency prevention and response.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Submissions are directed to one of four regional DNR Forest Service offices based on county: Central (Montgomery, Howard, Baltimore, Harford, Carroll, Cecil), Eastern (Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Prince George's, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's), or Western (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick).
requirements_list: Project must use $1 or more of state funding for highway construction
Construction activities must involve cutting or clearing of forested land (one or more acres)

Submit a completed Reforestation Site Review Form (UF920) along with a set of project construction plans to the appropriate regional DNR Forest Service office during initial design stages and prior to construction start
DNR Forestry Personnel will complete a field review within 20 working days of request receipt
Replanting must occur at a 1:1 (acre-for-acre) ratio on public land within two years or three growing seasons of project completion
Priority is given to reforestation sites within the same county or watershed as the cleared area
If on-site replanting is not feasible, the agency may purchase credits in a forest mitigation bank
If mitigation bank credits are not available, the agency must deposit into the Reforestation Fund at $0.10 per square foot ($4,356 per acre)

Annual reporting required: on or before July 1 of each year, the Department or local authority must submit a report per § 5-103(h) covering construction activities, acres cleared/planted, and fees collected
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a set of the project's construction plans along with a completed Reforestation Site Review Form (UF920) to the appropriate regional DNR Forest Service office (Central, Eastern, Southern, or Western Region) based on the county where construction occurs. This must be done during the initial design stages and prior to construction start (before any removal occurs). DNR will complete a field review within 20 working days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_name: Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) provides reimbursement-based matching grants to state and local government entities to support outdoor recreation projects, including land acquisition and development or renovation of outdoor recreation facilities. The program is federally funded through offshore oil and gas lease revenues and administered nationally by the National Park Service, with Maryland's Department of Natural Resources managing the state-level program, coordinating grant rounds, and monitoring past project sites for compliance. Eligible applicants include state agencies, federally recognized tribes, counties, municipalities, and special districts. Funding is reimbursement-based, meaning funds are issued after project completion, and funded properties must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Land Acquisition and Planning Unit
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based 50/50 matching grants requiring a 1:1 match with non-federal funds. Minimum grant request is $50,000 (minimum $100,000 total project cost). Maximum grant request is $3,000,000 (maximum $6,000,000 total project cost). Exceptions may be granted based on project applications received and available funds. Accepted matching sources include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI), Program Open Space, and Community Parks and Playground grants. Applicants must incur 100% of project costs upfront; funds are issued as reimbursement after project completion upon NPS approval and official grant closure. Projects must be completed within 3 years of NPS start date, with a possible 2-year extension. Allowable costs include land purchase, trails, boating/swimming facilities, athletic fields, camping, fishing/hunting facilities, parking, utilities, and design/construction per LWCF Manual guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, federally recognized tribes, counties, municipalities, and special districts in Maryland seeking funding for public outdoor recreation land acquisition or facility development and renovation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land for public outdoor recreation and development or renovation of outdoor recreation amenities and facilities. Allowable costs include site development plans, recreational improvements, and land acquisition per LWCF Manual guidelines. Funded properties must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use in perpetuity. No agricultural leases or for-profit activity permitted on assisted property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must reflect the priorities of Maryland's current Land Preservation and Recreation Plan (Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a government entity (state agency, federally recognized tribe, county, municipality, or special district)
Must be a local government or state agency
LWCF funding must be matched 1:1 (50/50) with non-federal funds
Acceptable federal matching sources include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, and Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI)
Program Open Space and Community Parks and Playground grants may be used as match
Minimum 50% matching funds required; applicant must incur 100% of costs upfront before seeking reimbursement
The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use in perpetuity
No agricultural leases permitted on assisted property
No property acquired or developed with LWCF assistance may be converted to other than public outdoor recreation uses without approval of the Secretary of the Interior (section 6(f)(3) LWCF Act)
Projects must be completed within 3 years of NPS start date (2-year extension possible)
Projects must reflect the policies and priorities of Maryland's most current Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (Land Preservation and Recreation Plan)
Local projects must also align with County Land Preservation, Parks, and Recreation Plan (LPPRP)
Applications go through a 2-step process: first to DNR via Open Project Selection Process (OPSP), then successful applicants submit full federal application to National Park Service
Acquisition projects require UASFLA or 'Yellow Book' appraisal no more than 1 year old and a purchase agreement; project must be acquisition-ready
Development projects require conceptual design and final construction plans; must be shovel-ready; subject to NEPA compliance review
Applicants must review projects for conformance with Forest Conservation Act of 1991 (MD Natural Resources Article §5-1601 through §5-1613) prior to state submission

Applicants must consult Maryland Historical Trust (Project Review and Compliance Program Division, MDP) before applying to assess whether projects will adversely affect properties listed in or eligible for Maryland Register of Historic Properties
Federal/state fund applications for development require Maryland Historical Trust review and approval through MDP State Clearinghouse process
Early consultation with Maryland Historical Trust encouraged for all projects to avoid historic/cultural resource impacts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two-step process. Step 1: Review the LWCF Competitive Grant Announcement and Open Project Selection Process Criteria. Optionally schedule an individual meeting (May 1–29) to review your application proposal. Complete the appropriate Preliminary Application (Local or State) and gather required documentation (site plan, ownership documentation such as SDAT records/deeds for development projects; appraisal and purchase agreement for acquisition projects). Requires coordination with Maryland DNR for Forest Conservation Act compliance and consultation with Maryland Historical Trust/MDP before submission. Submit preliminary application to molly.pickel@maryland.gov by 5 p.m. on June 24, 2026 as part of the Open Project Selection Process (OPSP). Local applicants use 'Local' materials; state agency applicants use 'State' materials. Step 2: DNR notifies selected applicants by September 15 to proceed with a full federal application to the National Park Service.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Forest Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources) offers a 50/50 cost-share program to help public land managers treat ash trees against the Emerald Ash Borer (EAB), an invasive insect that kills ash trees. The most effective treatment is trunk injection with emamectin benzoate, conducted by licensed pesticide applicators. The program covers half the cost of treatments performed on public lands statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50/50 cost-share for Emerald Ash Borer treatments on public land. The program covers half the cost of trunk injections with emamectin benzoate performed by licensed pesticide applicators.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public land managers including local governments and managers of conservation lands in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost-share for trunk injection treatments of ash trees to protect against Emerald Ash Borer infestation on public land using emamectin benzoate applied by licensed pesticide applicators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for public lands.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public land manager (e.g., local government or conservation land manager)
Applicant must manage public land
Treatments must be conducted by licensed pesticide applicators
Treatment method must be trunk injection with emamectin benzoate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Forest Service for information and apply using the Emerald Ash Borer Treatment Program Application (linked from the program page).

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Licensed Tree Expert (LTE) Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service, licenses individuals who perform professional tree care, treatment, or removal for compensation in the state. The program protects consumers, ensures responsible management of natural resources, and promotes industry safety. It sets qualification standards, administers examinations, requires continuing education, and enforces a code of ethics. Applicants must meet education or experience requirements, pass an in-person 140-question multiple-choice examination with a 70% passing score in each domain and overall, and carry liability and property damage insurance. The exam is held approximately 10 times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month except June and August) at the Tawes State Office Building in Annapolis. Licensed tree experts must renew their license every two years and complete 8 continuing education units (CEUs) per renewal cycle.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues a professional state tree expert license to qualified applicants who pay the required fee ($30 initial; $20 renewal; $20 per domain re-exam), meet age and education or experience requirements, pass a 140-question multiple-choice exam (70% passing score required in each domain and overall), and carry required insurance. Licensed tree experts may legally operate a tree care business in Maryland. Licensees must renew every two years and complete 8 CEUs per renewal period. The in-person exam is held approximately 10 times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month except June and August) at the Tawes State Office Building in Annapolis. License renewals are due January 1 and must be received by January 31.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: License renewals due January 1; must be received no later than January 31. 2026 renewals begin after November.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who want to work as tree experts in Maryland, including arborists and tree care professionals who perform professional tree care, treatment, or removal for compensation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensure authorizes the holder to legally engage in the work or business of a tree expert (treat, care for, or remove trees for compensation) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to all Maryland residents and those seeking to operate as tree experts in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years of age
Must pay the required licensing fee ($30 initial; $20 renewal; $20 per domain re-exam)

Must meet one of the following education/experience requirements: (1) 2 years of approved college education in forestry, arboriculture, horticulture, applied agricultural sciences, or equivalent, plus at least 1 year of experience with a licensed tree expert in Maryland or an acceptable tree expert company in another state; OR (2) at least 3 consecutive years of experience as a tree expert with a licensed tree expert in Maryland or an acceptable company in another state, immediately prior to application
Must pass the Department's licensing examination with a score of at least 70% in each domain and overall (140-question multiple-choice exam)
Must carry and show proof of liability and property damage insurance in the form and amount required by the Department
Must provide Workers' Compensation insurance or exemption letter (if applicable)
Must obtain 8 CEUs over the two-year renewal period
Must comply with the Code of Ethics in COMAR 08.07.07 and ANSI A300 standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application online via the Maryland Forest Service Submittable portal or by printable PDF (available in English and Spanish). All required verification must be completed and approved before an exam date is assigned. Once the application is verified, applicants receive a scheduled exam date. The in-person exam is held approximately 10 times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month except June and August) at the Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Avenue, Annapolis, Maryland 21401. Contact Veronica Guerra at lte.dnr@maryland.gov or (410) 260-8521 to register or for exam date information. CEU pre-approval for events requires submission of a completed form and full agenda at least 30 days prior to the event. Post-event CEU approval is also available by submitting the post-event request form with supporting documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tree-Mendous Maryland is a Maryland Forest Service program that helps citizens, local governments, and community groups restore tree cover on public land and community open space across Maryland. The program provides quality native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery agreement (clearridgenursery.com), with free delivery to three locations across the state each spring and fall. Eligible groups include local governments, schools, parks, scout troops, volunteers, and community organizations planting trees on public land. A Gift of Trees option is also available, allowing individuals to purchase native tree plantings in honor or memory of someone at $40 per tree or $400 for a grove of ten trees, with trees planted in Maryland during the next appropriate growing season.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery agreement. Free delivery is available to three locations across Maryland each spring and fall. Groups can also pay for direct delivery to their planting site for an additional fee. A Gift of Trees option is available at $40 per tree ($400 for a grove of ten trees), with trees planted on public lands in the recipient's county during the next appropriate growing season.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community groups, schools, scout troops, volunteers, parks, and individual Maryland residents seeking to plant native trees on public lands or community open space in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and planting of native trees and shrubs on public land, including schools, state and community parks, local open space, and street tree locations, to improve air quality, water quality, and community livability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Trees are planted in the county where the recipient lives for Gift of Trees orders, or at eligible public land sites across Maryland for group orders.
requirements_list: Trees must be planted on public land or community open space
Permission from land owners is required
Order form is password protected — organizations must contact ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov with their organization's information and location to qualify
Volunteers and groups must coordinate with the Tree-Mendous program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov with your organization's information and location to receive the password for the order form. Complete the order form through the wholesale nursery (clearridgenursery.com). Choose free delivery to one of three statewide drop-off locations each spring and fall, or pay an additional fee for direct site delivery. For the Gift of Trees, fill out a separate order form for each recipient and submit a $40 contribution per tree.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Volunteer Fire Assistance (VFA) Grant Program provides financial, technical, and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments in Maryland to enhance wildland fire suppression capabilities, improve firefighter safety, promote use of wildland personal protective equipment, and provide basic wildland fire training. The program awards competitive sub-grants on a 50/50 cost-share basis, reimbursing up to $3,500 per department for eligible wildland firefighting equipment and training. Funded through federal funds (USDA Forest Service) administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service, applications are scored using a points system and funded until annual federal funds are depleted. The 2025 cycle awarded $167,314 in federal grants against a total project cost of approximately $370,376.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive 50/50 cost-share sub-grants of up to $3,500 per rural volunteer fire department. Federal funds (USDA Forest Service) reimburse up to 50% of eligible costs after the department purchases approved equipment and submits documentation. Departments pay their share upfront and are reimbursed after purchases are made and documented. Applications are scored using a points system; prior grant recipients face a points deduction for each of the three prior years they received a grant. Grants are funded until annual federal funds are depleted. The 2025 cycle awarded $167,314 in federal grants against a total project cost of approximately $370,376; the 2024 cycle awarded $159,234 across 55 departments. Training assistance includes tuition for National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) wildfire or chainsaw training for volunteer fire department personnel. Additional financial, technical, and related assistance is also provided to rural volunteer fire departments and their communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments, volunteer fire companies, volunteer fire protection associations, and volunteer fire/rescue services serving communities with a population of 10,000 or less. In recent grant cycles, 55 volunteer fire departments across 18 Maryland counties have received awards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildland firefighting personal protective equipment (PPE), wildland firefighting power tools (chainsaws, leaf blowers), fire hose and nozzles under 2.5 inches in diameter, bladder bags, wildland fire engine and UTV pumping units, rehabilitation of federal excess wildland firefighting equipment, fire communications equipment (pagers, radios), off-road ATVs/UTVs and supporting equipment, and wildland firefighting training (NWCG courses). Cannot be used for capital construction, vehicle purchases, structural firefighting-only equipment, HAZMAT, rescue, or EMS/medical equipment, or fire hose larger than 2.5 inches in diameter.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible departments must serve a rural area or rural community with a population of 10,000 or less (per latest Census). Area fire departments serving an aggregate population greater than 10,000 may qualify if their service area includes a rural community of 10,000 or less. In recent cycles, awards have been distributed across 18 or more Maryland counties statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer fire department, volunteer fire company, volunteer fire protection association, or volunteer fire/rescue service serving a rural area or community with a population of 10,000 or less
Area fire departments may qualify if their service area includes a rural community of 10,000 or less
Must provide a 50% cost match — department pays at least 50% of equipment cost upfront and is reimbursed after purchases are made and documented
Equipment must primarily support wildland firefighting; equipment with no wildland firefighting use is disqualified
Purchases must occur between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025 for approved 2025 grants
Supporting documentation must be submitted by January 15, 2026

Grants will not be approved for medical, rescue, or HAZMAT equipment; capital construction; or vehicle purchases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a web-based application via the online portal before 4:00 p.m. on September 15, 2025. After submission, applicants receive a confirmation email with a copy of their responses. Applicants are notified by October 15, 2025 whether their application was approved or denied. If awarded, the department receives a Memorandum of Understanding, must make purchases by December 31, 2025, and submit supporting documentation by January 15, 2026. The Maryland Forest Service reimburses the department within 45 days of receiving complete documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Monocacy NRMA Agricultural Land Lease Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Park Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources) leases state-owned farmland at the Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area to interested farmers for short-term agricultural use. The leased lands contain prime agricultural soils and have a history of being farmed, located in areas where agriculture can coexist with passive recreation. The program supports open space, wildlife habitat, and locally sourced food production in Frederick County, Maryland. Two properties are available for bid: the Henderson property (103.27 acres, 11 fields) and the Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres, 6 fields), both located near Dickerson. Leases run on 3-year cycles; the current cycle covers May 2024 through March 2027.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Park Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term (3-year) leases of state-owned farmland parcels for crop farming use. Two properties are available: the Henderson property (103.27 acres, 11 fields) and the Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres, 6 fields), both located at Monocacy NRMA, 221 Dickerson Rd, Dickerson, MD 20842. Bidders submit annual rent per acre; minimum acceptable bid is $85/acre. Rent is paid in three equal annual installments due the first day of May each year. Tenants must use the premises for crop farming purposes only and implement Best Management Practices (BMPs) including cover crops, reduced tillage, field edge buffers, grassed waterways, filter strips, and riparian buffers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers interested in leasing agricultural land at Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area in Frederick County, Maryland. Minority businesses are encouraged to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term crop farming use of state parkland with prime agricultural soils and farming history, supporting open space, wildlife habitat, and locally sourced food production. Tenants must implement Best Management Practices (BMPs) on leased fields, including multi-species cover crops, reduced/no-till, native pollinator plantings, field edge buffers, grassed waterways, filter strips, riparian buffers, hedgerows, terracing, and forage/biomass production.

Two specific parcels are leased: the Henderson property (103.27 acres across 11 cropland fields) and the Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres across 6 fields).

Sealed bid submission; bidder submits per-acre rent amount and lump-sum total; bidder need not be present at bid opening. Leases run on 3-year cycles (current cycle: May 2024 – March 2027).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Outdoor Equity Mini-Grant Program supports equitable access to outdoor recreation for communities that have been historically underserved. It funds community-based projects that help Marylanders overcome social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to the outdoors — such as transportation costs, equipment costs, entry fees, lack of exposure to outdoor activities, and not feeling welcome in outdoor spaces. Funded projects must address at least one of these themes: creating outdoor recreation opportunities, outdoor and environmental education and stewardship, community capacity-building for long-term outdoor access, or connecting outdoor recreation to health benefits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Office of Outdoor Recreation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants ranging from $2,500 to $7,500. No matching funds required, though leveraging other resources is encouraged. Approximately 5 awards are made per cycle. Funds may be used for program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, outdoor gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals. Projects must be completed by September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits (501(c)(3)), Tribal entities, school districts, government agencies, and mission-aligned for-profit organizations based in or serving underserved communities in Maryland, focused on expanding outdoor recreation access for underrepresented communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, outdoor gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support outdoor equity project goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland, serve communities in Maryland, and host their event or activity within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Tribal entity, school district, government agency, or for-profit organization with a mission aligned with outdoor equity
Must be based in Maryland, serving communities in Maryland, and hosting the event/recreation/activity within Maryland
Must demonstrate readiness to manage and complete a small-scale community project within one year
Must submit a W-9 with the State of Maryland to receive funds

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application by filling out the Google Form at https://forms.gle/nfwWj3gMfCBGCy4x6 by June 30, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. The application requires organization information, a project description, an itemized budget and narrative, a timeline with key milestones, an evaluation plan, and optional letters of support or collaboration. Awardees must submit a final report by October 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Community Parks and Playgrounds (CPP) Program provides competitive grant funding to municipal corporations and Baltimore City to develop, restore, and revitalize parks and green spaces statewide. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources under Program Open Space Local. Eligible projects include rehabilitating, expanding, or improving existing parks; creating new parks; developing environmentally oriented parks and recreation projects; purchasing and installing playground equipment in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas; creating or extending trails; developing water recreation access points; and purchasing land for new parks. Grants are reimbursable, can fund up to 100% of eligible capital project costs, and have no established minimum or maximum award amount. The Governor's FY2026 budget included $5 million for 26 new projects. Projects receive final approval from the Board of Public Works.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Program Open Space Local
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive reimbursable grants that can fund up to 100% of eligible capital project costs. There is no established minimum or maximum grant amount. The Governor's FY2026 budget included $5 million for 26 new projects. Since CPP is a reimbursable program, grant recipients pay costs upfront and are reimbursed by the state up to the Board of Public Works-approved amount. Partial reimbursements are permitted to help with cash flow, and advance payments on anticipated allowable costs may be considered in limited cases. Grants cover capital costs only — not operating or maintenance expenses. Development projects must have a minimum 20-year lifespan; acquired land must be maintained for public use in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY2027 funding were due August 20, 2025 by 3:00 p.m. Awards are announced May/June 2026. The application period for Fiscal Year 2027 is now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Governing bodies of incorporated municipal corporations in Maryland and Baltimore City seeking funding for park and green space capital projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects to rehabilitate, expand, or improve existing parks; create new parks; develop environmentally oriented parks and recreation areas; purchase and install playground equipment in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas; create or extend trails; develop water recreation access points; or purchase land for new parks. Cannot be used for operating or maintenance costs, contingency reserves, or projects already started before funds are awarded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to incorporated municipalities and Baltimore City throughout Maryland. Not available to counties, nonprofits as direct applicants, or unincorporated areas. Project location must be within eligible areas as defined by the program eligibility map.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local grants staff prepare and distribute application materials to local governments and, if needed, conduct grant-writing workshops (e.g., June 24, 2025 and July 16, 2025 for FY2027 cycle). Applicants submit proposals by August using the fillable PDF application and project agreement, saved to their desktop with all required fields completed and necessary attachments including a deed or joint use agreement for the project property. Staff evaluate complete applications and recommend selections to the DNR Secretary for inclusion in the Governor's budget. Selected projects undergo State Clearinghouse review and must be approved by the Board of Public Works (BPW) before funds are encumbered. Applicants are notified by May/June of the following year whether their project is included in the upcoming fiscal year budget. After BPW approval and project completion, the grant recipient submits a reimbursement request including invoices, canceled checks, cost summaries, and supporting documentation, with sign-off from the Program Administrator and Fiscal Administrator, for project costs up to the BPW-approved amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: Outcome 2 funds planning projects that help local jurisdictions and organizations understand and address flood risks from coastal and precipitation-based events. Funded projects improve a local government's understanding of flood impacts and vulnerabilities at a community scale. Eligible projects include flood risk assessments, incorporating adaptation strategies into existing planning processes, and developing conceptual or engineered designs for flood adaptations. Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone and should produce risk-reduction strategies or higher regulatory standards that serve as a foundation for on-the-ground implementation projects. Projects may address short-term (1–10 years) and long-term (10+ years) flood impacts from tidal, sea level rise, and precipitation-induced flooding events.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Watershed & Climate Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards typically range from $40,000 to $100,000 for projects up to one year in duration, with a maximum request of $125,000. If awarded, applicants may receive either a direct financial grant or technical assistance provided through a Maryland DNR Watershed & Climate Services selected contractor. Funding becomes available October 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-governmental organizations, and institutions of higher education located within Maryland's Coastal Zone seeking to plan for and reduce flood risks from tidal, sea level rise, and precipitation-induced flooding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood risk assessments and vulnerability analyses; incorporating adaptation strategies into local planning processes; developing conceptual or engineered designs for flood adaptations; community and stakeholder engagement; planning projects addressing short-term (1–10 years) and long-term (10+ years) flood impacts that reduce risk and advance on-the-ground implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone. Project areas can encompass both public and private lands.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, non-governmental organization, or institution of higher education.

Applicants must be open to receiving either direct financial assistance or technical assistance through a DNR-selected provider.

Required attachments: transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive, letters of support from county or town council, town administrator, county executive, or appropriate decision-making body, photographs of impacted areas, complete Budget Table (available on Grants Gateway website), complete Appendix A (if applicable), and a Communication and Engagement Strategy.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Grants Gateway portal (WizeHive platform) at https://webportalapp.com/sp/login/grants_gateway. Submit a complete proposal including all required attachments. Proposals are reviewed based on completeness, identified need and problem statement, appropriateness of proposed work, use of climate tools and resources, advancement of flood risk reduction strategies, community engagement, partnerships, and readiness to proceed. Monitor the Grants Gateway and DNR's website for updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shoreline Erosion Loan Program (Shore Erosion Control / Shoreline Conservation Service)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Shoreline Conservation Service (part of the Department of Natural Resources, Watershed & Climate Services) provides 0% interest loans and technical assistance to waterfront property owners, groups of homeowners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, counties, municipalities, and businesses to fund living shoreline and erosion control projects along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries, as well as streambank restoration projects statewide. The program offers both financial and technical assistance to help fund the design, permitting, and construction of living shoreline projects and other nature-based erosion control measures such as breakwaters, sills, groins, marsh grass plantings, biologs, and native marsh plantings, as well as streambank restoration projects. Financial assistance for non-structural projects may also be awarded as 75% interest-free loans for projects on private and public lands using State special funds, or as 75%-25% matching grants for projects on public lands using Federal funds. Loan terms range from 5 to 20 years depending on the techniques used, associated costs, and their projected longevity. An administrative fee of 3% to 10% based on project construction cost is included. Loans are disbursed in portions as work is completed, and a shore erosion control lien (for private property) or a county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district (for community projects) must be established as a condition of the loan. For loans over $60,000 to individuals or groups of homeowners, an upfront cash contribution is required. Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded. The program also provides technical support including site visit evaluations and problem assessments to help applicants plan and implement shoreline protection measures.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Watershed & Climate Services

Technical and financial assistance is also available for design and installation of shoreline stabilization and streambank restoration projects, including site visit evaluations and problem assessments. Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not eligible for funding.

Structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded under the living shoreline component. Also covers site visit evaluations and problem assessments for shoreline erosion issues.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Boating Access Program is a federal grant program administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources' Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program, under the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration (WSFR) Program. It funds the construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps used by recreational, trailered motorboats. Funding comes from federal excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat and small engine fuels, apportioned to states by formula. At least 15% of each state's federal apportionment must go toward boating access. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 per year in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants funded primarily by excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat and small engine fuels, apportioned to states by formula under the Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Program. At least 15% of each state's apportionment must go toward boating access. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 per year. Grants cover up to 75% of project costs; a 25% local/state match is required. Eligible projects include construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps, trailer parking areas, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, piers, and associated amenities for recreational trailered motorboats. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis; no work or expenses are reimbursable until the Land Control Agreement (LCA) is fully executed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local/public jurisdictions seeking to construct or renovate publicly owned boat ramps used by recreational, trailered motorboats.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps, trailer parking areas, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, piers, and associated amenities for recreational trailered motorboats.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to local/public jurisdictions across all Maryland counties. No county-by-county exclusions stated.
requirements_list: Applicants must be local/public jurisdictions.
Projects must involve construction or renovation of publicly owned boat ramps and associated facilities (trailer parking, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, piers, and amenities).
Ramps must be used by recreational, trailered motorboats.

Non-discriminatory fees required.
Applicant must obtain all required permits and submit plans for Department review and approval.
