Facility must be maintained for its useful life (20–40 years per Professional Engineer determination).
Restrictions on conflicting activities at the facility apply.
Reimbursement clawback applies for non-compliance; failure to maintain public boating access use triggers full federal/state dollar reimbursement obligation.
Funds must be segregated as required by grant terms.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The BA Program is open year round. (1) Contact Jennifer Jackson at 410-897-2153 or jenniferl.jackson@maryland.gov to discuss project fit and interest in pursuing a federal BA grant. (2) Applicant prepares a federal grant application package with Department assistance, including a core 'Project Statement' with detailed project information, justification, and scope of work. (3) Application is submitted for USFWS approval. (4) Upon approval, a Land Control Agreement (LCA) is executed between the Department and the local jurisdiction — no work may begin and no expenses are reimbursable until the LCA is fully executed (except pre-approved pre-agreement costs). (5) Post-award, the applicant must obtain permits, submit plans for Department review/approval, advertise competitively for bids, and submit bid tabulations and recommended award for Department approval. (6) Eligible expenses are reimbursed after work is completed and documentation is submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Waterway Improvement Fund, administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, provides financial support to local governments, the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, and federal agencies through grants and/or loans for capital projects and services that benefit the boating public. Eligible projects include constructing, renovating, or maintaining boating access facilities; dredging high-use channels and harbors; purchasing fire and rescue vessels in partnership with local fire companies; marking channels and harbors; clearing debris from waterways; constructing jetties and marine facilities; and supporting services such as ice breaking, navigation aids, derelict boat removal, and boating safety programs. Grants of 100% are available for projects significantly benefiting the general boating public (e.g., harbor of refuge, anchorage, fueling/repair access); 50/50 matching grants are available for other eligible projects, with a maximum State allocation of $25,000 per year per project. The Matching Fund Fire & Rescue Grant provides up to $80,000 in state funds. Small Project Grants can be submitted any time throughout the fiscal year. In St. Mary's County, residents can access this program through a Special Taxing District coordinated by the Department of Public Works. The fund has provided more than $429 million for over 4,900 projects at more than 400 public boating access sites since 1966, funded primarily by a one-time 5% excise tax paid when a boat is purchased and titled in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and/or loans for capital projects and services benefiting the boating public. Grants of 100% are available if the project significantly benefits the general boating public (e.g., harbor of refuge, anchorage, fueling/repair access). 50/50 matching grants are available when the general boating public is not significantly benefited. Maximum State allocation is $25,000 per year per project for standard grants. The Matching Fund Fire & Rescue Grant provides up to $80,000 in state funds for marine fire/rescue facilities and vessels. Small Project Grants (up to $25,000) can be submitted any time throughout the fiscal year. In St. Mary's County, the State and County/residents split costs, and the County is reimbursed by the Taxing District over up to 25 years via interest-free loans. Funded primarily by a one-time 5% excise tax paid when a boat is purchased and titled in Maryland. The program has provided more than $429 million for over 4,900 projects at more than 400 public boating access sites since 1966. Applications are typically submitted between July and mid-September for the following fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically July through mid-September for the following fiscal year; Small Project Grants may be submitted any time throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county, town, or city), the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, federal agencies, and volunteer fire companies (with local government authorization) seeking to improve public boating facilities, navigation, and safety; also private property owners in St. Mary's County accessing the program through a Special Taxing District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Constructing, renovating, or maintaining boating access facilities; dredging high-use channels and harbors; purchasing fire and rescue vessels in partnership with local fire companies; marking channels and harbors; clearing debris from waterways; constructing jetties, breakwaters, and marine facilities; pump-out stations; bridge/drawbridge improvements; boating education and safety programs; shore erosion control; navigation aids; derelict boat removal; and ice breaking services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to public jurisdictions across all Maryland counties. In St. Mary's County, the program is also accessible to residents and property owners through a Special Taxing District coordinated through the Department of Public Works.
requirements_list: Applicants must be public jurisdictions (local governments — county, town, or city — the Department of Natural Resources, or federal agencies), volunteer fire companies (with local government authorization), or in St. Mary's County, private property owners through the Special Taxing District process.
Projects must meet the highest priority needs of the motorized boating public.

Eligible projects include navigation/dredging improvements, public boating facility construction or renovation, marine fire/rescue vessel acquisition, channel marking, debris clearing, and jetty/marine facility construction.
Applications must be submitted through Grants Gateway under Outcome 5 (for public jurisdictions).
Small Project Grant applications may be submitted any time throughout the fiscal year.

Submit a petition signed by at least 75% of benefited property owners to initiate the formal DNR Need and Feasibility review for private community improvements (St. Mary's County Special Taxing District).
Project must meet eligibility criteria under Natural Resources Article Section 8-707.
Maximum State allocation is $25,000 per year per project for standard grants; up to $80,000 for Matching Fund Fire & Rescue Grants.
Contracts of $250,000 or more with 25% or more state funding require prevailing wage compliance.
Public bidding required; DNR concurrence required on contracts.
DNR must be notified of construction start dates.
Licensed Marine Contractor required for work in/on/under tidal wetlands; all permits must precede construction.
Grantees must retain supporting documents for 3 years post-reimbursement.
Grant balances not disbursed after one year are subject to immediate reversion unless an extension is granted by the administration.

Recipient of Matching Fund Fire & Rescue Grant must own, operate, and maintain the facility or vessel; repayment required if asset is disposed of or if funds are misused or subject to negligent operation/maintenance.
All necessary federal, state, and local permits/approvals must be obtained before construction start.
Plans and specifications must be submitted for DNR review and approval prior to construction.
Applicant is responsible for ongoing operation and maintenance of completed project.
Bid tabulation or procurement documentation required for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Public jurisdictions create a user profile on Grants Gateway and submit applications within Outcome 5, typically between July and mid-September, for the following fiscal year's funding consideration. Small Project Grants (up to $25,000) may be submitted any time throughout the fiscal year. For the Matching Fund Fire & Rescue Grant, local governing bodies apply with authorization for volunteer fire/emergency response organizations. For St. Mary's County residents accessing the program through the Special Taxing District, submit a petition from at least 75% of benefited property owners to initiate a DNR Need and Feasibility review, followed by a 20-step formal district establishment and project approval workflow. Refer to the Special Taxing District Policy and Procedures documents and contact St. Mary's County Department of Public Works for assistance. Reimbursement requests require a transmittal letter, signed reimbursement form, invoices with proof of payment, in-house labor/equipment documentation, current grantee checklist, and photos (for final reimbursement), submitted via email to the Regional Administrator.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Master Naturalist Program provides scientific training in natural history, ecology, interpretation, and the relationship between humans and the natural world. Participants complete 60 hours of classroom and field experience — held at Maryland DNR headquarters in Annapolis on Wednesdays from 6pm to 9pm with four Saturday field days — pass content knowledge tests throughout the program, and complete a final interpretation project. After training, certified Master Naturalists volunteer 40 hours per year to give back to their community through teaching, leading field trips, and supporting ecological research. The program is developed in cooperation with the University of Maryland Extension, which manages fees and enrollment details.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive 60 hours of classroom and field training covering Maryland natural history, ecology, flora and fauna identification, ecological principles, human impacts on the landscape, and teaching and interpretation skills. Classes are held at the Maryland DNR headquarters in Annapolis on Wednesdays from 6pm to 9pm, with four Saturday field days. A fee applies (see University of Maryland Extension for details). Certification requires passing content knowledge tests throughout the program, completing a final interpretation project, and volunteering 40 hours in the first year with the hosting organization; 40 volunteer hours per year are required in each subsequent year to maintain certification. A criminal background check and three references are required as part of the application process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring 2026 registration is now closed; next class expected 2028
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and individuals interested in learning about the natural world and volunteering to share nature education, lead field trips, and support ecological research in their communities. Open to adults of varying age groups including youth, young adults, adults, and seniors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scientific training in natural history, ecology, flora and fauna identification, ecological principles, human impacts on the landscape, and teaching and interpretation skills; volunteer service to host organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training classes are held in Anne Arundel County at the Maryland DNR headquarters, 580 Taylor Ave, Annapolis, MD 21401, focusing on the natural history of Maryland's Coastal Plain including Chesapeake Bay and wetland ecosystems. Additional courses may be available through the University of Maryland Extension statewide.
requirements_list: Complete 60 hours of classroom and field training
Pass content knowledge tests throughout the program
Complete a final interpretation project
Volunteer 40 hours in the first year with the hosting organization
Continue volunteering 40 hours per year to maintain certification
Consent to a criminal background check
Provide three references
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration for the Spring 2026 class is now closed. To be placed on a waitlist for the 2028 class, contact Paula Becker at paula.becker@maryland.gov. The application is a printable form requiring personal information, background check authorization, three references, work history, and responses to open-ended questions about experience, motivation, and availability. Visit the University of Maryland Extension website for fees, policies, and application details. An application form is also available on the DNR website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program for private landowners who develop and manage waterfowl habitats on their land. Participants enter into 10-year renewable license agreements with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Wildlife and Heritage Service to carry out approved projects that create, develop, rehabilitate, or preserve waterfowl habitats for breeding, migrating, and wintering waterfowl. Expenditures made under the approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan are treated as contributions to the State of Maryland for tax purposes, providing a tax benefit to the landowner. The program also provides technical assistance from DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service biologists to help landowners prepare habitat management plans, with annual site inspections and a standard tax form provided each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants sign a 10-year renewable license agreement covering an approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan. Expenditures made under the plan are treated as contributions to the State of Maryland, giving the landowner a tax benefit. DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service biologists provide technical assistance in preparing the habitat management plan and conduct annual site inspections. A standard tax form is provided each year after inspection. The agreement is renewable after the initial 10-year period. Landowners are responsible for substantiating expenditure amounts if requested by the State Comptroller.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners with at least 10 contiguous acres of habitat that can provide food and/or cover for ducks, including at least one acre of semi-permanent water with nesting and resting habitat within or near it. Commercial hunting enterprises are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating, developing, rehabilitating, and/or preserving waterfowl habitats on private lands, including wetland improvement and management for breeding, migrating, and wintering waterfowl, and ensuring a diverse wetland plant community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to private landowners throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Project area must encompass a minimum of 10 contiguous acres of habitat providing food and/or cover for ducks
Project must include at least 1 acre of semi-permanent water with nesting and resting habitat within or near it
Private lands used for commercial hunting enterprises are not eligible
Landowner must enter into a 10-year license agreement with DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service
Landowner must agree to and carry out an approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan
Landowner is responsible for substantiating expenditure amounts if requested by the State Comptroller
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review project eligibility rules to determine if your land qualifies. 2. Complete the Maryland Waterfowl Restoration Program Application Form and mail it to the Wildlife and Heritage Service office at PO Box 68, Wye Mills, MD 21679, or call 410-827-8612 ext. 103. 3. The Regional Habitat Biologist for your county will review your application and contact you to arrange a site inspection. 4. If approved, you will receive an official information kit with all program documents.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project WILD is a hands-on professional development workshop for K-12 educators in formal and non-formal settings. The program emphasizes awareness, appreciation, and understanding of wildlife and natural resources through interdisciplinary activities covering art, language arts, math, science, and social studies. Participants receive one or two award-winning curriculum guides with over 100 lesson plans including STEM extensions and career connections. Educators may earn 1 MSDE continuing education credit (CPD: 18-66-13R) for attending 3 out of 5 workshops with certified trainers, and workshops also qualify for Maryland Green Schools professional development credit. Funding is provided through license fees, and private on-site training is available at no cost for groups of 15 or more. A once-yearly train-the-trainer facilitator workshop is also offered for educators wishing to lead their own workshops.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost professional development workshops (4-6 hours) funded by license fees. Upon completion, educators receive one or two award-winning curriculum guides with over 100 lesson plans including STEM extensions and career connections. Private on-site training is available at no cost for groups of at least 15 participants, tailored to the school or facility's needs. Educators may earn 1 MSDE continuing education credit (CPD: 18-66-13R) by attending 3 out of 5 workshops with certified trainers. Workshops also qualify for Maryland Green Schools professional development credit. A once-yearly train-the-trainer facilitator workshop is available for educators wishing to lead their own workshops.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 educators in formal (classroom) and non-formal (nature centers, museums, zoos, parks, scouts) settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development for educators in wildlife and natural resources education; curriculum guides and lesson plans for teaching local wildlife topics
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must attend a 4-6 hour professional development workshop to receive Project WILD materials
Private training requires a minimum of 15 participants
Facilitator Workshop is held once a year for educators who want to lead their own workshops
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the Workshop Schedule page to find an upcoming workshop near you. For private training at your facility, contact Sarah B. Witcher at sarah.witcher1@maryland.gov or 410-260-8566.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to eligible organizations to offset the costs of butchering and processing deer donated to programs that feed low-income individuals and people experiencing homelessness in Maryland, including food banks and other programs providing nutritional support to Marylanders in need.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 per applicant are available on a first-come, first-served basis to reimburse butchering and processing costs at a maximum of $60 per deer. Funds may be split among multiple applicants. Administrative costs are not eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal corporations, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that operate programs providing food or nutritional support to low-income individuals or the homeless in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Butchering and processing costs for donated deer. Administrative costs are not eligible. Maximum reimbursement is $60 per deer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Deer must be hunted in compliance with Maryland State hunting laws and regulations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county government, municipal corporation, or 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
Deer must be hunted in compliance with Maryland State hunting laws and regulations
Deer must be donated to a program that provides nutritional support or food for low-income individuals or the homeless
Deer must have a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds
Maximum reimbursable processing cost is $60 per deer when using grant funds
Grantees must identify and contract with processors and coordinate venison distribution
Quarterly reports are required, including DNR hunting confirmation numbers, processor names and deer counts, amounts paid per deer, pounds of venison distributed, and list of recipient organizations

501(c)(3) applicants must attach one of five acceptable forms of tax-exemption documentation: IRS listing reference, valid IRS tax exemption certificate, State certification of nonprofit status, certificate of incorporation, or parent organization proof plus affiliate statement
All fields on the application form must be completed for consideration

Applicants must provide organization name, point of contact, address, phone, email, EIN, funding amount requested, program history, geographic scope, lists of cooperating butchers/processors, and venison receiver organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all fields on the application form and submit it electronically to Brian Eyler at brian.eyler@maryland.gov by 11:59 pm on June 16, 2025. For 501(c)(3) applicants, attach one of five acceptable forms of tax-exemption documentation: (a) IRS listing reference, (b) valid IRS tax exemption certificate, (c) State certification of nonprofit status, (d) certificate of incorporation, or (e) parent organization proof plus affiliate statement. Quarterly reporting is required post-award and must include DNR hunting confirmation numbers per deer, processor names and counts, cost per deer, total venison available, and recipient organization list.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A $300,000 EPA-funded community-wide brownfields assessment grant administered by the Maryland Department of Planning. The project provides free Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs), Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) participation, and MDE Technical Review Services (TRS) to property owners in Baltimore County's East Side communities. The goal is to identify environmental impacts at brownfield sites, inform property owners of potential pollution, and help prepare sites for cleanup and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs), MDE Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) participation assistance, and MDE Technical Review Services (TRS) funded through a $300,000 EPA community-wide assessment grant. No direct cash is provided to property owners — services are delivered in-kind by qualified environmental consultants selected through a competitive procurement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Baltimore County's East Side communities (Sparrows Point, Bowleys Quarters, Lower Back River Neck Peninsula, North Point/Edgemere, Essex, Middle River, Perry Hall/White Marsh, and Dundalk) with brownfield sites seeking environmental assessment and redevelopment support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, MDE Voluntary Cleanup Program participation, and MDE Technical Review Services to assess and prepare brownfield properties for cleanup and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County East Side communities including Sparrows Point, Bowleys Quarters, Lower Back River Neck Peninsula, North Point/Edgemere, Essex, Middle River, Perry Hall/White Marsh, and Dundalk.
requirements_list: Property must be located in one of the designated East Side Baltimore County communities
Property must be a brownfield site (vacant or underutilized with known or perceived environmental contamination)
Property owner must participate in the outreach and assessment process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners are identified through an outreach process informed by an Advisory Committee. Interested property owners can visit the Property Owner Portal on the project webpage. Qualified environmental consultants selected via competitive RFP (posted December 20, 2022) conduct the assessments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Department of Planning Brownfield Redevelopment Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) provides free technical assistance to local governments, nonprofits, individuals, developers, property owners, and other parties interested in brownfield (contaminated or potentially contaminated properties) remediation and redevelopment statewide. MDP serves as a resource, liaison, and facilitator, helping clients identify brownfield sites, access funding and incentive resources, prepare and manage EPA Brownfield grant applications, and coordinating with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), the EPA Region III Technical Assistance for Brownfields (TAB) program through NJIT, and other federal and state agencies. MDP can also provide brownfields inventories, recommend comprehensive plan language or zoning code changes to support redevelopment, coordinate training, and provide general guidance on focusing brownfield redevelopment efforts and evaluating available incentives and funding opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDP provides free technical assistance including: brownfields inventories, help identifying brownfield sites, preparing and managing EPA Brownfield grant applications, liaison services with MDE and EPA Region III, coordination of training through NJIT TAB, recommendations for comprehensive plan language or zoning code updates to facilitate brownfield redevelopment, and connecting local jurisdictions and other interested parties with brownfield assessment, cleanup, planning, and redevelopment funding and incentive opportunities. Staff also provide general guidance on focusing brownfield efforts and evaluating available incentives and funding opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, local planning jurisdictions, nonprofits, property owners, developers, individuals, and other entities interested in brownfield remediation and redevelopment across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for brownfield site identification, assessment, and remediation planning; grant application preparation and management; brownfields inventories; coordination with state and federal agencies; planning and zoning code recommendations; training coordination; and identifying funding and tax incentive opportunities for brownfield cleanup and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, with a focus on expanding access beyond Baltimore City to other urban and rural areas.
requirements_list: Must be interested in brownfield remediation or redevelopment
Complete the online Request for Brownfield Assistance form to enlist Planning's assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Request for Brownfield Assistance form available on the MDP website, or contact Sylvia A. Mosser at the Maryland Department of Planning directly. Planning staff will then coordinate appropriate assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: An online education course that teaches local government officials how Tax Increment Financing (TIF) works — a method allowing local governments to use increased property tax revenue from new development to fund public improvements that promote economic development. The course covers benefits and risks of TIF, services available from the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) for TIF in designated Sustainable Communities, and how TIF can be used to promote revitalization. Completion is required by law before a local jurisdiction can use the TIF authority for Sustainable Communities established under the 2013 Sustainable Communities – Designation and Financing Law. MDP issues a certification upon completion. Note: the online course is currently offline for technical reasons; interested participants should contact Chuck Boyd at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov to take the course in the interim.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course on Tax Increment Financing (TIF). Upon completion, the Maryland Department of Planning provides a certification. Note: the online course is currently offline for technical reasons; interested participants should contact Chuck Boyd at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov to take the course in the interim.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Chief administrative officers and chief financial officers of local Maryland jurisdictions that want to use TIF authority for Sustainable Communities, as well as elected officials and community development advocates.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and certification on the use of Tax Increment Financing for community revitalization in designated Sustainable Communities, including understanding TIF principles, benefits, risks, and applicable MEDCO services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to local government officials across Maryland.
requirements_list: Participant must be the chief administrative officer or chief financial officer of a local jurisdiction to satisfy the legal requirement before using TIF authority for Sustainable Communities.
Complete the online TIF education course (currently offline; contact Chuck Boyd at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov to take the course).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Chuck Boyd at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov while the online training is offline. Once the course is completed, MDP provides a certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Planning provides outreach, education, technical assistance, and analysis support to local governments interested in Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) programs. TDR programs allow developers to buy development rights from rural landowners in designated 'sending areas' to preserve that land under a perpetual conservation easement, while using those rights to build more densely in designated 'receiving areas' where infrastructure supports growth. Planning staff help communities identify the best type of TDR program for their needs, provide educational presentations and materials, offer one-on-one consulting, policy development, plan review, ordinance creation, supply/demand analysis, tax revenue analysis, and infrastructure needs assessment to support TDR program development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning staff provide free technical assistance to local governments, including one-on-one consulting, educational presentations, workshops, policy development, plan review, ordinance creation, supply/demand analysis, tax revenue analysis, and infrastructure needs assessment to support TDR program development. No financial award is involved — this is advisory and planning support only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities) in Maryland interested in developing or improving Transfer of Development Rights programs to preserve rural land and direct development to appropriate areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to plan, design, and implement TDR programs at the local government level, including interjurisdictional TDR programs between municipalities and counties. Services include one-on-one consulting, policy development, plan review, ordinance creation, supply/demand analysis, tax revenue analysis, and infrastructure needs assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local governments. Counties with known existing or past TDR programs include Calvert, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester, among others. Technical assistance is tailored regionally across Central Maryland, Southern Maryland, and the Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local government (county or municipality)
Community must be interested in investigating or improving a TDR program
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in TDR program assistance are encouraged to contact Maryland Department of Planning staff directly. Staff are available to discuss program options and provide presentations and analysis. Contact Debbie Herr Cornwell at 410.767.4620 or deborah.herrcornwell@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certification of County Agricultural Land Preservation Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Certification Program allows counties to retain a larger share of locally generated agricultural land transfer tax revenue (75% instead of 33%) in exchange for creating and maintaining effective local agricultural land preservation programs. Jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) and the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), the program is voluntary and requires counties to meet ongoing standards, including establishing Priority Preservation Areas and farmland preservation acreage goals. Certified counties must spend or encumber retained funds for land preservation purposes within six years or the funds revert to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Planning and Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified counties retain 75% of locally generated agricultural land transfer tax revenue, compared to 33% for uncertified counties. Retained funds must be spent or encumbered for land preservation purposes (easement purchases, MALPF Matching Funds Program, past land preservation debt, or administrative expenses) within six years or they revert to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund. Recertification periods are up to five years, aligned with comprehensive plan update cycles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties with local agricultural land preservation programs seeking to retain a greater share of agricultural land transfer tax revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retained funds may be used to purchase land preservation easements through a local or State program, participate in MALPF's Matching Funds Program, service past debt from land preservation activities, and/or cover administrative expenses for the county's land preservation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any of Maryland's 23 counties on a voluntary basis. As of June 30, 2019, 16 counties are fully or conditionally certified.
requirements_list: County must have an effective local agricultural land preservation program
County must apply to both MDP and MALPF
County must establish Priority Preservation Areas (PPAs) in its comprehensive plan
County must set a farmland preservation acreage goal for the PPA
Retained funds must be spent or encumbered within six years or they revert to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund
Recertification (renewal) is required, with periods of up to five years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested counties apply to both the Maryland Department of Planning and MALPF. Counties with certified status must seek recertification to maintain their status, with recertification periods of up to five years.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS provides specialized vocational rehabilitation services for job seekers whose primary disability is an acquired brain injury (ABI). ABI includes injuries not present at birth, such as those caused by motor vehicle accidents, falls, assaults, sports injuries, concussions, brain aneurysms, strokes, or infections. DORS works with community rehabilitation partners to deliver individualized, long-term, and ongoing support to help people with ABI find and keep employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized, long-term, and ongoing support services delivered through specially trained ABI counselors located throughout Maryland and community rehabilitation partners. Services include employment counseling, job coaching, accommodations planning, benefits counseling, job placement, and assistive technology support focused on helping individuals get and keep a job.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with acquired brain injury (ABI/TBI) who want to work or return to work, as well as their supporters or case managers seeking employment support services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational rehabilitation and employment support services to help individuals with acquired brain injury find and maintain employment, including counseling, job coaching, job placement, accommodations, assistive technology, benefits counseling, and retraining referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through DORS counselors located throughout the state. No specific county, municipality, or regional limitations.
requirements_list: Primary disability must be an acquired brain injury (ABI)
ABI must be an injury not present at birth (e.g., traumatic or non-traumatic brain injury)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-554-9381 or email Derick Serra, Office of Field Services Program Manager, to learn more and start the process. Individuals may also start by contacting their state or local Vocational Rehabilitation office, Employment Networks, Centers for Independent Living, Protection & Advocacy offices, or local workforce centers.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS Apprenticeship Services help Marylanders with disabilities explore, access, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Services include consultations, academic assessments, exploration of apprenticeship opportunities, academic instruction, and support for pre-apprenticeship, registered apprenticeship, and youth apprenticeship programs. Assistance includes paid employment opportunities combined with on-the-job training and classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides consultation, academic assessment, exploration services, academic instruction, and ongoing support for individuals with disabilities pursuing registered apprenticeships. Services are delivered by an Apprenticeship Coordinator and an Academic Instructor for Apprenticeship Services. Support covers all stages from exploration through completion of a registered apprenticeship, including pre-apprenticeship and youth apprenticeship pathways. Assistance includes paid employment opportunities combined with on-the-job training and classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who are interested in exploring or participating in registered apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support preparation for, application to, and participation in registered apprenticeship programs, including academic remediation, testing preparation, and coordination with apprenticeship sponsors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, including connections to statewide American Job Centers for recruitment.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability served by DORS)
Must be interested in exploring or participating in a registered apprenticeship program
Age 18 or older
High school diploma, GED, or NEDP
Reliable transportation
Drug-free
Physically able to perform required tasks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For individuals: Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com to explore available apprenticeship occupations, then call (410) 767-2246 or email info@mdapprenticeship.com to connect with a navigator, and apply directly to the apprenticeship sponsor or employer. For employers/sponsors: Call (410) 767-2246, a navigator will connect with an existing program or develop a customized program, present plan for approval to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, then begin recruiting. For DORS consumers, contact DORS Apprenticeship Coordinator Sam Grimsley at 410-554-9288 or Samantha.Grimsley@maryland.gov to begin the process.

structured_extraction.program_name: DORS Wage Reimbursement for On-the-Job Training (OJT)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Business Relations Team reimburses businesses for wages paid while training a qualified DORS job seeker with disabilities through on-the-job training (OJT). Short-term OJT (one month) offers up to 100% salary reimbursement. Long-term OJT (up to four months) provides gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled and independent. The program connects employers with qualified job seekers with disabilities and supports workforce integration at no cost to the business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses that hire a qualified DORS job seeker receive wage reimbursement during on-the-job training. Short-term OJT (one month) reimburses up to 100% of salary. Long-term OJT (up to four months) provides gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee gains skills and independence. Additional services include recruitment assistance and pre-screening, technical assistance for accessing tax incentives, disability and employment training for staff, and retention services. The program is available at no cost to the employer.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of wages paid to employees with disabilities during on-the-job training periods. May also include recruitment assistance, technical assistance for tax incentives, staff disability/employment training, and retention services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS Business Relations/Business Services Representatives. Service regions include Western Maryland, Southern Maryland, Baltimore City, Eastern Shore, Central Maryland, D.C. Suburbs, and Blind Services statewide.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS provides specialized vocational rehabilitation and support services to Deaf-Blind individuals in Maryland. Services include Braille training from Deaf-Blind instructors, Orientation and Mobility (O&M) training, Job Coaching from providers trained to work with Deaf-Blind consumers, and Support Service Providers (SSPs) who help Deaf-Blind individuals access their environment and make informed decisions. DORS also offers Rehabilitation Counselors for the Deaf for those who prefer American Sign Language (ASL). Additional supports include communication technology options (Captel, RTT, VRS apps) and Communication Facilitator services for tactile signers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Specialized support services including Braille training, Orientation and Mobility training, job coaching, and Support Service Provider (SSP) assistance. SSPs provide visual and environmental information, sighted guide services, and communication accessibility to help Deaf-Blind individuals access community and vocational rehabilitation services. Additional supports include communication technology options (Captel, RTT, VRS apps) and Communication Facilitator services for tactile signers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DeafBlind individuals (adults and children) in Maryland seeking vocational rehabilitation and support services, as well as families of DeafBlind persons, professionals and educators serving DeafBlind populations, older adults with vision and hearing loss, transition-age youth (ages 14–21), and persons who are blind and hard of hearing.

Some national organizations also accept Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) provides home modification services to help eligible DORS consumers improve accessibility at their homes so they can achieve their employment goals. The Work Technology Center (WTC) home modification team assesses and improves bathroom accessibility, home entry and exit, and access to different levels of the home, then coordinates construction, monitors it on-site, and confirms all modifications comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides a limited range of home modification services at no cost to eligible consumers. Services include accessibility assessments of bathrooms, home entry/exit, and multi-level access, as well as coordination and monitoring of construction work and final inspections to ensure ADA compliance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP) trains, licenses, and supports people who are legally blind to manage retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal and State of Maryland facilities. The program prepares individuals to operate successful retail concession and food service businesses in public buildings, including federal, military, DOD, state, and county properties. BEP-licensed business operators manage approximately 50 long-term, successful businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A three-phase training program that includes: (1) an eight-week New Manager Training course at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Baltimore (2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218); (2) formal food service training with certified instructors leading to a National Restaurant Association food service sanitation certification; and (3) three to six months of on-the-job internship at BEP facilities. Graduates are licensed to operate vending and food service facilities in public buildings including federal, military, DOD, state, and county properties. Specific facility locations include Annapolis, Baltimore, NIH, IRS, FDA, Motor Vehicle Administration, Social Security Administration, US Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Legally blind individuals who are U.S. citizens, certified eligible by DORS, and have an aptitude for business management. Also serves persons with vision loss as primary disability, including legally blind individuals over age 55 with independent living goals. Program is open to persons who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and licensing to manage retail concession, food service, and vending operations in public facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — training is conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore (2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218); licensed facilities are located in federal, military, DOD, state, and county buildings in Maryland, including locations in Annapolis, Baltimore, NIH, IRS, FDA, Motor Vehicle Administration, Social Security Administration, US Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.

The program places participants in unpaid, voluntary internships within Maryland State agencies, typically for three-month periods in full or part-time positions. Internships may be extended beyond three months, and many QUEST interns go on to obtain paid positions in State agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program for individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience or who have been out of the workforce for an extended period. Work Readiness 1 is a six-week classroom-based course covering career exploration, soft skills, financial management, and workplace preparation. Work Readiness 2 is a six-week course focused on soft skills and hands-on work experience at community worksites. Participants may take both parts together or as standalone programs. Classes are held at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore with community-based activities at local worksites.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two six-week courses (Work Readiness 1 and 2) that can be taken together or separately. Work Readiness 1 uses videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing, covering career exploration, soft skills, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination, interpersonal skills, workplace prep, and job retention. Work Readiness 2 includes classroom instruction and real-world work experience at community worksites with drop-in support. Classes are held at the DORS WTC campus in Baltimore with community-based activities at local worksites.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing workplace readiness skills including career exploration, soft skills, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination, interpersonal skills, customer service, conflict management, resume writing, mock interviews, and real-world work experience at community worksites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — program is offered through the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in Baltimore, Maryland, with community-based activities at local worksites.

Work Readiness 2: Must demonstrate the ability to work in a real work environment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism (GCOSV), operated by the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI), awards formula grants to nonprofits, government agencies, higher education institutions, for-profit organizations, and other entities that want to join the Maryland AmeriCorps State and National portfolio. Grantees deploy full- or part-time AmeriCorps members to address critical community needs in areas such as education, economic opportunity, and capacity building across Maryland. Grant amounts are based on the number of AmeriCorps members placed with the organization; organizations must support the equivalent of at least 20 full-time AmeriCorps members in their first year of operation. Matching funds may be required. Grantees receive resources, compliance support, and strategic guidance to strengthen their programs. Individuals who complete a term of service can receive an educational award. Anticipated program start date is August 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Corps/Service Year Option (MC/SYO) is a full-time paid service year program operated by the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI). The program connects adults 18 and older who live in Maryland with service opportunities by placing participants (Members) with host site employers (Partners) — including nonprofits, for-profit businesses, government agencies, higher education institutions, and schools — across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Two pathways exist: Service Year Option (ages 18–24, requires a high school diploma, GED, or Certificate of Completion) and Maryland Corps (all eligible adults 18+, no education requirement, including individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities). Members complete a minimum 9-month (at least 41 weeks) placement, earning at least $15/hour for 30–40 hours per week. Members receive on-the-job training, monthly professional development training, weekly virtual learning, a dedicated Service Success Coach, mentoring, networking opportunities, and can explore career paths — including climate/clean energy, education, community health, public service, apprenticeships and trades, information technology, and public safety — through their placements. Members also receive a living allowance, access to health coverage and childcare assistance, and the opportunity to earn a Department of Labor Registered Apprenticeship Certificate. Upon completing the program, Members receive a taxable $6,000 Completion Award usable for any purpose, and may also receive a Segal AmeriCorps Education Award to help pay for college, vocational training, or student loans. For Host Site Partners, DSCI provides a supplemental cost-reimbursement grant to offset member salary and benefits costs; the amount varies based on organization type, operating budget, and number of Members hosted, up to approximately $20,000 per year per full-time member (covering roughly two-thirds of member wages). Reimbursements are paid quarterly after submission of documentation. Host sites cover the remaining wages, taxes, and benefits (estimated ~$7,450/year per member). A DSCI-sponsored payroll provider option and competitive cost-share waivers are available for organizations that cannot meet cost-sharing requirements. DSCI also provides dedicated Member Success coaches, monthly in-person professional development trainings, weekly virtual learning, and apprenticeship credential support at no additional cost to partners. The program runs an annual cycle launching in August/September with graduation in June, and is part of a broader set of AmeriCorps-affiliated Maryland service programs administered by DSCI. Members join a national AmeriCorps alumni network of over one million members.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members earn at least $15.00 per hour working full-time (30–40 hours/week) for at least 41 weeks (minimum 9 months). Host Site Partners are required to provide fringe benefits including healthcare. Upon successfully completing the service term, members receive a taxable $6,000 cash completion award (usable for any purpose) and, if applicable, a Department of Labor Registered Apprenticeship Certificate. Members may also receive a Segal AmeriCorps Education Award to help pay for college, vocational training, or student loans. Additional member benefits include a living allowance, access to health coverage and childcare assistance, monthly in-person professional development training, weekly virtual learning, mentoring, a dedicated Service Success Coach, networking opportunities, and access to an online platform to earn a registered apprenticeship. Members join a national AmeriCorps alumni network of over one million members. For Host Site Partner organizations, DSCI provides a supplemental cost-reimbursement grant to offset member salary and benefits; the amount varies based on organization type, operating budget, and number of Members hosted, up to approximately $20,000 per year per full-time member (covering roughly two-thirds of member wages). Reimbursements are paid quarterly after submission of documentation. The host site's estimated remaining cost is about $7,450 per year (~$180 per week). A DSCI-sponsored payroll provider option is available for organizations that cannot manage a cost-reimbursement structure. Competitive cost-share waivers are available for organizations unable to meet required cost-sharing. DSCI also covers the $6,000 Member completion award and pays for professional development training time and travel at no cost to the partner.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Next Application Deadline: May 1; Round 1 Deadline: April 1; cost-share waiver priority consideration deadline June 1, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 18 and older who want to serve full-time in their community, gain work experience, and build professional skills. Service Year Option is for ages 18–24 with a high school diploma, GED, or Certificate of Completion; Maryland Corps is open to all eligible adults 18+ with no education requirement (including individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities). Also open to Maryland-based organizations — including nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, schools, and higher education institutions — that want to serve as Host Site Partners hosting service year Members across Maryland to contribute to workforce development and community impact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For Members: living wage earnings (at least $15/hour) and a living allowance during the service year, plus a taxable $6,000 completion award upon finishing the program (usable for any purpose, including paying down debt, investing in education, or saving for the future), and a Segal AmeriCorps Education Award for use toward college, vocational training, or student loans. Members serve in industries including climate/clean energy, education, community health, public service, apprenticeships and trades, information technology, and public safety. For Partner organizations: supplemental grant funds offset Member salary and benefits costs; DSCI covers the $6,000 Member completion award and pays for professional development training time and travel. Member wages (at least $15/hour), payroll taxes, and benefits for full-time service year members, including health insurance access for members who need it (either through the organization's plan or by supporting enrollment through the Maryland Health Exchange with at least 50% premium reimbursement).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland — spanning all 24 jurisdictions from Western Maryland to the Eastern Shore. Members must reside in Maryland. Host site organizations must be based in Maryland and provide a physical location for Members to serve. Host sites in jurisdictions with minimum wages above $15/hour will have proportionally higher costs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Members: 1. Submit an application on DSCI's Application and Matching Portal (BuildWithin) at dsci.maryland.gov/apply-now/mcyso or app.buildwithin.io. Reasonable accommodations are available upon request. 2. DSCI reviews applications continuously and may follow up with questions via email. 3. Upon conditional acceptance, use the portal to explore positions, interview with Host Site Partner organizations, and accept an offer. 4. Attend Pre-Service Orientation before starting service in August/September. 5. Complete a minimum 9-month service term at your Host Site. 6. Graduate in June and receive the $6,000 completion award. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with periodic deadlines; the recurring application deadline is May 1, with a Round 1 deadline of April 1. Organizations needing a cost-share waiver submit a separate application by June 1, 2026 for priority consideration. For Host Site Partners: Submit a Host Site Partner application through DSCI's Application and Matching Portal (BuildWithin), including position descriptions for roles you want Members to fill. Attend a required webinar after submission. DSCI reviews applications on a rolling basis and may request clarification. Once accepted, use the portal to review candidates, conduct interviews, and extend offers. All HSPs and Members attend a required orientation before service begins in August/September. You may also email applytoserve@maryland.gov to schedule a virtual or in-person program overview. Additional AmeriCorps Maryland positions can be explored at dsci.maryland.gov/americorps-md.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bowie State MARC Joint Development Project
structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT seeks a qualified joint development partner to master plan and redevelop approximately 4.63 acres of underutilized state-owned land at the Bowie State MARC Station for transit-oriented development. The selected partner will lead master planning efforts and advance a Phase 1 development on an identified underutilized parking lot focused on affordable or mixed-income housing. MDOT has budgeted $1.5 million to support master planning and associated public infrastructure, including an extended MARC platform, a new pedestrian bridge to Bowie State University, and improved bike and pedestrian circulation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Employers provide cash payments to employees who surrender their dedicated paid parking space and instead commute by carpool, vanpool, bike, walking, or transit. structured_extraction.program_audience: Any employer, particularly those that lease parking, whose employees commute by carpool, vanpool, bike, walking, or transit and do not use a dedicated paid parking space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit for employers who provide cash payments to employees who give up their paid parking spaces; employers save on parking costs and employees receive a cash benefit in lieu of a parking space.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Any Maryland employer may claim the tax credit.

Program works best for employers that lease parking spaces
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers offer the cash payment benefit to eligible employees and then claim the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit. See the linked tax credit page for details on claiming the credit. For more information, contact Commuter Choice Maryland at CommuterChoiceMaryland.com or by phone Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program recognizes Maryland employers who offer transportation benefits and commuting incentives to their employees. Participating employers receive free support to build or expand their commuter benefits programs, including surveys, data, and materials. The program promotes partner employers through webinars, newsletters, and social media, and provides access to tax benefits related to commuter perks. The program aims to reduce traffic congestion, conserve energy, and improve quality of life for Maryland workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive free commuter program support including surveys, data, and materials to improve commuter benefits programs. Benefits include recognition and exposure through webinars, newsletters, and social media, and access to tax benefits related to commuter perks. No monetary grant amount is specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers who offer or wish to offer transportation benefits and commuting incentives to their employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building or expanding employee commuter benefits programs; offering transportation incentives to attract and retain employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employers located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must offer or be willing to offer transportation benefits and commuting incentives to employees.
Must be a Maryland employer offering or planning to offer transportation benefits.
Sign up by contacting the Commuter Choice Maryland Team or completing the online application.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Commuter Choice Maryland Team by email or complete the online program application at the SurveyMonkey link provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Maryland – MD 295 Corridor Pilot
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program run by Commuter Choice Maryland (an MDOT program) to improve commuting along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95, spanning from the Inner Harbor in Baltimore City to BWI Airport in Anne Arundel County. The program launched in January 2026 in response to reduced travel reliability following the Key Bridge collapse. It works directly with employers through free one-on-one consulting, workshops (Corridor Conversations), and custom resources to help them establish or improve commuter benefit programs, boost workforce recruitment, retention, and reliability, save money on taxes (up to $1,200 per employee per year via the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, plus federal payroll tax savings), reduce parking costs, and earn recognition through the Employer Partner Program. The pilot also conducts targeted outreach to individual commuters along the corridor to inform and encourage them to try alternative commuting modes. The program aims to increase employer participation in commuter benefits, encourage commuters to try modes other than driving alone, and share lessons learned with other employers and corridors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one consulting from the Commuter Choice Maryland team, including evaluation of current commuter benefit offerings and recommendations for improvement, free commuter survey development, custom resources and materials, and monthly Corridor Conversations workshops. Employers can save up to $1,200 per employee per year through the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, save on federal payroll taxes, and reduce parking costs. Participating employers earn recognition through Commuter Choice Maryland's Employer Partner Program. Targeted outreach is also provided to individual commuters along the MD 295 corridor to promote alternative commuting options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers (office managers, HR representatives, benefits administrators) located along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95 (Inner Harbor in Baltimore City to BWI Airport in Anne Arundel County), as well as individual commuters who live or work along that corridor.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing or improving employer commuter benefit programs; providing technical assistance and educational resources to help employers implement commuter benefits; encouraging employees and commuters to try alternative commuting modes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95, spanning from the Inner Harbor in Baltimore City to the BWI Airport area in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Employer must be located near MD 295 between West Nursery Road and I-95
Employer or individual must commute along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95
Employers must complete a commitment process including meeting with MDOT and earning the Employer Partner Badge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers and individuals can visit the program website to learn more. Employers can fill out the interest form on the program page or email the Commuter Choice Maryland team at [email protected] or call (410) 865-1100, Monday–Friday 8:30 am–5:30 pm EST. Employers then go through a five-step commitment process to become an Employer Partner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides registered commuters who regularly carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work with a free ride home in case of unexpected personal emergencies or unscheduled overtime, up to 6 times per year. The ride home can be by taxi, rental car, bus, or train. Registration is free. The program is available statewide in Maryland, with Frederick County offering its own local administration of the program through Frederick County Transit Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to six free emergency rides home per year for registered commuters who regularly use sustainable travel to get to work. Rides can be by taxi, rental car, bus, or train, covering unexpected personal emergencies or unscheduled overtime. Registration is free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters who regularly carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work and need a backup plan for unexpected personal emergencies or unscheduled overtime.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free rides home by taxi, rental car, bus, or train in case of unexpected personal emergencies or unscheduled overtime.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commuters throughout Maryland. Frederick County residents may also register through the Frederick County Transit Services portal.
requirements_list: Must be a registered commuter
Must regularly use a sustainable commuting method (carpooling, vanpooling, biking, walking, or transit)
Eligible for up to 6 rides per year
Rides must be for unexpected personal emergencies or unscheduled overtime
Participation guidelines apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account and register at the Commuter Connections website (commuterconnections.org) or sign up online through the GRH registration form available through Frederick County. Registration is free, fast, and easy.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Joint Development Program leverages state-owned land near transit stations to foster Transit-Oriented Development (TOD). The program seeks private development partners to build mixed-use communities that include housing (including affordable housing), jobs, retail, public amenities, and entertainment near transit stations. MDOT partners with qualified developers through a formal solicitation or unsolicited proposal process guided by its Joint Development Policy.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOT offers state-owned land near transit stations to qualified private development partners for joint development projects. Partners work with MDOT to build mixed-use, transit-oriented communities. MDOT's Office of Real Estate and Economic Development (ORED) manages the solicitation of partners, development agreements, and engagement with state and local stakeholders. Both competitive solicitation and unsolicited proposals are accepted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers and qualified partners interested in developing mixed-use, transit-oriented communities on MDOT-owned land near transit stations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of mixed-use communities near transit stations, including housing (including affordable housing), jobs, retail, public amenities, and entertainment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, at MDOT-owned sites near transit stations including Reisterstown Plaza Metro Station, Odenton MARC Station, Bowie State MARC Station, and Rogers Avenue Metro Station.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified development partner
Must be interested in developing mixed-use, transit-oriented communities on MDOT-owned land
Must align with MDOT's Joint Development Policy goals and objectives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested partners can contact MDOT's Office of Real Estate and Economic Development (ORED) to explore potential opportunities. MDOT solicits qualified development partners through competitive solicitation or accepts unsolicited proposals per its Joint Development Policy.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program provides grant funding for bicycle network development projects across Maryland. It supports projects that maximize bicycle access and improve last-mile connections to work, school, shopping, and transit. The program prioritizes projects that improve safety and access for disadvantaged communities, and seeks to leverage past investments in bicycle facilities while complementing existing state, local, and federal transportation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded on an annual cycle for three project types: (1) Design — up to $400,000 for design plans and feasibility assessments up to 65% design (2-year completion window); (2) Minor Retrofit — up to $200,000 for low-cost treatments such as bicycle route signing, pavement markings, bike parking, automated counters, and drainage grate replacement (2-year completion window); (3) Construction — up to $500,000 for construction of shared-use paths, bicycle and pedestrian bridges, protected bike lanes, and other major bicycle infrastructure at 65% design or greater (3-year completion window; 5 years if TAP match). Grants are reimbursable. Grantees must provide a minimum 20% match of total project cost in cash, in-kind, or third-party contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 applications open in April and run through May 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local governments, state agencies, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), transit entities, non-profit organizations, and federal public lands agencies seeking funding for bicycle infrastructure and network development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bicycle network development including: design plans and feasibility assessments (up to 65% design); minor retrofit treatments such as route signing, pavement markings, bike parking, automated counters, and drainage grate replacement; construction of shared-use paths, bicycle and pedestrian bridges, protected bike lanes, cycle tracks, and other major bicycle infrastructure; feasibility studies; preliminary (30%), semi-final (65%), and final design phases; state of good repair projects on existing routes; Complete Streets intersection treatments. Eligible expenses also include signs, pavement markings, trail/pathway construction, replacement of non-bicycle-friendly drainage grates, limited roadway repaving/patching for dedicated bicycle use (case-by-case approval required), capital equipment such as bike counters, racks, and repair stations (up to 10% of project costs unless authorized), contractual/consultant services, travel to project-relevant meetings, and educational/marketing materials (case-by-case, up to 10% or $10,000 per project). NOT eligible: salaries, land acquisition, general roadway/sidewalk work, training, paid media.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland and meet at least two of six eligibility criteria: within 3 miles of a rail transit station or major bus transit hub; identified as a county transportation priority in a county's most recent annual priority letter to MDOT; within or enhancing access to a Maryland Sustainable Community or Bicycle and Pedestrian Priority Area (BPPA); enhancing bicycle circulation within or access to a Maryland Main Street or major institution with more than 1,000 people on campus daily; improving access for disadvantaged/low-income communities as defined by the Climate Solutions Now Act's 2022 definitions; or providing a significant safety intervention in a Vulnerable Roadway User Area of Need or reducing Level of Traffic Stress by 3 or more levels.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local government, state agency, MPO, transit entity, non-profit, or federal public lands agency
Project must meet at least two of the six eligibility criteria
Access to Transit: within three miles of a rail transit station or major bus transit hub
County Priority: identified as a transportation priority in a county's most recent annual priority letter to MDOT
Sustainable Community or BPPA: enhances bicycle circulation within or access to a Maryland Sustainable Community area or Bicycle and Pedestrian Priority Area
Main Streets or Major Institution: enhances bicycle circulation within or access to a Maryland Main Street or institution with more than 1,000 people on campus daily
Access to Low Income Area: enhances bicycle circulation for disadvantaged communities as defined by the Climate Solutions Now Act's 2022 definitions
Safety Intervention: provides a significant safety intervention in a Vulnerable Roadway User Area of Need or reduces Level of Traffic Stress by 3 or more levels
Grantees must provide a minimum 20% match of total project cost in cash, in-kind, or third-party contributions
Construction projects must be at least 65% design at time of application
Design grants only cover up to 65% design; projects receiving final design funding may not pursue federal or future Bikeways funding for construction
Bikeways projects on State ROW must submit a Complete Streets objective statement (required as of FY27); projects on local ROW may optionally include one
