Goals should target vulnerable road users (people walking, biking, rolling, using transit)
Project Workplan required within 6 months of award or grant terminates
Grant Agreement execution required within 12 months of award or grant terminates
Quarterly progress reports mandatory
Final Report and all design/documentation deliverables required before final reimbursement
Provide electronic copies of project deliverables, final/design documents, and photographs of implemented improvements
Provide ArcGIS files for planned, designed, and installed bikeways (or contact MDOT if infeasible)
Maintenance responsibility identified prior to agreement execution
Applicant or identified entity must commit to own, manage, and maintain facilities
Facilities maintained for minimum 5 years (or grantee refunds award)
Records retained for 3 years post-final claim submission
Design and Minor Retrofit projects must be completed within two years of notification of grant award
Construction projects must be completed within three years of notification of grant award (five years if TAP match)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants are encouraged to submit a letter of intent by email to MDBikeways@mdot.maryland.gov before the application period opens. The letter of intent should include the project title, description, physical limits, estimated cost, anticipated funding request amount, and contact information. Letters of intent are accepted December through April. Full applications are accepted April through May (deadline mid-May for most cycles; FY27 deadline May 31). Applicants develop a Complete Streets objective statement using the MDOT template and submit it with the application (required for State ROW projects starting FY27; optional for local ROW projects). Awards are announced in September. Upon award, grantees submit a quarterly progress report within 30 days of award notification and every three months thereafter, submit a work plan within 6 months, and execute a Grant Agreement within 12 months. Final reimbursement is contingent on MDOT acceptance of a Final Report including all deliverables, photographs, and ArcGIS files.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Climate Focused Funding Portal identifies and funds transportation projects with climate benefits in Maryland. The transportation sector is Maryland's largest source of greenhouse gas emissions. The portal helps identify and implement projects that reduce emissions or improve resilience to climate impacts such as flooding, extreme heat, and storm damage. This is the second round of the portal, following a successful first round in 2024. Eligible applicants include Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), local governments, WMATA, and MDOT Modal Administrations. Funding is provided as federal pass-through grants (Carbon Reduction Program) for capital projects, with a 20% minimum cash match required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal pass-through grant funding (Carbon Reduction Program) for surface transportation emissions reduction and climate resilience projects. A 20% minimum cash match is required (cash only, not in-kind). Specific award amounts are not stated. Technical assistance is also provided through weekly virtual office hours during the solicitation window.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), local governments in Maryland, WMATA, and MDOT Modal Administrations (SHA, MPA, MTA, MAA, MVA). Organizations and entities with transportation projects that provide climate benefits in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects only (no operating expenses). Eligible uses include: fleet electrification and zero-emission vehicles, EV charging infrastructure (acquisition, installation, operation), Transportation Systems Management and Operations (TSMO), Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), congestion mitigation (excluding highway widening/expansion), VMT reduction, mode-shift, public transit, bicycle/pedestrian facilities, diesel retrofits, traffic management, pedestrian/bike trails, port emissions reduction, street lighting efficiency, congestion pricing, freight emissions reduction, CAV technologies, rail/freight modal shift, and sustainable pavements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Projects must be located within one of Maryland's MPO regions. Projects qualifying for resilience components must also be within CS-CRAB data layer boundaries (Riverine and/or Coastal layers).
requirements_list: Project must have climate benefits
Project must be transportation-related
Capital projects only — no operating expenses
20% minimum non-federal cash match required (cash only, not in-kind; 80/20 federal/non-federal split)
Project must be located within an MPO region in Maryland
Resilience projects must be within CS-CRAB data layer boundaries
Project must support state/local carbon reduction goals and plans
Federal procurement and regulations compliance expected
NEPA/environmental permitting required
Project manager federal-aid experience assessed (non-disqualifying)
STIP/TIP listing preferred
Highway widening/expansion is ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov/forms/mdot-climate-focused-funding-application-65eb238b6cb6f201814c2d24). Register on OneStop Portal, complete the Climate Focused Funding application form, sign and submit (drafts auto-saved). Required uploads include project cost estimate (PDF/Excel/Word). Weekly virtual office hours were available Wednesdays from 3:00–4:00 pm during the solicitation window (January 15 – March 26, 2025). Contact Allison Breitenother (abreitenother@mdot.maryland.gov) for application support and Deron Lovaas (dlovaas@mdot.maryland.gov) for program/emissions questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MDOT Fellows Internship Program introduces promising Maryland college undergraduates to working within Maryland's integrated transportation system. During the summer, interns are placed in senior-level assignments at one of MDOT's agencies. The program is offered by The Shriver Center at UMBC in partnership with the Office of the Secretary of Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer internship placements in senior-level assignments within MDOT agencies. Program is offered in partnership with The Shriver Center at UMBC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate college students in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on work experience within Maryland's transportation system during the summer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland college students statewide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MDOT Fellows Program page at The Shriver Center (UMBC) for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MDOT Freight Rail Grant Program (FRGP) is a state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Office of Rail and Intermodal Freight (RIF) of the Secretary's Office at the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT). The program offers grant assistance to local governments, railroads, businesses, and other key agencies to help preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, and foster sustainability and innovative technologies. It is designed to make targeted investments that allow MDOT to better leverage existing infrastructure, assets, and funding programs to support a safe, secure, and resilient multimodal freight network. Grants are awarded on a competitive basis and are reimbursable, meaning recipients pay costs upfront and are reimbursed by the state. Program focus areas include Expansion of Rail Service, Safety & Security, System Preservation & Modernization, Environmental Protection, and Fiscal Responsibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable state grants awarded on a competitive basis to support freight rail projects. Recipients pay for project costs upfront and are reimbursed by the state. Two eligible project types: Design (2-year completion window) and Construction (3-year completion window). A minimum 20% local cash match of overall project cost is required; projects matching more than 20% receive preferred consideration. The current solicitation is anticipated to be open April 1 – June 30, 2026, and annually based on available funding. Applications are submitted via the Maryland OneStop Portal (https://onestop.md.gov/). There is no application fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2026 (anticipated; open April 1 – June 30 annually based on available funding)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, counties, municipalities, state agencies, metropolitan planning organizations, railroad operators/owners, railroad-served businesses, local jurisdictions, commercial interests, and non-profit organizations involved in freight rail
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preserving railroad corridors, supporting economic development, fostering sustainability and innovative technologies, and improving multimodal freight infrastructure. Design projects: feasibility assessments, design plans, economic/environmental impact analysis, right-of-way assessment, cost estimation. Construction projects: sidings/sidetracks, grade crossing improvements, bridges/structures, drainage improvements, system modernization, safety improvements, and environmental protection measures. Eligible project components include pedestrian/bicycle trail facilities, innovative technologies, and other rail corridor improvements. Excludes routine maintenance unless involving innovative technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must align with the Maryland Transportation Plan, Maryland State Freight Plan, and the Maryland State Rail Plan.

The grant is reimbursable, so applicants must be able to cover initial project costs.
Applicants must demonstrate project readiness.

Projects matching more than 20% receive preferred consideration.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Maryland OneStop Portal (https://onestop.md.gov/). Complete the project readiness checklist corresponding to the project phase (design or construction) and submit required documentation including cost estimate, Project Readiness Form, permits, maps, and scope of work. Application resources including the application questions form, resources and guidance document, project readiness checklist, and FAQs are available on the program page. Contact FreightRail@mdot.maryland.gov to discuss project ideas or ask questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Renewable Energy Master Contract (Solar Energy Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Renewable Energy Master Contract establishes a framework that allows MDOT to install solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on MDOT-owned properties across Maryland, and also enables Maryland counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, other government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations to purchase solar PV installation services from MDOT's pre-selected Master Contractors. Six pre-qualified contractors (Abundant Solar Power, Ameresco, Forefront Power, KDC Solar, Siemens Industry, Standard Solar) compete to install, own, operate, and maintain PV systems under 20-25 year Task Orders. The purchasing organization pays no upfront capital costs and buys the generated solar power at a fixed rate equal to or less than current utility prices, achieving cost avoidance. Organizations may also benefit from Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs). Purchases by non-State entities constitute a separate Master Services Agreement between the contractor and that entity and are not binding on the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible organizations procure solar PV installation, operation, and maintenance services through MDOT's Master Services Agreement with six pre-selected contractors (Abundant Solar Power, Ameresco, Forefront Power, KDC Solar, Siemens Industry, Standard Solar). The contractor constructs, owns, operates, and maintains the PV system for 20-25 years. The purchasing organization pays no upfront capital costs and buys the generated solar power at a fixed rate equal to or less than current utility prices, achieving cost avoidance. Eligible organizations may also benefit from Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs). Purchases by non-State entities constitute a separate Master Services Agreement between the contractor and that entity and are not binding on the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state transportation facilities, Maryland counties and municipalities, state instrumentalities, other non-state government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in Maryland seeking to install solar PV systems on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation, operation, and maintenance of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on eligible organization properties. Organizations purchase the generated solar energy at a fixed rate equal to or less than current utility prices, with no upfront capital expenditure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Open to MDOT properties and, via the Master Services Agreement, to Maryland counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, other government agencies, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits within Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county, municipality, state instrumentality, non-state government or government agency, or a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization located in Maryland.
Site must have a minimum of one acre for a solar installation (approximately 250 kW capacity); four or more acres preferred.
Sites with significant tree coverage are less likely to be considered.
Purchases by non-State entities constitute a separate Master Services Agreement between the contractor and that entity and are not binding on the State of Maryland.
Organizations enter into a Master Services Agreement directly with the selected contractor.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDOT Program Manager Eddie Lukemire to request contract documents. Eligible organizations work with MDOT's pre-selected Master Contractors. Solar projects are awarded via Task Order Requests issued to the six pre-qualified Master Contractors through secondary competition, with award going to the contractor offering the most advantageous terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Urban Tree Program (Transportation Reforestation Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: A stewardship community tree planting grant program established by Maryland statute (Transportation §2–103.8) from the 2021 legislative session that helps plant trees in communities that have lost trees due to transportation construction projects. Developed in partnership with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (Maryland Forest Service) and the Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee (MUCFC), the program supports the Maryland Five Million Trees initiative. Eligible areas include communities impacted by Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. Replanting may occur on both public and private property, subject to project approval. Grants of up to $5,000 are available, with additional funds for pocket forest projects. Applications are reviewed twice a year: February 15 for spring planting and July 15 for fall planting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards up to $5,000 for tree planting projects, with additional funds available for pocket forest projects. Funds may also be used for project maintenance costs such as watering, weeding, and mulching (1 year for tree planting; 3 years for pocket forests); up to 5% of the grant may be used for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Replanting may occur on public or private property, subject to project approval. Applications are reviewed twice a year: February 15 for spring planting and July 15 for fall planting.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — reviewed February 15 (spring planting) and July 15 (fall planting) each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, organizations, schools, community/neighborhood associations, homeowners associations, civic groups, businesses, individuals, non-profits, higher education institutions, counties, municipalities, and forest conservancy district boards that want to plant trees in areas that have lost tree canopy due to transportation construction projects, including those impacted by the Purple Line corridor, urban heat islands, or environmental justice areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting projects, including pocket forest projects, in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure construction. Funds may also cover site preparation, soil amendment, mulch, project maintenance costs (watering, weeding, mulching — 1 year for tree planting; 3 years for pocket forests), and up to 5% for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Replanting may occur on public or private property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; priority for communities impacted by the Purple Line construction corridor, urban heat islands, and environmental justice areas. Projects must be in communities where a state transportation project (highways, transit, bridges, airports, seaports, etc.) removed trees.
requirements_list: Projects must involve planting trees in communities that have lost trees due to transportation construction projects.
Project area must have lost tree canopy due to transportation infrastructure projects (highways, transit, bridges, airports, seaports, etc.).
Eligible areas include communities impacted by the Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns.
Replanting may occur on public or private property subject to project approval (landowner approval required for private property).
Must get approval from the county Forestry Board before the application deadline.
Planted tree species must be native to the area.
Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive preference.
Funding cannot be used for required mitigation planting.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, get your project approved by your county Forestry Board. Then, submit an application through the Maryland OneStop system (onestop.md.gov) before the applicable deadline. Applications are open year-round and reviewed twice a year: February 15 for spring planting season and July 15 for fall planting season. Your application must include a site plan, a photo of the site, a list of proposed native plants, any required permit information, and a maintenance plan. A grant application is also available as a PDF at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/MDOTUrbanTreeprogramGrantApplication.pdf. For additional information, contact Dan Coy at daniel.coy@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Department of Transportation – Morgan State University Graduate School Internship Program (MDOT-MSU GSIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and Morgan State University's National Transportation Center, this program provides paid internship opportunities to graduate students pursuing careers in transportation. The goal is to increase and retain professionals entering the transportation field.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-year paid internship providing substantive work experience, mentorship, and professional networking opportunities within the transportation industry.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Graduate students enrolled at Morgan State University pursuing degrees in Engineering, Transportation, Landscape Architecture, Finance, Information Technology, or City and Regional Planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensated work experience complementing academic background and career aspirations in transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled in a Morgan State University graduate program.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a Morgan State University Graduate Studies Program pursuing a Masters in Engineering, Masters of Science in Transportation, Landscape Architecture, Finance, Information Technology, or City and Regional Planning
Must have successfully completed one semester of graduate level courses
Must be registered for a minimum of nine (9) credit hours per semester (except during the summer)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Morgan State University's National Transportation Center or MDOT's Office of Human Resources for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's process for evaluating and ranking surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects requesting state funding in the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP). The program uses data-driven, performance-based scoring — combining applicant-provided data, modeling/forecasting, and GIS analysis — to produce a ranked list of submitted projects. Projects are scored across 11 measures in 6 goal areas and ranked by a Score-Cost Ratio. A no-funding pilot round was conducted in 2025 (application window January 15 – February 18, 2025); the full program was introduced in the 2026 legislative session to replace the Chapter 30 scoring process. Project evaluation is conducted every other year, in Year 1 of a biennial implementation and evaluation cycle. The next full funding round is anticipated in mid-January to mid-February 2027, contingent on resource availability. Eligible project types include highway capacity, transit capacity, bike/pedestrian capacity, intercity passenger/commuter rail capacity, and intelligent transportation systems. State funding requests must be at least $5 million and less than $400 million. Submitted applications (excluding personal data) are made public on the MDOT website.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Biennial scoring and prioritization process for surface transportation capacity projects. Projects are scored across 11 measures in 6 goal areas and ranked by a Score-Cost Ratio for potential inclusion in the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP). The 2025 pilot round had no funding attached (application window January 15 – February 18, 2025). The full program targets projects where the state funding request (including federal funds controlled by MDOT) is at least $5 million and less than $400 million. Eligible project types include highway capacity, transit capacity, bike/pedestrian capacity, intercity passenger/commuter rail capacity, and intelligent transportation systems. Submitted applications (excluding personal data) are made public on the MDOT website.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 18, 2025 (2025 pilot round, closed); next round anticipated mid-January to mid-February 2027 contingent on resource availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal governments, state government agencies, independent cities, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), and Locally Operated Transit Systems (LOTS) seeking state funding for surface transportation capacity projects in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects on or benefiting the state transportation system, including highway, transit, bike/pedestrian, intercity rail, and intelligent transportation systems projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on or operate on the Maryland state transportation system, or provide benefits to the state system.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county government, municipal government, state government agency, independent city, MPO, or LOTS
Project must be a surface transportation capacity-enhancing project
State funding request (including federal funds controlled by MDOT) must be at least $5 million and less than $400 million
Project must be located on or operate on the state system, or provide benefits to the state system
Project must have progressed far enough in design to provide information necessary for scoring
Completed feasibility study or equivalent document required
Concept plan required
Signed resolution or letter of support from the applicant's elected or governing body required
Applicant attestation of authority and accuracy required
Applications must be submitted via the Maryland OneStop portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the Maryland OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov). Applicants provide project information; MDOT validates eligibility and conducts modeling/GIS analysis. Projects are scored across 11 measures in 6 goal areas and ranked by Score-Cost Ratio. Local entities submit endorsement letters to MDOT Prioritization Team. Priority letters may be submitted via a standalone form in the OneStop portal in May of the active cycle year. Draft CTP is published September 15–November 15 with CTP Tour meetings held in all 23 counties and Baltimore City. For the 2025 pilot, applications submitted by January 31, 2025 received a preliminary screening with feedback before the final February 18, 2025 deadline. Applicants are encouraged to coordinate with MDOT during the application process to ensure eligibility requirements are met.

structured_extraction.program_description: Launched by MDOT in 2024, the Safe Routes to School (SRTS) Coordinator Pilot Program allocates Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) funds to local jurisdictions to cover 80% of the salary of a dedicated SRTS coordinator. Coordinators lead local SRTS strategies, work directly with schools, manage programming, and prioritize infrastructure improvements around schools. The program is developed in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). Schools, non-profits, and local governments may also apply for TAP funding for SRTS infrastructure or non-infrastructure projects through a competitive award process administered by the State Highway Administration (SHA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TAP funds cover 80% of the salary for a local SRTS coordinator. Local jurisdictions must provide the remaining 20%. As of 2026, four counties have joined the pilot. Schools, non-profits, and local governments may also apply for TAP funding for SRTS infrastructure or non-infrastructure projects through a competitive award process. The TAP SRTS application window is announced by MDOT yearly and usually occurs in the Spring. Required application items include a complete scope of work, detailed cost estimate, project map (within approximately 2 miles of a school), and project schedule.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring annually (TAP SRTS); January to February annually (MHSO Safety Grants)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local county jurisdictions, school systems, non-profits, and local governments in Maryland seeking to hire a dedicated Safe Routes to School coordinator or fund SRTS infrastructure and non-infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary for a local SRTS coordinator who leads SRTS strategies, works with schools, manages programming, and prioritizes infrastructure improvements. Also supports feasibility studies, design projects, walking audits, walking school buses, bike trains, community engagement, and evaluations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; open to local jurisdictions across the state. Project sites must be within approximately 2 miles of a school.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (county), school, or non-profit
Jurisdiction must provide 20% salary match for coordinator position
Coordinator must lead SRTS strategies and work directly with schools
TAP project must be within approximately 2 miles of a school
TAP application requires complete scope of work, detailed cost estimate, project map, and project schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The TAP SRTS application window is announced by MDOT yearly and usually occurs in the Spring. Schools, non-profits, and local governments may apply for TAP funding through a competitive award process administered by the State Highway Administration (SHA). Contact MDOT's Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility at completestreets@mdot.maryland.gov for details. Reach out to Meg Young, Deputy Director.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Designation Program provides official state recognition to local jurisdictions that have developed intentional plans to advance transit-oriented development at eligible sites near transit stations or corridors. Designation unlocks access to state support including MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, additional scoring points for Low Income Housing Tax Credit applications, and priority consideration in state office and lab space procurement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State designation status that unlocks eligibility for MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, additional competitive scoring points for Maryland DHCD's Low Income Housing Tax Credit program, priority consideration when state agencies evaluate proposals for office or lab space, and priority advocacy from MDOT and partner agencies supporting development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and multicounty planning agencies seeking state recognition of transit-oriented development plans at sites near transit stations or corridors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State designation that enables access to capital grants, revolving loans, housing tax credits, and other state benefits to support transit-oriented development planning and construction near transit stations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local jurisdictions with sites adjacent to or within one-half mile of a planned or existing transit station, or adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or multicounty agency with land use and planning responsibility for the site
Site must be adjacent to or within one-half mile of a planned or existing transit station, or adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor
Local legislative body must adopt a resolution supporting the TOD designation

Applicant must develop a deliberate TOD plan addressing eight categories: Land Use, Bike/Pedestrian/Complete Streets, Housing, Action Plan, Parking, Transportation Network, Cohesion with local/regional plans, Green Infrastructure, and Economic Development
Plan must maximize use of transit, walking, and bicycling by residents and employees
Designation is awarded by the Smart Growth Subcabinet (SGSC) based on MDOT's recommendation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdiction develops a deliberate TOD plan and adopts a resolution through its legislative body. Jurisdiction submits an application to MDOT via the online TOD Designation Application Form. MDOT circulates the plan to transit modes and Smart Growth Subcabinet (SGSC) members, coordinates any issues with the applicant, and develops a recommendation to the SGSC. The SGSC deliberates and issues a resolution approving or denying designation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commuter Tax Credit / Commuter Choice Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: Commuter Choice Maryland (also known as the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit) is a set of Maryland state incentive programs administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) that encourage employers and employees to use commute alternatives instead of driving alone to work. Maryland employers — including for-profit businesses, nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4)), sole proprietorships, pass-through entities (partnerships, S-corps, LLCs, and business trusts), and government entities — can claim a state tax credit equal to 50% of eligible commuter benefit costs provided to employees, up to $100 per employee per month (up to $1,200 per employee per year). The credit can be applied against the state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. As of January 1, 2026, federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $340 per month in tax-free commuter benefits as a monthly transit pass or vanpool voucher; employees can pay for transit or vanpool costs through pre-tax salary deductions, reducing their taxable income; or both can share the cost through a combined option. Eligible benefits include transit subsidies, vanpool programs, carpool programs, Guaranteed Ride Home programs, Cash in Lieu of Parking (parking cash-out), active commuting support (e.g., bike maintenance, shared bike/scooter memberships), telework equipment and services (e.g., internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, and job-related software), and other qualifying commuting expenses for worksites in Maryland. The program also offers a mobile app called CommuterCash, where users can log commute trips to earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits (up to $600 per calendar year). Employers who contribute to employees' commuting costs also benefit from federal and state tax deductions and reductions on certain payroll taxes. The credit can be combined with the federal transportation fringe benefit to maximize savings. Employers must re-register annually for the tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can claim a Maryland state tax credit equal to 50% of eligible commuter benefit costs, capped at $100 per employee per month (up to $1,200 per employee per year). The credit can be applied against the state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. Non-profits exempt under IRS §501(c)(3) or (c)(4), sole proprietorships, and pass-through entities (partnerships, S-corps, LLCs, and business trusts) are also eligible. As of January 1, 2026, federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $340 per month in tax-free commuter benefits (monthly transit pass or vanpool voucher). Employees may pay for transit or vanpool costs through pre-tax salary deductions, reducing their taxable income. A combined option allows both employer contribution and employee pre-tax deduction to share the cost. Eligible programs include transit subsidies, vanpool programs (6+ seating, ≥3 employees per trip), carpool programs, Guaranteed Ride Home, Cash in Lieu of Parking (parking cash-out), active commuting support, telework equipment and services (internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, job-related software), and other qualifying commute alternative programs. Employers also receive federal payroll tax exemptions on transit benefit payments. The program includes a CommuterCash mobile app where users log commute trips to earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits (up to $600 per calendar year). A FareShare incentive is available in the Greater Baltimore area. Employers must re-register annually for the tax credit, track eligible expenses, and file required Maryland tax forms each year to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual re-registration is required; no specific calendar deadline stated
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers (for-profit businesses, nonprofits including 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4), sole proprietorships, pass-through entities, and government entities) that provide commute alternative programs or telework subsidies to employees, and Maryland employees who commute by transit or vanpool.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employer-funded commuter benefits including transit subsidies, vanpool programs (6+ seating, ≥3 employees per trip), guaranteed ride home, parking cash-out (Cash in Lieu of Parking), active commuting support (e.g., bike maintenance, shared bike/scooter memberships), telework equipment and services (internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, job-related software), monthly transit passes or vanpool vouchers, and other qualifying commute alternative programs. Also supports cash rewards through the CommuterCash app for commuters who log alternative commute trips (up to $600 per calendar year).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to employers with worksites in Maryland and employees commuting within Maryland. Benefits must relate to travel to or from a location in Maryland, and commutes must occur on weekdays between 5:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. The FareShare incentive and Baltimore Commutes Carpool Program are limited to the Greater Baltimore area (City of Baltimore, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Harford, Howard, and Queen Anne's counties).
requirements_list: Must be a business, 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) organization, sole proprietorship, pass-through entity (partnership, S-corp, LLC, or business trust), or government entity operating in Maryland and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Taxation
Must be a Maryland employee commuting by transit or vanpool (for employee pre-tax benefit)
Benefits must be employer-funded for the tax credit
Benefits must be used for commuting to Maryland worksites during typical weekday commuting hours (5:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.)
Must provide commute alternative programs or telework subsidies to employees

Eligible benefits include transit subsidies, vanpool, carpool, Guaranteed Ride Home, parking cash-out, active commuting support, telework equipment and services (internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, job-related software)
Vanpool vehicles must have 6+ seating capacity with ≥3 employees per trip; ≥80% annual mileage for employment-related commuting
Carpools must have ≥80% of trips shared
Benefits must relate to commuting to or from a location in Maryland
Tax credit is capped at $100 per employee per month ($1,200 per employee per year)
Federal employer-provided tax-free transit benefit capped at $340 per employee per month (as of January 1, 2026)
Employers must re-register annually for the tax credit
Employers must track eligible expenses
Employers must file required Maryland tax forms each year
Employer must participate to provide tax-free benefits to employees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Commuter Tax Credit: re-register for the credit annually through Maryland's OneStop portal, track eligible commuter benefit expenses, and file the required Maryland tax forms each year to claim the credit. Free guided assistance is available at any point in the program development through the Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner program. Visit the Commuter Choice Maryland website at commuterchoicemaryland.com, email commuterchoice@mdot.state.md.us, or call 410-865-1100 (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.) for more information on enrolling and claiming the tax credit. Employers can also join the Employer Partner program at mdot.maryland.gov/employerpartner and visit mdot.maryland.gov to calculate savings. To earn cash rewards via CommuterCash, download the mobile app and log commute trips.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE) certifies small businesses as Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBE), Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (ACDBE), and/or Small Business Enterprises (SBE). Certification allows eligible firms to participate in MDOT contracting programs aimed at increasing opportunities for small and disadvantaged businesses. Applicants can apply for all three certifications simultaneously using a single Uniform Certification Application. Race-and-gender neutral SBE certification is also available. Non-Maryland firms may apply and interstate certification is available under 49 CFR § 26.85.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) Office of Minority Business Enterprise
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification as a DBE, ACDBE, and/or SBE with no application fee. Certification enables eligible firms to participate in MDOT contracting programs. OMBE also offers free monthly workshops to help applicants prepare their application and navigate the certification process, and optional 30-minute application reviews upon request. The OMB-approved Uniform Certification Application (OMB Control No. 2105-0586, expiration 05/31/2027) is used for all three certifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and disadvantaged businesses seeking to participate in MDOT contracting programs as DBE, ACDBE, or SBE certified firms. Applicants must be for-profit firms with at least 51% ownership by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (DBE/ACDBE) or qualifying small business owners (SBE). Race-and-gender neutral SBE certification is also available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to compete for MDOT contracting opportunities set aside or otherwise available to DBE, ACDBE, and SBE firms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Non-Maryland firms may also apply and must provide home state DBE/SBE or any additional certifications. Interstate certification is available under 49 CFR § 26.85.

Submit all documents in PDF format with no redactions

No cost to apply

PNW includes cash, stocks/bonds, rental/commercial property, personal property, less liabilities

Entity-specific documentation required for sole proprietorships, LLCs, corporations, and partnerships
NAICS codes required; provide applicable industry classification
Non-Maryland firms must submit home state DBE/SBE certification or additional certifications
Submit supporting documents including personal net worth statements, tax returns, proof of ownership, licenses, bank records, and corporate/partnership agreements
Sign Declaration of Eligibility under penalty of perjury confirming 51% ownership and disadvantaged status
Complete all PNW worksheets with supporting documentation for each entry per USDOT Final Rule (April 9, 2024)
Firm must currently be conducting business operations
Firm must meet SBA and DBE/ACDBE program size standards (see https://www.transportation.gov/DBEsizestandards)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at marylandmdbe.mdbecert.com or download and print the Uniform Certification Application. Complete all sections, fill out the Personal Net Worth (PNW) form per the April 9, 2024 USDOT Final Rule, and gather required documents per the Document Checklist. Submit the complete application package online. OMBE will evaluate the application for eligibility across all applicable programs simultaneously. The process takes several months once a complete package is received. Free monthly workshops and optional 30-minute application reviews are available to assist applicants. For current PNW cap information, visit https://www.transportation.gov/DBEPNW.

structured_extraction.program_name: Section 5310-Enhanced Mobility for Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to organizations that offer transportation services to seniors and people with disabilities. It helps fund services where current options are not available or are not enough to meet their needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant covers 80% of the cost for capital projects, like buying vehicles, and 50% of the cost for operating projects. Applicants must provide a local cash match for the remaining 20% for capital and 50% for operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations that provide transportation services to seniors and individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can pay for capital and operating expenses. Capital expenses can include buses, vans, communication equipment, wheelchair lifts, vehicle maintenance, and computer hardware or software. Operating expenses can include costs for accessible taxi services, ride-sharing, vanpooling, voucher programs, and volunteer driver programs.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a cash match of 20% for capital projects and 50% for operating projects.
Services cannot compete with existing public transit or private for-profit providers.
Applicants must follow federal rules, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants get the application package from the Transportation Association of Maryland (TAM) website. You must submit the completed application electronically through the MDOT MTA Grant Application Portal. The agency will not accept applications by mail or delivery.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides federal funds to states to help develop and maintain recreational trails. The trails can be on land or water. They are for both motorized and non-motorized use.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration (MDOT SHA)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a reimbursable grant. It matches federal funds with local money or in-kind contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for county governments, municipal governments, and non-profit agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: Maintaining and restoring existing trails. Developing trailside facilities. Leasing trail construction equipment. Building new trails. Acquiring property or easements for trails. Assessing trail conditions for accessibility and maintenance. Creating educational materials about trail safety and environmental protection.
requirements_list: Requires matching funds or in-kind contributions

structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Business Enterprise (SBE) Certification is a race and gender neutral program administered by MDOT's Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE). Certified SBE firms are listed in the MDOT online directory and may participate in USDOT-assisted contracts. Firms that are already MDOT DBE certified are automatically certified as SBE; all other eligible firms must apply. Certification is free and must be renewed annually via an affidavit confirming continued eligibility.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation, Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification that qualifies small businesses to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts administered through MDOT. Certified firms appear in the MDOT online SBE directory. No monetary award is associated with the certification itself; the benefit is access to contracting opportunities. Annual renewal is required via an affidavit to OMBE.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses seeking to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts in Maryland, including firms that meet SBA size standards and ownership requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enabling participation in USDOT-assisted contracting opportunities through MDOT, including eligibility to compete as prime contractors on federally-aided MDOT projects (MDOT SHA, MDOT MTA, MDOT MAA).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to small businesses operating in Maryland seeking to work on USDOT-assisted contracts.
requirements_list: Firm must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards (13 CFR Part 121) applicable to its type of work.
Average annual gross receipts (averaged over previous three fiscal years) must not exceed the USDOT overall size standard of $30.72 million.
Average annual gross receipts must also not exceed the SBA industry-specific size standard per 49 CFR 26.65.
At least 51% of the firm's ownership must be held by individuals whose personal net worth (PNW) does not exceed $2,047,000 as prescribed by 49 CFR 26.67.
Firm must be organized for profit.
The 51% owner must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Application must be submitted with all required supporting documentation in PDF format, unredacted, following the Documentation Checklist.
Certified SBE firms must annually submit an affidavit to OMBE affirming continued eligibility.
Completed SBE Certification Application with NAICS codes and all owner information.
Declaration of Eligibility (wet ink signature) for disadvantage status claims.
U.S. citizenship proof and government photo ID.

Personal Net Worth Statement (wet ink) for owners holding 51% or more; retirement assets excluded from PNW calculations per USDOT Final Rule (April 9, 2024). PNW excludes business ownership interest in applicant firm and primary residence equity; includes cash, stocks/bonds, rental/vacation/commercial properties, and personal property (boats, jewelry, collectibles).
Applicants must complete all PNW worksheets with supporting documentation for each entry.
3 years personal federal tax returns (all owners with 51% or more ownership); wet ink signatures required.
5 years business federal tax returns (or life of business); wet ink signatures required.
5 years tax returns for other businesses owned.
Business registration documents and ownership structure documentation.
If already MDOT certified as a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE), automatic SBE certification applies and no separate application is needed.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at marylandmdbe.mdbecert.com. Submit a complete application package with all required supporting documents (in PDF format) per the Documentation Checklist, including personal and business tax returns, net worth statements, business registration documents, financial statements, and proof of citizenship. MDOT hosts free Application Assistance Workshops to help applicants prepare. Contact OMBE at 410-865-1269 or [email protected] with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free monthly workshop for businesses interested in applying for certification as a Minority Business Enterprise (MBE), Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE), Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (ACDBE), and/or Small Business Enterprise (SBE). The workshop covers eligibility standards, the full application process, the Uniform Certification Application, common application questions, and tips for connecting with state business opportunities and business development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation, Office of Small and Minority Business Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly webinar workshop held on the first Tuesday of every month. Morning sessions run from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM. Additional evening sessions (5:30 PM) are offered in March, June, September, and December. Spanish-language sessions are also offered. Space is limited. Participants can meet with a certification expert after the presentation. A Cursory Review of draft applications can also be scheduled separately (call 410-865-1269).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses seeking MBE, DBE, ACDBE, or SBE certification in Maryland. Applicants must be Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Owners (SEDO) constituting 51% ownership and U.S. citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance in completing a certification application; not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; sessions held at MDOT Headquarters, 7201 Corporate Center Dr., Hanover, MD 21076, and via webinar (GoToWebinar). Program may offer reciprocal recognition for non-Maryland firms.
requirements_list: Complete a registration form for each individual attending
Application should be at least 50% completed before scheduling a Cursory Review
Applicants must be Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Owners (SEDO) constituting 51% ownership
U.S. citizenship required
Business structure types eligible: sole proprietorship, LLC, corporation, partnership (if ownership criteria met)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the desired session using the registration links provided on the page. After registering, a confirmation email with joining instructions is sent. For Cursory Review of a draft application, contact the office at 410-865-1269.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal certification program that allows firms already certified as a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) or Airport Concession DBE (ACDBE) in another state to obtain certification in Maryland through an interstate application process. structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) – Wastewater/ENR and Onsite Disposal Systems (Septic) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF), administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA), encompasses complementary programs to reduce nutrient pollution flowing into the Chesapeake Bay. The Wastewater Program provides dedicated grant funding for capital improvement projects at publicly owned wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) and related infrastructure, including Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) upgrades to achieve effluent quality of 3 mg/L total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/L total phosphorus at major and minor WWTPs. ENR upgrades receive up to 100% state grant funding for eligible planning, design, and construction costs, provided on a reimbursable basis after the grantee submits a payment request. The program also covers combined sewer overflow (CSO) and sanitary sewer overflow (SSO) abatement, sewer rehabilitation, conveyance system and pump station upgrades, sewer extensions connecting homes on septic systems to nutrient-reducing treatment plants, nitrogen reduction at shared community septic systems, stormwater (MS4) projects by local governments with a stormwater or resilience enterprise fund, and flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects. The ENR Refinement Program provides 100% MDE-funded comprehensive engineering evaluations for WWTPs 15+ years post-ENR upgrade, plus prorated design and construction funding through BRF, with a new total nitrogen goal of 2.85 mg/L. The Onsite Disposal Systems (Septic/OSDS) Upgrade Program uses fees collected from septic system users to fund grants and loans for upgrades of existing conventional septic systems to best available technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal — cutting nitrogen output roughly in half — as well as connections to public sewer systems. Grant funding is tiered by income: 100% grant for homeowners with income ≤$300K/year; 50% grant for those above that threshold. Sewer connections are funded up to a maximum of $25,000 per connection. The program is administered statewide by MDE/MWIFA, with the Septic/OSDS Program implemented locally through county health departments including the Prince George's County Department of Health – Environmental Engineering (contact: EnvironEngProgram@co.pg.md.us, 301-883-7681; apply via momentum.princegeorgescountymd.gov). MWIFA accepts applications for the Wastewater/ENR Program from December 1 through January 31 each year; applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Approximately 40% of onsite fund revenues also support cover crop implementation to further reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Wastewater/ENR Program provides up to 100% state grant funding for eligible project costs (planning, design, and construction) at publicly owned wastewater treatment plants, provided on a reimbursable basis after the grantee submits a payment request. Eligible uses include: ENR upgrades to achieve 3 mg/L total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/L total phosphorus; sewerage distribution system upgrades (up to $5M/year through FY 2009); incremental cost of ENR operations and maintenance (up to 10% of annual revenue or approximately $6M/year starting FY 2010); CSO/SSO abatement; sewer rehabilitation; conveyance system and pump station upgrades; sewer extensions; community septic nitrogen reduction; stormwater MS4 projects by local governments with a stormwater or resilience enterprise fund; and flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects. The ENR Refinement Program provides 100% MDE-funded comprehensive engineering evaluations for WWTPs 15+ years post-ENR upgrade, plus prorated design and construction funding through BRF, with a new total nitrogen goal of 2.85 mg/L. The Septic/OSDS Upgrade Program provides grants covering the full cost (100% for homeowners with income ≤$300K/year; 50% for those above) for upgrading existing conventional septic systems to BAT for nitrogen removal (cutting nitrogen output roughly in half) or connecting properties to public sewer systems (up to $25,000 per connection). BAT system pricing ranges $19,055–$31,512 for purchase/install/2yr O&M; annual O&M varies $200–$383/year post-contract. In Prince George's County, residents apply through the county health department via the Momentum system at momentum.princegeorgescountymd.gov.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wastewater/ENR Program: applications accepted December 1 through January 31 annually (currently closed; next window opens December 1, 2026); Septic/OSDS Program is ongoing through local county health departments
structured_extraction.program_audience: Publicly owned wastewater treatment plant operators, local governments, utilities, homeowners, small businesses, non-profit entities, and property owners in Maryland seeking funding for ENR upgrades, sewer improvements, nutrient reduction projects, stormwater management, flood mitigation, or septic system upgrades to best available technology for nitrogen removal or connections to public sewer systems. Priority given to publicly owned WWTPs with design flow of 500,000 gallons per day or greater discharging to the Chesapeake Bay, and to failing and non-conforming septic systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters). In Prince George's County, property owners with existing septic systems or eligible to connect to public sewer may apply through the county health department.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction costs for ENR upgrades at wastewater treatment plants to achieve 3 mg/L total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/L total phosphorus; comprehensive engineering evaluations and design/construction for ENR Refinement Program (WWTPs 15+ years post-upgrade, new TN goal 2.85 mg/L); sewerage distribution system upgrades; incremental cost of ENR operations and maintenance; CSO and SSO abatement; sewer rehabilitation; conveyance system and pump station upgrades; sewer extensions to connect homes on septic to BNR/ENR treatment plants; nitrogen reduction at shared community septic systems; stormwater MS4 projects; flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects; upgrade of existing conventional onsite septic systems to best available technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal including purchase, installation, and 2-year O&M contracts; connections to public sewer systems for nitrogen reduction (up to $25,000 per connection); non-BAT component repair/replacement for low-income failing OSDS; community sewerage system replacement; cover crop implementation to reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay; installation of BAT nitrogen-reducing septic tanks or connection to public sewer in Prince George's County.

For the wastewater program, users served by plants discharging to the Chesapeake Bay and Coastal Bay watersheds pay $5.00/month; users outside those watersheds pay $2.50/month. For the septic program, systems discharging to the Chesapeake Bay and Coastal Bay watersheds pay $60/year; those outside pay $30/year. In Prince George's County, the program is administered locally through the county health department.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Wastewater/ENR Program: MWIFA accepts applications from December 1 through January 31 each year. Applications are currently closed and will reopen December 1, 2026. When open, submit a funding application to MWIFA during the annual application window. Projects are evaluated and ranked by priority; major facilities meeting BRF criteria receive priority funding, while minor and other facilities are evaluated using cost effectiveness guidelines (threshold: $150/lb TN reduced over 20 years). ENR funds are provided on a reimbursable basis; the grantee submits a payment request to receive reimbursement. For the ENR Refinement Program: WWTPs 15+ years post-upgrade should contact MDE to initiate a comprehensive engineering evaluation (100% MDE-funded); MDE makes a preliminary eligibility determination before design funding and a final eligibility determination after design completion. Then apply to WIFA during the regular solicitation for design/construction funding. For the Septic/OSDS Upgrade Program: contact your local county Environmental Health Division or the MDE Wastewater Permits Program Bay Restoration Fund at 410-537-3599. The program is administered by local county health departments as of July 1, 2010. In Prince George's County, submit an application through the Momentum system at momentum.princegeorgescountymd.gov, or contact the Prince George's County Department of Health – Environmental Engineering at EnvironEngProgram@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-7681. Homeowners should contact each BAT vendor to verify current technology pricing and availability. Review the FY2026 BRF Program Guidance and BRF Septic Eligibility Guidelines available on MDE's website for details on eligibility and how to apply. Contact Zoë Goodson (zoe.goodson@maryland.gov), Gerald Gorham, Jr. (gerald.gorham@maryland.gov), or MDE.PFAException@maryland.gov for additional information, or call 410-537-3908 for the Wastewater/ENR Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Best Available Technology (BAT) Grants for Onsite Systems
structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) provides grants to help homeowners upgrade their onsite sewage disposal systems (septic systems) to Best Available Technology (BAT) systems that reduce nitrogen pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay. Approved BAT systems are ranked by the Maryland Department of the Environment based on total nitrogen reduction, total cost, and cost per pound of nitrogen removed. Eligible systems include field-verified systems (e.g., BioMicrobics RetroFast, Norweco Singulair TNT, Fuji Clean CEN 5, AdvanTex, AquaKlear, SeptiTech, Hydro Action, Hoot BNR, Singulair Green) as well as systems currently under field verification. BAT systems are classified as BAT Class I (field verification complete) or BAT Class II (currently under field verification).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available to eligible homeowners to offset the cost of purchasing, installing, and obtaining a 2-year operation/maintenance contract for approved BAT onsite sewage disposal systems that reduce nitrogen. Total system costs (purchase + installation + 2-year O&M) range from approximately $19,055 to $31,512 per system. After the initial 2-year O&M period, homeowners are responsible for ongoing maintenance at approximately $200–$383/year. The BRF Program no longer funds non-field-verified systems for installation. Approved systems are classified as BAT Class I (field verification complete) or BAT Class II (currently under field verification).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with onsite septic systems seeking to upgrade to nitrogen-reducing Best Available Technology systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, installation, and 2-year operation/maintenance contract for an approved BAT onsite sewage disposal system that reduces total nitrogen discharge
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; program is administered through county Environmental Health Divisions and applicants must contact their county Environmental Health Division for the specific application process
requirements_list: System must be an MDE-approved BAT system (Class I or Class II)
System must have undergone rigorous third-party testing (e.g., NSF 245, NSF 40 Class I, CAN/BNQ 3680-600, EN 12566-3, or peer-reviewed university field study)
The BRF Program no longer funds non-field-verified systems for installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the county Environmental Health Division for the specific process on submitting an application. structured_extraction.program_description: The Biological Nutrient Removal (BNR) Program provides capital grant funds and low-interest loans to publicly owned wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) to retrofit or upgrade facilities with biological nitrification/denitrification technology. The goal is to achieve an annual average effluent concentration of 8 mg/l total nitrogen. Capital grants are provided on a 50/50 cost-share basis for eligible BNR upgrade costs; small low-income communities may receive up to 75% grant funding. Eligible costs include engineering and pilot studies, design, and construction. Upgrades are generally undertaken alongside Enhanced Nutrient Removal upgrades using Bay Restoration Fund grant funding. MDE also provides low-interest loans to local governments to finance the local share of BNR facility costs and other plant upgrade or expansion costs consistent with Smart Growth. The program operates on an annual application cycle with funding decisions made through a rated and ranked priority system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants on a 50/50 cost-share basis for eligible BNR upgrade costs at publicly owned WWTPs. Small low-income communities may receive up to 75% grant funding. Eligible costs include engineering and pilot studies, design, and construction. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursable basis after payment requests for eligible costs are submitted. MDE also provides low-interest loans to local governments to finance the local share of BNR facility costs and other plant upgrade or expansion costs consistent with Smart Growth. Other state, local, or federal funds may be used as local match.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commuter Choice Challenge encourages organizations to adopt commuter benefit programs that reduce employee commuting costs and carbon emissions. Organizations take one or more steps — such as claiming the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, offering tax-free federal transit benefits, promoting carpooling or vanpooling, installing bike racks, or implementing telework — and submit a form to enter a prize drawing. Taking more steps earns additional entries in the drawing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations that complete at least one qualifying commuter benefit step and submit the online form are entered into a prize drawing. Prizes include cycling gear, work-from-home accessories, and assistance from the Commuter Choice program with employee education. Taking 2–5 steps doubles the entry; 6 or more steps earns three entries. The Maryland Commuter Tax Credit provides 50% of eligible commuter benefit costs, up to $100 per employee per month. Technical support includes site assessment, employee survey design and analysis, and transportation plan development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers (businesses and nonprofits) seeking to improve employee commute options and reduce their organization's carbon footprint
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transit subsidies, vanpool subsidies, guaranteed ride home, cash-in-lieu parking; prize drawing entries are awarded for implementing qualifying commuter benefit steps
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Workplace must be physically located in Maryland; eligible transit includes Maryland-based MDOT MTA systems (Light Rail, Metro, MARC trains, Local Transit) and regionally-connected WMATA services. Program is available statewide with no county or municipality exclusions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program (CFMGP) is a Maryland state program established in 1976 following Hurricane Agnes that provides matching grant funding to Maryland counties and municipalities to reduce or eliminate flood risks and improve flood resilience. The program funds capital projects in comprehensive flood management plans, watershed studies, infrastructure repairs and retrofits, emergency flood protection work, and acquisition, relocation, and elevation of flood-prone properties. It can also fund flood warning systems, flood control structures, emergency preparedness measures, and watershed restoration, as well as help communities establish sustainable floodplain management programs to prevent future flooding risks. The program coordinates with federal hazard mitigation programs through FEMA and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. State bond funds are matched with local government funds, and grant awards are subject to Maryland General Assembly capital budget approval and Maryland Board of Public Works approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: When federal funds participate, CFMGP may fund up to 50% of project costs (with federal funds covering up to 75% and local governments covering the remaining 25%, split evenly between CFMGP and local share). When federal funds do not participate, CFMGP may fund up to 75% of project costs with a 25% local share (state bond funds matched 50/50 with local government funds). Eligible uses include property acquisitions, house relocations, house elevations, flood warning systems, flood control structures, infrastructure repairs and retrofits, watershed restoration, emergency protection and preparedness work, and establishing sustainable floodplain management programs. Grant awards are subject to Maryland General Assembly capital budget approval and Maryland Board of Public Works approval.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects in comprehensive flood management plans; infrastructure repairs and retrofits; watershed restoration; emergency protection and preparedness work associated with flood events; acquisition, relocation, and elevation of flood-prone structures; comprehensive watershed studies; flood warning systems; flood control structures; establishing sustainable floodplain management programs to prevent future flooding risks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Drinking Water Supply Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments and small communities for the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly owned water supply facilities across Maryland. The program helps fund projects that address water supply-related health problems, meet federal Safe Drinking Water Act requirements, and support community water supply infrastructure needs. Priority is given to disadvantaged communities and those out of compliance with drinking water standards. Grant awards are capped at $1.5 million and require a local match, with award amounts based on system size, compliance status, community affordability, and median household income. Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost, not to exceed $1.5 million per project. A 12.5% local match is required, which may be funded through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) Program. Grants are based on the median household income of the community. Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible. Costs for planning, engineering, and project administration are eligible for loans only. Applicants may receive a combination of a State grant and a Drinking Water Revolving Loan.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Upgrading water treatment facilities; well development; water storage tanks; water distribution facilities up to private property lines; consolidation of smaller water systems; water supply improvements and drinking water infrastructure projects; acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, voluntary membership program operated by the Maryland Department of the Environment that helps businesses, government agencies, nonprofits, and other organizations of all types and sizes set and meet their own sustainability and environmental goals. Members share at least five environmental best practices and at least one quantifiable measurable result on an online profile, then receive recognition, technical assistance, and access to networking and educational resources. Members commit to continually improving their environmental performance and updating their profile at least every three years. Benefits include posting of the member's environmental profile on the Maryland Green Registry website, use of the Maryland Green Registry logo on promotional materials, a window decal for display at the facility, free technical and informational assistance to help implement new environmental best practices, information about upcoming webinars and conferences, annual contests and prize drawings, access to the Maryland Green Registry LinkedIn group, and eligibility for the annual Maryland Green Registry Leadership Awards. Members collectively report saving $83 million annually through shared practices.

Members collectively report saving $83 million annually through shared practices.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) provides state oversight for the voluntary cleanup and redevelopment of properties contaminated with hazardous substances or oil (brownfields). The program streamlines the cleanup process while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations, giving participants certainty about environmental requirements and helping them predict costs and timelines. Eligible purchasers can substantially limit their liability for past contamination before buying a property. Participants who complete cleanup receive a No Further Requirements Determination (NFRD) or Certificate of Completion (COC), which provides liability protection including a federal agreement with the EPA treating completed sites as of no further federal interest. The program works alongside the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program to offer tax credits, loans, and grants for brownfield redevelopment. An expedited Inculpable Person (IP) approval process is also available, and applicants intending to use the property for clean or renewable energy generation may qualify for an application fee waiver.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State oversight and technical assistance for voluntary cleanup of contaminated (brownfield) properties. Applicants pay a $10,000 initial application fee (effective June 1, 2025); $2,000 for subsequent applications on the same or contiguous properties. Additional fees: $2,000 for NFRD/COC issuance; $2,000 for expedited inculpable person approval; $2,000 for Record of Determination alteration. An expedited Inculpable Person (IP) approval process is available for a $2,000 fee; the Department responds within 5 business days of receipt. Applicants intending to use the property for clean or renewable energy generation may qualify for an application fee waiver. Properties on the National Priorities List, subject to a controlled hazardous substance permit, or contaminated property owned by a responsible person after 10/1/1997 are ineligible. Phase II ESAs must conform to ASTM E1903 standards. Upon completion, MDE issues a No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion providing liability protections. In conjunction with the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program, eligible participants may also receive tax credits, loans, and grants for brownfield redevelopment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, prospective purchasers, developers, environmental consultants, property managers, HOAs, condominium associations, and other parties seeking to voluntarily clean up and redevelop contaminated (brownfield) properties in Maryland, including those interested in redevelopment for commercial, residential, or renewable energy use. Also includes inculpable persons (innocent new owners meeting criteria under Environment Article §7-501(j)) and property owners with existing VCP closures subject to land use control compliance obligations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investigation, assessment, and cleanup of contaminated properties; redevelopment of brownfield sites. State oversight and technical guidance for environmental cleanup and redevelopment. Fee waivers available for renewable energy siting and development projects. Ongoing land use control compliance for properties with NFRDs, COCs, or Environmental Covenants.
