structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Water Quality Trading Program (WQT) creates a public market for nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment reductions to support Chesapeake Bay restoration. Participants can generate and sell certified credits, or purchase credits to meet National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit requirements. The program is a voluntary, collaborative effort between the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). Credits can be generated by wastewater, stormwater, on-site septic systems, oyster aquaculture, and agricultural practices. Buyers purchase credits from sellers through individual market-based agreements, with prices negotiated between buyer and seller based on supply and demand. Buyers submit a completed Credit Purchase Form to the MDE Trading Administrator to register a purchase. Permits may require modification to allow purchased credits to count toward permit requirements. Three trading regions are established: Patuxent River Basin; Potomac River Basin; and Eastern Shore and Western Shore River Basins (including the Maryland portion of the Susquehanna Basin). Credits must be used within the same Bay Segment TMDL watershed where they were generated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants can generate certified water quality credits (for nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment reductions) and sell them on the State marketplace, or purchase credits to meet NPDES permit compliance requirements. Credits are generated by wastewater, stormwater, septic systems, oyster aquaculture, and agricultural practices. Agricultural credits are certified by MDA using the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool (MNTT). Buyers purchase credits from sellers through individual market-based agreements, with prices negotiated based on supply and demand. Buyers submit a completed Credit Purchase Form signed by both buyer and seller to the MDE Trading Administrator to register a purchase. Agricultural credit purchases are registered through the Maryland Department of Agriculture. All trades must be registered with the Department within 15 days. Credits must be verified at least every 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities that can generate nitrogen, phosphorus, or sediment reductions (wastewater facilities, stormwater managers, agricultural operators, oyster aquaculture operators, septic system owners) and entities that need to purchase credits to meet NPDES permit requirements or other water quality permit goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Buying or selling certified water quality credits to meet environmental permit requirements (nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment reductions), meet WIP target load reduction goals, address local impairment, or generate revenue from pollution reduction practices. Credits can be applied toward permit requirements for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Sediment reductions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, within the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed. Three trading regions are established: Patuxent River Basin; Potomac River Basin; and Eastern Shore and Western Shore River Basins (including the Maryland portion of the Susquehanna Basin). Credits must be used within the same Bay Segment TMDL watershed where they were generated.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant funding administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) under Section 319(h) of the Clean Water Act. The program provides financial assistance to reduce or eliminate water quality impairments caused by nonpoint source pollution — pollution from diffuse sources such as stormwater runoff, agricultural runoff, and urban land use. Funds can pay for planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce pollutant loads in impaired waters listed on Maryland's 303(d) List or in watersheds with approved Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs), as well as for implementing best management practices and public outreach initiatives. Grants are awarded through a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP) process released each spring with a summer submission deadline, on an annual cycle. Grants are reimbursement-style — recipients must spend funds first and then receive reimbursement. Approximately $1 million total is available per cycle, with individual grants ranging from $30,000 to $400,000. No matching funds are required from applicants — the State of Maryland covers the required 40% match.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-style federal grant distributed through a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP) process on an annual cycle. Individual grants range from $30,000 to $400,000 per proposal, with approximately $1 million total available per cycle. No matching funds are required from applicants — the State of Maryland covers the required 40% match. Covers planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of water quality improvement projects, as well as implementation of best management practices and public outreach to reduce nonpoint source pollution. Project duration is negotiable, typically less than 1 year to a maximum of 4 years. Projects may include subcontracts for private firms and nonprofits for consulting, engineering, and construction. Applicants must demonstrate capacity for grant management and upfront funding. The FFY26 RFP is now closed; the next RFP for FFY27 funding will open on July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FFY26 RFP is closed; next RFP for FFY27 funding will open on July 1, 2026 (RFP typically released each spring with a summer submission deadline)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jacey Brooks, Maryland CWA §319(h) Grant, Water and Science Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, State agencies, State institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations in Maryland seeking funding to implement projects that reduce nonpoint source water pollution through best management practices, construction, planning, and outreach.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments associated with nonpoint source pollution, particularly in watersheds with approved TMDLs or on the 303(d) impaired waters list. Eligible activities include stormwater management, agricultural best management practices, public outreach, and related water quality improvement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; implementation projects typically require an EPA-accepted watershed plan for the target watershed. EPA-accepted watersheds include Aaron Run, Antietam Creek, Assawoman Bay, Casselman River, Corsica River, Lower Jones Falls, Middle Gwynns Falls, Lower Monocacy River, Sassafras River, Spring Branch, Tidal Back River, Upper Back River, Upper Choptank River, and Upper Jennings Run.
requirements_list: Must address nonpoint source pollution causing water quality impairments listed on Maryland's 303(d) List or in TMDL watersheds
Implementation projects (in-the-ground construction) typically require prior EPA acceptance of a watershed-based plan meeting EPA criteria
Applicants must demonstrate capacity for grant management and upfront funding (reimbursement model)
Proposals must include justification of financial and management capacity
MDE may require additional oversight or documentation for selected projects
Must respond to the annual Request for Proposals released each spring
Submission deadline is typically in the summer
No matching funds required from applicants — State of Maryland covers the required 40% match
Grant amounts range from $30,000 to $400,000 per proposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a proposal in response to the annual Request for Proposals (RFP), which is typically released each spring with a summer submission deadline. Proposals must include justification of capacity for grant management and funding. MDE reviews and selects projects; selections for FFY26 were made in November 2025. The FFY27 RFP is expected to open July 1, 2026. Contact MDE at mde.nps319@maryland.gov to be notified via email for future opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: On-Site Pollution Prevention Technical Assistance for Maryland Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Free, confidential, on-site technical assistance visits for Maryland businesses to help reduce operating costs, improve energy and material efficiency, reduce waste disposal costs, lower regulatory compliance costs, and decrease worker exposure to hazardous materials. An independent engineering consultant or engineer from the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) visits the facility, assesses opportunities for pollution prevention, and provides a written report with recommendations and an offer for further assistance to implement them. Manufacturers in specific sectors may be eligible for targeted on-site assessments by an independent contractor. The 2024 cycle targeted manufacturers in five sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; and Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication. Assessments are confidential, voluntary, and non-regulatory, funded through a federal grant.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential on-site facility assessments conducted by engineers from the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) or independent engineering consultants. Visits typically take about one hour. After the visit, the business receives a written report summarizing energy, water, and waste reduction opportunities and recommendations, along with an offer for additional assistance to implement them. The program is funded through a federal grant. Assessments are confidential, voluntary, and non-regulatory. The 2024 cycle targeted five manufacturing sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; and Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses, particularly manufacturers in targeted sectors, looking to reduce operating costs, improve energy and material efficiency, reduce waste, lower compliance costs, and reduce worker exposure to hazardous materials.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site technical assessments to identify opportunities to improve energy and material efficiency, reduce waste disposal costs, lower regulatory compliance costs, and reduce worker exposure to hazardous substances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to businesses and facilities located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a business or facility located in Maryland
Participation is completely voluntary and confidential
Not an inspection or compliance evaluation

Manufacturers seeking the targeted sector assessment must be in one of five eligible sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; or Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For general inquiries or to schedule a site visit, call MDE's Pollution Prevention Program at 410-537-4119, 1-800-633-6101 (ext. 4119), or via MD Relay Service at 1-800-735-2258. For targeted sector assessments, complete the online interest form by the published deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Onsite Systems Training – MDE Certification Courses
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) Onsite Systems Division offers free, in-person and online training courses for individuals seeking certifications to install sand mound systems, at-grade systems, and Best Available Technology (BAT) systems for sewage disposal. Courses are also available for continuing education units (CEUs). Initial certification courses are full-day, in-person sessions held annually at MDE headquarters in Baltimore. Renewal courses for sand mound and at-grade installers are completed online every five years. Third-party approved courses are also available through partner organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, in-person certification courses (7.5 hours for sand mound and at-grade; 4 hours for BAT) offered annually at MDE headquarters in Baltimore. Online renewal courses (2 hours) are available on a rolling basis for existing certification holders. Certifications are valid for five years. Physical classroom space is prioritized for installers seeking new certifications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Courses offered annually, generally late winter and early spring; online renewal available at any time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking certification to install onsite sewage disposal systems (sand mound, at-grade, BAT) in Maryland, including contractors seeking certification renewal, and members of the on-site regulatory community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to obtain or renew certifications to install sand mound, at-grade, or BAT sewage disposal systems in Maryland. Courses count toward continuing education units (CEUs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Initial certification courses are held in-person at MDE headquarters in Baltimore. Renewal courses are available online.
requirements_list: Must pass a written examination for initial sand mound and at-grade certifications
BAT installer certification also requires certification by respective technology manufacturers
Local installation requirements may apply for BAT systems
Sand mound and at-grade certification renewal required every 5 years
Renewal courses completed online; must have access to a computer with a reliable internet connection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the desired course using the linked Google Forms registration links on the page. If registration is not currently open, complete the Course Interest List form to be notified when registration opens. Online renewal courses can be completed at any time by clicking the course link, entering required information, watching the embedded video, and answering knowledge check questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) partner to place engineering students as summer interns at Maryland manufacturing companies. Interns work with MD MEP staff to identify process and equipment improvements that save companies money and reduce environmental impact through energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency. Since 2000, the program has placed 13 interns at 17 Maryland companies, identifying over $3.7 million in cost savings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Engineering students are placed as summer interns at participating Maryland companies. Interns identify process and equipment improvements that reduce environmental impact and save money. Funding comes from a combination of the U.S. EPA, MDE, and participating companies. Since 2000, the program has placed 13 interns at 17 Maryland companies, identifying over $3.7 million in cost savings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland manufacturing companies seeking help identifying cost savings and environmental improvements through engineering intern placements; university engineering students placed as summer interns
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identifying process and equipment improvements for energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency at participating companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to manufacturing companies located in Maryland; interns placed at Maryland-based facilities statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland manufacturing or industrial company
Participating company contributes to program funding
Interns are selected by the university and trained in a relevant industry sector and general pollution prevention
Interns work with selected businesses to identify P2 opportunities, provide cost-benefit information, and assist with implementation of accepted changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Laura Armstrong at MDE (laura.armstrong@maryland.gov, 410-537-4119) or the MD MEP/MTECH partner to inquire about participation. Interns are selected by the university partner and placed at participating companies; companies are identified and coordinated through MDE and the university partner.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) awards CO2 offset allowances to projects that demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable, and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, energy efficiency improvements to reduce natural gas/oil/propane combustion, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, reduction in sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) emissions, and carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided land conversion. Projects may be located in any participating Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) state or other approved jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE awards CO2 offset allowances (tradeable credits under the RGGI cap-and-trade system) to qualifying emission-reduction projects. A consistency application must be submitted to MDE within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration/forest projects). MDE reviews and approves or denies verifier accreditation applications within 45 days of submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration/forest projects)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities operating emission-reduction projects in RGGI participating states, including landfill operators, agricultural operations, energy efficiency project developers, SF6 reduction projects (transmission and distribution entities in Maryland), and forest carbon sequestration/reforestation/improved forest management/avoided conversion projects. Also open to parties seeking accreditation as Independent Verifiers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — the program awards CO2 offset allowances (credits) rather than cash. Allowances can be used by regulated CO2 sources under the RGGI cap-and-trade program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. For U.S. Forest Projects (reforestation, improved forest management, avoided conversion), projects may be located in a RGGI participating state (excluding New York and Connecticut) or anywhere in the United States if the project state has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with RGGI states. For SF6 reduction projects, the service territory must be within the state of Maryland and may not span more than one state. For offset projects located in a state or United States jurisdiction that is not a participating state, the project sponsor must demonstrate compliance with all requirements of the cooperating regulatory agency. For verifier pre-engagement disclosure, the submittal is directed to MDE if the offset project is located in Maryland; if the offset project is not located in Maryland, a similar submittal should be provided to the applicable regulatory agency in the state where the offset project is located. Applications are administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment under COMAR 26.09.03; submissions are mailed to MDE Air Quality Planning Program, Offsets, 1800 Washington Boulevard, Baltimore MD 21230.
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable, and permanent avoidance or reduction of CO2 emissions
Consistency application must be submitted to MDE within six months of project commencement (one year for carbon sequestration/forest projects)
Applications must meet deadlines or project will be denied and remain ineligible
Projects must comply with COMAR 26.09.03 regulations
Accredited Independent Verifiers must meet qualifications listed in COMAR 26.09.03.08 and submit an Offset Verifier Application for Accreditation
Accredited Offset Verifier Pre-Engagement Disclosure Submittal must be submitted to MDE prior to engaging in verification services for each offset project
For offset projects located in a non-participating state or jurisdiction, documentation of compliance with the cooperating regulatory agency must be provided
Project sponsor must establish a RGGI COATS general account for submission of offset project documentation
For U.S. Forest Projects, projects on tribal lands require a waiver of sovereign immunity between the tribe and the Participating State
A Monitoring and Verification Report and Independent Verifier Report must be submitted annually to maintain eligibility
For SF6 reduction projects, service territory must be within Maryland and may not span more than one state; entity must serve electrical load within Maryland Public Service Commission jurisdiction

Forest offset projects require detailed M&V plans including forest inventory documentation, sampling plots, field measurements, modeling plan, forest management practices assessment, and quality assurance procedures
Independent verifier must be accredited and provide detailed report covering eligibility, baseline CO2-equivalent sequestration, and M&V adequacy
Forest project reversal risk rating must be completed per applicable RGGI U.S. Forest Protocol appendix
Accredited verifiers have an ongoing obligation to disclose conflicts of interest per COMAR 26.09.03.08
For Improved Forest Management and Avoided Conversion projects, forest management certification (ATFS, FSC, or SFI) is required if timber harvest occurs
Carbon stock calculations must cover all applicable carbon pools (above-ground live, below-ground live, standing dead, down dead, understory, and soil carbon as applicable)
Organizations seeking verifier accreditation must submit an Offset Verifier Application for Accreditation; MDE approves or denies within 45 days of submission
Offset projects commenced before December 20, 2005 are not eligible for the award of CO2 offset allowances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate consistency application and technical support documents for your project type to MDE. Applications for each project type (landfill methane, energy efficiency, agricultural methane, SF6 reduction, carbon sequestration/reforestation, improved forest management, avoided conversion) are available on the program page. Applications must be submitted within six months (or one year for carbon sequestration/forest projects) of commencing the project. Submissions are uploaded to the RGGI COATS system (https://rggi-coats.org/eats/rggi/) or mailed to MDE Air Quality Planning Program, Offsets, 1800 Washington Boulevard, Baltimore MD 21230. Parties seeking verifier accreditation submit an Offset Verifier Application for Accreditation; MDE approves or denies within 45 days. After receiving a consistency determination, project sponsors must submit annual Monitoring and Verification Reports and Independent Verifier Reports to maintain eligibility. Contact Scott Zacharko at (410) 537-4177 with questions or for further guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to counties to inspect and monitor sewage sludge sites. The program operates through contracts between the Maryland Department of the Environment and the counties. It also issues permits for using sewage sludge.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides formula grants to counties. It also offers regulatory services, technical help, and information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for county governments, for-profit businesses, individuals, municipalities, non-profits, and state colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counties can use funds for extra inspections and monitoring of sites where sewage sludge is used.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sewerage Facilities Supplemental Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to local governmental entities for planning, design, and construction of sewerage and wastewater facility improvements needed to address high-priority public health or water quality problems. The program supplements water quality loan programs, particularly when affordability is a concern. Awards are primarily targeted at small and disadvantaged communities, are capped at $1.5 million, and are based on system size, compliance status, and affordability. A local match is required. Applications are accepted December 1 through January 31 each year and will reopen in December 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1.5 million for planning, design, and construction of sewerage and wastewater facility improvements, supplementing water quality loan programs for local governments. Priority is given to small and disadvantaged communities facing affordability concerns or high-priority public health and water quality needs. Award amounts are based on system size, compliance status, and affordability. A local match is required. Low-interest loans through the State Revolving Fund are also available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 1 through January 31 each year; applications will reopen December 1, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governmental entities including municipalities and county water/sewer authorities with sewerage and wastewater facility needs, especially small and disadvantaged communities facing affordability challenges or public health and water quality issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction of sewerage and wastewater facility infrastructure improvements supplementing water quality loan programs. Eligible uses include wastewater treatment, CSO/SSO correction, sewer rehabilitation/replacement, septic-to-treatment connections, energy and water conservation, drinking water projects, stormwater/drainage management, best management practices (BMPs), and landfill capping.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, targeting small and disadvantaged communities. Projects must be consistent with the County's Comprehensive Land Use Plan and MDE-approved Water & Sewerage Plan, and must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or have an applicable PFA exception, categorical exception, or categorical exclusion under Smart Growth law.

Local match required
Awards based on system size, compliance status, and affordability
Maximum award is $1.5 million
Program primarily targets small and disadvantaged communities
Applications accepted December 1 through January 31 of each year
Project must be consistent with the County's Comprehensive Land Use Plan and MDE-approved Water & Sewerage Plan
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), or have a PFA exception, categorical exception, or categorical exclusion per Smart Growth law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed. They will reopen December 1, 2026. Submit application during the December 1 through January 31 application window each year through the Maryland Department of the Environment. Applicants should verify project location eligibility using the interactive PFA map and confirm consistency with local planning requirements. Contact the Water Resources Planning Division at MDE.PFAException@maryland.gov or the Maryland Department of Planning at (410) 767-5497 for PFA-related questions. For drinking water audit, conservation, or capacity planning questions, contact Zoë Goodson at zoe.goodson@maryland.gov. For loan financial review questions, contact Gerald Gorham, Jr. at gerald.gorham@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Smoke School - Visible Emissions Evaluation Training and Testing
structured_extraction.program_description: A training and testing course that teaches participants how to evaluate visible emissions (smoke opacity) from stationary sources. Courses are held approximately every six months at the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) Essex Campus. The program includes a virtual classroom session and in-person field sessions where participants observe and evaluate smoke opacity over multiple runs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Visible emissions evaluation training and testing conducted over multiple days. Includes a virtual classroom session and two in-person field sessions (10 runs total over 2 days). Registration is coordinated through the Community Colleges of Baltimore County by calling (443) 840-4700.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sessions held approximately every six months; next session April 27-30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and facility operators who need to conduct or certify visible emissions evaluations at stationary sources of air pollution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive training and certification in visible emissions evaluation (smoke opacity reading).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; field sessions held at CCBC Essex Campus in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must register through the Community Colleges of Baltimore County
Field sessions held at CCBC Essex Campus, Parking Lot 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (443) 840-4700 to register for the smoke school session. Classroom session is conducted live and virtually; field sessions are in-person at CCBC Essex.

structured_extraction.program_name: Source Collection And Threat Reduction (SCATR) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The SCATR Program helps Maryland radioactive material licensees dispose of unwanted sealed radioactive sources. The U.S. Department of Energy provides financial assistance to cover costs of packaging, transportation, and disposal of these unused sources, which are identified as potential security risks. The Conference of Radiation Control Program Directors (CRCPD) coordinates the program with Los Alamos National Laboratory and the Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance (SCATR funds combined with licensee funds) to cover costs of packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive material sealed sources. The exact amount of assistance is not specified on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Radioactive Material Licensees who have unwanted radioactive material sealed sources they wish to dispose of.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive material sealed sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Radioactive Material Licensees.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Radioactive Material Licensee
Must have unwanted radioactive material sealed sources
Must register the radioactive material to be disposed of
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Identify and register the radioactive material to be disposed of. Contact the Maryland Department of the Environment or visit the CRCPD website (crcpd.org) for registration instructions. Outlets for the material are found, SCATR funds are committed, a contract is made for packaging, transportation, and disposal, and the material is collected for disposition.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance funded by Maryland's share of the Volkswagen emissions cheating settlement. The program covers two main areas: (1) replacement of older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles with cleaner alternatives to reduce emissions, and (2) expansion of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across Maryland. The EV charging component includes two tracks: the Charge Ahead Grant Program (Level 2 charging at workplaces and community sites) and the Electric Corridors Grant Program (DC fast charging along major travel routes). Maryland received approximately $75.7 million from the Volkswagen Environmental Mitigation Trust, with about 15% available for zero emission vehicle (ZEV) charging infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants fund the replacement of older diesel heavy-duty vehicles with cleaner alternatives and the purchase and installation of EV charging equipment. Applicants fund costs first and are reimbursed after project completion. Two EV charging program tracks are available: Charge Ahead Grant Program (Level 2, hard-wired 208/240-volt charging at workplaces and community sites; eligible costs include purchase and installation, site design, labor, network fees for first 5 years, site prep, and utility upgrades) and Electric Corridors Grant Program (Level 3 DC fast charging along alternative fuel corridors, with higher power minimums of 175 kW per port in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, and 60 kW minimum in remaining counties; sites must be within 15 miles of an FHWA-designated EV corridor). Maryland received approximately $75.7 million from the Volkswagen Environmental Mitigation Trust, with about 15% available for zero emission vehicle (ZEV) charging infrastructure. Round 3 is the final round of EV charging infrastructure funding across both tracks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles, and non-profit and private employers, state/federal/local governmental agencies, and other organizations seeking to install EV charging infrastructure in Maryland. Utilities are explicitly ineligible for the EV charging tracks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of older diesel heavy-duty vehicles with cleaner alternatives, and purchase and installation of electric vehicle charging equipment, including Level 2 chargers (208/240-volt, hard-wired) and Level 3 DC fast chargers. Eligible costs for EV charging include site design, labor, network fees (first 5 years for networked chargers), site preparation, and utility upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be sited within Maryland at a fixed location. For the Electric Corridors Grant Program, sites must be located no more than 15 miles from a FHWA-designated EV corridor. Eligible corridors include I-270, I-495, I-68, I-695, I-70, I-795, I-81, I-83, I-95, I-97, US 1, US 13, US 15, US 301, US 50, MD 100, MD 140, MD 32, MD 4, MD 5, MD 528, and MD 295, among others. Higher power requirements (175 kW minimum per CCS/NACS port) apply in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties; lower power requirements (60 kW minimum) apply in Allegany, Charles, Garrett, Washington, Calvert, St. Mary's, Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.

For Electric Corridors: sites must be within 15 miles of a FHWA-designated EV corridor
Grantee must notify MDE of problems, operational changes, or ownership changes within 10 days
Grantee must obtain all local, State, and federal permits and licenses

Historic preservation review required under Section 106 NHPA and Maryland Historical Trust Act of 1985 (exemption available for sites without buildings/structures over 45 years old not in Maryland Inventory)
Grantee responsible for customer service, maintenance/repair, marketing, and station uptime monitoring

Submit proposals to MDE before the deadline. Applications for Round 3 (the final round of EV charging infrastructure funding) closed April 18, 2025. Grants are reimbursement-based: applicants fund project costs first and are reimbursed after project completion per the executed grant agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to expand electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across Maryland, funded by Maryland's share of the Volkswagen emissions cheating settlement. Grants support the purchase and installation of EV charging equipment to make charging more accessible, reduce air pollution, and help residents and businesses transition to cleaner transportation. The program includes two tracks: the Charge Ahead Grant Program (workplace and community charging) and the Electric Corridors Grant Program (DC fast charging along major travel routes).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund the purchase and installation of EV charging equipment. Two program tracks are available: Charge Ahead Grant Program (Level 2 charging at workplaces and community sites) and Electric Corridors Grant Program (Level 3 DC fast charging along alternative fuel corridors). Maryland received approximately $75.7 million from the Volkswagen Environmental Mitigation Trust, with about 15% available for zero emission vehicle (ZEV) charging infrastructure. Round 3 is described as the final round of funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, businesses, governments, and individuals seeking to install EV charging infrastructure in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of electric vehicle charging equipment, including Level 2 chargers and Level 3 DC fast chargers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must propose a project to purchase and/or install EV charging equipment
Must submit a project proposal form
Must follow updated program framework requirements for Round 3
Projects must align with either the Charge Ahead or Electric Corridors grant program frameworks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the applicable grant program framework (Charge Ahead or Electric Corridors) and complete the project proposal form. Submit proposals before the deadline. Applications for Round 3 (the final round) closed April 18, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) Clean and Renewable Energy Application Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) offers a fee waiver for developers who apply to the VCP with the intent to locate a clean or renewable energy project on a brownfield or other degraded land site. MDE adopted regulations establishing criteria for certifying a developer's intention to use an eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy, which qualifies them for the fee waiver. The standard VCP application fee is $6,000 for new projects or $2,000 for a subsequent application per property. The clean or renewable energy project must have an anticipated yearly energy output of at least 2 megawatts to qualify. Effective January 1, 2022.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fee waiver for the VCP application fee ($6,000 for new/initial projects or $2,000 for a subsequent application per property) when the developer certifies their intent to use the property to generate clean or renewable energy. The clean or renewable energy project must have an anticipated yearly energy output of at least 2 megawatts to qualify. Effective January 1, 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to redevelop brownfield or degraded land sites for clean or renewable energy projects in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of the VCP application fee for developers intending to site clean or renewable energy projects (solar PV, geothermal, wind, biofuels, fuel cells) on brownfields or other degraded lands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; property must be eligible under Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (Environment Article, Title 7, Subtitle 5, Annotated Code of Maryland); no county or municipality restrictions

Property must be eligible for the Voluntary Cleanup Program
Applicant must certify their intention to use the eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy
Property must be a brownfield or other degraded land site
Clean or renewable energy project must meet COMAR 26.14.3.02B(4) and (16) definitions
Anticipated yearly energy output must be at least 2 megawatts
Applicant must submit a site location map
Applicant must complete an eligible project affidavit under penalty of law
Authorized representative must certify accuracy and completeness of information
Application must meet criteria established in COMAR 26.14.03

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the VCP Fee Waiver Application form and proof of eligibility by mail to: Maryland Department of the Environment, Voluntary Cleanup Program, 1800 Washington Boulevard, Suite 625, Baltimore, Maryland 21230-1719. The fee waiver application must include a Clean or Renewable Energy Certification form (signed, dated, and notarized) specifying energy type, anticipated yearly output (in kilowatts), construction schedule, and anticipated generation start date, along with a site location map and an eligible project affidavit. Within 30 days after receipt, the Department will notify the applicant in writing whether the fee waiver is approved, incomplete, or denied. If denied, written reasons are provided. If the submission is incomplete or ineligible, the applicant must pay the fee or resubmit a complete form. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis with no stated deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: WIIN Act Section 2107 Grant for Lead Remediation in Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding provided by the U.S. EPA under the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation (WIIN) Act, Section 2107, to help local educational agencies (LEAs) test for and remove sources of lead in drinking water at schools across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant covering materials and labor costs for lead remediation projects at schools. Funds are prioritized for schools where at least 50% of children receive free/reduced-price meals or that have a Head Start program, and schools serving children 6 years old and under. Completed projects are reimbursed after award decision; proposed projects receive funding after work is completed and documentation is submitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local educational agencies (LEAs) — public and nonpublic school districts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Materials and labor costs for lead remediation in school drinking water systems, including permanent or long-term remediation measures as preferred by EPA guidance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland school districts are eligible.
requirements_list: Remediation projects must occur between November 15, 2021 and September 1, 2022
All required documentation must be received by MDE no later than September 8, 2022
Applicants must provide percentage of students receiving free or reduced-price meals
Applicants must indicate whether the school has a Head Start program
Applicants must provide lowest and highest grades served
Applicants must provide the amount of funding requested for completed and planned remediation projects
Applicants must provide general school and contact information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted from June 1 through June 22, 2022 using the attached Excel application form. Submit the form along with any available invoices or cost estimates. Applications are evaluated after the application period closes. MDE recommends submitting as early as possible.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps clean up illegal scrap tire piles. It also manages the collection, transport, recycling, and processing of scrap tires in Maryland. A fee on new tires funds the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program manages the cleanup of illegal scrap tire stockpiles. It also oversees the collection, transportation, recycling, and processing of scrap tires and issues the required licenses for these activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and individuals who collect, transport, process, or recycle scrap tires. The program also works with property owners who have illegal tire stockpiles.
requirements_list: Must obtain the appropriate license to transport, collect, process, recycle, dispose, incinerate, or use scrap tires as fuel.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides state grants to local governments. The grants help pay for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants to support capital improvements for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, including counties and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments and small communities for the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities and infrastructure across Maryland. The program helps fund projects that address water supply-related health problems, meet federal Safe Drinking Water Act requirements, and support community water supply infrastructure needs. Assistance includes grants covering up to 87.5% of total eligible project costs (not to exceed $1.5 million per project), with a required 12.5% local match that may be funded through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) Program. Grant awards are based on the median household income of the community, system size, compliance status, and affordability; only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible. Priority is given to disadvantaged communities and those out of compliance with drinking water standards. Projects are rated and ranked based on public health impact, regulatory compliance, safety, reliability, and applicant financial capability. The program also provides direct loans for land acquisition to protect source water and for planning, engineering, and project administration costs. Applications are accepted each December through January annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost, not to exceed $1.5 million per project, with a required 12.5% local match (which may be funded through the DWRLF Program). Grant amounts are based on the median household income of the community, system size, compliance status, and affordability; only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible. Eligible costs include upgrading water treatment facilities, well development, water storage tanks, water distribution facilities up to private property lines, and consolidation of smaller water systems. Planning, engineering, and project administration costs are eligible for loans only. Applicants may receive a combination of a State grant and a Drinking Water Revolving Loan. Also provides direct loans for land acquisition for source water protection and wellhead protection projects. State Revolving Fund low-interest loans are also available through the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 1 through January 31 annually; next window opens December 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zoë Goodson (drinking water); Gerald Gorham, Jr. (financial/loan)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and small communities in Maryland seeking to fund water supply facility improvements, drinking water infrastructure, wellhead protection projects, and source water land acquisition, particularly those with insufficient or limited financial capability, disadvantaged communities, and those non-compliant with drinking water standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities; upgrading water treatment facilities; well development; water storage tanks; water distribution facilities up to private property lines; consolidation of smaller water systems; wellhead protection projects; land acquisition for source water protection; planning, engineering, and project administration costs (loans only); stormwater management and non-hazardous landfill leachate treatment; water conservation, efficiency, and reuse projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (or obtain a PFA exception or categorical exemption), conform to Smart Growth Criteria, and be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan and County Comprehensive Land Use Plan. An interactive PFA map is available for location verification.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or small water supply community
Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible
Project must be eligible under the federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Project must conform to Smart Growth Criteria
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (or obtain a PFA exception or categorical exemption)
Project must be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan and County Comprehensive Land Use Plan
Applicant must submit a water audit
Water systems serving a population greater than 10,000 must submit a water conservation plan
Water supply capacity management plan required for community systems greater than 20,000 GPD under capacity stress
Local match of 12.5% required for grant awards (may be funded through the DWRLF Program)
Maximum grant award is $1.5 million (up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost)
Grant awards based on median household income, system size, compliance status, and affordability
Debt service coverage ratio must meet minimum requirements
Priority given to disadvantaged communities and/or communities non-compliant with drinking water standards

Projects are rated and ranked based on Environment Article 9-423 and COMAR 26.03.09.06 priority criteria including public health impact, regulatory compliance, safety, reliability, and applicant financial capability
Applications accepted December through January of each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Submit a funding application during the December 1 through January 31 annual application window through the Maryland Department of the Environment (administered by the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration, MWIFA). Projects are rated and ranked based on statutory and regulatory criteria. Applicants are also encouraged to seek funding from USDA Rural Development and Maryland DHCD's Small Cities CDBG Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Wellhead Protection Program helps local governments protect public drinking water supplies by managing land around drinking water wells. The program provides technical assistance, information, and funding to local communities to identify contamination sources, delineate wellhead protection areas, and manage those areas to prevent pollution of public supply wells.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of the Environment, Water Supply Program
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans are available to communities to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas. Technical assistance includes help delineating wellhead protection areas, providing lists of regulated activities within those areas, and connecting communities with other agencies that can support protection efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and public water suppliers in Maryland seeking to protect their public drinking water wells from contamination.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas; delineation of wellhead protection areas; contaminant source inventories; community planning and management activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to local governments with public drinking water supply wells.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or public water supplier
Must be protecting a public drinking water supply well
Program requires formation of a community planning team
Wellhead protection areas must be delineated and reviewed by MDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDE's Water Supply Program, Source Protection and Appropriation Division at (410) 537-3714 for assistance with delineating wellhead protection areas, obtaining lists of regulated activities, and accessing available funding and technical support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) occasionally offers competitive and non-competitive grants to counties, providers, nonprofits, and universities. Strategic funding priorities fall under six focus areas: Self-Determination, Self-Advocacy, Supporting Families, Housing, Employment, and Assistive Technology. Funding opportunities are released as requests for proposals (RFPs) as they arise and are announced in the DDA's bi-weekly newsletter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive and non-competitive grants awarded to eligible organizations supporting people with developmental disabilities. Funding falls under six focus areas: Self-Determination, Self-Advocacy, Supporting Families, Housing, Employment, and Assistive Technology. Specific funding amounts and terms vary by individual grant opportunity and are released with each request for proposals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties, service providers, nonprofits, and universities supporting individuals with developmental disabilities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities and initiatives aligned with DDA's six strategic focus areas: Self-Determination, Self-Advocacy, Supporting Families, Housing, Employment, and Assistive Technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county, provider, nonprofit, or university
Applications must be submitted in response to active requests for proposals
Applications must align with one or more of the six DDA strategic focus areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The DDA releases requests for proposals as funding opportunities arise. Active RFPs are posted on the DDA Grants page and announced in the DDA's bi-weekly newsletter. Subscribe to the newsletter to be notified of new funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) funds employment, day, residential, and support services for people with developmental disabilities. To access these services, individuals or someone acting on their behalf must complete and submit an eligibility application. DDA staff at regional offices can assist with the application process. Eligible services may include Autism Waiver, Personal Care, Living at Home Waiver, and other state or Medicaid-funded service programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DDA funds employment, day, residential, and support services for eligible people with developmental disabilities. The application determines eligibility to receive these funded services, which may include Autism Waiver, Personal Care, Living at Home Waiver, and other state or Medicaid-funded service programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and adults with developmental disabilities, and their families or representatives, in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment, day, residential, and support services for people with developmental disabilities, including state or Medicaid-funded service waivers (e.g., Autism Waiver, Personal Care, Living at Home Waiver).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — Maryland residency required. Applications are routed to one of four regional offices by county: Western (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Washington); Central (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Howard, Harford, Baltimore City); Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester); Southern (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's).
requirements_list: Must have a developmental disability
Must be a resident of Maryland
Must apply for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) before receiving DDA-funded services
Must complete the DDA Application for Services (or have someone complete it on your behalf)
Application must be signed and submitted to the appropriate DDA Regional Office (Attention: Eligibility and Access Unit)
Supporting documentation required, including medical records, neuropsychological/psychological evaluations, special education records, and/or vocational evaluations as applicable
Low Intensity Support Services (LISS) do not require this application
Applicant must provide true and complete information with proof; report changes within 10 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download, mail-request, or pick up the application from a DDA regional office. Fill out and sign the application (can be completed on a computer or handwritten). Submit the completed application to the appropriate DDA Regional Office listed on the last page of the application, addressed to the Eligibility and Access Unit. DDA will make a preliminary decision within 7 days and a final eligibility decision within 60 days of receipt of the completed application. Applicants may request time extensions for processing. DDA staff can assist with completion. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no fixed submission deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DDA Rent Subsidy Program provides rental assistance to individuals with developmental disabilities in Maryland, helping them afford housing in the community. The program is operated by the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The subsidy covers the gap between 30% of household income and the full rent plus basic utilities (gas, water, electricity). Eligible individuals must have household income at or below 50% of the area median income in the county where housing will be located.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidy covering the gap between 30% of household income and the full rent plus basic utilities (gas, water, electricity). Household income must be at or below 50% of area median income in the county where housing will be located.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 and above with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are currently receiving DDA services or on the waitlist for Crisis Resolution services, including unaccompanied youth under 25, families with children/youth, and individuals fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance covering the gap between 30% of household income and full rent plus basic utilities (gas, water, electricity).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Household income must be at or below 50% of area median income in the county where the housing will be located.
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a developmental disability
Must be served by the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration or on the waitlist for Crisis Resolution services
Must be age 18 or above (or unaccompanied youth under 25, or families with children/youth)
Household income must be at or below 50% of area median income in the county where housing will be located
Must have housing goals documented in a Person-Centered Plan (PCP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Person identifies housing need; CCS facilitates team meeting to identify goals in PCP and submits to DDA for approval. 2. Once authorized, person develops housing plan with support; CCS refers to Housing Support Services (HSS) provider. 3. Person is placed on MDOD Social Serve waitlist; HSS provider monitors and communicates updates. 4. Housing Support Specialist assists in gathering information and identifying housing. 5. Once housing is found, request for tenancy is submitted to DHCD for review/approval. 6. If approved: lease submitted to DHCD, moving arrangements made, tenant training provided, address updated in LTSS, PCP revised as needed. 7. If denied: assistance provided in finding alternative housing.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) - DDA Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) federal funding. Grants support community-based services providers, community coordination service (CCS) agencies, and other eligible organizations serving individuals with developmental disabilities in Maryland. Awards are described in the grant announcement and application materials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funded through the federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA). Specific award amounts and terms are described in the grant announcement and application materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based services providers, community coordination service (CCS) agencies, and other eligible organizations supporting individuals with developmental disabilities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting community-based services and programs for individuals with developmental disabilities, including providers in the developmental disabilities services system, as described in the grant announcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations and providers operating in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the MDH grant cloud portal at mdh.gvgrantcloud.com. Applicants are encouraged to review the grant announcement, webinar, PowerPoint presentation, and FAQs before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Governor's Transitioning Youth Initiative provides a special category of eligibility and priority for DDA services for individuals with developmental disabilities who are leaving the school system. The initiative earmarks funds in the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) budget to provide supported employment and other day services for eligible students graduating from special education, so they do not have to wait on the DDA Waiting List for adult services. The DDA works in collaboration with the Division of Rehabilitative Services (DORS) to deliver these services. Without this initiative, qualifying individuals would be placed on a lengthy waiting list for adult services, regardless of the severity of their situation. An 'Employment First' principle prioritizes community employment over other service models.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds supported employment and other day services for eligible students transitioning out of the school system. Services include person-centered planning, targeted case management through a Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) agency, employment supports, career exploration, job skills training, job placement support, community integration services, and other day services. Services are coordinated in collaboration with the Division of Rehabilitative Services (DORS). An 'Employment First' principle prioritizes community employment over other service models.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30 (annually; applies to year of individual's eligibility). Applications submitted after the deadline go to a waitlist.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Beryl Parker (Central MD), Jim Sullivan (Eastern Shore), Nicole Sheppard (Southern MD), Brenda Sperow (Western MD)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth with developmental disabilities transitioning from high school to adulthood (and their families). Individuals must reach out at age 14 to request TY-specific services, and must be age 21 through 22 (or up to one year after graduation if graduation occurs after the 21st birthday) to receive services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supported employment services and other day services for eligible students transitioning out of special education with developmental disabilities, including person-centered planning, targeted case management, employment supports, career exploration, job skills training, job placement support, community integration services, and community day services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through four regional offices: Central Maryland (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore, Harford, Howard counties), Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's counties), Western Maryland (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Washington counties), and Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester counties). All 24 Maryland counties are served.
requirements_list: Must be found fully eligible as developmentally disabled by the DDA
Must have a severe, chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole diagnosis of mental illness) or combination of impairments
Disability must have manifested before age 22
Disability is likely to continue indefinitely
Results in inability to live independently without external support or continuing and regular assistance
Reflects need for combination and sequence of special, interdisciplinary, or generic care, treatment, or other services that are individually planned and coordinated
Must be between 21st and 22nd birthday, OR within one year of graduation if graduation occurs after the 21st birthday
Should contact the servicing DDA regional office at age 14 to request TY-specific services
Must be a Maryland resident
All DDA waiver applications must be completed by June 30 of the eligibility year to be considered for funding; applications submitted after the deadline go to a waitlist
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the servicing DDA regional office at age 14 to request TY-specific services. Apply for DDA services through the DDA eligibility process (https://health.maryland.gov/dda/Pages/Eligibility.aspx) and/or apply for DORS services through the Division of Rehabilitative Services. All DDA waiver applications must be completed by June 30 of the eligibility year to be considered for funding. Once found eligible, a Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) agency will provide targeted case management and develop a person-centered plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: APPS (Autism Program Planning Success for Employment)
structured_extraction.program_description: APPS assists job seekers with Autism in developing self-determination and employment readiness skills through small group, interactive learning sessions. Topics include self-advocacy, decision making, career interests, job exploration, work expectations, employer expectations, employee responsibilities, and job readiness. Sessions are offered both in-person on-campus at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Baltimore and online, as well as in participants' communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small group, interactive learning sessions (in-person on-campus at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Baltimore and online) focused on self-determination, self-advocacy, decision making, career interests and skills, job exploration, work expectations, employer and employee responsibilities, and job readiness. Also offered in participants' communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with a documented diagnosis of Autism who require self-determination and employment readiness skills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment readiness and self-determination skills development through small group interactive learning sessions covering self-advocacy, decision-making, career interests and skills, job exploration, work expectations, employer and employee responsibilities, and job readiness
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in-person on-campus at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in Baltimore, online (no geographic restriction), and in participants' communities across Maryland
requirements_list: Documentation of Autism diagnosis
An interview with DORS Autism Services staff prior to program start
Ability to participate in all APPS programs and community activities with little supervision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain documentation of Autism diagnosis. 2. Schedule an interview with DORS Autism Services staff prior to program start. 3. Confirm ability to participate in APPS and community activities with little supervision. 4. Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services (QR code also available on program materials).

structured_extraction.program_description: Behavioral Health Services (BHS) provides support to individuals referred by DORS (Division of Rehabilitation Services) counselors who want to maintain a healthy recovery lifestyle as they work toward employment and self-sufficiency. Services include addictions assessment, behavioral health screening, counseling, consultation, and education. Health services such as diabetic assessments, education, and consultations are also offered. Services are available in person at a local DORS office, at the Work Training Center (WTC), or virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Counseling, assessment, education, and consultation services provided to DORS consumers at no cost. Services include behavioral health counseling, addictions assessment, behavioral health screening, diabetic assessments, health education, and related consultations to support employment goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers (individuals receiving vocational rehabilitation services) who are in recovery or managing chronic health conditions such as substance use, behavioral health challenges, diabetes, or other medication and physical health concerns, and who are working toward employment and self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health and health services to support recovery and employment goals, including addictions assessment, counseling, consultation, education, diabetic assessment, and health education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local DORS offices, the Work Training Center (WTC) / Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore, or virtually.
requirements_list: Must be referred by a DORS counselor (no self-referral pathway)
Must demonstrate a commitment to the recovery process
Consumers experiencing active withdrawal symptoms or with ongoing moderate-to-severe substance use will be assessed for readiness to participate and may be referred to outside treatment if not ready
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consumers must be referred by their DORS counselor to participate. No self-referral pathway or formal application form is required. Contact Michele Pinto, RN, at 410-554-9326 or Michele.Pinto@maryland.gov if already working with DORS.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-week retail training program for job seekers with disabilities who are interested in working in the retail industry. The program combines classroom instruction in a mock CVS store, hands-on learning activities at CVS stores, and a paid externship at CVS locations throughout Maryland. Participants develop skills in inventory tracking, customer service, cash register operation, and communication.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-week training program with three components: classroom study in a mock CVS store, practice in the mock store environment, and a paid externship in CVS stores throughout Maryland. Offered at the DORS Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) and select locations throughout Maryland, in partnership with Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are interested in working in the retail industry. Must be at least 16 years old (high school diploma preferred but not required), have a 6th-grade reading level, basic math skills, and an interest in retail work. Must meet physical requirements including ability to lift 25–50 lbs and stand, bend, and stoop for extended periods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retail industry skills training including inventory tracking, stock rotation, customer service, cash register skills, phone and intercom etiquette, and non-verbal communication.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the DORS WTC location and select locations throughout Maryland, in partnership with Maryland community colleges.
requirements_list: Be at least 16 years old (high school diploma preferred but not required)
Have a desire to work in retail
Have a 6th-grade reading level
Have basic math skills and ability to use a calculator
Ability to follow simple written and oral instructions
Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods of time
COVID-19 vaccination is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information, or request DORS services via the QR code on the program flyer. You may also contact DORS or a Maryland community college partner to inquire about enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS (Division of Rehabilitation Services) partners with businesses, educational institutions, and American Job Centers to design and deliver customized training programs tailored to specific employer needs. Training can take place at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center, on the job site, through an outside vendor, or a combination. Types include community college training partnerships, Registered Apprenticeships (earn-and-learn, paid work-based learning), and On-the-Job Training (OJT) placements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Customized training programs are developed to meet specific employer or industry needs. Formats include community college partnerships, Registered Apprenticeships with paid work-based learning, and on-the-job training placements where trainees learn critical tasks with the goal of employment upon completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers, including individuals with disabilities, seeking workforce training aligned with employer needs; also available to local employers seeking trained workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce skills training, including community college coursework, registered apprenticeship instruction, and on-the-job training placements in sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, and information technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; training may occur at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center or at employer job sites.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (job seeker) or an employer partnering with DORS
Training is matched to specific employer or industry sector needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers and job seekers partner with DORS, which works with businesses, educational institutions, and American Job Centers to identify needs and design appropriate training programs. Contact DORS or the Workforce & Technology Center to initiate a partnership.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Business Relations Team provides no-cost services to employers of any size or sector, including wage reimbursement for on-the-job training, ADA workplace consultation, disability awareness training, worksite assessments, recruitment assistance, tax incentive guidance, and retention services for job seekers and employees with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost services for businesses including wage reimbursement for on-the-job training (OJT), ADA workplace consultation and guidance on reasonable accommodations, worksite assessments, onsite disability awareness and sensitivity training, pre-screening of job candidates, recruitment assistance, apprenticeship liaison services, assistance with DORS-sponsored paid internships, tax incentive guidance, and retention services for employees with disabilities. 80% of DORS job seekers who become employed are still working after one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and businesses of any size or sector seeking to hire or retain individuals with disabilities, including for-profit, nonprofit, and government organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for on-the-job training; ADA workplace consultation; onsite training on disability awareness and employment practices; recruitment and candidate pre-screening services; apprenticeship liaison; paid internship support; tax incentive guidance; employee retention services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through local DORS Business Relations Representatives.
requirements_list: Business must be located in or hiring in Maryland
No cost to the employer
Business must be hiring or retaining individuals with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS Business Relations Representative for more information. General inquiries: 410-554-9408 or toll-free 888-554-0334; videophone: 443-798-2840; email dors@maryland.gov; web: www.dors.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services (RTS) – Assistive Technology, Worksite Services & Driver Rehabilitation / Vehicle Modification Services
