structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Rehabilitation Technology Services (RTS) program, operated through the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC), provides comprehensive assistive technology (AT), worksite evaluation, driver rehabilitation, and vehicle modification services to help people with disabilities get and keep jobs. RTS staff — including Rehabilitation Technologists and Occupational Therapists — deliver customized AT assessments to identify appropriate devices and software aligned with each individual's employment goals. Services include AT assessment and training (e.g., JAWS screen reading software, ZoomText magnification), provision of AT equipment such as video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software, mobile devices, hand controls for cars, ramps and stair glides, and alternative keyboards and mice. Worksite Services addresses individuals experiencing difficulty performing essential job functions due to disability-related limitations, working with individuals and their employers to identify and implement technology-based accommodations such as magnification and screen reading software, communication and assistive listening devices, adaptive keyboards, ergonomic equipment (e.g., sit-stand workstations), and physical access equipment. Driver rehabilitation services include driving assessments by certified instructors and occupational therapists, a 30-hour MVA-approved driver's education curriculum plus a 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel component (offered in person or virtually), a specialized driver's education track for individuals with autism, adapted driving training with adaptive equipment, and evaluations and provision of vehicle modifications for vehicles owned by the DORS consumer or their family. Additional services include blind and low vision services, occupational and physical therapy services, and home modification consultation. All services are provided as part of an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) through DORS. Services are delivered at the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC), in the individual's community, at the worksite, or virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS RTS staff provide: (1) customized assistive technology assessments and equipment (e.g., video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software including JAWS and ZoomText, mobile devices, hand controls, ramps and stair glides, alternative keyboards); (2) training on AT hardware and software for individuals and groups; (3) worksite job accommodation evaluations and implementation of accommodations such as magnification and screen reading software, communication and assistive listening devices, physical access equipment, sit-stand workstations, adaptive keyboards, and other ergonomic equipment; (4) blind and low vision services; (5) occupational and physical therapy services; (6) home modification consultations; (7) driving assessments by certified instructors and occupational therapists; (8) a 30-hour MVA-approved driver's education curriculum plus a 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel component, available in person or virtually, including a specialized track for individuals with autism (Track 1) and a general track for all other DORS participants with ASL interpreting available (Track 2); (9) adapted driving training on use of adaptive equipment; and (10) evaluation and provision of vehicle modifications for vehicles owned by the DORS consumer or their family. All services support employment goals and are delivered as part of an Individualized Plan for Employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking to obtain or maintain employment, including DORS consumers with an employment goal who need assistive technology, adaptive driving, vehicle modification, or worksite accommodation services; also businesses seeking to accommodate workers with disabilities. Program serves job seekers and students with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology assessments, equipment, and training to support employment goals for people with disabilities; worksite-based accommodations to enable employees with disabilities to perform essential job functions; adaptive driving services including driver's education, adapted driving training, and vehicle modifications; home modification consultation; blind and low vision services; occupational and physical therapy services — all to support employment goals for people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to DORS consumers statewide in Maryland. Services are delivered at the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in Baltimore, at the individual's worksite, in the individual's community, or virtually.
requirements_list: Must have a disability affecting communication, mobility, vision, or cognition
Must apply for DORS services and be determined eligible
Must be a DORS consumer with an employment goal
Services must be needed to help obtain or maintain employment
Driver and vehicle services must be included in the consumer's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE)
For vehicle modifications, the vehicle must be owned (not leased) by the DORS consumer or their family
A Learner's Permit is required to complete the 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel training component
For Worksite Services, must be experiencing difficulties performing job duties due to a disability-related limitation
For Worksite Services, must be referred by a DORS Counselor
For Worksite Services, a detailed description of the difficulties experienced is required
For Worksite Services, a position description is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS counselor or local DORS office, or complete the Request DORS Services form at the DORS website (also accessible via QR code in program documents). Once determined eligible, assistive technology, driver and vehicle, worksite, and other rehabilitation technology services can be added to your Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). For Worksite Services specifically, individuals must be referred by their DORS Counselor along with a detailed description of difficulties experienced and a position description. Services are accessible by enrolling as a DORS consumer with an employment goal and requesting a referral or consultation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) provides vocational rehabilitation services to active Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) consumers. Services are delivered on campus in northeast Baltimore (2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218), in the community, and virtually. The WTC offers academic tutoring and GED preparation, behavioral health services, career training programs, deaf and hard-of-hearing services, dormitory services, employment services, rehabilitation technology, and work readiness programs. Specialized services are also available for consumers who are blind or visually impaired. The WTC is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF) and offers both residential and day consumer program models.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides vocational rehabilitation services including career training, academic tutoring, GED preparation, behavioral health services, employment services, rehabilitation technology, work readiness programs, and deaf/hard-of-hearing services. Additional specialized services include apprenticeship services, autism services, center counseling and case management, enrichment services, office for blindness and vision services, and rehabilitation technology services. Services are delivered on-campus, in the community, and virtually. On-campus dormitory housing is available for consumers who cannot commute; residential consumers return home on weekends. Admission packets are available in English and Spanish, including large-print versions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active DORS consumers with disabilities, including individuals who are blind or visually impaired, individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing, and individuals with autism or behavioral health needs, seeking vocational rehabilitation, career development, and employment services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career training, academic tutoring, GED preparation, employment services, rehabilitation technology, behavioral health support, work readiness programming, apprenticeship services, autism services, enrichment services, and residential support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide in Maryland to active DORS consumers, delivered in the community, on the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore (2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218), or virtually.
requirements_list: Must be an active DORS consumer to access services
Regular, punctual attendance required (3 or more absences/tardies trigger a team conference; continued non-compliance may result in discharge)
Compliance with health and safety conduct standards (zero tolerance for weapons, drugs/alcohol, violence, sexual activity, theft, arson, and gambling)
Residential consumers must return home on weekends; departure by 4:30 p.m. Friday (effective 12/1/2024); return after 4:30 p.m. Sunday
Drug, alcohol, tobacco, vaping, and marijuana-free facility; legalized marijuana strictly prohibited
ID badge required for dining access
Service animals allowed with advance notice; emotional support animals prohibited
Compliance with mental health treatment recommendations
Participation in service plan development
Residential users must clean rooms (mandatory Wednesdays); nightly headcounts required (11:00 p.m. check-in)
Medical/social appointment documentation required upon return from absence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS counselor to access WTC services. Admission day registration includes ID badge issuance, vehicle registration, and orientation. Admission packets are available in English and Spanish, including large-print versions. Individuals interested in touring the WTC campus can call 410-554-9108 or 1-888-200-7117 or email wtc.dors@maryland.gov to make a reservation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Deaf and Hard of Hearing Unit (DHHU) Vocational Rehabilitation Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The DORS Deaf and Hard of Hearing Unit (DHHU) helps Maryland job seekers who are deaf or hard of hearing prepare for, find, and keep stable employment. The unit provides vocational rehabilitation (VR) employment services, student employment services, and Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS). Staff are fluent in American Sign Language (ASL) and knowledgeable about Deaf culture. The program also promotes self-advocacy and independence among participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: VR Employment Services including job skills training, career counseling, job coaching, job placement, and assistive technology solutions; Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) for students ages 14–21 with disabilities; Student Employment Services (SES); supported employment; interpreting services (including Video Remote Interpreting); and coordination of support services for deaf and hard of hearing job seekers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are deaf or hard of hearing seeking employment or transitioning from school to work, including students ages 14–21 with disabilities (documented via IEP, 504 plan, or medical records). Applications may be submitted by the job seeker or student themselves, a parent or family member, a medical provider, a teacher, or another representative.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment preparation, job search, job retention, Pre-Employment Transition Services, career assessment, job skills training, assistive technology, higher education support, and interpreting services for deaf and hard of hearing individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through DORS offices throughout Maryland, including a main office at 1890 North Market Street, Frederick, MD 21701. Services are also available virtually and via video phone.
requirements_list: Applicant must be deaf or hard of hearing
Applicant must be a Maryland job seeker or student transitioning from school to post-school life
Must have a physical or mental disability that seriously affects ability to work and need for employment rehabilitation services to obtain or keep a job
Deaf individuals automatically qualify for Category 2 (significantly disabled) priority level
Federal law requires DORS to serve individuals with the most significant disabilities first; those with less severe disabilities may be placed on a waiting list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Go to dors.maryland.gov and select 'Request DORS Services' to fill out the online referral form, OR contact the nearest Rehabilitation Counselor for the Deaf (RCD) by email or video phone. Step 2: Receive and complete an application packet and return it to DORS. Step 3: Schedule an intake appointment with an RCD (in-person at a DORS office or by video); applicants may bring a support person (family, friend, or advocate) and should bring employment history, education records, training records, and medical records if available. Eligibility is then determined; if eligible, applicants are categorized by disability severity level, which determines priority and potential wait-list status.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) provides driving rehabilitation and vehicle modification services for people with disabilities who need to drive to get or keep a job. Services include driving assessments by certified instructors and occupational therapists, driver's education classes (including a specialized track for individuals with autism), adapted driving training with adaptive equipment, and evaluations for vehicle modifications. These services are part of a consumer's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) through the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services include: (1) driving assessments by certified instructors and occupational therapists; (2) 30-hour MVA-approved driver's education curriculum plus a 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel component, offered in person or virtually; (3) adapted driving training on use of adaptive equipment; and (4) evaluation and provision of vehicle modifications for vehicles owned by the DORS consumer or their family. Services are provided as part of an Individualized Plan for Employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities (including those with autism and those who are deaf/hard of hearing) who need driver rehabilitation or vehicle modification services to obtain or maintain employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Driving assessment, driver's education, adapted driving training with adaptive equipment, and vehicle modification services to enable individuals with disabilities to drive to and from work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to DORS consumers statewide in Maryland. Services are delivered at the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) or through state-licensed evaluators in local communities.
requirements_list: Must apply for DORS services and be determined eligible
Driver and vehicle services must be included in the consumer's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE)
Services must be needed to help obtain or maintain employment
For vehicle modifications, the vehicle must be owned (not leased) by the DORS consumer or their family
A Learner's Permit is required to complete the 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel training component
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS office or DORS Counselor. Once determined eligible, driver and vehicle services can be added to your Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Vocational Rehabilitation Program – Employment Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), part of the Maryland State Department of Education, provides vocational rehabilitation services to Marylanders with physical or mental disabilities that seriously affect their ability to work. The program helps eligible individuals get ready to work, find a job, or stay employed through a range of support services tailored to each person's disability and employment goals. Services are developed through an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) created with a DORS counselor and include career assessment and counseling, assistive technology, vocational and college/career training, work-readiness training, job placement assistance, job coaching, higher education support, and other medical and support services. Employment Specialists match each person's skills and abilities to jobs and support Maryland businesses with recruitment, onboarding, and retention through customized training, recruitment scheduling, disability awareness education, and internship coordination. Services also include job-seeking skills training, resume and cover letter development, interview preparation, disability disclosure education, and job coaching referrals. Specialized counselors are available for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, blind or have vision loss, have a mental illness, or are students in transition (ages 14–21). Services are prioritized based on disability severity under Order of Selection: individuals with 'most significant' disabilities (substantial limitations in three or more functional areas) are served first; those with 'significant' disabilities may be placed on a waiting list. Many services are provided at no cost; others are subject to a financial need determination. Recipients of SSI or SSDI are presumed eligible and receive services at no cost. Services are delivered through DORS offices statewide, the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, in the community, and virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost individualized vocational rehabilitation and employment services including career assessment and counseling, college or career training, work-readiness training, assistive technology, job placement assistance, job coaching, higher education support, and related medical and support services. Employment Specialists provide job-seeking skills training, resume and cover letter development, interview preparation, disability disclosure education, and job coaching referrals. Maryland businesses can receive customized training, recruitment scheduling, disability awareness education, and internship coordination. Services are prioritized under Order of Selection based on disability severity: individuals with 'most significant' disabilities (limitations in three or more functional areas) are served first; those with 'significant' disabilities may be placed on a waiting list. Many services are provided at no cost; others are subject to a financial need determination. SSI/SSDI recipients are presumed eligible and receive services at no cost. Services are available through DORS offices statewide, the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, in the community, and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with a physical or mental disability (physical, emotional, intellectual, developmental, sensory, or learning disability) that seriously affects their ability to work and who need services to get, keep, or transition to employment, including those who are deaf or hard of hearing, blind or have vision loss (including ages 55+ for independent living services), have a mental illness, or are students ages 14–21 transitioning from school to work, and SSI/SSDI recipients who are presumed eligible. Also serves Maryland businesses seeking recruitment, onboarding, and disability support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career assessment and counseling, college or career training, work-readiness training, assistive technology, job placement assistance, job coaching, resume writing, interview preparation, disability disclosure education, higher education support, related medical and support services, employer recruitment support, disability awareness training, and other vocational rehabilitation support services to help people with disabilities enter or remain in the workforce.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through 20+ local DORS offices throughout the state, including the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, in the community, and virtually. Headquarters: 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218.
requirements_list: Must have a physical or mental disability that seriously affects the ability to work
Must need DORS services to help get or keep a job
Must meet DORS eligibility criteria (as determined by DORS staff)
SSI and/or SSDI recipients are presumed eligible and receive services at no cost
Priority given to individuals with 'most significant' disabilities (limitations in three or more functional areas); those with 'significant' disabilities may be placed on a waiting list
Must complete the Request DORS Services form and attend an application/intake meeting
Eligibility determination completed within 60 days of application
Must be seeking employment or assistance staying employed
Must be a job seeker with a disability who is ready to work (for Employment Services)
Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to access services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form online at dors.maryland.gov (can be submitted by the applicant, a family member, service provider, or medical provider), or contact the Division of Rehabilitation Services directly. DORS will contact you via text, email, or letter to schedule an application/intake meeting and advise what materials to bring (medical records, school records, job training records, and a list of previous jobs). At the meeting, a DORS staff member gathers information to determine eligibility. If eligible, your case is transferred to a local DORS office or placed on a waiting list. Once assigned a counselor, you will develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) together. Services may be provided by DORS staff or Community Rehabilitation Programs (CRPs). For Employment Services specifically, contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information. Applicants may bring a support person (family member, friend, or advocate) to any DORS appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pathways provides educational support services for people with Autism. It is a collaboration between DORS and community colleges throughout Maryland. Students enroll in credit/certificate classes and receive support from a DORS Pathways coordinator who works with students, families, DORS Counselors, Disability Support Services staff, and college faculty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Support services including adjustment to college life, career guidance and counseling, assessment services, employment and communication skills development, and individual and group sessions. Available at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with a documented Autism diagnosis who have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college as part of a vocational plan
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and career support services at community colleges, including adjustment to college life, assessment, career guidance and counseling, and employment and communication skills development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at community colleges throughout Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of a vocational plan
Register with the Disability Support Services program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information. Applicants must have a DORS IPE and register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) program at the participating community college.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-ETS autism programs provide Pre-Employment Transition Services to students with Autism Spectrum Disorder. The Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) track delivers classroom and community instruction in self-advocacy and social skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. The Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) track exposes students to post-secondary options including apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college, and includes a college tour. Eligible students must be age 14 to under 22 and have an IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation of an Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two program tracks for Pre-ETS students with Autism: (1) PEAS — classroom and community activities focused on self-advocacy and social skills for employment; (2) CPSEO — counseling and activities exploring post-secondary options (apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, college) plus a college tour.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) eligible students with Autism Spectrum Disorder; must be current high school, homeschool, alternative secondary, post-secondary/college, or trade school students; age 14 to under 22; must have an IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation of an Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy, social skills, and post-secondary education and employment readiness training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Pre-ETS eligible student with an Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
Must be a current high school student (including homeschool and alternative secondary programs), post-secondary/college student, or trade school student
Must be age 14 or older and under 22 years old
Must have an IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation of disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information. Applicants may also request DORS services via the QR code provided in program materials.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supported Employment for Mental & Behavioral Health Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: DORS (the Division of Rehabilitation Services) offers Supported Employment services to people with mental and behavioral health disabilities. Two tracks are available: Evidence-Based Supported Employment (using scientifically proven methods to help participants find jobs quickly based on their own work goals) and Traditional Mental Health Supported Employment (which includes broader support such as help choosing a job goal and assessing likelihood of success). In both tracks, participants receive support from a provider and a DORS counselor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing job support after employment begins, including training, supervision, and workplace adjustment assistance. Evidence-Based track focuses on quick job placement aligned with the individual's own work goals. Traditional track includes broader support for job goal selection and readiness assessment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with mental and behavioral health disabilities seeking employment support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job coaching, training, supervision, workplace adjustment support, and ongoing employment support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through DORS counselors and community rehabilitation partners
requirements_list: Must be eligible for DORS services
Must have a mental or behavioral health disability
Must be referred by a DORS counselor
May need to qualify through a mental health community rehabilitation partner (CRP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS counselor to determine eligibility. The counselor may refer the applicant to a mental health community rehabilitation partner (CRP) to assess qualification for ongoing support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). DORS works with participants to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and provides services to help them achieve and maintain employment. Services can include training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services. Participation is free and voluntary, and assigning a Ticket to DORS protects participants from Continuing Disability Reviews while they are making timely progress toward employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational rehabilitation services including training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing employment support services. The program is voluntary and at no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities ages 18–64 who receive SSDI or SSI benefits and have an employment goal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational rehabilitation services including job training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing employment support to help participants achieve and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents served by DORS. No sub-state geographic restrictions stated.
requirements_list: Must receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must be between ages 18 and 64
Must have a Ticket to Work issued by the Social Security Administration (SSA)
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS or engage with an Employment Network (EN)
Must respond to Social Security correspondence to maintain the pause on Continuing Disability Reviews
Participation is voluntary — individuals are not required to use their Ticket
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to connect with a counselor who will work with you to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). You do not need your paper Ticket to access services — DORS will work with SSA directly to verify your Ticket. Individuals may apply at any time as this is a continuous enrollment program. For national Ticket to Work information, call 1-866-YOURTICKET (1-866-968-7842), Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; TTY: 1-866-833-2967.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) provides Travel Training to help consumers learn how to use public transportation to commute between home, internship sites, and the WTC. Three tracks are offered: Individual instruction for navigating a specific route, a six-session group course tied to the Work Readiness Program, and a four-day Boot Camp group training for consumers entering a WTC core or partnership training program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free travel training provided in three formats: (1) Individual instruction for learning a specific route or destination; (2) a six-session group course for Work Readiness Program participants, including classroom instruction and a hands-on navigation session; (3) a four-day Boot Camp for consumers entering WTC training programs, held the last week of each month except May and December. All tracks include classroom instruction and hands-on experience navigating public transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers who need to learn to use public transportation to travel to and from the Workforce and Technology Center or internship sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Learning to navigate public transportation routes between home, internship sites, and the Workforce and Technology Center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is based at the DORS Workforce and Technology Center (WTC).
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Participation may occur before or during enrollment in another WTC class or program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consumers may participate in Travel Training while enrolled in another WTC program or before attending a WTC class. Contact DORS or the WTC for enrollment details.

structured_extraction.program_description: VCAMP is a virtual mentoring and support service for individuals on the autism spectrum who are attending college and not participating in the Pathways program. It helps students transition into and navigate college while developing self-advocacy and social skills. Available to students attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges who are DORS consumers and are not enrolled in the in-person Pathways program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remote mentoring program providing support to college students on the autism spectrum. Focuses on transitioning into college, navigating the college environment, and developing self-advocacy and social skills. Available to students at in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges who are not enrolled in the Pathways program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers on the autism spectrum attending college who are not participating in the Pathways program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College transition support, self-advocacy and social skills development; mentoring and skills training services delivered online
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending college in Maryland or out of state; program is delivered remotely. Restricted to students unable to access the in-person DORS Pathways program.
requirements_list: Must be on the autism spectrum
Must be attending a two- or four-year college (in-state or out-of-state)
Must not be participating in the Pathways program
Must be a DORS participant
Must have an approved Individualized Education Program (IEP) that includes college
Must participate in weekly sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information, or request DORS Services via the QR code on the program flyer.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week automotive detailing training program offered at the DORS Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore. The program prepares individuals with disabilities for entry-level detailing jobs through classroom instruction and hands-on experience, covering interior and exterior cleaning, paint correction, equipment use, and customer service skills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce & Technology Center
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 12-week course that includes videos, lectures, product demonstrations, and extensive hands-on detailing experience. Training covers customer service, interior and exterior cleaning techniques, equipment operation, chemical safety, clay bar use, scratch removal, compounding and waxing, and quality standards for high-end detail shops or dealerships.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level employment in automotive detailing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training in automotive detailing to prepare participants for employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than two points
3rd grade or higher reading comprehension level and basic math
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop, and kneel
Certain criminal backgrounds may disqualify an individual from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request DORS services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between DORS (Division of Rehabilitation Services), CVS Health, and the Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians. The program includes 14 weeks of classroom instruction, 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training, and an externship at CVS pharmacies across Maryland. Graduates are prepared to take the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) certification exam.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce & Technology Center (WTC)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational training program consisting of 14 weeks of classroom instruction at the DORS WTC facility and 6 weeks of externship at local CVS pharmacies (20 weeks total). Training covers CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements, and prepares participants for the PTCB national certification exam.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old with a high school diploma or GED and at least a 9th-grade reading and math level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training to become a Certified Pharmacy Technician, including classroom study, mock pharmacy practice, and on-the-job externship at CVS locations throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training is offered at the DORS WTC location; externship occurs at CVS pharmacies in the participant's local community throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Be at least 18 years of age and possess a high school diploma or GED
Desire to work in a retail environment and ability to provide excellent customer service
9th-grade reading comprehension level and 9th-grade math skills
Detail oriented, able to multitask, and work accurately and quickly
Efficient computer, telephone, and study skills
Pass a drug screen and background check prior to program start
Ability to lift up to 30 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods of time
Close visual acuity
COVID-19 vaccination required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request DORS services. Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements including passing a drug screen and background check before the program begins.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) provides academic assessment, Pre-GED, GED, and academic instruction services for job seekers with disabilities. Services help participants identify academic strengths and weaknesses, prepare for post-secondary training, and earn a high school diploma to pursue employment goals. Programs are offered at WTC, in the community, and virtually.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce and Technology Center
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Academic assessments (CASAS, TABE, ACCUPLACER), Pre-GED instruction (requires at least 7th grade reading and math skills), GED preparation program (requires at least 8th grade reading and math skills), and self-paced academic instruction in reading, math, and other subjects. Services are available individually, in small groups, and on a rolling admission basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who need academic assessment, GED preparation, or basic academic skills instruction to pursue employment goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic testing and assessment, GED and Pre-GED instruction, reading and math skills instruction, learner's permit instruction, and college readiness assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the WTC facility, in the community, and virtually to Maryland residents with disabilities.
requirements_list: Must be a job seeker with a disability
Pre-GED: at least 7th grade reading and math skills as recorded on CASAS or TABE
GED Program: at least 8th grade reading and math skills as recorded on CASAS or TABE
GED students are expected to take the formal GED test upon completion
Referral through a DORS counselor implied
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consumers work with their DORS rehabilitation counselors to plan for and access academic services. Programs are offered on a rolling admission basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) provides services for individuals who are blind or visually impaired to help them gain skills and technology needed for independence and employment. Services include a Low Vision Support Group (peer support meeting weekly for 8 weeks, offered 4 times per year), a Virtual Self-Advocacy Support Group for Pre-ETS and Transitioning Youth (10-week virtual sessions offered 4 times per year), and SMILE, a summer program for blind/visually impaired youth focused on career exploration, work readiness, advocacy, and independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) — Workforce and Technology Center
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free support groups and training programs delivered in-person at the Workforce and Technology Center, at local DORS offices, and virtually via Google Meet. Programs include an 8-week low vision peer support group (max 8 participants), a 10-week virtual self-advocacy group for youth (max 6 participants), and a summer program (SMILE) for transitioning youth covering career exploration, work readiness, and independence skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or visually impaired, including transitioning youth and pre-employment transition services (Pre-ETS) consumers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Skill-building for independence and employment, peer support, self-advocacy training, career exploration, and technology skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available statewide in Maryland, offered at the WTC, local DORS offices, and virtually.
requirements_list: Must be blind or visually impaired
SMILE and the Virtual Self-Advocacy Support Group are designed for Pre-ETS and transitioning youth consumers
Low Vision Support Group has a maximum capacity of 8 participants
Virtual Self-Advocacy Support Group has a maximum capacity of 6 participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS or the WTC to request enrollment. Groups are offered multiple times per year. Virtual sessions available for those unable to attend in person.

structured_extraction.program_name: OBVS Services at WTC (Orientation and Mobility, Communications, Daily Living, ABLE, and Employment Services)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Blindness and Vision Services (OBVS) provides evaluation, training, and case management services on the campus of the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) to help individuals who are blind or visually impaired live and work as independently as possible. Services include orientation and mobility training, communications skills (large print, Braille, keyboarding), household arts and daily living skills, the eight-week Adjustment to Blindness for Life & Employment (ABLE) program, interview preparation, disability advocacy, resume preparation, and pre-employment transition services for students.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), Office of Blindness and Vision Services (OBVS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational rehabilitation and independent living skills training provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center. Services include evaluation and training in orientation and mobility, communications, daily living, and employment readiness. The ABLE program runs eight weeks, four days per week (Monday–Thursday, 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.), offered twice per year in fall and spring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or visually impaired seeking to improve independent living skills and prepare for employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and evaluation services to develop orientation and mobility skills, communications skills, daily living skills, employment readiness (interview prep, resume prep, disability advocacy), and pre-employment transition services for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible Maryland residents served by DORS.
requirements_list: Must be blind or visually impaired
Must be referred through DORS vocational rehabilitation or OBVS case management
Resume Prep participants must have a current resume draft
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS or OBVS to initiate services and be referred to the WTC for evaluation and training programs.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free one-year subscription to Child Care Exchange magazine, including six issues and access to Articles on Demand. Limited to one subscription per program. Subscriptions do not auto-renew.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to Child Care Exchange magazine issues and online Articles on Demand for professional development purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) helps with public-private partnerships. MEDCO can assess if a project is workable and manage proposal requests. The agency can also issue revenue bonds and own, develop, or operate project assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. This includes evaluating project viability, managing solicitations for proposals, issuing revenue bonds, and owning, developing, or operating assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program assists county and state governments, municipalities, towns, for-profit businesses, and state universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. These services include project evaluation, solicitation management, and asset ownership, development, or operation. MEDCO can also issue revenue bonds for projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Ready Sites Program (MBRSP) aims to accelerate economic investment by growing Maryland's inventory of shovel-ready sites. It provides financial support to defray the costs of site characterization and site improvements, and offers collaborative marketing support. The program was created by Governor Wes Moore via Executive Order on December 19, 2024, and is implemented by MEDCO in coordination with state, county, and municipal economic development officials. The program focuses on site readiness as a pathway to economic competitiveness, helping prepare sites for business development and investment. Grants are awarded on a rolling basis until funds are depleted for the fiscal year, with a priority review cycle each May.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three components: (1) Site Characterization Grants — up to $10,000 (in-kind/grant) to offset the cost of retaining a site development professional to evaluate a site's development status and assign a Ready Score (1–5 tier scale); requires a 1-to-1 cash match from any source; (2) Site Improvement Grants — funding for infrastructure upgrades (due diligence, design/engineering, clearing and grading, construction), environmental remediation, and other site development needs; FY2026 grants ranged from $125,000 to $450,000, with a co-investment strategy targeting a 3:1 or 4:1 match from federal, state, local, and/or private sources expected for competitive projects; (3) Collaborative Marketing Support — publication in the MBRSP Sites Dashboard, Site Characterization Reports, and access to MEDCO's suite of services. Grants are awarded on a rolling basis until funds are depleted for the fiscal year, with a priority cycle each May; applicants submitting in May are notified of outcomes no later than July 1; applicants submitting June 1 or later are notified within 60 days of submission. Total FY2026 funding: $3.5 million.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; priority cycle each year in May
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public sector entities (counties, municipalities, and their authorities) and private sector entities that own and/or have development rights to eligible land in Maryland, as well as organizations seeking to prepare sites for economic development and business investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site characterization (retaining a site development professional to evaluate development status and future-use potential), infrastructure upgrades (due diligence, design/engineering, clearing and grading, construction), environmental remediation, and other site development improvements for high-value-added industrial or commercial use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland for eligible sites. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions stated in program guidelines.
requirements_list: Site must be a greenfield, brownfield, or redevelopment site in a pre-development phase
Site must be a minimum of 5 acres
Site must be intended solely for industrial or commercial purposes
Site must be intended to be occupied primarily by private sector companies in industries specified in the MBRSP Program Guidelines
Site must not be otherwise restricted from further development
Applicants must own and/or have development rights to the land and agree to conditions outlined in the MBRSP Program Guidelines
Site Characterization Grant requires a 1-to-1 cash match from any source
Site Improvement Grant requires a co-investment strategy targeting a 3:1 or 4:1 match from federal, state, local, and/or private sources
Ownership documentation required for approval (not required at submission for Site Characterization Grant)
Detailed project budget with timelines and deliverables required for Site Improvement Grant
All existing due diligence studies (environmental Phase 1 & 2, geotechnical, threatened/endangered species, wetlands, boundary/topo maps, PER, ALTA surveys) required for Site Improvement Grant
Letters of support from county and municipal governments required for Site Improvement Grant
Applicant must certify responses are true and agree to abide by program requirements
Site must demonstrate connection with Maryland's growth industries and emerging sectors as listed in the MBRSP Program Guidelines, or a jurisdiction-specific industry of focus
Site Improvement Grant applications must align with local or regional comprehensive plan(s)
Site must align with county/municipality economic development goals and comprehensive plans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications and supporting documents to [email protected]. Application forms for Site Characterization Grants and Site Improvement Grants are available as downloadable PDFs on the program page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a priority cycle each year in May. Applicants submitting a complete application in May will be notified of the outcome no later than July 1 of that calendar year. Applicants submitting on June 1 or later will be notified within 60 days of submission. MBRSP staff will request additional documents as needed as part of a collaborative and ongoing process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) Capital Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: MEDCO administers capital grants to fund the creation and improvement of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) — secure work environments for classified government and defense work — across Maryland. MEDCO acts on behalf of the State of Maryland, using its quasi-government nonprofit status to apply for and manage grant funding through the Maryland Department of General Services (DGS). The program supports Maryland's national security workforce and helps retain security-cleared professionals in the state, meeting growing demand for mission-critical work in the region. Funding supports the acquisition, planning, design, furnishing, and refurbishment of SCIF spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants used to acquire, plan, design, furnish, or refurbish SCIF spaces. MEDCO has awarded $5 million to date across five projects. For every dollar invested in SCIF space, an additional $2–$3 in private, nonprofit, or government match is typically generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities in Maryland seeking to build, acquire, or improve SCIF spaces to support security-cleared workforce and national security operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishing, and refurbishment of SCIF spaces; capital investment in SCIF construction or development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on regions poised to bring talent, jobs, and opportunity to the state.
requirements_list: Applicants must seek SCIF space acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishing, or refurbishment
MEDCO applies on behalf of the State of Maryland through the Maryland Department of General Services (DGS)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MEDCO navigates the application process with the Maryland Department of General Services (DGS) on behalf of recipients. Contact MEDCO for more information on how to participate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Infrastructure Loan Fund makes targeted investments into real estate and infrastructure projects that support transformative placemaking, transit-oriented development, community development, and inclusive and equitable economic growth. MEDCO serves as the link between public and private sector interests, raises capital, and builds a pipeline of project investments. The fund offers flexible financing terms to complement existing state programs supporting infill, redevelopment, and revitalization projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible-term loans intended to fill financing gaps in residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects positioned to drive community impact. Specific interest rates, loan amounts, and repayment terms are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and project sponsors pursuing real estate and infrastructure projects within Maryland Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, or Transit Oriented Development zones that support placemaking, community development, or equitable economic growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development costs, infrastructure, and other costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation of residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit Oriented Development area. Priority is given to projects that activate underutilized government or institutionally owned property, offer significant development or redevelopment value, leverage private investment, or promise significant job creation and retention.

Priority given to projects activating underutilized government or institutionally owned property
Priority given to projects with significant development or redevelopment value
Priority given to projects that leverage private investment
Priority given to projects with significant job creation or retention potential
Financing intended to fill gaps not covered by existing state programs

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Assistance (PA) Program provides supplemental federal grant funding to state agencies, local governments, and certain private non-profit organizations to support response and recovery activities following a Presidentially-declared disaster. Grants cover the repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged, publicly owned, and uninsured facilities. Funding is provided on a 75% federal / 25% applicant cost-share basis. The program helps alleviate the financial burden on state and local governments and eligible non-profit organizations following federally-declared disasters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant assistance provided at a 75% federal / 25% applicant cost-share formula. Funds are used to repair, replace, or restore disaster-damaged publicly owned or uninsured facilities across seven work categories: Category A (Debris Removal), Category B (Emergency Protective Measures), Category C (Roads & Bridges), Category D (Water Control Facilities), Category E (Buildings & Equipment), Category F (Utilities), and Category G (Parks, Recreational Facilities, and Other Facilities). Available only after a Presidential Disaster Declaration. Delivered as a formula grant with direct payment for specified use. FFY2025 small project threshold: under $1,037,000; minimum project threshold: $3,900 (adjusted annually to reflect CPI changes).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 30 days after the date the county/jurisdiction was designated for Public Assistance; RPAs submitted after this period reviewed case-by-case
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nora Lagola, State Public Assistance Officer
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, and certain private non-profit organizations (including those with IRS 501(c)(d)(e) tax exemption or state-recognized nonprofit status) in Maryland affected by a Presidentially-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged publicly owned and uninsured facilities; disaster response and recovery activities. Eligible work categories include: Category A (Debris Removal), Category B (Emergency Protective Measures), Category C (Roads & Bridges), Category D (Water Control Facilities), Category E (Buildings & Equipment), Category F (Utilities), and Category G (Parks, Recreational Facilities, and Other Facilities). Eligible costs include force account labor (regular, overtime, compensatory time), fringe benefits, equipment costs, contract costs, supplies and materials, and rented equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available only when a Presidential Disaster Declaration is in effect. Eligible areas are limited to the designated disaster areas approved under each declaration — no pre-specified county list applies. All 24 Maryland jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City) are potentially eligible depending on disaster designation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a state agency, local government, or eligible private non-profit organization (IRS 501(c)(d)(e) tax exemption or state-recognized nonprofit status)
A Presidential Disaster Declaration must be in effect under the Robert T. Stafford Act
Damages must be to publicly owned or uninsured facilities in a designated disaster area
Applicant must contribute a 25% cost share
Applicants must register through the FEMA Grants Portal
Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be submitted within 30 days from the date the county/jurisdiction was designated for Public Assistance
RPAs submitted after the 30-day deadline are reviewed by MDEM on a case-by-case basis and may be denied
MDEM reserves the right to deny any application submitted after the 30-day deadline has passed
MDEM may request an extension of the RPA filing deadline if necessary
Three State-recognized tribes in Maryland may apply as subrecipients
Debris removal on private property is generally ineligible unless widespread and posing a public health/safety/economic recovery threat (FEMA pre-approval required)
Insurance must be accounted for before FEMA reimbursement for buildings, equipment, and contents
USACE and NRCS have primary authority over flood control works; permanent repairs not eligible through PA
Restoration of engineered channels eligible only with pre-disaster capacity documentation
Subrecipients expending $750,000 or more in Federal awards must conduct audits per 2 CFR 200.302
Records must be retained for 3 years from closeout date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should create an account on the FEMA Grants Portal in advance of any disaster declaration. Following a Presidential Disaster Declaration, MDEM initiates activities and conducts an Applicants' Briefing. Applicants submit a Request for Public Assistance (RPA) through the FEMA Grants Portal within 30 days of the date their county/jurisdiction was designated for Public Assistance. After RPA submission, a Recovery Scoping Meeting is held within 21 days of an exploratory call, and a Program Delivery Manager is assigned. Applicants submit damage assessments and documentation through the FEMA Grants Portal. The State uses damage assessment data (Rapid Needs Assessment and Preliminary Damage Assessment) to support the Governor's request for federal assistance. Large projects require quarterly Project Status Reports (PSRs) due January 31, April 30, July 31, and October 31. Advance payments of up to 50% are available on request during a project. Contact the MDEM Public Assistance team for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilient Maryland Revolving Loan Fund (RLF) offers low-interest loans (no more than 1% interest) to local governments to help finance projects and activities that mitigate the effects of natural hazards. Local governments can take out loans on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities. The program was established under the Safeguarding Tomorrow Through Ongoing Risk Mitigation (STORM) Act and is designed to be accessible to underserved communities, with a goal that at least 40% of loans go to underserved recipients. Eligible natural hazards include floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, extreme heat, severe storms and storm surges, high water levels and shoreline erosion, drought, wildfires, and earthquakes. Projects in economically challenged geographic areas receive preferential interest rates (0.05%) under 42 U.S.C. §5135(f)(1)(A)(ii)(II). The program is codified in Md. Public Safety Code Ann. §14-110.4. A presidential disaster declaration is not required, nor is participation in the National Flood Insurance Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest revolving loans at no more than 1% interest rate (0.05% for projects in economically challenged geographic areas), with up to 30-year amortization. Local governments borrow on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofits, and communities for hazard mitigation and resilience projects. Loans can also be used to satisfy a local government's non-federal cost share requirement for hazard mitigation grants such as HMGP, FMA, or BRIC programs. Projects in economically challenged areas receive preferential interest rates under 42 U.S.C. §5135(f)(1)(A)(ii)(II).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — the link for local governments to submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) remains on MDEM's RLF webpage throughout the year; public comments on the Intended Use Plan historically due by May 31; specific NOFO cycles depend on FEMA annual releases. Note: FY25 NOFO was withdrawn by FEMA; Maryland did not apply for FY25 funds due to backlog from prior cycles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Maryland seeking to finance hazard mitigation and resilience projects on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofits, and communities. Priority given to jurisdictions in economically challenged geographic areas with high hazard exposure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increasing resilience and mitigating the effects of disasters including floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, extreme heat, severe storms and storm surges, high water levels and shoreline erosion, drought, wildfires, and earthquakes. May also fund low-impact development, wildland-urban interface management, conservation areas, floodplain reconnection and open space projects, building code adoption, zoning and land use planning, and satisfying non-federal cost share requirements for hazard mitigation grants (HMGP, FMA, BRIC). Examples of funded projects include detention ponds, stream restoration, and floodplain modification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to local governments. Projects in economically challenged geographic areas receive preferential loan terms (0.05% interest rate, 30-year amortization). Areas of documented focus include Howard County (Ellicott City), Montgomery County, Baltimore City, Allegany County, Frederick County, and the City of Crisfield (Somerset County).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government in Maryland
A presidential disaster declaration is NOT required
Participation in the National Flood Insurance Program is NOT required
Projects must address natural hazard mitigation or resilience
Local government must demonstrate ability to repay (underwriting required)
Compliance with 42 U.S.C. §5135, Maryland Public Safety §14-110.4, applicable NOFO requirements, and Maryland Hazard Mitigation Plan goals
Project ranking per 42 U.S.C. §5135 requirements
Alignment with Maryland's Hazard Mitigation Plan goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) via the link on MDEM's RLF webpage, which remains open throughout the year. MDEM posts an Intended Use Plan (IUP) and Project Proposal List (PPL) on the RLF webpage prior to applying for a Safeguarding Tomorrow grant from FEMA. Public comments on the IUP are accepted (historically by May 31). Contact the program at resilientloan.mdem@maryland.gov for questions. Funding availability depends on FEMA annual NOFO releases. Note: Maryland did not apply for FY25 funds due to a backlog of projects from prior cycles (FY23 and FY24); the FY25 NOFO was also withdrawn by FEMA shortly after release in December 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Management Association (MDEMA) offers five $1,500 scholarships each year to students pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in emergency management or a closely related field. One scholarship is awarded in each of Maryland's five geographic areas (Area I - Western Maryland, Area II - National Capital Area, Area III - Central Maryland, Area IV - Eastern Shore, Area V - Southern Maryland). The program aims to nurture and develop future emergency management professionals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five $1,500 scholarships are awarded annually — one per geographic area (Area I - Western Maryland, Area II - National Capital Area, Area III - Central Maryland, Area IV - Eastern Shore, Area V - Southern Maryland).
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors attending an accredited Maryland high school who have been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university, and current students enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university, who plan to pursue or are pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses for an associate or bachelor's degree in emergency management or a closely related career field.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in five geographic areas covering all of Maryland: Area I - Western Maryland, Area II - National Capital Area, Area III - Central Maryland, Area IV - Eastern Shore, Area V - Southern Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a high school senior attending an accredited Maryland high school accepted to a two- or four-year college or university planning to major in emergency management or a closely related field, OR a student currently enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.

structured_extraction.program_name: Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), through its Clean Buildings Hub initiative, provides customized one-on-one technical assistance to building owners and managers with properties covered by Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS). Assistance includes support with energy benchmarking, decarbonization planning, and multi-year retrofit planning to help building owners make informed energy investments and achieve BEPS compliance. The program is being developed through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process in partnership with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

The program is an initiative of the Clean Buildings Hub and is being developed through an RFP process in partnership with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical support with energy benchmarking, decarbonization planning, and multi-year retrofit planning to achieve BEPS compliance

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Burning Wood and Pellet Stove Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rebates for Maryland homeowners who purchase and install an eligible clean-burning wood or pellet stove at their primary residence. The stove must displace an electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating system, or an old wood or pellet stove. Rebates range from $500 for qualifying wood-burning stoves to $700 for qualifying pellet-burning stoves. The program has been permanently discontinued after FY24.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time rebate of $500 for qualifying wood-burning stoves or $700 for qualifying pellet-burning stoves. To qualify, stoves must meet EPA particulate emissions limits (no more than 3.0 g/hr for wood stoves, no more than 2.0 g/hr for pellet stoves) and have an EPA-published Higher Heating Value (HHV) efficiency rating of at least 75%.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners installing a clean-burning wood or pellet stove at their primary residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of an eligible clean-burning wood or pellet stove that displaces an electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel, or old wood/pellet heating system
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland homeowner installing stove at primary residence
Stove must displace an electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating system, or an old wood or pellet stove
Wood stove must emit no more than 3.0 grams of particulate matter per hour
Pellet stove must emit no more than 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour
Stove must have an EPA-published HHV efficiency rating of at least 75% (required beginning September 15, 2022)
Stove must have been purchased by January 4, 2024
System must be installed and application received or postmarked by March 31, 2024

Applications were processed first-come, first-served until the program budget was exhausted. The application was removed from the website on April 1, 2024. The program is permanently discontinued.
