structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) provides competitive grants to owners of Maryland-based commercial, industrial, data center, and non-profit facilities to invest in energy improvements that exceed current codes or standards. Both new construction and existing facilities qualify. There are three areas of interest: existing facilities serving general populations (AOI.1), existing facilities serving predominantly low-income populations eligible for 100% project cost coverage (AOI.2), and new construction or substantial rehabilitation (AOI.3). The program funds cost-effective energy efficiency investments to reduce operating costs and achieve energy performance that exceeds minimum codes and standards, with a 'pay for performance' grant model where grant value is a proportion of project cost varying by annual energy savings tier. Renewable energy investments are not supported.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants for energy improvement projects. The FY26 program has a total budget of $8,400,000 divided across three areas of interest. Maximum award is $500,000 per award and $2,000,000 per entity. Grants cover less than 100% of project costs in most cases; however, facilities where over 50% of clientele are from low-income populations (AOI.2) may receive 100% project cost reimbursement. Grantees may supplement a partial grant with a Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan from MEA. Renewable energy investments are not supported. Award values cannot be retroactively adjusted upward due to project cost escalation. For existing facilities, the cost basis is net total project cost (gross minus utility rebates); for new construction/rehab, the incremental cost of high-efficiency equipment vs. minimum-code alternative.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 30, 2026 at 3:00 P.M. ET (FY26); FY27 program expected to launch around September 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial, industrial, data center, and non-profit facilities in Maryland, including multifamily residential buildings with five or more units and private educational institutions. Federal agencies and GSA-owned facilities are ineligible. Publicly-funded K-12 schools are routed to a separate MEA program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements that exceed current codes or standards, including new construction, substantial rehabilitation, and improvements to existing facilities. Eligible measures include lighting/electrical improvements (LED fixtures, outdoor athletic field lighting), HVAC upgrades (air handler and compressor units, not ductwork extension), motor drives, fans, blowers, pumps, air compressors, belt drives, and conveyors. Renewable energy investments are not supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based facilities only. Applicants must be registered to do business in Maryland and be in good standing. No county or regional restrictions apply. Facilities located in utility service territories that do not offer rebates automatically receive full points in scoring. Applicants are encouraged to refer to building/energy codes enforced by the jurisdiction in which the proposed project is located.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered business entity (corporation, LLP, LLC, GP, etc.) or non-profit, registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing
Facility must be located in Maryland

Eligible facility types include manufacturing, industrial production/distribution/warehousing, data center operations, office/commercial/service/retail, private schools (Pre-K through university), multifamily residential with five or more units, and institutional human or community services
Proposed energy improvements must exceed current codes or standards
Project expenses eligible for reimbursement must be procured after the grant agreement is ratified
For 100% cost coverage (AOI.2), facility must serve a population that is more than 50% low-income as defined by at or below 80% of HUD median family income for the State of Maryland
Building must have commercial, industrial, data center, or non-profit use
Multifamily residential buildings must contain five or more units
Project must result in energy performance that exceeds current codes or standards
Renewable energy investments are not eligible
Federal agencies and GSA-owned facilities are ineligible
Publicly-funded K-12 schools are ineligible (routed to separate MEA program)
For non-profits, applicant must own the property and pay utility bills
Award values are capped at $500,000 per award and $2,000,000 per entity
Single-family homes and structures with four or fewer units are ineligible
Transportation equipment is not eligible
Solar panels and other renewable generation equipment are not eligible
Government-owned buildings are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application using the provided application form before the deadline of 3:00 P.M. ET on the closing date. The FY26 application template is designed to collect data for one building. Applications are scored by MEA using scoring templates for each Area of Interest, evaluating quality of documentation and magnitude of environmental benefits including measurable GHG emission reductions. Awards are issued in rank order until the program budget is exhausted. Applicants seeking a loan to cover remaining costs should submit a Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan application at the same time. MEA coordinates with utility EmPOWER implementers; rebates and grants are determined independently.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial and Canopy Solar Program (CCSP) provides grant funding to support solar energy installations on commercial properties in Maryland, including rooftop-mounted systems, ground-mounted systems, and solar canopies over parking areas or bodies of water. The program has two areas of interest: Area 1 targets nonprofits, Small Business Enterprises (SBEs), and veteran-owned businesses to expand equitable solar access; Area 2 serves Maryland businesses and organizations that own or operate eligible facilities. Both purchased and third-party owned solar energy systems are eligible. The program is statewide and non-competitive, awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. This program supersedes the former standalone Solar Canopy and Dual Use Technology Grant Program; solar canopy funding is now incorporated into this program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are calculated by formula based on area of interest, solar installation type, and system capacity. Area of Interest 1 (Equitable): Non-canopy systems — $2,000/kWDC or 90% of total project cost, whichever is lower; canopy systems — $2,500/kWDC or 90% of total project cost, whichever is lower. For third-party owned systems: non-canopy — $750/kWDC; canopy — $1,000/kWDC. Area of Interest 2 (Sustainability): Non-canopy — $1,700/kWDC or 75% of total project cost, whichever is lower; canopy — $2,125/kWDC or 75% of total project cost, whichever is lower. Third-party owned: non-canopy — $750/kWDC; canopy — $1,000/kWDC. Maximum grant award is $500,000 per property owner. Total FY26 program budget is $13,000,000. Grants are disbursed in two milestones: 30% at groundbreaking and the remainder at project completion. Third-party owned systems must guarantee 20% electricity cost savings over the agreement life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofits, Small Business Enterprises (SBEs), veteran-owned businesses, multifamily building owners serving low-to-moderate income tenants, and other businesses and organizations that own or operate commercial facilities; solar PV system purchasers and third-party owned solar energy system participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of rooftop-mounted solar PV systems, ground-mounted solar systems, and solar canopies over parking areas or bodies of water on commercial properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Applicants must be registered to operate in Maryland. Facilities must be geographically located within the State of Maryland and in a community classified as low-to-moderate income or overburdened, following definitions and boundaries established under State Government Article §9‑20B‑05(i)(1). Eligible census tracts can be verified using resources listed on the Census Tracts and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) Alternative Compliance Payment page.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit, Small Business Enterprise (SBE), or veteran-owned business (Area of Interest 1), or a Maryland business or organization owning or operating an eligible facility (Area of Interest 2)
Applicant must be registered to operate in Maryland
Solar PV system must be rooftop-mounted, ground-mounted, or a solar canopy over parking or bodies of water
Participating parking facilities must be 'EV ready' (per 2024 IECC Appendix CG101.2.3, minimum 4 EV-ready spaces)
Both purchased and third-party owned solar energy systems are eligible
Maximum grant award is $500,000 per property owner
Project facility must be located in a low-to-moderate income or overburdened community as defined by eligible census tracts
Cost match required (percentage varies by Area of Interest and project type)
Third-party owned systems must guarantee 20% electricity cost savings over the agreement life
For multifamily properties: rent freeze required for 2 years post-installation; new owner must honor agreement if property transfers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through MEA's JotForm Portal (https://form.jotform.com/marylandenergy/FY26-commercial-and-canopy-solar) on a first-come, first-served basis until funding is depleted or the deadline of February 11, 2026 is reached. The portal was previously closed due to FY26 funding being fully requested; applicants should check back for updates on whether the portal reopens.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community EVSE Grant Program provides grants to increase access to affordable and reliable electric vehicle (EV) charging networks and reduce transportation greenhouse gas emissions throughout Maryland, especially in overburdened, low-and-moderate income, and underserved communities. The program has two Areas of Interest (AOI): AOI 1 provides funds to help local governments offset feasibility and planning study costs for future EV charging infrastructure development; AOI 2 provides funds to offset costs of installing Level 2 or Level 3 (including Direct Current Fast Charging) EV charging equipment. Eligible applicants may apply to one or both areas of interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEA anticipates $10 million total available for FY 2026: $500,000 for AOI 1 (EV Infrastructure Planning) and $9,000,000 for AOI 2 (EVSE Installations). Awards are competitive and the total amount awarded may vary depending on available funds and the number and quality of applications received. Grants are reimbursement-based and support installation of EV charging infrastructure in low-and-moderate income, overburdened, and underserved communities. AOI 1 supports community-level planning feasibility studies and site-specific engineering/load analyses. AOI 2 supports purchase and installation of Level 2 or Level 3 (including DC Fast Charging) EV charging equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 27, 2026 at 3:00PM EST (AOI 2 deadline extended from February 25, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, businesses, nonprofits, higher education institutions, and other eligible applicants seeking to plan or install EV charging infrastructure in Maryland, with a focus on overburdened, low-and-moderate income, and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AOI 1: Community-level EV infrastructure planning feasibility studies; site-specific engineering designs, load analyses, site surveys, and associated services. AOI 2: Purchase and installation of Level 2 or Level 3 (including DC Fast Charging) EV charging equipment; contractor/subcontractor labor; permits and inspections; utility service upgrades at sites in or accessible to low-and-moderate income, overburdened, and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with emphasis on overburdened, low-and-moderate income, and underserved communities. Overburdened communities are defined as census tracts with 3 or more environmental health indicators above the 75th percentile statewide per Maryland's Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022 (identifiable via the MDEnviroscreen Tool). AOI 2 also gives preference to projects in areas more than 50 miles from existing charging infrastructure.
requirements_list: Applicants may apply to one or both Areas of Interest
AOI 1 is open to local governments (all counties including Baltimore City, and incorporated towns and cities in Maryland)

AOI 2 is open to businesses and LLCs registered with Maryland SDAT, incorporated nonprofits in good standing with SDAT, Maryland institutions of higher education accredited by Middle States, local education agencies, units of municipal or county governments, and Maryland-recognized Tribal governments
Residential homeowners (4 units and under) and regulated energy utilities are ineligible for AOI 2

Budget Workbook with breakdown of grant and leveraged funds is required
Budget Narrative is required

AOI 1: Project partner qualifications must be identified
AOI 1: Track record of community engagement required
AOI 1: Historic success serving overburdened communities preferred
Project completion deadline: 24 months from grant agreement execution date
No reimbursement for costs incurred before grant agreement execution unless MEA agrees in writing
No double-funding: applicant cannot receive another grant for the same project if previously funded by MEA
AOI 2: EVSE must accept multiple payment forms (not phone app only)
AOI 2: 97% uptime requirement for installed EVSE
AOI 2: ADA compliance required where feasible
AOI 2: IRS Form W-9 required
AOI 2: Certificate of Status from Maryland SDAT required (if applicable)
AOI 2: Project Narrative (maximum 10 pages) required covering applicant overview, project scope, timeline, and partners
AOI 1: Project Narrative (maximum 7 pages) required
Authorized representative of applicant must sign application
See the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for each AOI for full eligibility, project requirements, incentive amounts, and evaluation criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application via JotForm for AOI 1 (https://form.jotform.com/transportationmea/FY26-C-EVSE-AOI1) and/or AOI 2 (https://form.jotform.com/transportationmea/FY26-C-EVSE-AOI2-Installations). AOI 1 application requires a 7-tab JotForm submission including: applicant information, W-9, project narrative (max 7 pages), budget workbook, optional letters of support, acknowledgment of general provisions and confidentiality statement, and authorized signature. AOI 2 requires an 8-tab JotForm submission including: project narrative (max 10 pages), design drawings, equipment specs, budget workbook, vendor quotes, SDAT Certificate of Status, IRS Form W-9, and optional letters of support. Applications undergo a three-step review: eligibility screening, individual evaluation team scoring, and group review and recommendations. Evaluation criteria for AOI 2 include: Overall Project Feasibility (30%), Project Justification (20%), Budget & Cost Effectiveness (20%), Additional Programmatic Factors (20%), and Applicant Qualifications & Experience (10%). Selection notifications are expected Summer 2026. Review the FOA and Application Instructions for each AOI before applying. Deadline was February 27, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Solar Low-to-Moderate Income Power Purchase Agreement Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPA), enabling community solar projects to offer clean energy to low-income, overburdened, and underserved households at a lower cost. The program is statewide and competitive, with two areas of interest (AOI-1 and AOI-2) funded at different levels. Approximately $17 million in total funding is available from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding. AOI-1 receives $5 million and AOI-2 receives $12 million. AOI-2 projects must be sited on a Maryland landfill, rubble-fill, or brownfield site. The evaluation team may adjust rankings to ensure at least one project is available to low-income subscribers in each utility service territory. Residents do not receive funds directly from the Maryland Energy Administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $17 million in total funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding. AOI-1 receives $5 million and AOI-2 receives $12 million. Grants offset PPA costs for Community Solar Subscriber Organizations serving low-income households, enabling lower subscription rates for low-income subscribers. Disbursement is milestone- and completion-based. Any project funded must be completed, including all milestones and required reporting documents, by no later than May 30, 2030. Residents do not receive funds directly from MEA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3:00 P.M. ET, Tuesday, December 23, 2025 (FY26 cycle); grant agreement execution expected by May 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Solar Program Subscriber Organizations registered with the Maryland Public Service Commission seeking to provide discounted solar energy to low-income Maryland households through Power Purchase Agreements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) to enable community solar energy to be offered to low-income households at lower cost, thereby lowering community solar subscription rates for low-income subscribers. Funds may be used for community solar project development and capital costs, including installation and operation of solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays under the Maryland Community Solar Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Project site(s) and benefiting location(s) must be within Maryland. AOI-2 projects must be sited on a Maryland landfill, rubble-fill, or brownfield site. Eligibility is available within participating utility service territories statewide; evaluation team may adjust rankings to ensure at least one project is available to low-income subscribers in each utility service territory, including Potomac Edison service territory.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Solar Program Subscriber Organization registered with the Maryland Public Service Commission
Applicant must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing
Project must serve low-income households through a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA)
Project site(s) and benefiting location(s) must be located within the State of Maryland
AOI-2 projects must be sited on a Maryland landfill, rubble-fill, or brownfield site
Applicant must demonstrate 20-year site control
Project must guarantee 20-year savings for low-income subscribers
At least 80% of workers participating in the project must reside within 50 miles of the project (per §9-20B-05 of the State Government Article)
A NABCEP Solar PV Installation Professional (PVIP) or PV Design Specialist (PVDS) certified individual must be involved in design and/or installation
Components must comply with IEEE 1547, National Electric Code, and be listed/labeled by a recognized national testing laboratory
Application must be submitted by the deadline for either AOI-1 or AOI-2
Any project funded must be completed, including all milestones and required reporting documents, by no later than May 30, 2030
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application Worksheet FY26 and submit required documents including the application checklist for AOI-1 or AOI-2 by the deadline. Applicants must review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FY26, effective July 3, 2025) and use the provided application worksheet and checklists to apply. Post-award, grantees must submit completion certificates, attestations, and invoices per the FY26 grant agreement terms. Contact Program Manager David Comis for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), in partnership with the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC), provides grants to Local Education Agencies (LEAs, also known as school districts) to help them develop capacity and advance strategies for clean and efficient energy use in their K-12 schools and support facilities. The program covers four Areas of Interest (AOIs): (1) Capacity Building for Energy Management, Efficiency, Sustainability, and Portfolio Planning; (2) Energy Efficiency upgrades; (3) Solar on Schools installations; and (4) Net Zero Energy Schools design. Applicants may apply for one or multiple AOIs, for their entire district, a large multi-facility subset, or individual school facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $36 million in total grant funding is available from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, Climate Action Plan, and Alternative Compliance Program. AOI 1 (Capacity Building) has $1,500,000 available ($1,000,000 for Category 1, $500,000 for Category 2), with awards scaled by LEA student enrollment. AOI 2 (Energy Efficiency) has $15,000,000 available ($10M from Strategic Energy Investment Fund; $5M from Dedicated Purpose Account), with a minimum award of $50,000 and maximum of $3,000,000, reimbursing up to 75% of total project cost (applicants must match remaining 25%). Individual grant performance periods range from 24–27 months (energy efficiency) to 72–75 months (net zero energy schools). Funding is awarded on a formula and competitive basis with consideration of need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs/school districts) operating K-12 public schools in Maryland. Applications must be submitted by the LEA directly; third parties may not submit on behalf of an LEA. Must be signed by an LEA officer with authority to commit the agency (e.g., Chair of Board of Education, Chief Financial Officer, General Manager).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy data management, utility bill management strategies, energy policy development, net zero energy design considerations for school portfolio planning, solar installations on school buildings, energy efficiency upgrades (including electrification of HVAC/boilers/chillers, building envelope improvements, building controls, lighting upgrades, and incremental costs for new construction above code), and Net Zero Energy school design, construction, and post-occupancy commissioning in K-12 public schools and support facilities. Fossil-fuel or combustion technologies are ineligible except in limited circumstances with written MEA approval. For AOI 3 (Solar on Schools) and AOI 2 (Energy Efficiency), priority is given to schools in census tracts designated as overburdened or with median income at or below 80% of state median income, or schools where 50%+1 of enrolled students come from qualifying census tracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; all Maryland LEAs are eligible to apply. For AOI 2 (Energy Efficiency) and AOI 3 (Solar on Schools), schools must be located in census tracts designated as overburdened or with median income at or below 80% of state median income per §9-20B-05 of the State Government Article, Annotated Code of Maryland, or must demonstrate that ≥50%+1 of enrolled students come from qualifying census tracts. Reference tools include the Maryland Department of Environment's MDEnviroScreen Tool and MEA's approved census tract list.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (school district) in Maryland
Applications must be submitted by the LEA directly; third parties may not submit on behalf of the LEA
Applications may cover entire school district, a significantly sized multi-facility subset, or individual school facilities
Applicants may apply for one or multiple Areas of Interest (AOIs)
Must be signed by an LEA officer with authority to commit the applicant (e.g., Chair of Board of Education, Chief Financial Officer, General Manager)
A designated LEA staff person is required for ongoing oversight and continuity
For AOI 2 and AOI 3, schools must be in qualifying census tracts (overburdened or ≤80% of state median income) or serve a student population where ≥50%+1 come from qualifying census tracts
Electronic payment via ACH/Direct Deposit (Form X-10) required post-award
AOI 1 Category 1 is open to all LEAs, including those previously awarded funding in previous years
For AOI 4 (Net Zero Energy Schools), applicants new to the NZE planning process are encouraged to apply for AOI 1 funding first in FY26 and AOI 4 in subsequent years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by the deadline of November 21, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET. Applications may be submitted via online JotForm at https://form.jotform.com/251605585653159 or as a PDF via email to Schools.MEA@Maryland.gov. The Word document version of the application is provided for reference only; actual submission must be via JotForm portal. Alternative submission arrangements require at least 14 days advance notice to MEA. Program documents including AOI-specific guidelines, application form (Word Doc), project budget (Excel), and general provisions are available on the program page. A webinar was held on 09/09/2025. Contact Kristen Keim at schools.mea@maryland.gov or 443-571-6976 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The FY26 Maryland Electric School Bus Grant Program provides competitive grants to help public school districts and their private bus vendors purchase or lease electric school buses. The program directs $4.9 million toward eligible vehicles used for student transportation, with a strong focus on expanding access for overburdened and low-to-moderate income communities, including Title I schools. Funding covers up to 120% of the incremental cost of eligible electric school buses, plus charging infrastructure installation and associated costs, EVSE and facility planning, and technician training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000,000 per applicant (up to $2,500,000 for qualifying school districts based on income and district size) covering up to 120% of the incremental cost of new electric school buses, plus eligible charging infrastructure equipment and installation costs, EVSE and facility planning (up to $300,000), technician training (up to $7,200 for six technicians), and other associated costs. Total MEA and other state/federal incentives may not exceed the total project cost. $4.9 million is available in FY26. Funding is described as one-time funding to advance implementation of the Climate Solutions Now Act, with a total state commitment of $17 million across FY25 and FY26.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and fleets or private school bus vendors operating on behalf of LEAs to purchase school buses for Maryland public school students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or lease of new electric school buses for student transportation; eligible charging infrastructure equipment and installation costs; EVSE and facility planning (up to $300,000); technician training (up to $7,200 for six technicians); other associated costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Priority given to overburdened and low-to-moderate income communities facing economic challenges, and Title I schools.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public Local Education Agency (LEA) or a fleet/private school bus vendor operating on behalf of an LEA with a contract in place.
Vehicles must be purchased new — retrofits or repowered vehicles are not eligible.
Vehicles must be publicly funded and procured for routine transportation of students for school or school-related activities.
A vehicle already funded in whole or in part by another Maryland State grant is not eligible.
Combined MEA and other state/federal incentives may not exceed the total funding request or project cost.
Community partner collaboration required.
Cost documentation required if using other Maryland state funding.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application via the Jotform online application form by December 26, 2025 at 3:00PM ET. Full instructions and required attachments (including the Electric School Bus Summary Table and EVSE Summary Table) are provided in the FY26 FOA. Applications are evaluated on a competitive basis with priority given to Title I schools and overburdened/low-to-moderate income communities; criteria include fleet management concept plans. Applicants may contact MEA for 1-on-1 meetings or calls to discuss the application. Reimbursement and reporting are handled through separate Jotform links after award. Any updates (e.g., deadline extensions) will be posted on the Program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers rebates to support the acquisition and installation of qualified electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE), also known as EV charging stations, for both residential and commercial/business settings. For individuals, the rebate covers up to 50% of the purchase and installation costs of a qualifying home EV charger, capped at $700 per charger. For businesses and non-profits, the rebate covers up to 50% of the purchase and installation costs, capped at $5,000 per charger. Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023 is not eligible for a rebate. The total budget for fiscal year 2026 is $2.5 million, distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until program funds are exhausted. The program aims to reduce the upfront cost of EV charging infrastructure and increase EV adoption in support of the state's EV deployment and greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rebates for buying and installing EV charging stations. For residential projects, the rebate covers 50% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $700 per charger. For commercial projects (businesses, non-profits, government, and other commercial entities), the rebate covers 50% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $5,000 per charger. Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023 is not eligible for a rebate. The total budget for fiscal year 2026 is $2.5 million, distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-come, first-served until program funds are exhausted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents purchasing and installing a home EV charger, as well as businesses, non-profit organizations, higher education institutions, and government entities purchasing and installing commercial EV charging equipment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of qualifying EV charging stations (EVSE)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Equipment must be a qualified/eligible electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) model
Rebate covers up to 50% of purchase and installation costs
Maximum rebate for individuals is $700 per charger
Maximum rebate for businesses and non-profits is $5,000 per charger
Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023 is not eligible for a rebate
Funding is distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until program funds are exhausted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, read the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) carefully. The agency prefers online submission through the MyMEA portal. Commercial and residential application guides are available on the MEA website to assist with the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program operated by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides funding to community-serving buildings in Maryland. The program helps facilities replace fossil fuel-powered equipment with efficient electric alternatives, covering a portion of upfront building electrification costs. Eligible upgrades include heat pumps (air-source, water-source, ground-source), electric water heaters, electric appliances, building envelope improvements, and electrical panel upgrades. Eligible buildings include hospitals, medical facilities, multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities, schools, houses of worship, colleges, K-12 private or charter schools, pre-schools and daycare centers, nonprofits, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, private libraries, grocery stores, volunteer fire stations, performing arts centers, and state agencies. The program is part of Governor Moore's $50 million commitment to electrify hospitals, schools, multi-family housing, and other community buildings.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants from a total FY2026 budget of approximately $6,855,822. Minimum grant award is $25,000; maximum grant award is $1,500,000. MEA reimburses up to 50% of total project costs after utility incentives are applied. Funds are disbursed quarterly as reimbursement only (no upfront funding). Eligible projects include heat pumps (air-source, water-source, ground-source), electric water heaters, electric dryers, hot water/chilled water/steam management systems, ENERGY STAR electric appliances, building envelope improvements (insulation, air sealing), building controls, and electric panel and wiring upgrades. Project completion timeline is 24–27 months from grant agreement execution. Funds are limited to physical construction activities and purchase of materials/equipment; cannot supplant existing activities or offset pre-agreement costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of community-serving buildings in Maryland, including hospitals, medical facilities, houses of worship, universities, colleges, K-12 private or charter schools, preschools, daycare centers, nonprofits, community-based organizations, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, private libraries, grocery stores, volunteer fire stations, performing arts centers, state agencies (for state-owned or leased facilities), and multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building electrification upgrades including electric heat pumps (air-source, water-source, ground-source), electric water heaters, electric dryers, hot water/chilled water/steam management systems, ENERGY STAR electric appliances, building envelope improvements (insulation, air sealing), building controls, and electric panel and wiring upgrades. Funds are limited to physical construction activities and purchase of materials/equipment; cannot supplant existing activities or offset pre-agreement costs. Funds are disbursed as reimbursement only (no upfront funding).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. No geographic restrictions on eligible buildings. Priority scoring given to buildings located in overburdened census tracts as identified via the MDEnviroScreen Tool and Maryland statute § 1-701.
requirements_list: Building must be a community-serving building (hospitals, medical facilities, multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities, schools, houses of worship, colleges, preschools, daycare centers, nonprofits, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, private libraries, grocery stores, volunteer fire stations, performing arts centers, state agencies)
Project must facilitate efficient electrification of existing building systems
Funds cannot supplant existing activities or offset pre-agreement costs
Applications must be submitted electronically via JotForm by December 31, 2025 at 5:00pm EST; MEA will not accept any application packages after this deadline under any circumstances
Alternate submission arrangements available with 14+ days' notice to contact email or phone
Grant covers up to 50% of total project costs after utility incentives are applied
Minimum grant request is $25,000; maximum grant request is $1,500,000
Project must be completed within 24–27 months of grant agreement execution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a competitive grant application electronically via JotForm. A PDF Reference application form and Project Budget Template are available for preparation purposes only (the PDF form will not be accepted as a submission). Applicants can use the Energy Impact Calculator to estimate project impacts. Alternate submission arrangements must be requested at least 14 days in advance by contacting the program manager. Applications were due December 31, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: EmPOWER Maryland is a statewide energy efficiency program created by the EmPOWER Maryland Energy Efficiency Act of 2008. Maryland's largest electric and gas utilities offer incentives to help households and businesses save energy and money. Incentives include free or discounted energy audits, weatherization, and efficient appliances. Recent legislative updates require utilities to add incentives for switching from fossil fuel heating and appliances to electric alternatives, and remove incentives for natural gas upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Utilities offer a variety of incentives including free or discounted energy audits, weatherization assistance, and rebates or discounts on efficient appliances. The specific amounts and terms vary by utility and program track.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland households and businesses served by the five largest investor-owned electric utilities and Choptank Electric Cooperative
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including weatherization, energy audits, and efficient appliances; switching from fossil fuel heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to customers of participating utilities in Maryland: BGE, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power & Light, PEPCO, Washington Gas Light, and Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative (SMECO), and Choptank Electric Cooperative
requirements_list: Must be a customer of a participating EmPOWER utility in Maryland
Specific eligibility requirements vary by utility and program offering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact their utility provider directly. Each utility administers its own EmPOWER portfolio programs. Links to each utility's program pages are provided on the EmPOWER Maryland page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Energy Efficiency Equity Grant Program (EEE Program) is a competitive grant program offered by the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) to nonprofit organizations and local government entities. It supports energy efficiency projects and related activities that benefit Maryland residents with low to moderate incomes. Grants fund energy efficiency projects that generate significant reductions in energy usage and pass the benefits to income-qualifying residents. Program funding is allocated regionally based on the number of low- and moderate-income households in each region using US Census data. Note: the program page states the EEE Program is permanently closed and directs visitors to the newly created Residential Energy Equity Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded for energy efficiency projects. The FY25 program had an anticipated total budget of $11.2 million, allocated regionally across Maryland. Grants generate significant reductions in energy usage for income-qualifying residents.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Angel Saules, Program Manager for Energy Equity Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local government entities serving Maryland residents with low to moderate incomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency projects that generate significant reductions in energy usage and pass benefits to income-qualifying residents. Eligible project types include whole house retrofits, whole building commercial work, limited upgrades to residential-commercial buildings, and incremental new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; funding is allocated regionally based on the number of low- and moderate-income households per region.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization or local government entity
Projects must benefit Maryland residents experiencing low to moderate income
Projects must generate significant reductions in energy usage
Nonprofit applicants must disclose any closely affiliated relationships with for-profit entities proposed to participate in program-funded activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download, review, and complete the FY25 MEA EEE Program Application (Excel spreadsheet). Submit required application documents as specified in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA), including savings estimates and assumptions and, if applicable, a conflict of interest disclosure form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grants (EECBG)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEA received a federal Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant (EECBG) award from the U.S. Department of Energy and is directing those funds as competitive subgrants to Maryland counties and incorporated local governments that did not receive a direct EECBG grant from DOE. Grants support energy planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits and feasibility studies, and expansion or revision of existing energy plans and strategies. MEA is also using a portion of its allocation to fund community energy liaisons to help local governments develop energy efficiency and decarbonization strategies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive subgrants ranging from $100,000 to $350,000, with larger awards possible for exceptional proposals. Total available funding is up to $1,462,617. No matching funds required. Awards are subject to funding availability and relevant statutory requirements. Planning projects only: energy efficiency planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, and expansion/revision of existing energy plans. Capital expenditures are not covered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and incorporated units of local government that did not receive a direct EECBG formulaic allocation from the U.S. Department of Energy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits and feasibility studies, and expansion or revision of existing energy plans and strategies. Planning projects only — no capital expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to counties and incorporated units of local government in Maryland that did not receive a direct EECBG formulaic grant from DOE. Ineligible counties (received direct DOE funding): Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Carroll, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's. Regional allocations apply — see the Funding Opportunity Announcement for details.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county or incorporated unit of local government
Applicant must not have received a direct EECBG formulaic grant from DOE
No matching funds required
Proposals must align with eligible activities: energy planning, decarbonization strategy, energy audits/feasibility studies, or expansion of existing energy plans
Planning projects only; no capital expenditures
Complete applications only (incomplete applications are ineligible)
Execute Grant Agreement within 10 business days of award
Submit reimbursement requests within 60 days of project completion
Retain all documentation for 3 years from final reimbursement
Comply with all applicable environmental laws and building codes
Maintain $1M minimum liability insurance with State as additional insured
80% of workers must reside within 50 miles of project or within Maryland
Historic preservation review required before construction
Davis-Bacon prevailing wage requirements apply to construction work over $2,000
Buy America requirements apply for infrastructure materials
No lobbying of Congress with award funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application using the MEA EECBG Application Form (available online via JotForm or as a PDF). Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement for complete instructions, regional allocations, and eligibility details. Direct questions to msec.mea@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY23 Data Center Energy Efficiency Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers grants for clean energy projects in Maryland data centers. The program helps these facilities install cost-effective, energy-efficient technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The total program budget for fiscal year 2023 was $2.4 million. This funding was split between the commercial, industrial, non-profit sector and the agricultural sector.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves businesses, manufacturers, data centers, nonprofit organizations, private schools, privately-owned colleges and universities, and agricultural businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support clean energy projects and the installation of cost-effective energy efficiency technologies.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit the program's application form. The agency reviews applications on a first-come, first-served basis until all funds are awarded or the deadline passes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Energy (RISE) Program provides competitive grants to help fund improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure. The program aims to enhance the resilience and reliability of the electric grid through non-generation measures, addressing threats such as severe weather, cyberattacks, physical attacks, and aging components. The program supports Governor Moore's goal of reaching 100% clean energy by 2035.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling approximately $15,000,000 in federally-funded assistance. Individual grants up to $3,000,000. Cost-match requirements vary by applicant size and Area of Interest (AOI 1: 100% match; AOI 2 requirements vary). A minimum 15% non-federal share is required for all recipients; eligible entities performing resilience projects require 100% match (or 1/3 if entity sells 4,000,000 MWh/year or less). Grants fund improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure. Payment is made via reimbursement through the ASAP system. Final grant amounts are subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland electric grid operators, electricity storage operators, electricity generators, transmission owners/operators, distribution providers, fuel suppliers, and other relevant entities as determined by the U.S. Secretary of Energy
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure; enhancing resilience and reliability of the electric grid through non-generation measures. Allowable activities include weatherization, fire-resistant technologies, monitoring and control systems, undergrounding, utility pole management, power line relocation/reconductoring with advanced conductors, vegetation management, microgrids, battery storage (for adaptive capacity), hardening, and conductor replacement. Technical assistance (up to 5% of annual amounts) and subawards to eligible entities are permitted. Construction signage (DOE 'Investing in America' signage) is an allowable cost. Land acquisition is not permitted. Prohibited uses include new generation facilities, large-scale battery storage (unless for adaptive capacity), and cybersecurity measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — project site(s) must be located within the State of Maryland. To enhance geographic diversity and help meet federal Justice40 outcomes, MEA may consider a project's geographic location within the State when evaluating grant awards. Projects in Low-to-Moderate-Income Opportunity areas (LMIOU) and Justice40 communities receive scoring preference.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible Maryland electric grid operator or related stakeholder as defined in Section 40101(d) of the federal Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (electricity grid operator, electricity storage operator, electricity generator, transmission owner or operator, distribution provider, fuel supplier, or other entity approved by U.S. DOE)
Must meet federal requirements in addition to Maryland requirements
Eligible activities must generally focus on enhancing resilience and reliability of the electricity grid through non-generation measures
Minimum 15% non-federal cost match required; entities performing resilience projects may require up to 100% match (or 1/3 if selling 4,000,000 MWh/year or less)

Must complete Project Budget Workbook

Must complete Application Form
All costs must be incurred after grant agreement execution
SAM registration and maintenance required (prime recipient); unique entity identifier required for subrecipients
Must qualify as a domestic entity (organized/chartered/incorporated under US state/territory law, majority US ownership/control, physical US place of business)
NEPA compliance required (Categorical Exclusion or EA/EIS as applicable)
Federal, state, and municipal permit compliance required
100% direct labor costs must be in the United States (or DOE-approved exception)

See the Funding Opportunity Announcement for full terms, conditions, requirements, and restrictions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the FY25 Maryland RISE Application Form and Project Budget Workbook. Submit application by the deadline of 3:00 P.M. ET on January 21, 2025. Full instructions are provided in the Funding Opportunity Announcement. Contact MEA at GridResilience.MEA@Maryland.gov or 410.537.4000 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) Geothermal Rebate Program provides rebates to Maryland residents who install new geothermal heating and cooling (GHC) systems on residential properties. Eligible properties include single-family detached homes and single-family townhomes; multi-family properties are not eligible. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis for complete and eligible applications. FY26 is the final year of this program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A flat rebate of $3,000 is awarded for installation of a new geothermal heating and cooling system. Rebates are non-competitive and awarded first-come, first-served until the $150,000 FY26 budget is exhausted. As of January 6, 2026, the JotForm application portal is closed to new applications while MEA processes the existing queue.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 27, 2026 or until the budget is exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents installing new geothermal heating and cooling systems on single-family detached homes or single-family townhomes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of a new geothermal heating and cooling system on a Maryland residential property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents on Maryland residential properties statewide
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident
Property must be a single-family detached home or single-family townhome (multi-family properties not eligible)
System must be a new geothermal heating and cooling (GHC) system
Application must be complete and eligible
Application must be submitted by February 27, 2026 or until the budget is exhausted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the FY26 Geothermal Rebate Program Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) in full, then submit an application through the JotForm Application Portal. Note: as of January 6, 2026, the portal is closed to new applications while MEA processes the existing queue. Check back for updates on portal status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Higher Education Clean Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers competitive grants to Maryland's accredited two- and four-year colleges and universities to support solar installations, strategic sustainability and clean energy campus planning, clean energy curriculum development, and workforce training. The program aims to create energy-efficient campuses that serve as practical learning environments and hubs for renewable energy education and job creation. It also supports adopting on-site renewable energy technologies, integrating strategic energy planning into operations and academic curricula, and advancing workforce development in the renewable energy sector.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling up to $8,000,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). Maximum funding per application for solar installation is capped at $1 million. Solar installations funded at up to $2,500/kW (or $3,000/kW case-by-case) for applicant-purchased systems; up to $600/kW for 3rd-party-owned systems. For each applicant, maximum funding is $145,000 for campus clean energy master planning (first-time grantees only), $145,000 for clean energy sector course development, and $25,000 for student internships. Award amounts in prior cycles ranged from $414,300 to $1,315,000. Applicants may submit one or more applications. Funds support renewable energy adoption, strategic energy planning, and renewable energy workforce development. Ineligible activities include fossil fuel, natural gas, or combustion technologies and expansion of fossil fuel infrastructure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland accredited two- and four-year colleges and universities (Institutions of Higher Education accredited by the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools, Commission on Higher Education). Community colleges located in census tracts with median income ≤80% of state median income, overburdened communities, and underserved communities receive special competitive consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar system installations, strategic sustainability and clean energy campus planning, clean energy curriculum development, student workforce training and internships, on-site renewable energy adoption, and strategic energy planning integration into operations and academic curricula. Campus Clean Energy Master Plans (first-time grantees), clean energy sector course development, and student internships are also eligible. Ineligible uses include fossil fuel, natural gas, or combustion technologies, and expansion of fossil fuel infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Maryland's accredited institutions of higher education. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions. Community colleges in census tracts with median income ≤80% of state median income, overburdened communities (census tracts where ≥3 environmental health indicators exceed 75th percentile statewide per Maryland Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022, Ch. 38), and underserved communities receive special competitive emphasis.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited Maryland Institution of Higher Education
Must be accredited by the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools, Commission on Higher Education
Solar installation activity funding capped at $1 million per application
Campus clean energy master planning capped at $145,000 per applicant (first-time grantees only)
Clean energy sector course development capped at $145,000 per applicant
Student internships capped at $25,000 per applicant
Fossil fuel, natural gas, combustion technologies, and expansion of fossil fuel infrastructure are ineligible activities
IRS Form W9, Authorization Letter, and Budget required for application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an electronic application via the MY MEA online portal with required documents checklist. A Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) and Project Budget Table are available on the program page. A webinar was held on 09/09/2025. Contact MEA at Kristen.Keim@maryland.gov or Schools.MEA@Maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR) provides rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances (such as fuel oil or natural gas equipment) with electric alternatives, along with some supporting upgrades. The program is funded by the federal Inflation Reduction Act and administered by the Maryland Energy Administration. Final DOE approvals are still pending before the program can officially launch.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances with electric alternatives, along with qualifying supporting upgrades. Specific rebate amounts are not yet stated on the page. The program is not yet launched pending final DOE approval. Federal IRA funding is allocated to Maryland with multiple deployment pathways including serving areas where existing statewide incentives are not currently available.

Also supports whole-home energy efficiency upgrades. Low-income components delivered in partnership with Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.

Maryland utility service territories include Potomac Edison, BGE, Pepco, DPL, and SMECO.

Subscribe to email alerts at the Maryland Energy Administration for updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebate Programs (HERO and HEAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebate Programs include two tracks administered by the Maryland Energy Administration: the Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity Program (HERO), which provides rebates for qualifying whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that reduce energy use by at least 20%, and the Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR), which provides rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances (such as fuel oil or natural gas equipment) with electric alternatives, along with qualifying supporting upgrades. Both programs fund energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes, with a focus on low-and-moderate income beneficiaries. Funded by the federal Inflation Reduction Act, the programs are not yet launched pending final approval from the U.S. Department of Energy. Low-income components will be delivered in partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes. The HERO track requires whole-home upgrades that achieve at least 20% reduction in energy use. The HEAR track provides rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances (e.g., fuel oil, natural gas, propane) with electric alternatives, along with qualifying supporting upgrades; HEAR rebates are not available for electric-to-electric appliance replacements and cannot be applied retroactively to completed projects. Programs prioritize low-and-moderate income households (Section 50122 sets a hard threshold at 150% or less of Area Median Income) and are available through individual households or aggregator organizations. Specific rebate amounts are not yet published. Programs have not yet launched pending final DOE approval. At least 60 days prior to launch, MEA is required to submit a State Implementation Blueprint to the U.S. Department of Energy for approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual households and aggregator organizations serving low-and-moderate income residents across Maryland seeking whole-home energy efficiency or electrification improvements, as well as Maryland homeowners seeking to replace fossil-fuel appliances with electric alternatives. Special focus on homes heated with fuel oil or propane that are underserved by existing statewide efficiency programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes, including whole-home upgrades that reduce energy use by at least 20% (HERO), and replacement of fossil-fuel heating and appliance systems with electric alternatives plus supporting upgrades (HEAR)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. No county-by-county or municipality-level restrictions stated. Utility service territories referenced as context for alternative programs include Potomac Edison, Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Baltimore Gas & Electric, Pepco, and Delmarva Power & Light. Section 50122 (HEAR) specifically targets homes heated with fuel oil or propane that are not served by existing statewide efficiency programs.

HEAR rebates cannot be applied retroactively to completed projects
