Final DOE approval of the State Implementation Blueprint (required at least 60 days before launch) is still required before applications can be accepted. MEA cannot confirm a program launch date at this time. Subscribe to email alerts at the Maryland Energy Administration for updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers low-interest loans to Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and state agencies to finance cost-effective energy efficiency, conservation, and clean energy projects. The program prioritizes comprehensive projects that include multiple measures to maximize energy cost savings and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Funds are provided at below-market rates to nonprofits and businesses, and at zero financing cost (0% interest plus 1% administrative fee) to local governments and state agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans for energy efficiency, conservation, and clean energy projects. Interest rates vary by borrower type: 3% for businesses and nonprofits requesting a micro loan; 2% for businesses and nonprofits requesting a traditional loan; 0% (plus 1% administrative fee on loan balance) for Maryland state and local governments and their instrumentalities. Total FY26 program budget is $4,281,842. During the first 90 days of FY26, $2,140,842 was reserved for nonprofits and $2,140,842 for state governmental bodies; all remaining funds became available to all eligible applicants starting November 1, 2025. Loans are awarded on a first-come, first-serve basis subject to funding availability. Funds may reimburse project expenses incurred after Commitment Letter execution. Eligible project costs are limited to the purchase, installation, and commissioning of energy-efficiency and conservation projects. A minimum $250 cash contribution is required plus all fees. Prepayment is allowed without penalty or premium. Late payment charge of 5% applies if payment is more than 30 days late.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses (excluding home-based businesses), and state agencies seeking financing for energy efficiency, electrification, and clean energy building upgrades and conservation improvements at their facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy conservation measures (ECMs) and improvements that reduce energy consumption and cost at eligible facilities, including energy efficiency retrofits, electrification, and greenhouse gas emission reduction projects in buildings. Explicitly excludes projects that expand fossil fuel use or combustion technologies (with limited exceptions requiring technical infeasibility justification). Eligible project costs are limited to purchase, installation, and commissioning of energy-efficiency and conservation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible borrowers located in the State of Maryland. Projects must be located within the State of Maryland. Eligible applicants include Maryland businesses, Maryland nonprofit organizations, Maryland local governments (counties and municipalities), and Maryland State governmental bodies. No county-by-county restrictions; program is statewide within Maryland. 'County' is defined to include any of the 23 counties of the State and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland nonprofit organization, local government, Maryland business (excluding home-based businesses), or state agency.
Projects must be located within the State of Maryland.
Projects must be cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation improvements.
Loans are subject to funding availability on a first-come, first-serve basis.
Subject to statutory provisions at Md. Code Ann. State Gov't Art. §§ 9-20A-01 – 9-20A-10 and COMAR section 14.26.01.
State government loans carry a 0% interest rate and a 1% administrative fee, subject to approval.
Projects expanding fossil fuel use or combustion technologies are explicitly excluded (limited exceptions require technical infeasibility justification).
Minimum $250 cash contribution required plus all fees.

Borrower must maintain utility cost monitoring at least annually, ensure prompt payment of contractors and materialmen, maintain the project in good condition per equipment specifications, carry required insurance (comprehensive general liability naming Administration as additional insured, fire/hazard insurance naming Administration as additional insured and loss payee, workers' compensation broad form all states), provide 30 days' written notice to Administration prior to insurance cancellation/non-renewal, keep records until three years after project completion or state audit completion (whichever is first), and comply with non-discrimination requirements and all applicable laws.
Guarantor must maintain 100% Class A corporate stock ownership of borrower (where applicable).
No asset disposition without prior written consent (where applicable).
No conversion of equity to debt (where applicable).
Annual financial statements and copy of federal income tax returns with schedules due by May 15 each year (where personal guaranty applies).
Collateral/facilities must be located in Maryland.
Project terms, conditions, and requirements are subject to change throughout the fiscal year at the sole discretion of MEA.
Applicants should thoroughly review the MEA Lawton Loan webpage for the most current policies and guidelines when preparing an application.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate application online. Businesses, nonprofits, and local governments use one application form; state agencies use a separate form. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis; funding is limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Contact MEA at lawton.mea@maryland.gov before submission for clarification. Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for full program details before applying. Disbursement requests must be submitted with supporting documentation (invoices, bills of sale, etc.).

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Energy Modernization (L-GEM) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to support local governments in pursuing large-scale planning and implementation of sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficiency projects across portfolios of public facilities. The program aims to reduce energy usage and greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and support clean energy and economic development. For fiscal year 2026 (FY26) only, MEA anticipates offering over $60 million in one-time funding to accelerate clean energy adoption. This program replaces the Maryland Smart Energy Communities (MSEC) program for FY26.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of over $60 million (FY26 one-time funding) for large-scale planning and implementation of energy efficiency and clean energy projects across local government public facility portfolios.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland seeking to implement large-scale clean energy and energy efficiency improvements across public facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and implementation of energy efficiency and clean energy projects at local government public facilities, greenhouse gas emission reductions, cost savings, and economic development related to clean energy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county or municipal government

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Government Energy Modernization Program (L-GEM) supports local governments in pursuing sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficiency projects that reduce energy usage and greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and advance clean energy and economic development. For FY26, the program offered $64 million in one-time grants across four Areas of Interest (AOIs): a non-competitive formula block grant for counties and Baltimore City (AOI1), and competitive grants for planning activities (AOI2), implementation projects excluding electrification (AOI3), and electrification projects (AOI4). This program replaced the Maryland Smart Energy Communities (MSEC) Program for Fiscal Year 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $64 million total in one-time grants for FY26, distributed across four Areas of Interest: $50 million for planning and renewable energy projects (primarily AOI1 non-competitive formula block grants and AOI2 competitive planning grants), $10 million for energy efficiency implementation projects (AOI3), and $4 million for electrification projects (AOI4). AOI1 formula block grants are flexible multi-year funding for counties and Baltimore City only. AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 are competitive merit-based grants open to municipalities and, in some cases, counties not receiving AOI1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning activities (feasibility studies, energy audits, energy planning, strategy development), renewable energy installations (solar, geothermal, landfill-gas-to-energy), building envelope measures (weatherization, insulation), efficient equipment and appliance upgrades (heat pumps, LEDs), and electrification projects (replacing fossil fuel systems with electric systems).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland are eligible. Counties and the City of Baltimore may apply for the non-competitive formula block grant (AOI1); municipalities are not eligible for AOI1 but are eligible for AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an incorporated town, city, or county in Maryland
Counties applying for AOI1 are not eligible to apply for AOI2 or AOI3
Counties may apply for both AOI1 and AOI4
Municipalities are eligible for AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 but not AOI1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Funding Opportunity Announcements and sample applications for the relevant AOI(s). Attend or view the kick-off webinar. Review the FAQ document. Contact Lacey Allor for questions or schedule a one-on-one virtual meeting. Submit application by the December 5, 2025 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Cities and Communities Coalition (MDCC&C)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Cities and Communities Coalition (MDCC&C) is a U.S. Department of Energy-designated coalition that provides technical assistance and resources to help fleets, fuel providers, and stakeholders adopt alternative fuels, improve fuel economy, and deploy emerging clean transportation technologies. The coalition works with businesses, fleets, and communities to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and improve air quality through voluntary partnerships. MEA also offers expertise, advice, and available programs and financial support to vehicle fleets, fuel providers, utilities, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Expert technical assistance and data to help fleets, fuel providers, and stakeholders adopt alternative fuels, improve fuel economy, and deploy emerging transportation technologies. Resources include coalition support, access to the Alternative Fuels Data Center, FuelEconomy.gov, Technical Response Service, and specialized assistance from national labs. MEA also offers expertise, advice, and available programs and financial support to vehicle fleets, fuel providers, utilities, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fleets, fuel providers, businesses, utilities, community leaders, and communities seeking to adopt clean transportation solutions and alternative fuels in urban, suburban, and rural Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shifting to affordable, efficient, and clean transportation fuels and technologies; reducing greenhouse gas emissions; evaluating new mobility options; improving equitable access to advanced transportation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Coalition Director Natalie Buscemi by email at transportation.mea@maryland.gov to become a member of the coalition.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Administration Resilient Maryland Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funds to Maryland communities and organizations to offset the costs of planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resiliency hubs, and other distributed energy resources (DERs) for critical and community uses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds to offset the costs of planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resiliency hubs, and other distributed energy resources (DERs) for critical and community uses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities, organizations, and local governments seeking to build energy resilience through microgrids, resilient facility power systems, and resiliency hubs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resiliency hubs, and other distributed energy resources for critical and community uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for residential and commercial taxpayers in Maryland who have installed an energy storage system on their property. The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) awards tax credit certificates on a first-come, first-served basis up to $750,000 per tax year. This program expired at the end of calendar year 2024 and is no longer accepting applications. MEA is replacing it with a grant program starting in fiscal year 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit certificates awarded to eligible applicants on a first-come, first-served basis. MEA may award a total of $750,000 in tax credit certificates per tax year. The credit applies to the installation of an energy storage system on residential or commercial property in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15, 2025, at 3:00 P.M. EST (for Tax Year 2024 applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial taxpayers in Maryland who have installed an energy storage system on their property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax for the installation of an energy storage system on residential or commercial property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for energy storage systems installed on residential or commercial property in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a residential or commercial taxpayer in Maryland
Must have installed an energy storage system on residential or commercial property in Maryland
Applications awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted
Program expired at end of calendar year 2024 per state law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to MEA by the deadline. Applications are reviewed and approved on a rolling basis in the order received until funds are exhausted. Missing documents must be provided within 14 days of MEA notification or by January 20, 2025, whichever is earlier.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Ground Source Heat Pump Advantage Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Ground Source Heat Pump Advantage Pilot Program (MD GAP) provides per-installation incentives to residential builders, developers, housing authorities, and eligible businesses that install ground source heat pump (GSHP) systems in qualifying new residential construction developments. The program aims to lower the upfront cost of GSHP installation and support market transformation, with an emphasis on affordable housing in low-to-moderate income (LMI) and Overburdened census tracts. This is a pilot initiative for FY26; continuation beyond FY26 is not guaranteed.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program providing per-GSHP installation incentives to eligible applicants. Total anticipated funding is $2,000,000 for FY26. MEA anticipates funding between one and three proposals, with a focus on large-scale GSHP deployments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential builders, developers, housing authorities, and eligible business entities installing ground source heat pump systems in new residential construction developments located in qualifying low-to-moderate income (LMI) and/or Overburdened census tracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentivizing the installation of ground source heat pump (GSHP) systems at scale in qualifying new construction residential developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Developments must be located in low-to-moderate income (LMI) and/or Overburdened census tracts as defined in Chapter 98 of the 2023 Laws of Maryland (HB550).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a residential builder, developer, housing authority, or eligible business entity
Project must involve installation of GSHP systems in new construction residential developments
Development must be located in qualifying LMI and/or Overburdened census tracts as defined in Chapter 98 of the 2023 Laws of Maryland (HB550)
GSHP deployments must be at scale
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application via the Jotform online application (preferred) or the PDF application form by the deadline of March 15, 2026 at 3PM EST. Program documents including the Funding Opportunity Announcement are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Supply Chain Investment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers grant funding on a non-competitive, first-come-first-served basis to help new or existing businesses enter the offshore wind supply chain in Maryland. The program has two Areas of Interest (AOI): AOI 1 covers capital expenditures such as relocation costs, construction, renovations, and equipment purchases needed to enter the offshore wind industry (awards up to 50% of total project costs, not to exceed $400,000 per award, with at least 50% matching funds required); AOI 2 reimburses up to $5,000 for attending eligible offshore wind industry events held in the United States and its territories. MEA strongly encourages members of historically disenfranchised groups to apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total funding of up to $2,000,000 is available: $1,750,000 for AOI 1 (capital expenditures) and $250,000 for AOI 2 (industry events). AOI 1 awards up to 50% of total project costs, not to exceed $400,000 per award; applicants must provide at least 50% matching funds. Ineligible costs under AOI 1 include operating expenditures, real property purchase, and employee relocation costs. AOI 2 provides a one-time reimbursement of up to $5,000 per eligible applicant per fiscal year for attending offshore wind industry events (covers registration, exhibition, travel, and lodging; excludes food/drink, printing, consulting, gifts, and entertainment). Awards are made on a non-competitive, first-come-first-served basis. MEA may reallocate funds between AOIs based on demand and application quality.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2025 or until all program funding has been awarded
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government and public institutions, and emerging businesses (at least 51% owned and controlled by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 as adjusted for inflation) seeking to enter Maryland's offshore wind supply chain.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AOI 1: Business expansion, relocation costs, new construction or renovation of real property, and purchase/installation of equipment to enter the offshore wind industry. Ineligible: operating expenditures, real property purchase, employee relocation costs. AOI 2: Costs associated with attending eligible offshore wind industry events including registration fees, exhibition fees, scheduled travel, and lodging (reimbursement up to $5,000 per event, limited to one event per fiscal year per applicant); excludes food/drink, printing, consulting, gifts, and entertainment. Eligible events must be held in the United States and its territories; international events are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. MEA will also consider applications from businesses willing to relocate or expand into Maryland contingent on receiving a grant award. AOI 2 eligible events are limited to those held in the United States and its territories; international events are ineligible.
requirements_list: Applicants must be non-profit organizations, government/public institutions, or emerging businesses as defined by Md. Code Ann., State Gov't §9-20C-01(e).
Business applicants must be 'Emerging Businesses' — at least 51% owned and controlled by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 (adjusted annually for inflation per CPI).
Proposals must come from organizations interested in entering the offshore wind industry and able to contribute to Maryland's offshore wind supply chain and workforce.
Applications must be submitted via the online Jotform portal.
Applications must be administratively complete with all required materials as specified in each AOI's Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA).
For AOI 1, applicants must have a Market Entry Report detailing how capital expenditures will help them enter the offshore wind industry.
AOI 1 applicants must provide at least 50% matching funds; grant covers up to 50% of total project costs, not to exceed $400,000 per award.
AOI 1 Project Narrative (max 10 pages) must address: Applicant Overview, Project Scope, Needs Assessment, Project Timeline, Project Partners, and Sustainability Statement.
AOI 2 is limited to one award per applicant per fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications through the online Jotform portal (separate portals for AOI 1 and AOI 2 as listed on the program page). Applications are accepted on a first-come-first-served basis until the deadline or until all funding is awarded. AOI 1 applicants must submit a Project Narrative (max 10 pages) addressing Applicant Overview, Project Scope, Needs Assessment, Project Timeline, Project Partners, and Sustainability Statement, along with all required materials specified in the FOA. Applications are reviewed bi-monthly and applicants are notified within 90 days of submission. Questions may be directed to the primary MEA contact.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Workforce Training & Education Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program operated by the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) that provides funding to workforce training centers and academic institutions to expand their capacity to support offshore wind workforce training and education in Maryland and the broader U.S. offshore wind market. Funding is split between two Areas of Interest (AOIs): AOI 1 (Industry Education) supports developing or expanding offshore wind education programs for the general public at any education level, and AOI 2 (Workforce Training) supports new or existing workforce training centers developing or expanding offshore wind certification-based training programs. For fiscal year 2026, MEA is partnering with the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program to fund projects. Historical program information remains on the page for reference and does not constitute an active program announcement for prior fiscal years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling up to $3,000,000 split between two Areas of Interest: AOI 1 (Industry Education) with up to $1,500,000 and AOI 2 (Workforce Training) with up to $1,500,000. Under AOI 2, funding offsets up to 75% of total project costs with a maximum of $500,000 per awardee and a 25% cost-share required. MEA may reallocate funding between AOIs based on demand, application quality, and availability. For FY26, funding is administered through the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program. Specific funding restrictions are detailed in each AOI's Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3:00 PM ET, Friday, November 29, 2024 (FY25 AOI 2); 3:00 PM ET, December 13, 2024 (FY25 AOI 1); September 26, 2025 (FY26 via EARN Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, government and public institutions, emerging businesses (at least 51% owned by individuals with personal net worth ≤$6,500,000), and academic institutions seeking to develop or expand offshore wind education and workforce training programs, including training providers preparing workers for careers in skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics; outreach must include historically economically and socially disadvantaged communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenditures for developing or expanding offshore wind education programs (AOI 1), including curriculum development, program implementation, relocation costs, renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, and administrative expenses; developing or expanding offshore wind certification-based workforce training programs (AOI 2); eligible activities also include providing supportive services for trainees, outreach to historically economically and socially disadvantaged communities, and preparing workers for careers in skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, or logistics
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — programs must support offshore wind workforce training and education efforts in Maryland and the larger U.S. offshore wind market
requirements_list: Applicants must be nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, government/public institutions, or Maryland emerging businesses (at least 51% owned and controlled by individuals with personal net worth ≤$6,500,000, adjusted annually for inflation per Md. Code Ann., State Gov't §9-20C-01(e))
Proposed projects must provide general offshore wind education or training for employment in the offshore wind industry
Projects must relate to offshore wind work in Maryland or the larger U.S. offshore wind market and related industries
AOI 2 applicants must provide a 25% cost-share; funding covers up to 75% of total project costs with a maximum of $500,000 per awardee

Applications must include all materials specified in the respective AOI's FOA, including a Project Narrative (max 10 pages) with sections: Applicant Overview, Project Scope Statement, Needs Assessment, Project Work Plan, and Project Partners
Applications must include a detailed timeline of key milestones, marketing and outreach plan for disadvantaged communities, and course curricula or intended samples
Applications must be submitted through the online Jotform application portal (FY25) or via EARN Maryland process (FY26)
Applicants that received prior-year funding may apply for additional funding in subsequent fiscal years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For FY25: Review the relevant AOI's Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) before applying. Submit applications through the online Jotform portal accessible via MEA's website. AOI 1 and AOI 2 each have separate application portals and templates. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Applications are evaluated based on how well they meet listed criteria. For FY26: Visit the EARN Maryland Summer 2025 Solicitation for Implementation Grant Proposals webpage; the Maryland Department of Labor manages the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-to-moderate income Maryland residents install solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to power their homes with clean, affordable, and sustainable energy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for income-eligible Maryland households to install solar PV systems through participating contractors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households who contract with a solar PV vendor from the program's participating contractor list
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be income-eligible (low-to-moderate income)
Must contract with a solar PV vendor from the program's participating contractor list

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers grants to Maryland counties and municipalities to help cover costs associated with implementing the free-to-use NREL SolarAPP+ automated solar permitting software. The 2024 Brighter Tomorrow Act requires Maryland local jurisdictions to adopt automated solar permitting software, and MEA has determined that the NREL SolarAPP+ platform meets those requirements. Up to $3,900,000 in federal funding is available through the State Energy Program (SEP) Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) formulaic award. Grants are awarded on a noncompetitive, first-come, first-served basis to offset costs including contractual support, staff training, and software integration costs associated with implementing the SolarAPP+ permitting software. Grantees must meet certain federal requirements as a condition of receiving funds, including SAM registration, UEI, conflict of interest policy, export controls, and Buy American preference requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $3,900,000 in federal funding is available through the State Energy Program (SEP) Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) formulaic award. Grants are awarded on a noncompetitive, first-come, first-served basis to offset costs including contractual support, staff training, and software integration costs associated with implementing the SolarAPP+ permitting software. Grantees must meet certain federal requirements as a condition of receiving funds, including SAM registration, UEI, conflict of interest policy, export controls, Buy American preference requirements, and Davis-Bacon Act prevailing wage compliance where applicable. Project completion deadline is July 1, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 25, 2026, 3:00 P.M. ET (or until funding is exhausted, whichever comes first)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and municipalities seeking to implement automated solar permitting software as required by the 2024 Brighter Tomorrow Act.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with implementing the SolarAPP+ permitting software, including contractual support, staff training, software integration costs, and other related expenses. Iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials must meet Buy America Preference standards; waivers available for public interest, nonavailability, or unreasonable cost circumstances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties and municipalities statewide. Project site(s) and location(s) that will benefit from the project must be located within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county or municipality
Must implement the NREL SolarAPP+ solar permitting software platform
Must meet federal requirements as a condition of receiving funds (see FOA for details)
Must be registered in SAM and have a UEI
Must comply with Buy American preference requirements under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law
Must comply with Davis-Bacon Act prevailing wage requirements where applicable (weekly certified payroll documentation required, 3-year retention post-completion)
Must comply with NEPA authorization requirements; activities must fall within 'Bounded Categories' or receive written DOE approval
Must comply with Historic Preservation requirements via Programmatic Agreement
All work must be performed in the United States unless a waiver is granted
Foreign nationals may require DOE notification
Mandatory quarterly reporting via Federal Assistance Reporting Checklist
No lobbying of Congress with award funds
Semi-annual labor compliance reporting required (April 21 and October 21)
Full eligibility requirements provided in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for all terms, conditions, and requirements. Submit an application through the online portal (JotForm link provided on the program page). Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until the deadline (February 25, 2026, 3:00 P.M. ET) or funding is exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mechanical Insulation Grant Program provides grants to eligible individuals, nonprofit organizations, business entities, state agencies, local governments, public or private schools, and community colleges to help incentivize the installation of mechanical insulation on commercial or industrial properties located in Maryland. The goal is to enable energy-saving improvements to large-scale thermal distribution networks. Total funding pool is $400,000. Individual grant maximum is the lesser of 30% of project costs or $20,000, with a cumulative entity cap of $50,000 and a minimum eligible project cost of $10,000.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based grants available on a rolling basis until funding is fully awarded or the application deadline is reached. Total funding pool is $400,000. Individual grant maximum is the lesser of 30% of project costs or $20,000; cumulative entity cap is $50,000. Minimum eligible project cost is $10,000. Grants defray costs of installing mechanical insulation on commercial or industrial properties. Eligible costs include design, feasibility analysis, material acquisition, installation, and post-installation commissioning. Building envelope insulation and thermal system repair/remediation are excluded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until funding is fully awarded or until December 17, 2025 at 3 P.M., whichever occurs first.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, business entities, state agencies, local governments, public or private schools, and community colleges that own or operate commercial or industrial properties in Maryland and wish to install mechanical insulation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, feasibility analysis, material acquisition, installation, and post-installation commissioning of mechanical insulation on commercial or industrial properties to improve energy efficiency in large-scale thermal distribution networks. Excludes building envelope insulation and thermal system repair/remediation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible applicants throughout Maryland. Grant-eligible facilities must be located in the State of Maryland. Use of funds for projects benefitting facilities not located within Maryland is strictly prohibited.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an individual, nonprofit organization, Maryland business entity, state agency, local government, public or private school, or community college
Project must involve installation of mechanical insulation on a commercial or industrial property located in Maryland
Minimum project cost of $10,000
Individual grant maximum is the lesser of 30% of project costs or $20,000
Cumulative entity cap of $50,000
Scope of eligible project is limited to the portion of a single-site heating or cooling system owned by the applicant
Applications submitted earlier have a better chance of receiving funding before funds are exhausted
Maryland business entities must provide a valid SDAT certificate
Building envelope insulation and thermal system repair/remediation are not eligible costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an electronic PDF application to insulation.mea@maryland.gov using the FY26 Mechanical Insulation Application form. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until funding is fully awarded or the deadline of December 17, 2025 at 3 P.M. is reached. Contact MEA by email or phone for more information. The FY26 cycle closed December 17, 2025; check MEA website for FY27 announcement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers grants to Maryland fleet companies, organizations, and communities to help cover the cost of purchasing newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty vehicles and qualified heavy equipment property for commercial or industrial use. The program accelerates adoption of ZEVs in medium and heavy-duty applications, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting cleaner transportation. Separate funding pools exist for on-road vehicles and off-road equipment. MEA strongly encourages applications benefiting underserved or overburdened communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of the incremental cost of eligible zero-emission vehicles and heavy equipment property, with a maximum of $375,000 per applicant for AOI 2. Up to $10 million is available in Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26). Separate funding pools are available for on-road vehicles and off-road equipment. Grants are disbursed on a reimbursement basis (arrears), with payment via electronic transfer through the State Comptroller's Office. Quarterly operational reports are required for 3 years post-delivery.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland fleet companies, organizations, and communities — including commercial and industrial entities, agricultural businesses, fleet operators, manufacturers, and local governments — seeking to purchase zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty vehicles or heavy equipment for commercial or industrial use. Applications benefiting underserved or overburdened communities are strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty on-road vehicles (Class 3–8 BEV/FCEV rated >10,000 lbs GVWR) and off-road heavy equipment property for commercial or industrial use, including trucks, refuse trucks, terminal tractors, forklifts, excavators, skid steer loaders, and riding mowers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland. Vehicles must be registered in Maryland to the applicant, domiciled in Maryland, and operated or used primarily within the State for no less than three years from the vehicle delivery date. Program is available statewide.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a fleet company, organization, or community in Maryland
Vehicles and equipment must be newly manufactured and qualify as zero-emission
Eligible vehicles and equipment must be for commercial or industrial use
Both on-road vehicles and off-road equipment are eligible under separate funding pools
Vehicles must be registered in Maryland to the applicant
Vehicles must be domiciled and primarily operated within the State for no less than three (3) years from delivery date
Quarterly operational reports required for 3 years post-delivery
See the FY26 Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for full eligibility details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the FY26 MHD ZEV Grant Program FOA and Guide for Applicants. Submit application materials via the MyMEA Portal by November 20, 2025 at 3:00 P.M. ET. Reimbursement and reporting are completed via Jotform links and invoice templates provided on the program page after award. Payment is made in arrears via electronic transfer through the State Comptroller's Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides grants and other potential incentives for innovative energy projects focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving equitable access to clean energy, and reducing energy costs. The program is designed to support forward-thinking projects that typically fall outside MEA's established technology and sector-specific programs, with an emphasis on deploying clean energy technologies while promoting equity and affordability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and other potential incentives for innovative clean energy projects that fall outside MEA's established technology and sector-specific programs, targeting greenhouse gas reductions, energy equity, and affordability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofit organizations, local governments, state governments, higher education institutions, building owners, and other organizations seeking funding for innovative energy projects in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Innovative projects deploying clean energy technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve equitable access to clean energy, and reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Project must focus on deploying clean energy technologies
Project should fall outside MEA's established technology and sector-specific programs

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Facilities Solar FY25 Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding to city, county, or municipal government entities to support the planning and installation of solar arrays on existing public facilities. A public facility is a building where the local jurisdiction owns, controls, and uses the facility for official purposes. Installation can happen through direct purchase of solar modules or through a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with a third party. The program has two Areas of Interest (AOI): AOI 1 covers purchased systems, and AOI 2 covers third-party owned systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Up to $500,000 total is available for the program. Funds support planning and installation of solar arrays on public facilities, either through direct purchase (AOI 1) or through a third-party Power Purchase Agreement (AOI 2). Grants are reimbursement-based, paid after project completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City, county, and municipal government entities, public universities, community colleges, and public schools in Maryland seeking to install solar energy systems on public facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and installation of solar arrays on existing infrastructure of public facilities, either through direct purchase of solar modules or through a Power Purchase Agreement with a third party.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local government entities throughout Maryland. Project must be located in Maryland or undertaken for the direct benefit of a Maryland resident, business, community, campus, or facility located entirely within the State of Maryland. MEA may consider a project's location within the State when determining award decisions. For projects funded through solar alternative compliance fees (RPS-funded), eligible projects must be located in low-to-moderate income communities (census tracts with median household income at or below 80% of state average using 2021 Census data) or underserved/overburdened communities as identified by the Maryland Department of Environment Environmental Justice Screening Tool v2.0 Beta. A list of eligible census tracts is available on MEA's website. At least 80% of workers participating in the project must reside in Maryland or within 50 miles of Maryland's borders.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a city, county, or municipal government entity, public university, community college, or public school.
The facility must be owned and controlled by the local jurisdiction and used for its official purposes.
Installation must be on existing infrastructure of a public facility.
Systems must be installed through direct purchase (AOI 1) or through a Power Purchase Agreement with a third party (AOI 2).
Project must be located in Maryland or undertaken for the direct benefit of a Maryland resident, business, community, campus, or facility located entirely within the State of Maryland.
At least 80% of workers participating in the project must reside in Maryland or within 50 miles of Maryland's borders.

Grantee must certify authorization to apply, anti-collusion compliance, compliance with Maryland General Provisions § 5-502, no contingency fees, adherence to recordkeeping standards, non-debarment status, and no default on state obligations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants must submit the application form by the deadline of January 31, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EST. Contact MEA at msec.mea@maryland.gov or 410-507-7143 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Residential Energy Equity Program provides competitive grants to non-profit organizations and local government entities for energy efficiency and solar energy projects that benefit Maryland residents with low-to-moderate incomes. The program combines the former Energy Efficiency Equity Program and Solar Energy Equity Grant Program. Applicants can apply under two Areas of Interest: AOI 1 (Energy Efficiency Projects) with approximately $17.2 million available, and AOI 2 (Solar Energy Projects) with $8 million available. Grants are awarded for projects that generate significant reductions in residential energy usage and pass the financial benefits to income-qualifying residents. Residents do not receive funds directly from MEA. Starting FY26, nonprofits seeking funding for LMI-serving commercial facilities should apply to the Commercial and Industrial Grant Program. Note: The former Energy Efficiency Equity Grant Program and Solar Energy Equity Grant Program are permanently closed; applicants should apply to this new program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) Conservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) Conservation Easement Program allows landowners to voluntarily protect their land by donating a perpetual conservation easement to MET, the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR), or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Through a legal Deed of Conservation Easement, landowners permanently restrict future uses of the property — such as limiting subdivision or development — while retaining ownership and the right to continue living on, farming, selling, or passing on the land. The easement runs with the land and binds all future owners. MET evaluates each offer individually, monitors easement properties for compliance in perpetuity, and may co-hold easements with nonprofit land trust partners. In exchange for donating a qualifying perpetual conservation easement, landowners may receive significant tax benefits: (1) a federal income tax deduction for the appraised value of the easement as a charitable gift, up to 50% of adjusted gross income per year (100% for qualified farmers/ranchers), carried forward up to 15 years; (2) a Maryland state income tax credit of up to $5,000 per individual or pass-through entity per year for up to 15 years, for a maximum total credit of $80,000 (pass-through entities capped at $200,000 aggregate per tax year), directly offsetting tax owed rather than just reducing taxable income — or alternatively a Maryland state income tax deduction if the credit is not claimed; (3) a 15-year property tax credit — zero property tax on donated easement land for 15 years from the donation date, then assessed at the highest agricultural rate (does not apply to residential improvements or one surrounding acre); and (4) reduced federal and Maryland estate and inheritance taxes due to lower appraised land value, plus a federal 40% exclusion of land value up to $500,000 per owner for qualifying donated-easement land. The easement must be approved by the Board of Public Works, and a qualified appraiser must establish the value of the easement to calculate tax benefits. County-level additional property tax credits may also be available.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who donate a qualifying perpetual conservation easement to MET, DNR, or MALPF and receive Board of Public Works approval may receive the following tax benefits: (1) Federal income tax deduction — up to 50% of adjusted gross income per year (100% for qualified farmers/ranchers), carried forward up to 15 years, based on appraised value of the easement as a charitable gift; (2) Maryland state income tax credit — up to $5,000 per individual or pass-through entity per year, carried forward up to 15 years, for a maximum total credit of $80,000; pass-through entities capped at $200,000 aggregate per tax year; credits directly offset tax owed rather than just reducing taxable income; authorized under Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. §10–723; (3) Maryland state income tax deduction — available if the state tax credit is not claimed (a taxpayer may not claim both); (4) 15-year property tax credit — 100% tax credit applied to assessed value of unimproved, non-commercial land under perpetual conservation easement for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following the donation date, then assessed at the highest agricultural rate (does not apply to residential improvements or the surrounding minimum one acre); authorized under Md. Code Ann., Tax-Property §9-107; applies only to easements donated to MET or DNR; (5) Federal estate tax exclusion of 40% of land value up to $500,000 per owner; (6) Reduced federal and Maryland estate and inheritance taxes due to lower appraised land value. A qualified appraiser must establish the value of the easement to calculate tax benefits. MET works with landowners on a case-by-case basis and also co-holds easements with nonprofit land trust partners. Note: tax benefits may be impacted by US Treasury Decision 9864 regarding regulations on charitable contributions and state and local tax credits; consult a tax advisor for current applicability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No yearly deadline for easement donations; contact MET no later than June if donating within a particular calendar year. For the property tax credit, the conservation easement must be donated prior to July 1 of the taxable year, and the application must be submitted on or before October 1 of that taxable year. For subsequent years, a copy of the computation form must be submitted to each jurisdiction by June 1. County-specific deadlines vary (e.g., Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Queen Anne's: June 1; Prince George's: October 1 each year).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners (individuals, for-profit entities, and nonprofits) who own rural or exceptional urban properties with agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values — including woodland, wetlands, farmland, scenic areas, historic areas, wild and scenic rivers, or undisturbed natural areas — and who wish to permanently protect their land by donating a perpetual conservation easement to MET, DNR, or MALPF and seeking associated tax benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax savings and credits resulting from donating a perpetual conservation easement, including reductions in federal and state income tax liability (deduction or credit), federal and state estate and inheritance taxes, and a 15-year property tax exemption on unimproved, non-commercial easement land. No cash grant is provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, from Garrett County to the Chesapeake Bay, for any land whose conservation is in the public interest, for easements donated to MET, DNR, or MALPF and approved by the Board of Public Works. Eligible land types include farmland, woodlands, wetlands, wildlife habitat, Chesapeake Bay/tributary buffer lands, historic structures/sites, lands in Natural Heritage Areas, and lands adjacent to existing protected properties. Individual counties may also offer additional property tax credits for land under easement (counties with documented programs include Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Charles, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Queen Anne's). Rural properties generally require a minimum of 25 acres (with exceptions for extraordinary resources, clustering, public access, etc.); urban settings have a separate size policy with no minimum acreage requirement.
requirements_list: Property must contain agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values (rural properties) or be an exceptional urban property, especially those offering public access
Rural properties generally require a minimum of 25 acres (with exceptions for extraordinary resources, clustering, or public access); no minimum acreage for urban settings
Land must provide a significant public benefit as determined by MET

Easement must be perpetual and conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF); term easements only in unusual circumstances
Easement must be approved by the Board of Public Works
Easement offers are evaluated on a case-by-case basis by MET Board of Trustees

For the federal income tax deduction, the donation must be exclusively for conservation purposes and conveyed to a qualified organization or government unit; MET is a qualified organization under IRC §170(h)(3)(A)
A qualified appraiser must determine the value of the easement to calculate federal tax deduction or state income tax credit; donor is responsible for obtaining an independent appraisal
Qualified appraisal must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice and be performed by a state-licensed or state-certified appraiser
Appraisal must be completed no earlier than 60 days before the recordation date and no later than the tax return filing date

IRS Form 8283 and a supplemental statement must be submitted to MET no less than 10 working days before the tax return is due; donations exceeding $500,000 require a copy of the appraisal submitted to the IRS

Appraiser must sign Form 8283 before MET signs it; landowner completes Section B, Part 1 and Part 3 and Required Statement acknowledging conservation purposes, fair market value before/after easement, easement value, and related disclosures
All property owners must sign acknowledgment
Mortgage/lien subordination required for deductibility
State income tax credit is claimed using Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (pass-through entities)
A taxpayer may not claim both a Maryland income tax deduction and a Maryland income tax credit for the same easement donation
Total aggregate credits claimed by pass-through entity members cannot exceed $200,000 per taxable year
Maximum state income tax credit of $5,000 per year, with carryforward for up to 15 years for a maximum total of $80,000

Property tax credit applies only to conservation easements donated to MET or DNR; applies only to unimproved, non-commercial land and does not apply to residential improvements or the surrounding minimum one acre
Conservation easement must be donated prior to July 1 of the taxable year to be eligible for property tax credit for that year
Easement must have been approved after June 30, 1986 by the Board of Public Works to qualify for property tax credit

Conservation Property Tax Credit Application must be filed with the County Office of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation on or before October 1 of the taxable year, with a copy of the recorded Deed of Conservation Easement and Board of Public Works approval letter attached
For subsequent years, a copy of the computation form must be submitted to each jurisdiction by June 1
Landowner must agree to permanently restrict future uses of the property through a recorded Deed of Conservation Easement applicable to all future owners
Tax compliance responsibility rests with the landowner; MET review of Form 8283 does not constitute legal or tax advice
If property is entity-owned, corporate resolutions may be required
Ownership verification required as part of easement processing

For estate tax exclusion under IRC §2031(c): land must have been owned by decedent or family member for at least 3 years prior to death; perpetual conservation easement must be donated to a public charity or governmental entity; easement must protect outdoor recreation, wildlife habitat, or open space per IRC §170(h); easement must prohibit all but de minimis commercial recreational activities; post-mortem donations must be placed on land by executor/beneficiaries before estate tax filing (generally 9 months from death)
Within one year of recordation of the Conservation Easement, grantors shall obtain a Forest Stewardship Plan (Forest Stewardship Plans must be no more than 15 years old)
Within one year of recordation of the Conservation Easement, grantors shall have a Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan prepared
Tax benefits may be impacted by US Treasury Decision 9864 regarding regulations on charitable contributions and state and local tax credits; consult a tax advisor for current applicability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MET to express interest; if donating within a particular calendar year, contact MET no later than June of that year. MET staff will visit the potential easement site and meet with the landowner. MET reviews properties on a case-by-case basis (generally three or more months required from first contact), and the Board of Trustees makes the final decision on accepting each easement offer. If eligible, MET and the landowner work together — sometimes with a nonprofit land trust partner — to finalize the terms of the Deed of Conservation Easement, which is recorded in county land records and applies to all future owners. The conservation easement donation process can take anywhere from five months to a year depending on complexity. To claim the federal income tax deduction: obtain a qualified appraisal completed no earlier than 60 days before recordation and no later than the tax return filing date; complete IRS Form 8283 with an attached supplemental statement; send to MET for donee acknowledgment signature (allow at least 10 working days before the tax return is due); then file with your federal tax return. To claim the state income tax credit: file Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (pass-through entities) with your Maryland tax return. To claim the property tax credit: donate the easement prior to July 1 of the taxable year; download the Conservation Property Tax Credit Application form; file the completed application with your county's Office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation on or before October 1 of that year, attaching a copy of the recorded Deed of Conservation Easement and the Board of Public Works approval letter; for subsequent years, submit a copy of the computation form to each jurisdiction by June 1. County-specific deadlines for county tax credits vary (e.g., Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Queen Anne's: June 1; Prince George's: October 1 each year). Refer to the Conservation Easement Processing Steps document and program policy documents for detailed guidance. Contact the MET Easement Planner for the county where your property is located to begin the process. MET is located at 100 Community Place, Crownsville, MD 21032-2023; Phone: 410-697-9515. Visit http://www.dnr.maryland.gov/met/Pages/tax_benefits.aspx for additional tax benefit details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outreach and Engagement Program (Land Trust Assistance)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) Outreach and Engagement Program provides technical assistance and resources to local non-profit land trusts and conservation partners that co-hold or seek to co-hold conservation easements with MET. The program helps land trusts connect to services and programs offered by state agencies, counties, and other land trusts, and offers tools and direct support for easement and stewardship work, including monitoring resources and trainings, record-keeping guidance, publications and model easement documents, access to the online Land Trust Toolbox, and capacity-building mini-grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program. Through a Cooperative Agreement with MET, land trusts may also access programs such as the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, and Greenspace Equity Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance includes monitoring resources and trainings, record-keeping guidance, publications and aids (including a model easement document), access to MET's online Land Trust Toolbox, and capacity-building mini-grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program. Land trusts must have a Cooperative Agreement with MET to access most services. Through the Cooperative Agreement, land trusts may also access programs such as the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, and Greenspace Equity Program. Land trusts must adopt the Land Trust Alliance's Land Trust Standards and Practices (2017), maintain good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and hold 501(c)(3) status as a qualified organization under IRC §170(h)(3).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit land trusts and conservation partners that co-hold or seek to co-hold conservation easements with Maryland Environmental Trust. Land trusts must be 501(c)(3) qualified organizations under IRC §170(h)(3).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting easement and stewardship programs, monitoring, record keeping, capacity building, and land conservation activities. Cooperative Agreement provides access to state conservation funding programs including Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, and Greenspace Equity Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to land trusts operating anywhere in Maryland. MET partners are organized into four regions: Central (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County), Eastern (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington), plus regional and national land trusts with broader service areas.
requirements_list: Must be a local non-profit land trust or conservation partner working with MET
Must hold 501(c)(3) status and qualify as a 'qualified organization' under IRC §170(h)(3)
Must maintain good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (Md. Code Regs. 18.04.03.01)
Must have or obtain a Cooperative Agreement with MET to access most technical assistance
Must adopt the Land Trust Alliance's Land Trust Standards and Practices (2017) as guidelines
New Cooperative Agreement requests require review and approval by the Land Trust Outreach Committee (LTOC) and MET's Board of Trustees
Cooperative Agreement requests must be submitted at least 30 days before an LTOC meeting
Cooperative Agreements automatically terminate on December 31 of the agreement year; renewal is available if both parties agree
Must develop and implement a Records Policy
Must submit: 501(c)(3) letter, board resolution, conflict-of-interest policy, records policy, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, project-selection criteria, monitoring/stewardship policies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Land Trust Assistance Manager to discuss the status of your organization's Cooperative Agreement with MET. New Cooperative Agreement requests are reviewed by the Land Trust Outreach Committee and MET's Board of Trustees; submit requests at least 30 days before a scheduled LTOC meeting. Cooperative Agreements are renewable annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Keep Maryland Beautiful Community Stewardship Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Keep Maryland Beautiful Community Stewardship Grant awards up to $5,000 annually to schools, nonprofits, and other community organizations working to eliminate local environmental problems, encourage stewardship of the environment, and educate community members. Projects should activate citizens through hands-on education and outreach, elevate awareness of local environmental issues, develop innovative solutions to those problems, and support neighborhood beautification activities including litter removal, greening activities, community education, and citizen stewardship. The grants honor the legacies of Bill James and Margaret Rosch Jones.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Environmental Trust / Keep Maryland Beautiful Program / Maryland Department of Transportation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $5,000 are awarded annually to eligible organizations for environmental education, community stewardship projects, neighborhood beautification, litter removal, greening activities, community education, citizen stewardship projects, and developing innovative solutions to local environmental problems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, nonprofits, community groups, and other community organizations focused on environmental education, stewardship, litter prevention, neighborhood beautification, and community greening activities — especially those engaging children, young adults, and citizens in hands-on environmental action.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental education projects, community engagement and neighborhood greening activities, hands-on stewardship and outreach, litter removal, local beautification, initiatives that identify and address the root causes of local environmental problems, community beautification, and developing innovative solutions to local environmental problems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school, nonprofit, community group, or other community organization
Mission must be centered on engaging community members in environmental education and stewardship
Projects should activate citizens through hands-on education and outreach
Projects should elevate awareness of local environmental problems and work to reduce them
Projects should address local environmental problems and develop innovative solutions
Projects should support neighborhood beautification, litter removal, greening, or citizen stewardship
Projects should develop innovative solutions to local environmental problems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the program page at http://www.dnr.maryland.gov/met/Pages/Grant-EE-CI-CU.aspx for application details.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with earning the Child Development Associate (CDA) Credential

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Film Office: Sales and Use Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified film and video productions in Maryland can receive an exemption from the 6% state sales and use tax on purchases, rentals, and services related to production — including vehicle rentals, camera, lighting, sound, and recording equipment, costumes, props, scenery, special effects, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from Maryland's 6% state sales and use tax on purchases, rentals, and services used directly in connection with a film production activity. An approved production receives a numbered Certificate of Eligibility (sales tax exemption certificate) valid for the duration of that specific project. The certificate lists eligible items and is presented to vendors at the time of purchase. Eligible items include tangible personal property, digital codes, digital products, and taxable services such as camera, lighting, sound, recording, design, drafting, and special effects equipment and supplies; film and tape; costumes, props, scenery, and materials to construct them; short-term vehicle rentals; and fabrication, printing, and production of scripts, storyboards, costumes, wardrobes, props, scenery, and special effects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Producers of qualified feature films, television, cable, commercials, corporate films, infomercials, documentaries, music videos, digital/animation/multimedia projects, and other video productions intended for nationwide commercial distribution and filmed in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax exemption applies to tangible personal property, digital codes, digital products, and taxable services used directly in connection with film production activity, including: camera, lighting, sound, recording, design, drafting, and special effects equipment and supplies; film and tape; costumes, wardrobe, props, scenery, and materials to construct them; short-term vehicle rentals; fabrication, printing, and production of scripts, storyboards, costumes, wardrobes, props, scenery, and special effects. Excludes student films, noncommercial personal videos, and projects not intended for nationwide commercial distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for productions that qualify through the Maryland Film Office. The production must be intended for nationwide commercial distribution, defined as distribution extending primarily beyond Maryland's local or regional (Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia) market. Property and services must be used directly in connection with a film production activity in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified feature film, television project, commercial, corporate film, infomercial, music video, digital/animation/multimedia project, or similar production intended for nationwide commercial distribution
Project must be for compensated, nationwide commercial distribution extending primarily beyond Maryland's local or regional (Maryland, Virginia, and DC) market
Student films and noncommercial personal videos are excluded
Must receive a Certificate of Eligibility for Film Production Sales and Use Tax Exemption from the Maryland Film Office
Producer or production company must hold a currently valid federal tax ID number

Film producer (individual) or film production company (corporation, business trust, partnership, LLC, association, or other legal entity) must apply to the Film Office for qualification on the specific project
Application must be completed in its entirety and signed and dated before submission
Certificate is valid only for the specific approved project and expires at the conclusion of production
Tangible property and services must be used directly in connection with a film production activity
Vendor must retain a completed Buyer Certification Form COT/ST 131 including the Department of Commerce Certificate Number and expiration date
Authorized purchasing agents designated by the producer must present the certificate to vendors at time of purchase
Producer's purchase records are subject to periodic audits by the Comptroller's Office
A Production Expenditure Report must be submitted upon completion of filming
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Producer downloads and completes the application electronically on a form approved by the Maryland Film Office (Department), signs and dates it (digital signatures accepted), and submits it by email to the Film Office. The Film Office reviews and qualifies the application. If approved, a numbered Certificate of Eligibility (sales tax exemption certificate) is issued within 3 business days. The certificate lists eligible items and is presented to vendors at the time of purchase. The program operates on a rolling/continuous basis with no fixed application cycle dates.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides participating landowners with a free tree planting project on open land they want to convert into a forest, including all supplies, labor, and at least 3 years of maintenance and technical advice. The landowner must maintain the newly planted forest for a minimum of 10 years. Funded by the DNR Chesapeake and Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
