structured_extraction.program_description: The Delmarva Woodland Stewards (DWS) program empowers landowners across Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia to manage their forests for healthier wildlife habitat, cleaner water, wildfire resilience, and sustainable woodlands. The program blends hands-on training, demonstration and interpretive projects, and community outreach to improve forest management across public and private lands. It is funded by the USDA Forest Service Landscape Scale Restoration Grant and led by the Maryland Forest Service in partnership with University of Maryland Extension, The Nature Conservancy, Maryland Forests Association, and others. Nearly 60 participants from Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia have completed the Delmarva Woodland Stewards course covering forest management best practices, riparian buffers, agroforestry, prescribed fire, vegetation management, and wood product markets.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Forest Service, Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides hands-on training courses for landowners (built on the Maryland Woodland Stewards model) covering forest management best practices, riparian buffers, agroforestry, prescribed fire, vegetation management, and wood product markets. Also offers demonstration sites with interpretive signage, prescribed fire workshops, map-based habitat connectivity research, prescribed burn association networking, fact sheets, and community outreach to help landowners develop and implement forest stewardship plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, conservationists, and community members across the Delmarva Peninsula (Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia) interested in sustainable forest management, wildlife habitat improvement, and stewardship of public and private lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management training and education, demonstration projects, prescribed fire workshops, riparian buffer planting, agroforestry, vegetation management, habitat connectivity research, and community outreach for Delmarva landowners on public and private lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landowners and community members across the Delmarva Peninsula, including Maryland's Eastern Shore counties (Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, and Worcester), as well as Delaware and Virginia.
requirements_list: Must be a landowner, conservationist, or community member interested in forest management on the Delmarva Peninsula
No explicit eligibility restrictions stated beyond geographic focus on the Delmarva region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Eastern Shore Prescribed Burn Association interest form to join their mailing list. Contact Charly Sager at the Maryland Forest Service or visit the Maryland Woodland Stewards website through University of Maryland Extension for information on available courses. Additional resources and demonstration network sites (including Tuckahoe State Park in Caroline County, E.A. Vaughn Wildlife Management Area in Worcester County, Nanticoke River Wildlife Management Area in Wicomico County, and Idylwild Wildlife Management Area) are available via the Links & Resources tab at https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Pages/default.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Legacy Program is a federal-state partnership that protects environmentally sensitive private forests from conversion to non-forest uses. It does this by purchasing perpetual conservation easements at market value from willing private landowners. A conservation easement is a legal agreement that restricts future activities on the land to protect its conservation values, including wildlife habitat, water quality, wood products production, and public benefits. The federal government funds up to 75% of the cost; at least 25% comes from state, local, NGO funds, or a landowner donation. Applications are evaluated and ranked annually at both state and national levels for funding, with the highest-ranked submitted into the national ranking process for federal funding allocation. The number of parcels accepted each year depends on available funding and estimated parcel values.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Forest Service, Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases perpetual conservation easements from willing private forest landowners at market value. The federal government provides up to 75% of the purchase price; the remaining 25% or more comes from state, local, or NGO funds, or can be donated by the landowner. The number of parcels accepted each year depends on available funding and the estimated value of the parcels selected. Applications are evaluated and ranked annually, with the highest-ranked entering the national ranking process for federal funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications evaluated and ranked on an annual basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners within designated Forest Legacy Areas in Maryland who are willing to sell their development rights through a conservation easement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of perpetual conservation easements on private forestland to restrict future non-forest development and protect conservation values including wildlife habitat, water quality, and wood products production.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only available in areas identified as Forest Legacy Areas in Maryland's Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need — geographically defined areas with the highest economic and environmental conservation values for wildlife, water quality, wood products, and residents. Property must be in a designated Forest Legacy Area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Land must be located within a designated Forest Legacy Area in Maryland
Land must be privately owned forestland
At least 75% of the area placed under easement must be forested
The remaining up to 25% must be in a compatible land use such as agriculture
Landowner must be a willing seller
Properties are ranked at state and national level for funding
25% non-federal match required
Completed application required (incomplete applications will not be considered)
Four copies of application package must be submitted (one original plus three copies per non-contiguous parcel)
Signed consent agreement required
Property location map required (State Highway, USGS Topographic, or Street Atlas)
Legal description and/or copy of deed required
List of encumbrances/liens required
Property plan-map required (with scale, north arrow, date, title, forested/non-forested areas, wetlands, structures, etc.)
Forest management plan required prior to closing; must be updated at least every 15 years
No building sites reserved or withdrawn from eligible ownership (scoring criterion)
100% of easement area is forest (scoring criterion)
Written community support (scoring criterion)
Adjacency to other Forest Legacy parcels (scoring criterion)
Complementarity with federal investments such as wetland reserves or watershed projects (scoring criterion)
At least 50% of easement value donated or funded by other sources (scoring criterion)
Conveyance of additional rights such as public access (scoring criterion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners complete the Landowner Application (PDF available at https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/ForestLegacy-Application.pdf) and submit four copies of the application package to Maryland DNR. All applications are evaluated and ranked annually based on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives. Highest-ranked applications enter the national ranking process for federal funding. Funded projects move into easement negotiation and acquisition, including property inspection, appraisal, and survey conducted by DNR. If a project does not receive funding or negotiations do not produce acceptable terms, landowners may reapply in future years. Optional letters of support from land trusts, town officials, or state/regional conservation groups may be included.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority (MHHEFA) provides least-cost financing to non-profit educational institutions and hospitals and related health care organizations for the construction and acquisition of capital projects. Financing options include fixed and variable rate bonds (including commercial paper), leases and subleases, private placements, direct bank placements, public and limited public offerings, loans, and pooled loan programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHHEFA provides access to capital markets through fixed and variable rate bonds (including commercial paper), leases and subleases, private placements, direct bank placements, public and limited public offerings, loans, and pooled loan programs. Financing is tailored to meet the specific needs of each individual project.

Contact MHHEFA directly at 410.837.6220 or visit their office at 401 E. Pratt Street, Suite 1224, Baltimore, Maryland 21202.

structured_extraction.program_description: The 2+2 Transfer Scholarship, established in 2014, helps transfer students from Maryland community colleges attend a 4-year institution in Maryland and complete their bachelor's degrees. Students who transfer from a Maryland community college (with an associate's degree completed or in progress) to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year institution as full-time, degree-seeking undergraduates can receive annual scholarship funds toward tuition and mandatory fees. Awards range from $1,000 to $2,000 per year, with higher amounts for students enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing (workforce shortage fields). Awards are based on financial need and academic merit, and applicants are ranked accordingly due to high demand; a waiting list exists each year. The scholarship is renewable for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer, and all awards are contingent on availability of funds. Undocumented students are explicitly ineligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship of $2,000 ($1,000 per term) for students enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs; $1,000 annually ($500 per term) for all other programs. The maximum total award is $6,000 over 3 years for STEM/teaching/nursing programs and $3,000 over 3 years for standard programs. Funds may be used toward tuition and mandatory fees only (room, board, books, and supplies are excluded) at the 4-year Maryland institution. The scholarship may be renewed for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer. Applicants are ranked by academic merit and financial need (Student Aid Index must not exceed $10,000) due to high demand; a waiting list exists each year. All awards are contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are community college students completing or who have completed an associate's degree and are transferring to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year institution as full-time, degree-seeking undergraduates with demonstrated financial need (SAI not exceeding $10,000) and a minimum 2.5 GPA. Undocumented students are explicitly ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees only at the 4-year Maryland institution the student has transferred to. Room, board, books, and supplies are excluded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents attending a Maryland community college and transferring to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year higher education institution. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Submit a 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application via the MHEC One-App in MDCAPS by the applicable deadline
File the applicable year FAFSA by the application deadline (students ineligible to file FAFSA may not apply)

Be attending a Maryland community college with plans to finish an associate's degree by December of the application year, OR have completed an associate's degree from a Maryland community college in the prior academic year
Must obtain an associate degree from a Maryland community college before transfer
Maintain a minimum cumulative 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale at the Maryland community college
Transfer to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year institution as a full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate student
Demonstrate financial need (Student Aid Index must not exceed $10,000)
Cannot have received a bachelor's degree or associate's degree prior to July of the year before the award year
Submit all required documentation by the listed deadlines
Submit community college transcript showing current cumulative GPA by the transcript deadline
Submit final community college transcript showing degree conferment date by the required deadline once conditionally awarded
Provide proof of Selective Service registration if applicable by the required deadline

For renewal: remain eligible for in-state tuition, submit FAFSA annually, stay enrolled full-time at a qualifying 4-year Maryland institution, maintain a 2.5 cumulative GPA, and meet institutional standards
Undocumented students are not eligible
Must be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the MHEC One-App on MDCAPS (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us) by the applicable deadline. For the 2026-2027 cycle, the application opened January 15, 2026, with an initial deadline of October 15, 2026, documentation deadline of November 15, 2026, and proof of associate's degree deadline of February 15, 2027. Submit the corresponding year FAFSA by the same deadline. Submit a community college transcript showing current cumulative GPA by the transcript deadline. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and applicants are ranked by academic merit and financial need; a waiting list exists due to high demand. Once conditionally awarded, submit proof of associate's degree (final community college transcript showing degree conferment date) and proof of Selective Service registration if applicable by the required deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Academic Common Market (ACM) is a tuition-savings program for Maryland residents. If a Maryland public institution does not offer a degree program a student wants to pursue, the student may attend a participating out-of-state public college or university through the ACM and receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges. The program covers undergraduate, transfer, and graduate degree-seeking students. Students are charged in-state tuition rates at the out-of-state institution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible students receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges at participating public colleges and universities in other Southern Regional Education Board (SREB) member states when their desired degree program is not offered at a Maryland public institution. Students are charged in-state tuition rates at the out-of-state institution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Three cycles per year: March 1 - June 30, September 1 - November 15, January 2 - February 28
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are accepted or enrolled in an eligible degree program at a participating out-of-state public college or university (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate) whose desired major is not available at a Maryland public institution. Parents or legal guardians may also be involved in the application process for undergraduate students under age 24.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of out-of-state tuition charges at participating public institutions in other SREB member states.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents; the out-of-state institution must be a participating public college or university in an SREB member state. Note: North Carolina does not participate in the ACM.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be accepted or enrolled in an ACM-approved degree program at a participating public college or university as a degree-seeking student (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate)
Must be admitted to the academic program before applying — MHEC does not conduct pre-evaluations
Desired degree program must not be offered at a Maryland public institution
Must apply through the OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov) during one of the three annual application cycles
Must submit two qualifying documents proving Maryland residency (addresses must match)
Military students must also attach earnings statement and military orders signed by commander
Transfer students must contact MHEC by email for application submission instructions
Previously certified students must re-apply only if they change their major or have a break in enrollment
For undergraduate students under age 24, a parent or legal guardian signature is required on the Affirmation of Maryland Residency form
Student and parent/guardian (if applicable) must sign affirmation under penalties of perjury
All submitted information and supporting documentation must be truthful, accurate, and complete; misrepresentation may result in tuition repayment or dismissal
Applicant grants MHEC and the university access to academic records for verification purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students must first be admitted to their academic program, then apply through the ACM Application on the OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov) during one of three annual cycles. Applicants upload two qualifying residency documents as a single PDF. Students also complete the SREB Contact Page with student information. Applications are processed in the order received; once approved, MHEC emails certification to the student and forwards it to the university's ACM Coordinator, who then coordinates with the Financial Aid Office. Check with the institution's ACM Coordinator for any additional requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship program encourages active career and volunteer firefighters, ambulance, and rescue squad members serving Maryland communities to pursue credited college courses leading to a degree or employment in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management. The program aims to support those seeking careers in organized fire departments, ambulance, or rescue squads in Maryland. Enrollment may be full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6–11 credits) as an undergraduate degree-seeking student at an eligible Maryland institution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual award of at least 50% of the student's actual annual tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible institution. The award may not exceed the annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at a 2-year or 4-year public institution within the University System of Maryland (excluding UMGC and UMB). Awards are subject to availability of funds and are renewable for up to five years total. Renewal recipients receive priority over initial applicants; within groups, applicants are ranked by submission date of their completed application. Initial applicants who are awarded must electronically sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before receiving payment. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist pending available funding. If the post-completion service obligation is not fulfilled, the award converts to a service-obligation loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 (2025-2026 academic year); the 2026-2027 application opened January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Actively engaged career or volunteer firefighters, ambulance, or rescue squad members serving Maryland communities who are pursuing credited courses at an eligible institution leading to a degree or employment in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management. Enrollment may be full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6–11 credits) as an undergraduate degree-seeking student at an eligible Maryland institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible Maryland institution for credited courses leading to a degree or employment in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve a Maryland fire, ambulance, or rescue organization. Available to firefighters, ambulance, and rescue squad members actively serving Maryland communities.
requirements_list: Must be actively engaged as a career or volunteer firefighter, ambulance, or rescue squad member in an organized department or service in Maryland
Maryland residency required (dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents)
Volunteer members: must have recorded at least 50 LOSAP points (or equivalent county/municipality points) in at least two different categories in the tax year prior to the award year
Career members: must have worked a minimum of 1,000 hours as part of a fire, ambulance, or rescue squad in the tax year prior to the award year
Must be accepted or enrolled at a Maryland institution each semester
Must maintain a 2.5 GPA for renewal (no GPA requirement for initial applicants)
Must meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirements
Must submit online application through Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) by the closing date
Initial applicants must submit: Riley Application, Service Verification Form, Fire Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation, and LOSAP documentation (if active volunteer)
Initial applicants who are awarded must electronically sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before receiving payment
Renewal applicants must submit: Service Verification Form and LOSAP documentation (if active volunteer)
Renewal recipients are given priority over initial applicants; within groups, ranking is by submission date of completed application
Must commit to 1 year of post-completion service in a Maryland fire, ambulance, or rescue organization; failure to fulfill the obligation converts the award to a loan
FAFSA is not required
Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist pending available funding
Must sign a drug-free pledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. Submit all required documents through the MDCAPS account by the closing date. Initial applicants must provide a Riley Application, Service Verification Form, Fire Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation, and LOSAP documentation (if a volunteer). If awarded, initial applicants must electronically sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before receiving payment. Renewal applicants only need to submit a Service Verification Form and LOSAP documentation. The 2026-2027 application opened January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; renewal recipients receive priority and applicants are ranked by submission date within each group. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist. For questions, contact the Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance at osfamail.mhec@maryland.gov or (410) 767-3300 / (800) 974-0203 / (800) 735-2258 (TTY/Voice).

structured_extraction.program_description: CPIP is a Maryland state grant program that supports college access and completion goals. It provides financial support and fosters collaboration between high-need local education agencies (LEAs) and higher education institutions to raise the academic preparedness of economically and environmentally disadvantaged students in grades 6–12, helping them attend, persist, and succeed in college. The program encourages partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization. The project period runs August 5, 2025 through August 4, 2026, consistent with the State's postsecondary education plan and the College and Career Readiness and College Completion Act of 2013. A 25% institutional match (cash or in-kind) is required, and funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funding (up to $150,000 per project) provided to accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year higher education institutions. Partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization are welcome to apply. A 25% institutional match (cash or in-kind) is required. Budget categories include salaries, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials/supplies, consultant/contractual services, and indirect costs (maximum 8%). Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs. Project period runs August 5, 2025 through August 4, 2026. Disbursement is 50% upfront and 50% upon acceptance of interim report.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. (electronic and paper submission)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year institutions of higher education, in partnership with high-need Local Education Agencies (LEAs), serving middle and high school students (grades 6–12) who are economically and environmentally disadvantaged.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial support for programs that raise the level of academic preparedness of economically and environmentally disadvantaged middle and high school students (grades 6–12) to enable them to attend, persist, and succeed in college. Allowable budget categories include salaries/wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials/supplies, consultant/contractual services, indirect costs (max 8%), rental, and food for FARMS-eligible students. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland counties are listed in the eligibility table (Appendix A). High-need LEAs must meet at least three of four criteria: ≥44.4% FARM in feeder middle schools; ≥39.6% FARM in feeder high schools; FARM cohort graduation rate (2021) < 77.93%; or college remediation rate by residence > 32.7%. Eligible service regions specifically referenced include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Prince George's, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year institution of higher education
Applicant must possess legal authority to apply
Partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization are welcome to apply
Must serve students in grades 6–12 in high-need local education agencies (LEAs)
Must support college access and completion goals consistent with the State's postsecondary education plan and the College and Career Readiness and College Completion Act of 2013
25% institutional match required (cash or in-kind)
Formalized cooperative planning agreement required with participating LEA(s)
Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs
Participation in statewide assessment/evaluation as required by MHEC
Grant records must be retained for 5 years post-completion
Interim and final reports required; second disbursement contingent on acceptance of interim report
All publications must acknowledge MHEC support; non-academic materials must include specified disclaimer
Budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10% per category require prior written approval
Project director changes require prior written approval

High-need LEAs must meet at least three of four eligibility criteria: ≥44.4% FARM in feeder middle schools; ≥39.6% FARM in feeder high schools; FARM cohort graduation rate (2021) < 77.93%; or college remediation rate by residence > 32.7%
Comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act of 1964
Grant MHEC and Legislative Auditor record access rights
Certification by VP-level official required
Failure to submit a final report may result in the project director being ineligible to apply for future grants
Advisory committee required including secondary, postsecondary, business/labor, and community stakeholders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically and in paper form (original plus 2 hard copies plus electronic copy) by July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Electronic submission includes abstract (Word/.docx), full proposal (PDF), and budget (Excel/.xlsx); hard copy includes 1 original plus 5 copies with specified checklist items including cover sheet, abstract, table of contents, narrative, needs assessment, objectives, management plan, personnel forms, operation plan, evaluation plan, budget documents, assurances, cooperative agreements, and staff résumés; signed forms preferred in blue ink. Lead institution and LEA partnership agreement required. Budget narrative must address salaries, fringe, travel, equipment, materials, consultants, and other costs; indirect costs capped at 8%. Proposals are reviewed by a qualified panel; reviewers score proposals individually (100 points total) then convene to discuss and recommend funding to the Secretary of Higher Education. An appeal process is available for disapproved proposals. Contact Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@maryland.gov or 410-767-3087 for additional information. RFP documents (FY2025 CPIP RFP) and proposal forms (Appendix A and Appendix B) are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community College Tuition Waiver for Students with Disabilities Receiving SSI or SSDI
structured_extraction.program_description: This program waives tuition at Maryland community colleges for students who receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits. The waiver covers up to 12 credits per semester for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or up to 6 credits per semester for other enrollment purposes including continuing education leading to employment and life skills instruction. The waiver is applied to any remaining tuition balance after all grants and scholarships have been applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students remain responsible for all other costs such as books.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students are exempt from paying tuition at Maryland community colleges for up to 12 credits per semester when enrolled in a degree or certificate program designed to lead to employment. The waiver is limited to 6 credits per semester for other enrollment purposes, including continuing education leading to employment and life skills instruction. The waiver applies to the tuition balance remaining after all grants and scholarships have been applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students remain responsible for all other costs such as books.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 each year (FAFSA filing deadline for State aid consideration)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities who receive SSI or SSDI benefits and are enrolled or plan to enroll at a Maryland community college.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs at Maryland community colleges for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, continuing education leading to employment, and life skills instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at community colleges throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits
Must provide proof from the Social Security Administration (SSA) of receiving SSI or SSDI benefits
Must complete and file the FAFSA annually between January 1 and March 1 for State aid consideration
Must contact the financial aid office of the community college to activate the waiver
Eligible courses/programs must be degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, continuing education designed to lead to employment, or life skills instruction
A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply
Must request the waiver every time you enroll
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov between January 1 and March 1 each year. Then contact the financial aid office at the community college you plan to attend to have the waiver activated. The waiver must be requested each time you enroll.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Program provides scholarships to students enrolled in approved cybersecurity degree or certificate programs at public or private non-profit institutions in Maryland. Programs must be identified by the Secretary of Higher Education as directly relevant to cybersecurity. Recipients must be within three years of graduation, have at least a 3.0 cumulative GPA, have completed at least 25% of their total credit requirements, and be eligible for in-state tuition. Recipients must agree to work in the cybersecurity field for a qualifying Maryland employer (local education agency, public high school, community college, or state/county/city government unit) after graduation, or teach in a cybersecurity education program at a public high school or community college. If the service obligation is not fulfilled, the award converts to a repayable loan. Part-time students must take a minimum of 6 semester hours per semester (beginning with the 2023-2024 application period).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship award in an amount prescribed by MHEC that can be used for tuition, mandatory fees, room, and board at an eligible Maryland institution. Full-time students may receive the award for up to 3 years; part-time students may receive the award for up to 6 years (taking at least 6 semester hours per semester). Recipients must work 1 year for each scholarship year received in a qualifying cybersecurity position in Maryland. The award converts to a loan if the recipient fails to complete the approved cybersecurity program or fulfill the required work obligation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2025-2026 academic year application deadline April 1, 2026; 2026-2027 application opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled full-time or part-time at a Maryland public or private non-profit institution in an approved cybersecurity degree or certificate program who are within three years of graduation, have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0, have completed at least 25% of their total credit requirements, and are eligible for in-state tuition. Part-time students must take at least 6 semester hours per semester and may receive the award for up to 6 years (beginning with the 2023-2024 cycle). Also includes high school students in career/technology education programs related to cybersecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, room, and board at an eligible Maryland institution, as defined by MHEC.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland and must be eligible for in-state tuition under the provisions of Education Article, Title 15, Annotated Code of Maryland. The required post-graduation service obligation must be fulfilled in the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Enrolled full-time or part-time at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland in an approved, credit-bearing cybersecurity degree or certificate program identified by the Secretary of Higher Education as directly relevant to cybersecurity
Within three years of graduation from the approved program
Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 at the time of application
Completed at least 25% of total credit requirements toward the approved degree or certificate program
Eligible for in-state tuition under Education Article, Title 15, Annotated Code of Maryland
Must not be a recipient of a Federal Cyber Corps Scholarships for Service award

Must sign an agreement to work in Maryland in the cybersecurity field for a qualifying employer (local education agency, public high school, community college, or state/county/city/municipal government unit) or teach in a cybersecurity education program at a public high school or community college in Maryland
Must work 1 year for each scholarship year received in a full-time qualifying cybersecurity position in Maryland
Part-time students must take a minimum of 6 semester hours per semester (beginning with the 2023-2024 application period)
Must remain drug-free for the full award term
Cannot falsify or conceal material facts in the application
Renewal requires continued eligibility for in-state tuition, satisfactory academic progress, and at least a 3.0 GPA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us using the MHEC One App. Upload all required documents, including an official or unofficial college transcript and the Institutional Verification Form (completed by the institution), through your MDCAPS account by the closing date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland legislative scholarship program that provides financial assistance to Maryland residents attending college. Administered by state legislators (delegates and senators) through the Maryland Higher Education Commission, the scholarships are available to current high school seniors and degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students who have completed their FAFSA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funding for Maryland residents attending college. Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident high school seniors and degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students in Cecil County's legislative districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College education expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland residents; eligibility is tied to the applicant's legislative district
requirements_list: Maryland residency
Must be a current high school senior or degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student
Must have completed FAFSA
Must apply through the Maryland Higher Education Commission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find your legislative district, complete FAFSA, then contact your elected officials (delegates or senators) for more information. Apply through the Maryland Higher Education Commission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant is a need-based grant that provides financial assistance to eligible low-income Maryland residents enrolled full-time in undergraduate programs at eligible two-year or four-year Maryland postsecondary institutions. The grant covers up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first two academic years of enrollment, up to the annual maximum award amount ($18,000 for the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 academic years; minimum award $100–$400 per year depending on award year). Awards are calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation, and financial need. The grant is renewable for up to three additional years if renewal requirements are met, including maintaining full-time enrollment, satisfactory academic progress, and meeting income requirements. After two years of receipt, renewal requires completion of 30 credits annually for full renewal or 24–29 credits for a prorated renewal. Eligible students include U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition. All awarding is contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grant covering up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first two academic years of enrollment, or up to the maximum award amount (whichever is lower). The maximum award is $18,000 per academic year (2025-2026 and 2026-2027); the minimum award is $100–$400 per year. Grant amounts are based on cost of attendance, living situation, and financial need. Eligible expenses include tuition, fees, room and board, and approved educational expenses. The grant is renewable for up to three additional years with continued eligibility. Starting in year 3, renewal requires completion of at least 30 credits in the prior year for a full award; 24–29 credits results in a prorated award; fewer than 24 credits results in ineligibility. All awarding is contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1 of the award year; documentation by August 1 of the award year (e.g., March 1, 2026 for 2026-2027; August 1, 2026 for documentation)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents who are first-time or returning undergraduate students (under age 26 at time of first receipt; born after July 1, 2000 for 2026-2027) with family income at or below 130% of federal poverty guidelines for initial applicants and 150% (or Pell-eligible) for renewal applicants, enrolling full-time at eligible two- or four-year Maryland postsecondary institutions, including U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition. Must begin college within six years of high school graduation or GED receipt and be pursuing a first undergraduate degree.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses at eligible Maryland two-year or four-year postsecondary institutions, including tuition, fees, room and board, and approved educational expenses. Award amount covers up to 100% of calculated adjusted financial need (up to the annual maximum). For renewal recipients in years 3 and beyond, award amounts are tied to credit completion benchmarks: 30+ credits in the prior year for a full award; 24–29 credits for a prorated award; fewer than 24 credits results in ineligibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland and must list a Maryland college or university on their FAFSA or MHEC One-App, and must enroll at an eligible two-year or four-year Maryland postsecondary institution.
requirements_list: Be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland
File the FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1 of the award year with a Maryland institution listed

Meet initial income requirements: total family income at or below 130% of the federal poverty guidelines (e.g., $18,954 for household of 1; $39,000 for household of 4 based on 2023 guidelines; or at or below 130% of 2024 federal poverty guidelines for 2026-2027)
Submit any required documentation by the documentation deadline (July 15, 2025 for 2025-2026; August 1, 2026 for 2026-2027)
Be accepted for admission and plan to enroll full-time (12 credits/semester) as a degree-seeking undergraduate student at an eligible Maryland institution
Have completed high school or obtained a GED with a passing score of 145 per module
Begin college within 6 years of completing high school or obtaining a GED
Be under age 26 at time of first receiving the GA grant (born after July 1, 1999 for 2025-2026; born after July 1, 2000 for 2026-2027)
Cannot have previously received an Educational Assistance Grant or Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant
Cannot have previously received a bachelor's degree prior to the start of the award year

Renewal: remain eligible for in-state tuition, file FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1, meet renewal income requirements (at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines or remain Pell-eligible), enroll full-time, and maintain satisfactory academic progress
After two years of receipt, renewal requires completion of 30 credits annually for full renewal or 24–29 credits for a prorated renewal; fewer than 24 credits results in ineligibility

Only credits graded above 'F' count toward credit completion requirements; certificate program credits do not count; dual-enrolled high school students are excluded from credit completion requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no separate application for the GA Grant. Students must submit a FAFSA (U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens) or MHEC One-App (undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition) by March 1 of the applicable award year, with a Maryland institution listed. MHEC's MDCAPS system automatically considers students who meet basic eligibility requirements. Some students will be asked to submit additional documentation through their MDCAPS account (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us) by the applicable documentation deadline. For 2026-2027, awarding began in early April 2026 and continues on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted. Award disbursement to students typically begins in September for the fall term and February for the spring term. Students accept their award via the MDCAPS online portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship (VAIC) provides financial assistance to U.S. armed forces personnel who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts, and their eligible family members (son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter, or spouse), to attend a Maryland postsecondary institution as undergraduate students. Renewal recipients receive priority over new applicants, and eligible veterans receive priority over dependents or spouses. Awards supplement federal education benefits and may not exceed cost of attendance. Recipients may renew for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards up to 50% of the annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at the highest-cost four-year public University System of Maryland institution (excluding UMGC and UMB). Maximum award amounts for 2026-2027: On Campus up to $9,189; With Parents up to $5,186; Off Campus up to $5,756. For reference, 2025-2026 maximums were: On Campus up to $8,699; With Parents up to $5,067; Off Campus up to $5,637. Funds may be used at any eligible Maryland institution for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board. Awards supplement (not replace) federal education benefits and may not exceed cost of attendance. Renewal recipients receive priority over new applicants; eligible veterans receive priority over dependents or spouses. Recipients may renew for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15, 2026 (2026-2027 academic year); April 1, 2026 (2025-2026 academic year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. armed forces veterans and active duty members who served in Afghanistan or Iraq, members of reserve components or the Maryland National Guard activated for those conflicts, and their spouses, sons, daughters, stepsons, or stepdaughters who are Maryland residents enrolled or accepted at a Maryland postsecondary institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at any eligible Maryland postsecondary institution. Awards may be adjusted or canceled if total financial aid exceeds cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents enrolled or accepted in an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution. Active military members stationed in Maryland or whose home of residency is Maryland are considered residents.
requirements_list: Must have served in the Afghanistan Conflict on or after October 24, 2001 (or in Afghanistan or contiguous air space), or in the Iraq Conflict on or after March 19, 2003 (or in Iraq or contiguous waters or air space), or be an eligible family member (spouse, son, daughter, stepson, or stepdaughter) of such a servicemember.
Must be a Maryland resident (includes active military stationed in Maryland).
Must be enrolled or accepted in a regular undergraduate program or an eligible 2-year terminal certificate program at a Maryland postsecondary institution.
Must be enrolled at least part-time (6+ credits per semester; full-time is 12+ credits per semester).
If filing the FAFSA or MHEC One-App for Undocumented Students, it must be completed by March 1 of the applicable award year.

Required documentation varies by applicant type: veterans must submit DD-214; active duty must submit current military orders; spouses must submit marriage certificate and military orders; children must submit birth certificate and military orders.
Renewal recipients must remain enrolled in an eligible Maryland program, maintain Maryland residency, and make satisfactory academic progress.
For renewal: must maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale.
Award acceptance must be completed within six weeks of notification.
Total financial aid including this award may not exceed cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the MHEC One-App on the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. Upload all required supporting documents (DD-214, military orders, birth/marriage certificate as applicable) through your MDCAPS account by the applicable closing date. For the 2026-2027 academic year, applications open January 15, 2026 and close October 15, 2026. The 2025-2026 application opened April 15, 2025 and closed April 1, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; renewal students are prioritized and new applicants ranked by submission date. FAFSA or state aid application is not required to determine eligibility, but if filed, must meet the March 1 deadline. Award notifications sent via email; awardees must accept in MDCAPS within six weeks of notification. Payment is issued 6-8 weeks after the institution completes enrollment certification and payment request. Renewal recipients do not need to reapply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program & Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program provides student financial assistance to certain Maryland residents due to their eligible military or public safety service, or due to their family or marital relationship to such an individual. Eligible categories include children, stepchildren, surviving spouses, and veterans connected to military service or public safety employees killed or disabled in the line of duty, as well as September 11 victims' family members and Vietnam-era POW/MIA families. The Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program provides financial assistance to eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or sustained a 100% disabling injury as a victim of violence in the line of duty. Both programs are administered together through eligible Maryland higher education institutions and awards are available for undergraduate, graduate, professional, or two-year terminal certificate programs, including private career schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award up to $14,086 for the 2026-2027 academic year (up from $13,689 for 2025-2026). The award may not exceed the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland. A minimum of $3,000 or the institution's annual tuition/fees (whichever is less) applies. No more than 15 Conroy-Cryor scholarships may be awarded annually to veterans with a 25%+ service-connected disability. Awards may be held for up to 5 years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester), 8 years of part-time study (6–11 credits per semester), or a combination of both. Renewal is automatic through the institution's financial aid office. Funds cover tuition and mandatory fees only (not room, board, books, etc.).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are veterans with service-connected disabilities, active-duty military members, public safety employees, school employees, or their eligible children, stepchildren, or surviving spouses who meet specific disability, death, or service-related criteria, including September 11 victims' family members and Vietnam-era POW/MIA family members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student financial assistance for tuition and mandatory fees only (not room, board, books, or other expenses) at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions offering undergraduate, graduate, professional, or two-year terminal certificate programs, including private career schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must generally be Maryland residents at the time of application. Certain public safety employee family members (children and surviving spouses of public safety employees killed or disabled in the line of duty) and disabled public safety employees are exempt from the Maryland residency requirement.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled at least part-time in a regular undergraduate, graduate, professional, or two-year terminal certificate program at an eligible institution, or enrolled in a private career school
Must be at least 16 years old

Must qualify under at least one eligible category: child/stepchild or surviving spouse of a U.S. Armed Forces member who died or was 100% permanently disabled due to military service (service after December 7, 1941); veteran with a service-connected disability of 25% or greater who has exhausted federal veterans' educational benefits; child/stepchild or surviving spouse of a September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victim; POW/MIA of the Vietnam Conflict (on or after January 1, 1960) or their child/stepchild who was a Maryland resident when declared POW/MIA; child/stepchild or surviving spouse of a State or local public safety employee who died or was 100% disabled in the line of duty; State or local public safety employee or volunteer who was 100% disabled in the line of duty; child/stepchild or surviving spouse of a school employee who died or was 100% disabled due to an act of violence in the line of duty
Must generally be a Maryland resident at the time of application (with exceptions for certain public safety employee family members and disabled public safety employees)
Awards may be held for 5 years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or 8 years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester), or a combination of both
No more than 15 scholarships may be awarded annually to veterans with a 25% or greater service-connected disability
Award may be reduced or cancelled if total financial aid exceeds cost of attendance
FAFSA is not required (non-need-based scholarship)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants must contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions. All applications and required documentation are submitted directly to the institution — do not submit anything directly to MHEC. The institution processes applications and is reimbursed by the state. Initial awards are automatically renewed by the financial aid office for the next academic year. Apply by July 15 each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Next Generation Scholars of Maryland (NGS) Program is a college access program established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2016 (HB 1403). It supports low-income, first-generation college students in high-poverty school systems by providing a cohort-based model of mentoring, guidance, and postsecondary educational support. Cohorts are identified as early as 8th grade and receive support through high school graduation and into the first year of college. FY 2026 grants continue funding to nonprofit organizations that were awarded grants in FY 2025, with a Grant Information Guide issued on June 2, 2025. Required program components include high school graduation planning, summer work or internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, visits to college campuses and workplaces, intensive summer bridge programs, outreach and registration plans, and plans to matriculate and graduate from institutions of higher education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $5,000,000 are available for FY 2026, with an estimated 11–15 grants to be awarded. Funds support nonprofit organizations providing college access guidance, mentoring, and support services to cohort students who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant in eligible school districts, supporting them through high school graduation and into their first year of college. Allowable costs include salaries/wages, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials/supplies, travel, and equipment. Funds may not be used to supplant existing funds, for capital improvements, gift cards, or pre-approval costs. The grant period runs July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations that were awarded Next Generation Scholars Program grants in FY 2025 and serve grade 7–12 students in eligible high-poverty school districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing guidance, mentoring, and support services to cohort students who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant in eligible school districts, helping them successfully transition to college and receive support during their first year of college. Required program components include high school graduation planning, summer work or internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, visits to college campuses and workplaces, intensive summer bridge programs for students entering higher education directly from high school, outreach and registration plans, and plans to matriculate and graduate from institutions of higher education. Allowable expenditures include salaries/wages, contracted services, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials/supplies, travel, equipment, and indirect costs. Funds may not be used to supplant existing funds, for capital improvements, gift cards, or costs incurred prior to approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible school districts: Allegany County Public Schools, Baltimore City Public Schools, Caroline County Public Schools, Dorchester County Public Schools, Kent County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, Somerset County Public Schools, and Wicomico County Public Schools. Nonprofits must support students in one or more of these school systems.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization
Must have been awarded a Next Generation Scholars Program grant in FY 2025
Must support grade 7–12 students in one or more of the eligible school systems
Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025 via email to tiffany.majors1@maryland.gov

Application must include all required appendices: Cover Page (A), Budget Form & Narrative signed (B), Statement of Assurances (C), evidence of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status (D), and Key Personnel Resumes (E)
Must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and ADA
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation
Must maintain records for 5 years
Must not supplant non-grant funds
Prior written approval required for any significant changes to approved projects (timeline, activities, key staff, or budget changes >$1,000 or >10% of approved line item)
Amendment requests must be submitted at least 45 days before the grant period ends
Project period extension requests must be submitted no less than one month before the original expiration date
Final invoices must be submitted within 60 days after the grant period ends
Annual evaluation reports and quarterly progress reports are required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the fillable application form electronically by typing directly into the fillable fields and charts, do not alter or remove sections, and save the completed, signed application as a single PDF. Email the signed PDF to tiffany.majors1@maryland.gov with the subject line 'NGS FY26 Submission' by 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025. The application must include: (1) Proposal Cover Page signed by Superintendent/Head of Grantee Agency, (2) Project Abstract, (3) Extent of Need, (4) Evidence of Impact, (5) Goals, Measurable Outcomes, and Milestones, (6) Management Plan, (7) Evaluation Plan, and (8) Budget and Budget Narrative using MHEC's C-1-25 budget form. Required appendices: Cover Page (A), Budget Form & Narrative signed (B), Statement of Assurances (C), evidence of 501(c)(3) status (D), and Key Personnel Resumes (E). MHEC staff are available to provide technical assistance throughout the application process. Applications are reviewed July 2–9, 2025 by a committee of Maryland State Department of Education and MHEC representatives using a scoring rubric covering Extent of Need, Evidence of Impact, Goals/Outcomes/Milestones, Management Plan, Evaluation & Dissemination, and Budget & Narrative. Award notifications are issued July 10–18, 2025. The Grant Information Guide was released on June 2, 2025. Grant recipients must obtain prior written approval to make any significant changes to approved projects; extension requests must be submitted at least one month before the original expiration date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tuition assistance to students who are dependents or surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers. Students can be enrolled in undergraduate, graduate, professional, or 2-year terminal certificate programs at eligible institutions in Maryland, or in private career schools. Awards help cover tuition and mandatory fees at eligible Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance award up to the lesser of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident at the attended institution, and not to exceed the highest annual tuition and fees of a full-time resident undergraduate at a four-year public University System of Maryland institution (excluding UMUC and UM Baltimore). Awards may be held for up to 5 years of full-time study (12+ credits/semester) or 8 years of part-time study (6–11 credits/semester). The maximum award for 2026-2027 has not yet been determined. Awards are contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who are a dependent child, stepchild, or surviving spouse of a fallen transportation worker (who died on or after January 1, 2022, in a work-related accident while performing job duties for a transportation facility/project in Maryland), are at least 16 years old, and are enrolled or planning to enroll in an eligible higher education program in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees only at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions. May not be used for living expenses, books, or other costs of attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must attend an eligible institution in Maryland. Available to Maryland residents attending eligible institutions.
requirements_list: Must be at least 16 years old
Must be the child, stepchild, or surviving spouse (not remarried) of a fallen transportation worker who died on or after January 1, 2022
Death must have resulted from an accident while the worker was performing job duties for a transportation facility or project in Maryland

Must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits undergraduate; 9+ credits graduate) or part-time (6–11 credits undergraduate; 6–8 credits graduate) in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution, OR enrolled in a 2-year terminal certificate program with coursework transferable to an accredited baccalaureate program, OR enrolled in a private career school
Drug-free pledge required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions. Do not submit applications or documentation directly to MHEC. All required documentation should be submitted to the institution's financial aid office. Initial awards are automatically renewed by the financial aid office at the attending institution.

structured_extraction.program_description: The GEAR UP (Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs) Scholarship provides financial aid to students who previously participated in GEAR UP activities in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties. Awards are made after federal Pell Grant, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. Students must complete the FAFSA and a GEAR UP Scholarship Application to be considered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum award is $15,000 for fall and spring of the 2023-2024 academic year and $10,000 for summer 2023. Award amount varies based on financial need but will not exceed the student's cost of attendance (COA). Awards are made after federal Pell Grant, state aid, and other aid have been applied.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 each year (FAFSA); Summer 2023 application due July 1, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the 2014-2020 grant period, are Maryland residents, are under 22 years old, and are enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an eligible higher education program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Undergraduate education expenses up to the cost of attendance at an accredited two- or four-year institution of higher education, private career school, or state/regional accredited trade school/certificate program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must have participated in GEAR UP activities in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020) and be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must have participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020)
Must be a Maryland resident according to the institution's state residency policy
Must be enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an accredited two- or four-year institution, private career school, or state/regional accredited trade school/certificate program
Must have received a high school diploma or its recognized equivalent
Must be less than 22 years old at the time of the first scholarship award
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress per the institution's standards
Must complete the FAFSA by March 1 each year
Must complete the GEAR UP Scholarship Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov by March 1 each year, then complete and submit the GEAR UP Scholarship Application (available on the program page). Applications are processed and verified following the drop/add period at the institution. If eligible, students are notified via the email listed on the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund – Maryland Community College Workforce Development
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal COVID-19 relief grant allocated by Governor Hogan to Maryland community colleges to provide workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure. The program primarily targeted individuals who lost employment due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000,000 total distributed to 16 Maryland community colleges as grants to fund workforce development and continuing professional education courses. Individual awards ranged from $250,000 to approximately $1.48 million per college.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges serving individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to all 16 Maryland community colleges
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland community college
Courses must lead to government or industry certification or licensure
Primarily focused on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds were allocated directly to Maryland community colleges by the Governor. Contact Priscilla Moore for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief Fund II (GEER II)
structured_extraction.program_description: The GEER II Fund, authorized under the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations (CRRSA) Act of 2021 and funded through the U.S. Department of Education, provided supplemental grants to Maryland community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities for emergency COVID-19 relief. Governor Hogan allocated $10 million: $7.4 million to community colleges for workforce development and continuing professional education leading to certification or licensure, targeting individuals who lost employment due to COVID-19; and $2.6 million to Maryland independent colleges and universities to cover institutional costs from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time supplemental grants distributed to named institutions: $7.4 million total to 16 community colleges (ranging from $185,000 to $1,095,645 per institution) and $2.6 million total to 13 private nonprofit colleges and universities ($200,000 each).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities affected by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community colleges: workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, targeting individuals impacted by COVID-19 job loss. Private nonprofit colleges and universities: institutional costs resulting from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide — specific named institutions only
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland community college or private nonprofit college/university
Community college funding targets workforce development and continuing education leading to certification or licensure
Private nonprofit funding addresses institutional COVID-19 costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds were allocated directly by Governor Hogan to named institutions; no open application process described.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program provides financial assistance to degree-seeking graduate and professional students in Maryland who demonstrate financial need. Awards range from $1,000 to $5,000 per year and are available for graduate and professional programs in dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine at designated Maryland institutions. Awards are based on demonstrated financial need as shown on the FAFSA and may be renewed for up to eight semesters if eligibility requirements are maintained, including remaining enrolled in an eligible program, maintaining satisfactory academic progress, filing a FAFSA each year, and demonstrating continued financial need. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards ranging from a minimum of $1,000 to a maximum of $5,000 per year. Awards are based on demonstrated financial need as shown on the FAFSA. Recipients may receive funding for up to eight semesters if they remain enrolled in an eligible program, maintain satisfactory academic progress, file a FAFSA each year, and demonstrate continued financial need. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact the financial aid office of the school you will attend for their deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Degree-seeking graduate and professional students who are Maryland residents and demonstrate financial need, enrolled part-time or full-time in eligible programs (dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, or veterinary medicine) at designated Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for graduate and professional education expenses in eligible programs including dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine at qualifying Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Must attend one of the following eligible institutions: University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB) Schools of Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Pharmacy, or Social Work; University of Baltimore School of Law; The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; The Virginia-Maryland Regional College of Veterinary Medicine; or certain Maryland institutions offering a master's degree in nursing or social work or a first professional degree in pharmacy.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must demonstrate financial need as shown on the FAFSA
Must be enrolled as a degree-seeking student (part-time or full-time) in an eligible graduate or professional program
Must attend one of the designated eligible institutions
Eligible programs include dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine
For renewal: remain enrolled in an eligible program
For renewal: maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution
For renewal: file a FAFSA each year
For renewal: continue to demonstrate financial need
Maximum of eight semesters of funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the FAFSA at studentaid.gov. Then contact the financial aid office of the institution you plan to attend and request consideration for a Graduate and Professional Scholarship. The institution determines eligibility, deadlines, and renewal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program for graduate nursing students in Maryland who are preparing to become nursing faculty. The program is now closed — MHEC is no longer accepting new applications because funding is no longer available. Existing recipients may continue to access their awards through their approved graduate program, subject to their service obligation agreement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards for graduate nursing students committed to teaching as nursing faculty. Awards are disbursed through the recipient's institution. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation to prepare to teach nursing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No longer accepting applications; funding no longer available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Graduate nursing students in Maryland who intend to become nursing faculty
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Graduate nursing education costs for students preparing to teach nursing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a graduate nursing program
Must commit to preparing to teach nursing (service obligation)
Must sign a service obligation agreement and promissory note
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closed to new applicants. Current recipients should contact Peggy Daw or Kimberly Ford with questions about continuing eligibility and service obligations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant (CBEAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based financial aid grant program for full-time undergraduate students who missed Maryland's state FAFSA or MSFAA deadline (March 1st priority deadline) and were therefore not considered for the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant. Participating Maryland colleges and universities receive an annual allocation of state funds each academic year and select qualifying students to receive awards. Students at four-year institutions receive 40% of their OSFA adjusted financial need; students at community colleges receive 60%. Award amounts range from $400 to $3,000 per year. Total state aid may not exceed the cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less. Students are encouraged to complete the FAFSA each year by June 1st for other state grant opportunities; if the deadline is missed, they should contact their institution for CBEAG consideration. Students cannot hold the CBEAG simultaneously with the Guaranteed Access Grant, Part-Time Grant, or Educational Assistance Grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant ranging from $400 to $3,000 per year. Students at four-year institutions receive a CBEAG award equal to 40% of their OSFA (Office of Student Financial Assistance) adjusted financial need; students at community colleges receive 60% of OSFA adjusted need. Total state aid may not exceed the cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact your college's financial aid office; FAFSA must be filed after the March 1st state deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students who are Maryland residents and filed the FAFSA after the March 1st state priority deadline but are eligible for the federal Pell Grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance toward educational expenses (cost of attendance) at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university.
