structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant and parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Student must enroll at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident (and parents, if dependent student)
Must enroll full-time (12+ credits per semester) as a degree-seeking undergraduate at a Maryland two-year or four-year institution
Audited courses cannot count toward the 12-credit minimum for full-time status
Must have filed the FAFSA after the March 1st state priority deadline
Must be eligible to receive the federal Pell Grant
Cannot hold the CBEAG simultaneously with the Guaranteed Access Grant, Part-Time Grant, or Educational Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact their college or university's financial aid office directly to be considered. Institutions receive a CBEAG allocation each academic year and select eligible students from that pool. Students who did not submit the FAFSA by the March 1st deadline should reach out to their institution's financial aid office for CBEAG consideration. Students are encouraged to complete the FAFSA each year by June 1st for other state grant opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance (EA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Educational Assistance (EA) Grant is part of the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards. It is a need-based grant that provides financial assistance to eligible Maryland students enrolled at postsecondary institutions for educational expenses. Students may receive between $400 and $3,000 per year for up to four years (initial year plus up to three renewals), contingent on availability of funds. Award amounts are calculated based on the OSFA-adjusted institutional cost of attendance, adjusted for housing/living status and a regional cost of living factor, minus the Student Aid Index (SAI), certain state awards, and the federal Pell Grant. There is no separate application — students are automatically considered when they file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App and list a Maryland institution. Awards are renewable for up to three additional years contingent on continued eligibility and fund availability. Disbursement occurs in September (Fall) and February (Spring).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grants of $400 to $3,000 per year, renewable for up to four years total (initial year plus up to three renewals), contingent on availability of funds. Award is calculated using the OSFA-adjusted institutional cost of attendance, adjusted for regional cost of living, minus the Student Aid Index (SAI), certain state awards, and the federal Pell Grant. No separate application is required; students are automatically considered when they file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App with a Maryland institution listed. Disbursement occurs in September (Fall) and February (Spring). Awarding begins in Summer 2026 for the 2026-2027 award year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1, 2026 (FAFSA or MHEC One-App); August 1, 2026 (documentation deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland undergraduate students who are high school seniors or enrolled full-time at an eligible two- or four-year Maryland institution, who are eligible for in-state tuition, and who demonstrate financial need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses at eligible postsecondary institutions in Maryland. Award funds are disbursed directly to eligible students covering general educational expenses such as tuition, fees, and related costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland and must attend an eligible Maryland two-year or four-year institution (exception for deaf or hearing-impaired students requiring specialized out-of-state programs not available in Maryland, and limited exceptions for Academic Common Market reciprocal programs). Applicants must list a Maryland college or university on their FAFSA or MHEC One-App.
requirements_list: Be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland
File the FAFSA or MHEC One-App (for undocumented students) by March 1, 2026 with a Maryland institution listed
Demonstrate financial need
Be a currently enrolled high school senior OR enrolled full-time (12 credits/semester) as a degree-seeking undergraduate at an eligible Maryland two- or four-year institution
Must not have previously received a bachelor's degree before the start of the award year
Submit any required documentation by August 1, 2026 through MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us

Renewal requires maintaining in-state tuition eligibility, filing annual FAFSA or MHEC One-App, continuing to demonstrate financial need, enrolling full-time, and meeting satisfactory academic progress standards
After at least two years of receiving the award, must complete 30 credits annually for full renewal or 24–29 credits for a prorated renewal
Students who complete fewer than 24 credits in the third or fourth year are ineligible to renew
No Federal Title IV loan default
Cannot use audited courses toward full-time status credit minimum
Drug-free pledge required
Audited courses do not count toward credit completion requirements
High school seniors and dually enrolled students are excluded from credit completion requirements; dual enrollment credits do not count
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no separate application for the EA Grant. Students are automatically considered when they file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App (for undocumented students) by the applicable deadline and list a Maryland institution. The MDCAPS system automatically considers students who meet the basic eligibility requirements. Some students may be asked to submit additional documentation through their MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us by the documentation deadline. For the 2026-2027 award year, the FAFSA/One-App deadline is March 1, 2026 and the documentation deadline is August 1, 2026. Awarding begins in Summer 2026, with disbursement in September (Fall) and February (Spring).

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state grant program that funds public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers (RHECs) to address food insecurity among students. Goals include addressing student hunger, developing and implementing sustainable food solutions, raising awareness of on-campus food services, and building local, state, and national partnerships to combat food insecurity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to eligible Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers (RHECs) that have been designated as a hunger-free campus and pledge a 25% matching contribution. FY 2025 awards totaled $150,000. FY 2026 individual awards ranged from $10,000 to $22,000. The grant period runs October 15, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of total direct costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers that have been designated as hunger-free campuses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Efforts to address food insecurity among students, including implementing sustainable food solutions, raising awareness of on-campus food services, and building local, state, and national partnerships to address student hunger. May also support emergency assistance, hiring staff to manage program-related initiatives, and operational activities related to program implementation. Eligible cost categories include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment (with life expectancy and post-grant use plan), materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other costs. Funds must supplement new or existing programs and cannot supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland public institution of higher education or regional higher education center

Must be designated as a hunger-free campus by meeting six core criteria: task force, SNAP enrollment staff, SNAP eligibility staff, awareness event, food pantry or stigma-free arrangement, annual survey, and annual report; four-year and private institutions have additional requirements including SNAP at campus stores and a meal-sharing program
Must pledge a 25% matching contribution (cash or in-kind) to implement the goals of the program
Must possess legal authority; governing body authorization required
Authorized signatory must be President, VP level, or above
Funds must supplement new or existing programs and cannot supplant non-grant funds
Must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (employment discrimination prohibition)
Must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act and amendments
Must participate in statewide assessment and evaluation programs as required by MHEC
Must grant MHEC and Office of Legislative Audits access to all records related to the grant
Must comply with all MHEC special requirements and administrative requirements
Must submit interim and final financial and narrative reports; failure to submit final report may result in ineligibility for future grants

Prior written approval required for scope changes, program director replacement or absence exceeding 3 months, key personnel effort reductions, staff or consultant additions or deletions, budget changes of $1,000 or more or 10% or more per category (whichever is greater), and grant extension requests
Grant extensions limited to a single extension; must be requested at least one month before expiration with explanation of need and estimate of unobligated funds
Closeout required within 90 days of grant expiration; all financial, performance, and evaluation reports due at that time
All grant records must be retained for 5 years after completion
All publications must acknowledge MHEC and include required disclaimer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application electronically in PDF format to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@maryland.gov by the deadline (October 6, 2025 by 5:00 PM). Required components in order: Cover Sheet (Appendix A), Table of Contents, Grant Narrative (maximum 10 single-spaced pages, 8.5x11 inches, 1-inch margins, 12-point Arial/Times New Roman/Calibri, numbered pages), Budget Summary (Appendix B), Budget Narrative (detailed line-item justification for salaries/wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment with life expectancy and post-grant use plan, supplies, consultant/contractual services, and other costs; equipment requires written estimates/invoices and institutional procurement compliance; indirect costs capped at 8% of total direct costs), and Statement of Assurances (Appendix C). Application materials including RFA form, appendices, and budget summary are available on the program page. Award notification via email prior to midnight on October 15, 2025. Technical assistance is available from the contact throughout the process. Post-award, grantees must submit interim and final reports to the Office of Outreach and Grants Management; MHEC may conduct site visits, telephone interviews, or request written materials for monitoring purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inmate Training and Job Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funds to eligible public historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) and other designated institutions of higher education in Maryland to establish pilot programs offering educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in the 12 months preceding their release from Maryland correctional institutions. The goal is to expand and improve higher education pathways for incarcerated individuals. The FY 2025 grant period runs from August 8, 2025 through June 30, 2026, with eligible institutions including Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Initial grants of up to $25,000 are awarded to support a six-month implementation period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funds of up to $25,000 per institution are awarded to eligible HBCUs to support a six-month implementation period for educational and vocational training programs for incarcerated individuals. The FY 2025 grant period runs from August 8, 2025 through June 30, 2026, with a final report due September 30, 2026. Eligible institutions are Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Continuation grants are available for institutions that enroll participants by December 15, 2025. Allowable uses include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, and consultant/contractual services; indirect costs capped at 8%. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs. Record retention required for 5 years. MHEC and the Office of Legislative Audits retain right of access to records.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible institutions of higher education (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore) that can provide educational and vocational training to inmates at Maryland correctional institutions in the 12 months preceding their release.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing pilot programs to provide educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in the 12 months preceding their release from Maryland correctional institutions. Allowable costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, and consultant/contractual services (indirect costs capped at 8%). Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and may not be used to supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates at Maryland correctional institutions statewide. Eligible applicants are four designated Maryland public HBCUs.
requirements_list: Applicant must be one of the four eligible institutions: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
Program must target inmates in the 12 months preceding release from a Maryland correctional institution
Must respond to the FY 2025 Request for Proposals (RFP) by July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m.
Proposal must include: Statement of Need, Program Description, Goals/Objectives/Outcomes, Staffing Plan, Operations Plan, Program Evaluation, Sustainability Plan, Budget and Narrative
Proposals scored: 70% narrative, 20% budget, 10% approach/feasibility
Applicant must have legal authority to apply
Compliance with Title VI Civil Rights Act (1964) — no employment discrimination
Compliance with Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and amendments
Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs
Participation in statewide assessment/evaluation programs as required by MHEC
Record retention for 5 years
Right of access to records, books, and documents for MHEC and Office of Legislative Audits
Authorized under Annotated Code of Maryland, Education Article, Subtitle 13, §§ 24-1301 through 24-1306
To be eligible for continuation grants, institutions must enroll participants by December 15, 2025
Grantees who fail to submit a final report are ineligible for future grants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions submit a proposal in response to the RFP by the due date of July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Application forms and appendices (including Appendix A, B, and C) are available for download from the MHEC website. Proposals are submitted to the Office of Outreach and Grants Management, Maryland Higher Education Commission, 217 E. Redwood St, Suite 2100, Baltimore, MD 21202. For questions, contact Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov or (410) 767-3087.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program provides financial assistance of up to $500 per academic year to full-time students attending approved private career schools in Maryland. Awards are reviewed on a rolling basis and may be renewed one time if the student continues to meet enrollment and FAFSA filing requirements, including remaining enrolled in at least 18 clock hours per week at an approved Maryland private career school. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of up to $500 per academic year per eligible student. Awards are reviewed on a rolling basis. The award may be renewed one time if the student remains enrolled in at least 18 clock hours per week at an approved Maryland private career school and continues to file the FAFSA. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 15, 2026 (2025-2026 academic year); reviewed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time Maryland resident students enrolled in approved private career schools in Maryland, including dependent students whose parent is a Maryland resident.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for students attending approved private career schools in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (or, for dependent students, the parent must be a Maryland resident). Students must attend an approved Maryland private career school.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled at an approved Maryland private career school
Must be enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week
Must be a Maryland resident (dependent students require a Maryland resident parent)
Must complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
Must submit a Tolbert Grant Program application at the financial aid office of the private career school attended
Renewal: continues enrollment at an approved Maryland private career school, continues enrollment in at least 18 clock hours per week, and files the FAFSA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the financial aid office at your private career school. Complete and file the FAFSA and submit the Tolbert Grant Program application at the school's financial aid office. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; submit all required materials promptly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) provides State assistance to help repay educational loans for individuals who work full time in eligible public service employment fields serving low-income or underserved Maryland residents. Awards are based on total educational debt and structured as multi-year lock-in awards with annual payments up to $10,000. Recipients are locked into a three-year award tier based on their total educational debt. Eligible professions include lawyers, nurses, nurse faculty, licensed clinical counselors, physical and occupational therapists, social workers, speech pathologists, veterinary practitioners/technicians, teachers (public schools, Title I schools, MSDE-identified improvement schools), mental health professionals in public schools, and public school nurses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients receive annual loan repayment assistance payments based on their total educational debt. Awards are locked in for a three-year tier: debt over $75,001 receives up to $10,000/year (max $30,000 total); debt $40,001–$75,000 receives up to $6,000/year (max $18,000 total); debt $15,001–$40,000 receives up to $3,000/year (max $9,000 total); debt $15,000 or below receives up to $1,500/year (max $4,500 total). Payment amounts cannot exceed the applicant's total debt. Payment is issued as a single lump sum to the recipient, who must remit to their lender(s) within 120 days and provide proof of payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 (2025-2026 cycle, now closed); October 15, 2026 (2026-2027 award year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who have graduated from a Maryland institution, are employed full time in Maryland in an eligible public service field, have qualifying educational loans, and are serving low-income or underserved Maryland residents. Eligible professions include lawyers, nurses, nurse faculty, licensed clinical counselors, physical and occupational therapists, social workers, speech pathologists, veterinary practitioners/technicians, teachers (public schools, Title I schools, MSDE-identified improvement schools), mental health professionals in public schools, and public school nurses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of eligible student loans (excluding Parent PLUS loans and loans in default) for individuals employed in eligible public service fields providing services to low-income or underserved Maryland residents. Payment is issued as a lump sum to the recipient, who must remit to lender(s) within 120 days and provide proof of payment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed full time in the state of Maryland. Most applicants must have graduated from a Maryland institution (exception: lawyers; teachers without a Maryland degree must hold a Maryland Resident Teacher Certificate from MSDE).
requirements_list: Must work in a listed eligible public service employment field
Must have graduated from a Maryland institution (exception: lawyers; teachers without a Maryland degree must hold a Maryland Resident Teacher Certificate from MSDE)
Must be employed full time in Maryland
Loans cannot be Parent PLUS loans and cannot be in default

Income limits: single applicants (excluding Nurse Faculty) must earn $75,000 or less; married applicants (excluding Nurse Faculty) must earn $150,000 or less with individual income not exceeding $75,000; Nurse Faculty single income limit is $100,000; Nurse Faculty married income limit is $185,000 combined with individual income not exceeding $100,000
Must remain in an eligible employment field throughout the application cycle
Renewal recipients must submit annual employment, lender, and tax documentation by March 15 each year
Mid-Year Employment Verification must be submitted within 21 days of award notification, or award is cancelled
Urban Teacher Center (UTC) applicants must be in their 2nd year of the program and possess a Maryland Resident-Teaching Certificate; ineligible for lock-in award

Nancy Grasmick Professional track (teachers) must teach STEM subjects or in a school where at least 75% of students are enrolled in the free meal program for 2 years; must have the highest performance evaluation rating for the most recent year
Licensed Clinical Counselors must work in a high-need geographic area
Must not have active state service obligations from other Maryland scholarships (e.g., Hope, Nursing, Developmental Disabilities Scholarship)
Veterinary practitioners/technicians: 5 years state employment OR 100 hours/year volunteer work for 3 years at qualifying shelters
2026-2027 award year requires submission of signed 2025 Maryland state income tax return
Recipients may reapply as a new applicant for up to three additional award years if eligibility is maintained
Mental health professionals and school nurses must be employed by county school system or local health department for at least 2 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) via the MHEC One App at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. All required documents must be uploaded securely through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. Initial applicants must provide a prior-year federal or state income tax return, employment verification, lender verification, and institutional certification. Renewal applicants must provide a tax return, employment verification, and lender verification. For the 2026-2027 award year, applications opened January 15, 2026 with a deadline of October 15, 2026. Award payment is issued as a single lump sum to the recipient, who must remit to lender(s) within 120 days and provide proof of payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: MHEC One App for Undocumented Students
structured_extraction.program_description: The MHEC One App is Maryland's financial aid application for undocumented students and qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the in-state tuition exemption under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article (non-resident exemption). Eligible students apply through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS) and may be considered for multiple State of Maryland financial aid grants and scholarships, including the Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, Legislative Scholarship Program, and the Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship. Applicants do not need a Social Security Number to apply. Students are notified of Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant awards in late April; other grants and scholarships are awarded in summer. Awards must be accepted or declined within 2 weeks of notification through the MDCAPS portal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid grants and scholarships for eligible undocumented students attending Maryland public or private institutions. Specific programs include the Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, Legislative Scholarship Program, and the Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship. Award amounts and terms vary by individual program. Students are notified of Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant awards in late April; other grants and scholarships are awarded in summer. Awards must be accepted online within 2 weeks of notification through the MDCAPS portal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadlines vary by scholarship or grant program; application available each year when the FAFSA opens (October 1 for most programs, through June 30 of the award year). For the Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant, the deadline has historically been March 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undocumented students and qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident tuition exemption under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article and attend eligible Maryland public or private colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College financial aid — grants and scholarships to help cover higher education expenses at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution. Applicants must have filed a Maryland income tax return each year for 3 years while attending a public or nonpublic secondary school in Maryland, and for each year between graduation from secondary school and registration at a college in the State.
requirements_list: Must be undocumented or a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
Must meet the non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article (eligible for in-state tuition)
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
Must file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information
Must have filed a Maryland income tax return each year for 3 years while attending a public or nonpublic secondary school in Maryland
Males between ages 18 and 25 must register with the Selective Service System
Do not need a Social Security Number to apply
Must complete the MHEC One App through MDCAPS (not the FAFSA)
Dependent students under age 24 must provide parental information on the application
Must accept any awarded scholarship or grant within 2 weeks via the MDCAPS portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MHEC One App online through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS) at mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. The application opens each year at the same time as the FAFSA (October 1 for most programs). Submit by the applicable deadline for the specific grant or scholarship program you are applying for. Dependent students must provide parent information and a parent signature page. Up to 10 institutions can be added per application. After submission, monitor the 'Check Your Application Status' page in your MDCAPS account and submit any additional required documents by the deadline. MHEC reviews applications and notifies applicants by email of any awards. If awarded, accept or decline the award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: A last-dollar scholarship for eligible Maryland residents who enroll at a Maryland community college. After all federal and state financial aid (excluding loans) is applied, the scholarship covers any remaining tuition and mandatory fees, up to $5,000 per academic year, renewable for up to two years. It supports students in credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree programs; sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification; registered apprenticeship programs; and non-credit continuing education courses through the Promise Non-Credit Application. Applicants must generally attend the community college in their county or region of residence, with exceptions allowed if the program is not offered locally. For registered apprenticeship and non-credit participants, if recipients do not fulfill a post-graduation work requirement (working full-time in Maryland for at least one year per year the scholarship was awarded), the award converts to a repayable loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A last-dollar scholarship of up to $5,000 per academic year (minimum $100/year, or $50/semester) to cover remaining tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland community college after all other non-loan federal and state financial aid has been applied. The award equals the lesser of $5,000 or actual tuition and mandatory fees remaining after aid. Does not cover books, room, or board. Renewable for up to two years. For registered apprenticeship and non-credit program participants, the award converts to a loan repayable to the state if the recipient fails to fulfill the service obligation of working full-time in Maryland for at least one year per year the scholarship was received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 for Academic Year 2025-2026 (FAFSA/MHEC One App deadline for credit program applicants); March 1 (FAFSA/MSFAA deadline for registered apprenticeship and non-credit applicants); rolling deadline for Continuing Education (non-credit) applicants
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school graduates or GED recipients (including homeschooled applicants) who are eligible for in-state tuition and plan to enroll or are currently enrolled full or part time at a Maryland community college in a credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree program; a sequence of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification; or a registered apprenticeship program. Also includes Maryland residents who graduated from a Maryland high school or completed a GED in Maryland and enroll within two years at a Maryland community college in a registered apprenticeship or non-credit course sequence leading to licensure or certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers remaining tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland community college after all federal and state non-loan financial aid has been applied, for credit-bearing programs, registered apprenticeship programs, and non-credit course sequences leading to licensure or certification. Does not cover books, room, or board.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must attend the community college in their county of residence or the regional community college serving their region. Regional community colleges are Wor-Wic Community College, Chesapeake College, and College of Southern Maryland. If the local college does not offer the student's program, they may attend any Maryland community college that does. The scholarship can also be used at a community college with on-campus residential facilities.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland high school graduate or GED recipient eligible for in-state tuition

Must enroll full or part time at a Maryland community college in a credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree program; a sequence of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification; or a registered apprenticeship program

High school seniors must have an unweighted cumulative GPA of at least 2.3 at the end of the first semester of senior year or by end of senior year (exemption applies if graduated 5+ years before applying)
Students currently or previously enrolled at a community college must have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5
GED applicants must submit a copy of their examination
Adjusted gross income must not exceed $100,000 (single or single-parent household) or $150,000 (married or two-parent household); based on 2023 tax year for 2025-2026

Must submit FAFSA or MHEC One App (for those ineligible for FAFSA) by April 1 for credit programs; FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) by March 1 for registered apprenticeship and non-credit programs
Must submit required documentation directly to their institution
Credit program applicants must enroll in at least 6 credits per semester
Non-credit applicants must complete the Promise Non-Credit Application through MDCAPS
Registered apprenticeship and non-credit applicants must submit the Promise Apprenticeship/Non-Credit Inquiry Form to MHEC

Renewal recipients must maintain a 2.5 cumulative community college GPA, meet income requirements, file FAFSA or MHEC One App/MSFAA annually by the applicable deadline, and make satisfactory academic progress
Must attend the community college located in their county or region of residence (exceptions allowed if the program is not offered locally)
Has not earned a bachelor's or associate degree (for registered apprenticeship and non-credit applicants)
Has not been awarded another educational grant or scholarship covering full cost of attendance (for registered apprenticeship and non-credit applicants)
Enrolls at a Maryland community college within two years of high school graduation or GED completion in Maryland (for registered apprenticeship and non-credit applicants)

Service obligation: registered apprenticeship and non-credit recipients must work full-time in Maryland within one year of completing the program, for at least one year per year the scholarship was awarded, or the award converts to a repayable loan
Award is renewable for up to two years of undergraduate study
A drug-free pledge is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For credit programs: Submit the FAFSA or MHEC One App (for students ineligible for FAFSA) by April 1, then contact your local Maryland community college to apply and submit required documentation directly to your institution. Non-credit continuing education applicants must also complete the Promise Non-Credit Application online through MDCAPS. For registered apprenticeship and non-credit programs: 1. Complete the Apprenticeship/Non-Credit Inquiry Form and submit to MHEC (by email or mail, with Student Aid Report/SAR attached if FAFSA was used). 2. Submit the FAFSA at studentaid.ed.gov or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) through MDCAPS by March 1. 3. Submit any additional documentation required by MHEC. Applicants who listed a Maryland community college on their FAFSA or MSFAA will be notified by email of required documentation and can check their MDCAPS 'To Do List' for required documents. Note: Students in credited courses who completed the FAFSA or MSFAA by March 1 should NOT complete the Apprenticeship/Non-Credit Inquiry Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP) is part of Maryland GEAR UP and focuses on career exploration and educational planning for economically disadvantaged students. It promotes self-efficacy, leadership skills, and transferable employment skills. The program provides in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, and workplace readiness training and youth employment. It also educates students and their families about the benefits of postsecondary education and college financing options. Awards are made on a grant cycle basis (FY2020 and FY2021 cycles documented). FY2020 awards were up to $80,000 per institution; FY2021 awards were up to $90,000 per institution, with five or more awards anticipated. Grant funds are disbursed in two 50% payments. A 25% in-kind or cash match is required. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of direct costs. The Maryland GEAR UP grant was a six-year grant covering 2014 through 2020. Applicants must be accredited public or nonprofit two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with a Local Education Agency (LEA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funded grants support in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, and workplace readiness training and youth employment activities. Awards are made on a grant cycle basis (FY2020 and FY2021 cycles documented). FY2020 awards were up to $80,000 per institution; FY2021 awards were up to $90,000 per institution, with five or more awards anticipated. Grant funds are disbursed in two 50% payments. A 25% in-kind or cash match is required. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of direct costs. Applicants must be accredited public or nonprofit two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with a Local Education Agency (LEA).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Project Period: November 23, 2020 to September 15, 2021; Proposal deadline: November 13, 2020
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited public or nonprofit two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with a Local Education Agency (LEA) serving economically disadvantaged students in Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties. Ultimately serves low-income and first-generation high school students, GEAR UP cohort members at high-poverty middle and high schools, and their parents/guardians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment activities. Also used to educate students and families about the benefits of postsecondary education and college financing options. Allowable budget categories include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, and consultant/contractual services. Indirect costs capped at 8% of direct costs. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland GEAR UP school districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties. Partnership must include a Local Education Agency (LEA) from one of these three target counties. Service areas are proposed by applicants in partnership with participating LEAs and school districts; geographic scope is locally negotiated between the college/university applicant and participating school districts/LEAs.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited public or not-for-profit independent two- or four-year Institution of Higher Education (IHE)
Must apply in partnership with a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must serve economically disadvantaged students in the designated GEAR UP school districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico counties
25% in-kind or cash match required
Indirect costs capped at 8% of direct costs
Proposals must not exceed 15 pages (excluding cover, abstract, budget, and appendices)
Must possess legal authority to apply (governing body authorization required)
Must comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act 1964, ADA, FERPA, Pro-Children Act, and OMB SF 424B
Must execute formalized agreements with LEAs and collaborative partners
Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs
Must participate in MHEC statewide assessment/evaluation
Must grant MHEC and Legislative Auditor audit/access rights
Prior written approval required for scope changes or project director replacement
Quarterly time and effort reports required
Prior written approval required for budget variances exceeding $1,000 or 10% of budget
Required partners include: college/university project director, school district superintendent/CEO, LEA GEAR UP Coordinator, and high school principal
Records retention required for 3 years post-grant
No out-of-state conference travel (excluding Maryland and DC metro area)
Personnel must maintain normal pay rates; instructional compensation limited to one course load equivalent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an RFP response using the posted RFP documents and required forms including a Plan of Operation, Budget Summary, and Assurances and Cooperative Planning Agreement. The cooperative planning agreement requires signed commitments from the college/university project director, school district superintendent/CEO, LEA GEAR UP Coordinator, and high school principal. Additional partner organizations may also be included. Proposals are reviewed and scored by a panel; recommendations are forwarded to the Secretary of Higher Education for final approval. Contact Kendall Cook at kendall.cook@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Higher Education Outreach and College Access Program (MD-HEOCAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MD-HEOCAP is a state grant program that provides funds to eligible nonprofit organizations to increase college and career awareness and support college completion for low-income Maryland high school students. Grantees carry out statewide outreach efforts to encourage low-income students to attend and complete college. The program also creates a matching fund for nonprofits to increase outreach efforts. Priority is given to applicants targeting communities with the highest rates of concentrated child poverty in each county, specifically communities eligible under the Governor's Office for Children's ENOUGH Grant Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funds of up to $100,000 awarded to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to carry out statewide outreach efforts supporting low-income Maryland high school students in accessing and completing college. A 1:1 matching fund is required for nonprofits to increase outreach efforts. Grant period runs October 16, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of total direct costs. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and not supplant non-grant funds or be used for any purpose other than those specified in the grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Maryland that have been in existence for five or more consecutive years and provide college access activities, communication, and services to low-income high school students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Statewide outreach efforts to encourage low-income Maryland high school students to enroll in and complete college, including college access activities, communication, and services. Allowable budget categories include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant/contractual services, and other costs; indirect costs capped at 8% of total direct costs. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and may not supplant non-grant funds or be used for any purpose other than those specified in the grant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must be located in Maryland and serve low-income Maryland high school students. Priority is given to applicants targeting communities with the highest rates of concentrated child poverty in each county, specifically communities eligible under the Governor's Office for Children's ENOUGH Grant Program. In counties without ENOUGH-eligible communities, applicants should target the communities with the highest child poverty rate for that county.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must have been in existence for five or more consecutive years
Must be located in Maryland
Must have established partnership(s) with a local school system or higher education institution
Must provide college access activities, communication, and services with a proven track record of success
Must offer services to enhance and increase college access and completion for low-income Maryland high school students
Must comply with civil rights requirements including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and the ADA
Must not use grant funds to supplant non-grant funds
Must participate in statewide assessment
Must retain records for five years
Must allow MHEC audit access
Must provide 1:1 matching funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must respond to the FY 2026 Request for Proposals (RFP). Submit an electronic PDF proposal to Anthony Reiner (Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov) along with an abstract as a separate Word document. Required proposal components include: cover sheet (Appendix A), abstract, table of contents, proposal narrative (max 15 single-spaced pages), budget summary (Appendix B), budget narrative, and statement of assurances (Appendix C). Proposals are scored on a 100-point rubric across 7 criteria: Needs Assessment (10 pts), Organizational Capacity (10 pts), Goals/Objectives/Outcomes (15 pts), Operations Plan (15 pts), Management Plan (10 pts), Project Evaluation (20 pts), and Budget/Narrative (20 pts). Proposals go through a five-phase review: (1) Initial Review for formatting and completeness, (2) Review Panel Evaluation, (3) Request for Additional Information/Project Changes if needed, (4) Funding Recommendation Approval by the Secretary of Higher Education, and (5) Grant Award with award letters issued. For questions, contact Anthony Reiner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Foster Care Recipients (MLARP Foster Care)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state assistance to help repay educational loans owed by foster care recipients who are employed by the state or a county or municipality of Maryland and who earned a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award equals the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000 per year. Awards are automatically renewed annually for up to three years if required documentation is submitted by the deadline each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15th each year (applications available starting January 15th); current cycle deadline: October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster care recipients who are Maryland residents, were placed in out-of-home foster care for 3 or more years, earned a degree from a Maryland college, and are currently employed at least part-time (20 hours per week) in state, county, or local government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans from a university, government, or commercial source used to pay college expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a Maryland resident employed in state, county, or local government in Maryland, and must have earned a degree from a Maryland institution of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have been placed in out-of-home placement by a state or state government department of social services for 3 or more years (documented via court order)
Must have earned an undergraduate or graduate degree from a Maryland college
Must be employed at least part-time (20 hours per week) in state, county, or local government
Must have educational loans from a university, government, or commercial source used to pay college expenses
Must not be in default on any loan (deferment/grace status acceptable; consolidated loans acceptable; Parent PLUS loans excluded)
Must sign an employment obligation agreement to remain employed by the state or a county or municipality for at least one year after the award expires
Prior service obligations from other state scholarships must be completed before applying
Must make a drug-free pledge for the award term
Must submit a signed Maryland state income tax return from the previous year (or equivalent IRS non-filing statement/IRS Letter 1077)
Must work and live in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available each year starting January 15th. Submit the application (paper application from MHEC website) and all required supplemental documentation via Google form upload or email to careerbased.mhec@maryland.gov by October 15th each year. Required documents include: Employment Verification Form (applicant completes Section A; employer completes Section B — nonprofit employers must include 501(c)(3) or (4) verification), Institutional Certification Form (applicant completes Section A; institution completes Section B — transcript or National Student Clearinghouse documentation accepted as alternative), Lender Verification Form (submitted via secure upload through MDCAPS account; one form per loan), proof of foster care reflecting at least 3 years, and a signed Maryland state income tax return or IRS non-filing statement letter. All materials must be submitted to the Office of Student Financial Assistance by the closing date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MLARP) for Police Officers and Probation Agents provides state assistance to help repay educational loans for individuals working in eligible law enforcement or parole and probation roles in Maryland. Awards are calculated as a percentage of the applicant's annual salary applied against their total outstanding loan debt, with the percentage varying based on debt amount. Recipients may renew awards for up to three years. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with the 2026-2027 cycle deadline of October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award amounts are calculated by multiplying the applicant's annual salary by a percentage determined by total loan debt: 10% for debt below $15,000; 20% for debt $15,000–$39,999; 30% for debt $40,000–$74,999; 40% for debt $75,000 or more. Payment cannot exceed total debt. Awards may be renewed for up to three years (3-year lock-in with option to renew for 2 more years).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who received a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a public college or university in Maryland and have been employed as a police officer or probation/parole agent for at least 2 years at an eligible Maryland law enforcement or Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services agency. Eligible positions include state, county, and municipal police officers, sheriff offices, university police, community college police, fire and explosive investigators, specialized state enforcement bureaus (Comptroller Field Enforcement, Alcohol and Tobacco Commission), transit police, natural resources police, and capitol police.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of graduate, professional, or undergraduate educational loans taken to attend a public college or university in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed as a police officer or probation agent at an eligible law enforcement agency or the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services serving the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a public college or university in Maryland
Must have been employed as a police officer or probation agent for at least 2 years
Must be currently employed at an eligible law enforcement agency or the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services throughout the application cycle
Annual gross salary cannot exceed $85,000; if married, combined household salaries cannot exceed $170,000

Must submit a Maryland signed income tax return (2024 returns for 2025-2026 cycle; 2025 returns for 2026-2027 cycle), employment verification form, lender verification form, and documentation of degree completion by the deadline
Renewal recipients must submit annual employment, lender, and tax documentation by the established deadline each year

Eligible employers include 32 categories: state police, municipal/county police, university/community college police, specialized law enforcement (transit, natural resources, capitol police), field enforcement (Comptroller, Alcohol & Tobacco Commission), and fire and explosive investigators (State Fire Marshal, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Prince George's, Worcester, Hagerstown, Howard County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the MHEC One App in MDCAPS at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. All required documents must be uploaded through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. The 2025-2026 cycle deadline was March 15, 2026; the 2026-2027 cycle deadline is October 15, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Police Officer and Probation Agent Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides scholarship funding to current police officers, probation agents, or individuals planning to enter law enforcement who are enrolled in an academic program that furthers their career in law enforcement at a Maryland public senior institution. Recipients must commit to working as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years within eight years after graduation, signing a promissory note and service obligation agreement. The scholarship converts to a loan if the service obligation is not met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees charged to a resident undergraduate student at the eligible institution. The scholarship converts to a loan if the service obligation is not met. Recipients must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreement to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation. Payment is made approximately four weeks after the institution completes certification. Renewal requires a minimum 3.0 GPA, satisfactory academic progress, maintained Maryland residency, and continued full- or part-time enrollment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2025-2026 academic year closes April 1, 2026; 2026-2027 academic year opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Maryland police officers or probation agents, and individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents, who are enrolled full- or part-time in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution that furthers their career in law enforcement. Applicants must be Maryland residents or have graduated from a Maryland high school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible Maryland public senior institution for undergraduate or graduate programs that further the recipient's career in law enforcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or have graduated from a Maryland high school. Study must be at a Maryland public senior institution.
requirements_list: Must be a current police officer or probation agent, or planning to become one after graduation
Must be accepted for admission or currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution
Must be a Maryland resident or have graduated from a Maryland high school
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time in a program that furthers a career in law enforcement
Current police officers must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws of the state and be a member of one of the qualifying law enforcement agencies listed in the program
Probation agents must be serving as a parole and probation agent, supervisor, or regional administrator for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services in Maryland
Must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreement to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years within eight years after graduation
Renewal requires a minimum 3.0 GPA, satisfactory academic progress, maintained Maryland residency, and continued full- or part-time enrollment
Must maintain a drug-free status for the full award term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App by the established deadline. Upload required documentation including employment confirmation (if applicable), a copy of your final high school transcript (if not a Maryland resident but a Maryland high school graduate), and institutional confirmation of enrollment in a law enforcement-related program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Senatorial Scholarship provides financial aid to Maryland residents pursuing postsecondary credentials at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. Scholarships are awarded through a student's local state Senate delegation and are available to full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate students, as well as private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, and community college certificate/licensure program students. Awards may also be used at out-of-state institutions in limited circumstances such as unique majors not available in Maryland, active military duty, or disability accommodations. Awards are based on financial need as demonstrated on the FAFSA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are distributed through the student's local state Senator. The 2026-2027 minimum award is $400; the maximum amount has not yet been determined. Students may hold this scholarship alongside other state awards, but the total of all state scholarship awards may not exceed the student's cost of attendance as determined by their Financial Aid Office. The award is automatically renewed for up to three years or until degree completion, whichever occurs first, subject to continued enrollment and satisfactory academic progress. Awards are subject to the availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadline set by individual state Senator; FAFSA must be filed by March 1 if OSFA administers the award. Unique Major Application for out-of-state programs opens March 15 and closes July 1. Disability appeal (less than 6 credits): Fall 2026 opens July 1, 2026 and closes December 15, 2026; Spring 2027 opens October 1, 2026 and closes April 15, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are current high school seniors, current or prospective undergraduate or graduate students (full-time or part-time), private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, and community college certificate/licensure program students. Undergraduate full-time enrollment is 12+ credits/semester; part-time is 6–11 credits/semester. Graduate full-time enrollment is 9+ credits/semester; part-time is 6–8 credits/semester.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Postsecondary educational expenses (tuition, fees, cost of attendance) at a two-year or four-year Maryland college, university, or private career school. May also be used at out-of-state institutions in limited circumstances (e.g., unique major not available in Maryland, active military duty, or disability accommodation not available in Maryland). Total state scholarship awards may not exceed the student's financial need or cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition. Awards are distributed through the applicant's state senate district delegation and are generally limited to Maryland institutions, with out-of-state exceptions for unique majors (MHEC-approved), active military, or disability accommodations.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition

Must plan to attend a Maryland two-year or four-year college, university, or private career school (with limited out-of-state exceptions for unique/unavailable majors, active military duty, or disability accommodations)
Must be enrolled full-time (12+ undergraduate or 9+ graduate credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 undergraduate or 6-8 graduate credits per semester)

Must meet at least one eligibility category: current high school senior, degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student (full- or part-time), private career school enrollee, undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition, or community college certificate/licensure student
Must complete the FAFSA by the deadline set by the state Senator (or by March 1 if OSFA administers the award); students ineligible for federal aid must file the MHEC One-App instead
Must sign a drug-free pledge
Audited courses are not eligible
Prior OSFA/Senator approval required for changes from full-time to part-time enrollment
Any required documentation must be submitted directly to the Senator's office
Renewal requires continued full-time or part-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress; award automatically renewed for up to three years or until degree completion, whichever occurs first
Total state scholarship awards may not exceed the student's cost of attendance; automatic overaward reduction or cancellation if combined aid exceeds financial need or cost of attendance
Awards are subject to the availability of funds

Disability appeal (enrolled in less than 6 credits): disability status must be verified by a licensed medical/clinical practitioner; medical documentation must explain impact on half-time course load capacity; current class schedule/course enrollment documentation required; non-permanent disabilities require updated documentation each term of appeal filing; appeals must be filed per term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland state Senator's office for instructions on how to apply. A list of state senators and their contact information is available at the Maryland General Assembly website or the Maryland State Board of Elections website. Complete the FAFSA (or MHEC One-App if ineligible for federal aid) by the deadline set by your Senator. Submit any required documentation directly to the Senator's office. For out-of-state unique major requests, complete the online Unique Major Application between March 15 and July 1. For disability appeals (enrollment below 6 credits), submit the 2026-27 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form with medical documentation and course schedule; Fall 2026 appeals open July 1, 2026 and close December 15, 2026; Spring 2027 appeals open October 1, 2026 and close April 15, 2027. Institution certifies eligibility each semester; payment is processed approximately 4 weeks after institutional certification. Processing takes approximately 45 business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Teacher Quality and Diversity Competitive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants to teacher preparation programs at Maryland institutions of higher education. The goal is to help students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession — including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, people from low-income backgrounds, first-generation college students, and individuals with disabilities — achieve teacher preparation and certification requirements. Priority is given to proposals that create alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, consortium-based approaches, standards-aligned programming with mentoring, transcript analysis and licensure pathways, transfer pathways from community colleges, and targeted interventions and support for male-identifying students. Priority is also given to historically black colleges and universities and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers. Grantees must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period, and the program is not intended to supplant institutional investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual funding of $1,000,000 is available. Individual track awards range from $50,000 to $150,000. Consortium track awards range from $250,000 to $500,000. The FY 2026 grant period runs from December 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of direct costs. Grantees must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland, with priority given to historically black colleges and universities and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting students from historically underrepresented groups in achieving teacher preparation and certification requirements, including developing alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, consortium-based programs, transfer pathways from community colleges, mentoring and academic support, licensure coursework sequences, and targeted recruitment and support initiatives for underrepresented populations including male-identifying students. Allowable costs include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, curriculum development, competency-based assessments, student success services, and indirect costs up to 8% of direct costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to accredited institutions of higher education located in Maryland. Consortium applications must include at least one local education agency partner.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited institution of higher education in Maryland
Priority given to HBCUs and Hispanic-serving institutions
Proposals must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period
Program is not intended to supplant institutional investment
Proposals may be individual (single institution) or consortium-based (multiple institutions and school systems); consortium applications must include at least one local education agency partner
Applications must be submitted by email to MHEC by 4:00 p.m. on October 30, 2025
Budget narrative required with detailed line-item justification for all costs
Itemized listing of all key personnel with salary percentage of effort required
Travel must be designated by place, person, date, distance, and method
Equipment must include life-expectancy, maintenance plans, and post-grant use discussion
Consultant agreements and fees must be documented
Abstract required (maximum 300 words)
Proposals evaluated on a 105-point rubric covering Needs Statement, Goals/Objectives/Outcomes, Operation Plan, Program Management, Project Evaluation, Partnerships, and Budget and Cost Effectiveness
Statement of Assurances required (compliance with Title VI Civil Rights Act, ADA, Title IX if applicable, non-supplantation clause, participation in statewide assessment)
Five-year record retention required
Acknowledgment of MHEC support and required disclaimer must appear in all publications
Interim and final reports required; financial and narrative reports due at grant end (final report due August 31, 2026)
Prior written approval required for scope changes, project director replacement, staff/consultant changes, and budget changes above $1,000 or 10% in any category
Indirect costs may not exceed 8% of direct costs
Proposal must include all requisite forms
Compliance with Maryland procurement procedures required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit proposals in response to the Request for Proposals (RFP). Applications must be emailed to MHEC by 4:00 p.m. on October 30, 2025. Proposals are reviewed by a panel of qualified reviewers who score applications individually across evaluation criteria and then convene as a full panel for discussion and funding recommendations. Recommendations are submitted to the Secretary of Higher Education for final decisions. Award notifications are made by November 28, 2025. See the FY 2026 RFP documents for full application requirements. For technical assistance, contact Elena Quiroz-Livanis at elena.quiroz@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth exempts eligible homeless youth from paying tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public colleges and universities. Students can receive the waiver while pursuing an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate (including noncredit courses required for a vocational certificate). Eligible students are those verified as homeless under the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act within the 24 months before enrollment or while currently enrolled. The waiver lasts up to ten years after first enrolling, or until a bachelor's degree is awarded, whichever comes first, with potential renewal for up to an additional four years upon annual filing of FAFSA or MHEC One-App. Scholarships or grants awarded to a recipient may not be applied to tuition since it is already waived. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible students are fully exempt from paying tuition, registration fees, and all mandatory enrollment fees (including all fees required as a condition of enrollment and noncredit course fees for vocational certificates) at a Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a recipient may not be applied to tuition since it is already waived. The waiver lasts up to ten years after first enrolling, or until a bachelor's degree is awarded, whichever comes first. Students may renew for up to an additional four years upon filing FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless youth (as defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act) enrolled or planning to enroll in a Maryland public college or university seeking an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate, who must enroll on or before reaching age 25.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers tuition, registration fees, and all mandatory enrollment fees (including all fees required as a condition of enrollment and noncredit course fees for vocational certificates) at Maryland public institutions of higher education. Does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must attend a Maryland public institution of higher education and have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records.
requirements_list: Must be verified as a homeless child or youth as defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act
Homelessness must have occurred at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment in a public institution of higher education, or while currently enrolled
Must be enrolled as a candidate for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education
Must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records
Must complete and file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year to maintain eligibility
Must be enrolled on or before reaching age 25
Must be enrolled full time or part time in an associate, bachelor's, or vocational certificate program
Eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the FAFSA or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App
Undocumented applicants who do not qualify for the MHEC One-App should consult with the financial aid office at their institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution you plan to attend to apply for the waiver. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. File the FAFSA at studentaid.gov or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App each year to establish and maintain eligibility. Undocumented applicants who do not qualify for the MHEC One-App should consult with the financial aid office at their institution.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Near Completer Grant provides financial assistance to Maryland residents who previously enrolled in a degree program at a community college or senior higher education institution, did not complete it, and now plan to re-enroll to earn their associate or bachelor's degree. The award is applied toward tuition only, after all non-loan aid has been applied, on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge for re-enrollment at a Maryland community college, or up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge for re-enrollment at a public four-year institution. Award is applied to tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied. Awards are granted on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2023-2024 application is now closed; 2023-2024 is the last year of awarding for this scholarship
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who previously attended a community college or senior higher education institution, earned significant credit hours toward a degree but did not complete it, and are not currently enrolled at a post-secondary institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition only, applied after all non-loan aid has been used. Cannot be used for books or course fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition. Program is open to Maryland community colleges and public 4-year institutions of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition
Must not currently be enrolled at a post-secondary institution
For community college completers: earned at least 45 credit hours and have a minimum GPA of 2.0
For senior institution completers: earned at least 90 credits toward a bachelor's degree and have a minimum GPA of 2.0
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log into the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) to complete the online application. After completing the application, use the Electronic File Upload Tool to submit required transcripts from your previous institution showing the required credit hours.

structured_extraction.program_description: NSP II is a statewide program funded by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). It aims to expand Maryland's capacity to educate nurses by supporting nursing education programs at Maryland institutions. Specifically, it funds faculty development, doctoral education, and institutional interventions to address nursing workforce shortages. Sub-programs include Nurse Faculty Programs for New Nurse Faculty, Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research, Cohen Scholars, and Academic Nurse Educator Grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are funded by up to 0.1 percent of regulated gross hospital revenue collected by the HSCRC. Funds support nursing education programs at Maryland institutions through faculty development, doctoral education support, and institutional capacity-building. Specific sub-programs include nurse faculty grants, doctoral dissertation grants, Cohen Scholars, and academic nurse educator grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nursing education programs, nurse faculty, and nurses seeking advanced degrees at Maryland higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding nursing education program capacity, faculty development, doctoral education support, and nurse educator training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nursing education programs at Maryland higher education institutions statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland institution with a nursing education program
Sub-programs target nurse faculty, doctoral students, and academic nurse educators
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Nurse Support Program website at www.nursesupport.org for information on specific sub-program applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two- and four-year colleges and universities to identify, re-engage, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students — those who have earned 75% or more credits toward an associate or bachelor's degree but stopped out or dropped out for 12 or more consecutive months without earning a degree.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $60,000 per institution per grant period. Institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. The grant period for FY2025 runs from August 5, 2025 through August 31, 2026. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of total project costs.
