structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year associate and bachelor's degree-granting colleges and universities seeking to re-enroll near-completer students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to identify, contact, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students who have earned 75% or more credits toward an associate or bachelor's degree but have stopped out for 12 or more consecutive months. Allowable activities include outreach strategies, student support systems (academic, financial, and social advising), prior learning assessments, competency-based credit awards, accelerated completion tracks, general studies degree pathways, and financial aid (tuition discounts and textbook waivers). Allowable budget categories include salaries/wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials/supplies, consultant/contractual services, and indirect costs (capped at 8%).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to accredited colleges and universities located in Maryland. Geographic distribution of grant awards is considered in the final awarding process to ensure statewide equity, but there are no county, municipal, or regional restrictions on eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited Maryland public or nonprofit independent two-year or four-year college or university that grants associate or bachelor's degrees.
Must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost.
Must target near-completer students — those who have earned 75% or more credits toward a degree but stopped out or dropped out for 12 or more consecutive months without obtaining a degree.
Grant funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs.
Must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (1964), ADA, and applicable federal and state laws.
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation activities.
Must retain records for 5 years.
Prior written approval required for scope changes, staff replacements, or budget amendments exceeding $1,000 or 10% of a budget category.
A single 6-month extension is possible with 30-day notice.
Final report due within 90 days of grant expiration.
MHEC acknowledgment and disclaimer required in any publications produced with grant funds.
Projects must address at least 2 of 6 program objectives (outreach, student supports, re-enrollment, prior learning assessment, general studies degree pathways, sustainable financial aid).
Must track demographic data (gender, race, age, degree program) and credit hours for participants.
Applications must be signed by the institution's President or Provost.
Budget summary must be submitted in Excel format with a detailed budget narrative.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application in response to the Request for Proposals (RFP) by 4:00 p.m. on the deadline date to Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov. Application materials include the RFP, budget summary (Excel format), budget narrative, and signed assurances form. Award notifications are issued by MHEC following a review process that considers reviewer recommendations and geographic distribution of awards. Contact Anthony Reiner for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Part-Time Grant Program provides funds to Maryland public and independent colleges and universities based on the number of undergraduate part-time students with demonstrated financial need who are enrolled in degree-granting programs. Institutions receive allocated funds and then select and award individual recipients. Awards range from $200 to $2,000 per year and can be renewed annually for up to eight years, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress, continues to demonstrate financial need, and files the FAFSA or MHEC One App each year. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $200 to a maximum of $2,000 per year, awarded by the student's institution from funds allocated by the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Awards are renewable annually for up to eight years, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress, continues to demonstrate financial need, and refiles the FAFSA or MHEC One App each year. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 (FAFSA/MHEC One App filing deadline for renewal); contact your institution for additional application deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Part-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students and students dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and a Maryland institution of higher education who are Maryland residents and demonstrate financial need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for part-time undergraduate students enrolled in degree-granting programs at Maryland colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and their parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Students must be enrolled at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Must be a part-time (3–11 credits per semester), degree-seeking undergraduate student or dually enrolled high school/college student
Must be a Maryland resident (and parents must be Maryland residents if the student is a dependent)
Must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university
Must demonstrate financial need as determined by the FAFSA or MHEC One App (MSFAA)
Must file the FAFSA or MHEC One App by March 1
For renewal: must maintain satisfactory academic progress and refile FAFSA/MHEC One App each year
Maximum of eight years of eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the FAFSA or submit the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) through MDCAPS by the applicable deadline. Then contact the financial aid office at your institution to apply, as the institution selects and awards recipients and may have additional application deadlines. To renew, file the FAFSA/MHEC One App by March 1 each year (or earlier if required by your school).

structured_extraction.program_name: Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship promotes diversity in undergraduate and graduate student bodies and in Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) programs at designated Maryland Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). It provides annual scholarships to minority students and others historically underrepresented in ROTC who are enrolled at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Recipients with demonstrated financial need are prioritized, and awards are renewable for up to three additional years if eligibility and academic progress requirements continue to be met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award set by MHEC, with a minimum of $500 per semester ($1,000 per academic year), not to exceed the recipient's total education expenses (tuition, fees, and related costs of attending college). Recipients with demonstrated financial need are prioritized. The award is renewable for up to three additional years if the recipient continues to meet eligibility and academic progress requirements. Awards are subject to reduction if total aid exceeds the institutional cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate students (including undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition) who are minority students or members of groups historically underrepresented in ROTC, enrolled at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore, and participating in a ROTC program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education expenses (tuition, fees, and other related costs of attending college) at an eligible Maryland HBCU institution. Awards are subject to reduction if total aid exceeds the institutional cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must be enrolled at one of four designated Maryland HBCUs: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Must be eligible for in-state tuition and determined eligible by the institution.
requirements_list: Must be a current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student, or an undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition
Must be identified by the institution as a minority student or a member of a group historically underrepresented in ROTC programs
Must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6–11 credits) at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
Must be a member of a ROTC program
Must be determined eligible for in-state tuition by the institution
Must submit a FAFSA or MHEC One App (for students ineligible for federal aid but eligible for in-state tuition) by July 15
Must submit the online application through MDCAPS One-App by the closing date (October 15, 2026 for 2026-2027 cycle)
Must submit an Institutional Certification Form completed by the institution
Must submit documentation confirming ROTC membership to MDCAPS account
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress
Must remain drug-free (drug-free pledge required)
Annual reapplication required; awards may be renewed for up to three years total
Undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition may apply using the MHEC One App
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a FAFSA at studentaid.gov or the MHEC One App through MDCAPS (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us) by July 15. Complete and submit the online scholarship application through the MDCAPS One-App portal. Upload all required documents — including the Institutional Certification Form (completed by the institution) and documentation confirming ROTC membership — to your MDCAPS account by the closing date of October 15, 2026. Award status is tracked in the MDCAPS system; applicants are notified by email upon award and must accept the award within the established timeframe. The 2026-2027 application window is January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: SARA allows participating Maryland colleges and universities to offer distance-learning programs and courses to residents of other member states without seeking state-by-state approval. Maryland institutions apply to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) for authorization to participate. The agreement also provides quality assurance and consumer protection for Maryland residents taking distance-learning programs from institutions in other member states, including a complaint investigation and resolution process for students enrolled in distance education programs offered by SARA institutions in other SARA member states.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Institutional authorization to participate in SARA, allowing the institution to offer distance-learning programs across member states without individual state approvals. Annual fees range from $2,000 (fewer than 2,500 FTE students) to $4,000 (2,500–9,999 FTE) to $6,000 (10,000 or more FTE), paid to MHEC. A separate fee is also paid to NC-SARA. Processing takes two to three weeks after MHEC receives the application and fee. Additionally, MHEC provides a complaint investigation and resolution service for students enrolled in distance education programs from Maryland-based SARA institutions studying in other SARA states; MHEC investigates allegations of dishonest/fraudulent activity, false/misleading information, and course/program operation contrary to C-RAC Guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland accredited degree-granting institutions of higher education seeking to offer distance-learning programs to students in other SARA member states, and students enrolled in online degree programs from Maryland-based SARA institutions studying in other SARA states.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to deliver distance-learning programs and courses to residents of other SARA member states without seeking individual state approvals. Also covers complaint investigation and resolution for students in interstate distance education programs offered by participating SARA institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland institutions authorized to operate in Maryland as in-state institutions offering distance-learning programs to students in other SARA member states. The complaint process covers only interstate distance education (not in-state operations); complaints about a SARA institution's in-state operations are resolved under Maryland's standard complaint provisions.
requirements_list: Must be accredited as a degree-granting institution by a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accrediting body
Must be authorized to operate in Maryland as an in-state institution
If not a public institution, must document a composite score of at least 1.5 out of 3.0 on the USDOE financial stability scale
For student complaints: student must exhaust the institutional complaint process first
For student complaints: student must submit a written complaint form, additional information, and release to MHEC
For student complaints: complaint must concern interstate distance education only (not in-state operations)
For student complaints: allegations must involve dishonest/fraudulent activity, false/misleading information, or harm from non-compliance with C-RAC Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the NC-SARA Application and Approval Form for Institution Participation in SARA (with original signatures from the CEO or CAO) along with the applicable annual fee made payable to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Submit electronically to sara.mhec@maryland.gov or mail to MHEC-SARA, 217 East Redwood St., Suite 2100, Baltimore, MD 21202. After MHEC approval, complete NC-SARA's separate payment and approval process. For student complaints: exhaust the institutional complaint process first, then submit a written complaint form with additional information and a release to MHEC; the institution responds with additional information and a proposed resolution; MHEC negotiates in good faith if unresolved and issues an outcome letter to the student.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Delegate Scholarship provides financial assistance to Maryland residents pursuing postsecondary credentials at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. Students may attend full-time or part-time at the undergraduate or graduate level. The scholarship is awarded through individual State Delegates, who may set their own application instructions, or through the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) if the Delegate delegates that responsibility. Awards may be combined with other state scholarships as long as the total does not exceed the student's cost of attendance. The scholarship is not automatically renewable — students must reapply each year through their local Delegate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award ranging from a minimum of $200 for the 2026-2027 academic year; the maximum has not yet been determined. The scholarship may be combined with other state awards as long as the total does not exceed the student's cost of attendance. The scholarship is not renewable — students must re-apply each year through their local Delegate. Awards may also be used at out-of-state institutions under specific conditions (unique major not offered in Maryland, active military duty, or disability accommodations not available in Maryland).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 (if applying through OSFA via FAFSA); Unique Major out-of-state application opens March 15 and closes July 1; Disability Appeal FALL cycle: July 1 – December 15, 2026; SPRING cycle: October 1, 2026 – April 15, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are current high school seniors, current or prospective undergraduate or graduate students (full-time or part-time), private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, or community college certificate/license program enrollees. Also includes students enrolled in less than 6 credits due to a documented disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Postsecondary tuition and educational expenses at eligible Maryland institutions (two-year or four-year colleges, universities, or private career schools). May also be used at out-of-state institutions under qualifying conditions: the student's major is not available at any Maryland institution (with legislator approval), the student is on active U.S. military duty domiciled in Maryland, or the student has a disability requiring accommodations not available at Maryland institutions. Can reimburse educational expenses for community college certificate or license program enrollees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents attending eligible Maryland institutions. Out-of-state use permitted if the student's major is not available at any Maryland institution (with legislator approval), if the student is on active U.S. military duty domiciled in Maryland, or if the student has a disability requiring accommodations not available at Maryland institutions.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be enrolled or planning to enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college, university, or private career school (or qualify for out-of-state exception)
Must be pursuing a postsecondary credential full-time (12+ undergraduate or 9+ graduate credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 undergraduate or 6-8 graduate credits per semester)

Must meet at least one eligibility condition: current high school senior; current or prospective full- or part-time undergraduate or graduate degree-seeking student; private career school enrollee; undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition; or enrolled (or enrolled within last two years) in a community college certificate/license program
All in-state majors are eligible
If applying through OSFA, must complete FAFSA by March 1 (or MHEC One-App if ineligible for federal aid)
Must contact local State Delegate for instructions on how to apply
Students enrolled in fewer than 6 credits due to disability may submit a waiver for reconsideration
Scholarship is not renewable — students must reapply each year through their local Delegate

For disability appeal: medical documentation from a licensed practitioner (physician, specialist, psychologist, psychiatrist, or licensed clinical practitioner) confirming disability, its impact on ability to carry half-time course load, and permanence status is required
Updated medical documentation required each term if disability is non-permanent
Drug-free pledge required
In-state tuition eligibility required
Prior OSFA/Delegate approval required for full-time to part-time enrollment transition
No audited courses count toward credit totals
Awards are subject to the availability of funds and may not exceed cost of attendance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local State Delegate's office for specific application instructions. Find your delegate at mgaleg.maryland.gov or the Maryland State Board of Elections website. Delegates may handle applications directly or request that OSFA identify and award students. If the Delegate assigns OSFA to administer awards, complete the FAFSA by March 1 (or the MHEC One-App if ineligible for federal aid). Submit any required documentation directly to the Delegate's office. For out-of-state unique major exception, complete the online Unique Major Application (open March 15 – July 1, 2026). For disability appeals (students enrolled in fewer than 6 credits), complete the 2026-27 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form with all required documentation and upload all required documentation: FALL appeal cycle opens July 1, 2026 and closes December 15, 2026; SPRING appeal cycle opens October 1, 2026 and closes April 15, 2027. OSFA reviews appeals and responds within 45 business days. Incomplete or late appeals will be denied.

structured_extraction.program_name: Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state tax credit administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) for Maryland residents who have incurred significant student loan debt. Eligible residents can apply for a credit to reduce their Maryland state income tax liability. The credit is refundable if the credit amount exceeds the applicant's Maryland tax liability. A total of $18 million in tax credits has been available in recent cycles. Recipients must use the full credit award amount toward repayment of eligible college loan balances (principal and/or interest) within three years of the close of the taxable year for which the credit applies. Proof of payment must be submitted to MHEC through the OneStop portal; failure to provide proof results in recapture of the credit by the State Comptroller. Maryland State employees with student loan debt are given awarding priority.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit against Maryland state income taxes for eligible residents who have student loan debt. The total credit pool has been $18 million in recent cycles. The credit is refundable if the credit amount exceeds the applicant's Maryland tax liability. Recipients must pay the full credit award amount toward their college loan balances (principal and/or interest) within three years of the close of the taxable year for which the credit applies. Proof of payment must be submitted to MHEC through the OneStop portal. Failure to provide proof of payment results in recapture of the credit by the State Comptroller. Maryland State employees with student loan debt are given awarding priority.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tax Year 2025 Application is Closed; annual deadline is typically September 15th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt (debt must be incurred by the applicant; Parent PLUS Loans are excluded), have at least $5,000 in outstanding student loan debt at the time of applying, and file Maryland state income taxes. Maryland State employees with student loan debt are given priority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recipients must apply the tax credit award toward their college loan debt (principal and/or interest) within three years of the close of the taxable year for which the credit applies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must maintain Maryland residency for the tax year in which they apply.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland taxpayer who maintains Maryland residency for the applicable tax year
Must file Maryland state income taxes for the applicable tax year
Must have initially incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt
Debt must be incurred by the applicant (Parent PLUS Loans are not eligible)
Must have at least $5,000 in outstanding student loan debt at the time of applying
Maryland AGI is taken from Form 502, line 16 (full amount; no proration for joint filers)
Must pay the full tax credit award toward college loan balances (principal and/or interest) within three years of the close of the taxable year
Must submit proof of payment to MHEC via the OneStop portal
Correct lender documentation must be submitted with the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit Application available through the OneStop portal at onestop.md.gov before the annual September 15th deadline. Submit acceptable lender documents with the application. The credit is claimed on the Maryland income tax return and is refundable if it exceeds the applicant's tax liability. After receiving the credit, log into your OneStop account to submit proof of payment to lenders within the required three-year timeframe.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship provides financial awards to students who commit to working as a public school or public prekindergarten teacher in Maryland after completing their studies. Recipients must teach in a high-needs school (as identified by the Maryland State Department of Education, MSDE) or in a grade level or content area with a shortage of qualified educators. The scholarship is available to undergraduate and graduate students enrolled or planning to enroll at an eligible Maryland institution in a program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate, including career changers and teaching assistants with at least 2 years of experience at a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten program. Maryland residency is not required, and GPA, GRE, or SAT scores are not required for eligibility. Awards are contingent on availability of funds and may be renewed for up to three additional years (or four renewals for five-year programs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: At a Maryland public senior higher education institution, the award covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for a resident undergraduate or graduate student. At a Maryland private nonprofit institution, the award equals the lesser of: (1) 100% of UMCP resident tuition and mandatory fees plus 100% of the institution's room and board, or (2) 50% of the institution's resident tuition and mandatory fees plus 100% of the institution's room and board. Private nonprofit institutions must provide a matching scholarship equal to the State award for tuition and fees (room and board match not required). Students living off-campus or with parents receive a housing allowance based on room and board costs reported to MHEC. Recipients may renew the award for up to three additional years (four renewals if enrolled in a five-year program).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2025-2026 academic year deadline is April 1, 2026. The 2026-2027 application will become available on January 15, 2026, and will close on October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students enrolled or planning to enroll at an eligible Maryland institution in a program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate, including career changers and teaching assistants who have been employed at a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten for at least 2 years. Applicants must not already hold a Maryland professional teacher's certificate. Maryland residency, GPA, GRE, or SAT scores are not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at an eligible Maryland higher education institution for a program of study leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must attend an eligible Maryland institution and agree to fulfill a service obligation by teaching in a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten program in a high-needs school (as identified by MSDE) or in a grade level or content area with a shortage of qualified educators. Maryland residency is not required.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled or plan to enroll at an eligible Maryland institution in an undergraduate or graduate program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate
Must not currently hold a Maryland professional teacher's certificate

Must agree to a service obligation: teach for 2 years in a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten program in a high-needs school (as identified by MSDE) or in a grade level or content area with a shortage of qualified educators
Must begin teaching employment within 1 year of degree completion
Must achieve state certification within 2 years of degree completion
Full-time or part-time enrollment is acceptable
Maryland residency is not required; GPA, GRE, or SAT scores are not required
Teaching assistants must have been employed as a teaching assistant at a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten program for at least 2 years
Must submit required transcripts, Institutional Certification Form, and a typed essay of at least 600 words describing dedication to or aptitude for teaching
Teaching assistants must also submit an Employer Verification Form
Must sign and return a promissory note agreeing to fulfill the service obligation
Must remain drug-free for the full term of the award
Must not materially falsify any information on the application
Annual employment verification via Service Questionnaire required during service obligation period
For renewal: must continue as a full-time or part-time undergraduate or graduate student and maintain satisfactory academic progress
Awards are contingent on availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us using the MHEC One App. Required documentation includes an unofficial transcript, a typed essay of at least 600 words describing dedication to or aptitude for teaching, and an Institutional Certification Form completed by the applicant's institution via MDCAPS. Teaching assistants must also submit an Employer Verification Form. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. If awarded, a promissory note for the service obligation must be signed and returned.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings: Attorney Reimbursement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) pays attorney fees and certain costs for attorneys who represent students in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities. Attorneys may request reimbursement directly from MHEC for legal services provided on or after August 1, 2019, at a set hourly rate up to a maximum number of hours per case. Travel costs may also be reimbursed. Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Attorneys are reimbursed at $120 per hour for legal representation in Title IX proceedings, up to a maximum of 20 hours per case. MHEC List attorneys must certify fees do not exceed $100/hour (civil legal services rate under Maryland Human Services Article Title 11). Billing must be in increments of 6 minutes (0.1 hour) or less. Travel costs (mileage at $0.70/mile for FY2025, tolls, public transit, parking) up to $200 per case may also be reimbursed. Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds. Payment should be requested within 60 days of termination of representation, and processing takes at least 60 days. For MHEC List Attorneys, representation beyond 20 hours must be provided pro bono; for non-list attorneys, the student is responsible for fees beyond 20 hours. Attorneys do not need to be on the MHEC Attorney List to request payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 60 days of termination of representation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Attorneys representing students (complainants or respondents) in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities, and the students they represent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of attorney fees and travel costs for legal representation in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings only (including investigation, mediation, disciplinary hearing, and appeals). Does not cover civil, criminal, or non-Title IX student disciplinary proceedings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for Title IX proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities statewide. All 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City are implicitly covered as the program is administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
requirements_list: Legal services must have been provided on or after August 1, 2019
Payment is limited to Title IX proceedings only — does not cover civil, criminal, or non-Title IX student disciplinary proceedings
Maximum payment cap of 20 hours per case
Billing must be in increments of 6 minutes (0.1 hour) or less
Attorney does not need to be on the MHEC Attorney List to request payment
MHEC List attorneys must certify fees do not exceed $100/hour (civil legal services rate under Maryland Human Services Article Title 11)
For MHEC List Attorneys, representation beyond 20 hours must be provided pro bono; for non-list attorneys, the student is responsible for fees beyond 20 hours
Attorney must submit a completed Payment Request Form including a federal employer identification number (FEIN)
Attorney must submit an Additional Information Form
Attorney must submit a signed Retainer/Representation Agreement (confidential info may be redacted)
Attorney must submit a detailed billing statement
Student must complete and sign a Student Certification Form
Attorney must submit a notice of proceedings from the institution
Travel cost reimbursement requires a Travel Cost Reimbursement Form and receipts
Payment requests must be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation
Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The attorney submits a payment request directly to MHEC within 60 days of termination of representation. The student must sign a Student Certification Form provided by the attorney. Required documents include: Payment Request Form (with FEIN), Additional Information Form, Retainer/Representation Agreement, detailed billing statement, Student Certification Form (signed by student), notice of proceedings from the institution, and (if applicable) Travel Cost Reimbursement Form with receipts. Contact MHEC at TitleIXproceedings.mhec@maryland.gov for assistance. Allow at least 60 days for processing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Nursing Students
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a reduction in tuition for out-of-state students enrolled in a nursing program at a public two-year or four-year institution in Maryland. The award covers the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition (the tuition differential) and is adjusted directly by the institution so the student pays in-state rates. Awards renew automatically for up to the full duration of the program (two years at a two-year institution, four years at a four-year institution), provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution after graduation or repay the award with interest. Service must begin within six months of graduation, and if holding multiple awards with service obligations, service must be performed in consecutive years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The annual award equals the tuition differential — the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition at the same institution, for the same nursing program and number of credit hours. The institution adjusts tuition charges so the student pays the in-state rate. Awards renew automatically for up to two years at a two-year institution or up to four years at a four-year institution, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible program. Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse (35+ hrs/week) in a hospital or related institution in Maryland for two years (two-year institution) or four years (four-year institution) after graduation, or repay the award with interest. Service must begin within six months of graduation. If holding multiple awards with service obligations, service must be performed in consecutive years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2025-2026 academic year: April 1, 2026; 2026-2027 academic year: October 15, 2026 (application available January 15, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-residents of Maryland enrolled or planning to enroll in a nursing program at a public two-year or four-year institution in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of out-of-state tuition to in-state tuition levels for nursing program enrollment at a Maryland public institution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a non-resident of Maryland attending a two-year or four-year public institution in Maryland. Service obligation must be fulfilled at a Maryland hospital or related institution.
requirements_list: Must be a non-resident of Maryland
Must be enrolled in a nursing degree program at a two-year or four-year public institution in Maryland
Must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6–11 credits) as a degree-seeking student
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the attending institution
Must remain enrolled in an eligible nursing program for renewal
Must sign and return a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse (35+ hrs/week) in a Maryland hospital or related institution for the required service period
Service obligation is four years for four-year institution attendees and two years for two-year institution attendees
Recipients have six months from graduation to begin service
If holding multiple service-obligation awards, service must be performed in consecutive years
Must apply through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App
Must comply with drug-free requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App. Upon approval, the institution makes the tuition adjustment and reports the assistance amount annually to OSFA. The 2026-2027 application becomes available January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients provides financial assistance to eligible foster care youth pursuing higher education. The waiver exempts recipients from paying tuition and mandatory fees at any Maryland public institution of higher education for associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs (credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing). It applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer terms and does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a foster care recipient may not be applied to tuition since it is already waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible students from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other required enrollment fees) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. It applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer terms. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to the recipient may not be applied to tuition since tuition is already waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals under age 25 who have been placed in out-of-home care by the Maryland Department of Human Services and are enrolled at a Maryland public college or university.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public institutions of higher education for associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs (credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing). Does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be enrolled at a Maryland public institution of higher education. Must have resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at key points in their life (at high school graduation or GED completion, at age 18, on their 13th birthday with subsequent guardianship or adoption, or for at least one year on or after age 13 before returning to parents).
requirements_list: Must be under age 25 at the time of enrollment.
Must be enrolled full time or part time in an associate, bachelor's, or vocational certificate program at a Maryland public institution of higher education.
Must have been placed in an out-of-home placement by the Maryland Department of Human Services.

Must meet at least one of the following residency-in-care criteria: resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at the time of high school graduation or GED completion; resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at the time of their 18th birthday; resided in out-of-home placement on their 13th birthday and was placed into guardianship or adopted out of an out-of-home placement after their 13th birthday; or resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland for at least one year on or after their 13th birthday and returned to live with their parents after the placement ended.
Younger siblings concurrently placed into guardianship or adopted by the same guardianship or adoptive family as an eligible foster care recipient are also eligible.
Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services.
Eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the FAFSA or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App.
Undocumented applicants who do not qualify for the MHEC One-App should consult the financial aid office at their institution.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution you are currently attending or plan to attend. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Undocumented applicants who do not qualify for the MHEC One-App should consult the financial aid office directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to students enrolling in approved non-credit certificate programs at participating Maryland community colleges. Programs must lead to apprenticeships, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement. Recipients may be eligible for an additional award for an additional developmental sequence. Funds may only be used to pay tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance at a participating Maryland community college, and only to the extent those costs have not already been covered by another state grant, scholarship, or employer assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum award of $2,000 annually to cover tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance at a participating Maryland community college for non-credit workforce development courses. The award may be combined with other state grants or scholarships as long as the total does not exceed the student's tuition, mandatory fees, and other associated costs of attendance. Funds may not duplicate coverage already provided by another state grant, scholarship, or employer assistance. Recipients may be eligible for an additional award for an additional developmental sequence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident students or Maryland high school graduates, and active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland, enrolling in eligible non-credit Workforce Development Sequences at participating community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance for non-credit workforce development sequence courses related to job preparation, registered apprenticeship, licensure, certification, or job skill enhancement at a participating Maryland community college.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at participating community colleges in Maryland. Students must be Maryland residents, Maryland high school graduates, or active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident, Maryland high school graduate, or active duty U.S. Military member stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland
Must be enrolled in an eligible Workforce Development Sequence at a participating Maryland community college
Courses must be non-credit and related to job preparation, registered apprenticeship, licensure, certification, or job skill enhancement
Must enroll in an approved non-credit certificate program leading to apprenticeship, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement
Additional eligibility criteria may apply depending on the college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact their college's financial aid office to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant (WSSAG) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant (WSSAG) Program provides financial assistance to Maryland students who plan to work in specific high-need workforce shortage fields after graduation. Eligible fields include child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, public service, and law. Awards are granted based on a combination of academic merit (GPA) and financial need. Award amounts vary by institution type and enrollment status, and recipients must fulfill a service obligation by working in their eligible field in Maryland after completing their degree. Awards may be renewed for up to five years as long as eligibility requirements are met. All awards are subject to availability of funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant awards range from $1,000 to $4,000 per year depending on institution type and enrollment status. Students attending a Maryland community college receive $2,000/year full-time (12+ credits/semester) or $1,000/year part-time (6–11 credits/semester). Students attending a Maryland four-year institution receive $4,000/year full-time or $2,000/year part-time. Awards are set at the statutory minimum and may be automatically renewed for up to five years if eligibility requirements and satisfactory academic progress are maintained. All awards are subject to availability of funding. Recipients must sign a promissory note and fulfill a service obligation (one year of full-time work at 35+ hrs/week, or two years of part-time work at 20+ hrs/week, for each year of scholarship received) in their eligible field in Maryland within one year of completing their degree.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 1 annually (applications available each year starting mid-April via MDCAPS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident undergraduate and graduate students (including high school seniors) enrolled at least half-time in a degree program at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university, pursuing eligible majors in workforce shortage fields such as child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, public service, and law, who plan to work in those fields in Maryland after graduation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses (tuition and fees) at a Maryland community college or four-year institution while pursuing a degree in an eligible workforce shortage field, including child development, human services, education (critical shortage areas), nursing, physical/occupational therapy, law (public service), and social work, with a requirement to work in that field in Maryland after graduation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (dependent students must also have a Maryland resident parent) enrolled at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident (dependent students must also have a Maryland resident parent)
Enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university
Enroll full-time (12+ credits/semester undergraduate; 9+ credits/semester graduate) or part-time (6–11 credits/semester undergraduate; 6–8 credits/semester graduate)
Be a degree-seeking student in an eligible major leading to employment in an eligible workforce shortage field
Maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution
Undergraduate students must earn at least 12 credit hours per academic year; graduate students at least 9 credit hours per academic year (including summer term)
Remain drug-free (drug-free pledge required)

Submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App; all supporting documents must be received by July 1 to be considered on-time (faxed documents not accepted; electronic file upload only)
Filing the FAFSA is not required but recommended — it determines award priority by need (applicants without FAFSA are assumed to have zero financial need)
GPA transcripts required to determine merit ranking (cumulative GPA recalculated to 4.0 scale; five tiers: 3.8–4.0, 3.6–3.79, 3.4–3.59, 3.0–3.39, and below 3.0)
Nursing, occupational therapy, and physical therapy students must submit a departmental acceptance letter (no exceptions)
Official transcripts from all institutions attended required (high school transcripts for entering freshmen; certified report cards conditional for high school seniors)

Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to fulfill a service obligation in the eligible employment field within one year of completing their degree (1 year full-time at 35+ hrs/week or 2 years part-time at 20+ hrs/week per award year received)
Award notification is by email; recipients must accept within 3 weeks via MDCAPS and submit an online promissory note

Applicants who previously received awards under MHEC's former career/occupational programs (Child Care Provider; DD/MH/CW/JJ Workforce Tuition Assistance) are not eligible to also receive a WSSAG award
All awards are subject to availability of funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us or via the MHEC One App (applications available each year starting mid-April). Create a user ID and password and activate your account before login. Upload all supporting documents via the Electronic File Upload tool by July 1 (faxed documents not accepted). Optionally file the FAFSA at fafsa.gov for the applicable academic year to be considered for need-based ranking. Provide official transcripts from all institutions attended for GPA ranking. Nursing, occupational therapy, and physical therapy applicants must also submit a departmental acceptance letter. Awards are ranked by cumulative GPA (five tiers) and then by financial need within each tier. Award notifications are sent by email; recipients must accept within 3 weeks via MDCAPS and submit an online promissory note.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland John R. Justice Grant Student Loan Repayment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides student loan repayment assistance to Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors. The program makes payments directly on eligible federal student loans for qualifying attorneys who agree to remain employed in those roles for at least three years. Funds are distributed equally between prosecutors and public defenders across Appellate Court districts, with recipients ranked by their loan debt-to-adjusted gross income (AGI) ratio. Preference is given to applicants with an AGI of $60,000 or less (single) or $130,000 or less (married) and at least $40,000 in eligible student loan debt. The maximum award is $10,000 per calendar year with a lifetime aggregate cap of $60,000. Recipients must sign a three-year service obligation agreement; if the obligation is not fulfilled, the full grant award must be repaid to the U.S. Department of Justice. The most recent application cycle was 2021-2022, and the application is currently closed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds are provided to cover outstanding balances on qualified federal education loans, including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Payments are made directly to the loan holder. Parent PLUS loans and consolidation loans used to repay Parent PLUS loans are not eligible. The maximum award is $10,000 per calendar year with a lifetime aggregate cap of $60,000. Funds are distributed equally between prosecutors and public defenders across Appellate Court districts. Recipients are ranked by their loan debt-to-adjusted gross income (AGI) ratio. Preference is given to applicants with an AGI of $60,000 or less (single) or $130,000 or less (married) and at least $40,000 in eligible student loan debt. Recipients must sign a three-year service obligation agreement; failure to fulfill the obligation requires full repayment of the award to the U.S. Department of Justice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys and carry outstanding qualifying federal educational loan balances. Note: the FY 2021-2022 cycle was specific to public defenders only; applications were not accepted from state prosecutors during that cycle.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of eligible federal student loans including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Payments are made directly to the loan holder. Parent PLUS loans and consolidation loans used to repay Parent PLUS loans are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed in Maryland as full-time prosecutors or public defenders at the state, local, tribal, nonprofit contractor, or federal defender organization level.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. Citizen or eligible non-citizen
Must have an outstanding balance on an eligible federal education loan (Federal Stafford, Graduate PLUS, consolidation, or Perkins loans)
Must be an attorney continually licensed to practice law in Maryland

Must be a full-time prosecutor of criminal or juvenile delinquency cases for a state or local government, OR a full-time public defender providing legal representation to indigent persons for a state, local government, nonprofit contractor, or federal defender organization in Maryland — including full-time employees of the state of Maryland or a unit of local government who prosecutes criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, provides legal representation to indigent persons in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, is employed by a nonprofit under contract with the state providing such legal representation, or is employed as a full-time federal defender attorney in a qualifying defender organization

Must sign a three-year service obligation agreement to remain employed as a prosecutor or public defender; secondary/renewal terms require a minimum one-year (12 months) continuous employment commitment
Must not be in default on a federal guaranteed educational loan
Must not owe a refund on any scholarship or grant program administered by the Maryland Office of Student Financial Assistance
Must provide Social Security Number (mandatory; failure to provide renders agreement incomplete and applicant ineligible)
Must authorize the state agency to verify loan status, payment history, and balance with lender
Must notify the state agency without delay of job transfers, voluntary separation intent, or default on qualifying loans
Must continue personal loan payments during the grant period
Preference given to applicants with AGI of $60,000 or less (single) or $130,000 or less (married) and at least $40,000 in eligible student loan debt

Applicants are ranked by loan debt to adjusted gross income (AGI) ratio; a cost-of-living factor is applied for ties; geographic distribution by appellate court district is also considered in selection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Maryland John R. Justice Grant Application form along with supporting documentation each year you apply. For the most recent cycle (FY 2021-2022): Application opened March 7, 2022. Submit original documents postmarked by April 15, 2022 to Priscilla Moore, Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Outreach and Grants Management, 6 N. Liberty Street, 10th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21201. Required documents include: (1) completed and signed application form (Sections A–C); (2) Employment Verification form (applicant completes top section; employer completes bottom); (3) Proof of eligible loans — Lender Verification form per loan or recent account statements showing loan type and balance; (4) tax documentation — photocopy of signed 2020 Federal income tax return plus 2021 W-2s (or IRS non-filing verification if applicable); (5) Service Agreement (Appendix A for first-time applicants; Appendix B for years 2–3; Appendix C for applicants seeking an additional benefit after completing a 3-year obligation). Award notices were issued May 6, 2022; grant period ended May 6, 2023. The application is currently closed with no evidence of a subsequent cycle.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Financial Aid Grant and Scholarship Appeal Process
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) at the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) operates an appeal process that allows students receiving state financial aid grants and scholarships to request reconsideration of their award when special circumstances caused them to miss a requirement. Students can submit appeals under multiple categories — including special financial circumstances, late FAFSA/MHEC One-App, 5th year of award, program of study, delayed college entrance, credit completion issues due to academic program structure or disability, GPA requirements, and enrollment below required credits due to disability or academic program structure. Eligible programs include the Guaranteed Access Grant, Educational Assistance Grant, 2+2 Transfer Scholarship, Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship, Senatorial Scholarship, and Delegate Scholarship. Successful appeals allow students to receive or continue receiving state grant or scholarship funding that they otherwise would have lost due to failing to meet program requirements. Multiple appeal types are available with different opening and closing dates throughout the 2026–2027 academic year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students submit an online appeal request with required documentation. A decision is provided by email within 45 business days. Successful appeals allow students to receive or continue receiving state grant or scholarship funding that they otherwise would have lost. Appeal types and windows: Special Financial Circumstance (opens Feb 11, 2026, closes Jul 1, 2026); Late FAFSA/MHEC One-App (opens Mar 3, 2026, closes Jul 1, 2026); 5th Year of Award (opens Apr 1, 2026, closes Sep 1, 2026); Program of Study (opens Apr 1, 2026, closes Sep 1, 2026); Delayed College Entrance (opens Apr 1, 2026, closes Sep 1, 2026); Credit Completion Due to Academic Program (opens May 1, 2026, closes Oct 15, 2026); Credit Completion Due to Disability (opens May 1, 2026, closes Oct 15, 2026); 2.5 Cumulative GPA (opens May 1, 2026, closes Oct 15, 2026); Enrolled in Less Than 6 Credits Due to Disability (Fall: Jul 1–Dec 15, 2026; Spring: Oct 1–Apr 15, 2027); Enrolled in Less Than 12 Credits Due to Academic Program or Disability (Fall: Jul 1–Dec 15, 2026; Spring: Oct 1–Apr 15, 2027).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by appeal type: July 1, 2026; September 1, 2026; October 15, 2026; December 15, 2026; April 15, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland students currently receiving or applying for state financial aid grants and scholarships who have missed requirements due to special circumstances, including students enrolled in less than 6 or 12 credits due to disability or academic program structure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Continued or reinstated receipt of state financial aid grants and scholarships for higher education — not a direct cash award, but a process to restore or extend an existing grant or scholarship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland institutions and receiving Maryland state financial aid
requirements_list: Must be a recipient of or applicant for an eligible state grant or scholarship program
Must complete and submit appeal through the online form by the applicable deadline
All required documentation must be uploaded and submitted with the appeal request
Incomplete or late appeal requests will be denied
Each appeal type has specific eligible reasons and documentation requirements
Special Financial Circumstance Appeal open February 11–July 1, 2026
Late FAFSA/MHEC One-App Appeal open March 3–July 1, 2026
5th Year of Award Appeal open April 1–September 1, 2026
Program of Study Appeal open April 1–September 1, 2026
Delayed College Entrance Appeal open April 1–September 1, 2026
Credit Completion Due to Academic Program Appeal open May 1–October 15, 2026
Credit Completion Due to Disability Appeal open May 1–October 15, 2026

Enrolled in Less than 12 Credits Due to Academic Program Appeal open July 1–December 15, 2026 (Fall) and October 1–April 15, 2027 (Spring)
Enrolled in Less than 12 Credits Due to Disability Appeal open July 1–December 15, 2026 (Fall) and October 1–April 15, 2027 (Spring)
Students who have previously received the Educational Assistance Grant cannot be considered for the Guaranteed Access Grant regardless of any changes to circumstances
Delayed College Entrance Appeal requires letter explaining extenuating circumstances outside student's control causing 6+ year delay after high school completion or GED receipt
Credit Completion Appeal requires minimum 18 credit hours completed in prior year (2025-2026) and enrollment in third or fourth year of GA or EA funding
Medical documentation from licensed practitioner required for disability-based appeals

Enrolled in Less Than 6 Credits Due to Disability Appeal requires medical documentation from licensed practitioner confirming disability impact on half-time enrollment, class schedule documentation, and a separate appeal per term if applicable

Enrolled in Less Than 12 Credits Due to Academic Program Appeal requires Department Chair Certification Form, class schedule documentation, program curriculum structure documentation, and enrollment in 6–11 credits per term

Special Financial Circumstance allowable reasons include: death of income-earning family member, separation/divorce, involuntary unemployment, or loss of child support/SSB — all with specific documentation requirements
