Teaching Fellows Program of Study Appeal requires letter from student explaining circumstances, letter from academic advisor documenting 5-year program requirement, and copy of most recent transcript
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online 2026-2027 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form (Google Form linked on the program page) with all required documentation uploaded. Steps: (1) determine eligibility, (2) gather required documentation, (3) submit via the 2026-2027 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form with all required documents, (4) OSFA reviews and provides a decision by email within 45 business days. Incomplete and late requests will be denied.

structured_extraction.program_name: African American Heritage Preservation Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The African American Heritage Preservation Program (AAHPP) provides capital grants to help preserve buildings, sites, and communities significant to African American history and culture in Maryland. The program funds activities such as preserving or acquiring historically significant properties, restoring or rehabilitating historic sites, developing new facilities to interpret African American history, stabilizing endangered properties, and pre-construction planning work. The program is jointly administered by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) and the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture (MCAAHC). Typically, the program has an annual budget of $5 million for grants. The FY27 round is currently open for applications from individuals and organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants of up to $250,000 per applicant. No match is required. Funds may be used for preservation, acquisition, restoration, rehabilitation, stabilization of historic properties, development of new interpretive facilities, and pre-construction planning services. Grant funds cannot pay for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed. Typically, the program has an annual budget of $5 million for grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals seeking to preserve buildings, sites, or communities significant to African American history and culture in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preserving or acquiring buildings and sites significant to African American history; restoring or rehabilitating historic sites; developing new facilities to interpret or celebrate African American history; stabilizing endangered properties; pre-construction planning including architectural, engineering, and other special services. Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland. Available statewide across all counties.
requirements_list: Project must be located in Maryland
Project must demonstrate a clear, direct connection to African American history, culture, or heritage
Property or proposed use must have an association with African American heritage
Project must benefit the public to be competitive
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the application
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68)
Religious properties: grants can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery
Cemeteries: applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
Properties listed in or eligible for the National Register may be subject to a historic preservation easement held by MHT
Work that is already underway or completed is not eligible for funding
Applicants should review grant guidelines before applying
Applicants are encouraged to watch the general overview webinar
Applicants are encouraged to attend program webinars and workshops
Contact program staff with questions prior to applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines and sample materials. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Attend a pre-application workshop or webinar (a general overview webinar is available). 4. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, and proof of ownership or site control. 5. Submit a completed application through the online grants portal before July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Separate application links are available for individuals and organizations. Existing applications can be accessed by logging into the grant portal. The agency typically announces decisions by December each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Government (CLG) Program and Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Certified Local Government (CLG) Program recognizes local governments that meet high standards for historic preservation planning. Certified governments receive technical support, training, and annual competitive grant funding drawn from MHT's 10% allocation of its federal Historic Preservation Fund from the National Park Service. Grants help communities strengthen preservation programs, document historic resources, and promote education and outreach. Annual competitive project grants of up to $25,000 per project are available, along with non-competitive commissioner and staff training grants. No match is required, though a 15% match is encouraged. Technical assistance and periodic training sessions are also provided to participating CLGs. Currently 24 CLGs are certified, including 13 cities and 11 counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHT awards 10% of its federal Historic Preservation Fund allocation annually to Certified Local Governments. Competitive project grants are available up to $25,000 per project with no required match (15% encouraged). Non-competitive commissioner and staff training grants are also available up to amounts specified in annual grant guidelines. All grants are subject to available federal funding. Technical support, periodic training sessions, and consultation with MHT staff are additional benefits of CLG participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland that are certified participants in the CLG Program — i.e., those that have established a qualified historic preservation commission and meet CLG certification standards. Currently 24 CLGs are certified, including 13 cities and 11 counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic property surveys; National Register of Historic Places nominations; design guidelines for historic districts; training for local preservation commission members and staff; preservation plans or planning studies; public education and outreach about preservation topics; public outreach or interpretation projects that connect residents to local history; surveys, planning documents, and design guidelines that strengthen local preservation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Certified Local Governments throughout Maryland. Currently 24 CLGs are certified, including 13 cities and 11 counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Certified Local Government (CLG) participating in the CLG Program
Enact a preservation ordinance that meets state and federal standards
Appoint a qualified historic preservation commission
Maintain a system for identifying and protecting historic properties
Complete a certification process beginning with an application outlining all CLG standards
Complete training and a short report annually (to maintain certification)
Participate in an evaluation every four years (to maintain certification)
Review grant guidelines before applying
Confirm project eligibility and consult with MHT staff as needed
Submit completed application(s) through the MHT grants portal before the posted deadline
Projects must be non-capital in nature (except commissioner and staff training)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Check whether your jurisdiction is already certified. 2. Adopt a preservation ordinance, designate a qualified commission, and set up review procedures. Review the CLG Procedures Manual and application. 3. Application links, education and training application, project application, and grant guidelines are emailed directly to CLG contacts when the round opens (early February). Watch MHT's website each February for the CLG grant round. 4. Contact MHT staff early to discuss draft applications and align goals with grant priorities. 5. Submit completed application(s) through the MHT grants portal by end of February. Awards are announced in May.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program's competitive commercial tax credit is the state's largest preservation incentive. It provides a state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses (capped at $5 million) for qualifying historic rehabilitation projects on income-producing or commercial properties. An additional 5% credit may be earned for high-performance properties achieving LEED gold certification. The program spurs economic growth, promotes community reinvestment, and preserves Maryland's historic places. Projects in a qualified Opportunity Zone may be eligible for additional state tax credits. The state credit can be combined with federal and local historic tax credits. Applications are ranked competitively and credits are awarded to the highest priority projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $5 million per project. An additional 5% credit may be earned for high-performance properties achieving LEED gold certification. Projects must have eligible rehabilitation expenses greater than the adjusted basis value of the structure or $25,000 (whichever is less). Projects in a qualified Opportunity Zone may receive additional state tax credits. The credit is awarded through a competitive process with applications accepted by August 31 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, businesses, individuals, and nonprofit organizations that own or have permission to rehabilitate a certified historic structure used for income-producing or commercial purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible rehabilitation expenses for restoring or improving a certified historic structure to functional use while preserving its important historical, architectural, or cultural features, consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined eligible for the National Register. Some properties in a Maryland heritage area may also be eligible. Buildings must be certified as historic according to MHT standards.
requirements_list: Property must be a certified historic structure
Property must be primarily income-producing or rehabilitated for a commercial or nonprofit use
Project must qualify as a 'substantial rehabilitation' — eligible rehabilitation expenses must exceed the adjusted basis of the structure or $25,000
All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must not begin until Part 2 application is approved by MHT
Application must be submitted before commencement of rehabilitation work
Applicant must own the property or have the property owner's permission
Applications are due August 31st each year
Projects are ranked competitively

For tax credits of $1 million or more, applicants must meet corporate diversity requirements by filing a Corporate Diversity Addendum or an exemption affidavit (sole proprietors, single-member LLCs, certain family-owned businesses, and small businesses with under $5 million in annual budget/sales are exempt)

The Corporate Diversity Addendum (2026 form) must be completed with at least 33% (4 of 12) Corporate Diversity Indicators met to qualify for state benefits; the affidavit on Page 2 is mandatory and must be submitted with the Annual Report to SDAT
Response to Item I (demographic board/leadership representation disclosure) is required
Response to Item II (corporate diversity indicators checklist) is required; minimum threshold of at least 4 of 12 indicators must be met
Affidavit signature under penalties of perjury is mandatory; form must be submitted with the Annual Report to SDAT (P.O. Box 17052, Baltimore MD 21297-1052)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application has three parts: Part 1 describes the property and its historic significance; Part 2 describes the proposed rehabilitation work and must be approved before work begins; Part 3 documents the completed project for final certification. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT staff early in the planning process, before submitting applications. Applications are accepted by August 31 each year. The MHT review period typically runs approximately 30 to 45 days. If project scope changes, an amendment form must be submitted and approved before beginning new work. For tax credits of $1 million or more, complete the Corporate Diversity Addendum (per COMAR 24.01.07), check applicable diversity indicators (minimum 4 of 12 must be met), sign the affidavit under penalties of perjury, and attach to the Annual Report filed with SDAT (P.O. Box 17052, Baltimore MD 21297-1052).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Federal Historic Tax Credit (also called the Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives program or Federal Rehabilitation Tax Credits for Historic Properties) provides a federal income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified rehabilitation costs for certified historic income-producing structures. The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), as Maryland's State Historic Preservation Office, serves as the first point of contact for applicants in Maryland. MHT maintains National Register records, assists with National Register listings, advises on rehabilitation projects, conducts site visits, and makes certification recommendations to the National Park Service (NPS). The NPS administers the program and hosts the application, regulations, and guidance. The program aims to promote investment in historic buildings, create jobs, and revitalize communities.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A federal income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified rehabilitation expenditures for certified historic income-producing structures. The credit amount and specific terms are defined by federal law and detailed on the NPS website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, private investors, businesses, non-profits, and individuals who own income-producing historic properties and seek to rehabilitate buildings listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of certified historic structures; the tax credit applies to qualified costs for the rehabilitation of an eligible historic income-producing property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for eligible income-producing properties. MHT serves as the state-level point of contact for federal tax credit applicants in Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be a certified historic structure listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places
Property must be income-producing
Rehabilitation must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Certification recommendation from MHT to the National Park Service is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the Historic Preservation Certification Application from the NPS website. 2. Complete the application. 3. Submit a Teams channel request form. 4. Submit the application and any necessary documentation to the Teams channel. MHT reviews the application and forwards it to the National Park Service for final approval. MHT is available to advise applicants throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Rehabilitation Tax Credits for Historic Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps people invest in historic buildings. It offers a federal tax credit to cover part of the cost of renovating and reusing these properties. The program aims to create jobs and revitalize communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a federal income tax credit. The credit equals 20% of the money spent on approved renovation costs for an income-producing historic property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for private investors, businesses, non-profits, and individuals who own income-producing historic properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to qualified costs for the rehabilitation of an eligible historic property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available for eligible income-producing properties anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: The property must be a certified historic structure.
The property must be income-producing.
The rehabilitation project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit their Historic Preservation Certification Application electronically using the current forms. First, submit the application to the Maryland Historical Trust. They review it and then forward it to the National Park Service for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historic Preservation Capital Grant Program provides grants of up to $100,000 per project for the preservation of Maryland's historic properties and sites. With up to $1 million in total funding available annually, grants support important and urgently needed preservation projects that benefit the public, including acquiring historic properties, stabilizing or rehabilitating structures, and funding pre-construction planning work. The FY 2026 round opened February 2, 2026, with full applications due March 16, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 per project, with up to $1 million in total funding available annually. A 1:1 cash match is required for all applicants except nonprofits. If a property receives grant funding, a historic preservation easement must be conveyed to MHT.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Full applications due March 16, 2026 by 11:59 PM (annual cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals seeking to preserve Maryland historic properties listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring historic properties; stabilizing, rehabilitating, or restoring historic properties; pre-construction planning services such as architectural, engineering, or other special services (nonprofit and local government applicants only). Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties listed in or determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, individually or as part of a historic district.
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68).
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the application.
A 1:1 cash match is required for all applicants except nonprofits.
If funded, a historic preservation easement on the property must be conveyed to MHT.
Religious properties: grants can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery.
Cemeteries may qualify but applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership.
Grant funds cannot pay for work that has already started or been finished.
Applicant must be a nonprofit, local government, business, or individual (pre-construction planning limited to nonprofits and local governments).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are typically available in February and due in mid-March, with agency decisions made by July each year. 1. Review the current grant guidelines and sample materials. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Attend a pre-application workshop or webinar. 4. Prepare required attachments (cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, proof of ownership or site control). 5. Applications open February 2, 2026. Submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal by 11:59 PM on the posted deadline (March 16, 2026 for FY 2026). Check the program website starting in September for announcements about the next round.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Preservation Loan Program for Capital Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) offers low-interest capital loans to help preserve historic properties across Maryland. Loans support acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, and predevelopment projects that benefit the public. The fixed annual interest rate is set at 0.125% above the most recent state general obligation bond rate, with potentially lower rates for nonprofits and local governments. Certain qualified nonprofit organizations may also apply for non-repayable fund transfers (similar to grants) to acquire, restore, or re-lend for historic properties. Loan applications are accepted year-round as funds become available, with transfer applications opening in November and closing in January. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. If a loan is approved, the borrower must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate capital loans for historic preservation projects. The interest rate equals the most recent state general obligation bond rate plus 0.125%. Nonprofits and local governments may qualify for an even lower rate. Loan terms run up to two years for predevelopment projects and up to twenty years for other projects. The loan amount typically does not exceed 80% of the appraised property value and depends on available funds and the borrower's repayment ability. Qualified nonprofit organizations may also receive non-repayable fund transfers for acquisition, restoration, or re-lending purposes. A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount (whichever is less) is required. Loan applications are accepted year-round as funds become available; transfer applications open in November and close in January. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. If a loan is approved, the borrower must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT. Borrowers are responsible for appraisal fees, survey fees, title examination fees, attorney fees, and processing expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted year-round as funds become available; transfer applications open in November and close in January
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, business entities that cannot obtain private financing, and individuals that cannot obtain private financing seeking to preserve historic properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of historic properties (buildings, bridges, structures, sites); stabilization, rehabilitation, or restoration of historic properties; refinancing existing loans; predevelopment work including plans, specifications, and architectural, engineering, or other special services directly related to pre-construction. For qualified nonprofits receiving fund transfers: acquiring properties for resale, restoring properties, or providing loans to other organizations and individuals. Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed. Borrowers are responsible for appraisal fees, survey fees, title examination fees, attorney fees, and processing expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, individually or as part of a historic district.

If approved, MHT coordinates loan settlement. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds research, survey, documentation, planning, and education projects related to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources. Grants do not support preservation-related activities that involve building construction or major rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $75,000. Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind). Nonprofit organizations and state/federal agencies applying as nonprofits are not required to provide a match.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, and state/federal agencies seeking to fund research, survey, documentation, planning, and education projects related to Maryland's historic and cultural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Surveys and studies of historic buildings, archaeological sites, and cultural resources; reports on history and significance of historic properties; National Register of Historic Places nominations and historic contexts; improvements to qualifying archaeological collections; projects to identify and document cultural resources for emergency planning; educational materials, public programs, and publications about Maryland's history and archaeology; oral history and cultural heritage documentation; preservation plans, feasibility studies, and property assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must relate to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources.
requirements_list: Applicants must be nonprofit organizations, local governments, or state/federal agencies (applying as nonprofits).
Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind).
Work must not have begun prior to grant approval.
Projects may not focus mainly on fundraising, social or promotional events, or general administrative costs.
Projects may not involve building acquisition, major construction, or full rehabilitation.
Applications are evaluated on public value, readiness to proceed, diversity of project types and subject matter, and support for statewide preservation goals.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines and manual. 2. Attend a virtual workshop. 3. Submit an Intent to Apply form when the round opens (June). 4. Prepare a full application package including project description, budget, timeline, and explanation of significance and need. 5. Submit the completed application through the MHT grants portal before the August deadline. Awards are announced in November.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps public, non-profit museums with money and expert advice. The goal is to share Maryland's history, boost tourism, and support education. It also encourages professional museum standards. The program currently has no funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants and technical assistance. However, it is not currently funded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and non-profit museum organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that interpret Maryland's history, promote tourism, and provide public education.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mobile and virtual outreach program by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) that brings educational sessions about MHT programs, funding opportunities, and historic preservation to communities across Maryland. Sessions cover topics such as preservation grants, tax credits, heritage area programs, and how to apply for MHT funding. The program serves homeowners, local governments, nonprofits, and other interested groups, especially those with limited experience in preservation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual and in-person educational sessions offered annually. Typical format includes two virtual sessions covering general preservation programs and financial incentives, and two in-person events rotating among Maryland's regions. Each session includes Q&A with MHT staff. Custom briefings and longer presentations on financial incentives with application tips are also available. Partner organizations can request a local session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, local governments, nonprofits, heritage organizations, and anyone interested in Maryland's historic and cultural places — especially those with limited experience with MHT programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a no-cost educational outreach and training program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; in-person events rotate among Maryland's regions annually.
requirements_list: To request a hosted session, a partner organization (local government, planning commission, historical society, or nonprofit) must be willing to host and help market the event.
Requester must identify their audience and preferred topics before submitting a request.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Upcoming sessions and registration details are posted on MHT's Upcoming Events page. To request a local session, submit a request through the online form at the provided Google Forms link or contact MHT staff directly. MHT will assess availability and follow up.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program Project Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program awards approximately $3 million per grant cycle for capital and non-capital projects within Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas. Projects must create or enhance publicly accessible, place-based experiences or assets that preserve and promote Maryland's unique stories while contributing to local economic development. Capital projects may include buying property, building, repairing, restoring, or planning for construction. Non-capital projects may include planning, programs, and interpretation. Emergency grants are also available outside the regular cycle for sudden or unexpected needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants require a 1:1 match (any combination of cash or in-kind). Non-capital grants range from $5,000 to $50,000. Capital grants range from $5,000 to $100,000. Emergency grants are available outside the regular cycle for urgent, unexpected needs. The annual grant round opens in December, with intent to apply due in January, full applications due in March, and awards announced in July.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, and state or federal agencies with projects located within Maryland's certified heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects: property acquisition, construction, repair, restoration, or construction planning. Non-capital projects: planning, programs, and interpretation that create or enhance publicly accessible, place-based heritage experiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of one or more of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas.

Project must take place within a certified Maryland heritage area
1:1 match required (cash or in-kind)
Project must create or enhance publicly accessible, place-based experiences or assets
Project must preserve and promote Maryland's unique stories and contribute to local economic well-being

Submit full application through grants portal by March deadline

Submit an Intent to Apply form by the January deadline. 4. Contact the appropriate heritage area staff to discuss the project. 5. Prepare application materials including project description, timeline, budget, and optional letters of support. 6. Submit the full application through the grants portal by the March deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program – Heritage Area Management Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program provides annual grants to the management entities of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas. Grants support management operations, marketing, and mini-grants that local heritage area organizations can pass through to smaller local organizations. The program is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust through the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants provided to heritage area management entities for management, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations. Specific dollar amounts are not stated on this page.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage area management operations, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations to advance heritage tourism and resource preservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program boundaries touch all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City through the 13 designated heritage areas.
requirements_list: Must be a certified heritage area management entity recognized by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA)
Must operate within one of Maryland's 13 designated heritage areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should consult the heritage area management grant guidelines and budget template linked on the program page. No further application process details are provided on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program – Project Grants, Mini-Grants, and Loans (MHAA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program, administered by the Maryland Historical Trust through the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA), designates, supports, and collaborates with heritage areas and their partners to create place-based experiences for the public. It preserves and promotes Maryland's unique stories and contributes to the well-being of local economies through heritage tourism. The program provides both financial and technical assistance to help protect and enhance heritage resources within certified heritage areas, improve quality of life for residents, and maximize economic development. Financial assistance includes capital and non-capital project grants, mini-grants, loans, and tax credits. Non-capital grants are available up to $50,000 and capital grants up to $100,000; both grant types require a one-to-one match. Loans cover up to 50% of total project cost based on financial need and may be used for property acquisition, heritage tourism development, rehabilitation or restoration of historic properties, leasehold improvements, and purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory. Refinancing is not eligible as part of the project cost. A tax credit of up to 20% is available for eligible rehabilitation costs of qualifying historic structures. The program provides annual grants to support capital and non-capital projects within Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas, awarding approximately $3 million per grant cycle. Grants support management operations, marketing, and mini-grants that local heritage area organizations can pass through to smaller local organizations. Capital projects may include property acquisition, construction, repair, restoration, or construction planning. Non-capital projects may include planning, programs, and interpretation. Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may also offer mini-grants under $5,000 for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming and planning efforts, administered by individual heritage areas. Emergency grants are available outside the regular cycle for sudden or unexpected needs. Within specific heritage areas such as the Heart of the Civil War Heritage Area (Carroll, Frederick, and Washington counties), grants are also available to heritage organizations and local governments for heritage tourism projects. The FY 2027 grant cycle is open, with an Intent to Apply (ITA) form due by February 2, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual project grants provided to heritage area management entities and eligible nonprofits, local governments, and state/federal agencies for management, marketing, mini-grants to local organizations, and capital and non-capital projects. Non-capital grants range from $5,000 to $50,000; capital grants range from $5,000 to $100,000. A 1:1 match (cash or in-kind) is required for project grants. Mini-grants under $5,000 are also available through individual heritage areas for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts. Emergency grants are available outside the regular cycle for urgent, unexpected needs. The program also offers loans covering up to 50% of the total project cost based on the applicant's financial need; loan amount depends on available funding and refinancing is not eligible as part of the project cost. Leasehold improvements require a lease term at least as long as the loan term. A tax credit of up to 20% is available for eligible rehabilitation costs of qualifying historic structures. Technical assistance is also provided to support heritage area activities. The annual grant round opens in December, with an Intent to Apply (ITA) form due by early February (e.g., February 2, 2026 for the FY 2027 cycle), full applications due in March, and awards announced in July.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply due February 2, 2026 (FY 2027 cycle); full application due March (annual cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: The 13 certified heritage area management entities in Maryland and, through mini-grants and direct grants, nonprofit organizations, individuals, local governments, and state or federal agencies with projects located within Maryland's certified heritage areas. Also businesses and individuals seeking loans to create or improve place-based heritage resources within a heritage area, and organizations within the Heart of the Civil War Heritage Area (Carroll, Frederick, and Washington counties).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage area management operations, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations. Capital projects: property acquisition, construction, repair, restoration, or construction planning. Non-capital projects: planning, programs, and interpretation that create or enhance publicly accessible, place-based heritage experiences consistent with the Heritage Area Management Plan and Five-Year Action Plan. Mini-grants support heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming and planning efforts under $5,000. Loans may be used for: acquisition of property or property rights (easements); development or new construction for heritage tourism; rehabilitation or restoration of historic properties; leasehold improvements; purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory. Also supports strengthening local economies through heritage tourism and community enhancement; planning, creating exhibits and signs; funding educational programs or events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of one or more of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas, whose boundaries collectively touch all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Specific grant opportunities such as those for the Heart of the Civil War Heritage Area are limited to Carroll, Frederick, and Washington counties. Mini-grants must be located within one of Maryland's 13 designated heritage areas. Loans require projects to be located within a designated Maryland heritage area.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For project grants: 1. Review the grant guidelines available at the Maryland Historical Trust website. 2. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Preservation Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit program administered by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) for homeowners, commercial property owners, and small commercial property owners who rehabilitate certified historic structures in Maryland. Eligible properties include those listed individually or as contributing structures in the National Register of Historic Places or locally designated historic districts. Rehabilitation must be conducted in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. The program offers tax credits for homeowner, commercial, and small commercial projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit for qualifying rehabilitation costs on historic properties. Eligible costs include architectural, engineering, and consultant fees; plumbing, HVAC, and electrical upgrades; kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation; new appliances as part of a broader rehab; interior finishes that become part of the structure; and restoration of historically significant landscape features. Financing charges and building permit fees are not eligible. Rehabilitation must generally occur within a 24-month period, though projects may be phased. Each phase must meet a minimum cost threshold of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects. Credits are available for homeowner, commercial, and small commercial projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, commercial property owners, and small commercial property owners rehabilitating certified historic structures in Maryland; specifically owners of properties listed individually or as contributing structures in the National Register of Historic Places or locally designated historic districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of certified historic structures in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation, including plumbing, HVAC, electrical upgrades, kitchen and bathroom work, architectural and engineering fees, interior finishes, and restoration of historically significant landscape features.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties listed in the National Register of Historic Places or locally designated historic districts.
requirements_list: Property must be individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing structure in a National Register historic district, or a locally designated historic property.
Rehabilitation must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
Rehabilitation must occur within a 24-month period (projects may be phased).
Each phase must meet a minimum cost threshold: $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects.
MHT prefers that no work begin until plans have been approved.
Projects completed before application must be documented with before-and-after photographs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Jan Gowing at MHT (410-514-7644) to confirm property eligibility. Submit federal and state tax credit application forms — the federal form must be fully completed; only the first sheet of each part is required for the state form. MHT recommends obtaining plan approval before beginning work. For phased projects, the first application should describe all projected phases.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit (Heritage Area Properties)
structured_extraction.program_description: Within a Maryland heritage area, eligible property owners may receive a Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs for qualifying historic or heritage-area certified buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs. This benefit is in addition to other state tax credits available for qualified rehabilitation work on historic structures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners within Maryland heritage areas undertaking rehabilitation of historic or heritage-certified buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of eligible historic properties within heritage areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located within a Maryland heritage area.
requirements_list: Property must be individually listed or contributing to a historic district listed in the National Register of Historic Places, OR eligible for but not listed on the National Register, OR certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area
Project must involve eligible rehabilitation costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program page for full details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program encourages the preservation and rehabilitation of historic properties throughout Maryland by providing a state income tax credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses (qualified capital costs) spent on certified historic structures. The program is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT). The Homeowner Tax Credit is available to homeowners who own and occupy a certified historic property as their primary or secondary residence, with the credit capped at $50,000 in any 24-month period and a minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required. The program is also available for commercial properties (including small commercial property owners) and, within Maryland heritage areas, for any eligible property owner undertaking rehabilitation of historic or heritage-area certified buildings. Eligible properties include those individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, contributing resources in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated historic properties determined eligible for the National Register by MHT. All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation, and all projects must be reviewed and approved by MHT before work begins. The application has three parts: describing the property, proposing the rehabilitation work, and documenting the completed project. The credit may be used in conjunction with local historic tax credits, and MHT's review is independent of any local review. Rehabilitation must generally occur within a 24-month period, though projects may be phased, with each phase meeting the applicable minimum cost threshold.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses (qualified capital costs). For owner-occupied homeowners, the credit is capped at $50,000 in any 24-month period with a minimum eligible rehabilitation expense threshold of $5,000. For all other projects, the minimum threshold is the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000. Also available for commercial properties (including small commercial) and for property owners within Maryland heritage areas undertaking rehabilitation of historic or heritage-certified buildings. This benefit may be used in addition to other applicable state tax credits. Eligible costs include architectural, engineering, and consultant fees; plumbing, HVAC, and electrical upgrades; kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation; roof repair or replacement; chimney repair and relining; structural repairs; window and door restoration; new storm doors/windows; masonry repair or repointing; interior finish restoration (plaster, flooring, trim); tool/equipment rental; repair of historic outbuildings; new appliances as part of a broader rehab; interior finishes that become part of the structure; and restoration of historically significant landscape features. Financing charges and building permit fees are not eligible. May be used in conjunction with local historic tax credits. All projects must be reviewed and approved by MHT before work begins; MHT review is independent of local review.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and occupy a certified historic property as their primary or secondary residence, owners of commercial historic properties (including small commercial), non-profit organizations, government entities, and property owners within Maryland heritage areas seeking to rehabilitate qualifying historic structures in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of historic properties in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Eligible expenses include roof repair or replacement, chimney repair and relining, structural repairs, window and door restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry repair or repointing, mechanical/electrical/plumbing work, interior finish restoration (plaster, flooring, trim), professional design/architectural/engineering fees, tool/equipment rental, repair of historic outbuildings, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, new appliances as part of a broader rehab, interior finishes that become part of the structure, restoration of historically significant landscape features, and rehabilitation of historic commercial and heritage-area certified properties. Financing charges and building permit fees are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties that are certified historic structures (individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, contributing resources in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined eligible for the National Register by MHT). Within Maryland heritage areas, properties certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area are also eligible. MHT review is independent of local review and available throughout Maryland.
