Property must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence, a qualifying historic commercial property, or a heritage-area certified building, and must be a certified historic structure.

A certified historic structure must be individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, locally designated and determined by MHT to be eligible for the National Register, OR certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area.
Minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses for owner-occupied residential projects; for all other projects, the minimum is the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000.
All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
All work must be approved by MHT before it begins — work started prior to MHT review and approval will not qualify.
Rehabilitation must generally occur within a 24-month period (projects may be phased).
For phased projects, each phase must meet the applicable minimum cost threshold.
If the project changes or new work is added, an amendment form must be submitted and approved by MHT before starting the additional work.
MHT review is independent of local review and may not be waived or substituted for local approval.
Eligible for owner-occupied residences, commercial properties (including small commercial), and heritage-area properties.
Costs must be qualified capital costs related to rehabilitation.
Financing charges and building permit fees are not eligible.
Projects completed before application must be documented with before-and-after photographs.

Property must be individually listed or contributing to a historic district listed in the National Register of Historic Places, OR eligible for but not listed on the National Register, OR certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT early for large or complex projects. Confirm property eligibility with MHT before beginning work. Complete and submit all three parts of the application: Part 1 (property description and historic significance), Part 2 (proposed rehabilitation work for approval — must be submitted and approved before work begins), and Part 3 (documentation of completed project for final certification). Submit federal and state tax credit application forms — the federal form must be fully completed; only the first sheet of each part is required for the state form. For phased projects, the first application should describe all projected phases. MHT review typically takes 30–45 days after receiving a complete application. Submit applications electronically following the electronic submission instructions. For heritage area properties, visit the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program page for full details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program – Homeowner Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program offers homeowners a state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses (capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period) to encourage investment in historic neighborhoods and help Marylanders preserve their historic homes. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses and all work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. The application has three parts: describing the property, proposing the rehabilitation work, and documenting the completed project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in any 24-month period. The minimum eligible rehabilitation expense threshold is $5,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and occupy a certified historic property as their primary or secondary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible rehabilitation expenses include roof repair or replacement, chimney repair and relining, structural repairs, window and door restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry repair or repointing, mechanical/electrical/plumbing work, interior finish restoration (plaster, flooring, trim), professional design/architectural/engineering fees related to the project, tool/equipment rental, and repair of historic outbuildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties that are certified historic structures (individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, contributing resources in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined eligible for the National Register by MHT).
requirements_list: Applicant must own and occupy the property as their primary or secondary residence, individually or through a cooperative.
Property must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence and a certified historic structure.

A certified historic structure must be individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined by MHT to be eligible for the National Register.
Minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses.
All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
All work must be approved by MHT before it begins – work started prior to MHT review and approval will not qualify.
If the project changes or new work is added, an amendment form must be submitted and approved by MHT before starting the additional work.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT early for large or complex projects. Complete and submit all three parts of the application: Part 1 (property description and historic significance), Part 2 (proposed rehabilitation work for approval – must be submitted and approved before work begins), and Part 3 (documentation of completed project for final certification). MHT review typically takes 30–45 days after receiving a complete application. Submit applications electronically following the electronic submission instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historical Trust provides grants supporting a wide variety of historic preservation activities, including property acquisition and rehabilitation, documentation and survey, heritage tourism development, and educational programs. Available grant programs include Historic Preservation Capital Grants, Historic Preservation Non-Capital Grants, African American Heritage grants, Certified Local Governments grants, and the Maryland Heritage Areas Program. Each program has different eligibility standards and regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for historic preservation activities including capital and non-capital projects, African American heritage, certified local governments, and heritage areas. Amounts and terms vary by program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and individuals undertaking historic preservation activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and rehabilitation, documentation and survey, heritage tourism development, and educational programs related to historic preservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Eligibility varies by specific grant program
Each program has its own guidelines that applicants must review carefully
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Historical Trust Grants homepage at mht.maryland.gov for details on each specific grant program, eligibility, and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historical Trust Historic Preservation Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) offers low-interest capital loans to help preserve historic properties in Maryland. Loans support acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, and predevelopment projects that benefit the public. The fixed annual interest rate is set at 0.125% above the most recent state general obligation bond rate, with potentially lower rates for nonprofits and local governments. Loan applications are accepted year-round as funds become available, with transfer applications opening in November and closing in January. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. If a loan is approved, the borrower must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate capital loans for historic preservation projects. The interest rate equals the most recent state general obligation bond rate plus 0.125%. Nonprofits and local governments may qualify for an even lower rate. Loan applications are accepted year-round as funds become available. Transfer applications open in November and close in January. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. If a loan is approved, the borrower must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT. Borrowers are responsible for appraisal fees, survey fees, title examination fees, attorney fees, and processing expenses. A $250 application fee (check payable to Maryland Historical Trust) is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted year-round as funds become available; transfer applications open in November and close in January
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, business entities that cannot obtain private financing, and individuals that cannot obtain private financing seeking to preserve historic properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of historic properties (buildings, bridges, structures, sites); stabilization, rehabilitation, or restoration of historic properties; predevelopment work including plans, specifications, and architectural, engineering, or other special services directly related to pre-construction. Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed. Borrowers are responsible for appraisal fees, survey fees, title examination fees, attorney fees, and processing expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, individually or as part of a historic district.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68)
Business entities and individuals must demonstrate they cannot obtain private financing
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the loan application
If approved, a historic preservation easement must be conveyed to MHT
Loan funds cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed
Religious properties: loans can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery
Cemeteries: applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
Applicants must contact MHT staff as a first step before applying
$250 application fee (check payable to Maryland Historical Trust) required
Federal income tax returns (previous 2 years) required for business entities and individuals
Personal financial statements required for individuals, proprietors, limited partners (≥20%), general partners, stockholders (≥20% voting stock), or loan guarantors
Organizational documents required for nonprofits and business entities
501(c)(3) status confirmation required for nonprofits (if applicable)
Proof of good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) required
Easement Work Approval Documentation from MHT required (except acquisition-only projects)
Corporate Resolution required for entity applicants
Applicants must disclose all less-than-fee-simple interests (mortgages, leases, mineral rights, reversionary interests, etc.)
Applicants must describe public benefit, public access, disability accessibility provisions, and community revitalization impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact MHT staff to discuss eligibility and available funding — this is required as a first step. 2. Review program guidelines and manual. 3. Prepare and submit the application with required attachments including project description, financial statements, cost estimates, appraisal/report, evidence of public benefit, organizational documents, professional resumes, and a $250 application fee. 4. If approved, MHT coordinates loan settlement. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Museum Assistance Program (MAP) provides grants to Maryland museums and institutional collections. The program helps historical and cultural museums strengthen operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability. Eligible activities include everyday museum operations such as paying staff, training staff or volunteers, office or administrative costs, environmental monitoring, and security and safety systems. The program also supports public interpretation of Maryland's history, tourism promotion, and public education. Capital projects are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $20,000, typically between $10,000 and $15,000. In FY26, $285,000 was available statewide. No match required. Technical assistance may also be available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments that operate a museum open and operating for at least three years, interpreting Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology. Museums operated by state or federal government are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Everyday museum operations, including paying staff, training staff or volunteers, office or administrative costs (insurance, reporting, accounting), environmental monitoring (e.g., pest management or humidity control), and security and safety systems. Also supports projects that interpret Maryland's history, promote tourism, and provide public education. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit or local government
Museum must have been open and operating for at least three years
Nonprofits must be in good standing with the state
Nonprofits must be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status
Museum must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology
Museums operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government are not eligible
Each museum seeking funding requires a separate application if the applicant operates more than one museum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines. 2. Confirm project eligibility and applicant type. 3. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control. 4. Submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal before the posted deadline. Applications open in August and are due in October, with awards announced in winter.

structured_extraction.program_description: Administered by the Maryland Historical Trust on behalf of the National Park Service, this competitive grant program funds projects that protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage. Eligible projects must include a public education component and support activities such as identifying historic maritime resources, repairing or rehabilitating historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites, or improving public access to maritime resources. Projects addressing flooding, erosion, or changing environmental conditions on maritime resources while advancing public education are prioritized.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants ranging from $10,000 to $100,000 per project. Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000. A 1:1 non-federal match is required. Total available funding is $380,192.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state governments, local governments, and nonprofit organizations with projects that protect historic maritime resources and advance public education about maritime heritage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites; repair, rehabilitation, stabilization, maintenance, or limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites; improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. Grant funds cannot support work already started or completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Administered statewide in Maryland on behalf of the National Park Service.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a tribal government, state government, local government, or nonprofit organization
Project must demonstrate a clear public benefit
Project must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation
Where applicable, project must follow the Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects
Project must include a public education component
Project must support at least one eligible activity (identification, repair/rehabilitation/stabilization, or improved public access)
Applicants may request between $10,000 and $100,000
Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000
A 1:1 non-federal match is required
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the grant guidelines and manual for detailed requirements. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Prepare a complete application including scope of work, budget, and required documentation. 4. Submit through the MHT grants portal before June 1. Awards are announced in July. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in project planning.

structured_extraction.program_description: A legal agreement between a property owner and the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) to protect a property's historic character and ensure its long-term preservation. Property owners may voluntarily donate or convey an easement to MHT for properties individually listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, or those significant to Maryland's history, architecture, archaeology, or culture. An easement may also be required as a condition of certain MHT grants, loans, or other government funding. The easement specifies which portions of the property are protected and what changes require MHT approval, limits some development rights, requires maintenance of historic features, mandates limited public access, and requires prior MHT approval before making changes or alterations. The easement deed is recorded in county land records and applies to all future owners during its duration. MHT reviews and accepts preservation easements at no charge to property owners, though owners cover related costs such as title work, surveys, and recording fees. Processing typically takes several months to a year. MHT staff provide ongoing technical guidance on appropriate repairs, maintenance, and rehabilitation methods, and regularly inspect easement properties to confirm compliance. Donated easements may qualify property owners for charitable contribution tax deductions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHT reviews and accepts preservation easements at no charge to property owners. The easement deed specifies protections and is recorded in county land records. Donated easements may qualify property owners for charitable contribution tax deductions. MHT also provides ongoing technical guidance on historic preservation practices, repair, maintenance, and rehabilitation methods. Easements may be permanent or for a fixed term and apply to all future owners during their duration. Property owners cover related costs such as title work, surveys, and recording fees. Processing typically takes several months to a year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Maryland who wish to voluntarily donate a preservation easement, or who are required to convey an easement as a condition of MHT grants, loans, or other government funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection of a property's historic character through a legally recorded easement deed specifying which portions of the property are protected and what changes require MHT approval; potential charitable contribution deductions for donated easements; technical guidance on preservation, repair, and rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties individually listed in or eligible for individual listing on the National Register of Historic Places, or significant to Maryland's history, architecture, archaeology, or culture.
requirements_list: Property must be individually listed in or eligible for individual listing on the National Register of Historic Places, OR be significant in Maryland's history, architecture, archaeology, or culture
Owner must agree to limit some development rights
Owner must maintain the property and protect its historic features
Owner must provide limited public access
Owner must complete a short public access form each year to confirm compliance with access requirements
Owner must obtain prior MHT approval before making changes or alterations
MHT regularly inspects easement properties to confirm compliance
Owner must submit a letter expressing desire to donate and provide supporting information (property description, history, maps, photographs)
For conveyances tied to grants or loans, the easement must generally be recorded before funds are released
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact MHT easement program staff by email or phone before beginning. 2. Provide required documentation including ownership and property records, property descriptions, site plans, maps, insurance policy, deed information, and photographs. 3. Review draft easement deed prepared by MHT. 4. After both parties approve, sign and record the easement in county land records. 5. For projects involving MHT grants or loans, coordinate timing so the easement is recorded before funds are released. Visit the 'Donate or Convey an Easement' page on the MHT website to learn more about eligibility and documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge Workshop
structured_extraction.program_description: A two-weekend workshop in spring that allows Scouts BSA members to earn the Archaeology Merit Badge. One weekend focuses on classroom learning about archaeological methods and Maryland history, and the other involves hands-on fieldwork at an active archaeological site. Scouts work directly with Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) archaeologists and handle real artifacts in the state lab.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants attend two weekends of programming: one classroom-based session covering archaeological methods and Maryland history, and one fieldwork session at an active dig site. Scouts complete hands-on activities, work with real artifacts, and excavate alongside MHT archaeologists to fulfill requirements for the Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge. Space is limited.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Scouts BSA members, individually or with a troop, with no prior archaeology experience required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completing requirements for the Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge through classroom instruction and field excavation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Scouts BSA members; program is run by the Maryland Historical Trust and takes place in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be currently registered with Scouts BSA
Must participate in both weekends (classroom and fieldwork)
Must complete listed prerequisites for the merit badge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the interest list via a Google Form to be notified when future workshops are scheduled. Space is limited and spots fill quickly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit (Small Commercial)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit program that helps strengthen communities and encourages local economic growth by providing a tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of eligible historic, income-producing properties. Total project expenses must not exceed $500,000, and credits are capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. The program has a yearly funding cap of $2 million. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the annual program cap is reached. Projects located in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits. The building may not be used for more than 75% residential rental purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified rehabilitation costs. Total project expenses cannot exceed $500,000. The credit is capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses to qualify. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, on a first-come, first-served basis until the program cap is reached for the current fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of certified historic commercial buildings in Maryland planning small rehabilitation projects, including developers who plan to sell a rehabilitated property to a homeowner.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects that repair or alter a historic structure for a modern use while preserving its significant features. Eligible work includes roof and chimney repair, window restoration, structural repairs, and updating plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems. Funds cannot be used for landscaping, new construction, appliances, or tool purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. To be eligible, a building must be a certified historic structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, a designated local historic structure, or located within a certified heritage area.
requirements_list: Building must be certified as historic according to MHT standards
The building must be primarily income-producing, rehabilitated to be sold to a homeowner, or a targeted agricultural or post-WWII building
Total qualified rehabilitation expenses must not exceed $500,000
Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses
All project work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
The Maryland Historical Trust must review and approve all aspects of the project before work begins
Credit is capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period
Building may not be used for more than 75% residential rental purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process. The application has three parts. Part 1 certifies that the building is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets program requirements. Applicants must submit all parts for approval before starting work. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the annual program cap is reached.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Horse Industry Board Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Horse Industry Board (MHIB) Grant Program supports the development of Maryland's horse industry by funding research, education, and promotional activities. Each year, the MHIB accepts applications for projects that support horses or the equestrian community, or that develop new opportunities for the Maryland horse industry. Funding comes from the Maryland Feed Fund, which collects $6 on every ton of horse feed sold in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 per organization (only one grant application may be submitted per organization), with an average award of approximately $1,000. Projects are evaluated on value to the industry, degree of industry promotion, size and scope, financial need, potential for matching funds, benefits, and quality of the written presentation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically early October each year (FY2026 cycle deadline was October 4, 2025 — now closed); projects must be completed by June 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, clubs and associations, businesses, farms and stables, licensed horse rescues, government entities, schools, and educational institutions in Maryland involved in or supporting the Maryland horse industry, including youth, veterans, first responders, at-risk youth, and people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research, educational, and promotional projects that support horses or the equestrian community, or develop new opportunities for the Maryland horse industry, including educational programs, therapeutic riding and equine-assisted therapy, youth engagement and horsemanship training, emergency preparedness and animal welfare training, competitions and events, clinics, seminars, equipment/materials, and public awareness activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Eligible organizations must be located in Maryland, including not-for-profit and non-profit organizations, local and state government and university programs, clubs and associations, businesses, licensed farms, stables, horse rescues, schools, and educational institutions in Maryland. Awards have been distributed across 15+ counties including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, St. Mary's, Howard, Talbot, Frederick, Cecil, Charles, Montgomery, Calvert, Prince George's, Carroll, Anne Arundel, Queen Anne's, and others.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a not-for-profit or non-profit organization, club, association, business, farm, stable, licensed horse rescue, government entity, school, or educational institution in Maryland
Grant requests should not exceed $2,000
Only one grant application may be submitted per organization
Projects must be completed by June 30
Final report due by June 30 of the project completion year
Applications are typically due in early October each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application by the early October deadline. Sign up for the email distribution list via GovDelivery (choose Grants under Horse Industry Board) to receive application materials and announcements. Licensed stables are automatically added to the list. Contact Anne Litz with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's House Keys 4 Employees (HK4E) program is a partnership between Calvert County and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides matching funds for down payment and closing costs to help eligible employees purchase a home. Employers sign a participation agreement to become an Employer Partner, making their employees eligible for the assistance. Local match for private-sector and public-sector employees could total up to $5,000, equivalent to the state contribution. Calvert County government also participates as an employer and provides matching funds for county government and public school system employees. The program is designed to make homeownership more affordable for the county's working population.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Mortgage Program (Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching funds for down payment and closing costs for first-time homebuyers through employers who have signed a Participation Agreement with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Financial assistance is made available at settlement. Local match for private-sector and public-sector employees could total up to $5,000, equivalent to the state contribution. Calvert County government also participates as an employer and provides matching funds for county government and public school system employees. The type of assistance (loan or grant) and amount are determined per employer agreement. The Department may close HK4E or modify the terms at any time, with at least 30 days written notice to partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers (those who have not owned a principal residence in the last three years) who are employed by a participating Employer Partner in Calvert County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for purchasing a home; assistance is made available at settlement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (must not have owned a principal residence in the last three years)
Must be employed by a participating Employer Partner
Employer must complete and submit a Participation Agreement to Maryland DHCD
Must meet specific eligibility requirements of the Maryland Mortgage Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers interested in becoming an Employer Partner must complete a Participation Agreement and submit it to Maryland DHCD. Eligible employees then apply through the Maryland Mortgage Program at mmp.maryland.gov. A tutorial is available for download from the Calvert County website for complete information. Contact DHCD at SingleFamilyHousing.dhcd@maryland.gov or 800-756-0119 x3.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free license plates issued to Maryland resident veterans who are rated at 100% disabled or compensated at the 100% rate based on individual unemployability, in recognition of service-related injuries. Qualified veterans also receive permanent vehicle registration cards and stickers, eliminating the need to renew registration at the MVA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free disabled veteran license plates issued to 100% disabled veterans (or those compensated at 100% rate due to individual unemployability), with permanent registration cards and stickers so registration does not need to be renewed. Plates are available with or without the universal disability symbol. Vehicle classes eligible: passenger car (A), multi-purpose vehicle (M), truck with one ton or less manufacturer's rated capacity (EPO).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident veterans rated 100% disabled or compensated at 100% rate based on individual unemployability, permanent and total.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free license plates and permanent vehicle registration for eligible disabled veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident veteran
Must be rated 100% disabled or compensated at the 100% rate based on individual unemployability, permanent and total
Vehicle must be a passenger car (A), multi-purpose vehicle (M), or truck with one ton or less manufacturer's rated capacity (EPO)
Must provide proof of 100% disability or 100% compensation from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
If requesting plates with the universal disability symbol, must submit Application for Maryland Parking Placard/License Plates for Individuals with a Disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at any MVA full-service branch office, mail application to the Specialty Tag Unit at 6601 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie, MD 21062, or apply through an MVA licensed tag and title service.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers a state income tax credit of up to $3,000 per qualifying new electric vehicle purchased by individuals or businesses. For individuals, the credit is claimed on the state income tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service; the full credit is only available if the individual's tax bill is $3,000 or more. For businesses, the credit is limited to 10 vehicles per business per tax year. The credit is nonrefundable in both cases, cannot exceed the taxpayer's tax liability, and unused amounts cannot be carried forward.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit of up to $3,000 per new qualifying electric vehicle. Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000 and must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh. For individuals, the credit is nonrefundable and cannot exceed the individual's tax liability. For businesses, the credit is limited to 10 vehicles per business, is nonrefundable, cannot exceed the business's tax liability, and unused amounts cannot be carried forward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and businesses purchasing new qualifying electric vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset the purchase cost of new qualifying electric vehicles for personal or business use
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000
Vehicle must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh
Taxpayer's tax bill must be $3,000 or higher to claim the full individual credit
Credit is nonrefundable and cannot exceed the taxpayer's tax liability
For businesses, credit is limited to 10 vehicles per business
For businesses, unused credit cannot be applied to future tax years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit on the Maryland state income tax return (individual or business) for the year the vehicle is placed in service. Vehicle qualifications and instructions are available at the MVA website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration Excise Tax Credit for Plug-In Electric Vehicle Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers both an excise tax credit and a state income tax credit for the purchase of qualifying plug-in electric vehicles. Individuals purchasing a qualifying new plug-in electric vehicle may receive a reduction in excise tax owed at the time of purchase, as well as a state income tax credit of up to $3,000 claimed on the state tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service. The full credit is only available if the taxpayer's tax bill is $3,000 or more. Businesses and non-profits may also claim a state income tax credit of up to $3,000 per qualifying new electric vehicle placed in service, limited to 10 vehicles per business per tax year. To qualify, the vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000 and the vehicle must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh. The credits are nonrefundable, cannot exceed the taxpayer's tax liability, and any unused amount cannot be carried forward. The program is administered by the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Excise tax credit applied at time of purchase of a qualifying plug-in electric vehicle, plus a state income tax credit of up to $3,000 per qualifying new EV for individuals and businesses. Business credit is limited to 10 vehicles per business per tax year. Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000, vehicle must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh, credits are nonrefundable and cannot exceed the taxpayer's tax liability, and unused credit cannot be carried forward. The full credit is only available if the taxpayer's tax bill is $3,000 or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses (including non-profits) purchasing qualifying new plug-in electric vehicles in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Occupational Safety & Health (MOSH) offers a free, confidential on-site consultation service to help employers identify and control workplace safety and health hazards, improve their safety and health programs, train employees, and potentially qualify for a one-year exemption from routine OSHA inspections. The service is funded jointly by the Workers' Compensation Commission and the U.S. Department of Labor's OSHA. It is primarily targeted at smaller businesses (fewer than 250 employees per establishment or 500 nationwide) in high-hazard industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and construction, but all private-sector employers and public-sector entities may request a visit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Refugee Health Program: Medical Screenings and Health Promotion
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Office for Refugees and Asylees (MORA) administers two interconnected health programs for eligible refugee populations. The Refugee Medical Screenings program provides comprehensive health assessments for newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants, ensuring participants receive a health assessment and appropriate follow-up care and referrals, and helping prevent the spread of communicable diseases. In coordination with medical screenings, MORA partners with the Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH) at the Maryland Department of Health to deliver the Refugee Health Promotion Program, which provides health education services, increases health literacy, supports navigation of health care, and organizes wellness groups including mental wellness and peer support. Together, these programs help prevent the spread of communicable diseases and promote long-term health and well-being for refugee and asylee clients statewide.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive health assessment exam initiated within 90 days and completed within 180 days of U.S. arrival or granted asylum date, including physical and mental health screening, immunizations for children required for school enrollment, treatment, and referral to a primary care physician for preventive health and ongoing care. Additionally, health education services are provided including opportunities to increase health literacy, coordination and support for navigating health care, and wellness groups (including mental wellness and peer support). Services are provided in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area through Baltimore Medical Systems and in Montgomery and Prince George's Counties through CCI Health Services, with additional access through local Health Departments. Health promotion services are provided statewide in coordination with medical screenings.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Foreclosure Mediation program allows homeowners facing foreclosure to request a formal mediation session with their lender. A neutral administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings facilitates the session to help both parties reach a mutually acceptable solution. Homeowners must file the 'Request for Foreclosure Mediation' form with the Circuit Court in the county or city where the foreclosure was filed, pay a non-refundable $50 filing fee, and send a copy to the lender's attorney — all within 25 days of receiving the form from the lender. Mediation can only be requested once during the foreclosure process; missing the 25-day window forfeits the right.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners in foreclosure can request one mediation session with their lender facilitated by a trained administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings. The homeowner must file the 'Request for Foreclosure Mediation' form with the Circuit Court in the county or city where the foreclosure was filed and pay a non-refundable $50 filing fee within 25 days of receiving the form from the lender. A copy of the form must also be sent to the lender's attorney. The Office of Administrative Hearings will then schedule the mediation session. Only one mediation opportunity is available during the foreclosure process.

A copy of the form must also be sent to the attorney handling the foreclosure for the lender. The Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings will then schedule the mediation session.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program – Maryland Subgrantee Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's BEAD program awards federal grants to eligible subgrantees to expand high-speed internet access in unserved and underserved locations across the state, particularly in rural, low-income, and difficult-to-serve areas. The Maryland Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB) administers the program, which was funded with $267,738,400.71 from the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). Subgrantees apply through a competitive process that includes a prequalification phase followed by a full application.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB), Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants totaling $267,738,400.71 awarded to subgrantees to fund broadband infrastructure deployment and adoption programs. Subgrantees are selected through a competitive application process and must enter into formal grant agreements with OSB. A 15% BEAD outlay threshold gating mechanism is used during application review to identify lowest-cost offers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Internet service providers, units of local government, non-profit organizations, and other eligible entities seeking to deploy broadband infrastructure in unserved and underserved Maryland locations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure deployment and adoption programs to close coverage gaps in unserved and underserved areas of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; focus on rural, low-income, and difficult-to-serve areas identified as unserved or underserved in the NTIA-approved challenge process location data.
requirements_list: Must complete and pass a prequalification phase before submitting a full application
Must submit application through the OSB submission portal during the open application window (July 10–24, 2025)
Applications are evaluated against a 15% BEAD outlay threshold gating criterion
Applicants within the 15% threshold may be asked by OSB to submit revised proposals
Must enter into a formal subgrantee grant agreement with OSB upon selection
Must use the OSB Grant Management System for monitoring and reporting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the prequalification phase (window was February 28 – March 14, 2025; status notices sent March 28, 2025). 2. Download the BEAD Application Documents ZIP folder and review required materials. 3. Submit application through the EDAS submission portal between July 10 and July 24, 2025. 4. Optionally complete and submit the Supplemental Technical Questionnaire. 5. OSB applies 15% BEAD outlay gating threshold and notifies applicants. 6. Selected applicants finalize grant agreements with OSB.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program — Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: The BEAD program provides federal funding to expand high-speed internet access in Maryland by funding broadband infrastructure deployment, planning, and adoption programs. Maryland received $267,738,400.71 from the NTIA and the Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB) is administering the state's BEAD subgrant program. Subgrantees (internet service providers and other eligible entities) can apply for funding to deploy broadband infrastructure in unserved and underserved locations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB), Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland received $267,738,400.71 in federal BEAD funding from NTIA. The state OSB awards subgrants to eligible applicants to deploy broadband infrastructure in unserved and underserved locations. The application window opened July 10, 2025 and closed July 24, 2025. Subgrantees are evaluated on cost proposals with a 15% gating threshold. Award notifications were planned for December 8, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Internet service providers, units of local government, and other eligible entities seeking to deploy broadband infrastructure in unserved and underserved areas of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure deployment in unserved and underserved locations across Maryland, as well as planning and adoption programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; priority focus on rural, low-income, and difficult-to-serve areas identified as unserved or underserved in NTIA-approved location data.
requirements_list: Must complete a Prequalification phase before submitting a full application
Must submit required application documents and data through the BEAD Submission Portal
Subgrantees use the OSB Grant Management System for monitoring and reporting
Applications subject to 15% gating threshold on BEAD outlay offers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants first completed a Prequalification phase (February–March 2025). The full application window opened July 10, 2025 and closed July 24, 2025. Applications were submitted through the EDAS Submission Portal. OSB evaluated proposals, notified applicants within the 15% BEAD outlay threshold, allowed optional revisions, and finalized subgrantee selections before issuing formal award notifications in December 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Operation: Campout! is a free camping gear loan program offered by the Maryland Park Service for active-duty military personnel, veterans, wounded warriors, and their families. Participants can borrow a tent, sleeping pads, cook stove, chairs, lantern, roasting sticks, and other camping equipment at no charge at selected state parks. The program is designed for military individuals and families who are new to camping or are experienced campers stationed or recovering in the area, providing an opportunity to reconnect with nature in a comfortable, safe, and relaxing setting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of camping gear (tent, sleeping pads, cook stove, chairs, lantern, roasting sticks, and more) for use at participating Maryland state parks. Campsites are available at $25–$39/night depending on the park and amenities; some sites have electric hook-ups, picnic tables, and fire pits, with restrooms and shower facilities nearby. Gear locker and campsite reservation are made together by contacting the park directly. Up to 6 people per site.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active-duty military personnel, veterans, wounded warriors, and their families (including children; up to 6 people per site) who are new to camping or experienced campers stationed or recovering in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing camping equipment (tent, sleeping pads, cook stove, chairs, lantern, roasting sticks, and more) for a camping stay at a participating Maryland state park: Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, and Janes Island State Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at seven selected Maryland state parks: Cunningham Falls (Frederick County), Swallow Falls (Garrett County), New Germany (Garrett County), Rocky Gap (Allegany County), Patapsco Valley (Baltimore County), Pocomoke River (Worcester County), and Janes Island (Somerset County) State Parks.
requirements_list: Must be a military individual or military family (active duty, veteran, or wounded warrior)
Must be new to camping or an experienced camper stationed or recovering in the area
Contact the desired participating state park directly by phone to make a reservation for both the campsite and the Operation: Campout! gear locker simultaneously
Specify 'Operation Campout!' gear reservation when calling; park staff will verify available dates and confirm gear availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Decide which participating state park you want to visit (Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, or Janes Island). Contact that park directly by phone to make a reservation — specify 'Operation Campout!' to reserve both the campsite and the gear locker at the same time. Park staff will verify available dates and confirm gear availability. There is no centralized online portal; the process is park-by-park and phone-based.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide certification program for individuals who collect drinking water samples from public water systems in Maryland. Certification ensures that Safe Drinking Water Act compliance samples are collected properly and that samplers meet current state regulatory requirements. Primarily intended for laboratory personnel, water system operators and superintendents, and county and state health department staff.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants register for and complete a water sampler training class and required examination through MRWA. Standard cost is $160; discounted rate of $35 for public water system (PWS) employees, state agency employees, certified lab employees, and well drilling operation employees; free for County Environmental Health Department/Program and MDE employees. Upon passing exam, participants receive a certified water sampler credential (Sampler Certification Card) issued by MDE via email. First-time samplers must also complete a Hands-On Practicum skills test demonstration. Certification is valid for a maximum of three years. As of January 1, 2025, new requirements apply for first-time samplers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Laboratory personnel, water system operators and superintendents, and county and state health department staff who collect drinking water compliance samples in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and examination to obtain or renew water sampler certification required for Safe Drinking Water Act compliance sampling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for individuals collecting SDWA compliance samples from public water systems.
requirements_list: Must register through Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA)
Must complete required Water Sampler Class and examination
First-time samplers must also complete a Hands-On Practicum skills test demonstration
High school education required; no experience required
Certification is valid for a maximum of three years
New requirements for first-time samplers effective January 1, 2025
Those certified within the past three years are exempt from the practical exam
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register through MRWA (md-rwa.org) and complete the Water Sampler Class and required examination. 2. Upon passing the exam, receive certification card. 3. First-time applicants only: complete a Hands-On Practicum skills test demonstration. 4. After completion, MDE issues the Sampler Certification Card via email upon MRWA confirmation. Contact MRWA at training@md-rwa.org or (410) 489-5877 with all questions about registration. Contact MDE at mde.labcertification@maryland.gov or (410) 537-3729 for MDE-specific inquiries.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: SPDAP helps moderate-income Maryland residents enrolled in Medicare Part D who are not eligible for the federal Extra Help program. The program pays up to $100 per month toward a Medicare Part D prescription drug premium. Enrollees are also allowed to change their prescription drug coverage once per year outside of Open Enrollment. Income limits are: single monthly gross income under $3,990 or married monthly gross income under $5,410, with no asset limit.

Participants get access to small group virtual coaching, four on-demand training modules, and a library of 100 hours of books, articles, workbooks, and videos.

Includes four on-demand modules, 24/7 access to an Accelerator Virtual Library, and one-on-one virtual coaching as needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Business Consulting and Training
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC) provides free individualized business consulting and no-cost or low-cost training programs to aspiring entrepreneurs and existing small business owners across Maryland. Consulting covers money management, marketing, regulatory compliance, technology development, and international trade. Training ranges from startup topics to executive-level programs, including Boots to Business and Veterans programs, offered through workshops, conferences, seminars, and online courses covering business planning, marketing, finances, and long-range planning. The New Venture Series includes three workshops — 'Ready, Set, Go!', 'Business Plan Development', and 'My Business Plan' — designed to help new and aspiring business owners start and grow successfully. The SBDC also helps businesses access funding from a variety of sources. Most programs are available at no cost or a nominal fee. Five regional offices serve distinct areas: Corridor Region (College Park), Southern Region (LaPlata), Eastern Region (Salisbury), Northern Region (Bel Air), and Western Region (Frostburg).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one business consulting and no-cost or low-cost training programs (workshops, seminars, conferences, and online courses) covering business planning, money management, marketing, financial management, legal structure, tax reporting, insurance, regulatory compliance, technology development, and international trade. Training includes Boots to Business, Veterans programs, Women Veteran programs, and free online learning courses. The New Venture Series offers three workshops for startups: 'Ready, Set, Go!' (free), 'Business Plan Development', and 'My Business Plan'. Sessions are typically held in the evening and range from two hours to several weeks. The SBDC also connects clients to business funding sources and supports long-range planning from startup through established stages. Five regional offices serve distinct areas: Corridor Region (College Park), Southern Region (LaPlata), Eastern Region (Salisbury), Northern Region (Bel Air), and Western Region (Frostburg).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aspiring entrepreneurs and existing small business owners in Maryland who are legally present in the United States, including those seeking to start or grow a business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business consulting in money management, marketing, regulatory compliance, technology development, and international trade; training programs from startup to executive level covering business planning, marketing, financial management, legal structure, tax reporting, insurance, and entrepreneurship skills; assistance accessing business funding; long-range planning support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland to all legal residents and citizens in the U.S. who are operating or starting a business in Maryland, through five regional offices: Corridor Region (College Park), Southern Region (LaPlata), Eastern Region (Salisbury), Northern Region (Bel Air), and Western Region (Frostburg).

Must be an aspiring entrepreneur or existing small business owner in Maryland
Open to anyone starting or running a small business

Browse and register for training events at the training calendar at https://mdsbdc.ecenterdirect.com/events. Online courses are also available through SBDC Open Learning. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) – Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP) expands business ownership for socially and economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs and small businesses that cannot access adequate financing through normal channels. It provides loans, loan guaranties, and equity investments to help businesses purchase franchises, acquire existing businesses, develop technology ventures, or start and expand other small businesses. EPIP also receives federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funding — $45 million over 7 years — to support SEDI-owned and other small businesses. The program is part of Maryland's broader SSBCI initiative and is managed by MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.) on behalf of the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA). Equity investments may take the form of preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, qualified securities, convertible debt, limited partnership or LLC interests, Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE), and other equity-like structures. All financing must be recaptured within seven years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA), managed by MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided through loans, loan guaranties, and equity investments ranging from $25,000 to $2,000,000. Loans are generally offered at 7%–12% interest; equity investments target a 15%–22% return and interest rates can be as low as 2% depending on program terms. Equity investments may take the form of qualified securities, convertible debt, interest in a limited partnership or LLC, Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE), preferred stock, common stock, warrants, or other debt and equity instruments. SSBCI-funded assistance may be provided as subordinated term loans, lines of credit, demand loans, letters of credit, or equity investments. Requires a minimum 1:1 private capital match (private co-investment equal to or greater than the SSBCI funding amount), and the lender must have 20% at risk. Collateral for loans can include business and personal assets. All loans and equity investments must be recaptured by the end of the seventh year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) – Surety Bond Program (SBP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) Surety Bond Program (SBP) helps eligible small businesses in Maryland obtain bid, performance, or payment bonds needed to compete for and perform on contracts funded primarily by government agencies, regulated public utilities, or private entities. MSBDFA, managed by MMG Capital Group (Meridian Management Group, Inc.), can directly issue bonds up to $2,500,000 or guarantee a commercial surety's losses up to 90% of the bond face value (not exceeding $2,500,000, i.e., up to $2,250,000 of surety losses, whichever is less). Bond premiums for direct issuance generally range from 2% to 3% of the required bond amount with no additional fees; guaranty fees are 10%–20% of the surety's premium plus 0.5% of the bond amount payable by the contractor. Bonds remain in effect for the duration of the contract and any related warranty period. A surety bond revolving line of credit may also be established and renewed annually to directly issue or guarantee multiple bonds within pre-approved terms. Financing decisions are voted on and approved by members of the MSBDFA Authority.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) — Contract Financing Program (CFP), Surety Bond Program (SBP), and Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP)
structured_extraction.program_description:
The Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA), administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce and managed by MMG Capital Group (also known as Meridian Management Group), promotes the viability and expansion of small businesses in Maryland, with a focus on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs. MSBDFA operates several programs: the Contract Financing Program (CFP), the Surety Bond Program (SBP), the Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP), and the Long Term Guaranty Program (Guaranty Fund Program/GFP).

The Contract Financing Program (CFP) provides direct loans, revolving lines of credit, and equity investments to eligible small and minority-owned businesses. Loans are used for working capital, equipment, supplies, and materials needed to perform government or Public Service Commission-regulated utility contracts. Lines of credit advance up to 80% of a customer billing invoice (or up to 50% of a purchase order) less than 90 days old within 24 to 48 hours. Mobilization funding is also available as a short-term loan to cover initial purchases and payroll when starting a new contract. Loans are limited to $2,000,000 at generally Prime Rate plus 2% interest, with principal and interest repaid as contract proceeds are received. Term loan rates are fixed at 5%–8% (as low as 2% for SSBCI-eligible loans); lines of credit 4%–8%. Revolving lines of credit are renewable annually with 12 to 24 month terms, and applicants may qualify for financing prior to contract award. The program also offers equity investments through preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, and other equity-like structures, with investments ranging from $25,000 to $1,000,000.

The Surety Bond Program (SBP) helps eligible small businesses obtain bid, performance, or payment bonds needed to compete for and perform on contracts funded primarily by government agencies, regulated public utilities, or private entities. MSBDFA can directly issue bonds up to $2,500,000 at premiums of 2%–3% with no additional fees, or guarantee a surety company's losses (up to 90% of face value, not exceeding $2,250,000), with fees of 10%–20% of the surety's premium plus 0.5% of the bond amount payable by the contractor. Bonds remain in effect for the duration of the contract and any related warranty period. A surety bond revolving line of credit may also be established and renewed annually. The company must not subcontract more than 75% of the dollar value of any contract to be bonded, and must not have defaulted on a bond, loan, loan guarantee, or equity investment from MSBDFA within two years of the application date.

The Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP) expands business ownership for socially and economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs and small businesses that cannot access adequate financing through normal channels. It provides loans (at generally 7%–12% interest), loan guaranties, and equity investments (targeting 15%–22% return) to help businesses purchase franchises, acquire existing businesses, develop technology ventures, or start and expand other small businesses. Professional/technical assistance loans up to $25,000 at 2% interest are also available. Loan guarantees cover up to 80% with maximum exposure of $2,000,000; loan guaranty annual fees range 0.5%–1.5%. Loan terms run up to 7 years (amortization up to 20 years). Equity investments may take the form of qualified securities, convertible debt, interests in a limited partnership or LLC, Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE), or other instruments. Collateral for loans can include business and personal assets, and the company must have identified a probable investment exit.

The Long Term Guaranty Program (Guaranty Fund Program/GFP) provides loan guaranties up to the lesser of 80% of the loan or $2,000,000, with guaranties not exceeding 10 years and interest rates generally ranging from prime to prime plus 2%. GFP can also subsidize up to 4 percentage points of the interest rate charged by the lending institution, subject to annual review. Loan guaranty annual fees range from 0.75% to 1.5%.

EPIP and other components also receive federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funding — $45 million over 7 years — to support SEDI-owned and other small businesses, with interest rates as low as 2% and a required private co-investment equal to or greater than the SSBCI funding amount. All loans and equity investments must be recaptured by the end of the seventh year.

The program targets businesses that cannot obtain conventional financing due to physical handicaps, historical exclusion from financial resources based on race or other protected characteristics, or other social or economic barriers beyond their control. A non-refundable $250 application fee is required at submission (not required for loan guaranty or surety bond requests), and a $500 commitment fee is due at acceptance.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Meridian Management Group (MMG Capital Group) website at mmgcapitalgroup.com/msbdfa to review full MSBDFA guidelines, qualifications, and FAQs. Use the Application Questionnaire/Tool on the MMG website (mmgcapitalgroup.com/apply) to assess qualification and receive a recommendation for which program to apply to. If eligible, create an account and complete the full application form on the Maryland Department of Commerce online platform at programs.commerce.maryland.gov/m, pay the non-refundable $250 application fee, and upload all required documents. Applications are not processed until the fee is confirmed by Maryland Department of Commerce. An assigned Loan/Investment Officer (LIO) reviews the application and will advise on SSBCI eligibility. Applications over $350,000 are reviewed by the MSBDFA/MCBIF Board; applications of $350,000 or less may be reviewed by the MMG Internal Loan Committee. The approving body typically meets on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month (twice a month). If the LIO recommends approval, the application is submitted to the MSBDFA Board. Financing decisions are voted on and approved by members of the MSBDFA Authority. If approved, a commitment letter and term sheet are issued within approximately 3 business days. The applicant has 14 days to sign and return the commitment letter along with a $500 commitment fee. Closing generally occurs 3–6 weeks after acceptance of the Commitment Letter, and once closing occurs, loan proceeds are disbursed within 1–7 business days by check or ACH direct deposit. Applicants may qualify for financing prior to contract award. For surety bonds or EPIP, contact MMG Capital Group directly. See all Maryland SSBCI programs at open.maryland.gov/ssbci. Contact loan officer Taber J. Small at MMG Capital Group for assistance at (410) 333-4270 or taber.small@mmgcapitalgroup.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant program that provides financial support to fully developed and ready-to-implement public art initiatives in Maryland that celebrate America's 250th anniversary (Semiquincentennial). Eligible projects include the conservation and promotion of existing public artworks or the creation and installation of new works such as murals, tile mosaics, paintings, or sculptures. Projects must be located in Maryland and created by Maryland-based artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant funded by the National Endowment for the Arts to support public art projects aligned with America250 goals. Awarded funding may cover administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials (artwork, base, lighting, landscaping), contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental, signage or plaques, and dedication event expenses. Grant amounts are not specified on this page.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees (up to 15%), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials (artwork, base, lighting, landscaping), contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental to fabricate and assemble artwork, signage or plaques to identify the artwork, and dedication event expenses.

Applications are reviewed by MSAC staff and a representative from the Maryland250 Commission using criteria required by the National Endowment for the Arts. Review the America250 Public Art Grant Scoring Rubric before submitting. Grantees must file a final report in SmartSimple by September 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The A&E District Designation program allows Maryland counties and municipalities to apply for a state designation that unlocks tax incentives and other tools to encourage arts activity and investment in specific geographic areas where the arts are part of an economic development strategy. Designated districts must be located within Priority Funding Areas and coordinate with local economic development plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designated districts receive tax incentives (including tax credits) and other tools to encourage arts-related economic development activity and investment. The specific tax credits associated with the designation must be agreed upon by all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district prior to application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland county and municipal governments seeking to designate a geographic area with significant arts activity as an official Arts & Entertainment District to leverage tax incentives and economic development tools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Designation provides tax incentives and other tools to encourage arts activity, entertainment venues, arts businesses, and economic investment in the designated geographic area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any county or municipal government in Maryland. Proposed district must be located within a designated Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county or municipal government in Maryland
Selected geographic area must have a significant level of arts activity, entertainment venues, and/or arts businesses
Arts and entertainment must be included in the area's economic development strategy
Must communicate with all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district and obtain agreement with all impacted governments concerning the tax credits associated with the designation
Must complete an Intent to Apply form online at least 90 days before the chosen application deadline
Must follow detailed requirements in the A&E District Designation Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact MSAC staff to begin the process. Then communicate with all impacted governments and obtain agreement on tax credits. Submit the Intent to Apply form online at least 90 days before the chosen deadline (April 1 or October 1). Submit a full application per the A&E District Designation Guidelines. Applications are reviewed in three steps: (1) MSAC staff review for completeness and regulatory adherence; (2) review by the MSAC A&E Districts Advisory Committee (with representation from Commerce, Housing & Community Development, Transportation, and Planning, plus current A&E District managers); (3) final decision by the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts Operating Support Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual operating grants from the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) support activities, programs, and projects run by management entities of designated Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts throughout Maryland. Appointed management entities for designated A&E Districts may apply for MSAC operating support funds to support district priorities. Applicants submit either an 'On-Year' application (every fifth fiscal year post-designation, requiring updated goals, plans, and budget) or an 'Off-Year' application (all other years, requiring a shorter budget and updates overview).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual operating grants (approximately $15,000) to support district activities, programs, and projects. The FY2027 support period runs July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027. Payment is processed after grant agreement execution and received within 6–8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at the end of the funded fiscal year. Funding recommendations are subject to approval by the MSAC Council and the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management entities (nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations or local government agencies) of designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: District operating activities, programs, and projects aligned with district priorities, including district promotion, event/festival production, business attraction, artist support services, public art, real estate promotion, partnership management, fundraising, board management, and advocacy, as outlined in the proposed budget for A&E District activities for the next fiscal year
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland. The program serves communities throughout Maryland, with districts approved by the Secretary of Commerce.

Must complete a signed Letter of Agreement between the county or municipality holding the designation and the management entity
Must have a current contract or MOU with a county or municipality to manage a designated A&E District
Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization or local government agency designated as the management entity
A&E District must already be designated prior to applying for operating support
Adhere to MSAC grantmaking, crediting, and reporting requirements
Maintain equitable, community-responsive programs

Maintain constituent distribution list
