structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either an On-Year application (in the fifth fiscal year post-designation) with updated goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, management and marketing plans, and a proposed budget, or an Off-Year application (all other years) with a shorter form covering the proposed budget and any needed updates. A signed Letter of Agreement between the county or municipality and the management entity is required. On-Year applications are reviewed by the A&E Districts Advisory Committee with opportunity for revision; Off-Year applications are reviewed by MSAC staff. Recommendations go to the MSAC Council and the Secretary of Commerce for approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Income Tax Subtraction Modification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified residing artists who live in Maryland and sell artistic work within any of Maryland's designated Arts and Entertainment Districts — including Hagerstown's — can subtract income earned from in-district sales when calculating Maryland state income taxes. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district; for all qualifying artists it includes internet sales originating in a district. The program is available statewide across all of Maryland's designated Arts and Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax subtraction modification allowing qualified residing artists to subtract income derived from in-district sales of artistic work from their Maryland state taxable income. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district. For all qualifying artists, internet sales originating in a district also qualify. The subtraction reduces Maryland state income tax liability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified residing artists who live in Maryland and sell artistic work within any State-designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability by subtracting income earned from in-district sales of artistic work or performances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Artist must reside in Maryland and conduct sales or performances within any designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment District, including Hagerstown's district.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified residing artist
Must live in Maryland
Must sell artistic work within a designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment District
For performing artists, eligible income includes performances in a district
Internet sales originating in a district are eligible
Income must be derived from in-district sales or performances
Must file Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with state income tax return
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Maryland State Tax Form 502AE when filing state income tax returns.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts program offers tax-related incentives to qualifying artists and businesses located within one of Maryland's 29 designated A&E Districts. Three incentives are available: (1) a local property tax credit for owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial properties renovated for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises; (2) an income tax subtraction modification for qualified residing artists who sell artistic work within an A&E district; and (3) a local admissions and amusement tax exemption for arts and entertainment enterprises or qualifying residing artists operating within a district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three incentives apply in designated A&E Districts: (1) Property tax credit — local governments determine the amount and duration; based on the difference between pre- and post-renovation property assessments when a property is renovated for use by qualified artists or arts enterprises. (2) Income tax subtraction modification — qualified residing artists may subtract all eligible A&E district income from their Maryland state taxable income by filing Form 502AE with their annual state tax return; no dollar cap applies. (3) Admissions and amusement tax exemption — local governments may exempt gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges imposed by arts enterprises or qualifying artists within a district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified residing artists who live and conduct arts business in Maryland A&E Districts, and arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit or nonprofit) operating within a designated district, as well as property owners who renovate properties for arts use in a district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on income from sales or performances of artistic work within an A&E district, property tax relief on renovated arts-use properties, and exemption from admissions and amusement taxes for qualifying arts enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within any of Maryland's 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts statewide.
requirements_list: For income tax subtraction modification: must own or rent residential property in Maryland, conduct an arts business in an A&E district, and earn income from the sale or performance of artistic work produced and sold within an A&E district.

Artistic work must be original and creative and fall into one of the defined categories (writing, performance, music, visual art, sculpture, crafts, film, dance, jewelry/clothing/functional art, storytelling, digital/new media, or derivatives thereof).
The income tax subtraction modification is available only to independent individual artists and sole proprietors — not employees of organizations.
Royalties, licenses, and revenue from sale of publishing or reproduction rights do not qualify for the income tax subtraction modification.
Industry-related work produced at large volume or for commercial purposes does not qualify.

For property tax credit: property must be wholly or partially renovated for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises; amount, duration, and application process determined by local government.

For admissions and amusement tax exemption: must be an arts and entertainment enterprise or qualifying residing artist operating within a designated A&E district; exemption is at local government discretion.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the income tax subtraction modification, eligible artists file Form 502AE with their Maryland individual income tax return and retain documentation (receipts, books, accounts) proving income qualifies. For the property tax credit, contact the local district manager (found via the Maryland Arts Directory) to learn about the process in a specific district. For the admissions and amusement tax exemption, contact the State Comptroller's Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts Capital Grant program provides Maryland-based nonprofit arts organizations with direct access to state capital funding for projects that enhance or create complete, usable, and accessible arts facilities. Authorized by the Maryland General Assembly in 2021, the program allocates $3,000,000 per year for six fiscal years (FY24–FY29). Eligible projects include expansion, new construction, renovation, or major repairs to a facility or other infrastructure operated by an eligible organization. Projects that prioritize energy-efficient building methods, increase accessibility for people with disabilities, or expand programming capacity are strongly encouraged. Grants range from $50,000 to $500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital project grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000, funded at $3,000,000 per year for six years (FY24–FY29). Grant funds are disbursed in a single payment (100% of the award amount) after the grant agreement is signed by all required parties and the funded project is approved by the State Board of Public Works (BPW). Applicants should expect a minimum of 6 months from notification of grant status to receipt of funds. Past grantees who received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period are ineligible to reapply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that operate a physical property in Maryland (owned or leased), have an annual operating budget under $3,000,000, and either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, or are open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including expansion, new construction, renovation, or major repairs to an arts facility or infrastructure. Projects prioritizing energy efficiency, disability accessibility (including ramps, sensory-friendly spaces, adaptive technology), or expanded programming capacity are strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must be Maryland-based and operate a physical property in Maryland. Lease agreements must show a minimum of five years remaining at the time of application.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned by the applicant
Must have an annual operating budget of less than $3,000,000
Must either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, OR be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Must provide proof of property ownership or a lease agreement showing a minimum of five years remaining at time of application
Units of government are ineligible
Schools, colleges, or universities are ineligible
Fiscally-sponsored organizations are ineligible
Auxiliary nonprofits whose mission is primarily for the benefit and fundraising of otherwise ineligible entities are ineligible
Past grantees who have not completed projects for which Arts Capital funding was awarded (including MSAC staff approval of a final report) are ineligible
Past grantees who have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period are ineligible
Capital improvements to properties owned by schools, school systems, colleges, universities, the Maryland Department of General Services, or the Maryland Stadium Authority are ineligible projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically through MSAC's online grants management system, SmartSimple. Applicants must create a free account or log in at marylandarts.smartsimple.com. Electronic signatures are required. Technical support for SmartSimple is available during regular office hours. A multi-disciplinary statewide grant panel reviews applications and applicants receive electronic notification of award or denial. Grantees must submit a final report upon project completion. First-time applicants are strongly encouraged to contact program staff before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts in Education (AiE) Grant supports arts education programs in Maryland's schools and communities by funding teaching artists on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster. Grants help arts learning activities take place in schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, other government entities, and nonprofit organizations. The program strengthens and promotes lifelong learning in the arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded based on the applicant's request, with a maximum of $6,000 per grant. A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026). Lead Artists may receive awards up to 3% of the overall annual AiE grant budget ($21,000 maximum for FY 2026). Teaching artist organizations may receive awards up to 12% of the annual budget ($84,000 maximum for FY 2026). The total FY 2026 AiE grant budget is $700,000. Grant funds are disbursed directly to the teaching artist or their affiliated organization. Payment may take up to 90 days after award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis between July 2025 and January 2026, with deadlines of September 5, 2025; November 5, 2025; and January 5, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists, ensembles, and arts organizations on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster — spanning disciplines including Poetry, Media Arts, Theater, Music, Dance, Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Storytelling, and Multidisciplinary — who are collaborating with Maryland schools, nonprofit organizations, government entities, libraries, community centers, detention centers, or colleges and universities to deliver arts education programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Arts learning activities led by a teaching artist on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster in partnership with a Maryland school, nonprofit, government entity, or higher education institution. Eligible activities include residencies, visiting performances, workshops, out-of-school-time programming, online programs, professional development, and lecture/demonstrations. Specific expenses must be itemized by category per the program rubric.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Collaborating schools and organizations must be based in Maryland.
requirements_list: The teaching artist must be on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster.

The collaborating school or community site must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in Maryland (including private schools with 501(c)3 status), a unit of government based in Maryland (including public schools), or a college or university in Maryland.
The collaborating school or organization must have operated for one completed and documented fiscal year at the time of application submission with ongoing arts activities.
Applications must specify an artist, ensemble, or organization currently on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster.
Ensembles and organizations must indicate a Lead Artist on the application.
A coordinator affiliated with the collaborating school or organization must be identified in each application.
Prior to application, planning conversations between the site coordinator and artist/organization are required, with commitment to implementation if awarded.
Collaborating schools and organizations may participate in up to two AiE grant applications per fiscal year.
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
Applications are submitted through SmartSimple.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. The teaching artist and collaborating school or organization agree on services, timeline, and fees. 2. The collaborating school or organization identifies a coordinator. 3. The teaching artist (or affiliated organization) starts the application in SmartSimple. The Lead Artist signature is required. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with three deadlines per fiscal year (September, November, January). Applications are reviewed by a statewide panel using the FY 2026 AiE Grant Application Rubric, and notifications are sent the month following each deadline. A Letter of Intent template is available from MSAC.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts in Education (AiE) Teaching Artist Roster
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide roster of Maryland-based teaching artists who have experience providing group or classroom arts instruction and/or performances in educational settings. Artists are selected through a panel review process. Once approved, roster members become eligible to receive funding through the Arts in Education (AiE) Grant program, which covers teaching artist fees for Maryland schools and community groups. Membership on the roster does not guarantee grant funding, which requires a separate application. The roster includes 150+ teaching artists, ensembles, and organizations offering disciplines such as music, theater, dance, visual arts, literary arts, media arts, storytelling, and multidisciplinary offerings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved artists are listed on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster and become eligible for the Arts in Education Grant program, which covers teaching artist fees. Benefits also include connections to a statewide network of professional development organizations, individualized feedback and evaluation sessions, and visibility through MSAC's Arts Directory.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Currently paused; check back for updates in Spring 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based teaching artists (independent artists and organizations) who provide arts education programming in school and community settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roster membership enables eligibility for AiE grants that cover teaching artist fees for workshops, residencies, out-of-school-time programs, visiting performances, lecture/lecture demonstrations, and online programs in school and community settings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months prior to application). Organizations must be incorporated in Maryland or be a Maryland government unit or University System of Maryland member institution.
requirements_list: Independent artists must be Maryland residents for at least six months prior to application and at least 18 years old
Ensembles/collaborative groups must have all members 18 or older, with at least 50% meeting the residency requirement
Applicants must not be enrolled in any matriculated high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program at time of application
Artists must remain Maryland residents while active on the roster and during any AiE Grant-supported activities
Organizations must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)(3), a Maryland unit of government, or a University System of Maryland member institution
Organizations must have at least one completed and documented fiscal year at date of application, with ongoing arts activities
Organizations applying for multiple teaching artists must submit a separate application per artist
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed by a panel using a scoring rubric that evaluates arts discipline experience, lesson plan quality, inspiration statement, diversity/equity/justice commitment, inclusion/accessibility, and a live instruction/performance recording. Applicants are encouraged to schedule a virtual meeting or attend office hours with Arts in Education staff before applying. Application materials must include: information on training/experience and audiences served; examples of arts education programs; answers to questions about inspirations, values, and ability to adapt to different learners; and a sample recording of arts education instruction, performance, or online programs. See Application Guidelines for full details. Note: applications are currently paused.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Percent-for-Art program that commissions new, permanent, site-specific artworks for state-owned buildings. For all new or renovated state buildings, 0.05% of the estimated construction cost is reserved to commission or purchase original artwork. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) manages each commission from artist selection through installation. Artists apply by joining the Maryland Public Artist Roster or responding to open calls (Requests for Qualifications) posted for individual projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Artists receive a contract directly with the state agency responsible for the construction project. The commission budget equals 0.05% of the estimated construction cost for each qualifying state building project. MSAC anticipates initiating commissions for at least six state capital construction projects per year. Artists should expect a two-to-five year commitment from contract signing through artwork installation and dedication.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2025 (2026-2028 roster cycle; next cycle anticipated ~May 2028)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and artist-led teams who are residents of the United States and its territories interested in creating permanent, large-scale public artworks for Maryland state buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation and installation of permanent, site-specific original artworks integrated into the construction or renovation of eligible Maryland state buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide — projects are located at state-owned buildings across Maryland. Artists must be U.S. residents (any state or territory).
requirements_list: Artist must be a resident of the United States or its territories
Artist must be on the Maryland Public Artist Roster or respond to an open Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for a specific project
Selected artists contract directly with the state agency responsible for the building project
Artists must work with the project design team to integrate artwork into the building
Commitment of approximately two to five years depending on project scale and timeline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists apply to join the Maryland Public Artist Roster when it is open for applications. The roster operates on a 3-year cycle: the 2026–2028 roster opened in May 2025 with a deadline of June 30, 2025 (now closed). The next application window is anticipated around May 2028. For individual projects, MSAC may also issue open calls as Requests for Qualifications (RFQ), posted on the program page. An Artist Selection Committee reviews candidates from the Roster and selects artists for each project.

structured_extraction.program_description: The County Arts Development (CAD) Grant supports Maryland's designated county arts agencies with the goals of connecting artists, arts organizations, and audiences statewide; encouraging local arts activity across all disciplines and communities; and providing equitable, transparent arts funding at the local level. The program also offers technical assistance to help county arts agencies with their plans. Eligible agencies apply annually, alternating between On-Year applications (every 3 years, submitting a three-year plan) and Off-Year applications (the intervening 2 years, reporting on changes and financial activity).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based grants are awarded annually to designated county arts agencies, along with technical assistance to support planning. Payment is processed upon execution of the grant agreement and received within 6–8 weeks. Grantees must submit interim and annual reports on use of funds, and a final report at project completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local agencies or nonprofits officially designated by their county or jurisdiction's government as the county's official arts agency or council, covering Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting local arts activity, grant making, and programs that meet constituent needs and MSAC's goals across all disciplines and Maryland's diverse communities, including operations of county arts agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the local agency or nonprofit officially designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council.
On-Year applicants (every 3 years) must submit a three-year plan detailing how the agency will meet constituent needs and MSAC goals.
Off-Year applicants (intervening 2 years) must submit an application detailing changes to the three-year plan, required financial reporting, and any professional development requests.
Grantees must submit interim and annual reports on the use of funds.
Grantees must submit a final report at completion of the funded project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications annually to MSAC. On-Year: Submit a draft three-year plan for review by MSAC staff and a panel; revise based on feedback; submit revised plan for Council approval. Off-Year: Submit an off-year application with changes to the plan, financial reporting, and professional development requests for MSAC staff review. See the Grant Guidelines for detailed information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to strengthen the vitality and sustainability of small arts organizations in Maryland. The grant supports overall operations, covering an organization's arts activities or programming for an entire season or fiscal year. Note: this track permanently closed after December 31, 2025, and general operating support for arts organizations will transition to a revised Grants for Organizations (GFO) program starting in FY 2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards for general operating support. Payment is 100% of award amount, processed upon execution of a grant agreement, with receipt expected in 6-8 weeks (up to 90 days). Applications are reviewed monthly by a panel of statewide public members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small Maryland arts organizations including 501(c)3 nonprofits, units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges/universities/schools that produce or present public arts programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for an organization's arts activities or programming for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland-incorporated organization.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for one year or more and within grant income requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects relevant to the community and available to the public
Must not be enrolled in the Grants for Organizations (GFO) or County Arts Development (CAD) program, or an Arts & Entertainment District (A&E)
Independent artists are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit an application in SmartSimple (application ID must begin with '2026'). Applications submitted by the last day of the month are reviewed by a panel the following month, with notifications sent early the following month. Staff can review a draft application if requested at least 6 weeks before submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Creativity Grants for Projects, administered by the Maryland State Arts Council, strengthen the vitality and sustainability of artists and small organizations and provide opportunities to serve the growing needs of arts projects and collaborations within Maryland communities. The program is part of the broader Creativity Grant Program, which also includes a General Operating Support track for small organizations. The Projects track offers two grant options: a Planning & Development grant to support early-stage research and development for a proposed project, and an Implementation grant to support the execution of a specific arts project, event, or program. Grants range from $1,000 to $4,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 are awarded on a rolling monthly basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026. Applications submitted by the last day of the month are reviewed by a panel the following month, with notifications sent shortly after. Payment of 100% of the award amount is processed upon execution of a grant agreement, with receipt expected within 6-8 weeks (up to 90 days total). An applicant is eligible for only one Creativity Grant per fiscal year. The two grant options are: a Planning & Development grant for early-stage research and development of a proposed arts project, and an Implementation grant for the execution of a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and Maryland-incorporated 501(c)(3) nonprofit arts organizations (in operation one year or more and within grant income requirements), units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges, universities, and schools. Organizations using a Model A fiscal sponsorship are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development for a proposed arts project (Planning & Development grant) or execution of a specific arts project, event, or program (Implementation grant). For Planning & Development grants, funds support the planning and/or development phase including activities, timeline, and community engagement. For Implementation grants, funds support arts activity/event/project planning, promotion, implementation, and evaluation. The broader program also supports general operating costs for small arts organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be an independent artist or Maryland-incorporated organization. Projects/activities must occur within the application time frame. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be an independent artist, OR a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)(3) nonprofit in operation for one year or more and within grant income requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school
Organizations using fiscal sponsorships must operate under a Model A sponsorship arrangement
Identify a specific event, activity, or project to occur within the application time frame
An applicant is only eligible for one Creativity Grant per fiscal year

Organizations that receive funding through general operating programs (Grants for Organizations, County Arts Agencies, Arts & Entertainment Districts, Folklife Network, or Creativity Grant for General Operating) are not eligible for project-based support
Application ID must begin with '2026.' indicating a new FY 2026 application
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects that are available to the public

Planning & Development applications must include: clear explanation of planning/development process with overarching goals, creative process details, and community engagement/impact goals; detailed timeline with specific activities/tasks for planning/development phase with timing/dates tied to fund expenditure; detailed budget for planning/development phase including all expenses and anticipated income beyond MSAC request

Implementation applications must include: detailed project description with logistical specifics; community engagement plan and defined impact on specific geographic area; detailed timeline including planning, promotion, fund expenditure, implementation, and evaluation; clear budget with all projected expenses, other income sources, and MSAC use breakdown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through SmartSimple during the open application period (July 1, 2025 – March 31, 2026). Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed by a statewide panel the following month. Applicants are notified of grant status as soon as possible after the review. If approved, a formal grant agreement form is issued and payment is processed upon execution. Applications are scored using a rubric-based system (max 58 points across 3 categories) covering project description, timeline, and budget. Program Directors Emily Sollenberger and Laura Weiss are available to review draft applications prior to submission. For General Operating Support, see https://www.msac.org/programs/creativity-grants/creativity-grants-general-operating-support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that fund a mentor artist and an apprentice artist to work together for one year. The mentor passes down their knowledge of a living cultural tradition in Maryland to the apprentice. This program supports traditional arts education and is distinct from workforce-focused registered apprenticeships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to mentor-apprentice pairs for a one-year project. Payment is processed upon execution of a grant agreement and received within 6–8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at the end of the funded project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mentor artists and apprentice artists seeking to preserve and transmit living cultural traditions in Maryland. Apprentice artists must be Maryland residents; mentor artists must be U.S. residents and demonstrate vital contributions to a living cultural tradition in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting a one-year mentorship between a master artist and an apprentice to pass down knowledge of a traditional art or living cultural tradition. Project expenses must total at least $5,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Apprentice artists must be Maryland residents. Mentor artists must be U.S. residents or residents of a U.S. territory and demonstrate vital contributions to a living cultural tradition in Maryland. Out-of-state mentor artists are subject to additional requirements.
requirements_list: Mentor artist must be a resident of the United States or a U.S. territory
Mentor artist must demonstrate vital contributions to a particular living cultural tradition in Maryland
Apprentice artist must be a Maryland resident
Apprentice artist must demonstrate prior experience, a basic level of skill, and a commitment to long-term learning in a particular traditional art
If the mentor artist resides out of state, the apprentice must demonstrate that the desired mentor artist skillset is unavailable in Maryland
If the apprentice artist is under 18, a parent or guardian must provide contact information and e-signature acknowledging permission to participate
Project expenses must total at least $5,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application through SmartSimple including: narrative answers describing the cultural history and community practice of the traditional art, biographical information for both artists, a work plan with logistical, financial, and cultural details, and optional supplemental materials (written or audiovisual). Applicants may upload an audio or video recording instead of written narrative responses. See the Grant Guidelines for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Folklife Network grants program funds organizations that serve as regional folklife centers in Maryland. Grantees support activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities. The program grew from recommendations by folklife artists, folklife specialists, and other cultural workers during a 2019 program revision facilitated by the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC). Current grantees are located in Allegany, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Montgomery, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to organizations serving as regional folklife centers. The program provides grants of $85,000. Payment is processed upon execution of the grant agreement and received within 6–8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at the completion of the funded project. See Grant Guidelines for detailed information on amounts and requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations serving as regional folklife centers in Maryland that support traditional arts and living cultural traditions of diverse communities, such as museums, universities, and arts non-profits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; current grantees are located in Allegany, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Montgomery, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Must serve as a regional folklife center
Must support activities that identify, document, support, or present living cultural traditions
Must submit a final report at completion of the funded project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the Grant Guidelines on the MSAC website for detailed application and reporting requirements. Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6–8 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Grants for Artists (GFA) program provides funds to support artists' working or living expenses. The program aims to give artists holistic support — not just project-based funding — in order to strengthen Maryland's creative workforce, which is an important part of the state's economy and culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided directly to individual artists to support working or living expenses. Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual artists living or working in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working or living expenses for artists
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to artists throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the program's detail page at https://www.msac.org/programs/grants-artists/grants-artists for application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Arts Council's Grants for Organizations (GFO) program provides general operating support grants to nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, as well as units of government, that produce or present ongoing arts programming open to the public in Maryland. GFO grants help strengthen and sustain Maryland's arts infrastructure, create audiences, uplift communities, and stimulate economic impact across the state. A tiered funding formula, phased in starting FY2024, groups organizations into five budget tiers and distributes funds more equitably, with smaller organizations receiving a higher percentage of allowable expenses: Tier 1 ($50K–$500K budget) up to 15%; Tier 2 ($500K–$1.5M) up to 10%; Tier 3 ($1.5M–$5M) up to 6%; Tier 4 ($5M–$10M) up to 4.5%; Tier 5 ($10M+) up to 4%. Maximum grant caps phase down over five years: $1.4M (FY24), $1.3M (FY25), $1.2M (FY26), $1.1M (FY27), $1M (FY28). In FY2025, MSAC awarded GFO grants totaling $18,136,157 to 309 organizations. Starting FY2027, MSAC will implement a four-year application cycle. Organizations that did not receive GFO funding in the prior cycle must first submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually to determine eligibility before completing a standard grant application by November 15.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants are awarded based on a tiered funding formula grouped into five budget tiers: Tier 1 ($50K–$500K) up to 15% of allowable expenses; Tier 2 ($500K–$1.5M) up to 10%; Tier 3 ($1.5M–$5M) up to 6%; Tier 4 ($5M–$10M) up to 4.5%; Tier 5 ($10M+) up to 4%. Maximum grant caps phase down over five years: $1.4M (FY24), $1.3M (FY25), $1.2M (FY26), $1.1M (FY27), $1M (FY28). In FY25, MSAC awarded GFO grants totaling $18,136,157 to 309 organizations. New applicants or organizations that did not receive GFO funding in the prior cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually; if found eligible, they complete a standard GFO application by November 15. Grant agreement forms are emailed after July 1 to awardees; funds are distributed in full after the Grant Agreement Form and required reports are submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply form due September 15 annually; full GFO application due November 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and tax-exempt arts organizations (primary mission of producing/presenting arts via public programs/services) and arts programs (primary mission other, but provides ongoing arts programming), as well as units of local government and colleges and universities in Maryland that produce or present ongoing public arts programming. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants or organizations that did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually to determine eligibility. If determined eligible, they complete a standard GFO application by November 15. Applicants must self-classify as either an Arts Organization or an Arts Program per stated definitions in the FY27 GFO Grant Guidelines; applicants may contact the Program Director for classification assistance. All applicants must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov. Applications are evaluated by a panel of diverse experts from across Maryland. structured_extraction.program_description: The Heritage Awards are a sub-program of Maryland Traditions, the Maryland State Arts Council's (MSAC) traditional arts program that identifies, documents, supports, and presents traditional arts through grants to organizations and individuals, festivals and other events, direct outreach to artists, and archival activities. Each year, six Heritage Award winners are selected from nominations in one of three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Each awardee receives a $10,000 grant to use at their discretion. Nominees must be people, places, or traditions located in Maryland that demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts. Awards are not given posthumously, and each person, place, or tradition may receive the award only once. Other sub-programs of Maryland Traditions include Folklife Apprenticeships (funding mentor-apprentice pairs for one year of traditional arts education) and Folklife Network grants (funding regional folklife centers). The program grew from recommendations by folklife artists, folklife specialists, and other cultural workers during a 2019 program revision facilitated by MSAC.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each Heritage Award winner receives a $10,000 grant to use at their discretion. The grant is paid within 6–8 weeks after execution of the grant agreement. Grantees must submit a final report detailing the use of funds at the end of each fiscal year. For the broader Maryland Traditions program, grants are also awarded to organizations serving as regional folklife centers (Folklife Network) and to mentor-apprentice pairs for one-year traditional arts education projects (Folklife Apprenticeship). Folklife Apprenticeship expenses must total at least $5,000. See Grant Guidelines for detailed information on amounts and requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, places, and traditions in Maryland that demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts. Nominators may reside anywhere. Also relevant to organizations supporting community-based folk and traditional arts across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: At the Heritage Award awardee's discretion. For the broader Maryland Traditions program: supporting activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities, including funding regional folklife centers and supporting one-year mentor-apprentice traditional arts education partnerships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Heritage Award nominees must be people, places, or traditions located in Maryland. Nominators may reside anywhere. Current Folklife Network grantees are located in Allegany, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Montgomery, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Wicomico counties.

A completed nomination includes answers to prompts describing the nominee's long-term achievement in the traditional arts and optional supplemental materials. Contact State Folklorist Ryan Koons to have a draft nomination reviewed before submission. See sub-program pages for Folklife Apprenticeships and Folklife Network for specific application details.

The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) uses the roster to promote artistic collaboration between Maryland touring artists and Maryland presenters, with the goal of increasing touring engagements for Maryland professional performing artists.

Roster Artists renew their status once every three years. There are no reporting requirements for Roster Artists.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Listing on the MSAC Touring Roster and Arts Directory to be promoted to Maryland presenters for touring engagements

For groups, all members must be 18+ and at least 50% must be Maryland residents
For groups, the company's primary place of business must be located in Maryland
College and university-based performers must perform regularly off-campus for professional fees
If the company or group has its own nonprofit status, the performing ensemble must meet the eligibility criteria for Performing Companies/Groups

Applicants are notified of Roster status via SmartSimple following review and receive instructions for setting up an Arts Directory profile page.

Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6–8 weeks (100% of award amount). Payment may take up to 90 days for awarded activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Poetry Out Loud is a national arts education program that encourages high school students to study great poetry through recitation competitions. Students participate in local, regional, and state competitions, with winners advancing to national finals. The program helps students build public speaking skills, self-confidence, and knowledge of literary history. In Maryland, the program is administered by the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) in collaboration with Maryland Humanities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students who place 1st, 2nd, or 3rd in regional and state competitions receive monetary prizes. At the national finals, a total of $50,000 in awards and school stipends is awarded annually. Students who advance to regional and state competitions also have the opportunity to work with a Poetry Coach prior to competitions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Schools and organizations must host local competitions by Friday, January 16, 2026. Regional competitions take place in February 2026; state finals on March 7, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monetary prizes for students placing 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in regional and state competitions; school stipends at the national level.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; regional competitions held in Baltimore-central, west-central, and south-central regions.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Students select three poems from the Poetry Out Loud Anthology to recite
Local competitions must be hosted by January 16, 2026
Students not participating in a local competition may register directly for a regional competition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools or community organizations host local competitions. Winners advance to regional competitions (February 2026), then to the state finals (March 7, 2026). Independent or homeschooled students may register directly for regional competitions. Top regional finalists compete at the state level.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland (PAAM) Conservation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Art Across Maryland (PAAM) Conservation Grant supports organizations in conserving and preserving existing public artworks in Maryland. The program offers two tracks: a Conservation Planning Grant ($10,000) for planning efforts such as collection inventories, digitization, community outreach, and assessments; and a Conservation Implementation Grant (up to $30,000) for carrying out fully developed conservation or relocation projects on permanent public artworks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant types are available: (1) Conservation Planning Grant awards a fixed $10,000 to support conservation planning activities including administration, consultant fees, community engagement, and collection management technology. (2) Conservation Implementation Grant awards up to $30,000 to fund the execution of a fully developed conservation project on permanent public artwork, including relocation, cleaning, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting, and interpretive signage. Applicants may submit only one PAAM grant application per fiscal year. Grant funds may not exceed 10% of the grant request for organization administration/indirect costs.

Conservation Implementation: artwork relocation, cleaning and maintenance, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting and electrical work, interpretive signage, and project management (up to 10% of grant request).

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland (PAAM) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Art Across Maryland (PAAM) Grant Program, administered by the Maryland State Arts Council, supports artists and organizations in planning, creating, installing, and conserving public artworks across Maryland. The program promotes the inclusion of art in everyday experiences for Marylanders and offers four grant tracks across two categories: (1) New Artworks Planning Grants (up to $10,000) for independent artists or organizations developing public art proposals with communities; (2) New Artworks Project Grants (up to $30,000) for organizations to fabricate and install new public artworks developed through a community engagement process; (3) Conservation Planning Grants (fixed $10,000) for organizations to plan conservation efforts including collection inventories, digitization, community outreach, and assessments; and (4) Conservation Implementation Grants (up to $30,000) for organizations to carry out fully developed conservation or relocation projects on permanent public artworks. Public art is defined as artwork that is free, intentionally created for, and accessible to the public, in any media, indoors or outdoors, temporary or permanent. Applicants may submit only one PAAM grant application per fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Four grant tracks are available under two categories: New Artworks and Conservation. (1) New Artworks Planning Grant: up to $10,000 for independent artists or organizations to develop public art proposals with communities. (2) New Artworks Project Grant: up to $30,000 for organizations to fabricate and install new public artwork developed through a community engagement process. (3) Conservation Planning Grant: fixed $10,000 for planning activities including administration, consultant fees, community engagement, and collection management technology. (4) Conservation Implementation Grant: up to $30,000 for executing a fully developed conservation project on permanent public artwork, including relocation, cleaning, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting, and interpretive signage. Organization administration/indirect costs may not exceed 10% of the grant request. Applicants may submit only one PAAM grant application per fiscal year. Organizations that received a Project Grant in the prior fiscal year are not eligible to apply for a Project Grant the following year. Technical assistance, professional development resources, and information on how to apply are also available through the broader PAAM program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New Artworks Planning Grants: community outreach, artist fees and honorariums for proposal design, consultant fees, facility/equipment rentals, online application software fees, and artwork proposal design and development. New Artworks Project Grants: artist fees, contracted services (fabricators, installers, photographers), equipment/space rentals, artwork materials and tools, plaque/interpretive signage, transportation, insurance, permitting fees, organization administration/project management (up to 10% of grant request), and artwork dedication expenses. Conservation Planning Grants: project administration, professional conservator and consultant fees, community engagement activities, collection management software and services. Conservation Implementation Grants: artwork relocation, cleaning and maintenance, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting and electrical work, interpretive signage, and project management (up to 10% of grant request).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Art Across Maryland Program promotes and supports the inclusion of art in everyday experiences for Marylanders. Public art can be any kind of work in any media, indoors or outdoors, temporary or permanent, that is free, accessible, and engages the community.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Arts and Entertainment (A&E) Districts program designates unique community destinations that promote arts, tourism, and revitalization through tax incentives. Garrett County has two A&E Districts — one in Grantsville (established July 2015) and one in Oakland (established July 2017) — that attract artists, arts organizations, and creative enterprises through income tax, admissions tax, and property tax benefits.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives reduce income tax, admissions and amusement tax, and property tax obligations for eligible artists and arts-related businesses operating within designated A&E District boundaries.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program, administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), provides property tax relief to homeowners with limited income by limiting the amount of property taxes a homeowner must pay based on their gross household income. Originally created in 1975 for the elderly, the program is now available to homeowners of all ages. If a homeowner's property tax bill exceeds a fixed percentage of their gross household income, the state issues a credit for the difference. The credit applies to taxes on the first $300,000 of assessed value. Credits are displayed on tax bills and reduce the amount due; if issued after payment, a refund is automatically made by the county finance office. Homeowners must apply each year and disclose their income to receive the credit. The credit is calculated as: 0% of the first $8,000 of income; 4% of the next $4,000; 6.5% of the next $4,000; and 9% of all income above $16,000. In 2022, more than 37,000 homeowners received an average of $1,501 in relief. Many counties, including Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Charles County, Cecil County, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington, also provide supplemental credits automatically to approved applicants. Disabled veterans and surviving spouses may also qualify for a Veterans Tax Credit. The 2026 application (Form HTC-1 Long Form) is currently available.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit is applied against the homeowner's property tax bill for the amount by which property taxes exceed a percentage of gross household income, calculated as: 0% of the first $8,000 of income; 4% of the next $4,000; 6.5% of the next $4,000; and 9% of all income above $16,000. The credit applies only to taxes on the first $300,000 of assessed valuation. Eligibility requires a maximum combined gross household income of $60,000 for calendar year 2025 and net worth under $200,000 as of December 31, 2025 (excluding the subject property and qualified retirement savings/IRAs). Homeowners who apply by April 15, 2026 receive the credit directly on their initial July 1, 2026 tax bill; those who apply by October 1, 2026 receive a revised tax bill or refund check from their county finance office. Many counties, including Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Charles County, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington, also provide supplemental credits automatically to approved applicants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Exemptions for Veterans, Military Families, and Other Qualifying Individuals and Organizations (Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers real property tax exemptions for qualifying individuals and organizations through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. A primary focus is on veterans, active-duty service members, and surviving spouses. Veterans must have a disability the VA has determined is 100% service-connected, permanently and totally disabling (or be rated permanently unemployable by the VA at less than 100%). Disabled active-duty service members with a service-connected physical disability reasonably certain to continue for life (not caused by misconduct) may also qualify; annual recertification of active-duty status is required. Surviving spouses of 100% disabled veterans or military personnel killed in the line of duty may receive a full exemption on their principal residence; for subsequently acquired dwellings, the exemption amount equals that allowed on the prior dwelling; remarriage forfeits the exemption, but an annulment voiding the subsequent marriage allows reinstatement. Prior-year refunds may be available going back to the 2018–2019 tax year within a 3-year window from the calendar year the veteran, service member, or surviving spouse first became eligible. Blind persons (and surviving spouses of blind persons who have not remarried) may receive a $40,000 reduction in assessed value on their principal residence; the exemption is prorated for any remaining portion of the tax year when first applied for. Charitable, religious, fraternal, benevolent, and educational organizations may receive full exemptions on qualifying properties owned and actually and exclusively used for exempt purposes, with an application deadline of September 1; property under construction may qualify once a building permit has been issued and construction makes continual progress; vacant land generally does not qualify. Government-owned property holders and residents requiring medically necessary home improvements also qualify under applicable exemption categories; the medical improvement exemption excludes up to 10% of total market value for qualifying improvements. Veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time and do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline applicable to organizational exemptions. Charles County residents may also contact the local SDAT office at 301-932-2440 for further information.

The blind exemption provides a $40,000 reduction in assessed value on the principal residence; prorated for any remaining portion of the tax year when first applied for; a surviving spouse of a blind person who has not remarried may continue to receive the exemption. Disabled active-duty service members may receive a full exemption on their principal residence; annual recertification of active-duty status is required; prior-year refunds may be available starting with the 2018–2019 tax year within a 3-year window. Surviving spouses of disabled veterans or military casualties may receive an exemption on their principal residence; for subsequently acquired dwellings, the exemption amount equals the exemption allowed on the prior dwelling; refunds of previously paid taxes may be available starting with the 2018–2019 tax year within a 3-year window; remarriage forfeits the exemption, but an annulment voiding the subsequent marriage allows reinstatement. For the surviving spouse of a military casualty, complete the Application for Exemption for Surviving Spouses of Active Military Personnel Who Died in the Line of Duty along with VA certification of cause of death and submit to the local county assessment office. For the blind exemption, complete the Blind Persons Exemption Application including physician or optometrist certification of permanent blindness (confirming visual acuity standards met and effective date) and submit to the local county assessment office; surviving spouses of blind persons should complete the Surviving Spouse of Blind Persons Exemption Application with proof of Maryland residency and declaration that property is principal residence and not rented to others. For fraternal, benevolent, or educational property exemptions, complete the appropriate form with Articles of Incorporation and bylaws and file by September 1; property must be in use or under active construction for exempt purpose prior to July 1. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Homestead Property Tax Credit Program limits the annual increase in taxable assessments on a homeowner's principal residence to a fixed percentage, protecting homeowners from large property assessment-driven tax increases. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to limit taxable assessment increases to 10% or less each year. The State of Maryland caps its annual taxable assessment increase at 10%. Individual counties and municipalities may set their own lower caps: Baltimore County caps increases at 4% per year, Washington County at 5% per year, Howard County caps the county portion at 5% per year, Montgomery County uses a 10% cap (with the Town of Kensington using 5%), and other municipalities may also set their own caps. The credit is calculated on any assessment increase above that cap, so the homeowner pays no property tax on the portion of the market value increase above the limit. For example, if the assessment rises from $100,000 to $120,000 and the cap is 10% ($110,000), the credit covers the taxes on the $10,000 difference. The credit is not applicable in the first year after purchase of a new home. The credit reduces state, county, and municipal property tax liability and is administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). All homeowners must submit a one-time Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application to establish eligibility (required by 2007 law), ensuring the credit applies only to a homeowner's primary residence. Once approved, the credit appears on property tax bills automatically when assessments rise for all properties designated as 'Principal Residence.'
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that caps the annual increase in taxable property assessments on a principal residence to a fixed percentage (no more than 10% per year for each local government). The credit equals the tax owed on any assessment increase above the applicable cap. State of Maryland cap: 10% per year. Baltimore County cap: 4% per year. Washington County cap: 5% per year. Howard County cap: 5% per year (county portion), 10% (state portion). Montgomery County cap: 10% (Town of Kensington: 5%). Municipalities may also set their own lower caps. The credit is not applicable in the first year following purchase of a new home. A one-time Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application must be filed with SDAT. Once approved, the credit is applied automatically to property tax bills when assessments increase, reducing state, county, and municipal property tax liability. The credit is no longer automatically calculated — application is required. Applies regardless of property value or income level.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: One-time application required; no stated deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners (living persons on deed) who occupy or plan to occupy property as their principal residence, seeking protection from large increases in property tax liability. Includes owner-occupants throughout Maryland whose property is designated as 'Principal Residence' and who have lived in the property for at least six months of the year, including July 1 of the credit year. Married couples are limited to one principal residence. Includes residents in Baltimore County, Howard County, Washington County, Montgomery County, and all other Maryland counties and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Limits the annual increase in taxable property assessment, reducing state, county, and municipal property tax liability for qualifying homeowners. Specifically reduces the property tax owed on the portion of an assessed value increase that exceeds the annual cap (10% statewide, or a lower local cap such as 4% in Baltimore County, 5% in Washington County, 5% in Howard County for the county portion, and 5% in the Town of Kensington in Montgomery County).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to limit taxable assessment increases to 10% or less per year. Each county and municipality may set its own lower cap rate (e.g., Baltimore County at 4%, Washington County at 5%, Howard County at 5% for the county portion, Montgomery County at 10% with Town of Kensington at 5%). Available to homeowners throughout Maryland whose property is owner-occupied and designated as a principal residence.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a one-time application. Apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov — recommended) or at https://sdathtc.dat.maryland.gov/sign_in (browse by State Agencies, select Department of Assessments & Taxation, then 'Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application'). Alternatively, download the paper application (https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/Homestead_application.pdf), complete it, and mail or fax it to the Homestead Tax Credit Division. Application requires property ID, homeowner/spouse SSN, and residency verification cross-check against income tax and motor vehicle records. Homeowners can check whether they have already filed by looking up their property in the SDAT Real Property database before applying. In-person service appointments are also available at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202. Once approved, the credit is automatically applied to the property tax bill when assessments increase. If you believe you are eligible but did not receive the credit, contact the Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation at 410-767-2165 (toll-free 1-866-650-8783) or sdat.homestead@maryland.gov. For questions about eligibility or calculations in Baltimore County, contact SDAT's Credit Office at 410-512-4900 or the Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance at 410-887-2404 (financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov); additional information at https://www.baltimorecountymd.gov/departments/budfin/taxpayer-services/tax-credits/homestead. Washington County residents may contact 301-791-3050 or visit www.washco-md.net/treasurers-office/tax-credit-information. Montgomery County residents may also contact the SDAT Rockville office at (240) 314-4510. Howard County information is available at https://www.howardcountymd.gov/resource/all-tax-credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) helps limited-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners navigate the tax sale process. It removes eligible homeowners from the tax sale process for at least three years, connects them with resources and support, and provides short-term loans and individualized assistance to help homeowners resolve delinquent property taxes and avoid losing their homes through tax sale foreclosure. Eligible homeowners must have a primary residence assessed at no more than $300,000 and combined household income no more than $60,000 annually, with total non-dwelling assets not exceeding $200,000. The program also accepts voluntary donations through an online portal to support at-risk homeowners.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) / Office of the State Tax Sale Ombudsman
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Keeps eligible low-income homeowners out of tax sale for at least three years and may assist them in paying overdue property taxes to prevent foreclosure. Provides short-term loans and individualized assistance to help homeowners pay off delinquent property taxes and avoid tax sale foreclosure. Qualifying homeowners must have a primary residence with a current assessed value no more than $300,000 and combined household income no more than $60,000 annually, with total non-dwelling assets not exceeding $200,000. The program also accepts voluntary donations through an online portal to support at-risk homeowners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income, elderly, and disabled Maryland homeowners facing tax sale due to delinquent or overdue property taxes, with a primary residence assessed at no more than $300,000 and combined household income no more than $60,000 annually.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preventing a home from being placed in tax sale, assisting with payment of delinquent or overdue property taxes to prevent foreclosure, and connecting homeowners with housing support resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties and Baltimore City, including Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner with delinquent property taxes
Must meet limited income, elderly, or disabled eligibility criteria
Home must be in tax sale or at risk of tax sale
Dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence
Property's current assessed value cannot exceed $300,000
Combined household income must be no more than $60,000 annually
Total value of assets (excluding the dwelling) must not exceed $200,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the OneStop Maryland portal (recommended for faster processing) at https://onestop.md.gov/forms/state-tax-sale-ombudsman-homeowner-protection-program-63dacc5b81fbf9019f6185d3. Alternatively, contact the State Tax Sale Ombudsman by phone at (410) 767-4994 or toll-free at (833) 732-8411, or by email at sdat.taxsale@maryland.gov. In-person appointments are available at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202. More information is also available at dat.maryland.gov/taxsale.

structured_extraction.program_name: 2022 Equipment Assistance Grants for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) Operator
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) operators to purchase equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new, renovated, or replacement equipment. Individual items must have a value greater than $1,000. Priority is given to high-needs schools where 50% or more of enrolled students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, and to schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant. Phase 1 ran October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024; Phase 2 (reallocation) ran July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds totaling $954,126 (2022 cycle) for purchasing food service equipment with a per-item threshold greater than $1,000. Costs incurred before grant approval are not eligible for reimbursement. Awards made within 30 days of deadline; Notices of Grant Awards (NOGAs) follow notification. Phase 1 ran October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024; Phase 2 (reallocation) ran July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, February 1, 2023, no later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: National School Lunch Program (NSLP) operators, including schools and school districts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new, renovated, or replacement food service equipment to serve healthier meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Each item must cost more than $1,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to NSLP operators.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the MSDE Grant Recipient Assurances form. Access the Budget Template through the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS) or by contacting Sara Brandt. Submit application via MSDE Grants webpage by February 1, 2023. Awards made within 30 days of deadline; NOGAs follow notification. Refer to the Grant Information Guide for instructions, timelines, and submission requirements. Optional virtual customer service support sessions were held January 9 and January 18, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) grant program funds community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and additional services to complement their regular academic program. Centers must offer families of participating students literacy instruction and related educational development programs. The program targets students and families who attend Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Grantees also receive technical assistance through bi-monthly networking meetings organized by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive reimbursement grants provided to eligible organizations to establish and operate community learning centers. Total funding is approximately $22.6 million (FY25), with 93% allocated to out-of-school time programs. Subgrantees incur costs and invoice MSDE for reimbursement (typically 6–8 weeks processing). Grants are awarded for three-year periods; subsequent award years are contingent upon satisfactory performance and funding availability. Matching contributions are required (Year I: 10% in-kind; Year II: 15%; Year III: 20%). Grantees also receive technical assistance through bi-monthly networking meetings, including peer-to-peer support and resources from MSDE staff. Renewal applications are available for existing cohorts (FY2024 Cohort Year 3 and FY2025 Cohort Year 2).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, non-profit organizations, faith-based organizations, city or county government agencies, institutions of higher education, for-profit corporations, and consortiums of two or more such organizations that serve students and families attending Title I schools or schools with a high percentage of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment programs for students (reading, math, college/career readiness), family literacy instruction and educational development programs, behavioral health supports, service-learning, and other services that complement students' regular academic programs during school year and summer programming.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Participants must serve students and families who primarily attend schools eligible for Title I school-wide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families.
requirements_list: Must serve students and families who primarily attend Title I eligible schools or schools with a high percentage of low-income students
Must offer family literacy instruction and related educational development programs
Eligible applicants include local education agencies, non-profits, faith-based organizations, government agencies, higher education institutions, for-profit corporations, and consortiums
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings
Minimum 12 hours/week programming for 25 weeks (school year) OR 4 hours Saturdays only for 25 weeks; at least 4 hours academic per week
Summer-only alternative: at least 80 hours total programming
Dollar-for-dollar matching contributions required (Year I: 10% in-kind; Year II: 15%; Year III: 20%)
Finance agent/bookkeeper position required in budget
External evaluator cost capped at 7% of total requested funds
External evaluator required; annual and final summative evaluation reports required
Each grantee must undergo a periodic evaluation to assess progress toward providing high-quality academic enrichment opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a renewal grant application electronically via Qualtrics by the deadline. Two virtual customer service support sessions are available to assist applicants (August 7 and August 12, 2025). Separate application forms are available for each cohort (FY2024 Cohort Year 3 and FY2025 Cohort Year 2). Award notifications are issued via email no later than September 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Adult High School Pilot Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program that funds the two state-approved adult high school pilot programs in Maryland, authorized by House Bill 1381. The pilots are South Baltimore Adult High School (operated by Elev8 Baltimore in partnership with Baltimore City Community College) and The Excel Center (operated by Goodwill Industries of the Chesapeake).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided on a fiscal-year basis to approved adult high school pilot programs. The most recent grant cycle referenced is State Fiscal Year (SFY) 2025.
