structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating adult high school pilot programs for adult learners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide — currently limited to the two state-approved pilot schools
requirements_list: Must be an approved adult high school pilot program authorized under Maryland House Bill 1381
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the SFY 2025 grant page for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Afterschool Meals Program provides financial reimbursement to schools and organizations that serve snacks and/or suppers to children in afterschool programs. It can be administered through the USDA National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP). To participate, programs must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement is provided to eligible programs for snacks and/or suppers served to children in afterschool care. Reimbursement rates are set by the USDA and vary by program type (NSLP or CACFP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, school-based programs, non-profit organizations, and non-school-based organizations that operate afterschool care programs serving children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of snacks and/or suppers served to children during afterschool programs that include educational or enrichment activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

CACFP track is open to school-based, non-profit, and non-school-based organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland State Department of Education School and Community Nutrition division to enroll. Additional information is available on the USDA Afterschool website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registered apprenticeship program offering high school students (ages 16+, starting junior year) paid, credential-aligned career-connected learning opportunities. Students complete at least 450 hours of paid on-the-job training and at least one year of related classroom instruction, approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and delivered in partnership with local school districts. Adult apprentice programs may also help with college tuition. Piloted in Frederick and Washington Counties, the program is now available to all school systems statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive paid on-the-job training (at least 450 hours, minimum wage or higher) plus at least one year of related classroom instruction, culminating in a state skill certificate. Adult apprentice programs may include assistance with college tuition. A $12.2 million Maryland Works grant was used to expand youth apprenticeship opportunities across the state. Employers must pay minimum wage or higher, provide safety instruction, assign mentors, and comply with youth apprenticeship agreements and child labor laws.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training for students; related classroom instruction; state skill certificate attainment; may assist with college tuition for adult apprentices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local school districts. Originally piloted in Frederick and Washington Counties; now available to all school systems for adoption.

Employers should partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to register positions, identify required skills, assign mentors, and host student apprentices.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to help eligible low-income students attend participating nonpublic (private) schools in Maryland. Students must qualify for free or reduced-price meals (FARMs) and be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for grades K–12. Award amounts vary based on household income, student grade level, special education status (IEP/IFSP/504 plan), and financial assistance provided by the school. The scholarship check is sent directly to the school. Approximately $9 million is available for an estimated ~2,500 awards; the prior year funded ~2,800 students across 19 Maryland jurisdictions. Awards cannot be transferred to another student, and a prorated refund is required if the student withdraws before April 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards sent directly to the participating nonpublic school on behalf of the student. Award amounts depend on household income, student grade level, special education status (IEP/IFSP/504 plan), and school financial assistance. Approximately $9 million available for an estimated ~2,500 awards; prior year funded ~2,800 students across 19 Maryland jurisdictions. The award may not exceed the net tuition owed to the school. Scholarship checks are issued between September and December 11, 2026. Awards cannot be transferred to another student, and a prorated refund is required if the student withdraws before April 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland students in grades K–12 who qualify for free or reduced-price meals (FARMs) and are enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year; families at or below the federal poverty threshold
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at a participating nonpublic school in Maryland for the 2026-2027 school year. The BOOST Scholarship award must be deposited by the participating nonpublic school and applied to the student's tuition account. Funds may not be used for transportation or meals, and may not be carried over to another school year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; student must attend a participating nonpublic school registered in Maryland. Schools across all 23 Maryland counties are represented in the participating school list.

The parent/guardian application window for the 2026-2027 school year was open from March 9 to May 8, 2026 (now closed). Nonpublic school applications closed March 6, 2026. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and priority. Applicants will be notified by August 2026 of their award status, with award offers made from summer through December 11, 2026. MSDE offers virtual customer service support sessions to help with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) pays licensed child care providers in advance for child care scholarship services, based on enrollment rather than attendance. Payments are issued twice monthly — on the 15th and 30th — covering the two service periods of each month. A True-Up reconciliation process adjusts payments one month later to account for any children added or removed after the advance payment was calculated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE issues advance, enrollment-based payments to child care providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program. Payments are split into two disbursements per month: one on the 15th for services provided the 1st–14th, and one on the 30th for services provided the 15th through end of month. Payment amounts are based on enrolled scholarship children, including payment for absences up to 60 days per calendar year. A True-Up process one month later reconciles any adjustments for additions, early scholarship endings, or provider ineligibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed and regulated child care providers participating in the Maryland Child Care Scholarship program, as well as informal child care providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care provider reimbursement for child care services provided to children with Child Care Scholarships

Advance payments are calculated automatically based on enrollment data. Families apply for scholarships online at family.childcareportals.org. Providers or families with questions may contact CCS Central 2 at 1-877-227-0125 or submit inquiries via the escalation inbox at [email protected]. Customers may submit requests via Google Forms (separate forms for parents and providers); the vendor has 3 business days to resolve issues, with escalation to MSDE available thereafter; MSDE commits to 3-business-day response windows.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) reimburses child and adult care agencies with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. The program provides nutritionally balanced meals to young children enrolled at childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, and emergency shelters, as well as to older adults and people with chronic disabilities enrolled in adult day care facilities. Funds are used to offset meal and supplement costs to public, private nonprofit, or proprietary centers licensed to provide non-residential childcare services for daycare homes, eligible centers, and non-residential eligible adult daycare centers. Child care centers that participate can receive reimbursement for food costs to help ensure young children are well fed and ready for kindergarten. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture and administered in Maryland by MSDE's School and Community Nutrition Programs Branch.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating child and adult care agencies receive cash reimbursements for meals and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Sponsors also receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their meal reimbursements. Emergency shelters receive the highest reimbursement rates with the least paperwork of any facility type in the program. Child care centers serving low-income families receive reimbursement for food costs incurred. Annual maximum reimbursement is available for child/adult care centers serving 25 free-eligible participants (breakfast, lunch, snack, 5 days/week) and for family child care homes serving 6 Tier I participants (breakfast, lunch, snack, 5 days/week). Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities serving children, older adults (60+), adults with disabilities or chronic conditions, and low-income families in Maryland. Includes public, private non-profit, and for-profit licensed providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for meals and snacks served to enrolled participants that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns, including reimbursement for food costs at participating child care centers, helping offset meal and supplement costs for licensed care providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Family child care providers participate through sponsoring organizations serving specific counties, including Cecil County Government, Frederick County Community Action Agency, Montgomery County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, and The Planning Council.
requirements_list: Meals and snacks must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Participating sites include childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities
Adult participants must be over age 60 or living with a disability
Family child care providers must join through a sponsoring organization
Emergency shelters must serve children 18 years and younger
Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services
Must be a licensed child care center (for child care center participants)
Must serve low-income families (for child care center participants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Six-step process: (1) Call MSDE at 410-767-0199; (2) Complete a survey and budget worksheet; (3) Eligibility determination; (4) Complete CACFP Basics Training and online application; (5) Pre-approval visit; (6) Approval and reimbursement eligibility. Family child care providers should contact a sponsoring agency in their county to get started. Child care centers may also contact MSDE's School and Community Nutrition Programs Branch to learn about participation requirements. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS). A CACFP flyer is available to download for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) allows schools and school districts in low-income areas to serve free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students without collecting household income applications. Schools with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher — meaning at least 25% of students are directly certified for free meals through programs like SNAP or TANF — are eligible to elect CEP.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating schools and districts receive reimbursements to provide free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students at no cost, without requiring household income applications. The subsidy eliminates unpaid meal debt and reduces administrative costs for districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools and school districts in low-income areas of Maryland with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students, regardless of income, without collecting household income applications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for eligible schools and school districts.
requirements_list: School or school district must have an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
Identified students are those directly certified for free meals through programs such as SNAP and TANF
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible schools and school districts elect to participate in CEP. Visit the USDA CEP Resource Center or the Maryland State Department of Education for guidance on participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Early Literacy Coaching Network (ELCN) is a Maryland State Department of Education initiative that strengthens K–3 literacy instruction through aligned, job-embedded coaching. It brings early literacy coaches together to deepen their understanding of the Maryland Coaching Model and MSDE-developed tools that support evidence-based reading instruction. The network offers regional in-person convenings, virtual Communities of Practice, and opportunities to earn Professional Development Points (PDPs) toward Maryland Educator License renewal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn 1 Professional Development Point (PDP) for every clock hour spent in professional learning sessions. Sessions include in-person regional convenings (6-hour sessions) and virtual synchronous Communities of Practice (3-hour sessions). Invitations are sent to current network participants; information on the next cohort will be announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland elementary early literacy coaches working in K–3 settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development toward Maryland Educator License renewal; structured learning to apply MSDE literacy coaching tools, deepen understanding of evidence-based reading instruction, and engage in collaborative practice with peers statewide
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland elementary literacy coaches
requirements_list: Must be an early literacy coach working in Maryland elementary schools
Participation is by invitation to current network participants
Future cohort information to be announced
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Invitations are sent to current network participants. Prospective participants should stay tuned for information on the next cohort.

structured_extraction.program_description: MSDE invites local school systems (LEAs) to identify schools to support talent development initiatives that increase the participation of underserved student groups in gifted and advanced programming.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total funding available is $100,000. Awards of up to $10,000 per school. LEAs can develop plans for up to three participating schools and receive up to $30,000. MSDE anticipates awarding grants to at least ten schools. Awards are contingent on availability of funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, December 13, 2024, no later than 5:00 pm EST

MSDE reserves the right to take into consideration geographic distribution when making awards.

The GIG was released on September 13, 2024. MSDE held three customer service support sessions via video call to help applicants understand requirements and complete the application. MSDE staff were available to provide technical assistance throughout the process. Award notifications were issued January 24, 2025. The grant period runs July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enhanced Child Care Support and Teacher Retention Award (ECSTRA) Retention Bonus Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The ECSTRA program provides retention bonuses to early childhood educators in Maryland using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds. Educators who apply, meet eligibility criteria, and participate in a lottery to determine bonus size receive payments in two installments: one after remaining employed in the same program in an eligible role for at least 5 months, and a second after at least 8 months. The program aims to stabilize the child care workforce by supplementing wages and reducing turnover.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retention bonuses paid in two installments to eligible early childhood educators. Bonus amounts are determined by lottery. The first half is paid after at least 5 months of continued employment in the same program in an eligible role; the second half after at least 8 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood educators employed in eligible child care roles in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retention bonuses paid directly to early childhood educators who remain employed in the same program in an eligible role
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to early educators working in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland early educator in an eligible child care role
Must apply by the application deadline (October 3, 2023)
Must agree to participate in a lottery to determine bonus size
Must remain employed in the same program in an eligible role for at least 5 months to receive the first bonus installment
Must remain employed in the same program in an eligible role for at least 8 months to receive the second bonus installment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individual early educators apply directly through the program, provide up-to-date and accurate employment status information to MSDE, and agree to participate in a lottery. Applicants are notified in October 2023 whether they are selected for the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free fresh fruits and vegetables to children at eligible Maryland elementary schools and residential child care institutions during the school day. The program also promotes nutrition education about the fruits and vegetables served, aiming to introduce children to new varieties of fresh produce and increase overall consumption of fresh, unprocessed produce among young children. Funding is provided to eligible schools and residential child care institutions to encourage children to eat more fresh fruits and vegetables. In School Year 2022–2023, 196 Maryland schools participated in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible elementary schools and residential child care institutions receive direct funding to purchase and provide free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day. In School Year 2022–2023, 196 Maryland schools participated in the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland elementary schools and residential child care institutions seeking to provide free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day; nutrition education about the produce served.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible elementary schools and residential child care institutions throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an elementary school or residential child care institution in Maryland
School must be eligible to participate based on USDA criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted annually. See the USDA Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program Fact Sheet for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Hunger Free Kid's Act Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to eligible schools and residential child care institutions. The money helps them comply with meal pattern rules established by the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct payments for specific uses to help schools and child care institutions comply with federal meal pattern rules.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help schools and child care centers meet the meal pattern requirements of the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.

structured_extraction.program_name: MSDE Science of Reading Microcredential Courses
structured_extraction.program_description: Free professional development courses for Maryland educators on Science of Reading instructional methods. Funded through a $6.85 million philanthropic partnership with the Ibis Group, the initiative offers five online and in-person courses covering topics such as Science of Reading Fundamentals, Literacy Leadership, reading for English Learners, and Demystifying Dyslexia. Completing the SUNY microcredential course fulfills Maryland's reading proficiency requirement for teacher license renewal in key subject areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five free professional development courses offered at no cost to Maryland educators, available in online and in-person formats. Courses range from a 35-hour introductory SUNY New Paltz Science of Reading Fundamentals Microcredential to shorter AIM Institute courses (10-hour and 3-hour options), as well as courses for secondary educators and school/district leaders. Funded by a $6.85 million philanthropic partnership with the Ibis Group.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public school educators including paraeducators, teachers, specialists, and school and district leaders at all levels of Science of Reading knowledge
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning coursework in Science of Reading instructional methods; completing the SUNY microcredential fulfills Maryland's reading proficiency requirement for teacher license renewal
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to educators in Maryland public schools statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland public school educator (paraeducator, teacher, specialist, or school/district leader)
Specific courses are targeted to different levels of prior Science of Reading knowledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Educators select the course that matches their role and knowledge level, then access the course through either the AIM Institute or SUNY New Paltz websites linked on the page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Accreditation allows licensed child care centers and public prekindergarten programs to demonstrate their commitment to high-quality early learning. Programs complete a self-appraisal process, develop a program improvement plan, and receive a validation visit. Accreditation is awarded for 5 years and unlocks higher Maryland EXCELS quality rating and payment levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accredited programs gain eligibility for Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating 5, higher Maryland EXCELS subsidy payments, and access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials. Optional virtual or onsite technical assistance is available during the accreditation process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public prekindergarten programs in Maryland (Family Child Care programs are not currently eligible).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation Support Funds may be used to purchase instructional materials. Higher EXCELS payments support ongoing program quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed child care centers and public prekindergarten programs.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or public prekindergarten program
Family Child Care programs are not eligible
Must complete a Self-Appraisal including input from staff and enrolled families
Must develop a Program Improvement Plan based on identified areas for improvement
Must complete a Final Self-Appraisal to review improvements
Must undergo a Validation Visit with observation and feedback
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs use Maryland Accreditation Standards to complete a Self-Appraisal, develop a Program Improvement Plan, complete a Final Self-Appraisal, and receive a Validation Visit. Optional technical assistance (virtual or onsite) is available throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS, the state's Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS). Programs earn bonuses when they publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5. Bonuses range from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type (child care center, family child care, or large family home), quality rating level (1–5), and, for centers, licensed capacity. No application is required — eligible programs automatically receive payment by check or direct deposit within approximately 60 days of publishing a qualifying rating. Funding comes from the Blueprint for Maryland's Future legislation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flat bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 per qualifying event, paid by check or direct deposit within approximately 60 days. Bonus amounts vary by program type, quality rating level, and (for child care centers) licensed capacity. A program can receive multiple bonuses if it meets eligibility criteria multiple times within the active bonus cycle (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027). The bonus may be spent at the program's discretion. Examples include salary increases, hiring staff, purchasing high-quality learning materials, furniture replacement, nap mats, bikes for children, and accreditation preparation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs (child care centers, family child care providers, and large family homes) participating in Maryland EXCELS that publish or re-publish qualifying quality ratings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spent at the program's discretion. Examples include salary increases, hiring staff, purchasing high-quality learning materials, furniture replacement, nap mats, bikes for children, and accreditation preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS. Quality Assurance Specialists are assigned across all Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Washington, and the Eastern Shore region.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must publish a quality rating for the first time OR re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations, including participation in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required. Eligible programs automatically receive payment by check or direct deposit within approximately 60 days of publishing a qualifying quality rating. Payment status can be checked on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website after registering. Programs can contact their assigned county/regional Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance; specialist assignments are available at marylandexcels.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training program that is a mandatory step in the Maryland EXCELS Mentoring Pilot. Participants who successfully complete the training earn 2 COK (Core of Knowledge) hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Self-paced online Introduction to Mentoring training that awards 2 COK (Core of Knowledge) hours upon successful completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and mentors participating in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating and improvement system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completing mandatory mentoring training to earn COK hours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through the Maryland EXCELS program.
requirements_list: Must complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training
Training is a mandatory step in the Maryland EXCELS Mentoring Pilot
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring online training module available on the Maryland EXCELS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS Payments reward child care programs for providing high-quality services to families who use the Child Care Scholarship program. Programs rated at Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating levels 3, 4, or 5 receive increased reimbursement amounts on top of standard Child Care Scholarship payments, ranging from 10% to 44% depending on the child's age, type of care (family child care or child care center), and the program's quality rating level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs at EXCELS Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5 receive increased reimbursement percentages on Child Care Scholarship payments. For family child care, increases range from 10–29% depending on child age and rating level. For child care centers, increases range from 10–44% depending on child age and rating level. Payments appear as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers (family child care homes and child care centers) participating in Maryland EXCELS at Quality Rating levels 3, 4, or 5 that serve children using the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement on Child Care Scholarship payments for serving eligible children at high-quality rated programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed child care providers participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must hold a Quality Rating of Level 3, 4, or 5
Program must serve children using the Child Care Scholarship program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs must participate in Maryland EXCELS and achieve a Quality Rating of Level 3 or higher. Increased payments are automatically applied to Child Care Scholarship reimbursements and appear on the Invoice Detail Report as 'EXCELS' payments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The goal is to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services include one-on-one support (Intensive Individual Support Services), family consultation and training, respite care, therapeutic integration, residential habilitation, environmental accessibility adaptations, adult life planning, and more. Participants also receive full Medicaid benefits including health insurance, dental care, prescriptions, mental health services, and durable medical equipment. Funding levels and available slots are determined by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and approved by the Governor and Maryland State Legislature.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Autism Waiver covers home and community-based Medicaid waiver services delivered by approved Medicaid provider agencies. Services include Adult Life Planning, Environmental Accessibility Adaptations, Family Consultation, Intensive Individual Support Services (IISS), Residential Habilitation, Respite Care, and Therapeutic Integration. Participants also qualify for full Medicaid benefits such as health insurance, dental care, prescriptions, mental health services, and durable medical equipment. Funding levels and available slots are determined by CMS and approved by the Governor and Maryland State Legislature.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when they turn 21 who have a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or an educational classification of Autism, reside in Maryland, receive early intervention or special education services, and meet Medicaid financial eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services including one-on-one support, family consultation and training, respite care, therapeutic integration programs, residential habilitation, home accessibility adaptations, and adult life planning. Also covers full Medicaid benefits such as health insurance, dental care, prescriptions, mental health services, and durable medical equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Maryland. Program is available statewide across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester), each with dedicated Local Education Agency and Early Intervention contacts. No county-level or regional restrictions beyond Maryland residency.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
Ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21
Reside in Maryland
Receive early intervention or special education services (IFSP or IEP depending on age)
Have an IEP or IFSP that includes 15 or more hours per week of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports (first grade through exit from high school)
Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance: monthly income may not exceed 300% of SSI benefits, and countable assets may not exceed $2,000 or $2,500 depending on eligibility category
Must contact the Autism Waiver Registry at 866-417-3480 to be placed on the waitlist and apply when a vacancy occurs
Upon receiving an invitation letter, family has 45 days to accept the invitation, establish contact, complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the financial application

If technical eligibility checklist and financial application are not submitted within 30 days, a final notice is issued; family then has 15 days to submit information before the application is stopped
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families must contact the Autism Waiver Registry at 1-866-417-3480 to have the child's name added to the waiting list in chronological order. The program continuously accepts names for the waitlist. When a vacancy occurs, MDH conducts an initial screening (based on parent report) and sends an invitation letter; the family then has 45 days to accept the invitation, establish contact, complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the financial application. MSDE verifies Maryland residency and other eligibility criteria. If required documents are not submitted within 30 days, a final notice is issued with an additional 15 days to respond before the application is stopped. The local education agency (LEA) coordinates day-to-day implementation of services for enrolled participants, including multidisciplinary team meetings and Plan of Care development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Pathways in Technology Early College High School (P-TECH) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: P-TECH is a grade 9 to 14 public school program that creates clear pathways from high school to college and career. In six years or less, students graduate with a high school diploma and a no-cost, two-year Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree. Each P-TECH school partners with industry and a local community college to deliver academically rigorous, career-relevant curriculum. The program includes one-on-one mentoring, workplace visits, skills instruction, paid summer internships, and first-in-line consideration for jobs with partnering companies. MSDE awards competitive planning grants to local school systems to establish new P-TECH sites. The program was established under the P-TECH Act of 2017 (Chapter 591, Acts of 2017). Expansion of new P-TECH schools beyond the initial FY2017-2018 cohort was contingent on demonstrated program success per legislative evaluation criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive planning grants awarded by MSDE to local school systems to establish P-TECH sites. The program also delivers no-cost Associate of Applied Science degree education, paid summer internships, one-on-one mentoring, workplace visits, and first-in-line job consideration with partner employers. Beginning in fiscal year 2017 and each fiscal year thereafter, planning grants are available on an ongoing basis; however, beginning in fiscal year 2019, no new P-TECH planning grant may be awarded until the 2016-2017 cohort of P-TECH students completes the 6-year pathway sequence (i.e., approximately 2022-2023). As of 2026, that restriction period has passed. No more than one P-TECH planning grant per year beginning in fiscal year 2018.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems (partnering with community colleges and businesses) seeking to establish P-TECH schools; high school students from all academic backgrounds in grades 9-14 seeking a pathway to a no-cost associate degree and career. At least 50% of students served should be eligible for Free or Reduced-Price Meals (FARM). Local school systems may apply individually or as consortiums.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and establishing P-TECH school sites that provide students with a combined high school diploma and two-year Associate of Applied Science degree pathway, including curriculum development, mentoring, paid summer internships, and industry partnerships. Student pathways include fields such as Information Technology, Cyber Security, Nursing, Respiratory Care, Physical Therapy Assistant, Health Information Management, Hospitality Services Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering Technology, and Network & Information Technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Existing sites include Baltimore City (Carver Vocational-Technical High School and Paul Laurence Dunbar High School), Allegany County, Prince George's County, Baltimore County, and Montgomery County. Initial planning grants also targeted the Upper Eastern Shore (Queen Anne's, Talbot, and Caroline Counties).
requirements_list: Local school systems must partner with a community college and at least one industry/employer partner
Partnership must be formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the school system, community college, and business partners
Program is administered through a competitive grant process by MSDE
Established under the P-TECH Act of 2017 (Chapter 591, Acts of 2017); effective July 1, 2017
Expansion of new P-TECH schools is contingent on demonstrated program success as evaluated by MSDE and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
MSDE must report annually to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 1 each year
A comprehensive evaluation of program success was required on or before December 1, 2023
At least 50% of students served must be eligible for Free or Reduced-Price Meals (FARM)
Local school systems may apply individually or as consortiums
No more than one P-TECH planning grant per year beginning in fiscal year 2018

Beginning in fiscal year 2019, no new planning grant could be awarded until the 2016-2017 cohort completed the 6-year pathway (approximately 2022-2023); this restriction period has now passed as of 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MSDE administers a competitive grant process for local school systems to apply for planning grants to establish P-TECH sites. Applicants must form a three-entity partnership (local school system, community college, and employer/industry partner) and execute an MOU. Contact Kellise Williamson for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) grant program that used federal funds to stabilize, strengthen, and sustain Maryland's licensed child care system and reduce the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Grants were awarded under six high-leverage strategies: Expanding Access to Quality Child Care, Early Learning Models of Excellence, Expanding Mental Health Supports and Services, Growing a Highly Effective Child Care Workforce, Boosting Family Child Care, and Advancing a Coordinated Prekindergarten Enrollment System.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded under one or more of six strategy areas. Award notices were issued in December 2022. Specific award amounts are not listed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, early childhood organizations, higher education institutions, and other entities supporting Maryland's child care system
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Helping families access and afford child care; improving program quality; providing mental health supports; supporting the early childhood workforce; strengthening family child care businesses; and advancing coordinated prekindergarten enrollment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible child care providers and organizations across Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must choose at least one of the six high-leverage strategy areas
Must describe how planned activities align with the chosen strategy
Must describe products and/or services to be delivered
Must describe expected impact on the early childhood community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted to MSDE. Award notices were issued in December 2022. Grantee one-pagers and application materials are posted on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Rebuilds is a Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) grant program that uses federal funds to stabilize, strengthen, and sustain Maryland's child care system and reduce the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Grants are awarded under six strategies: Expanding Access to Quality Child Care, Early Learning Models of Excellence, Expanding Behavioral Health Supports and Services, Growing a Highly-Effective Child Care Workforce, Boosting Family Child Care, and Advancing a Coordinated Prekindergarten Enrollment System.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $43 million in total funding is available, with an estimated 40–55 grants awarded. The grant period runs from December 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024. Applicants must submit a separate application for each strategy they are applying to.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 11:59 p.m. on November 10, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs), Local School Systems (LSSs), Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (LECACs), Judy Centers, private child care providers, public prekindergarten programs, and collaborative partnerships working to support Maryland's child care system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stabilizing, strengthening, and sustaining the child care system; expanding access to quality child care; supporting early learning models of excellence; expanding behavioral health supports and services; growing the child care workforce; boosting family child care; and advancing coordinated prekindergarten enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; MSDE considers geographic distribution of need when making awards.
requirements_list: Applicants must attend at least one General Information Session before submitting an application
Applicants must attend a strategy-specific session for each strategy they intend to apply to
A separate application must be submitted for each strategy
All deliverables must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility standards as outlined in Senate Bill 617
Applications and all required attachments must be submitted via email by 11:59 p.m. on November 10, 2022
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend at least one General Information Session and one strategy-specific session. Download and complete the Maryland Rebuilds Application form. Submit the completed application and all required attachments via email to MSDE no later than 11:59 p.m. on November 10, 2022. Submit a separate application for each strategy you are applying to.

structured_extraction.program_description: The National School Lunch Program (NSLP) provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. Schools and residential child care institutions receive federal reimbursement for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, giving over 900,000 students access to nutritious lunches and snacks daily. Funds help offset the cost of producing meals for students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement dollars for each meal served that meets USDA nutrition standards. Children receive free or reduced-price (or no-cost) lunches based on eligibility criteria including household income, participation in federal assistance programs, or attendance at a Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) school. Direct payments help offset the cost of producing meals for students. Income must fall at or below published thresholds for household size; for mixed-frequency income, applicants must annualize all sources before comparison (weekly ×52, every two weeks ×26, twice monthly ×24, monthly ×12).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools, nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions in Maryland that serve lunches to students; children who qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on income or categorical eligibility; households with school-aged children applying for free or reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement to schools for meals served that meet USDA nutritional standards; provides free or low-cost lunches to eligible students. Funds help offset the cost of producing meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all 24 Maryland public school systems and participating nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions statewide.
requirements_list: Schools must serve meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards
Public schools are required to participate; nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions may elect to participate
Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in NSLP must have a local school wellness policy

Wellness policy must include goals for nutrition education, physical activity, and other wellness activities; standards for school meals and other foods sold on campus; policies for food and beverage marketing; and public reporting and triennial evaluation
Income must fall at or below published thresholds for household size
For mixed-frequency income, applicant must annualize all sources before comparison (weekly ×52, every two weeks ×26, twice monthly ×24, monthly ×12)

All foods and beverages sold to students on school campus must comply with Maryland Nutrition Standards (Smart Snacks), effective July 1, 2014, revised September 2025 to reflect USDA Final Rule changes effective July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools participate through their Local Education Agency's school nutrition office. Families apply for free or reduced-price meals by submitting income information on a free/reduced-price meal application; the school compares reported income to Income Eligibility Guidelines (IEGs) using established procedures. Families may also be directly certified through participation in qualifying federal assistance programs. Applications are submitted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Nonpublic Tuition Assistance Program (NTAP) provides state aid to cover the cost of educating students with disabilities who are placed in nonpublic (private) special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The state calculates its share of nonpublic special education costs under Education Article §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Students placed in nonpublic schools are counted in the September 30th enrollment count with a code 09 designation and are excluded from standard Foundation funding calculations due to the tuition reimbursement process. Covered costs include tuition for approved nonpublic day or residential special education placements and related IEP services such as audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, classroom aides, behavior modification, extended school year (ESY) services, IEP residential services, supplemental aides, and program modifications. Costs are tracked on a per diem basis. Funding sources for residential placements may include Autism Waiver, Home Circumstance, CSA, LSS, MSDE, DHMH, DJS, DSS, MA, and others. Out-of-state nonpublic special education placements are also explicitly eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State aid reimburses a portion of the tuition cost for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education schools through the IEP process. The state's share is calculated per Education Article §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Covered costs include tuition for approved nonpublic day or residential special education placements and related IEP services such as audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, classroom aides, behavior modification, extended school year (ESY) services, IEP residential services, supplemental aides, and program modifications. Costs are tracked on a per diem basis. Funding sources for residential placements may include Autism Waiver, Home Circumstance, CSA, LSS, MSDE, DHMH, DJS, DSS, MA, and others.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the Entry Date, Discharge Date, or Service Revision Date for the current fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (public school systems) and local school systems seeking state reimbursement for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education day or residential schools through the IEP process, including out-of-state placements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition reimbursement for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education schools (day and residential programs, including out-of-state). Covered services include standard educational and related services, extended school year (ESY) services, IEP residential services, related services (audiology, counseling, OT, PT, speech-language pathology), supplemental aides, classroom aides, behavior modification, and program modifications. Costs are tracked on a per diem basis per placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all local school systems (LEAs). Out-of-state nonpublic special education placements are also explicitly eligible. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions apply.
requirements_list: Student must be placed in a nonpublic special education school through the IEP process
Student must be included in the September 30th enrollment count with a code 09 designation
Student must not be included in Foundation funding calculations
Application must be submitted to MSDE within 30 calendar days of the Entry Date, Discharge Date, or Service Revision Date
Application categories include New, Renewal, Re-Entry, Discharge, Service Revision, and Correction
Legal authority: Education Article §8-406 and COMAR 13A.05.01, 13A.05.02
Financially Responsible LEA must be identified on the application
Placement must be in an MSDE-approved nonpublic program or, for individual placements, must be separately approved
Cost sheet must be submitted with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies submit the MSDE Approved Day and Residential Program Application, or request an Individual Placement application. Applications must be submitted to MSDE within 30 calendar days of the relevant placement event (Entry Date, Discharge Date, or Service Revision Date). Application forms and directions are available on the MSDE website. Application types include New, Renewal, Re-Entry, Discharge, Service Revision, and Correction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funding to Local School Systems (LSSs) to support professional learning for Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers of 3- and 4-year-old children. Professional learning is aligned to the Science of Reading research. The grant extends the Maryland Leads Science of Reading initiative to early childhood educators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards range between $40,000 and $80,000. Total funding available is $1,000,000, with an estimated 12–24 grants to be awarded. Funds are used for professional learning aligned to the Science of Reading for Pre-K educators, including salaries and wages, contracted services (approved Science of Reading training vendors), supplies and materials, equipment, indirect costs, facilitator fees, program evaluation, and dissemination activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSSs) and Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in Maryland seeking to provide professional learning to Pre-K educators, including teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, Education Support Professionals, and private childcare teachers on Science of Reading strategies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning for Prekindergarten teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers on Science of Reading strategies. Allowable costs include salaries and wages, contracted services (approved Science of Reading vendors), supplies and materials, equipment, indirect costs, facilitator fees, program evaluation, and dissemination activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Local School Systems in Maryland. MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making awards.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS) / Local Education Agency (LEA).
Funds must be obligated by December 30, 2022.
Grant period: September 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023 (subject to no-cost extension approval).
Professional learning must align to Science of Reading research.
Must include a management plan with key personnel identified.
Must include an evaluation and dissemination plan.
Must complete MSDE Grant Budget C-125 form.
Must submit scope of work from an approved Science of Reading vendor.
Demonstrate extent of need using qualitative and quantitative data.
Define clear, ambitious goals aligned to Science of Reading research.
Include approved vendor identification and alignment to Maryland Leads application.
Provide robust engagement plan for private child care and Head Start staff.
Include qualified facilitator credentials.
Assign grant tasks to qualified personnel with resumes.
Detailed budget with aligned line items.
Submit recipient assurances as required by MSDE.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Competitive grant evaluated on a 100-point rubric covering: extent of need, goals, implementation plan, evaluation and dissemination, management plan, and budget narrative. Download the Grant Information Guide (GIG) and application form from the program page. Submit the completed application by email by 5:00 p.m. on October 11, 2022. MSDE held customer service support sessions on September 14 and 15, 2022 for applicants with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Public-Private Partnership (PPP) classroom or program is a funding agreement between a Local School System (LSS) and a Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)-approved nonpublic special education program. The purpose is to serve students with significant and intensive needs in the Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) and enhance Individualized Education Program (IEP) services for students in their community. The program is especially beneficial for students with short-term needs, those experiencing a crisis, or those awaiting a more intensive placement. Two variants exist: Public/Private Partnership (PPP) classroom/program partnerships and Preventive Service Partnerships providing wrap-around services to support public school placement. Funding is structured as an annual contract/agreement, with state funds released after contracts are finalized and signed. The partnership must be cost neutral to the State.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funding contributions for tuition calculated on full-time equivalent (FTE) seats, structured as an annual contract/agreement between a Local School System and an MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program. State funds are released after contracts are finalized and signed. The partnership must be cost neutral to the State.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually (renewals); minimum 30 calendar days prior to request for State funding for new requests each fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSS) and MSDE-approved nonpublic special education programs serving students with significant and intensive special education needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting classroom or program placements for students with significant and intensive needs in a nonpublic special education setting as an alternative to or in anticipation of more intensive placement. Also covers Preventive Service Partnerships providing wrap-around services to support public school placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applies to local education agencies and local school systems throughout Maryland. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions.
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System (LSS) or MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program
Student must have significant and intensive special education needs
Designed for students with short-term needs, those in crisis, or awaiting more intensive placement
Application must be submitted at minimum 30 calendar days prior to the request for State funding each fiscal year
Renewal applications must be submitted by June 1 of each school year
Public/Private Partnership must be cost neutral to the State
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local School Systems initiate discussions with MSDE regarding proposals by February 1 annually. Applications are submitted to MSDE by June 1 annually (for renewals; new requests require submission at least 30 days before the state funding request). MSDE issues notice of funding intent by July 15. Contracts are finalized and signed prior to release of State funds. Required documents include: MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application, Public/Private Partnership Agreement or Contract, Budget (completed by nonpublic provider using MSDE budget packet), MSDE Public/Private Partnership Fiscal Worksheet, and biannual monitoring data (Student Attendance List for classroom/program partnerships; Outcome Evaluation form for Preventive Service Partnerships). Mid-year enrollment report is due January 15. Contact Sheila F. Philip for the application or see https://www.marylandpublicschools.org/programs/Pages/Special-Education/NonpublicSpEd/index.aspx for contact details and forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program (SBP) reimburses schools and residential child care institutions with federal dollars for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards. It provides students with a nutritious breakfast to support learning, with studies showing links to higher test scores, better behavior, reduced food insecurity, and fewer absences. Students from families with incomes at or below 130–185% of the federal poverty level may receive meals at free or reduced prices. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal meal reimbursements (direct payments) are provided to participating schools and residential child care institutions for each breakfast served that meets USDA nutrition standards. Funds help offset the costs of producing breakfast meals. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools, non-profit private schools, residential childcare institutions, and state colleges seeking federal reimbursement to provide nutritious breakfasts to school-age children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal reimbursements cover the cost of providing breakfasts to students that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Students from low-income families may receive free or reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 24 Maryland public school systems and participating non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions.
requirements_list: Schools must serve meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards
Students from families with incomes at or below 130–185% of the federal poverty level qualify for free or reduced-price meals
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and residential child care institutions participate by agreeing to serve meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and receive federal reimbursements for qualifying meals served. Applications are submitted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides annual grants to qualified non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations that deliver enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs offer experiential learning and one-on-one support services that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities and cannot be replicated in the classroom. Funded activities include free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers that links SAI programs to classroom curriculum. For fiscal year 2027, approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60–65 grants to be distributed. In FY2023 the program served approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants awarded to qualified non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations. For fiscal year 2027, approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60–65 grants to be distributed. Currently, there are 57–58 organizations in the SAI program; for fiscal year 2026, fifty-six programs are funded across the State. Eligible budget uses include salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials for educational programs; and outreach, engagement, and marketing tools. Funds cannot be used for operating costs, defined as property repair, maintenance, taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, administrative/leadership salaries, office supplies, or rent. Less than 50% of an organization's budget may come from state grants (with a noted exception for the Baltimore Zoo). Augmentation requests require projected costs needed to implement additional programming. New applicants should request funding in line with historical award amounts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations that provide enriching educational programs and experiential learning opportunities to Maryland students and teachers, including public schools, Title 1 schools, nonpublic schools, and homeschools (capped at 20% of participants)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational programs providing experiential learning experiences for Maryland students, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers that connect experiences to classroom curriculum are also funded. Funds may cover salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials; and outreach, engagement, and marketing tools. Funds cannot be used for operating costs such as property repair, maintenance, taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, administrative/leadership salaries, office supplies, or rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Organizations must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers, including Title I schools across Maryland. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions apply. Program emphasizes expansion of services to additional Local Education Agencies (LEAs) statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified non-profit 501(c)(3) organization
Programs must provide enriching educational experiences to Maryland students
Programs must align with the State's curricular and educational priorities, including the Blueprint for Maryland's Future
Programs must offer learning experiences that cannot be replicated in the classroom
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and/or one-on-one support services
Must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers
Less than 50% of the organization's budget may come from state grants (except for the Baltimore Zoo)
Nonpublic and homeschool participants may not exceed 20% of total participants
Application must include budget narrative, appendices, and C-1-25 grant budget form
Program operates under COMAR 13A.05.13.04 regulatory authority
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Grant Information Guide and application are released on April 24 each year. A complete grant application including budget narrative, appendices, and grant budget form is submitted by the deadline (e.g., June 10, 2024 for FY2026; June 13, 2025 for FY2027). MSDE holds customer service support sessions for interested applicants to review program requirements and walk through the application process. After submission, an MSDE review committee scores applications against a rubric and submits results to the State Superintendent (July). The State Board of Education reviews recommended awards (August). The Governor releases a draft budget bill in January of the following year; budget subcommittees then review and vote (January–April). The FY2027 application cycle (grant period July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027) closed June 13, 2025; the next cycle has not yet been announced.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teachers of Promise (TOP) program pairs pre-service education students from Maryland colleges and universities with veteran teachers — including Teachers of the Year and Milken Educators — to provide mentoring and professional development before they begin their teaching careers. Students nominated by their colleges are matched with award-winning educators for online mentoring throughout the spring and summer, culminating in a one-day Institute event.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-service teacher candidates receive online mentoring from veteran educators and attend a one-day Teachers of Promise Institute featuring keynote addresses and panel sessions. Mentors may invite mentees to observe their classrooms and help connect them to teaching positions in Maryland public schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-service teacher candidates in their final year at Maryland colleges and universities who plan to teach in Maryland public schools in the fall.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development, mentoring, and networking to support pre-service teachers entering the classroom.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must attend a Maryland college or university and plan to teach in Maryland public schools.
requirements_list: Must be nominated by a Maryland college or university
Must be in final year of an education degree program
Must plan to begin teaching in Maryland public schools in the fall
Program accepts 5–7 nominees per participating institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Colleges and universities nominate 5–7 of their top education students each year. Nominees are then matched with Maryland Teachers of the Year, Milken Educators, and other award-winning educators for online mentoring.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides additional funding to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022. The goal is to build state capacity to create new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products. MSDE funds staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and the purchase of food and supplies. Feedback from tasting events helps project partners refine recipes to match student preferences and school feasibility. Training and nutrition education resources are developed by Maryland SNAP-Ed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards to LEAs to fund staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for those events. Budget templates are available through the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in Maryland participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time for training and recipe tasting events; food and supplies for tasting events
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to LEAs throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Grant Information Guide for instructions, timelines, and submission requirements. Access the Budget Template through the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS). Submit application using the Grant Application Form. Questions can be emailed to Sara Booker, the Project Director.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Foods in Schools (Food Distribution Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Foods in Schools program (also known as the Food Distribution Program) supports domestic nutrition programs and American agricultural producers by purchasing 100% American-grown and -produced foods for use by schools and child care facilities. It provides USDA food commodities to eligible public schools, private nonprofit schools, residential child care institutions, and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors. Maryland schools can choose from a catalog of over 200 domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products to incorporate into their menus, reducing school food expenses by an average of 20%. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools and eligible child care facilities receive USDA-purchased foods (fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat) at no cost, reducing food expenses by an average of 20%. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their meal reimbursements. Assistance is delivered as direct food commodities and may include technical assistance and regulatory support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools, private nonprofit schools, residential child care institutions, and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing domestically grown and produced food items for school and child care menus, including fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools and CACFP sponsors in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a participating school or CACFP sponsor in Maryland
Must be a public school, private nonprofit school, residential child care institution, or CACFP sponsor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools choose from a catalog of over 200 USDA food products to incorporate into their menus. Schools can also allocate USDA Foods funds to the USDA DOD Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program for weekly delivery of fresh produce from a Maryland-based produce company. Applications are submitted annually.

As part of Maryland's Preschool Development Grant Birth through Age Five award, the grant amount was doubled from $500 to $1,000. Eligibility is based on certain income levels and family size requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program (CCQIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program (CCQIG) awards quarterly grants to licensed child care providers in Maryland to enhance the quality of care provided to children. The program supports quality improvements, start-up, and sustainability for family child care and center-based programs. It supports projects that improve professionalism and quality in child care programs and supports initiatives that improve children's school readiness. Funds help providers acquire supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments, implementing knowledge gained through participation in training. Emphasis is placed on educational curricula and activities in literacy, math, science, social studies, and physical development. Grant amounts are based on the number of children in the facility's care, and providers are eligible for an award once every three years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), Office of Child Care / Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded quarterly (January, April, July, October) each state fiscal year. Award amounts depend on facility size: up to $1,000 for facilities with fewer than 10 children; up to $1,500 for facilities with up to 29 children; up to $2,500 for facilities with more than 30 children. Providers may receive a grant once every three years. Grant funds may be spent only on approved supplies, materials, and equipment that improve the quality of child care and children's developmental skills. Eligible items include materials for active play, arts and crafts, dramatic play, literacy, manipulatives, math, science, program planning, and special needs equipment for children ages 0–16. MSDE-approved curriculum guides and computers for child care use are also eligible. The grants support quality improvements, start-up costs, and sustainability for family child care and center-based programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Coming soon — revised Grant Information Guide and Application pending review and approval; new grant opportunities in SFY 2022 noted as available soon; FY23 cycle previously referenced with check-back after December 1, 2022

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of approved supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments and enhance child care quality — including items for literacy, math, science, social studies, physical development, dramatic play, arts and crafts, active play, and special needs equipment for children ages 0–16. Also supports quality improvements, start-up costs, and sustainability for child care programs. MSDE-approved curriculum guides and computers for child care use are also eligible. Eligible expenses are detailed in the program guide.
