Applicants are notified in writing of approval or disapproval. The revised Grant Information Guide and Application are pending review and approval; information will be distributed through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website once available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Student Employment Services and Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) provides two complementary transition programs for students with disabilities aged 14–21 enrolled in secondary or post-secondary education. Student Employment Services (SES) help students with disabilities prepare for and obtain employment in a career field of their interest, earning at least minimum wage and working alongside peers without identified disabilities. Services are individualized to each student's career goal and specific needs, including development of an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). Students with the most significant disabilities are served first; others may be placed on a waiting list but can still receive Pre-ETS. Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) are five specific services provided at no cost to students with disabilities to help them explore career interests and prepare for employment and/or post-secondary education: Job Exploration Counseling, Instruction in Self-Advocacy, Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities, Workplace Readiness Training, and Work-Based Learning Experiences. Pre-ETS services are short-term and introductory in nature and are available immediately with no waiting list. Both programs are available statewide through local DORS offices. DORS counselors are assigned to every public high school in Maryland and may also participate in IEP meetings when invited. All services are provided at no cost to students or families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education - Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized employment and career readiness services for students with disabilities, provided at no cost. Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) include career exploration counseling, self-advocacy instruction, post-secondary education guidance, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. Student Employment Services include a broader range of vocational rehabilitation supports, individualized vocational rehabilitation planning via an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE), career preparation, job placement support, job coaching, supported employment, and assistive technology solutions. A DORS counselor helps identify funding sources and coordinates services. Students with the most significant disabilities are prioritized for Student Employment Services beyond Pre-ETS; others may be waitlisted but remain eligible for Pre-ETS. SSI/SSDI recipients are presumed eligible for Student Employment Services. Services are available in-person at DORS offices throughout Maryland (more than 20 offices statewide) and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 who are currently enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, or an approved educational program and have a documented disability (IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation), seeking career exploration, employment preparation, and job placement support. Referrals may be submitted by the student, parent/guardian, school staff, or medical provider.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career preparation, employment placement, transition services, career exploration counseling, self-advocacy instruction, post-secondary education counseling, workplace readiness training, work-based learning experiences, individualized vocational rehabilitation planning, job coaching, supported employment, and assistive technology solutions — all individualized to the student's career goal and disability-related needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through more than 20 local DORS offices located throughout Maryland. Services are also available virtually. DORS has counselors assigned to every public high school in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must meet DORS eligibility requirements for students with disabilities
Must be at least 14 years old and no more than 21 (less than age 22)
Must be currently enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, or an approved educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn
Must have a documented disability (IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation)
Must provide Social Security number, documentation of disability, proof of school enrollment, and proof of age
For Pre-ETS: must sign and date the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form

For Student Employment Services beyond Pre-ETS: eligibility determination by DORS based on significance of disability; may require copy of IEP, psychological testing, medical documentation, or triennial evaluation
SSI/SSDI recipients are presumed eligible for Student Employment Services
Federal law prioritizes individuals with most significant disabilities for Student Employment Services; a waiting list may apply for others
Parent/guardian consent required for referral of minor students
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete a 'Request DORS Services' referral form online at dors.maryland.gov (can be submitted by the student, parent/guardian, medical provider, or school staff on behalf of the student with parent/guardian consent), or contact the local DORS office by phone. Allow approximately 10 business days for a DORS representative to contact the applicant. 2. DORS contacts the student and family via email through the secure SARA system (also by text or letter) with next steps. 3. Student or parent/guardian submits additional documentation through SARA. 4. DORS reviews documentation and forwards qualifying student's information to the local DORS office. 5. A local DORS counselor contacts the student and family to schedule an intake or Pre-ETS Service Agreement Meeting to plan services. 6. At the meeting, bring Social Security number, documentation of disability (e.g., IEP, 504 plan, medical records), proof of school enrollment, and proof of age. 7. DORS staff will determine eligibility, potentially scheduling assessments if needed, and notify the student of eligibility determination by letter. If eligible for Student Employment Services, the student works with a DORS counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). DORS counselors may participate in IEP meetings when invited.

structured_extraction.program_description: WTC's Career & Technology Training programs prepare students to enter the workforce with entry-level skills needed for job success. Programs provide essential supports and accommodations for individuals with disabilities, and offer individualized instruction to help students with varying learning styles reach their employment goals. Available programs include Automotive Detailing, Automotive General Service Technician, Child Care Provider, CVS Retail Academy, CVS Pharmacy Technician, Environmental Services, and Food Service.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education - Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) / WTC
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Career and technology training programs that prepare individuals with disabilities for entry-level employment across multiple trade and service industries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level employment skills and career training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training in fields such as automotive services, child care, pharmacy technician, retail, environmental services, and food service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through Maryland's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) WTC campus.
requirements_list: Must have a disability

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week course offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) that prepares job seekers with disabilities for certification as childcare providers. The program includes classroom instruction on child development, managing activities, communication, infant/toddler care, and school-age care, as well as a nine-week community-based internship at a licensed childcare facility. Participants who complete the program receive First Aid and CPR certification and preparation for childcare provider certification.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) — Workforce & Technology Center (WTC)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 16-week training program including classroom instruction and a nine-week internship. Participants who complete the program receive First Aid and CPR certification and preparation for childcare provider certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking employment as childcare providers. Must be at least 18 years of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for certification as a childcare provider, including classroom instruction and community-based internship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is offered at DORS' Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) campus in Northeast Baltimore. The attachment notes availability at select locations throughout the state, though specific counties or regions are not named.

structured_extraction.program_name: Training & Technical Assistance – Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs (OSCNP) at the Maryland State Department of Education provides training and technical assistance to schools and participating community agencies. The goal is to ensure participants understand and meet nutritional standards and guidelines set by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). Training covers programs such as the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, Child and Adult Care Food Program, Summer Food Service Program, and food safety certification (ServSafe).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education – Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training sessions offered on a recurring basis, including twice-annual administrative meetings for public school systems and private schools, monthly CACFP basics training, required annual CACFP and Summer Food Service Program training, and ServSafe food safety certification courses. Technical assistance is also available to help agencies comply with USDA regulations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public school systems, residential child care institutions, nonprofit private schools, child care centers, adult day care centers, family child care sponsors, at-risk afterschool programs, and summer food service agencies participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to meet USDA nutritional standards, including professional development, regulatory updates, food safety certification, menu planning, and meal pattern compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to agencies participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs.
requirements_list: Must participate in a federally funded Child Nutrition Program (e.g., NSLP, SBP, CACFP, or SFSP)
Certain training sessions are required annually or twice annually depending on program type
ServSafe orders must be placed four weeks in advance with training dates scheduled before ordering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact OSCNP at 410-767-0199 for information on training dates and locations. ServSafe materials can be ordered via the online ServSafe Training Materials Order Form after scheduling training dates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant funded by the American Rescue Plan (ARP) Act of 2021 to help licensed child care providers in Maryland stay open and recover from the financial hardships caused by COVID-19. The grant provided a base award plus additional funds based on the number of licensed child care slots and criteria such as serving infants, toddlers, Child Care Scholarship recipients, Maryland EXCELS participants, or being located in a high social-vulnerability census tract.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards start at a $10,000 base and add $126 per licensed child care slot for each qualifying criterion met (serving infants, toddlers, Child Care Scholarship recipients, Maryland EXCELS participants, and/or located in a census tract with a Social Vulnerability Index above 0.6). Grants do not need to be repaid as long as required certifications are met. All grants are taxable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs operating under a Letter of Compliance in Maryland. Head Start and Early Head Start programs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs, benefits, premium pay, recruitment and retention; rent or mortgage payments, utilities, facilities maintenance and improvements, or insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, or health and safety training; equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services; behavioral health supports for children and employees; past expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed child care providers.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed family child care home, large family child care home, child care center, or education program under a Letter of Compliance

MSDE held virtual support sessions during the application window. The application window opened January 3, 2022 and closed January 23, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Accreditation Support Fund, administered by the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Early Childhood, provides financial support to help licensed child care centers and registered family child care homes cover costs associated with pursuing state or national accreditation. The fund includes two tracks: (1) National Accreditation Support covers required application fees for initial applications, renewals, and annual updates — Family Child Care providers may apply as a first step toward NAFCC accreditation; recognized accrediting bodies include AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia, COA/ASA, Lumen, MSDE, MSA-CESS, NAC, NAEYC, NAFCC, and NECPA; (2) Maryland Program Accreditation Support covers the cost of non-consumable instructional materials for licensed child care centers and school-age only programs pursuing Maryland Accreditation, with reimbursement caps of $2,500 (programs serving ≤100 children) or $3,000 (programs serving >100 children) per accreditation cycle. Funds cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, costs already covered by another funding source, or costs exceeding the fee charged by the accrediting organization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tracks of assistance: (1) National Accreditation Support — funds to cover required accreditation application fees (initial, renewal, annual update) paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant; 13 recognized accrediting bodies include AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia, COA/ASA, Lumen, MSDE, MSA-CESS, NAC, NAEYC, NAFCC, and NECPA. Family Child Care providers may apply for the National Accreditation Support Fund as a first step toward NAFCC accreditation. (2) Maryland Accreditation Support — reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials (e.g., curricula, books, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science/sensory materials) per the Infants and Toddlers and Preschool/School-Age Classroom Learning Materials Checklists. Reimbursement caps: up to $2,500 per accreditation cycle for programs serving 1–100 children; up to $3,000 per accreditation cycle for programs serving 101+ children. Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper) are not reimbursable. Purchases must be within 12 months before the date of application. Funds cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already covered by another funding source.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, and school-age only programs in Maryland pursuing state or national accreditation, including Maryland Accreditation and accreditation through recognized national bodies such as NAEYC, NAFCC, NAC, COA/ASA, Cognia, and others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: National Accreditation: required application fees (initial, renewal, annual update) paid directly to the accrediting organization, including NAFCC accreditation for Family Child Care providers. Maryland Accreditation: reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials including language and literacy materials, mathematics materials, discovery/science/nature materials, outdoor learning equipment, music and movement instruments, dramatic/imaginative play props, technology (computers, tablets, software, assistive tech), and other instructional materials. Consumable items are not reimbursable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, and school-age only programs.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, school-age only program, or registered family child care home
Must be pursuing Maryland Accreditation or national accreditation through a recognized accrediting organization
For Maryland Accreditation: purchases must be within 12 months before date of application
For Maryland Accreditation: individual license number required per site; each site may apply separately
For Maryland Accreditation: one reimbursement form per vendor with receipts/invoices attached
For National Accreditation: must submit completed accreditation application, Work Plan, accrediting organization fee page, and current accreditation certificate (if already accredited)
Funds cannot be used for facility improvement
Funds cannot be used for association membership fees
Funds cannot be used for staff training
Funds cannot cover costs already paid by another funding source
Funds cannot exceed the fee charged by the accrediting organization
Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper) are not reimbursable under Maryland Accreditation track
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the Maryland OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov). Separate applications exist for National Accreditation Support and Maryland Accreditation Support. For National Accreditation, submit a completed accreditation application, Work Plan, accrediting organization fee page, and current accreditation certificate (if applicable); processing takes approximately 30 days from submission of all required documents and payment is made directly to the accrediting organization. For Maryland Accreditation, submit separate reimbursement forms per vendor with receipts attached, using the applicable Classroom Learning Materials Checklist. Family Child Care providers can follow a video tutorial for guidance. For questions, contact [email protected]. FAQs and application details are available on the Maryland Public Schools Early Childhood website.

Eligible providers receive a base award plus a per-slot amount to cover personnel costs, rent, utilities, personal protective equipment, equipment updates, and behavioral health supports.

Grants do not need to be repaid as long as the provider meets all required certifications throughout the grant term. Grant period: September 6, 2021 – March 6, 2022.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs, employee benefits, premium pay, recruitment and retention; rent or mortgage payments, utilities, facilities maintenance and improvements, or insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, or health and safety training; equipment and supplies updates to respond to COVID-19; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services; behavioral health supports for children and employees; past expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, mandatory online training course for child care providers in Maryland. The training covers health and safety best practices required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG). All child care staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for children in a licensed child care program must complete it. The course consists of four modules and a final review, takes about three hours, and issues a certificate of completion to participants who score 80% or higher.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course available monthly. Registration opens one week each month following a published schedule. The course runs approximately 21 days per cohort. Participants must complete all four modules and a final review/survey, scoring at least 80%, to receive a certificate of completion. Two attempts are allowed per account. Participants who used all attempts and scored below 80% cannot retake the online course and must complete face-to-face training instead. A face-to-face option is also available through approved trainers (at a cost set by the trainer). An annual update module is also available via MSDE Canvas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens monthly; June cohort registration closes May 23 at 12:00 pm; new employees must complete within 90 days of hire
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed Maryland child care programs; early childhood educators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completion of state- and federally-required Basic Health and Safety Training for child care workers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland child care providers and staff
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for children in a licensed Maryland child care program
Must have a valid email address to register
Must complete all four modules and the Final Review and Survey
Must score 80% or higher on all topic reviews and the Final Review and Survey to receive a certificate
Training must be completed before the course end date for the registered cohort
New employees must complete the training within 90 days of hire to remain in compliance
Two attempts allowed per account; participants who use all attempts and score below 80% cannot retake the online course and must complete face-to-face training instead
Accounts expire at the end of the course period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration is open for one week each month per the published schedule. Complete the online registration form at https://msde.instructure.com. Participants receive login instructions via email before the course opens. Log in at msde.instructure.com using your email and password, complete the Introduction module (prerequisite), then unlock and complete remaining topic modules and the Final Review and Survey within the cohort window (typically 21 days), scoring at least 80% to unlock the Certificate of Completion. An annual update module is also available via MSDE Canvas: access the MSDE Canvas Welcome Page, click Educator Resources, click Early Childhood Modules, then click Basic Health and Safety Annual Update 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program helps eligible Maryland families pay for high-quality child care and early education. The program issues scholarships (vouchers) that cover part of child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS providers. There are three scholarship types: a temporary 60-day scholarship, a full 52-week scholarship, and an informal scholarship for care by relatives or non-relatives in the child's home. The state pays the scholarship rate directly to the provider, and the family pays a State-assigned co-payment based on income. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment and are exempt from the current enrollment freeze. Income eligibility thresholds vary by family size (e.g., up to $76,117/year initial or $86,266/year continuation for a family of 2; up to $111,936/year initial or $126,861/year continuation for a family of 4; up to $161,188/year for a family of 10). A Fast Track application process issues a temporary 60-day scholarship within 3 business days, followed by a full 52-week scholarship if the applicant is eligible and submits additional documentation within 15 days. Full/New applications result in two-year scholarships upon approval. As of May 1, 2025, the program placed an enrollment freeze on new scholarships due to reaching its maximum budget capacity after growing from about 21,000 children in January 2023 to over 45,000 in 2025. Families already enrolled continue to receive their scholarships. New applicants can still apply and, if eligible, will be placed on a Frozen Status List (waitlist) until the freeze is lifted. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the freeze and can receive scholarships immediately if eligible. Scholarships cover children under age 13, or individuals ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability. The program also serves migrant workers, unhoused individuals, emancipated minors, and single parents paying child support.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive a scholarship (voucher) that covers a portion of child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS licensed child care centers, registered family homes, or informal care by a relative or non-relative in the child's home. The State pays the scholarship rate directly to the provider; families pay a State-assigned co-payment ranging from $0–$3 per week (per federal regulation). TCA, TANF, and SSI recipients have a $0 co-payment and are exempt from the enrollment freeze. Income limits vary by family size (e.g., family of 2: up to $76,117 initial / $86,266 continuation; family of 4: up to $111,936 initial / $126,861 continuation; family of 10: up to $161,188). A temporary 60-day scholarship is issued within 3 business days via the Fast Track process; a full 52-week scholarship is available after submission of additional documentation within 15 days. Full/New applications result in two-year scholarships upon approval. As of May 1, 2025, an enrollment freeze is in effect for new families not exempt; newly approved non-exempt families are placed on a Frozen Status List until funding becomes available. Scholarships cover children under age 13, or individuals ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability, and can cover before and after school care.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No formal deadline — applications accepted at any time; as of May 1, 2025, new non-exempt applicants are placed on a Frozen Status List (waitlist) until the freeze is lifted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland resident families who need help paying for child care — parent/guardian must be working, in an approved training program, or attending school, and must meet income guidelines. Includes families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI. Also includes migrant workers, unhoused individuals, emancipated minors, and single parents paying child support. Care is available for children under age 13, or individuals aged 13–19 with a qualifying disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward the cost of child care and early education at a Maryland licensed child care center, registered family home, or informal child care by a relative or non-relative participating in Maryland EXCELS; can cover before and after school care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Available statewide. No county, municipal, or regional restrictions. Montgomery County residents with incomes above the CCS initial income scale may also be referred to the Montgomery County Working Parents Assistance Program.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Parent/guardian must be working, in an approved training program, or attending school; if both parents live in the same household, both must meet eligibility requirements
Must meet CCS income guidelines, or be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), TANF, or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Child must be under age 13, or ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability
Child must be immunized to Maryland state standards or have a documented exemption
Must provide proof that each child needing care is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien (parents are not required to be U.S. citizens)
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Head of household must provide a photo ID
Must provide four consecutive weeks of pay stubs (4 weekly, 2 bi-weekly, or 1 monthly) or other proof of income
Must provide proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage, or Maryland driver's license)
Must provide current school or training schedule on school/employer letterhead
Must provide child(ren)'s birth certificates or proof of age
Must provide child care provider information
For migrant workers: employer verification required
For unhoused individuals: agency letterhead confirmation required
For emancipated minors: emancipation verification documentation required
For single parents paying child support: current check, money order, or pay stub plus birth certificate required
Documentation of other benefits received (SNAP, WIC, TCA, WAG, GBI, housing assistance) if applicable — eligibility statement and/or voucher receipt
Families already enrolled must continue to qualify and submit renewal forms on time, including Redetermination Application submitted 45 days before end of eligibility period
Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are not subject to the enrollment freeze
Families can add new children to an existing scholarship (Change of Circumstance form required) without being subject to the freeze
Vaccination proof required for non-school-age children in informal care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can apply at any time through the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org (Spanish-language portal also available at https://family.childcareportals.org/s/?language=es). Three application pathways are available: (1) Fast Track — submit limited documentation (proof of employment/school enrollment, proof of residency, and proof of income) and receive a decision within 3 business days; a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued if eligible (or the family is placed on the Frozen Status List if subject to the enrollment freeze), then submit additional documentation within 15 days to be evaluated for a full 52-week scholarship. (2) Full/New Application — processed within up to 30–35 days (or 5 business days after all documents are received); results in a two-year scholarship upon approval. (3) Redetermination — families must submit 45 days before the end of their current eligibility period, with a hard deadline of at least 15 days before expiration. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the freeze and receive scholarships immediately upon approval. As of May 1, 2025, new non-exempt applicants who are determined eligible are placed on a Frozen Status List until the freeze is lifted. For assistance, call CCS Central at 1-877-227-0125 or visit www.money4childcare.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) helps low-income families pay for child care so parents can work or attend training or education. The program also works to improve the quality of child care and supports coordination among early childhood development, Head Start, pre-K, and afterschool programs. Families receive assistance through vouchers (certificates) or grants and contracts with child care providers. Parents can choose any provider that meets applicable state and local health and safety requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized child care services are provided to eligible low-income families through certificates (vouchers) or grants and contracts with child care providers. Families may select any provider that meets applicable state and local health and safety requirements. The federal CCDF program made $5.2 billion available to states, territories, and tribes in Fiscal Year 2012; Maryland's share supports child care subsidies and quality improvement efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families who need child care assistance so they can work or attend training or education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care services through vouchers or provider grants and contracts; quality improvement for child care providers; coordination among early childhood development, Head Start, pre-K, and afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Family must be low-income
Parent or guardian must be working or attending training/education

Child care provider must meet applicable state and local health and safety requirements, including infectious disease prevention, immunizations, building safety, and minimum health and safety training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families apply through Maryland's child care subsidy program. Contact the Maryland State Department of Education Division of Early Childhood for application information. The current state plan (2025-2027) governs eligibility and program rules; a public hearing on the 2025-2027 CCDF state plan was held June 13, 2024.

It funds referrals and services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers, and builds the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development. Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland with proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health (IECMH) services are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for non-profit and public agencies to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health (IECMH) services, including referrals and support services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are comprehensive early childhood support hubs located in Title I and high-needs elementary schools across Maryland. They serve children from birth through age 5 (prenatal to kindergarten) and their families, focusing on school readiness and family empowerment. Hubs provide or connect families to services including developmental screenings, parenting classes, home visiting, early intervention, case management, and referrals for community supports. As of FY2024, 86 Judy Centers operate across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, with ongoing expansion planned through 2030 under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, growing by 9 sites per year through 2025 and 18 sites per year from 2026–2030.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers provide free services and supports to families with children from birth (prenatal) through age 5 who live within the school zone of the Judy Center's host elementary school. Services include developmental screenings, on-site parent-child playgroups (average 3 per week in FY2024, minimum 2 per week required), family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, evidence-based home visiting, early intervention identification, case management using a family-centered approach (2,063 families served in FY2024 with 70% of family-driven goals achieved), referrals for support services, connections to adult education and workforce development, bilingual education support, and professional learning opportunities (976 offered in FY2024). FY2024 total program funding was $28,380,000 across 86 sites, sourced from American Rescue Plan Funds ($2,640,000), MSDE General Funds ($8,798,620), and Blueprint for Maryland's Future Funds ($16,941,380). In FY2024, 17,681 children and 14,750 families were served.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from birth (prenatal) through age 5 who live within a Judy Center school zone in Maryland, particularly those in Title I and high-needs school communities (schools scoring 0.6 or above on CDC Social Vulnerability Index); school staff; and community partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are not cash assistance; they provide developmental screenings, on-site parent-child playgroups, parenting education, home visiting, early intervention, case management using a family-centered approach, professional learning for partners, bilingual education support, speech and developmental support, and referrals to community supports including adult education and workforce development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 jurisdictions (all counties and Baltimore City); eligibility is limited to families living within the school zone of a Judy Center's host elementary school, which is located in a Title I or high-needs community.
requirements_list: Child must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located.
Children served are birth (prenatal) through age 5.
Host schools must be Title I or high-needs schools (scoring 0.6 or above on CDC Social Vulnerability Index).
Judy Centers must offer a minimum of 2 on-site parent-child playgroups per week.
Data collection on key performance measures is required.
Comprehensive needs assessment must be conducted for community partners.
Case management must use a family-centered approach.

Programs must meet 12 component standards including full-day/full-year services, meals, case management, family engagement, early identification, disability inclusion, health services, professional learning, adult education, accreditation, and partnerships.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly. A map and contact information for all Judy Centers is available at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Division of Early Childhood at the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It provides funding for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and local school systems (LSSs) to establish and expand Judy Center Early Learning Hubs that deliver high-quality, comprehensive full-day early childhood programming and family support services to children ages birth through five and their families. The goal is to promote school readiness and support families in high-needs communities. Judy Centers must be located in Title 1 school communities or high-needs communities as designated by the CDC Social Vulnerability Index score of 0.6 or above.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and local school systems (LSSs) to establish and expand Judy Center Early Learning Hubs. Renewal grants are structured as 3-year awards totaling $990,000 ($330,000 per year). Grant funds must be used to serve children ages birth through five and their families with comprehensive early care and education services. Priority is given to programs located in Title 1 school communities or communities with a CDC Social Vulnerability Index score of 0.6 or above. Additional priority goes to applicants demonstrating strong partnerships where both the Judy Center location and the LEA each provide at least 50% of funding for staff salaries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and local school systems (LSSs) in Maryland seeking to establish or expand Judy Center Early Learning Hubs in high-needs communities to serve young children and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and expanding Judy Center Early Learning Hubs; providing comprehensive early care and education services for children ages birth through five and their families; promoting school readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Local Education Agencies in Maryland. Priority given to communities with Title 1 schools or communities with a CDC Social Vulnerability Index score of 0.6 or above.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) or local school system (LSS).
Judy Center must be located in a community with a Title 1 school or a high-needs community (CDC Social Vulnerability Index score of 0.6 or above).
Must serve all children and families living within the catchment area of the school.
Application package must include a cover page signed in blue ink, project summary, projected enrollment and growth chart, Implementation Plans A and B, budget narrative, and all appendices.
Applications must be submitted in PDF format by email.
Additional priority given to applicants demonstrating strong partnership where each entity provides at least 50% of funding for Judy Center staff salaries.
Required appendices include: signed C-1-25 MSDE budget form for year 1, MOU meeting program provisions signed by all parties/partners, and signed recipient assurances page.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the FY2026 application available on the MSDE website. Download the Judy Center Grant Application from the Judy Center webpage. Prepare the full application package (cover page signed in blue ink, project summary, projected enrollment and growth chart, Implementation Plans A and B, budget narrative, and appendices including signed C-1-25 MSDE budget form, MOU, and signed recipient assurances page) and submit as a PDF by email to MSDE. See the Learn More link for full application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps registered family child care providers offset some of the costs of opening or maintaining their child care programs. It reimburses up to $1,000 in eligible expenses that a provider incurs to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. Eligibility is based on income level relative to 60% of Maryland's State Median Income (SMI) for the applicant's family size. The program is operated in accordance with COMAR 13A.14.07.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant of up to $1,000 for eligible expenses incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care licensing regulations. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, costs related to local water/sewer/fire/health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completing the registration process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers whose annual income does not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, costs related to local water/sewer/fire/health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completing the registration process.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to registered family child care providers meeting income eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Annual income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income for the applicant's family size
Expenses must be incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations
Program is operated in accordance with COMAR 13A.14.07
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application procedures are specified by COMAR 13A.14.07 regulations. More information noted as coming soon on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council Quality Improvement Grant FY24
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant administered by the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Early Childhood that provides funding to the 24 local early childhood advisory councils across Maryland. The grant supports councils in conducting periodic assessments of local early childhood needs, identifying opportunities and obstacles to collaboration and coordination of programs, and assessing the capacity and effectiveness of local programs for developing early childhood educators. It also supports the Blueprint for Maryland's Future goal of increasing access to high-quality early childhood education and growing the early childhood educator workforce.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided to the 24 local early childhood advisory councils throughout Maryland. Maximum award of $25,000 per applicant for the grant period (September 1, 2023 – June 30, 2024). Funding supports quality improvement work including membership building, professional development, program policy, and evaluation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31, 2023, no later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (ECACs) in Maryland, serving as governance and coordination bodies. Indirect beneficiaries include early childhood educators, teachers, staff at partnering agencies, council leadership, and the children and families they serve — including infants and toddlers (ages 0–3) and populations experiencing poverty, substance abuse/misuse, homelessness, housing instability, trauma, rural residence, special needs/disabilities, foster care, incarcerated caregivers, immigration, and multilingualism.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compiling data and conducting activities to assess local early childhood needs, identify collaboration opportunities and obstacles, and evaluate the capacity and effectiveness of local programs for developing early childhood educators. Also supports membership building, professional development, strategic planning, program policy, and evaluation within local ECACs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to the 24 local early childhood advisory councils throughout Maryland. Applicant must be the identified fiscal agent of a Local Early Childhood Advisory Council in the State of Maryland, as verified by the MSDE program manager. MSDE reserves the right to take into consideration geographic distribution when making awards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland EXCELS (Quality Rating and Improvement System with Additional Achievements)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS is a Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) for child care and early education programs across Maryland, including early childhood, school-age, and public prekindergarten programs. Using nationally recognized standards and best practices, the program assigns participating providers a quality rating from 1 to 5 based on standards in areas such as developmentally appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. Providers upload evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into an online system and receive ratings for each standard area and an overall rating. The program provides a road map, training, technical assistance, and incentives to support continuous quality improvement, along with guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist (QAS) who provides on-site and virtual training and Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) visits. Providers are also assigned a Program Coordinator for consultation and rating document review, and have access to the Maryland EXCELS Toolkit and connections to the Maryland Child Care Resource Network. Virtual training sessions are approved by MSDE's Office of Child Care and offer Core of Knowledge hours and certificates. Rated programs are eligible for Child Care Scholarship (subsidy) reimbursement, and providers serving families who use Child Care Scholarships are required to participate. Maryland EXCELS also recognizes programs that go above and beyond standard quality rating requirements through Additional Achievements — such as accreditation, asthma and allergy safety training, cultural and linguistic competency, eco-friendly practices, family engagement, health and wellness, Judy Center partnerships, military child care participation, and quality business practices — awarding public recognition badges displayed in the Maryland EXCELS Find a Program Directory. The published quality rating helps families make informed child care decisions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive a quality rating (1–5), guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist (QAS) for on-site and virtual support, a Program Coordinator for consultation and rating document review, Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) visits, virtual training sessions (MSDE Office of Child Care approved, with Core of Knowledge hours and certificates), access to the Maryland EXCELS Toolkit and Child Care Resource Centers statewide, and professional development resources to support continuous quality improvement based on nationally recognized standards. Rated programs are also eligible for Child Care Scholarship (subsidy) reimbursement. Programs that earn Additional Achievements receive recognition badges displayed publicly in the Maryland EXCELS online directory across categories including accreditation, asthma and allergy safety, cultural and linguistic competency, eco-friendly practices, family engagement, health and wellness, Judy Center partnerships, military child care participation, and quality business practices. No direct financial award is provided for Additional Achievements; the benefit is public recognition and credentialing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed Child Care Centers (including School-Age Only and Letter of Compliance programs), registered Family Child Care Homes, Head Start programs, Public Prekindergarten programs, and other early childhood and school-age child care programs in Maryland. Programs serving families who use Child Care Scholarships are required to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving the quality of child care and early education services through training, technical assistance, professional development, enhanced practices, family engagement supports, Continuous Quality Improvement visits, Program Coordinator guidance, and eligibility for Child Care Scholarship reimbursement. The Additional Achievements component supports public recognition and credentialing for programs that exceed standard quality requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all licensed and registered child care and early education programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in or create a user account at excels.marylandexcels.org (or sign up at marylandexcels.org), then complete a program application online. A step-by-step tutorial is available on the site. The 12-step online application process includes account creation, program lookup by license/registration/school ID, and application submission; applications are reviewed within 30 days of submission. Providers work with a regional Quality Assurance Specialist to create and upload evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into the online system. Evidence is reviewed and a rating is assigned for each standard area and overall. Upon acceptance, a Program Coordinator is assigned. Training sessions are announced via monthly emails to Maryland EXCELS participants. For Additional Achievements, complete the requirements specific to each achievement (trainings, applications, or program participation). Email your assigned Program Coordinator or info@marylandexcels.org for guidance on specific requirements. Some achievements require submitting an application form to MarylandExcels.msde@maryland.gov. To access and download Additional Achievement badges after earning them, log in to excels.marylandexcels.org, select Program Menu, then Certificate and Badge, and View and Download Additional Achievement Badge(s); extract the zip file to display badges on your website, social media, newsletters, and communications. Technology support is available 24/7 at 443-872-9250. Visit the 'Learn More About Participating' page at marylandexcels.org/commitment-to-quality/participate/ for additional details on how to join.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds local education agencies (LEAs) and private providers to deliver high-quality, full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). The program supports The Blueprint for Maryland's Future by broadening access to quality early childhood education across the state, and also supports capacity building for prekindergarten programs statewide. Technical assistance webinars are available in English and Spanish to help applicants understand the application process, program requirements, and eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for eligible providers to administer high-quality prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services, as well as capacity building for prekindergarten programs. Total available funding is approximately $26,644,000, with an estimated average award of $400,000 and approximately 50 awards. Per-slot funding is $19,950 per full-day slot for 3- and 4-year-olds. Eligible applicants include Local School Systems (LSSs), qualified vendors as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02, and private providers that hold a valid license or registration or are Head Start programs. Nonprofit indirect cost rate is 15% (effective July 1, 2025). A 20% advance payment option is available. Specific award amounts vary by grant cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSSs), qualified vendors, and private providers (including Head Start programs, licensed child care centers, Montessori programs, and family child care providers) that deliver prekindergarten services to three- and four-year-old children from low- to moderate-income families, including children with IEPs/IFSPs, multilingual learners, and children experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivering high-quality, full-day prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, as well as capacity building and expansion of prekindergarten programs. Allowable costs include lead teacher and assistant teacher salaries, professional development (20-hour minimum for teachers), curriculum and high-quality instructional materials (HQIM), classroom setup, contracted services (e.g., music therapy, health screenings, specialists), family engagement and support services, and quality rating/improvement activities. For Head Start programs: extended hours/days, additional services, quality enhancements, and teacher salary increases. Tuition is not an allowable cost.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. No county, municipality, or regional restrictions. MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making awards, with priority to areas of the state that have unmet need for Pre-K services.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the FY27 Grant Information Guide released January 21, 2026. Attend optional customer service support sessions or office hours for guidance. Technical assistance webinars are available in English and Spanish to walk applicants through the application process and program requirements. Complete and submit the grant application via the Qualtrics online portal (https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C). The application has four sections: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application, and Appendices. There are two application pathways (Modified vs. Full) based on Blueprint funding status. Applications undergo a two-part review: pre-screening for completeness, then committee scoring (80-point minimum required). Award notifications were made on approximately April 24, 2026. Supporting documentation (Appendices A–L) is required. FAQ will be posted to the Prekindergarten webpage following customer service support sessions. Full opportunity documents are available on the MSDE Office of Grants Administration and Compliance website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ready for Kindergarten (R4K) Grant, administered by the Division of Early Childhood at the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), provides funding to Local School Systems (LSSs) to support professional learning initiatives, the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for a coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment process, and accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program. Grant funds must be used to support continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten, including assessment administration fidelity, professional development for assessment reliability, data-based instructional decision-making, and research-based content and pedagogical best practices.

structured_extraction.program_name: IDEA Part B Grants for Local Education Agencies (LEA) and Public Agencies (PA) — Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) Part B grants require each Maryland local education agency (LEA) and public agency (PA) to submit an annual Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF) to receive and expend federal funds supporting special education services. These funds help LEAs and PAs provide a free appropriate public education (FAPE) to children and students with disabilities. The program covers IDEA Part B 611 (school-age) and 619 (preschool) funds. Recipients must submit applications, budgets, and post-application documents via the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site. LEAs required to address Significant Disproportionality must reserve 15% of Part B 611 and 619 funds for Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS). All applications, budgets, and post-application submissions must comply with applicable programmatic and fiscal regulations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal IDEA Part B funds are allocated to LEAs and PAs to support special education programs. LEAs required to address Significant Disproportionality must reserve 15% of Part B 611 and 619 funds for Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) and Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP) directs a family-centered system of early intervention services for young children (birth through age two, with an extended option through age three or beyond) who have developmental delays or disabilities. The program assists families by providing support, information, and coordinated services in community settings through 24 Local Infants and Toddlers Programs (LITPs) across Maryland. Services may include audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, transportation, speech-language pathology, family training, special instruction, assistive technology, health services, and home visits. The program also offers Maryland's Extended IFSP (Individualized Family Service Plan) Option, which allows eligible families to remain on an IFSP beyond their child's third birthday. The Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG) is the mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement these local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities, in compliance with IDEA Part C requirements. The designated Local Lead Agency (LLA) of each Local Infants & Toddlers Program aggregates information from partner agencies to complete the grant application and required submissions throughout the grant period. Grant funds are subject to budget submissions, reporting requirements, and compliance with federal and state regulations, with the grant period aligning with the state fiscal year (SFY). All evaluations and services are free to families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For families: Coordinated early intervention services delivered through 24 Local Infants and Toddlers Programs (LITPs) across Maryland, including audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, transportation, speech-language pathology, family training, special instruction, assistive technology, health services, and home visits. An Extended IFSP Option is available for families whose child is eligible for preschool special education beyond age three. All evaluations and services are free to families. For Local Lead Agencies: Federal and state funds are distributed via the CLIG to Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs to support implementation of early intervention services. Grant funds are subject to budget submissions, reporting requirements, and compliance with federal and state regulations. Recipients must submit a CLIG application, budget, and required reporting throughout the grant period via the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site. For SFY 2027, required documents include the CLIG Application, Budget Submissions Workbook, Linking Funds to Program Improvement Chart, Recipient Assurances, Federal Assurances, and GEPA Statement.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Two audiences: (1) Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITPs) in Maryland, including LEAs and non-LEA/PA grantees responsible for implementing early intervention services under IDEA Part C, across all Maryland local jurisdictions; and (2) Families of children with developmental delays, disabilities, or diagnosed physical or mental conditions that have a high probability of resulting in developmental delay, from birth through age two (or beyond via the Extended IFSP Option). Anyone can make a referral for a child.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures. Services include audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, family training, special instruction, assistive technology, health services, and home visits. For families, services also include free developmental screening, evaluation, in-home coaching, therapist/provider support, skill development, and community resource connection. Funds may also support direct early intervention services (salaries/fringe, contracted services, equipment, supplies, training, travel), family support and engagement, transition services (ages 3–K), evidence-based practice implementation and professional development, and Medicaid-related activities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Local Lead Agencies (CLIG): Download all required forms (CLIG Grant Information Guide, CLIG Application, Budget Submissions Workbook, Linking Funds to Program Improvement Chart, Recipient Assurances, Federal Certifications, GEPA Statement, and other documents) from the MSDE website just before completing them. Complete and upload all submissions to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (https://msde.sftp.md.gov/) following the published submission procedures and naming requirements. Follow the timeline for application submissions, budget amendments, invoicing, and reporting throughout the grant period. Award notification is within 30 days of deadline; Notice of Grant Award (NOGA) issued within 3 weeks of approval letter. Late applications may be reviewed on a rolling basis, subject to MSDE approval and availability of funds. For Families: (1) Submit referral online at referral.mditp.org or call 1-800-535-0182 or contact your county's Local Infants and Toddlers Program directly; (2) local program contacts family; (3) developmental evaluation scheduled at home or preferred location; (4) if eligible, family joins early intervention team to develop an individualized plan. All evaluations and services are free.

structured_extraction.program_description: CAP advocates for the rights of individuals with disabilities who are applying for or receiving services from Maryland's Centers for Independent Living (CILs) or the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). CAP provides free information, advice, and advocacy to help resolve concerns about vocational rehabilitation (VR) employment services, Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS), and independent living (IL) services. CAP can explain your rights, help communicate concerns to DORS or CIL staff, advocate if a service is denied, and arrange legal services for formal appeals when necessary. CAP specialists can assist with writing formal appeal requests. Optional mediation is available if both parties agree. Formal hearings are held within 60 days before an Administrative Law Judge through the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free information, advice, and advocacy services for individuals with disabilities. Services include explaining rights and responsibilities, helping communicate concerns to DORS or CIL staff, advocating for denied or disputed services, and arranging legal representation for formal appeals when necessary. CAP specialists can assist with writing formal appeal requests. Optional mediation is available if both parties agree. Formal hearings are held within 60 days before an Administrative Law Judge through the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who are applying for or receiving vocational rehabilitation, Pre-Employment Transition Services, or independent living services from DORS or Centers for Independent Living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advocacy and information services to resolve concerns about VR, Pre-ETS, and IL services received from DORS or CILs. Services include rights explanation, communication support, policy guidance, service denial advocacy, legal representation in appeals, and ADA employment rights information.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to citizens of Maryland with disabilities. Seven Centers for Independent Living (CILs) serve all of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability
Must be applying for or receiving services from DORS or a Maryland Center for Independent Living (CIL)
To file a formal appeal, a written request must be submitted within 60 days of the DORS decision or action being disputed

Written appeal request must include: the action/decision being appealed, a brief statement of reasons, the requested response from DORS, a signature (applicant or authorized representative), and contact information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact CAP by phone at 410-554-9361 or toll-free 1-800-638-6243, by fax at 410-554-9362, or by email at cap.dors@maryland.gov. To file a formal appeal, submit a written request within 60 days of the DORS decision to: Assistant State Superintendent in Rehabilitation Services, DORS, 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218, or by email at dors@maryland.gov. The written request must include the action/decision being appealed, a brief statement of reasons, the requested response from DORS, a signature, and contact information. CAP specialists are available to assist with writing the appeal. The request will be acknowledged in writing and a hearing will be scheduled through the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) within 60 days before an Administrative Law Judge. Optional mediation is available prior to a formal hearing if both parties agree.

structured_extraction.program_description: CCEIS requires local education agencies (LEAs) identified by Maryland as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or disciplinary actions to reserve 15% of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds. These funds must be used to implement a comprehensive system of proactive and responsive actions addressing the root causes of overidentification. Funded activities include educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports (including evidence-based literacy instruction and academic and behavioral interventions), as well as professional development for general and special education staff on implicit bias and equitable practices. Funds are subject to non-supplant requirements per 34 CFR §300.202(a)(3).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Special Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Identified LEAs must set aside 15% of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 federal funds to implement CCEIS plans. Funds may be used for educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports (including evidence-based literacy instruction), professional development, and other activities that address root causes of disproportionality in special education identification, placement, and disciplinary removals. Non-supplant compliance required per 34 CFR §300.202(a)(3).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (LEAs) in Maryland identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or disciplinary actions under IDEA Section 618(d).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports; evidence-based literacy instruction; evidence-based academic and behavioral interventions; professional development on implicit bias and equitable practices; addressing policies, practices, or procedures contributing to overidentification; building systemic awareness and leadership capacity; data review and root cause analysis; progress monitoring and evaluation systems. Funds are subject to non-supplant requirements (34 CFR §300.202).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to identified LEAs statewide in Maryland. Only LEAs flagged for significant disproportionality (risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in at least one racial/ethnic subgroup for identification, placement, or disciplinary actions per 34 CFR §300.646) are required to participate.
requirements_list: LEA must be identified by the State as having significant disproportionality (a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in at least one racial/ethnic subgroup for identification, placement, or disciplinary actions)
Must reserve 15% of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for CCEIS activities
Must implement a comprehensive plan addressing root cause factors
Must convene a local implementation team and a diverse stakeholder group
Must complete a self-assessment/data review process
Must develop a comprehensive evaluation plan emphasizing fidelity of implementation and measurable student outcomes
Must align expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root cause factors
Must comply with non-supplant requirements per 34 CFR §300.202(a)(3)
Must submit interim and final progress/cumulative variance reports per program schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Identified LEAs must develop and submit a CCEIS Plan using the SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan Template, along with the C-1-25 Budget Detail form. Plans are reviewed using the CCEIS Plan Review and Feedback Tool. Contact Interagency Equity Specialist Demetria White at demetria.white@maryland.gov for a copy of the review tool. Amendments to the plan (programmatic or fiscal) may be submitted using the provided amendment templates. Grantees must submit Interim Progress/Cumulative Variance Reports (due January 31 of each year) and a Final Progress/Cumulative Variance Report and Final Financial Report (due November 30 following grant period end). Grant amendment requests are due by August 15.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank

Families may borrow hearing aids for up to one year if they lack insurance coverage or are experiencing delays acquiring hearing aids. The loan bank also provides videos and links to help families learn their chosen language or communication method.
