structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) Scholarship
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) is a tuition assistance program for child care providers and staff in Maryland to earn a college degree at participating accredited colleges and universities. Funding covers tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Payments are made directly to the college or university — recipients are not reimbursed. Participants must be enrolled in or working toward eligibility through the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher. The program also provides grant funding to child care providers to support professional development activities in the early childhood care field.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of Child Care
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition, fees, and required textbooks paid directly to participating Maryland colleges and universities on behalf of eligible child care providers pursuing degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Funds are not paid as reimbursements to participants. Upon degree completion, recipients must fulfill a service commitment: 2 years (associate's), 4 years (bachelor's), or 2.5 years (master's) at minimum 20 hours/week in the child care field. MSDE notifies applicants of whether they have received fund approval. Additionally, grant funding is available for child care providers to support professional development activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications due March 1; continuation and transfer applications due June 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care professionals who participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential program at Level Two or higher, including licensed child care center workers and registered family child care providers in Maryland, seeking to earn a college degree or pursue professional development in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at participating accredited Maryland colleges and universities; professional development activities for child care providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland. Preferred institutions are those marked with an asterisk (*) as CCCPDF participants.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider or staff member participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher
Work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland, working at least 20 hours per week during coursework
Must pursue a degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
Must attend an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Preferred institutions are those marked with an asterisk (*) as CCCPDF participants
Meet entrance requirements at a participating college
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Maintain employment in child care in Maryland throughout the program
Participate in professional development
Service commitment upon degree completion: 2 years (associate's), 4 years (bachelor's), or 2.5 years (master's) at minimum 20 hours/week in child care field
Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative GPA from the point of first entering the program
Submit annual continuation application with required documentation
Provide letter of acceptance from participating college/university with declared major
Provide professional development plan with course timeline
Provide current employment verification or Family Child Care license
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact a participating college from the Participating Colleges directory. structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development and recognition program for individual child care workers in Maryland that supports career advancement and recognizes providers who go above and beyond the minimum state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience. Participants progress through seven staff credential levels or four administrator levels and earn achievement bonuses and other incentives as they advance. The program aims to develop a professional early childhood workforce, improve provider compensation, and provide a structure for career growth.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses ranging from $200–$1,500 upon reaching Credential Level 2 or higher, paid directly to the individual. All participants may apply for tuition assistance for approved college or university programs through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF). The program also provides voluntary credential recognition for providers who meet elevated training, education, and experience standards. Credentials are issued for 12-month periods and are renewable.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides eligible Maryland child care providers with up to $400 per year to cover the cost of approved training. structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) is a federally funded, state-administered program that reimburses organizations (sponsors) who serve free, healthy meals to children and teens age 18 and younger in low-income areas during the summer months when school is not in session. Funded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) through the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs, the program is administered locally by county-level sponsoring organizations—typically county public school systems or, in Baltimore City, the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). Non-profit organizations, churches, day camps, community groups, city agencies, and qualifying for-profit entities can apply to become meal-serving sites. Two meal delivery options are available: SUN Meals (on-site consumption) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes picked up and taken home). The 2026 Baltimore City program runs Monday through Friday, June 17 through August 22.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal reimbursement is provided to sponsoring organizations that serve free, nutritious meals (breakfasts and lunches) to children and teens age 18 and younger in low-income areas during the summer. Sponsors receive per-meal reimbursements for qualifying meals served. In Baltimore City, approved sites receive free meals to distribute to eligible youth ages 18 and under, with sites required to plan to serve a minimum of 10 eligible youth for at least two weeks. Organizations wanting to participate as a meal site must contact their county's sponsoring organization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, churches, day camps, community groups, city agencies, and qualifying for-profit entities seeking to become SUN Meals sites and serve free meals to children and teens age 18 and younger during summer months; children and teens in low-income areas who need free meals when school is out.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free, nutritious meals (breakfasts, lunches, and snacks) to children and teens age 18 and younger in low-income areas during summer months when school is not in session.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Each county has a designated sponsoring organization. Sites must be located in or serve low-income areas. In Baltimore City, sites must be located within the city; private homes and public school buildings are not eligible.

Must operate under a sponsoring organization for the county
SUN Meals sites must serve meals on-site
SUN Meals To-Go sites provide multi-day meal boxes; registration required for participants
Baltimore City sites must plan to receive meals for a minimum of two weeks and serve at least 10 eligible youth ages 18 or younger
Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible (Baltimore City)
Sites requesting breakfast must have adequate refrigeration to store perishables overnight
Sites are subject to a pre-operational inspection and must be approved by program staff
The site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend a mandatory 3-hour training session
Sites must agree to serve all meals in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations wishing to become a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization for their county using the contact information listed on the MSDE program page. Each county has a designated sponsoring organization (typically the county public school system or, in Baltimore City, the Department of Housing and Community Development). In Baltimore City, organizations can apply online via the SFSP website or download and mail a paper application to the Summer Food Service Program at 1135 N. Gilmor Street, 2nd Floor, Baltimore, MD 21217.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) - Safe Routes to School
structured_extraction.program_description: TAP is a competitively selected, federally funded reimbursement program administered by the Maryland State Highway Administration (SHA). Through TAP, Safe Routes to School (SRTS) projects and initiatives support the planning, development, and implementation of projects and activities that improve safety and reduce traffic around schools. TAP funds cover 80% of eligible project costs and require a 20% local match.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federally funded, competitively selected reimbursement grants covering 80% of eligible project costs. A 20% local match is required. Eligible projects include feasibility studies, design projects, construction projects, and safety awareness and program coordination projects. Non-infrastructure activities such as education materials, promotional/outreach materials, and behavioral studies are also eligible. Projects must be located within approximately 2 miles of a school serving grades K–12. The application window is announced by MDOT yearly and usually occurs in the Spring.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Announced by MDOT yearly; usually occurs in the Spring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, schools, non-profit organizations, community organizations, regional transportation agencies, and county-wide SRTS coordinators seeking to improve safety and reduce traffic around schools through planning, design, construction, or safety awareness projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Feasibility studies, design projects, construction projects, and safety awareness and program coordination projects related to Safe Routes to School. Also eligible: non-infrastructure activities including education materials, promotional/outreach materials, and behavioral studies. Projects must be within approximately 2 miles of a school serving grades K–12.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Program operates at the county level via SRTS coordinators across all 24 Maryland local education authority (LEA) jurisdictions. Individual projects must be within approximately 2 miles of a school.
requirements_list: Projects must relate to improving safety and reducing traffic around schools
Applicants must provide a 20% local match
Projects are competitively selected
Project must be located within approximately 2 miles of a school
Schools served must be grades K–12
When seeking construction funds, applicants must comply with the Safe Walk to Schools Act (2022 HB 19), which requires a Pedestrian Safety Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application window is announced by MDOT yearly and usually occurs in the Spring. The program uses a competitive award process. Contact the SHA Grants and Programs Management Division or MDOT Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility (completestreets@mdot.maryland.gov) for application details and to confirm current NOFA/NOFO cycle status.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual collegiate competition hosted by the Maryland Sustainable Growth Commission that engages students from Maryland's higher education institutions in planning, sustainability, and reinvestment issues. Students submit work completed during the academic year for consideration; finalists present their projects to the Commission. The competition enables students to conduct community planning exercises, analyze economic, social, and environmental aspects of sustainable growth, and develop creative community solutions. Projects must advance at least one of Maryland's Twelve Planning Visions and may focus on areas such as redevelopment of vacant lots, community charrettes, green infrastructure, public access, and coastal issues using a triple-bottom-line sustainability framework (economic, environmental, social justice).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recognition and awards for winning student submissions through a competitive annual challenge. Students interact with local leaders and engage in community planning processes. Winners receive recognition, a speaking/presentation opportunity at a statewide conference, and institutional promotion. No specific financial award amount is stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and/or graduate students in planning, architecture, engineering, or sustainability-focused concentrations, and faculty advisors, from Maryland institutions of higher learning working on planning, sustainability, and community reinvestment topics.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a competition providing recognition for student work on sustainable growth and community planning topics. Projects must advance at least one of Maryland's Twelve Planning Visions and may focus on areas such as redevelopment of vacant lots, community charrettes, green infrastructure, public access, and coastal issues using a triple-bottom-line sustainability framework (economic, environmental, social justice).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students and faculty from all Maryland institutions of higher learning. Projects should focus on Maryland's communities.
requirements_list: Work must be completed during a 2019 semester (for the 2019-20 cycle)
Submission must include a completed submission form, final student report/plan/project, and a 250–500 word description of how the project advances Maryland's Twelve Planning Visions
Submissions due January 17, 2020
Finalists must prepare for a Presentation Day scheduled for winter 2020
Eligible students must be in planning, architecture, engineering, or related subjects at a Maryland college or university
Project must advance at least one of Maryland's Twelve Planning Visions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed submission form along with a final student report, plan, or project and a 250–500 word project description to Joe Griffiths at Joseph.Griffiths@maryland.gov (or call 410-767-4553 if the file is too large to email). Final proposals are submitted to the Maryland Sustainable Growth Commission in Annapolis. Finalists are then scheduled for a Presentation Day in winter 2020, where they present to a judging panel of leaders in sustainable planning.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created to assist Maryland's rural and agricultural businesses negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and associated economic downturn. The program funds technology-empowered initiatives that help rural and agricultural businesses recover, rebuild, and pivot from the economic crisis. It encourages collaboration between rural businesses, research institutions, and industry partners. Example projects include development of an innovative product or a novel application of an existing technology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $200,000 per project for a period of one year. Funded through the Maryland RELIEF Act of 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland rural and agricultural businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology-empowered initiatives to help rural and agricultural businesses recover, rebuild, and pivot from the COVID-19 economic crisis, including development of innovative products or novel applications of existing technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland rural and agricultural businesses

Must have been detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and associated economic downturn
Projects must be technology-empowered initiatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are now closed. The program issued a Request for Applications (RFA) outlining eligibility requirements, funding structure, and review criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Innovation Initiative (BII) Pilot Program supports an equitable innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem at institutions of higher education in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA). As part of Maryland's matching contribution toward the Baltimore Tech Hub, BII funds two grant tracks: (1) Technology Advancement grants to help commercialize new or existing technology and support startup creation, and (2) Entrepreneurship Commercialization, Programming, and Infrastructure grants to create or enhance entrepreneurship programs and commercialization infrastructure for technology-based ventures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant tracks are available: (1) Technology Advancement grants up to $50,000 for individual applicants (up to $75,000 for joint applications by two or more qualifying universities), lasting up to 9 months; and (2) Entrepreneurship Commercialization, Programming, and Infrastructure grants up to $50,000, lasting up to 12 months. Technology-based startups collaborating with faculty, students, or staff at BII-participating institutions may also apply for Technology Advancement grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faculty, students, staff, and technology-based startups affiliated with eligible institutions of higher education in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson MSA
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology commercialization, startup creation, and development or enhancement of entrepreneurship programs and commercialization infrastructure at eligible institutions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible institutions must be located in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA)

Institution must formally opt in to participate in BII
Only collaborating organizations can submit project proposals
Applicants must engage with an onsite Project Lead at least 30 days before application submission
Application must include a current, dated letter of approval signed by the onsite Project Lead
Full-time faculty at MII-Qualifying Universities are not eligible to serve as lead applicants for a BII Technology Advancement Grant
Technology-based startups must collaborate with faculty, students, or staff from BII-participating institutions
Project proposals must either advance technology commercialization and support startup creation, or foster entrepreneurship development at the eligible university
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications follow a two-step process: (1) Submit an Indication of Interest (IOI) form; BII staff review for eligibility and issue a full application invitation within approximately two weeks. (2) After IOI acceptance, applicants receive a link to the full application portal and submit a complete application by the deadline. Applicants must also meet with an onsite Project Lead at least 30 days before submission and obtain a signed letter of approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Business Resource Information, Development, and Guidance Ecosystem (BRIDGE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BRIDGE Program provides legal, accounting, and financial advisory services to Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI)-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) connected to the federal technology commercialization ecosystem. The program offers resources and support to help disadvantaged individuals and very small businesses grow across the Mid-Atlantic region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Legal, accounting, and financial advisory services provided to eligible SEDI-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs), along with broader business resources and support to help disadvantaged individuals and very small businesses grow.

structured_extraction.program_description: Concept Capital is TEDCO's initiative to bridge the early-stage funding gap for underrepresented entrepreneurs across Maryland. The program provides flexible funding and specialized support to founders who are socially and economically disadvantaged or rural-based. Funding is provided as convertible notes ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 with zero interest, zero discount, and negotiable valuation caps. Eligible founders may also access mentoring, advisory services, advanced software for performance tracking, and tailored guidance to achieve critical venture milestones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Convertible notes ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 with zero interest, zero discount, and negotiable valuation caps. Beyond funding, eligible founders may access one-on-one mentoring and advisory services, advanced software for performance tracking and investment-readiness, and tailored guidance to achieve critical venture milestones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (including minority, disabled, or female founders) and rural-based founders in Maryland with technology-driven businesses founded within the last 7 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early-stage venture funding for technology-driven businesses to prepare for future venture opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based business required — principal office in Maryland with 51%+ of workforce in-state. Founder or business must be located in a rural or disadvantaged community, or founder must be a socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI).

Technology-driven business (non-retail focus)
Founded within the last 7 years
Founder or business located in a rural or disadvantaged community, OR founder is a socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) — including minority, disabled, or female founders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications will reopen in 2027. Entrepreneurs receive mentorship through RBII or UBII initiatives before applying for Concept Capital funding; advisory support is provided before and after funding. Apply through TEDCO's platform (MyTEDCO). Eligible startups may apply for convertible notes ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 based on eligibility criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Equitech Growth Fund (EGF), managed by TEDCO, provides grants for infrastructure and workforce development initiatives that support Maryland's economic competitiveness, foster economic opportunity for all, and accelerate growth of emerging and advanced industries. The goal is to position Maryland as a leading global and inclusive innovation economy by 2040. Two award tracks are available: Infrastructure Awards (up to $1M, 12–36 month projects) and Workforce Awards (up to $250K, 12–24 month projects). Subject to availability of funding, TEDCO accepts applications once a year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Infrastructure Awards of up to $1M per project (1–3 awards expected, ~$3M total annual pool, project duration 12–36 months) and Workforce Awards of up to $250K per project (8–10 awards expected, ~$2M total annual pool, project duration 12–24 months) are available as grants for eligible entities. Award proceeds and any leveraged funds must be used within the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 7, 2026, at 5:00 pm ET; questions due July 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public entities, nonprofits, private entities, public-private partnerships, and higher education institutions in Maryland working on infrastructure or workforce development in emerging and advanced industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure development and workforce development initiatives that support Maryland's innovation economy, including entrepreneurship development, STEM education, advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity and IT workforce development, advanced technology, and advanced laboratory space. Award proceeds and leveraged funds must be used in the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Proposed projects must be based in Maryland and benefit Maryland's innovation economy and workforce. Applicants must intend to maintain a physical presence in Maryland for at least 5 years and must use award proceeds and leveraged funds within Maryland. Multi-county projects are allowed. Preference given to proposals with greatest impact in Maryland, including economically distressed or rural areas.

Annual impact reports required for 5 years following project completion detailing fund usage, progress, and economic impact on Maryland economy, jobs, and innovation
Confidential information submitted must be marked 'Business Proprietary'
Letters of Commitment from matching-fund partners must be submitted with application
Multiple applications are permitted if for distinct projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply via the online Jotform portal at https://www.tedcomd.com/funding/cultivate-maryland. Submit questions to equitechgrowth@tedcomd.com by July 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET; answers will be posted on the program website by July 31, 2026. Informational webinars are offered (April 16, June 11, and July 23, 2026, 11 am–12 pm EST). Applications are reviewed in a multi-stage process: (1) Compliance Review (eligibility screening), (2) Screening Review (material completeness), (3) Detailed Review (scored by staff and external reviewers on 6 criteria, scale 1–5), (4) Due Diligence (verification, virtual meetings, documentation), and (5) Final Decision (CEO approval and notification). Finalists may be required to attend a virtual interview on or near the week of September 7, 2026. An FAQ document is available on the landing page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Labs Leveraging Innovation to Products (FLLIP) Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: FLLIP connects Maryland entrepreneurs and small businesses with federal laboratory resources to bridge the gap between public research and commercial success. The program uses a structured CASE approach (Connection, Assessment, Support, and Engagement) to provide education, expert guidance, matchmaking, and technical assistance for working with federal labs such as NIH, Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research, and the Defense Health Agency. It particularly focuses on health and medical businesses, including those that are underrepresented.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides technical assistance, market research, patent strategy support, matchmaking with federal lab scientists, lab tours, and facilitation of formal agreements between businesses and federal laboratory partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland entrepreneurs and small businesses, particularly small innovative medical or health-related businesses, including those traditionally underrepresented
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and support to pursue working relationships with federal labs; technical assistance, market research, patent strategy, and facilitation of formal agreements with federal lab partners

Must be ready to engage with federal labs

structured_extraction.program_name: Institute for Women Entrepreneur Excellence (IWEE) – BRIDGE Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BRIDGE Program (Building Resources for Investment, Development, and Growth in Entrepreneurship) is a cohort-based initiative operated by TEDCO's Institute for Women Entrepreneur Excellence. It supports Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) entrepreneurs — with a focus on women — by providing technical knowledge, resources, and personalized guidance to help them access debt and equity capital. The eight-week hybrid program combines weekly expert-led workshops, one-on-one mentoring, and applied assignments covering financial literacy, strategic planning, and investor readiness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An eight-week hybrid program with weekly expert-led workshops (3 hours/week), one-on-one mentoring (1–2 hours/week) from subject-matter experts, and applied assignments such as drafting loan applications, refining pitch decks, and revising financial projections. Delivered in-person with a virtual (Zoom) option.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) entrepreneurs, with a focus on women business owners and founders in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants build skills in financial literacy, strategic planning, investor readiness, financial statement analysis, loan application preparation, and pitch deck development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Sessions take place at multiple in-person locations across the state.

Must complete the application form to be considered for participation
Selected applicants notified following review process

structured_extraction.program_name: Intellectual Property Management Platform by IPGen
structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO offers eligible Maryland-based entrepreneurs and start-up businesses a free, one-year subscription to IPGen's IP (intellectual property) software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform. The platform helps users manage the full lifecycle of IP processes — including searching, drafting, and prosecuting patents — using AI and machine learning tools, templates, automation, collaboration features, and status tracking. Users also receive up to two trademark support services until the trademark side of the platform is fully released. Upon request, the IPGen team provides a 30-minute onboarding session and at least two hours of hands-on practical support such as advice, guidance, and application review.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free one-year subscription to the IPGen IP SaaS platform (normally a paid service), plus up to two trademark support services, a 30-minute onboarding session, and at least two hours of practical hands-on support. Users must sign a terms of service agreement with IPGen before accessing the platform.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based entrepreneurs and start-up businesses seeking to manage intellectual property processes including patents and trademarks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to IP lifecycle management software tools (patent searching, drafting, prosecution, collaboration, status tracking) and practical support for navigating patent and trademark processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland-based entrepreneurs and start-up businesses.

Must execute a terms of service agreement with IPGen before using the platform
Must request access via the TEDCO/IPGen request form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request through the online form at the TEDCO/IPGen request access link. Once approved, the IPGen team will onboard the user to the platform.

structured_extraction.program_name: Leading Women's Program (Montgomery County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month hybrid (in-person and virtual) entrepreneur leadership development program for tech-based female founders, co-founders, and CEOs. The program builds critical skills that foster resilience, develops a peer advisor network, and creates a community of collaborative entrepreneurial leaders. It is primarily designed for Montgomery County-based business owners but may accept entrepreneurs from outside the county based on available slots.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-month hybrid training program with monthly in-person sessions at the Universities at Shady Grove in Rockville, MD, and monthly virtual sessions. Participants pay a $250 registration fee; $200 is refunded upon course completion. The program covers leadership and communication, real-world business perspectives, and development planning.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leadership and communication skills development, peer networking, business development planning, and entrepreneur resilience training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily for Montgomery County-based business owners; entrepreneurs outside Montgomery County may be considered based on available slots.

Must pay a $250 registration fee upon acceptance
May miss no more than two sessions to graduate

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO provides eligible entrepreneurs and early-stage technology companies with free access to the GlobalData market intelligence database for two months. This gives users access to tools such as GlobalData Explorer, Explorer AI Hub, Disruptor Intelligence Center, and its AI Hub — covering market trends, competitors, industry analysis, and emerging technologies. The program is designed to help entrepreneurs conduct secondary market research, develop business plans, and prepare funding applications for TEDCO programs or SBIR/STTR proposals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two months of complimentary access to GlobalData's market intelligence platform, including GlobalData Explorer, Explorer AI Hub, and the Disruptor Intelligence Center. Access is provided free of charge to eligible users on a case-by-case basis, virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs and early-stage technology companies with fewer than 16 full-time employees or less than $1,000,000 in total investment who want to conduct market research to support TEDCO funding applications, SBIR/STTR proposals, or who are already in a TEDCO program or portfolio.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to market intelligence tools for conducting secondary market research, analyzing competitors and industry trends, supporting business plan development, and preparing SBIR/STTR or TEDCO funding applications.

Must have fewer than 16 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees OR have received less than $1,000,000 in any investment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Global Data Database Request form online at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/98. Contact Julia Deng at jdeng@tedcomd.com with any questions. Access is granted on a case-by-case basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DefTech Center is a joint initiative between TEDCO, the Maryland Department of Commerce, and the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) that helps entrepreneurs, technology companies, and DoD lab personnel commercialize defense technologies developed at Department of Defense labs in Maryland (NSA/Fort Meade, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Ft. Detrick, and others). Member companies developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using federal laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, and expertise receive proprietary professional services including access to technical experts, IP and technology due diligence, business support, research tools, credentialed training on technology transfer and government contracting, private DoD lab engagements, and monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors. The program also provides networking, education on IP and patent law, market-oriented product development, customer discovery, and one-on-one mentoring for licensing DoD technologies, market analysis, and commercialization planning. Membership is competitive with limited spots each year, focusing on high technology and bio innovation sectors. Established in 2018 as a pilot program in the APG community with DoD Office of Economic Adjustment funding, it expanded statewide in 2019 with U.S. Department of Commerce Economic Development Administration funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members receive proprietary professional services including: DefTech Academy & Certification (credentialed courses on technology transfer and government contracting), pre-lab engagement training, access to a monthly distribution of federal funding notices, private meetings with DoD federal labs, and monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors. Additionally, the program provides free technical assistance including guidance on navigating the DoD Technology Transfer (T2) process; networking with T2 staff, scientists, and engineers; education on topics such as IP and patent law, market-oriented product development, and customer discovery; and one-on-one mentoring for licensing DoD technologies, market analysis, and commercialization planning. Program costs are waived for the initial 30 companies in the first program year due to funding from the DoD Office of Local Community Cooperation (OLDCC), the Maryland Department of Commerce, and TEDCO.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs looking to commercialize DoD-developed technology, Maryland businesses developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using federal laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, and expertise, technology companies seeking to establish a presence in Maryland, and scientists or engineers working at DoD research labs in Maryland. Particular focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting businesses and entrepreneurs to federal labs for product development, testing, IP licensing, technology transfer education, market and tech assessments, access to federal funding opportunities, and commercialization planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland companies and entrepreneurs statewide, with focus on DoD labs in Maryland including NSA/Fort Meade, Aberdeen Proving Ground, and Ft. Detrick.
requirements_list: Must be an entrepreneur, technology company, DoD lab personnel, or business developing or interested in developing commercial products or services using federal laboratory IP, equipment, facilities, or expertise
Membership is highly competitive with limited spots each year
Focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors
Applicants undergo initial screening by a DefTech Advisor before online application
Accepted applicants are categorized as either resource-ready for immediate federal engagement or placed in preliminary training first
Interest in licensing or commercializing technology developed at a DoD research lab in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application following an initial screening by a DefTech Advisor. Accepted applicants are placed into one of two tracks: (1) resource-ready for immediate federal engagement and commencement of DefTech services, or (2) preliminary training followed by commencement of DefTech services. Alternatively, contact the program directly to learn more about Fort Meade technology transfer opportunities (www.deftechmd.com or info@deftechmd.com).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) promotes commercialization of research conducted at qualifying Maryland universities, administered by TEDCO. The program helps move promising technologies with significant commercial potential from university labs into the marketplace by funding technology validation, market assessment, and the creation of Maryland-based startup companies. MII operates in two phases: Technology Assessment/Technology Validation & Market Assessment (up to $130,000 for sole applicants or up to $180,000 for joint applications involving two or more qualifying universities, over 9 months) and Company Formation (up to $300,000 over 9 months, provided as a convertible debt note or revenue-based reimbursable grant, for startups that have licensed qualifying university technology). Qualifying universities include Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore (UMB), University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC), and University of Maryland College Park (UMCP). Applications are reviewed quarterly. The program requires applicants to engage with a Site Miner prior to submission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: (1) Technology Assessment/Validation & Market Assessment — up to $130,000 for a sole applicant or up to $180,000 for joint applications involving two or more qualifying universities, over a 9-month project period. (2) Company Formation — up to $300,000 over up to 9 months, structured as a convertible debt note (8% annual interest, 5-year term) OR a revenue-based reimbursable grant (3% quarterly revenue for 10 years). Indirect costs allowed up to 20% (up to $60K for startups; up to $30K for patent/licensing). Patent expenses capped at $12,500 for Technology Assessment track. Total potential funding is up to $430,000 across both phases for sole applicants. Companies must remain in Maryland or reimburse TEDCO the full amount plus interest from licensing revenue.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly deadlines: January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15 by 5:00pm (or first business day thereafter)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time faculty members at qualifying universities (Technology Assessment/Validation track) and Maryland-based startup companies that have licensed technology from a qualifying university within 12 months of applying (Company Formation track). Johns Hopkins faculty inventors with patent filings not yet licensed are also eligible for the Technology Validation track. Qualifying universities include Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, UMBC, and University of Maryland College Park.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology validation, market assessment, commercialization strategy, patent expense paydown (capped at $12,500 for Technology Assessment track), and startup company formation and commercial launch activities related to commercializing university-developed technologies. Allowable costs include personnel (salaries, fringe), equipment, materials and supplies, other direct costs (machining, subcontracts, patent expenses, tuition), and commercialization plan development (FDA/business consulting up to applicable limits, company formation up to $4,500, I-Corps up to $5,000). Indirect costs are explicitly prohibited for Technology Assessment track except patent expenses; indirect costs up to 20% allowed for Company Formation (up to $60,000 for startups; up to $30,000 for patent/licensing). Domestic travel allowed if justified; international travel is not allowable. Technologies must be owned by or disclosed to a qualifying university's technology transfer office with appropriate intellectual property protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be affiliated with one of the five qualifying universities: Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore (UMB), University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC), or University of Maryland College Park (UMCP). Company Formation applicants must be Maryland-based startups. Companies must remain in Maryland; if technology is licensed out of state, the university must repay TEDCO the full amount plus interest from licensing revenue.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Makerspace Initiative Program (Makerspace Program) supports the growth and development of Makerspaces throughout Maryland. It provides financial and technical assistance to local governments, entities designated by local governments, and nonprofit organizations seeking help with establishing, expanding, or operating Makerspaces. A Makerspace is defined as a community space that provides access to tools, technology, and knowledge for learners and entrepreneurs; results in the prototyping or creation of physical goods; and supports technical education opportunities for personal growth, workforce training, and early-stage business ventures. Technical assistance (up to 10 hours) is available from Open Works in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 are available for the establishment of a new Makerspace, the expansion of an existing Makerspace, or the development of programming for a Makerspace. A separate smaller grant of up to $25,000 is available for Makerspace programming. Applicants may apply for more than one grant type by submitting separate applications. A 1:1 match (cash or in-kind) is required; feasibility study applications require a cash match only (no in-kind contributions). Technical assistance of up to 10 hours is also available from Open Works (Baltimore City).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of a new Makerspace, expansion of an existing Makerspace, or development of programming for a Makerspace. Allowable expenses may include utility costs and third-party contracts, subject to reviewer evaluation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Applicants must be operating, or seeking to operate, a Makerspace in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the TEDCO JotForm application portal by May 15, 2026 at 5 PM ET. Upload all required documents, including a Letter of Intent for matching funds. Applications that advance to stage three of the review process may be asked to provide a presentation with additional information. The full review process takes up to 60 days from the application deadline. TEDCO runs one review cycle per year. Email questions to mmip@tedcomd.com or jferguson@tedcomd.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Stem Cell Research Fund (MSCRF) promotes state-funded human stem cell research and medical treatments by providing grants to public and private entities in Maryland. Established under the Maryland Stem Cell Research Act of 2006, MSCRF offers seven funding programs — Launch, Discovery, Validation, Commercialization, Clinical, Post-doctoral Fellowships, and Manufacturing Assistance — to accelerate research and commercialization of human stem cell-based technologies. MSCRF grants support young and established scientists, companies, and research organizations to advance innovative stem cell technologies for positive impact on human lives. Organizations and companies outside of Maryland are eligible to apply, provided that the research is conducted within the State. MSCRF also encourages collaborations between academia and industry; applicants forming a public-private partnership are eligible for an additional $100,000 above the maximum grant award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSCRF offers grants through seven programs: Launch, Discovery, Validation, Commercialization, Clinical, Post-doctoral Fellowships, and Manufacturing Assistance. Applicants forming a public-private partnership are eligible for an additional $100,000 above the maximum grant award amount. Grants are disbursed in tranches, with subsequent disbursements contingent on satisfactory annual reports. Annual reports are due 30 days before each anniversary; final report due 45 days after grant term end. Specific award amounts and terms for each program track are available on the MSCRF funding opportunities page at mscrf.org. Applications are submitted through TEDCO's MyTEDCO portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Scientists, companies, non-profit organizations, and public entities conducting human stem cell research, including those from outside Maryland provided the research is conducted within the State, at various stages from early discovery through clinical development and commercialization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Human stem cell research, medical treatment development, commercialization of stem cell-based technologies, post-doctoral fellowships, and manufacturing assistance. Research must be conducted within the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Research must be conducted within the State of Maryland; applicants may be located outside Maryland but must conduct their research within the State.

Grants are disbursed in tranches; subsequent disbursements are contingent on satisfactory annual reports due 30 days before each grant anniversary, with a final report due 45 days after the grant term ends.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO connects Maryland early-stage technology startups with a curated group of experienced business executives and entrepreneurs who serve as advisors. Advisors bring current, relevant expertise in specific areas to help startups grow. Entrepreneurs request an advisor through a form, and most advisory engagements are voluntary, with a few paid consulting roles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free (mostly volunteer) expert advisory services provided by experienced entrepreneurs and business executives. Advisors are matched to startups based on specific areas of need. Time commitment is up to 4 hours/month per advisor; initial meeting is typically 1 hour with follow-up at the advisor's discretion. A small number of engagements are paid consulting arrangements. No direct financial disbursement to startups.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland early-stage technology startup founders with 5–7 years or less operating history (exceptions for regulated industries and rural companies). Companies must be past the idea stage with demonstrated progress (e.g., prototype, customer discovery with 50+ interviews, revenue, funding, or patents). Must have a scalable business model in technology/innovation-driven sectors (industry-agnostic).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free, pro-bono executive-level advisory services providing strategic guidance, industry insights, and resource access to accelerate startup growth. Advisors assist with specific areas of need identified by the founder; no direct financial disbursement to startups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be headquartered in Maryland and intend to remain in Maryland. More than 50% of staff positions must be based in Maryland. Rural region companies may qualify for an extended operating period beyond the standard 5–7 year limit.
requirements_list: Company must be established and beyond the idea stage
Company must be technology-based
Company must be headquartered in Maryland and intend to remain in Maryland
More than 50% of staff positions must be based in Maryland
Operating history of 5–7 years or less (exceptions for regulated industries and rural companies)
Demonstrated progress such as prototype, customer discovery (50+ interviews), revenue, funding, or patents
Scalable business model in technology/innovation-driven sector
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Founder completes the Network Advisors Request Form on TEDCO's website. TEDCO reviews the request for clarity and scope, then conducts a curated search for matching advisors. The founder receives a prioritized list of potential advisors and TEDCO facilitates introductions. The typical initial meeting is 1 hour; follow-up engagement is discretionary. Due to high demand, response times may vary — refer to the request form for current timelines. Founders may re-apply after one month. Optionally, take the company stage assessment tool first to confirm eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Open Institute for Black Women Entrepreneur Excellence (Howard County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month hybrid entrepreneurship leadership development program for Black women business owners. TEDCO and Maryland's four HBCUs (Historically Black Colleges and Universities) bring together entrepreneurs in a cohort to build critical business skills, resilience, peer advisory networks, and collaborative community. Sessions cover leadership, communication, real-world business perspectives, and development planning. The program is designed primarily for Howard County-based business owners, though entrepreneurs outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay a $250 registration fee to join the 10-month program. If a participant completes the course, $200 of the fee is returned. The program consists of monthly in-person and virtual sessions held at the Maryland Innovation Center in Columbia, Maryland, covering leadership, communication, real-world business perspectives, and development planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black women entrepreneurs who are founders, co-founders, or CEOs of companies at pre-seed to growth stage (up to pre-Series A), primarily based in Howard County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers a portion of assessments in the prerequisite session. The program provides leadership development, entrepreneurship education, peer networking, and community building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designed for Howard County-based business owners; entrepreneurs outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots.

If a participant cancels after the cancellation date, the registration fee is forfeited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through TEDCO. The program is primarily for Howard County-based entrepreneurs, though outside applicants may be considered based on available slots.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Rural Business Innovation Initiative (RBII) assists small technology-based start-ups located in rural areas through mentoring and targeted projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mentoring and targeted project support for small technology-based start-ups in rural areas.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring and targeted projects to help rural start-ups advance toward key milestones

Located in a rural area

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural and Underserved Business Recovery from Impact of COVID-19 (RUBRIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: The RUBRIC program is a state emergency economic relief initiative that provided grants to socially and economically disadvantaged and rural early-stage technology-based businesses in Maryland that were hardest hit by the COVID-19 pandemic. TEDCO administered $5 million in state funds to help bridge-fund companies with the highest barriers to traditional financing so they could survive the economic downturn and continue toward the next phase of fundraising.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 were awarded to qualifying early-stage technology-based businesses impacted by COVID-19. Funds were intended as bridge funding to help companies survive the downturn and prepare for the next stage of fundraising.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and economically disadvantaged and rural early-stage technology-based businesses in Maryland that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding to help early-stage companies survive the COVID-19 economic downturn and scale to the next phase of fundraising.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

Must be socially and economically disadvantaged or located in a rural area

Questions were directed to Rubric@tedco.md.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBIR/STTR Matching Funds Program (TEDCO State Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive program that provides matching funds to Maryland small businesses that have received federal SBIR (Small Business Innovation Research) or STTR (Small Business Technology Transfer) awards. The program aims to strengthen SBIR/STTR awards, foster job creation and economic development, promote commercialization of research, facilitate technology transfer from universities and federal labs, and encourage small businesses — including economically disadvantaged ones — to pursue federal SBIR/STTR funding, advancing their R&D commercialization efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For Phase I SBIR/STTR awards: TEDCO can grant an additional award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase I award or $25,000. For Phase II SBIR/STTR awards: TEDCO can grant an award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase II award or $75,000. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis, subject to availability of funds. Awards are executed via a grant agreement. Recipients are required to submit economic impact reports every year for a period of 5 years following the award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly deadlines at 5:00 pm ET: March 30, June 30, September 30, December 31 each year (if a deadline falls on a weekend or Maryland State holiday, the effective date is the next non-holiday weekday). Current cycle: April 1 – June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses (fewer than 250 employees) in technology or life sciences that have received a federal SBIR or STTR award within six months of the application cycle. Businesses primarily engaged in retail, real estate, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services (accountants, attorneys, physicians) are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercialization of research conducted by small businesses; technology transfer from universities and federal labs to small businesses; advancing federally-funded R&D projects toward commercialization
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses operating in Maryland. Over half of the applicant's workforce must work at and from a physical location in Maryland, and principal business operations must be conducted from a physical location in Maryland.

Applicants will receive a confirmation email upon submission. Contact sbir-ta@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt if needed. Refer to the RFA document for complete program details.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's SBIR/STTR Proposal Lab helps Maryland life science and technology small businesses write and submit winning SBIR/STTR proposals to federal agencies. The program offers a two-part training series: Part I covers business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing through 2 live workshops; Part II provides 6 additional workshops for companies with approved NSF pitches to refine and submit full proposals. The goal is to position companies for up to $305,000 in non-dilutive Phase I funding from NSF and other federal agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-part virtual training program with live workshops, proposal writing support, feedback adjudication guidance, SAM.gov and Research.gov registration help, and access to market research tools. The program aims to prepare small businesses to compete for up to $305,000 in NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I funding.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proposal writing training and technical assistance to compete for federal SBIR/STTR Phase I funding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses across Maryland's 24 counties and Baltimore City

Must be in life science or technology sector
Must be located in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the Apply Here link on the program page. Accepted participants receive pre-course training materials and then participate in Part I and Part II workshops.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SBIR/STTR Technical Assistance program helps Maryland technology and life sciences small businesses build the expertise needed to access federal SBIR/STTR (Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer) funding. It guides companies with limited SBIR/STTR experience through program requirements, available resources, and the proposal process. The program includes workshops on federal SBIR/STTR overview, agency-specific sessions (DoD, NIH, DoE), proposal writing training, commercialization planning, and budget preparation, plus two rounds of individual expert proposal reviews.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses that have not yet been awarded an SBIR/STTR grant and want to learn how to access federal SBIR/STTR funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workshops and expert reviews to build proposal writing skills and understanding of federal SBIR/STTR programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland small businesses statewide.

Must not have previously been awarded an SBIR or STTR grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the TEDCO application portal at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/170. Contact sbir-ta@tedcomd.com for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Social Impact Funds (Pre-Seed Builder Fund and Inclusion Fund)
structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Social Impact Funds provide equity investments to economically underserved founders and early-stage technology startups in Maryland. The program includes two tracks: the Pre-Seed Builder Fund, which invests in pre-seed technology startups where at least 50% of founders demonstrate economic disadvantage, and the Inclusion Fund, which targets early-stage technology companies where at least 30% ownership is held by individuals who have demonstrated social and economic disadvantage. Funded companies also receive executive support, peer mentorship, and networking opportunities. Funding is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Builder Fund typically invests initial amounts of $100,000 via convertible notes, with total Social Impact Fund investments of up to $750,000 in a single deployment. Investments may be structured as convertible notes or equity in a range of $200,000–$500,000, with a minimum 1:1 private capital match required. Funded companies also receive hands-on and educational executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship and collaboration, and networking opportunities.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investment capital to support early-stage technology companies. Companies also receive executive support, mentorship, and networking to help grow and attract follow-on financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's evergreen Venture Funds provide equity investments to early-stage and technology-based businesses in Maryland. The funds are sector-agnostic and invest in Maryland-connected companies across any industry. There are two funding tracks: (1) Maryland Venture Fund — direct equity investments via convertible note or equity in technology-based businesses at the pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stage; and (2) Venture Capital Limited Partnership — funding for early-stage venture capital funds committed to investing in Maryland-based companies. TEDCO supplements the Venture Funds with capital from Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) and manages over $110 million in assets under management. TEDCO prefers to lead deals but will co-invest alongside other lead investors and assesses opportunities on an ongoing, rolling basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: (1) Maryland Venture Fund — convertible note or equity investment of $500,000 to $1,500,000 with a minimum 1:1 private capital match, targeting technology-based businesses with fewer than 251 employees and less than $15M in equity raised. (2) Venture Capital Limited Partnership — TEDCO Standard Limited Partnership terms with fees meeting SSBCI guidelines, targeting early-stage VC funds committed to investing in Maryland. TEDCO is evergreen and assesses opportunities on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing, assessed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage, Maryland-connected businesses and entrepreneurs seeking equity investment, including technology-based businesses at the pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stage, and early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland-based companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business growth and development for early-stage companies; technology business investment and growth at the pre-seed to pre-venture capital stage; investing in early-stage Maryland businesses through venture capital fund structures.

Will consider regional tech companies outside Maryland on a referral basis. For the Venture Capital Limited Partnership track, the fund must have a commitment to Maryland.

The program covers four investment categories: cyber tech/information technology, life sciences, general tech commercialization, and gap funding. It is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI). Note: The Technology Commercialization Fund was reported as 100% deployed for FY25; current availability of that specific fund should be verified.

A minimum 1:1 private capital match is required for the Gap Investment Fund (from non-governmental sources). The Technology Commercialization Fund caps prior dilutive funding at $2.5M. The program is backed partly by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funds. Opportunities are assessed on an ongoing/rolling basis. structured_extraction.program_name: MUCFC Community Tree Planting and Education Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Council (MUCFC), administered through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service, provides grants to support community-based tree planting, street tree maintenance, and urban forestry education projects across Maryland. Funded through the USDA Forest Service and administered through the Maryland Forest Service and local County Forestry Boards, these grants support hands-on efforts to increase urban tree canopy, engage community members, and build local capacity for long-term stewardship. Funded projects must occur on public lands such as school grounds, parks, town centers, streetscapes, or municipal properties. Projects that promote urban tree canopy, long-term maintenance, and citizen engagement receive preference, with priority given to those that include matching funds or in-kind support.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Council (MUCFC) / Maryland Forest Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $1,000 are awarded to organizations for tree planting and urban forestry education projects on public lands including parks, school campuses, streetscapes, and municipal properties. Tree planting projects must include a site plan, native/non-invasive tree species and sizes (shade-providing trees preferred; invasive species will not be funded), and a maintenance plan. Educational projects must include draft content or images, a target audience description and distribution plan, an explanation of the unmet informational need addressed, and clear MUCFC credit on all materials. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive priority. Unused funds must be returned with the final report, which is due one month after the proposed project completion date.

structured_extraction.program_name: PLANT Award Program (People Loving and Nurturing Trees)
structured_extraction.program_description: The PLANT Award (People Loving and Nurturing Trees) recognizes Maryland communities that plant, care for, and promote trees. Communities of all types can participate, including schools, homeowners associations (HOAs), parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, and faith-based organizations. Established in 1991, the program provides an accessible entry point for building long-term urban and community forestry programs, especially for communities that may not qualify for national recognition programs such as Tree City USA. Awards are given at four levels — Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Green — based on the community's level of tree-related activity over the past year. Bronze is for single events or one-time efforts; Silver is for communities beginning to organize; Gold is for communities actively managing trees through policies or programs; Green is for established programs with sustained effort. Communities recognized through Tree City USA or Tree Campus USA automatically qualify at the Green level.

No financial award is provided — the program provides acknowledgment and helps communities build long-term urban and community forestry programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) provides low-interest revolving loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible public and private community water systems and local governments to finance drinking water system upgrades and capital improvement projects. Projects must provide safe drinking water and protect the quality of Maryland's drinking water supply, achieving or maintaining compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act. The federal Safe Drinking Water Act requires that all community water systems demonstrate technical, managerial, and financial capacity to maintain their system before receiving a loan. The program is funded by federal EPA dollars and state funds, and the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA) issues revenue bonds subject to approval of the State Board of Public Works. MWIFA can also provide financial advisory services to help borrowers understand water rate structures and the financial impacts of a proposed loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest revolving loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness funded by federal EPA dollars and state funds for eligible drinking water infrastructure and capital improvement projects. SRF loans are available at 25% or 50% of Market Interest Rate with 30–40 year terms. Loan principal forgiveness is available up to 25–87.5% depending on system size and disadvantaged community (DAC) status. State Water Supply Grants of up to 25–87.5% are also available depending on system size and DAC status. Per-fiscal-year funding is capped at $1.5 million per applicant per fiscal year. The program issues revenue bonds subject to approval of the State Board of Public Works. Financial advisory services are also available to help borrowers determine water rate structures and assess the financial impact of a proposed loan. Applications are typically accepted from December 1 through January 31 each year; the next application window is expected to reopen in December 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will reopen in December 2026 (typically accepted December 1 through January 31 each year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private community water systems in Maryland, including local governments, for-profit entities, non-profits, and individuals seeking financing for drinking water supply improvements and infrastructure upgrades. Both small systems (under 10,000 population) and large systems are eligible, as are towns, cities, counties, nonprofit water services companies, private water companies, and water authorities.

Projects may also be categorically excepted or excluded from PFA requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund (WQRLF) provides below-market, low-interest revolving loans and financial assistance funded with federal EPA dollars and state funds for a wide variety of projects to protect or improve the quality of Maryland's rivers, streams, lakes, the Chesapeake Bay, and other water resources, consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act. The program covers both point source pollution prevention projects (for public entities and local governments only) and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects (for public and private entities), including wastewater treatment plant upgrades, nonpoint source pollution control, and other water quality and public health improvement projects. Loans are funded by federal EPA dollars and state funds, and the program issues revenue bonds subject to approval of the State Board of Public Works. Financial advisory services are also available to help applicants determine affordable user rate structures and model the fiscal impact of proposed loans. The program also offers grants, loan principal forgiveness (including up to 100% for eligible Enhanced Nutrient Removal components), and State supplemental grants. Additional subsidy is available for Disadvantaged Communities (DAC). The program is established as a perpetual revolving fund to maintain a continuous source of capital for future projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market, low-interest revolving loans funded by federal EPA dollars and state funds for water quality improvement projects. The program also provides project grants, loan principal forgiveness (including up to 100% for eligible Enhanced Nutrient Removal components), State supplemental grants, IIJA General Supplemental loans and loan forgiveness, and IIJA Emerging Contaminants grants. Additional subsidy is available for Disadvantaged Communities (DAC). Revenue bonds are issued subject to approval of the State Board of Public Works. Financial advisory services are available to help applicants determine affordable user rate structures and model the fiscal impact of the proposed loan on financial capacity. Applications are accepted December 1 through January 31 each year; the next application window reopens in December 2026.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Public entities, local governments, and private entities seeking financing for water quality improvement projects in Maryland, including wastewater treatment plant upgrades, nonpoint source pollution control, and other water quality and public health improvement projects. Eligible applicants include municipal governments, county governments, utility commissions, sanitary districts, regional authorities, and private entities (for nonpoint source projects). Also eligible: drinking water systems, community water systems, and agricultural entities (via Linked Deposit program).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Point source pollution prevention (public entities/local governments only): wastewater treatment plant improvements/expansion including Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) and Basic Nutrient Removal (BNR) upgrades, sewerage collection/conveyance systems, correction of excess sewerage infiltration/inflow and combined sewer overflow (CSO/SSO abatement), sewer rehabilitation/replacement, pump station upgrades, sludge handling facilities, landfill leachate pretreatment facilities, and back wash facilities at drinking water treatment plants. Nonpoint source pollution prevention (public and private entities): stormwater best management practices (gray and green infrastructure), wellhead protection, landfill closure, stream corridor restoration/protection, hazardous waste clean-up (brownfields), shoreline erosion control, agricultural nutrient management plans, and forestry financing tools. Also eligible: septic-to-sewer connections, resilience/flood mitigation projects, energy efficiency improvements, system consolidation, biosolids/biogas reuse, stormwater/wastewater reuse, dam repair, and other capital improvement projects that improve water quality generally.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Treatment works projects must be located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or receive a PFA exception from the Smart Growth Coordinating Committee (SGCC); BRF Wastewater Grant projects are not subject to the PFA requirement (except sewer extensions connecting septics to BNR/ENR wastewater treatment plants). Non-treatment works projects (e.g., stormwater BMPs) are not subject to the PFA requirement. Projects must be included in, or amended into, an MDE-approved County Water and Sewer Plan, and must be consistent with the County's Comprehensive Land Use Plan. Special consideration is given to projects in the Maryland Coastal Bays Watersheds and Chesapeake Bay Watershed.

Rates change monthly based on the Bond Buyer 11-Bond Index. An annual administrative fee of 5% of aggregate debt service divided by loan term is collected. Principal forgiveness and/or grants may also be available for Disadvantaged Communities.
