structured_extraction.program_description: MWIFA provides state and federal financial assistance — including low-interest loans, loan forgiveness, and grants — for eligible water quality, drinking water, and stormwater management capital projects in Maryland. Eligible projects include sanitary sewer and wastewater treatment, drinking water infrastructure and source water protection, nonpoint source pollution and watershed restoration, septic system upgrades and sewer connections, and stormwater management and flood mitigation. MWIFA administers several specific loan and grant programs: Water Quality Revolving Loan Program (WQRLF), Drinking Water Revolving Loan Program (DWRLF), Water Supply Assistance Grant Program, Bay Restoration Fund Wastewater Grant Program, Supplemental Assistance Grant Program, Bay Restoration Fund Septic System Upgrade Program, and Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA), Maryland Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans (below market rate), loan forgiveness, and grants for water infrastructure capital projects. The Water Supply Assistance Grant Program awards up to $1.5 million (based on system size, compliance status, and affordability) and requires a local match. The Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program provides grants covering up to 75% of total project costs for projects without federal sponsors, or up to 50% of the local match for federally sponsored projects. Both revolving loan programs receive federal EPA funding. For drinking water: small systems (serving <10,000 population) in disadvantaged communities may receive up to 50% SRF principal forgiveness plus up to 50% State Water Supply Grant; large systems in disadvantaged communities may receive up to 87.5% State Water Supply Grant; rate-shock mitigation provides up to 25% loan forgiveness if >20% user rate increase is required. For septic system upgrades (BRF SSUP): income-based eligibility caps ranging from 50%–100% grant coverage (homeowners with income ≤$300K/year receive 100% coverage; non-profits receive 100%; small businesses receive 75%; for-profit businesses receive 50%).

structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, water authorities, wastewater treatment entities, community water systems, nonprofit noncommunity water systems, homeowners, non-profit entities, and small businesses in Maryland seeking financing for water quality, drinking water, stormwater, septic system upgrades, and flood mitigation capital projects. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including: advanced wastewater treatment (BNR/ENR upgrades), CSO/SSO correction, sewer system rehabilitation, septic-to-sewer connections, landfill leachate treatment, energy/water conservation infrastructure; drinking water treatment, source water protection, transmission/distribution, storage, system consolidation, lead service line replacement, PFAS/emerging contaminant treatment; stormwater BMPs, MS4 compliance, stream restoration, shoreline erosion control; septic system upgrades to best available technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal including cost differential for BAT systems in new construction, community system replacement of multiple OSDS, and connection of septic-served properties to existing municipal wastewater facilities; and flood mitigation.

Disadvantaged Community (DAC) status determined by MDE Environmental Justice Tracking Tool score ≥75th percentile OR meeting ≥2 of: Median Household Income <80% of state average ($73,145 threshold), poverty rate >110% of state level (10.1% threshold), unemployment rate >120% of state level (6.4% threshold), or population change <-1.2%. Priority given to Chesapeake Bay Watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays Watersheds for certain programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funding solicitation opens annually (next opening December 2026, with applications accepted December 1 through January 31). structured_extraction.program_name: MarylandSaves WorkLife Account and Annual Report Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: MarylandSaves is a state-mandated and state-sponsored workplace retirement and emergency savings program that automatically enrolls eligible Maryland private-sector workers into a personal WorkLife Savings Account (a Roth IRA) funded by payroll deductions. Workers can use the account for both emergency savings and retirement savings, with tax-free growth on earnings. The default contribution rate is 5% of each paycheck, increasing 1% per year up to a maximum of 10% (minimum 1%). The first $1,000 is invested in an Emergency Savings Fund (guaranteed by Lincoln National Life Insurance Co.); remaining contributions go into a Target Retirement Date fund. Participants can customize contribution rates and investment options, opt out, or rejoin at any time. Account fees are $22.50 in year one (waived intro rate) plus an asset-based fee starting at 0.18% per year; after year one, $30 per year plus asset-based fees (no fee for the Emergency Savings Fund). Participation is voluntary — the account is portable and travels with the employee regardless of employer changes. Most Maryland private-sector employers are required by state law to offer employees a way to save for retirement. Employers must have been in operation for at least 2 calendar years, have at least one employee over age 18, and use an automated payroll system. Employers register their business, add employees, and submit payroll contributions to individual employee savings accounts at no cost to the employer. Employers already offering a qualified retirement plan may certify their exemption online instead of enrolling. Employers who register and submit payroll contributions (or certify an exemption) by December 31 each year qualify for a $300 waiver on their Maryland SDAT Annual Report filing fee. Businesses with no employees or manual payroll can also certify their exemption online. Self-employed individuals and others who want a convenient retirement savings account can also participate directly using a Social Security number or Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN). Federal Roth IRA income eligibility limits apply; participants are responsible for verifying their own eligibility.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Workers are automatically enrolled in a personal WorkLife Savings Account (Roth IRA) and contribute a percentage of their paycheck (default 5%, increasing 1% per year up to 10%; minimum 1%), or can contribute directly from a bank account. Account fees are $22.50 in year one (waived intro rate) plus an asset-based fee starting at 0.18% per year; after year one, $30 per year plus asset-based fees (no fee for the Emergency Savings Fund). Workers can access their money for emergencies or retirement, and the account is portable across employers. There is no employer match or required employer contributions. Employers who register and submit payroll contributions (or certify an exemption) by December 31 each year receive a $300 waiver/exemption on their SDAT Annual Report filing fee for the following year. The program is free to set up and administer for employers. Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan can claim the waiver online using their EIN and SDAT number; businesses with no employees or manual payroll can certify their exemption online. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For employers: 1. Receive a notification from MarylandSaves with your access code. 2. Register your business online at marylandsaves.vestwell.com using your EIN and access code. 3. Set up login credentials, upload bank information, and enter company and payroll information. 4. Add employees to the system (provide employee roster with name, contact info, date of birth, and SSN). 5. Employees receive a 30-day notification period to opt out or customize their account. 6. Begin submitting payroll contribution deductions for enrolled employees by December 31. 7. Claim the $300 SDAT Annual Report filing fee waiver online each year using your EIN. Employers should check the list of SDAT IDs compiled by MarylandSaves to confirm eligibility for the $300 Annual Report fee waiver on their SDAT filing. Employers already offering a qualified retirement plan can certify exemption online using their EIN and SDAT number instead. Businesses with no employees or manual payroll can certify their exemption online. For workers: Workers are automatically enrolled through their employer after 30 days and can customize or opt out. To set up or access an account, visit marylandsaves.com/gateway or sign in at marylandsaves.vestwell.com. To opt out, visit sumday.com/retrieve/marylandsaves or submit an opt-out form by mail or phone. Self-employed individuals or those without an employer in MarylandSaves can register directly at marylandsaves.com/gateway using their Social Security number or Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN), date of birth, and residential address. Participants can also enroll or manage accounts by phone at 1-833-811-7438 (employees, Mon–Fri 9am–6pm ET) or 1-833-811-7437 (employers), or by paper form submission. TTY/711 available.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2024 Continuum of Care (CoC) NOFO Program Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) program promotes a community-wide commitment to ending homelessness. It provides funding to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to quickly rehouse individuals and families experiencing homelessness while minimizing the impacts of trauma and dislocation. The program also promotes self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs for people experiencing homelessness. Baltimore City's Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) runs the local competition process to select projects for submission to HUD. Projects may be new, renewal, or expansion, and funding amounts are determined through the local competitive ranking process and HUD's final award decisions. Project types include Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Transitional Housing, Street Outreach, Safe Haven, Joint TH-RRH, and Supportive Services Only – Coordinated Entry (SSO-CE). Eligible costs include rental assistance, leasing, supportive services, operating costs, case management, outreach, housing counseling, utilities, and maintenance. A 25% match/leveraging requirement applies (cash or in-kind, excluding leasing costs). HUD issued a single 2-year NOFO covering fiscal years 2024 and 2025. Total FY 2024 funding requested was $31,418,189 across 43 projects (CoC Renewal $25.7M + New CoC $2.3M + Planning $1.4M + YHDP $1.9M).

Eligible costs include rental assistance, leasing, supportive services, operating costs, case management, outreach, housing counseling, utilities, and maintenance. structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Exemption for High-Density Development at WMATA Metro Stations (Bill 29-20)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County enacted Bill 29-20 to accelerate high-density housing development on property leased from the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) at metro stations throughout the county. New high-rise developments built on WMATA-leased land are exempt from all county property taxes for their first 15 years if they meet affordable housing requirements. The initiative aims to create approximately 8,600 new housing units — about 20 percent of the county's housing goal for 2030 — and support new businesses and jobs near metro stations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: New high-rise developments built on property leased from WMATA at metro stations are exempt from all property taxes for their first 15 years. To qualify, the development must include at least 50 percent rental housing, with 25 percent of those rental units designated as moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) for households earning 50 percent or less of the area median income (AMI). At least 25 percent of workers hired for construction must be Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers building high-rise mixed-use or residential projects on WMATA-owned land at metro stations in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption for the first 15 years of operation for qualifying high-density developments on WMATA-leased land near metro stations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Montgomery County, Maryland, on property leased from WMATA at metro rail stations.
requirements_list: Development must be built on property leased from WMATA at a metro station in Montgomery County
At least 50 percent of units must be rental housing
At least 25 percent of rental units must be moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) reserved for households earning 50 percent or less of the area median income
At least 25 percent of construction workers hired must be Montgomery County residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The tax exemption is established by Bill 29-20. No specific application process is described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Circuit Court Adult Drug Court is a voluntary treatment program for adult offenders with substance use disorders who are facing a violation of probation charge or referred through a binding plea agreement. The program lasts a minimum of 20 months and includes four phases plus aftercare. It aims to reduce recidivism and break the cycle of addiction and crime by providing intensive supervision, substance abuse treatment, recovery meetings, case management, frequent judicial status hearings, drug and alcohol monitoring, and community participation support. Participants must reside in Montgomery County throughout the program and live in court-approved sober housing. They must complete community service and meet work/school requirements. The program connects offenders to treatment providers, community organizations, and law enforcement partners as an alternative to traditional criminal case processing. Fees are charged on a sliding scale based on income and household size; Maryland Medicaid (MA) and Pharmacy Adult Care (PAC) are accepted, and no one is refused services due to inability to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive intensive outpatient/inpatient substance abuse treatment, case management, frequent judicial status hearings, drug and alcohol monitoring (including SCRAM bracelet), recovery meeting requirements, housing support, and graduated sanctions/positive reinforcement over a minimum 20-month program with four phases and aftercare. Second Chance serves as the primary treatment provider. Fees are charged on a sliding scale based on income and household size; Maryland Medicaid (MA) and Pharmacy Adult Care (PAC) are accepted, and no one is refused services due to inability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult residents of Montgomery County, Maryland (aged 18 and older) who are non-violent substance-abusing offenders with a substance use disorder diagnosis referred through a binding plea agreement approved by the State's Attorney's Office or as a condition of a probation violation before the Circuit Court of Montgomery County. The Intervention Track targets lower-level offenders with minimal backup/incarcerable time (18 months or less), high risk/high need clinically appropriate candidates, and fewer than 7 prior convictions (DWI offenders: 4 or fewer convictions for the Intervention Track; 5 or more convictions are routed to the traditional track).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse treatment, recovery support, case management, court supervision, drug and alcohol monitoring, housing placement coordination, education and employment support, and community participation support as an alternative to traditional criminal case disposition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to adult residents of Montgomery County, Maryland. Participants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland at all times while enrolled in the program and must live in court-approved sober housing within Montgomery County. Drug Court hearings are held at Montgomery County Circuit Court, 50 Maryland Ave, Rockville, MD 20850.
requirements_list: Must be an adult resident of Montgomery County, Maryland (aged 18 or older)
Must be a non-violent offender
Must be assessed as suffering from a substance use disorder
Must be referred via a binding plea agreement approved by the State's Attorney's Office or as a condition of a probation violation before the Circuit Court of Montgomery County
Must be fully capable of participating in Drug Court activities and programs
Must enter a guilty plea or admission of probation violation
Cases must transfer to Circuit Court (jury demand or appeal)
Must accept 3 years supervised probation upon admission

Must submit to on-demand drug and alcohol testing (urinalysis, oral fluid, SCRAM monitoring as ordered)
Must not use controlled substances, alcohol, marijuana, or mood-altering substances without physician approval
Must disclose all medications to case manager
Must enroll in GED coursework if education level is below 12th grade
Must comply with medication requirements (Antabuse, Vivitrol, Naltrexone) if directed by the court
Must obtain AA/NA sponsor, home group, and service position within 12-step program
Must comply with all laws and probation conditions
Must disclose all law enforcement contact to case manager within 24 hours
Re-admitted participants are subject to immediate termination for non-compliance (standard Menu of Sanctions no longer applies)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Any person can make a referral by contacting the Problem Solving Courts Coordinator at 240-777-9141 or jenna.davis@mdcourts.gov. A referral form is available online. Applicants should bring photo identification, copies of any insurance cards (including Medical Assistance and Primary Adult Care), and proof of residence. Cases originate in District Court and must transfer to Circuit Court. Participants sign a Drug Court Agreement and are placed on 3 years supervised probation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Adult Guardianship Assistant Program helps court-appointed guardians in Montgomery County fulfill their responsibilities. A Court Appointed Visitor is assigned to guardianship cases to meet with guardians and those under guardianship, help guardians understand their duties, identify resources and services, and connect guardians with assistance for housing, home health, respite, and financial help.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Court Appointed Visitor is assigned to the guardianship case to meet with the guardian and the person under guardianship, help the guardian understand their legal duties, locate home health agencies and respite programs, and identify housing options and financial assistance resources. The visitor provides guidance and referrals but does not provide direct services, legal advice, or fill out forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Co-Parenting Program (Parent Education and Custody Effectiveness, or PEACE)
structured_extraction.program_description: An online parent education program for families going through separation or divorce in Montgomery County. The program teaches parents skills to keep children out of family conflicts and help them thrive in two separate households. Classes cover the effects of divorce on adults and children, how parents can help children cope, and how to communicate effectively with the other parent.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Commission on Common Ownership Communities (CCOC) offers a mandatory training program called 'Community Governance Fundamentals' for board members and residents of common ownership communities (condominiums, cooperatives, and homeowners' associations). The curriculum covers ethics, board member roles and responsibilities, governing documents, financial management, meeting rules, and general administration. The approximately 3-hour program includes videos and quizzes and is also open to any member of the public interested in learning about common ownership community operations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Access Program (CAP) provides funding assistance to nonprofit and community organizations to help offset facility rental costs at the Silver Spring Civic Building and Veterans Plaza. structured_extraction.program_description: The federally funded PATH program provides case management, outreach, and transportation services to people who are homeless or imminently homeless and have a serious mental illness. structured_extraction.program_description: The ECOWISE program gives Montgomery County businesses (called Small Quantity Generators, or SQGs) that produce less than 220 pounds of hazardous waste per month an affordable and convenient way to dispose of hazardous materials. Fees are charged per pound at the point of collection, and businesses save up to 75% compared to hiring a private hazardous waste pickup company.

Credit card payments incur a surcharge not to exceed 3%; business checks made out to Clean Harbors Environmental Services are also accepted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Energy-Efficient Buildings Property Tax Credit (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a two-tiered property tax credit program for energy-efficient commercial and multi-family residential buildings. For existing buildings, owners can earn up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for two years by installing energy conservation devices and demonstrating measurable energy improvements tracked via ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager. The first tier (Energy Reduction Tax Credit) rewards measurable improvements in ENERGY STAR scores; the second tier (Building Sustainability Tax Credit) rewards third-party certifications such as LEED O+M, BREEAM In-Use, or equivalent. Existing buildings are eligible for one initial application plus up to two reapplications (maximum three applications per building). For newly constructed buildings, owners can earn up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for four years (or five years for Living Building Certification) by building above current energy code requirements (minimum 10% above code via the performance pathway). Credit amounts vary by percentage above code: 10–20% above: 5–10% credit; 21–30% above: 21–30% credit; 31–40% above: 46.5–60% credit; above 40%: 82–100% credit. A second-tier Building Sustainability Tax Credit (25% or 75%) is available for achieving recognized green building certifications (LEED Gold/Platinum, NGBS Gold/Emerald, PHIUS+/Passive House, BREEAM-NC Excellent/Outstanding, LBC Petal, or Living Building Certification) within 2 years of receiving a use and occupancy permit. Buildings located in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% of the building's annual County property tax liability per year. The program aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from existing and newly constructed buildings in Montgomery County and also encompasses green building tax credits for projects achieving LEED and other recognized certifications. Note: the newly constructed buildings application has been listed as 'Coming Soon' on some program pages — contact the Department of Environmental Protection for current availability.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two-tiered property tax credit against Montgomery County property taxes. Existing buildings: up to 100% credit per year for two years. Tier 1 (Energy Reduction Tax Credit): credit percentage is calculated by multiplying the improvement in ENERGY STAR score by a tiered multiplier (1.0–2.5 depending on improved score). Tier 2 (Building Sustainability Tax Credit): an additional 25% (LEED O+M Gold or BREEAM In-Use Excellent) or 50% (LEED O+M Platinum or BREEAM In-Use Outstanding) credit. Eligible for up to three applications per building (one initial plus two reapplications). Newly constructed buildings: up to 100% credit per year for four years (five years for Living Building Certification), calculated based on percentage above building code using a tiered factor (0.5–2.0): 10–20% above: 5–10% credit; 21–30% above: 21–30% credit; 31–40% above: 46.5–60% credit; above 40%: 82–100% credit. Tier 2 (Building Sustainability Tax Credit): an additional 25% credit for LEED Gold, NGBS Gold, PHIUS+/Passive House, or BREEAM-NC Excellent (or equivalent); 75% for LBC Petal Certification, LEED Platinum, NGBS Emerald, BREEAM-NC Outstanding, or Living Building Certification (or equivalent), within 2 years of receiving a use and occupancy permit. Newly constructed buildings are eligible for only one application; reapplications are not permitted. Buildings in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% of the building's annual County property tax liability per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 1 year of receiving a use and occupancy permit (newly constructed buildings); rolling for existing buildings
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of existing or newly constructed commercial and multi-family residential buildings in Montgomery County with at least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area, including projects achieving LEED or other green building certifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied against Montgomery County taxes owed — no direct cash disbursement. Reward for making energy efficiency improvements to existing buildings (via ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager improvements and/or third-party sustainability certifications) or constructing new buildings that exceed energy code requirements by at least 10%, including achieving LEED or other recognized green building certifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial and multi-family residential buildings located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Buildings in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas are eligible for an additional 10% credit.
requirements_list: Building must be a commercial or multi-family residential property in Montgomery County
Building must have at least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area
Must own a commercial or multi-family property in Montgomery County

Existing buildings: must have received a Certificate of Occupancy from the Department of Permitting Services, achieved at least 50% occupancy for at least 12 consecutive months, and demonstrate energy improvements per Montgomery County Code Section 52-103A
Existing buildings must make eligible energy efficiency improvements

Existing buildings Tier 1: must set a 12-month ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager baseline, document energy conservation device installations, and measure improved energy performance; baseline and improved ENERGY STAR Score 12-month periods must not overlap, must not include the installation period, and must not be more than 6 calendar years apart; baseline period cannot begin before August 26, 2018; improved ENERGY STAR 12-month period cannot be issued more than 12 months before application date; ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklists must be verified by a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) or Registered Architect (RA) in good standing
Existing buildings Tier 2: must first meet Tier 1 requirements, then obtain LEED O+M Gold or Platinum, BREEAM In-Use Excellent or Outstanding, or equivalent certification
Existing buildings are eligible for one initial application plus up to two reapplications (maximum 3 applications per building)

Newly constructed buildings Tier 1: must achieve at least 10% energy efficiency above current Montgomery County Building Code via the performance pathway, certified by the Department of Permitting Services within the last 12 months; application must be submitted within 1 year of receiving a use and occupancy permit; buildings demonstrating code compliance via the prescriptive pathway are not eligible
New construction must exceed current building code requirements

Newly constructed buildings must have or will have a certification from the Department of Permitting Services within the last 12 months showing the building's performance percentage above current Building Code at time of application
Newly constructed buildings must meet modeled energy performance requirements consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103B, validated by a DPS-stamped energy model

Newly constructed buildings Tier 2: must first meet Tier 1, then obtain LEED Gold/Platinum, NGBS Gold/Emerald, PHIUS+/Passive House, BREEAM-NC Excellent/Outstanding, LBC Petal, or Living Building Certification within 2 years of receiving a use and occupancy permit
Newly constructed buildings must not have previously received the Newly Constructed Energy-Efficient Buildings Tax Credit
Newly constructed buildings are eligible for only one application — reapplications are not permitted
Combined credits cannot exceed 100% of the building's annual County property tax liability per year
Building or reconstruction project must achieve LEED or other recognized green building certification (for Tier 2 credits)
Data Verification Checklists must be verified by a licensed Professional Engineer or Registered Architect
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Existing building owners apply online using the Energy-Efficient Existing Buildings Property Tax Credit application at https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/f/EnergyEfficientExistingBuildingsTaxCredit. Newly constructed building owners must apply within 1 year of receiving a use and occupancy permit via the online application form linked on the program page (note: the newly constructed buildings application has been listed as 'Coming Soon' — contact the Department of Environmental Protection for current status). Applicants must submit documentation of energy improvements, ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager data (for existing buildings), and certifications from the Department of Permitting Services or green building certification bodies as applicable. Contact the Department of Environmental Protection at energy@montgomerycountymd.gov with questions. Alternative compliance using Energy Use Intensity may be available for buildings that cannot achieve an ENERGY STAR score.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) offers incentives to help mobile food service businesses replace gasoline- and diesel-powered generators with clean battery power systems. Funded by a grant from the Maryland Energy Administration, the pilot provides cash incentives based on battery capacity and optional zero-interest financing to offset the cost of purchasing and installing battery energy storage systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash incentives range from $5,000 to $10,000 depending on battery capacity (5–40+ kWh). A loan option provides a 48-month loan at 7.99% APR for up to $35,000 through Climate First Bank; once installation is confirmed, the incentive amount is credited to the loan balance. A direct payment option pays the incentive after proof of installation is submitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of licensed mobile food service businesses (food trucks and trailers) in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of battery power systems (battery energy storage systems) to replace gasoline or diesel fuel generators in food truck operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to licensed mobile food service businesses in Montgomery County, MD. Mobile Reciprocity Licenses from another jurisdiction or the State of Maryland are allowed.
requirements_list: Must be the owner of a licensed mobile food service business in Montgomery County
Business must be registered with the State of Maryland and in 'good standing'
Battery must replace a gasoline or diesel fuel generator
Must purchase equipment meeting minimum specifications: 5,000 Wh (5 kWh) nominal energy capacity, 5,000 W minimum power output, 10-year or longer warranty
Must provide photographs of installed equipment and invoices for installation
Must allow Montgomery County DEP and/or Maryland Energy Administration to inspect and photograph the installed system upon request
For financing: must qualify for financing with Climate First Bank and use an electrician in Climate First Bank's qualified installer network
For direct payment: must register as a vendor in the County Vendor Registration System
Installation must be performed by an electrician licensed in the State of Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the online application form. 2. Receive eligibility confirmation from DEP; DEP connects applicants with participating vendors. 3. Contact vendors for power needs assessment and installation quotes. 4. Submit quotes to DEP for final approval. 5. If using the loan option, apply for zero-interest financing with Climate First Bank. 6. Order and install the battery power system. 7. Submit proof of installation to DEP and receive the incentive payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers rebates to residential and commercial/institutional property owners who voluntarily install a green roof — a rooftop system designed to hold special soil and plants that captures and treats the first inch of rainfall before it reaches the ground. Green roofs conserve energy, reduce stormwater pollution, and support pollinators. Only extensive green roofs constructed on existing buildings (retrofits) are eligible. Projects must be on private property and cannot be used to satisfy a county-required stormwater permit.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $9 per square foot of green roof installed. Maximum rebate is $7,500 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial/institutional properties. Minimum project size is 100 square feet for residential and 200 square feet for commercial/institutional. Installation costs typically range from $10 to $30 per square foot depending on the type of system, structural support, and plantings. Tax is subtracted from itemized receipts when calculating the rebate. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis.

Students grow plants during the second semester for use in watershed restoration projects. Schools return at least one-third of the plants to the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) for stormwater management, and may use the remaining plants for a native plant sale or other environmental project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers rebates to residential and commercial/institutional property owners who remove impervious hard pavement (such as driveways, walkways, or patios) and replace it with natural vegetation such as a rain garden, conservation landscaping, or sod/lawn. Removing pavement, decompacting soil, and planting vegetation reduces hard surfaces that contribute to stormwater runoff and improves local water quality. Properties must be located within Montgomery County but outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park, which collect the Water Quality Protection Charge separately. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
eligible_municipalities: Montgomery County (excluding Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate amounts vary by replacement type: $3 per square foot for sod/lawn replacement, $6 per square foot for conservation landscaping without temporary ponding, and $7 per square foot for conservation landscaping with 3 inches of temporary ponding (or at least 50% native species indigenous to the Chesapeake Bay Watershed). Maximum rebate is $7,500 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial/institutional properties. Minimum project size is 100 sq ft for residential properties and 200–300 sq ft for commercial/institutional properties. Taxes are subtracted from eligible costs. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Rewards Rebate Program – Stormwater Management Retrofits (Conservation Landscapes, Permeable Pavement, Cisterns & More)
structured_extraction.program_description: The RainScapes Rewards Rebate program provides cost-sharing (rebates) for stormwater management improvements on private properties in Montgomery County, Maryland. It is a voluntary branch of Clean Water Montgomery (CWM). Property owners install qualifying stormwater management projects using their own money upfront; after the project passes a final inspection, the county issues a rebate based on project type and size. Eligible projects include rain gardens, conservation landscapes (native plant gardens that replace lawn, invasive plants, or erosion-prone areas), water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns that attach to roof downspouts to store and reuse rainwater), green roofs, permeable pavement installation (including permeable interlocking concrete pavers/PICP to replace existing impervious surfaces such as driveways, walkways, and patios — specially engineered layers under the surface help filter and clean stormwater runoff), and pavement removal. These practices slow stormwater runoff, reduce erosion and flooding, recharge groundwater, and prevent pollution from reaching local streams. Eligible property types include residential properties, commercial/institutional properties, HOAs, congregations, multi-family properties, and institutional properties (including community pools). For conservation landscape projects, rebates are calculated at $5 per square foot (no temporary ponding) or $6 per square foot (3 inches of temporary ponding), with maximum rebates of $7,500 for residential and $20,000 (lifetime maximum per parcel based on tax ID number) for commercial/institutional properties. Permeable pavement retrofit is rebated at $14 per square foot, with a minimum project size of 100 sq ft (residential) or 200 sq ft (commercial/institutional), and the same maximum rebate caps apply. Contractors performing permeable pavement work must be certified by the Concrete Masonry and Hardscapes Association (CMHA) with PICP training. For water harvesting installations, rebates are $1 per gallon of capacity installed: maximum $250 for rain barrel projects, $500 for cisterns, and $750 combined if both are installed on the same property (with a 200-gallon minimum, or 100-gallon minimum for townhomes; minimum individual barrel size of 50 gallons). Exceptions for commercial/institutional properties may be considered case by case. Rebate checks for landscape projects are issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants may also become eligible for a reduction in the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) on their property tax bill after project completion. Properties in Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park are excluded as those municipalities operate separate programs. The program is funded by the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two rebate tracks: (1) Conservation landscape/stormwater projects: $5 per square foot for standard projects (no temporary ponding) or $6 per square foot for projects with 3 inches of temporary ponding (minimum 250 sq ft). Permeable pavement retrofit is rebated at $14 per square foot (minimum project size 100 sq ft residential, 200 sq ft commercial/institutional). Maximum rebate is $7,500 for residential and $20,000 (lifetime maximum per parcel based on tax ID number) for commercial/institutional properties. Eligible practices include rain gardens, conservation landscaping, water harvesting systems, green roofs, permeable pavement (PICP replacing existing impervious surfaces), and pavement removal. Eligible costs include plants, materials (mulch, compost, stone), hardware, equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project. Tools and general equipment are not eligible. Sales tax is excluded from the receipt total. Rebate checks issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. (2) Water harvesting installations (rain barrels and cisterns): $1 per gallon of capacity installed. Maximum rebate is $250 for rain barrel projects, $500 for cisterns, and $750 combined if both rain barrels and cisterns are installed on the same property. Minimum project size is 200 gallons total (100 gallons for townhomes); minimum individual barrel size is 50 gallons. Exceptions for commercial/institutional properties may be considered case by case. Tax amounts are subtracted from the rebate calculation. Both tracks funded by the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC). Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Property owners may also become eligible for a reduction in the WQPC on their property tax bill after project completion.

For water harvesting, minimum total project size is 200 gallons (100 gallons for townhomes) with a minimum individual barrel size of 50 gallons. Eligible costs include plants, soil amendment, mulch, barrels, cisterns, and related installation materials, as well as hardware (pipe and connectors), equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project. Tools and general equipment (shovels, wheelbarrows) are not eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Primer Guide, Water Harvesting Project Manual, and RainScapes Permeable Paver Manual on the RainScapes website (no paper application available; contact the program for help submitting electronically). 2. Submit an electronic application through the RainScapes Rewards online portal at https://www2.montgomerycountymd.gov/Rainscapes/. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants can also check the status of a current application online. 3. For permeable pavement projects, submit contractor certification and perc test results with the application. For cistern projects, submit required supporting documents (location plan, HOA approval letter if applicable). 4. A RainScapes planner conducts a site assessment (in person or virtually) within approximately 2–12 weeks of application acceptance to confirm site suitability. 5. Submit a plan for approval within 3 months of the site assessment report. 6. Receive an official project approval email and electronically sign the Property Owner Agreement. 7. Install the project within 6 months of approval; for permeable pavement projects, submit construction photos to your planner during installation. 8. Contact your planner to schedule a final inspection and submit receipts and photos. 9. Receive rebate payment, typically within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Call 311 (or 240-777-0311 outside the county; TTY 301-251-4850) or email RainScapes@MontgomeryCountyMd.gov with questions.
