structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit — Multi-Family, Non-Residential, and Nonprofit Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Multi-family residential, non-residential, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) property owners in Montgomery County can apply for a credit to reduce their annual Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) — a fee based on the amount of impervious surface area (roofs, parking lots, etc.) on their property, which typically appears on the yearly property tax bill. Credits are awarded based on the volume of stormwater managed by qualifying on-site practices such as rain gardens, permeable pavement, green roofs, or rain barrels. Eligible property owners can receive a reduction of up to 60% of their annual charge based on the volume of stormwater treated by a combination of environmental site design and stormwater management systems, or up to 80% if the entire property is treated using environmental site design practices. Properties treating both onsite and offsite stormwater volumes may qualify for up to 100% credit (with off-site credit capped at 40% of the onsite credit). Additional credits are available for off-site stormwater treatment. Property owners who are responsible for the structural maintenance of a stormwater pond on their property may also receive a credit off their annual WQPC, rewarding consistent maintenance of stormwater facilities. For nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations that are also exempt from real property ad valorem taxation and whose WQPC exceeds 0.2% of total revenues from the property, a separate hardship reduction (partial exemption) is also available. Credits must be renewed every three years.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners receive a credit reducing their annual Water Quality Protection Charge by up to 60% based on the volume of stormwater treated by a combination of environmental site design and stormwater management systems, or up to 80% if the entire property is treated by environmental site design (ESD) practices. Properties treating both onsite and offsite stormwater volumes may qualify for up to 100% credit (off-site credit capped at 40% of onsite credit). Credit is prorated based on treatment volume provided relative to the required Water Quality Volume (WQv) or Environmental Site Design Volume (ESDv). Additional credits are available for off-site stormwater treatment. Property owners responsible for the structural maintenance of a stormwater pond on their property may also receive a credit for consistent upkeep. For qualifying nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations, a separate hardship reduction is also available where the WQPC exceeds 0.2% of total revenues from the property. Credits must be renewed every three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multi-family residential, non-residential, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland, including businesses, Home Owner Associations, non-profit organizations, and government-owned properties, who have installed or plan to install qualifying stormwater management practices on their property, as well as property owners responsible for the structural maintenance of a stormwater pond.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the annual Water Quality Protection Charge fee assessed on impervious surface area on the property. Eligible stormwater management practices include green roofs, conservation landscaping, micro-bioretention, rain gardens, permeable pavements, rainwater harvesting (rain barrels/cisterns), sheet flow to conservation areas, wet ponds, bioretention, submerged gravel wetlands, swales, roof leader disconnection, dry wells, and micro-infiltration, among others. Also includes credit toward the WQPC for consistent structural maintenance of a stormwater pond.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to multi-family residential, non-residential, and nonprofit properties located in Montgomery County, Maryland. All Montgomery County property owners pay the WQPC, including businesses, Home Owner Associations, and non-profit organizations, but only those maintaining eligible stormwater practices qualify for a credit.
requirements_list: Property must be multi-family residential, non-residential, or nonprofit (IRS-designated 501(c)(3)) in nature
Must own property in Montgomery County
Stormwater management practice must be registered with Montgomery County, or property owner must be willing to install one
Property owner must maintain stormwater practices per DEP maintenance requirements (Section 19-28 of Montgomery County Code)
Must own and maintain on-site stormwater management practices

For new credit applications, engineer-certified plans must include total impervious area, year of installation, facility size and units, and impervious area treated by the stormwater management system
Design information required (may be waived if practice was permitted through Department of Permitting Services or RainScapes project)
A photograph of the stormwater management system must be included; underground practices require above-ground verification
Credits must be renewed every 3 years
Applications must be submitted by September 30
Applications must be submitted by the property owner or the owner's authorized agent
For hardship reduction (nonprofits only): property must also be exempt from real property ad valorem taxation under State law and the WQPC must exceed 0.2% of total revenues from the property
Hardship reduction applicants must provide the most recent federal tax return or other revenue verification
Must own property with a stormwater pond (for stormwater pond credit)
Must be responsible for the structural maintenance of the pond
Must have consistently maintained the stormwater pond
Offsite treatment credit requires that onsite credit of at least 60% has been achieved first
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a WQPC credit application using the online WQPC form portal. The application requires the 8-digit Account ID from the property tax bill, owner name, property address, mailing address, telephone number, email, and information about the stormwater management system. The County performs credit calculations for NR/MFR properties using either design volume or assumed volume based on permit era. A site visit may be coordinated by DEP. Applicants can use the NR/MFR Credit Calculator to determine the credit amount. Applications and renewals are due September 30. For questions, call 3-1-1 or submit a service request online. For stormwater pond credits, visit the Water Quality Protection Charge Credit Program page for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) offers a paid summer internship for college and graduate students to gain hands-on experience in watershed management, stormwater programs, GIS mapping, and community outreach. Interns work on real-world projects that protect local streams, improve water quality, and support sustainable practices across the county. Available tracks include Outreach, GIS Data Support for Tree Montgomery, and GIS Data Support for RainScapes, plus additional opportunities to shadow engineers, biologists, and environmental planners.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship at $18.15 per hour, running approximately 7–10 weeks between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Interns work 20–32 hours per week at 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD. The program provides hands-on technical training in watershed management, GIS mapping, stormwater programs, and community outreach.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current college or graduate students; Montgomery County residents preferred
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on experience in watershed management, stormwater programs, GIS mapping, and community outreach — not a grant or loan; compensation is hourly pay for work performed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to current college or graduate students; Montgomery County residents preferred. Work location is Wheaton, MD.
requirements_list: Must be a current college or graduate student
Montgomery County residents preferred
Applicants must submit an unofficial college transcript, resume or equivalent document
Must submit a personal statement (minimum one page) outlining project interests, career goals, and how the internship supports those goals
Personal statement must indicate top 2 project tracks of interest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an unofficial college transcript, resume or equivalent, and a personal statement (minimum one page) that outlines project interests, career goals, and indicates the applicant's top 2 project tracks. Applications are currently closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Single-Family Residential Food Scraps Recycling Collection Pilot
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a curbside food scraps recycling and composting pilot program for single-family homes in three pilot areas: parts of Silver Spring, Bethesda/Rockville, and Potomac. Volunteers receive a free kit including a 35-gallon green wheeled cart, an in-kitchen bin, compostable bag liners, and instructional materials. Registered households set out their cart on their normal recycling collection day each week. Collected food scraps are transported to a composting facility and processed into a nutrient-rich soil amendment.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection, Recycling and Resource Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible single-family households in designated pilot areas receive a free food scraps recycling kit (35-gallon green wheeled cart with locking lid, 2-gallon in-kitchen bin, two boxes of compostable bag liners, instructional materials) and free weekly curbside food scraps collection service. The program is limited to 850 participants per pilot area.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration closes when 850 participants per pilot area are reached
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family residents in the designated pilot areas of Silver Spring, Bethesda/Rockville, and Potomac who do not already use a private food scraps collection service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Curbside food scraps recycling collection service and starter kit for home food waste diversion and composting
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to residents in three specific pilot areas within Montgomery County: a part of Silver Spring, a part of Bethesda/Rockville, and a part of Potomac. Participants must look up their address to confirm eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a single-family household within one of the three designated pilot areas
Must not already be separating food scraps for recycling and paying for a private food scraps collection service
Must register to volunteer
Each pilot area is capped at 850 participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the online address lookup tool to confirm your address is in a pilot area, then register online at the provided link. A food scraps recycling kit will be delivered to your home. Once received, you can begin participating immediately.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts and Entertainment District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit against County property taxes for owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings located in an Arts and Entertainment District in Montgomery County, when the building is wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. The credit is based on growth in property assessment above a base year (pre-renovation assessment) and lasts 10 years. Credit rates: Years 1–5: 80%; Year 6: 70%; Year 7: 60%; Year 8: 50%; Year 9: 40%; Year 10: 30%. For properties also receiving an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment credit is an additional 20%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year real property tax credit based on growth in property assessment above a base year (pre-renovation assessment). Credit rates: Years 1–5: 80%; Year 6: 70%; Year 7: 60%; Year 8: 50%; Year 9: 40%; Year 10: 30%. For properties also receiving an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment credit is an additional 20%.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County renovated for use by qualifying residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property taxes following renovation of building for arts and entertainment use
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building must be manufacturing, commercial, or industrial
Building must be located in a designated Arts and Entertainment District
Building must be wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
Building must continue to be used by qualifying artist or enterprise throughout the 10-year credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Montgomery County Department of Finance for application details at (240) 777-8931.

structured_extraction.program_description: A County property tax credit equal to 100% of County real property taxes imposed on land that qualifies as conservation land, meaning land used for natural area preservation, environmental education, conservation promotion, or wildlife sanctuary, and subject to a perpetual conservation easement or owned by a qualifying land trust.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit equal to 100% of County real property taxes on qualifying conservation land (excluding improvements). Applies to land subject to a perpetual conservation easement donated to a land trust on or after July 1, 1991, or land acquired by a land trust by July 1, 1991 and owned in fee, subject to a letter of intent or agreement to convey to a government agency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of conservation land in Montgomery County subject to a perpetual conservation easement or held by a qualifying land trust
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full elimination of County real property taxes on qualifying conservation land (improvements excluded)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Land must be used for natural area preservation, environmental education, conservation promotion, or as a wildlife sanctuary

Land must be subject to a perpetual conservation easement donated to a land trust on or after July 1, 1991, OR acquired by a land trust by July 1, 1991 and owned in fee, subject to a letter of intent or agreement to convey to a government agency
Credit does not include improvements on the land
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Montgomery County Department of Finance for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) limits how much a homeowner's taxable property assessment can increase each year. The credit caps taxable assessment increases at no more than 10% per year (or 5% in the Town of Kensington), so homeowners pay no property tax on any assessment increase above the applicable limit. The credit applies only to owner-occupied residential properties and is not applicable in the first year after purchase of a new home. Administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) in coordination with Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied against property tax owed on the portion of a property's annual reassessment that exceeds 10% (or 5% in the Town of Kensington). The homeowner pays no property tax on the assessment increase above the cap limit. The same 10% cap applies to both the State and local portions of the property tax. Not applicable in the first year after purchase of a new home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Montgomery County who have experienced property assessment increases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability by crediting the tax owed on any annual assessment increase above the applicable cap (10% countywide, 5% in the Town of Kensington).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland. All municipalities in Montgomery County use a 10% cap except the Town of Kensington, which uses a 5% cap.
requirements_list: The dwelling must be the owner's principal residence and the owner must have lived there for at least six months of the year, including July 1 of the application year (unless temporarily unable due to illness).
The property was not transferred to new ownership.
There was no change in zoning classification requested by the homeowner that resulted in increased value.
A substantial change did not occur in the use of the property.
The previous assessment was not clearly erroneous.
Homeowner must have an approved Homestead Application on file with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) — application is required only once.
Not applicable in the first year following purchase of a new home.
Montgomery County uses a 10% homestead credit cap; the Town of Kensington uses a 5% cap.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check your Homestead Application status on the SDAT Real Property Search page by selecting Montgomery County and locating the Homestead Application Status row. If it says 'Approved' or 'Application Received,' no further action is needed. Step 2: If status shows 'No Application,' obtain your Real Property Account Number and apply either online at the SDAT Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application page or by mailing a paper application to SDAT. You only need to apply once. The credit is otherwise administered automatically by SDAT; contact the SDAT Rockville office for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County issues tax-exempt Economic Development Revenue Bonds (EDRB) to provide below-market financing for eligible non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses that want to construct, acquire, or rehabilitate facilities in the county. The county also supports financing through the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) program. The county acts as a conduit issuer — it does not pledge its own money, full faith, credit, or taxing power — but its tax-exempt bond authority allows borrowers to access lower-cost capital through the bond market. Bonds are issued on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt revenue bond financing arranged through the county as a conduit issuer, issued on a case-by-case basis. A non-refundable application fee of $5,000 is due at filing. An annual administrative fee of 10 basis points on the original issue amount is due at closing and each year while bonds are outstanding. All legal and administrative costs are borne by the applicant regardless of whether financing is completed. For non-profits, eligible uses include medical, educational, and charitable facilities. For for-profit businesses, eligible uses include small manufacturing facilities, solid waste disposal facilities, low-income housing projects, and other tax-favored activities. Loan amount and term are determined by the project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations qualified under IRS Section 501(c)(3) and selected for-profit businesses seeking to construct, acquire, or rehabilitate facilities, or locate or expand operations in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of facilities; purchase of new equipment; and related project costs such as land, architectural and engineering fees, legal fees, and financing costs. For non-profits: medical, educational, and charitable facilities. For for-profits: manufacturing, solid waste disposal, low-income housing, and other tax-favored capital projects. Projects must be non-speculative and developed for a specific occupant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects and applicants must be located in or relocating to Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit a non-refundable $5,000 application fee (check payable to Montgomery County, remitted to the Director of Finance)
Provide background information on the organization including three years of financial statements
Provide a detailed project description including financing amount requested, project costs, and site information
Provide corporate employment data including current and projected headcount in Montgomery County
Submit a Statement of Benefits to Montgomery County
Provide a Letter of Good Standing from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation at time of application
Bonds must state that neither the full faith and credit nor taxing power of Montgomery County is pledged to payment
For non-profits: must be a tax-exempt entity under IRS Section 501(c)(3); must provide IRS Determination Letter before bond closing
For non-profits: underwriter must provide a letter confirming the project is financially feasible
For non-profits: non-collegiate schools must hold a Certificate of Approval from the State Board of Education (or exemption determination)
For non-profits: medical or health service organizations must be licensed by the County, State, and/or Federal government
For non-profits: religious organizations must obtain a preliminary letter from bond counsel confirming no constitutional separation of church and state violation
For for-profits: project must be non-speculative and comply with federal tax legislation
For for-profits: business and/or landlord must pay and be current on all County and State property taxes
For for-profits: project should have a positive economic and fiscal impact on the County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Borrower submits completed application, supporting materials, and $5,000 non-refundable fee to the Department of Finance (DOF) and bond counsel. 2. DOF reviews the application and requests a Letter of Intent; bond counsel drafts a County Council Resolution. 3. DOF holds a TEFRA public hearing and forwards its recommendation to the County Executive. 4. If the County Executive accepts, the Resolution is forwarded to the County Council. 5. County Council votes on the Resolution. The full process takes at least 6 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) provides eligible county residents who own and live in their property a $692 credit on their property tax bill, listed as 'County Property Tax Credit' on tax bills. The credit is designed to offset increases in County income tax revenues resulting from a County income tax rate above 2.6%, with the credit amount set by County Council resolution. To receive the credit, residential property owners must have a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). This is a one-time application requirement — once approved, the credit applies automatically to future years. The HTC application must be filed by May 1 to ensure the credit appears on tax bills beginning July 1 of that year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $692 annual credit applied to the property tax bill of eligible Montgomery County homeowners, listed as 'County Property Tax Credit' on tax bills. The credit offsets in whole or in part increases in County income tax revenues from a County income tax rate above 2.6%, with the amount set by County Council resolution. The credit is automatic each year once a one-time Homestead Tax Credit application is approved by SDAT. The application must be filed by May 1 to ensure the credit appears on tax bills beginning July 1 of that year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residential property owners who own and occupy their property as a principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces the annual property tax bill by $692, offsetting increases in County income tax revenues resulting from an income tax rate above 2.6%.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owner-occupied principal residences in Montgomery County, Maryland. The underlying Homestead Tax Credit application is administered statewide by SDAT across all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must own and occupy the property as a principal residence in Montgomery County.
Must have a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
Property must be owner-occupied principal residence as determined by SDAT.
Homestead Tax Credit application must be filed by May 1 to ensure the credit appears on tax bills beginning July 1 of that year.
Only one application is required — the credit applies automatically in future years once approved.
Property must be used as a single principal residence for the full calendar year.
Federal and Maryland income tax returns must be filed at the property address.
Driver's license or state ID address must match the property address (if applicable).
Voter registration address must match the property address (if registered).
No portion of the residence may be rented out.
Married couples may only claim one principal residence.
Must provide SSN of all homeowners and spouses on the Homestead Tax Credit application.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check your Homestead Application Status on the SDAT Real Property website (sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty). If your status shows 'Approved' or 'Application Received,' no further action is needed. Step 2: If status shows 'No Application,' apply online via Maryland OneStop or by mail using the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application (available at dat.maryland.gov or as a paper PDF). Filing online is faster. You only need to apply once. Contact the Montgomery County Department of Finance for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individuals 65 and Above and Retired Military Services Members Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County property tax credit for homeowners who are 65 or older and either have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years, or are retired from the U.S. armed forces, uniformed services, or National Guard. The credit equals 20% of County property taxes only on the owner-occupied dwelling, granted for 7 consecutive years. Surviving spouses of eligible military retirees may also qualify. Properties must meet assessment value limits depending on the applicant category (up to $700,000 for 40-year homeowners; up to $550,000 for military retirees).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 20% credit on County property taxes only for owner-occupied dwellings. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years. For 40-year homeowners, the property assessment must be $700,000 or less at time of application. For military retirees, the assessment must be $550,000 or less. Even if an owner meets both criteria, the credit remains 20% for 7 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners who are 65 or older and have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years, or are retired from the U.S. armed forces, uniformed services, reserves, National Guard, Public Health Service uniformed corps, or NOAA uniformed corps. Surviving spouses of eligible military retirees may also qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Montgomery County property taxes on an owner-occupied dwelling by 20% for up to 7 consecutive years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Montgomery County, Maryland. The owner applying must be on the deed for the property.
requirements_list: Must be 65 or older (born on or before June 30, 1961 to receive credit beginning Levy Year 2026)
Must be an owner-occupant of the property

Must meet one of: (1) owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years (deed dated June 30, 1986 or earlier), or (2) retired from U.S. Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy, NOAA uniformed services, Public Health Service, military reserves, or National Guard
For 40-year owners: property assessment must be $700,000 or less
For military retirees: property assessment must be $550,000 or less

For properties titled in a trust: must submit a completed Affidavit Re Trust Ownership; applicant must be settler, grantor, or beneficiary of the trust and must not pay rent or other remuneration to reside in property

Surviving spouses of military retirees must be at least 65 years old, must not have remarried, and must provide: death certificate, signed affidavit of non-remarriage, and proof of retiree's retired status (DD-214 marked 'RETIRED' or Retired Military ID)
Application must be received on or before April 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Tax Credit Application (and Affidavit Re Trust Ownership if property is held in a trust, or Surviving Spouse Application and Affidavit if applicable). Mail the completed application with required documentation to: Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Bill 42-16 Tax Credit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Applications received by April 1 will be processed on the property tax bill issued in July of the same year. For assistance, call 240-777-0311 (or dial 311 within the county).

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Historic Preservation Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a property tax credit to encourage restoration and preservation of privately owned historically designated properties. The credit equals 25% of qualified costs spent on documented exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of properties designated as historic sites or within historic districts on the Montgomery County master plan for historic preservation, or designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council. The credit applies for the tax year following completion of the work and may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year on qualifying expenses. Eligible expenses include approved exterior work covered by a historic area work permit, such as painting, roof repairs, window repairs, chimney work, gutter replacement, repointing masonry, restoring documented features, uncovering original siding, and professional services. Interior work, additions, new construction, and owner labor costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs spent on exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year. The credit is applied against the following year's property taxes and may not exceed the total amount of County real property taxes. Any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five years. Eligible expenses include approved exterior work covered by a historic area work permit, such as painting, roof repairs, window repairs, chimney work, gutter replacement, repointing masonry, restoring documented features, uncovering original siding, and professional services (architects, engineers). Interior work, additions, new construction, and owner labor costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties designated as historic sites or located within historic districts on the Montgomery County master plan for historic preservation, including properties designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council or located within a Rockville historic district. Also applicable to businesses and property owners wanting to renovate historically designated properties in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work on historically designated properties, including painting, roof repair, window repair, chimney work, gutter replacement, repointing masonry, restoring documented features, uncovering original siding, and professional services such as architects and engineers. Reduction of County real property taxes based on qualifying expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. For properties in Rockville, properties must be designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council or located within a Rockville historic district regulated by the city. Properties listed only in the National Register of Historic Places are not eligible for this county credit.
requirements_list: Property must be an historic site or within a historic district on the master plan for historic preservation, or designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council or located within a Rockville historic district regulated by the city
Property must be listed in the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation
Work must be covered by an approved historic area work permit, or be ordinary maintenance exceeding $1,000
Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission (HDC)
Credit applies to exterior work only; interior work, additions, and new construction are not eligible
Owner must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year on qualifying expenses
Application must include copies of receipts for materials, paid receipts from a licensed contractor, and before-and-after photographs
Work requiring a Certificate of Approval (COA) must have obtained one prior to completion
Owner labor costs are not eligible; only materials costs may qualify
Unused credit may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years
Must be undertaking a renovation project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Historic District Commission (HDC) determines eligibility of expenditures and sends findings to the Montgomery County Department of Finance for processing. Applicants apply through the Montgomery County Planning Historic Preservation office. The director of finance reviews documentation and notifies the applicant of approval or disapproval. Contact Montgomery County Department of Finance at (240) 777-8931 for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Historic Preservation Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a property tax credit to encourage restoration and preservation of privately owned historically designated properties. The credit equals 25% of qualified costs spent on documented exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of properties designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs spent on exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year. The credit is applied against the following year's property taxes. Any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five years. Eligible expenses include approved exterior work such as painting, roof repairs, window repairs, chimney work, gutter replacement, and professional services. Interior work, additions, and routine maintenance are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties designated by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council, or properties within a Rockville historic district regulated by the city.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work on historically designated properties, including painting, roof repair, window repair, chimney work, gutter replacement, repointing masonry, restoring documented features, uncovering original siding, and professional services such as architects and engineers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owners of historic properties in Rockville, MD that are designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council. Properties listed only in the National Register of Historic Places are not eligible for this county credit.
requirements_list: Property must be designated historic by the City of Rockville's Mayor and Council or located within a Rockville historic district regulated by the city
Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission (HDC)
Owner must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year on qualifying expenses
Application must include copies of receipts for materials, paid receipts from a licensed contractor, and before-and-after photographs
Work requiring a Certificate of Approval (COA) must have obtained one prior to completion
Owner labor costs are not eligible; only materials costs may qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Historic District Commission (HDC) determines eligibility of expenditures and sends findings to the Montgomery County Department of Finance for processing. Applicants apply through the Montgomery County Planning Historic Preservation office. The director of finance reviews documentation and notifies the applicant of approval or disapproval.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers grants to employers in Montgomery County in select high-growth industries who create new full-time, permanent jobs paying $100,000 or more in base annual salary. Eligible industries include Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Hospitality, Life Sciences, and Quantum Computing Technology. Company headquarters and national nonprofit organizations are also eligible. Applicants must create at least five new qualifying jobs within twelve months of applying. Companies in Community Equity Index disadvantaged areas receive a higher award per job.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible companies receive a grant of $10,000 per new qualifying job created, or $12,000 per job if the business is located in a designated Community Equity Index disadvantaged area. The total award cannot exceed $500,000 per company. Each qualifying job must be a full-time, permanent position with a base annual salary of $100,000 or more. Applicants must create at least five new qualifying jobs within twelve months of applying, with an additional six-month window to hire beyond the initial five.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers located in Montgomery County, including company headquarters, national nonprofit organizations, and businesses in target industries: Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Hospitality, Life Sciences, and Quantum Computing Technology.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant supports business growth and expansion connected to hiring new full-time, permanent employees paying $100,000 or more annually.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Companies in Community Equity Index disadvantaged areas receive a higher award amount per job.
requirements_list: Must be a company headquarters, a national nonprofit organization, or operate in a target industry (Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Hospitality, Life Sciences, Quantum Computing Technology).
Must create at least five new full-time, permanent jobs within twelve months of applying.
Each new job must have a base annual salary of $100,000 or more, not including benefits.
Jobs must be created within a six-month period (with an additional 6-month window for positions beyond the initial five).
Business must be located in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Montgomery County Department of Finance via the online form at https://forms.montgomerycountymd.gov/f/JOBSFund. In the application, state the number of qualifying jobs you plan to create and the hiring schedule. The submission date starts a 12-month period in which you must hire at least 5 qualifying employees. You have an additional 6 months to hire positions beyond the initial five.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Property Tax Credit – Renewable Energy (Energy Conservation Devices)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County homeowners can receive a credit against County real property taxes for the installation of qualifying energy conservation devices on owner-occupied residential properties. Eligible improvements include air-sealing and insulation, heating and cooling equipment, windows, and doors — any device that reduces demand for conventional fuels or increases their efficiency. The credit is limited to $250 per property per fiscal year and can be claimed once per year for qualifying purchases made during that calendar year. The annual program pool is capped at $100,000, with credits granted in the order applications are received. Applications received after the cap is reached are carried over to the next fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County real property taxes of up to $250 per property per fiscal year for installation of qualifying energy conservation devices on owner-occupied residential properties. The credit may be claimed once per year for qualifying purchases made during that calendar year. Total annual program funding is capped at $100,000; applications are processed in the order received. Applications received after the cap is exhausted are carried to the next fiscal year. Applies to Section 2 (Energy Conservation Devices) of the Department of Finance renewable energy credits application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual; processed in order received until $100,000 pool is exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of owner-occupied residential properties in Montgomery County who install qualifying energy conservation devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property taxes based on installation of energy conservation devices, including air-sealing and insulation, heating and cooling equipment (HVAC), windows, and doors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland — homeowners with owner-occupied residential properties only
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied residential in Montgomery County
Device must reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase efficiency of those fuels
Device must meet safety and performance standards set by a nationally recognized testing laboratory
Qualifying improvements include air-sealing, insulation, HVAC equipment, windows, and doors
Standard household appliances do not qualify
Credit is limited to $250 per property per fiscal year
Credit may be claimed once per year for qualifying purchases made during that calendar year
Total annual credits capped at $100,000; applications processed in order received; excess applications carried to next fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application (Section 2 – Energy Conservation Devices) to the Montgomery County Department of Finance online or by mail, demonstrating eligibility of the installed device. Credits are granted in the order applications are received until the annual $100,000 cap is reached.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Refundable Earned Income Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County matches the State of Maryland's Refundable Earned Income Credit (EIC) at 56% for eligible low-income working residents. The County's program is administered through the Maryland Office of the Comptroller, which verifies eligibility and mails separate checks to qualifying residents on behalf of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County pays a refundable credit equal to approximately 56% of the Maryland State Refundable Earned Income Credit. Eligible residents receive a check from the Maryland Comptroller, paid for by Montgomery County. Checks are mailed based on when the tax return was filed: returns filed through June result in checks mailed by end of July; returns filed July through September result in checks mailed by end of October; returns filed through December result in checks mailed by end of January.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income working Montgomery County residents who qualify for the federal and Maryland State Earned Income Credit and have at least one dependent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct refundable credit payment to eligible low-income working residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident for the tax year in which the Refundable EIC is claimed.
requirements_list: Must have earned income in the tax year claimed
Must be eligible for the federal Earned Income Credit
Must claim the Maryland State Earned Income Credit
Must have at least one dependent
Must have filed as a Montgomery County resident for the applicable tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligibility is determined when the resident files their Maryland income tax return. No separate County application is required. The Maryland Comptroller verifies eligibility and notifies Montgomery County, which then mails a separate check to the taxpayer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for qualified disabled veterans or their surviving spouses against Montgomery County property taxes. Veterans with a permanent service-connected disability of 75% or more receive a credit equal to 50% of the County Tax. Veterans with a permanent service-connected disability between 50% and 74% (or a 100% non-permanent service-connected disability) receive a credit equal to 25% of the County Tax. Veterans who qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-208 of the Maryland Tax Property Article are not eligible. The property must be the principal residence occupied by no more than 2 families, and the veteran must have received an honorable discharge from the U.S. Armed Forces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against Montgomery County property taxes equal to 50% of the County Tax for veterans with a 75%+ permanent service-connected disability rating, or 25% of the County Tax for veterans with a 50%–74% permanent service-connected disability rating (or 100% non-permanent service-connected disability). Also available to qualified surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans. No cap on credit amount stated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before April 1 before the tax year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with a permanent service-connected disability rating of 50% or higher (or 100% non-permanent service-connected disability), and their qualified surviving spouses, who own and occupy property as their principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Montgomery County property tax liability on the veteran's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland only (Montgomery County Code, Section 52-113).
requirements_list: Must be a qualified disabled veteran with a permanent service-connected disability rating of 50% or higher, or 100% non-permanent service-connected disability, or a qualified surviving spouse of such a veteran
Must be subject to Montgomery County property taxes
Must not qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-208 of the Maryland Tax Property Article
Property must be the principal residence, occupied by no more than 2 families
Must have received an honorable discharge from the U.S. Armed Forces (38 U.S.C. § 101)
Federal Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) must be $100,000 or less

Application must be submitted with all three required documents: DD-214 discharge document (honorable conditions), VA disability certification showing percentage, and copy of most recent Federal Income Tax Return
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Disabled Veteran Tax Credit Application (PDF) on or before April 1 before the tax year for which the credit is sought. Three required attachments must be included: (1) DD-214 discharge document showing honorable conditions, (2) VA disability certification showing the disability percentage, and (3) a copy of the most recent Federal Income Tax Return (SSN may be redacted). If all three required documents are not submitted, the application will not be processed. Contact the Division of Treasury at 240-777-0311 or visit 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Public Safety Officers
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides a property tax credit on County property taxes for eligible active public safety officers, public safety communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and fire and rescue volunteers who own and live in a principal residence in Montgomery County. Expanded in 2025 to include full-time sworn police officers, firefighters, EMTs, and correctional officers employed by M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, County municipalities (Gaithersburg, Rockville, Takoma Park, Chevy Chase Village), and County employees assigned to the DHHS Crisis Center providing emergency response services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to the lesser of $2,500 or the amount of County property tax due on the applicant's principal residence. Applicants must apply annually by April 1 of the year prior to the Tax Levy Year for which the credit is sought.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 of the year prior to the Tax Levy Year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active County public safety officers, public safety communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, fire and rescue volunteers, and (as of February 2025) full-time sworn police officers, firefighters, EMTs, and correctional officers employed by M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, County municipalities, and County DHHS Crisis Center emergency response staff who own a principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces County property tax owed on the applicant's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be the legal owner of a principal residence in Montgomery County, MD.
requirements_list: Must be an active public safety officer, public safety communications specialist, deputy sheriff, correctional officer, or eligible fire and rescue volunteer — or a qualifying employee under the 2025 expansion
Must own and occupy a principal residence in Montgomery County
Must apply annually by April 1 of the year prior to the Tax Levy Year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Select and complete the appropriate online application link based on your employer (Active County Employee, Fire Rescue Volunteers, MNCPPC, WSSC, Gaithersburg, Rockville, Takoma Park, or Chevy Chase Village). An automatic email confirmation is sent upon successful submission. If no confirmation is received within 24 hours, contact MC311.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Local Income Tax Offset
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit against County property taxes on owner-occupied residential property, designed to offset increases in County income tax revenues resulting from a County income tax rate above 2.6%. The County establishes the credit amount by resolution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County real property taxes for owner-occupants of residential property, offsetting in whole or in part increases in County income tax revenues from an income tax rate above 2.6%. The amount is set by County Council resolution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential property in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied principal residence as determined by SDAT
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Determined by SDAT and Department of Finance; contact the Department of Finance for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Nonprofit Swim Clubs
structured_extraction.program_description: A County real property tax credit for nonprofit swim clubs in Montgomery County that use their facilities exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for the local community. Each year, qualifying clubs must provide documentation of nonprofit status and certify that their facilities are used solely for community recreation purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against General County tax and special service area taxes for qualifying nonprofit swim clubs. Each year, the club must provide documentation of nonprofit status and certify that its facilities are used solely for providing a recreational outlet to the local community. Required documents: copy of Articles of Incorporation and current Certificate of Good Standing from the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit swim clubs in Montgomery County using facilities exclusively for local community recreation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property taxes and special service area taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit entity
Must be a nonprofit swim club
Facilities must be used exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for the local community
Must provide: copy of Articles of Incorporation and current Certificate of Good Standing from the State of Maryland
Documentation and certification must be provided annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required documentation and certification to the Montgomery County Department of Finance each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Renters' Property Tax Relief Supplement (County Supplement)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides a supplemental property tax relief payment to renters who receive the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit. The County Supplement equals 50% of the State credit amount. No separate application is needed — when a renter applies for the State Renters' Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), the State shares credit information with the County, which then sends a check directly to the renter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A check equal to 50% of the State Renters' Tax Credit (which is up to $1,000) is mailed directly to eligible renters. No separate County application is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters in Montgomery County who qualify for and receive the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit — including renters age 60 or older, renters under 60 with at least one dependent child, or renters who are 100% disabled.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct payment to offset property tax burden for qualifying renters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to renters located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must receive the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit
Must be 60 years of age or older, under 60 with at least one dependent child, or 100% disabled (per State eligibility criteria)
No separate County application — eligibility is determined through the State application process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit through the SDAT website (dat.maryland.gov). The State will calculate the credit and notify the County. The County then calculates the supplement (50% of the State credit) and sends a check directly to the renter. Contact the County only if you received a State check but did not receive a County check within one year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Fire Sprinkler System Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time Montgomery County real property tax credit for homeowners and property owners who voluntarily install an approved complete automatic fire sprinkler system in a residential or multi-family building where such a system was not legally required. The credit is limited to the lesser of the total installation cost or 50% of the General County real property tax attributable to the unit or building. Applies to detached single-family homes, attached dwelling units, and units in multi-family buildings. The credit is applied in the tax year the sprinkler system is installed or the following tax year, and is one-time only per dwelling. The system must have been installed on or after July 1, 2000.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time credit against the General County real property tax for the voluntary installation of an approved complete automatic fire sprinkler system in a detached single-family dwelling, attached dwelling unit, or unit in a multi-family building where the system was not legally required. The credit is limited to the lesser of the total installation cost or 50% of the General County real property tax attributable to the unit or building. The credit applies in the tax year of installation or the following tax year, and is one-time only per dwelling. The system must have been installed on or after July 1, 2000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply in the year the sprinkler system is installed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of detached single-family homes, attached dwelling units, or units in multi-family buildings in Montgomery County who voluntarily install an approved complete automatic fire sprinkler system where such a system was not legally required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time reduction of General County real property tax to offset the cost of voluntarily installing a residential automatic fire sprinkler system for fire protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident or property owner in Montgomery County
Property must be a detached single-family home, attached dwelling unit, or unit in a multi-family building
The fire sprinkler system must not have been legally required to be installed
The sprinkler system must be an approved complete automatic system used for fire protection
System must be installed on or after July 1, 2000
Must apply in the year the sprinkler system is installed
Credit applies in the tax year of installation or the following tax year
Credit is one-time only per dwelling
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply to the Montgomery County Department of Finance in the year the sprinkler system is installed. Contact the Department of Finance at (240) 777-8931 or call 311 for assistance. Additional information is available on the Montgomery County Department of Finance website under Taxes > Individual Tax Credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Real Property Tax Deferral - General
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows eligible homeowners in Montgomery County to defer payment of annual increases in County property taxes on their principal residence, subject to income limits and residency requirements. Interest accrues on deferred amounts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Taxpayers may defer the portion of County property taxes that exceeds the prior year's County tax payment. Eligible taxes include General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues at a rate set annually by the County (not exceeding the prime lending rate). The total of deferred taxes plus interest may not exceed 50% of the full cash value of the property. Income limit: gross income of all residents of the dwelling must not have exceeded $120,000 in the preceding calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Montgomery County using the property as their principal residence with household income below $120,000
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of annual increases in County property taxes beyond prior-year tax amount
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must use property as principal residence
At least one owner must have resided in the dwelling as principal residence for at least 5 years
Gross income of all residents must not have exceeded $120,000 in the preceding calendar year
Accumulated deferred taxes plus interest may not exceed 50% of full cash value of the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Montgomery County Department of Finance for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Property Tax Credit (Montgomery County - Age 65+)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for eligible homeowners who are at least 65 years old and use the property as their principal residence. The credit equals 50% of the combined State Homeowners' Tax Credit and County Supplement, added to the County Supplement to further reduce the taxpayer's tax bill. The credit may be based on the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit, the Montgomery County Supplement, or both, depending on which applies. Taxpayers must apply for the State Homeowners' Tax Credit (HOTC) through SDAT to be considered; the senior credit is automatically calculated from that application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 50% of the combined State Homeowners' Tax Credit and County Supplement, added to the County Supplement to further reduce the taxpayer's County property tax bill. The credit amount may be based on the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit, the Montgomery County Supplement, or both, depending on which applies to the homeowner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners aged 65 or older for whom the property is their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County property tax liability for eligible senior homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be at least 65 years of age.
The home must be the applicant's principal residence.
Applicant must qualify for either the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit or the Montgomery County Supplement.
Must apply for the State Homeowners' Tax Credit (HOTC) through SDAT to be considered for the senior credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application for the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT); the senior credit is automatically considered from that application. A 2026 online application is available through the Maryland OneStop portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County invests funds in community banks headquartered in the county. Those banks match that amount with an equal commitment to lend, resulting in loans made to local small businesses to support job creation. All deposited County funds are covered by FDIC insurance. As of December 31, 2024, cumulative loans made from program deposits total over $180 million, with an estimated 4,299 jobs created since inception in 2012.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small businesses can access loans through participating community banks that have received County deposits under the program. As of 2024, participating banks include Capital Bank and Eagle Bank. The program channels lending to local small businesses — County funds are deposited in participating banks, which then make loans to small businesses at competitive rates. Participating banks must be headquartered in Montgomery County, have assets between $200 million and $10 billion, meet County safety and soundness standards (including minimum Veribanc rating), and originate loans within 12 calendar months of the County deposit commitment. County deposits are FDIC-insured.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Montgomery County seeking access to capital through community bank loans. As of 2024, participating lenders are Capital Bank and Eagle Bank, both headquartered in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business lending to promote job growth and small business development in Montgomery County; loans support working capital, expansion, and other standard small business credit purposes through participating community banks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses in Montgomery County, MD through participating community banks headquartered in the county
requirements_list: Loans must be originated through a participating community bank headquartered in Montgomery County
Participating banks must have assets greater than $200 million and no more than $10 billion
Participating banks must meet safety and soundness standards established by the County, including a minimum Veribanc rating
Loans must be originated within 12 calendar months of the County's program deposit commitment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for a loan through a participating community bank that is enrolled in the Small Business Plus! Program. As of 2024, participating banks are Capital Bank and Eagle Bank. The bank must be headquartered in Montgomery County and meet program eligibility criteria.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit - Home Computer Telecommuting Incentive (Montgomery County Telework Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual Montgomery County personal property tax credit for employers who purchase new home computers or laptops to establish new off-site employee workstations for telecommuting, for computers purchased after December 31, 2005. The County provides a credit against County personal property taxes equal to up to 50% of the cost of each personal computer purchased for teleworking employees, with a maximum annual credit of $2,000 per taxpayer per tax year. Credits are subject to an annual cap set by the County Council and are granted in the order received. The credit must be applied in the tax year of purchase or the following tax year, and applications must be submitted within 12 months of purchase. Employees must work from home at least 78 days per calendar year and certify that computers are used for business purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County personal property tax equal to up to 50% of the cost of each new home or laptop computer purchased to establish a new off-site employee telecommuting workstation. Maximum aggregate credit per taxpayer per tax year is $2,000. Annual cap on total credits issued set by County Council. Must be applied in the tax year of purchase or the following tax year. Application must be made within 12 months of purchase. Employees must certify that computers are used for business purposes and that they work from home at least 78 days per year (approximately 1.5 days per week).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and businesses in Montgomery County who purchase computers to support employee telecommuting from home, establishing new off-site workstations for remote workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County personal property tax based on cost of new home computers or laptops purchased for employees who telecommute from home at least 78 days per year; supports establishment of off-site employee workstations for telecommuting employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employers and businesses located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Montgomery County
Must establish a new off-site employee workstation
Computer must be purchased after December 31, 2005
Computer must be purchased for employees who telework from home
Employees must certify computers are used for business purposes
Employee must work at home at least 78 days per calendar year (approximately 1.5 days per week)
Employer must document date of purchase and cost
Credit must not exceed 50% of cost per computer
Aggregate credit per taxpayer per year must not exceed $2,000
Application must be submitted within 12 months of purchase
Credits granted in order received; subject to annual County Council cap
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply to the Montgomery County Department of Finance within 12 months of computer purchase by submitting the Telework Tax Credit Application form. See the Montgomery County property tax credit and exemption information page for more details. Credits are granted in order received and are subject to an annual cap set by the County Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Day Care Provider
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County real property tax credit for property owners whose improvements are used exclusively for licensed or registered day care services, including registered family day care homes, licensed child care centers, licensed day care centers for the elderly, and licensed day care centers for the medically handicapped. Also available to businesses with at least 25 employees that own property used exclusively for on-site day care services. The credit is limited to the lesser of $3,000 or the amount of the General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the qualifying improvement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County real property tax limited to the lesser of $3,000 or the amount of the General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the improvement used exclusively for day care services. Businesses with at least 25 employees using improvements exclusively for day care also qualify. Application must be submitted by April 1 for the credit to apply in the next taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and taxpayers making improvements to real property used exclusively for licensed or registered day care services; businesses with at least 25 employees providing on-site day care
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property taxes on improvements used exclusively for day care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Improvement must be used exclusively for: registered family day care home, licensed child care center, licensed day care center for the elderly, or licensed day care center for the medically handicapped
For business applicants: business must have at least 25 employees
Credit limited to lesser of $3,000 or applicable County/Special Area taxes on the improvement
Application must be submitted by April 1 for the credit to apply in the next taxable year
Property must be owned by the applicant (for business applicants)
Property must be used exclusively for day care services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Property Leased by Religious Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: A County real property tax credit for the portion of a property that is leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or supporting office space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County real property tax for the portion of a property leased and used by a religious organization exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support those activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners whose property is leased to and used exclusively by religious organizations for worship, education, or supporting office purposes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County real property tax on portions of property used for religious or educational purposes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Application must be filed with the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1 preceding the tax year in which the credit is to be used
Property must be leased to, occupied by, and used exclusively by a religious organization for public religious worship, educational purposes, or supporting office space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File application with the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1 for the credit to apply in the following tax year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Spouse of Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker
structured_extraction.program_description: A County real property tax credit equal to 100% of County property taxes on the dwelling of a surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker, provided the spouse has not remarried and meets qualifying conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit equal to 100% of County real property taxes on the principal dwelling of a surviving, unremarried spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker. The dwelling must have been owned by the officer/worker at their death, or acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years if the officer/worker or spouse was domiciled in Maryland at the time of death. Application must be submitted by April 1 for the credit in the next taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers or rescue workers in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full elimination of County real property taxes on the surviving spouse's principal dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Surviving spouse must not have remarried

Dwelling must have been owned by the fallen officer/worker at the time of death, OR acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of death if the officer/worker or spouse was domiciled in Maryland at time of death
Application must be submitted to the Division of Treasury by April 1 for credit in the next taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for urban agricultural use in Montgomery County. The credit is not issued on the annual July tax bill but is calculated and issued on a subsequent revision of the tax bill, appearing as a line item deduction. Once issued, the revised bill is available on the Real Property Tax Bill website or by calling 311. The program was enacted March 7, 2017 with no sunset date, and operates on a recurring annual cycle with 2-year credit terms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for urban agricultural properties in Montgomery County. The credit appears as a line item deduction on a revised property tax bill rather than the annual July bill. Credits are issued for 2-year terms, and property owners must reapply each tax year. Once issued, the revised bill is available on the Real Property Tax Bill website or by calling 311.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 of the tax year before the credit is sought; renewal no later than 90 days before expiration of the credit
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners (eligible taxpayers) in Montgomery County engaged in urban agriculture; no income cap or exclusions specified
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for qualifying urban agricultural properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be used for urban agricultural purposes
Application must be submitted to the Office of Agriculture
Application must be filed on or before April 1 of the tax year before the credit is sought
Renewal application must be filed no later than 90 days before expiration of the credit
Property owners must reapply each tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Urban Agricultural Property Tax Credit Application online or obtain a paper version from the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850. Submit the application to the Office of Agriculture at the address on the application. The initial application deadline is April 1 of the tax year before the credit is sought; renewals must be filed no later than 90 days before the credit expires.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Biotechnology Investor Incentive Program (BIIP) awards supplemental grants to qualified investors who have been approved for and received a final tax credit certificate from the State of Maryland's Biotechnology Investment Incentive Tax Credit Program and who have invested in biotechnology companies located in Montgomery County. The grant is prorated based on the program's appropriation and the investor's share of total state tax credits received by investors in County biotechnology businesses. The county typically pays out the grants between March and May for investments made in the previous calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Fund Grant & Loan Program (EDFGLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The EDFGLP is a discretionary strategic program focused on attracting and retaining businesses in targeted industry sectors that generate significant economic development impact in Montgomery County. The program provides grants and loans to private employers who retain existing jobs or create new jobs. Priority is given to high technology companies, manufacturing companies, businesses in urban revitalization areas, and private employers providing the greatest public benefits. The program typically provides assistance from $5,000 to $100,000, with larger projects potentially receiving more. Awards include conditions for disbursement, minimum performance measures, and clawback provisions if a business fails to meet expected economic output such as job growth, job retention, or capital investment.
