structured_extraction.program_description: The MOVE (Make Office Vacancies Extinct) program offers grants to businesses new to Montgomery County or expanding their existing office space, in order to reduce vacant Class A and B office or flex space. Businesses new to the County that sign a qualifying direct lease can receive a per-square-foot grant of $8.00 per square foot leased, up to a maximum of $80,000, for leases of at least three years covering up to 20,000 square feet of Class A or B office or flex space. Grants are also available for businesses signing their first commercial office lease or expanding their existing office space lease by at least 500 square feet. Retail businesses, restaurants, and independent financial or insurance agent/broker establishments are not eligible. Applications must be submitted within 180 days of lease execution on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's SBIR/STTR Matching Grant Program provides non-dilutive matching grants to small biotechnology, medical, and life sciences companies in Montgomery County that are applying for or have received federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) awards. Described as the only county-level SBIR/STTR match program of its kind in the country, it was established in 2018 and updated to reach more early-stage biotech companies. The program offers three tiers: Phase 0 (up to $5,000 to reimburse technical assistance costs for companies pursuing their first SBIR/STTR Phase I application), Phase I (up to $25,000, representing 25% of the federal Phase I award), and Phase II (up to $50,000–$75,000, representing 25% of the federal Phase II award). Up to 50% of each matching grant may be used to reimburse expenses for technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance. Funds cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by other federal or state sources. The program expired as of July 1, 2025, and is no longer accepting applications pending possible reintroduction by the County Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Jobs Tax Credit & Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A County property tax credit for businesses that expand their space and workforce in Montgomery County. The standard New Jobs Tax Credit is a six-year credit for businesses that increase space by at least 5,000 sq ft and add at least 25 new permanent full-time jobs. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit targets very large expansion projects in qualified industries, running 24 years at a flat rate, for businesses adding at least 250,000–700,000 sq ft and 500–1,250 new positions within six years of notification date. Both credits are based on the increase in real and personal property tax assessments resulting from expansion. Recipients may also qualify for an additional State income tax credit applicable against Individual or Corporation Income Tax, Financial Institution Franchise Tax, or Insurance Premiums Tax. Both credits include a recapture provision if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years. Businesses must notify the County before expanding to be eligible.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The standard New Jobs Tax Credit is a six-year credit against local real and personal property taxes: 52% of additional tax in years 1–2, 39% in years 3–4, and 26% in years 5–6. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit runs 24 years at a flat 58.5% of additional local tax liability. Recipients may also receive a State income tax credit (28%/21%/14% for the standard credit; 31.5% for all 24 years of the enhanced credit) applicable against Individual or Corporation Income Tax, Financial Institution Franchise Tax, or Insurance Premiums Tax. State credits can be rolled forward up to five years. Both credits include a recapture provision if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizens Real Property Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County allows eligible senior homeowners to defer the portion of their County residential property tax that exceeds the prior year's County property tax bill. Only the County Property Tax line on the tax bill is eligible for deferral — State taxes, municipal taxes, fees, and other charges are not eligible. The deferred amount accrues no interest during the deferral period. The total accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the property's fair market value. The deferred amount becomes a lien on the property and a personal liability of the applicant, secured by a Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement. Deferred taxes become due when the property is sold, transferred, the owner no longer uses it as their principal residence, the property goes to tax sale, or the use of the property changes. If approved, the deferral is applied to the second installment of the property tax bill or refunded if the bill was paid in full.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners may defer the amount by which their current County Property Tax exceeds their previous year's County Property Tax. The total accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the property's fair market value. A lien is recorded in Montgomery County land records for the total deferred amount with priority equal to current tax liens, and is a personal liability of the applicant, secured by a Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement. If approved, the deferral is applied to the second installment of the property tax bill or refunded if the bill was paid in full. The deferral ends when the property is transferred, the owner stops using it as their principal residence, the property goes to tax sale, or the use of the property changes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Adult Dental Program (separate from Dental Connections - different application process)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Adult Dental Program provides dental care services at reduced-cost county-run dental clinics for uninsured adults ages 19 to 59 who live in Montgomery County and meet income guidelines (family income no greater than 250% of the federal poverty level). Services include general dentistry, non-surgical extractions, and limited oral surgery; braces and dentures are not provided. Specialty care referrals are also provided as needed. Applications can be submitted via the Community Connect Portal, by email, by U.S. mail, or in person at one of four dental clinic locations in Rockville, Silver Spring, Germantown, or Gaithersburg.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Support Network (CSN) for People with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description:
The Community Support Network (CSN) provides services to help individuals with developmental disabilities remain in their home or the least restrictive environment in Montgomery County, Maryland. CSN coordinates and monitors services, provides crisis management and school-to-work transition assistance, and offers service coordination for young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder through the Maryland Home and Community Based Services Waiver. CSN also provides financial assistance to State-funded providers serving adults with developmental disabilities and conducts site visits to group homes serving people with various disabilities.

Within CSN, the Coordination of Community Services (CCS) sub-program provides case management and advocacy for individuals with developmental disabilities who have been determined eligible by Maryland's Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA). Coordinators help individuals and their families obtain appropriate services and supports in their community, meet health and safety needs, and pursue their own goals and preferences. Note: the Montgomery County DHHS CCS program is currently at capacity (500 clients) and is not accepting new clients or transfers; a waiting list of approximately 100 individuals exists.

Other CSN sub-programs include: My Turn (support for families with children ages 3–18 with developmental disabilities not connected to State resources, including summer camp placements and financial assistance); Autism Waiver coordination (service coordination for children ages 0–21 with Autism Spectrum Disorder); Respite Services (short-term relief for unpaid caregivers of children with severe medical conditions, children/adults with disabilities, or frail seniors); and financial assistance to State-funded providers serving adults with developmental disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Coordinated Entry System (CES) provides a streamlined process for individuals and families seeking homeless services. Through multiple access points, CES connects people in housing crisis to the most appropriate support, including permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, emergency shelter, and short-term rental assistance. The system uses real-time data and standardized assessments to prioritize housing placements based on need. The CES is open to all Montgomery County residents who meet the HUD definition of homelessness and operates under a Housing First, low-barrier approach. Veterans are explicitly prioritized, and dedicated pathways exist for families, youth, single adults, domestic violence survivors, and returning citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CES connects individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing crisis to appropriate housing services, including permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, emergency shelter, and short-term rental assistance. Outreach workers, emergency shelters, DHHS offices, libraries, hospitals, correctional facilities, drop-in centers, and youth-specific centers serve as access points covering the entire geographical area of Montgomery County. Standardized assessments (VI-SPDAT, Full SPDAT, Montgomery County Acuity Scale) prioritize placement based on level of need. Additional assistance includes case management, diversion, eviction prevention, utility assistance, and rental subsidies ($100–$503/month). Veterans are explicitly prioritized over non-veterans in each prioritization category. Matching meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of every month. Post-match referral timeline is 3 business days. Housing providers must meet with clients within 3 business days of referral.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families in Montgomery County experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis, including: literally homeless individuals and families (HUD Category 1), those at imminent risk of homelessness (Category 2), and those fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence (Category 4). Specific subpopulations served include veterans, young adults (18–24), single adults (18+), families with or without minor children, domestic violence survivors, returning citizens, and older adults (55+). Income-based prevention assistance available to households at or below 60% of Area Median Income. Note: As of August 1, 2025, a Youth CES component had not been finalized; status of that track may still be pending.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting individuals and families to homeless services and housing placements, including permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, emergency shelter, case management, outreach, diversion, eviction prevention, utility assistance, and rental subsidies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County residents. Access points cover the entire geographical area of Montgomery County, including Upcounty, Midcounty, East County, Germantown, Gaithersburg, Rockville, Wheaton, Silver Spring, and Bethesda. Referring providers must demonstrate that the program participant resides in Montgomery County. Domestic violence and trafficking survivors are exempt from the residency requirement for diversion services.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident (DV/trafficking survivors exempt from residency requirement for diversion services)
Must be experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis
Must meet the HUD definition of homelessness (Category 1, 2, or 4) or be at risk of homelessness
Must go through a standardized assessment (VI-SPDAT, Full SPDAT, or Montgomery County Acuity Scale) to prioritize housing placement
Montgomery County Acuity Scale must be completed within 1 month of initial assessment
Category 3 (Homeless Under Other Federal Statutes) is not utilized by the Montgomery County CoC
Prevention assistance requires household income at or below 60% of Area Median Income
Some programs require disability or age 55+ for eligibility
Asset limits apply for some programs (e.g., $10,000 for certain programs)
SHaRP rental assistance caps participant contribution at 40% of income over $1,000/month
Providers must comply with Fair Housing Act, ADA, and Section 504
Diversion: families must explore diversion alternatives before shelter referral
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the system through multiple entry points including outreach workers, emergency shelters, DHHS offices, correctional facilities, hospitals, drop-in centers, libraries, and youth-specific centers. A standardized assessment is conducted to determine appropriate housing services and prioritization. Different access points serve different household types: households with dependent children, adult-only households, youth ages 16–24, and domestic violence survivors have dedicated pathways (CES-FAM for families with minors; CES-IND for adult-only households). Matching meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of every month. Clients may decline housing matches. Program transfers are available with documented justification. For policy, procedures, prioritization, referrals, vacancies, or grievances, contact CES.Ind@montgomerycountymd.gov. The CES Program Manager holds weekly office hours.

structured_extraction.program_name: Dental Health Services Sliding Fee Discount and Financial Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Dental Program offers a Sliding Fee Discount that reduces the cost of dental care at county dental clinics based on family income, family size, insurance coverage, and number of visits needed. Additional financial assistance is available through an interest-free payment plan (up to 12 months) and/or a Dental Hardship Fee Reduction/Waiver for patients with qualifying debt obligations affecting their ability to pay.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A sliding fee discount scale set by the Maryland Department of Health reduces dental care costs based on income, family size, and insurance (Medicaid). Interest-free payment plans can be spread over up to 12 months. A Dental Hardship Fee Reduction or Waiver is available on a case-by-case basis for patients with qualifying financial obligations; if approved, eligible dental expenses incurred within 6 months of the hardship determination may be fully or partially waived. Hardship eligibility is reassessed every 6 months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Dental Health Services Sliding Fee Discount, Financial Assistance, Montgomery Cares Dental Program, and Dental Connections Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Dental Program offers multiple forms of dental assistance to low-income and uninsured residents. A Sliding Fee Discount reduces the cost of dental care at county dental clinics based on family income, family size, insurance coverage, and number of visits needed. Additional financial assistance is available through an interest-free payment plan (up to 12 months) and/or a Dental Hardship Fee Reduction/Waiver for patients with qualifying debt obligations affecting their ability to pay. Through the Montgomery Cares program, dental care services are provided to uninsured adult Montgomery County residents with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level who are not eligible for other health insurance coverage. The Dental Connections Program connects eligible Montgomery County residents enrolled in the county dental services program with community dentists and dental organizations to receive dental services—including exams, x-rays, cleanings, fluoride treatments, sealants, fillings, extractions, root canals, crowns, dentures, and oral health education—at a sliding fee discount based on income and family size. A Ryan White HIV Dental Program is also available for eligible individuals with HIV, with income eligibility up to 500% of the federal poverty level. Dental Connections availability is subject to funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A sliding fee discount scale set by the Maryland Department of Health reduces dental care costs based on income, family size, and insurance (Medicaid) at county dental clinics and through community dental offices. Interest-free payment plans can be spread over up to 12 months. A Dental Hardship Fee Reduction or Waiver is available on a case-by-case basis for patients with qualifying financial obligations; if approved, eligible dental expenses incurred within 6 months of the hardship determination may be fully or partially waived, and hardship eligibility is reassessed every 6 months. Through Montgomery Cares, dental care services are provided at reduced or no cost to eligible uninsured adults with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. Through the Dental Connections Program, enrolled patients can access dental services including exams, x-rays, cleanings, fluoride treatments, sealants, fillings, extractions, root canals, crowns, dentures, and oral health education at community dental offices at a sliding fee discount based on income and family size. Eligibility is based on family income up to 250% FPL for most programs, or up to 500% FPL for the Ryan White HIV Dental Program. Dental Connections availability is subject to funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Health Care for the Homeless Program (HCHP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Health Care for the Homeless Program improves health access, outcomes, and equity for single adults and families experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County. The program provides integrated medical and psychiatric care with service coordination, hospital discharge planning, emergency room diversion, assistance with medical and social benefit enrollment, and prescription access. Through nurse-led case management in shelters, street medicine for the unsheltered, and collaboration with local hospitals, clinics, and behavioral health providers, the program connects individuals to primary care, specialty services, rehabilitation, medical respite, and mental health support.

No fees for any services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) provides financial assistance to low-income households to help pay electric and heating bills. Eligibility is based on household size and gross income, with the income limit set at 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. Specific programs include EUSP (Electric Universal Service Program) for electric bill subsidies, MEAP (Maryland Energy Assistance Program) for heating/fuel assistance, ARA and GARA for electric and gas arrearage assistance up to $2,000 per application once every five years, USPP (Universal Service Protection Program) to prevent shut-offs via budget billing enrollment, and referrals for no-cost energy efficiency improvements through DHCD.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help low-income households pay their electric and/or heating bills. Benefit amount is based on household size and gross income (must be at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines). Income limits for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 range from $2,608/month for a 1-person household to $9,025/month for an 8-person household, with $917 added per additional member. Specific programs include: EUSP (Electric Universal Service Program) for electric bill subsidies; MEAP (Maryland Energy Assistance Program) for heating/fuel assistance; ARA (electric arrearage assistance) and GARA (gas arrearage assistance) up to $2,000 per application once every five years; USPP (Universal Service Protection Program) to prevent shut-offs via budget billing enrollment; emergency crisis assistance (disconnection prevention, heating fuel, system repair); and energy efficiency improvements (furnace clean/tune, insulation, efficient light bulbs) referred through DHCD at no cost to income-eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents needing help paying electric and/or heating bills, including renters, homeowners, and roomer/boarders who are the responsible party on utility accounts. Prioritizes households facing energy crisis or at risk of utility disconnection, those with medical equipment dependency, and those lacking heating fuel, with income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward electric bills (EUSP), heating/fuel bills (MEAP), electric arrearage assistance up to $2,000 once every five years (ARA), gas arrearage assistance up to $2,000 once every five years (GARA), budget billing enrollment to prevent shut-offs (USPP), emergency crisis assistance (disconnection prevention, heating fuel, system repair), and referrals for no-cost energy efficiency improvements (furnace clean/tune, insulation, efficient light bulbs) through DHCD.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland counties served through dedicated local OHEP offices: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Applicants must return their application and documents to their local OHEP office.

Montgomery County DHHS serves as a Supports Planning Agency for four Maryland Department of Health programs: Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS), Community First Choice (CFC), Community Options (CO) Waiver, and Increased Community Services (ICS). Eligible CO Waiver applicants in nursing homes can also receive help transitioning back to community living.
