structured_extraction.program_description: A post-arrest diversion program for homeless individuals charged with specific nonviolent misdemeanors or who have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses. Participants can choose to resolve their legal matters through the program rather than through traditional court processes. The program was developed in collaboration with the Montgomery County State's Attorney's Office and operates on a voluntary engagement model. After 90-day compliance, charges are dropped and an expungement filing is initiated.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive assistance resolving open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters — including outstanding warrants — outside of the traditional court system through post-arrest diversion. Eligible charges include alcohol offenses (non-DUI), disorderly conduct, drug possession, panhandling, public urination, theft, traffic offenses, trespass, property destruction, and other misdemeanors. The program is voluntary and provides case management support through an action plan, progress reporting, and participant exit process. Upon 90-day compliance, charges are dropped and an expungement filing is made.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless individuals in Montgomery County (on the street, in a shelter, doubled up with friends or family, in a motel, or in a place unfit for human habitation) who have been charged with nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors or transit/traffic offenses, with pending cases or warrants issued in Montgomery County District Court.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Resolving open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters including outstanding warrants through diversion rather than traditional prosecution or trial. Eligible charges include alcohol offenses, disorderly conduct, drug possession, panhandling, public urination, theft, traffic offenses, trespass, property destruction, and other non-violent misdemeanors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Cases must be pending or warrants must have been issued in Montgomery County District Court. Applicants must be experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County, broadly defined to include persons on the street, in a shelter, doubled up with friends or family, in a motel, or in a place unfit for human habitation. Cases pending in Montgomery County Circuit Court are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County (on the street, in a shelter, doubled up with friends or family, in a motel, or in a place unfit for human habitation)
Must have been charged with specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors, transit, or traffic offenses
Pending case(s) or warrant(s) must have been issued in Montgomery County District Court
Must not have pending criminal cases in Montgomery County Circuit Court
Participation is voluntary
Must complete approved service plan within 90 days to have charges withdrawn and record expunged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can come from multiple sources including law enforcement, courts, attorneys, case managers, and self-referral. Any person, service provider, legal entity, or self-referral can submit a referral via email to hpcdp@montgomerycountymd.gov. Participants complete a referral form and authorization, then develop an action plan. Progress is tracked through progress reports. Monthly diversion meetings are held; referrals and inquiries can be sent to hpcdp@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Housing Stabilization Services provides case management and limited financial grants to help Montgomery County residents who are at risk of homelessness. Services include needs assessment, emergency financial assistance, and case management to help households keep their current housing, obtain new housing, prevent utility shut-off, restore disconnected utility services, and access burial assistance grants. Eviction prevention grants are available to eligible households facing a court judgment or eviction notice.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited financial grants for eviction prevention, security deposits, first month's rent, utility bill assistance, and burial assistance. Case management is also provided. Eviction prevention grants are available to households that meet income guidelines (at or below 60% of area median income), have received a court judgment or eviction/put-out notice, and have not received an eviction prevention grant in the preceding 12 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness, including those facing eviction, utility shut-off, or housing instability, with household income at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eviction prevention, security deposits, first month's rent, utility bill payments to prevent shut-off or restore service, burial assistance, and case management support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may also be eligible for additional municipal support.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
Must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months (for eviction prevention grants)
Must have a court summons, judgment, red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office, or a landlord-issued put-out notice (for eviction prevention grants)
Must provide photo identification for all adults in the household
Must provide bank/financial statements for the last 30 days
Must provide income documentation for the last 30 days for all adults
Must provide proof of expenses (utility bills, rent, etc.)
Must provide emergency court/legal documentation if applicable
Must provide current rental ledger for eviction prevention cases
Must provide welcome letter and lease for security deposit and first month's rent assistance
Must sign a Release of Information Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of three HSS offices in person (Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring) during lobby hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.; sign-in by 4:30 p.m.). Bring all required documentation at the time of application. For housing emergencies (eviction judgment or red and white notice from the sheriff), call 311 to be connected with HSS. Reasonable accommodations, including electronic document submission, are available by contacting the office or calling 311.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation Support Services
structured_extraction.program_description: This program connects mental health professionals with licensed early care and education providers and families in Montgomery County. Consultants observe children and classrooms, gather information through conversations with parents and child care staff, and develop individualized strategies to support children's social and emotional development at child care and at home. The goal is to help educators understand how relationships affect young children's growth, foster positive environments, reduce challenging behaviors, prepare children for school, and lower the risk of expulsions.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mental health consultation services provided by licensed mental health professionals. Consultants observe children in child care settings, develop individualized strategies for both the child care setting and home, and provide families with referrals and resources. No fees charged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and licensed early care and education providers in Montgomery County with children ages birth to 5 years enrolled in licensed child care programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health consultation to support children's social and emotional development, build educator capacity, develop individualized strategies, and connect families with referrals and resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Services are available through licensed child care programs (not before or after school programs).
requirements_list: Child must be between birth and 5 years old
Child must be enrolled in a licensed child care program
Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Montgomery County Child Care Support Services at 240-777-4769 (240-777-GROW) to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County public health program that accepts referrals to case manage mothers and newborns with medical or social problems that could affect their health, development, or well-being. Public health nurses conduct home visits after receiving referrals, which are typically submitted by hospitals using the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form. The program targets teen mothers, those with no prenatal care, substance use issues, mental or behavioral health concerns, intimate partner violence, unstable housing, previous infant death or preterm birth, very low birthweight newborns, and other serious risks.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home visits by public health nurses to case manage at-risk mothers and newborns. There are no fees or payments required. Services are accessed through a referral form faxed to a health center.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mothers and newborns with medical or social risk factors, typically referred by hospitals where babies are born.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visiting case management services for at-risk mothers and newborns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Services provided at Silver Spring Health Center, Germantown Health Center, and DHHS Offices in Rockville.
requirements_list: Referral submitted via Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form

Must meet one or more risk criteria: teen mother, no prenatal care, substance use/misuse, mental/behavioral health concerns, intimate partner violence, unstable housing/homelessness, previous infant death, previous preterm birth, very low birthweight (<1500 grams), or other serious risk for mother or infant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fax the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form to the Silver Spring Health Center (fax: 240-777-3054) or the Germantown Health Center (fax: 240-777-4648). Once a referral is received, a public health nurse will contact the mother to set up home visits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund (LRMF) is a program run by Montgomery County's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) that offers financial incentives to landlords who rent to tenants referred through the county's homelessness services. Landlords who partner with the program can access incentive payments, direct connections to supported tenants, and networking opportunities, while helping to minimize risks associated with renting to individuals experiencing homelessness. Reimbursement is claims-based and covers property damages, unpaid rent, and vacancy losses, with financial limits of $5,000 annually per tenant and $10,000 lifetime per tenant.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Incentive payments and risk mitigation funds provided to landlords who lease units to tenants referred by the county's homelessness services. Reimbursement is claims-based and covers any combination of financial losses associated with property damages, unpaid rent, and vacancy losses. Financial limits are $5,000 annually per tenant and $10,000 lifetime per tenant. Security deposit must be applied first and landlord must attempt collection from tenant before claiming. For unpaid rent claims, required documentation includes notice to vacate, tenant contact letter, rent ledger, and insurance claim docs (if applicable). For property damage claims, required documentation includes notice to vacate, tenant contact letter, repair receipts/invoices, damage description attributing damage beyond ordinary wear and tear (per DHCA OLTA guidelines), and insurance claim docs (if applicable). Claims are eligible after 10 business days of non-payment. Payment is contingent upon approved claim amount to the extent of available funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords in Montgomery County who own and operate licensed rental property and are interested in renting to tenants referred by the county's homelessness prevention services (SEPH programs including SHaRP, RRH, and others).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentive payments to landlords to offset risks of renting to individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including reimbursement for any combination of financial losses associated with property damages, unpaid rent, and vacancy losses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Eligible landlords must own and operate licensed rental property located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Landlord must partner with Montgomery County's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH)
Unit must be available for lease to SEPH-referred tenants
Landlord must sign the LRMF Program Agreement
Unit must pass inspection per the LRMF Inspection Checklist
Tenancy must have initially begun on or after March 1, 2024
Security deposit must be applied before submitting a claim
Landlord must attempt collection from tenant before submitting a claim
Claim may be submitted after a 10 business day threshold of non-payment
Photos/videos required for property damage claims
Housing locator/service provider must assist with inspection process
For unpaid rent claims: notice to vacate, tenant contact letter, rent ledger, and insurance claim docs (if applicable) required

For property damage claims: notice to vacate, tenant contact letter, repair receipts/invoices, damage description attributing damage beyond ordinary wear and tear per DHCA OLTA guidelines, and insurance claim docs (if applicable) required
Security deposit accounting required with any claim
LRMF reserves the right to suspend or terminate new enrollment at any time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landlords interested in partnering can download the claim form, brochure/FAQ, program agreement, and inspection checklist from the program page. They then sign the agreement and work with SEPH to match with referred tenants. A pre-move-in inspection must be completed using the LRMF Inspection Checklist, signed by the tenant, landlord/property manager, and service provider/housing locator, with photos/videos submitted to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov. For claims, landlords must first apply security deposit and attempt tenant collection, then submit a completed claim form with supporting documentation to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov. Claims are reviewed by LRMF and SEPH staff against program policies and may be approved, denied, or partially approved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Landlord Supports – Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) partners with landlords to quickly match them with potential tenants experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Participating landlords receive financial incentives, risk protections, ongoing support services, and networking opportunities in exchange for leasing to supported tenants.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landlords who partner with SEPH can receive: free marketing of rental units, a Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund, double security deposit where appropriate, financial bonuses for signing leases and referring other landlords, access to care coordination and conflict mediation, technical assistance, and connection to other county resources. Consistent rent payments are facilitated through housing providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords and property owners in Montgomery County who are willing to lease units to tenants experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial bonuses, risk mitigation fund payments, and double security deposits are available to landlords who lease to SEPH-referred tenants. Technical assistance and care coordination services are also provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a landlord or property owner with rental units in Montgomery County
Must be willing to partner with SEPH to house tenants referred through the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landlords can partner directly with Montgomery County SEPH to begin receiving referrals and incentives. Contact information is not listed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Lead for Impact (LFI) is a six-month peer leadership development program for professionals working to end homelessness in Montgomery County. Participants gain leadership skills through group workshops, one-on-one coaching, small group peer meetings, and a personal leadership project. The program builds confidence, community, and practical tools for influencing decisions and driving change within the County's Continuum of Care.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-month cohort-based leadership program including: a virtual orientation session, six group workshops (mix of in-person and virtual), three one-on-one virtual coaching sessions per participant, monthly small group peer meetings, monthly pre-work (video lessons and reflection exercises), a 360-degree leadership profile, and development of a personal Leadership Project. Total time commitment is estimated at 2–4 hours per week. Application requires written responses and video submissions (estimated 60–90 minutes to complete).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professionals and leaders working to end homelessness in Montgomery County, including staff at direct service providers, nonprofit organizations, and county government agencies across the Continuum of Care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leadership development training — not a financial assistance program. Participants invest time to develop leadership skills and advance a Leadership Project aimed at ending homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals working in Montgomery County, Maryland on homelessness-related issues.
requirements_list: Committed to ending homelessness in Montgomery County
Ready to step into a leadership role
Able to attend all scheduled in-person and virtual sessions
Must submit an application by the deadline
Selection is competitive; applicants must demonstrate good fit and contribute to a diverse cohort
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the application instructions (PDF), then submit the application form online via Google Forms. Applications include written responses and video submissions (estimated 60–90 minutes). Applications due April 2nd at 5 p.m. Selected participants notified by April 17th. Space is limited and a selection process is used.

structured_extraction.program_description: Linkages to Learning provides accessible health, mental health, social services, and educational support to at-risk children and their families at school-based sites across Montgomery County. The program aims to improve children's adjustment to and performance in school, home, and community through prevention and early intervention services that address social, economic, health, and emotional barriers to academic success.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free therapy, family care management, and community engagement services provided at 33 elementary and middle schools across Montgomery County. Mental health services are free for uninsured students; Medicaid is billed when applicable. Some sites also include School-Based Health Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk children and their families in Montgomery County who attend participating schools, with therapy prioritizing uninsured or underinsured students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care, mental health therapy, family care management, community engagement, and educational support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must attend one of the 33 participating elementary and middle schools in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Student must attend a participating school
Therapy prioritizes uninsured or underinsured students
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through your school counselor or self-referral by contacting the program. Documents needed will be communicated when the appointment is made or at the first meeting.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides on-site and in-home Community Health Nurse Case Management services to uninsured pregnant women and their children up to age two. Services include health education, assessment and referral, and help accessing health, economic, and self-sufficiency programs. Three home visiting modalities: (1) Nurse Home Visiting for first-time moms, teens, and high-risk pregnancies; (2) Community Health Worker Home Visiting for those with low health literacy, first birth in the US, or social concerns; (3) Babies Born Healthy Program for African American pregnant persons in the Silver Spring region of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free nurse case management services delivered in-home or on-site. Services include health education, care coordination, assessment, and referrals to health, economic, and self-sufficiency programs. No fees charged. Referrals are submitted by healthcare providers via email to GHCReferrals@MontgomeryCountyMD.Gov or SSHCReferrals@MontgomeryCountyMD.Gov.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured pregnant women enrolled in the Montgomery County Maternity Partnership program and their infants up to age two who need nurse case management services. Priority populations include first-time mothers, teens, high-risk pregnant persons (those with diabetes, hypertension, history of pregnancy loss, preterm or low birth weight history, substance abuse or behavioral health concerns), pregnant persons with low health literacy, first birth in the USA, other social concerns, and African American pregnant persons in the Silver Spring region of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education during pregnancy, care coordination, referrals to community resources, preparation for delivery, and newborn care support. Includes home-based nursing case management and community health worker support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland enrolled in the Montgomery County Maternity Partnership program. One program track (Babies Born Healthy) specifically serves the Silver Spring region of Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be uninsured
Must be a pregnant woman enrolled in the Montgomery County Maternity Partnership program for prenatal services, or the infant of such a woman
Must need nurse case management services

Risk factors considered include: low health literacy, unsafe living environment, history of preterm birth, chronic medical conditions (e.g. diabetes, hypertension), depression or behavioral health concerns, prior pregnancy loss, close child spacing, low birth weight history, substance or alcohol use, tobacco use, teen status, first birth in the USA, advanced maternal age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No direct application required from the individual. Healthcare providers submit a completed perinatal program referral form on behalf of the pregnant person or family by email to GHCReferrals@MontgomeryCountyMD.Gov or SSHCReferrals@MontgomeryCountyMD.Gov. Women enrolled in the County Maternity Partnership prenatal program and their infants will be assessed and provided nurse case management if needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Medical Assistance Long Term Care (MA-LTC) helps Maryland residents living in a nursing home pay for their cost of care if they meet financial, technical, and medical eligibility criteria. The program also helps cover doctor, hospital, and other medical care services. Montgomery County's DHHS determines initial and ongoing eligibility for individuals residing in nursing homes who need help paying for their care.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays for nursing home care costs and other Medicaid-eligible services (doctor, hospital, and medical care) for eligible residents. There are no fees to apply. The applicant may be required to contribute a portion of their income toward nursing home costs, as determined by the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents living in a nursing home who need help paying for long-term care costs and meet financial, medical, and technical eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying for nursing home care costs and other Medicaid-eligible medical services including doctor and hospital care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County residents. Applicants must be Maryland residents and U.S. citizens.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be a Maryland resident
Must meet disability criteria if under age 65
Must meet income and asset eligibility requirements
Financial history over the past 60 months is reviewed
Must qualify for a nursing home level of care

Must provide documentation of citizenship and personal identification, Social Security number, health insurance, income from all sources, and assets (checking, savings, CDs, mutual funds, life insurance, trusts, stocks, bonds, real property, retirement accounts, IRA, etc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-3995 to request an application packet by mail, or pick it up in person at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Complete the packet and mail, deliver in person, or fax to 240-777-1330. You can also apply online through the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal at benefits.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medicaid/Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program (MHSDP) - Dental Services for Pregnant Women (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides dental services to pregnant women in Montgomery County who meet income and residency requirements, including U.S. citizens and non-citizens who do not qualify for Medicaid solely due to immigration status.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dental care coverage for eligible pregnant women through the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted prior to the final day of pregnancy
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women who are Montgomery County residents with income up to 250% of the federal poverty level, including non-citizens who do not qualify for Medicaid solely due to immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental services for pregnant women.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only.
requirements_list: Montgomery County resident
U.S. citizen or non-citizen who does not qualify for Medicaid solely due to immigration status
Currently pregnant
Application submitted prior to the final day of pregnancy
Income up to 250% of the federal poverty level

structured_extraction.program_description: Medical Assistance (also known as Medicaid) pays medical bills for low-income families and individuals in Montgomery County. It covers services including inpatient and outpatient hospital care, pharmacy, physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health, and substance abuse treatment. Coverage groups include families and children under 21, and pregnant women.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid health insurance coverage with no fees or payments required from recipients. Covers inpatient/outpatient hospital care, pharmacy, physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health, and substance abuse treatment. Managed care organization (MCO) plans are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income adults under 65, families, children under 21, and pregnant women who are Montgomery County residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care coverage including hospital care, pharmacy, physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health, and substance abuse treatment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County residents
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must be a county resident
Proof of income required (tax return or two recent pay stubs)
Proof of identity required (driver's license or photo ID)
Proof of citizenship required (birth certificate or passport)
Social Security number required
Pregnant women may qualify under Healthy Babies Equity Act (regardless of immigration status) or Full Medicaid (U.S. citizens and lawfully present individuals)
SSI recipients should contact their local office to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at Maryland Health Connection (marylandhealthconnection.gov), by phone at 855-642-8572, or in person at one of four regional Office of Eligibility and Support Services locations in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown. Applications are processed in approximately 10 days. Interpreter services are available for non-English speakers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medical Assistance (MA) for Aged, Blind, or Disabled and Medicare Savings Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Medical Assistance for the Aged, Blind, and Disabled (MA-ABD) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) are Medicaid-administered programs that help low-income residents cover healthcare costs. MA-ABD provides full Medicaid health coverage for people with very low income who are aged (65+), blind, or disabled. Medicare Savings Programs help Medicare beneficiaries pay for Medicare premiums and out-of-pocket costs through the Special Low Income Medicare Beneficiary Program (SLMB) and Qualified Medicare Beneficiary Program (QMB).
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MA-ABD provides full Medicaid health coverage for eligible low-income aged, blind, or disabled individuals. Medicare Savings Programs cover Medicare premiums (SLMB) and Medicare deductibles and co-pays (QMB) for eligible low-income Medicare beneficiaries. No fees or payments are required from recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Montgomery County residents who are aged (65+), blind, or disabled, and Medicare beneficiaries with income within specific limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Healthcare coverage including full Medicaid benefits (MA-ABD) or payment of Medicare premiums, deductibles, and co-pays (MSPs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, Maryland residents. Applications can be submitted online, by mail/fax, or in person at offices in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown.
requirements_list: Must be aged (65 or older), blind, or disabled — those under 65 may qualify with a documented disability or by receiving Social Security
Income and assets must be within program limits
Those receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) automatically qualify for MA-ABD
For Medicare Savings Programs, must be enrolled in Medicare with income within specific limits
Must provide proof of identity, Social Security number, proof of income, and proof of citizenship or immigration status (for non-U.S.-born applicants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal (benefits.maryland.gov), by mail or fax, or in person at regional offices in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown. Language interpretation is available. Processing takes approximately 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mental Health Services for Older Adults/Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides outreach and mental health services to older adults aged 60 and over and adults with disabilities in Montgomery County who are unable to access mental health services within traditional treatment settings. Services are delivered in the home and offered free of charge regardless of insurance status.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home mental health outreach and services, including therapy, delivered to eligible residents at no cost regardless of insurance status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are older adults (aged 60 and over) or adults with disabilities who cannot access mental health services in traditional treatment settings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home mental health outreach and therapy services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be an older adult aged 60 and over OR an adult with a disability
Must be unable to access mental health services within traditional treatment settings
Client must agree to receive services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Local Behavioral Health Authority at 240-777-4529 to be referred or apply for services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Cares - Medical Care for Uninsured Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery Cares is a network of community-based health care providers that offer free medical services to uninsured, low-income adults living in Montgomery County. Services include doctor and nurse visits, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, oral health care, and access to other health programs. Eligibility is determined at participating health centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free medical care services with no fees or payments required. Services include routine check-ups, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist access, and oral health care provided through a network of community health centers across Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured, low-income adults (age 18 or older) who are residents of Montgomery County with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level and not enrolled in any health insurance (Medicaid, Medicare, commercial, or employer-sponsored).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care including check-ups, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, oral health care, and other health programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be age 18 or older
Be uninsured
Have income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
Be a resident of Montgomery County
Not be enrolled in any health insurance including Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance, or employer-sponsored coverage
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the health center of your choice or call 311 to find a health center near you. Contact the health center to make an appointment. Bring proof of income (pay stubs, tax returns, or employer letter) and proof of Montgomery County residency (mortgage, lease, utility bill, driver's license, tax return, etc.) to your first appointment. Eligibility is determined at the health center.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Birth to Five Early Head Start Community Based Model
structured_extraction.program_description: An Early Head Start program that partners with registered family child care homes and licensed center-based child care programs in Montgomery County to provide full-year, full-day services for infants and toddlers. Child care programs apply to become Early Head Start child care hubs and receive funding plus wrap-around services. The program serves 75 children ages birth to 3. Income-eligible families with children birth to three years old living in Montgomery County may also apply for services, space permitting.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care programs receive $17,964 per child per year to provide a full-year (1,380 annual hours), full-day (9-hour) Early Head Start program. Programs also receive training, technical assistance, and coaching from the County's Early Childhood Services program, including the Child Care Resource Center, the Infants and Toddlers Early Intervention Program, Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation, and family engagement services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application Opens November 1st (year not specified; contextually November 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care homes and licensed center-based child care programs with a minimum Level 3 EXCELS rating in Montgomery County; income-eligible families with children birth to three years old living in Montgomery County may also apply for services, space permitting
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing full-day, full-year Early Head Start services to infants and toddlers; wrap-around staff and family support services including early childhood education, family engagement services, health services, training/technical assistance, and ECE coaching support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Families must reside in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care home OR a licensed center-based program
Must have a minimum Level 3 EXCELS rating
Families must be income-eligible and have children ages birth to three years old
Families must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible child care programs can contact Charlene Muhammad by phone (240-777-1769 English, 240-777-1426 Spanish) or email to learn more and apply. Families apply directly with Montgomery County and receive a list of participating childcare programs to select from; the application link is posted on Montgomery County Community resources. Application opens November 1st; program begins in Winter (January).

structured_extraction.program_description: Head Start and Pre-K program for children ages 3 to 4 in Montgomery County. Families must meet income requirements to qualify. The program provides early childhood education and developmental services for low-income families.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Head Start and Pre-K educational services for eligible children ages 3-4 whose families meet income requirements. Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is currently underway.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 3-4 who meet income requirements in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early childhood education and developmental services for children ages 3-4
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be 3 or 4 years old by September 1st
Family must meet income requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online through MCPS. New MCPS families must create an account; existing MCPS parents can log into the ParentVUE site. Call 240-740-4530 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Infants and Toddlers Program (MCITP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Infants and Toddlers Program (MCITP) provides free early intervention services to families with infants and toddlers (birth to 34.5 months) who have developmental delays or are at high risk for delays. Services include developmental assessment, individualized family service planning, service coordination, therapies (physical, occupational, speech/language), audiology, nursing, nutrition counseling, psychological services, special instruction, and family support. All services are delivered in the child's natural environment — home or community settings — at no cost to the family.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free early intervention services provided at no cost to families, including developmental assessment, individualized family service plan development, service coordination, and a range of therapies and support services tailored to each child's needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with infants and toddlers (birth to 34.5 months) who demonstrate a 25% developmental delay in one or more areas, have atypical development, or have a high-probability condition likely to result in developmental delays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services including assistive technology, audiology, family counseling and training, nursing, nutritional counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, psychological testing, special instruction, speech/language therapy, social work, transportation, and services for visual and hearing impairment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to families residing in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must be between birth and 34.5 months of age
Child must demonstrate a 25% delay in one or more developmental areas, OR have atypical development or a high-probability condition likely to result in developmental delays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can apply by visiting the referral website at http://referral.mditp.org/ or by calling the program at 240-777-3997. Interpreter services are available for all languages.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County MAT Program provides evidence-based treatment for individuals living with Opioid Use Disorder and other substance use challenges. The program combines FDA-approved medications (methadone, buprenorphine, naltrexone, and vivitrol) with individualized counseling, mental health support, and care coordination to support recovery and long-term wellness.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers individualized treatment planning, medication management, individual and group counseling, co-occurring mental health services through an Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP)/Outpatient (OP) program, and care coordination. Fees are charged on a sliding scale for uninsured individuals. Maryland Medicaid (MA) and Pharmacy Adult Care (PAC) are accepted. No one is refused services due to inability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents aged 18 and older who are addicted to narcotic drugs such as heroin, oxycodone, or Percocet.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder and other substance use challenges, including medication management, counseling, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be addicted to narcotic drugs such as heroin, oxycodone, or Percocet
Must provide proof of residency (mail with home address or letter from landlord)
Must provide valid identification (driver's license)
Must provide copy of any insurance cards including Medical Assistance and primary insurance card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1680 to apply. Walk-ins are also accepted at 1500 East Gude Drive, Rockville, MD 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a supplement to the state Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) for eligible county residents. The supplement provides a 56% match of the Maryland State EITC. Eligible ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) filers may also receive this credit. To receive this credit, residents must file a Maryland Tax return.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 56% match of the Maryland State EITC for eligible Montgomery County residents. ITIN filers are also eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income working residents of Montgomery County, including ITIN filers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to reduce or refund state income tax liability for eligible county residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible residents of Montgomery County, Maryland who file a Maryland Tax return
requirements_list: Must be an eligible Montgomery County resident
Must file a Maryland Tax return
Eligible ITIN filers may also receive this credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Maryland Tax return. Montgomery County's VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) program can provide free tax preparation assistance, including for ITIN taxpayers.

structured_extraction.program_description: The My Turn Program provides resources, education information, and short-term financial assistance to families and caregivers of children with intellectual or developmental disabilities. Funding can be used for recreational activities, summer camp, limited medical supplies, medical equipment, augmentative devices, and behavioral consultation. The program also offers referrals and educational seminars.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term, limited financial assistance provided one request at a time. Funding for recreational activities is available from July through January; summer camp funding requests are accepted from February through the first week of July. Only one request can be submitted at a time. The program also provides education, information, resources, referrals, and educational seminars.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; recreational activities July–January, summer camp February–first week of July
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and caregivers of Montgomery County residents ages 3 to 18 with a developmental disability as defined by the Maryland Developmental Disability Administration (DDA), who are not already receiving long-term funded programs through Montgomery County or Maryland State
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreational activities (e.g., swimming, horseback riding), summer camp, limited medical supplies, medical equipment, augmentative devices, behavioral consultation, referrals, and educational seminars. Cannot be used for therapeutic services such as occupational therapy, physical therapy, or speech therapy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident. Office located at 1401 Rockville Pike, 2nd Floor, Rockville, MD 20852.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Child must be between 3 and 18 years of age (must apply before child turns 19)

Child must have a developmental disability meeting the Maryland DDA definition: a physical or mental condition (other than a sole diagnosis of mental illness), likely to continue indefinitely, manifested before age 22, resulting in an inability to live independently
Must provide all documentation related to the child's developmental disability, including school records, Individualized Education Plan (IEP), and psychological evaluations
Child must not already be receiving long-term funded programs through Montgomery County or Maryland State
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1216 to schedule an intake interview with a My Turn Program staff member. Bring all documentation related to the child's developmental disability, including school records, IEP, and psychological evaluations. Office located at 1401 Rockville Pike, 2nd Floor, Rockville, MD 20852. TTY users may use MD Relay 711. Fax: 240-777-4625.

structured_extraction.program_name: Naloxone Free Training Program (Opioid Overdose Response Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services offers free 2-hour trainings on how to recognize an opioid overdose and use naloxone (a prescription medication that reverses opioid overdose effects) to save a life. Participants learn overdose identification, naloxone administration, overdose prevention tips, and information about local and national resources. The training is open to anyone aged 18 or older who is concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with an opioid addiction.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 2-hour in-person training on identifying opioid overdoses and administering naloxone. Training is provided at no cost to participants aged 18 and older who are concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with an opioid addiction. Participants also receive overdose prevention tips and information about local and national resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals aged 18 or older who are concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with an opioid addiction
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participating in training to learn overdose recognition, naloxone administration, and overdose prevention strategies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with an opioid addiction
Must register in advance by contacting the Overdose Response Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Overdose Response Program by phone at 240.777.1836 or by email at OverdoseResponseProgram@montgomerycountymd.gov to register for an upcoming training session.

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) & Housing Initiative Program (HIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: HIP and PSH provide long-term housing subsidies and case management to individuals exiting homelessness in Montgomery County. Participants pay 30% of their household's adjusted gross income directly to the landlord, with the remainder (approximately 70% of rent) paid by the housing provider. Assistance may also cover application fees, security deposit (up to 2 months rent), and a utility allowance for eligible participants. Case management includes in-home visits occurring 3–4 times per month. All participants are referred through the Montgomery County Coordinated Entry System (CES) and assessed for Permanent Supportive Housing eligibility.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 30% of adjusted gross household income to the landlord; the housing provider pays the remainder (approximately 70% of rent) directly to the landlord. Assistance may also cover application fees, security deposit (up to 2 months rent), utility allowance for eligible participants, and monthly case management with in-home visits 3–4 times per month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless or shelter-residing Montgomery County residents with specific disabilities or vulnerabilities and income at or below 30% AMI, as well as landlords partnering with Montgomery County SEPH.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Long-term rental subsidy (approximately 70% of rent), application fees, security deposit (up to 2 months rent), utility allowance for eligible participants, supportive and financial services, and monthly case management support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Participants must be Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Montgomery County resident
Homeless or in shelter placement
Income at or below 30% AMI
Must have specific disabilities or vulnerabilities as assessed through Coordinated Entry System
Participants pay 30% of adjusted gross household income toward rent
Participation is ongoing as long as participants qualify and remain eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All HIP participants are referred from the Montgomery County Coordinated Entry System (CES) and are assessed for Permanent Supportive Housing. Entry is referral-based, not direct application. No walk-in, online portal, or self-referral process is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: RRH offers a time-limited flexible housing subsidy and support services for individuals exiting homelessness. The subsidy lasts up to 12 to 24 months, and participants are expected to pay the full rent upon discharge from the program. Checks are paid directly to the landlord. The program includes security deposits (up to 2× monthly rental amount), monthly rental subsidy payments with a declining program contribution every 3 months based on tenant income, and financial services support and case management.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible housing subsidy for up to 12–24 months, paid directly to the landlord. Includes security deposits (up to 2× monthly rental amount), monthly rental subsidy payments (split between program and tenant contribution, declining every 3 months as tenant income increases), financial services support, and case management/support services. Participants pay full rent upon program discharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents exiting homelessness and landlords partnering with Montgomery County SEPH. Tenants must meet income recertification requirements and be eligible for ongoing support. Landlords interested in continued partnership should reach out to the program contact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Time-limited rental subsidy (up to 12–24 months) including security deposits (up to 2× monthly rental amount), monthly rental subsidy payments with declining program contribution every 3 months, financial services support, and case management/support services to help participants maintain housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Participants are expected to pay full rent upon discharge from the program
Tenant income recertification required
Tenant contribution based on income, with program contribution declining every 3 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tenant application pathway is not publicly documented. Landlords interested in partnering with the program should reach out to Elizabeth.Driggers@montgomerycountymd.gov to express interest in continued partnership.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides monthly rental assistance subsidies to Montgomery County residents who are currently homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness and have a household member with a documented disability or who is at least 55 years old. Benefits range from $100 to $503 per month and are approved for up to 12 months, with renewal possible. Checks are made payable to both the tenant and landlord (two-party check) and mailed to the applicant at the end of each month for the following month's rent. Tenants are responsible for 35–40% of rent depending on household size.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly rental assistance checks of $100 to $503 per month, based on household income and rental amount, mailed to the applicant's address at the end of each month for the following month's rent. Checks are made payable to both the tenant and landlord (two-party check). Benefits are approved for up to 12 months; the subsidy is designed to renew annually if the tenant's income and rental amount remain within program limits. Renewal requires a new application. Tenants are responsible for 35–40% of rent depending on household size.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County renters who are currently homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness, with a household member who has a documented disability or is age 55 or older, and whose income and assets fall within program limits. Landlords who rent to eligible tenants may also participate by registering with the Montgomery County CVRS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental subsidy payments of $100–$503 to cover a portion of rent costs on behalf of eligible households. Funds are paid directly toward rent only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident and renter in Montgomery County, Maryland. No sub-county breakdowns, excluded neighborhoods, or municipal carve-outs apply.
requirements_list: Must be currently homeless (living in a car, on the street, or in a shelter) or at imminent threat of homelessness (eviction notice or lack of resources to maintain housing)
A household member must have a documented disability OR be at least 55 years old
Must be a renter in Montgomery County
Monthly rent cannot exceed program limits
Monthly gross income cannot exceed program limits (e.g., $4,783/month for a household of 1)
Household assets must be less than $10,000
Applications must be submitted by a Montgomery County Health and Human Services social worker or case manager (referral only; no self-referrals)
Cannot be receiving a Housing Choice Voucher or living in Public Housing
Cannot rent from a relative
For room rentals, the unit cannot be owned by the tenant's relative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a referral-only program. New applications must be submitted by a Montgomery County Health and Human Services social worker or case manager working within the Montgomery County Homeless Continuum of Care (e.g., Housing Stabilization Services). Renewal applications are mailed two months before benefits expire; applicants can also request a renewal application by calling 240-777-4400 or emailing RAP@montgomerycountymd.gov. The subsidy is designed to renew annually if the tenant's income and rental amount remain within program limits, with annual recertification required. Landlords must register via the Montgomery County Client Vendor Registration System (CVRS).

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services provides affordable general dental care — including preventive, restorative, and emergency dental services — to uninsured or underinsured residents of all ages who are living with HIV in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area (District of Columbia, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Charles County, and Calvert County). Clients must be enrolled in HIV case management or medical case management under Ryan White Part A or Part B services. Income eligibility is up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level, and eligibility is redetermined every 6 months. Specialty care such as dentures is not covered.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Affordable general dental care (preventive, restorative, and emergency services) provided at Dennis Avenue Health Center, 2000 Dennis Ave., Silver Spring, MD 20902, to eligible HIV-positive clients. Income eligibility is up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level. Fees are determined by calling the program; patients must bring proof of income to each visit and update income information every 6 months. Specialty care such as dentures is not covered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Eligibility form good for 6 months; provide income updates every 6 months
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or underinsured residents living with HIV in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area (District of Columbia, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Charles County, and Calvert County) who are enrolled in HIV case management or medical case management under Ryan White Part A or Part B services and have income up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General dental care services including preventive, restorative, and emergency dental services for people living with HIV.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area: District of Columbia, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Charles County, and Calvert County.
requirements_list: Must be HIV-positive
Must be enrolled in HIV case management or medical case management under Ryan White Part A or Part B services
Must reside in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area
Proof of residency in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area
Income up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level
Provide proof of income at each visit and update every 6 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1737 to schedule an appointment at Dennis Avenue Health Center, 2000 Dennis Ave., Silver Spring, MD 20902. Bring a completed registration packet and proof of income to your first visit. Eligibility is redetermined every six months.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides on-site dental services to students at select Montgomery County Public Schools during normal school hours, in partnership with Montgomery County Public Schools.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dental services including screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, and sealants provided at select schools during school hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students at select Montgomery County Public Schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, and sealants provided on school premises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select Montgomery County Public Schools.
requirements_list: Must be a student at a participating Montgomery County Public School
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email the Dental Kids program at hhsdentalkids@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 240-777-4238. Registration forms are available on the Application Forms page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Senior Care provides case management and support services for people aged 65 or older who are at risk of nursing home (institutionalization) placement. Gap-filling funds may also be available to pay for Adult Day Care, medical supplies, Personal Emergency Response Systems (PERS), medical reimbursement, transportation, and health and wellness programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management and support services are provided at no cost. Gap-filling funds (subject to funding availability) can cover Adult Day Care, medical supplies, Personal Emergency Response Systems, medical reimbursement, transportation, and health and wellness programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents aged 65 or older who are at risk of nursing home placement and meet financial eligibility guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adult Day Care, medical supplies, Personal Emergency Response Systems (PERS), medical reimbursement, transportation, and health and wellness programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland, including those living in group homes or assisted living facilities.

Must be a U.S. citizen or qualified alien
Must be at risk of institutionalization
Must meet financial eligibility guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Services Resource Unit at 240-777-3000 to apply. An in-home social work assessment will be scheduled during which eligibility is determined. Financial, medical, and identifying documentation will be required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Senior Dental program provides dental care to low-income residents ages 60 and above who meet income requirements. Applications can be submitted through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized dental care services for eligible low-income seniors ages 60 and above. Applications can be submitted through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental care services

Age 60 and above
Income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level

structured_extraction.program_description: SHaRP provides security deposit, first month's rent, and an additional rental subsidy for up to 12 total months to help individuals exiting homelessness secure and maintain housing. Participant rent contribution is based on income: if income exceeds $1,000/month, the tenant pays 40% of income toward rent and SHaRP pays the remainder; if income is less than $1,000/month, SHaRP pays full rent for up to 12 months. Supportive and financial services are also provided for up to 12 months. Checks are paid directly to the landlord.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers security deposit (up to double the monthly rental amount), first month's rent, and a rental subsidy for up to 12 months. If tenant income exceeds $1,000/month, tenant pays 40% of income toward rent and SHaRP pays the remainder; if income is less than $1,000/month, SHaRP pays full rent for up to 12 months. Supportive and financial services also provided for up to 12 months. Checks are paid directly to the landlord.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County households exiting homelessness who qualify for this support, including low-income renters in housing instability; and landlords partnering with Montgomery County SEPH.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Security deposit (up to double the monthly rental amount), first month's rent, and ongoing rental subsidy for up to 12 months. If tenant income exceeds $1,000/month, tenant pays 40% of income toward rent; if income is less than $1,000/month, SHaRP covers full rent. Supportive and financial services also provided for up to 12 months.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Participant must be a Montgomery County household qualifying for the program
If income exceeds $1,000/month, tenant contribution is 40% of income toward rent; SHaRP pays the remainder
If income is less than $1,000/month, SHaRP pays full rent for up to 12 months
Applicants work through a Case Manager
Tenant receives case management throughout the program
Income recertification process applies during program participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tenants should contact their Case Manager to initiate the process. Landlords or others interested in program partnership can reach out to sharp@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers tobacco cessation classes and support to help residents quit smoking. Classes are held at various locations, including hospital-based settings.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tobacco cessation classes at various locations. Some hospital-based classes charge a fee. Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) products are available free through 1-800-Quit Now.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who want to quit smoking
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1222 for information about current classes and locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Peer group education program for pregnant and parenting Montgomery County Public School (MCPS) students. Facilitated support groups led by school nurses and assisted by MCPS staff and community partners are available in all high schools, depending on need. Groups meet during the school day and cover topics such as raising children, healthy relationships, and preventing repeat teenage pregnancy.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free facilitated peer support groups held during the school day at high schools across Montgomery County. Participants share experiences, learn from peers, and receive presentations and discussions led by school nurses, MCPS staff, and community partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and/or parenting Montgomery County Public School students (both teen mothers and teen fathers)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in peer education support groups covering child-rearing, healthy relationships, and repeat pregnancy prevention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at high schools in Montgomery County, MD, depending on need.

Attendance is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See your school nurse for information about joining a support group.

structured_extraction.program_name: Welcome Back Center of Suburban Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps internationally educated health professionals — including nurses, international medical graduates (IMGs), and behavioral health specialists — obtain U.S. licensure and re-enter Maryland's health workforce. The Center provides personalized guidance, English language instruction, board exam preparation, career development, job readiness training, and hands-on experience in Maryland hospitals and healthcare facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, comprehensive support services including one-on-one personalized guidance, English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction, board exam preparation courses, career development and job readiness training, professional mentoring, and hands-on experience in Maryland healthcare facilities. No fees or payments are required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Internationally educated health professionals (nurses, physicians, behavioral health specialists) currently residing in Montgomery County, Maryland who obtained their degree outside the United States and wish to re-enter the health workforce.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language classes, board exam preparation, career development, job readiness training, professional mentoring, and hands-on healthcare experience to support licensure and re-entry into the health workforce in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must currently reside in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have completed at least three academic years of nursing education in an international program, OR a medical degree, OR a degree in behavioral health from an international program
Must receive a level 2 English placement test result from an accredited English language school
Must commit to working in the health field in Maryland for 2 years after obtaining licensure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Center by phone or email to express interest. Your information will be added to the Center's database and you will be notified about future opportunities, including when the application process opens. The Center will provide a detailed list of required documents during the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Working Parents Assistance (WPA) Program helps eligible County residents pay for childcare. While parents are at work or school, they can feel confident that their children are in a safe and caring environment. The program provides monthly subsidy vouchers to help cover the cost of licensed childcare providers.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly childcare subsidy payments are made via vouchers. Each voucher covers a set period of months per eligible child and specifies the monthly subsidy amount. The parent is responsible for any provider fees above the voucher amount. Income eligibility ranges from a minimum (at which point applicants must apply to the State program) to a maximum annual income that varies by family size (e.g., $76,118–$95,175 for a family of 2; $167,905–$342,675 for a family of 12).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County resident parents or guardians of children from birth to age 13 (up to 19 if the child has a disability) who are employed 25+ hours per week or enrolled full-time in an undergraduate or vocational program and meet income guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for licensed childcare services while parents are working or attending school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must meet income guidelines (minimum and maximum annual income thresholds based on family size)
Must be a parent or guardian of a child from birth to 13 years old (up to 19 if the child has a disability)
Must be pursuing child support through the court, voluntarily, or claim good cause
Must be employed 25 or more hours per week, or enrolled in a full-time undergraduate or vocational program, or a combination of both
Selected childcare provider must be licensed by the State of Maryland
For two-parent households, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements
Immigration status is not a barrier to participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the CommunityConnect portal at communityconnect.montgomerycountymd.gov. Gather required documents including proof of income, proof of enrollment (if applicable), proof of identity, proof of address, birth certificates for all children, child support documentation, and a copy of the previous year's federal tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Community Action Agency's VITA program offers free tax preparation and filing help for low- and moderate-income residents of Montgomery County who earned less than $69,000. IRS-certified volunteers prepare federal and state tax returns at no cost, and help filers claim all eligible tax credits, including the federal EITC (up to $8,046), the Maryland EITC, and the Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement. The program also assists with Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) applications and renewals. Services are available during tax season (mid-January to mid-April) and post-tax season (mid-June through October).
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services - Community Action Agency
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person tax return preparation by IRS-certified volunteers. Helps low- to moderate-income residents file federal and state taxes and claim all available tax credits, including the federal EITC (up to $8,046), the Maryland EITC, and the Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement. Also assists taxpayers in filing returns to establish tax compliance history, which may support good moral character documentation for future immigration status adjustments. Available at IRS-certified tax partner sites or through free software. ITIN application and renewal assistance is available on Wednesdays by appointment. Post-tax season appointments available mid-June through October.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tax season: mid-January to mid-April; Post-tax season: mid-June through October
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income individuals and families in Montgomery County who earned less than $69,000 in 2025, including ITIN filers, immigrant residents, and undocumented immigrants with federally taxable income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free preparation and e-filing of federal and state income tax returns; assistance claiming eligible tax credits and refunds; ITIN applications and renewals; assistance filing returns to establish tax compliance history and good moral character documentation relevant for immigration status adjustments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Earned less than $69,000 in 2025 to qualify for EITC-related assistance
ITIN filers may qualify for Maryland EITC and Working Families Income Supplement
Must bring Social Security card and/or ITIN for each family member
Must bring photo ID for each filer
Must bring W-2 forms for all jobs worked in 2025
Must bring child care provider information if applicable

Must bring a copy of last year's tax return
Must bring all 1099 forms for other income
