Valid ITIN or SSN required to file
Must meet federal tax filing requirements

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA) provides financial and technical support to help property and business owners make significant physical improvements to the exterior of older commercial buildings. The program reimburses eligible participants up to 50% of approved design and construction costs (up to $500,000) for buildings that are 10 or more years old or do not meet current commercial standards. In exchange, participants must maintain the improvements for a negotiated term (3–7 years) under a facade easement agreement with the County. Eligible improvements include facade renovation, building and pylon signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscaping, murals, ADA compliance upgrades, green infrastructure, and other exterior amenities. A separate Façade Refresh Grant Program is also available for lower-cost improvements such as canopies, signs, and painting (up to $15,000, no easement required). The goal is to create more visually appealing and safer commercial environments across Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Housing (WFH) Program makes homes affordable for households whose incomes are too high to qualify for the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program but who still cannot afford market-rate housing in Montgomery County. The program supports the construction of homes affordable to families earning up to 120% of the area median income, and gives those households more options for housing close to where they work. Homes purchased through the program are subject to a 20-year Control Period with restrictions on rental, refinancing, and resale prices.

During the 20-year Control Period, owners must occupy the home as their primary residence, may not rent it out without prior DHCA consent, may not refinance above DHCA's set resale price or below $10,000 equity, and may only sell to other WFH-eligible buyers at the price set by DHCA. After the Control Period, owners must share half of any net gain from a sale with the County's Housing Initiative Fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's MPDU Program requires residential developers to set aside a percentage of housing units at prices affordable to low- and moderate-income households. The program has two components: a Purchase Program and a Rental Program. For purchase units, eligible first-time homebuyers must complete three required training courses in order — an MPDU Orientation Seminar (held on the second and fourth Thursdays of each month, registration through the Greater Washington Urban League), a First-Time Homebuyer class from a HUD-approved housing counselor (offered on the second Saturday of each month), and an online Application Tutorial (must score 80% or better) — before submitting an application through the MPDU Application Portal. Applicants must be pre-qualified for a mortgage of at least $150,000. Household income must be between a minimum of $40,000 and a maximum based on household size (e.g., $92,000 for 2 people, $114,500 for 4 people) at up to 70% of the Washington Metro Area Median Income (AMI). For-sale units are made available through a lottery (random selection drawing) process, with prices ranging from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse with a garage. Property taxes are assessed on the MPDU value rather than market value. A 30-year control period applies, during which resale is restricted to the MPDU-established price; after the control period, the owner may sell at market price but must pay 50% of excess profit to Montgomery County. The MPDU Rental Program provides below-market rental units in apartment communities throughout the county; new tenants in garden apartments must earn below 65% AMI and new tenants in high-rise apartments must earn below 70% AMI. Rents are recalculated annually and increases are capped at the county's Voluntary Rent Guideline. Renewing rental tenants may earn up to 130% of the new-tenant income maximum. No amenities fees or surface parking fees may be charged to MPDU tenants. A 99-year control period applies to rental units. Note: the cities of Rockville and Gaithersburg have separate MPDU programs with their own policies.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible buyers purchase homes at MPDU-controlled prices significantly below market rate, ranging from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse with a garage. Property taxes are assessed on the MPDU value rather than market value. Buyers must obtain their own mortgage financing (pre-qualification for at least $150,000 required). During the 30-year control period, resale is restricted to the MPDU-established price; after the control period, the owner may sell at market price but must pay 50% of excess profit to Montgomery County. For rentals, below-market units are available at rates set by county executive regulation and recalculated annually; new tenants in garden apartments must earn below 65% AMI and in high-rise apartments below 70% AMI. Renewing tenants may earn up to 130% of the new-tenant maximum. Rent can only increase once per 12-month period and increases are capped at the county's Voluntary Rent Guideline. No amenities fees or surface parking fees may be charged to MPDU tenants. Income limits for purchase units: minimum $40,000 annually; maximum varies by household size (1 person $80,500; 2 people $92,000; 3 people $103,500; 4 people $114,500; 5 people $124,000; 6 people $133,000).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For purchase units: (1) Complete a pre-screening intake form and submit it to the Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL) at MPDU@GWUL.org to register for the MPDU Orientation Seminar (held on the second and fourth Thursdays of each month). (2) Attend the virtual First-Time Homebuyer Class (offered on the second Saturday of each month) after completing the Orientation Seminar. (3) Receive an email from the DHCA MPDU office with your Orientation ID confirming eligibility to take the Application Tutorial. (4) Gather all required documents, including mortgage pre-qualification letter, government-issued photo ID, tax returns, and pay stubs. Applicants who have changed employers or whose income has changed since filing taxes must also complete a Verification of Income Form (Part I completed by applicant; Part II completed by employer and returned to the MPDU Office). (5) Use the Classes Validation Form to self-validate attendance and follow the User Guide to create an AccessMCG Extranet account. (6) Complete the online Application Tutorial via the MPDU Application Portal (must score 80% or better). (7) Submit completed application and supporting documents through the MPDU Application Portal. Applications are reviewed within 30 days of submission. Upon approval, receive a Certificate of Eligibility valid for one year (must be renewed within 60 days of expiration). (8) Enter random selection drawings for available MPDU properties. For rental units: Apply directly to an MPDU apartment community of your choice — the MPDU office does not accept applications or issue eligibility certificates for rentals. Steps: (1) Review the list of apartment communities with MPDU units at the county's online portal. (2) Identify communities of interest. (3) Contact one or more communities to apply. The management company will provide an application, verify income and credit history, and determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) program provides real property tax abatement to support the construction and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing. The program lowers or completely eliminates County real property and special area taxes on rental housing projects for a set number of years in exchange for the property owner's commitment to provide affordable housing units to low-income residents. Four tracks are available: (1) Standard PILOT — tax abatement negotiated on a case-by-case basis, underwritten based on the number and affordability period of affordable units, with a financial pro forma and evidence of financial need required; (2) 'By right' PILOT — abates all County real property taxes for at least 15 years for properties owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, or by non-profit developers where at least 50% of units are reserved for households earning at or below 60% of Area Median Income (AMI) for at least 15 years; (3) WMATA PILOT — abates all County real property taxes for at least 15 years for new high-rise residential developments on land leased from the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) at Metro stations, where at least 50% of the project is residential and at least 25% of required moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) are affordable to households at or below 50% AMI; (4) Office to Residential Conversion PILOT — in development following legislation adopted in April 2025. DHCA recommends PILOTs to the Director of Finance for approval following legal, budgetary, and procedural review. The County Council sets a maximum annual funding amount for PILOTs for a 10-year period for properties not owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC). The Finance Department calculates the abatement annually based on property tax rates and assessment values. A monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year is charged to property owners, due by September 30 each year. Annual compliance requirements include filing financial reports and compliance certificates confirming income-eligible occupancy at affordable rents. PILOTs are governed by a Regulatory Agreement recorded in land records.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County real property and special area taxes are abated and replaced with a negotiated payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) for a defined term. Standard PILOT: amount negotiated based on number of affordable units and affordability duration; abatement is typically equal to the average County homeowner tax credit per affordable unit (adjusted annually). 'By right' PILOT: 100% abatement of all County real property taxes for at least 15 years for qualifying non-profit-owned or Housing Opportunities Commission-controlled rental properties. WMATA PILOT: 100% abatement of all County real property taxes for at least 15 years for qualifying high-rise transit-oriented developments at Metro stations. The Finance Department calculates abatements annually based on property tax rates and assessment values. The County Council sets a maximum annual funding amount for PILOTs for a 10-year period for properties not owned or controlled by HOC. A monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year is due by September 30 each year. Property owners must still pay State real property taxes, municipal taxes, front foot benefit charges, and other applicable fees unless otherwise waived. Standard PILOTs are not transferable; 'by right' PILOTs may be transferable under certain conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental property owners and developers (non-profit, for-profit, and government entities including the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County) in Montgomery County seeking to provide affordable multifamily rental housing to low-income residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax abatement on County real property and special area taxes in exchange for providing affordable rental housing units at specified income levels for a defined term, supporting affordable housing development and preservation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for rental housing projects located in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be a rental housing project located in Montgomery County
Owner must commit to providing affordable housing to low-income residents
Standard PILOT: number and duration of affordable units are negotiated on a case-by-case basis; financial pro forma and evidence of financial need required

'By right' PILOT: property must be owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, or owned/controlled by a non-profit developer; at least 50% of units must be leased to households with incomes at or below 60% of AMI for the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area; term of at least 15 years

WMATA PILOT: at least 50% of the project must consist of high-rise residential apartment buildings (more than 8 stories); land must be at a Metro station on property leased from WMATA; at least 25% of required MPDUs must be affordable to households at or below 50% AMI; at least 25% of construction workers must be County residents; quarterly reporting required
All applicants must meet requirements of Maryland State law governing PILOTs (Sections 7-501 et seq. of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland)
Rent levels must be limited per PILOT requirements
Annual financial reports and compliance certificates must be filed confirming specified number of units are occupied by income-eligible tenants at affordable rents
PILOT monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year must be paid by September 30 each year
PILOT governed by a Regulatory Agreement signed by the property owner and the County, recorded in land records
Standard PILOTs are not transferable; 'by right' PILOTs may be transferable under certain conditions
Agreement subject to legal, budgetary, and procedural review by DHCA and Department of Finance
Annual funding cap set by County Council for properties not owned or controlled by HOC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required documents electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@montgomerymd.gov or by mail to: Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. Required documents vary by PILOT type but generally include: legal description of the property, project description with total and affordable unit counts, documentation of affordability (e.g., rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants), and any other information required by the County. Standard PILOT also requires a financial pro forma and evidence of site control. By-right PILOTs are available automatically when eligibility criteria are met. DHCA reviews and recommends the PILOT to the Director of Finance for approval following legal, budgetary, and procedural review. After negotiation, the Asset Management team monitors ongoing compliance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Productivity Housing program allows developers to build affordable housing (both rental and for-sale) in commercial and industrial zones where residential use is not normally permitted. Units are priced to be affordable to households earning up to 75% of the County median income, adjusted for family size. Developers must obtain a Special Exception from the Board of Appeals and execute a written agreement with the Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA). For-sale units are subject to a 10-year control period and rental units to a 20-year control period.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program permits developers to build multifamily housing in commercial and industrial zones (C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, O-M, I-1, I-3, I-4) that would otherwise not allow residential use, through a Special Exception process. Base density is 6 units per acre, increasing to 21.5 units per acre if at least 35% of units are affordable at or below County median income. No more than 25% of commercially/industrially zoned land in each master plan area may be converted.

In return, property owners receive a per-unit subsidy paid by the County. The subsidy is generally calculated as the difference between the stipulated affordable rent and the average market rate rent for a comparable unit in the same or adjacent property.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Right of First Refusal (ROFR) program requires owners of multifamily rental housing with 4 or more units to offer the County, the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC), or a certified tenant organization the opportunity to purchase the property before selling to another party. The program preserves affordable housing and prevents tenant displacement. The County may also assign its ROFR rights to qualified affordable housing developers, who must agree to restrictions including tenant protections and rent increase limits.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Any purchaser exercising ROFR must pay no more than 5% of the contract price as a down payment and must close within 180 days of DHCA receiving the ROFR packet. Assignees must comply with tenant protections and limit rent increases to the Voluntary Rent Guidelines (VRG) for 15 years.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Common Area Assistance Loan Fund (CAALF) is a gap financing loan program operated by Montgomery County's Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA) that provides zero-interest loans to Common Ownership Communities (COCs) — such as homeowner associations, condominium associations, and cooperative housing projects — in Montgomery County that face severe financial hardship and need to make critical health and safety repairs to common areas. Eligible repairs include failing water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, and parking lots. Funds are limited to documented, immediate health and safety risks that threaten occupancy and cannot be used for amenity repairs. Predevelopment construction-related services may also be included. Montgomery County approved $1.23 million for FY2025 and $1.85 million for FY2026 (July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026).

COCs must contribute a minimum of 20% of total project hard costs from their own funds. Montgomery County approved $1.23 million for FY2025 and $1.85 million for FY2026 (July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026); future funding is subject to appropriation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Affordable Housing Financing Program (Housing Initiative Fund and HOME)
structured_extraction.program_description: Since 1989, the Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA) has provided flexible financing to for-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers to acquire, construct, and rehabilitate multifamily housing developments. DHCA offers loans from the Housing Initiative Fund (HIF) — a Montgomery County-funded initiative to promote a broad range of housing opportunities — and federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds, as well as grants, Rental Agreements, and tax incentive agreements called Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOTs) to support affordable rental housing production and preservation. Funds may be used to construct or acquire affordable housing units, buy and rehabilitate existing rental units at risk of removal from the affordable housing supply, and support development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. The program targets projects serving low-income households, with a preference for those serving households at or below 50% AMI, and aligns with County priorities such as income level served, preservation, production, senior housing, and permanent supportive housing. The targeted interest rate is 3%, though the rate may vary based on project purpose and financing structure. Loan terms are set by the Director based on project needs, and repayment is generally structured to meet the project's financial requirements and senior lender requirements. Projects are underwritten for financial feasibility, targeting a 3:1 leverage ratio of other resources to County funds, with an expected equity contribution of 10% from the owner/sponsor. Two application tracks exist: a small project application for projects with fewer than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 in county funds, and a large project application for projects with 10 or more county-funded units and $500,000 or more in county funds.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible loans from the Housing Initiative Fund (HIF) and federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds for acquisition, construction, and rehabilitation of multifamily affordable housing, as well as development of mixed-use projects that include affordable housing units. Projects are underwritten for financial feasibility, targeting a 3:1 leverage ratio of other resources to County funds. The program also includes grants, Rental Agreements, and Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOTs), which are tax incentive agreements that reduce or replace property tax obligations for affordable housing developments. Two application tracks exist: a small project application for projects with fewer than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 in county funds, and a large project application for projects with 10 or more county-funded units and $500,000 or more in county funds.

Schedule a design consultation meeting through the DPS online portal. A case facilitator will be assigned to guide the project through permit application and final inspection.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life (DFL) Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Design for Life (DFL) program, effective July 1, 2014, is a voluntary certification and property tax credit program for visitability and liveability in single-family attached and detached homes in Montgomery County. It covers both new construction and renovation. The program offers property tax credits to homeowners, builders, and developers who add accessibility features to residential homes or complete accessibility improvements through the Design for Life permit process. The program encourages development and renovation of housing that accommodates a wider range of accessibility needs, helping County residents remain in their homes as their physical needs change. It is open to people of all ages and life stages, including first-time homebuyers, families, active adults, and people living with temporary or permanent disabilities. Three tiers of property tax credits are available: (1) Individual Accessibility Features: a credit equal to the lesser of 50% of eligible costs or $2,500 per property owner per tax year (minus government/non-profit subsidies), with a maximum of $2,000 applied in any single tax year and excess credits carrying forward and transferring with the property upon sale; annual program cap of $100,000 per fiscal year. (2) Level I (VISITable) Accessibility Standards: up to $3,000 for new or existing single-family residences, townhomes, and duplexes, with a $2,000 maximum per tax year and excess carrying over; annual program cap of $500,000 per tax year. (3) Level II (LIVEable) Accessibility Standards: up to $10,000 for new or existing single-family residences (must also meet all Level I requirements), with a $2,000 maximum per tax year and excess carrying over; annual program cap of $500,000 per tax year. Eligible expenditures must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application. For new single-family residential developments meeting accessibility standards, a Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credit is also available, ranging from $500 to $2,000 per residence based on the percentage of homes meeting Level I standards. The program features fast-tracked permits and a tiered certification system (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum). Eligible improvements include no-step entrances, wider doorways, accessible bathrooms and kitchens, ramps, elevators/lifts, grab bars, lever door handles, chair lifts, roll-in showers, relocated switches and controls, and other qualifying modifications. Properties in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must submit an additional affidavit from their respective city.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit assessed by the Montgomery County Department of Finance based on qualifying accessibility construction work completed under the Design for Life permit process. Three tiers of credits are available: (1) Accessible Feature (Individual Accessibility Features): a credit equal to the lesser of 50% of eligible costs or $2,500 per property owner per tax year (minus any governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit subsidies received); eligible costs must exceed $500. Annual program cap: $100,000 per fiscal year. (2) Level I (VISITable): credits up to $3,000 per property. Annual program cap: $500,000 per tax year. (3) Level II (LIVEable): credits up to $10,000 per property. Annual program cap: $500,000 per tax year. The maximum credit applied in any single tax year is $2,000. If the credit exceeds the annual property tax bill, the excess carries forward to future years and transfers to a new owner if the property is sold. Builders and developers constructing new residential buildings meeting Level I or II standards may qualify for a Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credit: $500 per residence if 5% meet Level I, $1,000 if 10% meet Level I, $1,500 if 25% meet Level I, and $2,000 if 30% meet Level I. Eligible expenditures must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application. The credit appears as a line item on the property owner's next property tax bill. Only one application per property per tax year is allowed. Credits run with the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners buying or renovating a primary residence (including first-time homebuyers, young families, active adults, and people living with temporary or permanent impairments), condominium owners, builders or developers constructing single-family homes, townhouses, or duplexes, home care facility owners seeking universal accessibility improvements, and residential and commercial property owners in Montgomery County who have completed or plan to complete accessibility-related construction under the Design for Life permit process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of accessibility features in residential homes, including no-step entrances, wider doorways (32-inch minimum nominal clear width), accessible bathrooms and kitchens, ramps, elevators/lifts, grab bars, lever door handles, chair lifts, stair glide units, roll-in showers, chair-height toilets, relocated switches and outlets, accessible circulation paths, closet renovations, sensory alarms, and other modifications meeting Level I or Level II Accessibility Standards in new or existing residential dwellings. Tax credits offset county property taxes owed on the property. Also covers improvements to make home care facilities more universally accessible. School impact tax credit for builders constructing a qualifying percentage of DFL-certified new homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland, including properties located in the City of Rockville and the City of Gaithersburg (with additional affidavit requirements for those cities). The property must be the owner's principal residence for the Accessible Feature and Level I/II property tax credit eligibility.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Montgomery County, MD
Property must be the owner's principal residence (the 'Occupancy' box on the real property tax bill must read 'Principal Residence') for Accessible Feature and Level I/II credits
Applicant must be the property owner of a new or existing residential dwelling (single-family home, townhouse, duplex, or condominium unit)
Accessibility features must be permanently installed
Eligible expenditures must exceed $500
Eligible expenditures must be incurred within 12 months of application
Costs must be documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices and paid by the applicant/property owner
For Level I/II standards: all required accessibility features must be completed before final approved inspection
Home must meet the applicable accessibility threshold for Level I (VISITable) or Level II (LIVEable) credits
Level I (VISITable) requires: at least one no-step entrance, accessible route to a place to visit on the entry level, a usable powder room or bathroom, and a 32-inch nominal clear-width interior door

Level II (LIVEable) requires all Level I elements plus: an accessible circulation path, an accessible kitchen, at least one accessible bedroom, and an accessibility-enhanced full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub
Must obtain a DFL permit (residential or commercial building permit) before work begins
Must check the DFL application checkbox when applying online, or submit a Supplemental Design for Life Application with paper permits
Building permit must be issued and construction completed
Final inspection must be completed (including both a standard final building code inspection and a Design for Life final inspection)
Application must be submitted after final building inspection
For the Development Impact Tax credit: must enter into an Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement before building permits are issued
For Level II credit: must also meet all Level I requirements
Only one application for a tax credit per property per tax year is allowed
Applicants must provide copies of applications for any other subsidies and receipts for subsidies received
An affidavit is required stating neither the previous owner nor applicant received other subsidies for modifications
Property owners of condominium units must apply for a COMMERCIAL building permit, not a residential building permit
Properties in the City of Rockville or Gaithersburg must submit a signed affidavit from the respective city verifying inspections and installation
Sellers of new single-family residences must disclose to buyers that a tax credit may be available before contract signing
School impact tax credits for builders apply only where there is no bonus density for DFL units
Work must be completed and certified by the Department of Permitting Services after building permit is issued
Submit Application for Design for Life Tax Credits with supporting documents to DPS after construction is finalized
New construction projects may qualify for a school impact tax credit if meeting Level I or Level II standards
Eligible property types: condominium units (Individual Features only), attached or detached single-family dwelling units
Must own a home care facility (if applying as a home care facility owner) and be making improvements for universal accessibility
Applications for tax credits cannot be submitted online; a paper application must be filed
Costs must be reduced by any other subsidies, grants, or credits received for the same features
For existing homes, an Alteration Permit must be obtained; application must specify the accessibility features included and include required plans
Builders or developers applying for the School Impact Tax Credit must sign a separate School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement before building permits are issued
Eligible residences include condominium units and attached or detached single-family dwelling units, townhomes, and duplexes
Applies to both new construction and renovation projects
Annual program funding caps apply: $100,000 per fiscal year for Individual Accessibility Features and $500,000 per tax year for Accessibility Standards (Level I/II)
Home must meet Level I or Level II accessibility standards as defined in the Design for Life Technical Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Review applicable DFL laws and information (technical guidelines, brochures, and FAQs available at the program resource center or www.designforlifemc.org). Step 2: Apply for a DFL permit before work begins — either online via eServices (check the DFL Application Box in the residential or commercial permit) or in person at Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902 (submitting both a building permit and a Supplemental Design for Life Application). Submit architectural and/or engineering plans documenting the DFL renovations. For existing homes with accessibility features, apply for an Alteration Permit and indicate the specific accessibility features on the application. Builders seeking the School Impact Tax Credit must also sign a separate Certification Agreement at time of permit application. Step 3: Building permit is issued and construction begins. Step 4: Construction ends and final inspection is completed and approved (both standard building code inspection and Design for Life final inspection). Step 5: Submit a completed Application for Design for Life Tax Credits (PDF available on the program website) along with the building permit copy, cost documentation, copies of any subsidy applications, and required affidavits to DPS via DPS.DesignforLife@montgomerycountymd.gov, in person, or by mail to Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. The tax credit application cannot be submitted online and must be submitted in person or by paper. Step 6: DPS confirms receipt, certifies compliance, and forwards approved application to the Department of Finance. Step 7: Department of Finance reviews and assesses the tax credit amount; credit appears as a line item on the next property tax bill. Plans may also be submitted via ePlans. Resources including technical guidelines, brochures, and FAQs are available on the program's resource center page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Free Residential Deck Maintenance Safety Inspections
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Department of Permitting Services offers free residential deck maintenance safety inspections to homeowners in May as part of Building Safety Month. Inspectors check decks for maintenance and safety issues — including wood integrity, ledger board attachment, fasteners, railings, stairs, and weatherproofing — to help homeowners keep their decks safe.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site residential deck maintenance safety inspection. Limited to the first 300 appointments. Properties inspected the previous year are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Limited to first 300 appointments; available in May 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residential property owners (homeowners) who want a free safety inspection of their residential deck
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site inspection to identify deck maintenance and safety issues, including wood integrity, ledger board attachment, fasteners, railings, stairs, and weatherproofing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only; no sub-county geographic restrictions
requirements_list: Property must be a residential deck in Montgomery County
Limited to first 300 appointments
Properties inspected the previous year are not eligible
Requestor must provide name (cannot be anonymous), address, and contact information
Annual inspection frequency recommended
Railings must have no gap greater than 4 inches
Stair openings must have no gap greater than 6 inches
Handrail height must be between 34 and 38 inches
Maintenance tasks include wood probing, fastener tightening, rot/damage assessment, and weatherproofing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MC 311 at 240-777-0311 beginning May 1, or submit an online service request at permittingservices.montgomerycountymd.gov. Include your name, address, contact information, and note in the description field that you are requesting a free residential deck maintenance inspection.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Department of Police offers rebates to property owners and tenants — including residents, businesses, and nonprofits — who install qualifying exterior security cameras. The program aims to deter and solve crime by encouraging camera installation across Montgomery County. Priority areas are identified by the Police Chief based on public safety indicators including crime levels, and are evaluated annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of up to $250 per qualifying security camera (camera cost only; installation, accessories, and subscriptions are not covered), capped at actual purchase cost. Residents may receive a rebate for up to 1 camera per residence (maximum $250). Businesses and nonprofits may receive rebates for up to 5 cameras per location (maximum $1,250). Funds are disbursed by the Montgomery County Department of Finance after application approval, subject to appropriation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Subject to availability of funds; no stated deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or tenants of residential, business, or nonprofit properties located in Montgomery County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase cost of a qualifying exterior security camera (up to $250 per camera, not to exceed actual purchase price). Cameras must meet minimum technical and video specifications, be weatherproof, and retain footage for at least 7 days. Cameras must have been purchased on or after November 15, 2023.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a property located within Montgomery County, MD. Priority areas are identified by the Police Chief based on public safety indicators including crime levels, and are evaluated annually. Applicants can use the Department's camera application website to determine if their property is within an eligible priority area.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an owner or tenant of a residential, business, or nonprofit property in Montgomery County, MD
Camera must be purchased on or after November 15, 2023
Camera must meet minimum technical specifications (at least 1 megapixel, 1280x720 resolution, 5 fps)
Camera must be installed on the exterior of a building and be weatherproof
Camera must retain video footage for at least 7 days
Applicant must register the camera with MCPD
Completed application form required
Proof of purchase required
Make, model, and serial number of camera required
Verification of installation required (either by licensed installer certification or on-site officer visit)
Businesses and nonprofits must submit a separate application for each camera
Funding is subject to appropriation
Program is limited to designated priority areas evaluated annually by the Police Chief
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application form including proof of purchase, camera make/model/serial number, and installation verification. The Department's camera application website allows applicants to determine if their property is within an eligible priority area. If installed by a licensed security business, that business certifies the installation with photo evidence. If installed by the owner or another unlicensed person, an officer from the local district station will conduct an on-site visit to verify installation. Upon approval and subject to available funds, the rebate is issued by the Montgomery County Department of Finance. The Police Chief reports annually to the County Council on rebates awarded and program efficacy.

structured_extraction.program_description: Part of Montgomery County's Pedestrian Safety Program, this annual program installs minor sidewalk projects each year to fill missing links in existing sidewalk networks. The main goals are improving access for people with disabilities and enhancing pedestrian access to schools, public transportation, and public facilities. Projects come from resident and community association requests, which are evaluated for feasibility and prioritized based on equity and budget.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county installs sidewalks and ADA-compliant infrastructure at no cost to residents. Projects are selected annually from resident and association requests based on feasibility and prioritization criteria. Budget constraints limit the number of projects completed each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and community associations requesting sidewalk installation or ADA infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of sidewalks and ADA-compliant pedestrian infrastructure to fill gaps in existing sidewalk networks, particularly near schools, public transit, and public facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit a request for sidewalk or ADA installation
Request is subject to field investigation to determine feasibility
Projects are prioritized based on equity criteria due to budget constraints
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents or associations submit a request online using the 'Request Sidewalk and ADA Installation' portal. The county conducts a field investigation to assess feasibility, then prioritizes projects for annual selection.

structured_extraction.program_description: BikeMatchMoCo connects Montgomery County residents and workers who have an unused bike to donate with people who need a bike for transportation. The program matches donors with recipients based on location, so neither party has to travel far. Bikes must be in ready-to-ride condition and exchanges are permanent and conducted outdoors in a public place.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free bike matching service that connects people who have an unused bicycle to donate with people who need a bike for transportation. The program facilitates a direct, permanent exchange between donor and recipient at a convenient public location near both parties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents or workers who have an unused bike to donate, or who need a bike for transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receiving a bicycle for personal transportation, including commuting to work or running errands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must either live or work in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must live or work in Montgomery County, Maryland
Donors must offer bikes in ready-to-ride condition
Donors must clean and disinfect the bike before the exchange
Both parties must participate in an outdoor exchange in a public place
All bike exchanges are permanent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online BikeMatchMoCo application form. The program will use the home and/or work address provided to match donors and recipients who are near each other. Application information is kept confidential.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Call-N-Ride program provides subsidized taxi trips to low-income older adults and individuals with disabilities to help them get to medical and personal appointments. Participants receive a swipe card loaded with value usable at participating taxi companies. The subsidy is on a sliding fee scale based on household size and income — for a $60 card value, participants pay between $5.25 and $30.00 depending on annual income (up to approximately $39,000 per year for a household of one), representing up to a 91% subsidy. Card values are available in $60 or $120 increments, with a maximum card balance of $360. The Same Day Access (SDA) track serves certified MetroAccess cardholders with no income requirement, providing $60 in card value for a flat $30 monthly payment. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with limited exceptions for approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC. Recertification is required every two years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sliding-scale subsidy loaded onto a swipe card for taxi trips. Card values are $60 or $120 per month, with a maximum card balance of $360. Depending on income and household size, participants pay between $5.25 and $30 for a $60 card value (up to ~91% subsidy). For a household of one, annual income must not exceed approximately $39,000. The Same Day Access (SDA) track offers a $60 card value for a flat $30 payment once per month, with no income requirement, for MetroAccess cardholders. Processing takes up to 30 days. Participants must recertify every two years. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with approved exceptions for certain medical facilities in designated service areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income older adults age 63 and older, and low-income adults ages 18–62 with a qualifying disability, who reside in Montgomery County, Maryland. The Same Day Access (SDA) track is open to all Montgomery County MetroAccess cardholders regardless of income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized taxi transportation to medical and/or personal appointments that begin and end in Montgomery County, with approved exceptions for certain medical facilities in designated service areas including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residents of Montgomery County, Maryland only. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with limited exceptions for approved medical facilities in designated service areas including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident (proof of current residence within last 6 months required; PO Box not acceptable)
Must be low-income (CNR track only; no income requirement for Same Day Access track)
Must be age 63 or older (older adults track) OR age 18–62 with a qualifying disability
Same Day Access applicants must hold a current MetroAccess identification card
All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County
Proof of age required
Proof of all household income required (paystubs or bank statements within 30 days)
Passport photo required
Disability Certification Form completed by Licensed Physician, PA, or CRNP required for applicants ages 18–62; short-term disabilities must be certified for a minimum of 6 months
Recertification required every two years; failure to recertify within 30 days of notice results in inactive swipe card
SDA swipe card becomes inactive upon MetroAccess ID expiration; recertification required within 30 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the CNR Application Form (Rev. 01/2026) and, if ages 18–62, the CNR Disability Certification Form completed by a Licensed Physician, PA, or CRNP. Supporting documents must be current (within the last six months for proof of age and residence; within 30 days for income documents). Submit the completed application by fax to 240-556-0999, by email to cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov, or by mail/hand delivery to Call-n-Ride Program, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. For Same Day Access, complete the SDA Application Form and submit the same ways. Call (301) 948-5409, Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m., for application questions. Processing takes up to 30 days; approved applicants receive a welcome packet. Once approved, participants schedule trips by calling participating taxi companies. Recertification is required every two years.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Division of Transportation Engineering (DTE) administers this program to solve drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or inadequate. The program addresses requests from residents to correct drainage problems where runoff water comes from a public right-of-way. Staff investigates drainage issues, determines the appropriate solution (either a 'spot solution' or a Capital Improvement Project), and coordinates construction or escalates to the County Executive and County Council for approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County staff reviews drainage assistance requests, investigates the nature and cause of drainage problems originating from public rights-of-way, and develops solutions. This may result in a spot fix coordinated with a construction contractor or a Capital Improvement Project prioritized for County Executive and County Council approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners in unincorporated Montgomery County experiencing drainage problems caused by runoff from public rights-of-way or inadequate/failing storm drain systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Correcting drainage problems where runoff originates from public rights-of-way, including spot fixes and Capital Improvement Projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unincorporated Montgomery County, Maryland. Drainage issues on State roads are referred to the State Highway Administration (District 3). Drainage issues within the City of Rockville are handled by Rockville DPWT, and drainage issues within the City of Gaithersburg are handled by Gaithersburg DPWT.
requirements_list: Drainage problem must be caused by runoff originating from a public right-of-way or from properties owned by Montgomery County
Existing storm drain system must be absent, failing, or inadequate
Request must be submitted to the Design Section of DTE

Requestor must provide: location of the problem, description of the problem including origin and destination of water flow, photos if available, requestor's name, address, and phone number, and permission for county staff to access the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request by telephone call, email, FAX, or letter to the Design Section of DTE. A county staff member will review the request, conduct an evaluation (including watershed calculation, property impact, and cost/benefit analysis), classify the issue as a 'spot solution' or Capital Improvement Project (CIP), and provide notification of proposed action.

structured_extraction.program_description: FareShare is a subsidy matching program operated by the Montgomery County Department of Transportation that encourages private employers in Montgomery County to provide transit and vanpool subsidies to their employees. Montgomery County reimburses private employers for transit benefit amounts above the minimum $25 per employee per month, up to $325 per month (the federal tax-free maximum as of January 1, 2025), with a maximum county reimbursement of $40,000 per employer per year. Employers may also receive a Maryland Commuter Choice Tax Credit equal to 50% of their contribution, up to $100 per employee per month, and can offer pre-tax payroll deductions through SmartBenefits. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month tax-free and do not need to live in Montgomery County; a Guaranteed Ride Home benefit is also available. The program is designed to help employers start or enhance a commuter benefits program, with FareShare staff visiting employer offices at no charge to set up a customized commuter benefits program. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible. Program operates on a first-come, first-served basis contingent upon availability of funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County reimburses private employers for any transit or vanpool benefit amount above the minimum $25 per employee per month, up to the full $325/month federal maximum (as of January 1, 2025), less the employer's own contribution. Maximum county reimbursement is $40,000 per employer per year. Employers may also receive a Maryland Commuter Choice Tax Credit equal to 50% of their contribution, up to $100 per employee per month, and pre-tax payroll deduction options via SmartBenefits. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month tax-free and a Guaranteed Ride Home benefit. FareShare staff will visit employer offices at no charge to help set up a customized commuter benefits program. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible. Program is contingent upon availability of funds and operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private-sector and non-profit employers located in Montgomery County, MD who want to provide or enhance transit and vanpool commuting benefits for their employees, as well as employees working in Montgomery County seeking to reduce commuting costs. Employees do not need to live in Montgomery County. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement to employers for employee transit and vanpool commuting subsidies above the $25/month minimum, up to $325/month per employee. Funds cover transit and vanpool commuting costs for employees working in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Employer must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Employees may live anywhere but must work in Montgomery County. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible.
requirements_list: Employer must be a private-sector or non-profit organization (public sector employers are not eligible)
Employer must be located in Montgomery County, MD
Employees must work in Montgomery County (employees may live anywhere)
Employer must offer a minimum transit/vanpool benefit of $25 per employee per month
Total benefit to any employee cannot exceed their actual commuting cost
Maximum county reimbursement is $40,000 per employer per year
Employer must complete the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form
Employer must submit an Employer Worksheet Invoice and WMATA SmartBenefits Order Confirmation Form
Employer must conduct a pre-program employee survey
Employer must participate in biennial (every other year) Commuter Surveys post-enrollment
Must achieve acceptable survey response rate
Program is contingent upon availability of funds; enrollment is first-come, first-served
Public sector employees are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact Commuter Services at 240-773-2989 or email mcdot.commuterservices@montgomerycountymd.gov to receive the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form and complete it. 2. FareShare marketing specialists can visit your office free of charge to create a customized commuting benefits program. 3. Submit the Employer Worksheet Invoice and WMATA SmartBenefits Order Confirmation Form. 4. Receive reimbursement from the County. A program brochure is available for download at https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/BWTW_FareShareBrochure_June2024%281%29.pdf. Employees participate through their employer's program. Program operates on a first-come, first-served basis contingent upon availability of funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County youth ages 18 and under ride free on all Montgomery County Department of Transportation (MCDOT) buses, including Ride On, Ride On extRa, Ride On Flex, and Flash buses. Starting June 29, 2025, fares are zero on all MCDOT buses. Montgomery County residents ages 5–18 (or older if still in high school) can also ride free on most Metrobuses within the county by using a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free bus rides on all MCDOT buses (Ride On, Ride On extRa, Ride On Flex, and Flash) for youth ages 18 and under at all times. Free rides on most Metrobuses within the county for residents ages 5–18 (or older if still in high school) using a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card. No fare is charged or deducted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County youth ages 18 and under (or older if still in high school) riding MCDOT buses; Montgomery County residents ages 5–18 for free Metrobus rides.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free public bus transportation within Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Montgomery County, MD on Ride On, Ride On extRa, Ride On Flex, and Flash buses. Free Metrobus rides are limited to covered routes within the county.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or under (students still in high school may be older than 18)
Children under 5 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian
For free Metrobus rides, must be a Montgomery County resident ages 5–18 (or older if still in high school)
As of February 1, 2026, a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card is mandatory for free rides on Metrobuses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required for Ride On buses — youth ride free automatically. For Metrobus rides, obtain a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card and tap the farebox when boarding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County transportation program that is part of the Call-n-Ride program. It provides subsidized same-day, on-demand taxicab transportation for certified MetroAccess participants who live in Montgomery County. Trips must originate or end in Montgomery County, with exceptions for approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C. Fare payment is via a prepaid CNR swipe card; balances can be checked or topped up by phone or online.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive $60.00 in value loaded onto a Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who hold a current MetroAccess identification card (Metro Access members). The program is also referenced as a Senior Transportation program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized same-day, on-demand taxicab transportation for certified MetroAccess participants in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County. Special exceptions allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas, including facilities in Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident (documented with proof within last 6 months: utility bill, Social Security Statement, W-2, property tax/mortgage/lease documents)
Must have a current MetroAccess identification card (photocopy required with application)
Must complete and sign the SDA application form
Recertification required when MetroAccess card expires; must resubmit within 30 days or SDA swipe card becomes inactive
Must possess a valid CNR swipe card with photograph (if no photo on card, must carry valid photo ID)
Must have sufficient funds on card or cash to cover fare
Must notify dispatcher of mobility/accessibility needs in advance
Must provide name, card number, and accurate pick-up/drop-off locations when ordering a ride
Must present card at start and end of trip
Cannot alter destination after vehicle arrival
All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County (with approved medical facility exceptions)
Receipts must be retained
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the single-page SDA Application Form (covering personal info, addresses, secondary contact, language needs, optional photo, and signature) and submit with required documentation: (1) photocopy of current MetroAccess ID card, and (2) one proof of current Montgomery County residence dated within the last 6 months (utility bill, Social Security statement, W-2, property tax/insurance/mortgage statement, or lease agreement). Submit via fax, email, mail, or in person to 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Call 301-948-5409 or 301-738-3252 for application and recertification questions. Recertification must be completed within 30 days of receiving a recertification notice or the swipe card will become inactive. To order a ride, call a participating taxicab company; provide name, CNR swipe card number, and pickup/drop-off information; present valid card to driver at trip start and end; pay fare with card or cash.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a free SmarTrip® card to residents age 65 and older. The card allows seniors to ride Ride On buses for free and pay senior fares on Metrobus and Metrorail. The card costs nothing and can be obtained at county libraries, the Silver Spring TRiPS store, or the Mobile Commuter Store by showing proof of age.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free SmarTrip® card (no purchase cost as of January 16, 2024) that allows seniors age 65+ to ride Ride On buses at no charge and pay reduced senior fares on Metrobus and Metrorail. No value is loaded on the card at the time of purchase; cardholders must add value separately to use WMATA express buses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents age 65 and older. US citizenship is not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free transit card for use on Ride On buses (free rides), Metrobus, and Metrorail at senior fare rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 65 or older
Must present proof of age: state ID, birth certificate, or passport
US citizenship is not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Bring proof of age (state ID, birth certificate, or passport) to any Montgomery County library, the Silver Spring TRiPS store, or the Mobile Commuter Store to obtain the card.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Vision Zero Youth Ambassador Program trains Montgomery County high school students to become the next generation of traffic safety leaders. Students learn about Vision Zero principles, roadway design, law enforcement, and community education, and complete hands-on group projects focused on engineering or education topics to improve traffic safety in their communities. Participants earn up to 35-46 Student Service-Learning (SSL) hours upon completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students participate in five in-person sessions plus orientation and graduation, completing hands-on group projects and earning up to 35-46 SSL (Student Service-Learning) hours. All sessions are held at the Executive Office Building in Rockville, with graduation at a separate Gaithersburg location. Sessions run 10 am to 1 pm.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County high school students interested in improving traffic safety in their communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leadership development, traffic safety education, hands-on community safety projects, social media engagement skills, and SSL hour accumulation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all Montgomery County high school students.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County high school student
Must commit to attending ALL required sessions
Must complete a group project on engineering or education topics related to traffic safety
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open in November and close in early December. Applicants are notified in mid-December. Selected ambassadors attend orientation in January followed by five in-person sessions and a graduation ceremony in May.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth Cruiser SmarTrip Card program provides free transit cards to Montgomery County youth ages 5 to 18 (or older if still in high school). The card allows students to ride Metrobuses for free through the Kids Ride Free program and can also store value for use on Metrorail and other SmarTrip-accepting transit agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free SmarTrip transit card for eligible youth that allows free rides on Metrobuses (via the Kids Ride Free program). Cards have no stored value when issued but value can be added for use on Metrorail and other transit agencies. First card and replacement cards are free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents ages 5 to 18 (or older if still in high school)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free rides on Metrobuses through the Kids Ride Free program; stored value can also be added for use on Metrorail and other SmarTrip-accepting transit systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be ages 5 to 18, or older if still enrolled in high school
Elementary school students must have a parent/guardian complete and sign the application form

At non-school locations, student or parent/guardian must appear in person with proof of age (birth certificate, passport, or state-issued ID) and proof of Montgomery County residency (state ID, learner's permit, school transcript, or school correspondence)
Cards are no longer valid after graduation from high school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the English or Spanish application form. At participating schools, bring the completed form to the designated administrative office and receive the card on the spot — no identification required. At other county locations (libraries, Silver Spring TRiPS store, Mobile Commuter Store, or Montgomery County Division of Treasury in Rockville), bring the completed form plus proof of age and proof of Montgomery County residency to receive the card on the spot. A list of card distribution locations is available at https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/DOT-Transit/fares/youth-cruiser.html.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, week-long immersive training camp run by Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service for young women ages 16–18 who want to explore a career as a firefighter or EMT. Participants experience fire, EMS, and rescue scenarios, physical training, CPR/AED certification, nutrition education, and life at a fire station. The program is held at Montgomery County Public Safety Training Academy in Gaithersburg, MD.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free five-day residential-style training program (July 6–10, 2026, 8AM–5PM daily with some later days) held at Montgomery County Public Safety Training Academy, 8751 Snouffer School Road, Gaithersburg, MD 20879. Uniforms and gear are provided at no cost. Participants receive hands-on fire suppression, EMS, and rescue training, CPR/AED certification, nutrition education, and a graduation ceremony on Day 5. Enrollment is limited.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young women ages 16–18 interested in exploring a firefighter or EMT career; no residential or school district requirement stated
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on fire suppression, EMS, and rescue training; physical fitness; CPR/AED certification; fire station experience; nutrition education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is hosted at Montgomery County Public Safety Training Academy in Gaithersburg, MD (Montgomery County). No explicit geographic residency restriction stated.
requirements_list: Must identify as female
Must be between the ages of 16 and 18
Must complete all parts of the application, including the Assumption of Risk and Waiver and Medical PAR-Q+ Form
Completed PDFs must be emailed to the program contact
Participants under 18 require parent/guardian consent
Participants responsible for communicating discomfort, illness, fatigue, or heat-related symptoms
Enrollment is limited to a certain number of applicants
