Applications close May 15; successful applicants are notified by May 22.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service offers free in-person or virtual home safety visits to Montgomery County residents. During the visit, trained personnel check smoke alarms, replace back-up batteries if needed, identify fire hazards, help develop home fire escape plans, and discuss fire safety topics. Free smoke alarm installation is targeted to high-risk individuals including older adults, people with disabilities, and economically challenged residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home safety visits (in-person or virtual) that include smoke alarm checks, battery replacement in hard-wired alarms, hazard identification, home fire escape plan assistance, and free smoke alarm installation for high-risk residents. Specialized alarms for deaf and hearing-impaired homeowners are available in limited quantities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents, especially older adults, seniors, individuals with mobility, vision, or hearing impairments, and economically challenged residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home fire safety inspection, smoke alarm checks and battery replacement, hazard identification, escape plan development, and free smoke alarm installation for eligible high-risk residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland
A family member 18 years or older must be home during the visit
Family must commit to maintaining and testing smoke alarms monthly, developing a home fire escape plan, and practicing escape routes
For rental properties, landlords are responsible for installation and replacement of alarms; MCFRS can assist with checking alarms and escape planning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request a home safety visit online using the request form linked on the program page. You can request an in-person or virtual appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Events Matching Fund Grant Program (NEMF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Neighborhood Events Matching Fund (NEMF) Grant Program provides matching grants to neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, civic clubs, and other community groups to support community events and activities in Montgomery County. The program promotes community engagement, capacity building, networking, and local economic activity and stimulation. Eligible activities must be open to all residents and create sustainable, lasting positive impacts for the neighborhood. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to first-time applicants. The program is administered through five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County (Wheaton area), Silver Spring, and UpCounty. Payment is issued after approved applicants submit receipts and a final report.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Government, Regional Service Office
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle, matched dollar-for-dollar (1:1) with the applicant's cash or in-kind donations (volunteer hours, donated materials/services, or cash). Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Payment is issued after approved applicants submit receipts and a final report. The group must be registered in the County Central Vendor System to receive payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Events must occur between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, civic clubs, community groups, and residents that are active and in good standing in Montgomery County, Maryland, seeking funds to hold community events open to the public.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hosting community events and activities, including neighborhood events and educational community gatherings, that are open to residents and create sustainable, lasting positive impacts for the neighborhood. Eligible expenses include food, paper products, printing, and materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to groups holding events within Montgomery County, Maryland. The program is administered through five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County (Wheaton area), Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a neighborhood organization, block group, tenant association, or civic club
Organization must be active and in good standing
Events must be open to everyone in the community
Events must create sustainable and lasting positive impacts for the neighborhood
All events must comply with Montgomery County law
Applicant must provide proof of payment (receipts) for eligible activity expenditures
Applicant must submit a final report before payment is issued
Funds must be matched 1:1 with cash or in-kind donations (volunteer hours, donated materials/services, or cash)
Matching funds must be equal to or greater than the grant amount requested
Maximum award is $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle
The group must be registered in the County Central Vendor System to receive funds
Application must be submitted to the correct Regional Service Office based on event location
Event must be open to the public or applicant must provide justification if not
Priority given to first-time applicants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the online application (or request a PDF or translated version from your Regional Service Office). 2. Your local Regional Service Office reviews the application to determine if the event qualifies. 3. If approved, you receive a notice stating the grant amount (up to $1,000). 4. Agree to the program rules, provide receipts for spending, and submit a final report. 5. Register your group in the County Central Vendor System to receive payment. Processing takes 1–2 weeks. Additional details are available in the Neighborhood Events Matching Fund fact sheet.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's C-PACE program allows commercial property owners to obtain low-cost, long-term financing for up to 100% of eligible property improvement costs through private lenders. The loan is repaid as an annual surcharge on the property tax bill for up to 20 years, spreading the cost of improvements over time without requiring upfront capital. The program covers energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, and environmental health and safety upgrades. It is available for renovations of existing buildings (including projects completed within the last 12 months) and new construction. The debt stays with the property, so repayment obligations transfer to any future owner upon property sale until the loan is fully repaid. The Montgomery County Green Bank became the program administrator in April 2021 and administers the program on behalf of Montgomery County. The Green Bank also serves as a direct capital provider for transactions up to $2.5 million to help stimulate the market. The program is authorized under Montgomery County Code Chapter 18A, Article 5. As of December 2025, the program had three active loans in its portfolio and one transaction in the pipeline intended to close in FY27. The MOU between Montgomery County and the Green Bank has been extended through December 2026.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private lender financing of up to 100% of eligible property improvement costs, repaid as an annual surcharge on the property tax bill over a repayment period of up to 20 years. The loan obligation transfers to subsequent property owners until fully repaid. The Montgomery County Green Bank also serves as a direct capital provider for transactions up to $2.5 million to help stimulate the market.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners (including nonprofits, faith-based organizations, and minority-owned businesses), capital providers, and contractors in Montgomery County, MD seeking financing for energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, water conservation, or related clean energy building improvements. Future outreach is planned for minority-owned businesses and low-income and disadvantaged community (LIDAC) property owners and developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements (e.g., LED lighting, insulation, windows, heat pumps), renewable energy installations (e.g., solar PV), climate resiliency and adaptation upgrades, water conservation measures, and environmental health and safety upgrades to commercial properties, including both renovations of existing buildings and new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for qualifying commercial properties located in Montgomery County, Maryland, including properties in Bethesda, Rockville, Silver Spring, Gaithersburg, and Chevy Chase. Not available for residential properties.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying commercial property in Montgomery County
Improvements must qualify as energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, or environmental health and safety upgrades
Existing building renovations must have been completed within the last 12 months to use C-PACE retroactively
Available for new construction as well as existing buildings
Program is authorized under Montgomery County Code Chapter 18A, Article 5
The MOU between Montgomery County and the Green Bank is currently extended through December 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Green Bank, which serves as program administrator. Visit the Montgomery County Green Bank C-PACE webpage at mcgreenbank.org/c-pace/ for application details and to get started. Additional information is also available at the Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection program page. The program operates on a rolling basis with properties evaluated individually. As of the FY26 Annual Report (March 2026), the Green Bank has one transaction in its pipeline intending to close in FY27 and is conducting targeted marketing, webinars, and in-person convenings to stimulate new activity.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Green Bank Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Green Bank subsidizes energy benchmarking, data verification, and gross floor area measurement services for building owners required to comply with Montgomery County's Benchmarking Law. The program matches applicants with vendors in its network and helps offset costs for first-time benchmarking and data verification, as well as subsequent-year benchmarking and verification for specially designated buildings such as affordable housing or nonprofit-owned buildings. Support is also available for energy audits, electrification feasibility studies, renewable energy studies, and electric vehicle studies.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offsets the cost of benchmarking, data verification, and gross floor area measurement services by matching applicants with vendors in the Green Bank's network. Cost subsidies are available for first-time benchmarking and data verification, and for subsequent-year benchmarking/verification for affordable housing or nonprofit-owned buildings. Additional support covers energy audits, electrification feasibility studies, renewable energy studies, and EV studies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and managers subject to Montgomery County's Energy Benchmarking Law, with additional support for affordable housing and nonprofit-owned buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy benchmarking, data verification, gross floor area measurement, energy audits, electrification feasibility studies, renewable energy studies, and electric vehicle studies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to buildings in Montgomery County, Maryland subject to the Benchmarking Law.
requirements_list: First-time benchmarking and data verification eligible for cost offset
Subsequent-year benchmarking/verification eligible for specially designated buildings (affordable housing or nonprofit-owned)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Green Bank's Technical Assistance Program application form. The Green Bank will match applicants with vendors in its network.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Agricultural Cost Share Reimbursement (ACRE) Program provides matching grant cost-share assistance to farmers for agricultural business projects that improve, expand, and increase the profitability of their agricultural operation. Eligible projects include deer fence, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, and refrigeration. The farmer must pay at least half of the total project cost. The lifetime maximum per farm or farmer is $15,000, and the annual total for all Montgomery County projects is $25,000 per fiscal year. A single agricultural enterprise may apply up to twice per fiscal year. Applicants must receive approval before making purchases or beginning any phase of the project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching cost-share grant that reimburses farmers for up to 50% of eligible project costs. Up to $3,000 per project (MARBIDCO + ACRE combined match); an additional $1,000 is available for projects over $20,000. Maximum lifetime award is $15,000 per farm or farmer. Total annual funding for all Montgomery County projects is capped at $25,000 per fiscal year. A single agricultural enterprise may apply up to twice per fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing agricultural enterprises in Montgomery County, including table crop farmers, vineyards, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and other non-traditional types of agriculture, seeking funding for projects that improve, expand, or increase the profitability of their agricultural operation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural business projects such as deer fencing, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, and refrigeration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to agricultural enterprises headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must be qualified Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs.
requirements_list: Farmer must pay at least half of the total project cost
Maximum lifetime amount is $15,000 per farm, farmer, or agricultural operation
Total annual Montgomery County funding is capped at $25,000 per fiscal year
Applicant must apply to and receive approval from the Office of Agriculture (OAG) before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project
The agricultural enterprise making an application must be headquartered in Montgomery County
A single agricultural enterprise may apply to this program up to twice per fiscal year
Program may be discontinued at any time due to lack of funding
MARBIDCO may also have limitations on its funding availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through MARBIDCO at the link provided. Contact Jacqueline Arnold at the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture for more information before applying. Approval must be obtained before any project expenses are incurred. Applications appear to be accepted on a rolling basis up to twice per fiscal year per enterprise.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy a Lot/Terminate a Lot (BLT) Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Buy a Lot/Terminate a Lot (BLT) Easement Program permanently retires an approved on-site waste disposal system (septic site plan) associated with a lot in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve. Because the landowner has already proven the lot can support a residence, the BLT easement payment is higher than a standard TDR. The County may purchase the BLT easement (retiring the development right), or the landowner may sell BLTs directly to developers for use in designated receiving areas such as the Life Science, Transit Mixed-Use, and Commercial/Residential zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases BLT easements at a value set annually by the County Executive based on recent agricultural easement prices, TDR prices, and fair market values. Alternatively, BLTs may be sold privately to developers in designated receiving zones. Easement value is determined by the BLT Ranking Formula, with the Base Value and Maximum Easement Value set each July 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve who hold an approved septic system site plan on a lot they wish to terminate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment for permanently retiring an approved on-site waste disposal lot, eliminating its development potential.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone.
requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone
Property must be at least 50 acres, or contiguous to other protected land if smaller
At least 50% of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Land must not be encumbered by Federal/State/County agricultural or conservation easements (except TDR easements)
Land must have an approved septic system site plan from the Department of Permitting Services demonstrating sufficient percolation rate
Any TDRs retained above the threshold of 1 TDR per 25 acres must be created or severed from the land prior to or simultaneously with settlement of the BLT easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Mike Weyand at michael.weyand@montgomerycountymd.gov with questions about BLT easements or preservation options for your property.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Composting Education Hub (CEH) provides hands-on composting training for county residents, Master Gardeners, and farmers. The program demonstrates composting methods for home, community, and farm-scale operations. It trains participants to become Extension Composters who can teach others about food scrap composting, the benefits of composting, and how to use finished compost. Farmers receive training on state and local rules for on-farm composting, system design, and best management practices to establish composting operations that can generate income and produce soil amendments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free multi-level training program to certify participants as Extension Composters. Covers home composting, community-scale composting, and farm-scale food scrap composting including state and local regulations, system siting and design, and best management practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents, Master Gardeners, and farmers interested in composting food scraps at home, in community gardens, schools, or on farms
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Composting education and training — becoming a certified Extension Composter to teach others about composting food scraps
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a county resident, Master Gardener, or farmer in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact natalia.salazar@montgomerycountymd.gov to be added to the mailing list for program updates and training opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Energy Tax Relief Program (Certified Agricultural Producers)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Energy Tax Relief Program allows qualified agricultural producers in Montgomery County to pay the county's energy tax (on fuel, propane, and electricity) at the lower residential rate rather than the higher industrial rate. The Office of Agriculture administers this program, known as the Fuel-Energy Tax Program for Certified Agricultural Producers. Eligible energy types include separately metered agricultural electricity, dyed diesel (off-road), and LP gas (non-residential use). Equestrian facilities are also eligible following a County Code amendment, and bona fide farming operations not falling into listed categories may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified agricultural producers pay the county's energy tax at the lower residential rate rather than the industrial rate. Eligible energy types include separately metered agricultural electricity, dyed diesel (off-road), and LP gas (non-residential use). To qualify, a producer must be enrolled in at least one of several eligible agricultural programs or hold a farm preservation easement (AEP, MALPF, BLT, RLP, MET, or LOS), or be enrolled with the Montgomery Soil Conservation District, Maryland Nutrient Management Program, USDA Farm Service Agency, Cooperative Extension Service, Montgomery County Farmers Market Association, certified as an organic grower by MDA, or enrolled in a Forest Conservation Management Agreement. Bona fide farming operations not falling into listed categories may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Equestrian facilities are now eligible following a County Code amendment. Once certified, producers receive a certification number and should self-notify their suppliers; the County also transmits the certified producer list to fuel-energy suppliers. Note: this program reduces only the county energy tax component, not the base utility rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers in Montgomery County who own or lease farmland and are engaged in producing agricultural commodities such as livestock, crops, nursery stock, equestrian operations, or other farm products.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces the county energy tax rate on fuel, propane, and electricity purchases for qualifying agricultural operations from the industrial rate to the lower residential rate. Does not alter the base utility rate — only the county energy tax component is reduced.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to agricultural producers operating within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in the business of agriculture in the production of an agricultural commodity in Montgomery County.
Must be enrolled in at least one eligible agricultural program or service, or have property encumbered by an eligible farm preservation easement (AEP, MALPF, BLT, RLP, MET, or LOS).

Eligible programs/services include: Montgomery Soil Conservation District, Maryland Nutrient Management Program, USDA Farm Service Agency, Montgomery County Extension, Montgomery County Farmers Market, and Maryland Department of Agriculture Certified Organic Growers.
Equestrian facilities are eligible following a County Code amendment.
Tenant farmers without land ownership may also apply.
Bona fide farming operations not fitting listed categories may be considered on a case-by-case basis by contacting the Office of Agriculture.
Must submit an application to the Office of Agriculture for certification as an Agricultural Producer.
Once certified, must have a Certification Letter and resolution documentation to verify correct tax rate is being applied on bills.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the SeamlessDocs application portal for the Certified Agricultural Producer Energy Tax Relief Program. Step-by-step instructions are available on the program page. Once certified, the Office of Agriculture transmits the list of certified producers to the Department of Finance, which then notifies fuel and energy suppliers in the county. Certified producers also receive a certification number and should self-notify their suppliers. To verify the correct tax rate is being applied, producers can compare their bill to the residential rate (e.g., .01106 per KWH for electricity), and if charged incorrectly, contact their utility with their Certification Letter and resolution documentation to request a credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MoCo MicroHub is a shared cold storage unit (20'x10' container-style) created by the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture and the Montgomery County Food Council. It gives small local farms access to shared refrigeration space for aggregating and storing produce after harvest before distribution to food pantries, schools, food assistance providers, and other farm-to-table programs. The unit holds about 10 standard pallets (roughly 8,750 lbs) of product at a time and can distribute an estimated 303,300 lbs of produce annually during peak season.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers access shared cold storage space by completing a brief training and then reserving space through the Food Corridor App. The unit provides centralized, safe cold storage for farm products destined for food pantries, schools, and businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small farms in Montgomery County, Maryland that need shared cold storage for aggregating and distributing produce.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shared cold storage space for aggregating farm products before distribution to food pantries, schools, and farm-to-table programs including farm2FoodBank and Farm-to-School.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small farms located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a county farmer
Must participate in a brief training
Must request space through the Food Corridor App
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a brief training, then reserve storage space through the Food Corridor App at app.thefoodcorridor.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Agricultural Land Preservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County purchases agricultural land preservation easements from eligible farmland owners in the Agricultural Reserve and nearby zones. By placing an easement on the property, the program permanently prevents future commercial, residential, or industrial development. The County uses a formula-based system (the Agricultural Value Formula, or AVF) to determine easement values based on farm size, soil quality, road frontage, and farm location. Applications are processed in approximately 6 to 12 months without requiring State approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural preservation easements. Easement value is determined by the Agricultural Value Formula (AVF), which considers farm size, soil quality, road frontage, land tenure, and proximity to the edge of the agricultural zone. The program does not use appraisals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmland owners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve, Rural Cluster Zone, Rural Zone, or other zones with significant agricultural value.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment for selling development rights (easements) on their agricultural land, permanently restricting non-agricultural development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones determined to possess significant agricultural value in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Farm must be located in the AR, RC, RZ, or other zones with significant agricultural value
Minimum property size of 50 acres, or 10 or more acres of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right (TDR) per 25 acres must be retained with the property prior to application to be eligible for maximum easement value
At least 50% of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Transferable Development Rights (TDR) Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Transferable Development Rights (TDR) program allows landowners in the Agricultural Reserve to sell their development rights to designated receiving areas elsewhere in the County. When a landowner creates and sells TDRs, a TDR easement is placed on the property, permanently restricting development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres regardless of future zoning changes. The program has preserved over 52,000 acres of farmland, generating $117 million in private funds from TDR purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners sell development rights (TDRs) to developers in designated receiving areas, recovering equity lost from the 1980 down-zoning. The price of TDRs is determined by the private market. A TDR easement is permanently placed on the sending property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve who wish to sell development rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive private market proceeds from selling Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) to developers in designated receiving areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve.
requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve
Development is permanently restricted to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres once a TDR easement is placed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a letter of intent at https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/ng/fa/fnvem23kcp1b to notify the County of your interest in creating TDRs from your land. Contact Mike Weyand at michael.weyand@montgomerycountymd.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides mentoring and specialized business training — including marketing, accounting, business planning, and advanced sustainable farm practices — for new farmers in Montgomery County. The program matches new farmers with private landowners in the Agricultural Reserve so farmers can start on a long-term leased site right away, skipping the shared-space incubator phase. Participants also get access to shared farm equipment and technical resources to help launch their farm enterprise. Note: the land matching and mentorship components are not fully active due to budget and staffing reductions; however, applications are still accepted and the Office will provide all other available assistance including trainings. Classroom training occurs January–March each year (typically once a week in the evening); equipment training occurs as weather permits.

Note: the land matching and mentorship components are not fully active due to budget and staffing reductions; however, applications are still accepted and the Office will provide all other available assistance including trainings. Classroom training occurs January–March each year (typically once a week in the evening); equipment training occurs as weather permits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Election Fund (2026 Election Cycle Public Campaign Financing Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Public Election Fund (PEF) is a public campaign financing program for candidates running for Montgomery County Council (Council-at-Large and District Council) and County Executive offices. The program provides matching public funds to qualifying candidates to encourage more residents to run for office, increase voter participation, and reduce the influence of large private contributions. Candidates who collect the required number of small-dollar contributions from Montgomery County residents can receive public dollars matched at tiered ratios to amplify grassroots fundraising. Certified candidates receive matching funds based on qualifying contributions: County Executive (up to $870,170 per election: 7:1 on first $50, 4:1 on $51–$100, 2:1 on $101–$150, no match on $151–$500); Council-at-Large (up to $290,060 per election: 5:1 on first $50, 3:1 on $51–$100, 2:1 on $101–$150); District Council (up to $145,030 per election: 5:1 on first $50, 3:1 on $51–$100, 2:1 on $101–$150). Distribution period runs June 23, 2025 through December 3, 2026, with monthly distribution reports issued according to the 2025–2026 reporting schedule. During the 2018 election cycle, 23 qualifying candidates received approximately $5.25 million in total matching funds. During the 2022 election cycle, 20 qualifying candidates received approximately $3.7 million in total matching funds. The Montgomery County Office of Consumer Protection serves as a liaison to assist candidates with operational and logistical questions; the Department of Finance administers the payments; and the Maryland State Board of Elections certifies candidates. The program is governed by Council Bill 20-24 and Executive Regulation #10-25. The program was established by Montgomery County legislation in 2014 and launched January 2015 for the 2018 cycle. Use of funds is restricted to expenses directly related to election campaign activities during the specific time period for either the primary or general election; personal use, office-holding expenses, personal endorsements, and late filing fees are explicitly excluded.

The program serves Montgomery and Prince George's Counties by placing kits in schools, government buildings, and other public facilities, and by offering in-person training, instructional videos, a mobile app, and printed materials.

Kit deployment is currently limited to Montgomery County Government, Montgomery County Public Schools, and Montgomery College facilities. Training requests are subject to resource availability.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trauma care kit deployment in public facilities; in-person bystander training on how to use kit contents to treat severe bleeding, penetrating trauma, and hypothermia.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Community Food Assistance (CFA) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grant funding to 501(c)(3) food assistance provider organizations that offer regularly scheduled, no-cost food services to Montgomery County residents at county-based sites at least once per month for a minimum of one year. Funds support the purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and/or prepared meals to residents experiencing food insecurity. Grants are awarded as direct cash grants for flexible food sourcing or as credits to order food through bulk-purchasing partnerships with Manna Food Center and the Capital Area Food Bank. The program aims to close service gaps, enhance program impact, standardize data collection, increase flexibility and transparency in funding, and strengthen the local food system. In FY25, $3,699,500 was awarded across 49 organizations. In FY26, $3.5 million was awarded to 56 active organizations. Awards are eligible for renewal for an additional one-year grant period (approximately November 1, 2026 – November 1, 2027) pending successful performance outcomes, grant administration compliance, and appropriation of funds. Four funding request options (Options 1–4) are available based on service model, with different eligibility criteria and cost caps. The program is administered by the Office of Food Systems Resilience and the Office of Grants Management in Montgomery County. FY26 grantees have been selected and announced.

In FY25, $3,699,500 was awarded across 49 organizations. In FY26, $3.5 million was awarded to 56 active 501(c)(3) food assistance provider organizations. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online grant application portal (eCivis). Review the NOFO and information session slide deck for details. The review process has three stages: (1) OGM Administrative Review for Montgomery County eligibility; (2) Programmatic Eligibility Review by OFSR; (3) Subject Matter Expert (SME) Review and scoring. Minor errors may be given approximately 2 business days to correct. Award notification letters are expected roughly one month after the application deadline. Application materials include: online data entry fields, PDF narrative uploads, and an MS Excel budget using the required FY26 CFA Grant Program Budget Template. Applicants must submit a Project Scope of Work, Budget Narrative (covering Food Sourcing, Operating Expenses, Reduced Funding Impact, Additional FY, and Outside Services sections), and Performance History (narrative plus supporting documentation such as service frequency proof and photos of typical distribution). Performance milestone targets are set at 6, 12, and 24 months. Applicants must complete and return Certifications, Acknowledgements, and Assurances in the online portal. The FY26 program opened for applications on Friday, August 15, 2025, with an information session held on Thursday, August 21, 2025 at 12:00 PM EST. Note: FY26 grantees have already been selected and announced; current grantees are in the active reporting phase (November 1, 2025 – October 31, 2026).

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Food As Medicine Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds innovative food-as-medicine initiatives that screen pediatric patients for food insecurity and provide nutritious food and food education services in Montgomery County. It addresses gaps in nutrition security and diet-related health challenges while increasing access to culturally diverse, medically relevant, nutritious, and locally produced food for children and families in underserved communities. Grants support healthcare and clinic-led programs serving Montgomery County households that screen positive for food insecurity and include at least one child aged 0–18 with a parent or child diagnosed with a diet-related disease. The program uses food and nutrition interventions to improve health outcomes. $750,000 in total grant funding is available for FY26.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $750,000 in total grant funding is available for FY26. Awards fund healthcare and clinic-led Food as Medicine programs. In FY25, six partnerships received awards ranging from $50,000 to $200,000 totaling $750,000. In FY24, five partnerships received awards totaling $449,337. Grant performance period runs May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027. Awards are eligible for renewal for one additional one-year performance period, contingent upon satisfactory program performance, compliance with grant administration and reporting requirements, continued programmatic need, and appropriation of funds by the Montgomery County Council. Match requirement: 15% (up to 10% in-kind) for Year 1; 25% (up to 15% in-kind) for renewal years.

Programs must source culturally diverse, locally produced food. If an organization provides services outside of Montgomery County, grant funds must be used exclusively to benefit Montgomery County residents. Food sourcing should prioritize local, Mid-Atlantic region farms and food businesses.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Local Food Aggregation Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The FY26 Local Food Aggregation Grant Program, administered by Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience, awards grant funding to a single successful applicant to aggregate, distribute, and market food grown by regional and Montgomery County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets. This is a multi-year grant opportunity with $550,000 in year-one funding for operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility, with the goal of meeting current and future wholesale and institutional market demand for locally produced food products. The application process has two stages: Stage One assesses eligibility for grant funding, and Stage Two assesses program alignment and viability of success. Applicants selected for Stage Two are contacted directly after completing Stage One. The performance period runs from approximately June 30, 2026 through June 30, 2030 (FY26–FY29). Multi-year continuation is contingent on appropriation of funding and compliance with reporting requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards $550,000 in year-one funding for operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility. This is a multi-year grant opportunity covering a performance period of approximately June 30, 2026 through June 30, 2030 (FY26–FY29). A single competitive award is made to one successful applicant to aggregate, distribute, and market food from regional and Montgomery County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets. Applications proceed through two stages: Stage One assessed eligibility and Stage Two assessed program alignment and viability of success. Multi-year continuation is contingent on appropriation of funding and compliance with reporting requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage One: Friday, February 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST (closed); Stage Two (tentative): Friday, April 17, 2026 (closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations that can aggregate, distribute, and market locally and regionally grown food to wholesale and institutional markets in Montgomery County, including those seeking to establish a food aggregation facility for locally produced food. Applicants must demonstrate prior experience contracting with at least 2 institutional buyers (K-12 schools, universities, hospitals, carceral sector), at least $1M annual gross revenue from food sales within the past 3 years, and procurement relationships with a minimum of 10 small farms.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aggregation, distribution, and marketing of food grown by regional and Montgomery County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets; operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland; regional and County-based farmers are the source of food to be aggregated. Preference for applicants with market channels in Montgomery County, Maryland, and the Mid-Atlantic region.
requirements_list: Must pass Stage One eligibility assessment
Must demonstrate program alignment and viability of success in Stage Two
Must complete Stage One application before being considered for Stage Two
Stage Two applicants are selected and contacted directly
Must demonstrate ability to aggregate, store, and distribute locally sourced foods

Stage One (deadline February 20, 2026, now closed) assessed eligibility for grant funding; Stage Two (tentative deadline April 17, 2026, now closed) assessed program alignment and viability of success — applicants selected for Stage Two were contacted directly. The Stage Two NOFO was released approximately four weeks after the Stage One closing date. Both application phases for FY26 appear to have concluded. Review Stage One and Stage Two NOFOs, information session materials, and FAQs linked on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program provides monthly online grocery benefits to eligible households with children who are not eligible for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program). Benefits are delivered through Instacart Fresh Funds and can be used to purchase fresh and shelf-stable food and beverage items via home delivery or store pickup. Eligible households receive $100 per month per child under age 18 (ages 0–18), up to a maximum of $400 per month. Benefits are loaded as Instacart Fresh Funds credits on the 15th of each month (or next business day). The current program period runs from July 15, 2025 to July 15, 2026, with a waitlist available for the upcoming July 2026–July 2027 cycle. The program is designed for families who do not qualify for SNAP benefits and have post-tax household income below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $124,000/year for a household of 4). Eligible fees including driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees are also covered; non-eligible items are charged to the backup payment method. The program was initially funded by Montgomery County Council Special Appropriation #24-37 (December 2023, $1.8M) with additional funds approved in the FY2025 County Operating Budget.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating households receive $100 per month for each eligible child under age 18, up to a maximum of $400 per month. Benefits are loaded as Instacart Fresh Funds credits on the 15th of each month (or the next business day) and can be used to purchase eligible fresh and shelf-stable food and beverage items through the Instacart platform (home delivery or store pickup). Eligible fees including driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees are also covered; non-eligible items are charged to the backup payment method. The current program period runs July 15, 2025 to July 15, 2026, with a waitlist available for the upcoming July 2026–July 2027 cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not currently open to new participants for the current cycle; waitlist available for upcoming benefits cycle (July 2026 – July 2027). Current program end date: July 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County households with at least one child under age 18 who does not receive SNAP benefits and whose post-tax household income is below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $124,000/year for a household of 4).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh and shelf-stable food and beverage items through the Instacart Fresh Funds platform (home delivery or store pickup). Eligible fees including driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees are covered. Non-eligible items are charged to the backup payment method.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland throughout the program period. Grocery delivery is restricted to the address registered with Montgomery County DHHS at enrollment; pickup is available at participating local retailers on the Instacart platform.
requirements_list: Reside in Montgomery County throughout the program
Have at least one child under age 18 who is not eligible for SNAP benefits
Post-tax household income below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $124,000/year for a household of 4)
Have access to a backup electronic payment method (debit card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, or Klarna)
Be able to navigate an English-only online platform
Consent to participate in a mid-year check-in
Provide proof of income (pay stubs from last 30 days)
Provide valid photo ID for parent(s) or guardian(s)
Provide proof of address
Provide government-issued proof of identity for all participating children (e.g., birth certificate or school documents)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants must first contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator (Montgomery County Food Council or DHHS Navigation Line) for a brief eligibility pre-screening. If eligible, the Navigator assists with completing an online waitlist form. When openings become available, waitlisted individuals are contacted to complete a full application and upload required documents (proof of income, valid photo ID, proof of address, and government-issued identity documents for all participating children). Enrollment is first-come, first-served based on completed applications. Once enrolled, participants receive instructions to create an Instacart Fresh Funds account (at instacart.com/signup or via the app, using email, Google, or Facebook authentication) and a unique code to access monthly benefits. One personal account per person/household is permitted.

Grantees implement innovative outreach and enrollment support approaches targeting underserved residents.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach and enrollment support to help eligible Montgomery County families enroll in SNAP, WIC, FMNP, and other federal and state nutrition benefits programs. structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds organizations to address gaps in healthy food access for children and families by co-locating food assistance at Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) school sites. Grantees establish, expand, or maintain school-based food assistance programs in partnership with MCPS, developing program models for new schools and addressing food resource needs identified by school personnel. Applications are submitted through the eCivis grants portal following a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Awards are eligible for renewal annually, pending successful performance outcomes, grant administration compliance, and fund appropriation.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually. FY26 awarded $2,303,775 to 13 organizations across 99 MCPS school sites. FY25 awarded $1,250,274 to 11 organizations across 60+ MCPS school sites. FY24 awarded $480,452 to 8 organizations across 30+ MCPS school sites. Individual awards ranged from approximately $15,750 to $146,250 in FY24. Awards are eligible for renewal annually, pending successful performance outcomes, grant administration compliance, and fund appropriation, for an additional one-year grant period. Applications are reviewed via the eCivis grants portal following a NOFO release. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis only after contract execution. Eligible costs include food purchases, staffing, operating costs (refrigeration, storage, transportation), and indirect costs up to 15%. Food cost ranges vary by format ($4–$25/unit).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and government entities that provide food assistance programs at Montgomery County Public School sites to increase food security for students and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing, expanding, or maintaining food pantries and food assistance programs at MCPS school sites, including providing fresh produce, shelf-stable food bags, snack bags, family food boxes, prepared meals, and grocery gift cards. Service formats include family pop-up markets, choice pantries, and pre-packed distributions. Eligible costs include staffing costs, food purchases, operating costs (refrigeration, storage, transportation), and indirect costs up to 15%.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be co-located at Montgomery County Public School (MCPS) sites in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Programs must be co-located at MCPS school sites
Must operate in partnership with MCPS
Must address food resource needs identified by school personnel
Must develop a program model for successful services at school(s)
Must distribute satisfaction survey to participants at least once per grant period
Must obtain photo releases for any uploaded materials
Must report sourcing of local/DMV farm products as percentages
Must maintain SDAT Good Standing verification
Must comply with Montgomery County Ethics disclosure requirements
Must comply with Title VII Civil Rights Act
Must acknowledge Maryland Public Information Act (MPIA)
Must provide proof of insurance
Funds are reimbursement only after contract execution
Must document cultural proficiency and racial equity efforts
Must submit MOUs with schools
Must submit financial receipts and photos of distributions
Must report participation and implementation metrics via OFSR online platform
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis online grant application portal following a NOFO release. The application includes: Task A (Applicant Information Form — legal registration, IRS docs, board info, SDAT Good Standing verification); Task B (Project Strategy — project title/overview, funding request, service format/food type/quantities/frequency, school cluster preferences, narrative on service delivery, referral collaboration, local economy support, community engagement, OFSR values alignment); Task C (Project Budget — Excel template, staffing FTEs, volunteer FTEs, financial management practices, NICRA, audit reports, current-year budget); Task D (Budget Narrative/Justification — staff roles, operating cost breakdown, funding reduction impact, renewal cost shifts, out-of-county service safeguards); Task E (Performance History — narrative with outcome data, satisfaction surveys, partnership documentation with MCPS, photos of distributions); Task F (Performance Reporting & Evaluation — mid-cycle and end-cycle programmatic and financial reports via OFSR online platform). Proposals are evaluated on five weighted criteria (25–15 points each) plus optional add-value characteristics (max 15 points) using confidence ratings on a 1–3 scale. Feedback reports available to unsuccessful applicants upon request. Late submissions are disqualified and will not be forwarded to the Review Panel.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports proven, scalable food gardening initiatives that expand resident and community food production capacity as a means of increasing local food security in Montgomery County. It funds eligible organizations to provide residents with access to yard, patio, and community gardening supplies, space, and education. Projects must be rooted in research and best practices, have demonstrated success in resident and community gardening program design and implementation, and measurably increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity. For FY26, $200,000 in total grant funding is available, with individual awards expected to range from $25,000 to $100,000 and a performance period of approximately June 30, 2026 to November 1, 2027, with the opportunity for renewal for one additional year contingent on performance, continued need, and availability of funds. In FY24, $210,559 was awarded to 7 grantees.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience / Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual awards are expected to range from $25,000 to $100,000, with $200,000 in total grant funding available for FY26. The grant performance period runs approximately 17 months (on/about June 30, 2026 to November 1, 2027), with the opportunity for renewal for one additional year contingent on performance, continued need, and availability of funds. If renewed in FY27, the renewed grant award will not exceed 25% of the initial grant award and must meet an increased match requirement of 75% (not including in-kind), pending Council appropriations. In FY24, $210,559 was awarded to 7 grantees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (federal 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status) and other eligible entities that operate resident and community gardening programs in Montgomery County, particularly those serving individuals and households who have been historically and disproportionately impacted by food insecurity, poor health outcomes, and land access barriers. Priority is given to projects that successfully implemented FY2023 and/or FY2024 Resident and Community Gardening Grant Programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding resident and community food production capacity, including gardening supplies, space, and education to measurably increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to food-insecure Montgomery County residents. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or exclusively benefit Montgomery County residents. Services or activities taking place outside of Montgomery County must exclusively benefit Montgomery County residents.

All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Target population includes individuals and households in Montgomery County who have been historically and disproportionately impacted by food insecurity, poor health outcomes, and land access barriers. Priority geographic areas include healthy food access priority geographic areas within Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Community Supports Partnership (CSP) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program providing community-based behavioral health services for K–12 students in Montgomery County, part of the Coordinated Community Supports (CSP) initiative under Maryland's Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC). The program uses a multi-tiered system of supports (MTSS) with Tier 1 (universal/prevention), Tier 2 (brief/small group), and Tier 3 (individual/intensive) services. Mandatory use of Evidence-Based Practices (EBPs) is required. The FY27 grant term is July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027, contingent on Montgomery County receiving state funding from Maryland's FY27 CSP grant program.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for coordinated community supports partnerships, contingent on county receiving state funding from Maryland's FY27 CSP grant program. Award amounts range from $50,000 to $3.5 million (average ~$750,000 in FY26 round). Grant term is 12 months (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027). Funds disbursed via reimbursement or fixed schedule (not lump sum); reimbursable expenses must be incurred after contract finalization and Notice to Proceed issued. Indirect costs capped at 15%. Schools are not direct recipients; only limited subcontracting with schools is permitted (buses, staff training stipends, behavioral health supplies).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations providing coordinated community-based behavioral health services for K–12 students in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health services and interventions for students using evidence-based practices across three MTSS tiers. Allowable costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, contractual (training, licenses), construction, and indirect costs (up to 15%). Medicaid billing encouraged; anticipated Medicaid and other revenues must be reflected in budget. Minimal subcontracting with schools permitted for buses, stipends for training outside contract hours, and behavioral health supplies. Schools may not be direct grant recipients.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Services must be strategically coordinated with Montgomery County Public Schools. Organization's principal place of business must be in Montgomery County, or national/regional organizations must have a Montgomery County location.
requirements_list: Board of Directors disclosure: must state if current Montgomery County Government employees or contractors serve in volunteer or paid board roles (triggers Ethics Commission review)
Conflict-of-interest disclosure: applicants must disclose all individuals affiliated with the organization and this program who are employed by Montgomery County
Insurance requirement: all grantees must show proof of insurance prior to receiving funds

Criminal background checks: any individual who has contact with children, adolescents, and students must obtain a CJIS State and federal criminal background check including fingerprinting, completed prior to commencing any work under this grant
Compliance with Title VII Civil Rights Act of 1964, Maryland Public Information Act (MPIA), and all applicable Federal, State, and Local laws

Applications may not be revised or altered after submission
Applicant must be officially authorized by governing board to file

Notification required if organization changes status, ceases operations, or becomes a subsidiary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis grants portal. Review the RFA and information session slide deck for details. RFA was issued November 20, 2025. Applications were due January 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM. After submission, LBHA develops the CSP grant application to CHRC (due early February 2026); CHRC reviews applications February through May 2026; CHRC makes awards based on final budgeted amounts approved by Maryland General Assembly in May 2026; award agreements finalized by June 30, 2026; service delivery begins July 1, 2026. An additional information session will be scheduled once the CHRC releases its RFA for the next cycle.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program that provides cost-sharing capital funding to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County for capital improvement projects. Grants match appropriated Maryland State Bond Bills or other forms of Maryland State capital funding. Two funding categories: Arts Facility Capital Grants and Non-Arts Facility Capital Grants. Multi-year support possible across FY26, FY27, and FY28 (contingent on continued appropriations and satisfactory project performance).
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-sharing capital grants awarded on a competitive basis in two stages. Stage One deadline was April 28, 2025; Stage Two deadline was September 8, 2025. Two funding categories: Arts Facility Capital Grants ($553,159 available) and Non-Arts Facility Capital Grants ($2,428,166 available). Grants match appropriated Maryland State Bond Bills or other Maryland State capital funding. Capital expenses must be at least $5,000 for one-time costs on fixed assets (land/building purchase, new construction, renovations). Disbursed on a cost-reimbursement or fixed-schedule basis (not lump sum). Multi-year funding possible across FY26, FY27, and FY28. Ineligible expenses include operating costs, rent, leases, salaries, utilities, staff benefits, contractor costs unrelated to capital, supplies, minor equipment ($5,000 or less), maintenance, indirect costs, loans/mortgage payments, lobbying, pre-award expenses, and supplantation of other grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage 1: Monday, April 28, 2025 at 11:59 PM; Stage 2: Monday, September 8, 2025 at 11:59 PM

Ineligible: operating costs, rent, leases, salaries, utilities, staff benefits, contractor costs unrelated to capital, supplies, minor equipment ($5,000 or less), maintenance, indirect costs, loans/mortgage payments, lobbying, pre-award expenses, and supplantation of other grants.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Emerging Business Improvement District (EBID) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program supporting the formation and development of emerging business improvement districts in Montgomery County. Provides subsidy for formation and support of non-profit commercial district management entities to conduct place making, place management, branding, and economic development activities in a designated neighborhood. Supports organizations working toward establishing Business Improvement Districts (BIDs) or Urban Development Corporations (UDCs) through three phases: (1) planning, (2) outreach, and (3) legislative approval. Selected awardees are anticipated to be at various points along the continuum of these three phases.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant awards of $100,000+ to support emerging business improvement districts in Montgomery County for FY26. Grant period is 12 months with possibility for renewal for up to three total years contingent on satisfactory performance and funds availability. Eligible costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment (≥$10K per unit), supplies (<$10K), contractual services, and construction/renovation. Indirect costs up to 15% if no NICRA, or applicant's NICRA rate if held. Ineligible costs include capital expenses (≥$5K one-time fixed asset purchases such as vehicles, property, or building additions) and purchases from Board Members' organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations at any stage of BID/UDC formation (planning, outreach, or legislative authorization), including nonprofit, business, or property owner entities eligible to form a BID or Urban Development Corporation in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Formation and organizational development of Business Improvement Districts (BIDs) or Urban Development Corporations (UDCs), including personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment (≥$10K per unit), supplies (<$10K per unit), contractual services, and construction/renovation. Indirect costs up to 15% if no NICRA. Ineligible uses include capital expenses (≥$5K one-time fixed asset purchases such as vehicles, property, or building additions), purchases of goods/services from Board Members' organizations, prior obligations/debts/fines/penalties, lobbying, supplanting other grant funds, and any purchases made outside the grant award period of performance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. All activities and expenditures must be in Montgomery County and benefit Montgomery County residents. Applicant's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, must have a location in Montgomery County. Applicants may serve specific zip codes within the county or countywide.

Cannot fund prior obligations, debts, fines, or penalties
No lobbying activities; cannot supplant other grant funds

Award notification letters are expected approximately one month after the application deadline (approximately early April 2026). For platform support or ADA accommodations, contact Ali Hoy at grants@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Healthy Communities Fund Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program soliciting applications from qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to administer culturally and linguistically appropriate programs and services improving the health and wellness of Montgomery County residents, with particular emphasis on Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) and Limited English Proficient (LEP) communities. Priority funding categories include Health & Social Support Services, Behavioral/Mental Health, and Senior Wellness. Collaborative, evidence-based approaches are encouraged.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $150,000 per awardee, with $1,500,000 in total available funding. Two award categories: grants of $50,000 or less, and grants over $50,000 (each with different application requirements). Grant term is 12 months. Disbursement structure: approximately 25% upfront plus quarterly payments conditioned on satisfactory program performance. Substance use treatment is explicitly excluded from funded activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations serving Montgomery County residents, particularly Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) and Limited English Proficient (LEP) communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (salaries), equipment, supplies, and activities aligned with Health and Social Support Services, Mental and Behavioral Health, or Senior Wellness programs. Services must include cultural and linguistic competency components. Substance use treatment is not an eligible use of funds. Prohibited uses also include lobbying, retroactive costs, supplanting other grants, purchases from board members' organizations, social media-only programs, online-only content, religious/cultural/political events without a services component, transportation/vehicle purchases, and services from other Montgomery County Government contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Applicants may be located outside Montgomery County, but proposed programs must serve residents of Montgomery County only.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Programs and services must be culturally and linguistically appropriate
Must serve Montgomery County residents
Emphasis on serving AAPI and Limited English Proficient (LEP) populations
Applicants encouraged to collaborate with other community organizations
Applications received after the deadline will be disqualified
Prior program performance may be considered in scoring
Must specify primary Montgomery County zip codes served
Organizations with current Montgomery County Government employees or contractors on staff must undergo ethics review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis grants portal. Review the NOFO and information session slide deck. An information session was held on August 13, 2025. Applications were due no later than Friday, August 29, 2025 at 11:59 PM. The FY26 cycle is now closed; a future FY27 cycle has not yet been announced as of May 2026.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for pre-weatherization repairs, electrification, and climate resilience improvements for income-eligible households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-weatherization repairs, electrification, and climate resilience improvements for homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be income-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anticipated launch in mid-March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program providing funding to one umbrella/lead organization to design, implement, and manage a countywide collaborative initiative delivering comprehensive, culturally and linguistically responsive services to socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating immigration-status challenges in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Single competitive grant award of $3,504,636.00 to one umbrella/lead organization. Project period runs October 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, with a potential one-time no-cost extension until October 1, 2026. Any future funding outside the project period is contingent on Montgomery County Council appropriations for FY27.
structured_extraction.program_audience: One umbrella/lead organization serving socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating immigration-status challenges in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive intake and needs assessment systems; culturally and linguistically responsive outreach, recruitment, and service delivery; navigation and case management services; emergency support for stabilization; intensive case management for integration and self-sufficiency; countywide collaborative initiative management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Lead applicant must be registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT) at time of application review, finalization of grant agreements, and for payments during the life of the grant agreement

Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services
All activities and expenditures under this Grant Program must be provided in Montgomery County, and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Single award to one umbrella/lead organization only
Must complete: Lead Applicant Information Task, Lead Applicant Background Task, Project Scope of Work Task, and Budget Task
Must submit Letters of Commitment (LOC) from partners
Must submit Monitoring and Evaluation Plan (4-page PDF) with identified key data points
Must submit Project Staffing Plan (2-page PDF)
Must submit Implementation Timeline (2-page PDF)
Must submit Budget Tool
Must demonstrate sound grant and fiscal management practices including ability to submit financial reports and audit documentation
Must demonstrate evaluation capability with KPIs, metrics, and milestones
Must collect granular demographic data (race/ethnicity, language, country of origin)
Must integrate with HHS databases
Ethics disclosure required if organization employs or has board members who are Montgomery County Government employees or contractors
Must comply with Title VII Civil Rights Act 1964, Maryland Public Information Act (MPIA), insurance requirements, and accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities
