structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program providing $1,200,000 in total funding (FY26 Approved Budget, Resolution 20-820) to qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit and faith-based organizations in Montgomery County that are at high risk of hate crimes, to improve their security posture. Maximum award is $15,000 per facility; organizations may apply for up to 5 facilities (separate applications required). Performance period is 12 months upon execution of grant agreement.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding up to $15,000 per facility for nonprofit and faith-based security improvements in Montgomery County. Total program budget is $1,200,000 for FY26. Organizations may apply for up to 5 facilities via separate applications. Performance period is 12 months upon execution of grant agreement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Extended to Tuesday, November 4, 2025 at 11:59 PM (Original deadline: October 28, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit and faith-based organizations in Montgomery County at high risk of hate crimes based on their work, community, or known hate crimes or threats to them or similar organizations or communities nationally
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hire or augment security personnel; security assessment or planning; security training; security drill development and execution; purchase new security cameras; fususCORE devices for camera feed sharing with Montgomery County Police Department. Excludes: other equipment, facility upgrades, supplies, pre-contract expenses, camera monitoring services, fususCORE subscriptions, lobbying, and supplanting other grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Organizations must serve Montgomery County residents and demonstrate a Montgomery County presence. County location assurance required in application.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit or faith-based organization
Must be located in or serve Montgomery County, Maryland
Must be at high risk of hate crimes based on their work, community, and/or known hate crimes or threats
Must be in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT) at application review, finalization, and payment stages
Separate applications required for each facility (up to 5 facilities per organization)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis grants portal. Review the NOFO and information session slide deck. Application window opened September 30, 2025 with a deadline of November 4, 2025 (extended from October 28, 2025). Award notifications expected January 2026 via email. Applications are scored on Criterion A (Security Needs & Risk) = 80 points and Criterion B (Grant Admin & Budget) = 20 points.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Nonprofit Strategic Planning Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Capacity building grant program supporting nonprofits in Montgomery County in conducting strategic planning in response to adverse Federal actions (e.g., federal funding cuts, policy changes). Grants support development of strategic plans with recommendations on consolidation of services and how nonprofits and the County can meet challenges together.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding of $20,000–$100,000 per recipient for nonprofit strategic planning activities in Montgomery County for FY26. Performance period up to 6 months. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis in bi-weekly clusters after the priority deadline until available funds are fully committed. Implementation start date no earlier than February 1, 2026. Budget categories include Personnel, Fringe Benefits, Travel, Equipment, Supplies, Contractual, Construction, Other, and Indirect Costs (up to 15% unless a higher rate qualifies).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Priority Deadline: Wednesday, January 14, 2025, 5:30 PM EST (extended from January 7, 2025); rolling deadline thereafter until all funds committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits in Montgomery County seeking to conduct strategic planning in response to adverse Federal actions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nonprofit strategic planning capacity building and technical assistance; specific deliverable is a strategic plan addressing consolidation of services and preparation for adverse Federal actions. Allowable budget categories include Personnel, Fringe Benefits, Travel, Equipment, Supplies, Contractual, Construction, Other, and Indirect Costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County, MD. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Organizations and staff based in Montgomery County are prioritized over those based in other jurisdictions. Service delivery locations, office locations, and staff based in Montgomery County are scoring factors (5 bonus points available).
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization operating in Montgomery County
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County, MD
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Must respond to five Scope of Work narrative questions: Adverse Federal Actions, Service Model Impact, Strategic Plan Utility, Supporting Capacity Building, and Consolidation of Services
Implementation start date must be no earlier than February 1, 2026
Performance period is up to 6 months
Must apply through the eCivis/Euna grants portal
Indirect costs capped at 15% unless a higher rate qualifies per Md. Code Ann., State Finance and Procurement § 2-208(c)
Must contact Office of Grants Management for clarification on ethics or eligibility questions
Collaborative applications are allowed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis/Euna grants portal. Review the NOFO and information session slide deck. Applications submitted after the priority deadline will be accepted on a rolling basis until available funds are fully committed, with proposals reviewed in bi-weekly clusters. The Euna application page will be updated once all funds have been committed. If additional funding becomes available, OGM will update the application page and send a notice through the Montgomery County Grant Opportunities Newsletter. OGM plans to open a separate NOFO in late Winter 2026 for finalized strategic plans seeking additional implementation funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Place Based Management (PBM) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program supporting place-based management organizations that provide services and improvements in specific commercial districts or neighborhoods in Montgomery County. Uses a Main Street Approach model (Economic Vitality, Design, Promotion, Organization) to support economic development in targeted geographic areas including Silver Spring Regional Services Center, Damascus Main Street Area, and other Montgomery County locations.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for place-based management organizations operating in Montgomery County commercial districts or neighborhoods. Award duration is 12 months with possibility for renewal up to 3 total years contingent on satisfactory performance and appropriation of funds. Silver Spring Regional Services Center area awards are $200,000 or more; Damascus Main Street Area awards are $50,000 or more (contingent on state award). Implementation start date for proposals should begin no earlier than May 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based management organizations in Montgomery County, specifically 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) tax-exempt entities (or collaborations with at least one tax-exempt partner) that serve businesses and residents of identified commercial corridors. Applicants must have Maryland SDAT registration and IRS 990 filing status or exemption.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to businesses in targeted economic corridors; marketing and promotion initiatives for district businesses; business rehabilitation and reinvestment support; data collection, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning; events, promotion, maintenance, and unification of commercial corridors. Prohibited uses include capital expenses ($5,000+ for fixed assets), goods/services from Board Members' organizations, pre-award purchases, lobbying, supplanting other grant funds, purchases/activities unnecessary to grant purpose, and prior debts/fines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, including Silver Spring Regional Services Center, Damascus Main Street Area, and other Montgomery County locations.
requirements_list: Organization must be a nonprofit (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6)) or a collaboration with at least one tax-exempt partner
Organization must have Maryland SDAT registration
Organization must have IRS 990 filing status or applicable exemption
Organization must not currently employ Montgomery County Government employees or contractors who are also paid by the County (exceptions: Montgomery College, MCPS, WorkSource Montgomery employees)
Organization's Board must not include current MCG employees/contractors in volunteer positions
Must comply with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Must be accessible to persons with disabilities
Must maintain proof of insurance prior to receiving funds
Must allow audit of expenditures and source documentation any time before final payment and three years thereafter
Must demonstrate ability to make project operational within 30 days of award
Must appropriately budget for staffing with clearly defined staff roles and responsibilities
Organizations funded under the program in the prior year are eligible to apply
Implementation start date for proposals should begin no earlier than May 1, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the eCivis/Euna Grants online portal. Three-stage review process: (1) OGM Administrative Review for eligibility and completeness (2-day cure window for minor errors); (2) CEC Proposal and Organization Eligibility Review (scope, budget, eligible expenses); (3) Subject Matter Expert (SME) Review Committee scoring. Required application tasks include: Applicant Information (legal name, tax ID, contact, IRS 990 or exemption), Applicant Background (staffing, budget, leadership demographics — optional, not scored), Goals section, Budget Tool, and Application Certification. Award notification expected approximately one month after the application deadline. Application window for FY26 opened January 14, 2026 and closed March 2, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Montgomery County Office of Human Resources and the Department of Health and Human Services that offers paid, two-year term employment positions to applicants with disabilities who have limited work experience. The goal is to help participants develop skills and gain experience that may lead to longer-term employment.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time or part-time paid two-year term positions with benefits and eligibility to participate in Montgomery County's retirement plan. Two to three positions are offered every few years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Each job posting is open for a minimum of two weeks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Applicants with severe disabilities certified by the Maryland Department of Education Division of Rehabilitation Services (or an equivalent out-of-state agency) who have limited work experience and have not previously held merit positions with Montgomery County Government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid county employment to develop job skills and gain work experience.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Must meet eligibility criteria for certification by the Maryland Department of Rehabilitation or equivalent out-of-state agency

Must be certified by the Maryland Department of Education Division of Rehabilitation Services or equivalent out-of-state vocational rehabilitation agency as having a severe disability (Schedule A Letter required)
Must meet minimum requirements for the specific position and be able to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation
Must provide proof of full COVID-19 vaccination prior to first date of employment (or contact OHR to discuss accommodations)
Must NOT be a current or prior County merit employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: LEAP4MCG positions are posted on the Montgomery County careers webpage and the Search Jobs section of the website with the job title and grade. Create an AccessMCG Extranet Account before applying. Each posting is open for a minimum of two weeks. Follow specific instructions in the job announcement to submit a Schedule A letter. Search for available positions by entering 'LEAP4MCG' in the Keywords search bar in the careers system.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Multilingual Certification Program allows county employees who are fluent in English and a second language to become certified and earn a pay differential for using their language skills to assist residents with Limited English Proficiency. Employees apply online, get supervisor and director approval, and pass a language certification exam. Certified employees receive an hourly pay differential for all hours worked and may be called upon to provide language assistance inside or outside their regular department.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified employees receive an hourly pay differential for all hours worked. MCGEO and non-represented employees: Basic $1.00/hour, Advanced $1.50/hour. IAFF employees: Basic $1.00/hour. FOP employees: Basic $1.00/hour, Advanced $2.00/hour, Expert $3.00/hour. Three certification levels exist: Basic (oral communication), Advanced (written and oral), and Expert (FOP members only, for use in interrogations and legal proceedings). Approved languages for non-FOP employees: American Sign Language, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, Spanish, and Vietnamese. FOP employees are not limited to the 7 approved languages. Certified employees are registered in the Language Certified Employees Database.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees who are fluent in English and a second language and work in front-facing positions that interact with the public daily
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pay differential compensates certified employees for providing language assistance — interpretation and/or written translation — to county residents with Limited English Proficiency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County Government employees only. The county serves more than 1 million residents. Non-FOP employees are limited to 7 approved languages; FOP employees may be certified in any language. Job applicants for positions requiring multilingual skills are processed separately through the OHR Recruiter managing the recruitment.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County government employee fluent in English and a second language
Basic level: must work in a front-facing position that interacts with residents daily and provide multilingual interpretation at least weekly to LEP customers
Advanced level: must provide written translation of official government documents at least weekly; work cannot be serviced by the Office of Community Partnership's Translations Unit
Expert level: must be a member of the FOP bargaining unit with mastery in the target language for use in interrogations, investigations, and legal proceedings
Must receive approval from supervisor and department director

Must pass a language certification exam in one of the approved languages (American Sign Language, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese for non-FOP employees; any language for FOP members)
IAFF members are eligible for Basic level only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Employee logs into the online eMultilingual system and submits a request. 2. Request is routed to supervisor for review and approval (FOP requests go directly to OHR). 3. Supervisor approves, denies, or returns the request. 4. If approved by supervisor, request is routed to department director or designee for approval. 5. OHR coordinates scheduling, testing, and rating. 6. Employee takes the language certification exam. 7. Employees and supervisors are notified of results and effective date. 8. Employees who pass receive the multilingual pay differential and are registered in the Language Certified Employees Database.

structured_extraction.program_description: Personify Health (formerly Virgin Pulse) is a free wellness program for eligible Montgomery County Government employees. Members can earn up to $350 per year in Rewards Cash for making healthy choices, receive a free fitness tracker, participate in step challenges, and manage their health and fitness through a personalized online portal. Rewards Cash can be used to donate, purchase from the rewards store, or obtain gift cards. Family members (up to 10) can also join the program, though they do not receive the cash incentive or free tracker.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible employees earn up to $350 per year in Rewards Cash for making healthy choices, redeemable for donations, store purchases, or gift cards. They also receive a free activity tracker (or can sync their own compatible device). Family members (up to 10) can join but do not receive the cash incentive or free tracker. Rewards are earned quarterly through activity points, health check completion, and preventative screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Insurance-eligible Montgomery County Government and participating agency employees (enrollment in a health plan is not required, only eligibility to enroll).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rewards Cash (up to $350/year) earned through activity points, health check completion, and preventative screenings; redeemable for donations, store purchases, or gift cards. Free fitness tracker also provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County Government and participating agency employees.
requirements_list: Must be insurance-eligible as a Montgomery County Government or participating agency employee
Do not need to be enrolled in a health plan, only eligible to enroll
Complete a Health Check and at least 2 preventative screenings to reach Level 1 and qualify for cash rewards
Ongoing activity and engagement required to earn quarterly cash rewards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New employees receive a registration email from Personify Health within 3–4 weeks of hire. Current employees enrolling for the first time should email LiveWell@montgomerycountymd.gov to request registration details. Support is also available at support.personifyhealth.com or 888-671-9395 (Mon–Fri, 8 am–9 pm ET), or via live chat.

structured_extraction.program_description: An unpaid internship and training program for young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Participants complete three 10-week intensive worksite internships supported by job coaches, plus daily classroom instruction, to build workforce and career development skills. A four-week trial period is required, and acceptance into the program is not a guarantee of employment. Programs begin late August to early September on an annual academic-year cycle.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unpaid, volunteer-basis internship placements running September through June. Participants work approximately 25 hours per week across three 10-week worksite rotations and attend one hour of daily classroom instruction. Program hours are 8:30 am to 2:30 pm. Programs begin late August to early September on an annual academic-year cycle. Job coaching and vocational rehabilitation services are provided in partnership with SEEC, The Ivymount School, Maryland DORS, DC RSA, Maryland DDA, and DC DDS.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults aged 18-30 with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities who are Maryland or DC residents and are eligible for DDA/DDS funding or can do Private Pay. Applicants must have an IEP and DDA/DDS support eligibility or private funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce and career development training through worksite internships, job coaching, and classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and DC residents eligible. Applicants must have DDA/DDS funding in place prior to the program start date or have a private pay agreement established with Ivymount.
requirements_list: Applicant must be between 18 and 30 years old
Applicant must have an intellectual and/or developmental disability
Applicant must have an IEP
Applicant must be eligible for DDA/DDS funding or be able to do Private Pay
Applicant must be a Maryland or DC resident with DDA/DDS funding in place prior to start date, or have a private pay agreement established with Ivymount
Attendance at one Information Session is required for acceptance into the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete SEEC's Project SEARCH Montgomery Application form. Once completed, follow the instructions in the application file to mail or email the application for review. Contact PSRecruitment@seeconline.org for alternate formats. Note that attendance at one Information Session is required for acceptance into the program. An Open House is held in the summer at the host business site.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Government's Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) provides tuition assistance funds to eligible county employees with merit system status. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis until all funding for the fiscal year is obligated. The program runs on an annual cycle beginning July 1 of each new fiscal year. Eligible employee groups include FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, and MCVFRA members, as well as active volunteers with the Montgomery County Volunteer Fire Rescue Service Association (MCVFRA). The FY26 program opened July 1, 2025 and runs through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of Human Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance funds are provided to eligible Montgomery County Government employees on a first-come, first-served basis each fiscal year. Funding levels vary by employee bargaining unit: FOP and IAFF employees may use funds for tuition plus direct/compulsory costs (matriculation, registration, lab fees, library services, technology fees); MCGEO and Unrepresented (UNREP) employees may use funds for tuition costs only; MCVFRA volunteers may use funds for tuition costs only for courses directly related to current volunteer duties. FY26 maximum per employee ranges from $865 to $2,300 depending on employment status (full-time vs. part-time) and bargaining unit. For example, IAFF FY26 maximum is $1,830 (FT) / $915 (PT); UNREP FY26 maximum is $2,300 (FT) / $1,150 (PT); MCVFRA FY26 maximum is $1,830. The FY26 program opened July 1, 2025 and runs through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 18, 2026 — all FY26 approved applications and required documents must be submitted and received by OHR by this date for payment processing
structured_extraction.contact_name: Teddy Ramet (Human Resources Specialist); Dr. Rochelle Plummer (Manager); Anithia Rhodes (TAP Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees with merit system status (including FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, and UNREP members), State's Attorney's Office employees, and active volunteers with the Montgomery County Volunteer Fire Rescue Service Association (MCVFRA)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for coursework or education pursued by eligible county employees leading to a certificate, associate, baccalaureate, or graduate degree, or for credit/non-credit courses and seminars. For IAFF and FOP employees, direct/compulsory costs such as matriculation, registration, laboratory fees, library services, and technology fees are also covered. For MCGEO and UNREP employees, tuition costs only (matriculation, registration, lab fees, library services are excluded). For MCVFRA volunteers, tuition costs only for courses directly related to current volunteer duties or skills for advancement in volunteer ranks. Explicitly excluded for all groups: books, supplies, application fees, exam fees, late registration fees, parking fees, audited courses, credit-by-examination courses, and benefits that duplicate other programs. For MCVFRA volunteers, all approved coursework must be held in the U.S.A.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Montgomery County Government and active volunteers with MCVFRA. Courses must be taken at accredited colleges or universities recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or the Higher Education Accreditation Commission (for degree programs).
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County Government employee with merit system status, or an active MCVFRA volunteer appearing on the certified active volunteer list
Must belong to one of the eligible bargaining units: FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, or MCVFRA
Must apply on a first-come, first-served basis while funds remain available for the fiscal year
Application must be submitted within the fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) to be considered
All FY26 approved applications and required documents must be submitted to OHR by June 18, 2026 for payment processing

FOP members must submit application at least three weeks prior to actual registration; IAFF and MCGEO members at least four weeks prior; UNREP members at least three weeks prior; MCVFRA members at least two weeks prior

Courses must be directly related to current County work, normal career progression, or an approved career change within the County (for employees); or directly related to current volunteer duties or skills for advancement in volunteer ranks (for MCVFRA)
Courses must be taken during off-duty hours or with prior supervisor authorization
Employee must complete course with a passing grade; failure to do so may require reimbursement to the County
One-year employment retention obligation post-completion (IAFF requirement noted; may apply to other units)
Cannot duplicate benefits received under other programs
All approved coursework for MCVFRA volunteers must be held in the U.S.A.
MCVFRA volunteers must meet point system requirements per MD Code § 21-21 and appear on the certified active volunteer list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees (FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP): Log in to the online employee portal using County USERID and password at the MCG HR Apps page. Submit application at least 3–4 weeks before course registration (varies by bargaining unit). OHR processes applications within 10–14 days. Upon approval, an authorization letter is sent to the school for direct billing, or reimbursement is available if the employee paid upfront. All FY26 approved applications and required documents must be received by OHR by June 18, 2026 for payment processing. MCVFRA volunteers: Obtain the electronic application form from the County website, obtain required departmental signatures, and submit to the LOSAP Administrator, MCFRS Division of Volunteer Services. All applications must be submitted within the current fiscal year (FY26: July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026). Contact OHR at ohr.tap@montgomerycountymd.gov or 240-777-5116 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Business Preference Program (LBPP) gives Montgomery County-based businesses a 10% preference advantage when competing for county contracts. On Invitations for Bids (IFBs), local businesses receive a 10% reduction to their bid price for evaluation purposes (capped at $200,000). On Requests for Proposals (RFPs), local businesses receive an evaluation factor worth 10% of total points. The program is designed to support economic growth and job creation in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified local businesses receive a 10% price preference on IFBs (bid price reduced by 10% for evaluation purposes, up to $200,000 maximum reduction) or an evaluation factor worth 10% of total points on RFPs for Montgomery County contracts. This preference is applied during the evaluation and award process only, not to the actual contract price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independently owned businesses with their principal place of business in Montgomery County that bid on county contracts via IFBs or RFPs issued after August 1, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preference points or price reduction applied during evaluation of county procurement bids and proposals to give local businesses a competitive advantage in winning county contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County — either all physical locations are in the county, or county-based locations account for over 50% of total employees or over 50% of gross sales.
requirements_list: Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County
Business must be independently owned (brokers and subsidiaries are not eligible)
Must have a federal tax number or W-9 in the name of the business
Must obtain local business certification before submitting a bid or proposal, or have applied for certification before the submission deadline
Certification must be valid at time of bid or proposal submission
Does not apply to Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP) IFBs or RFPs
Does not apply to solicitations where State or Federal funding prohibits local preference
Does not apply to awards by discount or line item
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit https://azex32.montgomerycountymd.gov/cvrs/ and follow the prompts to register or update your vendor profile. Select the option to enroll in the LBPP if you meet the criteria. Certification must be obtained before the bid or proposal due date.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires prime contractors on large Montgomery County government contracts to subcontract at least 10% of contract dollars to local businesses. The goal applies to individual contracts exceeding $10 million and in aggregate across all such contracts. Subcontractors must be certified by Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prime contractors on High Dollar Value Contracts (estimated value exceeding $10 million) must award at least 10% of contract dollars to local businesses. The performance plan specifies the percentage of total contract dollars (including modifications and renewals) to be paid to certified local business subcontractors. To qualify as a local business, the firm must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County — either exclusively in the county, or with the county location accounting for over 50% of total employees or gross sales. Subcontractors must be certified by Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses based in Montgomery County that wish to participate as subcontractors on large county procurement contracts, and prime contractors awarded county contracts valued at $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subcontracting work under county procurement contracts valued over $10 million, covering goods and/or services categories as specified per subcontract. Payments go to certified local business subcontractors for the life of the contract from execution through final expiration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County — either with all locations in the county, or with the county location(s) accounting for over 50% of total employees or gross sales.
requirements_list: Applies only to initial contract awards estimated to exceed $10 million
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County
If the business has locations inside and outside the county, the county location(s) must account for over 50% of total employees or over 50% of gross sales
Subcontractors must be certified by Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance (search: www.mcipcc.net)
Contractor must submit a Local Business Subcontracting Plan covering the life of the contract after contract award
Plan must include a good-faith-efforts statement or waiver request justification
Plan must include binding arbitration language for dispute resolution with local business subcontractors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This program operates as a contract compliance requirement under County Code Article XVII of Chapter 11B. After contract award, prime contractors on contracts with an initial estimated value exceeding $10 million must submit a Local Business Subcontracting Plan covering the life of the contract. The plan must include a good-faith-efforts statement or waiver request justification, and must include binding arbitration language for dispute resolution with local business subcontractors. Contractors should contact DBRC@montgomerycountymd.gov or 240-777-9913 for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP) requires Montgomery County departments to award 25% of their procurements for goods, services, and construction to registered and certified local small businesses. The program helps local small vendors — including non-profits — compete for county contracts against businesses of similar size and resources. Montgomery County-based retailers, construction and trades companies, wholesalers, service firms, and non-profits are encouraged to register and participate. A Veteran-Owned Business Preference Program (VBPP) amendment effective January 2, 2025 gives verified veteran-owned local small businesses an additional 5% evaluation points on LSBRP proposals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified businesses gain access to a reserved pool of county procurement opportunities. County departments must award at least 25% of their procurements to LSBRP-certified vendors. Veteran-owned local small businesses that also hold VBPP certification receive an additional 5% evaluation points on qualifying proposals. Registration and certification are free through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County-based independently-owned small businesses and non-profits seeking to compete for county government contracts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to reserved county government procurement contracts for goods, services, and construction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County — either all locations in Montgomery County, or the Montgomery County location(s) must account for over 50% of total employees or gross sales.
requirements_list: Must be independently owned (brokers and subsidiary businesses are not eligible)
Must have a federal tax number or W-9 in the name of the business
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County

Must meet size and revenue thresholds by business type: Retail — up to 30 employees OR up to $5M avg annual sales; Wholesale — up to 30 employees OR up to $5M avg annual sales; Services — up to 100 employees OR up to $10M avg annual sales; Construction — up to 50 employees OR up to $14M avg annual sales; Manufacturing — up to 40 employees OR up to $14M avg annual sales
Must register and apply for certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS)

For VBPP preference points: must hold both LSBRP and VBPP certifications, and have a valid VOSB or SDVOSB certificate from the U.S. Small Business Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses register and apply for LSBRP (and optionally VBPP) certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at azex32.montgomerycountymd.gov/cvrs. Registration is free. Upload required certification documents as prompted. Once certified, businesses become eligible to compete for reserved county procurements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Minority, Female & Disabled (MFD) Owned Business Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's MFD Program helps certified minority, female, and disabled-owned businesses access prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with County government agencies. The program sets participation goals for MFD firms across purchasing categories (construction, professional services, non-professional services, and goods) and conducts outreach activities, workshops, and forums to help MFD businesses explore contracting opportunities. Awarded prime contractors with contracts of $50,000 or more must demonstrate good-faith effort to subcontract a minimum percentage of contract dollars to certified MFD businesses, and non-compliance may result in liquidated damages, contract termination, or a 3-year declaration of non-responsibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program sets MFD participation goals for County contracts: 22% for construction, 25% for professional services, 24% for non-professional services, and 10% for goods (effective January 1, 2025). Certified MFD firms gain access to prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with County agencies through outreach, workshops, and networking forums. Contractors with contracts of $50,000 or more must demonstrate good-faith effort to subcontract a minimum percentage of contract dollars to certified MFD businesses. Non-compliance may result in liquidated damages, contract termination, or a 3-year declaration of non-responsibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that are at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed daily by minority persons, women, or disabled persons — including African Americans, Hispanic Americans, Asian Americans, Native Americans, disabled persons, and women — located in or seeking contracts with Montgomery County. Certain non-profits with at least 51% disabled workforce on a contract basis may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessing prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed daily by a minority person(s), woman, or disabled person
Eligible categories: African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, Native American, Disabled Persons, and Women
Must hold a valid certification from an accepted certifying agency (e.g., MDOT-MBE, SBA 8(a), SBA Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, WBENC, MSDC, or Baltimore City MWBOO)
Effective October 1, 2021, VA Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business certification qualifies under the 'disabled' category (not standard Veteran Owned certification)
Certain non-profits with at least 51% disabled workforce performing contract work may also qualify
Awarded prime contractors with contracts of $50,000 or more must submit an MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan approved by the Director of Procurement
MFD subcontracts must include a binding arbitration clause for dispute resolution
Compliance documentation (invoices, subcontracts, cancelled checks, affidavits, waivers, arbitration decisions) required before final payment on contracts
Designated subcontractors must submit monthly MFD Report of Payments Received for the duration of contract performance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain certification from one of the accepted certifying agencies (MDOT, Federal SBA 8(a), MSDC, WBENC, VA, or City of Baltimore). Register with Montgomery County's Office of Procurement to access contracting opportunities. For prime contractors awarded contracts of $50,000 or more, submit an MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan for Director of Procurement approval. Designated subcontractors submit monthly MFD Report of Payments Received for the duration of contract performance. Waiver of MFD requirement is available under Section 7.3.3 of the Procurement Regulations, determined by the Director of Procurement. Full procedural details are in Section 7 of Montgomery County Procurement Regulations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County operates four Business Innovation Centers — the Germantown Innovation Center, Rockville Innovation Center, Silver Spring Innovation Center, and AI Innovation Center (located in North Bethesda) — to help businesses grow. The centers provide office and incubator space, business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization assistance, and access to state and county funding programs. They are also part of the Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program, offering extra support to qualified international companies launching U.S. headquarters or East Coast operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of the County Executive
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive incubator or accelerator space at one of four innovation centers (AI-North Bethesda, Life Sciences-Germantown, MedTech-Rockville, Silver Spring) or a virtual option, along with business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization support, and connections to state and county funding programs. International companies may also receive additional support through the Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business founders and leadership (President/CEO) across all industries, with a particular focus on life sciences, MedTech, high-tech, and AI-enhanced technology companies, including international companies seeking to establish a U.S. presence in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Office and incubator space, business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization assistance, and access to funding programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Montgomery County, Maryland, with centers in Germantown (Life Sciences), Rockville (MedTech), Silver Spring, and North Bethesda (AI Innovation Center), plus a virtual participation option.
requirements_list: Complete the Innovation Center Intake Form
Submit articles of incorporation or company structure documentation
Submit a business plan or business proposal
Applicant must be a for-profit business entity (C-Corp, S-Corp, LLC, or Other)
President/CEO or equivalent leadership contact required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Innovation Center Intake Form (PDF), selecting preferred location(s) among AI-North Bethesda, Life Sciences-Germantown, MedTech-Rockville, Silver Spring, Virtual, or Other. Submit articles of incorporation/company structure documentation and a business plan or business proposal. Questions may be directed to BusinessCenter@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Innovation Accelerator is a project-based learning course for Montgomery County government employees. Participants work in cohorts to solve real workplace problems using structured problem-solving tools — improving processes, designing services, and making things more effective, efficient, and equitable — without requiring new budget, staff, or technology. The program also offers Civic Design coaching, journey mapping, user research facilitation, and structured problem-solving methods including human-centered design and process improvement.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County Office of the County Executive
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A multi-day, in-person cohort-based training course that teaches structured problem-solving skills through hands-on projects. Participants deliver improvements to real processes they are responsible for, with peer and community support. The program also offers Civic Design coaching, journey mapping, user research facilitation, and structured problem-solving methods including human-centered design and process improvement. No financial award is provided. As of FY23, 72.4% of 29 Operations & Administrative departments were involved, with 90+ completed improvements catalyzed since January 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees who want to improve processes and systems within their work, with manager support. Includes staff across MCG departments such as OHR, Housing, Transportation, Police, and others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training program, not a financial assistance program. The program provides structured problem-solving training, Civic Design coaching, and community support to help participants improve internal processes and systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to employees of Montgomery County government only. All program projects serve MCG departments and county residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County government employee
Must be committed to making things better
Must choose to participate voluntarily
Must have manager support acknowledging the time commitment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the linked Microsoft Forms application. Cohort dates are announced in advance; upcoming cohorts are January 14–16, 2026 and February 19, 20, and 23, 2026. For Civic Design projects, interested parties may fill out a short intake form; applicants do not need to fully articulate their challenge before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Etch and Catch - Catalytic Converter Etching Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Police Department's free catalytic converter etching program, called Etch and Catch, serializes and paints residents' vehicle catalytic converters to deter theft and help recover converters if stolen. Participating body shops and vehicle service centers perform the etching at no cost to residents. Participants also receive a window cling stating that their catalytic converter has been etched.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free catalytic converter serialization and painting performed by local body shops and vehicle service centers partnered with the Police Department. Participants receive a vehicle window cling indicating their catalytic converter has been etched.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who want to deter catalytic converter theft from their vehicles.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Catalytic converter etching and serialization to deter theft and assist in recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Montgomery County residents. Contact the Community Services Officer at your local police district to inquire about upcoming etching events.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must own or have a vehicle with a catalytic converter (vehicles made after 1974 with a combustion engine)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Community Services Officer at your local police district to ask about upcoming etching events in your area. District phone numbers are listed on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) work-based learning and apprenticeship programs connect high school students — including those involved with the juvenile justice system — with real-world work experience. Students in 11th or 12th grade can participate in apprenticeships and career training opportunities tied to their school enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Work-based learning and apprenticeship placements for eligible MCPS high school students. Students gain on-the-job experience at work sites coordinated through the school district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Motivated MCPS high school students aged 16 or older who are rising juniors or seniors and have a Social Security or I-9 number and access to transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Work-based learning and apprenticeship experiences at employer work sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students currently enrolled in a Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) high school.
requirements_list: Must be a highly motivated and responsible student
Must be 16 years of age or older
Must be a rising junior or senior currently enrolled in an MCPS high school
Must possess a Social Security or I-9 number
Must be able to coordinate public or personal transportation to and from a work site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MCPS Work-Based Learning program staff or the MCPS Court Liaison for guidance. External resource links for students are provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Bone Builders is a free, volunteer-led exercise program for adults 55 and older. One-hour classes held twice per week use ankle weights, hand weights, warm-up, cool-down, and balance exercises to increase bone density, improve balance, and enhance energy and well-being. Studies show that adults 55+ who participate in a weight training program twice weekly for a year gain an average of one percent of bone density.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free twice-weekly exercise classes offered at multiple locations throughout Montgomery County. Classes are one hour each and are volunteer-led.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration takes place each program season
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents aged 55 and older who want to improve bone density, balance, and overall well-being.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in free weight training and balance exercise classes to improve bone density and reduce fracture risk from osteoporosis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must be Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must attend classes twice per week consistently to maintain place in the class
May register for only one Bone Builders class through ActiveMONTGOMERY
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through ActiveMONTGOMERY online. Registration takes place each program season. Contact the center location for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that helps adults age 50 and older and adults with disabilities find transportation options in Montgomery County. Trained staff provide information about available public and private transportation services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free service where trained staff help adults age 50 and over and adults with disabilities identify and access public and private transportation options. Available by phone Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 50 and older and adults with disabilities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance identifying and accessing transportation options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be age 50 or older, or have a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Monday–Friday between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. at 301-738-3252, or email ConnectARide@accessJCA.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Excel Beyond the Bell Elementary is a free, comprehensive after-school program for elementary school students at participating Montgomery County public schools. It provides academic enrichment and recreational activities in a structured environment. The program serves meals, uses proven curricula, and employs certified teachers and recreation professionals to support student success. Parents of participants are required to contribute two hours per month to their school community in lieu of any program fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free after-school programming for eligible elementary school students. No cost to participate. Students receive a healthy meal and access to academic and recreational enrichment activities. Space is limited to 120 students per school; priority is given to students who need academic support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elementary school students attending participating Montgomery County Public Schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: After-school academic enrichment, recreational activities, and meals for elementary school students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 18 participating elementary schools in Montgomery County, Maryland, located in Silver Spring, Gaithersburg, Germantown, Montgomery Village, and Rockville.
requirements_list: Must attend one of the designated EBB Elementary schools
Space is limited to 120 students per school
Priority given to students needing academic support
Parents/guardians must invest two hours per month in the school community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator at your child's school to register or get on the waiting list. For general information, contact the Montgomery County Recreation Youth Development Office at 240-777-8080.

structured_extraction.program_description: Excel Beyond the Bell (EBB) Middle is an after-school program for middle school students at participating Montgomery County Public Schools. It provides recreational and social activities, academic support, extracurricular programming (creative arts, STEM, sports, leadership, and career exploration), nutritious meals, and bus transportation home. The program operates four days a week from the end of the school day until 5:30 p.m. across two sessions per school year (each lasting 10–14 weeks).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free after-school programming including extracurricular activities (creative arts, STEM, sports, leadership, career exploration, health and wellness), academic support, nutritious meals, and bus transportation home. Available four days per week until 5:30 p.m. at 10 participating middle schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle school students attending partnering Montgomery County Public Schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: After-school activities including creative arts, STEM, sports, leadership, career exploration, academic support, meals, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 10 participating middle schools in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a student at one of the partnering middle schools in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Excel Beyond the Bell Middle School Program by email at rec.excelbeyondthebell@montgomerycountymd.gov, call 240-777-8080, or register via ActiveMONTGOMERY.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Recreation provides accommodations and inclusion support for individuals with disabilities so they can fully participate in recreation programs, classes, and camps. Accommodations may include interpreters, large print materials, auxiliary aids, or inclusion support partners who help individuals participate alongside peers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Inclusion support partners and accommodations (such as interpreters, large print materials, and auxiliary aids) are provided to individuals with disabilities to enable full participation in Montgomery County Recreation programs, classes, and camps. Requests should be submitted two to three weeks in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who want to participate in Montgomery County Recreation programs, classes, or camps.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accommodations and inclusion support to enable full participation in recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Register for a Montgomery County Recreation program, class, or camp
Email rec.inclusion@montgomerycountymd.gov to request accommodation
Complete the Parent Participant Profile form
Submit requests two to three weeks in advance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register for any MCR program on ActiveMONTGOMERY. 2. Email rec.inclusion@montgomerycountymd.gov to request an accommodation. 3. Complete and submit the Parent Participant Profile form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rec Assist is Montgomery County Recreation's financial assistance program that subsidizes recreation activity and membership fees for eligible county residents who receive public assistance. Approved applicants receive $400 in Rec Assist credits per eligible family member, placed on their Recreation account, which can be used toward Montgomery County Recreation classes and programs such as yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and pool passes. A minimum 20% co-payment per activity or membership is required at registration, and funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis and are valid January 1 through December 31 of the program year, or until the fund is depleted. Applications are available in both English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $400 in Rec Assist credits placed on a Recreation account per eligible family member. Funds cover Montgomery County Recreation classes and memberships costing $25 or more, including yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and pool passes. A minimum 20% co-payment is required per activity or membership at registration. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis and are valid through December 31 of the program year or until depleted. Cannot be used for facility rentals, daily pool admissions, gift cards, activity fees under $25, supplemental fees, or aquatic merchandise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who currently receive public assistance from qualifying programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, Temporary Cash Assistance, Supplemental Security Income, Housing Assistance from a Shelter, FARMS, Care for Kids, Maryland Energy Assistance, Heat and Eat (H-EAT), or students attending a Montgomery County Public School participating in the Community Eligibility Provision. Applications are available in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Montgomery County Recreation classes and programs (e.g., yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance), annual pool passes, and 12-visit swim punch passes. Funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more. Cannot be used for sports league fees, facility rentals, daily pool admissions, gift cards, activity fees under $25, supplemental fees (deposits, withdrawals, materials, late pickup fees), swimwear purchases, past-due balances, or account modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident

Must currently receive public assistance from one of the following: FARMS, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Supplemental Security Income, Housing Assistance from a Shelter, SNAP, Maryland Medicaid, Care for Kids, Maryland Energy Assistance, WIC, or Heat and Eat (H-EAT)
OR must be a student enrolled in a Montgomery County Public School participating in the Community Eligibility Provision (proof of enrollment required)
Only one type of assistance per applicant may be used to qualify
Must submit required original supporting documents (member cards such as SNAP, WIC, and insurance cards are not accepted)
Minimum 20% co-payment per activity or membership is required at time of registration
Funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more
May qualify only once per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online by completing the Rec Assist online application form at www.mocorec.com/recassist, attaching required supporting documents, and submitting. Alternatively, download a paper application (available in English and Spanish) and mail or bring it in person to Montgomery County Recreation, Attention: Rec Assist, 2425 Reedie Drive, 10th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. Applications are processed within 10 business days of receipt, and approved funds are placed on the applicant's Recreation account. For questions before submission, call 240-777-6840.

structured_extraction.program_description: RecXtra is an after-school program run by Montgomery County Recreation in partnership with several middle schools in Montgomery County. It offers students activities not covered during the school day — such as sports, arts, cooking, dance, chess, yoga, theatre, and mentoring — helping them build skills, explore new interests, and connect with peers and teachers outside the classroom.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized after-school activities offered three days a week (Tuesday–Thursday) at partnering middle schools. Activities vary by school and are coordinated by an After School Activities Coordinator (ASAC) at each site.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Carlos Falcon, Malcolm Ayers, Lyrisd Charles (Recreation Specialists)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle school students attending partnering Montgomery County schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: After-school enrichment activities including sports, arts, babysitting instruction, chess, improv theatre, sewing, dancing, tennis, weight training, poms, cooking, yoga, and mentoring
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at specific partnering middle schools in Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Must be a student at a partnering RecXtra middle school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your school's After School Activities Coordinator (ASAC) to confirm program details and register. You may also contact Montgomery County Recreation specialists directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Recreation provides free curb-to-curb and fixed-route transportation to seniors at specific senior centers and Active Adult Program locations across Montgomery County. The service helps residents age 55 and over get to and from participating centers within the designated service area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free curb-to-curb and fixed-route transportation service (Monday through Friday) to participating senior centers (Damascus, Holiday Park, Long Branch, North Potomac, Schweinhaut, White Oak) and Active Adult Programs in Germantown. Service is available to County residents age 55 and over who live within the service area. Wheelchair and scooter accommodation with loading/unloading assistance available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents age 55 and over living within the service area of participating senior centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Curb-to-curb and fixed-route transportation (Monday through Friday) to and from participating senior centers and Active Adult Program locations, with wheelchair/scooter accommodation and loading/unloading assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County within the service area of participating senior centers (Damascus, Holiday Park, Long Branch, North Potomac, Schweinhaut, White Oak).

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Nutrition Program / Congregate Meal Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Recreation, in partnership with the Department of Health and Human Services Aging and Disability Services, provides nutritious hot lunch meals in congregate (group) settings at senior centers and recreation centers across Montgomery County. Meals meet federal dietary standards and are suitable for those with diabetes, heart disease, or hypertension. Specialized meal options—including Kosher, Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese meals—are available at certain sites. Monthly menus offer three daily options (hot, cold, and vegetarian); all meals include milk or yogurt and whole grain rolls/pastas unless otherwise noted. Adults age 60 and over pay a voluntary suggested donation ($3 recommended per meal) rather than the full meal price. Individuals under 60 may participate only if they are a spouse of an active participant, an SNP volunteer (minimum 2 hours/month), or a disabled adult child/person with disabilities living with or in the same building as an active registered participant, and pay the full meal price. The program also includes nutrition education (lectures, food demonstrations, cooking classes), nutrition screening and counseling, and connects participants to Meals on Wheels for home-delivered meals. Advance meal reservations are required by 10 AM the day prior per the monthly menu schedule, and some locations maintain a standby or waiting list for last-minute availability. The program operates at 13 meal sites throughout Montgomery County, including Bethesda, Chevy Chase, Colesville, Damascus, Gaithersburg, Germantown, Rockville, Silver Spring, Takoma Park, and Wheaton. Authorized under the Older Americans Act (Public Law 109-365).

structured_extraction.program_name: Live Healthy – Health, Dental and Prescription Discounts
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County and Montgomery County partner with the National Association of Counties (NACo) through the Live Healthy initiative to offer residents discounts on prescriptions, dental care, vision, hearing, and diabetes supplies. The prescription discount card is free and covers brand-name and generic drugs at participating pharmacies with no claim forms, no annual fee, and no usage limits. Cards are accepted at over 68,000 retail pharmacies nationwide. Low-fee Dental and Health Discount plans provide savings of 15–50% on dental procedures and up to 75% off vision, hearing aids, and other health products and services through a network of over 110,000 providers nationwide. These programs are not insurance but provide immediate access to providers with no waiting periods, no deductibles, and no benefit maximums.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free prescription discount cards cover all commonly prescribed brand-name and generic drugs with an average 24% savings on retail price, no claim forms, no annual fee, and no usage limits. Cards are accepted at over 68,000 retail pharmacies nationwide. Dental Discount plans cost $6.95/month per individual or $8.95/month per family ($69/year individual, $79/year family), providing 15–50% off dental procedures through a network of over 110,000 providers nationwide, with no deductibles or benefit maximums. Health Discount plans cost $6.95/month per individual or $8.95/month per family, providing 15–75% discounts on vision (glasses, exams, contact lenses, LASIK), hearing aids and screenings, diabetic supplies, and prepaid lab tests through a national network of providers. Combined Health + Dental plans are available for $13.90/month (individual) or $17.90/month (family). These programs are not insurance; members pay the full discounted cost out-of-pocket and are not eligible for Medicaid/Medicare reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund (AHOF) provides short-term loan financing to developers seeking to acquire and preserve affordable multifamily rental housing properties in Montgomery County that are at risk of losing affordability. The fund enables developers to bid competitively on such properties, allowing current renters to remain in their communities at affordable rents. The fund has a dedicated pool of $14 million in revolving County funds, matched at least 3:1 with private lending, and is managed in partnership with the National Housing Trust Community Development Fund (NHTCDF), which coordinates applications and arranges private capital alongside County funds. Initial funding has been distributed and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as loans are repaid and the fund is replenished. Final loan approvals are issued via a conditional commitment letter from DHCA. Loan terms are available via the NHTCDF Term Sheet on their webpage.

Once an application is reviewed by DHCA's partner underwriter, DHCA receives a recommendation package; the DHCA Director reviews and approves, modifies, or rejects the recommendation. Final approval is issued via a conditional commitment letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: NeighborWorks Capital provides flexible, fixed-rate loan capital to members of the NeighborWorks America network for community development projects. Loan types include acquisition, predevelopment, construction, permanent financing, and enterprise capital loans to help organizations build affordable housing and strengthen communities. NeighborWorks Capital has deployed over $600 million in funding to the NeighborWorks America network.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitively priced, flexible, fixed-rate loans with patient terms. Loan types and typical sizes: Acquisition loans up to $10–$15MM (36-month term for land/vacant; 60-month for operating property; LTV up to 85% unimproved/95% operating; $1,000 application + 1.00–1.50% origination fee) for purchasing vacant land or existing properties for residential/commercial development, affordability preservation, or redevelopment. Predevelopment loans up to $3MM (term or revolving, up to 36 months; unsecured up to $1MM; $1,000 application + 1.50–2.00% origination fee) for design, due diligence, engineering, studies, legal, and soft costs. Construction loans up to $20MM (36-month single-project; 60-month multi-phase; first mortgage/deed of trust; max 85% LTV/LTC; $1,000 application + 1.25–2.00% origination + third-party costs) for new construction or significant rehabilitation/renovation of apartment, condominium, single-family, commercial, or mixed-use projects; progress-based draws via inspection/requisition. Permanent loans up to $5MM (8–10 years standard; 18 years for LIHTC; max 95% LTV; DCR min 1.15x first position/1.05x second position) for refinancing or forward commitments on multifamily rental, LIHTC, or mixed-use properties. Enterprise Capital loans up to $2MM (3–5 years; term or revolving; unsecured up to $2MM; $1,000 application + 1.00–1.50% origination fee) for organizational liquidity, startup/growth of new business lines, geographic expansion, and early-period real estate development costs. Larger amounts available with participants. All rates fixed; current rates by phone inquiry. Terms subject to underwriting and approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reinvest Baltimore Down Payment Assistance (DPA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore (NHS Baltimore) administers the Reinvest Baltimore Down Payment Assistance Program, which provides forgivable and deferred loans to qualified homebuyers purchasing properties within designated BVRI areas in Baltimore City. The program is part of the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI) and UPLIFT-funded redevelopment efforts, aiming to increase homeownership opportunities in neighborhoods benefiting from vacant property redevelopment by eliminating upfront cost barriers. NHS housing counselors work one-on-one with buyers to identify programs matching their income, location, and homeownership goals. NHS operates two direct DPA programs: the Reinvest Baltimore DPA (forgivable loan up to $20,000 at 0% interest, with 20% of principal forgiven annually over five years, requires primary residence occupancy and a fixed-rate mortgage) and the BRNI Down Payment Assistance ($10,000 deferred loan at 0% interest, repayable upon sale or refinance). NHS also helps buyers access and combine additional city, state, and federal programs to reach up to $50,000 in total down payment and closing cost assistance. No household income restrictions apply, and the program is not limited to first-time homebuyers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homebuyer Education and One-on-One Counseling (Homebuyers Education Workshop)
structured_extraction.program_description: Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore (NHS) offers a HUD-certified homebuyer education program and individual counseling sessions to help Baltimore City residents prepare for homeownership. The education workshop teaches first-time and repeat homebuyers everything they need to know before purchasing a home, including qualifying for down payment assistance, finding a home within budget, real estate and mortgage terms, choosing a lender, credit health, budgeting, mortgage options, home maintenance, insurance, property taxes, and the closing process. The workshop is available in four formats: a one-day six-hour virtual Saturday session (9 AM–3 PM), two three-hour virtual Thursday evening sessions (5–8 PM), an online self-paced course, or a one-day six-hour in-person session. Upon completing the education component, participants receive a HUD-approved Homebuyer Education Certificate of completion accepted by lenders and required by most down payment assistance programs. Following the education workshop, participants can meet one-on-one with a HUD-certified and NeighborWorks-certified housing counselor who reviews credit, savings, and financial readiness; creates a personalized homeownership action plan; explores mortgage and loan options; connects clients with local down payment assistance programs; and helps prepare paperwork for pre-approval and closing.

Participants receive a HUD-approved Homebuyer Education Certificate of completion that satisfies education requirements for many down payment assistance and loan programs. Free one-on-one housing counseling sessions with a HUD-certified and NeighborWorks-certified counselor are also available; clients receive a personalized homeownership action plan and guidance on credit review, mortgage options, down payment assistance programs, and closing preparation.

structured_extraction.program_description: NHS Mortgage is an affordable home loan program offered by Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) of Baltimore, designed for Baltimore residents seeking to purchase a home. It provides flexible mortgage financing with low down payment options, competitive interest rates, reduced or waived PMI (Private Mortgage Insurance), lower closing costs, and access to grants and deferred loans. The loan is paired with NHS's full suite of services — including homebuyer education workshops, financial coaching, and access to rehabilitated homes for sale — to provide a comprehensive, end-to-end homebuying experience. Licensed loan officers provide personalized, one-on-one guidance throughout the homebuying process. Down payment assistance is also available to reduce upfront costs at closing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rehab Home Improvement Loan (Rapid Home Improvement Program / RHIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A home improvement loan program operated by Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore (NHS) that provides Baltimore City homeowners with access to affordable financing for home repair and renovation projects. The program offers two tracks: a Rapid Rehab track providing loans up to $20,000 at a fixed 6% interest rate for up to 10 years, with no income limit, no home equity or appraisal required, and funds available within approximately 30 days of applying — well-suited for new homeowners or those with urgent repair needs (minimum credit score of 680, continuously employed for one year, must have a bank account, property and water bills must be current); and a standard Rehab track providing loans up to $30,000 at 0%–6% interest for up to 20 years for major home repairs and renovations (such as roofing, heating, plumbing, or electrical work) available to homeowners earning up to 120% of Area Median Income (AMI), with payments potentially deferred until the home is sold based on ability to repay, and with NHS counselors providing hands-on support to help borrowers review contractor bids and manage project timelines. Both tracks serve Baltimore City homeowners seeking financing for repairs affecting safety, habitability, essential home systems, energy efficiency, or broader renovation goals. Neither track requires the homeowner to refinance their existing mortgage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rapid Rehab track: loans up to $20,000 at a fixed 6% interest rate, repayable over up to 10 years; no income limit, no home equity or appraisal required, funds disbursed within approximately 30 days; minimum credit score of 680, continuously employed for one year, must have a bank account, property and water bills must be current; monthly ACH payment optional; borrower manages own contractors and timelines. Standard Rehab track: loans up to $30,000 at 0%–6% interest, repayable over up to 20 years, for major renovations including roofing, heating, plumbing, and electrical work; available to homeowners earning up to 120% AMI; repayment schedule based on ability to repay, with payments potentially deferred until the home is sold; NHS counselors provide personalized support, help review contractor bids, and keep projects on track. Neither track requires a mortgage refinance.

The standard Rehab track is available to homeowners earning up to 120% of AMI. The Rapid Rehab track requires a credit score of 680 or above and one year of continuous employment.
