structured_extraction.program_name: Facility Fee Assistance Program (FFAP) – Community Use of Public Facility Subsidy
structured_extraction.program_description: The Facility Fee Assistance Program (FFAP), also referred to as the Facility Use Subsidy Program (FUSP), is a subsidy program administered by the Office of Community Use of Public Facilities (CUPF) in Montgomery County, Maryland. It helps Maryland-based nonprofit organizations cover the cost of using public facilities — such as county school rooms (Title I or high-FARMS preferred), public libraries, county office buildings, Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and the District 3 Police Station — to deliver free or low-cost programs that directly benefit vulnerable or at-risk youth (ages 12–18) or low-income individuals and their families in Montgomery County. The maximum annual award is $3,000 per organization per fiscal year (FY24), though historically the maximum has been as high as $5,400 (FY18). The subsidy is sufficient to fund an afterschool program two or three times per week for a full school year or an ongoing Saturday program. Awards are made until funds run out each fiscal year, and organizations may submit multiple applications per year up to the annual maximum. Subsidies do not cover gyms, stadium fields, auditoriums, kitchens, equipment, or MCPS support staff.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidizes facility room rental costs at eligible public spaces including county school classrooms (Title I or high-FARMS preferred), public library meeting rooms, county office buildings, Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and the District 3 Police Station. The maximum award per organization is $3,000 per fiscal year (FY24; historically up to $5,400 in FY18), sufficient to fund an afterschool program two or three times per week for a full school year or an ongoing Saturday program. Organizations may submit multiple applications per year up to the annual maximum. Awards are made on a rolling basis until funds run out each fiscal year. Subsidies do not cover gyms, stadium fields, auditoriums, kitchens, equipment, or MCPS support staff. Organizations must pay a portion of any remaining facility charges themselves.

Eligible activities include food and toy distribution, language classes, educational programs, youth development programs, and job-seeking skills programs. Allow at least 30 days for processing. 4. After a room use permit is approved through ActiveMONTGOMERY.org, contact CUPF. 5. Applications are reviewed for completeness, then forwarded to a review committee, with final determination made by the CUPF Director. 6. After program completion, submit a report to CUPF on the number of individuals served.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Food Recovery Network Coordination Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grant funding to support the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network (FRN) to reduce food waste and redirect surplus food to people in need. The program funds a single non-profit organization to coordinate the FRN, improving operational efficiency for food recovery operators, leveraging new resources, and boosting collaboration across the network. The program also supports projects that use collaborative, shared-use approaches to build capacity in the food recovery network, establish new donor recovery relationships, increase access to higher-value products, and reduce the climate impacts of food recovery and assistance. A previous award of $25,000 was made to the Montgomery County Food Council to coordinate the Food Recovery Network; in FY25, $306,000 was awarded to four organizations for food recovery network infrastructure projects. For FY26, a $125,000 competitive grant is awarded for coordination efforts.
structured_extraction.agency: Office of Food Systems Resilience, Montgomery County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for food recovery network coordination activities in Montgomery County. A single $125,000 competitive grant is awarded for FY26 to support the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network. In FY25, $306,000 was awarded to four organizations for food recovery network infrastructure projects. The performance period runs on/about September 30, 2025 through September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations that can coordinate or operate food recovery and assistance networks in Montgomery County, such as the Montgomery County Food Council. The coordinating organization must not directly distribute food but rather coordinate community partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, implement, and coordinate a centralized Food Recovery Network; build food recovery network capacity; establish new donor recovery relationships; increase access to higher-value products; improve operational efficiency; leverage new resources; boost collaboration among food recovery operators; provide technical assistance to member organizations; optimize logistics; expand donor recruitment; and reduce climate impacts of food recovery and assistance in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County, MD (or, for national/regional organizations, location must be in Montgomery County). All activities and expenditures must focus in Montgomery County, though food sources may be outside the County. Working knowledge of the food recovery landscape in the DMV region is required. Network partnerships may extend beyond the county.
requirements_list: Projects must reflect collaborative, shared-use approaches
Must build capacity of the overall food recovery network
Must establish new donor recovery relationships or increase access to higher-value products
Must reduce climate impacts of food recovery and assistance
Applicant must complete Certifications, Acknowledgements, and Assurances in online grant portal

Applicant must disclose any current Montgomery County Government employees or contractors on staff or board (Montgomery College, Montgomery County Public Schools, and WorkSource Montgomery are excluded from this definition)
Must show proof of insurance prior to fund receipt
Must comply with Title VII Civil Rights Act of 1964
Must comply with Maryland Public Information Act (Md. Code Ann., State Gov't., §10-611 through -628)
Funds must be spent after contract finalization and Notice to Proceed
Subject to audit for 3 years post-final payment
Applicant must notify County of any material changes or operational cessation
Organization must be in Good Standing with Maryland SDAT at application review, grant agreement finalization, and an additional checkpoint
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County, MD (or, for national/regional organizations, location must be in Montgomery County)
Eligible organization must be a non-profit and must coordinate community partners rather than directly distributing food
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Program Summary and Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and information session slide deck available at the program website, then apply through the eCivis online grants portal. The application includes sections covering: Applicant Information, Applicant Background, Project Scope of Work, Project Budget, Budget Narrative, Performance History, Performance Reporting Requirements, and Supporting Documentation. All proposals must use the provided budget template (FY26-FRC-Budget-Template.xlsx). Required attachments include: IRS 990 Form (or exemption explanation), Project Scope PDF (answering five narrative questions with specific word limits), Budget Narrative PDF, Performance History PDF, Performance Reporting attachment, and surveys/data collection strategies. Applications undergo a three-stage review: (1) OGM Administrative Review for Montgomery County eligibility conditions, completeness, and minimum standards; (2) Programmatic Eligibility Review; and (3) final evaluation. The application window was July 21, 2025 – August 18, 2025. An information session was held July 29, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Energy Initiative Loan Program provides low-interest financing to help Baltimore City nonprofit organizations and for-profit small businesses implement energy-saving building improvements. Improvements can include lighting, HVAC, building envelope upgrades, domestic hot water systems, ENERGY STAR equipment, distributed generation, and other efficiency measures that lower utility bills, improve comfort, and reduce energy waste. The program was launched by the City of Baltimore in 2014, is funded through the Maryland Public Service Commission's Customer Service Investment Fund, and is administered in partnership with Reinvestment Fund (handling loans of $150,000 and above) and Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. (handling loans under $150,000).
structured_extraction.agency: Office of Sustainable Energy, Baltimore City (with partners Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. and The Reinvestment Fund)
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans from under $150,000 up to $2,000,000, financing up to 90% of eligible energy project costs. For loans under $150,000, Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. is the lender with interest rates ranging from 3.0% to 4.0% and terms up to 15 years. For loans of $150,000 and above, Reinvestment Fund provides financing at a blended rate (BEI capital component priced at 4.0%, blended with other Reinvestment Fund capital); loan terms are typically up to 7 years. Nonprofits may use up to 20% of the loan amount (capped at $50,000) for certain non-energy improvements that enable the energy upgrades.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and for-profit small businesses located in eligible areas of Baltimore City seeking to implement energy-saving building improvements. Tier 2 borrowers include for-profit small-business real estate developers working in eligible geographies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving building improvements including building envelope upgrades, HVAC and controls, lighting and controls, domestic hot water systems, boiler and hot water heater replacement, efficient kitchen equipment, plumbing, plug loads, ENERGY STAR equipment, and distributed generation (e.g., solar PV, combined heat-and-power) when part of a broader energy project. Covers retrofits of existing buildings, gut rehab projects, and new construction energy improvements. Nonprofits may also use up to 20% of the loan (capped at $50,000) for certain non-energy improvements tied to enabling the energy upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Baltimore City in an eligible area — specifically in New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC)-eligible census tracts or Baltimore Main Streets Districts. A mapping tool is available to confirm whether a building's location qualifies.
requirements_list: Project must be located in Baltimore City within an NMTC-eligible census tract or a Baltimore Main Streets District
Must be a nonprofit organization, for-profit small business, or real estate project developer
Tier 1 nonprofits must provide at least 50% of their services to families with incomes at or below 80% of area median income
Tier 1 for-profit businesses must meet the SBA definition of 'small business' (tangible net worth <$15M, average net income <$5M after taxes over 2 years) and be located in an eligible geography

Tier 2 borrowers (nonprofit or for-profit small-business real estate developers) must be in an eligible geography and their projects must provide new neighborhood amenities, address widespread vacancy, or include affordability commitments (at least 50% of housing serving residents at or below 80% of AMI)
Retrofit projects (Extensive Retrofits) must achieve a minimum 15% whole-building energy savings (BTU basis, weather-normalized)
For Gut Rehab (Low-Rise Residential): meet International Residential Code 2012 Edition
For Gut Rehab (Other Buildings): meet International Green Construction Code 2012 Edition
For New Construction (Tier 1): 10% savings vs. applicable code; for New Construction (Tier 2): 15% savings vs. applicable code
Energy audit must be ASHRAE Level II (or comparable) by BPI-certified auditor
Energy modeling software must be DOE-2.2, EnergyPlus, eQuest, HAP, Trace, or RESNET HERS audit
Code-based modeling standards apply to substantial rehabilitation/reconstruction and new construction projects
Qualifying measures include building envelope, HVAC, lighting, hot water, plumbing, and plug loads
Loan recipients must participate in ongoing impact tracking including benchmarking via ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and providing building energy consumption data for 24 months post-implementation
Non-discrimination, MBE/WBE compliance, and insurance compliance per City of Baltimore contracting requirements
Technical review by contracted energy engineering firm required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Program Guidelines and Instructions, then complete and email the Initial Financing Request Form to BEI@reinvestment.com (or LoanRequests@EnergyLoansBEI.org). Reinvestment Fund staff will follow up to discuss eligibility, project readiness, and next steps. Program documents and forms are available at reinvestment.com/BEILoans and www.EnergyLoansBEI.org. For small projects under $150,000, contact Healthy Neighborhoods Inc.; for large projects $150,000 and above, contact The Reinvestment Fund.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Access to Banking Act – Assessment Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions can earn a credit against their annual regulatory assessment fee by opening new branches or keeping existing branches open in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. The credit is designed to incentivize financial institutions to maintain and expand their presence in underserved areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OFR), Maryland Department of Labor
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against the annual regulatory assessment fee charged to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions. The credit is earned by establishing new (de novo) branches or retaining existing branches in low-to-moderate income communities. Specific credit amounts and application details are forthcoming — subscribe to OFR emails for updates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions that operate or plan to open branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of annual regulatory assessment fees for maintaining or establishing branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions operating in low-to-moderate income communities.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union
Must operate a new (de novo) branch or retain an existing branch in a low-to-moderate income (LMI) community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Subscribe to OFR emails for updates on how to apply for and earn the assessment credit. Applications should be sent via email to ofr.venturefund@maryland.gov. Contact Stephen Clampett with questions about filing an application or paying an application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venture fund established under the Maryland Access to Banking Act that invests in financial technology (fintech) firms developing products and innovations to improve access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. The fund also makes those innovations available to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions to help them better serve LMI communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OFR), Maryland Department of Labor
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MCIV Fund is seeded with up to $2,500,000 in initial equity capital from OFR's Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund. Through June 30, 2028, the Commissioner of Financial Regulation may match investments made by Maryland state-chartered banks or credit unions in an amount equal to the assessment credit those institutions earned. The fund invests in fintech firms developing financial innovations for LMI communities and promotes those innovations to Maryland state-chartered depository institutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fintech firms developing financial products to improve access to capital and services in low-to-moderate income communities, and Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions interested in participating in the fund.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in fintech firms developing financial innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in LMI communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; focused on serving low-to-moderate income communities in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fintech firms must be developing financial products or innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in LMI communities
Maryland state-chartered depository institutions may participate and have their investments matched up to the amount of assessment credit earned
Matching investment opportunity available through June 30, 2028
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Subscribe to OFR emails for updates on next steps, eligibility criteria, and the application process. Applications and inquiries can be directed to ofr.venturefund@maryland.gov. Contact Stephen Clampett, Assistant Commissioner, at 410-230-6104 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of the State's Attorney for Prince George's County seeks community-based organizations and service providers to design and deliver a program that reduces student truancy and chronic absenteeism among youth ages 12–18. Partners will help build a coordinated framework of services addressing immediate barriers to school attendance and underlying causes of absenteeism, using evidence-based and culturally responsive strategies.

Multiple partners may be funded across categories based on need, capacity, and alignment with program goals.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivering services across focus areas including academic mentoring, family engagement and outreach, behavioral enrichment, wraparound services (workforce development and mental health support), culturally responsive interventions, technology solutions for attendance tracking, and re-engagement strategies for at-risk youth.

Must be able to collect and report data on outcomes
Must demonstrate track record of working with at-risk youth and families
Must demonstrate ability to collaborate with schools and community partners
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prepare a single PDF Expression of Interest (EOI) and attach any supporting materials as separate files. Email the submission to communitysao@co.pg.md.us with the subject line: 'SAO-PGC Truancy and Absenteeism Reduction Program – EOI Submission' by October 9, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Victims' Fund provides financial reimbursement to crime victims in Anne Arundel County who have no other means of replacing what was damaged or stolen. It covers emergency needs directly linked to the crime, such as emergency repairs to ensure safety (doors, windows, locks), insurance deductibles, and replacement or repair of items needed to resume school or work.
structured_extraction.agency: Office of the State's Attorney, Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for emergency needs directly caused by a crime. Covers emergency repairs (doors, windows, locks), all or part of an insurance deductible, and replacement or repair of items necessary to resume school or work. Does not ordinarily cover counseling, funeral, medical, or dental expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of crime in Anne Arundel County who have no other means of replacing damaged or stolen property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency repairs to ensure safety (doors, windows, locks); insurance deductibles; replacement or repair of items needed to resume school or work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have been the victim of a crime in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must have been the victim of a crime in Anne Arundel County
Must meet criteria established by the Victims' Fund Committee
Must report the crime to police or the Commissioner's office within 48 hours
Must contact the Fund Coordinator and provide the date of incident, officer's name, and police report number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Report the crime to police or the Commissioner's office within 48 hours. 2. Contact Fund Coordinator Joan Stammnitz at (410) 222-6165 with the date of incident, officer's name, and police report number.

structured_extraction.program_name: Family Stability Programs (Homelessness Prevention, Shelter Diversion, and Operation: Open Doors)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership for Children, Youth and Families provides assistance to families in Anne Arundel County who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Services include: Homelessness Prevention (intensive case management for families with school-aged children at risk of eviction or homelessness, with optional family coaching through a 2 Generation Project); Shelter Diversion/Rapid Rehousing (intensive case management for families with school-aged children who are experiencing homelessness, including those in non-traditional settings, shelters, hotels, or doubled up with others); and Operation: Open Doors (a collaboration with Anne Arundel County Public Schools that helps eligible families apply for Section 8 housing vouchers and provides ongoing case management to support housing stability and self-sufficiency).

Eligibility assessed by Intake Coordinator via Resource Line

structured_extraction.program_description: The Heritage Fund is a cooperative effort between Preservation Maryland and the Maryland Historical Trust. It provides grants to non-profit organizations and government instrumentalities for historic preservation projects, including direct assistance for protecting endangered cultural resources and support for innovative education projects. Historic sites, buildings, districts, objects, and archaeological resources are all eligible. Projects fall into three categories: education and research, planning and feasibility, and repair and rehabilitation. Applicants must be able to complete their project within one calendar year of receiving the award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance for protection of endangered cultural resources and innovative education projects. Grant funds may be used for education and research, planning and feasibility studies, and repair and rehabilitation of historic sites, buildings, districts, objects, and archaeological resources. Private property owners are not eligible. Applicants must demonstrate the ability to complete the project within one calendar year of the award. Extensions and modification requests are reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and instrumentalities of state, county, and municipal governments (local jurisdictions) in Maryland engaged in historic preservation projects involving tangible cultural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and research, planning and feasibility studies, and repair and rehabilitation of historic sites, buildings, districts, objects, and archaeological resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must involve a tangible cultural resource located in Maryland.

Private property owners are not eligible
Applicants must demonstrate ability to complete the project within one calendar year of receiving the award

Eligible project categories: education and research, planning and feasibility, or repair and rehabilitation

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home nursing assessments and monitoring visits to support individuals receiving personal care and community-based services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Mentor-Protégé Program is a local business development program that pairs large businesses (mentors) with county-based small businesses or minority business enterprises (protégés) through formal agreements. The goal is to enhance the protégé's capabilities and ability to compete for prime-level contracting opportunities. Protégés receive technical assistance, management assistance, financial assistance, business development support, and trade education over a 24-month period.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, technical and management assistance, financial assistance, and trade education to improve competitiveness for government contracting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be county-based small businesses or county-based Minority Business Enterprises located in Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the program. The Mentor-Protégé Committee will review the application within 14 business days of receipt. County solicitations with Mentor-Protégé Program requirements are posted at pgcbusinesshighway.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Children in Need of Support (CINS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A juvenile justice diversion program for youth ages 13-18 in Prince George's County. The program aims to interrupt pre-delinquent behavior patterns and redirect youth to prevent them from entering or progressing further into the juvenile justice system. It uses an evidence-based assessment to identify family strengths and needs, develops a comprehensive Family Service Plan, and assigns a case manager to connect families to community-based services. The program also includes an 8-week component for both parents and youth covering parenting skills, brain development, communication, conflict resolution, and positive youth development.

Program targets pre-delinquent or at-risk youth to divert them from the juvenile justice system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-265-8446 for assistance or more information about the CINS Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides support services to help formerly incarcerated individuals successfully reintegrate into Prince George's County. The program connects returning citizens who were incarcerated in local, state, or federal facilities with essential resources needed to become productive citizens, operating through a One Stop Re-Entry Center model. Participants are linked to housing, health and human services, employment opportunities, GED support and testing preparation, government ID and birth certificate assistance, expungement guidance, and federal bonding programs. Individuals can be referred by the Department of Corrections, other correctional facilities, government agencies, community nonprofits, or can self-refer. A Reentry Resource Guide details available resources.

An online Re-Entry Application is also available on the county website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project HIRE is an apprenticeship program that provides individuals with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities, ages 18 to 25, a paid job training experience within a Prince George's County Government agency. Participants are placed with a host county agency for one year to enhance current skills, learn new skills, and gain on-the-job work experience.

During the placement, they work Monday through Friday for up to 8 hours per day. Employers who hire participants may also be eligible for the Maryland Disability Employment Tax Credit (MDETC).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job work experience and skills development at a Prince George's County Government host agency for up to one year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Senior Nutrition Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Nutrition Program promotes meal services, nutrition education, and social, recreational, and educational opportunities for older adults in Prince George's County. It has two components: (1) Home-Delivered Meals — hot meals delivered five days a week to homebound older adults to help them remain in their own homes; and (2) Congregate Meals — hot nutritious meals served at senior centers, religious facilities, senior housing, and community centers, with transportation available to meal sites and access to recreational and educational programs. Each meal meets at least one-third of the Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults and follows the Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Diabetes Prevention Program (NDPP) / Prevent Type 2 Diabetes (Prediabetes Classes)
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County Health Department offers a CDC-recognized structured lifestyle change program for adults at high risk of developing Type 2 diabetes. The program is available as both a free 26-week format (PreventionLink's NDPP) and a year-long fee-for-service format delivered in three phases: weekly sessions (Phase 1), bi-weekly sessions (Phase 2), and sessions every four weeks (Phase 3). Both formats are offered online (telehealth/virtual), and the NDPP version is also available in-person. Led by trained lifestyle coaches in a group setting, the program covers healthy eating, physical activity, weight management (targeting 5–7% body weight loss), stress management, and motivation to prevent or delay the onset of Type 2 diabetes. Research shows participation can cut the risk of Type 2 diabetes by 50% and lower the risk of heart attack and stroke. Through PreventionLink, participants may also receive one-on-one support from a community health worker, connections to medication assistance programs, personalized medication reviews and schedules, and regular progress reports to referring healthcare providers. The County Health Department is a Medicare/Medicaid supplier with agreements with commercial health plans and managed care organizations, so eligible health plan members may access the program at no or low cost through self-referral. A PreventionLink track is also available at no cost for qualifying Southern Maryland residents. The telehealth delivery option is particularly beneficial for residents who find attending in-person sessions challenging.

Through PreventionLink, participants also receive lifestyle coaching, health education, one-on-one community health worker support, connections to medication assistance programs, personalized medication reviews and schedules, and regular progress reports to referring healthcare providers. structured_extraction.program_name: County Right of First Refusal Program: Multifamily Rental Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The Right of First Refusal (ROFR) Program requires owners of multifamily rental properties with 20 or more units to notify the Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) when they enter into a contract to sell their property. DHCD may then exercise its right to purchase the property — or assign that right to a third party — to preserve affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households in the county. The program also applies to transfers of majority interest within a 12-month period and leases longer than 7 years. Property owners and prospective buyers may also request an exception to the county's ROFR by executing a written agreement with DHCD before entering into a contract of sale.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD may purchase qualifying multifamily rental properties (20+ units) or assign its right to purchase to a third party in order to preserve affordable housing. Financing is provided through a subordinate loan at 0% interest, up to $3,000,000 (with exceptions at Department discretion), with a term of up to 40 years. LTV up to 110% (120% for high public purpose properties). Prepayment is allowed after year 20 with a 10% penalty. No repayments of principal or interest on the ROFR Loan are due prior to December 31, 2026. The program is funded in part by ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act of 2021) funds. The program has preserved over 2,991 housing units since 2020. Detailed terms are outlined in the ROFR Preservation Fund Term Sheet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of multifamily rental facilities with 20 or more units located in Prince George's County who are selling their property, transferring majority interest, or entering into leases longer than 7 years; prospective buyers seeking an exception to the county's right of first refusal.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All areas of Prince George's County, Maryland (per CR-51-2015, effective November 6, 2015). Properties located within the boundaries of a municipality must comply with municipal approval requirements under the ROFR Code (Section 13-1110 et seq. of Prince George's County Code); municipal approval is deemed granted if not provided within 180 days.

The County Executive or Department reports annually to the County Council by December 31 each year on prior fiscal year ROFR activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible tenants and landlords in Prince George's County affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Tenants at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI) who are having difficulty paying rent may apply directly. Tenants above 50% AMI must have an active eviction proceeding (court summons, court judgment, Warrant of Restitution, or Warrant for Possession); those at or below 50% AMI do not need eviction paperwork but must submit all available documentation. Assistance may also cover utility bills, with payments made to landlords or directly to tenants in some cases. Landlords may also apply on behalf of eligible tenants if the rental property is in a qualifying census tract or if the landlord applied in Fall 2020 without receiving assistance. Approved funds are paid directly to landlords to cover unpaid rent for eligible households; cumulative assistance is capped at 18 months, and approval does not guarantee the full requested amount.

The amount approved is determined by DHCD based on application review and funding availability. Approval does not guarantee the full requested amount.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tenants may submit an online application at erentalassistance.princegeorgescountymd.gov along with required residency and income verification documents, and work with their landlord to gather and submit additional required documents such as a rent ledger, rental license, W-9, and assistance agreement forms. Landlords may submit an application through the DHCD portal along with required documentation for both the landlord and tenant. DHCD reviews applications and contacts applicants by email regarding discrepancies or missing information. If approved, DHCD emails a notice of approval with the approved assistance amount; both landlord and tenant must accept the final approved amount before payment is issued. DHCD may request additional information to validate the application. For questions, call the ERAP Call Center at (301) 883-6504, then press option 9. Note: As of September 2023, the application portal was marked closed; no reopening date has been announced.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Investment Trust Fund provides workforce housing gap financing to support the development, rehabilitation, and preservation of workforce and affordable housing in Prince George's County. The fund targets households earning up to 120% of the area median income (AMI), with HITF-assisted units required to be affordable to households at 80% AMI or below. It encourages non-profit and for-profit developers to produce and rehabilitate housing, and assists Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) in creating housing opportunities for households of limited income. The program is codified in Prince George's County Code, Sections 10-294 through 10-300, with a statutorily mandated minimum of $10 million allocated annually from County recordation taxes.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided primarily in the form of subordinate interest-bearing loans. Construction phase loans carry a 0% interest rate; permanent loans carry a 2% simple interest rate with a 40-year amortization. The maximum loan amount is up to $2,500,000 per project (exceptions approved by Director). Loans are subordinate to senior financing and repaid from surplus cash flow after senior debt service. Predevelopment grants may also be provided at Director discretion. The amount of assistance is determined on a project-by-project basis throughout the fiscal year. A term sheet is available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pathway to Purchase is a first-time home buyer assistance program administered by Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development. The program provides up to $50,000 in down payment and closing cost assistance toward the purchase of a first home in Prince George's County. The assistance is structured as a 0% interest, deferred payment second mortgage loan that is fully forgiven after 10 years, as long as the home remains the buyer's primary residence. Full repayment is required if the home is sold, transferred, or ceases to be the primary residence within the 10-year affordability period. The program works through approved Certified Participating Lenders, HUD-certified housing counseling agencies, and approved title companies, and requires completion of a minimum 8-hour housing counseling course. Purchase price limits are $448,000 for resale properties and $485,000 for new construction. Eligible property types include resale, foreclosure (court-ratified), short sale, and new construction. Household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income. Funds are awarded on a first come, first ready basis. Program guidelines, participating lender lists, housing counseling agency listings, required forms, and other resources are available for both buyers and realtors.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 provided as a 0% interest, deferred payment second mortgage loan for down payment, closing costs, and mortgage principal reduction. The loan is forgiven after 10 years if the home remains the buyer's primary residence. Recapture applies on sale, transfer, cash-out refinance, or non-occupancy within the 10-year affordability period per a sliding recapture schedule (100% if less than 1 year, 0% if 10+ years). Purchase price limits are $448,000 for resale properties and $485,000 for new construction. Funds must be used through a Certified Participating Lender, approved title company, and HUD-certified housing counseling agency. The assistance is evidenced by a promissory note and deed of trust secured as a second trust on the property. Income limits apply (households must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income; ranges from $91,800 for a 1-person household to $173,100 for an 8-person household, per 24 CFR 5.609). No cash may be disbursed or reimbursed to the borrower at settlement. Funds are awarded on a first come, first ready basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time home buyers purchasing a home in Prince George's County, Maryland, who meet program income limits (up to 80% of Area Median Income), are at least 18 years old, and do not currently own or have not owned a home in the past 3 years. Also serves realtors working with eligible buyers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, closing cost assistance, and mortgage principal reduction for the purchase of a first home in Prince George's County. Housing counseling costs ($25–$125) may be included. No cash may be disbursed or reimbursed to the borrower at settlement. Funds may not be used for relocation of tenants or for acquisition/construction of buildings for sectarian religious worship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. All zip codes within Prince George's County are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time home buyer (no current or prior home ownership in the last 3 years)
Must be at least 18 years old
Must purchase a residential property in Prince George's County (single-family dwelling, townhouse, or condominium)
Property types include resale, foreclosure (court-ratified), short sale, and new construction; tenant-occupied resale properties are excluded
Must meet program income limits (household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income; income determined per 24 CFR 5.609; ranges from $91,800 for 1-person to $173,100 for 8-person household)
Debt ratios: 35% front-end, 47% back-end
Must qualify for a first mortgage loan through a Certified Participating Lender
Must complete a minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course (online accepted)
Must use an approved title company
Property must pass HQS (Housing Quality Standards) inspection ($139 fee)
Must sign Regulatory Agreement and Declaration of Covenants; annual residency certification required
Home must remain buyer's primary residence during the 10-year affordability period
Purchase price must not exceed $448,000 for resale or $485,000 for new construction
No cash disbursement or reimbursement to borrower at settlement
For foreclosed properties, sale must be court-ratified and property must not be lawfully occupied at initial contract submission
Contract must allow at least 60 days for settlement
Application must be submitted with at least 21 business days (not including federal holidays) remaining on the contract term
Compliance with 24 CFR Part 92 and Uniform Relocation Assistance Act required; no unlawful tenant evictions or lease non-renewals in anticipation of sale
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds are awarded on a first come, first ready basis. Contact one of the approved Certified Participating Lenders to qualify for a first mortgage loan. Work with an approved HUD-certified housing counseling agency (minimum 8-hour course required) and an approved title company. Complete all required forms including the borrower affidavit, seller affidavit, lead disclosure, EEOC form, loan application, HUD Part 5 income chart, and other required documents. The lender submits the lender submission checklist and all required documents to the Pathway to Purchase program for review and approval. Program requires at least 21 business days (not including federal holidays) remaining on the contract term at time of submission. The contract must allow at least 60 days for settlement. Property must pass HQS inspection prior to closing. Submit the HQS Move-in Inspection Checklist with the application; all utilities must be on for inspection.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) program is the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's (HUD) primary funding source for homeless services, providing competitive grants for housing and supportive services to address homelessness. Prince George's County Department of Social Services administers a local competition for FY 2025 CoC funds as the Collaborative Applicant for the Prince George's County CoC (MD-600). The FY2025 competition was delayed after HUD withdrew the original Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) in December 2025 and indicated it would reissue a modified NOFO before the funds obligation deadline. The program is a recurring annual federal competition. For-profit entities are explicitly ineligible. Organizations submit Letters of Intent and full applications through the Prince George's County CoC, which ranks and selects applicants for submission to HUD via the e-snaps system.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal HUD Continuum of Care Program grants awarded through a local competition process. Approximately $3,524,000,000 is available nationally through the FY 2025 NOFO, with $188,000,000 for non-competitive renewal and replacement of expiring YHDP grants and $52,000,000 for Domestic Violence Bonus projects. Organizations submit Letters of Intent and applications through the Prince George's County CoC (MD-600). Grants fund housing programs (including Permanent Supportive Housing/PSH, Rapid Re-Housing/RRH, Transitional Housing/TH, Supportive Services Only-Coordinated Entry/SSO-CE, Joint Component Projects, DV-dedicated projects, and YHDP projects), behavioral health services, shelter, rental assistance, leasing, operating costs, supportive services, HMIS, administrative costs, moving expenses, security deposits, and other supportive services for individuals and families experiencing homelessness. Estimated local funding includes a Permanent Housing Bonus of $690,223 and a DV Bonus of $544,115. For-profit entities are explicitly ineligible. The FY 2025 application deadline was August 29, 2025 at 8:00 PM EDT; the FY 2025 NOFO was subsequently withdrawn by HUD on December 8, 2025 pending revision. FY 2025 funds obligation deadline is expected to be September 30, 2027. FY 2024 obligated funds remain available for expenditure until September 30, 2031; FY 2025 funds expenditure deadline is expected to be September 30, 2032.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letters of Intent Due Wednesday, December 10 at 5:00 PM (deadline has passed; NOFO withdrawn by HUD on December 8, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and government organizations (for-profit entities ineligible) providing housing and services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Prince George's County, including chronically homeless, unsheltered, seniors, veterans, domestic violence survivors, and trafficking survivors. Collaborative Applicants, victim service providers, HMIS Leads, and project applicants including organizations with lived experience expertise. Medicaid billable entities receive bonus points in the ranking process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing programs (Permanent Supportive Housing/PSH, Rapid Re-Housing/RRH, Transitional Housing/TH, Supportive Services Only-Coordinated Entry/SSO-CE, Joint Component Projects, DV-dedicated projects, YHDP projects), behavioral health services, shelter, rental assistance, leasing, operating costs, supportive services, HMIS, administrative costs, moving expenses, security deposits, and other homeless services for individuals and families experiencing homelessness. Also includes VAWA emergency transfer facilitation and compliance monitoring, rural short-term housing assistance, staffing for homelessness assistance providers, and mainstream benefits connections.

All activities must meet or exceed HUD requirements and be aligned with community needs within the Prince George's County CoC jurisdiction. The HUD CoC Program is national in scope, administered through local Continuums of Care. This record pertains to the Prince George's County, MD CoC jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a Letter of Intent to the Prince George's County CoC. Upon receiving updated HUD guidance and a revised NOFO, applicants complete a two-track submission: (1) submit Applicant Profile and Project Application via HUD's e-snaps electronic application system; and (2) email required organizational and project documentation in PDF format (including SAM registration, UEI, IRS documentation, audit, and Supplemental Addendum) to COC.princegeorges@maryland.gov. The county CoC ranks and selects applicants for submission to HUD. Form HUD-2991 must be completed and dated within the specified window. HUD evaluates applications, notifies successful applicants, and finalizes awards subject to FY 2025 appropriations. Conditionally selected applicants must submit additional project information no later than 30 days after the date of the award letter. Correction of technical deficiencies must be received by HUD within 7 calendar days after notification. Appeals for denied or decreased funding and Consolidated Plan certification disputes are available within 45 days of funding announcement (appeals contact: snapsappeals@hud.gov; general inquiry: CoCNOFO@hud.gov). Prince George's County Department of Social Services (PGCDSS) serves as Collaborative Applicant, with the Homeless Services Partnership (HSP) involved in program administration. Apply via the Homeless Services page on the Prince George's County website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) Energy Assistance Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) provides financial assistance to low-income households in Prince George's County to help pay heating bills, electric bills, and past-due energy bills, along with information on how to decrease energy costs. The program includes four components: the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) for home heating bills, the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) for electric bills, Arrearage Retirement Assistance (grants up to $2,000 for past-due electric and gas bills of $300 or more), and the Utility Service Protection Program (USPP) to protect low-income families from utility shutoffs during the heating season. All eligibility is income-based and a turn-off notice is not required. The program also helps prevent loss of energy service and restore service when needed.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of Social Services, Office of Home Energy Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided in several forms: (1) MEAP pays heating bills directly to fuel suppliers and utility companies on the customer's behalf; (2) EUSP pays a portion of current electric bills and places customers on a budget billing plan; (3) Arrearage Retirement Assistance provides a one-time grant of up to $2,000 toward past-due electric or gas bills (requires a past-due balance of at least $300; available once every five years); (4) USPP protects eligible low-income families from utility shutoffs during the heating season and requires year-round even monthly budget billing payments. Energy conservation information is also provided. Assistance helps prevent energy service disconnection and can help restore service when needed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; apply at any time during the year. Benefits can only be received once per fiscal year (July–June) and you must reapply each fiscal year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of home heating bills, electric bills, and past-due electric or gas bills. Payments are made directly to the fuel supplier or utility company on the customer's behalf. Assistance also helps prevent service disconnection or restore service when needed.

Schools must plant during spring or fall (not summer), develop a maintenance plan, and commit to a two-year post-planting maintenance commitment (watering every 7 days during dry periods, weeding/mulching up to 2x/year, pruning).
structured_extraction.program_audience: K–12 schools (Prince George's County Public Schools), project organizers, teachers, and environmental clubs in Prince George's County seeking to plant native trees and shrubs on school grounds; students learn about the importance of native trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees and shrubs on school campuses; developing and maintaining a post-planting maintenance plan for two years after planting, including watering, weeding, mulching, and pruning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to K–12 schools (PGCPS) located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Project site must be a school campus.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Climate-Smart Local Producers Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year USDA-funded pilot program to support farmers and food producers in Prince George's County 	at especially those from historically underserved communities 	at in adopting climate-smart, climate-centric farming practices. The program aims to reduce barriers to practice implementation, develop a marketing strategy for climate-smart commodities grown locally, and build green markets. It partners with Bowie State University to develop greenhouse gas monitoring methodology and leverages state of Maryland sequestration measurement tools. Major partners include the County Government, Department of the Environment (DoE), Prince George's Soil Conservation District (PGSCD), Economic Development Corporation (EDC), Food Equity Council (FEC), Latino Immigrant Development Center (LIDC), Bowie State University, and University of Maryland Extension.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $3.25 million in total grant funding (awarded via USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities) to support farmers and producers in implementing climate-smart practices, entering new green markets, and reducing barriers to farm operation. The County leads the pilot and distributes support to eligible producers over a five-year project period. Assistance includes marketing support and removal of practice-implementation barriers for farms using climate-smart methods, as well as monitoring and GHG reduction measurement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and food producers in Prince George's County, particularly historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers. Woman and minority-owned farms are prioritized in marketing strategy development. County residents as consumers of locally-grown climate-smart commodities are also a secondary audience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing climate-smart farming practices, marketing climate-smart commodities, reducing barriers to farm entry and expansion, supporting green market development, marketing strategy development, greenhouse gas monitoring methodology, and greenhouse gas reduction analysis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland (Primary States Expected: MD)
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or food producer in Prince George's County
Priority given to historically underserved producers (beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged, veteran, limited resource, women farmers, specialty crop growers)
Must grow fruits, vegetables, specialty crops, or other qualifying commodities using climate-smart practices
Woman and minority-owned farms are prioritized in marketing strategy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Monitor the program webpage for updates as the pilot program details become available. structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County provides funds to community groups and municipalities to plant native trees and shrubs in public or private common areas. Funded projects include tree plantings in parks and on playgrounds, memorial and street tree plantings, and reforestation projects along streams. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis upon submission of receipts after project completion. Projects must use native tree and shrub species; planting window is October 1 – May 1.

Eligible costs include plant material, tree protectors, site preparation (soil amendment, invasive removal), and planting costs. Per-plant cost cap: $150 for 5-foot/5-gallon tree; larger stock requires program manager consultation. Projects must use native tree and shrub species; planting window is October 1 – May 1.

Eligible costs include plant material, tree protectors, site preparation (soil amendment, invasive removal), planting costs, mulch, and protective fencing. Includes planning and maintenance guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Clean Energy Program – Solar Energy Grant (Solarize Prince George's) and Energy Efficiency Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Clean Energy Program, administered by the Department of the Environment – Sustainable Energy, provides supplemental grant funds to county residents through multiple related initiatives: (1) the Solar Energy Grant (branded as Solarize Prince George's), which helps homeowners lower the cost of installing rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems; (2) the Energy Efficiency Grant, which helps residents in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) offset the cost of home energy efficiency improvements; (3) a Solar Water Heater Grant; and (4) an ENERGY STAR Certification and Green Leasing Grant for commercial buildings. The Solar Energy Grant connects residents with grant funding, state-vetted installers, and expert guidance through every step of the solar process — from home assessment and permitting to final installation. It builds on the statewide EmPOWER Maryland Program and aims to break down energy injustice and barriers while supporting Maryland and the County's carbon reduction goals. The official Solar Energy Grant (per the December 2025 revision) is open to all eligible Prince George's County homeowners, with enhanced incentives for ERC residents who are Pepco customers. A Solar Energy Grant research pilot ran February 10–August 15, 2025, assisting residents who had already completed energy efficiency improvements with the cost of installing rooftop solar PV panels (minimum 2.0 kW system), including thermal battery storage and distributed energy resources. The Energy Efficiency Grant provides up to $6,250 to residents in the nine ERCs to cover costs of measures recommended by a home energy assessment (currently funded for natural gas incentives only — electric incentives are no longer funded — including Washington Gas incentives, air sealing, and insulation); applicants must also apply to an applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program (Pepco Home Performance with ENERGY STAR for market-rate applicants, or Maryland DHCD's Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program for income-qualified applicants). ERCs are designated neighborhoods identified through the County's Transforming Neighborhoods Initiative based on economic, health, public safety, and educational need. Funding for the program comes in part from the merger agreement between Pepco and Exelon and federal EECBG (Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant) funds under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Grant awards are available on a first-come, first-served basis and can be combined with other state, local, and utility incentives.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of the Environment – Sustainable Energy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Four grant types are available: (1) Solar Energy Grant — up to $10,000 for Pepco customers in a designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) for homeowner-owned rooftop solar PV systems; up to $5,000 for all other qualifying Prince George's County homeowners; minimum system size 2.0 kW DC; up to 20% of system cost may cover ancillary costs (tree trimming, panel upgrades, roof repairs, mold remediation); energy storage components are excluded from the official grant but were included in the research pilot. An additional $2,000 may be available for a solar power outlet (research pilot). For third-party-owned systems, up to $2,000 is available. The Solar Energy Grant research pilot (February 10–August 15, 2025) provided up to $10,000 for residents who had already completed energy efficiency improvements, for rooftop solar PV panels (minimum 2.0 kW; no maximum system size), including thermal battery storage and distributed energy resources. Solar grants are paid on a reimbursement basis upon receipt of invoice after prequalification. (2) Energy Efficiency Grant — up to $6,250 for residential energy efficiency measures recommended by a home energy assessment (currently: up to $2,500 for natural gas incentives via Washington Gas; up to 60% of total award ($3,750) for air sealing and insulation; includes up to $100 for home energy assessment; electric incentives are no longer funded). Additional incentives from Pepco and Washington Gas may also be available. (3) Solar Water Heater Grant — up to $7,500 for homeowner-owned systems or $2,000 for third-party-owned systems. (4) ENERGY STAR Certification and Green Leasing Grant — maximum $150,000 per application, covering ASHRAE Level 2 Audit costs up to $50,000 and energy measures up to $100,000–$150,000. All awards are available on a first-come, first-served basis dependent on funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Solar Energy Grant (current cycle per December 2025 revision): November 10, 2025 to February 27, 2026 (deadline may be extended); Solar Energy Grant research pilot: February 10–August 15, 2025 (closed); Energy Efficiency Grant: rolling, no deadline specified; Federal EECBG Period of Performance: work to be complete by April 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who own single-family residences, townhouses (where the owner owns the roof), or individually metered condominiums built before March 23, 2016. The Solar Energy Grant is available to all eligible Prince George's County homeowners wishing to install new rooftop solar PV systems, with enhanced incentives (up to $10,000) for Pepco customers residing in one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs). The Energy Efficiency Grant is available to residents of the nine designated ERCs who are both Pepco and Washington Gas customers. Income-qualified residents may access the Low Income Energy Efficiency Program track; market-rate residents participate through Home Performance with ENERGY STAR. Commercial property owners in Prince George's County may apply for the ENERGY STAR Certification and Green Leasing Grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: (1) Installation of new rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on single-family homes in Prince George's County, including ancillary costs such as tree trimming, panel upgrades, roof repairs, and mold remediation (capped at 20% of system cost); thermal battery storage and distributed energy resources where applicable (research pilot only); (2) Solar water heater installation; (3) Residential energy efficiency improvements including natural gas upgrades (Washington Gas incentives), air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, HVAC service/repair, lighting, water heating, appliances (ENERGY STAR certified), and other eligible measures identified during a whole-home energy assessment, including addressing barriers to adoption such as health and safety issues; (4) ENERGY STAR building certification costs (ASHRAE Level 2 Audit and energy measures for commercial buildings). Energy storage components are explicitly excluded from the standard solar grant eligibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland. The Solar Energy Grant per the December 2025 revision is available to all Prince George's County homeowners, with enhanced incentives (up to $10,000) for Pepco customers residing in the designated ERCs (Bladensburg–East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights–Marlow Heights; Kentland–Palmer Park; Oxon Hill–Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland–Coral Hills; Woodlawn–West Lanham; Langley Park); all other eligible Prince George's County homeowners may receive up to $5,000. The Energy Efficiency Grant requires applicants to reside within one of the nine designated ERCs; the City of Bowie is not eligible for the Energy Efficiency Grant. The ENERGY STAR Certification grant is available for commercial properties in Prince George's County. Use the ERC Address Locator tool to confirm eligibility.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Solar Energy Grant (current cycle per December 2025 revision): (1) Check eligibility using the ERC Address Locator tool if applicable. (2) Obtain quotes from at least two solar companies from the approved contractor list (contractor must have at least one NABCEP PVIP Certified person). (3) Apply for grant prequalification by submitting the completed grant application, Affidavit of Income, invoice template, recent electricity bill, contractor qualifications, solar PV analysis and proposal, pre-install photos, and the contractual agreement. Prequalification review takes approximately 30 business days from completed submission (resets if errors found). (4) Receive a Prequalification Notice; grant awardees have 2 weeks to accept the award. (5) Install the solar system within 4 months of prequalification approval (do not install prior to receiving Prequalification Notice). (6) After installation, submit final invoice, close-out documents, utility Authorization to Operate letter, interconnection agreement, permits, inspection sticker, installation photos, proof of registration with the Maryland PSC, and proof of one month of solar generation. Final payment is issued 30–60 business days after approval. Download the application from the program page and submit by email, hand delivery, or mail. For the Solar Energy Grant research pilot: complete energy efficiency upgrades first, then apply for grant prequalification; the grant is paid upon receipt of invoice. For the Energy Efficiency Grant: (1) Select a pre-approved contractor to schedule an energy audit; low-income residents apply through the Maryland DHCD website. (2) Contractor performs the energy audit and provides a prioritized list of recommended improvements; homeowner selects measures and signs a proposal. (3) Contractor completes the work and initiates the grant application for the homeowner to sign and submit with required supporting documents including recent utility bills (within last 3 months), W-9 form, Affidavit of Income, and contractor licensure. Prequalification review for Energy Efficiency Grant takes approximately 15 business days; prequalification letters issued within 15 business days; work must be completed within 90 days (extendable once, max 6 months total); final approval within 10 business days; payment within 30 business days. Contact CleanE@co.pg.md.us or call 301-883-5810 for questions. Mailing address: Prince George's County Department of the Environment, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary partnership between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based or other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. Participating organizations agree to take actions that improve local water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. In exchange, they receive a reduction on the Impervious Area Fee portion of their Clean Water Act Fee. Three options are available: providing a property easement for county-installed stormwater improvements (50% fee reduction), participating in outreach and education activities (25% fee reduction), or adopting green care and good housekeeping practices (25% fee reduction). Organizations may select one or all three options.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Stormwater Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified organizations can receive a reduction of up to 50% on the Impervious Area Fee portion of their Clean Water Act Fee. Option 1 (easement) provides a 50% fee reduction; Option 2 (outreach and education) provides 25%; Option 3 (green care and good housekeeping) provides 25%. Reductions can be combined. A mandatory Administrative Fee of $20.58 per tax account per year still applies and cannot be waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt faith-based organizations and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Prince George's County that pay the Clean Water Act Fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in the Impervious Area Fee portion of the Clean Water Act Fee in exchange for stormwater improvement actions on the organization's property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt faith-based organization or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must agree to participate in at least one of three program options

Option 1: Provide a Temporary Right-of-Entry Agreement and Temporary Construction Easement for county stormwater BMP installation, and sign a Maintenance Agreement to continuously maintain installed BMPs subject to triennial inspection

Option 2: Participate in the County's education and outreach campaign and/or annually host one qualifying activity (Rain Check Rebate Program, on-site recycling, trash pick-up event, or planting at least 5 trees)

Option 3: Use lawn and landscaping companies certified in proper fertilizer use (listed in Maryland Department of Agriculture's pesticide database) and/or commit to at least 3 good housekeeping practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select participation options and complete the application form, sign it digitally, then submit online and by mail to the Stormwater Management Division at 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774. Step 2: Meet with the County's agent to develop an alternative compliance plan. Step 3: Submit the written alternative compliance plan to the Department of the Environment (DoE) for review and determination of the fee credit amount.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Act Fee Reduction Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners in Prince George's County can apply for reductions on their Clean Water Act Fee (CWAF) — a charge based on impervious area (hard surfaces like roofs, driveways, and parking lots) on their property. Eligible property owners who have installed stormwater management practices such as Best Management Practices (BMPs) or Environmental Site Design (ESD) features can receive a credit of up to 100% of the impervious area fee. Different credit schedules apply depending on property type (single-family residential, multi-family/condo, or non-residential) and the type of stormwater control installed. Properties located within the City of Bowie are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Stormwater Management Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credits reduce the impervious area portion of the annual Clean Water Act Fee by up to 100%, depending on property type and the type of stormwater control installed. The Administrative Fee of $20.58 per tax account per year still applies regardless of credits. Residential credits vary by surface type (roof: up to 40%, driveway/parking lot: up to 50%, other impervious areas: up to 10%). Non-residential properties with existing BMPs/ESD receive up to 45% per surface type (roof: 45%, parking lot: 45%, green lawn care: 5%). Non-residential properties with legacy stormwater ponds receive 0–100% depending on when the pond was built (pre-1985: ineligible unless easement granted for retrofit; 1985–2002: up to 50%; post-2002: up to 100%). Alternative compliance options (easements: 50%, outreach/education: 25%, green care/housekeeping: 25%) can provide up to 100% combined credits. Credits appear on the following year's annual property tax bill. The administrative fee ($20.58/account) and impact fees ($20.90/account/ESU) are not subject to reduction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual deadlines apply by track: October 1 for most residential/non-residential BMP credits (for credit in current tax year); March 31 for Alternative Compliance track (for credit in next taxable year). Properties located within the City of Bowie are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Prince George's County (excluding City of Bowie), including single-family homeowners, condominium and multi-family property associations, and commercial/industrial/institutional property owners who have installed qualifying stormwater management practices. Tax-exempt religious organizations and 501(c) nonprofits are eligible for the alternative compliance track.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces the annual Clean Water Act Fee charged on impervious surfaces on the property. Credits reduce the impact (impervious area) fee only; the administrative fee always applies. Eligible BMPs include rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, reforestation, green lawn care, easements, and public outreach/education activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland only. Properties located within the municipal limits of the City of Bowie are exempt and not eligible for the credit program.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Prince George's County (City of Bowie properties are excluded)
Stormwater BMPs or ESD practices must be installed and, for non-residential properties, approved and certified by the County
BMPs must be maintained in good condition and have a current inspection record proving maintenance compliance
Property owner must allow County inspector access to verify BMP condition

Legacy stormwater ponds must have passed the County's triennial inspection; eligibility percentage depends on pond construction date (pre-1985: ineligible unless easement granted for retrofit; 1985–2002: up to 50%; post-2002: up to 100%)
Non-residential fee credits are calculated using the Water Quality Volume (WQv) method developed by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE)

For most BMP tracks, applications must be submitted by October 1 to receive credit in the current taxable year (July 1–June 30); applications received after October 1 are credited in the following year
For the Alternative Compliance track, applications must be received by March 31 to be eligible for a fee reduction credit in the next taxable year
Tax-exempt religious organizations or 501(c)(3) nonprofits may apply for alternative compliance credits
Applicable form must be completed and submitted for the correct property type
Applicant must be current property owner
For condominium/multi-family properties, certification by HOA President is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate application form for your property type (single-family residential, condominium/multi-family, non-residential with ESD/BMPs, non-residential with legacy stormwater management ponds, or alternative compliance for nonprofits/faith-based organizations). Submit the completed form via the CountyClick 311 online portal (http://countyclick.princegeorgescountymd.gov/), by email to CleanWaterActFee@co.pg.md.us, or by mail to the Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Stormwater Management Division, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774. The County will process the request and may send an inspector to verify BMP condition. Upon verification, the credit will appear on the following year's annual property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_name: ENERGY STAR Certification & Green Leasing Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding to owners of existing commercial office and multifamily buildings in Prince George's County who are Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers to install energy conservation measures (ECMs), perform energy and water efficiency retrofits, achieve EPA ENERGY STAR® certification, and adopt green leasing best practices. Funding reimburses costs for energy auditing, electric conservation measures, natural gas conservation measures, and water efficiency retrofits. Buildings must maintain ENERGY STAR certification for at least three years and adopt green leasing best practices after receiving the grant. The program encourages landlords and tenants to engage in energy-efficient practices. Applicants must be Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers located within Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Sustainable Energy
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants up to $150,000 per location address. Up to $50,000 for auditing and ENERGY STAR benchmarking (including up to $1,500 for a Licensed Professional to verify and stamp the ENERGY STAR certification application), up to $50,000 for natural gas conservation measures, and up to $50,000 for electric conservation measures. Green leasing measures must be included but cannot exceed 20% of the total grant amount. Grants cover a portion of the net customer cost after other incentives are applied. Up to 80% of the grant is paid upon complete request submission; the remaining balance is paid upon proof of ENERGY STAR Certification. Funding also supports water efficiency retrofits and adoption of Green Leasing best practices. Note: Washington Gas equipment rebates were only confirmed through end of 2024; status of gas ECM funding for 2025 and beyond may be subject to change.
