structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers property tax credits to encourage revitalization in existing communities. Eligible property owners receive a credit on the county property tax imposed on the increased assessed value resulting from qualifying real property improvements. The credit phases out over 5 years for non-residential properties (100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%) and over 3 years for residential properties (100%, 66%, 33%). Residential improvements are capped at $200,000 per dwelling unit. Both non-residential and residential improvements qualify, with different phase-in schedules for each. County Council approval is required for developments of ten or more single-family dwellings and for multifamily units.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A phased property tax credit on the incremental increase in assessed value resulting from qualifying real property improvements. Non-residential properties receive a 100% credit on county property taxes on the increased assessment in year 1, phasing down to 80% in year 2, 60% in year 3, 40% in year 4, and 20% in year 5. Residential properties receive a 100% credit in year 1, 66% in year 2, and 33% in year 3. The maximum eligible improvement for residential properties is $200,000 per dwelling unit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers making qualifying real property improvements in Prince George's County, including non-residential and residential projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on the increased county property tax assessment resulting from qualifying real property improvements — both non-residential and residential. Reduces county property taxes on the incremental assessed value created by improvements, phased in over multiple years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Prince George's County
Project must involve qualifying real property improvements that increase assessed value
Non-residential or residential improvements are eligible
Residential improvements capped at $200,000 per dwelling unit
Developments of ten or more single-family dwellings and multifamily units require County Council approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Business Development Specialist at the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 for more information on applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers a property tax credit program to encourage revitalization and redevelopment in inner-beltway communities. Eligible property owners receive a credit against County real property taxes on the increased assessed value resulting from qualifying real property improvements. The credit phases out over 5 years for non-residential properties (100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%) and over 3 years for residential properties (100%, 66%, 33%). Residential improvements are capped at $200,000 per dwelling unit. Qualifying improvements must require a County building permit and be completed and assessed. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; new single-family construction on razed/demolished lots or vacant lots between adjacent single-family structures; and new construction in developments of fewer than 10 one-family dwellings. County Council approval is required for developments of 10 or more single-family dwellings and for multifamily units. Both residential and non-residential property improvements may qualify, provided the property is located in a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District (census tracts inside the Capital Beltway where the median household income does not exceed the County median).

For residential improvements: 100% credit in year 1, 66% in year 2, and 33% in year 3. The maximum eligible residential improvement amount is $200,000 per dwelling unit. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; new single-family construction on razed/demolished lots or vacant lots between adjacent single-family structures; and new construction in developments of fewer than 10 one-family dwellings.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County reduces or eliminates the school facilities surcharge — a per-unit fee applied to new residential developments or redevelopments to cover anticipated increases in public educational services — to encourage multifamily housing development near transit. Qualifying multifamily properties within one-quarter mile of a Metro station, the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ) receive a 50% reduction in the surcharge. Studio and efficiency apartment units in those same transit-proximate areas and other limited circumstances are fully exempt from the surcharge. These reductions and exemptions are established per Maryland State Law and county ordinances CR-063-2023 and CR-069-2023, with surcharge amounts indexed to the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying multifamily residential developments near transit receive a 50% reduction in the school facilities surcharge (from $15,489 to $7,745 per unit outside the Capital Beltway, or from $9,035 to $4,518 per unit inside the Capital Beltway, as of FY 2015). Studio or efficiency apartment units in eligible transit areas — within one-quarter mile of a Metro station, within an approved TDOZ, or in other limited qualifying circumstances — are fully exempt from the surcharge. Surcharge amounts are indexed to the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers per county ordinances CR-063-2023 and CR-069-2023.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) is a mechanism that helps fund public improvements related to economic development, such as parking facilities, roadways, stormwater management infrastructure, and other public infrastructure. When a development or redevelopment project will generate additional tax revenues, Prince George's County can issue bonds to pay for related infrastructure improvements and finance those bonds through the incremental increase in tax revenue the project generates above the established base-year assessed valuation. The county pre-designates certain areas as TIF Districts, giving projects within them increased certainty of approval for a TIF bond, though exact terms must still be negotiated with the county. Pre-designated TIF Districts include the New Carrollton Metro Development District, Largo Town Center Metro Development, Prince George's Plaza Metro Development District, and Suitland-Naylor Road Development District.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues bonds to finance public infrastructure improvements (roads, parking, stormwater management) associated with a qualifying development or redevelopment project. The bonds are repaid using the incremental increase in tax revenue generated by the project above the base-year assessed valuation. Projects within designated TIF Districts have increased certainty of approval, though exact terms are negotiated with the county.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County's public campaign financing program designed to promote broader access to elected office and reduce the influence of large donations. The program allows county residents to run for office by gathering small donations from ordinary people, which are then matched with public funds from the Fair Election Fund. The program operates on recurring election cycles, with the current 2026 cycle covering candidates for County Executive, At-Large Council Member, and District Council Member.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Fair Election Fund Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching public funds provided to eligible certified candidates who collect qualifying small donations from Prince George's County residents. Maximum public contributions per election cycle: County Executive up to $750,000; At-Large Council Member up to $200,000; District Council Member up to $75,000. Funds may only be used for expenses directly related to election campaign activities during the specific primary or general election period. Prohibited uses include personal use, expenses relating to holding office, personal endorsements, and late filing fees. The Distribution Period for the 2026 election cycle runs from June 30, 2025 through November 18, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: General election receipt submission deadline: November 3, 2026 (submissions due no later than 11:59 PM on the date of the general election). Primary qualifying period ended May 16, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates for Prince George's County elective office — specifically County Executive, At-Large Council Member, and District Council Member — who are seeking public campaign financing by collecting qualifying small donations from Prince George's County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign financing — matching public funds support candidates running for Prince George's County elected office. Allowable uses include expenses directly related to election campaign activities incurred during the primary or general election period. Prohibited uses include personal expenses, expenses related to holding office, personal endorsements, late filing fees, and pre-filing purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to candidates running for elected office in Prince George's County, Maryland. Qualifying contributions must come from Prince George's County residents; contributions from non-residents do not receive matching funds.
requirements_list: Must be a candidate for a covered County elective office (County Executive, At-Large Council Member, or District Council Member)
Must file a Notice of Intent to participate no later than 9pm on the last Tuesday in February of the election year (2026 deadline: February 24, 2026)
Must collect qualifying small donations from Prince George's County residents to receive matching funds
Must apply for certification; only one application per election allowed (one resubmission permitted if denied, before end of Qualifying Period)
State Board must certify an applicant candidate no later than 10 business days after receiving required documentation
Submissions for matching funds due no later than 11:59 PM on the date of the primary or general election
Must return unspent funds by the end of the Distribution Period (November 18, 2026 for the 2026 cycle; candidates not on general ballot must return funds by approximately July 30, 2026)
Candidate must be in a contested election to receive public contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. File a Notice of Intent to participate no later than 9pm on the last Tuesday in February of the election year. 2. Collect qualifying small donations from Prince George's County residents during the Qualifying Period (1/1/2023–5/16/2026 for primary; general election window still active). 3. Submit an application for certification via MDCRIS (one application per election; one resubmission allowed if denied before end of Qualifying Period). 4. Submit receipts for matching funds no later than 11:59 PM on the date of the primary or general election. 5. Return any unspent funds by the close of the Distribution Period. Contact the Fair Election Fund Commission at fairelections@co.pg.md.us for information. Review the Program Summary Guide for full eligibility and participation details.

Partner organizations include Suburban Hospital, University of Maryland Capital Region Health, and M-NCPPC Parks & Recreation.

Pregnant women must have a risk factor associated with poor pregnancy outcomes
Infants and children must be up to age 2 with risk factors associated with poor health and developmental outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals are accepted from individuals, family members, physicians, managed care organizations, health care workers, hospitals, and government and community agencies. structured_extraction.program_description: Provides specialized HIV/AIDS services for youth and young adults who are minorities, between the ages of 13 and 30. Services include outpatient and ambulatory medical care, medical case management, psycho-social support, early intervention, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Specialized medical and support services for minority youth and young adults (ages 13–30) affected by HIV/AIDS, including medical case management, mental health services, and early intervention.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority youth and young adults ages 13–30 affected by HIV/AIDS in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outpatient/ambulatory medical care, medical case management, psycho-social support services, early intervention services, and mental health services.

Must be a minority
Must be HIV-positive or at risk (implied by service context)

structured_extraction.program_description: Free training program that teaches participants how to recognize and reverse an opioid overdose using Naloxone (Narcan). Participants receive a complimentary Naloxone nasal spray kit upon completing the training. Training is available in person or via Zoom.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Naloxone (Narcan) training session plus a complimentary Naloxone nasal spray kit. Sessions are available Monday through Friday, 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM, either in person or via Zoom. Anyone 18 years or older may attend.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents 18 years or older in Prince George's County who want to learn how to reverse an opioid overdose, including people at risk of overdose from drug use or accidental ingestion of prescribed opioids. Organizations interested in becoming Naloxone distribution sites are also eligible. The program is open to the general public — anyone can learn.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on how to administer Naloxone to reverse an opioid overdose; includes a free Naloxone nasal spray kit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of and organizations in Prince George's County, Maryland. Maryland law protects those who administer Naloxone to a person in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (301) 883-7828 or email SaveALife@co.pg.md.us to sign up for a training session. Appointments are available Monday through Friday from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM. Virtual and in-person training available.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Health Department PrEP Program provides comprehensive education and clinical services for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP), a daily medication that is highly effective for preventing HIV when taken as prescribed. The program serves HIV-negative individuals who are at risk of getting HIV through sex or injection drug use. Services include a PrEP Navigator/Health Educator, clinician and phlebotomist consultations, STI/HIV prevention education and risk reduction counseling, initial eligibility assessments, in-house lab monitoring, and referrals to community support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free clinical services including PrEP medication management, STI/HIV education, risk reduction counseling, in-house lab services, initial and follow-up clinician consultations, and referrals to support services. Services are available Wednesdays 8:00 am–12:00 pm at the Cheverly Health Center, with other times available by appointment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HIV-negative individuals at risk of HIV infection through sexual contact or injection drug use, including those with HIV-positive partners, those who have had an STI in the past 6 months, and people who inject drugs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: PrEP medication, clinical consultations, lab monitoring, health education, and referrals to support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services provided at Cheverly Health Center, 3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 3048, Cheverly, Maryland 20785.
requirements_list: Must be HIV negative
Must be at risk for HIV through sex or injection drug use (e.g., partner with HIV, inconsistent condom use, recent STI diagnosis, shared injection equipment)
Must complete an initial assessment to determine eligibility to start PrEP medication
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by phone at 301-583-5989 or walk in to the Cheverly Health Center during operating hours (Wednesdays 8:00 am–12:00 pm). Appointments can be arranged for other times.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program – Prince George's County (HIV/AIDS Program, HAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The HIV/AIDS Program (HAP), funded through the federal Ryan White Comprehensive AIDS Resources Emergency (CARE) Act, provides comprehensive HIV/AIDS medical care and support services to uninsured or underinsured people living with HIV/AIDS in Prince George's County and surrounding Maryland counties. Using a centralized 'one-stop shopping' model, the program acts as a payer of last resort when no other resources or coverage are available. Services include comprehensive health assessments, medical treatment, dental care, medical case management, mental health and substance abuse treatment, medical transportation, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance, outpatient ambulatory services, medical nutrition therapy, HIV medication assistance, outreach services, referrals for housing and social services, and free confidential HIV testing. Clients are evaluated for cost based on their current financial status per Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-cost and some free medical and support services are available to eligible clients. Services include comprehensive health assessments, medical treatment, dental care, case management, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost-sharing support, transportation to medical appointments, HIV medication assistance, nutrition counseling, substance use and mental health counseling, outpatient ambulatory services, outreach services, and referrals for housing and social services. HIV testing is free. Acts as payer of last resort when no other coverage is available; clients are evaluated for cost based on their current financial status per Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are HIV-positive and uninsured or underinsured, residing in Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care and treatment, dental care, case management, mental health and substance abuse treatment, medical nutrition therapy, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost-sharing support, medical transportation, HIV medication assistance, outpatient ambulatory services, outreach services, and referrals for housing and social services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary services target Prince George's County residents; however, eligible Maryland residents living in Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County may also access services. Some services (dental, outpatient ambulatory, mental health/substance abuse) may be available to individuals living outside Prince George's County. Services are provided at two locations: Cheverly Health Center (3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 1055, Cheverly, MD) and D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center (9314 Piscataway Road, Clinton, MD).
requirements_list: Must be HIV-positive
Must be uninsured or underinsured based on criteria under the federal Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act
Must be a resident of Maryland in Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County
Must meet income guidelines
Must meet eligibility criteria under the federal Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-583-3700 for more information and hours of operation, or call (301) 883-7879 to contact the Prince George's County Health Department. Services are available at two locations: Cheverly Health Center (3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 1055, Cheverly, MD) and D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center (9314 Piscataway Road, Clinton, MD). HIV counseling and testing services are available by appointment or walk-in.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Bridge Center at Adam's House
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, one-stop reentry and transition support program operated by a collaboration of Prince George's County's Health Department, Department of Social Services, and Department of Family Services. The program connects returning citizens, transitional-aged youth (ages 18-25), and Veterans in Prince George's County to a comprehensive array of free support services to facilitate a successful transition into the community. Services include behavioral health screenings and assessments, case management and referrals, peer support, job training and employment assistance, transportation support, benefits enrollment, Veterans Affairs and claims assistance, anger management courses, child support assistance, mentoring programs, legal help, and vital documents assistance. The program also connects clients to partner organizations for mental health and substance use treatment, GED/college enrollment, medical care, and family reunification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including behavioral health screenings and assessments, case management and referrals, peer support, job training and employment assistance, transportation support, benefits enrollment, Veterans Affairs and claims assistance, anger management courses, child support assistance, mentoring programs, legal help, and vital documents assistance. The program also connects clients to partner organizations for mental health and substance use treatment, GED/college enrollment, medical care, and family reunification. No cost for any services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Returning citizens, transitional-aged youth (ages 18-25), and Veterans who are Prince George's County residents ages 18 and older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free support services for reentry and community transition including behavioral health screenings and assessments, case management, employment assistance, job training, transportation, benefits enrollment, Veterans Affairs and claims assistance, legal help, vital documents assistance, and connections to partner organizations for additional support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be age 18 or older
Must be a returning citizen, transitional-aged youth (ages 18-25), or Veteran
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk in or contact the Bridge Center at Adam's House at 5001 Silver Hill Road, Suite 300, Suitland, MD. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Call 301-817-1900 or email bridgecenter@co.pg.md.us. The program uses a 'no wrong door' approach — staff will help connect you to the right services regardless of your entry point.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tobacco Control Program partners with public and private organizations to help Prince George's County residents quit smoking. It offers free quit smoking classes, nicotine patches and gum, and counseling sessions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including quit smoking classes, nicotine replacement therapy (patches and gum), and counseling sessions for county residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who want to quit smoking
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quit smoking classes, nicotine patches and gum, and counseling sessions

Must provide photo identification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Tobacco Program appointment line at 301-883-6121 to schedule an appointment. Services are available Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at 9201 Basil Court, Suite 318, Largo, MD 20774.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-stop shop providing free essential health and human services to Prince George's County residents, especially Spanish-speaking individuals. A bilingual team helps residents access medical care, benefits enrollment, legal services, employment support, disability services, and prenatal care, and connects them to community partners for food, behavioral health, ESL resources, domestic violence support, and more.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Health Department and Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including screening and care planning, benefits and health insurance enrollment, family legal services, community health worker assistance, employment and career services, disability services, and pre/post-natal care. Also connects residents to food banks, behavioral health, ESL resources, domestic violence support, legal services, WIC, Social Security assistance, and medical care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents ages 18 and older, with a focus on Spanish-speaking individuals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to health and human services including benefits enrollment, legal aid, employment services, medical care referrals, and more
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County residents only

Must be 18 years of age or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (301) 856-9454 for assistance. Walk-in services available Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM (center currently closed, reopening soon).

structured_extraction.program_name: Telehealth Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, evidence-based telehealth program that helps adults with Type 2 diabetes self-manage their condition. Certified diabetes care and education specialists lead live, interactive virtual classes covering medication adherence, healthy eating, blood glucose monitoring, physical activity, risk reduction, and coping strategies. Classes are recognized by the American Diabetes Association or accredited by the Association of Diabetes Care and Education Specialists.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Health Department – PreventionLink
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual diabetes self-management education and support sessions delivered via online video. Sessions include live instruction from certified diabetes care and education specialists and licensed health professionals, plus regular progress reports sent to referring providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Southern Maryland residents diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes who want to better manage their condition, improve their diet, and reduce the risk of diabetic complications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in virtual diabetes self-management education classes covering medication adherence, healthy eating, blood glucose self-monitoring, physical activity, complication risk reduction, and healthy coping.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Southern Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (documentation required)

Diagnosis must be confirmed by one of the following: fasting blood glucose ≥126 mg/dL; 2-hour plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL during a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT); HbA1c ≥6.5% (lab test required); random plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL with symptoms of hyperglycemia; or, if no signs of hyperglycemia, an abnormal result from the same or two separate test samples
Must have supporting test results such as HbA1c, oral glucose tolerance test, and/or fasting plasma glucose as determined by a doctor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact PreventionLink at (301) 883-7220 or preventionlink@co.pg.md.us to get started. Bring documentation of a Type 2 diabetes diagnosis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Improvements to Historic Resources Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers a property tax credit for expenses incurred to restore and preserve structures with historic, architectural, or cultural value that are classified as a Historic Site or Historic District in Prince George's County's Historic Sites and Districts Plan. The credit applies to work completed in the prior year and unused credits can be carried forward within a five-year window.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Historic Preservation Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for restoration, preservation, or new construction costs on qualifying historic structures. The credit is applied for the tax year immediately following the year the work is completed. A claim may be filed within 5 years of completion. Any unused portion of the credit can be carried over within the same 5-year period. If taxes were already paid, a refund will be issued.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 5 years of completion of restoration or preservation work
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of structures classified as Historic Sites or Historic Districts in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset costs of restoring, preserving, or constructing on historic structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Structure must be located in Prince George's County and classified as a Historic Site or Historic District in the Prince George's County Historic Sites and Districts Plan, or recommended for such classification by the Historic Preservation Commission.
requirements_list: Structure must be classified (or recommended for classification) as a Historic Site or Historic District on the Prince George's County Historic Sites and Districts Plan
Expenses must be for restoration, preservation, or new construction on the qualifying structure
Application must be submitted within 5 years of project completion
Credit is applied to the tax year immediately following the year the work is completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and receipts to the Historic Preservation Commission. Claims may be filed within 5 years of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HUD-VASH Program combines Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance for homeless veterans with case management and clinical services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA screens and refers eligible veterans to the Housing Authority, and provides services at VA medical centers and community-based outreach clinics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) rental assistance combined with case management and clinical services from the VA for eligible homeless veterans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless veterans in Prince George's County who are referred through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance (Housing Choice Voucher) and supportive services including case management and clinical care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must be homeless or at risk of homelessness
Must be screened and referred by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The VA screens veterans and makes referrals to the Housing Authority. Interested veterans should contact their local VA medical center or community-based outreach clinic.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher Homeownership Program (HCVHP) converts an existing Housing Choice Voucher — previously used to help families pay rent — into a subsidy that helps first-time homebuyers purchase their own home.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A voucher subsidy is redirected from paying rent to a landlord toward helping a first-time homebuyer purchase a home. Applicants submit a pre-eligibility application; please allow 60 days for processing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Housing Choice Voucher Program participants in good standing who wish to become first-time homeowners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a home by an eligible first-time homebuyer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Housing Choice Voucher participants served by the Prince George's County Housing Authority (HAPGC) in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current participant of the Housing Choice Voucher Program in good standing
Must be a first-time homebuyer who has not owned a home in the last 3 years
Must have a good rental payment history
Must have consistent employment history during the last 12 months (waived for disabled/elderly)
Must have a minimum annual income of $30,000 (waived for disabled/elderly)
Must have a minimum credit score of 620
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Homeownership Program Application (available to download from the agency website) to begin the pre-eligibility process. Information provided on the application will be used to determine pre-eligibility. Please allow 60 days for processing. Email hcvhomeownership@co.pg.md.us or call 301.883.5501 to learn more. For ADA/504 accommodation requests, contact the 504 Coordinator at 301.883.5576 or dhcd-504@co.pg.md.us.

structured_extraction.program_description: Online briefings designed to educate rental property owners and managers about how the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program works, including its rules and regulations. The sessions help landlords understand program requirements so they can participate in providing housing to voucher holders, including elderly, disabled, and low-income working families.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training sessions held monthly from 9:30 A.M. to 12:00 P.M. Briefings cover the Housing Choice Voucher Program rules, regulations, and how to participate as a landlord. Sessions are scheduled monthly through November 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental property owners and managers interested in participating in the Housing Choice Voucher Program in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a rental property owner or manager
Register by emailing full name and desired briefing date to LandlordBriefing@co.pg.md.us
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email your full name and the date of the briefing you wish to attend to LandlordBriefing@co.pg.md.us to register for an online session.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding for home modifications to help Housing Choice Voucher participants with disabilities make their homes accessible. The fund has a per-family expense cap of $15,000 (may be exceeded if justified) and an initial total fund cap of $200,000. Funding is available on a first come, first served basis and is subject to availability. Applicants submit a modification fund application through the Prince George's County Housing Authority.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for accessibility modifications to housing units for Housing Choice Voucher program participants with disabilities. Per-family expense cap of $15,000 (may be exceeded if justified). Fund total initially capped at $200,000. Funding is available on a first come, first served basis and is subject to availability. Can be used for both modifications and returning the property to its pre-modification condition. Contractor selection and work completion follows a 10-step process spanning approximately 40–60+ business days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Available until depleted on or before December 6, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCVP) participants with disabilities, including individuals who are Deaf or hard of hearing, blind or limited vision, have psychiatric disabilities, or mobility disabilities. At least one family member must have a qualifying disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility modifications to the participant's rental housing unit in Prince George's County, including installation of grab bars, handheld shower, raised toilet, flashing fire alarm, stair glide, motion sensor, wheelchair lift or ramp, widened doorway, curb cut, and tub seat. Can also be used to return the property to its pre-modification condition. Per-family cap of $15,000 (may be exceeded if justified).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a current Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCVP) participant
Must be a current HAPGC participant
Must have a disability requiring a home modification (qualifying disabilities include Deaf/hard of hearing, blind/low vision, psychiatric/mental impairments, or mobility disabilities)
At least one family member must have a qualifying disability
Modifications must align with approved Scope of Work and bid
Tenant must sign Modification Fund Agreement
Landlord approval required prior to dispersal
HAPGC approval required
Final invoice cannot exceed contracted price
Tenant responsible for quality inspection
COVID-19 safety protocols required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Housing Choice Voucher Modification Fund Application and return it to your Rental Specialist, Site Manager, or Nicole Garrett, Fair Housing/504 Coordinator. Verbal requests can be made by calling 301-883-5576. Funding is available on a first come, first served basis and subject to availability. The process follows 10 steps from application submission through final invoicing, with an estimated total timeframe of approximately 40–60+ business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Specialty Care for First Episode Psychosis (FEP) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Local Behavioral Health Authority (LBHA) is seeking applications from providers to deliver Coordinated Specialty Care for individuals experiencing a first episode of psychosis, specifically targeting young people ages 15-30. This is a funding opportunity through a Request for Application (RFA) process for licensed behavioral health service providers in Prince George's County. The contract period runs from May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 (single 5-year award cycle), subject to availability of funding and successful implementation.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Local Behavioral Health Authority (LBHA)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-reimbursement contract/grant funding through a Request for Application (RFA) process to support Coordinated Specialty Care for First Episode Psychosis programs. Total funding available is approximately $377,433 for a 12-month fiscal year (includes 5% indirect cost). Contract period runs from May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 (single 5-year award cycle). All future years' awards are subject to availability of funding and successful implementation. FY27 and FY28 funding to be added by future amendments. Funding subject to cancellation with 60-day notice. Annual CPA audit required if grant is $100,000 or more, due by March 1 of the following fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed behavioral health service providers with an Agreement to Cooperate with the LBHA in Prince George's County interested in delivering Coordinated Specialty Care for First Episode Psychosis for young people ages 15-30 (with transition-age youth ages 15-25 as a priority) experiencing a first episode of psychosis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of Coordinated Specialty Care services for individuals experiencing a first episode of psychosis in Prince George's County, including direct service delivery, required participation in provider meetings, data/progress reporting to LBHA, and compliance with annual site visits and monitoring requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed behavioral health services provider
Must have or be seeking an Agreement to Cooperate with the LBHA
Must comply with Maryland state accreditation and licensure requirements
Must provide Certificate of Insurance per Attachment C with specified liability limits
Must submit Annual Expenditure Report for the fiscal year on LBHA-provided Form 440 by August 10th
Must participate in annual site visits and policy/personnel record reviews
Must submit required data/progress reports to the LBHA
Annual CPA audit required if grant is $100,000 or more, due by March 1 of the following fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submission by email only to PGC_LBHA@pgcmd.gov; no mail or hand-delivered applications accepted. Applications consist of two parts: Part I (Project Narrative including Scope of Work, mandatory documentation per Section 3.1.4 including three attestation letters, technical response, and ADA acknowledgment) and Part II (Budget Narrative and Budget Forms using Excel attachment PGCHD/LBHA 432 Budget Package tabs 432B-432E). A pre-application conference was held on March 27, 2026, 2:00-3:00 PM via Microsoft Teams. Submit application by April 3, 2026 at 5:00 PM EST. Contract award announcement was anticipated on or before April 10, 2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of enhanced rehabilitation services for transitional age youth through a Residential Rehabilitation Program in Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Impact Grant provides funding from gaming revenue to nonprofit organizations located within or serving communities near National Harbor (within a 6-mile radius of the MGM Resort). The Local Development Council oversees a multi-year spending plan for these funds, which are dedicated by Maryland law to benefit communities in immediate proximity to National Harbor. Grant categories include General, Project, Capacity Building, and Capital initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Local Development Council
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by a portion of gaming revenue from the MGM National Harbor casino. Award amounts have ranged from $2,000 to $50,000 per awardee depending on the fiscal year cycle. Funds are issued by June 30 of the grant year, with a mid-year progress report due January 31 and a final closeout report due July 31 of the following year. Grant categories include General, Project, Capacity Building, and Capital initiatives. Eligible budget line items include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, printing, telephone/internet, postage, rent, utilities, in-kind support, and depreciation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations located within or providing services within a 6-mile radius of the MGM National Harbor Resort in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community programs and projects serving the local impact zone near National Harbor, including staffing costs (job descriptions required for positions requesting financial support). Eligible expenses include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, printing, telephone/internet, postage, rent, utilities, in-kind support, and depreciation. Past awardees have supported community development, youth services, housing, education, and public safety training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located within and/or provide services or activities within a 6-mile radius of the MGM National Harbor Resort. Mailing address: C/O Wayne K. Curry Administration Building, 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 4000, Largo, MD 20774.
requirements_list: Must be incorporated as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be located within or provide services within a 6-mile radius of the MGM National Harbor Resort
Must demonstrate 'good standing' status from the state of incorporation (Maryland, DC, or Virginia)
Must submit organizational/project budget information
Must provide IRS tax determination letter verifying 501(c)(3) status
Must provide IRS Exempt Select Check search results
Must provide most recently filed Financial Audit Report or IRS Form 990/990EZ
Must submit signed IRS Form W-9
Must provide current Certificate of Good Standing from state of incorporation
Must submit ACH Enrollment Form
Must provide a Letter of Support from an organization within a 6-mile radius
Must provide job descriptions for each position requesting financial support
Must submit a conflict of interest statement/policy
Must provide a list of Board of Trustees
Must provide a copy of the organization's Mission Statement
Must have an OMB-verified SAP vendor number
Must submit mid-year progress report by January 31
Must submit final closeout report by July 31 of the year following the grant award
Budget variances greater than 10% must be explained in reporting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the grant application workshop (held in February). Submit the completed application with all required documents by the deadline (March 22 for FY2024). Incomplete applications are disqualified. Applications are reviewed April through June by the Grant Review Committee, which recommends awardees for a vote. Applicants are notified of results by June 30. After receiving an award, recipients must submit a mid-year report by January 31 and a final report by July 31 documenting fund expenditure, financial detail, and narrative outcomes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free, flexible online training for community governance. Participants complete modules at their own pace and earn certification. The program is open to the general public and covers skills in community governance and common ownership community management.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Technology Facilities Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: The High Technology Facilities Real Property Tax Credit encourages growth and development of existing and new high-technology facilities in Prince George's County. It provides a real property tax credit to businesses primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development that construct or expand qualifying facilities in Prince George's County. High technology is defined using 33 U.S. Standard Industrial Classification codes across six clusters: Biotechnology and Biomedical, Information Technology and Services, High Tech Machinery and Instruments, Defense and Aerospace, Energy and Chemicals, and High Technology Research. The credit is phased in over five years on the increased property assessment: 100% in year one, 80% in year two, 60% in year three, 40% in year four, and 20% in year five. Eligible businesses include developers leasing to high-technology government agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Office of Finance
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against real property tax on the increased property assessment for qualifying high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development facilities. The credit is phased over five years: 100% in year one, 80% in year two, 60% in year three, 40% in year four, and 20% in year five. Eligible companies must construct or expand a building of at least 5,000 square feet, invest at least $500,000 in construction or expansion, and create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions within the County over a three-year period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High-technology businesses, including developers leasing to high-technology government agencies, primarily involved in engineering, life sciences, computer sciences, research and development, or production of related materials, parts, or equipment that construct or expand facilities in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credit on the increased assessment of newly constructed or substantially improved manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development, including engineering, life sciences, computer sciences, or production of related materials, parts, or equipment
Must construct or expand a building in the County with at least 5,000 square feet of gross floor area that is newly constructed or substantially improved
Must invest at least $500,000 in the construction or expansion of real property
Must create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions located within the building over a three-year period
Relocation of existing positions from elsewhere in the County does not qualify as new positions

Must provide written description of business, legal description of property, floor plans, documentation of investment, valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other information required by the Director of Finance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible businesses apply through the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation (EDC), which reviews the application. Each project is then subject to approval by the County's Finance Department (Director of Finance). Required application materials include a written description of the company's business, legal description of property, business activity description, floor plans, investment documentation, a valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other information required by the Director of Finance. Implementation timing varies by project.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) program trains community volunteers in basic disaster response skills so they can assist during emergencies before professional responders arrive. The 22-hour basic training covers disaster preparedness, fire safety, disaster medical operations, light search and rescue, disaster psychology, CERT organization, and terrorism awareness, ending with a simulation exercise. Volunteers can also pursue advanced training in areas such as CPR/AED, National Incident Management Systems, shelter management, and animal rescue. Trained members support local emergency responders at events, shelters, and during activations of the County's Emergency Operations Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP), administered by the Prince George's County Office of Human Resources Management, connects county youth and young adults (ages 14–24) with paid summer work experiences at community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies during July and August, including the Police Department. Youth participants receive paid placements at host employer worksites (up to 32–40 hours/week depending on age) plus job readiness training; stipends are available for completing 75% of training programs. Organizations can participate as host employers — hiring youth directly or serving as a designated worksite under a Referral Agreement (corporate partners) or Memorandum of Understanding (nonprofit and government partners) — or as Sponsorship Partners who contribute financially to support youth employment. Sponsorship contributions help fund transportation subsidies, technology access, program curriculum, workforce training, and additional work opportunities for county youth. Sponsorship Partners receive recognition on program marketing materials and social media, plus invitations to special events.
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Office of Human Resources Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid summer work placements for eligible youth and young adults ages 14 to 24 in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies during July and August. Youth participants receive paid work experiences (up to 32–40 hours/week depending on age) plus job readiness training; hourly wages of $13–$15/hr depending on age; stipends of $300–$500 available for completing 75% of training programs. Organizations can host county-funded youth interns through a Referral Agreement (corporate partners) or Memorandum of Understanding (nonprofit and government partners). Sponsorship Partners provide financial contributions at two tiers: Capstone Sponsorships ($5K–$100K) fund program curriculum, workforce training, and transportation; Student Sponsorships fund individual youth employment at three levels — $5,000/youth (ages 16–22), $3,500/youth (ages 14–15), or $1,500/youth (transportation only). Sponsorship Partners receive recognition on program marketing materials and social media, plus invitations to special events.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth@Work Internship Program offers temporary and permanent employment opportunities for young adults ages 18 to 24 who previously participated in the Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP). The internship extends employment to former SYEP participants to retain talent and fill entry-level staffing gaps in Prince George's County government agencies. The program is funded through a $3,000,000 U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration Community Projects Grant for the performance period of June 1, 2024 – May 31, 2027, with cohorts projected through 2027.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship placements at $18.00/hour for 6-month assignments (approximately 2,080 hours per year) in Prince George's County government agencies across 8 career pathways: Budget Management & Finance, Community & Customer Relations, Environmental Services, Government Operations, Health & Human Services, Infrastructure & Development, Information Technology, and Public Safety. Interns may transition to permanent County employment based on performance. Training funds are also available to help interns obtain certifications (e.g., IT, SHRM) or pursue additional career development opportunities. The program is funded by a $3,000,000 U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration grant (June 1, 2024 – May 31, 2027).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Partnership Grant (CPG) Program is the main discretionary grant initiative offered by the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive. It provides funding to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits that deliver services or programs benefiting Prince George's County residents, with emphasis on underserved populations and the county administration's strategic priorities. Grants are awarded annually for one-year periods, with awards disbursed in a single lump-sum payment.

Awards are disbursed in a single lump-sum payment. Previous awards have ranged from $1,000 to $125,000. One proposal per organization per fiscal year is accepted.

Programs must align with county administration strategic priorities and support underserved populations. Multiple program initiatives are limited to one application per organization.

Organizations located outside the County may apply if they provide services within the County. Applicants may be incorporated in Maryland, the District of Columbia, or the Commonwealth of Virginia.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County offers a Long Driveway Grant Program to help residents whose homes are located far from existing broadband infrastructure connect to high-speed internet service. The county covers 90% of the construction cost to extend broadband down a long driveway, up to a maximum grant award of $13,500 per household. Eligible properties must have internet service available at or near the end of the driveway (within approximately 1,500 feet) and must not fall within another grant-funded broadband build area. Approximately 106 addresses may be eligible, and residents can verify eligibility using the County's grant application map. Program guidelines were revised in January 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county pays 90% of the cost to extend broadband down a long driveway to a residence, up to a maximum of $13,500 per household. The grant covers broadband infrastructure construction costs to connect eligible homes to high-speed internet service. Eligible properties must have broadband available at or near the end of the driveway (within approximately 1,500 feet) but not yet connected. Applicants must not be located in any other active grant-funded broadband build area.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extending broadband internet service down a long driveway to a residence; broadband infrastructure construction costs to connect eligible homes to high-speed internet service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to addresses located within broadband grant areas in Queen Anne's County, Maryland. Approximately 106 addresses may be eligible. Property must not fall within another grant-funded broadband build area. More information is available at https://onboard.qac.org/board/4323. structured_extraction.program_description: County Ride is Queen Anne's County's public transit program. It launched a 'Ride for Free' pilot campaign in 2023, eliminating fares for all riders on its fixed public routes. The free-fare pilot has continued each year and is slated to continue in 2027. The program also offers free door-to-door rides with at least two days' advance notice, subject to availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Riders pay no fare to use County Ride fixed public routes (a pilot program running since 2023 and continuing through at least 2027). Free door-to-door rides are also available with at least two days' advance notice, subject to availability. Outside the free-fare pilot, standard fares apply: General Public — 1-Way $3, Day Pass $5, 10-Ticket Booklet $30, Monthly Pass $80, Student Monthly Pass $40. Seniors, Disabled, and Medicare cardholders — 1-Way $1.50, 10-Ticket Booklet $15, Monthly Pass $35. Independence Card holders — $1 per trip.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced-cost public transit rides on four fixed routes (Monday–Friday, 6:30 a.m.–4:45 p.m.) and door-to-door service

requirements_list: No fare required during the Ride for Free pilot period

Independence Card holders must present a picture ID and Independence Card
Bus tickets and bus passes cannot be used for specialized services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Board any County Ride fixed route bus with no payment required during the Ride for Free pilot. For door-to-door service, call (410) 758-2357 with at least two days' advance notice. Passes can be purchased at Kent Island, Sudlersville, Grasonville, and Centreville Senior Centers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled or Fallen Emergency Worker Property Tax Credit Program / Heroes Act Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: These are two separate but similar county-level property tax credit programs for permanently and totally disabled emergency workers and surviving spouses of fallen emergency workers. Queen Anne's County offers a credit equal to 100% of the County Property Tax on the applicant's principal dwelling, beginning July 1 following approval and continuing without reapplication as long as an Annual Eligibility Certification is filed each year. Wicomico County's Heroes Act Credit Program provides a property tax credit to permanently disabled first responders and surviving spouses of fallen first responders who were employed by an entity located in Wicomico County. Both programs cover law enforcement officers, firefighters, rescue workers, correctional officers, and emergency medical service workers injured or killed in the line of duty.

Wicomico County (Heroes Act): A property tax credit available to permanently disabled first responders and surviving spouses of first responders who died as a result of their work, per Legislative Bill 2022-07.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Queen Anne's County Economic Development Incentive Fund (EDIF) provides financial assistance to individuals and businesses starting a new business, expanding an existing business, or relocating operations to Queen Anne's County. It also supports existing businesses and helps attract or enhance businesses that complement the county's major industry sectors. Strong preference is given to Advanced Manufacturing, Agriculture and Seafood, Technology, and Hospitality/Tourism industries. Funding is discretionary and authorized by the County Commissioners as funding is available, with preference for projects demonstrating significant economic impact such as job creation, retention, increased production, or niche market potential. The program offers loans and conditional loans that may become grants if the business meets certain goals.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development, in partnership with the Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC), offers two business accelerator programs for local entrepreneurs and business owners. The Ignite Business Accelerator is designed for startups and early-stage businesses, running 8 weeks on Tuesday evenings (April 1 – May 20), covering business idea development, market needs, financial goals, cash flow, and business planning. The Elevate Business Accelerator targets established businesses generating $50,000+ in annual revenue, delivered in two intensive 6-hour in-person weekday sessions (May 6 and May 13) plus virtual training, covering revenue growth, profitability, operational efficiency, marketing, legal/HR strategies, and cash flow management. Both programs provide structured group coaching, peer-to-peer advising, one-on-one mentoring with internationally certified business coach Russell Teeter, and access to exclusive resources to help participants launch, grow, and scale their businesses. Participants develop entrepreneurial vision into launch plans, draft financing proposals, create investor pitches, and build financial and operational strategies for growth. Sessions are hosted at the Queen Anne's County Family YMCA. The programs are funded through a grant from the Upper Shore Regional Council and the Maryland Department of Commerce in partnership with the SBDC.

Participants develop a launch plan, draft a financing proposal, and create a 4-minute investor pitch. (2) Elevate — two 6-hour in-person weekday sessions (May 6 and May 13) plus virtual training, $85 per participant, covering revenue growth, profitability, operational efficiency, marketing, legal/HR strategies, and cash flow management. Participants work on strategic improvements, financial/operational processes, and expansion or exit planning. Both programs are hosted at the Queen Anne's County Family YMCA and include group coaching, peer advising, one-on-one mentoring, and help developing business plans, financing proposals, and growth strategies.

structured_extraction.program_name: CatalystQ: The Catalyst of Minority Business Excellence in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.program_description: CatalystQ is a minority business training accelerator program run by Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development. It selects minority-owned small businesses in Queen Anne's County and provides them with a hands-on business coach and mentor to help draft a business plan, create marketing materials, and build relationships with local banks, accountants, insurance providers, and attorneys. Each selected business also receives a microgrant to fund strategic growth initiatives. The program addresses key barriers faced by minority entrepreneurs including access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and networking. Graduates receive a Certificate of Completion from Queen Anne's County Commissioners and Continuing Education Credits from Chesapeake College. The goal is to help minority-owned businesses grow revenues, improve resilience to economic shocks, and become job creators.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County Economic Development operates a Career Technology Liaison position that connects local youth with internship and apprenticeship opportunities at area businesses. The liaison helps businesses develop and navigate the Maryland Department of Labor Youth Apprenticeship program, supports students and schools in accessing information about available youth apprenticeships, and connects students with local internship positions. The program serves both Queen Anne's and Kent Counties and all industries are encouraged to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Career Technology Liaison provides free matchmaking and navigation support to connect local youth with internships and apprenticeships at local businesses. Youth apprentices earn wages, gain employment experience, and confirm career goals; employers build their workforce and develop a skilled worker pipeline. Youth apprenticeships require 450 hours of employment and 141 hours of related instruction with an approved business. Youth internships provide students 1 credit toward graduation per internship, requiring 7.5 hours of work per week at the host business.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Adult Vaccine Program is a statewide initiative launched by Governor Wes Moore and the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to immunizations for uninsured and underinsured adults. The program aims to reduce barriers to vaccination and help prevent the spread of vaccine-preventable diseases across Maryland. All vaccines are provided free of charge to eligible adults age 19 and older. No one is turned away due to inability to pay, though confirmation of insurance status may be requested. 'Underinsured' means health insurance does not cover recommended vaccines, or the individual has high deductibles creating a financial burden.

structured_extraction.program_description: ReBUILD Metro's Legacy Homeowner Repair program provides no-cost home repairs and façade improvements to long-term (legacy) homeowners in the Johnston Square neighborhood of Baltimore City. The program is designed as an anti-displacement strategy, ensuring existing residents are not displaced as the neighborhood undergoes revitalization, while helping them upgrade their homes and build equity. Major deferred repairs and structural improvements are provided at no charge to eligible homeowners. As of October 2024, the program was expanded, with Rebuilding Together Baltimore selected to lead home repairs. A waiting list has been in place while the program seeks additional resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Path to Own is a free homeownership readiness program run by ReBUILD Metro that helps aspiring first-time and underserved homebuyers in East Baltimore assess their financial situation, access homebuyer education workshops, connect with HUD-certified housing counselors, find favorable mortgage products, and identify down payment assistance programs. The program assesses participants' credit and financial readiness, provides guidance on navigating the homebuying process, and works to help those who have faced systemic barriers — particularly African American Baltimoreans — achieve sustainable homeownership and build generational wealth in East Baltimore neighborhoods such as Johnston Square and Broadway East. Participants complete a registration and intake process, and the program assesses their eligibility for services such as credit counseling, homebuyer education, and related support. In-person workshops are offered bimonthly in 2026 (February 24, April 28, June 23, August 25, October 27) from 6–8 PM at The Hammond, 1100 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore MD 21202.

Also provides a pathway to affordable homeownership for underserved homebuyers, helping them build generational wealth. Workshops are held bimonthly in 2026 (February 24, April 28, June 23, August 25, October 27) from 6–8 PM at The Hammond, 1100 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore MD 21202.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP), operated by the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County, provides matching grants to help retail shopping centers and main street retail spaces make exterior improvements and major building systems upgrades. The program targets obsolete and underperforming retail centers — especially those in designated Sustainable Community areas with high visibility — to boost economic performance, improve appearance, and enhance the retail experience for Prince George's County residents. Eligible improvements include exterior façade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems improvements such as energy efficiency upgrades, signage, parking lot work, roof replacement, landscaping, exterior painting, awnings, doors/windows, and architectural features. Grants reimburse up to 50% of approved construction costs as incurred and documented, with a minimum grant of $25,000 (requiring at least $50,000 in total project costs) and a maximum of $125,000 (requiring at least $250,000 in total project costs). The program operates in annual funding cycles; the 2025/2026 cycle has $250,000 in total available funding.

A 50% applicant match is required. Total available funding for the 2025/2026 cycle is $250,000. Architectural design and permit costs are not reimbursed until construction is complete. Construction must begin within 90 days of grant approval and be completed within 270 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Impact Grant Program (CIG) provides small capital grants to civic and neighborhood associations and community-based nonprofit (501(c)(3)) organizations in Prince George's County. Administered by the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County, the program funds innovative capital projects in priority areas including Neighborhood Beautification (streetscaping, signage, façade improvements, public art) and Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability (park restoration, urban agriculture, stormwater management, historic preservation). The program aims to strengthen communities and build organizational capacity. Up to $250,000 in total grant funding is available per cycle, split into two geographic funding buckets: $100,000 earmarked for organizations located within previously designated Sustainable Communities boundaries inside the Beltway (National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas), and $150,000 for county-wide projects in the remainder of Prince George's County. The FY 2026 application deadline was May 18, 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small capital grants distributed on a reimbursable basis among eligible community-based organizations, with up to $250,000 in total grant funding available per cycle. Maximum individual award is $50,000. Funding is split into two geographic buckets: $100,000 earmarked for organizations located within previously designated Sustainable Communities boundaries inside the Beltway (National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas), and $150,000 for county-wide projects in the remainder of Prince George's County. Grants fund capital projects such as equipment and materials purchases. Grants cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, personnel, or projects previously funded through the CIG. Eligible project categories: Neighborhood Beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian and recreational improvements, signage, commercial façade improvements, improvements to public-use commercial buildings, permanent public art) and Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability (park, stream, and open space restoration; urban agriculture and tree canopy replenishment; green roofs, low impact development, and stormwater management; preservation of historic landmarks and structures).

Organizations located in municipalities must provide written approval from town leadership (Mayor or Council). Projects must also be located within Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HBCU Brilliance Initiative is a national program operated by Reinvestment Fund that provides targeted financial support, technical assistance, and capacity-building resources to Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). The program offers debt capital (loans) for infrastructure improvements, balance sheet restructuring, new real estate development, and increased access to capital. It also provides learning and training opportunities for HBCU staff and leadership, policy advocacy, research, and grant opportunities. Through the HBCU Brilliance Initiative Cohort program, a first-of-its-kind track, selected cohort members (10–11 institutions) receive $40,000 in grants and up to $1,000,000 in financing, along with technical assistance administered by Reinvestment Fund and a council of HBCU leaders, advocates, and financial experts, to strengthen institutional capacity, campus infrastructure, and sustainability. Since 2018, Reinvestment Fund has loaned more than $50 million to HBCUs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides debt capital solutions (loans) for infrastructure improvements, balance sheet restructuring, new real estate development, and increased access to capital. Since 2018, Reinvestment Fund has loaned more than $50 million to HBCUs. Through the Cohort track, selected institutions receive $40,000 in grants and up to $1,000,000 in flexible financing. Grants fund developmental projects such as campus infrastructure improvements, predevelopment and planning, and sustainability and environmental initiatives. Technical assistance is provided through a curriculum administered by Reinvestment Fund and a council of HBCU leaders, advocates, and financial experts. Learning and training opportunities are also available for HBCU staff and leadership.

structured_extraction.program_description: Invest Health is a cross-sector national initiative—a collaboration between the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and Reinvestment Fund—that brings together diverse leaders from small to mid-sized U.S. cities to develop new strategies to increase and leverage private and public investment and accelerate improvements in neighborhoods facing the biggest barriers to better health. The program supports a learning network of 50 cities, providing each selected city team with a $60,000 grant, access to a learning community, faculty advisors and coaches, peer learning exchanges, and convenings. The program focuses on developing a pipeline of financeable built-environment projects, improving community development investment systems, prioritizing community engagement, data, and equity, and addressing social drivers of health including jobs, housing, education, community safety, and environmental conditions.

The program includes charter school lending supported by credit enhancement from the U.S. Department of Education, which allows higher loan-to-value limits (up to 100%), leasehold or second-position collateral, longer interest-only periods, and predevelopment loans.
