structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Early Childhood Education (ECE) Facility Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps licensed child care providers in Montgomery County, Maryland grow, improve quality, and serve more families. It offers three types of loans: (1) forgivable loans (up to $74,000) for both home-based and center-based providers to expand or improve facilities, with repayment forgiven 20% annually over 5 years if the provider stays open and licensed and completes annual business training; (2) zero-interest (0%) loans (up to $300,000 for expansion or $200,000 for quality improvements) for centers only; and (3) predevelopment forgivable loans ($1,000–$10,000 for home-based, $5,000–$50,000 for centers) for pre-construction planning costs, fully forgiven after 1 year if requirements are met. The program prioritizes equity, with a focus on underserved and low-income communities, and aims to ensure equitable access to safe, quality child care — especially in areas with infant/toddler child care shortages. It is administered by the Reinvestment Fund on behalf of Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three loan types are available. (1) Forgivable Loans: up to $74,000 for home-based (family child care) or center-based providers; used for facility expansion or improvement. Repayment is forgiven 20% annually over 5 years if the provider stays open and licensed for five years and completes 12 hours of business training annually. (2) Zero-Interest (0%) Loans: up to $300,000 for expansion or up to $200,000 for quality improvements, for centers only; must be repaid but accrue no interest. (3) Predevelopment Forgivable Loans: $1,000–$10,000 for home-based providers, $5,000–$50,000 for centers; fully forgiven after 1 year if requirements are met; used for pre-construction planning costs (zoning contracts, architect contracts, building permits). Funds may NOT be used for salaries or staff training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are closed. Decisions were communicated in April 2026. Funding was available through May 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers in Montgomery County, MD — including family child care (home-based) providers and child care centers — with a published Maryland EXCELS quality rating, especially those serving areas with a shortage of infant/toddler child care (per The State of Supply and Demand for Childcare in Montgomery County, MD report) or serving low-income and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating new child care slots or expanding existing capacity; renovating or improving existing child care spaces; covering pre-development planning costs (architect fees, permits, zoning contracts); purchasing equipment, furniture, fixtures, and educational/learning materials; HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roofing systems; playground equipment and safety surfacing; fire suppression/alarm systems; security systems; accessibility upgrades; energy efficiency improvements. Funds may NOT be used for salaries or staff training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Projects must be located in Montgomery County to qualify. Within the county, programs must be located in areas with a shortage of infant/toddler child care (as identified in 'The State of Supply and Demand for Childcare in Montgomery County, MD' report) OR serve low-income and underserved communities. Providers located within the city limits of Rockville or Gaithersburg should contact those municipalities directly for permitting purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reinvestment Fund is a CDFI that provides flexible loans to support community development projects across the United States. Loans are available for affordable housing, clean energy, early childhood education, food systems, health services, HBCUs, K-12 education, arts and culture, other community facilities, and social impact real estate. Eligible uses include predevelopment, acquisition, construction, leasehold improvements, bridge financing, contract receivables, equipment, and fund-to-fund lending. Loan terms vary and include short-term and mini-permanent options. Projects may also leverage New Markets Tax Credits, Historic Tax Credits, or Low Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible loans with varying terms including short-term and mini-permanent financing. Eligible uses include predevelopment, acquisition, construction, leasehold improvements, bridge financing (capital campaign, tax credit equity, etc.), contract receivables, equipment, and fund-to-fund lending. Projects may also leverage New Markets Tax Credits, Historic Tax Credits, or LIHTC funds. Working capital loans for small businesses are generally not provided, but may be considered as part of a real estate loan request.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reinvestment Fund offers Promissory Notes — a direct community investment vehicle through which individuals, organizations, and institutions can invest in a diversified loan fund that finances community development projects. Investors earn a modest financial return while their capital funds socially and environmentally responsible development projects that benefit low-income communities, including housing, health, education, and food access. The fund has operated since 1985, has maintained a 100% repayment rate plus interest, and has made over $3 billion in loans to community businesses. Investments are not government-insured and are not tax-deductible charitable gifts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Promissory Notes start at $1,000 with a maximum offering of $7,000,000 (with approximately $3,500,000 expected in new cash proceeds, with the remainder from rollovers/reinvestments or unsold). Available interest rates: 3.75% for a 3–4 year term, 4.50% for a 5–10 year term (including 5-, 7-, or 10-year terms), and 5.00% for a 15-year term. The program has maintained a 100% repayment rate plus interest since 1985. Investments are not government-insured and are not tax-deductible charitable gifts. Notes are unsecured, illiquid instruments with no public market. Interest is calculated on an Actual/Actual basis from the deposit date. Investors may elect to receive annual interest payments or to reinvest interest payments. No early redemption or call prior to maturity without mutual written consent. Upon maturity, investors receive at least 30 days prior notice to elect renewal or redemption; subject to automatic reinvestment if investor does not respond within 60 days of maturity date. The Fund is a certified CDFI and S&P AA– rated Pennsylvania nonprofit (501(c)(3)).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, faith-based organizations, family foundations, banks, civic organizations, and other investors seeking a modest financial return while supporting community development projects in low-income communities in 17 eligible jurisdictions including Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital is deployed as loans and equity investments to organizations and businesses working to alleviate poverty, build wealth, and create economic opportunity for low-wealth communities and low- and moderate-income individuals. Eligible uses include housing, community facilities (schools, health centers), healthy food access, commercial real estate, charter schools, community health centers, business development, sustainable and clean energy projects (wind, solar, energy-efficient buildings), local food systems, and social programs. Proceeds may also be used to refinance existing obligations or capitalize Fund affiliates.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Prospectus and accompanying pricing supplement from the Reinvestment Fund website and review the toolkit. The Fund solicits directly from persons or organizations known to the Fund and believed to be interested in community development projects and capable of bearing the risks; the Fund may also publicly disseminate information about the offering. To invest, remit funds via wire, automated clearing house (ACH), or check payable to 'Reinvestment Fund, Inc.' for the desired Promissory Note amount; the Fund will issue a Promissory Note in substantially the form set forth in Exhibit A of the prospectus. Interest rates and terms are set at the time of issuance based on market conditions and detailed in the accompanying pricing supplement. Investors may elect to receive annual interest payments or to reinvest interest payments. Pennsylvania residents may withdraw their acceptance within two business days of receiving the prospectus by providing written notice via fax (215-574-5919) or email (investorrelations@reinvestment.com) for a full refund with no further liability. Annual audited financial statements are provided to note holders within 120 days of fiscal year-end. Contact the investor relations team by phone at 215-574-5819 or email at investorrelations@reinvestment.com for questions. Reinvestment Fund, Inc., 1700 Market Street, 19th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19103.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding for existing WeVision EarlyEd Solutions Lab sites seeking to create brand continuity and consistency across multiple early childhood education (ECE) locations. Two grant options are available: a Program Alignment Fund (up to $100k) for lab sites aligning non-lab locations with WeVision EarlyEd standards, and a Program Alignment and Expansion Fund (up to $300k) for lab sites that have recently expanded or plan to expand to an additional site. The fund emphasizes quality standards, child impact documentation, cost-per-child modeling, educator compensation pegged to public school wages, and affordability for both subsidized and non-subsidized families.

After applying, selected sites must complete a workplan (including updated org chart/staffing plan, enrollment & marketing plan, 4-year financial projections, zoning approval, architect and building plans, construction contract, contractor insurance & license, landlord/HOA approval if applicable, and documentation of additional funding sources if budget exceeds grant) to access the expansion grant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF) / Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF) supports rural community development in Maryland, including capacity-building grants to rural nonprofit service providers through the Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF), regional infrastructure projects, rural entrepreneurship development, and rural health care organizations. At the statewide level, the Rural Maryland Council administers competitive grants to rural-serving nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities, community colleges, and government bodies to promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, and agricultural and forestry education in rural Maryland. The program operates on an annual grant cycle (e.g., FY2026) with a two-phase application process consisting of a Letter of Intent followed by a full application. In Western Maryland, RMPIF funding is combined with the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland's (TCCWMD) Summit Financing Solutions loan fund to improve access to capital for small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses, and to provide technical assistance to help businesses secure professional services and financing. The Fiscal Year 2026 grant cycle made $6,000,000 in funding available for projects in rural Maryland. The RMC is particularly interested in proposals addressing agriculture, energy, rural broadband, healthcare, youth engagement, and workforce/economic development. RMPIF was established in 2006 and is authorized through June 30, 2030 under state law, with annual appropriations at the Governor's discretion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are awarded to eligible rural-serving nonprofits, for-profit businesses, community colleges, and government entities through an annual grant cycle (e.g., FY2026) via a two-phase application process. The Fiscal Year 2026 grant cycle made $6,000,000 in funding available. For MAERDAF grants, the maximum award is $25,000 per grant (historically averaging approximately $18,000). Priority is given to applicants with matching funds from non-state sources (equal match from a non-state source in the prior fiscal year or a documented commitment for the current fiscal year), though matching funds are not required. In Western Maryland, RMPIF funding is also combined with TCCWMD's Summit Financing Solutions loan fund to enhance access to capital for small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses. Technical assistance is provided to help businesses acquire professional services and improve their ability to secure financing. Capacity-building funds are available to rural nonprofit service providers through MAERDAF. The FY2026 grant performance period runs August 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Regional and statewide planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, training and technical assistance for small and agricultural businesses, access to capital for businesses, professional services, capacity building for nonprofits, rural entrepreneurship, community development, rural health care, jobs creation, and capital items.

In Western Maryland, the program specifically serves Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties through TCCWMD's loan and technical assistance programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program operates on an annual cycle with a two-phase application process. Phase I: Submit a Letter of Intent by the stated deadline (e.g., May 16, 2025 at 11:59 PM for the FY2026 cycle). structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF) and Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF) – FY2027 Grant Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Two competitive grant programs administered by the Rural Maryland Council and funded through a shared state appropriation. MAERDAF provides grants to nonprofit organizations and community colleges to increase their capacity to meet rural development challenges, establish public/private partnerships, and leverage non-state funding. Eligible activities include statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, and training and technical assistance for agricultural and small businesses. RMPIF promotes economic prosperity in traditionally disadvantaged and underserved rural communities by raising the overall standard of living in rural areas to meet or exceed statewide benchmark averages while preserving cultural heritage and the rural way of life. RMPIF supports significant targeted investments in economic and community development, entrepreneurship, infrastructure, rural health, workforce development, cooperative development, agricultural development, rural community development, and regional and intergovernmental cooperation. In Western Maryland, RMPIF funding is combined with the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland's (TCCWMD) Summit Financing Solutions loan fund to improve access to capital for small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses and to provide technical assistance to help businesses secure professional services and financing. Together, these programs support the state's five rural regional councils, rural nonprofits, community colleges, and other rural-serving organizations. Both programs use a two-phase application process (Letter of Intent followed by Full Application) and share the same funding cycle administered by the Rural Maryland Council. A total of $6,047,464 in state operating budget funds is available for FY2027 (the FY2026 cycle had $6,118,485). The two-phase online grant application opened April 20, 2026. RMPIF was established in 2006 and is authorized through June 30, 2030 under state law, with annual appropriations at the Governor's discretion. The RMC is particularly interested in proposals addressing agriculture, energy, rural broadband, healthcare, youth engagement, and workforce/economic development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A total of $6,047,464 in state operating budget funds is available for FY2027 (the FY2026 cycle had $6,118,485). Grants are awarded through a two-phase application process. For MAERDAF, the maximum grant is $25,000 per award; the historical average has been approximately $18,000. Priority is given to MAERDAF applicants with matching funds from non-state sources (equal match from a non-state source in the prior fiscal year or a documented commitment for the current fiscal year), though matching funds are not required. Grants support capacity building, entrepreneurship, infrastructure, rural health care, regional economic development and planning, workforce development, cooperative development, agricultural development, and rural community development. In Western Maryland, RMPIF funding is used alongside TCCWMD's Summit Financing Solutions loan fund to enhance access to capital for small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses. Technical assistance is also provided to help businesses acquire professional services and improve their ability to secure financing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Maryland Foundation Research Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: One-year grants to support applied policy research or identify local strategies that can lead to legislative or program policy recommendations for rural Maryland. Researchers submit a Letter of Intent, and invited applicants then submit a full proposal. Targeted topics for 2023 included transfer of wealth, food distribution, solar development on farmland, rural economic development, and volunteerism. Open topic proposals addressing the Rural Maryland Council's priorities were also considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SWED Ag Grant Fund provides financial assistance to foster growth in Wicomico County's emerging agriculture and resource-based industries. The fund supports new and existing businesses involved in farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, and the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products. It is capitalized through a public-private partnership between SWED, Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) through MARBIDCO's Local Government Agriculture & Resource Based Industry Project Cost Share Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching cost-share grants to support growth in agriculture and resource-based industries in Wicomico County. Standard grant up to $10,000; up to $25,000 under special circumstances. FSMA matching grants capped at $5,000. Deer fences and farm solar/generators capped at $3,000. Annual cap per jurisdiction: $25,000 per fiscal year. Applicants must contribute at least 50% of the total project cost. Grants are one-time payments and are reimbursement-based. Funded through a public-private partnership including SWED, Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and MARBIDCO.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses involved in agriculture and resource-based industries in Wicomico County, including those involved in farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, and the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products. Includes minority-owned, women-owned, and disabled-owned businesses. Nonprofits are not eligible per FAQ guidance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include agri-tourism (new or expansion), agricultural business diversification (new or expansion), deer fencing, farm solar/generators, FSMA compliance projects, and other uses determined by MARBIDCO. Ineligible uses include operating expenses, personal expenses, refinancing, loan payoffs, and vehicles.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SWED Shovel Ready Site program helps Wicomico County better compete for large-scale economic development projects by providing upfront and creative financing to encourage sites that are ready for immediate development. The program targets industrial and manufacturing sites that meet specific infrastructure, zoning, and size requirements, with the goal of attracting major employers and economic development users to the Salisbury-Wicomico region. Financing is typically structured as interest-only loans with principal payment due upon sale or lease, with loan terms determined by committee based on project risk and collateralization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Upfront and creative financing to prepare sites for large-scale economic development, typically structured as interest-only loans with principal payment due upon sale or lease. Loan terms are determined by committee based on project risk and collateralization. Sites must be at least 10 acres or able to support a minimum 100,000 sq ft facility (ideally expandable to 200,000 sq ft), with all utilities on-site, adequate transportation network, and appropriate industrial zoning. The program targets a minimum of 100 jobs and one end user per site.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NextGen Leaders for Public Service program prepares University of Baltimore undergraduate and graduate students from any major to explore careers in public service. structured_extraction.program_description: A zero percent interest deferred loan program designed to help homeowners aged 55 and older make accessibility improvements to their homes so they can age in place. Eligible improvements include installing ramps, widening doorways, adding grab bars, creating first-floor laundry or bathroom facilities, converting hardware to lever-style handles, and adding a bedroom and bath on the main level for the homeowner. Additions for caregivers are considered on a case-by-case basis. Loans are zero percent interest with payments deferred for 30 years, funded through State of Maryland funds, and carry a lien on the property. Monthly payments can be set up at the borrower's request but are not required. The average loan is anticipated to be around $10,000–$15,000 but can be more. The program is administered locally through the Frederick County Senior Services Division (Area Office on Aging), part of the statewide network of 19 local Area Offices on Aging. Repayment is triggered when the home is sold or transferred (unless transferred to a family member who continues to live there as their primary residence); if the homeowner refinances and takes cash out, the loan must be repaid in full. Upon the death of the original borrower, repayment rules depend on whether the new occupant lives in the home as their principal residence. The deferral period may be extended if the borrower is still living in the home and unable to repay at the end of the 30-year term. Rental properties are not eligible, though landlords with 1–4 units may apply to the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program instead. Mobile/manufactured homes must be permanently affixed to a foundation and the applicant must own the land beneath. Condominiums are considered on a case-by-case basis. The program is designed to help seniors avoid moving to assisted living or other facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Senior Services Division, Frederick County / Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest deferred loans with no payments required for 30 years. Monthly payments can be set up at the borrower's request but are not required. There is no set loan limit; the average loan is anticipated to be around $10,000–$15,000 but can be more. Loans are funded through State funds, carry a lien on the property, and are structured as required by State law. Repayment is triggered when the home is sold or transferred (unless transferred to a family member who occupies it as their primary residence), upon the death of the borrower (with some exceptions for family members who continue to occupy the home as their primary residence), or when the homeowner refinances and takes cash out. The deferral period may be extended if the borrower is still living in the home and unable to repay at the end of the 30-year term. DHCD processes a two-party check made out to both the homeowner and contractor as work progresses. All 19 local Area Offices on Aging are accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners aged 55 or older (only one co-owner or occupant needs to meet the age requirement for couples) who want to make accessibility improvements to their principal residence in Frederick County to support aging in place. Must meet established income limits and be the owner of record on the property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements to a principal residence, such as ramps, widened doorways, grab bars, first-floor bathroom or laundry additions, lever-style door and sink hardware, and adding a bedroom and bath on the main level for the homeowner. Additions for caregivers are considered on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland, through the local Area Office on Aging (Frederick County Senior Services Division). Staff can arrange to take the application in the applicant's home if needed. The program is administered statewide through all 19 local Area Offices on Aging in Maryland, with this record specifically covering Frederick County.
requirements_list: Must be at least 55 years old (only one co-owner or occupant needs to meet this requirement for couples)
Home must be the applicant's principal residence
Must meet established income limits
Must be the owner of record on the property; all other names on the deed must provide consent
No outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Mobile/manufactured homes must be permanently affixed to a foundation and the applicant must own the land beneath
Condominiums are considered on a case-by-case basis depending on condominium covenants
Rental properties are not eligible (landlords with 1–4 units may apply to the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program instead)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local Area Office on Aging to apply. All 19 local Area Offices on Aging accept applications. Staff can come to the applicant's home to take the application if needed. An inspector from DHCD staff or local government housing network staff will inspect the property and prepare a work write-up listing all work to be done. The homeowner then solicits contractor bids based on the write-up and hires a contractor. As work progresses, an inspector authorizes payments to the contractor after the homeowner confirms the work is satisfactory; DHCD processes a two-party check made out to both the homeowner and contractor, who signs it and delivers it to the contractor.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County's Property Tax Challenge offers a property tax incentive to encourage investment in commercial real property in designated challenged areas. Commercial property owners who invest at least 10% of the property's assessed value (minimum $25,000) in eligible improvements — such as exterior façade work, structural improvements, signage, canopies, landscaping, and new construction — are eligible to apply. Investments of 10–15% of assessed value qualify for a 7-year property tax freeze, while investments of 16% or more qualify for a 10-year freeze, meaning County property taxes are held constant with no increase in assessed value or tax rate for the duration. The investment must be made as a one-time expenditure within a 12-month period, and the total value of the assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award. The County Commissioners review applications and decide whether to award the incentive. If approved, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement is executed outlining project details, anticipated outcomes, timeline, and terms.

The total value of the assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award. If approved by the County Commissioners, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement is prepared and signed by both parties.

structured_extraction.program_description: Opportunity Zones (O-Zones) are federally designated areas targeted for economic development. Investors who direct capital gains into the Lexington Park Opportunity Zone in St. Mary's County can receive special federal tax benefits, including deferral of capital gains taxes, a reduction in the tax owed after 5 or 7 years of investment, and a permanent exemption from capital gains tax on gains accrued after 10 years of investment. Eligible investments include single-asset real estate, company stock in O-Zone-based startups, and privately managed Opportunity Funds (O-Funds) that hold at least 90% of assets in O-Zones.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tiered federal tax benefits for investors who invest capital gains in the Lexington Park Opportunity Zone within 180 days of a capital gain event: (1) Immediate deferral of capital gains tax payments until December 31, 2026; (2) Up to 10% reduction in tax owed after a 5-year investment, or up to 15% after a 7-year investment; (3) Permanent exemption from capital gains tax on gains accrued after a 10-year investment in an Opportunity Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Invest within 180 days of capital gain event; tax deferral available until December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with capital gains seeking tax advantages by investing in designated Opportunity Zone areas in Lexington Park, St. Mary's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in single-asset real estate, company stock in O-Zone-based startups, or Opportunity Funds (O-Funds) located within the Lexington Park Opportunity Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Investment must be made within the Lexington Park Opportunity Zone in St. Mary's County, Maryland, which coincides with the Lexington Park Redevelopment District Master Plan area.
requirements_list: Investor must have realized a capital gain triggering the investment.
Investment must be made within 180 days of the capital gain event.
Investment must be directed into the designated Lexington Park Opportunity Zone.
For O-Fund investments, the fund must hold at least 90% of its assets in Opportunity Zones.
For the 10-year tax exemption, investment must be held for at least 10 years in an Opportunity Fund.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development (Chris Kaselemis) for guidance. Invest capital gains into an eligible O-Zone investment vehicle (real estate LLC, company stock, or an Opportunity Fund) within 180 days of the capital gain event.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Agricultural Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A county tax credit for landowners in St. Mary's County who participate in agricultural preservation districts. Landowners enter into a five-year agreement to keep their land in agricultural use in exchange for a tax credit.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county-level tax credit for landowners who join an agricultural preservation district. Participation requires a five-year agreement to maintain the land in agricultural use.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in St. Mary's County who want to keep their land in agricultural use and receive a tax credit in return.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against county taxes for participating agricultural preservation district landowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Landowner must enter into a five-year Agricultural Tax Credit Agreement
Land must be maintained in agricultural use for the term of the agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the St. Mary's County Agricultural Preservation District Tax Credit Application and the five-year Agricultural Tax Credit Agreement Form. Contact the Agriculture and Seafood Division for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Façade and Streetscape Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses commercial property and business owners for expenses incurred rehabilitating their buildings, storefronts, and adjacent streetscapes. The goal is to create positive visual impact, stimulate private investment, improve safety, and support community revitalization in designated areas of Lexington Park and Charlotte Hall. Funding comes from a Community Legacy grant from Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses 50% of eligible project costs, with a maximum reimbursement of $6,000 per address per calendar year. Projects must rehabilitate buildings, storefronts, or adjacent streetscapes within the designated grant area (the 'Downtown' and 'Great Mills Corridor' of Lexington Park as defined in the Lexington Park Master Plan, or the Charlotte Hall Sustainable Communities footprint). The project must be completed within six (6) months after Grant Agreement execution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and business owners (with property owner permission) located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park or the Charlotte Hall Sustainable Communities footprint.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of commercial building exteriors, storefronts, and streetscapes adjacent to eligible properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the designated Façade and Streetscape Grant Area — the 'Downtown' and 'Great Mills Corridor' of Lexington Park as defined in the Lexington Park Master Plan, or the Charlotte Hall Sustainable Communities footprint.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the designated Façade and Streetscape Grant Area
Proposed work must align with eligible reimbursement projects per Program Guidelines
Must use licensed and insured contractors
Limited to one application per address per calendar year
Business owners must have written permission from the property/building owner
Application must be complete and accurate
Must be a commercial property owner or business owner in Lexington Park or Charlotte Hall
Must complete a qualifying project rehabilitating a building, storefront, or adjacent streetscape
Only non-residential and multi-use buildings are eligible; tenants must have written authorization from the property owner
Application cannot be saved and returned to — it must be completed in a single session
The project must be completed within six (6) months after Grant Agreement execution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Confirm property is in the grant area, verify the scope of work aligns with eligible projects, obtain contractor estimates, identify the reimbursement amount requested (50% of project cost, max $6,000), gather required documents, and submit via the online application form. Note that the application cannot be saved and returned to — it must be completed in a single session. Incomplete applications may result in ineligibility. Complete applications are scored using a points-based review committee criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) grant program provides federal funding to reduce flood risk to homes insured under the National Flood Insurance Program. St. Mary's County residents whose homes are at high risk for flood damage can inquire about applying. The St. Mary's County Department of Emergency Services (DES) applies on behalf of eligible homeowners as a subrecipient of funding received from FEMA through the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). Projects are selected based on eligibility, ranking, and cost-effectiveness. Submission of an application does not guarantee funding.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Emergency Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover 75% of the total eligible project cost (federal share), with homeowners required to provide 25% of the total project cost in an escrow account upon approval. Projects are ranked by MDEM and then FEMA before funding is awarded. Once approved, funding release and project start may take approximately one to two additional years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual basis; due dates communicated each year based on fund availability from FEMA
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County homeowners whose homes are at high risk for flood damage and are actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood damage mitigation projects for residential properties located in a flood zone
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within a flood zone in St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Home must be actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
Home must be located within a flood zone
Homeowner must be willing and able to commit to providing 25% of the total project cost in an escrow account upon approval
Elevation Certificate required
Copy of NFIP Declaration required
Documentation of previous losses due to flooding (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Email EMA@stmaryscountymd.gov with required documents (Elevation Certificate, NFIP Declaration, documentation of prior flood losses if applicable) and express interest in applying. 2. Emergency Management staff will contact you about the next available application cycle and any additional requirements. 3. Staff will work with you to obtain project proposals and additional documentation, then submit the application on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County FIRE/EMS Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An Extended Education Scholarship program for active members of St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Departments, Rescue Squads, or Advance Life Support Units. Awards support courses leading to a certificate, diploma, or other evidence of qualification from a recognized post-secondary educational facility. Award amount is determined by the number of credit hours planned, cost per credit hour, and a properly submitted application. Reimbursement equals the lesser of the scholarship award or actual cost, limited to a maximum of 36 credit hours per year. Payment is processed after satisfactory course completion (minimum 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale) and grade verification. Applications are submitted to the Department of Emergency Services for consideration.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Emergency Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual reimbursement-based scholarship awards for tuition and course materials. Award amount is determined by the number of credit hours planned, cost per credit hour, and a properly submitted application. Reimbursement equals the lesser of the scholarship award or actual cost. Limited to a maximum of 36 credit hours per year. Payment is processed after satisfactory course completion (minimum 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale) and grade verification. Bookstore receipts are required for course materials reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active members of a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advance Life Support Unit (LOSAP-qualified) interested in pursuing fire and EMS education or training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and course materials (bookstore receipts required) for courses leading to a certificate, diploma, or other evidence of qualification from a recognized post-secondary educational facility. Limited to a maximum of 36 credit hours per year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an active member of a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advance Life Support Unit (LOSAP-qualified)
Application must be received on or before 31 August 2025
Must submit completed application form, signed Agreement, IRS W-9, and acceptance letter(s)
Coursework must fall within the eligibility window of 1 July 2025 through 30 June 2026 (FY2026 cycle)
Minimum 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale required for satisfactory course completion to trigger reimbursement payment
Bookstore receipts required for course materials reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form, signed Agreement, IRS W-9, and acceptance letter(s) to Angel Clem by 31 August. Mail to: St. Mary's County Emergency Services, Attention: Angel Clem, Post Office Box 653, Leonardtown, MD 20650-0653. Notification of award on or about 30 October. Payment is processed after grade verification confirming satisfactory completion (minimum 2.0 GPA).

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteer Fire & EMS Recruitment and Retention Incentives
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers a range of incentives to recruit and retain volunteers at its fire departments, rescue squads, and Advanced Life Support unit. Incentives include college scholarship programs, a length of service award program, a dependent care reimbursement program, and a Maryland State tax incentive after three years of service. Training to become a certified firefighter or EMT is provided at no cost. A Fire and E.M.S. Cadet Program is also available for high school juniors and seniors.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Emergency Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Incentives include college scholarships, a length of service award program, dependent care reimbursement, and a Maryland State tax incentive after three years of volunteer service. Free training is provided to become a certified firefighter or EMT.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Citizens interested in volunteering at fire departments and rescue squads in St. Mary's County, including those who want to become certified firefighters or EMTs and those interested in administrative or fundraising roles. Active members must be 18+; Junior members ages 16–17; Cadet members ages 13–15; Auxiliary/Associate members ages 11+. A Fire and E.M.S. Cadet Program is available for high school juniors and seniors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College education, length of service awards, dependent care expenses, and tax reduction after three years of volunteer service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland. Participating departments are located in Leonardtown, Mechanicsville, Bay District, Lexington Park, Ridge, Seventh District, Hollywood, and Second District. Mutual aid extends to surrounding counties and the Patuxent River Naval Air Station.
requirements_list: Must volunteer at a fire department or rescue squad in St. Mary's County
Maryland State tax incentive requires at least three years of service
Fire & EMS Cadet Program requires applicant to be a junior or senior in high school
Must maintain a 'C' average (2.0 GPA) if attending high school
All organizations require CPR training and orientation (pre-basic) course to start
Minimum age varies by membership type: Active members must be 18+; Junior members 16–17; Cadets 13–15; Auxiliary members 11+ in some organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Emergency Services Recruitment & Retention Coordinator at 301-475-4200 ext. 2114 or FireEMSRecruitment@stmaryscountymd.gov for more information, or visit one of the participating volunteer fire department or rescue squad websites in St. Mary's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Nonprofit Distribution Proposals (NPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County distributes public funds to nonprofit organizations that provide services to county residents in areas including behavioral health, community services, disability services, homeless prevention, conservation of natural resources, economic development, workforce development, community events, cultural activities, and historical and heritage interpretation. Proposals are evaluated by county department staff.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Finance
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County grant funding distributed to nonprofits through a competitive proposal process. Applicants may only submit one application per organization, and must submit separate proposals for each funding category they wish to be considered under. Grant recipients must submit a semi-annual performance report due January 15, 2026 and an annual report due July 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations serving St. Mary's County residents in areas of behavioral health, community services, disability services, homeless prevention, natural resources conservation, economic development, workforce development, community events, cultural activities, and historical interpretation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services in the following categories: behavioral health, community services, disability services, homeless prevention, conservation of natural resources, economic development, workforce development, community events, cultural activities, and historical and heritage interpretation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs and services must serve residents of St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization in good standing with the State
Must submit Contact Information Form, Revenue & Expenditures, Summary of Changes, Project Budget Summary, and Selected Statistics
Must upload an Executive Summary, Audited Financial Statement (latest version if required), and IRS Form 990 (most recent filing)
Must attend a Nonprofit Institute class and supply attendance certificate
Only one application per nonprofit organization will be accepted
Separate complete NPP packages must be submitted for each category
Grant recipients must submit semi-annual performance report due 01/15/2026 and annual report due 07/15/2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete NPP package online at www.stmaryscountymd.gov/finance/nonprofit by January 12, 2026. Packages must include all required online fillable forms and uploaded documents. An online training class on how to navigate the application process was held on December 4, 2025. Contact nonprofithelp@stmaryscountymd.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides new, internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) to eligible households in St. Mary's County who cannot afford a connected device. The program is designed to support digital equity and inclusion efforts in Maryland by giving low-income families the technology needed to access the internet.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Information Technologies
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive a new internet-enabled HP Chromebook 14 G7 (or similar) device. St. Mary's County was approved for 4,500 devices valued at $894,375, plus $27,000 in grant funding to support distribution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in St. Mary's County who lack a connected device to access the internet.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of new internet-enabled Chromebook devices to eligible households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible households throughout St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible household in St. Mary's County
Must be in need of a connected device to access the internet
See eligibility requirements page for full criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-register online at the county's Connected Devices page to receive an HP Chromebook.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County works with existing cable service providers to extend wired broadband connectivity to unserved residential addresses ('last mile' locations). When eligible participants are identified, the county initiates a grant process to fund the infrastructure extension needed to connect those unserved addresses to the existing cable plant. Grants are funded by American Rescue Plan (ARP) funds totaling approximately $5.7 million, approved in multiple rounds in 2021 and 2022.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Information Technologies
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by American Rescue Plan (ARP) funds totaling approximately $5.7 million (approved in multiple rounds in 2021 and 2022) to extend wired broadband to unserved 'last mile' addresses in St. Mary's County. Eligible participants are identified by the county and then the grant process is initiated on their behalf. Addresses must meet BUS Grant maximum distance threshold; cost-sharing may apply for addresses beyond threshold.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners and occupants in St. Mary's County, Maryland whose addresses are mapped as 'Last Mile' (unserved or underserved for wired broadband).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extending wired broadband cable infrastructure to unserved residential addresses in St. Mary's County, including construction of last-mile connectivity from the existing cable plant to eligible addresses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to unserved or underserved addresses in St. Mary's County, Maryland, as determined by the county's Broadband Availability Check tool.
requirements_list: Address must be in St. Mary's County
Address must not currently have access to wired broadband service
Address must be identified as eligible ('Last Mile') through the county's Broadband Availability Check tool
Address must meet BUS Grant maximum distance threshold; cost-sharing may apply for addresses beyond threshold
Applicant must register contact information and submit a digitally signed grant application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm eligibility via the Broadband Availability Check tool at www.stmarysmd.com/broadband. 2. Register contact information to automatically receive updates for the address. 3. County performs a vendor assessment and cost confirmation. 4. Grant application is sent to the applicant via email; applicant digitally signs and submits; county approves and returns a copy. 5. County coordinates construction scheduling with the cable provider and issues a purchase order; provider schedules installation. 6. County notifies applicant upon completion. 7. Applicant signs up for service with the cable provider. 8. County issues payment to provider. Note: Exact construction dates cannot be guaranteed due to weather and supply chain variability.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows property owners in St. Mary's County to transfer Sewer Equivalent Dwelling Units (EDUs) — the allocated capacity to connect to the public sewer system — from one property or owner to another. Parties can file a Notice of Intent to Transfer and submit an application to receive EDUs. Both sending and receiving properties must be within the same wastewater treatment plant service area, and the receiving property must be in the correct sewerage Service Category (S-1 or S-3D) per the Comprehensive Water and Sewer Plan (CWSP). A Standard Operating Procedure (LUGM SOP24-0002, revised September 19, 2025) governs the process.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Land Use & Growth Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows the transfer of Sewer EDU capacity allocations between properties or owners. The Sending Property must have inactive (unconnected) EDUs, and the Receiving Property must demonstrate need (failing onsite system or development permit application). Participants must file a Notice of Intent to Transfer and complete an Application to Receive Sewer EDUs. A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP, LUGM SOP24-0002, revised September 19, 2025) governs the process. Applications may be filed at any time as part of the development review process. Price per EDU is negotiated privately between parties. A $20 application fee applies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners (residential or commercial, including individuals, LLCs, corporations, and other entities) in St. Mary's County who hold or need sewer EDU capacity allocations, including owners of sending and receiving properties within the same wastewater treatment plant service area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transfer of sewer system connection capacity (EDUs) from one party or property to another. The Sending Property must retain EDUs sufficient for existing/approved uses. Price per EDU is negotiated privately between the transferring parties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland only. Both sending and receiving properties must be within the same wastewater treatment plant service area and the receiving property must be in the correct sewerage Service Category (S-1 or S-3D) per the Comprehensive Water and Sewer Plan (CWSP).
requirements_list: File a Notice of Intent to Transfer Sewer EDU(s)
Sending Property must have inactive (unconnected) EDU(s)
Sending Property must retain EDUs sufficient for existing/approved uses
Receiving Property must demonstrate need (failing onsite system or development permit application)
Department publishes Notice on its webpage within 5 business days
30-day waiting period after Notice publication before Application to Receive can be filed (unless an exemption applies)
Exemptions to the 30-day notice period: transfers to self, lineal descendant, sibling, spouse, or entity with cross-ownership (per LUGM SOP24-0002 § 2.1.3.1)
Submit an Affidavit certifying no agreement was reached with failing-septic-system owners during the notice period, or claiming an eligible exemption
Submit an Application to Receive Sewer EDU(s) at time of development review for the Receiving Property
Receiving Property must be in the correct sewerage Service Category (S-1 or S-3D) per CWSP
Both properties must be within the same wastewater treatment plant service area
All MetCom accounts must be in good standing
Pay $20 application fee
Follow the Standard Operating Procedure (LUGM SOP24-0002, revised 9-19-2025)
Director approval triggers Certificate of Transfer execution and recording in Land Records
Certificate recorded and allocation letter sent to MetCom for billing adjustment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. File a Notice of Intent to Transfer Sewer EDUs with the Department. 2. Department publishes the Notice on its webpage within 5 business days. 3. Wait 30 days after publication before filing the Application to Receive Sewer EDUs (unless an eligible exemption applies per LUGM SOP24-0002 § 2.1.3.1). 4. File an Affidavit certifying compliance with the notice-period requirements (or claiming an eligible exemption). 5. Submit the Application to Receive Sewer EDUs (with signatures from owners of both sending and receiving properties) and pay the $20 application fee at the time of development review for the Receiving Property. 6. Upon Director approval, a Certificate of Transfer is executed and recorded in Land Records. 7. Certificate is recorded and an allocation letter is sent to MetCom for billing adjustment. Applications may be filed at any time as part of the development review process. Contact the Department at (301) 475-4200, ext. 1500 or MetCom at (301) 737-7400 to confirm sewer facility details.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County can establish Special Drainage Districts to allow landowners to collectively fund drainage improvements in their subdivisions and neighborhoods. Design, construction, and interest costs are assessed to all benefited properties over up to 15 years. The County may also maintain the system and allocate maintenance costs as a perpetual annual assessment.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Drainage improvement costs (design, construction, interest) are spread equitably across all benefited properties over a period not to exceed 15 years. The County may maintain the system with ongoing annual maintenance assessments allocated to the district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods experiencing recurring drainage problems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, and maintenance of storm drainage improvements within a special taxing district.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Submit a petition signed by more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a petition with signatures from more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district. Contact the Department of Public Works & Transportation at (301) 475-4200 for procedures, or access procedures online.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County can create Special Taxing Districts to fund the upgrading of substandard subdivision roads to meet County Highway Maintenance System standards. The County borrows the construction funds, and benefited lot owners repay principal and interest over up to 20 years through a special tax assessment. Property owners bear design, construction, and utility costs; the County bears administrative, preliminary engineering, and inspection costs. Roads eligible for consideration must have been constructed prior to January 1, 1977, and must connect to an existing street or road in the County Highway Maintenance System or maintained by the State.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County finances road construction by borrowing funds. Benefited lot owners repay costs of principal and interest over a period not to exceed 20 years through special tax assessments. Property owners bear design, construction, and utility costs; the County bears administrative, preliminary engineering, and inspection costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lot owners in St. Mary's County subdivisions with substandard roads seeking to have roads accepted into the County Highway Maintenance System.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Upgrading substandard subdivision roads to make them suitable for acceptance into the County Highway Maintenance System.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland only. Subdivision streets or roads constructed prior to January 1, 1977 are eligible for consideration. Roads must connect to an existing street or road either in the County Highway Maintenance System or maintained by the State.
requirements_list: Submit initial Letter of Interest (Step 1) to initiate the process
Participate in formal public informational meeting
Road must be substandard and not in the County Highway Maintenance System
Road must have been constructed prior to January 1, 1977
Road must connect to an existing street or road in the County Highway Maintenance System or maintained by the State
Two-thirds (2/3) of benefited property owners must petition to advance from the informational phase to formal establishment ordinance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Public Works at (301) 475-4200 for a copy of the formal Policy outlining procedures. Refer to the Special Taxing District Procedures document. Process includes: (1) submission of a Letter of Interest, (2) public informational meeting, (3) two-thirds petition by benefited property owners, (4) ordinance preparation, (5) public hearing, (6) budget request, (7) construction, and (8) acceptance phases.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Statewide Specialized Transportation Assistance Program (SSTAP) provides door-to-door transportation for elderly residents and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who are not close enough to use regular public transportation routes. The program operates a zone-based schedule across the county, serving different areas on different days of the week. Riders are transported to medical appointments, senior nutrition centers, and other destinations. The program is funded by the State of Maryland with a required local match.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Public Works, Transportation Division
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Door-to-door transportation service provided at a discounted fare of $6.00 round trip (one stop). Additional stops cost $3.00 each. Between $130,000 and $175,000 in annual grant funding supports the program, with a required local match. Over 17,000 riders use the service each year. Preference is given to individuals with scheduled medical appointments, on a first-come, first-served basis. Wheelchair accessible vehicles with platform lifts are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly residents (seniors 60+) and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who lack access to regular public transportation routes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments, senior nutrition centers, shopping, weekly recurring appointments (such as dialysis and therapy), and other destinations. Service is door-to-door within designated zone areas on scheduled days, Monday through Saturday.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in five zones covering communities throughout St. Mary's County, including Charlotte Hall, Leonardtown, California, Lexington Park, Piney Point, and surrounding areas. Service area is within ¾ mile of existing STS public transportation routes.
requirements_list: Must be elderly (senior 60+) or a person with a disability
Must not be sufficiently close to regular public transportation routes
Seniors must present proof of age to receive discount fares
Appointments must be scheduled appropriately between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m.
Appointments can be made up to 30 days in advance
Continuous no-shows may be denied transportation
A paratransit application must be completed to qualify
Disability certification requires evaluation within 21 days and notification of results within 5 days
Re-certification required every 2 years for disability-based eligibility
All persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County are to be given an opportunity for certification under one of four eligibility criteria categories
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the STS Transit office by phone at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 or 1121, or by email at SDispatchers@stmaryscountymd.gov. Office hours are Monday–Saturday, 8 AM–5 PM. Special identification cards are available and issued by the STS Transit office at 44829 St. Andrews Church Road, California, MD 20619. For ADA paratransit certification, an application will be mailed to the person requesting certification; eligibility is evaluated within 21 days and results are communicated within 5 days; an ID card is issued upon approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Preservation Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit available to owners of historic landmarks and properties in local historic districts in St. Mary's County. Property owners who rehabilitate or maintain qualifying historic properties may receive a credit against their real property tax bill. The credit applies commencing the tax year after the completion year of qualifying work, and unused credit may carry forward up to 4 subsequent tax years.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Historic Preservation Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against St. Mary's County real property taxes for qualifying historic landmark properties and properties in local historic districts. The credit applies commencing the tax year after the completion year of qualifying work. Unused credit may carry forward up to 4 subsequent tax years. The tax credit is non-refundable and may carry forward up to four subsequent tax years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic landmark properties and properties located in local historic districts in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation, maintenance, or improvements to qualifying historic properties. Applicant must itemize work by description and estimated cost. Work must conform to building permits and Historic Preservation Commission standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland — properties located within local historic districts or designated as historic landmarks.
requirements_list: Property must be a designated historic landmark or located within a local historic district
Must submit a Historic Preservation Tax Credit Application with photos and cost proposal before work begins
Application must be submitted prior to the start of work
Work must conform to building permits and Historic Preservation Commission standards
Applicant must submit receipts for actual expenditures to HPC for review and final approval after work is completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application (with photos and cost proposal) before work begins — the application must be submitted prior to the start of work. The Historic Preservation Commission reviews and grants preliminary approval. Applicant completes the approved work. Applicant then submits receipts for actual expenditures to HPC for review and final approval before recommendation to County Commissioners. If approved, the tax credit applies to St. Mary's County real estate taxes commencing the tax year after the completion year. Unused credit may carry forward up to 4 subsequent tax years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship fund that helps St. Mary's County residents afford summer camp programs offered by the county's Recreation & Parks department. Scholarships provide a prorated reduction off registration fees for eligible youth and adults, funded by local civic organization contributions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships provide a prorated reduction off registration fees for one camp program and one sport/leisure program per family, up to a maximum amount per calendar year. Funding comes from local civic organization contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st of each year, prior to open camp registration
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents ages 5–20 who receive Free or Reduced Lunch from St. Mary's County Public Schools (SMCPS) or are enrolled at Community Eligibility Provision schools, and adults 18+ with a Maryland Independence Card. Excludes those receiving Purchase of Care or DSS/other County or State funding for summer programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer camp registration fees and sport/leisure program registration fees (prorated reduction off registration fees for one camp program and one sport/leisure program per family per calendar year, up to a maximum amount).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland. Only current St. Mary's County residents will be considered for scholarship.
requirements_list: Must be a current St. Mary's County resident (only St. Mary's County residents will be considered)

Ages 5–20 who receive Free or Reduced Lunch from St. Mary's County Public Schools (SMCPS), OR ages 5–20 enrolled at a Community Eligibility Provision school, OR adults 18+ with a Maryland Independence Card
Must not be receiving Purchase of Care or DSS/other County or State funding for summer programs
Applications must be completed and submitted prior to the designated deadline each year, prior to open camp registration on March 1st of each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed scholarship application form via CivicPlus (online platform) prior to the annual deadline of March 1st. Applicants must provide proof of eligibility: a Free or Reduced Lunch Approval Form (for students ages 5–20), proof of enrollment at a Community Eligibility Provision school, or a Maryland Independence Card (for adults 18+). Applicants should indicate the requested weeks of assistance. Contact RPinfo@stmaryscountymd.gov or 301-475-4200 ext. 1800 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Senior Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers three property tax credit programs for senior citizens who own and occupy their principal residence in the county. (1) Senior Matching Tax Credit — matches the credit received from the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit for seniors age 70 or older; (2) Senior CAP Tax Credit — freezes county tax liability at the base year amount for seniors age 70 or older with household taxable net income at or below $80,000; (3) 65-10 Senior Tax Credit — provides a 10% credit off county tax liability for up to 5 years for seniors age 65 or older who are retired active-duty military or have held their deed for at least 40 years, with assessed value under $400,000 and income at or below $80,000. The Treasurer's Office evaluates each application and applies the most valuable credit. Applications must be submitted annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three county property tax credit options applied to county tax liability: (1) Matching Tax Credit matches the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit for seniors age 70+; (2) CAP Tax Credit freezes county tax liability at the base year level for seniors age 70+ with income ≤$80,000; (3) 65-10 Tax Credit provides 10% off county tax liability for up to 5 years for eligible seniors age 65+. Only one credit is applied per account per tax year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 1, 2026 (preferred); applications received after May 1 but before September 1 may still be eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens age 65 or older (age 70+ for Matching and CAP credits) who own and occupy their principal residence in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property tax liability on primary dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal residence must be located in St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years old (or 70 for Matching/CAP credits) as of July 1 of the tax year
Property must be the applicant's principal residence in St. Mary's County
For CAP and 65-10 credits: household taxable net income must be $80,000 or less
For 65-10 credit: assessed property value must be less than $400,000
For 65-10 credit: must be a retired active-duty military member OR have name on the deed for at least 40 years as of July 1
For Matching Tax Credit: must also receive the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit
Must submit application annually with required documentation

Required documents: 2025 Maryland or Federal Income Tax Return (or SSA-1099/retirement income proof if no return filed); proof of age for first-time applicants; proof of military retirement (DD214) for first-time applicants if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application at the Treasurer's Office website, answer all 9 eligibility questions, attach required documents (proof of income, age, and military retirement if applicable), sign the application, and submit. Applications received before May 1 may appear on the tax bill; applications received May 1–September 1 may still receive a credit. Assistance is also available through St. Mary's County Department of Aging & Human Services at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1064, 1654, or 3104, and at all senior activity centers in St. Mary's County.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 or older who do not have a high school diploma and need to prepare for the GED exam.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED test preparation covering math, science, social studies, and language arts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Based at the Stanton Community Center in Annapolis, MD.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must not have a high school diploma
Must attend an orientation through AACC before registering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AACC at gedprogram@aacc.edu or 410-777-1823 to schedule a required orientation. Register for the class after completing orientation.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a property tax credit. It encourages new and existing businesses to move to or expand in state-designated enterprise zones. These zones are in economically distressed areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps children drink more milk. It provides money to public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites. The funds help lower the cost of milk served to children.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps at-risk children from birth to age six and their families prepare for school. It gives grants to child care providers. Providers can use the funds for accreditation and staff training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Switch Together Solar Group Purchasing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Switch Together is a cooperative (group) purchasing program that helps homeowners and small businesses buy rooftop solar panels, battery storage, and electric vehicle charging stations at reduced prices. Frederick County participates in this regional program, which organizes a reverse auction among pre-vetted contractors to secure competitive group pricing. A typical project is expected to save participants at least $6,500 on a solar panel purchase and installation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants join a group purchasing pool that secures discounted pricing on rooftop solar panels, battery storage, and EV charging stations through a reverse auction. A typical project saves at least $6,500 compared to standard pricing. Registration is free and there is no obligation to purchase. A small, fully refundable deposit is required only if the participant chooses to accept a customized offer and lock in a contract.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens each spring and fall
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and small business owners in the MD-VA-DC region, with Frederick County participation encouraged
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of rooftop solar panels, battery storage systems, and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and small businesses in Frederick County, Maryland, as part of the broader MD-VA-DC regional program
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner or small business owner
Must be able to have solar panels installed at home or small business site
Registration requires basic contact information, home details, and current energy usage or costs
Roof suitability must be verified by the installer before installation proceeds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online for free at SwitchTogether.com/Solar/FrederickCounty with no obligation to purchase. You receive a customized offer based on your registration details. You decide whether to accept the offer. If you choose to proceed, you pay a small, 100% refundable deposit to lock in the contract. The installer verifies your roof and confirms the package cost. If you proceed, an installation date is set.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the TTAP website at https://www.targeted-tap.org/ for participation details.
