structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) provides grants to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing Best Available Technology (BAT) units, including a two-year operations and maintenance package, or to fund sewer connections for existing dwellings where public sewer is available. The program's goal is to reduce harmful nutrients like nitrogen that septic systems discharge into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Talbot County locally administers the state-supported program.
structured_extraction.agency: Talbot County Department of Public Works
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover the cost and installation of a BAT septic system plus a two-year operations and maintenance package. Funding levels vary by income: households with income under $300,000 may receive 100% of the BAT unit cost; households with income over $300,000 may receive 50%. Business-owned properties (e.g., LLCs) are eligible for 50%, or up to 75% if the owner qualifies as a small business. Non-profit organizations are eligible for 100% of the BAT unit cost. New construction projects require a $1,200 deductible from the grant amount. Low-income applicants may also receive funding for non-BAT components such as drain fields.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Talbot County with conventional septic systems, including residential owners, businesses, and non-profits, seeking to upgrade to nitrogen-reducing BAT septic systems or connect to public sewer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost and installation of a Best Available Technology (BAT) septic system, two-year operations and maintenance package, and for low-income applicants, repairs or replacement of non-BAT components such as drain fields. May also fund sewer connections where public sewer is available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Talbot County, Maryland. Properties in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of tidal waters) receive higher priority.
requirements_list: Submit a completed application including all required documents
Provide a Public Works Agreement (PWA) signed by all property owners before a notary
Provide a copy of the current year's Federal Tax Return (Form 1040) for all owners; trusts or life estates must submit income info for all listed owners
Obtain an SB554 Letter of Determination from the Office of Environmental Health (OEH)
Provide a copy of the approved Sanitary Construction Permit from OEH
Provide a Three-Way Agreement signed by the BAT unit vendor, property owner, and septic contractor
Provide proof of income (copy of 2024 Federal Income Tax Return) for applicants seeking 100% funding; non-filers must provide an IRS verification transcript or non-filing status letter
For low-income applicants requiring non-BAT components, submit three contractor bids for DPW and MDE approval
If any owner listed on the deed is deceased, provide a copy of the death certificate
Non-profit organizations must submit federal income tax Form 990 as verification
Additional information may be required per Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Talbot County Department of Public Works to initiate a Public Works Agreement. Gather all required documents including tax returns, OEH letters and permits, and contractor agreements. Submit the complete application package to Public Works. Applicants are placed on a funding list upon receipt of complete documentation and are prioritized based on septic system status and location relative to the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area.
attachment_urls: https://www.talbotcountymd.gov/departments/publicworks/resources-4/uploads/File/publicworks/Bay%20Restoration Fund/OSDS BRF BAT Funding Summary FY2026.pdf

structured_extraction.program_description: Remote Conference Captioning (RCC) is a free real-time captioning service for people with hearing loss who participate in conference calls. A captionist listens to the call and types everything said, streaming the text to the user's internet-connected device within seconds. No special software is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free real-time captioning of conference calls delivered via streaming text to any internet-connected device. Users must schedule at least 24 hours in advance by submitting the RCC Scheduling Request Form. No special software is needed, but access to a conference bridge or high-quality audio is required.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real-time captioning of conference call audio so that users with hearing loss can read the conversation as text on their device.

requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident, business, or organization

Must submit the RCC Scheduling Request Form at least 24 hours in advance of the call
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the RCC Scheduling Request Form at hamiltonrelay.com at least 24 hours before the scheduled call. The user will receive an email with a link to view captions on their computer or mobile device.

Grant awards range from $1,000 to $10,000 and fund technology literacy programs, public awareness campaigns, and direct communication services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 for projects that enhance communication access. Activities must be completed by March 31, 2026. A final programmatic and financial report is required within 30 calendar days of project completion and no later than April 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, May 7, 2025, no later than 5 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations serving Marylanders who are Deaf, hard of hearing, late-deafened, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, or speech difficulties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology literacy initiatives (training workshops, curriculum development), public awareness campaigns (educational videos, accessible communication tools), and direct services (interpreters, CART services for events). Preference given to direct programming over administrative or organizational costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Communication Facilitator (CF) service provides DeafBlind Marylanders with equal access to communication. A skilled signer (the Communication Facilitator) copies sign language from a video caller and conveys it to the DeafBlind consumer through close-vision, tactile sign language, tracking, or other methods. The service is provided through the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program and supports video calls over any platform — including VP, Video Relay Services, FaceTime, Zoom, Skype, and Google Meet — and can be initiated at home, at a library, coffee shop, or other public space. Available communication modalities include Spoken English, Spoken English with sign language, Close-Visual Sign Language, Tracking, Tactile Sign Language, and ProTactile.
structured_extraction.agency: Telecommunications Access of Maryland (TAM), Maryland Department of Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free communication facilitation service for DeafBlind consumers. A Communication Facilitator assists during video calls by relaying sign language between the DeafBlind individual and a video caller using close-vision, tactile sign language, tracking, ProTactile, or other communication methods. Service scheduling and matching is handled through the MAT program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DeafBlind Marylanders (individuals with combined hearing and vision loss) who have been approved by the MAT program via the DeafBlind Consumer Application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Communication facilitation during video calls with friends, family, coworkers, and others, conducted at the consumer's residence, library, coffee shop, or other specified location.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents who are DeafBlind.
requirements_list: Must be a Marylander living with combined hearing and vision loss (DeafBlind)
Must complete the Communication Facilitator Service DeafBlind Consumer Application
Must be approved by the MAT program before requesting services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DeafBlind Consumer Application (available at MDRelay.org) for approval by the MAT program. Once approved, submit the Communication Facilitator Service Request Form to CF.Scheduler@Maryland.gov to schedule services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program provides free assistive telecommunications equipment to qualified Maryland residents who have difficulty using a standard telephone due to a disability. Eligible participants receive a free one-on-one evaluation with a MAT specialist (in-person at statewide evaluation centers or virtually) to identify the right equipment solution, which is then shipped to their home. Equipment options include amplified phones, captioned telephones, TTYs, Braille TTYs, large-button phones, picture/photo dial phones, hands-free phones, wheelchair pad phone switches, HCO (Hearing Carry-Over) phones, tablets, and other adaptive communication devices. The program can also create custom solutions based on individual needs. Equipment remains state property and is on long-term loan to the recipient; it must be returned if the recipient moves out of state. The program serves people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties. Applicants must be age 3 or older and meet income eligibility criteria. Each device comes with personalized setup instructions, and initial and additional free training is available by contacting the MAT evaluator.
structured_extraction.agency: Telecommunications Access of Maryland (TAM), Maryland Department of Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state-supplied assistive telecommunications equipment at no cost to approved applicants on a long-term loan basis. Equipment types include amplified phones, captioned telephones, TTYs, Braille TTYs, large-button phones, photo dial phones, hands-free phones, wheelchair pad phone switches, HCO phones, tablets, and other adaptive devices. A free one-on-one evaluation with a MAT specialist (virtual or in-person at statewide MAT evaluation centers) is conducted to match participants with appropriate equipment, which is then shipped to the recipient's home via UPS within 4–6 weeks of approval. Each device comes with personalized setup instructions; initial training is included with the evaluation, and additional free training is available by contacting the MAT evaluator. Equipment remains state property on long-term loan and must be returned if the recipient moves out of state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 3 and older who have difficulty using a standard telephone due to a disability, including those who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties, and who meet income eligibility criteria (fixed income or recipients of SSA, SSI, SSDI, VA, TDAP, TANF, or pharmacy/medical/housing assistance).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining free assistive telecommunications equipment such as amplified phones, captioned telephones, TTYs, Braille TTYs, large-button phones, photo dial phones, hands-free phones, tablets, and other adaptive devices, as well as free one-on-one evaluations and training to help individuals with disabilities independently make or receive phone calls. Also includes custom solutions based on individual needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Must be a Maryland resident. Equipment must be returned if the recipient moves out of state.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at least 3 years old (applicants under 18 need a parent or legal guardian signature)
Must need adaptive telecommunications equipment due to a disability
Must have difficulty using a standard telephone

Must be certified as Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or having cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties by a licensed physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, rehabilitation counselor, social worker, psychologist, mental health counselor, registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or physical therapist

Must be on a fixed income or receive at least one of the following: Social Security (SSA) benefits, Veterans (VA) benefits, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or pharmacy/medical/housing assistance
Must have or be applying for home phone service, high-speed internet/WiFi
Must submit copy of photo ID and telephone or utility bill
Must submit proof of income eligibility (e.g., SSA Award Letter or benefit documentation)
Must complete the Disability Certification form signed by a qualifying professional
Each applicant or their power of attorney must sign page 3 of the application
Must provide required eligibility documents with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review qualification criteria at mat-apply.org or the MAT program page. 2. Complete the application online at mat-apply.org, download the paper application, or request one by mail or email. 3. Have the Disability Certification Form completed and signed by a licensed physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, rehabilitation counselor, social worker, psychologist, mental health counselor, registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or physical therapist. 4. Enclose required documentation (proof of benefits, photo ID, utility/phone bill). 5. Sign and submit all forms online (with digital signatures), by mail to: State of Maryland – MAT Program, 301 W. Preston St., Suite 1008A, Baltimore, MD 21201, or by email to MAT. A notification letter is mailed approximately two weeks after receipt. If approved, MAT contacts the applicant to schedule a free one-on-one evaluation (virtual or in-person) with a MAT specialist to select appropriate equipment. After the evaluation, equipment is ordered and shipped via UPS within 4–6 weeks. For assistance, call 800-552-7724, 410-767-7253 (Voice/TTY), or 410-801-9618 (Video Phone).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Economic Development Administration (EDA) helps economically distressed communities generate jobs, retain existing jobs, and stimulate industrial and commercial growth. EDA supports strategic investment planning to help communities plan for new technologies, job creation, and enterprise development. It invests in modern infrastructure, local capital markets, and human capital to help distressed areas compete in regional, national, and global markets. TCCWMD also operates a Revolving Loan Fund (RLF), Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) account funding, and Small Business Development Center support through Summit Financing Solutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EDA provides financial and technical assistance to economically distressed communities and areas experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress. Assistance supports physical, financial, and human capital investments including infrastructure, strategic planning, and enterprise development. TCCWMD also operates a Revolving Loan Fund (RLF), Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) account funding, and Small Business Development Center support through Summit Financing Solutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Generally submitted by a deadline in April each year; TCCWMD begins seeking projects in February of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural and urban communities, government agencies, non-profits, municipalities, educational institutions, and businesses in economically distressed areas of Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties) experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements, strategic investment planning, job creation, enterprise development, technology access, capacity building, workforce development, advanced manufacturing, broadband expansion, transportation infrastructure, information technology and innovation, and business development support in economically distressed communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to economically distressed rural and urban areas in Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties), encompassing 24 municipalities within the three counties. Allegany County has been designated by the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) as At-Risk for FY2026.
requirements_list: Located in an economically distressed area experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress
Applicants include government agencies, non-profits, municipalities, and educational institutions
Projects evaluated on degree of need, project evaluation, scope of work, readiness to move forward, cost effectiveness, and leveraged private investment
One-page project request format required as part of submission process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: TCCWMD begins seeking projects in February of each year, when procedures and timelines are established. County Points of Contact (one per county) solicit projects from government agencies, non-profits, municipalities, and educational institutions. TCCWMD provides a format for a one-page project request containing a brief summary and expected funding sources. County evaluates and prioritizes projects using a matrix criteria system (degree of need, project evaluation, scope of work, readiness to move forward, cost effectiveness, leveraged private investment). County rankings are subject to change by public commissioner vote. Ranked lists are generally submitted by a deadline in April to each individual county, then compiled into an annual Investment Package. Contact the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for further information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) 5310 and Senior Rides Programs – Western Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland serves as a Regional Coordinating Body for the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) and distributes Federal Transit Administration funds annually to eligible applicants in Western Maryland through the 5310 and Senior Rides programs. Projects must align with the coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan for the region. The Council provides technical assistance to applicants, reviews and scores 5310 applications, and forwards them to the MTA for consideration. The Council also identifies unmet transportation needs in the region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual federal funding disbursed through the MTA's 5310 and Senior Rides programs to qualifying applicants. The Council provides technical assistance to help applicants prepare transportation-related grant applications and reviews applications for consistency with the regional long-range transportation plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations providing public transit and human services transportation in Western Maryland, including services for seniors, people with disabilities, and those in rural areas outside fixed-route service areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services including paratransit vehicles, long-distance medical transportation, dialysis trips, access to jobs outside standard hours, and related transportation needs in the region.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington Counties, as well as rural parts of Frederick County in Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be derived from the coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan for the Western Maryland region
Applications must be consistent with the regionally adopted long-range transportation plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the MTA 5310 Application or MTA Senior Rides Application (available as downloads on the program page). The Tri-County Council coordinates a local review committee that reviews, scores, and forwards applications to the MTA for final consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Western Maryland Revolving Loan Fund is a pool of money from federal and state sources used to make loans to small businesses in order to create and/or save jobs in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington Counties in Maryland. As borrowers repay loans, the money returns to the fund to finance additional loans, making it a revolving financial tool. The program has operated since 1980 and partners with banks and other lenders to help finance business projects that support business location and expansion in western Maryland's Appalachian region. It supports business acquisition, real estate, equipment, improvements, start-up costs, and working capital. Applications are accepted on a continual basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Summit Financing Solutions)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing loans ranging from $10,000 to $500,000. Interest rate is tied to the prime rate, currently prime plus 1%, with a floor of 5%. Maximum loan terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Application fee is $250 (non-refundable); loans between $10,000–$25,000 require a $25 application fee. Approved borrowers pay a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing (no origination fee for loans $10,000–$25,000). Collateral required includes deeds of trust, machinery and equipment liens, personal guaranties, and key man life insurance. The project must create or retain at least one job per $30,000 of RLF funds requested. Borrowers repay loans, and money is returned to the fund to make additional loans.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ms. Chris Funk, Business Development Loan Officer, Tri County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, non-profits, partnerships, sole proprietorships, and county/municipal governments located in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County, Maryland that need financing to create or retain jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition, commercial real estate acquisition, building improvements, equipment purchase, leasehold improvements, business start-up costs, and working capital. Ineligible uses include real estate speculation, projects that do not create or retain permanent jobs, and projects that qualify for financing through traditional lenders or other programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in western Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit corporation, non-profit organization, partnership, sole proprietorship, or local government entity
Must be located in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County, Maryland
Project must create or retain at least one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested
Must meet standard underwriting criteria including repayment capacity, financial strength of company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral protection
Collateral required: deeds of trust, machinery and equipment liens, personal guaranties, and key man life insurance
Application fee of $250 (non-refundable); $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000
A 1.5% loan origination fee is charged at closing (waived for loans between $10,000–$25,000)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an inquiry form available through Summit Financing Solutions. A non-refundable application fee is required for loan processing. Standard underwriting practices apply. Applications are accepted on a continual basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senator George C. Edwards Fund (Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Senator George C. Edwards Fund, also known as the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, was established in 2022 to help drive economic growth in Western Maryland. It provides grants and loans to support economic development projects that create significant job opportunities or increase the local tax base in Western Maryland's tri-county area of Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants and loans for two types of projects: infrastructure and business development. The minimum award amount is typically $150,000, but the board may consider smaller projects on a case-by-case basis. Infrastructure uses can include broadband connectivity, road access improvements, utility connections, property purchases, and building construction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, or local governments with qualifying economic development projects that will have a major economic impact in Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support capital infrastructure and business development projects. Infrastructure uses can include broadband connectivity, road access improvements, utility connections, property purchases, and building construction. Business development projects must create significant jobs or provide a significant increase to the tax base.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County in Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located in or benefit Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County)
Projects must create new jobs that pay at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage
Infrastructure projects require a minimum 20% match from the local government, the business, or another approved source
Business development projects require a minimum 10% match from the local government, the business, or another approved source
Projects must create significant jobs or provide a significant increase to the tax base
Project must qualify under the fund's criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, first make an inquiry to the Executive Director, a Member of the Board, or the Economic Development Director in the county where the project is located. You may also contact the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team to help determine if your project qualifies and to assist with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Development Housing Rehabilitation Program (Section 504 Home Repair)
structured_extraction.program_description: Also known as the Section 504 Home Repair program, this USDA Rural Development program provides loans to very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes. It also provides grants to elderly very-low-income homeowners to remove health and safety hazards from their homes. The program is available in USDA-eligible rural areas across Maryland, including Wicomico County, and is administered through the USDA Hagerstown Office.

Grants are available to homeowners age 62 or older who cannot repay a repair loan, specifically to remove health and safety hazards. Both forms of assistance are available in USDA-eligible rural areas of Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair, improve, or modernize a home; remove health and safety hazards.

Must be unable to obtain affordable credit elsewhere

structured_extraction.program_description: The Wetlands Reserve Program (WRP) is a voluntary federal program that offers landowners the opportunity to protect, restore, and enhance wetlands on their property. USDA's Natural Resources Conservation Service provides technical and financial support, including payment based on the agricultural value of the land for previously drained or converted wetlands.
structured_extraction.agency: U.S. Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners can enroll under three options: permanent easements, 30-year easements, or 10-year restoration cost-share agreements. Payment is based on the agricultural value of the land. Technical assistance is provided for restoration planning and implementation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with restorable wetlands on their property, particularly those previously drained or converted for agriculture or timber production
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration and enhancement of wetlands on private land; landowner retains ownership and can continue compatible uses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Land must be restorable and suitable for wildlife benefits
For permanent or 30-year easement, must have owned land for at least one year prior to enrollment (with limited exceptions)
For 10-year cost-share agreement, evidence of ownership is required
Wetlands converted after December 23, 1985 are ineligible
Federal lands are ineligible
Land currently enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, or similar programs is ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local USDA Service Center or NRCS office to apply. NRCS helps prepare a restoration plan and enters into a cost-share agreement or easement with the landowner.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Wildlife Habitat Incentives Program (WHIP) is a voluntary USDA program that provides technical assistance and cost-share payments to help landowners develop and improve wildlife habitat primarily on private lands.
structured_extraction.agency: U.S. Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA pays up to 75% of the cost of installing wildlife habitat practices under a cost-share agreement lasting 5 to 10 years. NRCS also provides technical assistance to help prepare and implement a wildlife habitat development plan. Total program budget was $50 million through 2002.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners and those who control private land who want to develop and improve wildlife habitat
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment and improvement of wildlife habitat, including new practices or replacement of failed practices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland; excludes federal lands and lands already enrolled in certain conservation programs
requirements_list: Applicant must own or control the land
Federal land is ineligible
Land enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, Wetlands Reserve Program, or similar programs is ineligible
Land subject to an Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement is ineligible
WHIP funds cannot be used for mitigation or on land designated as converted wetland
Participant must prepare and implement a wildlife habitat development plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local USDA Service Center. NRCS helps participants prepare a wildlife habitat development plan in consultation with the local conservation district. USDA and the participant then enter into a cost-share agreement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education (TEACH) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provides funding to graduate and undergraduate students who plan to teach full time in high-need subject areas at schools serving students from low-income families. Recipients must complete at least 4 years of qualifying teaching service or the grant converts to an unsubsidized loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant for students who commit to teaching full time in high-need subject areas at schools serving low-income families for at least 4 years. If the teaching obligation is not fulfilled, the grant converts to an unsubsidized student loan with interest accruing from the date the grant was paid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Graduate and undergraduate students who intend to teach full time in high-need subject areas at schools serving students from low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Higher education expenses for students pursuing teaching in high-need subject areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a graduate or undergraduate student
Must intend to teach full time in a high-need subject area for at least 4 years
Must teach at a school that serves students from low-income families
Freshmen must have a cumulative high school GPA of 3.25
Continuing students must have a cumulative college GPA of 3.25
Must complete the FAFSA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.ed.gov either electronically or by paper.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program forgives the remaining balance on Direct federal student loans for employees of government or qualifying not-for-profit organizations who have made 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for an eligible employer.
structured_extraction.agency: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgives the remaining balance on Direct federal student loans after the borrower has made the equivalent of 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan while working full-time for an eligible employer (government or qualifying non-profit).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time employees of U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government agencies or qualifying not-for-profit organizations who have Direct federal student loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forgiveness of remaining federal student loan balance (Direct Loans) after 120 qualifying monthly payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of qualifying employers nationwide, including Prince George's County employees in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be employed full-time by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government or qualifying not-for-profit organization
Have Direct Loans (or consolidate other federal student loans into a Direct Loan)
Repay loans under an income-driven repayment plan or a 10-year Standard Repayment Plan
Make a total of 120 qualifying monthly payments (need not be consecutive)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a PSLF form using the PSLF Help Tool at studentaid.gov/pslf: log in with your FSA ID, complete and sign the form digitally, request your employer's digital signature (using HRService@co.pg.md.us for Prince George's County employees), and the form is electronically submitted to the PSLF servicer MOHELA. Alternatively, download and print a paper form, obtain required signatures, and mail, fax, or upload to MOHELA. Certify employment every year and any time you change employers.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rapid rehousing, minimizing trauma and dislocation caused by homelessness, access to mainstream programs, and promoting self-sufficiency

requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit provider or state/local government
Must serve homeless individuals and families
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through local Continuum of Care competitive grant process administered by HUD.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) that provides funding to local, regional, and Tribal communities to support comprehensive efforts aimed at reducing roadway fatalities and serious injuries for all users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and motorists. The program funds development and enhancement of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies. Implementation grants support construction of projects or operational strategies identified in an approved Safety Action Plan, including project feasibility, design, and development. Planning grants fund the development or update of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning activities, road safety audits, and demonstration activities such as quick-build feasibility studies, MUTCD engineering studies, pilot programs for safety behaviors, and pilot projects utilizing innovative technologies like speed cameras or adaptive signal timing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for roadway safety improvements. Two grant types are available: Implementation grants fund construction of projects or operational strategies from an approved Safety Action Plan, as well as project design and development; Planning grants fund development or updating of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning activities, safety audits, and demonstration activities. Emphasizes data-driven, systemwide approaches grounded in the Safe System Approach.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local, regional, and Tribal communities of varying sizes and capacities — including county governments, municipalities/towns, non-profit organizations, and state agencies — seeking to reduce roadway fatalities and serious injuries
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and enhancement of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies to reduce roadway fatalities and serious injuries. Planning grants support Safety Action Plan development, updates, road safety audits, and demonstration activities. Implementation grants fund construction projects, operational safety strategies, and project design and development identified in an approved Safety Action Plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program available to Maryland applicants; county governments, municipalities, non-profits, regional entities, and state government are eligible
requirements_list: Projects must use data-driven, systemwide approaches based on the Safe System Approach
Focus on improving safety outcomes, advancing equitable investments, and supporting innovative, scalable solutions
Implementation grants require an approved Safety Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply by May 26, 2026 for FY 2026. Informational webinars are offered for Action Plans (April 9) and Supplemental Planning and Demonstration Activities (April 14). Consult the NOFO at https://www.transportation.gov/grants/ss4a/fy26-nofo for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Community Air Service Development Program (SCASDP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program that provides funding to help small and underserved communities improve and expand commercial air service. Eligible activities include service subsidies, revenue guarantees, marketing and promotion efforts, and other initiatives to enhance air service availability and affordability at local airports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding; only one application permitted per community. Cost sharing is not required but is viewed favorably. Award amounts vary based on project scope and merit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and underserved communities seeking to improve or expand commercial air service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service subsidies, revenue guarantees, marketing and promotion efforts, and other initiatives to enhance air service availability and affordability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, available to Maryland applicants
requirements_list: Eligible applicants are public entities, including individual communities or consortia
Only one application permitted per community
Cost sharing not required but viewed favorably
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by May 4, 2026. Consult the NOFO for program-specific guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: VA Aid and Attendance Benefits and Housebound Allowance
structured_extraction.program_description: Monthly payments added to an existing VA pension for eligible veterans and survivors who need help with daily activities, are housebound due to a permanent disability, or meet other qualifying medical criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly payments added to an existing VA pension amount. The exact payment amount is not specified on this page. Recipients cannot receive both Aid and Attendance benefits and Housebound benefits at the same time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans and survivors who already receive a VA pension and need help with daily activities, are largely confined to bed due to illness, reside in a nursing home due to disability, have severely limited eyesight, or are housebound due to a permanent disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplemental monthly income to support veterans and survivors who need daily living assistance or are housebound.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must already receive a VA pension

For Aid and Attendance: must meet at least one of — need help with daily activities (bathing, feeding, dressing); spend large portion of day in bed due to illness; be a nursing home patient due to loss of mental or physical abilities; or have severely limited eyesight (5/200 or less in both eyes, or visual field contraction to 5 degrees or less)
For Housebound: must spend most of time at home because of a permanent disability
Cannot receive both Aid and Attendance and Housebound benefits simultaneously
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at va.gov, by mail using VA Form 21-2680 (a medical examiner must complete the examination section), or in person at a VA regional office. Nursing home residents must also submit VA Form 21-0779. Mail applications go to the VA Pension Intake Center, PO Box 5365, Janesville, WI 53547-5365.

structured_extraction.program_name: North American Wetlands Conservation Act Matching Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The North American Wetlands Conservation Act provides federal matching grants to states, private groups, and individuals for wetlands conservation projects. Projects must further the goals of the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and international migratory bird treaties, and must involve public/private partnerships. Grants fund acquisition of land or water rights and restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal matching grants available to acquire land and water rights for restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands. Projects must be consistent with the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and involve public/private partnerships.
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, private groups, and individuals pursuing wetlands conservation projects that further the goals of the North American Waterfowl Management Plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land or water rights, and restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands for migratory birds, fish, and wildlife.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program available in Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must further the goals of the North American Waterfowl Management Plan
Projects must further international migratory bird treaties
Projects must entail public/private partnerships
Matching funds required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, North American Waterfowl and Wetlands Office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partners for Fish and Wildlife Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Partners for Fish and Wildlife Program provides technical and financial assistance to private (non-federal) landowners to voluntarily restore wetlands, streams and river corridors, prairies, grasslands, and other important fish and wildlife habitats. The program offers informal design advice as well as funding for restoration projects under voluntary cooperative agreements. Landowners must agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides technical assistance (design advice) and financial assistance to implement habitat restoration projects on private land under voluntary cooperative agreements requiring 10-year maintenance commitments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private (non-federal) landowners seeking to restore wetlands, streams, native grasslands, and other fish and wildlife habitats on their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoring wetland hydrology, planting native trees and shrubs, installing fencing and off-stream livestock watering, removing exotic species, prescribed burning, streambank revegetation, and in-stream aquatic habitat reconstruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program available in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a private (non-federal) landowner
Landowner must agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years under a voluntary cooperative agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Division of Habitat Conservation, Branch of Habitat Restoration.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Disaster Loan Program (Allegany County Flood)
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest disaster loans to homeowners, renters, businesses, and private nonprofits in Allegany County affected by the May 2025 flooding. Loans can cover repair or replacement of real estate and personal property not fully covered by insurance, as well as economic injury for eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners may borrow up to $500,000 to repair or replace their primary residence and up to $100,000 to replace personal property. Businesses and most private nonprofits may borrow up to $2 million for physical disaster losses. Small businesses and most private nonprofits in the declared disaster area may also apply for an Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL). Repayment terms up to 30 years; terms set based on borrower's ability to repay. Referenced under Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 21, 2025 for physical damage loans; February 23, 2026 for economic injury (EIDL) loans
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, renters, businesses, and private nonprofits in Allegany County affected by the May 2025 flood
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replace damaged primary residences, personal property, or business assets; cover economic injury losses not fully covered by insurance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to applicants located in Allegany County, MD (declared disaster area contiguous to Somerset County, PA)
requirements_list: Must be located in a declared disaster area
Must have sustained damages from flooding
Homeowners and renters must use funds for primary residence or personal property
Businesses may apply for up to $2 million for uninsured disaster losses
Small businesses and private nonprofits may apply for EIDL for economic injury
Applications for physical damage due by July 21, 2025; EIDL applications due by February 23, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the SBA Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955, email DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov referencing PA-20019, or apply online. Deaf/hard-of-hearing callers use 1-800-877-8339.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) – Maryland Drought 2023
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers federal Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations that suffered economic losses due to the drought conditions that began on September 5, 2023 in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) are available to eligible applicants that suffered economic losses due to drought conditions. Applicants should apply under SBA declaration #20069. Applications must be submitted by July 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations with economic losses due to drought conditions in the eligible Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering economic injury losses resulting from drought conditions that began September 5, 2023.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick and Washington counties and the contiguous counties of Allegany, Carroll, Howard, and Montgomery in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small business engaged in aquaculture, or most private nonprofit organizations
Must have suffered economic losses due to drought conditions beginning September 5, 2023
Must apply under SBA declaration #20069
Application must be submitted no later than July 1, 2024
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster under SBA declaration #20069, call the SBA Customer Service Center at 800-659-2955, email DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov, or download and mail a completed application to: U.S. Small Business Administration, Processing and Disbursement Center, 14925 Kingsport Road, Fort Worth, TX 76155.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Program, run by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), certifies eligible small businesses located in designated HUBZone areas for preferential treatment in federal government contracting. Certified businesses gain access to set-aside awards, sole source awards, a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions, and subcontracting opportunities. The federal government targets 3% of all prime contract dollars to HUBZone businesses. In Maryland, designated HUBZone areas include all of Garrett County, certain areas in and around Hagerstown in Washington County, and areas within the City of Frederick in Frederick County. Federal HUBZone contracting was valued at $16.3 billion in Fiscal Year 2022.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUBZone-certified small businesses receive preferential status in federal government contracting, including access to set-aside awards, sole source awards, and a 10% price evaluation preference (PEP) in full and open contract competitions. The federal government has a goal of awarding 3% of all federal prime contract dollars to HUBZone-certified firms. Annual recertification is required, and a program examination is required at least every three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with a principal office in a designated HUBZone area (all of Garrett County qualifies, as do certain areas in and around Hagerstown in Washington County, and areas within the City of Frederick in Frederick County), with at least 35% of employees residing in a HUBZone, and at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or qualifying entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preferential access to federal government contracts — not direct funding. Businesses compete for federal prime contracts and subcontracts with preferential scoring advantages, including set-aside awards, sole source awards, and a 10% price evaluation preference.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated HUBZone areas in Maryland include all of Garrett County, certain areas in and around Hagerstown in Washington County, and areas within the City of Frederick in Frederick County. The principal office must be located in a HUBZone and at least 35% of employees must reside in a HUBZone.
requirements_list: Must qualify as a small business under SBA Size Standards
Principal office must be located in a HUBZone
At least 35% of employees must reside in a HUBZone

Must be at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens, a Community Development Corporation, an agricultural cooperative, an Alaska Native corporation, a Native Hawaiian organization, or an Indian tribe
Must be certified by the SBA before participating
Must recertify annually
Program examination required at least every three years
Must notify SBA if involved in a merger or acquisition or if HUBZone employee residency drops below 20% while performing on a HUBZone contract
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for certification through the SBA. An eligibility workbook tool is available to help applicants organize and present information about their principal office and employee residency — uploading this workbook with the application can help expedite SBA's review. See the SBA's tip sheet for step-by-step certification guidance. The SBA determines eligibility and maintains a listing of qualified HUBZone small businesses for use by federal agencies. Visit https://www.sba.gov/federal-contracting/contracting-assistance-programs/hubzone-program for full instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) Program – Maryland Drought 2025
structured_extraction.program_description: The SBA's Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program provides low-interest federal disaster loans to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations in designated Maryland counties that suffered economic losses from the drought that began March 15, 2025. Loans cover working capital needs even if the business or organization had no physical damage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest disaster loans up to $2 million. Interest rates as low as 4% for small businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits, with repayment terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months after the first loan disbursement. Loan amounts and terms are based on each applicant's financial condition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Feb. 02, 2026 (with a 60-day grace period after the deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations in designated Maryland counties affected by the March 2025 drought. Agricultural producers, farmers, and ranchers are not eligible except for small aquaculture enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital needs caused by the disaster, including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that could not be paid due to the disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Covers Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington counties in Maryland, as well as designated counties in Pennsylvania and Virginia.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, or private nonprofit organization
Must have financial losses directly related to the March 15, 2025 drought disaster
Physical damage to the business or organization is not required
Agricultural producers, farmers, and ranchers are not eligible (except small aquaculture enterprises)
Must be located in a designated disaster declaration county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster, call SBA's Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. Applicants with speech or hearing disabilities may dial 7-1-1 for relay services.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) — Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Businesses can borrow up to $2 million to help cover temporary revenue losses and working capital needs caused by the disaster. Funds can be used for normal operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills that cannot be paid due to the disruption. In-person Business Recovery Centers are available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, long-term loans of up to $2 million to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations overcome temporary loss of revenue and working capital needs resulting from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Funds can be used for normal operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills that cannot be paid due to the disruption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills that cannot be paid due to the disruption; working capital needs during the disaster recovery period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses and qualifying non-profits impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in the Mid-Atlantic region; in-person Business Recovery Centers are available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small business engaged in aquaculture, or a private nonprofit organization
Must have been affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Must demonstrate temporary loss of revenue or economic injury resulting from the collapse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://lending.sba.gov/search-disaster/?disaster=MD-20001 or at sba.gov/disaster, call SBA's Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. In-person Business Recovery Centers are available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County. Application deadline was December 30, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $1.04 million program specific to Maryland and Delaware, funded by offshore wind developer US Wind Inc., that provides eligible coastal commercial fishing captains and vessel operators with funding to enhance safety and navigation equipment or participate in training related to operating in and around the offshore wind energy area (BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490, approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $1.04 million fund specific to Maryland and Delaware. Eligible ocean-going commercial fishing captains and vessel operators (including for-hire/charter vessels) may choose to participate in radar and navigation training or upgrade navigation equipment on their vessels to enhance safety in and around the offshore wind energy area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490). Assistance is delivered via a grant or voucher system. The claim and payment period opens on the Offshore Commercial Operation Date (COD — the date the final turbine is commissioned and the Project is fully operational) and concludes five years following that COD. The NETP will be funded and established no later than 120 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date. The amount was determined based on the eligible number of vessels and individuals and the equipment and vendors preferred by the coastal fishing industries. US Wind will provide annual summary reports on implementation of the voucher system, and the parties will meet annually to review the MOU.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Five years following the Commercial Operation Date (COD) of the Project; COD not yet publicly announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland and Delaware ocean-going commercial fishing captains and vessel operators, including for-hire (charter) recreational fishing vessels, who fish in or around the offshore wind energy area (BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490 east of Ocean City, Maryland). Excludes entities whose primary objectives are litigation, regulatory work, or petitioning activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigation equipment acquisition and upgrades on fishing vessels, radar training, and experiential learning opportunities to enhance safety and navigation in and around the offshore wind energy area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specific to Maryland and Delaware commercial and charter vessels that are directly or reasonably expected to be impacted by the presence of wind turbines in BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490, approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland. The broader Regional Fund serves 11 states (Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina), but NETP is specific to Maryland and Delaware participants.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland or Delaware ocean-going commercial fishing captain or vessel operator, including for-hire (charter) vessels
Must be an eligible vessel or individual as determined by program criteria
Must operate in or around BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490 east of Ocean City, Maryland
Entities whose primary objectives are litigation, regulatory work, or petitioning activities are excluded
Claims must be made no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period during which the loss is alleged to have occurred
Unclaimed NETP funds revert five years after the COD of the Project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The NETP will be administered via a voucher program or system to be established by US Wind no later than 120 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date. The claim and payment period opens on the Commercial Operation Date (COD) and runs for five years. For the most up-to-date information about the Regional Fund Administrator process, visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind page at rfainfo.com. The program is governed by an MOU between Maryland DNR and US Wind Inc. executed May 13, 2025. US Wind must elect which Resilience Fund Option to pursue no later than July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fisheries Compensatory Mitigation – Compensatory Direct Mitigation Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A $5.46 million fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and offshore wind developer US Wind Inc. to provide direct monetary compensation to commercial vessel owners, operators, and crew — regardless of home port — who are impacted by the construction, operation, or decommissioning of US Wind's offshore wind energy project in the Atlantic Ocean off the Delmarva Peninsula. Compensation amounts are based on estimates of vessel revenues derived from historical and current federal and state fishery landings data in the offshore project area. The fund is divided into three project period reserves: Construction Period ($1,546,864), Operations Period ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning Period ($2,014,757). Claims are managed through a Regional Fund Administrator, and funds become available once offshore project construction begins for fishermen who experience and can document an impact. The MOU was executed on May 13, 2025, and also references related components including the Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP), Facility Displacement Component, West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component, and Programmatic Funds Component.
structured_extraction.agency: US Wind Inc. / Maryland Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $5.46 million total fund providing direct monetary compensation to commercial vessel owners, operators, and crew impacted by the construction, operation, or decommissioning of the US Wind offshore wind project off the Delmarva Peninsula. The fund is divided into three project period reserves: Construction Period ($1,546,864), Operations Period ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning Period ($2,014,757). Individual compensation amounts depend in part on past landings from the affected area as determined by historical and current federal and state fishery landings data. Claims must be filed no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period (extendable to five years if data is unavailable or for good cause). Funds become available once offshore project construction begins for fishermen who experience and can document an impact. The MOU was executed May 13, 2025; the Mitigation Fund must be established no later than 120 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date, and the Regional Fund Administrator must be selected at least 60 days prior to that date. The Operations Project Period may be extended by subsequent agreement of the Parties beyond its default five-year term after COD.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and for-hire (charter) vessel owners, operators, and crew — regardless of home port — who have fished in the US Wind offshore wind project area in the Atlantic Ocean off the Delmarva Peninsula (BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490) and are impacted by the project's construction, operation, or decommissioning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct monetary compensation for documented economic losses attributable to the construction, operation, and decommissioning of US Wind's offshore wind energy project. Related components also provide navigation equipment grants/vouchers (NETP), training, facility displacement mitigation, and resilience fund support tied to West Ocean City Harbor operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to commercial vessel owners, operators, and crew regardless of home port who have fished in the US Wind offshore project area (BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490) off the Delmarva Peninsula, approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, MD. Related facility displacement components are geographically focused on the West Ocean City Harbor area (12929 and 12933 South Harbor Road).
requirements_list: Must be a commercial vessel owner, operator, or crew member (or for-hire/charter fishing operator)
Must have fished in the offshore wind project area (BOEM Lease Area OCS-A 0490)
Must have been impacted by the construction, operation, or decommissioning of the US Wind offshore wind project
Must be able to experience and document the impact
Compensation based on past landings from the affected area as determined by historical and current federal and state fishery landings data
Claims must be filed no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period (extendable to five years if data is unavailable or for good cause shown)
Fund is not yet operational — activation is contingent on offshore construction commencement date
Mitigation Fund must be established no later than 120 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date
Regional Fund Administrator must be selected at least 60 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date
MOU executed May 13, 2025; parties revisit MOU annually to ensure proper implementation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claims process details are managed through the MOU (executed May 13, 2025) and Regional Fund Administrator. The Regional Fund Administrator must be selected at least 60 days prior to the Offshore Construction Commencement Date, and the Mitigation Fund must be established no later than 120 days prior to construction commencement. Parties reconvene one year prior to the estimated Offshore Construction Commencement Date to confirm RFA readiness. For the most up-to-date information about the Regional Fund Administrator process, visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind page at rfainfo.com. US Wind's mariners' resources are also available at uswindinc.com/mariners/. No public application window is currently open; the program is pre-operational pending construction commencement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fisheries Compensatory Mitigation – Maryland Multi-Use Resilience Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A $13.5 million fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and offshore wind developer US Wind Inc. to address impacts to fish landing facilities in West Ocean City and support harbor maintenance and associated fishing businesses affected by US Wind's offshore wind energy project. Eligible uses include bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry. Specific timing of fund availability depends on when US Wind begins work on its operations and maintenance facility. Specific funding needs were identified through discussions with local fishing industry representatives. Fund disbursement is triggered by project development phases (construction, operations, decommissioning) and contingent on US Wind's Financial Investment Decision (FID) closing.
structured_extraction.agency: US Wind Inc. / Maryland Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $13.5 million fund available for capital improvements such as bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry. Specific timing of fund availability depends on when US Wind begins work on its operations and maintenance facility in West Ocean City Harbor. Fund disbursement is triggered by project milestones (construction commencement, COD, decommissioning) and is contingent on US Wind's Financial Investment Decision (FID) closing.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Katherine Charbonneau, Assistant Secretary for Aquatic Resources
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial fishing operators, fish landing facilities, harbor businesses, and associated fishing industry participants in the West Ocean City Harbor area impacted by US Wind's offshore wind energy project and operations and maintenance facility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: West Ocean City Harbor, Maryland (Worcester County), specifically 12929 and 12933 South Harbor Road ('Martin' and 'Reese' parcels). Maryland-specific fund focused on West Ocean City Harbor area.
requirements_list: Must be a fish landing facility, harbor business, or fishing industry participant impacted by US Wind's operations and maintenance facility in West Ocean City Harbor
Must be impacted by US Wind's operations and maintenance facility construction in West Ocean City Harbor
Eligible uses must relate to fish landing facilities, harbor maintenance, or associated fishing businesses
Commercial and for-hire recreational fishing industry participants are eligible stakeholders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Details on the claims and distribution process are managed through the MOU. For up-to-date information about the Regional Fund Administrator process, visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind at rfainfo.com. Fund disbursement is triggered by project milestones (construction commencement, COD, decommissioning) rather than a public application window. Claims must be filed no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period, or up to five years after the date of loss if data is not available or for other good cause shown.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Farm Service Agency Emergency Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) provides emergency loans to agricultural producers in federally designated natural disaster areas. Following a drought designation for Carroll County, Maryland, eligible farmers can apply for emergency credit to help recover from losses caused by the disaster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency loans are available to producers recovering from natural disasters. Loans can be used to replace essential items such as equipment or livestock, reorganize a farming operation, or refinance certain debts. FSA reviews loans based on the extent of losses, security available, and repayment ability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers in Carroll County, MD and contiguous counties (Baltimore, Frederick, Howard in MD; Adams and York in PA) affected by drought.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of essential items such as equipment or livestock, reorganization of a farming operation, or refinancing of certain debts.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) is a federal program that helps agricultural producers and rural small businesses reduce energy costs and consumption, and supports the integration of renewable energy technologies into their facilities. Administered by USDA Rural Development, the program provides guaranteed loan financing and grant funding for the purchase or installation of renewable energy systems or energy efficiency improvements. Eligible applicants can receive grants covering up to 25% of eligible project costs. Agricultural producers must earn at least 51% of income from farming or ranching; rural small businesses must be located in areas with populations of 50,000 or fewer. Renewable energy system grants range from a minimum of $2,500 up to $500,000; loans up to $25 million. Energy efficiency improvement grants range from a minimum of $1,500 up to $250,000. Energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants are available up to $100,000 aggregate per recipient. State, Tribal, and local government units, public institutions, rural electric cooperatives, public power entities, and councils may also be eligible for certain grant types.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides guaranteed loan financing and grant funding for the purchase or installation of renewable energy systems or energy efficiency improvements. Grants may cover up to 25% of eligible project costs for qualifying agricultural producers and rural small businesses. Renewable energy system grants range from a minimum of $2,500 up to $500,000; loans range from a minimum of $5,000 up to $25 million. Energy efficiency improvement grants range from a minimum of $1,500 up to $250,000. Energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants available up to $100,000 aggregate per recipient per fiscal year. Eligible renewable energy systems include wind, solar, renewable biomass (including anaerobic digesters), small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from these renewable resources. Combined grant and guaranteed loan applications are also accepted. Federal funding may cover up to 75% of total project costs (grant portion limited to 25%); 25% cost-share required for energy audits.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers who earn at least 51% of income from farming or ranching, and rural small businesses located in areas with populations of 50,000 or fewer, including Maryland farms and small businesses located in rural areas. State, Tribal, and local government units, institutions of higher education, rural electric cooperatives, public power entities, and councils may also be eligible for certain grant types.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or installation of renewable energy systems (including wind, solar, renewable biomass, anaerobic digesters, small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from renewable resources) or energy efficiency improvements where the technology is readily available for purchase. Also covers energy audits and renewable energy development assistance.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility requirements on the USDA Rural Development website. Applications may be submitted to the USDA Rural Development State Office or via grants.gov; applications are competed by submission date and scored per 7 CFR 4280.120, 4280.135, and 4280.192. Contact Bruce Weaver, DE/MD Energy Coordinator, at (302) 857-3629 or bruce.weaver@de.usda.gov for additional questions. Review the Notice of Solicitation for Applications for full details. Guaranteed loans are processed in monthly competitions starting when 8 applications are received. Note: MCEC no longer provides technical assistance for applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, comprehensive training certification program for professional loggers in Maryland. Loggers who complete a series of courses covering best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety/OSHA requirements, and first aid/CPR earn the Maryland Master Logger designation. Certified Master Loggers must complete at least one continuing education course per year to maintain their status. Landowners, foresters, and other interested parties may also attend the courses. Periodic job-site visits may also be conducted to maintain designation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A series of comprehensive training courses for logging professionals. Initial training covers five areas: best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, and logging safety/OSHA. First aid and CPR certification is also required. After initial certification, Master Loggers must attend at least one continuing education course per year to maintain their designation. Most courses cost between $20 and $40. Periodic job-site visits may also be conducted. Continuing education topics include log grading, environmental regulations, trucking safety, and timber estimation.
