structured_extraction.program_description: The Upper Shore Regional Council (USRC) Business Mentoring Program connects small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties with free, confidential, one-on-one mentoring from experienced volunteer business professionals. Whether just starting out or looking to grow, mentors help clients develop business plans, manage finances, plan marketing, identify funding and financing sources, prepare financial documents, register a business, navigate licensing and permits, address customer relations, and tackle ongoing operations and long-range planning challenges. Volunteer mentors bring professional experience across a wide variety of fields and provide guidance tailored to each client's unique goals. All mentoring services are provided at no cost.

All services are provided at no cost and are tailored to the business owner's unique goals.

structured_extraction.program_name: WACIF Small Business Lending and Advisory Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Washington Area Community Investment Fund (WACIF) is a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) that provides flexible loan programs, bonus grant components, and personalized small business advising to entrepreneurs in the Washington, D.C. metro area, with a focus on low- and moderate-income and underserved communities. Three loan products are available: (1) Term Loans ($10,000–$250,000) with terms of 3 to 6 years at competitive fixed interest rates, no minimum credit score, and no prepayment penalties — proceeds may be used for operations, inventory, working capital, equipment, or renovations; fees include an origination fee (up to 3%), a $50 application fee, and late payment fees; (2) the Green Growth Loan for sustainable upgrades or operations, including a bonus grant component; and (3) the Resilience Growth Loan for businesses navigating recovery or growth, including a bonus grant component. WACIF takes a flexible, character-based approach to lending and can assist businesses with limited or poor credit that may not qualify for traditional bank financing. Businesses must have been operating for at least one year and have generated at least $50,000 in revenue in the last fiscal year for Term Loans. In addition to lending, WACIF provides personalized small business advising, one-on-one technical assistance, post-loan annual check-ins, and referrals to advisors throughout the application process and beyond. Prospective clients complete a brief intake form or prequalification self-assessment, and a dedicated small business advisor contacts them to discuss needs and develop goals for the consultation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three loan products are available: (1) Term Loans ranging from $10,000 to $250,000 with terms of 3 to 6 years at competitive fixed interest rates, no minimum credit score requirement, and no prepayment penalties — proceeds may be used for equipment purchases, inventory, working capital, or renovations; fees include an origination fee (up to 3%), a $50 application fee, and late payment fees; (2) Green Growth Loan supporting sustainable upgrades or operations with a bonus grant component; (3) Resilience Growth Loan providing capital for businesses navigating recovery or growth with a bonus grant component. Collateral is evaluated on a case-by-case basis; personal guarantees and business assets are required. Post-loan technical assistance, annual check-ins, and referrals to advisors are also provided. In addition, WACIF offers personalized small business advising and one-on-one technical assistance for low- and moderate-income entrepreneurs before and during the application process.

For-profit businesses and qualifying non-profits (including child care centers) that have been in business at least 1 year with annual revenue of $50,000 or more are prioritized for Term Loans. Also serves businesses that may not qualify for conventional bank loans.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three components: (1) Real Property Tax Credit — a ten-year credit against local real property taxes on the increased assessed value of improvements, starting at 80% in years 1–5 and stepping down to 30% in year 10. Applies to both City and County property taxes for properties in Hagerstown. The State reimburses local jurisdictions 50% of lost revenue. Must apply before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits. Minimum investment thresholds apply: $5,000 investment or 1 new job in City Center (CC-MU zoning); $50,000 investment or 5 new jobs outside City Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: Nearly 1,800 acres of industrial and commercial properties in Washington County, Maryland are located within Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) #255. Businesses operating in the FTZ can defer, reduce, or eliminate customs duties on imports and benefit from exemptions on state and local taxes for goods held for export. The zone is strategically located near major transportation corridors (I-81 and I-70), providing access to major markets and enabling streamlined supply chains and improved competitiveness in international trade. Imports may enter and be held in the FTZ without customs duties; duties are not paid on merchandise re-exported, on labor/overhead/profit from FTZ operations, or on inbound zone-to-zone transfers. Tangible personal property held for export is exempt from state and local ad valorem taxes.

These benefits help minimize supply chain costs and improve competitiveness in international trade.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program offering 3 to 15 years of credits on the county portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that expand, relocate, or locate in Washington County and increase employment. Three tiers are available based on square footage acquired, new jobs created, and capital investment levels: Tier 1 (existing business, 3-year credits at 55%/40%/25%) for businesses adding new/expanded space and at least 1 new full-time job; Tier 2 (new business, 6-year credits at 55%/55%/40%/40%/25%/25%) for businesses adding 2,500+ sq ft and 5+ new full-time employees within 24 months; Tier 3 (new or existing business, 15-year credits at 75% for the first 5 years then declining 5% annually to 25%) for businesses investing $10M+ and creating 100+ new full-time jobs. The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Washington County. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible. Applications must be submitted before construction is complete, and annual employment reports are required to maintain the credit. Program effective July 1, 2025.

Credit period ranges from 3 to 15 years depending on tier. If property is leased, the lessor must reduce the lessee's contractual tax liability by the credit amount. structured_extraction.program_name: Agricultural Land Preservation District / Agricultural Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners in Washington County voluntarily agree not to develop their agricultural land for ten years and commit to remaining in agricultural related pursuits. In return, they are enrolled in a designated Agricultural Preservation District, receive protection from nuisance complaints under the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program (MALPP/MALPF), and receive a real property tax credit against Washington County real property taxes based on the assessed value of qualified agricultural land and improvements, as established by the Washington County Agricultural Real Property Tax Credit Ordinance. The credit takes effect for the tax year immediately following application and approval. Early termination results in back taxes being assessed. The County also encourages enrolled landowners to apply to MALPF for a permanent agricultural preservation easement.

The credit takes effect for the tax year immediately following application and approval. Landowners also receive protection under the Right to Farm Ordinance and become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through MALPP/MALPF. Early termination results in back taxes being assessed.

requirements_list: Landowner voluntarily agrees not to develop land for ten years (renewable in five-year increments)
Owner must commit to remain in agricultural related pursuits for ten years
Land must be agricultural
Property must be located within a designated agricultural preservation district
Minimum of 50 acres, or 20 acres if contiguous to qualifying land
At least 50% of soils must be of soil classes I through III
Land must be outside water/sewer service areas and outside designated growth areas
Soil conservation plan must be implemented within 10 years of enrollment
Land must be kept in agricultural use; no commercial, industrial, or residential use except as permitted by regulations
No subdivision, off-conveyance, or boundary-line movement without written County approval
No non-agricultural structures unless County approves
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Ag District Intake Form (collecting owner information, property details, acreage, soil characteristics, and operational structure) and the District Agreement, then submit to the Washington County Land Preservation Office (Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning). The County reviews the application, executes the Agreement, and records it in the Land Records. Contact the Washington County Planning Department at (240) 313-2430 for assistance. The tax credit is processed by the Washington County Treasurer's Office following application and approval. The County also encourages enrolled landowners to apply to MALPF for a permanent agricultural preservation easement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Accelerates land preservation easement purchases by allowing qualifying agricultural landowners to sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement to Washington County, with payment made over ten years via an Installment Purchase Agreement (IPA) at a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement on their contiguous acreage (less one acre per existing dwelling). Payment is made via a ten-year Installment Purchase Agreement: 10% of principal paid at settlement plus annual interest, then 10% of principal plus interest paid annually for nine more years. The interest rate is fixed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who meet minimum qualifications and wish to sell development rights to the County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent agricultural preservation easement purchased by the County from qualifying landowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Land must meet minimum qualifications for agricultural use
Easement covers entire contiguous acreage minus one acre per existing dwelling
Payment made over 10-year Installment Purchase Agreement
Program is competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply to the Washington County Land Preservation Office. If accepted, an Installment Purchase Agreement is negotiated between the County and the landowner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for water and wastewater bills to low-income households experiencing hardship paying their water bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Benefits to help low-income households cover water and wastewater utility bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households experiencing hardship paying water and wastewater bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of water and wastewater utility bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a low-income household
Must be experiencing hardship with water bills
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/low-income-household-water-assistance-program/ or schedule an appointment at Washington County Department of Social Services (122 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown, MD 21740, 240-420-2100) or Washington County Community Action Council (117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740, (301) 797-4161).

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Gaming Commission Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Washington County Gaming Commission administers grants funded by the Washington County Gaming Fund, which is supported by tip jar (pull-tab) gaming revenues collected within the county. The seven-member Commission reviews applications annually and has sole authority to approve grants in accordance with state statute and county regulations. Nonprofit and community organizations can apply for funding to support their programs and services. Applications are scored using a scoring rubric. Each April, the Gaming Commission Grant applications are released for the annual funding cycle. Maximum award is $100,000 per application. The performance period is one year from the award announcement; unspent funds must be returned.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Grant Management / Washington County Gaming Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded from the Washington County Gaming Fund, supported by tip jar (pull-tab) gaming revenues collected within the county. Maximum award is $100,000 per application. Performance period is one year from award announcement; unspent funds must be returned. Applications are scored using a scoring rubric covering Statement of Need (20 pts), Program Plan (20 pts), Advance Project Preparation (5 pts), Past Performance (5 pts), Collaborations (10 pts), and Project Funding (5 pts).
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations and unincorporated associations located in Washington County, Maryland, including homeless shelters, food pantry distribution sites, booster organizations (with restrictions), and other nonprofit community organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used exclusively within Washington County to support: Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, and educational and cultural activities. Eligible expenses include operating expenses and equipment or capital projects. Indirect costs are capped at 15% of direct costs; salaries and fringe benefits are eligible if position and rate are identified. Funds must be used for the purpose for which they were requested; unspent funds must be returned. Real property and distributions outside Washington County are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in Washington County, Maryland, or have a place of business within Washington County. All funds must be used exclusively within Washington County and cannot be distributed outside the County.
requirements_list: Organization must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization or unincorporated association
Organization must be located in or have a place of business in Washington County, Maryland
All funds must be used exclusively within Washington County
Complete application packet must be submitted by April 30, 2026 at 3:00 p.m.

Incomplete applications will not be reviewed
Applications are scored using a scoring rubric
Organizations that received Gaming Funds in FY25 must submit a gaming grant report by June 30, 2026
Applicant must provide proof that distributed funds were used for the purpose for which they were requested
Funds not used for the stated purpose must be restored
Complete application with required signatures and attachments
Concise, thorough statement of need with substantial community impact
Detailed program plan describing function and beneficiaries
Evidence of advance project preparation (permits, preliminary work)
Track record of past performance with county funds
Letters of support from partner organizations
One-time project (not recurring funding ask)
Demonstrated organizational capacity and staffing
Clear, detailed budget narrative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the full application packet from the Washington County website. Packets are made available online each April (April 1, 2026 for the 2026 cycle). Submit completed application as electronic .pdf via email and 6 hard copies (one with original signature) to the Grant Management office (100 West Washington Street, Suite 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740) by April 30, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. A funding hearing is held in June (June 9, 2026 for the 2026 cycle) and award announcements are made in August. An informational workshop was offered on April 6, 2026 via Zoom.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program administered locally by Washington County's Office of Grant Management. It supports projects in Appalachian communities across five goal areas: economic development and entrepreneurship, workforce readiness and health, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater), natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Washington County collects preliminary proposals each spring, ranks them, and forwards top projects to the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking before eligible projects advance to a formal ARC application.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants require a 50% match from the applicant; matching funds must be identified and committed at the time of application, with commitment letters required for all committed matching funds. If funds are pending other grants, anticipated award dates must be provided. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. The review committee may reduce funding amounts. Grant amounts are not specified on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities in Washington County seeking funding for community and economic development projects in Appalachian communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic and business development, workforce education and health improvements, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater), natural and cultural asset development, and leadership and community capacity building. Eligible project types include technology development, broadband, education and workforce development, tourism, energy, recovery ecosystems, and traditional infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible entities in Washington County, Maryland (an Appalachian region county). The program focuses on Maryland's Appalachian counties in alignment with ARC's regional priorities.
requirements_list: 50% matching funds required and must be identified and committed at time of application
Commitment letters required for all matching funds with 'committed' status
If matching funds are pending other grants, anticipated award dates must be provided
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
Submit Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management
Projects will be reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners before regional submission
Organizational capacity narrative required
Project description required
Goals/objectives must be aligned to ARC Investment Goal and State Objective/Strategy
Quantifiable performance measures with timeframes required
Proposed funding sources/amounts required
Projects must be consistent with ARC Strategic Goals and Objectives (2024-2028)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management (by email to Maria Kramer). 2. Projects are reviewed and ranked by the Washington County Commissioners. 3. County-ranked projects are submitted to the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. 4. Top-ranked projects receive an invitation letter in early Fall to submit a formal grant application to ARC, due in November.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County's Community Organization Funding program provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that improve the community and quality of life for county residents. Each year, the Board of County Commissioners determines the allocation set aside for the fund. The Office of Grant Management administers the application, award process, and oversight of grantees. The program uses a prioritized approach to funding local nonprofits based on specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding for charitable organizations on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws). The annual allocation amount is determined each year during the county budgeting process. A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is sent to eligible organizations specifying procedures, opening dates, and closing dates. Applications are only accepted within the published application window.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable nonprofit organizations on Washington County's Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108) that provide services improving the community and quality of life for Washington County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must operate within Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Organization must be on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Applications are only accepted during the published application window specified in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)
Written letter of request from organization
Copy of IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Proof that organization is active and in good standing with Maryland Business Express
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is sent to all organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List each funding cycle. The NOFA provides procedures, opening dates, and closing dates. Applications may be submitted by mail to 100 West Washington Street, Suite 1101, Hagerstown, MD 21740 or by email. Organizations not yet on the 1-108 list must first apply to be added before being eligible for the next funding cycle by reviewing the 1-108 List Application Check List or contacting the County Attorney's Office at countyattorneyoffice@washco-md.net.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created to assist eligible local nonprofit organizations in Washington County that were impacted by the COVID-19 health emergency. Funded with $1,500,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, the program provides awards of up to $40,000 to nonprofits that can demonstrate financial impact such as decreased revenue, increased costs, or downsizing of staff and services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of up to $40,000 per eligible organization. Total program funding is $1,500,000 in ARPA funds.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs, revenue losses, and capacity needs resulting from the COVID-19 health emergency, including decreased revenue, financial insecurity, increased costs, and staff/service reductions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application along with required documents and the financial budget template by the deadline. Questions can be submitted to the program email address.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County offers a tax credit against County real property taxes for the rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation of designated historic properties. The credit equals 10% of the owner's qualifying restoration or preservation expenses for existing historic structures, or 5% for new construction attached to an existing historic structure, up to the total amount of County real estate taxes owed. Unused credits may be carried forward up to five tax years. Eligible properties must be located within a Washington County Historic Preservation District, the Antietam Overlay zone (AO1 or AO2), be a contributing structure in a surveyed Historic Rural Village, be under a Maryland Historical Trust easement, or be designated as a historic site on the Washington County master plan for historic preservation. The program is governed by Ordinance 2024-23 and work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines. The county credit may be stackable with state (20%) and federal (20%) historic tax credits, potentially reaching up to 70% combined.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 10% of qualifying restoration/preservation expenses for existing historic structures, or 5% for new construction attached to a historic structure, up to the total amount of County real estate taxes owed. Unused credits carry forward up to 5 years. The county credit may be stackable with state (20%) and federal (20%) historic tax credits, potentially reaching up to 70% combined. Applications are submitted in three parts with supporting expense documentation to the Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning / Historic District Commission. Part II approval is required before work begins; Part III is submitted after project completion with invoices, receipts, proof of payment, and photographs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application for credit must be submitted before work starts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners of historic sites or properties within qualifying historic districts, overlay zones, or Historic Rural Villages designated in Washington County, including individual owners, for-profit, and non-profit entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation of historic structures (Qualified Rehabilitation Expenses); or new construction attached to an existing historic structure. Eligible expenses must be itemized with invoices, receipts, and proof of payment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a Washington County Historic Preservation District, the Antietam Overlay zone (AO1 or AO2), be a contributing structure in a surveyed Historic Rural Village (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton), be under a Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) easement, be in an eligible municipality with appropriate zoning and design guidelines, or be designated as a historic site on the Washington County master plan for historic preservation. Property must also be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a qualifying area: Historic Preservation District, Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2), contributing structure in a Historic Rural Village, under MHT easement, or designated on the master plan for historic preservation in Washington County
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must qualify as rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation of a historic structure (or new construction attached to a historic structure)
Work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must comply with Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Work must comply with applicable zoning, building, and safety codes
Work must comply with Federal, State, and local licensing, permitting, and environmental requirements
Part II (pre-approval of rehabilitation plan) must be approved by the Historic District Commission before work begins
Application must be submitted in three parts (Part I: qualification; Part II: pre-approval; Part III: post-completion certification with expense sheet)
Supporting documentation required: itemized expenses with invoices/receipts and proof of payment (credit card receipt or cancelled check), and photographs of completed work
The credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following completion of qualifying work
Unused credits may be carried forward up to five tax years
HDC reserves the right to inspect property up to 5 years after project completion and may revoke certification if work diverges from approved scope
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a three-part application to the Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning / Historic District Commission: Part I establishes qualification of the historic structure and its location within an eligible area; Part II documents the proposed rehabilitation work and must be approved by the HDC before any work begins; Part III is submitted after project completion and includes an itemized expense sheet with invoices, receipts, proof of payment, and photographs of completed work. Application forms and directions are available on the Historic District Commission page. Contact the department at askplanning@washco-md.net or (240) 313-2430 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ride Assist Program provides subsidized transportation vouchers to elderly residents (age 60+) and individuals with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses. Eligible participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate and use them to pay registered taxi providers for rides, saving at least 50% on taxi fares.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible participants purchase a set number of transportation vouchers per month at a reduced rate, saving at least 50% on taxi fares. Vouchers come in multiple denominations and expire June 30 of each year. Vouchers cannot be used for tipping.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications expire June 30 of every year; must reapply annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County residents age 60 or older, and individuals with disabilities who cannot use the fixed-route bus system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment to registered transportation providers (taxi) for rides.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible residents of Washington County, Maryland. Service area covers Washington County Transit's service territory.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older, OR have a qualifying disability that prevents use of fixed-route buses
Applicants under age 60 must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging their disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Applications must be submitted by mail or in person (faxes not accepted)
Vouchers expire June 30 of each year; program participation must be renewed annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the WCT office at 240-313-2750 to request a mailed application, or pick one up in person at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD. Complete the application (healthcare professional certification required if applicant is under 60). Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office. Applicants are notified by mail of eligibility. Vouchers may then be purchased at the WCT office or by mail using check, money order, or credit card.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County real property tax credit available to surviving spouses or family members of fallen heroes — including law enforcement officers, correctional officers, judicial officers, fire and rescue personnel, and emergency medical service personnel killed in the line of duty. The credit reduces Washington County real property taxes owed on qualifying real estate; it does not apply to state or municipal taxes. Annual renewal is available after the initial application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit on qualifying Washington County real estate taxes only (not applicable to state or municipal taxes) for eligible surviving spouses or family members of fallen heroes (law enforcement officers, correctional officers, judicial officers, fire and rescue personnel, and emergency medical service personnel killed in the line of duty). Annual renewal is available after initial application. Authorized under Section 9-210, Tax Property Article, Annotated Code of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses or family members of fallen heroes — including law enforcement officers, correctional officers, judicial officers, fire and rescue personnel, and emergency medical service personnel killed in the line of duty — who own real property in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Washington County real property tax liability only; not applicable to state or municipal taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. Credit applies to Washington County real estate taxes; other jurisdictions' taxes are excluded.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a surviving spouse or family member of a fallen hero (law enforcement officer, correctional officer, judicial officer, fire and rescue personnel, or emergency medical service personnel killed in the line of duty)
Must qualify as a fallen hero or surviving family member as defined in the program ordinance (Section 9-210, Tax Property Article, Annotated Code of Maryland)
Must own real property (principal residence or other qualifying property) in Washington County
Certificate of death required at initial application
Documentation of loss of life in line of duty required
Proof of employment/active service status at time of death required
Must submit the Washington County Real Property Tax Credit for Fallen Heroes Application (annual renewal available after initial application)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Washington County Real Property Tax Credit for Fallen Heroes Application form and submit to the Washington County Treasurer's Office. Required documentation includes certificate of death, documentation of loss of life in the line of duty, and proof of employment/active service status at time of death. The application form is available on the Treasurer's Office website. Annual renewal is available after initial application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizen Supplement – Homeowners Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County supplement to the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit that eases the property tax burden on homeowners age 65 and over who meet income qualifications. Effective July 1, 2012. The supplement may significantly increase the overall tax credit received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supplements the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for eligible seniors. The credit reduces the amount by which State and County property taxes exceed a percentage of the homeowner's combined income. Under the State formula, the first $8,000 of income is excluded; Washington County's supplement may significantly increase the overall credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 of each year (same as State program)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County homeowners age 65 and over who meet income qualifications
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Washington County real property taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, MD; must be owner-occupied residential property
requirements_list: Must be age 65 or over
Must meet income qualifications
Must be a homeowner of an owner-occupied residential property in Washington County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the State's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Application Form HTC-60. Eligibility for both the Washington County credit and State credit is determined by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real estate property tax credit for Washington County homeowners classified as 1% to 100% service-connected disabled American veterans and their surviving spouses. The credit amount equals the percentage of Washington County property tax equal to the disabled veteran's service-connected disability rating percentage. The disability must be service-connected, not incurred through misconduct, permanent in character, and reasonably certain to continue throughout life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real estate property tax credit for qualifying disabled veterans and surviving spouses. The credit amount equals the percentage of Washington County property tax equal to the disabled veteran's service-connected disability rating percentage (e.g., 50% disability rating = 50% property tax credit). Two tracks: disabled veteran (active) and surviving spouse (upon veteran's death).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real estate property taxes on the veteran's or surviving spouse's primary dwelling house in Washington County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland properties only
requirements_list: Must be a Washington County homeowner
Must be classified as a 1%–100% service-connected disabled American veteran, or unremarried surviving spouse of a deceased disabled veteran
Disability must be service-connected and not incurred through misconduct
Disability must be permanent in character and reasonably certain to continue throughout life

Must obtain certification from the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
Property must be primary residence (for surviving spouse track)
Surviving spouse must be unremarried
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Veterans Credit Application form (available on the Washington County website). The application requires a three-step process: (1) property owner/veteran completes the applicant section, (2) Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs (410-230-4444) verifies the disability rating and forwards certification, (3) completed form is returned to the Washington County Treasurer's Office (240-313-2110) for tax credit processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership of Maryland state agencies, the Chesapeake Bay Trust, University of Maryland Sea Grant Extension, University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center, NOAA, and the EPA that provides coordinated technical assistance and capacity-building services to local communities to support watershed protection and restoration activities in Maryland. Services include planning and design grants, project management assistance, stormwater financing support, and training opportunities. The program connects and coordinates various resources and technical assistance available across the state to local governments, nonprofits, universities, and community groups. Five Regional Watershed Restoration Specialists provide on-the-ground assistance to communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Watershed Assistance Collaborative (Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake Bay Trust, and partners)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Collaborative offers coordinated capacity-building services including planning and design grants (through the Chesapeake Bay Trust), project management and coordination assistance (through Maryland Sea Grant), stormwater financing and watershed plan development support (through the Maryland Environmental Finance Center), and training for local government staff (through Maryland's Coastal Training Program). Additional non-financial assistance includes services, technical assistance/information, and project management support. Five Regional Watershed Restoration Specialists provide on-the-ground assistance to communities across Eastern Shore, Central MD, Mid- and Upper Shore, Southern MD, and Northern Maryland regions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profits, universities, and community groups in Maryland seeking to implement watershed protection and restoration projects, including county governments, municipalities/towns, state colleges, and state agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed protection and restoration activities, non-point source pollution reduction, stormwater financing, watershed planning, design and program development, project management assistance, capacity building for local implementers, and stakeholder outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
requirements_list: Community must be interested in undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities
Must fill out the Request for Resources and Services Form to access services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Request for Resources and Services Form on the website to access technical assistance and services. For grant information, visit cbtrust.org. Contact Carrie Decker by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: WesBanco offers a Federal Relief Loan to help federal employees and their families facing financial challenges during the federal government shutdown. The loan is unsecured, up to $5,000, with an 18-month repayment period, up to 90 days before the first payment (45 days in PA), a 7.00% APR (as of October 2, 2025), and no loan or closing fees.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General emergency/relief funds for federal employees and families facing financial hardship due to the government shutdown; no stated restrictions on use.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply over the phone by calling 800-905-9043, in-person at any WesBanco location, or visit WesBanco's website for additional information on applying and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows employers to train a worker at the actual job location before hiring them. For six weeks, the Western Maryland Consortium covers all costs including wages, workers' compensation, and taxes for the worker to train full-time. After the training period, the employer agrees to hire the employee permanently pending satisfactory evaluation. In some cases, Work Experience can be combined with On-the-Job Training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Consortium pays all costs — wages, workers' compensation, and taxes — for a worker to train at the employer's location for six weeks at no cost to the employer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington Counties seeking to evaluate and train workers before hiring
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers wages, workers' compensation, and taxes for a trainee for six weeks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany, Garrett, and Washington Counties in Maryland
requirements_list: Worker must be eligible through the Western Maryland Consortium
Training lasts six weeks
Employer agrees to hire the employee permanently pending satisfactory evaluation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Western Maryland Consortium at 301-334-8136 for eligibility and enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Wicomico County tax credit for hotel and multifamily residential development projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit for hotel and multifamily residential development. Full details are contained in Legislative Bill 2021-02.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants and loans to owner-occupied homes in Worcester County for general rehabilitation and lead abatement. It helps low- to moderate-income homeowners bring their homes up to the County's Minimum Livability Code. Priority is given to senior citizens, people with disabilities, families with extremely low income, and homes with safety or health hazards.
structured_extraction.agency: Worcester County Department of Development, Review and Permitting
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover general rehabilitation and lead abatement for qualifying owner-occupied homes. Grant terms are 5–15 years with no repayment unless the property is sold or refinanced during the grant period; grants are secured with a recorded property lien. Lead abatement grants have no minimum term and no repayment if the home is sold or refinanced, though a 10% match is required if family income is over 80% of median. Loans are available to low- to moderate-income homeowners at interest rates between 0% and 7%, scaled to the family's ability to repay; loans may be fully deferred, with the full balance due when the property is sold or transferred.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of homes in Worcester County, with priority given to senior citizens, people with disabilities, and families with extremely low income
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General home rehabilitation to meet the County's Minimum Livability Code, and lead abatement services. Up to 40% of loan-funded work may be cosmetic in nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in rural areas or any incorporated township of Worcester County, Maryland. Lead abatement grants require the home to be in an eligible census tract.
requirements_list: Homeowner must occupy the dwelling as their principal residence
Homeowner may not own other houses or properties
Dwelling must have conditions that do not meet the County's Minimum Livability Code (for general rehabilitation grants)
Mobile homes are only eligible if secured on a permanent block or brick foundation and not located in a mobile home park
Property taxes must be paid in full at time of application
Homeowner must have acceptable credit or be willing to set up payment plans on non-medical collection accounts; judgments must be paid in full
Current or retired Worcester County employees, their immediate families, or individuals holding contracts with Worcester County are generally ineligible for grant assistance
For lead abatement grants: family must be extremely low income or have insufficient funds for loan payments, or abatement cost must exceed dwelling's assessed value; home must be structurally sound
For loans: family must be of low to moderate income
Homes assisted with grants may only receive grant funding once
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Special Loans Rehabilitation Application from the Worcester County website and submit it to the program administrator. The same application is used for all grant and loan programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) Septic Upgrade Program helps Worcester County property owners upgrade their onsite septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal. The goal is to reduce nutrients flowing into the Chesapeake Bay. The program prioritizes failing systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (CBCA) and Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area (MCBCA), but other systems may also be eligible depending on funding availability. Grant funds can also be used to abandon an existing septic system and connect to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal (ENR). Households with income under $300,000 qualify for a 100% grant; households with income at or above $300,000 qualify for a 50% grant.
structured_extraction.agency: Worcester County Department of Environmental Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds cover up to 100% of the cost and installation of a BAT nitrogen-removal unit plus two years of maintenance for households with income under $300,000; households with income at or above $300,000 are eligible for a 50% grant. Income is verified via federal tax return. Funds may not be used for drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners), pump systems, electrical, grading, or for permit or recordation fees. Funding eligibility for residential properties is based on homeowner income. Funds are prioritized by system type and location, with failing systems in the CBCA/MCBCA receiving the highest priority.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Worcester County property owners with septic systems, particularly those with failing systems or systems located within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area or Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost and installation of a BAT nitrogen-removal unit plus two years of maintenance and inspection. Can also be used to abandon an existing septic system and connect to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal. Cannot be used for drainfield costs (except qualifying low-income owners), pump systems, electrical, grading, or permit/recordation fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Worcester County property owners. Highest priority given to properties within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (CBCA) and Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area (MCBCA), defined as property within 1,000 feet of mean high tide.
requirements_list: Must be a Worcester County property owner
Must submit application form and proof of income (verified via latest federal tax return)
Household income under $300,000 qualifies for 100% grant; household income at or above $300,000 qualifies for 50% grant
Must allow Department of Environmental Programs access for an initial site inspection
If approved, must sign and record a BAT Agreement to maintain the BAT system with a qualified operator for as long as the septic system is in use
Must allow periodic county onsite inspections to ensure BAT unit is operating satisfactorily
Property owner is responsible for annual O&M contracts after the initial 2-year grant-funded maintenance period
Properties with access to public sewer may be denied and required to connect to the public system instead
Sites with holding tanks only considered if a viable soil-based disposal area can be identified
The BRF Program no longer funds non-field-verified systems for installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download, complete, and submit the application form (PDF) to the Department of Environmental Programs by mail, fax, or email. The department will review the application, assess public sewer availability, and conduct an initial site inspection if the application is approved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Zanvyl and Isabelle Krieger Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Krieger Fund awards grants to nonprofit organizations doing direct service and/or advocacy work (non-lobbying) in Baltimore, with a focus on affordable housing and community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, and support for families with children from birth to three years old. Most grants range from $2,500 to $25,000 per year. Grants are awarded twice a year following Board of Directors meetings in June and December, with applications due March 1 (for the June meeting) and September 1 (for the December meeting). Organizations may reapply each year but cannot apply in back-to-back grant cycles.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants typically range from $2,500 to $25,000 per year. Grants are awarded twice a year following Board of Directors meetings in June and December; complete applications are due March 1 (for the June meeting) and September 1 (for the December meeting). No multi-year commitments; organizations may reapply annually but not in consecutive grant cycles. All grant funds must be used for direct program expenses — no overhead, indirect costs, endowments, capital campaigns, special events, or publications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations doing direct service and/or advocacy (non-lobbying) work in Baltimore focused on affordable housing and community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, or families with children from birth to three years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct service and/or advocacy (non-lobbying) program expenses in the focus areas of affordable housing/community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, and support for families with young children (birth to age three). Cannot be used for endowments, overhead/indirect costs, capital or annual campaigns, special events, or publications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Work must be focused in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Organization must work in one or more of the fund's focus areas: affordable housing/community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, or families with children from birth to three years old
Work must be direct service and/or advocacy (non-lobbying)
All grant funds must be used for direct program expenses
No overhead or indirect costs for large organizations or academic institutions
Organizations may apply once per year
Organizations may not apply in back-to-back grant cycles

First-time applicants must submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) addressing the organization's mission, community issue addressed, approach, partnerships, ecosystem fit, evidence of impact, requested dollar amount, organizational budget with current funding sources, and a list of current board members
Returning applicants submit renewal proposals via Google form
Complete grant applications are due March 1 (June board meeting) or September 1 (December board meeting)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants submit a brief Letter of Intent (LOI) by email to Jen Eames (jeames@associated.org). Renewal applicants submit proposals using a Google form that combines the cover letter, final report, and narrative; all supplemental documents are uploaded with the form. Applicants applying to both the Krieger Fund and Fund for Change use a separate Google form. Grants are awarded at Board meetings held in June and December.
